The project originated in Birmingham in the early 1990s while Skinner was a teenager, though no music was released until the early 2000s. During its initial run, five studio albums were issued: Original Pirate Material (2002), A Grand Don't Come for Free (2004), The Hardest Way to Make an Easy Living (2006), Everything Is Borrowed (2008), and Computers and Blues (2011). A number of singles reached the UK Top 40, with notable tracks including Has It Come to This?, Fit but You Know It, Dry Your Eyes, the group's only number-one single, When You Wasn't Famous, and Prangin Out. The Streets disbanded in 2011, with Skinner pursuing other projects before reviving the act in 2017. A 2020 mixtape, None of Us Are Getting Out of This Life Alive, followed, and the sixth studio album, The Darker the Shadow the Brighter the Light, was released in September 2023.
One principal drawback associated with cock rings is that adding additional accessories can increase the likelihood of discomfort. Moreover, the device can cause cold sensations for the user.

A cock ring is a device worn at the base of the penis. Its primary function is to restrict venous blood flow, which helps produce a stronger erection. It can also augment girth and extend the duration of an erection. In some cases, it is used as a medical device to address erectile dysfunction, either on its own or in combination with a penis pump. Additionally, it is sometimes used for genital adornment or repositioning to enhance appearance.

Elias Kane's body was initially returned to the family farm in Randolph County, Illinois, but, because the gravesite was repeatedly desecrated, he was reinterred in 1984 at Evergreen Cemetery in Chester, Illinois, in a grave adjacent to Shadrach Bond, Illinois's first governor and a sometime political opponent. The Kane family gravesite includes his wife Frances Pelletier (1799–1851), two children who died young, and four sons, among them Elias Kent Kane, Jr. (1822–1853), who served in the United States Army. One of Kane's daughters married Illinois governor William H. Bissell, a vocal opponent of slavery. Kane's father, also named Elias Kane, is buried in Congressional Cemetery in Washington, D.C. The elder Kane survived his son by five years and secured admission to West Point for his namesake grandson.

Elias Kane was an American political figure in early Illinois who, in 1820, mounted an unsuccessful bid for the 17th United States Congress, publishing letters in the Edwardsville Spectator in which he discussed slavery; his anti-slavery opponent, Daniel Pope Cook, won the seat. He subsequently became Illinois's first Secretary of State, serving from 1820 to 1824. In 1824, Kane led proslavery forces within the Illinois House of Representatives in an effort to convene another constitutional convention. The initiative was defeated by a coalition led by Governor Edward Coles, along withU.S. Representative Daniel Pope Cook and religious leaders from multiple denominations.

German Type XXI submarines (Elektroboote) were developed to sustain submerged operations for extended periods, marking a significant advance in underwater endurance. Although initial plans envisioned hydrogen peroxide as a means of long-term air-independent propulsion, the vessels were ultimately built with very large batteries to power electric motors while submerged. As World War II ended, both the British and the Soviets tested hydrogen peroxide/kerosene propulsion systems that could operate in both surfaced and submerged conditions, but the results of these experiments were not encouraging. The Soviet Union later deployed a class of submarines using this propulsion method (NATO reporting name Quebec), a design that did not prove successful.

At the surface, surface ships and submarines that are not fully submerged exhibit positive buoyancy, meaning their total weight is less than the weight of the water they would displace if completely submerged. To submerge, a submarine must become negatively buoyant, which is achieved either by increasing its overall weight or by decreasing the amount of water it displaces. The principal means of doing so is a ballast system consisting of ballast tanks that can hold varying amounts of water and air; filling ballast tanks with water raises the vehicle’s weight and lowers its buoyancy to permit descent, while expelling water and introducing air reduces weight and increases buoyancy for ascent. In this way, ballast tanks provide precise control over both displacement and weight, enabling depth changes and station-keeping.

ISSN, which serves as a unique identifier for serial publications, does not provide a mechanism to resolve a given identifier into a location or resource on the web. In contrast, DOIs offer resolvable links to digital content and can function as a Uniform Resource Name for individual articles. Consequently, DOIs are commonly used as the URN for scholarly articles within many publishing and indexing workflows. Historically, the utility of ISSNs in this specific capacity has been regarded as largely unnecessary, reflecting a shift toward DOI-based-resolution systems for article identification.

ISSN codes are issued by a global network of National Centres, typically housed within national libraries, and are coordinated by the ISSN International Centre (CIEPS) based in Paris. The ISSN International Centre operates as an intergovernmental organization that was established in 1974 through an agreement between UNESCO and the government of France.

On August 7, Nixon met in the Oval Office with Republican congressional leaders to discuss the prospects for impeachment. They told him that his support in Congress had all but disappeared and warned that he faced impeachment in the House and a potential conviction in the Senate, with perhaps as few as fifteen senators inclined to vote for acquittal. That night, realizing his presidency was effectively over, Nixon chose to resign.

Richard Nixon's presidency is characterized by the adoption of New Federalism, which sought to shift certain powers and responsibilities from the federal government to the states through expanded use of block grants. He faced a Democratic-controlled Congress that occasionally enacted legislation despite his veto. His proposed federal welfare reform did not pass Congress, which instead enacted the Supplemental Security Income program to assist low-income elderly and disabled individuals. On civil rights and education, the administration pursued a relatively low-profile approach to school desegregation while enforcing court orders and implementing the first affirmative action plan to promote minority participation in federal projects. In environmental policy, Nixon oversaw the creation of the Environmental Protection Agency and the passage of major environmental laws, including the Clean Water Act, which he vetoed but Congress subsequently overrode. Economically, the period initiated the stagflation trend—a combination of inflation and slow growth—that would persist into the 1970s.

Natalie Glebova, who held the Miss Universe title, promoted HIV/AIDS awareness as part of her platform. In August 2005 she attended the G8 Summit in New York City, where attendees discussed efforts to end poverty in developing regions and to address gang activity and drug cartels in Colombia. In November, she participated in the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in Delhi and conducted a week-long AIDS awareness program tour across Indian cities. In December she attended the national pageants of Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic. Later that year she returned to Thailand to commemorate the one-year anniversary of the 2004 tsunami tragedy.

Natalie Glebova, noted for her long-standing commitment to wildlife conservation, was named in June 2015 as an Ambassador for the Year of the Gibbon, an initiative of the IUCN SSC Primate Specialist Group – Section on Small Apes. The ambassadorial role was designed to raise public awareness of gibbon conservation issues. As part of the Year of the Gibbon, she also initiated a public awareness campaign addressing the negative impact of photo-prop tourism on gibbons.

The phrase is traced to Adelaide's Lament, a number in the 1950 Broadway musical Guys and Dolls, where Adelaide’s perpetual cold is attributed to her fiancé’s refusal to marry. In the song, a Niagara Falls excursion unfolds with details such as church bells, an air‑conditioned compartment, and a mood described as sublime. The travelers disembark at Saratoga on what is depicted as the fourteenth such stop. A later line of the piece humorously attributes the possibility of catching influenza to the Saratoga trips, linking illness to the locale in a playful fashion.

Saratoga Springs, New York, owes part of its early historical significance to Sir William Johnson, a British colonial officer whose activities helped shape frontier diplomacy in the region. In 1756 he was appointed British Superintendent of Indian Affairs in the Northeast after success in forging alliances with the Mohawk and other Iroquois nations, and he learned the Iroquois language while building extensive trading networks that yielded substantial wealth from commerce and landholdings. He was knighted in recognition of his service to the Crown through his management of Iroquois relations. In 1767, Native American friends brought Johnson to the spring to treat his war wounds, an episode that linked the mineral springs to colonial diplomacy and commerce and aided the site's later development as a therapeutic and social destination. Taken together, Johnson’s influence and the enduring Indigenous alliances contributed to the early growth of the area and its emergence as a notable center in upstate New York.

In September 584, Chilperic I was fatally stabbed as he returned from a royal hunting party at his Chelles villa. The assailant responsible for the murder remains unknown. He was buried in the Basilica of Saint-Vincent in Paris, a structure that later became incorporated into Saint-Germain-des-Prés.

Chilperic I, a Merovingian king, after the death of his father in 561, sought to seize the entire realm, entering Paris after taking the royal treasure at Berny; however, his brothers compelled a division of the kingdom. Chilperic received Soissons and the surrounding towns of Amiens, Arras, Cambrai, Thérouanne, Tournai, and Boulogne, while Charibert, the eldest, was allotted Paris. Guntram, the second eldest, acquired Burgundy with its capital at Orléans, and Sigebert received Austrasia. In 567 Charibert died, and the surviving brothers redivided Charibert’s domain, agreeing to share Paris and the surrounding territory.

During the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2021), Caffè Lena shifted to streaming live music, initiating a series of online performances. The streams operated on a donation-based pay model, enabling audiences to contribute at their discretion. The program featured folk musicians such as Kate McDonnell and Natalie Haas.
Lena Spencer (January 4, 1923 – October 23, 1989) was associated with Caffè Lena, and since her death, the venue has operated as a not-for-profit organization.

Kiss Network is a radio network that has operated since 2000, featuring a broad roster of DJs and presenters. Over the years it has included a wide range of notable figures in the electronic and dance music scenes, such as Bam Bam, Andy C, John Digweed, Ali B, Robin Banks, Adam F, DJ EZ, Carl Cox, DJ Hype, Logan Sama, DJ Hatcha, Paul Oakenfold, Armin van Buuren, Rickie Haywood Williams, Melvin Odoom, Charlie Hedges, Hed Kandi, Philip George, DJ S.K.T, Jordan Banjo, Perri Kiely, and Tyler West.

David Rodigan had been with Kiss Network since its official launch in 1990 and resigned in November 2012, citing the ongoing marginalisation of reggae music within the station's programming as the reason for his departure.

Type C5-S-75a was a cargo liner of the Type C5 class built by Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Co. in Newport News, Virginia, for the American Mail Line of Seattle, Washington. The vessel was designed to operate as either a break-bulk cargo carrier or a container ship, delivering 21,600 shaft horsepower (16,100 kW) and carrying about 15,950 tons. It maintained a speed of 21.0 knots (38.9 km/h; 24.2 mph). In 1969 it was noted as one of the largest general cargo liners in service.

C5-S-73b was a Sea Witch class container ship built by Bath Iron Works in 1968 for American Export-Isbrandtsen Lines. The vessel was designed to carry 928 twenty-foot equivalent containers (TEU), corresponding to standard containers of approximately 6.1 meters in length.

The Barbie Diaries presents a plot in which Barbie worries about not having a bracelet, prompting Kevin to wrap a guitar string around her wrist to create a makeshift accessory. She initially dismisses it as a worthless piece of bent metal, until she realizes it matches her original bracelet. At the concert the girls perform confidently, with Courtney finally executing a drum-stick maneuver she had been unable to perform before. Barbie dances with Todd and asks about notes she has heard mentioned in her locker; Todd claims he knows nothing about any notes. Barbie recalls other people connected to the places named in the notes and comes to understand that Kevin was behind the notes all along. She leaves the dance to confront him, and Kevin returns the charm bracelet he found on the ground. Barbie apologizes for not realizing sooner, noting that the rhyming within the notes was the giveaway. Barbie and Kevin then dance together and become a couple, and the tale ends with them watching a movie and eating ziti.

In The Barbie Diaries, Raquelle ends her relationship with Todd, the boy Barbie has a crush on, setting the stage for Todd and Barbie to start hanging out and become a couple. Todd then asks Barbie to accompany him to the Fall Formal. When Barbie and her friends, Tia and Courtney, learn that Raquelle and Todd are together again, they hurry to buy a dress. At the counter, a mysterious woman named Stephanie offers guidance and complimentary charm bracelets. Barbie’s own charm bracelet includes a diary she uses to record her hopes.

The 2023 Meistriliiga, sponsored as the A. Le Coq Premium Liiga, was the 33rd season of Estonia's top-tier association football league, the Meistriliiga, which has operated since its establishment in 1992. The season also marked the first use of video assistant referee (VAR) technology in the league.

In the 2023 Meistriliiga season, Tammeka finished in ninth place, while Viimsi, as the runners-up in the 2023 Esiliiga, contested the promotion/relegation playoff to determine the final berth for the next season's Meistriliiga.

Newsweek saw its advertising revenue fall by 37 percent in 2009. The magazine division recorded an operating loss of $29.3 million for 2009, equivalent to about $42.94 million in 2024 dollars. The previous year, 2008, the division incurred an operating loss of $16 million (about $23.37 million in 2024 dollars). In the first quarter of 2010, the magazine division posted an operating loss of nearly $11 million (approximately $15.86 million in 2024 dollars).

Newsweek is an American weekly news magazine headquartered in New York City. It was established in 1933 as a weekly print publication and went on to attain broad distribution across the United States for much of the 20th century. Over the years, the publication has been led by several notable editors-in-chief. Currently, ownership is shared by Dev Pragad, who serves as president and chief executive officer, and Johnathan Davis, a board member, with each holding a 50 percent stake in the company.

Construction of the Dachongkou station's enclosure commenced on 29 April 2017, concurrently with the initiation of works on the adjacent Shachong station on the same line. To accommodate the construction activities, the nearby northbound Dachongkou Public Bus Stop was temporarily relocated approximately 200 meters north of its original position. The Dachongkou station was sealed on 27 July 2020.

Dachongkou station was constructed with an emphasis on minimizing disruption to surface transportation and the surrounding old houses, employing a full-cover and excavation technique to carry out the works.

The replenishment oiler emerged in step with the transition from coal- to oil-fired boilers aboard warships, enabling ships to sail longer between refits. Before oil became dominant, navies extended their range through reliance on overseas coaling stations or by transferring coal at sea from colliers. Although fuel-security concerns were voiced, the relative ease of transferring liquid fuel facilitated the global adoption of replenishment oilers. An early long-range example was the British Royal Fleet Auxiliary vessel Kharki, which operated in 1911, before World War I. Consequently, oilers signaled the shift from coal to oil and reduced dependence on fixed coaling infrastructure. In World War II, the United States Navy's expansion in the Pacific required vast quantities of fuel oils, diesel, aviation gasoline, and related lubricants, prompting refinements in oiler operations and the development of underway replenishment procedures to move highly combustible liquids through hostile waters and over great distances.

Replenishment oiler refers to a class of naval auxiliary ships designed to supply underway replenishment of fuel and other materials. The first fleet oilers carried the hull designation AO, a classification that remains in use today. Larger, fast oilers capable of also resupplying ammunition and dry stores are designated as Fast Combat Support Ships (AOE). Mid-size oilers were previously designated Replenishment Oilers (AOR), but the AOR designation is no longer in use. Collectively, these vessels provide the combined capabilities of the AO, AE, AFS and AK, enabling underway replenishment of fuel, ordnance and stores.

Guided-missile destroyers are naval combatants designed to carry and deploy missiles from substantial onboard magazines, enabling sustained warfare capability. In modern designs, these ships typically employ vertical-launch system (VLS) cells, which provide flexible, rapid-fire missile deployment and the ability to carry multiple missile types. A subset of destroyers integrates advanced integrated weapons systems, such as the United States' Aegis Combat System, which coordinates radar data, fire control, and interceptors. Depending on configuration, guided-missile destroyers can be assigned to anti-missile or ballistic-missile defense missions, contributing to layered air and missile defense networks. This role is particularly important for navies that no longer operate cruisers, as destroyers help fill the gap in heavy air-defense and long-range strike capabilities.

Guided-missile destroyers are multirole warships designed to undertake a variety of combat tasks. In the anti-surface mission, they deploy surface-to-surface missiles alongside naval artillery to counter enemy ships. For anti-submarine warfare, they rely on torpedoes and helicopter platforms to detect and engage submarine threats. Through a combination of guided missiles, guns, anti-submarine weapons, and aviation support, these ships are able to operate effectively across different domains.

In the system of national accounts, disposable income is defined for each institutional sector. For corporations, disposable income corresponds to the portion of profit that is retained within the firm as retained earnings. For the government sector, disposable income consists of tax revenue plus income received from public corporations. National disposable income is the aggregate of the disposable incomes across all institutional sectors.

Disposable income is a term used in economics to denote the income left after mandatory deductions; however, it is frequently misapplied in everyday language to denote discretionary income. Laypeople commonly describe it as the amount available for discretionary spending or saving, a notion that emphasizes flexibility rather than its formal accounting meaning. This discrepancy highlights a mismatch between the technical definitions used by economists and the way the term is commonly understood.

The 2008 season marked Guangzhou FC's first participation in the Chinese Super League. The article presents the club's player statistics for the year and provides a complete record of all matches played by Guangzhou Pharmaceutical F.C. during the season. It notes that the club is referred to by the name variant Guangzhou Pharmaceutical F.C. in the article title.

Like many professional clubs, Guangzhou Pharmaceutical F.C.'s 2008 season squad lists displayed players' nationalities using flag indicators that denote the country for which they are eligible to represent under FIFA rules. The presentation adheres to FIFA's eligibility criteria, though a few limited exceptions are acknowledged in certain cases. In addition, some players hold more than one non-FIFA nationality, resulting in multiple citizenships that do not necessarily correspond to a single national team designation.

Formerly the United States Navy stores ship USS Mizar (AF-12), the vessel was transferred by United Fruit Company to its British subsidiary Elders and Fyffes. It subsequently operated under the name Samala, a designation adopted after an earlier Fyffes vessel. The ship was scrapped in 1964.

The United Fruit Company steamer Chiriqui, launched on 14 November 1931 and built by Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Company, was delivered to the War Shipping Administration in New York under a bareboat charter on 4 June 1941 and immediately subchartered to the Navy. After undergoing conversion at Brewer's Drydock Company in Staten Island, New York, she was commissioned as USS Tarazed (AF-13) on 14 June 1941. Decommissioned at New Orleans on 4 January 1946 and delivered to the WSA, the vessel continued to operate for WSA with United Fruit as agent under a General Agency Agreement until 15 June 1947, when she was returned to the company in New Orleans. She was later sold in September 1957 to Union-Partenreederei T/S (Germany), renamed Blexen, and was scrapped in 1969.

Concord Pacific Place is a large-scale redevelopment project in Vancouver, British Columbia. In 1988 Concord Pacific Developments acquired the site, with investors led by Li Ka-shing. The project expanded during Vancouver's housing booms of the 1990s and 2000s, driven by increased port traffic, broader economic activity, waves of Asian immigration, and the 2010 Winter Olympics. Estimates for the final size of the development vary: some assessments place the project at about C$2 billion on a 200-acre site containing roughly 8,000 units; others cite a C$4 billion development on more than 200 acres with over 20,000 residents; and some descriptions indicate around 50 buildings housing roughly 10,000 homes.

In 2010, Vancouver city councillor Geoff Meggs stated that the Vancouver City Council would not pressure Concord Pacific Developments to advance development of the land designated for the Concord Pacific Place project.

Battle stars are service decorations earned for participation in designated campaign phases. All periods eligible for these awards occur within the defined campaign phases, ensuring that qualification is tied to specific campaign participation rather than to general service alone. The campaign medal cannot be earned independently for these awards and must be worn together with at least one campaign star.

Battle stars, also referred to as service stars or campaign stars, were insignia authorized for wear on several U.S. military decorations to denote participation in designated campaigns. They were applied to the World War I Victory Medal, the American Defense Service Medal, the American Campaign Medal, the European–African–Middle Eastern Campaign Medal, and the Asiatic–Pacific Campaign Medal, though the method of wear and the symbolism attached varied by medal. For instance, a bronze service star on the American Campaign Medal indicated involvement in an antisubmarine campaign. On other medals, bronze service stars were placed on the medal’s service ribbon to show that the recipient earned one or more campaign clasps.

Japan maintains an extensive transportation network, comprising 280 airports as of 2025. Haneda Airport in Tokyo serves as the nation's largest domestic airport and, in 2019, was Asia's second-busiest airport by passenger traffic. In maritime logistics, the Keihin and Hanshin superport hubs rank among the world's largest, with container throughput of about 7.98 million TEU and 5.22 million TEU respectively in 2017.

Japan has been a member of the United Nations since 1956 and is part of the G4 group advocating reform of the UN Security Council. It participates in the G7, APEC, and ASEAN Plus Three, and attends the East Asia Summit. The country ranks as the fifth-largest donor of official development assistance, providing about US$9.2 billion in 2014. By 2024, Japan maintained the fourth-largest diplomatic network in the world. Widely regarded as a great power, its status reflects substantial economic strength alongside influential political, cultural, and military influence.
Paradorn Srichaphan's year began with the end of his streak of reaching finals at the Chennai Open, where he was defeated in the quarterfinals by Kristof Vliegen in straight sets.

Paradorn Srichaphan entered the ATP Tour's top 10 for the first time on 21 April, becoming the first Asian man to reach the singles top 10. He achieved a career-high ranking of No. 9 on 12 May. At the French Open, he was seeded 10th, the highest seed he had received in a Grand Slam event.

On 21 May 2014, SAP AG announced at its annual general meeting that 99 percent of shareholder votes approved converting to a Societas Europaea (SE). The first supervisory board of SAP SE was elected. The conversion to an SE would take effect upon entry in the commercial register, expected in July 2014.

SAP, the German multinational software company, reached a valuation of €320 billion in June 2025. By that month, approximately four-fifths of its client operations were managed through its cloud business at a hyperscale capacity. In September 2025, the European Commission opened an investigation into SAP for anti-competitive practices.

SS Wilson is a steam-powered general cargo vessel owned by Sealift Incorporated. The keel was laid in 1968 and she was delivered in 1969, and she is registered under the United States flag with the port of registry at Dover, Delaware. Over her career she carried several names: Hong Kong Mail until 1978, President Wilson until 1987, and Sue Lykes until 1995. The ship holds the IMO number 6909911 and the call sign WNPD. Classified as a Type C5 class ship, she belongs to the C5-S-75a design. Wilson was built by Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Company in Newport News, Virginia, for American Mail Line of Seattle, Washington. The C5-S-75a variants were designed for break-bulk cargo operations or container service. The vessel has 21,600 shaft horsepower, a tonnage of 15,950, and a maximum speed of 21.0 knots. At the time of its commission in 1969, it was among the largest general cargo liners in service.

Clotilda was a schooner built by Timothy Meaher, a wealthy Mobile shipyard owner and steamboat captain, in 1855 or 1856. It was designed for the lumber trade and possessed two masts. The vessel measured 86 feet (26 m) in length and had a beam of 23 feet (7.0 m), with a copper-sheathed hull. Captain William Foster commanded Clotilda during its operations for Meaher.

Descendant is a 2022 documentary released by Brown that surveys the Africatown community in the present day, highlighting environmental and social inequities that persist more than 160 years after the Clotilda’s voyage. The film also addresses the impact of the 2019 discovery of Clotilda on the local area. Produced by Netflix, Descendant premiered at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival.

Cailín Áine Ní Toibín (born 25 February 1994) is an Irish beauty pageant titleholder who was crowned Miss Universe Ireland 2017 on 31 August 2017. She subsequently represented Ireland at the Miss Universe 2017 competition.

Cailín Áine Ní Toibín is an Irish beauty pageant contestant who first gained recognition when she was named Miss Universe Cork in 2015. That same year she finished as the second runner-up at Miss Universe Ireland, with Joanna Cooper taking the national crown. Ní Toibín later won Miss Universe Ireland in 2017, thereby securing the national title.

Alexander Rose, the executive director of the Long Now Foundation, has warned that over generations only a small portion of digital material will remain usable. Even if technological civilization endures, much data will persist primarily as findable and searchable bare information, while the original delivery formats will be largely unrecognizable. The challenge is compounded by the fact that contemporary websites often rely on complex back-ends and content-management approaches—such as Drupal and web frameworks like Ruby on Rails and Django—making faithful long-term archiving more difficult. These concerns inform the aims and limitations of web preservation efforts such as the Wayback Machine.

The Wayback Machine provides three public Application Programming Interfaces that enable programmatic interaction with its archived content: SavePageNow, used to capture and store pages from the web; Availability, which reports whether an archived version exists for a given URL and returns its availability status; and CDX, which supports advanced querying, filtering, and analysis of captured snapshots.

Within Geography Markup Language (GML) application schemas, the location of a Building feature is captured by a Point geometry, while the Building itself is modeled as a separate entity from the geometry that encodes its position. A feature may include multiple geometry properties or none at all, depending on the schema. Common geometry properties include extent and position.

Geography Markup Language employs a streamlined feature model with a single-tier hierarchy, reflecting a one-level depth in its structural design. Under this approach, features are not nested within other features, and the specification does not allow arbitrary nesting of both features and their associated properties.

English continually expands through the creation of neologisms that are frequently built from Greek and Latin roots, a productive pattern evident in English and many other modern European languages; illustrative examples include television and optometry. The origin of such coinages is often difficult to determine, given their blending of classical roots with contemporary usage and cross-linguistic influence. Some scholars, notably Philip Gove, attributed many of these terms to a broad international scientific vocabulary, a categorization described in Webster's Third New International Dictionary (1961). In addition to affix-based neology, English also generates new words through acronyms, formed by pronouncing the shortened forms of longer phrases as single lexical units, as in NATO, laser, and scuba.

Across most dialects of English, the second-person pronoun system treats the singular and plural forms as identical, with the subject and object form being "you" and the possessive determiner "your" and possessive pronoun "yours," while the reflexive forms are "yourself" for singular and "yourselves" for plural. In certain regional varieties, however, distinct second-person plural pronouns are maintained; for example, "y’all" is used in Southern American English and among some speakers of African American Vernacular English, "youse" appears in Australian English, and the archaic or regional "ye" is found in Hiberno-English.

False Creek is a medium-density district that features a spectrum of architectural designs and offers diverse ownership opportunities across housing types. The area supports a wide range of recreational activities and accommodates multiple modes of transportation, with urban design elements that promote easier mobility within the community, including interconnected pedestrian networks, cycling routes, and convenient access to water-based transit. Collectively, these features contribute to a more picturesque landscape and enhance the overall livability of the district.

False Creek is a short, narrow inlet situated in the heart of Vancouver. In French, it is known as Faux ruisseau. The waterway serves as a boundary that separates the Downtown and West End neighbourhoods from the rest of the city. It is one of Vancouver’s four principal bodies of water, alongside English Bay (considered an inland extension), Burrard Inlet, and the Fraser River. Within the inlet lies Granville Island, a notable cultural and commercial hub.

The Best FIFA Football Awards 2019 recognized the most notable fan moments or gestures from September 2018 to September 2019, highlighting acts by supporters rather than players. The awards are independent of any championship, gender, or nationality. A panel of FIFA experts compiled the shortlist, selecting the candidates for public voting. The final vote was open to all registered FIFA.com users, who could participate until 23 September 2019.

The Best FIFA Football Awards 2019 featured The Best FIFA Men's Team, with Alisson Becker as the goalkeeper and a defensive line consisting of Matthijs de Ligt, Marcelo, Sergio Ramos, and Virgil van Dijk; the midfield comprised Frenkie de Jong, Eden Hazard, and Luka Modrić, while the forward line included Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappé, and Lionel Messi.

During modernization, the Victoria-class submarines received upgrades to their sonar systems. The refit included the installation of the BAE Type 2007 array and the Type 2046 towed array, with the Canadian Towed Array Sonar (CANTASS) integrated into the towed sonar suite.

The Victoria-class submarine was a proposed class of diesel-electric submarines developed by the United Kingdom's Ministry of Defence in the late 1970s to replace the Oberon class. It was designed to be cost-effective for training and coastal defence, emphasizing simplicity and affordability. The programme was announced in September 1979, with five designs submitted; the Ministry selected the configuration displacing about 1,960 tonnes. Anticipated export potential prompted raising the permissible displacement to 2,400 tonnes to allow for flexible construction using alternative propulsion and related systems.

Declarations of war during World War II refer to formal acts whereby states announce their intention to enter armed conflict with one another. These declarations are typically conveyed through a public proclamation or a signed instrument issued by an authorized government representative, and they create a state of war between the involved sovereign states. The international protocol governing such declarations was established at the Hague Peace Conference of 1907 (Hague II). The diplomatic maneuvering surrounding these events in the lead-up to and during World War II is discussed in the broader context of the Diplomatic history of World War II.

During World War II, the accompanying table records the outbreaks of interstate conflicts and marks dates that signal the escalation toward or onset of hostilities, thereby indicating a de facto state of war. It identifies the initiating nation or nations and their targeted counterparts, and it covers events ranging from diplomatic breakups to formal declarations of war and acts of aggression. In a minority of instances, the same conflict reoccurred after a lull, producing two distinct episodes of fighting. The compilation excludes peace treaties and armistice periods.

Guangdong Business Center is a high-rise located in the Pazhou Central Business District of the Haizhu District in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, China. The structure rises to a height of 375.5 meters (1,232 feet) and contains 60 floors. It is the tallest skyscraper outside the Tianhe District of Guangzhou and is distinguished as the tallest pure steel-structured skyscraper in Asia.

The Guangdong Business Center (Chinese: 广商中心; also known as Guangshang Center) is a mixed-use supertall skyscraper under construction in Guangzhou, China. The project is planned for completion between 2018 and 2025 and is designed to reach a height of 375.5 meters (1,232 feet) with 60 floors. It currently ranks as the fourth-tallest building in Guangzhou.
In the Madrid Masters, Robin Söderling defeated Santiago Giraldo and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga to reach the quarterfinals, where he faced Roger Federer and was defeated.

During 2000, Söderling spent his first full season on the junior tour, capturing four tournament titles. In 2001, he claimed three junior championships, including the Orange Bowl, a title he won without dropping a set. At the end of 2001, he was ranked No. 4 in the junior world rankings.

Sally Fingerett (born December 25, 1955, in Chicago, Illinois) is an American folk singer-songwriter who is a founding member of the group Four Bitchin' Babes. She contributed extensively to the band's catalog, recording numerous albums with the ensemble over the years.

Sally Fingerett married producer Dan Green, with whom she collaborated on producing commercial music. Green produced four of Fingerett's solo CDs, and he also produced the Four Bitchin' Babes album Fax It, Charge It, Don't Ask Me What's For Dinner.

By the end of 2023, the United Kingdom's offshore proved and probable gas reserves were estimated at 1.1 billion barrels of oil equivalent, while offshore proved and probable oil reserves stood at 2.3 billion barrels of oil equivalent. These reserves help reduce reliance on imports, contributing to energy security and supporting the transition toward renewable energy sources. Emissions from UK gas production are reported to be about one-quarter of those associated with imported liquefied natural gas, according to the UK oil and gas regulator.

The United Kingdom has played a pivotal role in the development of British empiricism, a tradition that holds knowledge to be validated through experience. It is also closely linked with Scottish philosophy, particularly the Scottish School of Common Sense, which stressed the reliability of ordinary human judgment. Prominent British empiricists associated with the country include John Locke, George Berkeley, and David Hume. Leaders of the Scottish common-sense movement encompassed Dugald Stewart, Thomas Reid, and William Hamilton. In moral philosophy, utilitarianism originated with Jeremy Bentham, who introduced its foundational ideas, and was later expanded by John Stuart Mill, whose work Utilitarianism elaborated and defended the doctrine.

In the 1950s, a distinct movement arose among Coimbra's fado singers that incorporated ballad forms and folk elements, marking a shift within the Coimbra tradition. This school drew on verses from renowned poets, spanning classical and contemporary voices, using their lines as a form of resistance to the Salazar dictatorship. Leading figures in this revival included Adriano Correia de Oliveira and José Afonso, commonly known as Zeca Afonso. Their work helped shape popular music in Portugal and they played a central role during the Carnation Revolution of 1974.

Fado commonly draws on modal frameworks, engaging the Dorian mode or the Ionian mode (the natural major scale). Performers may shift between these two modes within a single melodic line or across verses, allowing tonal changes that contribute to the characteristic expressiveness of the genre.

The American Mail Line operated trans-Pacific shipping routes that linked West Coast and Canadian ports with major East Asian and Pacific destinations, including Seattle and Victoria on the American side and Yokohama, Kobe, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Manila, and Honolulu on the opposite shores. Passenger service on these routes was organized in cooperation with Dollar Steamship Lines and the line's principal owner, providing integrated, joint operations for travelers across the network.

American Mail Line operated a fleet of five C5-S-75a cargo vessels, each constructed by Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Co. in Newport News, Virginia. The ships were designed to handle break-bulk cargoes as well as containerized freight, and they were propelled by a system delivering 21,600 shaft horsepower (16,100 kW). With a tonnage of about 15,950 tons and a service speed of 21.0 knots (38.9 km/h; 24.2 mph), they stood among the largest general cargo liners in 1969.

MAB Paints articulates its commitment to reliable service through a service motto that guarantees on-time performance, with compensation provided if the promise is not fulfilled. The safeguard underscores the company's pledge of timely service and is publicly displayed within M.A.B. stores and facilities and printed on the organization’s business cards.

M.A.B. Paints was a regional paint company prominent in the Philadelphia metropolitan area. It gained recognition through its involvement in the Make America Beautiful campaign, which helped raise the firm’s profile in the community. In addition to civic engagement, the company supported local sports and charitable efforts by sponsoring both professional and amateur teams and various charities. A notable example of its sponsorship was backing the 2007 USCLA champions, the Philadelphia M.A.B. Paints Lacrosse Club.

ISO 14617 is a multi-part international standard related to graphical symbols. Part 1, titled General information and indexes, functions as an introductory section and provides guidance on registration numbers as well as rules for presenting and applying the symbols. It also contains an index listing all symbols defined within the standard. The remaining parts of ISO 14617 are devoted to the symbols themselves, with entries organized according to type or intended application.

ISO 14617 is an international standard developed in cooperation with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). It shares some elements with IEC 60617, the IEC’s standard for graphical symbols used in diagrams, reflecting a degree of alignment between the two standards.

United States Fleet Activities Yokosuka, Japan, is the United States Navy's largest overseas base. It functions as the home port for the service's largest forward-deployed fleet and acts as a major base of operations in the Western Pacific, supporting naval readiness and regional security in the area.

The United States Navy underwent significant strategic and industrial shifts in the interwar period, beginning with the Washington Naval Conference of 1921–22, which established limits on naval construction and is regarded as the first arms-control negotiation in history. Within that framework, the aircraft carriers USS Lexington (CV-2) and USS Saratoga (CV-3) were completed on hulls originally laid out for canceled battle-cruiser designs, a consequence of the treaty’s constraints. During the New Deal era, public works funding facilitated additional warship construction, notably the carriers Yorktown (CV-5) and Enterprise (CV-6). By 1936, after the completion of USS Wasp (CV-7), the U.S. Navy’s carrier force measured roughly 165,000 tonnes in displacement, though official records nominally set the limit at about 135,000 tonnes to comply with treaty ceilings. Franklin D. Roosevelt, who had served as assistant secretary of the Navy during World War I, supported the service’s development, while senior leaders fostered innovation and the testing of new technologies, such as magnetic torpedoes. In parallel, the Navy formulated War Plan Orange, a contingency doctrine for achieving victory in the Pacific against Japan, a scenario that ultimately materialized in the decades that followed.

David Bowie's third studio album, The Man Who Sold the World (1970), explores themes relating to schizophrenia, paranoia, and delusion, and signals a shift from the acoustic guitar and folk-rock textures of his prior release toward a harder, more electric rock sound. In early 1971, Mercury Records financed a coast-to-coast publicity tour across the United States in January and February, accompanied by a series of media interviews. The original UK cover depicted Bowie wearing a dress to play up his androgynous persona, a look he continued to wear during interviews; contemporary critics responded positively, with Rolling Stone’s John Mendelsohn praising his appearance and comparing him to screen icon Lauren Bacall.

David Bowie was appointed a Commander of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres by the French government in 1999, and he received an honorary doctorate from Berklee College of Music. He later declined the royal honor of Commander of the Order of the British Empire in 2000 and rejected a knighthood in 2003. Bowie publicly stated that he would never accept such honours and questioned their purpose, noting that they did not align with what he had spent his life working for.

The Nuclear football, officially designated as the Presidential Emergency Satchel, is a portable case used by the president to communicate and authorize a nuclear strike while away from fixed command centers. It functions as a mobile hub within the United States' strategic defense framework, ensuring presidential command and control during travel and in situations where routine facilities are not accessible. The satchel is carried by a military aide whenever the president journeys away from locations such as the White House Situation Room or the Presidential Emergency Operations Center.

The nuclear football remains in close proximity to the president at all times, a practice that keeps the accompanying military aides visible in press imagery. In February 2017, during a stay at Mar-a-Lago, a guest posted a photo of a military aide carrying the football and identified the aide by his first name; the image was taken while President Donald Trump hosted Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe. Around the same period, North Korea reportedly launched a nuclear-capable Pukguksong-2 ballistic missile over the Sea of Japan. U.S. military officials stated that the officer’s appearance in the photograph did not violate any law or proper procedure, though the situation was viewed as unusual.

During the Ice Age, the coastline along the British Columbia coast stood roughly 100 metres lower than its present position, reflecting lower sea levels. Queen Charlotte Sound, situated between Haida Gwaii and the northern tip of Vancouver Island, constituted a coastal plain at that time. All inland straits radiating from Queen Charlotte Sound likewise formed coastal plains, except for those that were carved as mountain valleys.

The Port of Vancouver, located on the British Columbia coast, is the largest commercial shipping port in Canada and on the Pacific coast of North America by cargo tonnage. It handles about 76.5 million metric tons of cargo annually, and by the same measurement it ranks as the fifth-largest commercial shipping port in North America.

Chelsea Cooley represented North Carolina at Miss USA 2005, the national pageant held in Baltimore, Maryland and broadcast live on April 21, 2005. In the final question, she drew a prompt from former Miss USA Shandi Finnessey asking which famous person her personality most closely parallels. Cooley identified Oprah Winfrey as the public figure whose personality most resembles her own, citing Oprah’s passion for life, love of her work, and dedication to hard work in achieving goals. She stated that she strives to emulate Oprah.

Chelsea Cooley relocated to a Trump Tower apartment in New York City shortly after her Miss USA victory in Baltimore, sharing the residence with the holders of the Miss Universe and Miss Teen USA titles. She subsequently traveled to Thailand to compete in Miss Universe, and she and Natalie Glebova, who had just been crowned Miss Universe, remained in Thailand for a week after the pageant.

"Flashlight" is a ballad originally performed by Jessie J. In the film's narrative, the character Emily is depicted as a songwriter who composes original material, and Beca Mitchell proposes a collaboration with Emily to produce and record the song in a studio setting. During the movie's climactic sequence, the Bellas perform "Flashlight" as part of their World Championships setlist, marking a pivotal moment in the storyline and illustrating the song's integration into the film's emotional arc.

Hailee Steinfeld recorded a rendition of Jessie J's "Flashlight" titled the "Sweet Life Mix" for Pitch Perfect 2. This version appears on the Pitch Perfect 2 special edition soundtrack, and is also included on the Japanese edition of Steinfeld's debut EP Haiz (2015). The track has earned Gold certification from Recorded Music NZ (RMNZ). Additionally, a "Math Club Remix" is included on the Target-exclusive edition of the special edition soundtrack.

Fortuna Arena serves as the home venue of SK Slavia Prague. It has also been used intermittently as the home ground of the Czech Republic national football team. During the 2010–11 and 2011–12 seasons, Bohemians 1905 played their home matches there. In the 2011–12 season, FC Viktoria Plzeň hosted its Champions League group-stage games at the arena. The stadium was the host venue for the 2013 UEFA Super Cup.

In the early 1950s, Slavia Prague relocated from the Letná stadium to a new facility at Eden in Prague’s Vršovice district. The Eden stadium accommodated roughly 50,000 spectators, with the majority of space designated as standing room. The main western stand was wooden and had been transferred from the old Letná stadium, while the other stands were constructed from concrete. The venue also featured an athletics track surrounding the pitch. The first match held at Eden occurred on 27 September 1953, when Slavia drew 1–1 with Křídla vlasti Olomouc, with Josef Bican scoring Slavia’s goal.

During the 20th century, folk music saw regional repertoires gain wider recognition beyond their local contexts. In Spain, flamenco broadened its appeal, while northern traditions including Galicia’s Celtic-influenced music likewise expanded their reach. Concurrently, French classical composers from Bizet to Ravel drew on Spanish themes, illustrating a cross-cultural exchange that informed both concert music and popular perception. Together, these movements contributed to the emergence of distinctive Spanish genres as internationally recognized forms within the broader folk-music landscape.

Folk music encompasses traditional forms and performances, and during the Eastern Bloc era the state actively promoted national folk dancing as part of cultural policy. Dance troupes originating in Russia and Poland toured non-communist Europe from roughly 1937 to 1990, helping to spread Eastern European repertoires beyond their borders. The Red Army Choir, a renowned military ensemble, recorded numerous albums and attained wide popularity as one of the era’s most prominent military bands. Additionally, Eastern Europe is recognised as the origin of the Jewish Klezmer tradition, a distinctive branch of folk music with deep roots in the region.

Pre-dreadnought battleships were powered predominantly by reciprocating steam engines rather than the turbine propulsion that would come later, with top speeds typically ranging from 16 to 18 knots (about 18–21 mph or 30–33 km/h). In the 1880s, ironclads commonly employed compound engines, and by the end of that decade triple-expansion compound engines had become standard. Some fleets experimented with quadruple-expansion steam engines, but this configuration did not see adoption in the British navy.

Key propulsion improvements during the pre-dreadnought era stemmed from boilers able to generate higher-pressure steam. This period saw the replacement of Scotch marine boilers with compact water-tube designs, which produced higher-pressure steam and, for the same or reduced fuel consumption, greater efficiency. In addition to efficiency, water-tube boilers offered enhanced safety with a lower explosion risk and provided greater flexibility in ship machinery layouts. Belleville-type water-tube boilers were introduced into the French fleet by 1879, and the Royal Navy subsequently adopted Belleville boilers for armored cruisers and later pre-dreadnought battleships in 1894. Following these advancements, navies worldwide transitioned to water-tube boiler systems, reflecting a broad shift away from traditional fire-tube designs.

Miss Universe 2008 featured eighty contestants representing eighty countries and territories. Two entrants were appointed rather than selected through the standard national pageant, having previously finished as runners-up or been chosen via a casting process. Furthermore, six participants were selected to replace an original winner who had been dethroned.

The Crown Convention Center, built to host the Miss Universe 2008 pageant, is a 7,500-seat indoor arena spanning 10,000 square meters. Located at the Diamond Bay Resort, the facility opened on June 30, 2008, and is the third-largest convention center in Southeast Asia.

During the Battle of Changsha (1941–1942), Japanese forces conducted a withdrawal under considerable hardship, a characterization reflected in post-war Japanese accounts. They faced persistent assaults from large enemy formations throughout the retreat and were obliged to escort a substantial number of casualties and rear service units in addition to frontline troops. Despite the severity of the engagement and the logistical burdens, the operation avoided annihilation, owing to near-complete air superiority that prevented total destruction of Japanese forces.

On 24 January 1942, Xue Yue and Li Yutang were awarded the Order of Blue Sky and White Sun in recognition of their roles in the third Battle of Changsha. On the same day Li Yutang received a promotion to deputy commander of the 27th Army Group, while continuing to command the 10th Corps. The 10th Corps earned the nickname “Mt. Tai Army” and was held in high regard for its performance. On 28 March 1942 Li Yutang resigned as commander of the 10th Corps to devote his duties fully to the deputy army group command. Subsequently Fang Xianjue, formerly commander of the 10th Reserve Division, was promoted to corps commander.

Mass (music) refers to musical settings of the liturgical Mass. In eighteenth‑century Vienna, mass composition fused operatic features associated with cantata masses with the evolving idioms of the symphony and concerto to shape the structure of the choral material. Large‑scale masses from the first half of the century typically contain many movements within the Gloria and Credo, in contrast to smaller works written for ordinary parish churches. Mozart’s masses are frequently missa brevis, a trait shared by some of Haydn’s early masses. In the later eighteenth century, particularly in Haydn’s output, the form adopts a more symphonic character, with extended sections subdivided into a smaller number of movements and arranged in a manner reminiscent of a symphony. Soloists are often integrated as part of the ensemble rather than highlighted as individuals. In the nineteenth century, a distinction develops between concert masses and liturgical masses, reflecting divergent aims and contexts for performance.

Mass (music) comprises musical settings of the liturgical Mass, with the majority traditionally composed in Latin, the sacred language of the Catholic Church’s Roman Rite. A substantial portion of Mass compositions are nonetheless written in vernacular languages used in countries outside the Catholic tradition. In the United States, English-language Mass settings have become common since the Second Vatican Council. For the Church of England, such musical settings are typically identified as Communion services rather than Mass.

James Edward Murray (May 3, 1876 – March 23, 1961) was an American politician who served as a United States senator representing Montana from 1934 to 1961. He emerged as a leading liberal figure within the Democratic Party, shaping policy and providing influential direction during his extended tenure in the Senate.

James E. Murray held several leadership roles within Congress, including serving as chairman of the Committee on Education and Labor. He also contributed as co-chairman of the Joint Committee on Labor-Management Relations. In addition, Murray chaired the Committee on Labor and Public Welfare and served on the Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs, reflecting a focus on labor, public welfare, and domestic affairs throughout his legislative career.

Tianhe Park station provides four toilet and nursery facilities distributed across the concourse and platform levels. In the Line 13 concourse, one facility is located near Exit D. On the Line 11/21 side, facilities are situated at the northern ends of both island platforms. The Line 13 platform itself contains another facility at its eastern end. Together, these spaces offer restrooms and nursery rooms across the station.

Personal income tax schedules have evolved over time, with reforms in many jurisdictions producing flatter marginal rate structures; at the same time, several countries have introduced measures that make the system more attractive for low-income households and for married couples. These reforms and reliefs have, in various settings, increased the overall progressivity of the personal income tax. The role of personal income tax in total tax revenue varies across countries, reflecting differing tax architectures and revenue priorities. Relative to other taxes, including social security contributions, the personal income tax often shows only modest progressivity.

Personal income comprises all earnings received by an individual, with passive income representing a portion earned with little ongoing active effort or involvement on the part of the recipient. This type of income typically stems from assets or ventures that continue to generate revenue after initial setup or routine management. Common examples include earnings from rental properties, royalties derived from intellectual property, and certain forms of business income that require minimal day-to-day participation.

Recorded Music NZ presents the Aotearoa Music Awards (AMA) on an annual basis. The awards acknowledge distinguished artistic and technical achievement in the recording field and stand as among the most prestigious honors for New Zealand groups and artists. The ceremony has been held annually since 1965.

Recorded Music New Zealand is the national body representing the New Zealand recording industry. Prior to June 2013, the association was known as the Recording Industry Association of New Zealand (RIANZ). In 2013, RIANZ merged with PPNZ Music Licensing, and the merged entity adopted the name Recorded Music NZ.

Knockout ties in the 2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League are two-legged fixtures, with each club hosting one leg. The team with the higher aggregate score over the two legs progresses. If the aggregate score is level, thirty minutes of extra time are played, and the away goals rule is not applied; if still level after extra time, a penalty shoot-out decides the winner. The final, by contrast, is played as a single match. If level at the end of normal time in the final, extra time is played, and if necessary, a penalty shoot-out decides the winner.

The knockout phase of the 2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League commenced on 15 February with the knockout round play-offs and was completed on 29 May 2024 with the final, staged at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, Greece. A total of 24 teams competed in the knockout phase.

Disposable Income is an album by the English punk rock band Snuff. It was released in March 2003 on the Union 2112 label. Prior to this release, Snuff had issued numerous albums for Fat Wreck Chords, an American independent label.
Luo Xi (simplified Chinese: 罗希; traditional Chinese: 羅希; pinyin: Luó Xī), born 2 March 1991, is a Chinese professional footballer who plays as a defender for the Chinese club Hunan HBS Mangguoba.
Luo Xi made his professional league debut for Shenzhen Ruby in the 2011 Chinese Super League on 1 April 2011, in a match against Tianjin TEDA that Shenzhen Ruby lost 0–1.

Frith's analysis of popular music traces its development from the 1950s to the 1980s, examining how genre categories and their naming shaped perceptions of musical influence. B. J. Moore-Gilbert has criticized Frith and other scholars for overemphasizing rock's centrality, arguing that the persistent practice of labeling new styles with the "rock" suffix—such as folk rock in the 1960s and pop rock in the 1970s—unduly elevates rock and treats other influences as ancillary to rock rather than as independent forces.

During the early years, rock influences extended into Britain's broader music scene. Prominent figures such as Cliff Richard achieved success with rock and roll material, with hits including Move It. Tommy Steele became a teen idol, drawing on Elvis Presley as an influence to shape youthful, rock-oriented appeal. Collectively, these early forms and influences laid the groundwork for pop rock, which emerged in the 1960s.

AC Sparta Prague's 2023–24 season marked the club's 130th year of existence and its 31st consecutive season in the Czech First League. The team also competed in the Czech Cup and participated in European competition, beginning in the UEFA Champions League but was eliminated in the third qualifying round by Copenhagen, after which Sparta Prague competed in the UEFA Europa League.

During the 2023–24 season, AC Sparta Prague’s squad listings employ flag icons to indicate each player's national team as defined by FIFA eligibility rules, with a small number of limited exceptions to this practice. In addition, several players may hold multiple nationalities that are not captured by FIFA's eligibility criteria, and such cases are noted in individual player profiles.

During the Vietnam War, the operational capability of the People's Army of Vietnam (PAVN) and the Viet Cong depended on unobstructed movement of personnel along the Ho Chi Minh Trail. In response, U.S. Marines established a combat base on the South Vietnamese side of the Laotian frontier near Khe Sanh to threaten this flow and to monitor activity across the border. The base served as a border surveillance position overlooking Route 9, the province’s sole east–west road crossing the border. General William C. Westmoreland hoped to use Khe Sanh as a staging point for future incursions into the Laotian Trail system. In spring 1967, a series of small-unit actions near Khe Sanh prompted MACV to increase its forces in the area. These actions, together with intelligence assessments, indicated that the PAVN was building up significant forces just across the border in Laos.

Within the discourse surrounding the U.S. involvement in Vietnam, Malcolm X—an influential Black nationalist and spokesman for African American communities—condemned the war in his 1964 address The Ballot or the Bullet. He argued that Washington’s conduct abroad was hypocritical given the denial of civil rights to Black Americans at home. The speech presented his political philosophy and framed the Vietnam War as evidence of what he viewed as irrational decisions by the U.S. government. He asserted that Black Americans were still fighting for equal rights while being sent to fight in Korea and Vietnam, and described himself as a victim of American democracy, distinguishing white audience members as opponents. In his view, the United States fought for international freedom in Vietnam while failing to guarantee full rights at home, a charge that underscored his critique of national hypocrisy.

Following the Budapest offensive, the main forces of Army Group South were effectively collapsed, undermining German defenses in the region. A broad corridor opened toward Vienna, into Czechoslovakia, and toward the southern border of Germany, enabling significant movement by Soviet and Allied forces into Central Europe. This newly opened route benefited the Soviet forces and their allies by facilitating their advances and accelerating the collapse of German positions in the area.

The Budapest offensive was a Soviet military operation undertaken in the final stages of World War II with the aim of capturing Budapest from German and Hungarian forces. Soviet claims regarding the offensive asserted that 49,000 German and Hungarian soldiers were killed, 110,000 were captured, and 269 tanks were destroyed.

In March 2007, Discovery Communications repurchased the Travel Channel stake from Cox Communications in exchange for Cox's stake in Discovery, effectively rebalancing ownership between the two companies. A year later, in June 2008, Discovery Home was discontinued and replaced by Planet Green, a network devoted to environmentalism and sustainable living. In 2009, Cox sold its controlling interest in the Travel Channel to Scripps Networks Interactive, marking another major shift in the channel's ownership and governance.

Discovery Communications announced on July 31, 2017, that it would acquire Scripps Networks Interactive for $14.6 billion, subject to regulatory approvals. SNI owned networks such as Food Network, HGTV, and DIY Network. The acquisition was completed on March 6, 2018, after which the combined company adopted the name Discovery, Inc. As part of the deal, SNI shareholders held a 20 percent stake in the newly formed entity. Discovery retained an operational hub in Knoxville, Tennessee, the former home city of SNI. The company also planned to relocate its corporate headquarters from Silver Spring, Maryland, where it had been based since 2003, to New York City in 2019.

Structurae was established in 1998 by Nicolas Janberg, a civil engineer educated at Princeton University. In March 2012, the platform was acquired by Ernst & Sohn, a subsidiary of John Wiley & Sons, Inc., with Janberg assuming the role of editor-in-chief. At that time, the site attracted more than one million pageviews per month and offered content in English, French, and German. In 2015, Janberg repurchased the site to operate it as a freelancer.

Structurae is an online database that catalogs structural and civil engineering works, offering a collection of photographs and accompanying information about each project. In addition to project details, the database identifies the professionals associated with the work, including engineers, architects, and builders.

After World War II, the Federal Republic of Germany, commonly known as West Germany, continued the Deutscher Fußball-Bund (DFB). With recognition from FIFA and UEFA, the DFB was permitted to preserve the pre-war national team record and maintain continuity of the German football legacy. West Germany’s first post-war international opponent was Switzerland in 1950, marking the beginning of its renewed participation on the international stage. The team then qualified for the 1954 World Cup, a tournament hosted by Switzerland.

Julius Hirsch was a pioneering figure for the Germany national football team, noted as the first Jewish player to represent the side. He earned his first cap in 1911, and in 1912 he scored four goals in a fixture against the Netherlands, making him the first German to score four times in a single international match.

Wet Leg is a British indie rock duo that emerged in 2021, with their debut single “Chaise Longue” released on 15 June 2021 and rapidly accumulating millions of streams and video views. The second single, “Wet Dream,” followed on 28 September 2021, and commentators noted the rarity of a new act delivering two tracks that are both highly regarded. The band appeared on BBC2’s Later... with Jools Holland on 30 October 2021, and on 29 November 2021 they announced their debut album, self-titled Wet Leg, which was released on 8 April 2022 through Domino. In conjunction with the album announcement, they released a double-A-side single featuring “Too Late Now” and “Oh No” on 29 November 2021.

Wet Leg received its initial nominations at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards in three categories: Best New Artist, Best Alternative Music Performance for "Chaise Longue," and Best Alternative Music Album. The group subsequently won Best Alternative Music Performance and Best Alternative Music Album at the Grammys. At the Brit Awards 2023, Wet Leg was awarded Best New Artist and Group of the Year. During the Brit Awards ceremony, they performed "Chaise Longue" with the Morris dance troupe Boss Morris and their Morris beasts.

Advanced Video Coding (AVC), version 11 (Edition 4) of the H.264/AVC standard, released on March 16, 2009, represents a major enhancement to the specification through the introduction of the Multiview Video Coding (MVC) extension. The MVC extension facilitates efficient coding of multiple views for stereoscopic and multiview applications and defines the Multiview High profile as part of its repertoire.

Multiview Video Coding (MVC) is an extension to the H.264/AVC standard specified in Annex H, enabling bitstreams that encode more than one view of a scene. This capability allows simultaneous representation of multiple perspectives, with stereoscopic 3D video serving as a notable application. The MVC specification defines two profiles: Multiview High, which supports an arbitrary number of views, and Stereo High, limited to two-view stereoscopic configurations. The MVC extensions were finalized in November 2009.

Grammofonleverantörernas förening (GLF) formerly served as Sweden's Recording Industry Association, representing the country's recorded-music sector. From 1975 onward, it compiled and published the official Swedish record charts, including the Albums Chart and the Singles Chart. The publication of these charts is now handled by IFPI Sverige. Chart data derive from sales of albums and singles, as well as DVD sales, digital downloads, and streaming. The GLF is no longer active.

National symbols of Taiwan reflect the island's complex political history, having been governed by several regimes throughout its past; since 1945, political authority on Taiwan has rested with the Republic of China (ROC).

National symbols of Taiwan reflect the political history and ongoing claims of the Republic of China (ROC). The ROC governed mainland China from 1912 until 1949, when it retreated to Taiwan after the Chinese Civil War. Today the state is commonly referred to as Taiwan. While it formerly controlled most of China, its effective sovereignty since 1949 is limited to Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu, and nearby smaller islands. In line with its continuing assertion of sovereignty over all of China, several of its official symbols are framed to represent the broader Chinese realm, rather than just the territories it currently governs.

Scholarly accounts diverge on the mood following Nero's death. Some ancient writers, including Suetonius and Cassius Dio, portray widespread celebrations among Romans after the emperor's demise, while Tacitus offers a more nuanced view of the ensuing political landscape. Among the elite—senators, the nobility, and the urban upper class—Nero's death was largely welcomed as the end of a tyrannical rule. In contrast, among the lower strata, including enslaved people, spectators of arena and theater performances, and Nero's remaining supporters, the news was not universally greeted with approval. The military stance was mixed as well: portions of the troops remained loyal to Nero, but others were induced—or bribed—to join in his overthrow, reflecting a divided and transitional period in the power shift.

Lucan (c. 39–65 CE) was a Roman poet whose work is regarded more for literary merit than as strict historical chronicle. He offers one of the most favorable depictions of Nero's reign, portraying an era of peace and prosperity and contrasting it with the earlier periods of war and turmoil. In later years, Lucan became involved in a conspiracy to overthrow Nero, and he was executed.

The Attorney General of the United States serves as the chief legal advisor to the President, advising on appointments to federal judicial positions and to Department of Justice leadership roles, including United States Attorneys and United States Marshals. The office may represent the United States in the Supreme Court and in other courts, though such advocacy is typically handled by the Solicitor General. The Attorney General also performs or supervises other duties as mandated by statute or executive order.

Following the inauguration of President Donald Trump on January 20, 2017, Loretta Lynch left the office of Attorney General. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates, who had also tendered her resignation, remained in place to serve as acting attorney general, a role she exercised pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 508. Yates's tenure as acting head of the Department of Justice continued until Jeff Sessions was confirmed as the new attorney general. Sessions had been nominated by President-elect Trump in November 2016.

Steve Goodman’s posthumously released album Santa Ana Winds includes a tribute to Carl Martin in the form of the song You Better Get It While You Can (The Ballad of Carl Martin). The track honors the joy found in their music, and its chorus conveys a sense of life's brevity, urging listeners to appreciate and seize moments while they can.

Steve Goodman was an American folk singer-songwriter who performed at the Philadelphia Folk Festival six times between 1970 and 1978. His songs first appeared on Gathering at The Earl of Old Town, released in 1971 and produced by Dunwich Records. A close friend of Earl Pionke, owner of The Earl of Old Town, Goodman regularly performed there, totaling dozens of appearances including New Year’s Eve concerts. He maintained a sustained involvement with Chicago’s Old Town School of Folk Music, where he met and mentored John Prine.

Line 4 of the Guangzhou Metro operates as a south-to-north corridor, extending from Nansha Passenger Port in the south to Huangcun in the north. It covers a total length of 60.03 kilometers (37.30 miles) and comprises 24 stations, with Guanqiao station not yet in service. The line includes both underground and surface segments: Xinzao to Huangcun and Feishajiao to Nansha Passenger Port run underground, while the section from Jinzhou to Guanqiao is above ground. Its designated color is dark green. Trains on Line 4 use linear motor propulsion, the same technology employed by Lines 5 and 6.

On 23 October 2020, a Friday, BBC Radio 1 aired the third edition of Europe's Biggest Dance Show. French Mouv' withdrew from the broadcast until further notice, while Finnish YleX and Norwegian NRK mP3 joined the show.

February 2014 marked the end of Sara Cox's tenure at BBC Radio 1, as she returned to Radio 2 after presenting her final show on the station. In March 2014, Gemma Cairney left the weekend breakfast programme to take the weekday early breakfast slot, swapping shows with Dev.

ISO 8583 is an international standard governing the interchange of electronic transaction messages in card-based payment systems, including ATM and point-of-sale networks. The article notes that a table of response codes and their meanings is provided for the ISO 8583-1987 edition. As the standard evolved in later versions, the response codes were expanded to three- and four-digit formats, allowing more detailed status information to be conveyed.

ISO 8583 is an international standard governing the exchange of electronic messages between payment systems and participating entities such as card issuers and acquirers. It covers a broad spectrum of transactions initiated by cardholders, including purchases, cash withdrawals, deposits, refunds, reversals, balance inquiries, payments, and inter-account transfers. In addition, the standard specifies the structure and semantics of system-to-system messages that support administrative and operational functions, notably secure cryptographic key exchanges, the reconciliation of totals, and other management tasks.

Siren 7 and Siren 14 are components of the Siren codec family and, in many jurisdictions, their deployment requires obtaining patent licenses from Polycom. Polycom also provides a royalty-free licensing option for Siren 7 and Siren 14 to entities that meet a defined set of basic conditions.

Siren is an audio coding format utilized within FreeSWITCH, an open-source communications platform. The codec family includes Siren 7, corresponding to the G.722.1 standard, and Siren 14, corresponding to the G.722.1C variant. FreeSWITCH supports transcoding between these Siren formats, enables conference calls, and provides bridging between Siren 7 and Siren 14 streams, thereby facilitating interoperability among endpoints that use either variant.

Lauriela Martins was crowned Miss Angola 2017 on 18 December 2016, receiving the national title for the 2017 edition. She subsequently represented Angola at Miss Universe 2017, which took place in Las Vegas, Nevada, in November 2017, but she did not place among the top 16.

Lauriela Martins is an Angolan beauty pageant titleholder who secured the Miss Angola crown in 2017. Subsequently, she represented Angola at the Miss Universe pageant held in 2017. She is slated to represent Angola at Miss International 2025, scheduled to take place in Tokyo, Japan.
The 1996–97 Czech Cup was the fourth edition of the annual football knockout cup competition in the Czech Republic. It was organized by the Czech Football Association of the Czech Republic.

Double entendre is a term that originates from a now-rare French expression denoting a double meaning or ambiguity. In English, it acquired its current suggestive twist after the first recorded use by John Dryden in 1673. The corresponding French phrase has fallen out of use for centuries and would be ungrammatical in modern French. There is no exact French equivalent; while similar constructions such as à double entente or à double sens exist, they do not carry the same insinuating nuance as the English term.

Double entendre refers to a figure of speech in which a statement has two meanings, one of which is typically risqué, and it is a prominent feature of Shakespearean drama. Across his plays, the dramatist repeatedly employs this device to generate humor, suggest sexual subtext, or critique social norms while maintaining plausible deniability. In Twelfth Night, Sir Toby Belch’s remark about Sir Andrew’s hair is commonly read as containing sexual innuendo, implying intimate anatomy and acts without direct explicitness. In Romeo and Juliet, the Nurse’s aside about learning to walk carries a sexual insinuation, hinting at risqué consequences as wit grows. Mercutio’s line that combines coarse language with clock imagery further blends erotic suggestion with temporal reference to signal noon. Hamlet likewise subjects Ophelia to sexual puns, including a phrase that is explicitly tied to genitalia and a wider theme of sexual propriety. The comedy Much Ado About Nothing is frequently interpreted as having a title pun that plays on Elizabethan slang for female genitalia. Collectively, these examples illustrate how Shakespeare used double entendre to enrich dialogue, intensify characterization, and probe themes of desire, wit, and social decorum within his audience’s expectations.

Johannes Christian "Hans" Pflügler (born 27 March 1960) is a German former professional footballer who played as a left-back or central defender.
