Initially, only two statues were installed, while two others were represented by plaster models painted to resemble cast iron. By 27 December, six statues had been installed; the remaining six followed over time: two on 15 January 1823, one on 22 December 1823, one on 10 March 1825, and two on 17 June 1826. The monument's front side faces northeast toward the Hallesches Tor (Halle Gate).

Christian Daniel Rauch and Christian Friedrich Tieck were initially commissioned to design and model six statues apiece for the Prussian National Monument for the Liberation Wars. Delays followed as both artists were busy with other duties and not always present in Berlin. To keep the project moving, Ludwig Wilhelm Wichmann was appointed to model several of the genii in alignment with Rauch's and Tieck's designs. Additionally, Schinkel recommended using Pietro Perugino's frescoes in the audience hall of the Collegio del Cambio in Perugia as a reference for the genii.

JBIG2 defines three region types—text, halftone, and generic—that partition the data during compression. For each region type, either arithmetic coding or Huffman coding may be employed, providing flexibility in encoding efficiency. The standard uses the MQ coder as its entropy encoder, a mechanism that is also used in JPEG 2000.

JBIG2 employs two complementary strategies for halftone image compression. The first method uses a context-based coding technique, akin to arithmetic coding, that dynamically selects the placement of template pixels to exploit spatial correlations among adjacent pixels. The second method performs descreening to convert the halftone image back into grayscale, after which the grayscale values are interpreted as indices into a fixed-size halftone bitmap dictionary composed of small patterns. The decoder then reconstructs the halftone image by assembling neighboring dictionary bitmap patterns according to these indices, effectively rendering the final image.

During the early 2000s, progressive house developed through a synthesis of elements drawn from deep house, tech house, and progressive trance. Pioneering figures such as Sasha, John Digweed, Hernán Cattáneo, and Sander Kleinenberg played key roles in shaping its distinctive sound. The genre also intersected with progressive trance, with Deep Dish and Nick Warren incorporating more ethereal and cinematic textures into their productions and sets. A darker variant, known as dark progressive house, emerged as a deep, hypnotic, and atmospheric substyle within the broader genre.

The term progressive emerged in the 1970s popular music scene to distinguish experimental rock from mainstream styles, signaling an openness to exploring alternative production approaches within rock. In disco and later in house music, DJs and producers adopted the label to differentiate styles that were more exploratory from conventional approaches.

Rafieya Aasieya Husain, also known as Zara Husain, (born 24 May 1992) is a Guyanese model and beauty pageant titleholder. She captured the Miss World Guyana title in 2014 and subsequently represented Guyana at Miss World 2014 in London, where she advanced to the Top 11. In 2017 she earned the Miss Universe Guyana crown and went on to compete at Miss Universe 2017.

Delhi's urban agglomeration comprises Ghaziabad, Faridabad, Gurgaon, Noida, Greater Noida, and YEIDA city, and lies within the National Capital Region (NCR). The metropolitan area has a population of more than 28 million, making it the largest urban agglomeration in India and the second-largest in the world after Tokyo. It ranks fifth among Indian states and union territories in the human development index and possesses the second-highest GDP per capita in India, after Goa. The National Capital Territory of Delhi is a union territory with state-like features, including its own legislature, a high court, and an executive council of ministers headed by a chief minister. New Delhi is jointly administered by the central government and the local government and serves as the capital of both India and the NCT. Delhi is the core of the National Capital Region, an interstate regional planning area established in 1985. The territory has hosted a number of major events, including the 1951 and 1982 Asian Games; the 1983 Non-Aligned Movement summit; the 2010 Men's Hockey World Cup; the 2010 Commonwealth Games; the 2012 BRICS summit; the 2023 G20 summit, and has been a primary host city for the Cricket World Cups in 2011 and 2023.

According to the 50th report of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities in India, submitted in 2014, Delhi's language distribution shows Hindi as the predominant language at 80.94%, with Punjabi at 7.14%, Urdu at 6.31%, Bengali at 1.50%, and other languages making up 4.11%. In terms of official language policy, Hindi is the official language of Delhi, while Urdu and Punjabi are designated as additional official languages.

The Apache License is a permissive open-source license that does not require derivative works or modifications to be distributed under the same license. Nevertheless, it requires the license to be applied to all unmodified portions of the work. In every licensed file, the original copyright, patent, and trademark notices, along with attribution statements, must be preserved, except for notices not pertaining to any part of the derivative works. Whenever a licensed file is changed, a notice must be added to indicate that alterations have been made to that file.

Under the Apache License, contributions made by a licensee to the licensor are governed by the license’s own terms, and such contributions carry no additional terms or conditions beyond those terms. This default position remains in force unless an explicit provision indicates otherwise. The license does not preclude the parties from entering into separate agreements with the licensor regarding those contributions.
Marina di Campo Airport is a small airport that serves the island of Elba in the Tuscany region. It provides direct connections to the Italian mainland, with these routes operated by Silver Air.

Tuscany, a region of central Italy, witnessed the collapse of the Italian Social Republic and the transition from the Kingdom of Italy to the modern Italian Republic. During the postwar period, it emerged as a prominent cultural center within the nation, contributing to Italy's artistic and intellectual life. The regional government of Tuscany was established in 1970, creating a formal framework for regional administration. Since its creation, the region has been governed by centre-left administrations.

Not My Neighbour is a track by Walters that forms part of his forthcoming debut album Escape. The song is intentionally experimental, diverging from his usual soul-inspired style. Its conception drew on the literary sensibilities of Leonard Cohen and the filmic style of Quentin Tarantino, with the aim of telling a story through detailed visual imagery and offering a novel take on a classic love song. The track was produced with the help of Rory Noble, who serves as producer and musician, and Mikey Dam, a singer-songwriter, who contributed to its creation.

Known as the Last Gospel, the Gospel of John is best known for its opening prologue, which in the Latin tradition begins with a renowned phrase that presents the Word as existing from the beginning and as being with God. In standard English rendering, the passage is commonly translated as stating that the Word was present at the start, was with God, and was God.

The Last Gospel was incorporated into the Armenian Rite, which is employed by both the Armenian Apostolic Church and the Armenian Catholic Church. Its adoption reflects the historical contact between Latin Rite Crusaders and the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, illustrating how medieval interactions helped shape Armenian liturgical practice.

Set in the Tianbao era of the Tang dynasty, the tale unfolds in an imperial garden where Yang Guifei stands as the central figure, admiring a cluster of blossoms. As she reaches out to touch a flower, its petals fold toward the center and its leaves droop as if shy. A palace maid who witnesses the moment later records the scene. In the legend, Yang Guifei’s beauty is said to surpass the flowers themselves, prompting the blooms to bow their heads in reverent shame.

In the late Eastern Han dynasty period, Diao Chan is depicted in a garden offering prayers to the moon. A cloud drifts across the sky, veiling the moonlight. The narrative notes that Wang Yun commented that her beauty surpassed the moon’s own glow. In response to the comparison, the moon, feeling eclipsed by her radiance, retreats behind the clouds.

During the mid-20th century, popular resentment toward the aristocracy undermined traditional authority, while the sangha was divided into two rival factions and suffered from a low level of religious education and discipline. This milieu, together with opposition to Western influence, left many monks receptive to overtures from the Pathet Lao. The politicization of the sangha by both sides undermined its authority, yet its influence at the village level helped to reinforce support for the Pathet Lao. Taken together, these factors contributed to the 1975 change in government.

Religious life in Laos is characterized by a broad spectrum of beliefs, with Tai folk religion serving as the main tradition among northern Tai communities, including the Thai Dam and Thai Daeng, as well as among Mon-Khmer and Tibeto-Burman groups. In the lowland Lao population, many pre-Buddhist phi beliefs have been incorporated into Theravada Buddhist practices, producing a syncretic religious landscape. Christians—primarily Catholics and Protestants—make up about one to two percent of the population. Other minority faiths present in Laos include the Bahá’í Faith, Islam, Mahayana Buddhism, and Confucianism. A very small portion of citizens identify as atheist or agnostic.

The 1993 Australian Open men's singles event culminated in a final in which defending champion Jim Courier defeated Stefan Edberg in a rematch of the previous year's championship. The match concluded with a four-set score of 6–2, 6–1, 2–6, 7–5. The victory marked Courier's second Australian Open title and his fourth and final major singles title overall. For Edberg, the result represented his third runner-up finish at the Australian Open within the last four years.

Another Suitcase in Another Hall has been covered by several artists, including Elaine Paige, Marti Webb, Kimberley Walsh (Girls Aloud), and Samantha Barks. For the 1996 film adaptation, Madonna recorded a notable rendition in which her character Eva performs the song. Madonna's version was released on 3 March 1997 by Warner Bros as the third and final single from the film's soundtrack. In the film, the track is sung by Eva rather than the mistress, unlike in the stage musical. The release received positive reviews from music critics and reached the top ten in Italy and the United Kingdom.

Madonna's rendition of Another Suitcase in Another Hall begins with a softly strummed guitar delivering broken chords, establishing an intimate texture. The vocal delivery is breathy, underscoring a sense of vulnerability. The opening vocal entrance introduces a memorable melodic idea that poses the question of what comes next, a motif that is repeated twice at the start. According to Musicnotes.com, the arrangement is set in common time with a tempo of 50 BPM. It is written in C-flat major, and the vocal range extends from A3 to E♭5. The opening verse employs a C-flat–F-flat progression to accompany the line about love affairs not lasting long.

After the Northern Expedition, the Kuomintang consolidated its leadership in China and began constructing a Nationalist government grounded in Sun Yat-sen’s ideology. Within the Kuomintang’s party-state framework, five Yuans were established to oversee the principal state functions. The Auditing Yuan was founded in February 1928, and in February 1931 the Control Yuan was established, signaling the final addition to the five Yuans. The Auditing Yuan was subsequently downgraded to the National Audit Office, a ministry-level body operating within the Control Yuan. The creation of the Control Yuan on 16 February 1931 thus completed the five Yuans.

Taiwan's move toward democracy in the late 1980s culminated in constitutional reforms known as the Additional Articles of the Constitution. In the second amendment, dated May 27, 1992, the Control Yuan was removed from the parliament’s chambers and its members were relieved of legislative duties. The process for selecting and appointing Control Yuan leaders and members is modeled after the procedures of the Judicial Yuan and Examination Yuan, with officials nominated by the President and confirmed by the National Assembly, which served as the confirmation body to maintain separation of powers.

Lon Nol began his career in public service by joining the French colonial civil service in 1937, serving as a magistrate and enforcing French authority during anti-colonial disturbances in 1939. By 1946 he had risen to the post of Governor of Kratie Province. He subsequently became an associate of King Norodom Sihanouk, and in the late 1940s he established a right-wing, monarchist faction that advocated independence, marking his entry into Cambodian political life. In 1952 he joined the army, where he carried out military operations against the Viet Minh.

Lon Nol was appointed Army Chief of Staff in 1955. He subsequently rose to commander-in-chief of the armed forces in 1960, while also serving as minister of defence. A trusted ally of Sihanouk, Nol’s police helped suppress Cambodia’s clandestine communist movement. In 1963 he was appointed deputy prime minister. As Sihanouk pursued a policy of extreme neutrality and engaged with China while tolerating North Vietnamese activity along Cambodia’s eastern border, Nol remained friendly toward the United States and later regretted the end of American aid after 1963.

During his early teens, Dizzee Rascal began working as an amateur drum-and-bass DJ, rapping over tracks and making occasional appearances on local pirate radio stations. Two years later, at age 16, he self-produced his first single, "I Luv U," which was included on his debut. In the same year, he secured a solo contract with XL Recordings.

Boy in da Corner is the debut studio album by English grime artist Dizzee Rascal. It was released in the United Kingdom on 21 July 2003 through XL Recordings and in the United States on 20 January 2004 via Matador Records. The album peaked at number 23 on the UK Albums Chart and was certified Gold by the British Phonographic Industry for shipments of 100,000 copies. By 2004, it had sold over 250,000 copies worldwide, with US sales surpassing 58,000 copies by 2007. In July 2018, it was certified Platinum for 300,000 copies sold, marking Rascal's second Platinum-certified album after Tongue n' Cheek.

FV Northern Belle was a fishing vessel that sank in the Gulf of Alaska on April 20, 2010. Four crew members were aboard at the time, and three were rescued alive, while Captain Robert Royer died before rescue teams could reach the scene.

FV Northern Belle was involved in a maritime distress situation in which the vessel’s EPIRB did not operate. Captain Robert Royer returned to the bridge to send a distress call, an action that is believed to have saved the other crew members. Royer sustained a major head injury while attempting to jump overboard, and when the U.S. Coast Guard arrived, he was found without vital signs.

Chris Tompkins is an American songwriter who collaborated with Carrie Underwood on her 2012 album Blown Away, most notably on the album’s second single “Blown Away.” The track was co-written with Tompkins’s frequent collaborator Josh Kear. Music critic Kurt Wolff described the melody and overall sound as fresh and markedly different. Tompkins characterized “Blown Away” as an attempt at melodic pop that remains distinctly country, noting that it marks a departure for Underwood and draws on pop influences and a broad range of artists, a sensibility he says is evident in his own work and in the song. The single peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart and reached number one on Billboard’s Country Airplay chart, and it won the Grammy Award for Best Country Song in 2013.

Chris Tompkins launched his professional songwriting career after signing his initial publishing deal at age 22, an event that prompted his move to Nashville, Tennessee. In 2004, he earned his first top-20 hit on the Billboard charts through co-authorship of the song “Me and Emily” recorded by Rachel Proctor. A couple of years later, during the summer of 2006, Tompkins began collaborating with Big Loud Shirt Industries as a songwriter, marking a new phase in his industry involvement.

Square dance refers to a form of social dance whose organization varies across regions. It typically relies on a small repertoire of calls performed in a prescribed sequence. In revival circles, it is frequently interleaved with contra dances, providing alternating programs. Additionally, at certain local gatherings, performances may emphasize freestyle couple dancing rather than the traditional square patterns.

Within the square dance tradition, Irish and Scottish dances are ordinarily performed to traditional tunes. English dances may also be set to traditional melodies, but there is ongoing experimentation with a wide variety of musical styles. This exploratory approach is especially evident at ceilidhs, social gatherings that emphasize communal music and dancing.

ROKS Soyang (AOE-51) is a replenishment ship of the Republic of Korea Navy. Built by Hyundai Heavy Industries, the vessel was laid down on 13 July 2015, launched on 29 November 2016, and commissioned on 18 September 2018.

On 17 November 2020, the Republic of Korea Navy replenishment oiler ROKS Soyang (AOE-51) transferred medical supplies to the Philippine Navy's BRP Conrado Yap off Manila, Philippines. The items included three speed boats alongside COVID-19 prevention supplies such as masks and sanitizers, exchanged between the two ships during the transfer operation as part of a bilateral aid exchange.

The music video for Ain't Back Yet was directed by Shaun Silva and Joe Thomas. Thomas is also the director of the film Summer In 3D. The clip showcases Kenny Chesney performing live in concert, interwoven with archival footage from his earlier tours.

"Ain't Back Yet" is a song that elicited mixed reactions from music critics. Matt Bjorke of Roughstock praised the track for not adopting a Buffett-influenced country style and said it fits Kenny Chesney's approach, while also noting that the lyrics describe life on the road since the artist began touring. In contrast, Juli Thanki of Engine 145 offered a negative assessment, likening the song to a second-rate Jason Aldean track and criticizing the vocal performance as average and the lyrics as bland.

Net tonnage (NT) is a dimensionless index derived from the total molded volume of a vessel’s cargo spaces through a prescribed mathematical formula. It was defined by the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969, adopted under the auspices of the International Maritime Organization. NT superseded the earlier net register tonnage (NRT), which represented revenue-earning space expressed in register tons, with one register ton equal to 100 cubic feet (about 2.83 cubic metres). The measurement is employed in calculating port duties. International rules also require that NT not be less than 30 percent of the ship’s gross tonnage, i.e., NT ≥ 0.3 GT.

Net tonnage and gross tonnage are determined by measuring a ship’s volume and applying a defined mathematical formula to convert that volume into tonnage figures. Net tonnage is based on the moulded volume of all cargo spaces, while gross tonnage is based on the moulded volume of all enclosed spaces. In typical practice, the net tonnage must be at least thirty percent of the gross tonnage.

Hawaii experienced the largest shift in Senate seniority among states between the 112th and 113th Congresses. The state’s two senators previously ranked first and twenty-first in seniority, but the delegation was subsequently filled by Brian Schatz and Mazie Hirono, both newcomers to the Senate.

Following the 1893 coup, controversy surrounded Liliʻuokalani's bid to regain the throne. According to Lydia Kualapai, she yielded to United States force rather than to the Provisional Government and wrote to the U.S. president seeking allied support and restoration of sovereignty. In the aftermath, royalists sought to overthrow the white-led Republic of Hawaiʻi, with hundreds of rifles secretly shipped to Hawaii and concealed in caves. A patrol of the Republic of Hawaiʻi uncovered the rebel faction, and on January 6, 1895, gunfire began as the rebels were surrounded and captured. Over the next ten days, several skirmishes occurred until the remaining opposition surrendered or was taken into custody. The Republic of Hawaiʻi imprisoned 123 troops as prisoners of war, while approximately 300 more individuals, including Queen Liliʻuokalani, were arrested as political prisoners to incapacitate resistance. In March 1895, a military tribunal convicted 170 prisoners of treason; six troops were to be hanged, while others received sentences ranging from five to 35 years of hard labor, with lesser charges yielding six months to six years. The queen herself received a five-year sentence but spent eight months under house arrest before being released on parole. In total, 406 people were arrested in connection with the 1895 Kaua Kūloko.

The New Jersey sound, also known as the Jersey sound, is a subgenre of house music that blends deep house and garage house elements with a strong emphasis on soulful vocal performances. It originated in Newark, New Jersey, during the early 1980s, emerging from the city’s club culture and production milieu. The style draws on Newark’s gospel legacy, incorporating spiritual-inflected melodies and expressive, gospel-tinged vocals that distinguish it within the wider house music landscape.

Originating in the 1980s from Newark's Club Zanzibar and the residency of DJ Tony Humphries beginning in 1982, the New Jersey sound emerged as a raw yet soulful subgenre of deep house with gospel-infused textures, commonly referred to as the Jersey sound or New Jersey house. Regional variations in naming developed: in the United Kingdom the style was labeled garage music, a nod to Paradise Garage, while in New Jersey it was frequently described as the club sound or the Jersey sound. Mixmag documented these naming variations in a July 2020 issue. The scene also intersected with Newark's female vocalists whose performances were remixed by Larry Levan, including Gwen Guthrie with Ain't Nothin' Goin On But The Rent and Taana Gardner with Heartbeat.

West Asia encompasses a number of small, ancient Jewish communities alongside the Jewish-majority state of Israel, where Judaism is the predominant faith. The region is home to enduring Jewish communities with roots dating back centuries. Within this area, Turkey is home to approximately 14,300 Jews, Azerbaijan about 9,100, and Iran around 8,756.

West Asia, the westernmost region of the Asian continent, is also known as Western Asia or Southwest Asia. Its subregional constituents include Anatolia, the Arabian Peninsula, Iran, Mesopotamia, the Armenian Highlands, the Levant, the island of Cyprus, the Sinai Peninsula, and the South Caucasus. Geographically, it is separated from Africa by the Isthmus of Suez and from Europe by the Turkish Straits and the Greater Caucasus watershed. Its neighbors include Central Asia to the northeast and South Asia to the east. The region is bordered by a sequence of seas from the Aegean to the Mediterranean, namely the Aegean Sea, the Sea of Marmara, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea, the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Oman, the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aqaba, the Gulf of Suez, and the Mediterranean Sea. West Asia contains the majority of what is commonly termed the Middle East; however, the Middle East is a political term with varied territorial definitions, whereas West Asia represents a geographical designation with greater consistency. In terms of territorial boundaries, the region excludes most of Egypt and the northwestern part of Turkey, while it includes the southern Caucasus.

A songwriter works to extend a song's musical material by broadening both its melodic line and its harmonic progression; this often involves introducing an instrumental melody that complements the vocal line. The instrumental thread may be presented prior to the vocal melody, after it, or woven concurrently with the vocal line, depending on artistic intention and arrangement. Such expansion typically yields a more intricate song form, with additional structural elements such as verses, choruses, bridges, and instrumental solos.

Advances in digital audio workstations, plugin ecosystems, and affordable hardware have enabled songwriters to craft commercially viable music largely on personal laptops. This technological shift has increased the visibility and prevalence of the producer–songwriter role, with many individuals adopting both writing and production duties. Because audiences generally lack a clear understanding of the producer's function, listeners often fail to recognize when an artist also acts as a producer.

Nansha Passenger Port station serves as the southern terminus of Guangzhou Metro Line 4. The station began operations on 28 December 2017. In Simplified Chinese it is written as 南沙客运港站, in Traditional Chinese as 南沙客運港站, and in Cantonese Yale it is romanized as Nàahmsā Haak'wahngóng Jaahm.

InfoSpace was founded in March 1996 by Naveen Jain after his departure from Microsoft. The company began with six employees, and Jain served as chief executive officer until 2000. It provided content and services such as phone directories, maps, games, and stock market information to partner websites and mobile device manufacturers. Growth was pursued at low cost through co-branding strategies and by leveraging relationships with partner sites rather than attracting direct traffic, with Lycos, Excite, and Playboy embedding InfoSpace features and displaying the InfoSpace icon on their pages. Revenue was generated from a limited share of licensing, subscription, or advertising fees. The firm went public on December 15, 1998, under the ticker INSP, and raised about $75 million.

InfoSpace Corporation acquired TaxAct in January 2012, expanding its portfolio into online tax preparation services. To distinguish itself from TaxAct and from its own InfoSpace search unit, the company rebranded as Blucora. On April 21, 2014, Discovery Communications announced the sale of HowStuffWorks to Blucora for $45 million.

The 2024 End of Year Charts constitute the official year-end rankings for New Zealand singles for the calendar year 2024. The rankings are determined from a combination of sales and streaming data, and they include any single that was eligible to appear on the weekly Official Aotearoa Music Charts at any point during 2024.

New Zealand top 50 singles of 2024 presents the end-of-year ranking of the year's top-selling singles in New Zealand, based on data from the Official New Zealand Music Chart. The list is compiled by Recorded Music NZ (RMNZ). In addition to the main chart, RMNZ published two supplementary 2024 charts: a Top 20 of singles released by New Zealand artists and a Top 20 of singles predominantly performed in te reo Māori.

In Ukraine, the language regime governing court proceedings has evolved to accommodate linguistic diversity. Beginning in 2010, courts were permitted to conduct hearings in Russian with the mutual consent of the parties involved. Individuals who do not speak Ukrainian or Russian may participate using their native language or with the help of a translator. Previously, all court proceedings were conducted exclusively in Ukrainian, reflecting a monolingual framework.

Ukraine is the second-largest country in Europe by area after Russia, and the largest country entirely in Europe. It lies roughly between 44° N and 53° N latitudes and 22° E and 41° E longitudes. The country is situated largely on the East European Plain. It covers an area of 603,550 square kilometres (233,030 square miles) and has a coastline of 2,782 kilometres (1,729 miles).

Jakub Menšík attained the ITF junior combined ranking of world No. 3 on 31 January 2022 while competing on the junior tour. In 2022, he progressed to the final of the Australian Open junior singles event, highlighting his standing among rising junior players.

Jakub Menšík, selected under the ATP’s new NextGen programme to compete at the 2024 Qatar ExxonMobil Open (ATP 250), began the event ranked at No. 116 in the world. He opened with a straight-sets victory over Alejandro Davidovich Fokina to reach the second round, then stunned Andy Murray in a three-set clash featuring three tiebreaks that lasted 3 hours and 23 minutes, advancing to his first ATP quarterfinal. There, he defeated top seed Andrey Rublev in straight sets, recording his first win over a player in the top 10 and top five, and reaching his first ATP semifinal; he became the youngest player to defeat a top-5 opponent since Carlos Alcaraz in the 2021 US Open. He continued by defeating Gaël Monfils in three sets to reach his first ATP final. The sequence propelled him upward by roughly 30 ranking places, making him the youngest player in the top 100. In the final, he was defeated by second seed Karen Khachanov.

Research on sexual arousal indicates sex-based differences in arousal patterns that appear to be largely independent of an individual's sexual orientation. In women, genital arousal has been observed in response to both human sexual stimuli and non-human visual stimuli, such as those depicting bonobos. Women also show arousal to erotic material involving partners of both sexes, indicating responsiveness to heterosexual and homosexual human-sexual stimuli. In contrast, men did not exhibit sexual arousal to non-human visual stimuli like bonobos. Instead, men’s arousal patterns tend to correspond to their sexual orientation, with heterosexual men aroused by female stimuli and homosexual men by male stimuli.

Sexual orientation refers to enduring patterns of emotional, romantic, and sexual attraction, and the mechanisms by which it develops remain unclear. It is not a matter of choice, and individuals do not choose to be homosexual or heterosexual. A range of theories about potential influences has been proposed, and it is likely that orientation arises from a combination of genetic, hormonal, and environmental factors rather than a single cause. In recent decades, biologically based explanations have gained prominence, though there remains ongoing controversy and uncertainty about the origins of different sexual orientations. There is no scientific evidence that abnormal parenting, sexual abuse, or other adverse life events determine one's orientation. Sexual orientation is typically established during early childhood.

The Bombing of Chongqing refers to the Japanese aerial bombardment campaign against Chongqing, the wartime capital of China, during the Second Sino-Japanese War, in which Chinese airmen mounted determined defenses over the city. The air battles occurred after Japanese forces had driven the Chinese authorities from the former capitals of Nanjing and Wuhan, leaving Chongqing as the principal focus of military engagement in the skies. The episode has been dramatized in the action-war film Air Strike, which features Bruce Willis alongside Liu Ye and Song Seung-heon, among others.

Between 1939 and 1942, Chongqing was subjected to roughly 3,000 tons of aerial bombs. In the spring of 1941, contemporary photographer Carl Mydans described these bombardments as the most destructive shelling of a city up to that date. By way of comparison, Berlin endured about 2,300 tons in a single night during the Battle of Berlin. Across the campaign, Chongqing endured a total of 268 air raids.

Balboa is a brisk eight-count partner dance performed in closed position. The earliest form, Pure Balboa, arose in conservative Southern California dance halls where space was limited and etiquette codes were strict, leading to prohibitions on the wild kicks associated with Charleston and Lindy Hop. Pure Balboa is characterized by an upright posture with partners in chest-to-chest contact, while its step variations emphasize the rhythm and feel sourced from below the knee and frequent changes in direction. It is typically danced to fast jazz, with tempos commonly ranging from about 180 to 320 beats per minute, though some dancers prefer approximately 170 to 190 BPM. Pure Balboa and Bal-Swing are distinct but both belong to the Balboa family; Bal-Swing emerged as dancers developed more elaborate variations that loosened the chest-to-chest connection, incorporating spins, turns, dips, tricks, and air steps.

Swing dancing is placed within the American Rhythm category. In competitive contexts, events typically comprise several divisions, with categories that vary by the specific dance style being performed.

During the Bournemouth Blitz, several prominent buildings were targeted in Bournemouth, including the Central Hotel on Richmond Hill, the Shamrock and Rambler coach station on Holdenhurst Road, and Beales department store; the Methodist church on Exeter Road was destroyed, and 77 people were killed.

On 27 March 1941, a lone German bomber targeted the canteen at the Bourne Valley gasworks, resulting in 33 fatalities. The attack was the deadliest air raid Poole experienced during the Bournemouth Blitz.

Chilcotin author and hunting guide Ted "Chilco" Choate, based at Gaspard Lake in the southeastern Chilcotin, writes about wildlife, hunting, and the region's wilderness lifestyle. His work emphasizes the relationships between animals and people within the Chilcotin's rugged landscape. Choate has advocated merging several adjacent wilderness areas—Tweedsmuir, Tsʼilʔos, Spruce Lake/South Chilcotin, Big Creek, and Churn Creek—into a single extensive national park. He contends that such a park would span the Coast Mountains and the plateau between the Fraser River and the spine of the Coast Mountains, creating a continuous protected region.

Chilcotin Country contains two World Heritage Site designations: Edwards's cabin and the trumpeter habitat. Edwards's cabin, listed as a World Heritage Site, was destroyed by extensive forest fires in the summer of 2004. The trumpeter habitat is also recognized as a World Heritage Site, underscoring the region's ecological significance.

Hubei Province in central China contains the Hubei Provincial Museum in Wuhan, which houses a broad array of archaeological artifacts and cultural displays and also presents performances of ancient music and dance. The museum is a leading resource for understanding the ancient state of Chu, a polity that flourished in the territory corresponding to present-day Hubei and that existed during the Eastern Zhou dynasty. Chu developed its own distinctive cultural tradition, setting it apart from the northern Shang and Zhou civilizations.

Hubei Province, located in central China, is predominantly inhabited by Han Chinese. In the province’s southwestern region, sizeable populations of Miao and Tujia people contribute to the area’s ethnic diversity. The Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture stands out as a key area for Miao and Tujia communities within Hubei, reflecting the significance of these groups in the province’s demographic makeup.

In June 1998, Curtis Wilbur entered a second shipyard availability period at Yokosuka, a nine-week overhaul during which the ship received upgrades to its communications and combat systems, including JTIDS/Link 16, JMCIS 98, and INMARSAT B, along with numerous engineering and combat-system enhancements, changes described as rendering the destroyer among the most capable units in the U.S. Seventh Fleet. By August 1998 the availability period and sea trials were completed, and a new training cycle began as the ship deployed with FOAL Eagle ’98 alongside the Republic of Korea Navy, where Curtis Wilbur earned Cruise Missile Tactical Qualification and Naval Surface Fire Support qualification. The training cycle also included certification of the Main Space Fire Drill for ECERT at TSTA II, achieving a near flawless ECERT performance. After completing a second full training cycle while forward deployed, the ship participated in Exercise Sharem 127 with the Korean Navy. In March 1999, Curtis Wilbur deployed with the Kitty Hawk Battle Group.

USS Curtis Wilbur (DDG-54) participated in Missilex '02, a United States Navy exercise designed to practice anti-ship missile defense, conducted on February 7–8, 2002, in a training area off Okinawa. The event involved a number of U.S. ships, including Curtis Wilbur, Essex, Cowpens, Chancellorsville, O'Brien, Cushing, John S. McCain, Vandegrift, Gary, and the supply vessel John Ericsson, alongside a Japanese participant, Sagami. On February 7–8, all vessels took part except John Ericsson and Sagami, which conducted replenishment-at-sea operations earlier in the exercise.

Zhongnan University of Economics and Law comprises 19 schools and offers a wide array of degree programs, including 51 undergraduate programs, 104 master’s programs, 57 doctoral programs, and 6 post-doctoral programs. The institution also maintains a state-level key humanities research base and four state-level key disciplines, along with ten provincial-level key humanities research bases and nineteen ministerial- or provincial-level key disciplines, reflecting a strong emphasis on research excellence across humanities and related fields.

Zhongnan University of Economics and Law maintains a research‑intensive faculty comprising more than 2,660 full‑time teaching and administrative staff. The faculty includes 219 professors, 500 associate professors, and 160 doctoral supervisors, underscoring the institution’s emphasis on academic leadership and graduate training. The university is authorized to confer a range of degrees, including the MBA, EMBA, JM, MPAcc, MPA, and ME (Master of Education). It also enrolls students from overseas as well as from Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macao. The MBA program has earned accreditation from the Association of MBAs.

At the Ultra Music Festival on 19 March 2016, Avicii (Bergling) unveiled several new Sandro Cavazza demos—“We Burn (Faster Than Light)”, “Lord”, “Our Love”, and “Unbreakable”—as well as a collaboration with Sia titled “All I Need,” all of which remained unreleased. On 29 March 2016, he announced via Facebook that he would retire from performing later that year due to health concerns. A few weeks later, on 7 April 2016, he stated that he was working on a third studio album. On 3 June 2016, he released a collaboration with Otto Knows titled “Back Where I Belong.”
On December 9, 2015, Avicii released a remix of his track “Broken Arrows.” The remix was featured on the YouTube Rewind 2015 soundtrack.

China Railway High-speed (CRH) is the high-speed rail service in China, established as part of the sixth national railway speedup and becoming operational on 18 April 2007. By the end of 2020, CRH networks connected every province and operated roughly 38,000 kilometers of passenger‑carrying track, accounting for about two‑thirds of the global high‑speed rail lines in commercial use. Plans envisage expanding the system to approximately 70,000 kilometers by 2035. The service is the most extensively used railway system worldwide, with ridership totaling 2.29 billion in 2019 and 2.16 billion in 2020, bringing the cumulative total to around 13 billion by 2020.

China Railway operates passenger and freight transportation throughout the country and is organized into 18 regional bureaus. As of September 2022, the total assets of China Railway Group stood at CNY 9.06 trillion (about USD 1.24 trillion). China records the highest level of railway usage globally.
John A. Lardner (May 4, 1912 – March 24, 1960) was an American sports writer, a World War II correspondent, and an author. He was the son of Ring Lardner.

John Lardner attended Phillips Academy, graduating in 1929, and after a year at Harvard he spent a year studying at the Sorbonne in Paris, writing for the International Herald Tribune. He did not complete his college degree. In 1931, he began working for the New York Herald Tribune, following his father into sports journalism. He authored a weekly Newsweek column titled "Sport Week" and was associated with Newsweek from 1939 onward, continuing until his death. From 1933 to 1948, he served as a sports columnist and war correspondent for the North American Newspaper Alliance.

Doppler weather radar determines the radial component of motion by measuring the Doppler shift of backscattered energy. In a representative configuration with a pulse repetition frequency of 2 kHz and a transmit frequency of 1 GHz, the highest unambiguous radial velocity that can be reliably retrieved is about 150 m/s (roughly 340 mph). This limit follows from the Nyquist criterion, given the radar wavelength λ ≈ c/f ≈ 0.3 meters, which yields a maximum unambiguous velocity v_max = (λ·PRF)/4 ≈ 150 m/s. As a result, objects moving faster than this—such as an aircraft traveling at 1,000 m/s (approximately 2,200 mph)—would exceed the unambiguous Doppler range, rendering their radial velocity measurements unreliable without adjustments such as increasing the PRF or employing additional observing strategies.

Radar collects historical position data from its sensors over a span of several minutes, which is used to forecast the future positions of observed objects. This predictive information underpins a range of applications, including air traffic control, threat estimation, combat-system doctrine, gun aiming, and missile guidance. By accumulating positional data over short time intervals, radar provides the basis for trajectory forecasting and related decision-making in these domains.

The flight deck cruiser refers to a proposed class of warship intended to combine a full aircraft flight deck with cruiser‑type armament and defenses; however, no such vessel was built by the United States Navy. The Soviet Kiev-class aircraft carrier, developed in the 1970s, bears a notable resemblance to the original flight‑deck cruiser concept, sharing the arrangement of an angled flight deck located at the aft for aircraft operations and forward anti‑ship missile launchers to boost its strike capability.

Proposals for a flight-deck cruiser emerged in 1934, with a design that envisioned a warship carrying a dedicated flight deck. The armament was to consist of twelve 6-inch (152 mm) guns arranged fore and aft. The 200-foot (61 m) flight deck was planned to lie between the ship’s gun batteries. In 1939 a revived concept proposed mounting two triple turrets at the fore and aft ends of the vessel, while the later version located the flight deck amidships, effectively placing it near the center of the hull.

Landing platform helicopter (LPH) denotes a class of naval vessels configured to operate helicopters, and in Royal Navy terminology ships converted to helicopter-only operations were commonly described as Commando Carriers. HMS Ocean served in the LPH role before being sold to the Brazilian Navy in 2018. After the Harrier withdrawal at the end of 2010, HMS Illustrious, previously a light fleet carrier, also operated in this helicopter-oriented capacity until its decommissioning in 2014.

Landing Platform Helicopter (LPH) denotes an amphibious warfare ship designed primarily to launch and recover helicopters and other vertical takeoff and landing aircraft. It is considered a type of helicopter carrier.

In July 2018, Navantia announced an agreement with the Royal Saudi Navy for the construction of five Avante 2000-class corvettes. The programme envisions the final vessel being delivered by 2022, with an estimated total cost of approximately €2 billion.

In December 2014, the United States awarded Lockheed Martin a Foreign Military Sale contract for the Mk 41 Vertical Launching System to Saudi Arabia. The lack of Saudi surface ships compatible with the Mk 41 and the absence of announced plans for a land-based missile defense led observers to infer that Riyadh was moving toward the acquisition of a VLS-equipped surface combatant. Saudi Arabia evaluated several platforms capable of hosting VLS, including the Arleigh Burke-class destroyer and the Freedom-class littoral combat ship variant known as the Multi-Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC). In October 2015, the U.S. Congress was informed of a possible sale of MMSC ships, a variant of the LCS, to Saudi Arabia, signaling continued consideration of a modern, VLS-capable surface combatant within the Royal Saudi Navy.

During the draw for the 1982 FIFA World Cup, organizers operated under a rule that forbade any group from containing more than one South American team. Pot B comprised two South American teams and four European sides, and the plan was to place the first two European teams drawn from Pot B into Groups 3 and 6, which already hosted Argentina and Brazil, with Chile and Peru subsequently added to the pot and the draw proceeding normally. However, Blatter and Neuberger overlooked the stipulation, placing the first team drawn from Pot B, Belgium, into Group 1 rather than Group 3. The second team drawn, Scotland, was subsequently allocated to Group 3; to correct the error, Belgium was moved to Group 3 and Scotland to Group 6. Complicating the ceremony further, a revolving drum used to draw the teams broke down during the proceedings.

The 1982 FIFA World Cup in Spain utilized seventeen stadiums across fourteen cities, a configuration that set a World Cup record for the number of venues, a record that would stand until 2002 when twenty stadiums across two countries were used. Camp Nou in Barcelona, the home ground of FC Barcelona, was the most frequently used venue, hosting five matches including a semi-final, and it was the largest stadium employed. Sarrià Stadium, also in Barcelona, hosted three matches. In terms of city distribution, Barcelona hosted eight matches—more than any other Spanish city—while Madrid hosted seven. The tournament’s only newly constructed venue was Estadio José Zorrilla in Valladolid.

On 3 May 1945, fighting in Innsbruck ended as the United States 103rd Infantry Division entered the city, bringing the combat to a close there. Earlier, Gauleiter Franz Hofer delivered a radio speech in which he urged the population to discontinue resistance and to submit to the advancing Allied forces.

During the Innsbruck bombing mission in World War II, aircrew members who had been wounded nonetheless remained at their assigned posts. On the second approach to the target, the bomber formation encountered heavy, intense, and accurate anti-aircraft fire. Despite the intense fire, the group leader kept the remaining aircraft cohesive and led the formation through a flawless bombing run, delivering a precise strike on the target.

Chongqing Xiannüshan Airport is a regional facility that serves Wulong, Chongqing, China. It bears the IATA code CQW and the ICAO code ZUWL. The airport is located in Xiannüshan town (also spelled Xiannyushan or Xiannvshan), about 20 km (12 mi) north of the urban center of Wulong District. It was conceived primarily to support tourism to the Wulong Karst landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Construction began in 2014 and continued for five years. The project was estimated to cost about 1.333 billion yuan (approximately $145 million).

Slovakia is home to nine national parks, collectively accounting for about 6.5 percent of the country’s land area. The parks are Tatra National Park, Low Tatras National Park, Veľká Fatra National Park, Slovak Karst National Park, Poloniny National Park, Malá Fatra National Park, Muránska planina National Park, Slovak Paradise National Park, and Pieniny National Park.

In Slovakia, autumn is commonly considered to begin on 23 September, marking a seasonal transition that is frequently accompanied by variable weather. The period is typically associated with wet and windy conditions overall, though the opening weeks of autumn can bring comparatively warm and sunny spells. September usually records an average temperature near 14 °C (57 °F), while November averages around 3 °C (37 °F). The late September to early October interval is often drier and sunnier than other parts of the season, a pattern sometimes described as an Indian summer.

Jeffery Lamar Williams, known professionally as Young Thug, was born on August 16, 1991, in Atlanta, Georgia, and is the tenth of eleven children. Although he is associated with the Sylvan Hills area, he spent his formative years in the Jonesboro South housing projects near Cleveland Avenue. The Jonesboro South neighborhood has produced other notable rappers, including Waka Flocka Flame and Ludacris. Peewee Longway is cited as Williams's childhood friend from Jonesboro South, and Williams lived four doors down from him during their youth.

In April 2015, gunfire was directed at the Lil Wayne tour bus by individuals linked to the Bloods street gang. The bus driver subsequently filed a civil lawsuit naming Young Thug alongside Cash Money Records, Young Money Entertainment, and Birdman as defendants.

The International DOI Foundation (IDF) oversees the integration of technologies and the operation of the DOI system through both a technical framework and a social infrastructure. The social infrastructure comprises a federation of autonomous registration agencies that provide DOI-related services. This federated model draws on precedents from other successful distributed identifier systems, such as GS1 and ISBN, to ensure interoperability and governance across participants.

The International DOI Foundation (IDF) is governed by a board elected by its Foundation members. An appointed managing agent coordinates and plans the foundation’s activities. Membership is open to any organization with an interest in electronic publishing and the enabling technologies that support it. Each year, the IDF convenes open meetings focused on DOI matters and related topics.

Architecture originates from the interaction between human needs—such as shelter, security, and ritual spaces—and the resources available, including materials and skilled labor. As societies advance and knowledge becomes formalized, frequently through oral tradition, construction evolves from a practical craft into a formal discipline, with architecture signaling the recognized, deliberate aspects of designing and erecting buildings. Success in architectural practice is widely regarded as the result of iterative experimentation, where methods and forms are refined and increasingly replicated as outcomes improve. Today, vernacular architecture continues to be produced across many regions, reflecting local climates, cultures, and resources while coexisting with more formal architectural traditions.

Since the 1980s, the design and construction of buildings have grown more complex across structural systems, building services, energy performance, and related technologies. This complexity has driven architecture to become increasingly multidisciplinary, with distinct specializations tied to project type, technical domains, or preferred delivery methods. Consequently, there has been a greater separation between the design architect, who conceptualizes the overall approach, and the project architect, who ensures standards, coordinates compliance, and assumes liability. Preparatory design for large-scale buildings has likewise grown more intricate, requiring systematic analyses of durability, sustainability, quality, cost, and adherence to local regulations. As a result, the creation of substantial structures no longer rests with a single practitioner, but depends on the collaboration of multiple professionals across disciplines.
Tangkeng station (塘坑站) is a Guangzhou Metro station on Line 4. The station opened to passengers on 28 December 2017. In Cantonese Yale, the name is pronounced Tòhnghāang Jaahm.

The Order of Myths is a 2008 documentary directed by Margaret Brown that examines Mardi Gras celebrations in Mobile, Alabama. It notes that Mobile hosts the oldest Mardi Gras celebration in the United States and investigates the existence of separate mystic societies created and sustained by Black and White communities. By highlighting these divisions, the film acknowledges Mobile’s complex racial history and its legacy of slavery, placing contemporary festivities within a broader historical context.

The Order of Myths garnered notable recognition from critics in 2008, appearing on several year-end top-ten lists of the best films of that year. Among those acknowledgments, Andrew O’Hehir of Salon placed it ninth on his list, Ella Taylor of LA Weekly likewise ranked it ninth (tied with Moving Midway), and Wesley Morris of The Boston Globe also identified it as ninth. The film later received a Peabody Award in 2010, reflecting its significance and impact within documentary filmmaking.

Critics offered a largely positive appraisal of Masterpiece, with Entertainment Weekly’s Kyle Anderson describing it as a throwback to Madonna’s mid-1990s style, while The National’s Nick Levine suggested the track would fit on her 1995 ballads collection Something to Remember. Blogcritics’ Tyrone S. Reid characterized the song as a slow-burning, instantly memorable piece that recalls the Ray of Light era, and Idolator’s writer commended the restrained production for placing emphasis on the lyrics and vocal performance, implying strong potential for Madonna’s MDNA era. Digital Spy’s Robert Copsey also praised the production as more organic, deeming the song a solid pop composition.

During Madonna's MDNA Tour, the addition of the Kalakan trio enriched the live rendition of Masterpiece, augmenting its arrangement and overall impact. The studio track had already been singled out as a stand-out on the MDNA album. Critics highlighted the performance, with Melissa Ruggieri of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution naming it the show's highlight, and a writer for The Glasgow Herald stating that the performance invigorated Madonna's artistic sensibilities.

Fat Wreck Chords operated two subsidiary labels, Honest Don's and Pink & Black. Honest Don's issued records by Chixdiggit and Teen Idols, among others. Pink & Black released albums from female-fronted bands, including Fabulous Disaster and Dance Hall Crashers.

Fat Wreck Chords has issued a series of charitable and commemorative compilations since its previous Fat Music release. Liberation: Songs to Benefit PETA functions as a fundraiser for the animal-rights organization PETA. PROTECT: A Benefit for the National Association to Protect Children supports the rights of children through the organization PROTECT. Between these releases, Rock Against Bush, Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 appeared as protest albums directed at President George W. Bush and his administration. To mark twenty years in operation, the label released Wrecktrospective, a three-disc compilation on December 8, 2009; Disc 1 collects the label's greatest-hits selections, Disc 2 comprises unreleased demos and rarities, and Disc 3 presents the entire Fat Club 7" series.

Tropical rock is a fusion of rock music with tropical-inspired motifs and imagery, and its development has been shaped in part by Jimmy Buffett, who is widely regarded as a leading figure in the genre. Buffett is associated with the Coral Reefer Band, the ensemble with which he performs and records. In the early to mid-1980s, Higgins helped cultivate a tropical subculture that supported the growth of this musical scene. Over time, Trop Rock has been embraced by a number of mainstream artists, including Jack Johnson, Zac Brown Band, Alan Jackson, and Kenny Chesney, who have released Trop Rock songs or incorporated tropical elements into their broader repertoires.

Tropical rock is a music genre associated with southern Florida and the Gulf Coast of the United States, rooted in a fusion of calypso, rock, and country traditions. Its early foundations are evident in the work of artists such as Jerry Jeff Walker, while Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band helped foster a tropical subculture around the style. This subculture emerged in the early to mid-1980s, with other performers, including Bertie Higgins, contributing to its development and visibility.

Waco, Texas, sits along the Brazos River and contains a mix of recreational, historical, and cultural landmarks. Hawaiian Falls water park is a notable local attraction, while the Grand Lodge of Texas ranks among the largest fraternal lodges in the world. The Waco Suspension Bridge, completed in 1870, is a single-span suspension bridge that spans the Brazos River. Indian Spring Park preserves the town’s origins, marking where the Huaco Indians settled on the riverbank at the site of an icy spring. The Doris Miller Memorial is a public art installation along the riverfront, and on December 7, 2017, a nine-foot bronze statue honoring Doris Miller was unveiled and temporarily located at Bledsoe-Miller Park.

On August 6, 1930, at Katy Park in Waco, Texas, a night game between Waco and Beaumont was played. Gene Rye, the Waco left fielder, delivered a historic performance by hitting three home runs in a single inning, the eighth. This achievement remains the only instance in professional baseball history of a player hitting three homers in one inning.

Pixlet, a name formed as a shortened form of the term Pixar wavelet, was introduced by Steve Jobs at the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) in 2003. Contemporary reports from that period indicated that the codec had been developed at Pixar's request.

Pixlet is a wavelet-based video codec developed by Apple Inc. that supports real-time playback of full-resolution high-definition footage at data rates comparable to DV. Apple described its compression efficiency as roughly 20 to 25:1. Like DV, Pixlet relies on intraframe compression and does not employ interframe techniques. The codec is intended as an editing format and is particularly suitable for previewing material in production environments and within visual effects workflows. However, its low bitrates limit its applicability for broadcast use.

John Henry Newman described Pope Pius V as stern and severe, yet aflame with divine love. His energetic leadership was regarded as essential for the era's pressing needs, and he is portrayed as a soldier of Christ amid a period of insurrection and rebellion within Christendom. In a spiritual sense, his governance imposed a form of martial discipline, enforcing order and reform within the Church.

During his papacy, Pope Pius V pursued a policy marked by strict enforcement and disciplined governance. A central element was the effort to sustain and enhance the effectiveness of the Roman Inquisition, reinforcing its role in doctrinal policing. Simultaneously, the enforcement of the canons and decrees of the Council of Trent was prioritized as a central objective, reflecting the broader Counter-Reformation program. Collectively, these priorities took precedence over other considerations in shaping his administration and religious policy.

Jiangsu, as of 2022, has 168 higher education institutions, the most of any Chinese province. The province hosts two Project 985 universities and eleven Project 211 universities, and it has sixteen Double First-Class Construction universities. In addition, 93 members of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Chinese Academy of Engineering are based in Jiangsu, reflecting the region's substantial concentration of leading scientists and engineers.

Wuxi Metro, the rapid transit system serving the city of Wuxi in Jiangsu Province, began operations in July 2014. By 2022, the network comprised four lines in operation—Line 1, Line 2, Line 3, and Line 4. Two additional lines were under construction, namely Line S1 and an extension of Line 4.

ISO/IEC 23092-5, a part of the MPEG-G standard, defines conformance testing for the coding of genomic information. Part 5 provides a normative method to test and validate correct MPEG-G implementations across devices and applications, with the overarching aim of ensuring interoperability among all systems that handle MPEG-G data. The specification prescribes a formal procedure to assess conformity to the standard, utilizing an exhaustive set of compressed data to verify client and device compliance.

MPEG-G, formally ISO/IEC 23092, defines a unified and efficient format for representing and compressing the broad spectrum of genomic data generated by high-throughput sequencing. The growth of HTS has transformed quantitative biology by enabling the routine creation of large genomic datasets that underpin numerous fields, including personalized medicine. Historically, genomic data have been exchanged using domain-specific formats such as FASTA and FASTQ for unaligned reads, and SAM, BAM, or CRAM for aligned reads. MPEG-G is intended to support both file storage and data transport, offering a single framework capable of handling diverse data types and workflows. The standard is organized into several parts, each addressing different aspects such as encoding methods, metadata, access mechanisms, and interoperability.

Pontianak Teochew is a variety of the Teochew language spoken in Pontianak, Indonesia. It retains the final -t associated with the entering tone from Middle Chinese, whereas the majority of Teochew dialects no longer exhibit this ending. Consequently, Pontianak Teochew is viewed as preserving an older Middle Chinese phonological feature relative to other Teochew dialects.

Pontianak Teochew, a regional variety of Teochew spoken in Pontianak, Indonesia, exhibits syntactic patterns that align with the broader typology of Chinese varieties. Existential constructions in Pontianak Teochew employ a word order that mirrors that of Mandarin and other Chinese dialects. In verbal-predicate clauses, the language predominantly follows a subject–verb–object configuration, a pattern that is characteristic of many Chinese languages.

In English, the terms modern and contemporary are frequently treated as synonyms, a convention that can foster conflation and confusion between modern art and contemporary art among non-specialists. This equivalence has led some experts to view the boundary separating the two as blurred or not clearly defined, reflecting differing methodological approaches and historical contexts. A concrete illustration of this ambiguity appears in the practices of the Musée National d'Art Moderne, whose collections do not distinguish between modern and contemporary works, signaling a practical lack of formal separation between the categories.

Contemporary art exists at the intersection of publicly funded organizations and the commercial sector, with close relationships between the two spheres. A 2005 source noted that in Britain a small number of dealers represented artists who were featured in leading publicly funded contemporary art museums. The commercial art sector comprises galleries and art fairs, which operate alongside publicly funded institutions in presenting and circulating contemporary work.

Miscarriage, defined as the spontaneous loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently, is the most common complication of early pregnancy. The most common symptom is vaginal bleeding, with or without pain, and it may be evidenced by the passage of clot-like material through the vagina. About 80 percent of miscarriages occur during the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. In about half of cases, the underlying cause involves chromosomal abnormalities.

Globally, pregnancy-related ill health affects more than 20 million women each year, with some conditions resulting in lasting impairment. Mortality from pregnancy complications has declined from 377,000 deaths in 1990 to 230,600 deaths in 2016. The major recorded causes of death include hemorrhage (72,000), infections (20,000), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (32,000), obstructed labour (10,000), and pregnancy with abortive outcomes (20,000), the latter encompassing miscarriage, abortion, and ectopic pregnancy.

The article provides a catalog of the military operations carried out during 1967 in the Vietnam War. These operations were conducted by the armed forces of the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam), the United States, and their allies.

In 1999, Books-A-Million acquired NetCentral, the firm responsible for designing the company’s website. Subsequently, the company began operating American Wholesale Book Company, a book wholesaler and distributor.

Books-A-Million maintains a diversified portfolio of subsidiaries, including Yogurt Mountain Holding, a frozen yogurt retailer and franchisor with 40 locations; Preferred Growth Properties, which develops and manages commercial real estate investments; American Wholesale Book Company (AWBC), the company’s e-commerce arm that operates the booksamillion.com online store; and NetCentral, an internet development and services firm based in Nashville, Tennessee.

Among Asian seiners, the wheelhouse is typically placed toward the bow with the working deck toward the stern, a configuration reminiscent of stern trawlers. In labor-intensive, low-technology regions, such vessels are often undecked. In those regions, propulsion may come from outboard motors or from sails.

Seiners are a category of fishing vessels that employ surrounding nets in combination with seine nets to encircle and capture schools of fish. This group spans a wide range of sizes, from small open-boat forms roughly 10 meters in length (about 33 feet) to large ocean-going ships. In addition to their standard gear, some vessels are equipped with specialized configurations that enable targeting of demersal species, extending their fishing range to species associated with the seabed.

Nanheng station (Simplified Chinese: 南横站; Traditional Chinese: 南橫站; Cantonese Yale: Nàahmwàahng Jaahm) is a Guangzhou Metro station on Line 4. The station commenced service on 28 December 2017 and stands as the southernmost stop in the Guangzhou Metro system.

Puerto Ricans have participated in a variety of United States military conflicts dating back to the American Revolutionary War. In 1779, volunteers from Puerto Rico alongside contingents from Cuba and Mexico fought British forces under the command of General Bernardo de Gálvez. In more recent times, Puerto Rican service members have been disproportionately represented in U.S. operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. The 65th Infantry Regiment, commonly known as the Borinqueneers, is a notable all-Puerto Rican unit whose name derives from Borinquen, the Taíno term for the island. The regiment served in World War I, World War II, the Korean War, and the post-9/11 era of the War on Terror. In 2014, the 65th Infantry Regiment was awarded the Congressional Gold Medal in recognition of its heroism during the Korean War.

Taíno spiritual traditions on the island were rediscovered and reinterpreted by a small group of advocates. Alongside these, certain African religious practices persisted among enslaved Africans, with Yoruba-influenced beliefs appearing in forms such as Santería and Ifá. Palo Mayombe, rooted in the Kongo tradition, is also part of the African-influenced religious landscape in Puerto Rico. Indigenous and African religious practices have frequently been blended with Christian ones, resulting in syncretic forms shared across communities. In 1940, Juanita García Peraza founded the Mita Congregation, which is identified as the first religion of Puerto Rican origin.

Originating from the 1961 acquisition by the City of Zurich of Gottfried Hotz's private collection, the North American Native Museum Zurich was established as the foundation for the institution. In 1963 the collection was relocated to a school in Aussersihl and publicly exhibited as Indianermuseum der Stadt Zürich. Gottfried Hotz led the institution as director until 1977, when Hans Läng succeeded him as curator and continued to expand the collection in a manner similar to Hotz until his retirement in 1993. In 1993 Denise Daenzer assumed the roles of director and curator, reorienting the museum's work by introducing varying presentations of the collection and topic-specific special exhibitions.

A portion of the museum's collection is permanently displayed on the second floor. The exhibits are organized by the cultural regions of the Americas, a framework commonly used in North American cultural anthropology.

Guangdong Province, in southern China, underwent a rapid reorientation of its economy after Deng Xiaoping's opening-up reforms, which liberalized markets and attracted foreign investment to the region. Its geographic and historical advantages include access to the ocean, proximity to Hong Kong, and long-standing ties to overseas Chinese communities, factors that helped establish Guangdong as a key hub for manufacturing and trade. The province was among the earliest to be authorized by the central government to receive foreign investment, reinforcing its role in China's reform era. Before the 1990s tax reforms, Guangdong benefited from relatively low central taxes owing to its post-Liberation status as economically underdeveloped, a fiscal setup that supported early industrial growth.

Guangdong’s prehistoric chronology centers on the Pearl River Delta, where the Neolithic era began around 7,000 years before present. The early Neolithic phase in this delta spans roughly 7,000–5,000 BP (about 5,050–3,050 BC), followed by a late Neolithic period dating to roughly 5,000–3,500 BP (approximately 3,050–1,550 BC). The coastal area of Guangdong is thought to have experienced Neolithic influences or population movements from the middle Yangtze region, a view associated with Jiao (2013). Inland Guangdong shows evidence of Neolithic settlement emerging around 4,600 BP, while the northern inland belt is represented by the Shixia culture, dated to 4,600–4,200 BP (roughly 2,650–2,250 BC).

The War Shipping Administration maintained close cooperation with the British Ministry of War Transport, coordinating their efforts through the Combined Shipping Adjustment Board. This arrangement aimed to optimize the utilization of available ship hulls and cargo-carrying capacity, ensuring efficient deployment of maritime resources.

The War Shipping Administration (WSA) was a United States government emergency war agency created during World War II to procure and operate the civilian merchant fleet needed for the war effort. It controlled the purchase and operation of civilian shipping tonnage and worked in close coordination with the Maritime Commission, which handled shipbuilding, so that production and allocation supported military requirements. Leadership was provided by Vice Admiral Emory S. Land, who headed both the Maritime Commission and the WSA, reflecting integrated oversight of the nation’s civilian shipping program. Among its notable initiatives were programs to build the Liberty Ships and Victory Ships, which expanded the wartime cargo capacity.

From 16 to 28 February 1966, USS Guam (LPH-9) patrolled south of the Dominican Republic, prepared to land forces on Hispaniola if the situation required. The ship then conducted amphibious exercises through 1 June 1966. On 1 June 1966, Guam entered the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard for post-shakedown availability.

In early 1985, USS Guam (LPH-9) entered drydock at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard for a comprehensive overhaul. The maintenance period extended over several months as the ship underwent modernization. As part of the overhaul, two Phalanx close-in weapon systems were installed to bolster its self-defense capabilities.

Long-distance intercity travel in the United States is provided primarily by airlines, with rail playing a comparatively smaller role outside of certain corridors. Rail travel is most prevalent along the Northeast Corridor, which also stands as the only high-speed rail line in the country that meets international standards. Amtrak, the government-sponsored national passenger rail operator, runs a substantial portion of intercity rail service, though its network remains relatively sparse when compared with Western European systems. The carrier’s coverage is heavily concentrated in the Northeast, and it also maintains notable routes in California, the Midwest, the Pacific Northwest, and the Virginia/Southeast region.

Beginning in the mid-2000s, the United States experienced a housing market bubble that culminated in 2007 and precipitated the Great Recession, the largest economic contraction since the Great Depression. In the 2010s and into the early 2020s, political polarization intensified and concerns about democratic backsliding grew. This polarization was starkly evident on January 6, 2021, when a mob attacked the U.S. Capitol in an attempt to overturn the certification of the presidential election and obstruct the peaceful transfer of power.

Nasty Crew is a British grime collective formed around producer Jammer, whose productions largely employ sounds drawn from the Korg Trinity keyboard. Marcus Nasty credits Jammer with steering the group’s sonic evolution from garage toward grime. The crew’s early material was laid over Jammer’s instrumentals, including D Double E’s Birds in the Sky and Sharky Major’s Dis Ain’t a Game. Jammer produced the group’s October 2002 debut single, Good U Know, which sold out during its promotional phase. In 2002 Kano joined the lineup, having grown up knowing Sharky, and Monkstar also joined that year; he had formerly performed as Monkey and had been a member of D Double E’s prior crew M.A.D. Both Kano and Monkstar were required to prove themselves with a back-to-back freestyle session in Jammer’s basement before being invited into the group. Jammer has stated that he was faced with choosing between Kano and Dizzee Rascal, ultimately selecting the artist whose tonal palette would best complement his productions.

In March 2005, Younger Nasty merged into Nasty Crew, bringing in junior members Lil Nasty, Griminal, Brutal, Lightnin, and Yunga Hunga, some of whom had previously been part of Lil Nasty's Straight From Hell and Griminal's M.I.C. In April 2005, Nasty Crew collaborated with producer Agent X on two tracks released on his Heatseeker label: Nasty Bonanza, which also featured Dynasty Crew, and City Life, with Stormin, Demon, and Big Seac appearing as Nasty Crew. City Life was issued exclusively on the RWD Access All Artists Mixtape Vol. 1, mixed by Logan Sama. Later in 2005, Kano, Ghetts, and Demon left the group following a fallout between Marcus Nasty and Kano, an event that Ghetts later referenced on his 2021 track "Autobiography."

In Hong Kong and Macau, traditional Chinese characters remained in use during the colonial era, whereas mainland China adopted a system of simplified characters. In recent times, simplified characters have become more prevalent to accommodate immigrants and visitors, particularly those from the mainland. This greater reliance on simplified script has sparked concerns among residents about preserving local cultural heritage.

Traditional Chinese characters (TC) refer to the character set used in Taiwan, while simplified Chinese characters (SC) denote the form adopted in Mainland China and other regions. In typography, the Noto typeface family provides distinct font releases to accommodate Taiwan's traditional character repertoire (TC) and Hong Kong's traditional forms (HK), reflecting regional typographic conventions within a single font family.

DJ Pied Piper and the Masters of Ceremonies was a UK garage collaboration comprising producer and DJ Pied Piper alongside MCs DT, Melody, Sharky P, and Kamanchi Sly, formerly of Hijack. Active in the early 2000s, the group is best known for the chart-topping single Do You Really Like It?, which reached number one on the UK Singles Chart. DT contributed the distinctive vocal shout that became closely associated with the track, helping to anchor its memorable hook within the UK garage scene.

DJ Pied Piper and the Masters of Ceremonies achieved a commercial breakthrough in June 2001 when their debut single "Do You Really Like It?" reached number one on the UK Singles Chart for a single week, and it remained on the chart for a total of 14 weeks during the summer of that year. The track has been included on several albums within the Pure Garage UK garage compilation series, underscoring its lasting association with the genre. Additionally, the group occasionally appeared as guests on DJ EZ's weekly UK garage show on Kiss 100.

Education in Laos remains concentrated at the secondary level in provincial capitals and a number of district centers, with access closely tied to urbanized areas and local infrastructure. While dropout rates for secondary and technical education are not as high as those observed in primary schooling, inequalities by gender and ethnicity are more pronounced at these levels. In the 1980s, students from Lao Sung or Lao Theung communities comprised about 7% of lower-secondary enrollment, a share that declined to around 3% at the upper-secondary stage. Students residing outside provincial centers often must live in makeshift boarding facilities, a circumstance that discourages rural enrollment and disproportionately affects girls and minority groups. Vientiane hosts the majority of advanced institutions, including the national teachers’ training school at Dong Dok, the irrigation college at Tad Thong, the agriculture college at Na Phok, the National Polytechnic Institute, and the University of Medical Sciences.

Education in Laos has long contended with structural challenges, including irregular remuneration for teachers, who often supplement their incomes through farming or other livelihoods, reducing instructional time. This, together with inconsistent class schedules, overcrowding, and a scarcity of learning resources, contributed to a prolonged path to complete the five-year primary course during the 1980s, with the average duration reaching about 11–12 years. Repetition remained high across the early grades, ranging from around 40% in the first year to about 14% by the fifth year. Early dropout was also a concern, as roughly 22% of children entering the first grade left school before completing the second. Despite these difficulties, there was some improvement over time: in the 1980s, about 45% of entering first graders completed all five years of primary schooling, up from 18% in 1969.

Ye's Nine Points, officially titled the Nine-Point Policy on the Peaceful Reunification of Taiwan, is a policy framework proposed by Ye Jianying, who served as chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The proposal was conveyed to a Xinhua News Agency reporter on October 1, 1981, and was intended to serve as the basis for negotiations with the government of the Republic of China in Taiwan. As one of mainland China's policy documents on Taiwan, it remains a notable element of the PRC's approach to cross-strait relations.
