In Chinese, the policy is known as 有关和平统一台湾的九条方针政策; 叶九条; Pinyin: Yǒuguān Hépíng Tǒngyī Táiwān de Jiǔtiáo Fāngzhēn Zhèngcè; Yè Jiǔtiáo.

Ye's Nine Points is believed to have already encompassed the core meaning of the doctrine commonly referred to as "one country, two systems." In February 1984, Deng Xiaoping discussed the concept with Zbigniew Brzezinski, drawing on the framework of Ye's Nine Points. Later that year, Premier Zhao Ziyang formally proposed the notion of "one country, two systems" at the second session of the 6th National People's Congress.

Introduced by IBM in 1931, the IBM 601 Multiplying Punch was an electromechanical device designed to read two eight-digit numbers from a punched card and punch their product onto the same card. In 1934, Wallace Eckert employed a rigged IBM 601 Multiplying Punch to automate the integration of differential equations, illustrating an early practical application of automated computation to mathematical problems.

During the 1960s, notable developments in mathematical notation accompanied advances in physics and abstract mathematics. In 1960, Geoffrey Chew and colleagues promoted matrix notation as a tool for describing the strong interaction in particle physics and the bootstrap principle. In the same decade, set-builder notation was developed to define a set by the properties its members must satisfy. Also in the 1960s, tensors were abstracted within category theory through the concept of a monoidal category. In later periods, multi-index notation emerged to generalize the notion of an index from a single integer to an ordered tuple, progressively supplanting conventional index conventions in multivariable calculus, partial differential equations, and distribution theory.

Red Hot + Riot: The Music and Spirit of Fela Kuti is the fifth installment in the Red Hot series to concentrate primarily on the work of a single musician, in this case Fela Kuti. It continues the series’ pattern of dedicated tributes by following earlier projects honoring Cole Porter (Red Hot + Blue), Antônio Carlos Jobim (Red Hot + Rio), George Gershwin (Red Hot + Rhapsody: The Gershwin Groove), and Duke Ellington (Red Hot + Indigo).

Red Hot + Riot, also known as Red Hot + Riot: The Music and Spirit of Fela Kuti, is the fourteenth compilation released by the Red Hot Organization. The project was produced by Paul Heck, John Carlin of the Red Hot Organization, and Grammy-winning Andres Levin, and functions as a fundraising vehicle to raise AIDS awareness. Drawing inspiration from the late Nigerian musician Fela Kuti, the collection was issued by MCA on October 15, 2002, and features more than three dozen artists across a score of tracks.

Josef Gabriel Rheinberger (1839–1901) was an organist and composer from Liechtenstein who spent most of his career in Bavaria. He served as court conductor in Munich and was responsible for music in the royal chapel. Rheinberger is best known for his sacred music, organ repertoire, and vocal works, which include numerous masses, a Christmas cantata, and the motet Abendlied. In addition to sacred vocal music, he produced two operas and three singspiele, as well as incidental music and secular choral compositions. His instrumental output comprises two symphonies along with other instrumental pieces, complemented by chamber music and additional organ works.

Josef Rheinberger married Franziska von Hoffnaaß in 1867, who had previously been his pupil and was known as a poet and socialite. The couple had no children. Franziska provided texts for a substantial portion of his vocal repertoire, supplying the words for many of his vocal works.

During the early 1960s, African American activists in Maryland participated in the broader civil rights movement. Morgan State College students organized sit-ins at Baltimore department stores and restaurants by spring 1960, following the Greensboro demonstrations in North Carolina. In 1961, the movement was furthered when the Freedom Riders passed through Maryland on their route toward the Deep South, beginning in Washington, D.C. The decade witnessed a variety of civil rights activity in the state, including rallies, marches, protests, and, at times, violence, with the most intense episodes occurring in 1968 after the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. Notable episodes of unrest include the Cambridge riot of 1963, the Cambridge riot of 1967, and the Baltimore riot of 1968.

Mathias de Sousa, one of nine indentured servants brought to Maryland by Jesuit missionaries, sailed aboard the Ark when Lord Baltimore's expedition reached the St. Mary's River in 1634. He was among the colony's earliest individuals of African descent to settle in Maryland, and his indenture concluded by 1638, after which he became a freeman. He pursued maritime and trading careers as a mariner and fur trader, commanding a trading voyage to the Susquehannock in 1641 and serving as master of a small cargo vessel in 1642. In the same year he was elected to and served in the legislative assembly of freemen, making him the first man of African descent to participate in an Assembly or Legislature in America.

At Finglesham in Kent, a well-preserved Anglo-Saxon cemetery dating to the late 6th and early 7th centuries preserves two graves. Among the finds are a bronze pendant and a gilt buckle, with designs that appear related, indicating a linked set of ornament and symbolism. Some scholars interpret the motifs as reflecting religious activity connected with the Germanic god Woden. The objects are thought to date to the period of the pagan reaction, a time of continued or renewed traditional beliefs amid Christianization in Kent. Together, these finds illuminate the religious milieu of Eadbald’s Kent during his reign.

Eadbald of Kent, under the influence of Archbishop Laurence of Canterbury, was persuaded to embrace Christianity and to abandon his first wife. After his conversion he remarried, taking a second wife named Ymme, who is described in Kentish tradition (the Kentish Royal Legend) as possessing Frankish royal blood. Some modern scholarship has proposed that Ymme may have been the daughter of Erchinoald, the mayor of the palace in Neustria (western Francia).

Regional discrimination in China refers to the unequal treatment of individuals or groups on the basis of the language or dialect they speak. It can affect people who speak a particular regional language or dialect, with linguistic differences serving as the basis for discriminatory behavior.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, residents of Hubei Province and people originating from the region faced refusals by many mainland Chinese. The denials affected service in everyday settings, particularly in dining establishments and in lodging accommodations. These episodes are regarded as evidence of regional discrimination against Hubei.

From 2016 onward, the United States experienced a pronounced decline in public transportation ridership as the COVID-19 pandemic took hold, with levels not returning to pre-pandemic figures in the following years. In contrast, Brightline emerged as the first privately operated passenger rail line in nearly a century, inaugurating service in Florida in January 2018 on the West Palm Beach–Fort Lauderdale corridor. The service was expanded to Miami in May 2018, and the network continued to grow with the addition of an Orlando extension in September 2023.

In March 2021, Thomas J. Christensen of Columbia University stated that a U.S.–China cold war was unlikely to resemble the original Cold War. He attributed this to China’s prominence in global production networks and the absence of the familiar liberal-democracy versus authoritarianism dynamic in the bilateral relationship. Christensen suggested that those concerned about rising tensions should study China’s role in the global economy as well as its foreign policy toward international conflicts and civil wars between liberal and authoritarian forces.

During November 2021, 5Star introduced a slate of new programming, including fresh episodes of Filthy House SOS and Oxford Street 24/7. The network also announced Better Homes, a new series from Nick Knowles, known for presenting Channel 5's Big House Clearout. Viacom Studios UK commissioned Our Secret World, a reality-format program featuring Babestation personalities such as Atlanta Moreno and Jess West as they explore their leisure time. In addition, The Act, a drama series from Hulu, began airing new episodes on 5Star at 10:00 pm on Thursdays, with late-night repeats on 5Select a few days later.

A time-shift version of 5Star was shut down on 3 February 2014 to make way for Channel 5 +24. The channel subsequently returned and relaunched on Freesat on 16 September 2014. It then launched on Sky in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 4 November 2014, replacing BET +1 on the platform. The addition of the channel to the Irish service was later deemed an error, and it was removed on 6 November 2014.

At commissioning, each of the four Iowa-class battleships was fitted with twenty quadruple 40 mm anti-aircraft mounts and forty-nine single 20 mm mounts, forming a substantial short-range air-defense belt. The batteries were augmented by the Mk 14 range sight and Mk 51 fire-control system to improve targeting accuracy and the overall effectiveness of the anti-aircraft armament.

On Iowa-class battleships, the 5-inch/38 caliber gun served as the dual‑purpose secondary armament. The gun weighs about 4,000 pounds without the breech, while the complete mounting reaches roughly 156,000 pounds. Its overall length is 223.8 inches, with a bore length of 190 inches and a rifling length of 157.2 inches. Muzzle velocity for its projectiles runs around 2,500 to 2,600 feet per second (760–790 m/s). The barrel life is approximately 4,600 rounds before replacement. Elevation covers from −15° to +85°, with an elevation rate near 15° per second, and traverse varies by mount—from bow/stern positions of −150° to +150° to other mounts of −80° to +80°, at about 25° per second. Fire control is provided by four Mark 37 systems connected through remote power control (RPC).

Apache Beehive was a discontinued Java application framework under the Apache Software Foundation that aimed to simplify the development of Java EE–based applications. The project integrated several Apache open-source components, notably XMLBeans. It ran on Java 5 and included JSR-175 for annotating fields, methods, and classes to assist runtime tools. The framework built on the platform developed for BEA Systems' WebLogic Workshop 8.1, and BEA donated the Beehive code to Apache.

Apache Beehive's third component enables the creation of web services through declarative metadata and annotations. These annotations support the development of complex web services with features such as conversational interactions and maintained state. All the relevant metadata and annotations are consolidated into a single file, which simplifies debugging and maintenance. By annotating the source code of any plain Java class, it can be exposed as a web service without altering its core behavior. This annotation-driven approach is grounded in JSR-181, which itself builds on JSR-175.

Opium is an American record label and rap collective founded in 2019 by Carter and based in Atlanta, Georgia. It comprises five acts: Carter, Ken Carson, Destroy Lonely, ASAP Nast, and Homixide Gang; all are Atlanta natives except ASAP Nast. The label is affiliated with producers KP Beatz, Lil 88, and F1lthy, who worked extensively on Carter's second album Whole Lotta Red.

According to TMZ, in a report dated February 14, 2023, Playboi Carti (Carter) was arrested on December 29, 2022, on a felony assault charge stemming from an alleged choking incident involving his girlfriend, who was about 14 weeks pregnant at the time. Carter was released on bond the day after his arrest.

The Kalamazoo Institute of Arts (KIA) presents a program of 10 to 15 temporary exhibitions annually across its ten galleries. The exhibitions are staged throughout the institution’s spaces, with recurring showcases such as the West Michigan Area Show, the High School Area Show, and the Young Artists of Kalamazoo County. In addition to these recurring events, other exhibitions are organized around works loaned from museums, galleries, corporations, or private collections, enabling a diverse range of works to be displayed.

The Kalamazoo Institute of Arts traces its origins to 1924, when members of the Kalamazoo Chapter of the American Federation of Arts established an art center to cultivate public interest in the arts, advance arts education, and foster appreciation for a broad spectrum of artistic disciplines.

The Batanic languages form a dialect continuum within the Austronesian language family. They are sometimes referred to as Bashiic or Ivatanic. Geographically, the languages are spoken on Babuyan Island, which lies north of Luzon; on three of the Batanes Islands, situated between the Philippines and Taiwan; and on Orchid Island off southern Taiwan.

The Batanic languages are often grouped with the Philippine languages, though there is no full consensus on this classification. Some scholars regard them as a primary branch within the Malayo-Polynesian languages. Blench concludes that the Batanic languages have been diverging from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian for a long time. They contain many roots that are not standard Austronesian in origin. The relationship between Batanic and the Northern Luzon languages remains uncertain.
MPEG-D denotes a suite of standards for audio coding. Its formal designation is ISO/IEC 23003, MPEG audio technologies. The standards in this family have been published since 2007.

ACE Limited expanded into a global insurer through leadership changes, beginning with Walter Scott serving as Chairman, President, and CEO in 1990 and the firm’s listing on the New York Stock Exchange in 1993. In 1994, Brian Duperreault succeeded Scott as Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. In the following decade, ACE pursued an active program of acquisitions and diversification to broaden its international footprint. A landmark transaction was the acquisition of Cigna Corporation's global property and casualty business, including the Insurance Company of North America, for $3.45 billion in 1999.
Spitzer investigations triggered civil litigation involving Chubb, in which the plaintiffs were policyholders alleging they were victimized by bid-rigging and commission schemes.

Smartwool is a brand that produces products branded under its own name, with a primary reliance on merino wool. Merino wool offers moisture management, temperature regulation, and odor resistance, traits that make it well suited for performance apparel. Most wool fabrics, including those used by Smartwool, are treated with Hercosett, a chlorine-based process developed in the 1950s by the United Kingdom Wool Board to improve the commercial appeal of wool. The treatment smooths the edges of the microscopic scales on wool fibers; when wet, scales can interlock and felt, then constrict on drying, causing shrinkage. Hercosett modifies the fiber's engineering specifications to reduce shrinkage, addressing consumer demand for fabrics that do not shrink. Smartwool product reviews typically appear in the context of hiking and other outdoor activities. The company offers socks, apparel, and other accessories for women, men, and children.

Smartwool is an American clothing company founded in 1994 in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, by ski instructors Peter and Patty Duke. The firm was later acquired by Timberland Company in 2005, and after VF Corporation purchased Timberland in 2011, Smartwool became a subsidiary of VF Corporation.

Apache CloudStack, originally known as VMOps, was a Cupertino, California-based cloud-computing software company. It raised $17.6 million in venture funding from Redpoint Ventures, Nexus Ventures, and Index Ventures, with Redpoint and Nexus leading the initial Series A round. The firm emerged from stealth mode with the public announcement of its product, and on May 4, 2010 it changed its name from VMOps to Cloud.com.

Apache CloudStack is an open-source cloud-computing software platform that originated with Cloud.com and later became part of the Apache Software Foundation. Citrix Systems acquired Cloud.com on July 12, 2011, for approximately $200 million. Shortly thereafter, in August 2011, Citrix released the remaining CloudStack code under the Apache Software License, placing its development under the governance of the Apache Foundation. In February 2012, Citrix released CloudStack 3.0, a milestone update that added support for Swift, OpenStack's S3-compatible object storage service.

Monticello, Arkansas, is a college town and the county seat of Drew County, located in the southeastern part of the state; it is pronounced MON-tiss-EL-oh. As of 2023, the population was approximately 8,175. Founded in 1849, it developed in the timberlands of eastern Arkansas near the Delta region. The city serves as a commercial, cultural, and educational hub for southeast Arkansas, with its historical economy rooted in agriculture and silviculture. In the contemporary period, its economy has diversified, reflecting growth in the medical sector and the presence of the University of Arkansas at Monticello.

According to the United States Census Bureau, Monticello covers a total area of 11.0 square miles (28.6 square kilometers), of which 0.02 square miles (0.04 square kilometers), or 0.14 percent, is water.

In 1962, General Electric began developing the GE Computer System Operating System (GECOS), later renamed GCOS, initially for batch processing and subsequently extended to time-sharing and transaction processing, with GCOS variants continuing in use today. Between 1964 and 1969, GE cooperated with Bell Laboratories (which soon withdrew) and MIT to develop Multics for the GE 645 mainframe. The project extended beyond initial expectations and did not achieve broad commercial success, but it introduced influential concepts such as single-level storage architecture, dynamic linking, a hierarchical file system, and ring-based security. Active development of Multics continued through 1985.

In 2018, General Electric revised the discount rate used to measure the actuarial liabilities of its pension plans, increasing it from 3.64 percent to 4.34 percent. This adjustment reduced the reported underfunded pension liabilities by $7 billion year over year. Consequently, the underfunded pension liability declined from $34.2 billion in 2017 to $27.2 billion in 2018.

In 1958, the institution that would become the Wuhan Conservatory of Music was established as Hubei Arts College, formed through the merger of the Central–South Music Vocational School and the Wuhan Art Teachers College. In 1985, it adopted its current name, Wuhan Conservatory of Music.

Wuhan Conservatory of Music is a provincial-level public college located in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China. It operates under the jurisdiction of Hubei Province and is supported by the Hubei Provincial People's Government. Its Chinese name is Wuhan Yinyue Xueyuan (武汉音乐学院).

Training, frequently described in conjunction with development, refers to workplace learning designed to improve employee performance. While many programs are provided directly by employers, there exists a range of online training services beyond the corporate setting, including career counseling, skill assessment, and supportive services intended to aid professional growth. Training methods are commonly categorized into on-the-job training, conducted within the work environment, and off-the-job training, carried out outside daily duties and often involving formal courses or simulations.

An On-the-Job Training Plan (OJT Plan) represents a relatively new approach to job training, emphasizing structured, workplace-based instruction. According to the United States Department of the Interior, an effective OJT plan should include several key elements: a clear overview of the subjects to be covered, the expected number of training hours, an estimated completion date, and the method by which the training will be evaluated. These components collectively establish the scope, duration, timeline, and assessment framework necessary to track progress and ensure the intended competencies are attained.

Some accounts indicate that Sun Yat-sen proposed incorporating elements of the Soviet political model into the Republic of China’s governance to accelerate modernization. Under Chiang Kai-shek, the Kuomintang wielded tight control over both the Nationalist government and the National Revolutionary Army, with the latter sometimes described as “the Party’s Army” (黨軍). The bureaucracy of the Republic of China increasingly served as an instrument of the Kuomintang, and the party determined the principal national policies. Consequently, the Kuomintang held supreme power over the nation.

Dang Guo, literally translated as "party-state," refers to the one-party governance system of the Republic of China under the Kuomintang, lasting from 1924 to 1987. The framework emerged after Sun Yat-sen acknowledged the efficacy of the Soviet political model, including its centralised dictatorship. In practice, the regime incorporated elements associated with fascist regimes. Chiang Kai-shek relied on the Kuomintang to control and administer the Nationalist government and the National Revolutionary Army. The party monopolized the formulation of major national policies and held ideological supremacy across the country. Dang Guo thus dominated Chinese politics for several decades, until the rise of the Chinese Communist Party altered the political landscape.

Pierre Bénézech was appointed Minister of the Interior on 3 November 1795 during the Directory era. In this role, he demonstrated notable organizational skill and remained highly active in the administration of the ministry. He established councils overseeing agriculture, commerce, and the arts, and initiated reforms of the École polytechnique as well as broader changes to the education system. Additionally, he promoted the fine arts, giving particular support to the Louvre relative to other institutions.

Pierre Bénézech advocated the revolutionary ideals at the outbreak of the French Revolution. He subsequently assumed command of the National Guard, directing its activities in the early years of the era. Later in his career, he served as administrator for the department of Seine-et-Oise, overseeing regional governance.

Kaifeng, a Chinese destroyer, was initially outfitted with the Thomson-CSF Tavitac combat data system and the Type 393 surface-search radar, and it mounted HQ-7 missiles—a derivative of the Crotale system—which replaced its X turret. In 1999, the armament was updated with YJ-8 missiles, replacing the HY-series missiles, and the ship's electronic warfare capabilities were enhanced through upgrades to its EW suite. Later, the destroyer was further equipped with YJ-83 anti-ship missiles, expanding its strike capacity against surface targets.

Kaifeng was a People's Liberation Army Navy destroyer belonging to the late-20th-century Type 051 class, commonly referred to as the Luda class, and is associated with the second batch of that series, which is sometimes designated Type 051D by naval historians. Construction of the second batch began in 1977, with the series’ ships continuing to enter service until the last member was commissioned in 1991. The decision to procure a second batch is believed to have reflected the Cultural Revolution’s disruption of the development of a successor design. Modern classifications for these ships sometimes use the Type 051D designation. In 1982 the PLAN initiated an abortive modernization program aimed at reconstructing the early ships with British Aerospace weapons and sensors; however, the upgrades were judged impractical in light of the Falklands War, and the project was cancelled in 1984. A separate 1986 plan to upgrade with American power plants, weapons, sensors, and computing systems was likewise abandoned following the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre.

During the 2023–24 UEFA Conference League, the pathway for cup winners from associations ranked 30–39 in UEFA's coefficient standings was adjusted so they commenced in the second qualifying round rather than the first. The change affected the national associations of Slovakia, Slovenia, Belarus, Moldova, Lithuania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Finland, Luxembourg, Latvia, and Kosovo.

The 2023–24 UEFA Conference League season article notes that the Czech Republic's domestic cup winners, assigned to UEFA association 16, were allocated to the Europa League rather than the Conference League, and thus began in the third qualifying round of the Europa League instead of the second round.

Arms procurement involves governments awarding contracts to supply their military forces, a process that carries considerable political significance by shaping policy choices, budgeting, and international relations. The intersection of politics and the arms trade can give rise to a military–industrial complex, a network in which the armed forces, defense industry, and political actors become closely interconnected. In such a configuration, military, commercial, and governmental interests interact in ways that influence procurement decisions, strategic priorities, and economic incentives.

Many contemporary military systems are built on incremental updates to World War II–era designs, reflecting a lineage of refinements rather than wholly new platforms. World War II stands as the most intense period of weapon development in human history, during which a vast array of new designs and concepts entered service and existing technologies were substantially improved. From 1939 to 1945, innovations proliferated across multiple domains, culminating in capabilities that transformed warfare, among them the nuclear bomb, which emerged as the era’s most powerful weapon. In addition, jet aircraft and radar are recognized as highly influential technologies that advanced air power and early detection systems. However, the prominence and visibility of nuclear weapons, together with the later development of long-range rockets, tended to overshadow these earlier innovations.

NOAAS Oceanographer (R 101) was a United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration ship that participated in the agency’s Fleet Modernization Program during the 1990s. As part of this initiative, Oceanographer, along with Discoverer and Malcolm Baldrige (and the ex-Researcher), was replaced by the newer Ronald H. Brown. The vessel was decommissioned in 1996. Subsequently, Oceanographer was sold to the Kirkland Yacht Club Marina in Kirkland, Washington, where it was repurposed to function as a breakwater and renamed MV Protector. The MV Protector remained tied up at the marina from 1997 to 2005.

NOAAS Oceanographer (R 101) was a United States government oceanographic research vessel operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. In 1969, the ship participated in BOMEX, the first large-scale, coordinated international study of sea–air interactions. It subsequently carried out environmental baseline studies for deep-ocean mining under the DOMES program. In 1980, Oceanographer became the first U.S. government vessel to be permitted entry into a port of the People’s Republic of China.

ISO/IEC 7816 encompasses a suite of standards for interworking with contact smart cards and their interfaces; however, the selection and use conditions of cryptographic mechanisms can influence a card’s exportability under applicable regulations. Furthermore, the assessment of whether particular algorithms or protocols are suitable is not within the remit of ISO/IEC 7816-8.

ISO/IEC 7816 is an international standard that specifies a set of commands for integrated circuit cards, including both contact-based and contactless devices. The command suite governs card and file management, supporting operations such as creating and deleting files. The scope of the specification extends across the card’s entire life cycle, covering stages from pre-issuance through post-expiration use, thereby facilitating interoperability among applications, readers, and issuers.

On 17 September 1997, Bill Drummond and Jimmy Cauty resurfaced publicly under the alias 2K, staging a one-off Barbican Arts Centre performance that featured Mark Manning, Acid Brass, the Liverpool Dockers, and Gimpo. During the event, two elderly men in motorised wheelchairs caused disruption in the venue, with observers noting their resemblance to Drummond and Cauty. The performance centred on a track titled "***k the Millennium," a remix of their earlier hit What Time Is Love? that incorporated Acid Brass and motifs from the hymn Eternal Father, Strong to Save, and it was released as a single. The events were accompanied by full-page press advertisements inviting readers to vote on the question "***k The Millennium: Yes/No?" via a telephone voting line. Separately, Drummond and Cauty operated K2 Plant Hire, with plans to construct a "People's Pyramid" from used house bricks, a project that ultimately did not materialize. K2 Plant Hire Ltd had been registered with Companies House since 1995, with Cauty and Drummond listed as directors; the Directors' Report for the period ending 31 March 1996 described the company’s activities as "a music company." Accounts also note a transaction with "KLF Communications Residual Royalties," identified as a partnership between Cauty and Drummond.

Drummond and Cauty, the duo behind The KLF, were noted for their idiosyncratic and humorous public personas. They appeared on Top of the Pops on several occasions, often wearing costumes. They granted relatively few interviews. Instead, they communicated through semi-regular newsletters and cryptically phrased full-page adverts published in UK national newspapers and the music press. The adverts were stark in design, featuring large white lettering on a black background.

Faith earned Album of the Year at the 31st Grammy Awards for George Michael. At the 1989 American Music Awards, the album received three honors: Favorite Pop/Rock Male Artist, Favorite Soul/R&B Male Artist, and Favorite Soul/R&B Album. Michael was also recognized with the MTV Video Vanguard Award for the work. Commercially, Faith was the best-selling album in the United States for 1988 and has attained Diamond certification from the RIAA. Nielsen SoundScan lists US sales at approximately 11 million copies, ranking it as the 52nd best-selling album in the country. Worldwide, Faith has sold around 20 million copies.

Faith employed a broad array of electronic and acoustic instruments to achieve its sound. A collection of synthesizers—the Yamaha DX7, Roland S-50, Roland D-50, and Roland Juno-106—provided the core textures, with the Juno-106 chiefly responsible for most of the synth bass lines and string timbres. The rhythm section relied primarily on the LinnDrum as the album’s main drum machine, though the Linn 9000 was not utilized; additional percussion was supplied by the Roland TR-808 and Yamaha RX-5. Some drum parts were actually played on a Pearl drum kit for tracks such as "Look at Your Hands," complemented by a Roland Octapad. On rare occasions, Chris Porter’s Greengate DS-3 sampler was used alongside the Linn to generate specific drum sounds, though the Linn’s own sounds remained preferred. Non-synthesized passages were played by Michael on a Fender Precision Bass.

The DuPont Building, situated on Rodney Square, served as DuPont's corporate headquarters until early 2015, after the company announced in December 2014 that it would relocate and consolidate its headquarters at nearby Chestnut Run Plaza. Following this corporate realignment, The Chemours Company, spun off from DuPont in 2015, was to move into the DuPont Building. In addition to offices, the building houses The Playhouse on Rodney Square (formerly the DuPont Playhouse), the Hotel duPont, and a branch of M&T Bank.

The DuPont Building occupies the entire block bounded by 10th, 11th, Orange, and Market streets in Wilmington, Delaware, and stands as one of the city’s early high-rise structures overlooking Rodney Square. The structure was built in phases, with the original 1908 building fronting Rodney Square serving as DuPont offices. In 1913 it was expanded into a U-shaped plan with wings along 10th and 11th streets, during which the DuPont Playhouse was added and a portion of the 1908 section was converted into the Hotel du Pont. The Hotel du Pont is a member of Historic Hotels of America, the official program of the National Trust for Historic Preservation. A final addition in 1923 on Orange Street added two floors, bringing the complex to 13 floors and a height of 124 feet (38 meters).

Misolic was ranked No. 241 when he made his Grand Slam debut at the 2024 French Open after qualifying for the main draw, and he went on to defeat Otto Virtanen in five sets, Virtanen having entered the tournament as a lucky loser. By 10 June 2024, he had advanced more than 50 places to re-enter the top 200 in the rankings.

Filip Misolic, who had been ranked world No. 301, won the ATP Challenger singles title at the 2022 Zagreb Open. The victory propelled him up the ATP rankings by 76 places, reaching No. 225 on 16 May 2022.

Tianhe Sports Center South Station (Chinese: 体育中心南站; pinyin: Tǐyù Zhōngxīn Nán Zhàn; Jyutping: tai2juk6 zung1 sam1 naam4 zaam6) is a Guangzhou Metro station on the APM line. It is situated beneath the entrance of the Tianhe Sports Center along Tianhe Road in the Tianhe District. The station lies approximately 200 metres (660 feet) from Tianhe Sports Center station on Line 1, providing convenient interchanges between the two lines. It commenced operations on 8 November 2010.

Codesharing arrangements enable travelers to follow a single, coherent itinerary by presenting a multi-leg journey under one airline's flight number. They allow booking from origin A to destination C via connector B with a single carrier's code, simplifying ticketing and reducing the need to reconcile multiple carriers. Without codesharing, customers would typically book the first leg with one airline and the subsequent leg with another, potentially complicating purchases and increasing the risk of missed connections. In practice, participating airlines coordinate schedules in addition to sharing flight numbers to improve connection times, reliability, and overall travel convenience.

Codesharing is a business arrangement in aviation in which two or more airlines publish and market the same flight within their respective timetables, each under its own airline designator and flight number. Typically, the flight is operated by a single airline, designated as the operating carrier or administrating carrier. Seats on the flight are sold by all participating airlines, with each carrier offering seats under its own designator and flight number.

During the Firebase Bird engagement, acts of valor were formally recognized by U.S. military decorations. Piper and Crain were awarded the Distinguished Service Cross for their actions during the combat. Five service members received the Silver Star: Specialist 4 Turnage, Specialist 4 Campanella, Staff Sergeant Gregerio Nieto, Specialist 4 Frederick Weidman, and Specialist 4 David Osborne. Additionally, five of those killed in the engagement were Silver Star recipients.

During the engagement at Firebase Bird, United States forces suffered 27 fatalities and 67 wounded, accounting for more than 60 percent of the defenders. American authorities estimated that 267 PAVN soldiers were killed as a result of the assault and the subsequent four-day pursuit.

In Teochew, the agent phrase pung nâng (分儂; bung1 nang5) is positioned immediately after the subject and is not placed at the end of the sentence, nor between the auxiliary and the past participle. This contrasts with some European languages, such as German and Dutch, where the agent phrase may appear at the end of the clause or between the auxiliary and the past participle.

Teochew features two parallel reading systems for Chinese characters. Some characters have literary readings that exist only in Hokkien, and these Hokkien readings are traditionally used in the declamation of Classical Chinese texts. By contrast, there are numerous vernacular readings that are used exclusively in Teochew for everyday language. Accordingly, a formal distinction is drawn between the literary readings, which originate in Hokkien, and the vernacular readings, which are native to Teochew.

Filippo Tommaso Marinetti, a leading Futurist writer and poet, was a staunch Mussolini loyalist who helped shape Fascist doctrine. During the Italian Social Republic he remained in the regime as a propagandist, continuing to disseminate its messaging until his death from a heart attack in Bellagio in December 1944.

After the Kingdom of Italy's government surrendered, a significant portion of Italian troops in the Aegean grew weary of the conflict and opposed Mussolini. At the same time, Italian Fascist loyalists who remained allied to Germany persisted in supporting the Greek campaign. German forces in Greece managed to persuade roughly 10,000 Italians in the Aegean to continue backing the German war effort, illustrating the enduring influence of Axis loyalties among Italian forces in the area. These developments were part of the broader German-led realignment of Italian governance that culminated in the establishment of the Italian Social Republic.

According to the 2009 census of the Greater Nouméa urban area, which covered residents aged 15 years and older, the survey assessed French language abilities. The results indicated that 98.7% could speak French, 97.1% were able to read and write in French, and 1.3% had no knowledge of French.

During World War II, the United States Navy established a naval base at Nouméa, which subsequently served as the headquarters of the U.S. military in the South Pacific, anchored by a distinctive five‑sided command complex. After the war, the complex was repurposed as the base for the South Pacific Commission, a regional intergovernmental development organization. This body later evolved into the Secretariat of the Pacific Community, and was subsequently renamed the Pacific Community.

Thales of Miletus (c. 624–c. 546 BCE) is among the earliest figures recognized in the history of mathematics. He is commonly described as the earliest mathematician whose mathematical contributions are attributed to a named individual. He is credited with introducing deductive reasoning to geometry, signaling a shift toward rigorous geometric proof. He also derived four corollaries to Thales's theorem.

Professional societies in mathematics, notably the American Mathematical Society (AMS) and the Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM), along with other related organizations, sponsor prizes. These awards are designed to increase the representation of women and minorities in mathematics, aiming to broaden participation and ensure a more diverse and inclusive future for the discipline.

Within the Ballymena & Provincial Football League, the Intermediate Division currently comprises eighteen clubs. The league champions may be promoted to the NIFL Premier Intermediate League, provided they meet the admittance requirements.

In 2023, the Ballymena & Provincial Football League announced a restructuring of its competition format, introducing a two-tier structure comprising Division One and Division Two. The plan aims to broaden the league’s competitive framework, with the new system scheduled to take effect in the 2024–25 season.

ISO 15926 is an international standard designed to enable lifecycle information modelling and interoperability for facilities in the process industries. Its development began in 1991 when the EU ESPRIT project ProcessBase started work on a lifecycle information data model for process industry facilities. Following ProcessBase, the consortium EPISTLE (European Process Industries STEP Technical Liaison Executive) was established to coordinate these efforts. Initially, EPISTLE consisted of individual company members, but its membership was later consolidated into three national consortia: PISTEP in the United Kingdom, POSC/Caesar representing Norway, and USPI-NL serving the Netherlands. In later developments, PISTEP merged into POSC/Caesar, and USPI-NL was renamed to USPI.

POSC/Caesar proposed ISO 15926 as a modelling-oriented alternative to ISO 10303 on technical grounds related to modelling. The standard was formally named ISO 15926. The initiative received backing from EPISTLE and from the International Organization for Standardization, which continued the modelling program and produced Part 2 of ISO 15926. Part 2 has held the status of an ISO International Standard since 2003.

Before his breakout role on Stranger Things, Joe Keery appeared in several commercial campaigns, including for KFC, Domino's, and Nintendo's Amiibo line. He later pursued television work with roles in the series Empire and Chicago Fire. Keery's first feature-film appearance came in Stephen Cone's independent drama Henry Gamble's Birthday Party.

Joe Keery, an American actor and musician, was a founding member of the psychedelic rock group Post Animal, departing in 2018 to focus on acting commitments. He later pursued a solo career under the moniker Djo, releasing the albums Twenty Twenty in 2019 and Decide in 2022. In 2024, his track End of Beginning achieved viral popularity on TikTok and marked his first entry on the Billboard Hot 100. Keery’s third Djo album, The Crux, was issued on April 4, 2025, with a deluxe edition, The Crux Deluxe, following on September 12, 2025. He rejoined Post Animal in 2025, and the band released IRON on July 25 of that year. On the live circuit, Djo headlined the Back On You tour, with Post Animal serving as the opening act.

Irish solo dances are traditionally divided into two principal categories, distinguished by the footwear worn during performance. The classification comprises hard shoe and soft shoe, with the former often described as jig shoes or heavy shoes, and the latter referred to as light shoes.

Irish dance encompasses a range of traditional forms, including Sean-nÓs, the so‑called old style that originated in western Ireland. This form is described as either a regional variant of stepdancing or as a distinct style largely unknown beyond small communities until the late twentieth century. It is characterized by percussion-heavy, low-to-the-ground footwork and a freer, more improvisational approach to movement. Performers typically maintain a relaxed posture and invent steps to match the music as they perform. Performances are commonly held in very confined spaces, historically with doors laid flat on the floor and makeshift surfaces such as tabletops serving as stages.

Philadelphia Inquirer, LLC is a media company in the United States that was previously known as Philadelphia Media Network (PMN). It owns two newspapers, The Philadelphia Inquirer and the Philadelphia Daily News. The entity is owned by The Philadelphia Foundation, a nonprofit organization based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.
In 2014, Gerry Lenfest, a Philadelphia businessman, purchased Philadelphia Media Network. In 2016, Lenfest donated the company to The Philadelphia Foundation, a nonprofit organization.

Knot is a unit of speed used primarily in maritime and aviation contexts, defined as one nautical mile traversed in one hour. Describing velocity in a form that includes an additional per-hour component would be incorrect, since it would amount to nautical miles per hour per hour, effectively an acceleration term rather than speed. Therefore, speed is ordinarily expressed simply in knots, not in a per-hour form.

Knots are the unit in which indicated airspeed (IAS) and true airspeed (TAS) are expressed in aviation, but the relationship between the two speeds varies with altitude and atmospheric conditions. IAS closely approximates TAS only at sea level under standard atmospheric conditions and at low speeds. At higher altitudes, such as 11,000 meters (36,000 feet), an IAS of 300 kn may correspond to a TAS of about 500 kn under standard conditions.

Robert Recorde entered the University of Oxford circa 1525 and was elected a fellow of All Souls College in 1531. He pursued medicine, earning an M.D. degree from Cambridge in 1545, before returning to Oxford to teach mathematics publicly. He is credited with introducing the equals sign, a symbol formed by two parallel horizontal lines, accompanied by the assertion that no two things can be more equal. Later he relocated to London and served as physician to King Edward VI and to Queen Mary, with several of his works dedicated to the royal figures. He also held official posts, including Controller of the Royal Mint and Comptroller of Mines and Monies in Ireland. Recorde faced a defamation suit brought by a political adversary and was imprisoned for debt. He died in the King's Bench Prison, Southwark, by mid-June 1558.

Robert Recorde (c. 1510–1558) was a Welsh physician and mathematician. He is credited with introducing the equals sign (=) to express equality, and in 1557 he introduced the plus (+) and minus (−) signs to English speakers, broadening the notation available for arithmetic. His work thus contributed to the development of standardized mathematical notation during the 16th century.

NOAAS Discoverer (R 102) operated on a rotating schedule of assignments during its cruises, with multiple projects frequently pursued in parallel. The vessel conducted work across biological, chemical, geological, and physical oceanography, as well as meteorological and seismic research. Its major initiatives included the Aerosol Characterization Experiment (ACE); Radiatively Important Trace Species (RITS); World Ocean Circulation Experiment (WOCE); Combined Sensor Project (CSP); Global Ocean-Atmosphere-Land System (GOALS); and NOAA’s Vents project, which investigated submarine volcanic and venting activity within about 100 nautical miles of the Washington coast along the southern Juan de Fuca Ridge, incorporating the Blanco fracture zone and a nearby marginal subduction zone. In addition to these primary objectives, several ancillary programs operated on Discoverer, such as the Automated Shipboard Aerological Program (ASAP); the Cadet Training Program with students from the California Maritime Academy, the United States Military Academy, and the United States Naval Academy; regular marine mammal observations averaging around 23 sightings per year; the Shipboard Environmental Data Acquisition System (SEAS), which produced roughly 1,700 weather reports annually and saw Discoverer consistently among the top ten reporting ships from 1989 to 1996, including the top reporter in 1992–1994; and the Teacher at Sea Program, which placed educators aboard to observe operations in the Vents program.

NOAAS Discoverer (R 102) was repurposed by the United States Navy in 1987 to serve as a replacement for the Military Sea Transportation Command's oceanographic survey vessel USNS Bowditch. Bowditch's equipment, comprising narrow-beam mapping sonar systems, a Doppler sonar, and navigational electronics, was transferred to and installed aboard Discoverer.

Fraser Valley, along the lower Fraser River, experienced early sovereignty disputes when the Treaty of Oregon delineated U.S. and British claims to the river valley, yet Indigenous peoples were not consulted in its negotiation. The treaty overstepped jurisdiction, limiting Britain's ability to enforce its asserted authority over the valley's lands and waters. The prospect of settlement attracted immigrants during the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush, a development that intensified tensions and challenged British efforts to maintain order without the cooperation of local Indigenous communities. The ensuing Fraser Canyon War ended with a series of treaties that regulated immigration and allowed continued mining by both Indigenous inhabitants and new arrivals; none of these agreements remains in force today. These conflicts were part of broader clashes over land rights and settler arrival that helped shape the pattern of settlement on Canada’s West Coast and the adjacent United States.

The Fraser Valley is a term whose geographic scope varies by context. In casual usage it refers to the Fraser River basin downstream of the Fraser Canyon, while outside British Columbia the expression can denote the entire Fraser River system from its headwaters through the canyon. Within British Columbia, it specifically designates the portion of the Lower Mainland west of the mouth of the Coquihalla River near Hope, and includes the Canadian portion of the Fraser Lowland as well as adjacent valleys and uplands. The valley is divided into the Upper Fraser Valley and the Lower Fraser Valley by the Vedder River mouth at the eastern foothills of Sumas Mountain. Additionally, the stretch of the Lower Fraser Valley upstream of McMillan Island and the Salmon River mouth at Fort Langley was known as the Central Fraser Valley until 1995.

Scarlett O’Hara is initially framed by the Southern Lady ideal, a standard that is presented at the outset and reflected in her circle, most prominently by Melanie Wilkes. As she confronts extreme hardship, she wrestles with these norms and begins to challenge them, since the codes prove inadequate for meeting her immediate physical needs and securing survival. Consequently, the standards are abandoned because they fail to aid her practical ends or economic self-preservation. Scholar Fox-Genovese argues that the public obligation of being a "lady" is conspicuously disregarded in Scarlett’s struggle to endure, underscoring a tension between social expectations and pragmatic necessity. This shift leads to her ostracism by peers who cling to the traditional code. Over time, Scarlett’s motivations move away from social or class status toward economic and physical survival, prompting her to relinquish the original code in pursuit of personal viability.

Scarlett O'Hara's pursuit centers on Ashley Wilkes, a fixation that remains misdirected for much of the narrative until the climactic turning point. The death of Melanie Wilkes prompts Scarlett to confront the reality that her pursuit of Ashley was a juvenile romance, and she comes to recognize that her true feelings have long been for Rhett Butler. She pursues Rhett from the Wilkes residence to their own home, where he believes there is little chance of accepting her love and contemplates leaving. When Scarlett finally confesses her love, Rhett refuses to stay, delivering a blunt rejection. Wracked with grief but determined, Scarlett returns to Tara to regain strength and to devise a plan to reunite with Rhett.
Incumbent Vancouver mayor Gregor Robertson announced on January 10, 2018 that he would not seek another term in the 2018 Vancouver municipal election; Robertson had held the office since 2008.

The 2018 Vancouver municipal election was held on October 20, 2018, aligning with the statewide schedule in which other British Columbia municipalities and regional districts elected new local governments. Voters selected the mayor, ten city councillors, seven park board commissioners, and nine Vancouver School Board trustees. The election used a plurality-at-large voting system, and candidate registration opened on September 4, 2018 and closed on September 14, 2018.

Swæfheard held the position of sub-king in West Kent, ruling that portion under the authority of his father, while Oswine governed the eastern half. Bede records that Swæfheard was still reigning jointly with Withred in July 692.

Swæfheard is known from early medieval charter evidence. A charter dated 1 March 689 records the second regnal year of his reign and identifies his father as Sæbbi, the king of Essex, with his paternal consent noted. He also appears as a witness on two charters issued by Oswine, of which one is dated 27 January 690.

An annex to ISO 3103 describes two alternative pairs of vessels for tea tasting, each consisting of a pot and a matching bowl. The pots have capacities of 310 ml and 150 ml, while their corresponding bowls hold 380 ml and 200 ml, respectively, and these vessels are noted as being in widespread use for tea tasting. The annex further includes engineering drawings that illustrate the cross-sectional profiles of the pots and bowls. The pot type described in the annex is also known as a taster's mug.

ISO 3103 is an international standard that describes a standardized process for brewing tea, with the aim of enabling meaningful sensory evaluation rather than serving as a general consumer brewing instruction. The procedure specifies controlled parameters and steps to minimize variation in preparation, thereby allowing reliable comparisons of aroma, flavor, and other sensory attributes among samples. It is often employed in professional taste-testing contexts, for example when selecting a tea blend for a brand or label. The standard also seeks to maintain a consistently tasting brewed beverage from harvest to harvest, reducing sensory differences caused by changes in raw materials and production conditions.

Following an extended hiatus from international play, the Dominican Republic national football team returned to competition in March 1970, taking part in the Central American and Caribbean Games held in Panama. In the event, they were grouped with Puerto Rico and Venezuela. The side opened with a 5–0 defeat to Venezuela on March 4, and two days later secured their first-ever victory by defeating Puerto Rico 5–0. However, the team did not advance to the next round.

The Dominican Republic men's national football team competed at the 1971 Pan American Games in Colombia, where they were drawn into a group with the Bahamas and Canada. They were defeated 4–2 by the Bahamas on July 31, 1971, and followed by a 4–0 loss to Canada on August 2, 1971, leaving the team eliminated from the tournament.

Igreja da Memória is a church located in the Ajuda parish of Lisbon, Portugal. It houses the mausoleum of Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, the 1st Marquis of Pombal. The building has been designated as a National Monument.

The Memory Church (Igreja da Memória) is a church built entirely of limestone, constructed to commemorate the survival of King Joseph I during the 1758 assassination attempt associated with the Távora affair. Its architecture combines Baroque design with neoclassical features, and the building is crowned by a dome.

SS Lurline adopted a southerly course to circumvent the Japanese Navy on its voyage to Sydney. The ship called at Wellington and later Auckland, New Zealand. After leaving Auckland, it entered a zone in which two freighters had been sunk by Japanese submarines in recent days. The soldiers aboard remained fully dressed and wide-eyed for the two-day transit to Sydney, as the voyage proceeded toward its destination.

SS Lurline maintained high occupancy in the early 1950s. Matson refitted her sister ship Monterey and renamed her SS Matsonia. Together, the two vessels operated a Hawaii-to-the-American mainland service restricted to first-class passengers from June 1957 through September 1962, with occasional Pacific cruises. The advent of jet air travel reduced passenger demand in the early 1960s, and Matsonia was withdrawn from service and laid up in late 1962.

Demonyms are terms used to designate the residents or natives of a place, and they can carry different meanings depending on geographic or contextual factors. For example, Macedonians may refer to residents of North Macedonia, to people from the broader Macedonia region, or to the Greek population of Greek Macedonia. Some demonyms are borrowed from other languages and function as nicknames or descriptive adjectives for a group. An illustration is Québécois and Québécoise, the feminine form, which in English are used for natives of Quebec, whether the province or the city; alternative forms such as Quebecer or Quebecker are also used.

Demonym refers to a term used for inhabitants of a geographically defined area, and it is distinct in meaning from ethnonym, which names an ethnic group. In English, many words are polysemous and may function as either demonyms or ethnonyms, with the intended sense determined by context. An example is "Thai," which can denote a resident of Thailand or a member of the Thai ethnic group. Some terms are capable of serving as both demonyms and ethnonyms, depending on usage. Additionally, several populations have multiple demonyms; for instance, people from the United Kingdom may be called British, Briton, or Brit in informal usage.

On-the-job training (OJT) and off-the-job training are two principal approaches to onboarding new employees. Both methods can be effective, but they differ markedly and require specific measures to optimize outcomes. OJT takes place at the actual work site and is usually delivered by an experienced supervisor or manager who is enthusiastic about the work, focusing on relaying practical knowledge and skills to the newcomer through direct, hands-on instruction. By contrast, off-the-job training occurs at a location separate from the real workplace and relies on simulations, videos, and tests rather than continuous personal interaction, frequently provided by an external vendor outside the company. The choice between these methods, or a combination of them, depends on factors such as the desired balance between immediacy and realism, availability of instructional resources, and the nature of the job being learned.

On-the-job training (OJT) refers to instruction delivered to workers while they perform tasks, though some companies do not view it as essential. In 1962, Gary Becker described OJT as an investment akin to conventional schooling, implying that such training can contribute to human capital formation. Both on-the-job training and schooling have the potential to improve abilities and raise real income prospects, although the earnings effects may differ in scale or pattern. OJT can help individuals obtain employment or upgrade their skills to become more valuable in the labor market. The apprenticeship system represents an early form of on-the-job training dating to the Middle Ages (5th–15th century), through which pre-industrial individuals learned skilled crafts to become specialized artisans. Apprenticeship contracts typically lasted about six years, and young girls (~12) and boys (~14) would work and receive training to pursue artisan status.

Gloriæ Dei Cantores performed and recorded Gordon Myers's ninety-minute choral work, a musical setting based on James Weldon Johnson's God’s Trombones, which Myers composed as his doctoral dissertation. Myers served as chairman of the Music Department at Columbia College in Columbia, South Carolina, from 1965 to 1968. The work was published by Eastlane Music Corporation. In 1996, Paraclete Press acquired the copyright; Paraclete Press operates as the publishing arm of the Community of Jesus. The work was recorded by Gloriæ Dei Cantores in the mid-1990s, and Paraclete Records subsequently used the master recordings to prepare a 2018 re-release. In the composition, the Gloriæ Dei Cantores choir functions as the chorus accompanying Myers's baritone. C. Michael Bailey, writing for All That Jazz, recommended the recording, describing it as a highly listenable collection of biblical tales.

Gloriæ Dei Cantores is a distinguished choral ensemble whose activities span concert performance, broadcasting, and soundtrack work. Formerly directed by Elizabeth Patterson, the group is currently led by artistic director and principal conductor Richard K. Pugsley. It has undertaken three invitational tours to Russia and took part in the opening ceremonies of the 900th anniversary celebrations of St. Mark's Basilica in Venice, Italy. The choir has been involved in live radio and television broadcasts with the BBC, contributed to film soundtracks, and performed at public events such as the tree-lighting ceremony at Rockefeller Plaza.

The Library Freedom Project, a initiative supporting library access to anonymous networks, drew backing from the Electronic Frontier Foundation and the Massachusetts and New Hampshire affiliates of the American Civil Liberties Union, from the Tor Project, from a Valley News editorial, and from broad public testimony, which collectively helped push the project forward. On 15 September 2015, the library board renewed the anonymity service, upholding the prior unanimous vote to establish a middle relay within the Tor network. Following public disclosure of Department of Homeland Security involvement, roughly a dozen libraries and supporters nationwide expressed interest in hosting their own Tor nodes, an effect widely described as the Streisand effect. On 10 December 2015, Representative Zoe Lofgren sent a letter to DHS seeking clarification of procedures and voiced concern about federal pressure on organizations to degrade privacy and anonymity services. Kilton Public Library’s board ultimately voted to restore its Tor relay.

The Library Freedom Project offers classes for library patrons on online security and privacy, with privacy advocate librarians tailoring instructional materials to a broad range of user levels—from beginners to advanced—to help participants identify their own privacy needs. The program emphasizes that certain patrons may require enhanced privacy approaches, including survivors of domestic violence, political activists, whistleblowers, journalists, and LGBTQ youth or adults. In its approach to digital security, the emphasis is on understanding potential threats and how to counter them rather than on the specific tools employed. Achieving greater security involves individuals determining what they need to protect and from whom, and threat levels can vary based on location, activities, and the people with whom one collaborates or engages.

Input method editors originated in the context of CJK computing to describe the mechanisms used for entering Chinese, Japanese, and Korean characters. CJK stands for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Over time, the term has broadened and is now applied generically to software that provides text-entry support for any language. In the X Window System, the corresponding facility for inputting Latin characters with diacritics is termed an input method, illustrating how the broader concept extends beyond the original CJK focus.

Input method editors (IMEs) are software components that enable the input of non-Latin scripts and other complex character sets; they are also referred to as input methods or Text Input Processors. In Windows, these editors are implemented using the Text Services Framework API (TSF), a platform designed to support text input and processing tasks. The technology is supported starting with Windows XP and remains available in later Windows releases.

The Peabody Awards were established to honor excellence in radio programming. The scope later expanded to include television, with television awards introduced in 1948. In the late 1990s, the organization broadened eligibility to cover material distributed via the World Wide Web, adding new online-content categories. Works created solely for theatrical motion picture release are not eligible for Peabody recognition.

The Peabody Awards recognize programs across eight categories, including Entertainment, Documentary, Arts, Children's and Youth, News, Podcast and Radio, Interactive and Immersive, and Public Service. Entries are judged against standards established for the specific context of each work, emphasizing how effectively the program achieves those criteria within its genre. Winners and honorees have ranged from radio and television stations and networks to online media outlets, producing organizations, and individual creators from countries around the world.

Separation processes often require a cascade of separation steps, with successive operations arranged to progress toward the target composition and to produce the desired end products; this approach can achieve either complete separation of all constituents or partial separation aimed at specific fractions. In oil refining, an extended sequence of distillation stages is customary, and each stage yields a distinct product or intermediate, enabling the overall fractionation of crude oil into multiple usable streams.

Natural elements and compounds are rarely pure, as they typically contain impurities to varying degrees. Consequently, raw materials often require separation before they can be used productively, with the removal of unwanted constituents facilitating improved performance and compatibility with subsequent processing steps. Separation techniques are therefore a vital component of the modern industrial economy, underpinning the production of a wide range of goods by yielding usable substances from raw inputs.

ISO 8666 governs small craft and defines the length of hull (LOH) as the measurement of the hull itself. This figure may be shorter than the vessel’s length overall (LOA), which incorporates extensions and equipment beyond the hull. LOH excludes components attached to the hull, such as bowsprits and similar protruding elements.

Length overall (LOA) denotes the greatest length of a vessel’s hull measured along the waterline, and is commonly abbreviated as o/a, o.a., or oa. It represents the maximum longitudinal extent of the hull and remains the most widely used indicator of a ship’s size. LOA is routinely used to determine docking requirements and marina berth charges, with typical rates expressed per metre of LOA, for example £2.50 per metre.

Charles Hutton resigned his professorship in 1807 owing to ill health, but he continued to influence military education as the principal examiner of the Royal Military Academy. He also served for several years after retirement as the principal examiner for the Addiscombe Military Seminary. The Board of Ordnance granted him an annual pension of £500. In his final years he undertook work on revised editions of his earlier writings.

In the last year of his life, friends funded a marble bust of Charles Hutton, sculpted by Sebastian Gahagan. Subscriptions to the project exceeded its cost, and a medal was issued as well, engraved by Benjamin Wyon. The medal features Hutton's portrait on the obverse, with the reverse bearing emblems alluding to his discoveries concerning the explosive force of gunpowder and the density of the Earth.

In the 2023 Icelandic Cup, the third round brought together the twenty second-round winners and twelve Tier 1 clubs. The matches were staged on 19–20 April. The round's highest-scoring fixture was Víkingur Reykjavík's 6–2 victory over Magni Grenivík.
The second round of the 2023 Icelandic Cup featured 40 participating teams and was played from 6 to 11 April. Fjölnir emerged as the round’s biggest winners, recording a 10–0 away victory over Kría.

Karl Sieveking studied law and political science at the universities of Göttingen and Heidelberg from 1806 to 1810. He briefly served as secretary to his uncle, Charles-Frédéric Reinhard, who was the French minister plenipotentiary in the Kingdom of Westphalia. Sieveking then returned to Göttingen and obtained a post-doctoral qualification. In 1815, he helped establish the Hamburg Burgher Militia and moved there.

Karl Sieveking was involved in a 1841 proposal by the New Zealand Company to establish a German settlement on the Chatham Islands, located about 500 miles east of New Zealand. For the company, John Ward signed an agreement with Sieveking on 12 September 1841. The British Colonial Office stated that any Germans who settled there would be treated as aliens. The venture’s intended leader, John Beit, subsequently shifted the expedition to Nelson, New Zealand. The expedition was to be conducted on the ship Sankt Pauli.

China PR, South Korea, and Japan qualified automatically for the finals of the 2005 East Asian Football Championship, while the remaining finalist position was determined through a regional qualifying competition that included North Korea, Guam, Hong Kong, Chinese Taipei, and Mongolia. North Korea emerged as the winner of these qualifiers, thereby securing the fourth and final berth in the finals.

The 2005 East Asian Football Championship final tournament began on 31 July 2005. China won their first international title at the competition, marking a historic achievement for the nation. The next edition of the tournament was scheduled to take place in 2008.

The Kaman SH-2 Seasprite is a search-and-rescue helicopter. In certain configurations, it was equipped with a chin-mounted turret housing a single minigun and two waist-mounted 7.62 mm machine guns. A total of six aircraft were converted to this armament arrangement.

The SH-2 Seasprite was adapted for the Navy’s LAMPS program, with October 1970 marking the selection of the UH-2 as the interim LAMPS helicopter. LAMPS, developed during the 1960s, aimed to provide non-aviation ships with manned support and anti-submarine warfare helicopters. The LAMPS Mark I suite integrated advanced sensors, processors, and display capabilities to enhance operational awareness. Subsequently, UH-2 helicopters were upgraded with the LAMPS system and redesignated as SH-2Ds. In this configuration, the SH-2D served as a mobile radar and sonar platform, boosting the situational awareness of the ships they accompanied.

Within the Mongolian–Manchurian grassland, the steppe's population is predominantly composed of Mongolian pastoral nomads. Households reside in gers, large portable tents that can be moved with the seasons. Mongolian communities are renowned for horsemanship, with many families owning sizable herds that roam the grasslands. The animals provide sustenance, yielding food and dairy products for the inhabitants. The region also fosters a notable musical culture, featuring a broad repertoire of traditional Mongolian songs.

Within the Mongolian–Manchurian grassland zone, the brown eared pheasant, Crossoptilon mantchuricum, is associated with rugged mountainous woodland habitats rather than open grassland alone. Its primary distribution centers on Northeast China, where montane forested landscapes form a characteristic component of its range. The species also demonstrates adaptability to other ecologically similar ecoregions, indicating its capacity to occupy comparable forested and hilly environments beyond its core northeast Chinese habitat.

Maria Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers (born February 1, 1965) is an American lawyer and jurist who serves as a United States district judge for the Northern District of California. She was appointed to the federal bench in 2011 by President Barack Obama. Prior to her federal judgeship, she served on the Alameda County Superior Court in California from 2008 to 2011.
Gonzalez Rogers is married to Matthew C. Rogers, who has served in various positions in the Obama administration. The couple lives in Piedmont, California.

Early tank designs frequently incorporated multiple weapon mounts on a single chassis, a multi-mount concept that persisted into the interwar years in Britain, Germany, and the Soviet Union. The British Vickers A1E1 Independent tank stands as perhaps the most extreme expression of this approach, though the project was abandoned shortly thereafter. In a related line of development, the Soviet Union pursued a similar path with the T-35, a vehicle nicknamed the land battleship, which was produced and saw combat in defense of the USSR.

On modern surface warships, gun armament typically comprises larger-calibre guns in the range of 3–5 inches (76–127 mm). These calibres are employed to engage both air and surface targets. Gunhouses function as weatherproof shelters for mounting equipment and are generally constructed from lightweight, unarmoured materials such as glass-reinforced plastic. Contemporary turrets are often automated and operate without personnel inside, with a small team responsible for loading fixed ammunition into the system. By contrast, smaller-calibre weapons commonly follow an autocannon approach and may not be arranged as turrets, instead being bolted directly to the deck.

METRORail is a light rail system that serves Houston, Texas, covering 22.7 miles (36.5 km). In 2024, the system carried approximately 13.46 million riders, and by the second quarter of 2025 it averaged about 42,000 weekday riders. It ranks as the second most-traveled light rail system in the Southern United States and tenth nationwide, and it holds the highest ridership per mile among Southern U.S. light rail networks. The service is operated by the Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County (METRO).

METRORail, Houston’s light-rail system, progressed through a sequence of federal approvals and construction phases beginning in 2008–2009. In July 2008, the Federal Transit Administration issued records of decision approving the North and Southeast corridors for the project. Construction started in July 2009 on the North/Red Line Extension, a 5.3-mile segment with nine stations extending from the UH–Downtown area to the Northline Transit Center/HCC; at the same time, work commenced on the Purple Line along the Southeast Corridor, a 6.6-mile route with ten stations, and on the Green Line, a 3.3-mile segment with nine stations. The original timetable projected revenue service for the Red Line Extension in 2013 and for the Green Line in 2014. On September 9, 2010, METRO announced that the opening dates for the Red Line Extension, as well as the Purple and Green lines, would be pushed back to 2014. By September 2014, the start date for these affected lines was further delayed to April 4, 2015.

Australian singer-songwriter Sia signed with Sony Music's sub-label DancePool in 2000, releasing the single "Taken for Granted" which peaked at number 10 on the UK Singles Chart. In 2001 she issued her second solo album, Healing Is Difficult, a synthesis of retro jazz and soul whose lyrics address the death of her first love. Due to promotion concerns, she dismissed her manager, left Sony Music, and aligned with Go! Beat, a subsidiary of Universal Music Group. At the 2002 APRA Awards she received the Breakthrough Songwriter honor, shared with Jennifer Waite and Grant Wallis of Aneiki.

Australian singer-songwriter Sia began her career with the band Crisp, performing acid jazz in Australia before relocating to London to pursue the genre further. Her first solo single, Taken for Granted, marked an early exploration of trip hop, and she subsequently joined Zero 7, contributing vocals to their downtempo material. The albums Colour the Small One (2004) and Some People Have Real Problems (2007) signaled a shift toward jazz-inflected and folktronica textures, with the track Breathe Me frequently described as an alternative rock piece and a power ballad. The latter album also broadened her connections to indie pop. In discussing Colour the Small One, she indicated that the record drew on influences such as Kings of Convenience and James Taylor as well as the music associated with Zero 7’s tour environment, noting a degree of susceptibility to external influences.

Pixelon announced that iBash would be broadcast over the Internet as a demonstration of streaming technology. The live webcast encountered widespread error messages that appeared to thousands of viewers. The majority of audiences watched via Microsoft's streaming software rather than Pixelon’s own client. To promote the event, Pixelon leased the large video screen at One Times Square in New York City to display an eight-hour-plus live feed. An edited two-hour version of the program later aired on October 30, 1999 on Pax TV (now Ion Television).

Pixelon organized iBASH ’99, its product launch party, at the MGM Grand Las Vegas on October 29, 1999. Reported to have a budget of US$16 million, the event featured a broad lineup of musical acts, including Chely Wright, LeAnn Rimes, Faith Hill, the Dixie Chicks, Sugar Ray, Natalie Cole, KISS, Tony Bennett, the Brian Setzer Orchestra, and a reunion performance by The Who.

Hijack features Kamanchi Sly and DJ Supreme, with Sly releasing two EPs in 2004, while DJ Supreme remains active as a DJ on the European nightclub circuit and also works in record production. DJ Supreme attended Scratchcon 2000 in San Francisco, an event hosted by DJ Qbert. His recent project is The Turntable Trixters, a semi-biographical documentary about Hijack's history, which was screened by the British Film Institute and for which a DVD release is available.

Hijack, a British hip hop group, did not have their album released in the United States by Warner Brothers, leading to a parting of ways with the label and, ultimately, the group's dissolution due to musical differences. In the years that followed, DJ Supreme founded Backbone Records, while Kamanchi Sly and DJ Undercover established Reservoir Records and issued material under the aliases Mr Pink and Mr Blonde for a brief period. Sly also contributed to Nicolas Dresti’s singles “Tha Wildstyle” and “Tha Horns of Jericho.” Nicolas Dresti subsequently adopted the stage name DJ Supreme in 1996 and used it through 1998. Kamanchi Sly later changed his name to Unknown MC and achieved chart success alongside his brother, DJ Pied Piper. The latter, DJ Pied Piper and the Masters of Ceremonies, released the single “Do You Really Like It?” on Relentless Records in 2001, which reached number one in the UK.

William L. Couch became the sole leader of the Boomer movement after the death of David L. Payne on November 28, 1884, in Wellington, Kansas. He led a group of about 300 prospective settlers from Wellington across the Cherokee Outlet to a suitable area within Indian Territory. On December 12, 1884, the expedition reached a stream they named Still Water. A United States Cavalry detachment arrived to halt the Boomer expedition’s supplies; the participants were arrested and forced to abandon the territory. After his release, Couch spent several years in Washington, D.C., lobbying for the opening of the Unassigned Lands to public settlement, and his efforts ultimately achieved success.

William L. Couch, born November 20, 1850, in Wilkes County, North Carolina, was the eldest son of Meshach H. Couch and Mary Bryan Couch. After the Civil War his family relocated to Kansas, where he had little formal schooling but was an avid reader. He married Cynthia Gordon, an older Quaker woman, and in 1871 the couple moved to Butler County, Kansas, purchasing a farm near Douglass. Around 1874, as the Emporia–Wichita railroad was being constructed, Couch left farming to pursue entrepreneurship in Wichita. His ventures encompassed grain merchandising and operating a grain elevator, trading in horses and mules, and running a hardware and grocery store. He endured substantial losses from reversals in the financial markets, with only the profits from the livestock business sustaining his family.

SS California (1928) was a passenger liner later employed as a troop transport during the Second World War. The sequence of movements given in the supplied notes appears to pertain to the S.S.
