On April 26, 2016, Tyka Nelson filed probate documents in Carver County stating that no will had been found. Prince had been twice-divorced, was not married at the time of death, and had no known surviving children. Under Minnesota law, in the absence of a will, the full sister and five half-siblings could claim the estate, which included cash, real estate, stocks, and cars, totaling millions. Within three weeks of death, about 700 people claimed to be half-siblings or descendants. Bremer Trust received temporary control of the estate, had Prince’s vault drilled open, and was authorized to obtain a DNA blood sample from the coroner who performed the autopsy.

Prince wrote his first song, "Funk Machine," on his father's piano at age seven, a early display of his musical inclination. His parents divorced when he was ten, and his mother subsequently married Hayward Baker, who had a son named Omarr. A fraught relationship with Omarr contributed to a itinerant childhood, with Prince alternating between living with his father and with his mother and stepfather. Baker occasionally took him to see James Brown in concert, and Prince has credited Baker with improving the family’s finances. After a brief period living with his father, who bought him his first guitar, Prince moved into the basement of the Anderson family following his father’s decision to throw him out. There, he befriended the Andersons’ son, André Cymone, who would later collaborate with Prince.

On May 4, 2018, it was announced that the Ribbed: Live in a Dive series would return, with Ribbed: Live in a Dive slated for release in August 2018. A track from the album was featured on Fat Music for Wrecked People: Punk in Drublic 2018, released in May 2018; the song identified was "Just the Flu," which was later made available for streaming during 2018. In June 2018, the track "Cheese/Where's My Slice" was uploaded online.

Ribbed: Live in a Dive is a release in Fat Wreck Chords' Live in a Dive series, notable for re-launching the franchise after a hiatus of more than thirteen years since Lagwagon's own contribution to the series. The release is the first to adopt a title distinct from the customary "Live in a Dive" naming scheme. It also marks the inaugural instance within the sequence to capture a live performance of a previously issued album, specifically Lagwagon's Ribbed, performed live in its entirety. In connection with this release, Fat Wreck Chords indicated that additional Live in a Dive titles would be produced in the future.

Chemical hazard refers to the risk that chemicals contaminate food or beverages through contact with unwashed hands, contaminated clothing, or improper handling during preparation or storage. Ingestion occurs when a chemical is absorbed into the digestive tract after contact with food or drink, and it may be indirect, through contaminated items, or direct, by consuming the chemical itself. If food or drink is kept in an environment containing unsealed harmful chemicals, vapors or particulates can transfer onto the consumables, resulting in contamination. Direct ingestion of a chemical is possible but relatively uncommon. Additionally, inadequate labeling or unsecured containers can lead to accidental ingestion due to misidentification of the chemical.

Chemical hazard refers to risks arising from exposure to chemicals and their potential health effects on workers. Annually, exposure to chemicals is linked to approximately 190,000 illnesses and 50,000 deaths among workers. The precise link between chemical exposure and subsequent illness or death remains unknown. Consequently, most illnesses and deaths are believed to result from a lack of knowledge or awareness of chemical dangers. The most effective control method is the elimination or substitution of all chemicals that are thought or known to cause illness or death.

Louis Marx and Company filed a lawsuit against Mattel in March 1961, alleging that Mattel infringed Greiner & Hausser's patent for the Bild-Lilli doll's hip joint after licensing the Lilli design. The plaintiffs contended that Barbie was a direct take-off and copy of Bild-Lilli and that Mattel had falsely claimed to originate the design. Mattel counter-claimed in response. The litigation was settled out of court in 1963. In 1964, Mattel purchased Greiner & Hausser's copyright and patent rights to the Bild-Lilli doll for $21,600, an amount equivalent to about $213,000 in 2024 dollars.

In July 2025, Mattel introduced a Barbie doll designed to portray a character with Type 1 diabetes. The doll features an insulin pump, a glucose monitor, and a phone for checking blood sugar levels, reflecting contemporary tools used in diabetes management.

Within MPEG-1, a B-frame (bi-directionally predicted frame) may contain blocks encoded without reference to other frames, blocks predicted from forward references, blocks predicted from backward references, and blocks predicted by combining forward and backward information. The quantity of blocks encoded without reference and the number of forward-predicted blocks in a B-frame are not fixed and may vary.

Within the MPEG-1 standard, Audio Layer I represents a streamlined variant of Audio Layer II. It employs a narrower frame consisting of 384 samples, a design choice that yields reduced processing delay and finer time resolution. This characteristic makes Layer I particularly suitable for real-time applications such as teleconferencing and studio audio editing. Compared with Layer II, Layer I imposes lower computational complexity, facilitating real-time encoding on hardware available circa 1990.

World Refrigeration Day was conceived by Stephen Gill, a refrigeration consultant who previously served as president of the Institute of Refrigeration in the United Kingdom. In October 2018, the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) pledged its support for the observance. In January 2019, ASHRAE awarded Gill the John F James International Award at a ceremony in Atlanta. In February 2019, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) pledged its support at the UNEP national ozone officers meeting in Paris.

World Refrigeration Day is an international observance established by the World Refrigeration Day Secretariat, based in Derbyshire, England. It is observed annually on 26 June. The day seeks to raise public awareness of refrigeration technologies in daily life and to elevate the profile of the refrigeration, air-conditioning and heat-pump sector. The date was selected to commemorate the birth of Lord Kelvin on 26 June 1824.

PowerShell is bundled with current versions of Windows and can be installed on macOS and Linux. Since Windows 10 build 14971, PowerShell has replaced the Command Prompt as the default command shell exposed by File Explorer.

PowerShell provides support for binary prefix notation in numeric literals, enabling values to be expressed in binary form. This approach to numeric representation is analogous to the scientific notation found in many languages in the C family.

On 13 August 2018, Sony Movie Channel became fully free-to-air on satellite in preparation for its official launch on the Freesat programme guide on 9 October 2018. To enable SMC’s Freesat entry, Sony reorganised the surrounding movie-channel lineup within the guide. As part of this reorganization, Movies4Men +1 was no longer listed on the Freesat guide, though it remained freely accessible via manual tune-in. Encryption was removed from Sony Movie Channel +1 at the same time, although this encryption removal for SMC +1 was not incorporated into the Freesat full guide.

On 4 September 2025, Great! Mystery took the place of Great! Movies on Freeview, Sky, and Virgin Media. The FAST variant of Great! Mystery on Samsung, Rakuten, and Netgem TV platforms was replaced with a FAST channel carrying Great! Christmas. On Freeview, the FAST channel previously labeled as Great! Mystery was substituted with the FAST version of Great! Movies.

Debreceni Vasutas Sport Club, commonly known as Debreceni VSC, was founded on 12 March 1902 under its original name Debreceni Vasutas Sport Club. The club first reached Nemzeti Bajnokság I, Hungary's top division, in the 1943–44 season. It rose to national prominence in the early 2000s after securing its inaugural Hungarian league title in the 2004–05 season. In the following decade, the club claimed seven league championships, establishing itself as a dominant force in Hungarian football during the 2010s. A decline followed in the late 2010s after the withdrawal of government backing. The club escaped relegation in the 2016–17 Nemzeti Bajnokság I season.

Debreceni VSC, a Hungarian football club based in Debrecen, used the Oláh Gábor utcai Stadion as its home ground from 1989 to 2014, a venue with a capacity of 12,500 spectators. After the club secured its first Nemzeti Bajnokság I championship, the stadium was found not to meet UEFA's stadium criteria, leading to the relocation of key UEFA fixtures to the Ferenc Puskás Stadium. Consequently, matches in the 2009–10 UEFA Champions League group stage and the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League group stage were moved there.

As of November 2013, Google+'s user base was composed of roughly 60 percent male users, 25 percent female users, and 15 percent identifying as other or unknown. In mid-2011, the service’s early adopters were predominantly male, accounting for about 71.24 percent. Among these early adopters, the largest age group was 25–34 years, representing approximately 35 percent. A survey conducted in August 2011 estimated that 13 percent of U.S. adults had joined Google+.

Hashtags on Google+ were supported in two formats, using either the prefix symbol "#" or CamelCase capitalization, and these tags functioned as hyperlinks to a Google+ search for the term, typically surfacing either the most recent results or the most-trending discussions. The feature was introduced on October 12, 2011, and was later augmented by the addition of autocompletion for hashtags on January 17, 2012. The implementation drew attention for its resemblance to microblogging practices associated with Twitter, highlighting Google's attempt to integrate hashtag-driven discourse within the Google+ platform.

The Atlantic Ocean is bounded to the west by the continents of North and South America and to the east by Europe and Africa. Its northern extent leads to the Arctic Ocean through a sequence of marginal seas—the Labrador Sea, the Denmark Strait, the Greenland Sea, the Norwegian Sea, and the Barents Sea—along a dividing line that runs between Iceland and Svalbard. The Strait of Gibraltar serves as the gateway to the Mediterranean Sea, which is considered a marginal sea of the Atlantic. The Mediterranean connects onward to the Black Sea, and both seas lie at the confluence of Europe and Asia.

Approximately 50 million years ago, the Drake Passage began to open as the relative movement and separation rate between the South American and Antarctic plates changed. In the Middle Eocene, nascent ocean basins formed and a shallow gateway emerged. From about 34 to 30 million years ago, the passage deepened into a more substantial seaway. This tectonic and oceanographic evolution coincided with the Eocene–Oligocene climatic downturn and the growth of the Antarctic ice sheet.

In 2021, the Chinese Communist Party's 19th Central Committee approved a historical resolution. The document endorses the proposition that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to a single family. Accordingly, this concept is integrated into the CCP's policy toward Taiwan.

Chaos Communication Congress is an annual conference in Germany organized by the Chaos Computer Club. It originated in 1984 in Hamburg, later relocating to Berlin in 1998. In 2012 it returned to Hamburg after Berlin's venue exceeded its capacity of about 4,500 attendees. Attendance subsequently grew, with roughly 6,600 participants in 2012, over 13,000 in 2015, and more than 15,000 in 2017. From 2017 to 2019, the congress was held at the Trade Fair Grounds in Leipzig because Hamburg’s venue, the Congress Center Hamburg (CCH), was closed for renovations and could not accommodate further growth. The event moved back to Hamburg in 2023 after the CCH renovations were completed.

The Chaos Communication Congress (CCC) was planned to return to Hamburg's Congress Center, following its renovations, for the 37th edition of the event, titled 37C3. The congress was scheduled to take place from 27 to 30 December 2023, aligning with the conference’s customary late‑December window. In October 2022, organizers announced that there would be no CCC gathering that year. Subsequently, on 6 October 2023, CCC reiterated that 37C3 would proceed within the usual late‑December dates, specifically 27–30 December 2023.

The fastest-selling album in the first chart week on the UK Albums Chart is Adele's 25, released in November 2015, which posted first-week sales in excess of 800,000 copies. Oasis's Be Here Now is widely treated as controversial for its second-place status because its release occurred on a Thursday rather than the standard Monday release. Be Here Now, released on 21 August 1997, is reported to have sold about 813,000 copies in its first seven days, a figure that would have surpassed Adele's first-week total, though this claim is contested.

In July 2021 the Official Charts Company announced that ABBA’s Gold: Greatest Hits became the first album to accumulate more than 1,000 weeks on the UK Albums Chart. The tally of 1,000+ weeks omits the 2014 Gold – 40th Anniversary Edition, which is a three-CD set that also includes More ABBA Gold: More ABBA Hits and The Golden B-sides, in a configuration akin to Queen’s Platinum Collection. The stated total further excludes additional weeks that would have fallen within the Top 100 but are absent from OCC’s database prior to February 1994. Music Week historically published only the Top 75 as the public-facing chart, while the Top 150 Artist Albums Chart existed for industry insiders and ChartsPlus subscribers.

According to PC World, RealPlayer was singled out in two separate rankings for its perceived drawbacks: in 2006, the 1999 version ranked second on The 25 Worst Tech Products of All Time, with critics pointing to its tendency to install as the default media player, modifications to the Windows Registry, and the display of advertising messages; and in 2007, PC World placed RealPlayer across its 1996–2004 releases at fifth on The 20 Most Annoying Tech Products.

RealPlayer for macOS was historically distributed at no cost, reflecting its earlier pricing model. By December 2018, Real's official website did not offer any macOS download of RealPlayer, indicating that a Mac-compatible version was not available through the site at that time.

Chinese opera, historically the principal form of entertainment for centuries among both urban and rural residents in China and within the Chinese diaspora, remained a central cultural activity before undergoing a marked decline in the latter half of the 20th century due to a combination of political and market pressures. Factors commonly cited include language policies in Taiwan and Singapore that discouraged topolects, official hostility toward rural religious festivals in mainland China, and the process of de-Sinicization in Taiwan, with the decline attributed to two major forces: the Cultural Revolution and modernization. During the Cultural Revolution, traditional cultural forms were eradicated, many theatre professionals were persecuted, and exposure to opera among the younger generation diminished. In the modernization era, sweeping social changes and imported values weakened opera’s appeal, and it largely failed to counter these trends. Regional genres numbered more than 350 in 1957, and by the 21st century the government identified 162 forms for the intangible cultural heritage list, with many regarded as endangered. For younger audiences, Chinese opera is no longer part of everyday popular music culture, though it retains appeal for many older people who associate it with national or regional identity.

Canjun Opera, also known as Adjutant Play (參軍戲), represents an early stage in the history of Chinese drama and originated during the Later Zhao Dynasty (319–351 CE). The initial performances were a simple, comic form featuring only two performers. Central to the plot is a corrupt adjutant who is ridiculed by a jester named Grey Hawk (蒼鶻). Scholars regard these characters as precursors to the fixed role types that would come to characterize later Chinese opera, particularly the comic chou (丑) character.

InStyle is a magazine that covers a broad range of topics, including beauty and fashion, home décor, entertaining, and philanthropic endeavors. It also features coverage of celebrity lifestyles, feminist issues, and human-interest narratives, positioning itself as a source for insights into contemporary culture and trends.

InStyle announced in 2018 that it would discontinue both photographing fur and running fur-related advertisements, thereby becoming the first prominent fashion magazine to adopt a fur-free policy. The decision was framed as an effort to illuminate the cruelty associated with fur production and to encourage readers as well as the wider industry to abstain from fur consumption. The move received support from the animal-rights organization PETA, which endorsed the editorial change.

The 1950 United States census collected population and housing data across the nation, expanding upon the basic questions with a supplementary module administered to a sample of respondents. This additional component gathered information on income, marital history, fertility, and other topics. Comprehensive documentation for the 1950 census, including the census forms and a procedural history of its operation, is available from IPUMS (Integrated Public Use Microdata Series).

On April 1, 2022, the National Archives and Records Administration released scanned enumeration sheets from the 1950 United States census to the general public, in accordance with the 72-year rule that governs census confidentiality. The release made the 1950 census the most recent decennial census to be fully accessible to researchers and the public.

Within dance terminology, a lock step refers to an alternative form of the chassé in which the moving foot stops across the trajectory of the standing foot rather than closing beside it. In Latin dances, the combination of a crossed position and turnout directs the rear toe to point toward the heel of the opposite foot. By contrast, Standard dances often exhibit parallel feet when turnout is limited. In Standard styles, the fundamental locking motion is typically preceded and followed by a left side lead. The Latin version of the lock step is frequently used when cha-cha is danced in open position with a one-handed hold.

The entry describes a dance move that starts with the knee being lifted upward, followed by a swift downward kick of the foot, and finishes with the ankle extended while the toes are pointed downward.

Following the 2012 merger of Foxtel and Austar, XYZ Networks was dissolved. Subsequently, on 30 November 2012, Sky News Australia assumed management and operational responsibility for The Weather Channel. The channel was subsequently relaunched under the new brand as Sky News Weather in 2013, with the official rebrand taking effect on 25 January 2013.

In the early 2000s, the service relocated from its former site at 21 and underwent a rebranding to The Weather Channel. As the hours of live presentation were extended, the presenting lineup expanded with the addition of Tracey Malmborg, Jaynie Seal, Rebecca LeTourneau, and Garry Youngberry.

Talvin Singh pursued a range of artistic ventures alongside his music career, engaging in creative projects beyond recording. He founded ANOKHA, a London club widely regarded as seminal within its scene, reflecting his influence on the cultural landscape. Singh has performed at the Tate Gallery in London and developed a sound installation for Frith Street Gallery, illustrating his commitment to interdisciplinary work. He has also composed music for experimental dance, theatre, and film projects, extending his impact into various performing arts. In 1990 he conceived the Tablatronic, a hybrid electronic/analog tabla instrument that incorporates a rare internal microphone system. In a 2017 interview, he stated that he did not pursue fusion music and criticized the pressure on Indian musicians to fuse genres.
Talvin Singh received a UK Asian Music Award in 2010 for his sustained commitment to the music scene. In the 2014 Birthday Honours, he was appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE).

Zenzizenzizenzic is a historical mathematical term that has drawn attention as an oddity within its field, and it is also recognized as a linguistic oddity due to its highly unusual orthography. In the Oxford English Dictionary, it contains more Z letters than any other word, making it the form with the highest Z count among dictionary entries.

Zenzizenzizenzic is a term once used in a mathematical framework to denote a particular concept; both the word and the associated system are now obsolete. Today they survive mainly as curiosities rather than as part of regular practice. The Oxford English Dictionary records only a single citation for the term, reflecting its scant contemporary attestation.

Portugal received a bye to the elite round as the team with the highest seeding coefficient. The remaining 52 teams were drawn into 13 groups of four, with each group contest conducted as a single round-robin and the host nation for each group chosen after the draw. Advancing to the elite round were the 13 group winners, 13 runners-up, and the best third-placed team, the latter determined by their results against the first- and second-placed teams in their group.

The 2024 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification is a competition for men's national under-19 teams organized by UEFA to determine seven nations that will join the host nation, Northern Ireland, in the final tournament, with the latter automatically qualifying as hosts. Eligible players are those born on or after 1 January 2005.

By 2025, several Fujian counties had established local Taiwan Affairs Offices, though such county-level offices remain uncommon, with province-level divisions more typically hosting them. Zhou Qingsong, director of the Organization Department of the CCP Fujian Provincial Committee, announced that vocational schools would recruit Taiwanese teachers and that universities and public schools in Fujian would make it easier for Taiwanese students to enroll. On 27 February 2025, Fujian unveiled a package of 17 measures to strengthen cross-strait relations, including the creation of 100 annual positions in Ningde for Taiwanese workers in the lithium battery sector over the next three years; providing incentives in Putian to support Taiwanese biopharmaceutical enterprises establishing operations in a designated industrial park; offering incentives to industrial design companies to operate in Fujian; and attracting companies from the Matsu Islands to operate in Fuzhou.

On 12 September 2023, the CCP Central Committee and the State Council released a white paper titled "Opinions on Supporting Fujian in Exploring New Paths for Cross-Strait Integration and Development and Building a Cross-Strait Integration and Development Demonstration Zone," which outlines 21 measures to advance cross-strait integration in Fujian. The document aims to ease the lives of Taiwanese residents in Fujian by facilitating easier settlement, property purchases, access to social services, and education, while also seeking to bolster industrial cooperation across the Strait. A notable policy change is that Taiwanese would no longer be required to register for temporary residence in Fujian. It also encourages Taiwanese to acquire property in Fujian and participate in mainland China's social welfare system. Additionally, the white paper contains proposals to support Taiwanese companies in increasing their hiring of workers from Taiwan and to pilot allowing Taiwanese entities to establish radio and television programme production companies in Fujian.

In the run-up to the Battle off Ulsan, telegrams from August 1904 described Admiral Vitgeft’s plan to break through the Japanese blockade of Port Arthur, with instructions for Vice Admiral Jessen to sortie the Vladivostok Cruiser Squadron to aid the operation. A separate 5 August communication suggested Vitgeft intended to perish with Port Arthur, a notion that led the Vladivostok cruisers to take time to prepare for action. These delays in sailing diminished the chances of aiding the First Pacific Squadron as it attempted the passage through the Tsushima Straits. Had Vitgeft succeeded, the two Russian squadrons were to rendezvous in the Sea of Japan.

During the 1904 Russo-Japanese War, the Vladivostok Independent Cruiser Squadron conducted six commerce-raiding sorties from Vladivostok, sinking a total of fifteen transports. The first raid, from February 9 to 14, operated along the Japanese coastline and sank a single transport. The second, February 24 to March 1, along the Korean coast, yielded no results. In the third sortie, April 23 to 27, the squadron ambushed Japanese troop transports near GenSan, Korea, causing considerable damage. The fourth raid, June 12 to 19 in the Tsushima Strait, included the Hitachi Maru incident and resulted in the sinking of several transports, with the British transport Allantown captured. The fifth operation, June 28 to July 3, also in the Tsushima Strait, saw the British transport Cheltenham captured. The sixth and final raid, July 17 to August 1, targeted the Pacific coast of Japan and led to the sinking of one British freighter and one German freighter. In response, Japan assigned the Imperial Japanese Navy’s 2nd Fleet under Vice Admiral Kamimura Hikonojō with substantial resources to locate and destroy the Russian squadron, but Kamimura failed to locate or destroy it on several occasions, provoking adverse public comment in Japan.

Following the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, Siberia experienced a severe economic downturn as Russia transitioned to a market economy, characterized by hyperinflation, industrial collapse, and the rapid privatization of state resources. In the 1990s, discussions arose about greater regional autonomy, including proposals for a Siberian Republic and the formation of a Siberian Agreement; however, these initiatives did not alter the constitutional framework, and Siberia remained under Russian federal authority. Economic restructuring subsequently led to a shift toward resource-based specialization, with emphasis on extraction and related industries. Population declined, particularly in the Russian Arctic, and the traditional emphasis on large, centralized industrial settlements was largely abandoned in favor of new economic arrangements and settlement patterns.

The etymology of Siberia remains uncertain. The name was adopted into Russian toponymy through contact with the Khanate of Sibir beginning in the 15th century. By contrast, Yugra referred to the northern lands east of the Ural Mountains and is attested from the 11th century or earlier. The first explicit Russian chronicle reference to Siberia dates to the early 15th century, in connection with the death of Khan Tokhtamysh in the territory described as Siberia.

Chase Strangio has described himself as a constitutional lawyer who fundamentally doubts the Constitution's authority. He has characterized civil marriage as inherently violent. He rejects the notion that transgender women can be born with male anatomy, and he has argued that there is no such thing as a male body. He has further stated that a penis is not a male body part, describing it as an unusual bodily feature for a woman.

Chase Strangio is an American attorney and prominent advocate for LGBTQ rights, affiliated with the American Civil Liberties Union. He participated in the Bostock v. Clayton County case, which reached the Supreme Court in June 2020, a decision delivered by a 6–3 majority. The litigation concerned Gerald Bostock, a gay man who had been terminated from his employment due to discrimination based on sexual orientation. The Court held that it is illegal to discriminate in employment on the basis of sexual orientation or transgender identity.

Kimberly J. Mueller issued several of the earliest judicial interpretations of the First Step Act, focusing on petitions for compassionate release. Her rulings addressed requests filed by incarcerated individuals with comorbidities who faced increased risk from COVID-19.

Kimberly J. Mueller began her public-service career as an extern for California State Assemblyman Lloyd Connelly. She subsequently moved to Sacramento’s Tahoe Park neighborhood and was elected to the Sacramento City Council, where she served from 1987 to 1992.

Marvin the Paranoid Android was brought to life on screen in the 2005 film with Warwick Davis wearing the Marvin costume, while the character was voiced by Alan Rickman. The 2005 design marked a departure from the original television appearance, featuring a shorter stature with a disproportionately large head and stubby limbs. The original 1981 TV costume was refurbished for a cameo in the film, appearing in a Vogon office on Vogsphere where the main characters attempt to release Tricia alongside other life forms.

Marvin the Paranoid Android survived the collision with the sun of Kakrafoon and was sent back in time by the Heart of Gold’s Improbability Field to be rescued on Sqornshellous Zeta. A scrap-metal merchant affixed a steel rod to Marvin’s now-lost leg and sold him to a Mind Zoo, where onlookers sought to induce happiness from him. He gained celebrity status on Sqornshellous Zeta and was invited to inaugurate a newly constructed bridge intended to revive the planet’s economy. When Marvin connected to the bridge’s opening circuit, the device self-destructed, taking the assembled crowd with it. He eventually ended up in a swamp, his artificial leg trapped in the mud, and he spent about 1.5 million years walking in circles to illustrate his point, planning to continue for another million years before attempting the motion in reverse for variety.

Following World War II, Asia experienced rapid decolonization as European powers were weakened and Japan’s imperial rule ended. India achieved independence in 1947, a year that also saw the creation of a separate Muslim-majority nation in the subcontinent, resulting in the partition of British India into India and Pakistan. In 1971, East Pakistan became the independent state of Bangladesh, altering South Asian geopolitics. The Cold War era shaped regional security dynamics, intensifying India–Pakistan rivalries and influencing wider Asian affairs. With the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991, five Central Asian republics—Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan—emerged as independent states, marking a significant post–Cold War realignment in the region.

Asia features a diverse array of religious and philosophical traditions, many of which are understood through a largely philosophical lens and encompass a broad spectrum of ideas. Indian thought includes Hindu philosophy and Buddhist philosophy as major strands, with some schools emphasizing nonmaterial aims while the Cārvāka tradition advocates the enjoyment of the material world. Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism originated in India, in the South Asian region. In East Asia, particularly China and Japan, Confucianism, Taoism, and Zen Buddhism took shape, contributing signficant and enduring influences on regional ethics, governance, and personal cultivation.

Google Maps originated as a mobile application released in 2006. In its newer iterations, the service has incorporated features such as GPS turn-by-turn navigation and parking assistance. By 2013, it was reported as the world's most popular smartphone app, used by over 54 percent of global smartphone owners. In 2017, the Android version of the app reached two billion users.

In April 2015, an image created via Google Map Maker and placed on a map near Rawalpindi, Pakistan, depicted the Android logo urinating on the Apple logo and subsequently appeared on Google Maps. Google issued a public apology for the incident, and the company temporarily disabled user moderation on Map Maker. On May 12, 2015, worldwide editing was paused until a new policy could be devised, with the aim of establishing guidelines for approving edits and preventing vandalism.

The HQ-7 is a short-range surface-to-air missile developed by the People's Republic of China. In Chinese, it is designated 红旗-7 in simplified characters and 紅旗-7 in traditional characters, with the pinyin Hóng Qí-7 and a literal translation of "Red Banner-7"; its NATO reporting name is CH-SA-4. The system was reverse-engineered by the Changfeng Electromechanical Technology Design Institute from the French R-440 Crotale surface-to-air missile. It entered service in the early 1980s.

The Agusta A.103 was an Italian prototype single-seat light helicopter. It first flew in October 1959. The pilot sat within a cockpit enclosed by a transparent perspex bubble. The engine was mounted at the rear of the fuselage. The tail rotor was carried on an enclosed tail boom.

Radio formats are not static and continually evolve as audience tastes, technological developments, and regulatory environments change. Each broad format can be subdivided into multiple specialty formats that target narrower audiences or specific themes. Additionally, some formats are available only in certain regions or through specialized venues such as satellite radio or Internet radio, extending their reach beyond traditional terrestrial broadcasting.

Radio format is the overall content strategy of a radio station, designed to attract a specific audience by shaping its programming type. Formats can be thematic, concentrating on a particular genre or topic, or general in scope. They may emphasize informational content, music-oriented programming, or various other blends. As a marketing tool, the format informs branding, listener expectations, and advertising alignment. Formats are frequently revised, and stations may implement temporary changes known as stunting to draw attention or experiment with new directions.

Leonardo da Vinci proposed the concept of a double-hulled vessel as part of his studies in naval architecture. The design sought to protect the craft against ramming and damage from submerged hazards such as reefs or wreckage. A secondary inner hull was intended to provide buoyancy, allowing the ship to remain afloat even if the outer hull sustained a breach.

In submarines, a double hull comprises an outer light hull and an inner pressure hull, with the outer shell chiefly governing the vessel’s hydrodynamic form rather than the cylindrical inner pressure hull. The concept was introduced in the late 1890s by French naval designer Maxime Laubeuf on the submarine Narval. The outer hull is engineered to tailor water flow around the submarine, effectively providing a hydrodynamic bypass that enhances efficiency and handling. Additionally, the outer hull can serve as a mounting surface for anechoic tiles, which absorb sonar energy to reduce the submarine’s detectability.

Amid the 2021–2022 global energy crisis, European gas customers voluntarily reduced their consumption in response to price signals. In August, gas usage dropped by 23% relative to the average consumption in August over the previous three years. For the year 2022 up to that point, overall gas consumption was about 7% below the three-year average.

During the 2021–2022 global energy crisis, Marc-Antoine Eyl-Mazzega, director of IFRI's Energy and Climate Center, stated that Europe no longer represents the stable and peaceful region it once did. He argued that Europe now experiences some of the highest energy prices in the world, and that this situation has shifted comparative advantages toward strategic competitors, which hold an edge over European actors in energy markets.

During the Early Neolithic, farming relied on a relatively limited selection of plants, notably einkorn wheat, millet, and spelt, with spelt occurring in both wild and domesticated forms, while dogs were kept by farming communities. By around 8000 BCE, domesticated animals included sheep, goats, cattle, and pigs.

Genetic analyses of Anatolian Neolithic populations indicate that the farmers of Anatolia derive a substantial share of their ancestry from local Anatolian hunter-gatherers (AHG). This finding suggests that agriculture was adopted locally by these forager groups rather than introduced by incoming farming populations. As a result, the observed ancestry pattern in early Anatolian Neolithic communities argues against demic diffusion being the primary mechanism by which agriculture spread into the region.

USS J. Franklin Bell (APA-16) returned to San Diego on 29 September 1942 to resume coastal operations and amphibious training for the Attu invasion in the Aleutians. She was reclassified as APA-16 on 1 February 1943 and continued rehearsals until sailing for San Francisco on 16 April to embark troops and equipment. Departing on 24 April for Cold Bay, Alaska, she arrived off Attu on 11 May 1943 amid dense fog and heavy seas. Under the command of Commander J. B. McGovern, she began landing operations, but submerged rocks, pea-soup weather, and narrow beaches limited unloading to two or three boats at a time. After two days of around-the-clock unloading, the operation was completed, casualties were embarked, and the ship headed home by 16 May 1943.

Prior to entering U.S. Navy service as USS J. Franklin Bell (APA-16), the vessel operated for the Pacific Mail Steamship Company as a combined passenger and cargo liner, beginning on 28 May 1921. Her maiden voyage under the Pacific Mail commenced on 6 August 1921, sailing from Seattle to the Far East.
Pakistan does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Israel. In 2005, the two countries conducted an exchange that was facilitated by Turkey, which served as an intermediary in the process.

Pakistan gained independence in 1947 and emerged as a dominion within the British Commonwealth. Muhammad Ali Jinnah, who led the Muslim League, became Pakistan's first Governor-General and also presided as President of the Constituent Assembly, but died of tuberculosis on 11 September 1948. The founding leaders appointed Liaquat Ali Khan, then the secretary-general of the Muslim League, as Pakistan's first Prime Minister. From 1947 until 1956, the country remained a monarchy within the Commonwealth, with George VI and later Elizabeth II as head of state, before Pakistan adopted a republican constitution in 1956.

MTV Video Music Brasil (VMB) did not take place in 2013, as MTV Brasil declined to stage the ceremony in light of the substantial prize pool and the transfer of the brand to Viacom. In 2014, Pay TV MTV Brazil considered reviving the awards, but those plans were abandoned to prioritize MTV's international ceremonies, the VMAs and MTV EMA. As a result, the VMB came to be regarded as extinct. In 2018, MTV began producing the MTV MIAW Awards Brazil, a program centered on Brazilian pop culture that is viewed as the successor to the VMB.

MTV Video Music Brasil, the Brazilian counterpart to the MTV Video Music Awards, traditionally crowned its premier honor as the Viewer's Choice Award until 2005, when that accolade was merged with Video of the Year. In 2007, the ceremony underwent a major rebranding that saw the elimination of several categories, notably the genre-based divisions, and a redesigned trophy. After these changes, the event shifted its focus from presenting music videos to honoring artists, with Artist of the Year becoming the most prestigious prize. Despite the rebranding, the Video of the Year category continued to be presented.

R'Bonney Nola Gabriel was born in Houston, Texas, to Remigio Bonzon "R. Bon" Gabriel, a Filipino from Malate, Manila, who immigrated to Washington at age 25 and earned a psychology degree from the University of Houston before owning a car repair shop, and Dana Walker, an American from Beaumont, Texas. Her parents married in the Philippines. Gabriel grew up in Missouri City and Friendswood, Texas, and has three older brothers. She spent part of her childhood in Manila, where she enjoyed street life, played tong-its, and watched fiesta parades. The family continues to visit the Philippines for holidays and summers, and she has occasionally lived in Malate on the same street as her father. She is in a long-term relationship with musician Kevin Bong.

William Lewis FRS (c. 1708 – 21 January 1781) was a British chemist and physician who was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society. He is recognized for his writings on pharmacy and medicine, contributing to the pharmacological and medical literature of his era. In addition, Lewis carried out investigations into metals, exploring their properties and potential uses. His interdisciplinary work reflects the broader scientific interests of eighteenth-century Britain, spanning chemistry, medicine, and metallurgy.

William Lewis was born in Richmond, Surrey, the son of John Lewis, a brewer. He matriculated at Christ Church, Oxford on 17 March 1730, receiving a BA in 1734, an MA in 1737, an MB in 1741, and an MD in 1745. He practiced as a physician, and by 1746 was living in Dover Street, London before soon transferring his residence to Kingston upon Thames. In 1749 he delivered the oration at the opening ceremony of the Radcliffe Library.

Investigation Discovery's European feed primarily broadcasts in English, with local subtitles or dubbing employed in certain regions to accommodate regional audiences. In some markets, advertisements are localized to reflect local brands and regulatory requirements, while in other countries, announcements between programs are localized as part of local scheduling and presentation practices.

Investigation Discovery (European TV channel) has undergone changes in its French distribution. Since 15 December 2015, it has been carried exclusively by SFR TV in France, as part of a distribution agreement between SFR and Discovery. In June 2024, with the launch of HBO Max in France, Investigation Discovery was made available on HBO Max for all subscribers of the service.

Kilowatt (kW) is a unit of power equal to 1,000 watts. It is widely used to express the output power of engines, electric motors, tools, machinery, and heaters, and it is also used to quantify the electromagnetic power output of broadcast radio and television transmitters. One kilowatt is approximately equivalent to 1.34 horsepower. In practical terms, a small electric heater with a single heating element may draw about 1 kW. The average electrical power consumption of a typical United States household is about 1 kW. Solar irradiance near the equator under clear midday conditions delivers roughly 1 kW of solar power per square meter.

In radio broadcasting, transmitter power is commonly reported as effective radiated power (ERP), expressed in watts. ERP is defined as the amount of power a hypothetical half-wave dipole antenna would need to radiate to produce the same peak radiation intensity in the main lobe as the actual antenna system. Consequently, ERP provides a link between the transmitter’s output and the resulting radiation level in the main lobe, offering a standardized means of characterizing radiated power.

Located at the bottom-right of the keyboard, the correction key backspaces the carriage by one space. It also switches the machine into a dedicated correction mode that uses correction tape for the next character, instead of the standard typing ribbon. In this mode, the carriage does not advance when the next character is typed. The typist presses the correction key and then retypes the erroneous character. The erroneous character can be lifted from the page or covered with white-out (if the correction ribbon is not employed). The correct character is then typed. This allows any number of mistakes to be corrected in sequence. The process is manual, and the machine has no memory of typed characters.

Selectric-based mechanisms were adopted as computer terminals due to their speed of about 14.8 characters per second, immunity to clashing type elements, reliable paper path, high-quality output, and overall reliability. They supplanted Teletype machines and older typebar-based output devices as terminal interfaces. The IBM 2741 terminal stands as a well-known example of a Selectric-based terminal, employing a specialized typing element. The 2741 also played a key role in the early development and use of the APL programming language.

Peking glass, or overlay carved glass, is produced by layering glass around a central core and then removing portions to form a relief image, a technique reminiscent of cameo glass. A glassblower shapes the initial form, after which the piece is repeatedly dipped into molten glass to accumulate several successive layers of color. The layered material is then carved to produce a textured image, with the contrasting colors of the different strata revealed as the outer layers are removed. Historically, many examples employ yellow glass, referred to as Imperial Yellow, reflecting its association with the Qing dynasty’s Aisin Gioro clan.

Peking glass originated in 18th-century Qing dynasty China, developing within a context in which European glassmaking innovations had begun to influence Asia during the 17th century and Jesuit missionaries had brought contemporary Italian techniques to China while the country maintained limited contact with the West. In 1696, the Kangxi Emperor established an Imperial glass-works to enhance the production of this material. The resulting glass was widely used in snuff bottles and vases to imitate jade and other precious stones. Over time, the production technique spread beyond the court workshops to artisans across the population. The period commonly regarded as its golden age falls in the mid-18th century, during the reign of the Qianlong Emperor. Although production declined in the 19th century, Peking glass continued to be produced in China through the Republican era and into the present day.

The Financial District is one of Vancouver's most densely developed areas, containing more than 60% of the city's office space. It functions as a central hub for financial and professional services, housing major banks, corporate headquarters, and firms in accounting, law, and other financial sectors. Beyond commercial offices, the district includes government buildings, embassies and consulates, non-governmental organizations, and a number of luxury hotels.

Vancouver's Financial District is served by an extensive network of local and commuter bus routes along Burrard and Georgia streets, providing convenient access for workers and visitors. Burrard Station lies at the heart of the district and offers SkyTrain Expo Line service, connecting thousands of daily commuters. To the north of the district, Waterfront Station provides connections to SeaBus, the West Coast Express commuter rail, and the SkyTrain Canada Line, linking the area to regional and metropolitan transit networks.

On2 Technologies developed a family of video codecs known as TrueMotion, including VP3/VP4, VP5, VP6, and VP7. Under the name The Duck Corporation, the company released additional TrueMotion variants such as TrueMotion S, TrueMotion 2, and TrueMotion RT 2.0.

Linear PCM (LPCM), commonly referred to as PCM, represents the encoding of uncompressed audio in media files. It serves as the standard for Compact Disc Digital Audio (CD-DA). In computing contexts, PCM data is typically packaged within container formats such as WAV, AIFF, or AU, although it can also exist as a standalone raw audio stream. The use of containers is not strictly required, since PCM data may be stored without any wrapper as raw audio.

Close to the Edge has continued to attract favorable retrospective assessments across several outlets. AllMusic's Dave Thompson awarded it five stars and described the work as a flawless masterpiece. In Paul Stump's History of Progressive Rock (1997), the album's ambition and heartfelt performance are noted as elements that still earn grudging respect from Yes's critics. The 2005 Q & Mojo special edition ranks the album third in its 40 Cosmic Rock Albums list. It is also included in Robert Dimery's 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die. In Guitar World, the reader poll places it at No. 67 in the "100 Greatest Guitar Albums of All Time," and Sound & Vision lists it No. 32 on its Top 50 Albums of All Time. Rolling Stone positions the record at No. 5 among the greatest progressive rock albums, while Colin Larkin's All Time Top 1000 Albums places it at No. 130. Prog magazine designates Close to the Edge as the top progressive rock release of all time, and Rolling Stone also ranks it No. 445 on its broader top 500 albums list. More recent assessments include Sean Murphy of PopMatters (2023), who praises the title track as one of progressive rock's ultimate statements of purpose—epic and rewarding, and John Cunningham of WhatCulture (2023), who describes the LP as a confronting journey through the subconscious marked by several colorful songs and calls it a standout work.

Close to the Edge opens with a tape-loop introduction that blends keyboard textures with field recordings of natural sounds, including flowing water and birds. The loop extended roughly 40 feet and took two days to record, and Anderson was inspired to incorporate the birdsong into the texture. The instrumental section of I Get Up, I Get Down drew inspiration from Wendy Carlos's Sonic Seasonings (1972). Anderson proposed beginning with an improvised group jam, an approach deemed adventurous and influential in shaping the band’s entrance on the final take. The track was assembled from several segments, with drummer Bill Bruford describing them as ten-, twelve-, and sixteen-bar sections. The concept for the introduction originated after Yes toured with the Mahavishnu Orchestra, when a band member suggested opening with improvisation and pre-arranged pauses.

Three former RSA Insurance Ireland employees were fined by the United Kingdom's accounting regulator under sanctions linked to an inquiry into financial irregularities at the company in 2012, with the total penalties amounting to £182,000 (€206,090).

On 4 February 2014, Stephen Hester was named chief executive of RSA Insurance Group, with the appointment taking effect immediately. Hester had previously served as the chief executive of the Royal Bank of Scotland Group.

Thomas Johansson is a Swedish former professional tennis player. Growing up, he idolized Mats Wilander, who served as captain of Sweden's Davis Cup team. In addition to tennis, Johansson pursued interests in golf and floorball and is a fan of ice hockey. He participated in a Montreal street hockey charity event in 2001, where he scored two goals and recorded one assist as the ATP Stars defeated the NHL Players 6–5. He married Gisella Kaltenecker on 3 December 2005.

Thomas Johansson joined the professional tour at the outset of his career and turned professional the following year. Over the course of his career he won nine top-level singles titles and one doubles title on the ATP Tour. He captured the 1999 Canada Masters crown by defeating world No. 4 Yevgeny Kafelnikov from a set down in the final. His breakout Grand Slam came at the 2002 Australian Open, where, having never previously advanced beyond the quarterfinals in 24 major appearances, he defeated Jacobo Díaz, Markus Hipfl, Younes El Aynaoui, Adrian Voinea, Jonas Björkman and Jiří Novák to reach the final and then beat Marat Safin in four sets after dropping the first. Safin later commented, "He was overpowering me from the baseline, backhand to backhand." Johansson became the first Swedish Grand Slam winner since Stefan Edberg at the 1992 US Open and the first Swede to win the Australian Open since Mats Wilander in 1988.

Metro Vancouver structures its work around a series of action areas, with the specifics laid out in subsections. About 84 percent of the organization’s budget is directed to three main utilities: water, liquid waste, and solid waste. The commitments of Metro Vancouver and its member jurisdictions to each action area are articulated in eight management plans that have been approved by the board.

Metro Vancouver operates and maintains the regional liquid-waste facility and oversees the network of trunk sewers, pumping stations, and wastewater treatment plants that connect with municipal sewer systems. The organization is dedicated to protecting public health and the environment, ensuring safe and reliable wastewater services across the region. It also pursues extensive resource recovery from the waste stream, aiming to reclaim energy, nutrients, and other usable materials wherever feasible.

Sky, excluded from the ONdigital consortium, operated as a competitor by default within the UK digital television market. It subsequently joined Freeview, the free-to-air platform created by ITV Digital, and held an equal stake alongside the BBC, ITV, Channel 4, and Arqiva. Prior to October 2005, Freeview carried three Sky channels: Sky News, Sky Three, and Sky Sports News. Sky Travel served as Freeview's first Sky channel, but was replaced by Sky Three on 31 October 2005. Sky Three was later re-branded as Pick TV in 2011.

Sky (UK and Ireland) permits channel listings on its electronic programme guide without a veto, with open access mandated by Ofcom’s licensing obligations. Any channel capable of being carried on a suitable satellite beam at the 28° East orbital position is eligible for inclusion on Sky’s EPG. Access is subject to a fee that can range from about £15 up to £100,000. Third-party channels that employ encryption may receive discounts, including reduced charges, complimentary EPG entries, free carriage on a Sky-leased transponder, or even direct payments for carriage. Sky does not exercise control over a channel’s content or carriage issues, such as picture quality, even for encrypted services.

Group N of the 2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup was one of four classification groups designed to determine the final placements for teams not advancing to the knockout rounds. The round was staged from 6 to 8 September 2019 and included the bottom-two finishers from Groups C and D. Results from the preliminary round were carried over into this phase, and Group C teams faced Group D teams in inter-group games, all held at Wukesong Arena in Beijing. The final standings defined the teams’ positions in the tournament’s classification bracket, with the first-placed team occupying the 17–20 range, the second 21–24, the third 25–28, and the fourth 29–32.

Mexico's national team maintains a notable intercontinental rivalry with Argentina, reflecting the geographic and confederational gap between CONCACAF and CONMEBOL. Both nations are among the most renowned Spanish-speaking countries. The rivalry is more strongly felt by Mexican supporters, while many Argentines do not view Mexico as a major adversary; instead, Argentines typically consider Brazil, Uruguay, England, and Germany as bigger rivals. In head-to-head matches, Mexico has recorded 4 wins, 16 losses, and 12 draws against Argentina.

In January 2019, Gerardo Martino was appointed head coach of the Mexico national football team, becoming the third Argentine to lead the side. In the 2019 CONCACAF Gold Cup, Mexico swept the group stage with three wins. In the quarterfinal, Mexico defeated Costa Rica on penalties after a 1–1 draw, 5–4 in the shootout. They then defeated Haiti in the semifinal, and in the final secured a 1–0 victory over the United States to capture the Gold Cup title.

Huckarde encompasses the site of the hillfort known as Sigiburg, located in the southern part of present-day Dortmund and commanding a view of the Ruhr near its confluence with the Lenne. The ruins that later became Hohensyburg castle stand on the same location, linking the prehistoric fortification to a later medieval landmark. While the hillfort is generally regarded as of Saxon origin, there is no archaeological or documentary proof to confirm this attribution. During the Saxon Wars, Frankish forces under Charlemagne captured the site in 772, it was allegedly retaken by the Saxons (possibly under Widukind) in 774, and Charlemagne then seized and refortified it in 775. Archaeological evidence, however, indicates that the Sigiburg site was inhabited as early as the Neolithic era, reflecting a longer chronicle of human occupation beyond the medieval fortifications.

Huckarde is a district of Dortmund in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Dortmund is home to more than twenty museums, making the city one of the places with the broadest museum variety in the Ruhr Valley. Among these institutions is the LWL Industrial Museum Zollern II/IV Colliery, which also functions as an anchor site on the European Route of Industrial Heritage.

Unisys has been recognized as a leader in the NelsonHall NEAT Vendor Evaluation for Advanced Digital Workplace Services, a designation awarded by the NelsonHall Evaluation & Assessment Tool (NEAT). The company received this leadership status in four separate evaluations conducted in 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2023.

In 1998, Unisys agreed to pay the United States government $2.25 million to settle allegations related to its handling of federal contracts. The allegations claimed that the company supplied refurbished, rather than new, computer materials to several federal agencies, thereby violating contract terms. Unisys acknowledged that in the early 1990s it provided reworked or refurbished computer components to both civilian and military agencies where contracts required new equipment. The case was tied to the fact that refurbished material generally commanded a lower market price than the government paid for new equipment.

On February 22, 2011, Moseley Braun finished fourth in a six-candidate Chicago mayoral race, receiving about nine percent of the vote. In her concession speech, she stated that her young niece could become Chicago’s first female mayor, though Jane Byrne had already served in that role as the city’s first female mayor.

Following Chicago mayor Richard M. Daley’s November 2010 announcement that he would not seek re-election, Carol Moseley Braun declared her bid to become mayor in 2011. In early 2011, U.S. Representative Danny Davis and former Illinois State Senator James Meeks dropped out of the race and endorsed Moseley Braun, a move that established her as the consensus Black candidate. The consolidation of support occurred amid discussions about who was the strongest candidate, with emphasis placed on Moseley Braun’s background as a former U.S. senator, ambassador, and presidential contender; participants in these conversations included civil rights leader Jesse Jackson and Chicago alderman Walter Burnett Jr.

On February 5, 2019, lawsuits were filed by a number of 1970s-era musicians, including David Johansen and John Waite, against Sony Music Entertainment and UMG Recordings, Inc. The plaintiffs argue that the companies improperly blocked the reclaiming of rights to songs that the artists had previously assigned, asserting that U.S. copyright law permits creators to reclaim ownership after 35 years by submitting termination notices. They further contend that Sony and UMG have routinely and systematically ignored hundreds of such notices. The defendants counter that the disputed recordings are works made for hire and therefore not subject to reclamation.

Sony Music UK integrated Essential Music and Marketing, an independent sales and distribution company, into its operations. Essential Music and Marketing was subsequently renamed Red Essential. In August 2016, Sony Music acquired Ministry of Sound Recordings, expanding its label portfolio. Ministry of Sound Recordings is home to artists including London Grammar, DJ Fresh, and Sigala.

Within the European Union, the Commission conducts strategic studies aimed at fostering discussion, encouraging innovation, and disseminating best practices among member states. The mainstream activities of Community programmes support mobility and the development of transnational partnerships, thereby expanding opportunities for cross-border cooperation. Consequently, these measures motivate participants to learn languages as part of broader educational and professional exchanges facilitated by EU initiatives.

Within the European Union, the Romani population numbers over two million, representing a substantial minority. The language Romani comprises a family of related languages, with several distinct varieties spoken by different communities. Romani does not have official status in any EU member state, though it is recognised as an official minority language in Sweden and Finland. In terms of media and education, however, Romani has a limited footprint across the Union, with near-negligible presence in mass media and in educational institutions.

Speed Drive is a song by Charli XCX that achieved chart success in both the United Kingdom and the United States. In the UK, it peaked at number nine on the Official Singles Chart, becoming XCX's sixth top-10 single there and her first top-10 as a lead artist since Doing It, a 2015 collaboration with Rita Ora. In the US, the track marked XCX's first appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 since Break the Rules (2014), giving her a fifth entry on that chart.

"Speed Drive" is a track performed by Charli and included on the Barbie soundtrack. Alex Gonzalez of Uproxx characterized the song as channeling a gleaming pink energy and as a standout, high-energy entry within the Barbie universe. Liberty Dunworth of NME noted that, despite its under-two-minute length, the track delivers a strong punch and ranks among the most energetic selections on the soundtrack.

In England, the list of radio stations is organized according to the official statistical regional divisions, with coverage divided among East Midlands, East, Greater London, Greater Manchester, North East, North West, South East, South West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

In the United Kingdom, a substantial number of universities and several colleges operate student radio stations. The majority of these outlets broadcast exclusively online rather than via conventional terrestrial channels. The Student Radio Association represents about 65 student radio stations.

Apache CXF is an open-source services framework for building and deploying web services in Java. It provides support for JAX-WS and JAX-RS, enabling SOAP-based and RESTful services, respectively, and offers integration with JBI and JCA. The project also supports Java Management Extensions (JMX) for administration, and allows JMS messaging over SOAP. In addition, CXF integrates with the Spring framework and supports multiple data-binding technologies, including JAXB, Aegis, and Apache XMLBeans, as well as the Service Data Objects (SDO) standard.
Apache CXF is commonly used in service-oriented architecture (SOA) infrastructure projects, where it is frequently integrated with Apache ServiceMix, Apache Camel, and Apache ActiveMQ.

The qualifying stage of the 1995 UEFA European Under-18 Championship was conducted during 1994 and 1995. The format consisted of two rounds, through which seven national teams earned a place in the final tournament. These qualifiers joined the host nation Greece in the finals.

Houston, Texas, features the Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park in its Uptown District, a popular tourist attraction that also serves as a venue for weddings and other celebrations. In terms of pedestrian accessibility, a 2011 Walk Score assessment ranked Houston as the 23rd most walkable among the 50 largest U.S. cities.

Houston is celebrated for its diverse culinary landscape and expansive dining options, reflecting a dynamic and multicultural restaurant culture. The city holds the official nickname Space City, a designation granted in 1967 to acknowledge the presence of NASA's Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center within the area. In addition to Space City, Houston is known by several local epithets, including Bayou City, Clutch City, Crush City, Magnolia City, and H-Town, as well as a label emphasizing its status as a premier Southern culinary hub.

World Hypotheses posits that the significance of historical events is not inherent but arises from their placement within a broader sequence and the interpretations applied to them. Events examined in isolation lack intrinsic meaning, since their significance emerges only through their relationships to preceding and following events and the readings attributed to them. The historical-context metaphor, or contextualist approach, involves selecting particular events, their surrounding contexts, and interpretive frameworks and weaving them into a coherent and meaningful historical narrative. Notable contextualist philosophers associated with this view include Charles Sanders Peirce, William James, Henri Bergson, and John Dewey.

World Hypotheses summarizes Pepper's argument that utter skepticism and dogmatism are both weak epistemic positions and are intimately related forms of the same underlying issue. He defends a stance of relative skepticism, whereby belief is suspended until justification is provided. He portrays utter skepticism as comparable to a dogmatic approach that persistently doubts everything, while a dogmatist is described as someone whose beliefs exceed the cognitive grounds available to support them. If neither extreme can be cognitively justified, Pepper contends that knowledge about the world must lie between these poles, specifically between common sense and refined knowledge.

Bell YAH-63 was Bell's entry in the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter (AAH) program. A number of proposals were submitted for the competition by Bell, Boeing-Vertol (with Grumman), Hughes, Lockheed, and Sikorsky. In June 1973, Bell and Hughes were selected as finalists for the program. Subsequently, each finalist was awarded a contract to construct two prototype aircraft for testing and evaluation.

Bell YAH-63 was Bell’s submission to the United States Army’s Advanced Aerial Fire Support System (AAFSS) program, launched in the mid-1960s with the aim of fielding an anti-tank gunship built around the Lockheed AH-56 Cheyenne. In the interim, the Army used the AH-1G HueyCobra to perform jungle warfare duties while the broader program contemplated a system capable of countering armored threats. The overarching objective of AAFSS was to provide Western Europe with airpower able to deter and defeat Warsaw Pact tanks advancing from the east.

Solidarity (Polish trade union) is a social movement and trade union that emerged in Poland in 1980 as a major force in challenging the communist regime. According to Lech Wałęsa, Pope John Paul II's 1979 visit to Poland played a significant role in the formation of Solidarity, helping to inspire and mobilize opposition within the country. The pope, being Polish, was personally relatable to Poles while simultaneously appearing beyond the regime's reach, a combination that reporters and observers have noted as influential in shaping public sentiment. In addition, many world leaders, including Wałęsa, have credited the pope's actions during his papacy as a principal contributor to the downfall of the Polish regime and to the broader decline of Communism in Europe.

During the 1970s, the government raised food prices while wages remained stagnant, sparking protests in 1976 and a subsequent crackdown. In response, dissident circles such as KOR, ROPCiO, and other groups formed underground networks to monitor government actions and coordinate opposition, with labor unions playing a significant role within these clandestine structures. The period also saw worsening economic conditions, including a 2 percent contraction in 1979—the first decline since World War II—and by 1980 foreign debt rising to about $18 billion. These pressures contributed to the growth of independent worker organizations, including Solidarity, which emerged from and operated within these underground networks.

Michael Finley, a Toronto-based lawyer, has highlighted an emerging legal trend in which international plaintiffs are increasingly able to sue Canadian parent companies for the wrongful conduct of their foreign subsidiaries. The development signals that the corporate veil is no longer an automatic barrier to liability in these cross-border disputes, indicating a broader shift in accountability for multinational corporations and the potential reach of Canadian entities in international litigation.

Typically, a parent or holding company holds strategic assets such as intellectual property or trade secrets, while an operating company conducts the business using those assets. In this arrangement, the assets are kept within the holding structure and are insulated from the operating company, creating a formal separation between ownership and day-to-day operations. This separation reduces the risk to the assets in the event of litigation, since claims tied to operating activities are generally directed at the operating entity rather than the asset-holding entity. The standard configuration thus involves a parent or holding company alongside one or more operating companies, forming a corporate framework designed to segregate asset ownership from operational risk.

The draw for the eighth round of the 2023–24 Belgian Cup was held on 2 November 2023, one day after the preceding round concluded. No seedings were applied in the draw, and Knokke enjoyed home-ground advantage as the only non-professional side remaining. Among the notable fixtures were Anderlecht vs Standard, a clash often referred to as a Clasico, Club Brugge facing Zulte Waregem in a tie marked by Ruud Vormer’s return to Brugge with his new club, and Knokke meeting Oud-Heverlee Leuven. The defending champions Antwerp were drawn at home against Charleroi, a club that had not yet won the competition.

The 2023–24 Belgian Cup, also known as the Croky Cup for sponsorship reasons, was the 69th edition of Belgium's annual knockout football competition. It began on 29 July 2023 and concluded with the final on 9 May 2024, with the victors earning qualification for the 2024–25 UEFA Europa League play-off round. Match times were listed in Central European Summer Time (UTC+2) until 29 October 2023 and again from 31 March 2024, with Central European Time (UTC+1) observed on winter days. Antwerp were the defending cup holders.

During its early years, the Züri-Metzgete was dominated by Swiss riders, with 34 of the first 41 editions won by Swiss competitors between 1914 and 1956. A notable foreign victor in that period was Gino Bartali. In the 1946 race, Bartali defeated his arch rival Fausto Coppi in a highly disputed contest, as the two Italians rode together at a breakneck pace, Bartali securing victory under controversial circumstances while Coppi was tightening his toe straps. This episode is commonly regarded as marking the start of the Bartali–Coppi rivalry. The 1946 edition also posted an average speed of 42.228 km/h (26.239 mph), a record speed that would stand for over fifty years. In 2004, Juan Antonio Flecha of Spain won the race, recording an average speed of 42.707 km/h (26.537 mph), which set a new record for the event.

The Züri-Metzgete is a prestigious one-day professional road race held in Switzerland, which currently both starts and finishes in the city of Zürich. The event’s finish line in Zürich replaces a former conclusion at the Oerlikon velodrome, a venue that was abandoned several years ago. The race covers about 241 kilometres and features more than 3,000 metres of elevation gain, structured around one 72.5-kilometre opening lap and four 42.1-kilometre circuits. Each of the shorter circuits contains four ascents of both the Pfannenstiel and Forch climbs, with the final Pfannenstiel ascent occurring roughly 15 kilometres from the Zürich finish and frequently serving as the decisive move in the race. Between 1993 and 1999, the event ran from Basel to Zürich and was known as the Grand Prix Suisse.

AllMusic was purchased in 2015 by BlinkX, a company that was later renamed RhythmOne. The site’s database infrastructure uses a hybrid approach that combines MySQL, a relational database, with MongoDB, a document-oriented database, to manage its catalog and metadata.

AllMusic, an online music reference site, originated when its founder Erlewine hired Vladimir Bogdanov, a database engineer, to design the All Music Guide framework. He then recruited his nephew, Stephen Thomas Erlewine, to develop editorial content, while Chris Woodstra joined the staff as an engineer in 1993 and was described as a devoted music enthusiast with encyclopedic knowledge. The project developed a taxonomy featuring roughly 1,400 subgenres, a central element of the site's utility. A 2016 article in Tedium by Ernie Smith later described AllMusic as one of the most ambitious early internet sites and as fundamental to understanding pop culture. Functionally, AllMusic tracks styles, genres, subgenres, and the tonal qualities of music, as well as the platforms on which it is sold, and ties this data together to describe broad categories of music from classical to niche areas such as sadcore.

Clark's Lookout State Park is a Montana state park located about one mile north of Dillon. The park covers eight acres (approximately 3.2 hectares) and encompasses a hill that overlooks the Beaverhead River, which William Clark climbed on August 13, 1805, during the Lewis and Clark Expedition. From this vantage point, Clark took compass readings and drafted a map of the Beaverhead Valley. The park offers facilities for picnicking and interpretive signage, and visitors can ascend the hill to stand at the historic site where Clark stood.

Ongoing work within ISO standards committees aims to extend STEP-NC to new technologies and to incorporate refinements identified through practical use. Process models for emerging technologies are typically produced by ISO TC184/SC1/WG7, the subcommittee charged with STEP-NC development. Currently, models for wire EDM and sinker EDM are under investigation, and research is also underway into contour-cutting applications for wood and stone.

In June 2006, Airbus organized a live demonstration of five-axis STEP-NC machining at the Laboratory of Mechanical Engineering at Université Paul Sabatier in Toulouse. The following year, 2007, additional demonstrations focusing on machining and metrology were conducted in Ibusuki, Japan, contributing to continued international demonstrations of STEP-NC technology.

China Circle is a coalition of Japanese companies investing in China, established when its members faced economic disadvantages and sought to pursue explicit economic objectives. The alliance aims to leverage China’s comparatively low operating costs to generate mutual benefits for investors and host economies. Japanese technology and electronics brands have prioritized China as a site for product development and technology transfer. The circle also signals opportunities in Hong Kong and Taiwan and expands as foreign firms deepen their presence in those markets. It is designed to protect members’ rights within its framework, and its proponents argue that Japanese firms’ strength in technological implementation helps attract participation from other regions through collaboration with the circle. Members support the union because of advantages for electronics companies. Japanese corporations operating in China are credited with elevating the region’s technological status, as technology firms facilitate interactions with local communities at multiple levels, fostering attitudes toward technology and enabling knowledge exchange with other countries.

The China Circle is viewed as a framework in which the United States maintains substantial global influence and favorable diplomatic relations with its member states, creating a climate conducive to the access and operation of American electronics firms within the circle. US–China Circle diplomacy enables American brands to operate with relatively few barriers, and trade between the China Circle and the United States—facilitated by these brands—expands access to the U.S. market for Circle members. American electronics firms pursue profit maximization and extend their affiliate networks across the Circle. The China Circle aims to benefit from the presence of American electronics firms, and the interaction is described as mutually advantageous. The Circle champions the economic benefits for all its members, with China gaining more given its regional authority. The engagement with American electronics companies is said to contribute to China’s technological advancement, while domestic Chinese electronics firms borrow heavily from U.S. brands. By contrast, the American electronics industry is regarded as more advanced than its Chinese counterpart, and the arrival of foreign electronics companies within the Circle is considered a resource for domestic Chinese firms.

Elementary algebra uses symbols to express mathematical relations. A coefficient is a numerical factor, or occasionally a letter used to denote a numerical constant, that multiplies a variable, with the multiplication typically implicit in the notation (for example, 3x or xy). A term refers to an individual addend or summand in an expression; it can consist of coefficients, variables, constants, and exponents, and terms are separated from one another by plus or minus signs. Letters serve to represent quantities as either variables, whose values can vary, or constants that remain fixed within a given context.

Elementary algebra is the branch of mathematics that employs symbols, such as variables, and a standardized set of algebraic notation to express and manipulate relationships among quantities. It rests on the general rules of arithmetic—addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division—and extends these operations to expressions and equations that involve unknowns. The scope of elementary algebra is primarily limited to real and complex numbers, and it does not address other algebraic structures. Consequently, it differs from abstract algebra, which explores broader algebraic systems and their properties; elementary algebra concentrates on symbol manipulation and number-based relationships rather than the general structural theories studied in higher branches of mathematics.

FIFA has faced significant governance and ethics challenges, including the suspension by the FIFA Ethics Committee of several officials, among them Sepp Blatter and Michel Platini. In early 2017, media reports suggested that Gianni Infantino sought to block the re-election of ethics committee chairs Cornel Borbély and Hans-Joachim Eckert at the May 2017 FIFA Congress. On 9 May 2017, the FIFA Council accepted Infantino's proposal and decided not to renew the mandates of Borbély and Eckert. As a consequence, eleven of the thirteen ethics committee members were removed, together with the two chairs.
