Separately, FIFA has faced allegations of corruption relating to the bidding process for the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

FIFA+ holds rights to competitions in the Oceania region, including the OFC Champions League and the OFC Women's Olympic Qualifying Tournament. It also has rights to New Zealand domestic competitions and to the New Zealand national teams.

Cachorro Grande released its first album in 2001, a self-titled collection that garnered regional acclaim for its early sound. The music video for the song Lunático received a nomination in the Best New Artist category at the 2003 MTV Video Music Brazil ceremony, signaling the band's rising prominence. In 2007, Cachorro Grande won the MTV Video Music Brazil award for Best Live Performance, highlighting recognition of their live presentations.

Cachorro Grande, a Brazilian rock band, experienced notable personnel changes. The original bassist Jerônimo "Bocudo" departed in 2005 and was replaced by Rodolfo Krieger. In 2018, guitarist Marcelo Gross was replaced by Gustavo X, but Gross rejoined the band for its farewell tour in 2019.

Ventilation in architecture involves exchanging indoor air with outdoor air, yet contaminated outdoor air can be drawn into buildings through intake flows, thereby contributing to indoor pollution. Outdoor contaminants include industrial effluents and volatile organic compounds associated with nearby construction activities. In urban European buildings lacking outdoor air filtration, exposure to pollutants originating from outside has been associated with a greater burden of disease, measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), than exposure to pollutants emitted indoors. These findings emphasize the importance of incorporating outdoor air filtration within ventilation systems to reduce the indoor pollutant burden and protect occupant health.

Smart ventilation systems in architecture employ sensors to monitor performance, including measurements of airflow, system pressure, and fan energy consumption. This continuous monitoring enables the detection of faults within the ventilation network, and identified faults can subsequently be repaired. In addition, ongoing monitoring informs maintenance scheduling by signaling when service is needed, such as filter replacement.

Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953. During his tenure he pursued rapid industrialization, the nationalization of private industry, and the collectivization of private plots that had been permitted under Lenin's New Economic Policy. As the dominant figure within the Politburo, he consolidated near-total authority by 1938, following the Great Purge, a campaign marked by political killings, repression, and widespread persecution. In World War II, Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941, and by December Soviet forces had halted the Axis advance just short of Moscow. Under Stalin's direction the Soviet Union launched a counter-offensive that ultimately defeated Germany in 1945. Stalin died in March 1953, triggering a power struggle in which Nikita Khrushchev prevailed over Georgy Malenkov.

Following Joseph Stalin's ascent and consolidation of power in the late 1920s, the General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party became synonymous with leadership of the Soviet Union. The office controlled both the Communist Party and, through party membership, the state apparatus, and the officeholder commonly held senior government positions as well. Because the post lacked formal succession rules, a would-be leader typically required the backing of key party and government bodies—such as the Politburo and Central Committee—to consolidate power. In March 1990, the Presidency of the Soviet Union was created, replacing the general secretary as the highest political office.

Situbondo Madurese describes the Madurese linguistic situation in Situbondo and Bondowoso regencies in East Java, Indonesia. The two regencies exhibit a broadly homogeneous Madurese speech community, though dialectal variation is evident within Situbondo. The prevailing variety across both regencies is Eastern Madurese. In Situbondo, the western area around Panarukan and Besuki up to the Probolinggo border uses a Western Madurese dialect, while the eastern portion from Situbondo Kota to the Banyuwangi border near Banyuputih employs the Eastern Madurese variant. This geographic pattern of variation aligns with proximity to neighboring districts, reflecting a west–east dialect distribution within the regency.

Situbondo Madurese refers to Madurese communities in East Java, particularly in Situbondo Regency, that originated from a broader migration during which forests were cleared to establish new settlements. The movement involved a substantial number of Madurese, contributing to widespread dispersal across Java, with a notable concentration along the northern coastal belt of East Java. In this region, Madurese communities established settlements in Gresik, Surabaya, Bangil, Probolinggo, Situbondo, Bondowoso, and Banyuwangi, while other Madurese populations settled along the southern coast in Jember, Lumajang, and Malang. Over time, they integrated with local societies and environments, adapting their livelihoods to the prevailing ecological conditions and continuing to persist to the present day.

Freddy Lim, together with several friends, founded the band ChthoniC in 1995. In 2000, ChthoniC received an invitation to perform at the Fuji Rock Festival in Japan, an experience that inspired Lim's later work in festival promotion. The group had previously performed at the Formoz Festival, an intercollegiate event organized by the Northern Taiwan Rock Association. To broaden the reach of such festivals, Lim established the Taiwan Rock Association as a dedicated organizing body. The Taiwan Rock Association festival continued through 2008 and was reestablished in 2013.

In Taiwan, early exposure to Western rock music developed primarily within the university community, where scholars and students fluent in foreign languages engaged with the genre. Xue Yue, also known as Simon Hsueh (1954–1990), is regarded as a pioneer of Taiwanese rock. He emerged during the campus folk movement that preceded the lifting of martial law in Taiwan and later contributed to the scene as a core figure. In addition to his guitar and songwriting work, he served as a part‑time drummer at the American Military Club. His debut album, The Stage of Rock and Roll, was released in 1984, and he would go on to collaborate with poets Chen Ko-hua and Hsia Yu, providing lyrics for his subsequent records. Xue Yue died in 1990, shortly after the release of his fifth album, marking a significant, if brief, formative period for Taiwanese rock.

James Densmore was an advocate for women's suffrage in Wisconsin. In his capacity as editor of the Oshkosh True Democrat, he guided the newspaper to publicly endorse the suffrage cause and defend the right of women to vote.

James Densmore (February 3, 1820 – September 16, 1889) was an American businessman and inventor. He is noted for his role as a business associate of Christopher Latham Sholes, a pivotal figure in the development of the first widely used typewriters. Sholes, along with Carlos Glidden and Samuel W. Soule, contributed to the creation of one of the earliest practical typewriters, with the work conducted at a machine shop in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

In Tear Along the Dotted Line, Zerocalcare appears as a version of himself, known to viewers by the nickname "Zero." In the first five episodes, he provides the voices for all other characters, with the exception of Armadillo. The work is characterized by frequent fourth-wall breaks, as Zerocalcare directly addresses the audience, and by moments in which he interrupts his own flashbacks to clarify or justify his mistakes.

Secco, voiced by Paolo Vivio in episode 6, is depicted as a close friend of Zero. He abandoned his formal schooling to pursue online poker as a career, and his deadpan, low-key demeanor sets him apart from Zero and Sarah. He often appears indifferent to the surrounding world, contributing to an impression of emotional detachment. A notable personal trait is his affection for ice cream, which he frequently suggests they obtain at every opportunity.

Since their creation, United States magistrate judges have operated within the federal judiciary, with authority expanded in 1979 to cover all misdemeanors recognized by the federal criminal code, and with their title officially changed to magistrate judges in 1990. Proponents contend that the system has functioned relatively well over the last thirty years and has helped balance the federal courts’ caseload. Critics, however, argue that expanding powers has drawn criticism and note that magistrate judges are not appointed by the President nor confirmed by the Senate. Selection for vacant positions is merit-based: statutes require public notice of vacancies and the formation of merit selection panels that include attorneys and at least two non-lawyers. The panel assesses candidates on scholarly achievement, experience, and knowledge of the federal court system, as well as personal attributes such as integrity, maturity, demeanor, temperament, and the ability to work with others. Applicants must undergo personal interviews and receive a recommendation for appointment. In terms of compensation, magistrate judges are paid somewhat less than district judges and do not receive the full benefits accorded to district judges. The increased involvement of magistrate judges has yielded cost savings for the federal courts.

United States Magistrate Judges are federal judicial officers assigned to assist district courts in handling pretrial matters, conducting hearings, and, with the parties' consent, adjudicating civil matters and issuing binding judgments on dispositive issues under statutory authority. Although they exercise authority within the district court's framework rather than as Article III judges, the consent of the parties to a magistrate judge proceeding reflects a constitutional option recognized by the Supreme Court. In Commodity Futures Trading Commission v. Schor, the Court held that litigants may voluntarily relinquish their right to an Article III forum, thereby submitting to a binding decision from an Article I tribunal. This principle underpins the practice of consenting to magistrate-judge adjudication in appropriate cases, whereby the resulting judgment is binding under the Article I framework and, as provided by statute, subject to the usual post-judgment review procedures.

Entertainment architecture refers to buildings whose design aims to amuse, astonish, or inspire, often pushing technical and aesthetic boundaries to deliver visually striking results that surpass conventional expectations. Practitioners who push these limits produce structures that are as much about spectacle as function, and many become notable landmarks due to their inventive form and public appeal. The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, designed by Frank Gehry, is a prominent example, having attracted widespread international attention and evolving into a major tourist destination as well as an important museum. Occasionally, buildings that appear usable are in fact follies—deliberately decorative constructions not intended for practical use.

Entertainment has continually evolved in response to social upheavals, including wars and revolutions, giving rise to new forms, genres, and modes of distribution. In China, the Cultural Revolution saw the Communist Party endorse a distinctive form of performance known as Revolutionary opera, aligning artistic expression with political aims. Major conflicts and global events have also shaped entertainment, with World War I reshaping audience preferences, production practices, and the role of media. Economic crises such as the Great Depression further transformed the sector, affecting what content was produced and how audiences accessed it. Similarly, the Russian Revolution brought substantial changes to the cultural landscape, influencing both the creation and regulation of entertainment.

Laos operates as a one-party state, with the Lao People's Revolutionary Party (LPRP) as the only political party that wields effective political power. The Lao Front for National Construction (LFNC) is a mass organization affiliated with the LPRP and is charged with engaging non-party citizens in government and cultural affairs.

Merengue music is characterized by brisk, energetic arrangements organized around a 24-beat rhythmic framework. The traditional ensemble, known as conjunto típico, typically comprises a diatonic accordion, tambora—a two-sided drum held on the lap—and a güira. The güira is a metal cylinder studded with small bumps and produces a rasping timbre akin to a maraca when brushed with a stiff implement; its patterns range from a steady downbeat brushing with occasional "and-a" accents to more complex, time-marking figures. A common rhythmic device is the caballito pattern, which consists of a quarter note followed by two eighth notes. Additionally, the double-headed drum contributes a layered texture by being struck with a stick on one side and the palm on the other, adding further syncopation to the ensemble.

Merengue, a Dominican popular music genre, achieved substantial radio traction by the 1980s, with its airplay surpassing that of salsa. The decade also marked a notable rise in all-female orchestras, among which Las Chicas del Can attained particular popularity. Pioneering artists such as Juan Luis Guerra, Toño Rosario, and Luis Díaz helped internationalize merengue by introducing it to audiences abroad. Guerra, who trained at the Berklee College of Music, collaborated with African guitarists, explored indigenous Caribbean sonorities, and investigated Dominican roots with típico accordionist Francisco Ulloa. Luis Díaz, an innovator dating from his work with Convite in the 1970s, fused merengue with rock, merengue típico, and bachata.

Shengavit Settlement, part of the Kura-Araxes (Shengavitian) cultural complex, represents a distinctive mountain-centered phenomenon in the South Caucasus that developed in parallel with Mesopotamian cultures rather than serving as their source. In discussions of regional interaction, Rothman described the Uruk Expansion trading network and suggested that raw materials and technologies from the South Caucasus may have reached Mesopotamia. A popular-press misrepresentation of a 2010 press conference in Yerevan claimed that Armenian culture was a source for Mesopotamian culture; however, this interpretation is not supported by scholarly consensus. The Kura-Araxes/Shengavitian cultures are thus regarded as a unique highland tradition, evolving alongside Mesopotamian cultures but not being the direct progenitors or sources of them.

Beginning in 2000, a major excavation program was conducted at the Shengavit Settlement under the direction of archaeologist Hakop Simonyan. To refine the stratigraphy, researchers established stratigraphic trenches along the edges of the preexisting trenches, which had been opened by Bayburdian and Sardarian.

In October 1946, delegates from 25 countries affiliated with the ISA and UNSCC gathered in London and agreed to establish an international standardization organization. This agreement led to the formation of the International Organization for Standardization, which began operating on 23 February 1947.

ISO maintains a council composed of twenty member bodies, with rotating representation. The council provides governance and strategic guidance for the organization, shaping policy and oversight of its activities. It is responsible for determining the annual budget of the central secretariat, allocating financial resources to support its operations.

Mathematics provides essential tools across the geosciences and related disciplines. In structural geology and climatology, probabilistic models are used to assess and predict the risk of natural catastrophes, supplying a rigorous framework for uncertainty and risk estimation. Likewise, meteorology, oceanography, and planetology depend heavily on mathematical methods, given their extensive reliance on models to describe and forecast complex phenomena, from atmospheric dynamics to ocean circulation and planetary processes.

Historically, mathematics in the Western world before the nineteenth century was largely driven by needs in technology and science, and a clear division between pure and applied mathematics did not yet exist. Arithmetic arose from counting, while geometry was motivated by tasks such as land surveying, construction, and astronomical observation. Isaac Newton developed the calculus of infinitesimals to explain planetary motion in accordance with his law of gravitation. Throughout this period, most mathematicians were active scientists and many scientists engaged in mathematical work, though the ancient Greek tradition stands out as an exception in treating mathematics as a pure, abstract pursuit. The problem of factoring integers, studied by Euclid around 300 BCE, found practical applications only with the advent of modern cryptography, notably RSA, which is now widely used to secure communications over computer networks.

In 2005, the JPEG 2000–based image browsing protocol JPIP was published as ISO/IEC 15444-9. JPIP enables the selective transmission of portions of potentially very large images by allowing a client to request specific regions, resolutions, or quality levels from an image server. Transmission occurs in response to the client’s requests, and this approach reduces the bandwidth required to view large image data sets.

JPEG 2000 employs a wavelet-based decomposition that yields a collection of sub-bands across multiple approximation levels. Each sub-band consists of real-valued coefficients that encode image information for a defined frequency range. The coefficients capture aspects of the image at a given scale and are associated with specific spatial regions of the image, providing simultaneous frequency and spatial localization. Collectively, these sub-bands across the approximation scales form a multiresolution representation that underpins the standard’s approach to efficient compression and scalable reconstruction.
Stadium Park/Astrodome station contains the system's sole closed platform; a second platform sits on the southbound side opposite the island platform, but it is not in use.

Stadium Park/Astrodome station is an island-platform METRORail light rail stop in Houston, Texas. It opened on January 1, 2004 and was originally named Reliant Park station. The station is operated by METRO (Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County, Texas). It is located at the intersection of Fannin Street and Holly Hall Street, adjacent to NRG Park. The station features photographic displays that recall the Astrodome's history, including the rodeo, the Houston Astros, and an Elvis concert.

Future Nostalgia’s cover artwork was photographed by Hugo Comte, who also directed the campaign’s creative concept and led the photography for the album. The album’s design was by Guillaume Sbalchiero. The cover image was captured on 13 November 2019. On 29 January 2020, Dua Lipa revealed the cover together with the announcement of the album’s release date. During the promotional shoots, Comte played a single song on repeat for each shot to establish the mood.

Future Nostalgia is designed to feel cohesive, presenting its tracks as parts of a single shared narrative rather than a disparate collection. Throughout the album, bass lines recur across several songs and are often complemented by string arrangements, reinforcing musical continuity. The production pursues an organic character, emphasizing live instrumentation to achieve a more natural sound. Critics have frequently described the record as buoyant and very happy in tone. Lyrically and thematically, the work centers on dancing, enjoying life, feeling free, and experiences of being in love.

Brad Paisley's music video for "Alcohol" was directed by Jim Shea and features a cameo by Little Jimmy Dickens, who wears a lampshade on his head in one scene. The clip was released in June 2005, and in late 2010 a new 3D live version directed by Scott Scovill was released, offering an updated rendition for contemporary audiences.

“Alcohol” is a mid-tempo track by Brad Paisley, arranged in 6/8 time and presented in the key of C major, though the original recording features a down-tuned arrangement. The lyrics personify alcohol, describing its influence on people as a central idea and using it to illustrate how it can affect behavior. It is shown to prompt activities such as dancing, while also noting potential outcomes ranging from making new friends to risking employment. The song’s overarching message suggests that time spent with alcohol can produce some of the best moments that listeners may not fully remember, highlighting the paradox at the heart of the track.
In October 2018, Portnow attended the White House for the signing of the Music Modernization Act, having long been a vocal advocate for the bill's passage and enactment into law.

Neil Portnow served on the executive board of City of Hope's Music & Entertainment Industry group in 2018, and previously led the group's chapter as president from 2000 to 2002, directing fundraising efforts for City of Hope. In October 2003, he was honored with the Spirit of Life Award, City of Hope's top philanthropic distinction. The accompanying Spirit of Life Award gala that year raised more than $2.3 million to support cancer research and treatment initiatives.

Humid subtropical climates, as categorized by the Köppen system, are typically found along the eastern coasts of continents and on their eastern flanks, occupying latitudinal bands roughly in the upper twenties to around thirty degrees. These climates are driven by a persistent warm and moist air flow originating in tropical regions, which fosters hot, humid summers. Accordingly, summer is often the wettest season in these areas, a pattern that contrasts with Mediterranean climates, where winter tends to bring the majority of annual precipitation.

Within the Köppen climate classification, the designation Cfb denotes a temperate climate category typically described as a temperate oceanic climate, and in some contexts may be associated with subtropical highland conditions. The temperature criteria can be stated in variant forms: the coldest month averages above 0°C, or in certain classifications above −3°C; furthermore, no month has an average warmer than 22°C, and at least four months exceed 10°C. Precipitation shows little seasonal contrast, with rainfall distributed relatively evenly throughout the year.

"I'm Gonna Hire a Wino to Decorate Our Home" achieved a peak of number three on the magazine's Top Country Tracks chart, indicating strong performance within the country genre. Unexpectedly, the song crossed over into the Canadian mainstream, where it reached number 20 on RPM's Top Singles chart, reflecting its broader pop appeal in the country.

The song tells the story of a wife who is fed up with her husband's frequent nights out and the rapid spending of their money. In a bid to curb his behavior, she plans to redecorate their home into a bar-like setting and will take on the roles of bartender and server to keep him at home. She hopes his friends will come along to spend their earnings there as well, transforming the house into a social venue. The following morning, the proceeds are deposited into the couple's bank account.

In 1987, Nicaragua's new constitution established the Charter of Autonomy for the former Zelaya Department, which covered the eastern half of the country. The department was subsequently divided into two autonomous regions, the North Caribbean Coast Autonomous Region and the South Caribbean Coast Autonomous Region. The Charter of Autonomy drew largely on the Spanish model of regional autonomy. Governance within these regions is provided by a Governor and a Regional Council.
Nicaragua is a unitary republic, and for administrative purposes it is subdivided into fifteen departments (departamentos) and two autonomous regions (regiones autónomas).

Frank Rogers is a record producer working in country music who has produced for a range of artists since 1999, including Trace Adkins, Brad Paisley, Josh Turner, Darius Rucker, Phil Vassar, and Darryl Worley. He has earned 13 nominations from the Country Music Association, including a win for Album of the Year for Brad Paisley's Time Well Wasted in 2006. He has also received five ACM Awards. On Billboard's Hot Country Producers chart, Rogers attained the No. 1 position for five consecutive years, from 2006 to 2010. Additionally, Music Row honored him as Producer of the Year in 2005, 2007, 2008, and 2009.

Frank Rogers is a record producer and songwriter whose writing credits appear on a number of chart-topping songs. Notable contributions include Brad Paisley’s “I’m Gonna Miss Her (The Fishin’ Song)” and “Who Needs Pictures” as well as “Me Neither,” Scotty McCreery’s “Five More Minutes” and “This Is It” (the latter co-written with Aaron Eshuis), Granger Smith’s “Backroad Song,” Darius Rucker’s “Alright,” “This,” and “History in the Making,” Trace Adkins’ “Don’t Lie” and “Swing,” Steve Holy’s “Don’t Make Me Beg,” Kenny Rogers’s “He Will, She Knows,” and the collaboration on Ed Sheeran’s “Blow” with Chris Stapleton and Bruno Mars.

South Korea's indigenous space-launch vehicle program faced ongoing political pressure from the United States, centered on concerns that it could be linked to clandestine ballistic missile activities and might violate restrictions on rocket technology. Seoul maintained that its research and development did not breach the US-Korea guidelines governing rocket technology. To augment restricted domestic capabilities, South Korea sought foreign assistance, notably from Russia, under MTCR commitments. The two unsuccessful KSLV-I launches employed a design that combined a first stage derived from Russia's Universal Rocket Module in the Angara family with a solid-fueled second stage produced domestically.

During the 19th century, the Joseon dynasty faced economic difficulties and popular uprisings, including the Donghak Peasant Revolution. At the same time, royal in-law families tightened their grip on the government, leading to extensive corruption and a weakening of state institutions. The long-standing isolationist policy, often described as the hermit kingdom, proved unable to withstand external pressure as encroachments by Japan, Russia, and the United States intensified. The Joseon–United States Treaty of 1882 stands as a clear example of foreign encroachment, forcing Joseon to open its borders and illustrating the extent to which external powers influenced its sovereignty.

The Football Association has updated its logo several times over its history. To mark its 150th anniversary, it introduced a commemorative logo for the 2013–2014 season. The emblem preserves the shield shape drawn from the coat of arms, but the three lions, rosettes, and border are rendered in gold on a white background. The upper title strip reads “The FA” in white on a gold field, while a lower scroll bears the inscription “150 years” in white on gold, positioned between the years 1863 and 2013.

The Football Association oversaw reforms regarding women's football beginning in 1969 when the formal exclusion of women from the sport was reversed. Prompted by England's 1966 World Cup victory, interest in women's football grew and led to the founding of the Women's Football Association (WFA). Two years later, and under a UEFA directive, the men’s FA was compelled to remove restrictions on playing rights for women's teams. The WFA subsequently gained affiliate status with the FA as a County Association in 1983, signaling formal integration into the English football governance framework. In 1993, the FA established the Women's Football Committee to oversee the administration and development of women's football in England. The body now known as the Women's Football Conference has representation on the FA Council equivalent to that of a County Football Association, reinforcing its role in the governance of the sport at the national level.

Loophole originally referred to an arrowslit, a narrow vertical opening designed for firing. In the United States, loopholes were a common feature in forts constructed during the 19th century, and these openings were typically located in the sally port. They served as a last-ditch defense, enabling defenders to deliver small arms fire while remaining protected. The design allowed guards to close off both inner and outer doors, effectively trapping attacking soldiers inside the entrance area. Through the slits, soldiers could engage foes without exposing themselves to direct return fire.

Loopholes are identified and exploited strategically by individuals or groups seeking to circumvent rules or gain advantages. They occur across a wide range of domains, including electoral processes, political activities, taxation, the criminal justice system, and security-related vulnerabilities, where gaps or ambiguities in established frameworks can be leveraged to achieve particular outcomes.

The Zhi Xian Party, known in English as the Chinese Constitutionalist Party, was a political party operating without official registration in the People's Republic of China. It was founded on November 6, 2013, by citizen activist Wang Zheng. The group supported the continued leadership of the Chinese Communist Party while advocating a return to a Maoist governance model and urging remedies to what it viewed as constitutional violations by the ruling party. Bo Xilai was elected the party’s Chairman for Life, with adherents arguing that his trial had been unjust. The party was banned in December 2013.

Following 1886, alternating current (AC) power systems were rapidly developed and adopted. In March 1886, William Stanley of Westinghouse designed a system drawing on the transformer concept developed by Gaulard and Gibbs. A demonstration in Great Barrington used a Siemens generator supplying 500 volts, which was increased to 3,000 volts for distribution and then stepped down to 500 volts by six Westinghouse transformers; the setup illuminated thirty 100-volt incandescent lamps in twenty shops along the town’s main street. Later that year, in the autumn, engineers from Ganz installed a ZBD transformer-based AC power system with AC generators in Rome.

In 1876, Pavel Yablochkov introduced a lighting system that used induction coils arranged along a high-voltage alternating-current line, transferring power from primary windings to secondary windings connected to arc lamps he had designed, with multiple lamps incorporated to prevent complete circuit failure. The illumination relied on his proprietary arc lamp design. In 1878, the Ganz factory at Budapest began producing electric lighting equipment. By 1883, Ganz had installed more than fifty alternating-current lighting systems in Austria-Hungary. Ganz’s AC installations employed both arc and incandescent lamps, along with generators and ancillary equipment.

Karin Immergut spent five years as a deputy district attorney in Portland, Oregon, where she primarily prosecuted white-collar crimes. In 1998, while serving as a deputy D.A., she joined Kenneth Starr's independent counsel team conducting the investigation into President Bill Clinton, and she personally questioned Monica Lewinsky during an August 6, 1998 deposition. In 2001, Immergut joined the United States Attorney's Office in Portland as an Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Oregon, where she served two years prosecuting white-collar crimes and contributing to Project Safe Neighborhoods, a national gun-violence reduction initiative.

Karin Johanna Immergut (born 1960) is an American lawyer who has served as a United States district judge for the District of Oregon since 2019. Since 2024, she has concurrently served as a judge on the United States Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court.

A common front refers to a political alliance formed among diverse groups, forces, or interests in order to advance a shared objective or to oppose a common adversary. The arrangement is frequently regarded as equivalent to an alliance or coalition, though the term emphasizes its typically temporary character. Within such a front, individual participants retain their own autonomy and do not perceive themselves as subordinate to the partnership, allowing them to cooperate for a specific goal while preserving separate identities.

Common front, or frontism, denotes the political strategy of uniting diverse actors against a shared enemy. Throughout modern history, Marxist–Leninist parties have formed coalitions with non-communist forces during revolutionary movements to pursue common objectives. In left-wing political practice, this strategy has crystallized into two principal forms: the popular front and the united front.

Two prosecution attempts in West Germany, launched in 1978 and 1983, concerning the bombing of the Wieluń hospital, were dismissed by West German judges, who ruled that the pilots could not discern the hospital's civilian nature due to the morning fog surrounding the attack.

The bombing of Wieluń refers to the aerial attacks on the town of Wieluń, located near the German border, which at the time was undefended, with no anti-aircraft defenses and no military garrison. Despite the lack of military targets, airstrikes continued, and German intelligence claimed that a Polish cavalry brigade was stationed in the town. The Luftwaffe reportedly bombed a hospital that had been clearly marked, and fleeing civilians were strafed. In the broader area, nearby towns Działoszyn, Radomsko, and Sulejów were also bombed with no identified military objectives.

Alcohol produced by home distilleries is common worldwide but can contravene local laws. In the United States, illicit distillate is commonly called moonshine. In Ireland, illegal distillate is referred to as poitín. Poitín was made illegal in 1661 and has been legal for export from Ireland since 1997. The term moonshine is often misused; it can refer to any illicitly distilled alcohol, not limited to corn-based high-proof liquor.

A still is a device that distills liquid mixtures by applying heat to favor selective boiling, followed by cooling to condense the resulting vapors. It operates on the same fundamental principle as a basic distillation apparatus, but on a substantially larger scale for industrial use. Historically and in contemporary practice, stills have been employed to manufacture fragrances and medicinal preparations, and they are used in pharmaceutical settings to produce water for injection (WFI). In general, stills serve to separate and purify distinct chemical components, and they are also employed to produce distilled alcoholic beverages containing ethanol.

Armenia did not participate in the qualifying competition for the 2019 UEFA European Under-19 Championship. A total of 54 UEFA member national teams entered the qualifying rounds. Eligibility requirements restricted players to those born on or after 1 January 2000. In line with recent changes to match rules, the season introduced an expanded substitution policy permitting up to five replacements per team per match.

On 6 December 2017, the draw determining the qualifying round for the 2019 UEFA European Under-19 Championship took place at the UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland, with proceedings starting at 10:00 CET (UTC+1).

Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A had a population of 18,612 according to the 2021 Census. There were 9,201 total dwellings, of which 7,682 were occupied. The population represented a 15.4% increase from 2016, when it was 16,133. The area encompasses 815.21 square kilometres (314.75 square miles). The population density was 22.8 people per square kilometre (59.1 per square mile) in 2011.
Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A is represented on the regional district board by a single director, who is elected to serve a four-year term. The current director is Jen McCutcheon.

The Liwan District Government proposed renaming Line 22's Fangcun Station to Fangcun Baietan Station. However, Article 7 of the Guangzhou Metro Naming Rules (issued in March 2019) requires transfer stations that connect two or more lines to use the same name across those lines, with the name first used prevailing in such cases. Consequently, the proposed renaming was not adopted, and Fangcun Station retained its original designation in line with the rule.

Fangcun station comprises two concourse sections on the first underground level, dedicated to Line 1 and Line 11 respectively. The east side of the Line 1 concourse operates as a fare-paid area, while the central area of the Line 11 concourse also functions as a fare-paid zone. The Line 11 fare-paid area extends to interface with the Line 1 concourse to facilitate transfers between the two lines. A staircase and a ramp are provided to accommodate the height difference between the two concourses.

On May 12, 2005, an unauthorized aircraft approached the White House, prompting evacuation of the presidential complex and a tightening of air security in the capital. In response, two F-16 fighter jets and a Black Hawk helicopter intercepted the aircraft and forced it to land at a nearby small airport. The pilot was later identified as a student pilot, and authorities concluded that the breach was accidental and occurred without the pilot’s knowledge.

The White House is the official residence and principal workplace of the President of the United States, situated at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Washington, D.C. Since 1800, when the capital relocated from Philadelphia, it has housed the residence of every U.S. president. The term is also used as a metonym for the Executive Office of the President.

Margaret Brown is an American filmmaker who has worked in both cinematography and directing. In 1999 she served as cinematographer on the project 99 Threadwaxing, and she subsequently directed Ice Fishing in 2000. Her feature-length debut, Be Here To Love Me: A Film About Townes Van Zandt (2004), documents the tumultuous life of the American singer-songwriter Townes Van Zandt. The film has been critically recognized, with Time Out magazine ranking Be Here To Love Me seventh on its list of the 50 Greatest Music Films Ever.

Margaret Brown directed the feature documentary The Great Invisible, released in 2014. The film received the SXSW Grand Jury Prize for Documentary at the South by Southwest festival and later earned an Emmy nomination for Exceptional Merit in Documentary Filmmaking. It was broadcast on PBS's Independent Lens in April 2015. The Great Invisible examines the 2010 BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico and the broader aftermath of the Deepwater Horizon disaster.

During Operation Tempest, Polish forces carried out a series of rapid advances in late July 1944. From July 21 to 22, the Volhynian 27th Division seized Kock, Lubartów, and Firlej. In the western portion of the voivodeship, the 8th and 15th Infantry Regiments liberated Kurów, Urzędów, Nałęczów, Garbów, Wąwolnica, Sobolew, Ryki, and Końskowola. By July 26, Polish units had begun cooperating with Soviet forces engaged in battles around Puławy. The operations also included the destruction of several German rail transports, disrupting enemy logistics. Additionally, Polish soldiers saved Końskowola from German plans to set the town on fire, preserving it from destruction.

Operation Tempest was a Polish resistance operation during World War II that sought to leverage the approaching Soviet advance to secure Polish sovereignty in liberated areas. The German suppression of the Warsaw Uprising without Soviet aid signaled the end of the operation. Militarily, the campaign achieved certain tactical objectives, but politically it amounted to a defeat. The Red Army, with the NKVD following Polish units, demonstrated Soviet priorities and revealed the limits of Polish autonomy within the broader wartime context. Approximately half of the Polish soldiers who took part were arrested, with the detainees forcibly conscripted into Berling's Army, deported deep into the Soviet Union, or killed.

As the Soviet Red Army drew closer in the spring of 1945, the SS leadership ordered the evacuation of Ravensbrück to erase evidence of the camp’s crimes. By the end of March, all physically capable women were compelled to join a northbound column toward northern Mecklenburg, resulting in more than 24,500 prisoners subjected to a lethal march. After the evacuation, 2,500 ethnic German inmates who remained were released, and shortly thereafter 500 women were handed over to Swedish and Danish Red Cross authorities. On 30 April 1945, the Red Army liberated Ravensbrück, finding fewer than 3,500 malnourished and ailing prisoners still alive. The survivors of the death march were liberated within hours by a Soviet scout unit.
Johann Schwarzhuber, an assistant to commandant Fritz Suhren, succeeded Edmund Bräuning in January 1945 at Ravensbrück. During his tenure, he introduced the gas chamber at the Ravensbrück camp.

In March 1980, the African-American studies field encompassed the Second Congress on Black Culture in the Americas, an international gathering hosted by the Afro-Panamanian Studies Center and conducted in collaboration with the Panamanian government.

At the University of California, Berkeley, students were active participants in the Civil Rights Movement and had become more activist by 1964. On October 1, 1964, Jack Weinberg sat at a CORE table distributing literature encouraging student protest against institutional racism. When police asked for his student ID, Weinberg refused and was arrested. About 3,000 students surrounded the police car, using it as a podium to speak about the right to political protest on campus. This impromptu demonstration was the first of many protests, and contributed to the institutionalization of Black studies.

North Korea were barred from taking part in the qualification competition for the 2007 AFC Asian Cup after authorities determined they had engaged in improper conduct during the 2004 qualifying round.

During the qualification phase for the 2007 AFC Asian Cup, Lebanon and Kuwait played a match on 22 February 2006. The result was subsequently declared null and void, and it did not count toward the group rankings in the 2007 AFC Asian Cup qualification.

In the 2022 and 2023 election cycles, statewide referendums on cannabis legalization were conducted in several states. Maryland, Missouri, and Ohio approved the legalization of recreational cannabis, whereas Arkansas, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Oklahoma voted against proposed measures to legalize recreational cannabis.

During the Biden administration, a high-profile case connected to cannabis policy was the Viktor Bout–Brittney Griner prisoner exchange, which occurred on December 8, 2022. The exchange involved Brittney Griner, an American WNBA athlete who had been convicted of cannabis possession on Russian soil.

Benj Pasek is an American songwriter and composer who collaborates with Justin Paul as the duo Pasek and Paul. Their musical premiered in the West End at the Noël Coward Theatre in London on 19 November 2019, following previews in October of that year. At the 2020 Laurence Olivier Awards, the production received seven nominations and went on to win three prizes: Best New Musical, Best Actor in a Musical for Sam Tutty, and Best Original Score or New Orchestrations for Pasek and Paul.

Benj Pasek, together with his longtime writing partner Justin Paul, has written original music for several television programs. In 2007 and 2008, the duo composed songs for Disney Channel's Johnny and the Sprites. Music from the series was featured in six episodes and was used for a single storyline in the season's premiere.

Duruflé's Requiem exists in a full‑orchestral edition that significantly enlarges the scoring beyond the work’s more intimate realizations. The woodwind section comprises three flutes (the 2nd and 3rd players doubling piccolo) and two oboes, with the 2nd oboe doubling on the English horn in certain passages, in addition to a distinct English horn; two clarinets and a bass clarinet are included, complemented by two bassoons. Brass is allocated to four French horns, three trumpets, three trombones, and a tuba. The percussion lineup features timpani, cymbals, bass drum, and tam-tam, while the keyboard department includes celesta, harp, and organ. The strings cover the standard ensembles of violins, violas, cellos, and double basses.

Requiem, the composition by Maurice Duruflé, was published in 1948 by the French publishing house Durand. It was first issued in a version for SATB choir and organ. Although Duruflé was commissioned to receive 10,000 francs, he ultimately received 30,000 francs, a sum attributed to the work’s complexity and to prevailing inflation at the time.

GB is an abbreviation used in LGBTQ terminology that stands for gay and bisexual. It is most commonly applied to describe men who are attracted to men. The term appears in discussions of male sexual orientation and is also used in contexts where gender is not explicitly specified.

In discussions of LGBTQ terminology, MLM and WLW are acronyms used to describe patterns of romantic and sexual attraction. MLM stands for men loving men, while WLW stands for women loving women. These terms can include non-binary people who experience attraction to men or to women, reflecting a broader understanding of sexuality beyond traditional gender binaries. They relate to a range of orientations, including gay, bisexual, and pansexual identities, among others.

Liber Usualis is a liturgical compendium of Gregorian chants widely used in the Catholic tradition. It was compiled by the monks of the Abbey of Solesmes in France and first published in 1898. The volume consolidates ordinary and proper chants from the Kyriale and Graduale for Sundays and major holy days, and it also incorporates the Vespers chants from the Antiphonale. Furthermore, it includes Matins chants for Christmas, Holy Week, and the Office of the Dead drawn from the Nocturnale. Notable omissions include the chants assigned to the weekdays of Lent and Ember Days. The work’s Latin designation refers to a Book for Use at Masses and Offices of Sundays and Feasts with Gregorian chants, and it is commonly known in English as Book for Use at Masses and Offices of Sundays and Feasts with their Gregorian Chants.

The Liber Usualis, a comprehensive compilation of Gregorian chant used in the Latin liturgy, was first edited in 1896 under the direction of Solesmes Abbot Dom André Mocquereau (1849–1930). Its prominence declined after the 1970 liturgical reforms, which replaced the Tridentine Mass with the Mass of Paul VI and the Divine Office with the Liturgy of the Hours. In response to Vatican II’s mandate that Gregorian chant be accorded a principal role in liturgy (Sacrosanctum Concilium, 116), the 1974 Graduale Romanum and the 1990 Gregorian Missal were issued. The revision aligned the chant practice with the new liturgical calendar, discontinuing much of the traditional repertory, and the spread of the vernacular languages limited the widespread use of Latin chant. The 1964 Liber Usualis continues to be used locally where permission exists for celebrations according to the vetus ordo.
On November 3, 2014, Rovi Corporation acquired Fanhattan, the company operating the Fan TV service, along with the owners of The Movie Database, for a cash consideration of $12.0 million.

In December 2019, TiVo Corporation announced its intention to merge with Xperi, with the surviving entity to operate under the Xperi name. The deal was valued at approximately $3 billion, and TiVo had previously considered separating its hardware operations from its licensing activities. The merger was completed on June 1, 2020.

Six Flags AstroWorld, the Houston, Texas amusement park, navigated a succession of parent‑company restructurings beginning in the early 1980s. Bally Manufacturing acquired Six Flags in 1982, followed by Wesray Corporation's purchase in 1987, then Time Warner's acquisition of a minority stake in 1990 and eventual full ownership by September 1993. During its first two decades, AstroWorld welcomed more than 30 million visitors, and it thrived even as Houston experienced the emergence of competing projects such as Busch Gardens, Hanna-Barbera Land, and SeaArama Marineworld that ultimately did not endure. Attendance rose in those early years, and in the early 1990s the Six Flags chain gained access to DC Comics characters through Time Warner, enhancing the park's offerings; Batman: The Escape was installed for the 1993 season. In February 1998 Premier Parks, led by CEO Kieran Burke, acquired Six Flags Entertainment Corporation. Premier's expansion into theme parks traces back to 1984, when the company (then Tierco) hired Gary Story to rehabilitate Frontier City in Oklahoma City, a turnaround that launched its program of park acquisitions.

Six Flags AstroWorld is now encompassed within a 102-acre parcel owned by the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo (HLSR), bounded by West Bellfort Drive, Fannin Street, Kirby Drive, and the I-610 loop. Within this tract, the original AstroWorld site occupied 57 acres. The development status is mixed, with portions of the land developed and other parts remaining undeveloped. HLSR uses some of the property for overflow parking and maintains a long pedestrian viaduct that carries visitors across the site; the viaduct is the last remnant of the former amusement park. The acreage includes a large grassy field and has been stabilized and partially paved with asphalt, enabling its use as a parking area.

Keith Wilson is a mayor who has personally funded multiple trips to cities and countries to discuss homelessness with experts. He served as a delegate to the 2024 Democratic National Convention and is a member of the Democratic National Committee's Platform Committee.

Keith Wilson studied at Portland Community College and Oregon State University before relocating to New York City to work in NBC's sales department. He experienced a period of homelessness, living at LaGuardia Airport, before returning to Portland in 1990 to assist his father in running the family business. In 1998, he merged his father's two companies into Titan Freight Systems. He later founded Shelter Portland, a nonprofit organization dedicated to ending homelessness.

The Hutter Prize was announced on August 6, 2006, with an initial dataset of enwik8, a 100 MB text file, and an inaugural prize fund of €50,000. On February 21, 2020, the dataset was expanded to enwik9, a 1 GB corpus, and the prize pool was increased to €500,000, representing a tenfold rise in both dataset size and funding.

The Hutter Prize, launched in 2006, is a competition that rewards advances in lossless text compression on a fixed dataset. Prizes amount to 5,000 euros for each percentage point improvement in the compressed size of enwik9, a file used in the Large Text Compression Benchmark (LTCB). The total endowment for the prize stands at 500,000 euros. Enwik9 is the larger of the two LTCB data files and consists of the first 109 bytes of a specific version of English Wikipedia. The contest is organized by Hutter, Matt Mahoney, and Jim Bowery.

Makrem Ben Romdhane (Arabic: مكرم بن رمضان; also spelled Makram or Macram; born 27 March 1989) is a Tunisian professional basketball player who plays for Benfica and the Tunisia national team. A versatile frontcourt performer, he can operate at small forward, power forward, or center.

Makrem Ben Romdhane is a Tunisian professional basketball player who competed for US Monastir in the BAL's inaugural 2021 season. He contributed to Monastir’s advancement to the Finals of the tournament, playing a key role in their deep run in the initial BAL campaign. At the end of the season, he was awarded the BAL Sportsmanship Award and was named to the All-BAL First Team, recognizing his conduct and on-court performance throughout the competition.

Axalta Coating Systems is a major manufacturer of paints and coatings whose product portfolio includes several longstanding brands, notably Standox and Spies Hecker, among its oldest lines. The company broadened its 1990s offerings with Cromax, a water-based coating system; Nap-Gard, a powder coating developed for oil and gas pipeline applications; and Voltatex, a coating designed for electrical insulation. In addition to these, Axalta markets a wide range of other products, including Abcite, Alesta, AquaEC, Audurra, Centari, Challenger, Harmonized Coating Technologies, Imron, and Nason.

Axalta sponsors the Judnick Motorsport/Polaris Racing snocross team, featuring riders Ross Martin and James Johnstad. The team competes in the AMSOIL Championship Snocross series, with the sponsorship extending through the 2017 season.

Umbro is a sportswear brand that specializes in equipment for football and rugby union. Its product lines encompass team kits, which include jerseys, shorts and socks, as well as football boots. Beyond these core items, the company also manufactures a range of other clothing, such as t-shirts and jackets.
In October 2007, JJB Sports acquired a 10.1% stake in Umbro, a move designed to safeguard its position in the market for England football shirts.

AeroVironment developed SkyTote, a vertical take-off and landing fixed-wing hybrid unmanned aerial vehicle. SkyTote provides VTOL takeoff capability and is associated with decreased energy consumption, reflecting an improvement in energy efficiency.

AeroVironment holds a minority stake in HAPSMobile, a SoftBank subsidiary that plans to operate high-altitude platform station networks. HAPSMobile is developing the Hawk30, a solar-powered unmanned aircraft intended for stratospheric telecommunications. The company maintains a strategic relationship with Loon LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., the parent company of Google.

Prediction Units (PUs) in the Audio Video Standard define all prediction modes available to Coding Units (CUs) and serve as the fundamental unit for both intra-frame and inter-frame prediction. A PU’s size is constrained by the size of the CU to which it belongs and cannot exceed it. In AVS1, intra-frame prediction is enhanced by introducing non-square block partitions in addition to the conventional square partitions. For inter-frame prediction, the framework adopts a symmetric partitioning scheme but adds four asymmetric partition modes, broadening the range of allowable partition configurations.

AVS2 uses an eight-tap interpolation filter for motion compensation, engineered within a discrete cosine transform framework. The filter simplifies the motion-compensation process by requiring only a single filtering operation, reducing computational complexity. It also enables sub-pixel motion-vector precision that surpasses a quarter-pixel accuracy.

Within the Iranian rock scene, since 2019 Kaveh Yaghmaei has been active in cultural and musical initiatives supporting freedom and human rights in Iran. Through his compositions, collaborations, and live performances both in Iran and internationally, he has raised awareness about the struggles of women and artists under oppressive regimes. His work frequently addresses themes of exile, censorship, and resistance, reflecting his personal experiences and his commitment to artistic freedom.

Iranian rock developed in large part around Couchini Restaurant, a venue established in the early 1960s by Vida Ghahremani that became a crucial incubator for the Iranian rock scene and a launching pad for artists such as Farhad Mehrad and the Black Cats. At Couchini, Mehrad played piano and served as the Black Cats’ lead singer; his performances included renditions of Ray Charles songs, earning him the nickname "Ray Charles of Iran" from American listeners in the area. Ebi gave his first public performance there. After the Black Cats achieved fame, they stopped performing at the venue, and successor groups such as Scorpio began to appear. Overall, Couchini Restaurant is regarded as the most important site for cultivating Iranian rock music.

Microfiltration is a membrane-based separation process that uses relatively large pores. In contrast, nanofiltration membranes provide pores in the range of 0.001–0.01 μm and are capable of separating multivalent ions, synthetic dyes, sugars, and certain salts while permitting smaller molecules to pass. The transition from microfiltration to nanofiltration, with decreasing pore size, is associated with a higher requirement for osmotic pressure to sustain filtration.

Microfiltration (MF) membranes are used in dairy processing to treat milk and whey, enabling the selective rejection of bacteria and spores and thereby enhancing product safety. As a pre-treatment step, MF can precede pasteurisation and contribute to extended shelf-life. The most notable application of MF is the separation of casein from whey (serum) proteins, producing two streams: a casein-rich concentrate for cheese production and a whey-derived serum protein stream for further processing. The whey stream is then subjected to ultrafiltration to yield whey protein concentrate (WPC), and subsequent fat removal by additional filtration raises the protein content to support the production of WPC products and whey protein isolate (WPI) powders.

Yuntai Garden station, a part of Line 11, began substantive construction on 5 March 2017, with the diaphragm wall work completed on 12 November 2018 and the main structure topped out on 28 November 2019, making it the first Line 11 station to reach that milestone. The project advanced with the completion of the three rights transfer on 3 July 2024, and the station subsequently opened for service together with Line 11 on 28 December 2024.

Yuntai Garden Station is an underground Guangzhou Metro station on Line 11. It commenced operations on 28 December 2024 and is located in Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, near the intersection of Guangyuan Road Middle and Luhu Road. The station is named in Simplified Chinese as 云台花园站 and in Traditional Chinese as 雲台花園站, with the pinyin transcription Yúntáihuāyuán Zhàn and the Cantonese Yale pronunciation Wàntòifāyùn Jaahm.

PL-5 was designed and developed at the Luoyang Electro-Optics Technology Development Centre (EOTDC), also known as Institute 612. The design team consisted of Chen Jiali, Dong Chunfeng, Hu Rongchao, Huang Bin, Zhang Ming, and Zheng Zhiwei. Production was reportedly carried out at the Hanzhong Nanfeng Machine Factory (Hanzhong Air-to-Air Missile Factory), a facility that is part of the China Aviation Industry Corporation I (AVIC I).

The PL-5 is a Chinese short-range air-to-air missile. The J-10 and J-11 aircraft primarily deploy the PL-8, while the J-20 and J-35 stealth fighters are equipped with the PL-10. Relative to the PL-5, both the PL-8 and PL-10 represent more advanced short-range air-to-air missiles. For lighter or older platforms such as the F-7 and JH-7, however, the greater weight and larger dimensions of the PL-8 and PL-10 constrain their use, making the PL-5, together with the PL-7 and PL-9, the preferred air-to-air missiles for those aircraft at this stage.

Lossless audio formats used in portable media players compress digital audio data without sacrificing quality, ensuring that the decoded output preserves all information from the original recording. This approach provides bit-for-bit fidelity and full dynamic range, allowing listeners to experience the same sound as the source material. Notable examples include Apple Lossless (ALAC) and FLAC, formats that have gained broad support across hardware players and software, enabling high-fidelity playback on portable devices.

Portable media players are compact electronic devices capable of reading and playing Compact Discs (CDs). They can play standard audio CDs, and many models are also able to read homemade data CDs that contain MP3 files or other types of digital audio formats.

An executive chair is a distinct senior corporate office separate from the chief executive officer, yet one that retains influence over a company's operations. Notable examples include Larry Ellison at Oracle, Douglas Flint at HSBC, and Steve Case at AOL Time Warner. In HSBC, the group chair occupies the topmost position, outranking the CEO, chairs the board, and represents the company to government officials. Historically, before 2006 the chair often carried duties akin to those of a chief executive, with the CEO acting as deputy. After the 2006 reorganization that created the group management board, the management cadre was tasked with running the business, while the chair's remit focused on overseeing controls such as compliance and audit and guiding the overall direction of the enterprise.

Chairman is a title used for the person who presides over a meeting, board, or committee. In some organizations, the role is effectively equivalent to that of a president, or may be designated by another title. In other organizations, the chair and the president are distinct offices, with the board electing or appointing a separate president to lead. The term can be employed in a gender-neutral way, without implying the holder’s gender. To chair a meeting or conference means to preside over and guide the proceedings of the event.

Among the wealthier Americo-Liberians, architectural tastes were guided by the antebellum architecture of the American South, adopting neoclassical and neo-Greco-Roman elements drawn from plantation great houses for Liberian residences. This influence encompassed the era’s prominent styles—Georgian, Neoclassical, and Greek Revival—whose characteristics are evident in Americo-Liberian buildings throughout the 19th century and into the early 20th century, shaping the design of many homes and related structures.

The Americo-Liberian community established a network of settlements across coastal and inland parts of Liberia, including Monrovia as well as Careysburg, Clay-Ashland, Buchanan in Maryland County, Mississippi-in-Africa, Cape Mount, and Greenville, along with numerous smaller towns situated along the St. Paul River. In addition, families of Barbadian origin—among them Barclays, Morgans, Bests, Thorpes, Weeks, and Portemans—formed Crozierville.

The Atlantic has issued editorial endorsements in U.S. presidential contests. In 2020, it backed Joe Biden and urged readers to oppose the reelection bid of incumbent President Donald Trump. Early in 2024, the publication released a 24-article issue under the title If Trump Wins, warning that a second term for Trump could be more damaging than his first. In October 2024, it endorsed Kamala Harris, the Democratic nominee, in the race against Trump.

In 1878, The Atlantic absorbed The Galaxy, a rival monthly magazine established around 1866 by William Conant Church and his brother Francis P. Church. The Galaxy featured contributions from notable writers such as Mark Twain, Walt Whitman, Ion Hanford Perdicaris, and Henry James.

During the 1970s, mainstream Spanish rock declined, while underground currents in progressive rock and rock urbano began to take shape. Spanish progressive rock failed to achieve commercial success, whereas in the mid-1970s Andalusian rock emerged, fusing flamenco with progressive sensibilities and producing acts such as Triana, which is regarded as a prominent example. In the late 1970s, amid Spain’s transition to democracy, hard rock acts came to the fore, and several of these groups drew on early punk influences—Leño being a notable case—contributing to the emergence of the rock urbano movement.

Rock music in Spain witnessed a significant punk-inflected phase led by acts such as Kortatu, La Polla Records, and Eskorbuto. The ensuing La Movida Madrileña emerged as a countercultural movement that produced numerous groups drawing from punk and new wave influences, including Kaka de Luxe, Derribos Arias, Radio Futura, Alaska y Dinarama, Gabinete Caligari, Nacha Pop, Loquillo y los Trogloditas, Glutamato Ye-Yé, and Los Secretos. Although many La Movida bands did not achieve substantial commercial success, their recordings frequently featured them as supporting acts for more widely known groups such as Mecano, which enjoyed international popularity, as well as Siniestro Total and Aerolíneas Federales. The Madrid scene also resonated beyond the capital, spawning parallel currents in Barcelona (represented by Loquillo y los Trogloditas and Los Rebeldes), León (Los Cardiacos, Los Flechazos), Vigo (Siniestro Total, Golpes Bajos, Os Resentidos, Aerolíneas Federales, Semen Up), and Granada (091). Concurrently, hard rock bands such as Los Suaves and Barricada emerged, though they benefited from relatively limited promotional support. The early 1980s also saw the rise of Spanish heavy metal groups, notably Barón Rojo and Obús.

The Military Demarcation Line on the Korean Peninsula is delineated by 1,292 identical boundary markers placed at regular intervals along the length of the border. The northern-facing faces of the markers are inscribed in Korean and Chinese, while the southern-facing faces bear inscriptions in Korean and English. Over time, the markers have aged and begun to rust.

The Military Demarcation Line in Korea runs near the 38th parallel and extends for roughly 248 kilometers (154 miles). On the southern side, patrols are conducted by American and South Korean forces, while on the northern side, North Korean troops carry out patrols.

ETIAS, or the European Travel Information and Authorisation System, imposes entry requirements for travelers arriving by land, air, or sea to thirty European countries, a group that comprises the 29 Schengen Area member states along with Cyprus. Ireland, by contrast, is part of the Common Travel Area and maintains its own visa policy. It is the only EU member state that does not plan to join Schengen or to require ETIAS.

ETIAS, the European Travel Information and Authorization System, is a proposed European Union framework designed to pre-screen visa-exempt travelers seeking to enter the Schengen Area. The system follows the same model as other electronic travel authorisation programs, requiring a prior automated assessment of travelers before boarding. In comparative terms, notable counterparts include the United States' Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) and the United Kingdom's Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA).

Michigan is a state in the United States situated in the Great Lakes region. The Great Lakes basin has been inhabited by human communities for millennia. Among the Indigenous peoples historically linked to this area are the Ojibwe, Odawa, Potawatomi, and Wyandot.

Michigan’s early territorial framework was shaped by the 1794 Jay Treaty, under which British forces withdrew from Detroit and Michilimackinac in 1796, while retaining jurisdiction over lands east and south of the Detroit River that would later become part of Ontario, Canada; border questions persisted for many years as sovereignty over adjacent areas remained contested. The United States did not achieve uncontested control of the Upper Peninsula until 1818, and full, undisputed sovereignty over Drummond Island was not established until 1847.

Beijing Daxing International Airport has gradually drawn services from both domestic and international carriers, with SkyTeam members progressively transferring operations to the new facility. XiamenAir relocated its routes to Daxing, while Aeroflot terminated flights from Beijing Capital International Airport in June 2020 in favor of operations at Daxing. China Eastern Airlines shifted all its Beijing operations to Daxing, with the exception of services to Shanghai-Hongqiao. The airline had planned to introduce new international routes to Paris and Tokyo by the end of March 2020, but these plans were not realized due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Delta Air Lines announced an intention to move its Beijing services to Daxing by the end of April 2020, but the timetable was delayed by the slow reopening of China–United States flight allocations.

Beijing Daxing International Airport is an international airport located in the southern part of Beijing's Daxing District, near the boundary with Hebei Province. The project received formal authorization from the National Development and Reform Commission on 22 December 2014, and at that time no design or detailed plans had been released due to ongoing negotiations. It was planned to include seven runways—six for civilian use and one for military purposes. Construction was completed in September 2019. The airport was intended to achieve an annual capacity of about 75 million passengers by 2025. The estimated cost was at least 70 billion yuan (approximately US$11.2 billion), including the 37-kilometer Beijing–Xiong'an intercity railway segment to Beijing West railway station.

During the bombing, residential neighborhoods in Sukabumi were targeted, resulting in numerous injuries among civilians. A city police officer, at home on a night shift, was fatally struck by bomb fragments. The attack also struck a village school, killing 43 people. In the aftermath, surviving students assisted in transporting the injured to receive medical care.

During the Japanese invasion, Sukabumi was subjected to a bombing that caught residents by surprise despite expectations of an attack. The strike affected several sites, including Dr. de Vogelweg (present-day Jalan Bhayangkara) and Wilhelminaweg (present-day Jalan R. E. Martadinata). Principal targets were the police academy and the Muhammadiyah school, at which 26 children were killed. Additional facilities damaged or struck included the Forestry Bureau offices (Boschwezen), the NIROM building, and the Sukabumi Regency offices. Several homes on Wilhelminaweg were damaged, and a forester from the Forestry Bureau sustained injuries.

Under Criterion 9 of the Ramsar designation framework, a site is considered eligible if it regularly supports at least 1% of the individuals in a population, with that population belonging to a single species or subspecies. The species in question must be dependent on wetlands and must be non-avian, i.e., not a bird.

The Ramsar Classification System for Wetland Type, also referred to as the Ramsar wetland typology, is a classification framework developed under the auspices of the Ramsar Convention. It is designed to enable rapid identification of the principal wetland categories, with aims and applications that are aligned with the objectives of the Ramsar Convention.

EU officials have recognized a link between the European deposit insurance framework and RTSE, reflecting how discussions of deposit protection are interwoven with RTSE considerations within the broader banking union agenda. This linkage is embedded in the negotiating frameworks employed by the Council, signaling that policy debates on insurance and RTSE are being addressed in tandem. Nevertheless, by mid-2020, no concrete progress had been achieved toward a policy consensus on the issue.

The European banking union is a framework that transfers banking policy responsibility from national authorities to a union-wide level in several EU member states. It was launched in 2012 in response to the 2009 Eurozone crisis, with the aim of addressing the fragility of many Eurozone banks and the bank–sovereign vicious circle that links bank credit conditions to sovereign credit strength. In some countries, private debts arising from a property bubble were effectively shifted to the sovereign through bailouts and subsequent government actions after the bubble burst. Compounding these pressures, weak sovereign credit also worsened banks’ balance sheets due to high domestic sovereign exposures.

The Apuan Alps region hosts a diverse avifauna, with more than 300 bird species documented. Among the notable species observed are the red-billed chough, the common raven, the buzzard, the golden eagle, the peregrine falcon, and the kestrel. In addition, the area is home to several owl species, including the barn owl, little owl, tawny owl, and common owl.

The Apuan Alps originate from marine sediments deposited during the middle Triassic, predating the rest of the Apennines and exhibiting a distinct geological configuration. Over time those sediments consolidated into rock types including limestone, dolomite, sandstone, and shale. Around 25 million years ago, substantial tectonic pressure transformed much of the limestone into the celebrated Carrara marble. The marble derives its name from the nearby city of Carrara. The range is widely associated with Carrara marble as a defining feature. Erosion subsequently sculpted the remaining sedimentary rocks into a rugged karst landscape.

The vast majority of criminal cases are resolved without a trial through non-trial dispositions. When the accused admits guilt, the process is typically shorter and sentencing can occur more quickly. Plea bargaining exists in some jurisdictions—most notably in the United States—and may involve negotiated pleas of guilty, no contest, or not guilty; such arrangements can include diversionary measures or reduced penalties, especially when the prosecution’s case is weak or in exchange for cooperation. Reduced sentences achieved through plea bargains can also lower the costs associated with conducting a formal trial. By contrast, many countries do not permit plea bargaining, arguing that it can coerce innocent defendants into pleading guilty to avoid harsher punishment. At the same time, courts are increasingly seeking alternatives to incarceration, favoring measures that divert offenders from immediate imprisonment where appropriate.

Following a guilty verdict, offenders are handed from the judiciary to correctional authorities for the implementation of penalties. The administration of punishment has manifested in numerous forms across different historical periods and societies. In the earliest eras, when resources to construct or maintain prisons were limited, exile and capital punishment served as the primary sanctions. Historically, techniques aimed at shaming individuals and the practice of exile have also functioned as instruments of social censure.

In 2002, the Advertising Standards Authority ruled on a campaign developed by HHCL for Easynet’s broadband services. The advertisements depicted scenes in which male and female bosses punched employees for wasting company money, while employees retaliated by punching bosses over slow internet speeds. The ASA concluded that the material was capable of causing serious or widespread offence and that the adverts condoned violence and anti-social behaviour, thereby breaching the relevant advertising codes.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) in the United Kingdom regulates a range of promotional communications, including direct mailings, circulars, leaflets, unsolicited emails, brochures, and catalogues. Timetables and price lists are generally outside its remit, as is private correspondence such as a doctor's letter or a bill. However, a leaflet that is included with private correspondence may fall under the ASA’s oversight if it promotes a new or different product.

Microsoft Customer Care Framework (CCF) is a platform for building customer-service applications on Microsoft technologies that emphasizes separating business rules from the integration method used to connect with target applications. In CCF, the business rules are managed within the HAT layer by Windows Workflow Foundation, while the application interfaces are handled by Data Driven Adapters. XML-based bindings link the WF-managed rules to the appropriate DDAs, enabling decoupled operation. The 2009 SP1 release ships with three DDAs corresponding to Win32, Web, and Java (JDK 1.6). These DDAs are designed to be customizable or extended to support additional application types.

Microsoft Customer Care Framework (CCF) 2005 for the .NET Framework 2.0, version 2.6, is an updated release built on a modified base derived from the 2.5.3 version. It requires the .NET Framework 2.0 runtime and includes substantial bug fixes in key areas of the framework where the source code is not publicly available.

Buddhist meditation is commonly divided into two principal forms: samatha and vipassanā. Samatha, also known as calming meditation, aims to quiet the mind and cultivate concentration, or samadhi, proceeding through the four dhyānas. Vipassanā is associated with the development of penetrating, discerning insight (paññā) into the nature of reality. This characterization of vipassanā’s focus has been attributed to the scholar Damien Keown.

The Noble Eightfold Path is a principal framework in Buddhism that comprises eight interrelated factors designed to promote ethical conduct, mental discipline, and wisdom. When developed together, these factors lead to the cessation of dukkha, the Buddhist term for unsatisfactory experience or suffering. The eight elements are Right View (or Understanding), Right Intention (or Thought), Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

Maximilian I’s death coincided with Dürer’s anxieties about potential loss of vision and the use of his hand, concerns that some scholars attribute to arthritis, even as his interest in Martin Luther’s writings deepened. In July 1520 he undertook his fourth and final major journey to renew Maximilian’s Imperial pension and to seek patronage from the newly elevated emperor, Charles V, who would be crowned at Aachen. Traveling with his wife and her maid, he followed the Rhine first to Cologne and then to Antwerp, where he was well received and produced a large number of drawings in silverpoint, chalk, and charcoal. In addition to attending the coronation, he visited several places, including Cologne (where he admired Stefan Lochner), Nijmegen, ’s-Hertogenbosch, Bruges (where he saw Michelangelo’s Madonna of Bruges), Ghent (where he studied Jan van Eyck’s Ghent Altarpiece), and Zeeland.

Albrecht Dürer's life is well documented despite the absence of autobiographical writings, and he was already widely recognized by his mid-twenties. After a brief period of schooling, he learned goldsmithing and drawing from his father, who wished to keep him in the metal trades; however, Dürer's exceptional talent for drawing led him to pursue an apprenticeship with Michael Wolgemut in 1486 at the age of fifteen. An early work, a silverpoint self-portrait dated 1484 and housed in the Albertina in Vienna, is among the earliest surviving children’s drawings and helps define the initial phase of his oeuvre, often referred to as Opus One. Wolgemut was the leading artist in Nuremberg, directing a large workshop that produced numerous works, particularly woodcuts for books. Nuremberg itself was a prosperous city, a center of publishing and luxury trade with strong connections to Italy, especially Venice, across the Alps.

An ISIL consists of a prefix identifying the issuing authority, a hyphen, and then an identifier issued by that authority. Two-letter prefixes are reserved for ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, and after the country code the national library authority assigns the specific identifier.
