There are also global-level identifiers not linked to any country, for example the oclc- prefix used by the Online Computer Library Center. The suffix relies on an existing system for identifying libraries rather than creating a new scheme. Overall, ISIL serves to unify pre-existing library identification systems worldwide rather than establishing an entirely new framework.

International Standard Identifier for Libraries and Related Organisations (ISIL) is an international identifier framework designed to provide unique codes for libraries and related institutions. The framework is standardized as ISO 15511. ISIL assigns distinct identifiers to individual organisations within the library sector and its related fields, with archives and museums among the categories encompassed by “related organisations.”

The Kettle Moraine is a region in the state of Wisconsin that extends from Green Bay to the south-central portion of the state. It comprises numerous kettles and moraines, along with other glacial landforms, and contains a substantial number of kettle lakes. Some of these lakes are 100 to 200 feet deep (about 61 meters).

Kettle holes are depressions on sandur plains formed when floods from the sudden drainage of ice-dammed lakes (jökulhlaups) rapidly deposit large amounts of sediment onto the surface. The holes themselves arise as blocks of sediment-rich ice that were transported and subsequently buried by the floodwaters melt, leaving cavities when the ice disappears. Maizels (1992) documented the presence of ramparts around the margins of kettle holes generated by jökulhlaups, based on both field observations and laboratory simulations. The development and variation of these ramparts depend on factors such as the concentration of rock fragments within the melting ice block and how deeply the block was buried by sediment, which together govern the amount and distribution of debris deposited during melt-out.

The 1793 Constitution of the French Republic exemplifies an understanding of limited government grounded in legislative supremacy and framed as the product of rational democratic self-government. Drawing on Rousseau's ideas, the constitution held that true constraint of political power arises when citizens participate in self-rule within a rational framework, rather than through monarchic authority. A central tenet was that the government should express the general will, conceived as the collective interest of the people, and the general will was regarded as a safeguard against the arbitrary rule characteristic of absolute monarchy.

Limited government refers to the constraint of political authority by constitutional rules and institutions, a principle central to constitutionalism. It is reflected in the United States Constitution of 1789 and the French Constitution of 1793, each attempting to reaffirm the idea through distinct institutional designs. In the United States, the design relied primarily on a horizontal separation of powers among the legislative, executive, and judiciary, supplemented by constitutional checks and balances that allow one branch to resist encroachment by the others. A vertical dimension, federalism, assigns authority between the national government and the state governments. James Madison observed that the Framers sought a government that could be controlled and could, in turn, exercise control. Federalist No. 51 contends that the most reliable guard against power concentration is to endow each department with the means and incentives to oppose the encroachments of the other branches.

On 16 September 2008, it was announced that And Another Thing..., a new entry in Douglas Adams's Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series, would be written by Eoin Colfer. Colfer initially expressed mixed feelings about another author contributing to the franchise. In later remarks, he described the commission as a valuable opportunity to engage with the series' beloved characters and to imprint his own voice while remaining faithful to Adams's spirit. Adams's widow, Jane Belson, supported the project and believed Colfer could transport Arthur, Zaphod, and Marvin to new settings.

In And Another Thing... (novel), Zaphod Beeblebrox gains access to Valhalla in Asgard, where he encounters Thor, an old acquaintance. After negotiations, Thor agrees to aid Zaphod and to become Nano's god, with the arrangement including Thor's obligation to kill Wowbagger.

Foxtel One is an Australian subscription television channel that focuses on non-premium drama programming. It launched on 7 November 2019 under the title FOX One and has since been rebranded as Foxtel One, with the earlier branding being Fox One.

As of autumn 1933, the United Socialist Party (PSU) had three regional committees and fifteen autonomous county-level committees. The counties included Baia, Bacău, Cahul, Cernăuți, Cetatea Albă, Dâmbovița, Ilfov, Ismail, Neamț, Prahova, Sibiu, and Tighina. Proletarul served as the party's central press organ. The Central Commission of Independent and United Trade Unions of Romania functioned as the party's labour wing (Comisia Centrală de independență și unificare sindicală din România).

Formed in 1933 in Romania through the merger of the Independent Socialist Party (PSI) and the Socialist Party led by Constantin Popovici, the Partidul Socialist Unitar (P.S.U.) operated as a small party within the left-wing movement yet exerted notable influence. It contributed to the broader left-wing agenda by advocating for closer ties between the Romanian Communist Party (PCR) and the Social Democratic Party (PSD), and it repeatedly sought to unite the PCR and PSD. The P.S.U. was affiliated with the London-based International Bureau of Revolutionary Socialist Unity.

Anti-submarine warfare during the Cold War evolved into a specialized arena of military competition between the United States and the Soviet Union, marked by a sustained development rivalry. Each side sought to produce quieter, more capable submarines while simultaneously enhancing the effectiveness and accuracy of anti-submarine weapons designed to detect, track, and neutralize submarine threats. In addition to improvements in submarines and weapon systems, the period saw the introduction of new delivery platforms to support ASW operations, with helicopters among the notable additions that expanded airborne reconnaissance and deployment options. This rapid pace of innovation in submarine design and anti-submarine technology helped shape strategic priorities and maintained a persistent focus on undersea warfare throughout the era.

Anti-submarine mines are naval munitions intended to counter submarines, functioning similarly to conventional surface-attack mines. They can be deployed to lie in wait for an approaching submarine and detonate to produce a damaging blast. Some designs are mobile, able to advance toward a submarine to reach lethal range. Other variants are capable of launching a torpedo encased in a capsule at a detected submarine. Mines may be laid by submarines, surface ships, or aircraft, reflecting the flexible options for deploying underwater defense measures.

Racloirs are primarily associated with the Neanderthal Mousterian industry. Retouch is concentrated along the ridge that delineates the striking platform from the dorsal surface, yielding deliberately shaped edges. In addition, racloirs are modified by abrupt flaking originating from the dorsal face, shaping their final form.

The racloir is a type of side scraper distinctive of Mousterian assemblages, fashioned from a flint flake. It presents as a large scraper in outline and was used for scraping hides and bark, with the possibility that it may also have served as a knife.

Dugout boats represent the oldest identified form of watercraft uncovered by archaeologists. They date to around 8,000 years ago during the Neolithic period of the Stone Age. Constructed from massive timbers, often carved from a single large log, their wooden build tends to preserve more readily than bark-based canoes.

In 1991, remains of a linden wood log-boat were recovered at Männedorf-Strandbad on Lake Zürich in Switzerland. The craft measures nearly six metres in length (about 20 feet) and has been identified as a dugout log-boat. Radiocarbon dating places its origin at roughly 6,500 years ago, dating to circa 3500 BCE.

Liquid oxygen has played a central role as an oxidizer in rocket propulsion. It was used in the first liquid-fueled rocket, marking an early application of liquid oxygen in flight propulsion. During World War II, the German V-2 missile employed liquid oxygen, which was referred to at the time as A-Stoff and Sauerstoff. The 1950s saw the adoption of liquid oxygen in major US and Soviet launch vehicles, with the United States’ Redstone and Atlas rockets and the Soviet R-7 Semyorka utilizing LOX. In the 1960s and 1970s, liquid oxygen powered the ascent stages of the Apollo Saturn launch vehicles and was employed in the Space Shuttle main engines.

Liquid oxygen is a highly reactive oxidizer that greatly accelerates combustion. Organic materials in contact with liquid oxygen burn with exceptional speed and intensity. Some substances, when saturated with liquid oxygen, can detonate unpredictably in the presence of ignition sources such as flames, sparks, or impacts; coal briquettes and carbon black are given as examples. Petrochemicals, including asphalt, often exhibit this behavior, highlighting the elevated danger associated with LOX in the presence of combustible organic materials.

Into the Groove has been subject to numerous remixes and reinterpretations over the years. An early and notable remix was produced by Shep Pettibone for Madonna's 1987 remix collection You Can Dance, featuring extended instrumental breaks and additional vocal overdubs. Pettibone later collaborated with Goh Hotoda to produce another version that appeared on The Immaculate Collection (1990). In 2003, a mashup entitled Into the Hollywood Groove—a combination of Into the Groove and Hollywood—was created for a Gap advertisement that featured Missy Elliott, and it was subsequently released on Remixed & Revisited. Elements of this mashup were incorporated into Madonna's live performances during the Re-Invention Tour (2004) and the Celebration tours (2023–2024). A shortened remix with stuttering vocal effects was later released on the 2022 compilation Finally Enough Love: 50 Number Ones.

In 2003, Dannii Minogue became the first artist officially authorized to sample Madonna's music, incorporating Into the Groove into the track Dont Wanna Lose This Feeling; Minogue later recalled the moment with disbelief and described the song as legendary. In December 2021, Madonna publicly accused Tory Lanez of illegally sampling Into the Groove on his track Pluto's Last Comet from the album Alone at Prom, and she commented on Lanez's Instagram post regarding the alleged infringement. It remains unclear whether any legal action was pursued. In a Rolling Stone interview, Madonna stated that she is tired of being taken advantage of and signaled a decisive stance toward unauthorized uses of her music.

During the late 1980s, the Soviet rock scene broadened, with Armenian groups such as Asparez and Ayas drawing international attention through the oriental rock style, a phenomenon described in Melodie und Rhythmus magazine. Ayas, formed in 1986 by conservatory graduate Artur Mitinyan, earned recognition by winning the Best Song of the Year at Yerevan's Rock, Rock, Rock Festival in 1987 and later receiving the Sisian Rock Festival award. Elips, another notable Armenian band formed in 1986, toured Latvia in the summer of that year with the Riga-based ensemble Pilligrim, but faced prohibition by Soviet authorities on anti-Soviet grounds. Elips is best remembered for its song Patkeratsrek (Imagine), which is regarded as one of the hymns of Armenian rock.

Armenian rock has been shaped in part by Harutyun Ayvazyan (also known as Artyom), who became the first Armenian journalist to publish a rock encyclopedia. The encyclopedia was issued in St. Petersburg and released in Russian by Avgust Publishing House. In the contemporary Armenian rock scene, the group Vara is noted for featuring an Armenian lead singer.

During the late 18th century, the Michigan region existed as an unorganized area under British control prior to the establishment of U.S. territorial governance. With the creation of the Northwest Territory, Arthur St. Clair, the territory’s first governor, sought to establish a formal administrative framework for the region, albeit largely on paper. On June 20, 1790, Knox County was established, comprising the western half of the Lower Peninsula and roughly the middle third of the Upper Peninsula. In 1792, Hamilton County’s boundaries were expanded to include the eastern portions of Michigan that lay outside Knox County.

The Toledo War of 1835 involved the Michigan Territory and Ohio over the Toledo Strip, with the territory seeking to retain the area. The dispute ended when Ohio ceded the Toledo region in exchange for Michigan's western Upper Peninsula, a settlement that helped shape the boundary between the two states.

The genus Jacaranda is divided into two sections, Monolobos and Dilobos DC., based on the number of thecae on the anthers. Monolobos comprises 18 species distributed across western South America, Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean, while Dilobos includes 31 species found principally in southeastern Brazil, including the Paraná River valley, and is considered the primitive lineage of the group. Wood anatomy differs between the two sections, reflecting their divergent characteristics. Jacaranda copaia is typically placed in Monolobos but may be intermediate between the two sections in some assessments (Dos Santos & Miller 1997).

Jacaranda thrives in full sun and sandy soils and is abundant in warmer climates. In colder regions, mature plants can withstand temperatures down to about −7 °C (19 °F), though flowering may be less prolific than in milder conditions. Younger plants are more fragile and may not survive freezing temperatures, making establishment in cold areas more challenging.

Radioactive waste is categorized into three main classes: low-level waste (LLW), intermediate-level waste (ILW), and high-level waste (HLW). Low-level waste comprises items such as paper, rags, tools, and clothing, and contains small quantities of predominantly short-lived radioactivity. Intermediate-level waste holds higher concentrations of radioactivity and requires a certain degree of shielding. High-level waste is highly radioactive and thermally hot due to decay heat, and it necessitates cooling as well as shielding.

Decommissioned nuclear weapons waste generally exhibits low beta and gamma activity, with notable exceptions including traces of tritium and americium. The waste is more likely to contain alpha-emitting actinides, most prominently plutonium-239, a fissile material used in nuclear weapons. In some cases, certain materials may display substantially higher specific activities, such as plutonium-238 or polonium, which reflect shorter half-lives and stronger alpha emission. These radiological characteristics influence safety, containment, and handling requirements during storage and disposal.

Susan Hayward established herself as a leading actress through three major box-office successes in the early 1950s. In David and Bathsheba (1951), she co-starred with Gregory Peck, and the film was the year's most popular release. The following year, she starred in With a Song in My Heart, a biographical musical about Jane Froman, which earned her an Academy Award nomination. That same year she appeared in The Snows of Kilimanjaro with Gregory Peck and Ava Gardner, further reinforcing her rising stature in Hollywood.

Susan Hayward's early screen work included a 1943 assignment secured by producer Sam Bronston for the United Artists release Jack London. In 1944 she appeared for Republic Pictures as John Wayne's love interest in The Fighting Seabees. That film was the studio's largest-budget production in Republic Pictures' history.

Combustion-driven pumps have been proposed as an alternative to cycles of gas buildup and release for generating pressure. Pressure is produced through the combustion of hydrocarbons, and the resulting impulse is transmitted directly through an actuation membrane to drive the pump fluid. Realizing direct transmission requires the pump to be predominantly composed of elastomeric material, such as silicone rubber. As combustion causes the membrane to expand, fluid is pumped out of the adjacent pumping chamber. The first combustion-driven soft pump was developed by ETH Zurich.

Rotary pumps constitute a class of positive-displacement devices in which fluid movement is driven by the rotation of internal members such as gears, screws, or vanes. They are distinguished by high efficiency and by their ability to handle highly viscous fluids, enabling effective transfer of thick liquids in a variety of industrial settings. In certain rotary designs, the flow rate increases as the viscosity of the pumped fluid rises, a behavior that distinguishes them from many other pump types and is influenced by geometry and operating conditions. Collectively, these characteristics contribute to the prominence of rotary pumps in applications that require efficient, viscous-fluid transfer.

Majestic Athletic, a former supplier of Major League Baseball uniforms, played a notable role in MLB's awards program when the Always Game Award, sponsored by Majestic Athletic, was introduced in 2015 as the third all-MLB category in the Players Choice Awards. In December 2016, Under Armour announced it would replace Majestic as MLB’s official on-field uniform provider, with the transition set for 2020. This schedule was later adjusted in May 2017, when MLB indicated the switch would occur in 2019, moving the timeline up by a year. In January 2019, MLB announced that Nike would instead replace Majestic as the official on-field uniform provider beginning with the 2020 season. Majestic continued to supply MLB uniforms through the 2019 season.

Majestic Athletic was established in 1976 by Faust Capobianco III, continuing a family enterprise that had previously operated Maria Rose Fashions. The company initially produced fashion apparel, but its manufacturing operations were relocated from the Lehigh Valley to the southern United States. This strategic shift coincided with a renewed emphasis on athletic teamwear, establishing the firm’s core focus in the sports apparel sector.

Eugene du Pont was a member of the prominent Du Pont family. His daughter, Amy Elizabeth du Pont, became a notable donor to the University of Delaware, contributing to its development and programs. His granddaughter, Ethel du Pont (1916–1965), was the first wife of Franklin D. Roosevelt Jr. (1914–1988).

Eugene du Pont graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1861 and subsequently joined his older cousin Lammot du Pont at the Brandywine Mills laboratory as an assistant. He was promoted to junior partner in 1864, and by 1886 had filed two patent applications, one for a gunpowder press and another for a new powder variety called brown prismatic. In 1889 he succeeded his uncle Henry du Pont as senior partner, continuing the family leadership of the enterprise.

Uhlsport is a German company that operates with an indirect distribution approach. It maintains subsidiaries in France, Spain, and Sweden, and appoints country managers in the United Kingdom, the Benelux region, and Switzerland. The firm counts around 80 distribution partners worldwide. In 1998, the Uhl family sold the company to the Daiss family.

Uhlsport GmbH is a German producer of sporting goods with an international presence. It traces its origins to 1948, when it was founded as Haase & Uhl OHG, later reorganized as Karl Uhl GmbH, and in 1994 adopted the name uhlsport GmbH. Today, the company operates internationally, with its permanent headquarters located in Balingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

Palace Hotel (Copenhagen) was acquired in November 1999 by Fritz Schur. From 2005 to 2009, Starwood managed the property, during which time it underwent renovations to upgrade it to a five-star hotel under the Le Méridien brand. Following unsuccessful negotiations between Schur and Starwood, Scandic Hotels assumed control of the hotel.

The Palace Hotel in Copenhagen served as the venue for the first and founding congress of the International Handball Federation, with the meeting held from 10 to 13 July 1946, marking the establishment of the federation.

A vehicle requires an energy source to enable propulsion, and this energy may be drawn from external sources or stored on board for on-demand use. External energy can be harnessed from sources such as wind for sail-powered craft, sunlight for solar-powered vehicles, or electric traction supplied by overhead lines for streetcars. Alternatively, energy can be stored in an on-board medium and converted to usable power as needed. The chosen storage medium must offer sufficient energy content and the ability to deliver adequate power to meet the vehicle’s performance requirements.

In certain vehicle applications, energy can be stored mechanically by deforming elastic elements such as rubber bands or metal springs, with the stored energy released when these components return to their original state. Elastic-material systems inherently display hysteresis, meaning that loading and unloading follow different paths and some energy is lost in the process. Because metal springs tend to be dense, their usefulness is limited in many cases, prompting the exploration of lighter or alternative energy-storage or damping solutions in vehicle design.

Proprietary software has been viewed by governments with concern that defects or hidden features could be exploited to compromise sensitive information. In response, Microsoft established the Government Security Program in 2003, which enables government entities to access and review source code alongside Microsoft security documentation, with the Chinese government among its early participants. The GSP operates as a component of Microsoft’s broader Shared Source Initiative, which provides varying levels of source-code access for selected products. Within this framework, the Reference Source License (Ms-RSL) and the Limited Public License (Ms-LPL) are proprietary licenses that make the underlying source code available to qualified users.

Proprietary software vendors sometimes use obfuscation to hinder reverse engineering, with the aim of impeding users who would analyze or modify the software. The practice is particularly common for certain programming languages, where protecting intellectual property through code transformation is more feasible. For example, Java bytecode can be decompiled into code that remains partially usable, making obfuscation a notable protective step. In contrast, scripting languages such as PHP or JavaScript expose their source code at run time, which diminishes the protective value of obfuscation in such contexts.

Rubric has figurative senses extended from its original meaning, and in modern usage these senses frequently appear in phrases that indicate a framework or standard applied to a matter. These figurative senses include an authoritative rule; the title of a statute; a category under which a thing is classified; an explanatory or introductory commentary; an established rule, tradition, or custom; and a guide that specifies the criteria used for grading or scoring academic assignments.

Rubric refers to the red ink or pigment used to mark or decorate manuscript text, a practice traditionally known as rubrication. While red remained the most common color, the late Middle Ages saw the use of other hues for similar purposes, and the term rubric came to be applied to these non-red colors as well. In scholarly usage, patterns of rubrication are employed by medievalists to identify and differentiate textual traditions, helping to trace the development and transmission of manuscripts across regions and periods.
Taman is an Austronesian language of the Dayak group spoken on the island of Borneo. Together with Embaloh, it constitutes the Tamanic branch, a subdivision of the South Sulawesi language family.

Boogie rock developed in the postwar era from electric blues traditions, most prominently through John Lee Hooker's 1948 recording "Boogie Chillen'," an urban electric blues piece rooted in the North Mississippi Hill Country style. Musicologist Robert Palmer noted that Hooker was not copying piano boogie; instead he employed a rocking, single-chord ostinato with accents pushed slightly ahead of the beat, creating a distinctive rhythmic propulsion. Hooker's repetitive single-string riff provided the central motif of the track and was later adapted by Canned Heat for "Fried Hockey Boogie" (1968), included on the album Boogie with Canned Heat.

Boogie rock is a subgenre of blues rock that emerged in the late 1960s. Its defining feature is a persistent, driving rhythm designed to foreground the groove, giving the music a strong, propulsive feel. The style drew inspiration from earlier forms, notably the piano-based boogie-woogie, and is often described as having a heavier, more aggressively edged instrumental approach.

Warwick Davis is a British actor known for his work across film, television, and theatre. He portrayed Nikabrik the Dwarf in The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian, having previously been involved in television adaptations of the Chronicles of Narnia. In 2007, he appeared as a contestant on Celebrity Scissorhands for Children in Need. He later starred as a fictional version of himself in Life's Too Short, a series written by and starring Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant. In December 2012, Davis returned to the New Wimbledon Theatre to reprise his role in the pantomime Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
In April 2010, Warwick Davis published his autobiography, titled Size Matters Not: The Extraordinary Life and Career of Warwick Davis, with a foreword written by George Lucas.

Alleghany Corporation is an American investment holding company that was formed by railroad entrepreneurs Oris and Mantis Van Sweringen to serve as the structure for their railroad ventures. The firm was incorporated in 1929 and later reincorporated in Delaware in 1984. In March 2022, Berkshire Hathaway disclosed an offer valued at $11.6 billion to acquire Alleghany, with the transaction closing in October 2022.

Alleghany Corporation included retained railroad investments in its asset portfolio. John J. Burns served as the company's president and chief executive officer. In addition to his responsibilities at Alleghany, Burns was a member of the board of Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corporation, with his tenure on that board lasting from 1995 to 2004.

Salisbury Plain hosts nationally scarce invertebrates across three insect orders: Orthoptera, Heteroptera, and Coleoptera. Orthoptera includes grasshoppers and crickets, Heteroptera is commonly referred to as true bugs, and Coleoptera comprises the beetles. Within the Coleoptera, the soldier beetle Cantharis fusca is listed in the Red Data Book.

The Hampshire Avon runs through the eastern half of Salisbury Plain. To the south, the plain narrows as river valleys converge before meeting at Salisbury; the Avon then continues south to the English Channel at Christchurch. Surrounding Salisbury Plain are chalk downlands, with the Hampshire Downs to the east and the Berkshire Downs to the north, while Dorset Downs and Cranborne Chase lie to the southwest. In the western and northwestern sectors, the geology is dominated by clays and limestones of the Blackmore Vale, Avon Vale, and Vale of Wardour. The Mendip Hills lie to the west of Salisbury Plain, and the Cotswolds lie to the northwest.

The Billboard Argentina Hot 100 is the principal chart used to gauge song popularity in Argentina and is published weekly by Billboard together with the Billboard Argentina magazine. The ranking identifies the most popular songs in the country and is derived from a formula that blends local streaming activity across platforms such as YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Music, among others, with national radio airplay and exposure on Argentine television networks. Streaming data for the chart is provided by Luminate, while the measurement of radio and TV activity is conducted by BMAT/Vericast.

The Argentina Hot 100 is a weekly singles chart compiled in Argentina that ranks the country’s top-performing songs across genres. It began on 13 October 2018, with the inaugural number-one single being “Cuando Te Besé” by Becky G and Paulo Londra. By the week ending 29 March 2025, there had been 63 different songs reaching the top position. The record for the longest tenure at number one is held by “Tusa,” a collaboration between Karol G and Nicki Minaj, which led the chart for 25 weeks. The current number-one, as of the latest update, is “Amor de Vago” by La T y La M featuring Malandro.

Emerson's religious thought was considered radical for its assertion that the divine pervades all things and that the universe is interwoven with God. Critics, including Henry Ware Jr., argued that such a stance risked diminishing the central figure of God by reducing the Father of the Universe to a community of humanity without a transcendent sovereign. He drew on German philosophy and Biblical criticism to shape a Transcendentalist approach in which truth is not necessarily disclosed by revelation but can be apprehended directly through intuition grounded in nature. He described his outlook as resembling Quaker sensibilities, maintaining that an inner, still and small voice embodies Christ within individuals.

Ralph Waldo Emerson is a central figure in the Boston literary tradition, within which the Saturday Club formed part of the era's intellectual life. The Saturday Club was a largely literary association that met on the last Saturday of each month at the Parker House in Boston (now the Omni Parker House). William James Stillman, a painter who founded the art journal Crayon, was connected to this circle; he was born and raised in Schenectady, a city south of the Adirondack Mountains, and traveled there to paint wilderness landscapes as well as to fish and hunt. Stillman shared these wilderness experiences with the Saturday Club, thereby stirring its members' interest in the Adirondacks, a region previously unknown to many of them.

Surjectivity, also called onto, is a property of a function, indicating that every element of the codomain is the image of at least one element from the domain. In other words, a surjective function guarantees that each codomain element has a preimage under the mapping. In the accompanying diagram, the green relationship is depicted as a surjection, whereas the red, blue, and black relationships do not possess this property.

The relation illustrated is neither injective nor a function. In the diagram, the black segment demonstrates a many-to-many correspondence, meaning that elements of the domain relate to multiple elements of the codomain and vice versa. Likewise, the red, green, and blue portions likewise fail to be injective as well as functional, indicating that a single input can be related to several outputs and that distinct inputs may map to the same output.

Jethro Tull's 1984 album Under Wraps represented a shift toward electronic production, featuring a drum-machine-driven rhythm section in lieu of a traditional live drummer, a move that paralleled the band's earlier Walk into Light. The work was not well received by critics and audiences, though members of the group embraced the sonic approach, with guitarist Martin Barre describing it as among his personal favourites. The accompanying video for the track "Lap of Luxury" enjoyed moderate airplay on MTV. Keyboardist Peter Vettese departed from the lineup after the tour, reportedly upset by the critical backlash to The Broadsword and the Beast (1982), Walk into Light (1983), and Under Wraps (1984). The band subsequently entered a hiatus of about three years, triggered by Ian Anderson's vocal cord problems that developed during the touring of the Under Wraps material. During this interval, Anderson ran a salmon farming operation on the Isle of Skye, a venture he had founded in 1978. In 1986, the single "Coronach" was released in the United Kingdom after being used as the theme tune for Channel 4's Blood of the British.

Ian Anderson rejected critics’ claim that Aqualung was a concept album, insisting it was a varied collection of songs, and in response resolved to create what he described as an exceptionally ambitious concept project. Drawing on Monty Python’s satirical sensibilities, he composed a suite that fused intricate musical structures with offbeat humor, aiming to mock the band, its audience, and critics. Thick as a Brick, issued in 1972, presents a single continuous composition of roughly 43 minutes’ duration, spread over two sides of a vinyl LP, a format then uncommon for rock records. The work was conceived and recorded in stages, with the entire band contributing to arrangements, and it carried a credit for a fictional schoolboy named Gerald Bostock. Thick as a Brick became Jethro Tull’s first album to reach number one on the US Billboard Pop Albums chart. In the following year, A Passion Play was the only other Jethro Tull release to achieve the same chart position.

The Gambian Creole people are associated with the Krio language, which is spoken by 96 percent of Sierra Leone's population. Krio serves as a principal vehicle for trade and for social exchanges among various ethnic groups, illustrating its role as a common lingua franca that underpins interethnic interaction in the region.

In The Gambia, the Aku name refers to the Creole community, a Christian group living mainly in and around Banjul. By contrast, in Sierra Leone the terms Aku Marabout and Aku Mohammedan are used to designate the Oku people. Additionally, The Gambia is home to a non-Creole migrant group known as the Aku Marabout, whose members are descended from the Oku people of Sierra Leone.

The Catalogue of Life is a collaborative online database that uses a straightforward data structure to assemble information on synonymy, taxonomic groupings, common names, distribution, and ecological environments. It provides two editions: a dynamically updated monthly edition, in which data may change without a formal record of updates, and an Annual Checklist that serves as a dated, verifiable reference for current name usage and related data. Development funding for the project from 2003 to 2013 originated with the Species 2000 europa (EuroCat), the 4d4Life and i4Life initiatives, with subsequent support provided by Naturalis Biodiversity Center in Leiden, Netherlands, and the Species Files group at the Illinois Natural History Survey in Champaign-Urbana.

During 2015, an expert panel presented a consensus hierarchical classification of life, noting that certain sectors remained unrepresented in the published Catalogue of Life. In the same year, the Catalogue of Life (CoL), Barcode of Life Data System (BOLD), Biodiversity Heritage Library (BHL), Encyclopedia of Life (EOL), and GBIF discussed establishing a single, shared authoritative nomenclature and taxonomic foundation provisionally named Catalogue of Life Plus (COL+). COL+ was intended to organize and connect biodiversity data, including material not yet in CoL but available from other sources, through a common infrastructure accessible to CoL users and users of extended taxonomic content such as GBIF. It would create a clearinghouse for scientific names across all life, provide a unified taxonomic view, and offer a channel for feedback from content authorities. The Catalogue of Life is being developed in conjunction with the Global Species List Working Group to minimize duplication and advance toward an authoritative global list of species.

The Klan originated as an offshoot of the Belgian rock group Les Ombres, evolving from members of that band into a distinct act. They issued a series of singles and released the album Join Us in 1967 on the Palette label. The band further gained recognition by opening for the Rolling Stones at their Paris concert on April 10, 1967.

Rock music in Belgium features a number of acts noted for jazz rock influences, including The Cos and The Kandahar. The Cos formed in 1973 and released the album Postaeolian Train Robbery in 1974 on Plus Records. The Kandahar debuted with a 7-inch single, Survivin' Boogie / The Dark Hole Rag, in 1974, and their first album, In The Court Of Catherina Squeezer, followed in 1975 on Dwarf. The Esperanto Rock Orchestra achieved international fame with a self-titled album issued by A&M Records. Other notable Belgian bands in the scene include Tideline, Magenta, Machiavel, the Isopoda, the Nessie, the Phylter, the Flyte, and the Dragon. The symphonic prog rock band Banzai released Hora Nata in 1974 on the Dutch label Delta.

The Kashmir Princess refers to an aircraft involved in an explosion later believed to have been caused by a time-delayed explosive device. The weapon was reportedly planted by a Kuomintang secret agent as part of an assassination attempt against Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai. Zhou had been scheduled to board the plane for a conference, but he altered his travel plans at the last minute, preventing the attack from taking place.

The Kashmir Princess, officially Air India Flight 300, was a chartered Lockheed L-749A Constellation that, on 11 April 1955, was damaged by a midair bomb explosion and crashed into the South China Sea. The aircraft was en route from Bombay, India, via Hong Kong to Jakarta, Indonesia, with 16 people killed and three survivors. The explosion was an assassination attempt targeting Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai, who did not fly on the plane due to a medical emergency or, according to one historian, prior knowledge of the attack. The Chinese government urged Hong Kong authorities to investigate, and Hong Kong investigators concluded that the Kuomintang were responsible for the bombing.

Under Hanyu Pinyin, tone marks are written on the finals of syllables to denote the four Mandarin tones (and the neutral tone). When the tone mark is placed on the letter i, it replaces the i’s dot, as in the spelling yī.

In China, published materials increasingly space pinyin syllables individually, treating each syllable as a separate unit rather than forming words in a continuous sequence. The practice intensified after 1985, when the Script Reform Committee's power was weakened, and the body was renamed the State Language Commission and placed under the Ministry of Education. Victor H. Mair has argued that some educational bureaucrats feared that a word-based pinyin could become a de facto script for writing Mandarin, potentially displacing Chinese characters. Consequently, authorities mandated that all pinyin syllables be written separately.

Within political philosophy, anarchism comprises several distinct traditions that differ in their assessment of state authority. Absolute (a priori) anarchism holds that state power is illegitimate in principle. By contrast, contingent (a posteriori) anarchism contends that states are not inherently harmful but typically fail in practice. Consequentialist strands oppose the state on the grounds that it yields negative outcomes, including increased inequality, discrimination, and unhappiness. Individualist anarchism emphasizes personal liberty and resists social structures that restrict autonomy, and it encompasses currents such as libertarian anarchism and anarcho-capitalism. Collectivist and socialist forms stress communal life, voluntary cooperation, and collective ownership of resources and means of production. In particular, anarchist communism advocates decentralized organization and communal sharing designed to promote well-being for all.

Political philosophy has long contrasted two overarching approaches to political action: realism and idealism. Realism treats political behavior as driven by self-interest and the pursuit of power to extend influence, with realists arguing that political life should not be indiscriminately constrained by moral considerations and that conflicts over power can entail coercive or violent means when interests collide. They emphasize responding to concrete, practical factors and see the aim as shaping historical reality rather than pursuing abstract ideals. In international relations, realism holds that state self-interest operates without a higher authority enforcing universal rules. By comparison, idealism contends that political action should be guided by moral principles and universal ethical norms, aspiring to a just and fair social order grounded in these norms rather than narrow self-interest. Idealists reject existing practices and institutions that sustain unjust power and advocate for reforms toward fair governance, even if their vision may be utopian and distant from current circumstances.

The fourth annual Grammy Awards ceremony was held on May 29, 1962, in Chicago, Los Angeles, and New York, recognizing musical achievements from the year 1961. Henry Mancini won five awards at the ceremony.

Apache Cayenne is an open-source persistence framework released under the Apache License. It offers object-relational mapping and remoting capabilities, mapping one or more database schemas directly to Java objects. The framework handles atomic commits and rollbacks, SQL generation, joins, sequences, and related tasks. Its Remote Object Persistence feature enables persisting Java objects for remote clients via Web Services, while native XML serialization supports persisting objects to non-Java clients, such as AJAX-enabled browsers.

Apache Cayenne is a persistence framework that emphasizes caching, provides a complete object query syntax, and supports pre-fetching of related objects to optimize performance. It implements on-demand faulting of objects and their relationships, enabling lazy loading as needed, while supporting object inheritance within its data model. The framework can automatically detect the underlying database, supports generic persisted objects, and is designed to scale to virtually any project size.

Staccato refers to an articulation in music in which each note is performed briefly and detached from the following one. It stands in opposition to legato, whose aim is a smooth and connected phrasing. In standard musical notation, staccato is indicated by a small dot placed above or below the note head, signaling this detached articulation.

In piano terminology, the term string refers to the use of the soft pedal. Engaging the pedal alters the action so that the hammer strikes either a single string or three strings, producing a softer dynamic and a distinct timbre. Related terms una corda (one string) and tre corde (three strings) denote these configurations and are explained in later sections.

Runtime injection is a profiling technique that involves modifying a program’s code during execution in order to divert control flow to dedicated helper functions. Compared with runtime instrumentation, it is typically more lightweight, since it avoids broad instrumentation and relies on inserting small jumps to the appropriate helpers rather than instrumenting large portions of the code. This approach enables collection of performance data with lower overhead while still providing insight into runtime behavior.

Profiling in computer programming involves collecting information about a program's behavior during execution, typically by inserting instrumentation or extra instructions into the target code. This instrumentation can alter performance characteristics, potentially causing noticeable slowdowns and, in some cases, yielding biased or inaccurate results such as Heisenbugs, where the act of measurement changes the program’s behavior. The extent of such impact depends on the type of information collected, the level of timing detail required, and whether basic-block profiling is used in conjunction with instrumentation. Overhead is not uniform; for instance, counting every function or procedure call generally imposes less burden than tallying how often each individual statement is executed. In some systems, hardware support for profiling provides dedicated mechanisms or performance counters that minimize the observable effect on the program.

At The Independent, Zach Leonard, who had served as chief executive of IDNML, relocated to the United States to assume the posts of global chief operating officer and president for North America. Christian Broughton, the newspaper’s former editor, was subsequently appointed chief executive. In March 2024, Louise Thomas was named US editor.
The Independent reported war crimes in the Darfur region of Sudan, with the perpetrators described as pro-government forces.

Brian Teacher prevailed over Kim Warwick in the final of the 1980 Australian Open men's singles, securing a three-set victory with scores of 7–5, 7–6(7–4), 6–3. This triumph marked Teacher's first and only major singles title. The men's tournament ran from late December 1980 into early January 1981, and was staged separately from the women's event, which was held in late November.

Tongyong Pinyin served as Taiwan's official romanization system, but its use was voluntary rather than mandatory throughout the country. In practice, the choice of romanization often depends on the government authority responsible for a given facility or area. Street signage across many urban districts uses Tongyong Pinyin, with Kaohsiung, Tainan, and neighboring counties cited as examples. The situation in Taichung reflects administrative split: Taichung County employed Tongyong Pinyin, while Taichung City has used Hanyu Pinyin since at least 2004. In Taipei, then-mayor Ma Ying-jeou supported retaining Hanyu Pinyin as the standard for the capital, whereas Taipei County—now known as New Taipei City—continued to use Tongyong Pinyin, though Taipei Metro stations often present Tongyong in parentheses after Hanyu. Beyond official systems, many proper names, especially people and businesses, are commonly rendered with modified Wade–Giles spellings.

In August 2002, the government issued an administrative order adopting Tongyong Pinyin, while allowing local governments to override the system within their jurisdictions. In October 2007, the administration led by the Democratic Progressive Party announced plans to standardize the English transliterations of Mandarin place names nationwide by the end of that year, with Tongyong Pinyin, the locally developed system, designated as the standard. The rationale for the move was to address years of confusion arising from multiple spellings in use across various contexts.

Isparta has extensive road links to other parts of Turkey, reflecting its role in regional connectivity. Antalya is located about 130 kilometers to the south of Isparta, while Eskişehir lies roughly 350 kilometers to the north, situating the city relative to major regional centers.

Towards the end of the 19th century, Muslim refugees from the Balkans settled in and around Isparta. A subset of these new arrivals were Bulgarians who brought with them expertise in the Kazanlak-style distillation of rosewater. The transfer of this knowledge enriched the local rose industry and contributed to Isparta's long-standing nickname, the city of roses.

RawFaith was built in Addison, Maine, by George McKay and his three sons. The construction spanned 28 months over a four-year period and relied on improvised methods, including a half-hull model as a design guide, a steam box, and an attempt to replicate 16th-century hull lines, augmented by contemporary power tools and laminating techniques. The vessel was constructed from a diverse array of woods and other materials not typically used in conventional marine construction. It was not designed or built by professional shipwrights or naval architects. The project proved highly controversial, with the majority of professionals considering its workmanship and design deficient.

RawFaith was criticized for its lack of seaworthiness. On Thanksgiving Day in 2004, the vessel was rescued by the United States Coast Guard about 80 miles (130 km) off the coast of Maine. The incident was attributed to a failure in the rudder mechanism, with the foremast’s top snapping off. After the rescue, RawFaith was towed to Rockland, Maine, for repairs.

Ben Bridge Jeweler traces its origins to 1912, when Samuel Silverman opened the first jewelry store in downtown Seattle. In 1922 his son-in-law, Ben Bridge, joined as a partner, and soon after he purchased Silverman’s firm, which was renamed Ben Bridge Jeweler. The company subsequently expanded to more than 70 retail locations across 11 states, with a focus on the western United States. In May 2000 it was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway. Today the business remains family-operated and is managed by Lisa Bridge, Ben Bridge’s great-granddaughter.

Ben Bridge Jeweler is a premier American luxury jewelry retailer that offers engagement rings, diamonds, and timepieces, including Rolex watches, along with other high-end goods. Established in Seattle, Washington, in 1912, the company operates more than 80 stores across the United States. It is owned by Berkshire Hathaway, the holding company led by Warren Buffett.

Yellow fever is a viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is endemic in parts of Africa and the Americas, while Asia, though not yet affected, faces potential risk due to the presence of vectors and susceptible non-human primates. Some countries require travelers who have passed through yellow fever–endemic areas to show proof of vaccination to prevent the introduction of the disease. Proof is provided by a vaccination certificate that becomes valid ten days after vaccination and remains in effect for ten years. The World Health Organization’s guidance issued on May 17, 2013 states that booster doses are unnecessary for most individuals, but older certificates dating beyond ten years may not be accepted at all border posts in all affected countries. The WHO also publishes a list of countries that require yellow fever vaccination. In cases where vaccination cannot be delivered, dispensation may be possible, requiring an exemption certificate from a WHO-approved vaccination center. Of the 44 endemic countries, 32 have vaccination programs, but many achieve vaccination coverage well below 50 percent.

Personal protection against yellow fever emphasizes reducing exposure to mosquitoes. Mosquitoes may bite through thin clothing, so lightweight garments may not provide complete protection. Spraying clothing with repellents containing permethrin or with other EPA-registered repellents provides an additional level of defense. Permethrin-treated clothing is commercially available. Repellents containing permethrin are not approved for application directly to the skin.

Guangzhou Martyrs' Memorial Garden is a commemorative site in Guangzhou established to mark the 30th anniversary of the Guangzhou Uprising. Construction began in 1954 and was completed in 1957, reflecting the period's commemoration efforts. A doorway set into a stone wall carries an inscription identifying the site as the Guangzhou uprising martyrs cemetery, which was engraved by Zhou Enlai, China's first premier.

The Guangzhou Martyrs' Memorial Garden is a park located on Zhongshan 3rd Road in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, China. It is dedicated to commemorating fallen members of the Chinese Communist Party who participated in the Guangzhou Uprising against the Kuomintang, an event that took place on December 11, 1927.

The ISO base media file format (ISOBMFF) is a container file format that defines a general structure for files containing time-based multimedia data. It is used to store multimedia content such as video and audio.

The ISO base media file format is an extensible container framework designed to support a broad range of media types and specifications. A public registry of all registered extensions is maintained by the registration authority, with the complete list accessible on the mp4ra.org website. The registration of code points (identifier values) within MP4 family files is overseen by Apple Inc., a role described in Annex D of MPEG-4 Part 12. Although codec designers are encouraged to register new codes, registration remains voluntary and some codes may remain unregistered. In developing new specifications derived from the ISO base media file format, designers should consult existing specifications for definitions and technical conventions and use them as sources. When a media type is already defined by an existing specification (for example, how MPEG-4 audio or video is stored in MP4), that definition should be adopted rather than invented anew.

"Portrait of a Young Venetian Woman" (also referred to as "Portrait of a Venetian Woman") is a small bust-length portrait executed in oil on an elm panel by the German artist Albrecht Dürer in 1505. It was painted during Dürer's second visit to Italy, a period in which he produced several other portraits of high-society individuals.

The Portrait of a Venetian Woman shares a pose and tonal approach with the artist's circa 1507 painting depicting a German woman from Venice. Two additional studies of Venetian women by the same artist are known, both described as particularly daring. One of these studies presents the model wearing a plunging neckline, while the other reveals bare shoulders.

Ed Overholser (June 20, 1869 – April 21, 1931) was an American political figure who served as the sixteenth mayor of Oklahoma City and later served as president of the Oklahoma City Chamber of Commerce.

Ed Overholser was born in Sullivan, Indiana, the son of Henry Overholser and Emma Hanna Overholser. He was educated in public schools and later attended a preparatory school for boys in Kansas. He arrived in Oklahoma City on April 2, 1890, and subsequently assumed management of the Overholser Opera House.

Municipalities represent the lowest level of Brazil's political divisions and have both political and economic autonomy. The country is divided into 5,569 municipalities, which together cover nearly the entire national territory. The Federal District diverges from this pattern, as it is not subdivided into municipalities; instead, it is divided into 35 administrative regions and lacks political autonomy. A further exception is the Fernando de Noronha archipelago, which is designated as a state district of Pernambuco rather than a municipality.

Brazilian states and the Federal District are subdivided for statistical purposes into Intermediate Geographic Regions, each of which is further divided into Immediate Geographic Regions; the latter are designed to correspond to metropolitan areas. From 1989 to 2017, these divisions were grouped into mesoregions and microregions as the previous organizational framework.

Private Eye is a British satirical magazine that has occasionally drawn complaints tied to its coverage of major events. Following the Ladbroke Grove rail crash in 1999, issue 987 sparked reader complaints, while the September 11 attacks in 2001 prompted further criticisms in issue 1037, which also included a subscription cancellation coupon for dissatisfied readers. The Soham murders in 2002 attracted similar complaints, and after the 7/7 London bombings in 2005, issue 1137 featured a Blair–Livingstone cover about tracking down the mastermind and inviting him for tea, in connection with Yusuf al-Qaradawi’s invitation to London.

Private Eye has drawn sustained attention for its combination of humor and investigative reporting aimed at challenging elite hypocrisy and has, for roughly five decades, provoked strong reactions among powerful interests. Unite chief of staff Andrew Murray described the magazine as a publication created by diligent public-school alumni and argued that its treatment of trade unions has consistently reflected cynicism and hostility. The Socialist Worker credited Private Eye with upsetting and enraging the powerful for around fifty years through this distinctive mix of wit and scrutiny, while also noting criticisms such as snobbery and prejudice; it contended that jokes about the poor, women, and young people rely on crude stereotypes and described the publication as embodying an anti-establishment stance that sits within establishment circles.

Derde Klasse is a Dutch football division in which each division comprises fourteen teams. The champion of the division is promoted to the Tweede Klasse, while the teams finishing in 13th and 14th place are relegated to the Vierde Klasse. The season is divided into a number of periodes (periods), and the winners of these periods earn a place in the promotion playoffs, provided they also finish among the top nine overall in the season standings. The team finishing 12th in the final rankings enters relegation playoffs.

Derde Klasse, a term translating to "Third Class," denotes the eighth tier of Dutch football and the sixth tier within Dutch amateur football. The competition is organized into 37 divisions, of which 20 are played on Saturdays and 17 on Sundays.

On 23 May 2001, the final of the 2000–01 UEFA Champions League was staged at the San Siro in Milan, Italy, between Bayern Munich and Valencia. The match finished 1–1 and was decided on penalties, with Bayern prevailing 5–4. The victory gave Bayern their fourth European Cup/Champions League title and their first since 1976, ending a 25-year wait. The game is noted for featuring only goals from penalties, with Bayern missing a spot kick in normal time. Valencia suffered a second consecutive final defeat and had, up to that point, reached finals in the competition on only two occasions. Both clubs had been runners-up in the previous season, Bayern in 1999 to Manchester United and Valencia in 2000 to Real Madrid.

The 2001 UEFA Champions League Final was the sixth European Cup/Champions League final decided by a penalty shootout and the second final contested under the Champions League format. Ottmar Hitzfeld secured his second Champions League trophy, having previously won with Borussia Dortmund in 1997, and thus became the second coach to lift the competition with two different clubs, a distinction previously achieved by Ernst Happel. Conversely, Héctor Cúper endured his third consecutive European final defeat, after losses in the 1999 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final with Mallorca and the 2000 Champions League final with Valencia.

On Debian, the alien utility is used to facilitate practical Linux Standard Base compatibility, enabling Debian systems to work with LSB-conformant packages in practice. By contrast, the description that accompanies the lsb package explicitly states that its mere presence does not imply that Debian fully conforms to the Linux Standard Base, and it should not be taken as an assertion that Debian is LSB-compliant.

Linux Standard Base implements an interface deprecation policy designed to preserve backward compatibility across its releases. Under this policy, interfaces slated for removal are first designated as deprecated in a given LSB release. The deprecated interfaces remain supported during that release and for at least two subsequent LSB releases, providing a predictable window for transition. This approach gives developers time to adapt and plan for changes, enabling continued reliance on chosen interfaces for a known period before they are removed.

The Allegiance Council, a Saudi body established to oversee royal succession and related appointments, has in practice reflected a preselected line of succession after Crown Prince Sultan, with three successors treated as automatic. The appointment of the second deputy prime minister is governed by the king's writ, underscoring the primacy of the monarch's prerogative in high-level staffing. Additionally, the designation deputy crown prince is a relatively recent honorific compared with the substantive office it denotes. Consequently, the Allegiance Council has effectively functioned as a rubber-stamp body, approving outcomes rather than independently determining them.

The Allegiance Council, known in Arabic as Hay’at al-Bay‘ah, is a Saudi body established to determine future succession to the throne. It has also been referred to as the Allegiance Commission, the Allegiance Institution, or the Succession Commission. Formed on 7 December 2007 by King Abdullah, the council was created with the principal aim of overseeing the selection of a Crown Prince upon the accession of a new king, thereby shaping the line of succession.

Music recording sales certifications are typically awarded in the form of physical plaques that encase a variety of items under glass. In modern practice, many of these awards favor compact discs over vinyl records. In many cases, the so-called gold or platinum records are, in fact, vinyl discs that have undergone vacuum metallization to apply a metallic layer and have been color-tinted to achieve their signature appearance. In the early era of these awards, the production chain relied on metal components—trimmed and plated “masters,” “mothers,” or “stampers”—which were used to press the vinyl records. It is possible that the music encoded in the grooves does not always align with the specific recording recognized by the award.

IMPALA, an acronym for the Independent Music Companies Association, was established in April 2000 with the aim of nurturing the independent music sector and promoting autonomy for artists, entrepreneurial initiatives, and cultural diversity across Europe. The organization seeks to foster growth within independent music and to support diverse artistic and commercial ecosystems, emphasizing independence in both creative and business spheres. In 2005, IMPALA launched its own sales awards, the first pan-European recognition scheme to acknowledge that broad European success can begin before reaching one million sales.

Stream pools are deeper, slower-flowing sections of streams that provide specialized aquatic habitat for organisms that struggle to feed or navigate in faster reaches or in seasonally warmer water. They can serve as important fish habitat, especially where streams experience high summer temperatures and markedly reduced flows during the dry season. In warm and arid regions, thermal stratification within pools yields cooler sub-surface waters that favor species adapted to lower temperatures, such as redband trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) in the Western United States. Additionally, the relatively calm or still conditions in pools support mosquito larvae, which prefer low-velocity water environments.

A stream pool is a term in hydrology that designates a particular reach of a river or stream. In such a pool, the water depth exceeds the average depth for the channel, and the flow velocity is lower than average.
COVID-19 is a contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2. In January 2020, the illness spread worldwide, and this extensive transmission culminated in the COVID-19 pandemic.

Immunocompromised individuals are generally considered more likely to experience severe illness from SARS-CoV-2 infection. A study of hospitalized COVID-19 cases among kidney transplant recipients found an 11% mortality rate, illustrating the elevated risk faced by this immunosuppressed subgroup.

Following the January 1947 promulgation of the Republic of China's constitution, the China Democratic Socialist Party established branches in numerous provinces and cities across China. The party participated in the inaugural elections for the National Assembly, Legislative Yuan, and Control Yuan. In the 1948 First National Assembly held in Nanking, the CDSP nominated Hsu Fu-lin as its candidate for vice-president of the Assembly.

The China Democratic Socialist Party (CDSP) was established in Shanghai on 14 August 1946 through the merger of the Chinese State Socialist Party and the Democratic Constitutionalist Party. Its inaugural leader was Carsun Chang. The party became one of the longest-running political organizations within Nationalist China and, after the civil war, in the rump Republic of China based in Taiwan, operating alongside the Kuomintang, the Young China Party, and the China Democratic League.

Vat Phou is a Khmer temple complex that formed part of the Khmer Empire, whose political center was Angkor located to the southwest, a status evidenced at least by the reign of Yasovarman I in the early 10th century. The city known as Shrestapura was later superseded by a new Angkorian-period urban center situated directly south of the temple. In subsequent periods, the original structures were replaced, with some of the earlier stone blocks reused in the construction of the present edifice, which mostly dates to the Koh Ker and Baphuon phases of the 11th century. Minor changes were made during the following two centuries. As was typical for Khmer temples, Vat Phou was subsequently converted to Theravada Buddhist use.

Vat Phou, also known as Vat Phu, is a ruined temple complex of Khmer-Hindu origin located in southern Laos at the base of Mount Phou Khao in Champasak Province, about six kilometres (3.7 miles) from the Mekong River. The Lao name ວັດພູ, transliterated as wāt pʰúː, means "temple-mountain." The site is recognized as one of the oldest places of worship in Southeast Asia, reflecting its long-standing religious significance in the region.

On the eve of the United States entry into World War II, American air warfare policy was shaped by a transitional reorganization and strategic emphasis. In late June 1941, the Army Air Corps was transformed into the United States Army Air Forces, signaling a shift toward a more centralized and expansive air-centric military framework prior to Pearl Harbor. President Franklin D. Roosevelt directed Admiral Ernest J. King to lead the Navy with a mandate to pursue an aviation-focused war in the Pacific, including authority to bolster land-based naval and Marine aviation and to seize control of long-range bombers then employed in antisubmarine patrols in the Atlantic. Roosevelt also aligned with Lovett’s perspective that air power would be essential to victory but cautioned that it would not be the sole determinant of the war’s outcome.

Facing the prospect of intensified Japanese resistance, including an uptick in kamikaze attacks if the main islands were invaded, United States high command rethought its air warfare strategy and adjusted its operational priorities accordingly. Atomic weapons were then employed to hasten the end of the war, with the aim of compelling Japan to surrender and thereby making a costly invasion of the home islands unnecessary.

Animation Magazine Inc publishes a suite of annual and special issues for the animation industry, including an annual Tradeshow Calendar, a Career and Education guide, and five special issues devoted to the Oscars and Emmys issued throughout the year. The publication's website provides daily animation news updates on weekdays. AniMagTV is a portal on the site featuring concise reports on animation events, short films, and trailers. The publisher maintains archives of earlier editions, and offers subscriptions in both digital and print formats.

Animation Magazine is an American publication available in both print and online formats, providing coverage of the animation sector, its educational dimensions, and visual effects. The print edition is issued ten times annually in the United States.

Driglam Namzha is the Bhutanese code of dress and etiquette that governs traditional attire. In men's clothing, the gho is a heavy knee-length robe secured with a belt, with the fabric folded to create a pocket in front of the abdomen. Women's dress comprises a wonju, a long-sleeved blouse, paired with a kira, a large rectangular cloth folded and clasped to form an ankle-length dress. An optional outer layer, either a short silk jacket or a toego, may be worn over the kira. Everyday versions of the gho and kira are typically made from cotton or wool and chosen according to the season, featuring simple checks and stripes in earth-tone hues. For special occasions, a variegated, patterned silk kira may be worn, with the gho being worn less frequently.

Driglam Namzha is a codified set of guidelines governing Bhutan's dress, etiquette, architecture, and ceremonial practices, with origins in 17th-century decrees issued by Ngawang Namgyal, the first Zhabdrung Rinpoche. Ngawang Namgyal, a Tibetan lama and military leader, sought to unify Bhutan politically and culturally, and accordingly established normative rules for dzong architecture—the fortress-monasteries that characterize Bhutan's religious and administrative centers—and formalized numerous traditions associated with the Tshechu district festivals, including the Cham dance. The codification was intended to foster a distinct Bhutanese identity by standardizing political, cultural, and ceremonial practices across the country.

Oryol's urban planning history begins with proposals from 1728 prepared by Mikhail Buzovlev and Petr Botvinev. In 1778, a plan solidified the radial layout of the city, and the following year a radial-semicircular configuration was proposed. By 1848, a renewed plan incorporating Polesskaya Square received approval, marking a significant development in the city's architectural planning.

Oryol has been connected by rail to Moscow since 1868, illustrating its long-standing role in the Russian railway network. The city now functions as a major railway hub, with five lines converging there: to Yelets, Moscow, Kursk, Bryansk, and the Mikhailovsky mine.

Soho, a district in central London, is notable for John Snow's study of the 1854 cholera outbreak that occurred there. Snow identified the outbreak's source as the public water pump at the junction of Broad Street (now Broadwick Street) and Cambridge Street (now Lexington Street), a finding widely regarded as a watershed in epidemiology and public health. The pump stood near the rear wall of the building that today houses the John Snow public house.

During the 20th century, Soho’s pubs and private members clubs attracted notoriety for their owners and the circles of clientele they served. Notable regulars included Jeffrey Barnard and the artist Francis Bacon, as identified by Clive Jennings. A notorious trio—comprising The French, The Coach & Horses, and The Colony—functioned as staging points for the Dean Street shuffle, with occasional forays to other venues such as The Gargoyle, Mandrake, The Groucho, or Blacks. Christopher Howse describes a bohemian coterie of heavy drinkers in Soho, and notes that pensions mattered little because life expectancy reportedly remained short.

The Requiem in D minor by Anton Bruckner is a setting of the Missa pro defunctis for mixed choir with vocal soloists, three trombones, a horn, strings and organ with figured bass. Composed in memory of Franz Sailer, the notary of the St. Florian Monastery who bequeathed Bruckner a Bösendorfer piano, the work reflects his early sacred choral concerns. It was first performed on 15 September 1849 in the St. Florian Monastery, roughly a year after Sailer's death, with a second performance taking place on 11 December 1849 at the Abbey of Kremsmünster. The original manuscript is preserved in the archive of the St. Florian Monastery.

The Requiem by Anton Bruckner occupies a comparatively modest place within his body of work, attracting less attention than his more prominent compositions. There are approximately twenty recordings of the Requiem, with the majority originating from live performances. These live recordings have not been released on the commercial market, resulting in limited availability in standard consumer catalogs.

Apache Directory is an open-source project of the Apache Software Foundation. The Apache Directory Server is an embeddable directory server written entirely in Java. The project was originally authored by Alex Karasulu. In 2006, The Open Group certified its LDAPv3 compatibility. The server also supports protocols beyond LDAP.

Religious life in Tonga includes the Baháʼí Faith, which began to be introduced through a targeted effort in 1953 and saw Baháʼís arrive in 1954. The community grew sufficiently that the first Local Spiritual Assembly was elected in 1958, reflecting both local conversions and the work of early pioneers. In 1996, the Ocean of Light International School was established and subsequently became Tonga's principal Baháʼí educational institution. By around 2004, there were 29 Local Spiritual Assemblies and approximately 5% of the nation's population identifying as Baháʼí. The religion's activities experienced state-level restrictions, with the Tonga Broadcasting Commission prohibiting discussions of Baháʼu'lláh, the Baháʼí founder, on its radio broadcasts.

Religion in Tonga is rooted in a predominantly Christian landscape, where Tongan Christians and other Pacific Islanders have developed contextual theologies tailored to Pacific realities. These theological approaches seek to address questions raised by Pacific communities about faith, culture, and everyday life, and they are expressed across denominations. Notable examples include the coconut theology advanced within the Methodist tradition by Sione ’Amanaki Havea, which uses the coconut as a culturally resonant symbol for Christian meaning, and the incarnational theology associated with Patelesio Finau, the Catholic Bishop of Tonga, which emphasizes the presence of the divine in human embodiment within local contexts.

Ring III: Berlanga vs. Sheeraz was the third installment in The Ring's boxing series, and it represented the first occasion on which the event title explicitly employed The Ring branding. The event took place on July 12, 2025.

The Ring, commonly referred to as Ring magazine, is a periodical devoted to boxing. It first appeared in 1922 as a publication that covered both boxing and professional wrestling. Subsequently, the magazine narrowed its focus to boxing, abandoning the broader coverage after questions arose about the legitimacy of professional wrestling.

Musselman Lake, Ontario contains Coultice Park, a five-acre municipal park that officially opened on June 17, 2017. The park is situated on land that was formerly part of the Wagon Wheel Ranch, and the property was donated to the town by the Coultice family.

Musselman's Lake is a community in Ontario that sits near several regional transportation routes. It is accessible from Highway 48, the route that links Toronto with Beaverton. About nine kilometres to the west, Highway 404 can be reached via Aurora Road or Bloomington Road, the latter identified as a limited-access 400-Series highway. Ontario Highway 407 lies roughly twenty kilometres south, accessed along Ninth Line in Markham. In the community, the principal thoroughfares are Ninth Line on the western side and Lakeshore Road on the eastern edge. The surrounding area includes a cluster of smaller kettle lakes, namely Island Lake, Shadow Lake, Staley Lake, and Windsor Lake. The Musselman's Lake area drains into a small tributary that feeds the East Holland River, which runs westward.

List of U.S. state mottos documents that all 50 states have an official motto, and the District of Columbia and three territories also maintain mottos. A motto is a concise phrase intended to describe the general motivation or guiding aim of an organization or polity. State mottos may appear on state seals or on state flags. Some states officially designate their motto by act of the legislature, while in others the motto exists as part of the state seal without separate statutory designation. The national motto of the United States is In God We Trust, proclaimed by Congress and signed into law by President Eisenhower on July 30, 1956. By contrast, E pluribus unum was approved for the Great Seal in 1782 but was never adopted as the national motto through legislative action.

Dates displayed in the list reflect, where possible, the earliest official usage of each motto. When a motto is not officially adopted but appears on the state seal, the adoption date of that seal is provided instead. Notably, the earliest recorded use of a motto still in use today is Puerto Rico’s Joannes est nomen ejus, a Latin motto granted by the Crown of Spain in 1511.

The Garfagnana is a predominantly mountainous region in northern Tuscany, characterized by heavy rainfall and extensive woodlands, where stands of Castanea sativa (sweet chestnut) are common. Historically, chestnuts formed an important part of the local diet, contributing to the cultural and agricultural landscape of the area. The region is also recognized for its specialty products, including Farina di Neccio della Garfagnana (chestnut flour), which has DOP status, and Farro della Garfagnana, which has IGP status. In addition to chestnuts, the Garfagnana is known for lentils and porcini mushrooms. It is the origin of several traditional livestock breeds, notably the Garfagnina cattle, the Garfagnina goat, and the Garfagnina Bianca sheep.

A powerful earthquake struck the Garfagnana and Lunigiana regions on 7 September 1920, causing extensive damage and casualties. Villa Collemandina endured the most severe destruction and registered the highest death toll in the affected area. Seismic intensity measurements recorded the strongest shaking at Villa Collemandina and at Fivizzano, reflecting the localized severity of the event.

Austria maintains some of the highest costs for health services within the European Union. In 2019, health spending per capita in Austria was the third highest among EU member states. Additionally, out-of-pocket expenditures for health care in Austria exceed the EU average.

Austria's long-standing status as a European power and its rich cultural milieu have supported wide-ranging contributions to the arts, notably music. The country is the birthplace of numerous celebrated composers, including Joseph Haydn, Michael Haydn, Franz Liszt, Franz Schubert, Anton Bruckner, Johann Strauss Sr., and Johann Strauss Jr. Austria also produced several figures associated with the Second Viennese School, such as Arnold Schoenberg, Anton Webern, and Alban Berg. Mozart was born in Salzburg, then an independent Church Principality within the Holy Roman Empire and later part of Austria, and he spent a substantial portion of his career in Vienna.

Léon Blum, a leading figure of the French Socialist Party and a former architect of the Popular Front, faced a decisive moment in July 1940 as the country confronted the prospect of dissolution under Vichy rule. In a speech by Laval, the former prime minister argued that the Front populaire had weakened France and contributed to the 1940 defeat, while Blum was accused of undermining Laval’s policy toward Italy, a claim Laval connected to the outbreak of war. Blum chose not to rebut the speech, stating he felt overwhelmed by what he had witnessed, including caucus corruption, and perceived the republic’s collapse. He stood largely alone during the joint session as numerous pro-democracy leaders were absent.
