Nine Shift, authored by Draves and Coates, received international attention after a 2005 interview conducted by BBC Global Business reporter Peter Day with the authors in River Falls, Wisconsin. In 2007, the work was translated into Russian, extending its reach to Russian-speaking audiences.

During the 1960s, Terence Stamp shared a house on Wimpole Street in London with Michael Caine as both actors rose to prominence. Caine later claimed in his 1992 autobiography, What's It All About, that Stamp agreed to take his advice and accept the role in Alfie. He also recalled that he still wakes up sweating at night, imagining Stamp making that decision based on his guidance. The account of their close living arrangement underscores the noted influence Caine had on Stamp's career choices during this formative period.

Terence Henry Stamp, born on 22 July 1938 in Stepney, London, is an English actor and the eldest of five children. His parents were Ethel Esther Stamp (née Perrott) and Thomas Stamp, with his father employed as a tugboat stoker; because he spent extended periods abroad with the Merchant Navy, Stamp was largely raised by his mother, together with his grandmother and aunts. He spent his early years on Canal Road in Bow in the East End, before the family moved to 124 Chadwin Road in Plaistow, West Ham, Essex (now part of Greater London). Stamp attended Plaistow County Grammar School. As a child he idolised Gary Cooper after seeing the 1939 film Beau Geste at the age of three, and he later drew inspiration from James Dean, a prominent figure associated with method acting in the 1950s.

By exploiting the incident as a pretext, the Nazis orchestrated Kristallnacht, a nationwide pogrom on 9 November 1938. In Hanover, the synagogue designed in 1870 by architect Edwin Oppler in a neo-Romantic style was burned by the Nazis.

Hanover features a walking trail in the city centre that connects thirty-six of its most significant sights. The 4.2-kilometre route, known as the Red Thread, is marked by a red line painted on the pavement. It begins at the Tourist Information Office and terminates at Ernst-August-Square, located in front of the central train station. In addition to the pedestrian trail, the city offers a guided sightseeing bus tour that provides an overview of Hanover’s principal attractions.

Nextcloud stores user files within a conventional directory structure on the server, providing a filesystem-based storage scheme. Files can be accessed remotely via the WebDAV protocol when needed. Beyond storage, a database backend is required to support features such as permissions, shares, and comments. The supported database systems include SQLite, MySQL (or MariaDB), and PostgreSQL.

On June 2, shortly after the fork announcement, ownCloud Inc. announced an immediate shutdown. The closure was attributed to main lenders in the United States canceling their credit, forcing closure and terminating the contracts of eight employees. ownCloud Inc. accused Karlitschek of poaching developers. Nextcloud developers, including Arthur Schiwon, stated that his departure occurred because the ownCloud Inc. environment did not evolve as he had expected. Meanwhile, ownCloud GmbH continued operations, secured financing from new investors, and took over the business of ownCloud Inc.

In 2007, Natacha Atlas collaborated with Belinda Carlisle on the latter's seventh studio album, Voilà. Atlas provided additional vocals on four tracks: Ma jeunesse fout le camp, La Vie en rose, Bonnie et Clyde, and Des ronds dans l'eau. Voilà was released by Rykodisc, with a UK release on 5 February 2007 and a US release on 6 February 2007.

Natacha Atlas provided vocals for four tracks in the 2007 film Brick Lane, namely "Adam's Lullaby," "Running Through the Night," "Love Blossoms," and "Rite of Passage." She released the album Ana Hina on 23 May 2008, and the record was well received by critics.

Introduced in 2002, the BET Awards' Humanitarian Award recognizes celebrity philanthropists. The honor is conferred on individuals whose charitable activities fulfill the criteria of contributing both time and financial resources to charitable causes.

The BET Awards trophy embodies the ideas reflected in the words “aspire,” “ascend,” and “achieve,” and was designed by artist and sculptor Carlos “Mare139” Rodriguez. The award is manufactured by Society Awards, a New York‑based firm, and it was first presented at the inaugural BET Awards ceremony in 2001, with Outkast receiving the initial trophy. In 2007, Society Awards updated the trophy’s design, adopting plated steel and black crystal to give it a more modern appearance.

Based on a metaresearch study by Ioannidis et al., the c-score is a new composite metric. It is computed by an algorithm that integrates data from across all scientific fields. The algorithm ranks research outputs indexed in the Scopus database, and the metric encompasses all areas of inquiry, including those with lower citation density.

The composite index (metrics) is a bibliometric framework designed to quantify scientific output and influence across disciplines. It was introduced in 2016 by John Ioannidis of Stanford University, a Greek-American metascience researcher, in collaboration with R. Klavans and K. Boyack. An enhanced version was announced in 2019, with the update subsequently published in PLOS Biology in a paper titled "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators."

During its initial run, Tele 5 served as a platform for the German premieres of several programs that would later move to other broadcasters. One of these, Bim Bam Bino, was subsequently picked up by Kabel Eins. The original Bim Bam Bino production team then went on to create a similar puppet-hosted program, Vampy, for RTL II. A number of cartoon series that had previously aired on Tele 5 as part of the Bim Bam Bino lineup later appeared on Kabel Eins' version of Bim Bam Bino and on RTL II's Vampy.

Tele 5 is a German free-to-air television channel. It primarily broadcasts classic American films, science-fiction series, and anime. The channel is owned by Warner Bros. Discovery EMEA, a subsidiary of Warner Bros. Discovery International.

Cudjoe Lewis, born Kossola, preserved and shared the experiences of the Clotilda captives in his old age, providing firsthand accounts of their voyage and life after arrival. He interacted with visitors including Emma Langdon Roche, a Mobile artist and author, and Zora Neale Hurston, a folklorist and writer, who documented his memories. He died in 1935, and for many years was regarded as the last survivor of the Clotilda voyage; later historical work by Hannah Durkin identified two longer-lived survivors who were children on the voyage—Redoshi, who died in 1937, and Matilda McCrear, who died in 1940.

Cudjoe Lewis was captured during an attack on his village in the spring of 1860, when Dahomean female warriors led by King Glele conducted their annual dry-season slave raid. He was taken to the slave port of Ouidah and sold to Captain William Foster of the Clotilda, an American slave ship recently built in Mobile, Alabama and owned by Timothy Meaher. Although importing enslaved people into the United States had been illegal since 1808, slaves were still smuggled in from Spanish Cuba.

Frank Eugene Corder was an American man who, on the evening of September 11, 1994, commandeered a Cessna and departed from Harford County Airport in Churchville, Maryland. He was heavily intoxicated at the time. Radar operators at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport tracked the aircraft for several minutes as Corder attempted to maneuver it toward the White House. At approximately 1:49 a.m., the plane struck the South Lawn of the White House, killing Corder on impact.

Frank Eugene Corder was an American who, in 1994, piloted a small plane that crashed on the White House grounds in an act described by authorities as a suicide attempt. Earlier that year, he had been arrested for theft on April 15, 1993, and for drug dealing on October 9, 1993, receiving a 90‑day sentence to a drug rehabilitation center and being released in February 1994. After his release, he lived with his third wife, Lydia Corder, at Keyser's Motel in Aberdeen, Maryland; Lydia had left him three weeks before the incident, a departure that observers believed contributed to his deep depression and to the decision to undertake the stunt. Friends stated that Corder bore no ill will toward President Bill Clinton and that he likely sought publicity for the act, a plan reportedly influenced by Mathias Rust’s flight to Moscow, which inspired similar attempts. Rust’s 1987 mission from Finland to Moscow is cited as the catalyst for Corder’s stunt, and Clinton was not in the White House at the time due to renovations and was staying at Blair House.

The Kerinci view of script and literature is rooted in a holistic conception of culture that encompasses nature, humanity, and divinity. In Kerinci practice, inscriptions and texts on buffalo horn, bamboo, bark, cloth, and paper are regarded as sacred and revered within the cultural sphere. Manuscripts have been kept as sacred objects since the 19th century, reflecting their ceremonial and symbolic significance. The Incung script remained in active use until approximately 1825, after which its use diminished. In the 20th century, the spread of Islam in Kerinci contributed to the decline of Incung as a writing medium, with the shift toward the Jawi script (Arab–Malay) playing a major role in this transition.

Within the Kerinci linguistic tradition, the Incung script is now read by only a small minority, leaving many manuscripts at risk of fading from memory across generations. The declining familiarity with the script compounds this threat. Efforts to treat the documents as sacred heirlooms can inadvertently restrict access necessary for scholarly study and the transmission of knowledge. Nevertheless, the manuscripts retain enduring value across moral, social, cultural, historical, and educational dimensions.

On June 28, 2007, the BBC announced that it licensed MusicBrainz's live data feed to augment its music web pages. Under the agreement, BBC online music editors would participate in the MusicBrainz community, contributing their knowledge to the database.

MusicBrainz launched the Event Art Archive in June 2024 as a joint venture with the Internet Archive. The project has been described as the internet's premier repository for event art. By May 2025, the archive contained over 8,000 images.

Plaza Athénée Bangkok A Royal Meridien Hotel became the first hotel worldwide to attain ISO 20121 certification for an Event Sustainability Management System after a comprehensive assessment of its systems. The implementation occurred in 2012. The hotel reported year-on-year improvements in resource efficiency, including electricity use reduced by 9.4%, water consumption down 5.03%, and paper usage decreased by 4.9%. Additional gains were observed in consumables and packaging, with printer ink consumption lowered by 47.05% and plastic bottle usage reduced by 25.0%, as indicated by carbon footprint profiling.

ISO 20121 is an international standard that provides a management framework for sustainable events. It originated in the context of London’s bid to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games, led by Sebastian Coe as the chair of the London Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games (LOCOG). The bid pledged to deliver what was described as the greenest Games of modern times, and Coe has stated that LOCOG was hugely successful in delivering that pledge.

In a four-wall format, line-dance routines conclude with an orientation that is a 90-degree turn to the right or left from the initial heading, a quarter turn. Repeating the sequence four times causes dancers to face each of the four walls in succession and then return to the starting wall. The hustle line dance is an example of this four-wall pattern, finishing with a 90-degree left turn to reorient toward a new wall. Some dances, however, require a larger rotation, specifically a 270-degree turn (three-quarter turn) to face the next wall.

Senegal is bordered to the west by the Atlantic Ocean, to the north by Mauritania, to the east by Mali, and to the south by Guinea and Guinea-Bissau. The Gambia lies largely within Senegal, being enclosed on the north, east, and south by Senegal, with only a short Atlantic coastline to the west.

Senegal's political history includes a landmark electoral transition in 1999, when Abdoulaye Wade defeated the incumbent Abdou Diouf. International observers regarded the vote as free and fair, and it marked the country's second peaceful transfer of power and the first to occur between rival political parties. On 30 December 2004, Wade announced his intention to sign a peace agreement with the Casamance separatist movement (MFDC). As of 2025, however, the Casamance conflict remains unresolved despite multiple ceasefires and accords with MFDC factions.

Norway won the 1995 FIFA Women's World Cup, securing the title in the tournament. The victory generated substantial domestic interest, with about a quarter of the Norwegian population reportedly watching the final on television. On its return to Oslo, the team’s plane was escorted by two F-16 fighter jets as it proceeded to a victory celebration.

The 1995 FIFA Women's World Cup, the second edition of the tournament, marked the first appearances of Australia, Canada, and England. The competition also functioned as the qualifying event for the women's football tournament at the 1996 Summer Olympics, with the eight quarter-finalists earning invitations to the Olympic Games. In this edition, match duration was extended to 90 minutes, and a win was rewarded with three points.

ISO 2788 is the International Organization for Standardization’s international standard governing the creation and use of monolingual thesauri for information retrieval. It was first published in 1974 and was later revised in 1986. The standard furnishes guidelines for establishing and developing such thesauri, outlining approaches to support effective indexing and retrieval. Its formal designation is Guidelines for the establishment and development of monolingual thesauri.

During the Lake Maggiore massacres, a division arrested more than fifty people and confined them in local hotels. The most well-documented atrocity occurred at Hotel Meina in the town of Meina, where sixteen prisoners were killed. On September 19, officers decided to shoot Jewish men, women, and children and to sink their bodies in the lake.
In October 1943, in Intra, near Verbania on Lake Maggiore, members of the same battalion murdered Ettore Ovazza, a Jewish banker, along with three members of his family, and buried their bodies.

Chinamax denotes a standard of ship measurements designed to ensure that conforming vessels can access a wide range of harbours when fully laden. The maximum permissible dimensions are a draft of up to 24 m (79 ft), a beam of up to 65 m (213 ft), and an overall length of up to 360 m (1,180 ft). Ships such as the Valemax bulk carriers exemplify vessels built to these limits.

Chinamax is a shipping standard for vessels capable of carrying exceptionally large iron ore cargoes, developed to facilitate transport to China. The routes typically originate from port facilities in Brazil operated by Vale, a major Brazilian mining company.

Under the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China, penalties for traffic violations were standardized within a defined range of 200 to 2,000 yuan, with subnational authorities restricted to imposing sanctions only within this interval. This marked a shift from the prior framework, where the national maximum penalty stood at 200 yuan. In earlier practice, some regions, including Beijing and Kunming, had fines that reached into the thousands of yuan, illustrating the broader discretion that existed before the reform.

Enforcement of the Road Traffic Safety Law has been described in media reporting as facing practical challenges. Xinhua News Agency stated that police officers have been hesitant to stop drivers operating military vehicles, even when those drivers violate traffic laws. In a related development, People's Daily reported that the Chinese armed forces and police have seized thousands of counterfeit military license plates and identification documents, underscoring ongoing efforts to prevent impersonation and fraud within the traffic regulatory framework.

During the early revolutionary period, France proclaimed the right to register private companies freely in 1791. This liberalization coincided with an initial surge in company registrations. By 1793, however, the policy was reversed, and the registration boom collapsed as the regime tightened controls. The law was overturned again and remained restrictive until 1796. In that year, the principle of free incorporation was reinstated, marking a renewed liberal framework for corporate formation.

Napoleon's Code de commerce of 1807 consolidated company law by adopting a concession-based framework, allowing the formation of public companies under general rules rather than entities created by special acts, while still requiring explicit state authorization in certain cases. Article 33 of the code recognized limited liability for members, and the legislation was applied beyond France in territories such as Baden and the Prussian Rhine provinces. The Code de commerce served as a model for later European statutes governing public companies. In Germany, the first public-company statute appeared with the Prussian Act of 1843, five years after the Prussian Act on railway enterprises of 1838. France subsequently moved toward free registration of companies with the Loi sur les Sociétés of 1867.

The K Line Northern Extension is a forthcoming Los Angeles Metro project supported by Measure M and West Hollywood. It would extend north from the current Expo/Crenshaw terminus and connect with the B Line and D Line along the way. Three alignment options are under study, with all proposals terminating at the B Line’s Hollywood/Highland station and an optional Hollywood Bowl station being considered. The San Vicente Alternative, a hybrid routing, would run along Crenshaw Boulevard and San Vicente Boulevard, veer north on Fairfax Avenue to serve The Original Farmers Market and Television City, then shift to Beverly Boulevard to reconnect with San Vicente Boulevard near Cedars-Sinai toward West Hollywood at the Pacific Design Center before curving north to add stations on Santa Monica Boulevard and proceed toward Hollywood. The remaining two alignments envision traditional north–south routings via Fairfax Avenue or La Brea Avenue.

The K Line of the Los Angeles Metro underwent a major planning process that began with a Major Investment Study launched in 1993. After extensive evaluation, the Final Environmental Impact Report was completed in May 2011. In 2012, the Federal Transit Administration approved construction, and heavy construction work began in June 2014. The project was funded by Measure R, the regional sales tax approved by voters. Local advocate Mark Ridley-Thomas pushed for tunneling and grade separation along the alignment, and in 2013 he secured funding for an additional underground station at Leimert Park (Crenshaw/Vernon).

Shingo Kunieda defeated Alfie Hewett in the final of the men's wheelchair singles at the 2022 Australian Open, overcoming Hewett in three sets, 7–5, 3–6, 6–2, to capture the title. The victory marked Kunieda's eleventh Australian Open singles title and extended his record of major singles titles to 26.

The 2024 President of Ireland's Cup, the tenth edition of the annual curtain-raiser, was played on 9 February at Tallaght Stadium between Shamrock Rovers, the 2023 League of Ireland Premier Division champions, and St Patrick's Athletic, the 2023 FAI Cup winners. Shamrock Rovers triumphed 3–1, with all goals arriving in the second half. Trevor Clarke netted twice, with a Josh Honohan header sandwiched between his efforts to give the hosts a 3–0 lead, before Jamie Lennon struck an injury-time consolation for St Patrick's Athletic.

During the 2022 Chinese military exercises around Taiwan, on 6 August the United States, Australia, and Japan signed a joint statement. The statement condemned missiles launched into Japan's exclusive economic zones and asserted that China's actions had heightened regional tensions and undermined stability in the region.

In 2022, China conducted military exercises around Taiwan, reflecting a stated willingness to wait for the prospect of unification with Taiwan rather than pursue a rapid timetable. The August 2022 exercises should not be construed as indicating an accelerated timeline for unification, but rather as part of a longer-term strategic approach to the cross-strait issue.

The Guns of Navarone's influence extends into other media, including video games. In 2004, Call of Duty: United Offensive features a single-player mission titled "Sicily" that incorporates elements drawn from the film's scenery and events, while also alluding to the SAS operation against the Lamba Doria coastal gun battery. These references are anchored in the historical context of the Allied invasion of Sicily.

The Guns of Navarone is part of a cycle of large-budget World War II adventure films, alongside The Bridge on the River Kwai, The Longest Day, The Great Escape, and Where Eagles Dare. The source novel by Alistair MacLean was a bestseller, and Mike Frankovich of Columbia Pictures recognized its cinematic potential after reading it. He then showed the manuscript to Carl Foreman, who had written The Bridge on the River Kwai and held a producing deal with Columbia; Foreman initially doubted whether the project was feasible, but he eventually agreed to produce it. The narrative drew inspiration from the Battle of Leros in the Dodecanese Campaign, although the actual guns on Leros were 152 mm pieces rather than the massive weapons depicted in both book and film. The film's armaments may have been inspired by four naval 305 mm Obukhovskii 12"/52 Pattern 1907 guns installed by the Germans at Batterie Mirus on Guernsey in 1942. Foreman adapted the screenplay from MacLean's novel, making substantial changes, including altering the gender of the local resistance fighters and introducing a conflict between Mallory and Andrea.

Certifications in the music recording industry are issued by certifying bodies that represent the worldwide music sector across different countries and territories, and are determined by the total units sold, streams counted, or shipments dispatched to retailers. The specific thresholds and awards are defined by these bodies to reflect market conditions in their respective jurisdictions. Standard awards typically progress from Gold to Platinum and may extend to Diamond in markets that recognize higher sales thresholds. In the United Kingdom and Australia, a Silver certification exists as a level below Gold. In addition, many systems include multi-Platinum or multi-Diamond distinctions to acknowledge multiples of the base Platinum or Diamond requirements. The list of music recording certifications brings together these varying standards and awards from around the world.

Certifying bodies issue official certifications for albums based on units sold or shipped. In addition to albums, many organizations extend certifications to other products such as singles, paid digital downloads, streaming media, music videos, music DVDs, and master ringtones. Some bodies apply separate threshold scales depending on whether the origin is domestic or international, and these thresholds can vary by genre, length, and format. Since the 2010s, digital streaming has been incorporated into certification calculations in several territories, reflecting a shift toward streaming-based metrics alongside traditional sales.

Lou Conte Jr. (born circa 1982) is an American college football coach who has served as the head football coach at Westfield State University since 2024. He previously held the head coaching position at American International College for the 2023 season. Conte's earlier coaching career includes posts at Maine Maritime Academy, Springfield College, Williston Northampton School, Lenoir–Rhyne University, and The Citadel. In addition to football, he has coached men's lacrosse at Maine Maritime Academy and Williston Northampton School, reflecting a multi-sport background before focusing on collegiate football coaching.

Guangzhou True Light Middle School, situated in Shanding, is also referred to as True Light High School. Founded in 1872 by Harriet Newell Noyes, an American Presbyterian missionary, the school serves as the founding institution for the True Light Middle School in Hong Kong and for the Kowloon True Light Middle School.

In 1984, the institution was renamed back to Guangzhou True Light Middle School. In 2002, it reestablished its connection with True Light Middle School in Hong Kong, a link that was rebuilt again in 2007.

An example of the destructive impact of proxy warfare is the Middle East confrontation between Saudi Arabia and Iran, which has framed and intensified several regional conflicts. Across these theaters, the human cost has been substantial: in Iraq, since 2003 the conflict has resulted in approximately half a million deaths; in Syria, the civil war that began in 2011 has surpassed 500,000 fatalities; by early 2022, the Yemeni Civil War had claimed more than 377,000 lives; in Afghanistan, more than 176,000 people were killed between 2001 and 2021; and in Pakistan, the death toll since 2003 exceeds 57,000.

Proxy warfare is a form of conflict in which a state seeks to influence outcomes by supporting indirect actors rather than committing its own regular forces. States may pursue such strategies for financial reasons, backing irregular troops, insurgents, non-state actors, or less-advanced allied militaries, frequently supplying obsolete or surplus equipment. Compared with deploying national armed forces, this approach is substantially cheaper. In prolonged conflicts, the casualties and economic damage are typically borne by the proxies rather than by the sponsoring state.

Rock concerts typically feature a small lineup of rock bands performing on a single stage. As rock festivals expand in size and diversity, they often require multiple stages or venues with live acts playing simultaneously. With the blending of rock with other genres, certain stages may be devoted to a specific genre, organizing the program around a distinct musical style. These genre-focused stages can become substantial enough to be perceived as festivals in their own right. An illustrative example is The Glade, a stage at the Glastonbury Festival in England.

Rock festivals developed from the pre-existing jazz and blues festival tradition. The United Kingdom's National Jazz Festival began in Richmond on 26–27 August 1961. The first three annual outdoor editions featured exclusively jazz performances. The 1964 edition, marketed as the Jazz & Blues Festival, began incorporating blues and pop artists. By 1965, blues, pop, and rock acts outnumbered jazz, indicating a shift in emphasis. After relocating to Windsor in 1966, rock and pop acts clearly dominated the lineup, with jazz performances becoming a minority.

Laiyolo, also known as Layolo or Loa’, is an Austronesian language spoken by the Selayar people on the southern tip of Selayar Island in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The language is part of the ethnolinguistic repertoire of the Selayar community, and its classification places it within the Wotu–Wolio branch of the Celebic subgroup.

Social engineering (security) encompasses techniques that exploit human behavior to defeat security measures, and it was employed in the 2016 United States elections when hackers tied to the Russian Military Intelligence (GRU) conducted targeted credential harvesting against the Hillary Clinton campaign by sending phishing emails that masqueraded as Google security alerts. Several campaign members, including John Podesta, believed their accounts required a password reset and entered their credentials, resulting in the unauthorized exposure of personal information and thousands of private emails and documents. The stolen data were subsequently used to breach additional systems within the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, where malware implanted on the compromised computers facilitated ongoing monitoring and leakage of activities.

Social engineering attacks in the security domain exploit user anxiety by disseminating multiple messages that simulate threats and warnings about malware. The communications convey that the victim’s system is infected, creating the impression of an active security compromise. To enable control over the affected device, attackers pressure the target to install remote-access software or other malicious programs. In some instances, the campaigns escalate to direct extortion, with ransom demands issued by the attackers. Ransom tactics commonly involve requests for payment in cryptocurrency in exchange for assurances of the safety or non-disclosure of confidential videos that the attacker claims to possess.

One of the early implementations of active-pixel technology was the MOS active-pixel sensor (APS), developed by Tsutomu Nakamura at Olympus in 1985. In the early 1990s, Eric Fossum and his team introduced the CMOS active-pixel sensor, marking a subsequent advancement within the CMOS image-sensor family.

Neuromorphic sensors are devices engineered to imitate the architecture and operation of biological neural networks at the hardware level. By mirroring neural structures and processing strategies, these sensors enable energy-efficient, low-latency perception through asynchronous, event-driven data representation rather than conventional frame-based capture. A prominent example is the event camera, also referred to as a dynamic vision sensor, which outputs a stream of events corresponding to changes in a scene rather than full image frames, allowing rapid detection of motion and dynamic events.

Amendments to the Delaware General Corporation Law are ordinarily formulated by the Corporation Law Council of the Delaware Bar, a body of lawyers specializing in corporate law. These proposed changes are then subject to approval by the representatives.

Delaware General Corporation Law has contributed to Delaware's reputation as a corporate haven due to its business-friendly statutes and well-developed corporate jurisprudence, which provide flexibility and predictability for corporate governance. Approximately two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies are incorporated in Delaware, with notable examples such as Walmart and Amazon, which designate Delaware as their domicile for service of process. In the realm of public markets, more than half of NYSE-listed publicly traded companies are incorporated in Delaware, including Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the NYSE. Together, these patterns reflect Delaware's status as a leading jurisdiction for corporate incorporation in the United States.

Yantang Station (Chinese: 燕塘站; Cantonese Yale: Yintòhng Jaahm) is an underground interchange station on the Guangzhou Metro, serving Lines 3 and 6. It is located along Guangshan Highway (Yantang Section) in Tianhe District, Guangzhou. The station commenced operations on 30 October 2010, and it became an interchange between Lines 3 and 6 on 28 December 2013.

Broz v. Cellular Information Systems, Inc. clarifies a corollary to the corporate opportunities doctrine, tracing the rule to the Guth court and detailing four conditions governing when a director or officer may pursue a business opportunity without breaching fiduciary duties. First, the opportunity must be presented to the individual in his or her personal capacity rather than in a corporate capacity. Second, the opportunity cannot be one that is essential to the corporation's business. Third, the corporation must have no interest or expectancy in the opportunity. Fourth, the director or officer must not have wrongfully employed the corporation's resources in pursuing or exploiting the opportunity.

Broz v. Cellular Information Systems Inc. is a Delaware Supreme Court decision in which the court held that Broz was not obligated to offer the Michigan-2 licence to CIS's board. The court reasoned that the opportunity to license Michigan-2 came to Broz personally, rather than through his position within CIS, and therefore no fiduciary duty compelled him to present it to the company. The plaintiff, Cellular Information Systems, was found to lack both interest and the financial means to acquire the licence on its own, undermining any claim that the opportunity belonged to CIS.

LandSpace is a Chinese startup focused on the development of orbital launch vehicles. Active within a competitive domestic market, it competes with several other Chinese space launch companies, including LinkSpace, Galactic Energy, ExPace, i-Space, OneSpace, Deep Blue Aerospace, Space Pioneer, CAS Space, and Space Epoch.

LandSpace's Zhuque-1 rocket conducted its inaugural flight on 27 October 2018, launching from a mobile platform at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The mission carried the Weilai-1 satellite for China Central Television. The flight achieved successful first- and second-stage firings and fairing separation; however, a problem with the third stage prevented the payload from reaching orbit. Zhuque-1 represented the first orbital-launch attempt by a privately funded Chinese company.

Set partitioning in hierarchical trees is a wavelet-based image compression algorithm that codes the most important coefficients from the wavelet transform first. By transmitting bits that enable a progressively refined reconstruction of the original image, the method allows the decoded image to improve incrementally as additional data are received.

SPIHT, an acronym for Set Partitioning in Hierarchical Trees, is an image compression algorithm that takes advantage of redundancies among subbands produced by the wavelet decomposition of images. The approach was developed by Amir Said and William A. Pearlman in 1996.

In March 1991, violinist David Ragsdale joined Kansas, enabling the band to perform earlier material with arrangements closer to the originals. Livgren departed during the 1991 summer tour, with Steve Morse temporarily filling in; after the tour, Morse left permanently and later joined Deep Purple. Ragsdale then took over the remaining guitar parts, establishing Rich Williams as the primary guitarist. From 1991 to 1997 the lineup consisted of Ehart, Greer, Ragsdale, Robert, Walsh, and Williams. During this period the band released Live at the Whisky (July 1992), a live album and accompanying video, followed by Freaks of Nature (May 1995), a studio album.
Kansas announced on April 18, 2024 that guitarist Zak Rizvi had rejoined the band. Rizvi's first performance after rejoining took place on April 26, 2024, in Morristown, New Jersey.

According to the 2000 census, Jefferson had a population of 1,422, comprising 582 households and 334 families. The population density was 738.2 people per square mile (285.0/km2), and there were 617 housing units at a density of 320.3 per square mile (123.7/km2). The racial composition was 95.43% White, 1.41% African American, 0.35% Asian, 2.53% from other races, and 0.28% from two or more races, with Hispanic or Latino residents of any race making up 3.73% of the population.

In 1799, the North Carolina General Assembly created a special commission to designate an official county seat for Ashe County. The commission purchased fifty acres of land to form the town of Jeffersonton, which was later renamed Jefferson. The town is among the earliest in the United States to be named after Thomas Jefferson, who served as Vice President in 1799.

Gary Muller is a former professional tennis player who turned professional in 1985 and spent 12 years on the ATP Tour. He defeated several notable opponents, including Andre Agassi, Jim Courier, Michael Chang, and Stefan Edberg. His best singles Grand Slam result came at the 1987 Australian Open, where he advanced to the third round before losing to Miloslav Mečíř. Muller found greater success in doubles, capturing eight titles with six different partners and achieving a career-high doubles ranking of World No. 7 in November 1993. He reached the doubles semifinals at four Grand Slam events—the US Open in 1986, Wimbledon in 1988, the Australian Open in 1990, and Wimbledon in 1993. Additionally, he holds a Wimbledon record for the most aces in a three-set match, with 54 aces in a qualifying match against Peter Lundgren in 1993.

Gary Muller is a former professional tennis player who retired in 1997. After retirement, he spent eight years as an ATP Tour coach, guiding players such as Jonas Björkman, Stefan Koubek, Sargis Sargsian, and Thomas Johansson. He later served as Dominic Thiem's touring coach, and was with Thiem when the Austrian won the Rio Open title in 2017.

Zhou Wenyong and Chen Tiejun, Communist Party members who had participated in preparations for the Guangzhou uprising, were detained by the Kuomintang in January 1928. They subsequently returned to Guangzhou to rebuild the party’s underground apparatus, but were executed on February 6, 1928.

On 11 December 1927, the Communist Party leadership ordered roughly 20,000 soldiers and armed workers sympathetic to communism to form a Red Guard and seize Guangzhou. The plan faced notable objections from senior commanders, including Ye Ting, Ye Jianying, and Xu Xiangqian, revealing substantial dissent within the military ranks. Despite being poorly armed—with only about 2,000 rifles—the insurgents nevertheless captured most of the city within hours through a surprise assault, even in the face of the government’s numerical and technical superiority. The uprising led to the establishment of the Guangzhou Soviet, the Soviet of Workers, Soldiers and Peasant Deputies. In response, some 15,000 National Revolutionary Army troops were deployed, followed by five additional NRA divisions, which gradually pushed the revolt back. After the initial takeover, the uprising was quickly crushed, resulting in heavy casualties among the insurgents and forcing survivors to flee or go into hiding. The Comintern, particularly the envoy Neumann, was blamed for insisting that the communists must hold Guangzhou at all costs. Zhang Tailei, the leading Red Guard organizer, was killed in an ambush while returning from a meeting, and the takeover had dissolved by the early morning of 13 December 1927.

The Mediterranean Sea has long served as a central conduit for intercontinental commerce, a role that was transformed by the 1869 opening of the lockless Suez Canal, which accelerated Europe–Asia trade and redirected the fastest sea route through the Mediterranean toward East Africa and Asia. Mediterranean countries and ports with direct connections to Central and Eastern Europe, such as Trieste, experienced rapid economic growth as a result. In the 20th century, conflicts and geopolitical events—including World War I, World War II, the Suez Crisis, and the Cold War—shifted trade routes toward northern European ports. Subsequently, trade patterns shifted again in favor of southern Mediterranean ports as European integration progressed, the revival of Silk Road initiatives gained influence, and broader open-trade regimes promoted free world commerce.

Greek names for the Mediterranean include hē thálassa ('the Sea'), hē megálē thálassa ('the Great Sea'), hē hēmetérā thálassa ('Our Sea'), and hē thálassa hē kath’hēmâs ('the sea around us'). Some scholars attribute to Knobloch the idea that Levantine cultures in classical antiquity used color to denote cardinal points, with black for north, yellow or blue for east, red for south, and white for west. This color-based framework is cited to explain regional denominators such as Greek Áspri Thálassa, Bulgarian Byalo More, Turkish Akdeniz, and Arab nomenclature that translates to "White Sea."

PDF, a widely used portable document format, supports a range of annotation and markup features that are implemented across multiple software packages. Adobe Acrobat is a proprietary program that enables users to annotate, highlight, and add notes to PDF files. PDFedit is a UNIX-based free software project licensed under the GNU General Public License and also provides annotation capabilities. Foxit Reader, distributed as freeware for Windows, macOS, and Linux, permits document annotations. PDF-XChange Viewer is freeware and offers annotations and markups without notable restrictions. On macOS, Preview functions as the built‑in PDF viewer with built‑in annotation tools. Skim is an open-source application focused on reading and annotating PDFs, and it integrates with LaTeX workflows as well as SyncTeX, PDFSync, and BibDesk. Qiqqa is freeware that can generate annotation reports that summarize notes across a user's PDF library. The Text Verification Tool can export differences between documents as annotations and markups.

Within the PDF specification, a font object encapsulates a digital typeface. It may specify the characteristics of the typeface or include an embedded font file; when an embedded font file is present, the font is termed an embedded font, whereas in the absence of such a file it is described as unembedded. The embedded font formats supported by PDF include Type 1 (along with its compressed variant, CFF), TrueType, and OpenType (supported from PDF 1.6 onward). In addition, PDF provides support for Type 3 fonts, in which the font's glyphs are defined by PDF graphic operators.

City of Literature is a designation that recognizes urban centers with substantial literary heritage and ongoing cultural activity. Within this framework, several notable libraries anchor the literary life of their cities, including the Braidense National Library in Milan, the Heidelberg University Library in Heidelberg, and the National Library of Ireland in Dublin. These institutions are located in other cities celebrated for their own rich literary traditions, illustrating the global presence of major libraries that preserve literary heritage and support scholarly access.

City of Literature is associated with a network founded in 2004 that brings together member cities across seven creative fields. In addition to literature, the six other fields recognized by the network are Crafts and Folk Arts, Design, Film, Gastronomy, Media Arts, and Music.

During the Crusades, several religious communities broadened their purposes to include armed protection and combat duties, giving rise to a distinct class of religious military orders. These groups integrated monastic devotion with military obligations and operated as both religious bodies and fighting orders in support of Crusader states and pilgrim safety. Prominent examples include the Knights Hospitaller, formally the Order of Saint John of Jerusalem; the Knights Templar, the Order of the Temple; and the Knights of the Holy Sepulchre.

Non-monastic religious institutes are typically governed from a central house, which may be called the motherhouse, generalate, or general curia. This central body holds jurisdiction over a number of dependent communities within the institute, coordinating governance and doctrinal matters across them. Members may be reassigned by the superior general to different communities as required by the institute's needs, enabling flexible staffing and cohesion across the order.

KRIV (TV) is a Houston, Texas-based Fox-owned station that, by 1982, was part of Metromedia’s group of major, news-producing independent outlets pursuing a national news program and courting prominent anchors such as Charles Kuralt and John Hart; the station itself considered launching its own news department. In August 1983, KRIV debuted a 7 p.m. newscast, the first prime-time newscast in the Houston market, conceived as a television analogue to NPR’s All Things Considered and intended to be more sophisticated than competing local newscasts. By 1986, the program had attracted an audience that at times rivaled KHOU’s third-place 6 p.m. broadcast, and a 12:30 p.m. newscast was added that year. When Fox began providing network programming in prime time, KRIV moved its newscast to 9 p.m., its present time slot, a change that yielded higher ratings and a more loyal news audience.

KRIV produces additional news and public affairs programming beyond its local newscasts. The Isiah Factor: Uncensored is a nightly program on KRIV, hosted by Isiah Carey, and it features interviews with newsmakers. Another KRIV program, What's Your Point?, is a political show hosted by Greg Groogan.

Recreational mathematics refers to the area of mathematics focused on puzzles, games, and problems pursued for enjoyment rather than practical utility. It includes mathematical competitions, which present participants with challenging problems that emphasize ingenuity and problem-solving techniques. Examples of these competitions are those sponsored by mathematical associations, which organize events to promote interest in mathematics among students and enthusiasts.

Recreational mathematics is the branch of mathematics pursued primarily for entertainment rather than for professional research or formal education. It is not restricted to amateurs, as many topics can be approached without requiring advanced mathematical knowledge. The field emphasizes mathematical puzzles and games, and it frequently appeals to children and laypersons, with the potential to inspire continued study of mathematics.

First Colony is a planned community that hosts a range of recreational facilities managed by the resident association. Patriot Park, a park located within First Colony, is operated by the association. The organization also maintains a series of playgrounds across First Colony, namely Austin Meadows Playground, Colony Meadows 1 Playground, Colony Meadows 2 Playground, Edgwater Playground, The Enclave Playground, Heritage Colony Playground, and Riverbend Playground. In addition, the association runs several pools in First Colony, including Alcorn Oaks Pool, Austin Park Pool, The Lakes Pool, and Woodstream Pool.

Within the First Colony area, the Texas Legislature established the public community college service areas by designating Wharton County Junior College to serve the City of Sugar Land and its extraterritorial jurisdiction, and by naming Houston Community College as the college for the City of Missouri City. These designations define which community college districts residents in those jurisdictions may enroll with for higher education programs.

Adam Clayton is an Irish musician best known as the longtime bassist for U2, with a history of participating in various side projects. In 1987 he contributed to Robbie Robertson's self-titled album, performing alongside his U2 bandmates. He has also performed with Maria McKee. In 1989 he joined U2 producer Daniel Lanois and fellow band member Larry Mullen Jr. on Lanois's album Acadie, playing bass on the tracks Still Water and Jolie Louise. Clayton contributed to Sharon Shannon's self-titled debut album (released October 1991), appearing on The Marguerita Suite. In 1994 he and Mullen played bass on Nanci Griffith's Flyer, featuring on tracks such as These Days in an Open Book, Don't Forget About Me, On Grafton Street and This Heart.
Adam Clayton became an ambassador in 2011 for the Walk in My Shoes facility of the Mental Health Service at St Patrick's Hospital in Dublin.

Hubble Bubble was formed in 1973 by Alain Bureau and subsequently managed by Bernard Schol. In 1977 the group released an eponymous album on Barclay Records. Plastic Bertrand is credited on the record as the songwriter, singer, and drummer, performing under the alias Roger Junior.

Hubble Bubble encountered difficulties following the death of their bassist, Daniel Massart, who died in an accident while returning from a rehearsal. Plastic Bertrand subsequently departed from the group, and his later success overshadowed the group's own achievements.

The earliest known written reference to Lewisham survives in a charter dated 862, where the place is named in Old English as liofshema. The document also defines Lewisham's boundaries with the neighboring area of Bromley, thereby recording the limits of the settlement at that period.

In the mid-17th century, Abraham Colfe, then vicar of Lewisham, established a group of philanthropic educational and housing institutions, comprising a grammar school, an elementary school, and six almshouses, all intended for the residents of Lewisham.

ISO/IEC 10116 is an international standard in the field of information technology, within the security techniques family, that addresses modes of operation for an n-bit block cipher. The document specifies the various modes of operation that may be used with block ciphers and applies to ciphers of any block length, providing standardized approaches for secure data processing.

ISO/IEC 10116 covers padding considerations for block cipher modes, noting that certain modes require the plaintext to be padded to fit the block size. The standard itself does not define or govern padding schemes, as padding techniques lie outside its scope. Consequently, while padding is necessary in some modes, the specification leaves the details of padding methods to other standards or implementations.

The term Southeast Asia was first introduced in 1839 by American pastor Howard Malcolm in Travels in South-Eastern Asia, where it referred to Mainland Southeast Asia but excluded Maritime Southeast Asia. During World War II, the Allies formalized the designation with the formation of the South East Asia Command (SEAC) in 1943, which helped popularise the term; however, its geographic scope was not fixed, as SEAC largely excluded the Philippines and much of Indonesia while including Ceylon. By the late 1970s, a broadly standard understanding of the term and its encompassed territories had emerged. In contemporary usage, definitions vary by cultural or linguistic context, but most commonly they cover the sovereign states and dependent territories located within Southeast Asia.

Southeast Asia covers approximately 4,500,000 square kilometers (1,700,000 square miles), representing about eight percent of Eurasia's land area and roughly three percent of the Earth's total land area. The region is home to more than 675 million people, comprising about 8.5 percent of the world's population, making it the third most populous geographical region in Asia after South Asia and East Asia. It is culturally and ethnically diverse, with hundreds of languages spoken by numerous ethnic groups. Eleven states in the region are members of ASEAN, a regional organization established to promote economic, political, military, educational, and cultural integration among its members.

According to census data, Asian Brazilian Buddhists declined from 150,571 in 1950 to 76,896 in 2010, indicating a substantial demographic shift within the country's Buddhist communities. Among younger Japanese Brazilians, understanding of Buddhism has weakened and is often seen as a tradition tied to elders rather than a living practice. The community has attracted few new Japanese immigrants to revitalize its ranks, and many temples struggle to reach out to younger generations, with a notable portion not offering regular services. Japanese remains the preferred language in many Buddhist settings, a pattern that may leave younger adherents less proficient and less engaged if they do not speak it. This language and practice pattern is linked to the historical view of Brazil as a temporary home among initial migrants, who did not consistently incorporate Portuguese into religious life.

Within Brazil, the Chinese Chan tradition of Mahayana Buddhism is anchored by Zu Lai Temple in Cotia and its companion Buddhist University in the state of São Paulo. Both institutions were inaugurated in 2003 by Fo Guang Shan, a Taiwanese Buddhist order. Located near the city of São Paulo, Zu Lai Temple is the largest Buddhist temple in Latin America. The project was financed through fundraising by American Buddhist organizations and individual donors.

Military engineering is the application of engineering methods to support military operations, planning, construction, and maintenance of related infrastructure. In some countries, military engineers may undertake civilian construction tasks during peacetime, including flood-control projects and improvements to river navigation. These activities are not regarded as part of military engineering.

Military engineering comprises educational programs designed to integrate military training with higher education. These offerings include the Civil Engineer Collegiate program, the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC), and undergraduate and graduate professional programs, all intended to pair military instruction with the completion of a college degree. The Civil Engineer Collegiate program, in particular, enables aspiring officers of the Civil Engineer Corps to complete a college degree and prepare for duties as officers.

While the discussion of double albums centers on releases containing two units, the same principles extend to triple albums, which are comprised of three distinct units. When a package includes more than three units, it is commonly described as a box set.

Bath and Leaving Your Body Map are two albums by The Maudlin of the Well, released in 2001 and issued as a single double album. In 2012, Blood Music released a vinyl box set reissuing both records together.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, aerial demands at Canton and Taiyuan forced the Republic of China Air Force to split the 28th Pursuit Squadron, 5th Pursuit Group from Jurong Airbase into two separate squadrons. The Canton-bound unit was led by Lieutenant Arthur Chin, while Captain Chan Kee-Wong commanded the force bound for Taiyuan. On 27 September 1937, Chin, with four Hawk II fighters from Shaoguan, and Lieutenant Chen Shun-Nan, with three Hawk IIIs from Tianhe, intercepted Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service G3M bombers en route to attack the Canton–Hankow railway. The two flights engaged the bombers over Canton, claiming at least two kills; one G3M reportedly dumped fuel and ditched off Swatow, its crew rescued by a British freighter, and one gunner died from battle wounds. In October 1937, China ordered 36 Gloster Gladiator Mk.I fighters, which outperformed the Hawk IIs and IIIs, and most were deployed as frontline fighters for the Canton defense sector into 1938.

During the Sino-Japanese conflict, the Soviet Union provided direct military support to China with the aim of prolonging the war effort. In August 1937, the Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact was signed, and a barter arrangement was established in which Soviet munitions were exchanged for Chinese strategic minerals, notably tungsten and antimony. Beginning in 1937, Soviet military matériel entered China through the Xinjiang–Lanzhou corridor, transported by an estimated 20,000 camels. Chinese raw materials traveled back along the same route or via Hong Kong to Vladivostok. By 1940, the logistical system had expanded to include about 50,000 camels and hundreds of trucks, delivering roughly 2,000–3,000 tons of Soviet war materiel into China each month.

Songs in the Key of Life was the second-best selling album in the United States in 1977, behind Fleetwood Mac's Rumours. It also ranked as the highest selling R&B/Soul album on the Billboard Year-End chart for that year. The album was certified Diamond by the RIAA in 2005, a designation that, for this release, corresponds to five million copies sold in the United States due to the RIAA counting each disc included with the album as a separate unit within multi-disc sets. Although Diamond thresholds are ten million units, the RIAA’s counting method can influence the reported figure.

Songs in the Key of Life was anticipated for an October 1975 release, but its rollout was delayed after Wonder insisted on additional remixing. During the postponement, Motown marketing circulated “We’re almost finished” T-shirts as a lighthearted acknowledgment of the delay, while production continued into early 1976. The project began under a provisional title intended to convey an unvarnished portrayal of life, a label later superseded by the final title, which was interpreted as signaling a sophisticated key-of-life concept and the prospect of enduring success. The album ultimately was released on September 28, 1976, after about two years of anticipation, issued as a double LP accompanied by a bonus seven-inch EP, A Something’s Extra. The EP comprises the tracks Saturn, Ebony Eyes, All Day Sucker, and Easy Goin' Evening (My Mama's Call). In addition, the package included a 24-page lyric and credits booklet.

Whittman-Hart, a services firm specializing in digital communications, was established in 1984. It expanded steadily through the 1990s, and in 1999 it acquired USWeb/CKS, significantly enlarging its scale. The combined enterprise was re-incorporated on March 1, 2000, as marchFIRST, Inc. In April 2001, marchFIRST declared bankruptcy, and the company was liquidated the following May.

MarchFirst emerged from a December 1999 announcement that Whittman-Hart would combine with USWeb/CKS, a California-based web consulting firm, in a transaction valued at roughly $5.7 billion in Whittman-Hart stock. Under the terms, USWeb/CKS shareholders would exchange their shares for Whittman-Hart stock and own about 57% of the merged company. The arrangement was described as closer to a merger than a conventional acquisition, signaling a substantial integration of the two firms to form a single enterprise.

The Dominican Republic national under-17 football team is the national association football team of the Dominican Republic for players aged under 17. It represents the Dominican Republic at the under-17 level in international play and functions within the country’s football structure to compete in international competitions for this age group.

The Dominican Republic national under-17 football team announced a final squad of 20 players for the 2023 CONCACAF Men's Under-17 Championship. The tournament took place in Guatemala from February 11 to 26, 2023.

Case fatality rate (CFR) is expressed as a value between zero and one, corresponding to 0% to 100%, and denotes the risk that a diagnosed case will die, i.e., the proportion of cases that die from the disease. It measures case fatality risk rather than the disease’s incidence in the population. CFR is not a rate, incidence rate, nor a ratio, and those measures are not constrained to the 0–1 interval. Additionally, it does not account for the time elapsed from disease onset to death.

The case fatality rate (CFR) is defined as the proportion of diagnosed cases that result in death from the disease. For instance, if 100 cases are diagnosed and 9 deaths occur, the CFR is 9%. The CFR can change as the disease remains under investigation; once additional deaths are identified among unresolved cases, the CFR may increase. Conversely, if unresolved cases were previously treated as recovered, the reclassification as more deaths are recorded can yield a higher updated CFR. By contrast, the infection fatality rate (IFR) estimates fatality across all infections, including subclinical and unreported ones, and is therefore typically lower than the CFR. In general, the IFR is less than or equal to the CFR, depending on the total number of infections that go undetected.

The Tanzania Music Awards are the national music awards presented annually in Tanzania. They are commonly referred to as the Kilimanjaro Music Awards or Kili Music Awards, and their name derives from sponsorship by Kilimanjaro Premium Lager. The ceremony was established in 1999 by the National Arts Council of Tanzania, known by its acronym BASATA, which operates under the Ministry of Education and Culture.

Artistic inspiration has been conceptualized in various theoretical terms across different historical periods. In the eighteenth century, John Locke advanced associationism, positing that the mind is composed of ideas that connect or resonate with one another through mental associations. The nineteenth century saw Coleridge and Shelley framing inspiration as arising when a poet becomes attuned to transcendent or mystical forces, enabling the soul to receive visions. In the early twentieth century, Sigmund Freud located the source of inspiration within the artist’s inner psyche, while Carl Jung attributed it to a creative impulse that encodes the archetypal content of the human mind.

Artistic inspiration, in northern traditions such as Old Norse culture, is often conceived as a divine gift bestowed by the gods. The Norse skalds describe being seized by a magical or divine state that precedes their deliberate shaping of verse, a process that blends trance-like inspiration with conscious craft. Training in these traditions aims not merely at technical proficiency but at learning to channel forces perceived as transcending human capacity. In the historical account of Cædmon by Bede, the Christian and Germanic strands converge, illustrating a synthesis of belief systems. Cædmon, a herdsman with no formal poetic education, is said to have dreamt that Jesus commanded him to sing, after which he produced what is now known as Cædmon's Hymn and subsequently earned lasting renown. Across these accounts, inspiration is often characterized as grace: it arrives without solicitation, it is not wholly controllable, and it compels utterance. Accordingly, a poet's performance engages the mind and body but rests ultimately on an intuitive gift.

In the late 1960s, archaeological excavations were conducted at Urartian sites in northwestern Iran. In 1976, an Italian expedition led by Mirjo Salvini reached the Kelishin stele, reportedly under heavy military protection. The Gulf War subsequently closed these sites to archaeological research. In Turkey, excavation work on Urartian sites was continued by Oktay Belli, and in 1989 the fortress at Ayanis, dating to the seventh century BCE and associated with Rusa II of Urartu, was uncovered about 35 kilometers north of Van. According to Wartke (1993), only roughly one-third to one-half of the approximately 300 known Urartian sites across Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Armenia had been examined. In addition, without adequate protection, many sites have suffered looting by local residents seeking treasure and other saleable antiquities.

Urartu was a kingdom of the Iron Age in the Near East that emerged in the mid-9th century BCE. Its domain stretched roughly 850 kilometers from the western Euphrates to lands west of Ardabil, Iran, and extended about 500 kilometers from Lake Çıldır near Ardahan in present-day Turkey to Rawandiz in Iraqi Kurdistan. The state dominated the Armenian highlands during the 8th and 7th centuries BCE and frequently clashed with Assyria, at times ranking as the region’s most powerful polity. It waned due to prolonged military pressure and was ultimately conquered in the early 6th century BCE, traditionally attributed to either the Median Empire or to Cyrus the Great during that century. Archaeological remains underscore the strength of its fortifications and its sophisticated metalworking.

The Kingdom of Luang Prabang (1945) was a short-lived puppet state established by Imperial Japan during the latter stages of World War II. It existed from 8 April 1945 to 12 October 1945. The polity carried local and Japanese names, including Lao ອານາຈັກຫຼວງພະບາງ (anachak ruangphabang) and Japanese ルアンプラバン王国.

Territorial losses in Indochina represented a significant setback for French prestige, prompting the Kingdom of Luang Prabang to press for sovereignty over all Laos as compensation, under the leadership of the French-educated Crown Prince Sisavang Vatthana. A secret French memorandum from March 1941 acknowledged Lao nationalist aspirations but warned that subordinating the Champassak royal house to another lineage could drive it to align with Thailand. On 21 August 1941, Savang Vatthana, together with Resident-Superior Maurice Roques, formalized the attachment of Xiangkhouang and Vientiane to the Kingdom of Luang Prabang, placing the protectorate on an equal footing with Cambodia and Annam. The renewed focus on Laos contributed to a modernization of the kingdom’s administration, and French authorities indicated they would not oppose further southern expansion. Prince Phetsarath became the first prime minister, and a new advisory council for King Sisavang Vong was chaired by Savang Vatthana.

AC/DC has been the subject of discussions about the sexual humor in its lyrics, with supporters arguing that the bawdy tone is a deliberate stylistic element. The band members have dismissed accusations of sexism, maintaining that the lyrics are meant in jest rather than as a serious statement. In a Mojo interview conducted by Sylvie Simmons, Angus Young described the group as pranksters more than anything else. Malcolm Young likewise suggested that the band should be judged by its music rather than its words, stating that they take the music seriously while treating the lyrics as throwaway lines. Music critic Marchese noted that the musical force is strong enough to render the words largely a secondary consideration, describing the approach as deceptively plain, highly effective, and financially successful.

AC/DC's fourteenth studio album, Stiff Upper Lip, was recorded in 1999 at The Warehouse Studio in Vancouver and produced by George. It was released in February 2000 and received a warmer reception than Ballbreaker, though critics noted a lack of fresh ideas. The title track was issued as a single in January 2000 and topped the US Mainstream Rock chart for four weeks; additional singles included Satellite Blues, which reached number one on the same chart, and Safe in New York City, which peaked at number seven. In December 2002 the band signed a long-term, multi-album deal with Sony Music and began issuing remastered editions of its catalog. In 2003 the entire back catalog, excluding Ballbreaker and Stiff Upper Lip, was remastered and reissued, while Ballbreaker and Stiff Upper Lip themselves were reissued in the United Kingdom in 2004. AC/DC was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003, with the class including Brian Johnson, Cliff Williams, Phil Rudd, Angus Young, Malcolm Young, and Bon Scott. Former bassist Mark Evans was initially announced as an inductee but was subsequently omitted six weeks later.

The Chersky Range, in conjunction with the adjacent Verkhoyansk Range, influences Siberia's climate. The mountain ridges act as barriers to air masses moving westward, leading to reduced snowfall in the western plains.

Within the Chersky Range, the Kolyma River occupies the eastern, southeastern, and southern portions of its drainage system. Among the most notable rivers feeding this system are Zyryanka, Rassokha, Omulyovka, Yasachnaya, Taskan, Debin, and Byoryolyokh. In addition to these, there are numerous other rivers that form part of the range's extensive hydrographic network.
In 1989, a statue commemorating the renowned chess champion Tigran Petrosian was unveiled in front of the Tigran Petrosian Chess House. The sculpture was created by Armenian artist Ara Shiraz.

The Tigran Petrosian Chess House serves as the center of chess life in Yerevan, Armenia. It opened in 1970 and was renamed in 1984 to honor the former world chess champion Tigran Petrosian. The triangular-shaped building was designed by architect Zhanna Meshcheryakova, and Petrosian laid the first stone of its foundation. The current director is Hrachik Tavadyan. In Armenian, the institution is known as Տիգրան Պետրոսյանի անվան Շախմատի Տուն, and its formal designation translates to the Central House of Chess Players named after Tigran Petrosian.

The LDAC encoder is released as open‑source software under the Apache License 2.0, enabling developers to implement devices that can transmit LDAC streams without incurring patent royalties or licensing barriers. By contrast, the LDAC decoder design remains proprietary.

LDAC is a proprietary lossy audio coding technology developed by Sony for wireless transmission of audio over Bluetooth. It is designed to deliver high-fidelity streaming by supporting data rates up to 990 kbps at a sample rate of 32-bit/96 kHz. The codec has been adopted across a wide range of consumer electronics, including headphones, earphones, smartphones, portable media players, active speakers, and home theater systems.

Mark Lawson became the main presenter of BBC Radio 4's Front Row in 1998. He wrote several BBC Radio 4 plays, including St Graham and St Evelyn (2003), which focuses on Graham Greene and Evelyn Waugh, and The Third Soldier Holds His Thighs (2005), about Mary Whitehouse's litigation against The Romans in Britain. Lawson contributed to television as well, writing episodes for the adaptation of Absolute Power and appearing as himself in Series 1, Episode 2, "Pope Idol." He has been spoofed by the Dead Ringers team, who dubbed him "Britain's brainiest potato" and "the thinking woman's potato" in reference to his baldness. From 2006 to 2015, he conducted in-depth one-to-one interviews for BBC Four in the series Mark Lawson Talks to….

Mark Gerard Lawson (born 11 April 1962) is an English journalist, broadcaster and author who specialises in culture and the arts. He rose to prominence as the presenter of Front Row, BBC Radio 4's flagship arts programme, a role he held from 1998 to 2014. In addition to his radio work, Lawson has contributed as a columnist for The Guardian. He also fronted the interview series Mark Lawson Talks To... on BBC Four, which ran from 2006 to 2015.

Ionizing radiation transfers energy to matter, initiating radiolysis in which chemical bonds are broken and highly reactive free radicals are produced. These reactive species can continue to react with neighboring materials after irradiation ends; for example, ozone generated in air during irradiation can cause ozone-induced cracking of polymers. Ionizing radiation can also promote existing chemical reactions, such as polymerization and corrosion, by influencing the activation energy of those processes, effectively accelerating them. Additionally, optical materials exposed to ionizing radiation are prone to deterioration.

Guidance from the International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) advises that artificial irradiation of the general public be limited to an average annual effective dose of 1 mSv (0.001 Sv). This recommended limit does not include exposures arising from medical procedures and is not applicable to occupational exposures, which are addressed separately within radiological protection frameworks.

Frequent flyer programs typically allocate earned miles or points to the individual employee rather than to the employer, a design that has prompted discussion about the offsetting tax implications and the potential misappropriation of value that belongs to the company. Critics argue that since rewards function as personal assets, they could influence travel decisions or encourage unnecessary business trips, effectively acting as a form of bribery to sway choices. By contrast, many organizations view the miles as a valuable personal perk that helps offset the burden of frequent travel for staff. In the public sector, some government agencies pursue policies to restrict or prohibit employees from accumulating mileage on official travel to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure proper accountability of resources.

Frequent-flyer programs are a form of virtual currency managed by airlines or airline coalitions that allocate points to customers based on travel and related purchases. Money flows unidirectionally into the program as individuals pay to acquire these points, creating a funding stream for the reward scheme. There is no mechanism to convert points back into money, i.e., no cash-out, so the points function within the program as a non-cashable store of value rather than a directly withdrawable monetary asset.

In 2023, San Diego issued more housing permits than in decades, with the total nearly doubling the number issued in 2022. The uptick in housing supply followed reforms designed to ease the construction of new housing.

Todd Gloria became interim mayor of San Diego following Mayor Bob Filner's resignation on August 30, 2013, taking office with limited powers during the transition. His interim tenure coincided with San Diego being described as the second-largest U.S. city after Houston and with Gloria as an openly gay mayor. He served in that capacity until March 3, 2014, when mayor-elect Kevin Faulconer was sworn in. During the interim period, Gloria remained the City Councilmember for District 3 and retained the title of City Council President, though the daily duties of the presidency were performed by Pro Tem Sherri Lightner. Gloria was considered a possible candidate to replace Filner but chose not to run.

In June 2006, Blender was ranked eighth among the 50 best magazines by the Chicago Tribune, reflecting its notable position in the publication landscape at the time. The Tribune described Blender as a standout title within rock-oriented magazines, highlighting its appeal to readers of music and culture.

Blender was an American music magazine published from 1994 to 2009, which billed itself as the ultimate guide to pop culture. The publication became known for its provocative celebrity photo spreads, while also presenting extensive ranking compilations of albums, artists, and songs that included both top selections and critical lowlights. Each issue featured a comprehensive survey of an artist’s entire discography, with methodical analysis of each album presented in sequence.

In 2013, the Ministry of Transport announced the National Highway Network Planning for 2013–2030, detailing a major expansion of China’s highway system. The plan envisions increasing the total number of national highways to 119, with 81 interconnecting routes to link the network, and expanding total highway mileage to roughly 265,000 kilometers (165,000 miles). It also emphasizes pursuing greater development in western and other less-developed regions to promote more balanced regional growth through improved road connectivity.

China's nationwide highway network uses a designation that combines the letter G with a three-digit number, exemplified by routes such as G107. The initial letter G is derived from guójiā, the Chinese term for "national," indicating the routes' status within the country’s official network.

NBC Europe was based in London at 19-22 Rathbone Place, occupying the same building as Music Box. The Music Box building would later become the home of CNN International until 2007. Transmission facilities for NBC Europe were provided by Molinare at Fouberts Place for several months, with a brief return of facilities thereafter. The Marcucci family acquired Melrose House, 14 Lanark Square in Limeharbour, where NBC Europe established a modern broadcasting centre.

NBC Europe delivered the majority of NBC’s prime-time programming in the European market. Beginning after 10:00 pm CET on weekdays, the network aired late-night offerings such as The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, Late Night with Conan O'Brien, and Later, aligning with its branding that highlighted night-time star programming. A number of NBC News programs, including Dateline, Time and Again, and NBC Nightly News, were carried live on NBC Europe. The Today Show was originally broadcast live in the afternoon but was later shown the following morning, resulting in a delay of more than half a day. To offset the lag, NBC News segments were substituted with European updates produced by ITN in London, which had also supplied the main newscasts before and after the General Electric takeover. European weather forecasts were initially provided by the BBC, with NBC in the United States later taking on the duty on occasion.

COBOL was developed with readability in mind, adopting an English-like syntax and a structured architecture that includes nouns, verbs, clauses, sentences, and a division of programs into sections and divisions. By 1984, maintainers faced growing difficulty in deciphering large COBOL codebases, which could impede maintenance. The COBOL-85 revision was then designed to ease maintenance, aiming to simplify and clarify the language to support ongoing upkeep of existing systems.

In October, the intermediate-range committee received copies of the FACT language specification, which had been developed by Roy Nutt. The committee was impressed by FACT’s features, and subsequently passed a resolution to base COBOL on the FACT language specification.
In July 2008, IVillage formed a partnership with BlogHer, a digital network delivering news, entertainment, and information aimed at women.

IVillage originated at Universal Orlando Resort as NBC pursued an early on-air synergy with Universal Studios following NBC’s acquisition of Universal. Production responsibilities were handled by WTVJ in Miami. The program was hosted by Molly Pesce, Stefani Schaeffer, and Guy Yovan, with Naamua Delaney and Bob Oschack serving as contributing correspondents. At its launch, the series was broadcast on Bravo with a one-day delay, and repeats continued on Bravo for three weeks.

Official Italian sales data began to be compiled from 1995 onward by the Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana (FIMI), the national body responsible for official sales statistics. Before this framework was established, organizations such as Hit Parade Italy sought to standardize earlier data. Earlier figures and estimates were drawn from sources including Musica e dischi, TV Sorrisi e Canzoni, Ciao 2001, and Doxa. From 1990 to 1995, no corporate entity provided official sales data or estimates for Italian music artists.

Estimates of sales for Italian music artists in the list are predominantly derived from major Italian newspapers and national media, which are regarded as reliable sources for such figures. The newspapers most frequently cited include Il Corriere della Sera, La Repubblica, Il Giornale, and Il Messaggero. In addition, national radio and television channels—Rai, Mediaset, MTV, and Radio Italia TV—are commonly referenced when presenting or corroborating these sales estimates.

Harmonic Vector Excitation Coding (HVXC) is a speech coding method that employs linear predictive coding with block-based adaptation at 20-millisecond intervals. The LPC parameters are transformed into line spectral pair coefficients, which are then quantized jointly. The LPC residual signal is analyzed to determine whether it is voiced or unvoiced. In voiced sections, the residual is encoded using a parametric representation, effectively serving as a vocoder, while in unvoiced sections the residual waveform is quantized, functioning as a hybrid speech codec.

Harmonic Vector Excitation Coding (HVXC) was published as the second subcomponent of ISO/IEC 14496-3:1999 (MPEG-4 Audio) in 1999. An expanded version of HVXC was published later in MPEG-4 Audio Version 2, ISO/IEC 14496-3:1999/Amd 1:2000 (Amendment 1, 2000).
