During the surrender of Japan, rebels led by Hatanaka sought Imperial House Minister Sōtarō Ishiwata, Lord of the Privy Seal Kōichi Kido, and the recordings of the surrender speech, but their efforts were concentrated in the bank vault, a large chamber beneath the Imperial Palace. The search was impeded by a blackout implemented in response to Allied bombings, and it was further hindered by the archaic organization and layout of the Imperial House Ministry, whose numerous room names were unfamiliar to the intruders. Although the rebels succeeded in locating chamberlain Yoshihiro Tokugawa, Hatanaka threatened him with disembowelment using a samurai sword, and Tokugawa lied, claiming that he did not know where the recordings or the two men were.

During August, a faction of Hatanaka's rebels led by Captain Takeo Sasaki devised an assassination plot against Prime Minister Kantarō Suzuki. The group attacked Suzuki’s office, firing machine guns and setting the building on fire before proceeding to Suzuki’s residence. Hisatsune Sakomizu, the chief secretary to Suzuki’s cabinet, warned Suzuki, who escaped mere minutes before the assailants arrived. After burning Suzuki’s home, the rebels moved on to Kiichirō Hiranuma’s estate with the aim of murdering him; Hiranuma escaped through a side gate, and his house was also set aflame. In the aftermath, Suzuki spent the remainder of August under police protection, sleeping in a different bed each night.

Longgui Station (simplified Chinese: 龙归站; traditional Chinese: 龍歸站; Cantonese Yale: Lùhnggwāi Jaahm) is an underground station on Line 3 of the Guangzhou Metro. It lies to the north of Guanghua Highway and Nancun Avenue in Baiyun District, Guangzhou. The station commenced operations on 30 October 2010.

As of 2020, the Internet Archive's Old Time Radio collection comprises 5,121 recordings. A dedicated community of collectors actively digitizes extensive broadcast archives and makes them available on CDs or as downloadable files. RadioEchoes.com maintains a collection totaling 98,949 episodes, though not all of its entries are strictly old-time radio.

Old time radio helped shape the format of modern radio news by incorporating elements such as headline-driven coverage, remote reporting, on-the-street interviews in the Vox Pop tradition, panel discussions, and regular weather and farm reports. Its expansion into news programming triggered a clash between radio and newspaper interests in the mid-1930s. Newspapers amplified sensational reports of mass hysteria attributed to the fictional radio presentation of The War of the Worlds, which was presented as a faux newscast.

Diphthongs show cross-linguistic variation in their phonemic length. In some languages, a contrast between short and long diphthongs exists, forming a distinct quantity system. In historical varieties such as Old English, diphthongs behaved similarly to vowels in terms of quantity, occupying one mora for short forms and two morae for long forms. Three-way quantity contrasts among diphthongs are exceedingly rare. Northern Sami, however, features a three-way distinction among diphthongs—long, short, and final-stressed—with the final-stressed type distinguished by a relatively longer second element.

In phonology, certain sound changes involve the interaction between diphthongs and monophthongs. A process known as vowel breaking or diphthongization occurs when a monophthong develops into a diphthong, altering its quality to incorporate a glide. Conversely, monophthongization, also referred to as smoothing, describes the opposite outcome in which a diphthong becomes a single, stable vowel sound.

In September 2017, Feinstein issued a statement in response to President Donald Trump’s first address to the United Nations General Assembly, a speech that threatened North Korea. She expressed disagreement with the remarks, describing the threat as bombastic and criticizing the absence of constructive pathways to tackle global challenges as a severe disappointment.

Dianne Feinstein, a long-serving United States Senator from California, has been a prominent advocate for farm animal welfare in her public work. In 2008 she became the first major statewide elected California official to endorse Proposition 2, which restricts the most intensive confinement of certain farm animals. In 2022 she led a letter to Solicitor General Elizabeth Prelogar urging the defense of California’s Prop 12 before the Supreme Court, a move intended to extend Prop 2 protections to all animals raised for pork, veal, and egg products sold in the state. After the Supreme Court dismissed a challenge to Prop 12 in 2023, Feinstein led a letter opposing language in the 2023 Farm Bill that would overturn Prop 12 and other state farm animal welfare laws.

The Saint soundtrack highlights a roster of prominent late-1990s artists, including Duran Duran, Sneaker Pimps, Orbital, Moby, Fluke, Luscious Jackson, The Chemical Brothers, Underworld, Daft Punk, David Bowie, Superior, Dreadzone, Duncan Sheik, and Everything but the Girl. The compilation also features an updated version of the theme music from the 1960s television series.

Mixed Raster Content (MRC) is a technique used by some image scanners when scanning to PDF, enabling the image to be processed in distinct layers for text and graphics. In the absence of MRC, the scanned image is produced in a single pass, with no explicit distinction between textual and graphical content. When MRC is employed, separate processing streams handle text, graphics, and other elements, which can yield clearer graphics and sharper text, though processing may be slightly slower. MRC is recommended for documents that contain hard-to-read text or low-quality graphics. Additionally, MRC can reduce the overall size of the scanned file. However, higher compression approaches such as JBIG2 can sometimes introduce character substitution errors in scanned documents.
Mixed raster content is a file format whose practical use remains uncertain. By contrast, formats like DjVu and PDF incorporate their own methods for defining layers and masks.

In 1951, WSK-Świdnik was established as the third national aerospace production facility in Świdnik, and in 1957 it was renamed WSK PZL-Świdnik. From 1956 onward, the plant developed into one of the world's leading helicopter manufacturers, producing aircraft under Soviet licence beginning with the SM-1 Mil Mi-1; Świdnik became the principal producer of the Mi-1 and held exclusive rights to manufacture the Mi-2. From the late 1980s, the company also produced the Polish-designed medium helicopter PZL W-3 Sokół, alongside the light helicopter PZL SW-4 Puszczyk. In 1991 the state factory was reorganized as a state-owned corporation, WSK "PZL-Świdnik" SA. The facility also produced gliders such as the Pirat, PW-5 and PW-6, and has engaged in international cooperation, including work on Agusta A109 fuselages.

During the period from 1954 to 1980, WSK PZL-Świdnik produced motorcycles under the WSK brand. The operation yielded approximately two million motorcycles in total, with the product lines comprising the WSK M06 (125 cc) and the WSK M21 (175 cc) families.

The Dictionary of National Biography (DNB) originally contained biographical entries only for individuals who were deceased. It was subsequently expanded by three supplementary volumes. The supplements addressed subjects who had died between 1885 and 1900 or who had been overlooked in the original alphabetical sequence. Together, they brought the work up to the death of Queen Victoria on 22 January 1901. Corrections were also added in the supplements.

Following the death of Matthew in October 1999, Brian Harrison took over as editor in January 2000, signaling the shift from the Dictionary of National Biography to the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography (ODNB). The ODNB was issued on 23 September 2004 in 60 print volumes, priced at £7,500, with an online edition available to subscribers; in the United Kingdom, online access is also available free to library card holders. The print edition has since been offered new at a substantially reduced price. The 2004 edition comprises 50,113 biographical articles covering 54,922 lives and includes entries on all subjects contained in the old DNB, while earlier DNB entries remain accessible via the DNB Archive link. Some of the longer DNB entries continue to be highly regarded. A small permanent staff remains in Oxford to maintain and expand the online edition. Harrison was succeeded as editor by Lawrence Goldman in October 2004. The first online update appeared on 4 January 2005 (including subjects who died in 2001), followed by updates on 23 May 2005 and 6 October 2005; additions of new subjects who died in 2002 were published online on 5 January 2006, with subsequent May and October releases in ensuing years consistent with the 2005 pattern. The ODNB also includes biographies of individuals who died before the DNB’s publication but became notable later, such as William Eyre (fl. 1634–1675).

Demand controlled ventilation (DCV) systems employ local sensors and monitoring devices to evaluate ventilation performance and indoor air quality, particularly when occupants cannot directly assess air conditions. These measurements compensate for the limitations of human perception in judging ventilation effectiveness, enabling condition-driven adjustments. Local ventilation control enables varied ventilation rates for individual rooms or spaces, rather than a single centralized setting governing the entire building. In this way, DCV contrasts with centralized ventilation control, which applies a uniform rate across all zones.

Demand controlled ventilation is an approach in which local sensors monitor both the presence and number of occupants in an enclosed space and the real-time concentration of pollutants, enabling the ventilation rate to be dynamically adjusted. By modulating airflow according to occupancy and contaminant levels, the system seeks to minimize occupants’ exposure to pollutants. When the space is unoccupied or pollutant concentrations are low, it operates at the minimum required ventilation level to conserve energy while maintaining safety standards.

Dragontrail is an alkali-aluminosilicate sheet glass manufactured by AGC Inc., engineered to be notably thin and lightweight while offering strong damage resistance. It is often compared to Corning's Gorilla Glass due to its similar function as a protective cover glass for electronic devices. The key properties include high strength that enables a thin form factor without marked fragility, substantial scratch resistance, and a Vickers hardness in the range of 595–673.

On June 25, 2015, Billboard updated its charting rules, shifting the official street date for new album releases in the United States from Tuesday to Friday. As a result, sales-based charts now report the first seven days of an album's release, and several major chart categories—including the Billboard 200, Top Album Sales, genre-specific albums, digital songs, genre-specific downloads, streaming songs, and genre-focused streaming tallies—are set on a Friday-to-Thursday tracking week. The Radio Songs chart, which influences the Hot 100, moved to a Monday-to-Sunday period, from the prior Wednesday-to-Tuesday schedule, while all remaining radio charts and genre tallies follow Monday-to-Sunday. The adjustment was designed to harmonize Billboard's timing with the IFPI's global practice of releasing all singles and albums on Fridays.

Canada Country describes Billboard's practice of compiling year-end chart results for each calendar year, with the final rankings published in a dedicated year-end issue and subsequently broadcast on year-end editions of American Top 40 and American Country Countdown. The historical record begins with the first annual year-end charts for 1946, published in the January 4, 1947 issue, while an undifferentiated 1945 chart based on the "Honor Roll of Hits" is also noted. From 1991 through 2006, the top single, album, and artist(s) highlighted on these year-end lists were honored at the Billboard Music Awards. The Billboard Music Awards were traditionally held in December until they went dormant in 2007, and the awards were revived in May 2011.

In 2003, a meta-analysis assessing the efficacy of hypnotherapy reviewed existing studies and concluded that the effectiveness of hypnosis has not been verified for a considerable portion of psychotherapeutic practice.

In Australia, professional bodies representing hypnotism and hypnotherapy, including the Australian Hypnotherapists Association, have advocated for formal government regulation of the practice. They argue that such regulation should be comparable to that governing other mental health professions to ensure standards and consumer protection. At present, hypnotherapy is not government-regulated and remains outside the regulatory framework of the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).

The position of the Badaic languages within regional language families has long been debated. Historically, they have been treated as a subdivision of the Kaili–Pamona language group. In addition, they share numerous linguistic features with languages in the Seko subgroup of the South Sulawesi language family. More recently, some subgrouping proposals place the Badaic languages within South Sulawesi, arguing that they retain strong Kaili–Pamona influence in their development.

The Badaic languages constitute a closely related subgroup within the Austronesian language family. The group comprises Bada (Bada’), Behoa (Besoa), Napu, and Limola. The varieties Bada, Behoa, and Napu are spoken in the North Lore and South Lore districts of Poso Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, while Limola is spoken in North Luwu Regency in South Sulawesi. Lexical similarity among Bada, Behoa, and Napu ranges from about 80 to 91 percent, and these languages are largely mutually intelligible. Nevertheless, the speech communities remain culturally distinct.

Shlensky v. Wrigley addresses whether the plaintiff, as a shareholder, had standing to pursue a derivative action against Wrigley on behalf of the corporation. In derivative suits, a shareholder claimant typically must show that the directors engaged in fraud, illegality, or a conflict of interest. The court’s analysis concentrated on the nature of the legal claim rather than evaluating the substantive merits of Wrigley’s conduct. As a result, the ruling concerned the appropriateness of the claim’s form rather than making a determination about whether Wrigley’s actions were good or bad.

Shlensky v. Wrigley, 237 N.E.2d 776 (Ill. App. 1968), is a leading case in United States corporate law addressing the permissible scope of a board of directors' discretion to balance the interests of stakeholders. The court affirmed the applicability of the business judgment rule to directors' good-faith assessments of long-term shareholder value, thereby granting deference to managerial decisions in pursuit of the corporation's enduring welfare. In the broader doctrinal landscape, the decision is often viewed as signaling a shift away from the notion that corporations exist solely to maximize shareholder value, in contrast to Dodge v. Ford Motor Co., an older Michigan ruling that stressed the primacy of pursuing shareholder value as the corporate objective.

According to Menahem Meiri, halachic criteria determine when a war is mandatory. The wars undertaken to conquer the Land of Israel, as depicted in biblical narratives such as Joshua, are regarded as obligatory rather than voluntary, while all other wars are classified as voluntary unless they are defensive or religious in nature. A ruler is not authorized to compel participation in voluntary wars without approval from the Great Sanhedrin, the 71-judge governing body. When Israel is attacked for any reason, the conflict is regarded as a religious war, obligating all members of the community to take part. In this framework, a religious war is treated as equivalent to a mandatory war, imposing a duty on all Israelites to resist.

According to Jewish legal opinions, a Jew residing in the remaining Israeli cities and towns attacked by the enemy bears a binding obligation to go out to battle in order to assist threatened countrymen. The purpose of this duty is to help rescue fellow citizens. After rescuing them, they are allowed to return to their place on the Sabbath with their own weapons in hand. This allowance is intended to prevent refraining from assisting in future conflicts.

Floria Sigismondi is a filmmaker best known for writing and directing The Runaways. She has directed music videos for a wide range of artists, including Dua Lipa, Sam Smith, Jimmy Page and Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, Marilyn Manson, Christina Aguilera, Justin Timberlake, Rihanna, Leonard Cohen, Katy Perry, Björk, The White Stripes, and David Bowie. Sigismondi has also directed commercials for Gucci, MAC, Target, and Nike. In television, she has directed two episodes of The Handmaid’s Tale and has worked on American Gods.

Floria Sigismondi began her career as a fashion photographer before transitioning to directing music videos after being approached by The Revolver Film Co. She subsequently directed videos for several Canadian bands, with a body of work noted for its innovative and unsettling character, often set in entropic underworlds inhabited by tormented souls and omnipotent beings. Her distinctive approach attracted a number of prominent musicians. She describes her style as a synthesis of two realms: a textural, brutal sensibility paired with beauty and light.

The designation of voice type is a labeling practice concerned with a singer’s inherent range and tessitura, yet numerous vocal pedagogues argue that assigning such classifications too early can lead to misidentification and potential harm. A recurring admonition within the field is to avoid rapid categorization of a student’s voice, with notable voices such as William Vennard urging practitioners not to rush to label beginners. Premature diagnoses have often proved inaccurate and can adversely affect a student’s development while also risking embarrassment for the teacher. Proponents of a cautious approach recommend beginning with the middle portion of the voice and exploring upward and downward from there, allowing the voice to reveal its own class through ongoing study and authentic singing rather than through an early, imposed label.

Within classical vocal taxonomy, the soprano represents the highest singing voice in the female range. The typical range runs roughly from C4 (middle C) to C6 (high C). The lower limit is about A3, just below middle C, with individual singers showing variation. Most soprano roles do not require singing above C6; however, several standard roles demand notes up to D6. Additionally, coloratura soprano parts may reach F6, the F above high C.

Conquest of the Planet of the Apes is a 1972 American science fiction film directed by J. Lee Thompson and written by Paul Dehn. It serves as a sequel to Escape from the Planet of the Apes (1971) and is the fourth installment in the original Planet of the Apes film series. The cast includes Roddy McDowall, Don Murray, Ricardo Montalbán, Natalie Trundy, and Hari Rhodes. Set in a future world that has embraced ape slavery, the narrative centers on Caesar, the son of Cornelius and Zira. Caesar surfaces from hiding and organizes a rebellion against humanity.

Conquest of the Planet of the Apes is the only film in the series to omit a pre-title sequence. In the screenplay and the novelization, a nighttime prologue depicts police shooting an escaped ape, with the body showing welts that suggest severe abuse. Governor Breck's later remark about the ape who assaulted his master prompts MacDonald to attribute the escape to mistreatment. The scene also appears in John Jakes’ novelization (chapter 1) and in the Marvel Comics adaptation, likely drawn from the screenplay rather than the final film edit. A Cinefantastique article from 1972, written by Dale Winogura, documents the scene being shot, though the reasons for its removal remain unclear. The Blu-ray extended cut of the film does not include this pre-credit opening.

Spotting is a dance technique used during turning movements to maintain the head and eyes in a consistently oriented position. By stabilizing the gaze throughout rotation, it enhances a dancer’s control over movement and balance. The technique also helps prevent dizziness that can accompany spins, making turns smoother and more reliable.

Spotting is a dance technique used to stabilize performers during many turns by maintaining a brief, fixed gaze that aids orientation and control. It is commonly applied to movements such as pirouettes and chaînés, though in some turning styles it is deliberately avoided or minimized to suit the choreography. Adagio turns, which aim to convey serenity and calm, would be disturbed by the abrupt head motions associated with traditional spotting. As a result, adagio-style turns may be executed with more restrained head movement, and can include turns performed in positions such as arabesque or attitude.

Pop, the British and Irish television channel, began producing original content for the first time in 2022. As part of this foray into in‑house programming, the channel approached Joe Tasker to develop a new show, with the proposed program bearing the title "Swipe It! With Joe Tasker."

During the channel's early years, links were presented by Rorry, a lime-green animated dragon who had previously hosted a Saturday morning show in autumn 1997 and was later repurposed for Pop. Rorry's predecessor Tricky had spoken with a northern English dialect, while Rorry used a Scottish accent; both versions were animated live using computer-generated cues. Rorry was accompanied by Purrdy, a dragon–cat hybrid who also appeared in Tricky's original ITV programme. The linking segments were sometimes followed by The Cheeky Monkey Show, which featured live links from The Cheeky Monkeys, a group of animated colored monkeys.

Maritime call signs are allocated by a national licensing authority to identify both commercial and naval vessels during radio communications. In flags of convenience such as Liberia and Panama, the assigned signs typically consist of a national prefix followed by three letters, for example 3LXY, and may be extended with a numeral to form forms like 3LXY2. United States-flagged merchant ships carry call signs that start with W or K, whereas United States Navy ships use call signs beginning with N. Historically, ship and broadcasting station call signs were three or four letters long, but growing demand led American-flagged vessels to adopt longer call signs that mix letters and numbers.

Maritime call signs in the United States are typically not assigned to leisure vessels equipped with VHF radios, which commonly operate under the vessel’s registered name. Those that pursue an official radio license fall under the FCC’s Ship Recreational or Voluntarily Equipped service, designated as SA. When a call sign is issued to such ships, it follows the land mobile pattern used in the country: it begins with the prefix K or W, is followed by one or two letters, and then ends with three or four numerals. Examples of this format include KX0983 and WXX0029.

Rebecca Bligh serves as president of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM). The FCM is a national association that represents the interests of Canadian cities to the federal government, coordinating advocacy and policy initiatives to advance municipal priorities.

Rebecca Bligh was elected to Vancouver’s city council as a member of the Non-Partisan Association (NPA). She left the NPA in 2019, arguing that the party’s ideology had shifted toward the far-right after a new executive was elected. In 2018, NPA mayoral candidate Ken Sim voiced concerns that echoed Bligh’s assessment. Bligh’s fellow NPA councillors Melissa De Genova, Lisa Dominato, Colleen Hardwick, and Sarah Kirby-Yung did not resign from the party but distanced themselves from its board. By 2022, all except De Genova had departed from the NPA. Bligh, Dominato, and Kirby-Yung subsequently re-affiliated with ABC Vancouver, while Hardwick joined TEAM for a Livable Vancouver.

World Cup 98 is a video game that features every national team that qualified for the 1998 FIFA World Cup in France. The game also includes eight non-qualifying teams: Australia, Canada, China, Greece, Portugal, Republic of Ireland, Russia, and Sweden. All teams are depicted with authentic kits.

World Cup 98 is a football simulation video game whose central feature is a mode that replicates the FIFA World Cup tournament. Players can choose either the real final-tournament groups from the 1998 World Cup or groups drawn at random from a pool of 40 teams included in the game. Each match is staged in a recreation of the venue where the corresponding real-world match was played, adding authenticity to the experience. In the group stage, games conclude within regulation time without extra time or penalties, while knockout-round matches proceed to extra time and, if needed, penalties.

Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum Stadium (Arabic: ملعب مكتوم بن راشد آل مكتوم) is a multi-use stadium located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Named in honor of Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the venue is primarily used for football matches. It formerly served as the home stadium of the Al Shabab Al Arabi Club in the UAE Pro League. Following the merger of Al Shabab with Al Ahli and Dubai to form Shabab Al-Ahli Club, the facility operates as a secondary stadium for Shabab Al Ahli. The stadium has a capacity of 12,000 spectators.

A casemate is a design in which the main gun is mounted directly in the hull without a rotating turret. This arrangement simplifies the mechanical layout, reduces production costs, lowers weight, and yields a reduced overall silhouette. The resulting weight savings can be redirected toward mounting a more powerful gun or toward enhanced armor protection compared with turreted tanks. A principal drawback is that the crew must rotate the entire vehicle to bear on targets outside the gun's limited traverse, a limitation that proves disadvantageous in combat.

Casemate is a term in naval architecture that has been employed in several configurations within warship design. It generally denotes a protected space for mounting and operating artillery within the body of the ship, whether inside the hull or in a dedicated portion of the superstructure, allowing weapons to be operated from a sheltered position. The concept emphasizes enclosure and protection for the guns and crews, distinguishing these positions from unprotected, deck-mounted armament.

Between 1991 and 2012, the Netherlands national basketball team experienced a pronounced decline in competitive performance. During this period, the team failed to qualify for the European Championship, highlighting a sustained struggle at the continental level.
Basketball Nederland (Dutch: Basketbal Nederland) is the governing body of basketball in the Netherlands. The organization was founded in 1947 and is headquartered in Nieuwegein.

Bluetooth A2DP historically supported only unidirectional audio transmission, limiting headsets to playback without microphone input. Cambridge Silicon Radio (CSR) developed a technique to append a reverse-direction voice channel alongside the main stereo stream, enabling microphone-enabled headsets to operate over A2DP. The practical implementation of this approach is realized in the FastStream codec, which builds on SBC by using fixed parameters and an additional voice-back channel.

SBC, short for Low-Complexity Subband Coding, is an audio subband codec specified by the Bluetooth Special Interest Group for use with the A2DP profile. It operates as a digital encoder and decoder for transmitting audio data to Bluetooth audio output devices such as headphones and loudspeakers, and it can also be employed for streaming over the Internet. The design emphasizes efficiency to accommodate Bluetooth bandwidth limitations and processing power, aiming to provide reasonable audio quality at medium bitrates with low computational complexity. Since A2DP version 1.3, Low-Complexity Subband Coding has been the default codec for the profile, and its use is mandatory for devices that support the profile, though vendors may add their own codecs.

Membership in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints becomes official after baptism, a blessing, or parental request. The church records the membership and maintains membership records to establish and sustain individuals as members.

The article presents membership statistics for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, drawing on figures officially reported by the Church as of December 31, 2023. Population denominators are sourced from the latest CIA estimates, primarily for 2024 unless noted otherwise, and the share of adherents is calculated using those CIA-derived population figures. Additionally, the text notes that hyperlinks attached to country or territory names lead to concise histories and statistical information for the respective area.

In 1891 the Liberal Party rose to power as New Zealand's first organized political party, inaugurating a reformist era in national politics. The Liberal Government, led for much of its tenure by Richard Seddon, pursued a broad program of social and economic reforms. In 1893, New Zealand became the first country to grant women the right to vote. The following year, the government introduced compulsory arbitration between employers and unions and established a legally guaranteed minimum wage, a milestone on the global stage.

New Zealand experiences a general snow season that typically runs from early June to early October, though cold snaps may occur outside this period. Snowfall is particularly common in the eastern and southern parts of the South Island, while mountain regions across the country regularly receive snow, reflecting the country's widespread alpine conditions.

During the War in the Vendée, the Vendéen forces fighting under Catholic and royalist banners displayed a marked reluctance to remain away from their homes for extended periods, returning to their villages after only brief engagements. This pattern undermined their ability to hold captured towns, as their attachment to homeland and local ties prevented sustained occupation. Consequently, urban centers such as Angers, Saumur, Thouars, and Fontenay-le-Comte were progressively abandoned by the Vendéens, and these towns were subsequently retaken by Republican forces without difficulty.

Clerical opponents of the Revolution did not participate directly in the war. A small number of priests did secure seats on royalist councils, where their duties were largely limited to handling correspondence rather than engaging in battlefield command. Among the Vendéens, serving as an officer or taking part in combat was generally regarded unfavorably.

Teva Pharmaceuticals exported medical products from the British Mandate of Palestine to Arab countries during the period, reflecting early regional trade activity. In 1941, Friedländer presented Teva’s products at an exhibition in Cairo, Egypt, an event sponsored by the General Agent and Sole Distributor of medicines in Egypt and Sudan, Syria and Lebanon. Subsequently, Teva expanded its exports to the United States, the Soviet Union, and to health institutes in Denmark, Czechoslovakia, Persia, and Burma.

In February 2022, Teva Pharmaceuticals reached a settlement with the state of Texas worth $225 million, resolving allegations that the company contributed to Texas’s opioid epidemic through the improper promotion of pain medications. The claims centered on Teva’s marketing of these analgesic drugs, and the agreement brought an end to the litigation over these marketing practices.

Archaeological finds in Normandy, including the golden Gaulish helmet uncovered at Amfreville-sous-les-Monts and an iron helmet now housed in the Louviers museum, illustrate a Celtic presence in the region. The Pîtres necropolis in Eure yields cremation urns, swords with a coiled design, and traces of chariot tombs, while the Ifs necropolis in Calvados is dated to the late Hallstatt period or the early La Tène period. Taken together, these discoveries indicate a Celtic population in present-day Normandy. The Celtic communities of this area are understood to have been part of Armorica, a confederation of culturally related groups along the English Channel and Atlantic coast from the Seine to the Loire.

Normandy is renowned for its pastry tradition and features a range of distinctive regional specialties. Notable pastries include douillons (pears baked in pastry), craquelins, roulettes from Rouen, fouaces from Caen, fallues and sablés from Lisieux. The region is also the birthplace of brioches, especially associated with Évreux and Gisors. In addition to baked confections, Normandy’s regional sweets encompass Rouen apple sugar, Isigny caramels, Bayeux mint chews, Falaise berlingots, Le Havre marzipans, Argentan croquettes, and Rouen macaroons.

Following the cessation of hostilities, the United States Navy continued the large-scale repatriation of Allied personnel, and the USS Wharton (AP-7) played a key role in this effort. During three western Pacific voyages conducted through the end of 1945 as part of Operation Magic Carpet, the ship carried veterans from the Army, Navy, and Marine Corps back to the United States. Her ports of call during these operations included Eniwetok, Guam, Saipan, Samar, Tacloban, and Puerto Princesa, among others, as she facilitated the return of personnel homeward. In February 1946, Wharton completed one additional Magic Carpet voyage to Yokosuka, Japan.

USS Wharton (AP-7) served as a United States Navy troop transport during World War II, principally in the Southwest Pacific and the Aleutian theater from 1942 to 1943. In the June–September 1942 interval she completed three Southwest Pacific voyages with calls at Pago Pago, Auckland, Espiritu Santo, Nouméa, Canton Island, and Suva. During August 6–11, 1942 she carried 15 officers and 465 enlisted of the 6th Naval Construction Battalion from American Samoa to Espiritu Santo, while the balance of the 6th NCB (7 officers, 433 enlisted) remained aboard the SS President Polk, which ferried the 7th NCB from Samoa. Wharton then returned to the West Coast for an overhaul that extended into October 1942. From December 1942 through February 1943 she undertook Aleutian runs, transporting troops from Seattle to Kodiak and Dutch Harbor and returning with civilians, troops, and patients. The remainder of 1942 included five additional Southwest Pacific trips, revisiting Pago Pago, Nouméa, Suva, Espiritu Santo (where the 7th NCB was embarked for return to the United States on 20 November 1943) and Wellington. Subsequent itineraries added Apia in British Samoa, Guadalcanal in the Solomons, and Efate in the New Hebrides.

In 2019, planners proposed splitting the eastern segment of Line 6, located to the east of Botanical Garden Station, into a distinct line. Under the plan, the eastern portion would be operated as a separate line, taking over the section beyond Botanical Garden and running southward to Canton Tower station. The proposed line was provisionally designated as Line 20.

Line 6 of the Guangzhou Metro was originally conceived as an auxiliary light-metro line, with forecasts predicting about 428,000 daily riders two years after opening and roughly 507,000 after nine years, based on a 2010 opening date and a smaller city population. These projections matched earlier ridership levels observed on Lines 1 and 2 before 2004, which were considered underutilized. National policy favored short, high-frequency trains, leading to a shift away from Type A rolling stock toward smaller configurations such as Type B and L trains. After Line 3 experienced overcrowding by 2006, scrutiny increased toward lines under construction with limited design capacity, particularly Lines 5 and 6. Line 6 was built with four-car Type L trains, reflecting limited capacity, and upgrading to longer trains proved impractical because station structures had already been completed. A 2009 internal Guangzhou Metro report proposed six-car B-type stock, similar to that used on Line 3, which could have increased Line 6 capacity by about 50 percent. Expansion would have been complicated by land expropriation and resident relocation, as evidenced by delays at Yide Lu and Shahe stations. The line opened in 2013, and by 2014 daily ridership reached around 600,000 and continued to rise. Peak ridership reached 858,000 on 16 September 2016. The Phase II Changban–Xiangxue extension opened in late 2016, and ridership averaged about 850,000 per day by April 2018. Since 2017, daily ridership frequently exceeds 1 million during peak periods such as holidays.

During Gurtenfestival, the British band Oasis headlined a Saturday night performance in Switzerland; the show marked the group's final concert in the country, occurring before Oasis disbanded in August 2009.
At Gurtenfestival, the French hip hop group IAM was scheduled to perform; however, a crew member fell ill several days before the event, resulting in IAM's absence from the festival.

On 18 August 1843, the Linden Opera was destroyed by fire, after which reconstruction was overseen by architect Carl Ferdinand Langhans, and the Königliches Opernhaus, known as the Royal Opera House, was inaugurated in the autumn following the blaze. The inaugural performance was Giacomo Meyerbeer’s Ein Feldlager in Schlesien. In 1849, Otto Nicolai’s Die lustigen Weiber von Windsor premiered at the Royal Opera House, conducted by Nicolai himself.

During the 1920s, the Berlin State Opera hosted a distinguished roster of conductors, including Kurt Adler, Wilhelm Furtwängler, Erich Kleiber, Otto Klemperer, Alexander von Zemlinsky, and Bruno Walter, whose leadership helped shape the company's artistic profile. A notable event from this era occurred in 1925, when Alban Berg's Wozzeck received its premiere in a production conducted by Kleiber, with the composer himself in attendance, highlighting the institution's prominence in presenting contemporary music.

Major newspapers retired Linotype and other hot metal typesetting machines predominantly during the 1970s and 1980s, as operations shifted to phototypesetting and later to computerized typesetting and page composition systems. This transition marked the move from traditional mechanical typesetting to modern digital workflows across the industry. By 2023, the Saguache Crescent of Colorado was the last-known U.S. newspaper still using Linotype, while Le Démocrate de l'Aisne in Western Europe was identified as the last Linotype newspaper in the region.

On a Linotype machine, once enough text has been prepared for a line, the operator activates the casting lever located at the front-right of the keyboard. The lever raises the completed line into the delivery channel situated between the operator’s two fingers and releases the catch holding it. A spring-operated delivery channel then transports the line into the casting section and engages a clutch to drive the casting mechanism and move the line to the distribution section. The operator is finished with that line, and the remaining processing occurs automatically. While the line is being cast, the operator can continue entering text for the next line.

Peosta, Iowa, has a median age of 30.2 years, indicating a relatively young population. The age distribution comprises 38.9% under 18, 4.9% from 18 to 24, 35.8% from 25 to 44, 16.1% from 45 to 64, and 4.3% aged 65 and over. The gender composition is 48.7% male and 51.3% female, reflecting a near-even split between sexes.

Peosta, Iowa, was historically a quiet rural town with about 100 residents, and a post office opened there in 1858. The groundwork for growth occurred in the 1960s with the opening of a four-lane U.S. Route 20 along the town’s southern edge, providing rapid access to Dubuque. In 1979, Northeast Iowa Technical Institute opened in Peosta, later known as Northeast Iowa Community College (NICC). Significant growth began in the 1990s as the industrial park flourished. The population increased from 128 in 1990 to more than 1,300 in recent decades, a rise of roughly 1,000 percent over twenty years, and this expansion attracted new businesses and services. Today, Peosta offers two elementary schools, a community center, a hotel, a church, an active industrial park, and expanding neighborhoods.

Terschelling Frisian, also known in Frisian as Skylgersk, constitutes the language variety spoken on the island of Terschelling. Within this variety, Westersk is the western dialect and Aastersk the eastern dialect. Westersk is estimated to have about 800 speakers, while Aastersk accounts for around 400 speakers. The Frisian name for the island itself is Skylge.

Schiermonnikoog Frisian (Skiermûntseagersk) is the most endangered variety within the West Frisian languages. It is spoken on the island of Schiermonnikoog, where the population stands at about 900 residents, and it is also known by the alternative name Skiermûntseach. The language is estimated to have no more than roughly 50 to 100 speakers.

This article enumerates the individuals who have represented West Virginia in the United States Senate. The state’s two Senate seats are assigned to Class 1 and Class 2. The current holders are Shelley Moore Capito, a Republican, in office since 2015, and Jim Justice, a Republican, in office since 2025.

Robert Byrd holds the distinction of West Virginia's longest-serving senator, representing the state from 1959 until his death in 2010. Across more than five decades in the United States Senate, Byrd achieved the status of the longest-serving member in the history of the chamber.

Taipei County was elevated to a special municipality in 2010 and renamed New Taipei City. The Chinese name 新北市 literally translates as "New Northern City." The initial English rendering, based on pinyin, was Xinbei City, a form opposed by both candidates in the first mayoral election. In response to public opinion, Mayor Eric Chu sought approval from the Ministry of the Interior to adopt "New Taipei City" as the English name. The ministry granted the rendering, making "New Taipei City" official on 31 December 2010.

Taipei County, now known as New Taipei City, functions as Taiwan's second-most important business center after Taipei, a status attributed to its strategic location. The area encompasses more than 250,000 privately owned companies, including Acer Computers Inc., and contains about 20,000 factories distributed across five industrial parks, with total capital of NT$1.8 trillion. In terms of economic composition, the high‑tech, service, and tourism sectors make substantial contributions to Taiwan's GDP, underpinned by five principal industries: information technology, telecommunications, digital contents, biotechnology, and precision instruments. In information technology production, it ranks among the top three globally, accounting for more than half of the world's market share in products such as motherboards, notebooks, LCD monitors, and CRT monitors.

Banjarese restricts syllable structure so that CVC syllables can be closed only by the consonants /p t k m n ŋ s h r l/; word-initial positions do not permit consonant clusters. Within a root, nasal-consonant (NC) sequences are always homorganic, sharing the same place of articulation. Through reduplication and certain prefixes (for example, the prefix sing-), additional NC sequences can be formed, such as /ŋb, ŋp, ŋt, ŋr, ŋl, kr/. In addition, the language exhibits a range of medial sequences, including /kt/, /kn/, /ŋn/, /nɲ/, /st/, /sn/, /hk/, /hj/, /lk/, and /rɡ/.

Banjarese is a Malayo-Polynesian language spoken by the Banjar people of southern Kalimantan and comprises several dialects, including Banjar Hulu, which is predominantly used by Banjar communities in the South Hulu Sungai and North Hulu Sungai regencies. The Berangas language, also a member of the Barito language subgroup, is nearly extinct in South Kalimantan. Berangas maintains a close relationship with the Banjar Kuala dialect, and within Banjar Kuala it has absorbed a substantial portion of Banjarese vocabulary. Lexically, Berangas shows greater similarity to other Barito languages, particularly Bakumpai.

In its standard orientation, the Mercator projection features a scale that increases with latitude, causing the size of geographic features to be exaggerated as one moves away from the equator. This results in a distorted representation of the Earth's overall geometry. As latitude approaches the polar regions, the scale factor grows without bound, rendering the projection practically unusable beyond roughly 70 degrees north or south, and it cannot fully render polar areas. Other variants, namely oblique and transverse Mercator projections, have practical uses for specific applications.

Because the Mercator projection maps latitude to a vertical coordinate that diverges toward infinity at the poles, practical maps truncate the representation at latitudes below 90 degrees. This truncation need not be symmetric about the equator. The original Mercator map was cut off at 80°N in the northern hemisphere and 66°S in the southern hemisphere, a choice that tends to move European countries toward the map’s center. The aspect ratio of the original map is 198/120, approximately 1.65. More extreme truncations have been used, such as a Finnish atlas that ends at about 76°N and 56°S, with an aspect ratio around 1.97.

Ben Peters contributed three songs to Jeannie C. Riley's 1968 album The Harper Valley P.T.A., including "The Little Town Square," "That's A No No," and "Satan Place." The album, released in 1968, achieved million-seller status for Riley.
Ben Peters contributed two songs, "Mr. Mistletoe" and "Soon It Will Be Christmas Day," to Lynn Anderson's holiday album The Christmas Album, which was released in 1971.

D.A.V. Public School Sreshtha Vihar (DAVSV) is part of the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Schools System, a network of educational institutions with campuses across India and Pakistan. The school is located in East Delhi, in the Sreshtha Vihar locality of Delhi, India.

D.A.V Public School Sreshtha Vihar organizes an annual sports day that showcases a wide range of athletic and competitive events. In addition to this, the school hosts a variety of contests throughout the year, with participation from students, teachers, and other staff members.

Wichita, Kansas is home to several notable sports venues, including Intrust Bank Arena, a downtown 15,000-seat multi-purpose arena that serves as the home venue of the Wichita Thunder. Nearby, Lawrence–Dumont Stadium sits just west of downtown as a mid-sized baseball stadium that has housed Wichita’s various minor-league teams over the years. The same stadium also served as the home of the National Baseball Congress and was the site of the Congress's annual National Tournament.

Wichita, Kansas, grew into a major oil town largely due to the early 20th-century oil boom in adjacent Butler County, which spurred a wide range of oil-exploration firms and related support enterprises in the city. The local industry included a number of notable companies, with Koch, Inc. standing out as the most prominent and later evolving into a global natural-resources conglomerate under Koch Industries. Wichita also served as the headquarters for the Derby Oil Company for a period, a firm that was eventually purchased by Coastal Corporation in 1988.

UEFA Euro 2020 was staged across 11 host countries, though only nine of them qualified for the final tournament. Among the hosts, seven qualified automatically: Denmark, England, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Russia, and Spain, while Hungary and Scotland advanced through the hosts’ play-off route. Azerbaijan and Romania did not reach the finals, with Azerbaijan eliminated in the group stage and Romania ousted in the play-offs. Ireland, initially designated as a host nation, was stripped of hosting duties by UEFA two months before the tournament amid a surge of COVID-19 cases in early 2021, and subsequently failed to qualify after losing in the play-offs.

Amid concerns over the COVID-19 pandemic and to ease player fatigue from congested fixtures, UEFA explored increasing the squad size for UEFA Euro 2020 from 23 to 26 players in April 2021. The expansion received provisional approval from the UEFA National Team Competitions Committee on 27 April 2021, pending confirmation by the UEFA Executive Committee. The Executive Committee subsequently confirmed on 4 May 2021 that 26-player squads would be used. Teams were still required to name a maximum of 23 players on the match sheet for each fixture, with 12 substitutes available, and the group of 23 had to include at least three goalkeepers. Additionally, after a team's first match, a goalkeeper may be replaced due to physical incapacity, even if other goalkeepers from the squad are available.

Critical reception of The Joy centered on its lyrical content and retro-inflected production. Pitchfork’s Ryan Dombal described the lyrics as hypocritical, citing a line he deemed revisionist given West’s history of Daft Punk sampling, the success of Flashing Lights, and the designer image West had cultivated; nonetheless he praised Rock’s production and argued that the perceived hypocrisy is softened by the artists’ strong hip-hop lineage, calling the track a distinctive throwback that flattens time and sustains an endless flow. The Guardian’s Alex Peditris echoed the lyric critique, highlighting a warm Curtis Mayfield sample moment and a remark attributed to Jay-Z, while noting West’s complaints about South Park and some clumsy wordplay. Amrit Singh of Stereogum regarded the track as evidence that Jay-Z is back in fighting shape on the project. Taken together, critics identify a deliberate retro sensibility paired with polished production and a robust hip-hop lineage, even as they acknowledge tensions in the lyric writing.

The Joy (song) is a track whose lyrics explore nostalgia and abortion, as well as the regret associated with those themes. Critics have described its mood as laid-back and smooth, contributing to a restrained, easygoing tonal quality. The production was handled by Rock in collaboration with West, with additional production by Mike Dean and Jeff Bhasker.

Archaeological investigations in the Niger region indicate early metalworking, with copper and bronze production sites that may date to roughly 1500 BCE, and evidence of ironworking at Termit, Niger around the same period. By contrast, Nubia developed into a major producer and exporter of iron following the Assyrian expulsion of the Nubian dynasty from Egypt in the seventh century BCE, reflecting a shift in metallurgical specialization and regional trade during the Iron Age.

During the Iron Age, Lingnan metallurgical practices merged bivalve shell moulding, rooted in southern traditions, with piece-mould casting techniques borrowed from the Zhongyuan. This integrated approach facilitated the production of a range of cast objects, including bells, vessels, weapons, and ornaments. The resulting castings are regarded as highly sophisticated in design and workmanship.

The Northeast-10 Conference, whose name originated in 1987 with the admission of Saint Michael's College and Quinnipiac College, underwent several membership changes in the following years. Springfield College departed in 1995 to compete at the Division III level. Le Moyne College joined in 1996, transferring from the New England Collegiate Conference and keeping the conference at ten members. Pace University then joined in 1997 from the New York Collegiate Athletic Conference, briefly expanding the membership to eleven. Subsequently, Quinnipiac left to compete in Division I, joining the Northeast Conference and returning the total membership to ten.

During the late 2000s, the Northeast-10 Conference pursued growth and shifts in its membership. In 2008, Bryant University announced a five-year plan to attain full Division I membership by 2012. The conference also extended a bid to the University of New Haven, which accepted the invitation to join. Adelphi University announced in December 2007 its intention to join the league and began competing in the 2009–10 academic year. As a result of these changes, the NE10’s membership increased from fifteen institutions at the start of the 2008–09 academic year to sixteen in 2009–10.

The fiscorn is a low brass instrument whose origins lie in polka bands across Germany and the former Czechoslovakia, as well as in Italian military ensembles, before migrating to Catalonia where it has become established. It is favored over other valved low brass for its haunting, mellow timbre and bell-front projection, and it subsequently developed into a core component of the cobla ensemble alongside the tenora, tible, and flabiol. Over time, however, it fell out of favor in many musical groups due to intonation difficulties. The instrument possesses a powerful baritone range with no exact organological counterpart, though some similarities have been drawn to the piston-valved marching baritone. Its forward-projecting sound supports pairing two fiscorns with the shrill Catalan shawms—tenora and tible—and the flabiol, along with trumpets and trombone, in outdoor cobla performances for sardana dancers.

The fiscorn is a low brass instrument that is commonly played by trombonists. Its conical bore is readily accessible to players accustomed to the tuba or euphonium. In recent years, manufacturers have attempted to address its intonation discrepancies, with mixed results. The instrument is taught across Catalonia, notably at the Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya (ESMUC) in Barcelona and at the Conservatoire à Rayonnement Régional (CRR) in Perpignan, France.

Slotsholmen, an island at the heart of Copenhagen, is dominated by Christiansborg Palace, which houses the Danish Parliament, the Supreme Court, and the Prime Minister's Office, together with the King’s State Rooms. The island also hosts major ministries and is home to both the Danish National Archives and the Royal Danish Library. In addition, it contains several museums and preserves historic structures from Christian IV's Stock Exchange, including the Chancellery and Christian IV's Brewhouse.

On Slotsholmen, the small, aging castle persisted into the eighteenth century despite repeated attempts to substitute it with a modern royal residence for an absolute king. Over time, several renovations were undertaken, with the most notable being a major project commissioned by Frederick IV from 1721 to 1729. This rebuilding altered the castle’s irregular silhouette, giving it a more regular and cohesive shape.

Ion Television, as part of Ion Media, was affected by the acquisition of Ion Media by the E. W. Scripps Company, a transaction that included a merger with Katz Broadcasting. As a result of the deal, Qubo ceased broadcasting on February 28, 2021.

During its period as Pax TV, Ion Television pursued a strategy of increasing paid programming in response to low viewership and financial difficulties, leading infomercials and other brokered programs to become the dominant daytime fare. By January 2005, entertainment programming had been trimmed to six hours on weekdays (5:00 p.m.–11:00 p.m.) and five hours on weekends (5:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m. Central Time). Original programming declined from roughly five to six new series per season to only two in 2003, with the two 2003 introductions—Sue Thomas: F.B.Eye (canceled in 2005) and Doc (canceled in 2004 after international backer CTV pulled out). The network rebounded in 2004–05 with seven new series added to the schedule.

On 28 May 2013, the Indian Space Research Organisation established a new satellite navigation centre, located within the ISRO Deep Space Network facility at Byalalu in Karnataka. The centre coordinates a nationwide network of 21 ranging stations distributed across India, which collect measurements used to determine the orbits of the satellites and to monitor the navigation signal.

As of September 2024, only four satellites within the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System were capable of delivering navigation services. These satellites are IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1F, IRNSS-1I, and NVS-01.

The Bell XP-83 was an experimental fighter aircraft whose first prototype embarked on its initial flight on 25 February 1945, with Jack Woolams at the controls; while the handling characteristics were deemed satisfactory, the design lacked sufficient power. Instability was later confirmed, and spins were avoided until a larger tail fin was installed to improve directional and aerodynamic stability. The second prototype incorporated a redesigned tail and an aileron boost system to enhance controllability. The aircraft tended to achieve very high landing speeds, a consequence of its sleek aerodynamics, the absence of drag brakes, and elevated minimum thrust levels required to prevent flame-outs. Consequently, test pilots had to carry out stabilized, long, flat landing approaches to manage the aircraft's demanding approach and landing characteristics.

Bell XP-83 was an experimental postwar fighter aircraft developed by Bell Aircraft to evaluate ramjet propulsion. The first prototype, completed in 1946, served primarily as a ramjet test-bed and featured an engineer’s station located in the fuselage behind the pilot. On 14 September 1946, a ramjet fire forced the pilot, nicknamed 'Slick' Goodlin, and engineer Charles Fay to bail out. The second prototype flew on 19 October 1946 and was scrapped in 1947. Apart from range, the XP-83 was inferior to the Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star, and the project was canceled in 1947 for that reason.

Within the Dominican Republic’s First Republic, the constitution codified a clear separation between church and state, ensuring that religious institutions operated outside the realm of political governance. This principle complemented the broader division of powers among the government’s branches, reinforcing a system of checks and balances. The state was restricted from intervening in religious affairs, and individuals were guaranteed the freedom to profess the religion of their choice, reflecting a constitutional commitment to religious liberty.

In 1857, tobacco farmers from the Cibao region and Santiago merchants rose in revolt against the Báez government under the leadership of José Desiderio Valverde. The insurgents besieged Santo Domingo, proclaimed a liberal constitution, and moved the capital to Santiago. They accepted the return of Santana and appointed him commander of the besieging forces. After defeating Báez, Santana turned on the Cibaeño liberals, reasserted control, and brought the Cibao Revolution to an end. Exploiting international conditions, including the American Civil War and the expansion of European colonialism, Santana pursued a project of annexation. These developments laid the groundwork for the Dominican Republic’s 1861 annexation to Spain.

MassMutual, short for Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Company, began operations on May 15, 1851, in Springfield, Massachusetts. It was founded by George W. Rice, who contributed $100,000 in guaranteed capital to establish the enterprise. Rice, then an insurance agent who sold policies for the Connecticut Mutual Life Insurance Company in Hartford, sought to create a company of his own within Massachusetts. The venture developed into a mutual life insurance company, adopting a structure similar to that of Connecticut Mutual Life Insurance Company.

MassMutual issued its first $1,000 policy on August 2, 1851. In 1861, Massachusetts enacted a non-forfeiture law that prohibited cancellation of policies for missed premiums and required conversion to term life with death benefits paid during the term, a measure that contributed to increased life-insurance sales. The company grew in tandem with the expanding industry, and by 1873 its assets had reached $4,501,909.

Léon Say was a French statesman and an early advocate of the cooperative movement in France. He was elected to the Assembly of 1871 for the departments of Seine and Seine-et-Oise, and aligned himself with the Department of Seine, sitting with the Moderate Liberals whose principles he would uphold for life. Immediately thereafter, he was named rapporteur to the parliamentary commission on the state of French national finances, and in that capacity produced two substantial analyses. Although Thiers opposed publication on grounds of public expediency, he was nonetheless impressed by the quality of the work. On 5 June, Thiers appointed Say as Prefect of the Seine.

Following the upheavals of the post-war period—the fall of the Second Empire, the siege of Paris, and the Commune—Paris's administration remained in disarray and reconstruction proved arduous. Léon Say was well suited to lead the reconstruction of the prefecture's administration, guiding its reorganization through the difficult years after the conflict. He left the prefecture in December 1872 to accept the post of Minister of Finance. Thiers, whose protectionist views shaped his government, paid him a notable tribute by appointing him to the ministerial rank. In 1872, Say was elected a member of the American Philosophical Society.

Al-Fahaheel Sporting Club, commonly known as Al-Fahaheel, is a Kuwaiti multi-sport club based in Kuwait City. Founded on 19 April 1964, the club fields teams across several disciplines, with its football section competing in the Kuwait Premier League, the top tier of Kuwaiti football.

Al-Fahaheel FC presents its players with national flags denoting their national team eligibility according to FIFA rules, reflecting the standard convention used in contemporary football; there are limited exceptions to this rule, accommodating special cases; and players may hold more than one nationality that is not governed by FIFA.

ISO 5427 is an eight-bit extension of the KOI-7 N1 Cyrillic character set, standardized by the International Organization for Standardization. The specification was issued in two parts, with the first portion published in 1979 and the second in 1981. It provides Cyrillic support for Russian (including the pre-1918 orthography), Belarusian, Bulgarian (including the pre-1945 orthography), Ukrainian, Macedonian, and Serbian languages. Revisions to ISO 5427 were published in July 1983 and October 1983.

Rock on Top of Another Rock presents Fischli and Weiss’s ongoing practice, with director Hans-Ulrich Obrist having been an enthusiastic admirer since first encountering their photography show Equilibres/Quiet Afternoon. Created in 1984, the Equilibres/Quiet Afternoon exhibition remains on view at the gallery, underscoring the enduring relevance of the artists’ work for Obrist. He regards the duo’s newer productions as a convergence point for dialogue, describing this idea through a metaphor in which observers could meet beneath the rocks and discuss a rock resting atop another rock.

Rock on Top of Another Rock is a sculptural installation that presents a rock balanced on another rock, prompting reflection on materiality and display. The work highlights how a rock in the practice of Fischli and Weiss differs from a rock in Smiljan Radic's own approach, illustrating that the same object can be engaged with in distinct ways. Although the subjects are similar, the artists conceive them through different conceptual lenses, and the arrangement of the rocks in space yields markedly different spatial readings. In the end, the object remains fundamentally a rock, a fact underscored by Radic's expressed appreciation for the piece.

Trikiti is a term used for the diatonic button accordion in the Basque musical tradition, and it is generally regarded as having been introduced by Italian migrants from the Alpine regions. The earliest documentary evidence dates to 1889, when a diatonic accordion was used at a popular pilgrimage festival in Urkiola, Biscay. A decade later, in 1890, the instrument appears in a photograph from Altsasu (Navarre), a railway junction, providing one of the first visual attestations of its presence in the area. The precise origins of its spread are debated: some scholars attribute its transmission to Italian influence arriving via the port of Bilbao into the Basque Country, while others contend that Italian railway workers from the Alps brought the instrument directly. The diatonic button accordion itself originated in Vienna in 1829 and subsequently disseminated across Europe, a development that facilitated its adoption in the Basque region.

Trikiti denotes the diatonic button accordion. In traditional practice, ensembles typically consist of two players on trikiti, accompanied by a tambourine and vocal accompaniment. The playing style is highly ornamented and swift, with performers frequently employing staccato triplets to articulate phrases.

In Varanasi, a segment of young Hindu widows cultivates an identity anchored in the Shakti goddess as a strategy to resist social restrictions surrounding widowhood. They align themselves with the cosmic Mother-Goddess and recast widowhood in positive terms, expressing that all children belong to them and that all women are embodiments of the Mother-Goddess, while their own children receive only unconditional affection, akin to the Goddess. This self-identification is said to bolster their positive self-regard. An intimate relationship with the Mother-Goddess is described as fostering an internalized sense of Shakti, conceived as an intrinsic power rather than an external deity. Proponents hold that Shakti represents the true strength and fiery energy of Mahadevi, and that women embody this force more abundantly than men. The widows actively work to build wealth to sustain themselves and their dependents, viewing financial self-sufficiency as a validation of their robust Shakti, or pakka shakti. The case is noted by Indira Goswami, a widowed Indian scholar and writer, who credited Shakti with transforming her own sense of empowerment from powerless to empowered.

Shakti, in Hindu thought, encompasses both widely venerated pan-Indian goddesses and numerous locally worshipped manifestations. The pan-Indian forms are regarded as orthodox and intrinsically pure, approached mainly on ceremonial occasions and typically occupying a peripheral position in everyday life, with limited direct involvement in routine matters. By contrast, local expressions of Shakti address devotees’ daily concerns and are invoked for even minor problems, reflecting a close integration with day-to-day activities. These regional and village deities hold central importance for the practical functioning of Hindu life, guiding rituals, calendars, and community practices. The relationship between devotees and local manifestations is intimate and mutually constitutive, with the two realms—personal devotion and local deity worship—being deeply interwoven in the fabric of daily existence.

Prasat Baksei Chamkrong is a small Hindu temple within the Angkor complex near Siem Reap, Cambodia. It is dedicated to the god Shiva and is believed to have housed a gilded image of the deity in its early history. The structure is visible to the left as one enters Angkor Thom from the southern gate. The temple was dedicated to Yasovarman by his son, King Harshavarman I, and its completion occurred during the reign of Rajendravarman II (944–968 CE).

Prasat Baksei Chamkrong derives its name from a legend, with the name interpreted as referring to a bird that shelters beneath its wings. According to the tale, a king attempting to flee Angkor during a siege was saved when a huge bird landed and shielded him under its wings.

Brooklyn is home to the Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM), which encompasses a 2,109-seat opera house and an 874-seat theater, together with BAM Rose Cinemas, the institution’s in-house art-house venue. Across Downtown Brooklyn in the DUMBO arts district lie Bargemusic and St. Ann’s Warehouse, prominent performance spaces in the neighboring area. The borough’s educational facilities include Brooklyn Technical High School, whose auditorium seats more than 3,000, ranking as the second-largest in New York City after Radio City Music Hall.

Brooklyn hosts several periodicals devoted to arts, culture, and politics. The Brooklyn Rail is a monthly publication that covers arts and politics and is published in Brooklyn. The Cabinet is a quarterly magazine focusing on arts and culture and is published from Brooklyn. Hello Mr. is another publication issued in Brooklyn.

Soul music dominated the United States' African-American music charts during the 1960s and crossed over into the mainstream pop charts, signaling its broad appeal. Otis Redding achieved major exposure at the Monterey International Pop Festival in 1967, helping elevate the genre's profile. The style also gained substantial popularity in the United Kingdom, where many leading acts toured extensively in the late 1960s. As an umbrella category, soul encompassed a broad spectrum of R&B-based forms, ranging from Motown's dance-oriented pop acts such as the Temptations, Marvin Gaye, and Stevie Wonder to the more austere, deep soul performers like Percy Sledge and James Carr. Regional scenes across major U.S. cities—New York City, Detroit, Chicago, Memphis, New Orleans, Philadelphia, and Muscle Shoals, Alabama—developed distinct subgenres and recording styles. In particular, Muscle Shoals is home to FAME Studios and the Muscle Shoals Sound Studios.

Soul has exerted a substantial influence on a broad range of electronic music artists, shaping the sound and approach of many producers. Several subgenres, including house, drum and bass, UK garage, and downtempo, incorporate soulful elements in rhythm, harmony, and vocal delivery. As a result of this cross-pollination, a considerable body of music across these styles features soul-inspired characteristics, blending traditional soulful aesthetics with contemporary electronic production.

The tropical monsoon climate is principally governed by its relationship to the monsoon circulation, a system defined by a seasonal reversal of winds. The monsoon, by definition, involves a cyclical change in wind direction over the year. In Asia, the summer or high-sun season is marked by onshore flow, with air moving from the ocean toward the land, while the winter or low-sun season experiences offshore flow, with air moving from the land toward the sea. This directional shift is driven by the differential heating of land and sea, since the land heats and cools at different rates than the adjacent ocean.

The tropical monsoon climate is defined by a highly seasonal pattern featuring an extremely wet season and a clearly defined dry season. The dry season is similar in duration and character to that found in tropical savanna climates. Following this dry interval, there is a prolonged spell of exceptionally heavy rainfall, which in some regions can produce monthly totals reaching or exceeding 1,000 millimeters for two or more consecutive months. By comparison, tropical savanna climates generally do not experience such extended periods of intense rainfall.

USS Guadalcanal (LPH-7) was decommissioned in 1994 and subsequently stored as part of the James River Reserve Fleet. It was later utilized as a target and sunk in the Virginia Capes area, with the sinking occurring on 19 May 2005.

USS Guadalcanal (LPH-7) undertook leadership of minesweeping operations in the Persian Gulf in 1987 during the Iran–Iraq War, where it encountered the Iranian vessel Ajr laying mines in shipping lanes; its helicopters attacked Ajr, and a boarding party subsequently captured the ship. The capture is noted as the second instance of an enemy warship seized on the high seas by the United States Navy since 1815, the first having been the German submarine U-505, taken in 1944 by the first USS Guadalcanal, then an escort carrier. Later, Guadalcanal supplied Marines for the initial wave of Operation Provide Comfort, the Kurdish relief mission in Northern Iraq following the 1991 Persian Gulf War.

Power projection denotes a state's capacity to extend its influence beyond its borders. Its global reach became feasible through innovations associated with the Industrial Revolution, which stimulated modernization across technology, communications, finance, and bureaucratic administration. These shifts collectively enhanced the ability of states to generate unparalleled wealth, expanding the scale of resources at their disposal. With this wealth, governments could marshal capabilities—economic, technical, and military—to extend power over great distances and influence events abroad.

Power projection in contemporary warfare has to contend with cyber operations, geography, and logistics. In January 2022 Ukrainian government websites were subjected to cyberattacks attributed to hostile actors, illustrating cyberspace as a dimension of strategic influence. The seasonal snows give way to a muddy period that can hamper armored advances and complicate supply lines, potentially slowing any invasion. When considering a rapid fait accompli followed by consolidation, critics argue that Russia’s logistics would struggle to support a large-scale land grab because it relies primarily on rail corridors rather than trucks; without rail transport, estimates place Russia’s logistical reach at around 90 miles (approximately 140 kilometers) before replenishment is required. Sebastien Roblin has proposed a scenario of a short, decisive war emulating the 2008 Georgian conflict, with aims such as installing a pro-Russian administration in Ukraine, Ukraine’s withdrawal from NATO, and bypassing Kyiv to avoid urban stalemate. By contrast, a protracted conflict featuring determined Ukrainian resistance and guerrilla operations could overturn such calculations and potentially derail Moscow’s objectives, drawing a parallel with the long, irregular war in Afghanistan. Historical parallels also note that the First Chechen War provoked an antiwar movement within Russia within two months of its outset.

Chiaroscuro, as it appears in European painting, varied in intensity across regions. Outside the Low Countries, artists such as Georges de La Tour, Trophime Bigot, and Joseph Wright of Derby pursued a strong yet graduated candlelight chiaroscuro. Watteau, by contrast, employed a gentler chiaroscuro in the leafy backgrounds of his fêtes galantes. This softer treatment was continued by many French painters, most notably Fragonard. Toward the end of the eighteenth century, Fuseli and others began to use a heavier chiaroscuro to heighten romantic effects. In the nineteenth century, painters including Delacroix likewise adopted a more pronounced chiaroscuro.

Chiaroscuro denotes the treatment of light and shadow used to give form and volume, often through strong tonal contrasts that create drama. In the 20th century, the rising reputation of Caravaggio helped popularize the term among non-specialists, broadening its application beyond technical discourse. Consequently, it is frequently used to describe powerful lighting effects associated with artists such as Caravaggio or Rembrandt, rather than to denote a formal art-theoretical category. The Tate defines chiaroscuro as a feature that is typically noted only when it forms a particularly prominent aspect of a work, usually involving extreme contrasts between light and shade.

Public opinion in Taiwan largely opposed the PRC's Anti-Secession Law, according to surveys showing broad dissatisfaction. Some observers questioned Beijing's authority to enact such legislation, contending that Taiwan is not under PRC jurisdiction. The Pan-Green Coalition reacted with distaste and urged the Legislative Yuan to pass an anti-annexation law in response. Premier Frank Hsieh argued that the PRC law infringed ROC sovereignty and could meet the ROC constitution's criteria for initiating a defensive referendum, though the decision to invoke such a referendum would rest with the ROC president.

The Anti-Secession Law refers to proposals and leaked drafts within the People’s Republic of China that were intended to formalize the unification of Taiwan under PRC authority. These efforts formed part of unsuccessful attempts to shift public opinion in Taiwan toward acceptance of unification. In May 2004, Premier Wen Jiabao told Chinese expatriates in London that serious consideration of such a law would be pursued. A few days later, Yu’s suggestion emerged, described as similar to a green paper.

MediaFire is a file hosting, file synchronization, and cloud storage service based in Shenandoah, Texas, United States. It was founded in June 2006 by Derek Labian and Tom Langridge. The company provides client software for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, BlackBerry 10, and web browsers.

MediaFire offers business accounts that enable shared storage across sub-accounts, accompanied by centralized billing and administrative controls suited for organizations with multiple users within a single company. The free tier preserves uploaded files without requiring download activity, making it primarily appropriate for backup-oriented use rather than regular file access. MediaFire does not officially support free data warehousing, or long-term storage for free and inactive accounts.

The 2025 Supercopa de España is the 41st edition of the competition, an annual football tournament for clubs within the Spanish football league system. Qualified clubs are those that achieved success in the major competitions during the preceding season.
The Icelandic Music Awards, known in Icelandic as Íslensku tónlistarverðlaunin, are the official annual music awards of Iceland. They commemorate the musical achievements of the year.

Icelandic Music Awards, established in 1993, originated as an annual rock prize presented by the Union of Icelandic Musicians (Félag íslenskra hljómlistarmanna, FÍH). Since then it has evolved into a multi-category awards ceremony that covers a broad range of Icelandic music. The event is typically held in January or February, with awards honoring achievements from the preceding year.

Connecticut's air transportation network centers on Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks, the state's largest facility, located about 15 miles (24 km) north of Hartford. For international travel, central and southern residents often utilize John F. Kennedy International Airport and Newark Liberty International Airport. Tweed New Haven Regional Airport serves as a smaller regional facility. Other significant civil airports include Danbury Municipal Airport and Waterbury-Oxford Airport in western Connecticut, Hartford–Brainard Airport in the central region, and Groton–New London Airport in the eastern part of the state. Sikorsky Memorial Airport in Stratford primarily handles cargo, helicopter operations, and private aviation.

Connecticut has been described as one of the states with pronounced racial segregation. The nonwhite population is largely concentrated in the state's principal urban centers, namely Bridgeport, Hartford, New Haven, and Waterbury.
