In many cases, nearby towns are markedly segregated from these urban areas, producing a clear geographic division in racial composition between core cities and their adjacent communities.

ISO/TS 80004 is the designation for a family of ISO technical specifications focused on nanoscale terminology. The initial component, ISO/TS 27687:2008, defined terms and definitions for nano-objects, including nanoparticles, nanofibres, and nanoplate, within nanotechnologies. This standard was subsequently withdrawn and superseded by ISO/TS 80004-2:2015, which forms part of the ongoing ISO/TS 80004 series.

ISO/TS 80004 provides guidance on recognizing and assessing potential risks associated with the development and use of manufactured nanomaterials, as well as on addressing, deciding on, and communicating those risks. The standard is intended to safeguard the health and safety of the public, consumers, workers, and the environment. It covers risk evaluation and the selection of risk-management actions in the face of incomplete or uncertain information. It also sets out methods for updating underlying assumptions, decisions, and practices as new information becomes available. In addition, it describes approaches organizations can use to promote openness and accountability in how nanomaterials are managed. Finally, it outlines a structured process for organizing, documenting, and communicating about these risks.

Hispanic and Latino Americans demonstrate notable rates of LGBT identification. A 2022 poll found that approximately 11% of Hispanic American adults identify as gay, lesbian, bisexual, or transgender, a figure that is more than twice as high as that observed among White Americans and African Americans. Among younger generations, more than 20% of Hispanic Millennials and members of Gen Z report an LGBT identity. Scholars have linked the growth of the young Hispanic population to an overall expansion of the LGBT community within the United States. In addition, research indicates that Hispanic Americans are disproportionately represented among transgender people in the country.

Within the broader context of immigration policy affecting Hispanic and Latino Americans, the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 expanded the class of “qualified aliens” under 8 U.S.C. § 1641 to include certain battered individuals who have experienced battery or extreme cruelty at the hands of a spouse, parent, or another family member living with them. Eligibility for these benefits requires a substantial connection between the abuse and the need for the requested assistance. The expansion applies to aliens with pending INA petitions, such as those based on a spousal or child relationship to a U.S. citizen or applications for suspension of deportation, and it extends to aliens whose children have suffered similar abuse, provided the alien did not actively participate in the abuse. It also covers alien children who reside with an abused parent, though the provisions do not apply if the abuser resides in the same household as the victim. The statute further directs the Attorney General to issue guidance clarifying the meanings of “battery” and “extreme cruelty” and to establish standards for linking abuse to benefit eligibility.

The Open Archival Information System (OAIS) reference model was fully implemented by an architecture demonstrated as part of the #WeMissiPres initiative. It was presented by Frank Obermeit, a computer scientist at the State Archives of Saxony-Anhalt in Germany, on 22 September 2020. An appliance implementing the architecture has been available since October 2020. The model is based exclusively on established standards, drawing on both de facto and de jure specifications, and the appliance is built entirely from open-source components. The design centers on three principal standards: BPMN for process modeling, REST for web services, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for identity management. Its emphasis on scalability, distributability, and extensibility aims to enable deployment across organizations of varying sizes.

Open Archival Information System (OAIS) is a conceptual framework that positions digital information as the primary form for archived materials while treating accompanying information as essential to preservation; it explicitly accommodates non-digital items within its scope, such as physical samples, but does not specify how such information should be modeled or preserved. The model is independent of any specific computing platform or design, and it does not mandate particular technologies, environments, methodologies, database management systems, programming languages, interfaces, or media to meet compliance. Rather, its aim is to standardize the activities involved in preserving a digital archive, rather than prescribing the concrete methods used to implement those activities.

Café & Conditorei 1842 traces its origins to 1842, when baker Johann Georg Eberle established Eberles Süsskramladen. In 1874 his son Julius Carl Heinrich sold the business to Theodor Schrober, a family friend, who renamed it Conditorei von Thomas Schober. The Eberle and Schrober families both hailed from Pfullendorf, Germany. By 2011 the establishment had become known as the Conditorei Schrober Tearoom. It was later acquired by restaurateur Michel Péclard, who renamed it Conditorei Péclard im Schober. In 2019 the current owners, the Arbeitskette Foundation, renamed the venue Café & Conditorei 1842.

Café & Conditorei 1842 is a café and confectionery in Zurich, Switzerland. Founded in 1842, it is the oldest café in the city. The establishment sits on Napfgasse in Zurich's Old Town, in proximity to the Grossmünster. The building comprises six floors, including a basement.

Wilshire/Western station is an underground rapid transit station on the D Line of the Los Angeles Metro Rail system. It is located beneath Wilshire Boulevard at its intersection with Western Avenue. The station's name reflects its position at the Wilshire Boulevard and Western Avenue junction. It lies within the Mid-Wilshire and Koreatown districts of Los Angeles. It is the current western terminus of the D Line.

Wilshire/Western station serves as the current western terminus of the D Line following the termination of plans to extend the line west to Fairfax Avenue and then north into the San Fernando Valley, a project halted by political disagreements. The B Line provides service to the San Fernando Valley via Vermont Avenue. Metro is constructing the D Line Extension to extend westward from Wilshire/Western to a Westwood/VA Hospital station near UCLA.

During 1907 and 1908, Picasso produced notable works from this phase, including Nude with Raised Arms (1907) and Three Women (1908). The formal ideas developed during this period directly informed the Cubist period that followed, providing the groundwork for Picasso's transition into Cubism.

Pablo Picasso was born at 23:15 on 25 October 1881 in Málaga, Andalusia, southern Spain. He was the first child of José Ruiz y Blasco (1838–1913) and María Picasso y López, members of a middle-class family. His father, José Ruiz y Blasco, was a painter who specialized in naturalistic depictions of birds and other game, and he served as a professor of art at the School of Crafts and as a curator of a local museum for most of his life.

On 14 October 1950, tram and bus services linking West Berlin with East German suburbs were discontinued, these routes having been operated by BVG West (Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe Gesellschaft, BVG West). The move followed the detention and arrest of West Berlin drivers by East German police for possessing Western currency, which was illegal in the German Democratic Republic. BVG West terminated the East Germany–connected segments: the southern end of tram line 47 to Schönefeld, the southwestern end of tram line 96 to Kleinmachnow, and two bus lines serving Glienicke along the Nordbahn in the north and Falkensee in the northwest. The East German section of tram line 96 continued to operate with eastern personnel and rolling stock. Eastern passengers, typically Westerners with special entry permits, were required to switch from eastern to western trains by foot at the border. This arrangement lasted until the line was closed by the Berlin Wall.

During the period when West Berlin existed as a western enclave in East Germany, its residents commonly used West German passports to travel to Western countries that required visas, such as the United States. In destinations where a visa stamp was not required, West Berlin identity cards were accepted for entry. The visa-exemption group included Switzerland, Austria, and many European Economic Community members, including the United Kingdom.

A panel unanimously concluded that residents of Puerto Rico do not have the right to vote for members of the U.S. House of Representatives, a determination grounded in the constitutional status of Puerto Rico, which is not a U.S. state under the Constitution.

Critics contend that the federal voting rights framework in Puerto Rico has been shaped by a judiciary that, at times, parrots outdated and retrograde foundations, thereby sustaining perceptions of inferiority. The rules were established in a bygone era and reflect distorted views, remaining out of step with modern times. Legal and societal changes have long undermined the legitimacy of these judge-made rules. While unequal treatment based on skin color or other irrelevant factors was once widespread and accepted, it is now outdated and unacceptable. By continuing to enforce these rules, U.S. courts tarnish the judiciary’s role as a standard-bearer of national values. Given that unequal treatment is now constitutionally, morally, and culturally unacceptable nationwide, as highlighted by Brown v. Board of Education, allowing antiquated rules to persist is intolerable. The persistence of these rules cannot be justified by any theory of law.

Willie Nelson developed an interest in martial arts from a young age, initially acquiring self-defense manuals on jujitsu and judo through Batman and Superman comic advertisements. After relocating to Nashville in the 1960s, he began formal kung fu training, and in the 1980s he expanded into taekwondo, earning a second-degree black belt. In the 1990s he began practicing GongKwon Yusul, a pursuit that continued for about two decades before receiving a fifth-degree black belt in 2014 from Grand Master Sam Um in Austin, Texas. A Tae Kwon Do Times interview from that year highlighted his unconventional training methods during touring, noting that he trained aboard his tour bus, the Honeysuckle Rose, and submitted videos to his supervising master for review.

Willie Nelson returned to the recording business after a period away from the studio, hiring manager Neil Reshen to negotiate with RCA, which agreed to terminate Nelson's contract upon repayment of $14,000. Reshen subsequently secured Nelson a deal with Atlantic Records for $25,000 per year, making him the label's first country artist. He then formed his backing band, The Family, and by February 1973 was recording Shotgun Willie at Atlantic Studios in New York City.

New York Harbor comprises the Port of New York and New Jersey, the principal maritime gateway for the five boroughs of New York City and nearby Northern New Jersey communities. Since 1921, the port’s commercial activities have been overseen by the bi-state Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The port serves as the nation’s largest oil-import terminal and, by container throughput, the third-largest port in the United States. Beginning in the 1950s, the New York and Brooklyn port facilities were largely eclipsed by Port Newark-Elizabeth Marine Terminal in Newark Bay, which became the region’s largest container facility and the busiest on the Eastern Seaboard. In terms of passenger travel, its relative prominence has diminished, while the Port Authority operates three major airports—LaGuardia (opened 1939), John F. Kennedy International (Idlewild, opened 1948), and Newark Liberty International (opened 1928).

New York Harbor has long been central to the commerce of the New York metropolitan area, functioning as a vital hub for shipping, trade, and related economic activity. In addition to its commercial importance, the harbor is home to the Statue of Liberty National Monument, which commemorates the immigrant experience in the United States during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

The Sharp PC-1500 series uses a seven-bit character set derived from ASCII. Deviations from ASCII are indicated by placing the corresponding Unicode code point beneath each glyph, providing a direct reference to how the PC-1500’s symbols differ from the standard ASCII set.

Sharp's PC-14xx pocket computer line, including the PC-1403 (1986), the PC-1403H, and the PC-1475, uses an eight-bit extended ASCII character set. The lower half largely mirrors the standard seven-bit ASCII, with a few minor deviations. By contrast, the upper half encompasses a full set of half-width Katakana glyphs along with a range of graphical and mathematical symbols. The Japanese glyphs are not documented and are accessible only by enabling an unofficial Japanese mode.

The Internet Low Bitrate Codec (iLBC) is a royalty-free narrowband speech audio coding format designed for low-bandwidth communications, and it includes an open-source reference implementation of the codec. It was developed by Global IP Solutions (GIPS), formerly Global IP Sound, a company that was acquired by Google in 2011. In 2011 iLBC transitioned from freeware with commercial-use limitations to a free/open-source release under the 3-clause BSD license. The codec is maintained as part of the open-source WebRTC project and is suitable for a range of applications, including voice-over-IP, streaming audio, archival storage, and messaging. Its algorithm represents a version of block-independent linear predictive coding, with data frame lengths of 20 milliseconds and 30 milliseconds, and encoded blocks are typically transported using a protocol such as RTP.

Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Dutch-Flemish Renaissance painter whose oeuvre marks a transition in Northern art. Several of his early works, including Landscape with the Flight into Egypt (1563, Courtauld Gallery), align closely with Patinir’s conventions by integrating expansive landscapes that accommodate narrative content. In Landscape with the Fall of Icarus, known from two extant copies, Bruegel again adopts a Patinir-style landscape in which the most conspicuous figure is a generic genre-type observer who appears to be unaware of the surrounding mythic subject. The dating of Bruegel’s lost original of Icarus remains uncertain, but it is generally regarded as relatively early, suggesting an initial work that forecasts his later development. By the 1560s, his compositions evolve from crowded scenes with numerous small figures to arrangements that depict a smaller number of considerably larger figures, signaling a shift toward more monumental figures within narrative settings.

Pieter Bruegel the Elder produced allegorical series, including The Seven Deadly Sins and The Virtues, in which he adopted many of Hieronymus Bosch's mannerisms. The sinners are depicted as grotesque and unidentifiable, while the virtues are shown wearing odd headgear. Imitations of Bosch proved commercially successful, with Big Fish Eat Little Fish in the Albertina serving as a notable example; Bruegel signed the work, but the print version was attributed to Bosch by Cock.

Hans Günter Merz (born 1947 in Tailfingen) is a German architect and museum designer. He founded and serves as director of hg merz architekten museumsgestalter, a practice that concentrates on museum and exhibition design as well as the refurbishment of listed buildings. The firm operates from branches in Stuttgart and Berlin.

HG Merz served as a professor for exhibition design in the Visual Communication department at the University of Applied Sciences Pforzheim from 1993 to 2007. He then held the position of professor for experimental design in the Architecture department at Technische Universität Darmstadt from 2008 to 2014. In 2014, Merz was awarded an honorary doctorate by TU Darmstadt.

Low Lights features vocal samples taken from the a cappella version of Kings of Tomorrow's "So Alive" and is characterized as a gospel-tinged piece that examines spirituality and frequently references God. It appears as the sixth track on The Life of Pablo and transitions into the following track, "Highlights." The song drew positive critical reception for its religious themes. In addition to its album presence, Alicia Keys later sampled Low Lights in her 2017 track "That's What's Up." In 2016, it charted at number 22 on the US Billboard Bubbling Under Hot 100.

Low Lights debuted at number 22 on the US Billboard Bubbling Under Hot 100 chart during the album’s release week, remaining on the chart for one week. It later reached its peak at number 1 on the US Bubbling Under R&B/Hip-Hop Singles chart, spending two weeks on that chart. In the United Kingdom, the track opened at number 134 on the UK Singles Chart.

The Four Witches engraving has been the subject of prolonged scholarly analysis and remains enigmatic; there is nothing in the engraver’s writings to indicate his intent. There is no consensus on the subject matter or intended meaning, with art historians associating it either with witch hunting or with figures from classical mythology. In the composition, the four women stand beneath a suspended globe or sphere and before an open stone window, while a skull and thigh bone placed nearby may imply a gateway to death. Some scholars suggest the women are engaged in a nefarious scheme, perhaps linked to the 1487 witch-hunting treatise Malleus Maleficarum. An alternative interpretation posits that the figures represent Greek or Roman goddesses, perhaps Hecate, the patroness of evil magic, poisonous plants, and ghosts, or her earthly counterpart Diana.

The Four Witches, an engraving by Albrecht Dürer, has no clearly established interpretation. It has attracted extensive scholarly analysis, yet broad agreement on its meaning remains elusive. Proposals have ranged widely, including readings tied to four seasons or the four elements, as well as identifications such as Aphrodite with the Graces (the rightmost figure bearing a myrtle wreath), the Three Fates, or allegorical depictions of four witches or four girls in a brothel. Some scholars have urged caution in seeking a single message, and art historian Marcel Briton has suggested that there may be no specific meaning at all, perhaps presenting four nude figures as a whimsical departure from puritanical convention.

Wikimapia uses a tiered user system in which registered participants advance through levels based on accumulated experience points. As users reach higher levels, they gain access to more sophisticated editing tools and encounter fewer editing restrictions. Promotion to Advanced User (AU) status is conducted by existing Advanced Users. Individuals designated as Advanced Users receive enhanced editing and moderation capabilities, including the authority to ban other users. Advanced Users are responsible for countering vandalism on the map and helping to maintain the reliability of contributed information.

Wikimapia introduced an application programming interface (API) in December 2009, and at that time made its content available in multiple formats for non-commercial use. A year later, in December 2010, the project announced that its data would be released under a Non-Commercial Creative Commons license.

Chess Scotland is the national governing body for chess in Scotland. It was established in 2001, following the merger of the Scottish Chess Association and the Scottish Junior Chess Association to form a single governing organization.

Chess Scotland maintains an online rating system that is important for many players, serving as a widely used benchmark for evaluating competitive results. The rating system also represents a major source of revenue for Chess Scotland, supporting its operations and development. In addition, submitting an application to Chess Scotland for the recognition of an event or a player for rating purposes brings that event or player within Chess Scotland's rating jurisdiction and subject to its procedures.

Ma Ying-jeou, a Kuomintang politician, was elected president of Taiwan in 2008 and subsequently pursued closer economic and political ties with mainland China, signaling a willingness to engage with Beijing. In the realm of panda diplomacy, the mainland government presented two giant pandas, Tuan Tuan and Yuan Yuan, to the Taipei Zoo as part of this outreach. The zoo anticipated that their arrival would attract roughly 30,000 visitors per day. The move drew criticism from Taiwan independence supporters and the Democratic Progressive Party, who contended that the pandas symbolized a rapprochement with Beijing and aligned with its objective to bring Taiwan under its influence.

Tuan Tuan and Yuan Yuan are two giant pandas that were presented by the People's Republic of China (PRC) to the Republic of China (ROC, Taiwan) in 2008 as part of a cultural exchange program. The concept of the gift was first proposed in 2005, and discussions continued over the ensuing years before the donation. The previous ROC administration in Taipei initially refused to accept the pandas.

The Judiciary of Macau is the branch responsible for administering justice in the Macau Special Administrative Region. It handles criminal prosecutions and civil disputes, including cases between private parties and the government. Judicial independence from the executive and legislative branches is a fundamental principle of Macau's legal framework. The judiciary comprises the Court of Final Appeal and eleven additional courts. The head of the judiciary is the President of the Court of Final Appeal of the Macau Special Administrative Region. The system operates on a bilingual basis, allowing proceedings in Chinese, Portuguese, or both, in accordance with the Basic Law.

Judges in Macau are appointed by the Chief Executive, based on the recommendation of an independent commission comprised of local judges, lawyers, and eminent persons. The commission serves as the selecting body, drawing from local legal professionals and respected members of the community. While the majority of judges are local Macanese, the framework allows for the appointment of foreign judges when appropriate.

Alfred Stieglitz treated photography as an art form and developed his aesthetic through intensive self-directed study. In 1887, he published his first article, "A Word or Two about Amateur Photography in Germany," in the newly launched magazine Amateur Photographer.

Stieglitz returned to New York in the late autumn and, on December 15, two weeks before his sixty-fifth birthday, opened An American Place, his largest gallery to date. The new space contained the first darkroom he had in the city, since previously he relied on borrowed facilities or worked at Lake George. Over the ensuing sixteen years, he continued presenting group and solo exhibitions by friends John Marin, Charles Demuth, Marsden Hartley, Arthur Dove, and Paul Strand. Georgia O’Keeffe received at least one major exhibition each year, and Stieglitz maintained tight control over access to her works while actively promoting her, even when critics were biased against her. The two often saw one another only in the summer, when it was too hot at her New Mexico home, yet they sustained nearly weekly correspondence, reflecting a deeply interconnected personal and artistic relationship.

Around 500 CE, the Indian mathematician Aryabhata composed the Aryabhatiya, a concise treatise on astronomy and mathematics written in verse. The work was intended to supplement the rules of calculation employed in astronomical computations and mathematical mensuration, but it did not adopt a formal deductive framework or logical method. It is notable for containing the first known description of the decimal place-value system. Centuries later, the Persian scholar Abu Rayhan Biruni described the Aryabhatiya as a mixture of simple, everyday elements and more refined, valuable ideas.

Historically, the development of mathematics includes several notable antiquarian milestones. Eratosthenes of Cyrene (c. 276–194 BCE) devised the Sieve of Eratosthenes, a method for locating prime numbers. The 3rd century BCE is commonly regarded as the Golden Age of Greek mathematics, a period when pure mathematical theory expanded even as applied mathematics, particularly trigonometry, progressed more rapidly in later centuries. Hipparchus of Nicaea (c. 190–120 BCE) established trigonometry as a formal discipline, compiling the first known trigonometric table and introducing the systematic use of a 360-degree circle. In the early centuries of the imperial era, Heron of Alexandria (c. 10–70 AD) is credited with Heron's formula for the area of a scalene triangle and is among the earliest to recognize the possibility of square roots of negative numbers. Around the same era, Menelaus of Alexandria (c. 100 AD) contributed to spherical trigonometry through what is now called Menelaus' theorem. The Almagest of Ptolemy (c. AD 90–168) stands as the most comprehensive and influential trigonometric work of antiquity, its tables guiding astronomical computations for the ensuing millennium. Ptolemy himself is associated with Ptolemy's theorem for deriving trigonometric quantities, and he furnished the most accurate value of π outside China for many centuries: 3.1416.

Exposé was an American vocal group that achieved popularity in U.S. dance clubs as well as on mainstream Top 40 and adult contemporary charts. The ensemble toured and recorded from 1984 to 1995, after which they retired from recording and public performances and remained inactive from 1995 until 2003.

Exposé underwent a prolonged hiatus before returning in 2003, when key members Ann Curless, Jeanette Jurado, and Kelly Moneymaker briefly reformed the group for a reunion performance. The concert was held at the California Mid-State Fair in Paso Robles, California.

Marine conservation has been shaped by international guidance, notably the Vulnerable Marine Ecosystems (VMEs) concept introduced by the United Nations in 2006 to guide the management of deep-sea fisheries in areas beyond national jurisdiction. Subsequently, the European Parliament transposed this VMEs concept for Atlantic European waters, incorporating its framework into regional policy.

Marine conservation encompasses efforts to restore ecological systems and safeguard biodiversity within marine environments. A turning point occurred in 1972 with the enactment of the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act (MPRSA), which helped launch the modern marine conservation movement. The statute authorized the Environmental Protection Agency to regulate the dumping of waste into the oceans, establishing a regulatory framework for ocean pollution control. The act has since been amended to expand and adjust its provisions. Alongside other major developments, MPRSA stands as a significant milestone that brought greater attention to marine issues in United States environmental policy and public discourse.

In January 2020, after the United States carried out an operation that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani, Instagram removed posts expressing support for Soleimani. The company stated that the removals were in accordance with U.S. sanctions targeting Iran. Some officials criticized the move as undemocratic.

Instagram began as a solely photo-sharing service. In June 2013, the platform expanded to support short video clips of up to 15 seconds, a move that some observers regarded as part of Facebook's effort to compete with Vine. In August 2015, Instagram added support for widescreen video formats, broadening the aspect ratios it could accommodate. In March 2016, the maximum video length was increased from 15 seconds to one minute. Later, in February 2017, the service introduced Albums, which enabled posts to include up to ten minutes of video content.

Harpa is characterized by a flattened head bearing paired, long, thick, conical tentacles, with the internal base presenting a small protuberance that houses the eyes. The organism possesses a simple mouth encircled by a muscular margin, accompanied by a small, slender, pointed trunk. An elongated, cylindrical organ of excitement lies on the right side. The locomotive organ is notably large, with the anterior portion broad and ear-shaped and featuring a deep emargination on each side. The posterior extremity is detachable and lacks an operculum.

In Harpa, the foot is divided into two regions: a broad, arched anterior portion that resembles an ear and bears a marginal groove, connected to the posterior portion by a narrow neck. The posterior portion is comparatively longer, oval and pointed, with a slight inflation on its upper side, and it lacks an operculum. When subjected to abrupt disturbance, the animal breaks off the posterior end of its foot to withdraw further into its shell. Because such rupture would carry away any operculum, an operculum would be useless, and consequently Harpa does not possess one.

The sievert is the SI unit used to express the stochastic health risk associated with ionizing radiation, incorporating biological context into the assessment of dose. In practice, calculation begins with the absorbed dose in grays, which is multiplied by a radiation-type weighting factor to obtain the equivalent dose in sieverts; this step accounts for the varying biological effectiveness of different radiation types. The next step multiplies the equivalent dose by tissue weighting factors to produce the effective dose, also measured in sieverts, providing a single value for the overall risk to an individual. The weighting factors employed in these calculations are published by the International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) and the International Commission on Radiation Units and Measurements (ICRU). Historically, the rem served as a CGS dose-equivalent unit, with 1 sievert equal to 100 rem, making the rem a legacy unit no longer in standard use.

At the 3rd International Symposium on Radiological Protection, held in October 2015, a collaborative set of proposals from the ICRU and the ICRP was introduced. The proposals intend to redefine the operational quantities used in radiological protection. They are designed to preserve existing practices concerning calibration phantoms and the use of reference radiation fields.

On 30 May 2013, the Oryol Law Institute was awarded the honorary title of Honoured Lawyer of Russia by Vladimir Kolokoltsev, who at that time served as Russia's Minister of Internal Affairs. Valery Vitalyevich Lukyanov is a Doctor of Law and has held the rank of Lieutenant General of militia.

In 1991, building on the OSSShM, the Oryol Higher School of the Ministry of the Interior of the RSFSR was established. On 17 May 1997, the Government of Russia reorganized the institution as the Oryol Law Institute of the Ministry of the Interior of Russia. Beginning on 1 September 2008, the institute started training specialists for the traffic police units (GIBDD).

During dose-rate survey work, Geiger counters are used to locate radiation sources, providing rapid identification of areas with activity. Ionization chamber instruments are then employed to obtain more accurate quantitative measurements. Ion chambers generally offer greater measurement accuracy than Geiger counters and are capable of handling higher dose-rate levels, making them the preferred tool for precise assessment in challenging conditions.

Survey meters that use Geiger end-window configurations are unable to distinguish between alpha and beta radiation. In alpha counting, detector efficiency is maximized only when the sensor is placed within roughly 10 millimeters of the alpha source, and increasing the separation leads to a noticeable drop in the alpha count; observing this attenuation can indicate the simultaneous presence of both alpha and beta radiation. By contrast, beta/gamma Geiger instruments can show beta contributions to readings over metre-scale distances, with the extent depending on beta energy, which may lead to the erroneous impression that gamma radiation is being detected alone. To address this, a sliding shield arrangement can be employed to selectively attenuate beta particles, leaving the gamma component isolated for measurement.

The church of St. Jakob, located outside Zurich, developed around a charitable sick-house and an affiliated chapel that date from the 11th century. The first documentary reference to the St. Jakob church appears in 1221. It was the site of the Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl in 1443. In 1677 the sick-house was repurposed as a Pfrundhaus, a residence for elderly residents, and this use continued until its disestablishment in 1842. The present St. Jakob church building was inaugurated in 1901.

The tram stop is officially named Stauffacher and is not the same as the nearby square. A separate Stauffacherplatz existed about 200 metres farther toward the Sihl and was established in 1898. The coincidence between the stop’s name and Stauffacherplatz led many to conflate the two, causing confusion with the actual square. In 2003, to address the confusion, the real Stauffacherplatz was renamed Ernst-Nobs-Platz.

In December 2015, Jordan's Furniture opened a location in New Haven, Connecticut, occupying the former New Haven Register building, with Warren Buffett among the attendees at the ceremonial opening. In 2020, the company expanded with a store at The Maine Mall in South Portland, Maine. In 2023, a new location was opened at Westfarms Mall in Farmington, Connecticut.

Jordan's Furniture, founded by Barry and Eliot, opened its Nashua, New Hampshire location in 1983, marking the company's first showroom outside its original base. The firms expanded again with a second location in Avon, Massachusetts, in 1987. The Avon opening was associated with substantial traffic disruption, reportedly the largest traffic jam ever recorded on Route 24. In an effort to manage the surge in visitors, Barry and Eliot appeared on local radio to urge potential customers not to travel to the new showroom. Nevertheless, many patrons queued for hours to enter the Avon showroom.

A blast damper is a device designed to protect occupants and equipment from explosion overpressures. It is typically used to safeguard air inlets and exhaust penetrations in hardened structures, where it helps mitigate the effects of shock waves entering through these openings. The concept is closely related to blast valves, and in some contexts the terms are used interchangeably; however, blast valves are the term commonly applied to devices associated with nuclear explosions.

Blast dampers are passive protective devices consisting of blades that are held in the open position by tension from a spring. When an overpressure event occurs, the blades close automatically if the blast pressure exceeds the spring’s resistance, sealing the opening. Models differ in their blast protection ratings, with many providing around 1 bar (14.5 psi) or lower capability. Additionally, dampers vary in post-event behavior: some units remain closed after activation, while others are designed to reset and continue to function for subsequent use.

Activism, particularly in the area of human rights, seeks to safeguard the basic liberties and protections enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Proponents emphasize core civil and political rights such as the inherent right to life, citizenship, and property, as well as the freedom of movement. They also defend constitutional freedoms related to thought, expression, religion, and the right to peaceful assembly. Beyond the listed examples, activists contend that additional rights exist to address evolving circumstances and needs. The foundations of the global human rights movement are rooted in resistance to colonialism and imperialism, as well as struggles against slavery, racism, segregation, patriarchal structures, and the oppression of indigenous peoples, forming a historical basis for ongoing advocacy and reform.

The terms activism and activist entered political discourse as early as 1920 and 1915, respectively, according to the Online Etymology Dictionary. The concept itself traces back to earlier notions of collective behavior and social action, with historians locating its roots in preexisting ideas about organized groups pursuing change. In 1969, definitions distinguished activism as the policy or practice of pursuing actions with determination and energy, independent of political signification, while social action was described as organized activity by a group aimed at improving social conditions, detached from normative status. The 1960s context, marked by the rise of new social movements in the United States, contributed to understanding activism as a rational and legitimate democratic form of protest or appeal.

Hazardous waste may be stored in a hazardous waste landfill or in another permanent disposal facility designed for hazardous waste containment. A landfill is a disposal facility, or a portion of one, where hazardous waste is placed on land. The regulatory definition excludes several structures and formations, specifying that a landfill is not a pile, a land treatment facility, a surface impoundment, an underground injection well, a salt dome formation, a salt bed formation, an underground mine, a cave, or a corrective action management unit. This definition is provided in the Code of Federal Regulations at 40 CFR 260.10.

Under U.S. regulations, the Environmental Protection Agency designates certain wastes as hazardous and maintains published lists that identify these wastes. The F-list encompasses wastes from non-specific sources (40 CFR 261.31), the K-list covers wastes from specific sources (40 CFR 261.32), and the P-list and U-list comprise discarded commercial chemical products (40 CFR 261.33). These EPA-issued lists are used to categorize wastes as hazardous for regulatory purposes.

Zhiyi, a central figure in early Chinese Buddhism, is said to have taught a lineage that included thirty-two direct disciples. Among them, Guanding (561–632) is generally regarded as Zhiyi's most influential successor, responsible for recording and preserving his master's legacy. Guanding edited and published Zhiyi's lectures as the Mohe Zhiguan, thereby disseminating Zhiyi's teachings to a broader audience. He also prepared two major commentaries on the Lotus Sutra and produced original works, including two commentaries on the Nirvana Sutra, contributing to the expansion and interpretation of Zhiyi's Buddhist framework.

Zhiyi founded the Tiantai school, which became one of the most influential Buddhist traditions in imperial China. Its teachings subsequently spread to Korea, Japan, and Vietnam, shaping the Buddhist landscapes of those regions. He integrated doctrinal theory with meditative practice, creating a coherent synthesis that stands as a cornerstone of East Asian Buddhist philosophy. His three core works—Great Cessation-Contemplation; Profound Meaning of The Lotus Sutra; and Words and Phrases of The Lotus Sutra—are foundational treatises for Tiantai, Tendai in Japan, and Cheontae in Korea. These writings also influenced Chan/Zen, Pure Land, and Nichiren Buddhism. They remain widely studied by Asian Buddhists for their depth, clarity, and systematic organization. Zhiyi's framework offers a universal Mahayana approach, adaptable to evolving times and diverse cultural contexts.

Adam (1983) is a film whose narrative is set in Hollywood, Florida, with production undertaken on location in and around Houston, and it draws on the 1981 disappearance and murder of Adam Walsh; the work is included in the list of films featured in Houston.

Apollo 10 1/2: A Space Age Childhood (2022) is set in Houston and the nearby suburb of Clear Lake, with the Johnson Space Center and Rice University featured as prominent local institutions depicted in the film.

omg! (Yahoo Celebrity) debuted on June 12, 2007, with its initial press release published on Yahoo’s corporate blog to announce the new celebrity-focused service. The venture was aimed at appealing primarily to a female audience, and its official sponsorships were restricted to Unilever, Pepsi, and Axiata (represented by Celcom and XL). Through intensive front-page promotion and strategic partnerships, the site experienced rapid early growth, drawing approximately four million readers within its first 19 days. By autumn 2007, omg! claimed more than eight million monthly readers and had established itself as the second-most-read gossip site in the United States, behind TMZ and ahead of People.

Yahoo News, launched in 2000, introduced features that tracked the site’s most viewed content and the articles most often shared via email. The list of articles most frequently forwarded by email was described as an innovation in online news aggregation. The platform allows readers to comment on articles, though between late 2006 and early 2010, user comments were disabled in part due to moderation challenges.

Pandora TV is a South Korea–based video sharing website that experienced rapid growth in the mid-2000s. In 2007 it was the fastest-growing website in South Korea, and by 2008 it had become the country's largest video-sharing platform. By that year it had approximately 3.6 million registered members and held about 35 percent of the Korean video-sharing market share.

Pandora TV (Korean: 판도라TV) was a South Korean video-sharing platform that hosted user-generated content. Established in October 2004, it was the first video-sharing service to attach advertisements to user-submitted clips and the first to offer unlimited storage for uploads. The site was operated by Pandora TV Co., Ltd., and it was headquartered in the Seoul-Gangnam Building in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul.

Al-Arabi SC (Kuwait) was founded in mid-1953 under the original name Al-Uruba, making it one of the earliest football clubs established in Kuwait. Throughout its history, the club has been recognized as a pioneer in Kuwaiti football. Notable players associated with the team include Abdulwahab Al-Awadie, Abdulaziz Al-Khatieb, Musad Al-Musad, Mohammed Al-Dawlee, Abdulmajied Mohammed, Mohammed Al-Somale, Dasman Bakhiet, Ahmad Bodha, Monaier Al-Dagag, Fuad Al-Ashgar, Ahmad Hussain, Abbas Al-Shemaly, Mossa Al-Somale, Nayef Dalool, and Mohammed Salah Al-Roomy.
Al-Arabi SC (Kuwait) is a prominent Kuwaiti football club that has claimed seven Kuwait Premier League titles, three Joint League titles, six Emir Cups, and one Federation Cup.

PacWest Center is a commercial office building whose construction began in October 1982 and was formally dedicated on November 1, 1984. The name derives from its former anchor tenant, Pacific Western Bank of Oregon, which was owned by PacWest Bancorp. In 1986, PacWest's Oregon operations were acquired by KeyCorp and became part of KeyBank. Tokyo-based Mitsubishi Estate Co. had been the majority owner since the building rose in 1984.

PacWest Center is a downtown Portland, Oregon, office high-rise whose design earned the Portland chapter of the American Institute of Architects’ top honor in 1985, a project developed by Hugh Stubbins & Associates in collaboration with Skidmore, Owings & Merrill. The complex underwent a lobby remodel in 2002. In December 2007, the property was sold to Ashforth Pacific Inc. for $161.5 million. A December 2014 windstorm blew a fragment of sheet metal from the tower, causing damage to nearby Standard Plaza. In 2016, the building changed hands again when LPC Realty Advisors I LP purchased it for $170 million, the sale occurring from Ashforth.

The Federation of the Italian Music Industry established a certification system in Italy in the mid-1970s. At its outset, album certifications designated Silver at 500,000 units and Gold at 1,000,000 units, while singles earned Gold at 1,000,000 units; these levels applied uniformly to both domestic and international repertoire. In December 1982, the thresholds were revised to Gold at 250,000 copies and Platinum at 500,000 copies. Certification oversight was conducted by AFI with the involvement of an auditing company. By 1987, the thresholds were lowered again to Gold at 100,000 copies and Platinum at 200,000 copies.

From 2005 to the end of 2011, the Diamond qualification established by the Federation of the Italian Music Industry (FIMI) required five-times platinum in sales to qualify. In January 2012, FIMI revised the Diamond threshold upward, setting the criterion at ten-times platinum.

Conway is a city located in the southwestern part of Faulkner County in Arkansas. Interstate 40 traverses the northeastern and eastern Perimeter of the city, with access to the freeway available from exits 124 through 132. The I-40 corridor connects Conway with several regional destinations, including Memphis, which lies about 160 miles (260 km) to the east along the highway, and Little Rock, approximately 30 miles (48 km) to the east, with the route generally proceeding in a southeasterly direction. To the west, Russellville is about 46 miles (74 km) away via I-40, while Oklahoma City sits roughly 307 miles (494 km) to the west on the same interstate corridor.

The Conway Public School District serves the majority of Conway’s city limits and is governed by the Conway Board of Education, a seven-member body elected in a citywide vote on the third Tuesday in September. The district operates with an annual budget of about $88 million and enrolls roughly 10,000 students, making it the eighth-largest in Arkansas. It comprises 16 campuses: one preschool, nine elementary schools, four middle schools, one junior high, and one high school. Faculty qualifications include more than 65 percent of teachers holding a master's degree or higher, and 67 teachers are National Board Certified.

Lungalunga is classified within the Oceanic branch of the Austronesian language family. Its immediate subgroup is the Patpatar–Tolai cluster, which also comprises the Kuanua and Patpatar languages. Kuanua is spoken on the Gazelle Peninsula, while Patpatar is spoken on New Ireland.

The Lungalunga language is characterized by a four-way number system that differentiates singular, dual, trial, and plural forms. Its person system comprises three categories—first, second, and third person—and it marks an inclusive versus exclusive distinction in the first-person plural. The language does not feature gender distinctions.

Apple Lossless Audio Codec (ALAC) data are commonly stored in MP4-derived files with the .m4a extension. The .m4a suffix is also used by Apple to designate AAC audio within an MP4 container, meaning the same container format can carry either lossless ALAC or lossy AAC depending on the encoding. Additionally, ALAC data can be embedded in the .CAF (Core Audio Format) container, though this usage is far less common.

In June 2021, Apple Music expanded its catalog by introducing ALAC-based lossless audio encoded with the Apple Lossless Audio Codec, making lossless tracks available to subscribers. The service was offered to all subscribers at no additional cost. The highest fidelity supported in the lossless tier is 24-bit depth at 192 kHz sampling rate.

In 1979, Tony Lacey assumed the editorial chair at Penguin by invitation of managing director Peter Mayer. At that time Puffin was among Penguin's few profitable divisions, and Mayer pursued a more aggressive commercialisation of the Penguin brand. Lacey reduced the number of Puffin imprints and consolidated popular titles under the Puffin Classics umbrella, while also launching the Fighting Fantasy interactive gamebook series. Under his leadership, the Puffin Club and the Puffin School Book Club expanded significantly, with the latter directed toward schools and other organizations. By 1983, Puffin accounted for roughly one-third of Penguin's book sales.

Penguin Books' postwar illustrated-book program began in 1945 when Allen Lane approached the architectural historian Nikolaus Pevsner with the aim of producing illustrated volumes that would rival the publisher’s King Penguins line. Pevsner proposed two ambitious series, The Pelican History of Art and The Buildings of England, each projected at roughly 40–50 volumes, and Lane agreed to pursue both, ending the meeting with a concrete plan. By 1946 the first contracts were signed for Summerson’s Architecture in Britain, Blunt’s Art and Architecture in France, and Wittkower’s Italian art and architecture, while the first title, Painting in Britain, 1530–1790 by Ellis Waterhouse, appeared in 1953. A 1955 prospectus announced four additional volumes and laid out a total plan of 47 titles; the undertaking would outscale earlier multi‑volume art histories such as Histoire de l’art and Propyläen Kunstgeschichte. By Pevsner’s retirement in 1977, 41 volumes had been published, after which the project was continued by Judy Nairn and Peter Lasko. Yale University Press acquired the series in 1992, at which point 45 titles had been completed; by 2004 Yale had published 21 volumes, largely revisions of existing editions, with new volumes continuing to appear in the 2010s alongside new editions of older volumes.

Luan Santana (born March 13, 1991) is a Brazilian singer and musician from Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul. He first drew his family's attention at age three and, as a child, performed in the sertanejo tradition, singing classic standards such as "Muda de vida," "Chico Mineiro," and "Cabocla."

Luan Santana is a Brazilian singer who has received four nominations for the Latin Grammy Awards. He is the all-time winner of the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards, Troféu Imprensa (Troféu Imprensa Awards), and Prêmio Jovem Brasileiro (Jovem Brasileiro Awards).

The 2022 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira was staged at the Estádio Municipal de Aveiro, marking the venue's twelfth occasion hosting the competition. Since 2009, the Estádio Municipal de Aveiro has hosted virtually all Supertaça matches, with the exceptions of 2015 and 2019, when the game was held at the Estádio Algarve.

The 2022 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira was the 44th edition of Portugal's season-opening football super cup, played on 30 July 2022. It featured Porto, the champions of the 2021–22 Primeira Liga and the 2021–22 Taça de Portugal, against Tondela, who had finished as runners-up in the 2021–22 Taça de Portugal. Porto won the match 3–0, claiming their 23rd Supertaça title.

The first air raid on Ferrara during World War II was conducted by bombers of the 15th Air Force. The target of the attack was the city’s marshalling yard, but a large portion of the bombs fell on the urban area, resulting in 312 civilian victims.

The bombing of Ferrara was a series of aerial bombardments on the Italian city of Ferrara carried out by the United States Army Air Forces and the Royal Air Force during the final two years of World War II. The operations aimed to disable Ferrara's marshalling yard, a critical rail hub, by targeting its railway facilities and related infrastructure. The campaigns inflicted substantial collateral damage on the city and resulted in over a thousand fatalities among the civilian population.

In 2018, the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture of Saudi Arabia introduced a new plan aimed at expanding organic farming across the country. The initiative seeks a substantial rise in organic cultivation, targeting a 300 percent increase in organic farming. The program is financed with an allocated budget of US$200 million.

Although Saudi Arabia is widely perceived as a desert, the country includes regions that are suitable for agriculture. Winter precipitation averages around 100 millimeters, though rainfall is notably higher in the southern regions. The government has converted extensive tracts of desert into arable land through major irrigation projects. Through expansive mechanization and ongoing irrigation development, the area available for cultivation has grown, increasing overall agricultural capacity.

FFDshow is a collection of open-source DirectShow filters that leverage FFmpeg libraries to decode a broad array of video and audio formats. The first releases appeared in May 2002. It was created as an alternative to the DivX decoders, specifically DivX 3.11 and DivX 5.02, the latter of which was bundled with the Gator software. The project sought to blend the speed and quality associated with MPlayer with compatibility for popular Windows video players. It has continued to broaden its format support, adding both new and legacy formats as FFmpeg developers extend support.

Ffdshow is a collection of open-source DirectShow filters that enables decoding a wide range of audio and video formats within Windows media players. For playing transport stream containers, such as those carrying AVC/H.264 video, an additional media splitter is typically required to demultiplex the streams before they can be decoded by ffdshow. Free media splitters are available, with LAV Filters given as an example.

Flowchart, sometimes written as flow chart, is a diagrammatic representation of the sequence of steps, decisions, or actions that comprise a process or algorithm. The concept is known under a broad set of alternative names, including process flowchart, functional flowchart, process map, process chart, functional process chart, business process model, process model, process flow diagram, work flow diagram, and business flow diagram. In common usage, the two spellings flowchart and flow chart are used interchangeably.

Flowcharts are diagrams that illustrate the sequence of operations, decisions, and data flows within a process and have been classified in several different schemes. In 1978, Veronis identified three primary types: system flowcharts, general flowcharts, and detailed flowcharts. In the same year, Bohl described two categories used in the planning of solutions: system flowcharts and program flowcharts. Later, Fryman (2001) expanded the classification by introducing additional varieties, such as decision flowcharts, logic flowcharts, systems flowcharts, product flowcharts, and process flowcharts. Flowcharts are applied in both business and government contexts to analyze procedures, convey information, and support decision making.

During October 2025, the United States conducted two military strikes in the Pacific Ocean against vessels believed to be involved in drug trafficking. On 21 October, a strike against an alleged drug-smuggling boat killed at least two people and was described by an unnamed U.S. official as the first U.S. strike in the Pacific Ocean; the strike was reported to have taken place off the coast of Colombia. On 22 October, a second strike in the Pacific resulted in three fatalities.

On 13 November 2025, Hegseth announced the unveiling of Operation Southern Spear, a United States military initiative directed at Latin American drug trafficking networks. The operation was led by the Joint Task Force Southern Spear and relied on a fleet equipped with robotics and autonomous systems.
ISO 20400 is an international standard for sustainable procurement. Balfour Beatty, a construction company, became the first organisation to undertake a full evaluation of ISO 20400.

ISO 20400:2017, Sustainable procurement — Guidance, is an International Organization for Standardization standard that provides guidance applicable to organizations of any activity or size. It assists in embedding sustainability considerations throughout procurement processes and purchasing decisions. The guidance is intended for all stakeholders involved in or affected by procurement activities and outcomes. ISO 20400 complements ISO 26000, which offers guidance on social responsibility, by concentrating specifically on the purchasing function within organizations.

Following the war, the Consultative Council was established roughly one year later, as the state sought to respond to evolving conditions that had emerged within the country. Its creation, driven by these postwar developments, marked a move toward formalized advisory governance and helped shape the constitutional framework later embodied by the Basic Law of Saudi Arabia, which sets out the structure and authorities of the government.

Within the Basic Law of Saudi Arabia, Article 27 establishes a social security system for citizens. The provision is described as feasible without expropriation or high taxes, a condition attributed to the country's oil wealth and an estimated population of about 33 million. Article 39 obligates all media outlets to conform to state regulations and prohibits any act that fosters sedition or division, a clause that is frequently cited in censorship cases.

San Vittore Prison served as a transit facility for Jews arrested in northern Italy; those detainees were brought to the prison before being moved onward to Milano Centrale railway station, where they were loaded into freight cars on a concealed track beneath the station.

During the Fascist occupation, San Vittore Prison held a broad range of adversaries, including political detainees and other enemies of the state. In 1943, after Germany assumed authority over Italy, the facility underwent extensive changes. Those alterations and reorganizations continued through the subsequent years, culminating in the major riots that broke out in April 1946.

Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution faced challenges arising from a lack of coherence and collaboration between vendors and technologists, a gap that hindered the development process and limited the international visibility and recognition of its standards. As a result, the standards did not achieve broad acceptance by international bodies. In later versions, including BSCII, the approach was seen by some as largely a formal endorsement of a Unicode encoding scheme rather than a thoroughly validated standard.

After independence in 1971, the Bangladesh Standards Institution (BDSI) was established as the national standards body. BDSI joined the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 1974. In 1985, Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1985 merged BDSI with CTL to form the present-day Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI). The merger sought to consolidate standards development, testing, and certification functions.

From 2009 to 2013, the United States Marine Corps faced sustained budgetary pressures amid broader defense reform efforts. In spring 2009, Obama administration defense spending reductions led by Secretary of Defense Robert Gates sought to trim costs, but the adjustments did not substantially reduce the Marine Corps’ budget or core programs; however, the plan included the cancellation of the VH-71 Kestrel helicopter and a reset of the VXX program. In late 2010, the National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform identified the Marine Corps as bearing a disproportionate share of recommended cuts. During the 2013 sequestration, General James Amos set a floor of about 174,000 Marines, a level described as the minimum necessary to respond to a single contingency, yet one that would push peacetime time at home bases to a historical low due to extended deployments.

Throughout its participation in the Iraq War, the United States Marine Corps fought alongside sister services as part of a broader coalition. The I Marine Expeditionary Force (I MEF), together with the U.S. Army's 3rd Infantry Division, spearheaded the 2003 invasion, after which Marine units briefly withdrew in the summer of 2003 and returned in early 2004 with responsibility for Al Anbar Province, west of Baghdad. They conducted major offensives against Fallujah in April 2004 (Operation Vigilant Resolve) and November 2004 (Operation Phantom Fury) and fought intensely in Ramadi, Al-Qa’im, and Hīt. The campaign was marked by controversy, including the Haditha killings and the Hamdania incident. Following the Anbar Awakening and the 2007 surge, violence fell substantially. The Marine Corps formally ended its Iraq mission on 23 January 2010, transferring control of Al Anbar to the U.S. Army, though Marines returned to Iraq in the summer of 2014 in response to renewed regional instability.

Hdl (identifier) describes an interoperable network of distributed handle resolver servers, known as the Proxy Server System. These servers are linked through a Global Resolver, a single logical entity that is physically decentralised and mirrored across multiple locations. Users obtain a handle prefix issued by the Global Handle Registry. The Global Handle Registry maintains and resolves the prefixes used by locally run handle services. Through the Global Resolver, any local handle service can resolve any handle.

The Handle System originated in digital object management but does not mandate any single model of how identified entities are related. It is capable of representing non-digital entities by mapping them to corresponding digital objects for management and resolution, though defining such objects and their connections to non-digital entities requires careful consideration. Guidelines for modeling these relationships are provided by established frameworks such as FRBR, CIDOC CRM, and the indecs content model. Some applications integrate the Handle System with broader standards, as illustrated by the ADL Initiative, which combines handles with distributed learning standards using SCORM. In the DOI system, the Handle System implementation has adopted SCORM and the indecs framework to support semantic interoperability.

B Line (Los Angeles Metro) is the designation given to the route previously known as the Red Line after Los Angeles Metro implemented a system-wide renaming in 2020 that assigned letters and colors to all lines. Under the new scheme, the former Red Line became the B Line, with the red color retained in its service bullet on maps and materials. The Purple Line was likewise renamed the D Line, aligning with the same updated nomenclature.

The B Line is one of two fully underground subway lines in Los Angeles, with the other being the D Line. The B Line and D Line operate on shared tracks through Koreatown and Downtown Los Angeles. As of 2024, the combined B and D lines averaged 66,642 boardings per weekday.

Emma Langdon Roche (born 1878 in Mobile, Alabama) was the third of four surviving children of Thomas T. Roche and Annie Laura (James) Roche. Her father, born in Ireland, immigrated to the United States at the age of two in 1845 with his parents to escape the Great Famine, and he later worked as a funeral director in Mobile, Alabama. Her mother was born in Alabama to parents who had moved from Virginia to Alabama, and Emma's maternal grandmother was born in Vermont.

Emma Langdon Roche belonged to a family that included three surviving brothers: Edward J. (b. 1872), Frank L. (b. 1875), and Thomas Sheppard Roche (b. 1883). Edward J. went on to become a funeral director. Two of the other children died young, and their maternal aunt Margaret James lived with the family.

Hose, formed in 1981 by guitarist Rick Rubin, bassist Warren Bell, drummer Joel Horne, and lead singer Rick Rosen, was described as an early artcore collective and the East Coast’s answer to Flipper, marked by a slow, blues-influenced groove. Rubin shaped and produced the group’s sound, embodying the DIY ethos of the era and later rising to prominence as a leading producer and tastemaker. The band’s debut recording was a 12-inch EP (SLP) captured in a dormitory activity room with minimal equipment—a boombox and a single microphone. Rubin designed the record’s jacket in a Mondrian-inspired style to illustrate how bass and drums provide structure while guitars and vocals add color. The release blended original material with slowed-down covers of pop-soul tunes, including Hot Chocolate’s “You Sexy Thing” and Rick James’s “Superfreak.” Onstage, Bell typically performed seated, while an Electrolux vacuum was miked offstage to create white noise, and Rosen would push aggressively into the audience during performances. Both the band and the album drew favorable critical attention from critic Robert Christgau.

In 1982, Rick Rosen departed amicably and Mike Espindle took over as vocalist, bringing a larger-than-life stage presence and growling vocal style that contributed a rowdier energy to the band’s live performances. Autumn Goft replaced Joel Horne on drums, described as a skilled, practiced drummer with a Bonham-like off-beat. Hose recorded a seven-inch single that became Def Jam’s official first recording; the release featured three tracks—“Mobo,” a cover of an obscure French disco song; “Girls,” a twenty-second hardcore thrash piece; and “Zoo,” a simplified version of “We’re All Going to the Zoo Tomorrow.” The single was produced by Rubin in a Long Island City studio and released with center etchings gouged by Espindle, distributed in a brown paper bag with stickers. NME published a positive review of the release shortly after it appeared. Bassists during this period rotated among Bell, Steve Williams, Tony Scheitinger, and a San Francisco tour pickup bassist known as “Sweet.” The band undertook heavy touring, sharing stages with Hüsker Dü, the Meat Puppets, the Butthole Surfers, Circle Jerks, Red Kross, and MDC.

According to the 2000 census, the Madison metropolitan statistical area (MSA) had a population of 501,774, with 202,687 households and 121,171 families. The racial composition was 90.26% White, 3.50% African American, 0.32% Native American, 2.99% Asian, 0.03% Pacific Islander, 1.27% from other races, and 1.63% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino individuals of any race made up 3.05% of the population.

The data concern the Madison metropolitan area (MSA). The median household income in the MSA stands at $45,602, while the median family income is $55,159. The median income for males is $35,250, and for females is $26,322. The per capita income is $21,832.

Quartz analog wristwatches commonly rely on compact stepping motors to advance the hands. These devices typically feature a single coil, draw only a small amount of power, and employ a rotor made from a permanent magnet. This same type of motor is used to drive battery-powered quartz clocks, illustrating a shared technology across timekeeping devices. In some watches, such as chronographs, more than one stepping motor may be installed to control multiple hands or display functions.

Frank J. Sprague developed what is regarded as the first practically usable direct-current motor in 1886, notable for its non-sparking operation and for maintaining a relatively constant speed under changing loads. His broader work improved electric-grid distribution, enabling power to be returned to the grid, and facilitated electric traction by providing power to trolleys through overhead lines and trolley poles, while also advancing control systems for electric operations. Building on these advances, Sprague helped bring about the earliest electric trolley system (1887–88) in Richmond, Virginia; the electric elevator and its control mechanism in 1892; and an electric subway featuring centrally controlled cars that could be powered independently. The first electric subway cars were installed in 1892 in Chicago by the South Side Elevated Railroad and came to be known as the "L." Sprague's motor and related innovations spurred rapid growth in the use of electric motors across industry. However, widespread development of motors with acceptable efficiency was delayed for several decades because the critical importance of the air gap between the rotor and stator had not been recognized; efficient designs today employ relatively small air gaps. The St. Louis motor, long used in classrooms to illustrate motor principles, is inefficient for the same reason and bears little resemblance to modern machines.

Timeline of the 2014 Venezuelan protests documents a wave of demonstrations that began in February 2014. Across the country, hundreds of thousands took part in the protests, reflecting broad participation. The demonstrations were driven by concerns over high crime, inflation, and persistent shortages of basic goods, linked to government policies. The protests endured for several months, and the article organizes the events in a month-by-month sequence to show how the movement unfolded over time.

Wyoming features expansive basins spanning diverse ecoregions, from shrublands to arid desert patches. These basin areas contain geologic formations, sand dunes, and broad tracts of sparsely populated land. The landscapes sit at lower elevations and include rolling hills, valleys, mesas, terraces, and rugged terrain. They host natural springs, rivers, and several man-made reservoirs. Vegetation comprises sagebrush subspecies, junipers, and grasses such as wheatgrass. The basins are noted for supporting a high diversity of plant and animal life.

Wyoming's property tax regime encompasses several exemptions designed to relieve taxpayers in specific cases. Personal property used for individual use, as well as inventory held for resale, is exempt, and pollution-control equipment is likewise exempt. Financial assets such as cash, accounts receivable, stocks, and bonds are exempt as well. Property used for religious, educational, charitable, fraternal, benevolent, or governmental purposes is exempt, and improvements that facilitate handicapped access are likewise excluded from taxation. Additional exemptions apply to mine lands, underground mining equipment, and equipment employed in oil and gas extraction. In the minerals sector, the state imposes a gross products levy on mineral outputs and a severance levy on mineral extraction.

Windows 98 could be upgraded directly to Windows XP if the system met Windows XP requirements. The original plan for Windows 98 support to end was June 30, 2003. In December 2002, Microsoft extended the support window to January 16, 2004, and on January 13, 2004, it was extended again to June 30, 2006. The final end-of-support date was July 11, 2006. These extensions were attributed to higher support volumes in emerging markets.

Windows 98 introduced enhancements to its networking components, including an updated DHCP client that performs address assignment with conflict detection and features longer timeout intervals to improve reliability in dynamic networks. In addition, the NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NetBT) configuration for the WINS client was refined to persistently query multiple configured WINS servers if the initial session fails, continuing the process until all specified servers have been queried or a connection is successfully established.

The International Herald Tribune traces its physical offices to the Herald Tribune European Edition, with operations dating back to 1931. The original premises were located at 21 Rue de Berri, near the Champs-Élysées in Paris. American columnist Art Buchwald described the offices as grubby and antiquated, although he regarded their location as ideal for an American newspaper operating abroad. In 1978, the paper relocated its facilities to Neuilly-sur-Seine, a suburb of Paris.

The International Herald Tribune (IHT) was a daily English-language newspaper published in Paris for international English-speaking readers. Its origins as an international newspaper trace back to 1887, and in 1967 it began publishing under the name International Herald Tribune. The paper was sold in more than 160 countries. In 2013, it was relaunched as The International New York Times, the second incarnation of that title, an change that followed The New York Times Company’s attainment of sole ownership in 2003.

Samuel Sánchez’s 2007 season included a top-ten at Paris–Nice (ninth), a victory in the concluding time trial of the Tour of the Basque Country that helped him finish third overall, and, after a winless classics season, a stage win on the final day of the Volta a Catalunya. In the Vuelta a España, he claimed Stage 15 ahead of Manuel Beltrán after launching a late attack at Alto de Monachil and descending to Granada; although Beltrán asked to concede the victory, Sánchez chose to dedicate it to his future son due in March 2008, finishing by only a few metres and appearing to cradle a baby as he crossed the line. He went on to win the race’s final mountain stage to Alto de Abantos and the concluding time trial, which moved him up to third place overall and marked him as the first Euskaltel–Euskadi rider to podium in a Grand Tour.

Samuel Sánchez, a Spanish rider and pre-race favourite, began the Tour de France as one of the leading contenders but suffered an early crash that pushed him down the general classification as the race moved into the Pyrenees. In Stage 12 he claimed the first summit finish victory, breaking clear of the main rivals and regaining time. Under a revised scoring system for the King of the Mountains, Sánchez briefly wore the polka dot jersey, only to surrender it the following day to Jérémy Roy. Stage 14 saw him again attack on another ascent, finishing second and climbing to sixth overall. A descent into Gap on Stage 16 allowed Evans and Contador to gain time on others, moving Sánchez up to fifth place. On Stage 18 he lost time on the Col du Galibier, dropping to eighth. In the subsequent stage he and Contador launched an attack on Alpe d'Huez, with Sánchez finishing second to Rolland and advancing to seventh overall, effectively securing the mountains classification as no further climbs remained. In the Final Time Trial, Sánchez moved ahead of Cunego, finishing sixth overall (fifth after Contador's suspension) and winning the mountains classification.

The 2022–23 Football Superleague of Kosovo comprises ten clubs, combining the eight highest finishers from the previous season with two clubs promoted from the Kosovo First League. The promoted teams are Trepça '89 and Ferizaj, which thereby displaced Ulpiana and Feronikeli from the top flight.

At the conclusion of the 2022–23 Football Superleague of Kosovo, Liria Prizren earned promotion to the 2023–24 Football Superleague of Kosovo, advancing to the top division for the following season, while Ferizaj were relegated to the 2023–24 First Football League of Kosovo, dropping to the second tier for the next campaign.

During the British Expedition to Abyssinia, official assurances stated that the supplies required for soldiers would be paid for, and that no peaceable inhabitant would be molested. The declared sole objective of the British Force was the liberation of Her Majesty's subjects, and there was no intention to permanently occupy any part of Abyssinian territory. Additionally, authorities asserted that there was no plan to interfere with the Abyssinian government.

The 1868 British Expedition to Abyssinia is widely described as unlike any modern colonial campaign, proceeding with the decorum and inevitability associated with a Victorian state banquet and culminating in protracted ceremonial addresses. The undertaking was regarded as formidable because Ethiopia had not been invaded for centuries and its rugged terrain posed substantial risks of failure. Planning proved difficult, given that the conflict was fought on land rather than at sea, complicating military logistics and expectations. Moreover, Ethiopia’s lack of a seaboard meant there were no coastal cities or forts to bombard, no vessels to attack, and no ready targets for seizure of commerce.

Shidzue Katō (1897–2001) was a prominent Japanese socialist activist and advocate for women's rights who played a pivotal role in the suffrage movement. As a member of the Japanese Socialist Party, she became the first woman to be elected to Japan’s Imperial Diet, marking a landmark achievement for female political participation. Throughout her life, she dedicated herself to advancing women's reproductive and political rights, contributing to broader efforts to secure gender equality in Japan. In addition to her public advocacy, Katō challenged contemporary gender norms by annulling her marriage and remarrying, an action that was exceedingly uncommon for women of her era and underscored her commitment to female autonomy.

In Japan, families frequently sent women to work in factories, with the workers’ earnings typically sent back to support their households. Employers often provided room and board as part of the employment arrangement, but the living and working environments were commonly deplorable. These harsh conditions contributed to widespread illness and disease among female workers. The combination of substandard salaries, hazardous working conditions, and the risk of life-threatening illness helped mobilize the suffrage movement, which framed political rights as a means to secure improvements in women’s workplaces.

Giovanni Gronchi (Italian: [dʒoˈvanni ˈɡroŋki]; born 10 September 1887, died 17 October 1978) was an Italian Christian Democrat politician who served as President of Italy from 1955 to 1962. He is noted for his controversial, ultimately unsuccessful effort to pursue a rapprochement with left-wing forces in Italian politics. Some observers have argued that he exercised de facto executive power during his presidency, acting behind the scenes relative to the prime ministers. His tenure coincided with the end of the Italian Empire, marked by the independence of the Somali Republic in 1960.

Giovanni Gronchi volunteered for military service during World War I. He was a founding member of the Catholic Italian Popular Party in 1919 and was elected to represent Pisa in the 1919 and 1921 parliamentary elections. As a trade union leader, he headed the Catholic faction within the Italian Confederation of Christian Workers. Gronchi served as Under-Secretary for Industry and Commerce in Mussolini's first government from 1922 to 1923. In April 1923, at the Turin meeting of the Popular Party, all PPI representatives were withdrawn from the government. He subsequently returned to the leadership of Catholic trade unions and faced violence from fascist squads.

Close-mid front unrounded vowel is a vowel sound characterized by frontness of the tongue position, with the tongue raised toward the front of the mouth, and produced without any constriction that would qualify it as a consonant.

The close-mid front unrounded vowel is characterized by a vowel height that lies in the close-mid (high-mid) range, indicating a position between a close (high) vowel and a mid vowel. The tongue is placed roughly halfway between the high vowel position and the mid vowel position.

Insects vs Robots was a five-piece band based in Venice, California. The ensemble employed an unusual assortment of instruments, including violin, charango, harp, banjo, kazoo, harmonium, and sitar. It gained a reputation for engaging live performances, and its sound was diverse, formed from a wide mix of influences.
Insects vs Robots is a band that released a self-titled EP in 2009, followed by Geryl & The Great Homunculus in 2010, Tales From The Blue House in 2011, and an eponymous full-length album in 2013.
