The Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China established overseas police service stations in 2022, which prompted investigations by law enforcement authorities in several countries. In 2023, the United States Department of Justice asserted that the MPS conducts covert intelligence and national security operations beyond Chinese borders, describing these activities as illicit, transnational repression schemes. The DoJ charged 34 MPS officers in connection with these allegations, alleging that the officers used fake social media accounts to harass dissidents living overseas.

The Ministry of Public Security (MPS) of the People's Republic of China is led by the minister of public security; since June 2022, Wang Xiaohong has held the post. The MPS is organized into functional departments and oversees a hierarchical structure that includes provincial and municipal public security bureaus (PSBs) as well as sub-bureaus at the county and urban-district levels. Grassroots police stations (Pàichūsuǒ) operate as the direct point of contact between the police and ordinary citizens. Some external observers have argued that public security influence is increasingly felt at lower levels of government. Provincial PSBs are subject to dual supervision by local provincial governments and the central government. The ministry maintains a close association with surveillance-technology development through the Third Research Institute (Dì-sān Yánjiūsuǒ), which focuses on artificial intelligence–driven smart surveillance and censorship technologies.

Nagykanizsa FC follows standard conventions for indicating player nationality on its rosters; the national flags displayed with players denote their membership in national teams as defined by FIFA eligibility rules, with a small number of exceptions. Furthermore, players may hold more than one non‑FIFA nationality, reflecting multiple citizenships outside the FIFA framework.

Nasser Al-Shatti's first senior-team tenure occurred with Al-Arabi, after he signed a short-term contract on 7 March 2017 that was slated to expire at the end of the 2016–17 season. During his time with the club, he promoted several players from its youth ranks, including Bader Al-Fadhel. He departed Al-Arabi in July 2017.
Nasser Al-Shatti (born 14 July 1986) is a retired professional footballer who played as a midfielder. He is currently the head coach of Al-Arabi.
The Last Round-Up is a 1934 American Pre-Code Western film directed by Henry Hathaway and starring Randolph Scott, Monte Blue, and Barbara Adams.

American teenagers in the early 1960s grew weary of pop acts that prioritized single releases, as illustrated by Fabian and a group of artists known as the Bobby acts (for example, Bobby Darin, Bobby Vinton, Bobby Rydell, and Bobby Vee). In mid-1960s Britain, the Mod and Rocker youth movements shaped the milieu of the British Invasion, with bands adopting the Mod aesthetic quickly rising to prominence within the scene. Those groups able to blend Mod styling with other influences—exemplified by the Beatles—also achieved broad success, underscoring the varied approaches that contributed to the era’s transatlantic musical impact.

In the mid- to late 2000s, a notable rise of British R&B and soul artists achieved significant success on U.S. music charts, signaling a renewed British presence in American popular music. This development spurred discussion of a potential Third British Invasion, sometimes labeled the British Soul Invasion, as British acts extended their reach in the United States. Prominent figures associated with this movement include Amy Winehouse, Estelle, Joss Stone, Duffy, Natasha Bedingfield, Florence Welch, Adele, Floetry, Jessie J, Leona Lewis, Jay Sean, and Taio Cruz. Additionally, One Direction emerged as a major component of this new wave, given that their debut album reached the top of the U.S. charts and contributed to a broader pattern of British success in the American market.

Broadcast licenses in the United States have historically been issued for nominal payments rather than through market-based pricing. Economist Ronald Coase challenged the FCC’s method of allocating spectrum, proposing instead that the radio spectrum be managed by market mechanisms similar to other scarce resources such as land or metals. His argument relies on the Coase theorem: when property rights are clearly defined and transaction costs are low, a free market will allocate resources to their most valuable use. Consequently, Coase maintained that licenses for a bounded portion of spectrum carry significant economic value and should be transacted in open markets rather than allocated gratis. In line with this view, licensing has increasingly been conducted through spectrum auctions. However, auctions have been criticized for neglecting non-commercial educational users, who are excluded from the process on economic grounds.

Broadcast licenses authorize station operation within a defined service area and, in certain circumstances, two stations may operate on the same frequency within the same market or facility. Time-sharing arrangements have been employed when competing applicants hold equal point totals, a solution that has been used especially with low-power FM stations. In the United States, the FCC’s Auction 1000 for the 600 MHz band required TV stations in crowded markets to relinquish air occupancy to enable repacking of stations on channels 38–51 into the spectrum already allocated to channels 2–36. Television licenses may be transferred to another existing station while preserving the original station’s virtual channel and must-carry rights. Each licensee is responsible for the content broadcast on their channels, and the two licensees involved share responsibility for the technical operation of the transmitter, antenna, and tower.

MaxiCode is a 1-inch square barcode symbol, sometimes referred to as Bird's Eye, Target, dense code, or the UPS code. Its design centers on a bullseye at the core, surrounded by hexagonal dots, forming a symmetrical pattern that aids rapid recognition. The code can encode roughly 93 characters, and in certain configurations up to eight linked symbols may be used to convey additional data. The symmetric bullseye design supports fast, accurate scanning, even when applied to moving packages.

MaxiCode comprises several encoding modes, with Mode 0 now considered obsolete and superseded by Modes 2 and 3. Despite this, some legacy printers equipped with outdated firmware may still produce MaxiCode symbols in Mode 0. A distinctive feature of Mode 0 is the presence of two white horizontal hexagons located in the upper-right corner of the symbol; in all other modes, these two hexagons are rendered black.

Ipili verbs are inflected through suffixation to convey tense, mood, aspect, as well as person and number. The inflectional suffixes fall into two main classes: tense suffixes and person suffixes. In a given verb form, a person suffix is attached after a tense suffix, so the tense information precedes the person marking within the suffix chain.

Ipili is described as having a five-vowel system, with phonemic vowels /a, e, i, o, u/. The language's consonant inventory comprises thirteen phonemes, including the voiceless stops /p, t, k/; the prenasalized stops /mb, nd, nj, ŋg/; the nasals /m, n/; the fricative /s/; and the approximants /l, y, w/. In addition, there are reports that Ipili may exhibit tonal contrasts, indicating that tone could be a possible phonemic feature.

During the 2022–23 Ekstraklasa season, Wisła Kraków was relegated to the I liga, ending a 26-year uninterrupted top-flight presence and marking the club’s first relegation since the 1993–94 campaign. Bruk-Bet Termalica Nieciecza and Górnik Łęczna also dropped down after only one season at the highest level. Miedź Legnica earned promotion to the Ekstraklasa, returning to the top flight after a three-year absence (last competing in 2018–19). Widzew Łódź gained promotion on 22 May following a 2–1 win over Podbeskidzie Bielsko-Biała, returning to the Ekstraklasa after eight years (last appeared in 2013–14). Korona Kielce also earned promotion to the top division, returning after two seasons away (their last season in 2019–20).

Defending champions Lech Poznań entered the 2022–23 Ekstraklasa season following their eighth Polish title in the previous campaign. Raków Częstochowa then secured their first Ekstraklasa championship on 7 May, after Legia Warszawa suffered a 1–2 defeat away to Pogoń Szczecin with three games remaining. Legia Warszawa finished the season in second place, while Lech Poznań completed the campaign in third.

The rock castle is characterized by its deliberate integration with the bedrock on which it stands. When the underlying stone is relatively easy to work, such as sandstone, it was cut or hacked to form rooms, passages, stairs, well shafts, and cisterns. Buildings—whether wooden or stone—were placed on or adjacent to the rock, using it as a foundation or as part of the walls. Wooden remnants are rarely preserved, but their former locations can be inferred from joist bearings and holes that remain visible in the rock.

Rock castle, a term used by the castle researcher Otto Piper, derives from the German ausgehauene Burg, literally meaning "hewn-out castle." It denotes fortifications in which interior rooms are artificially carved from the rock that forms the foundation or walls of the structure. Examples commonly cited include Fleckenstein, Trifels, and Altwindstein. The concept is closely related to cave castles, since both typologies involve spaces cut directly out of rock rather than being formed by standard masonry.

Operator, as a professional designation, is used across diverse industries, including broadcasting, computing, power generation and transmission, customer service, physics, and construction. Operators are the day-to-day end users of the systems they operate, which may be mission-critical or non-mission-critical in nature. The systems involved are typically managed and maintained by technicians or engineers, while operators focus on routine operation. In many contexts, operators work on a 24-hour rotating shift schedule to ensure continuous coverage.

Oracle Cloud comprises its public cloud and government cloud offerings, delivered through a global network of Oracle-managed data centers linked by an Oracle-controlled backbone. Exadata Cloud at Customer uses this network to support its control-plane services. The cloud is organized into Regions, typically deployed in two geographically distributed Regions per country to enhance disaster resiliency and meet data sovereignty requirements. Within a Region, there is at least one fault-independent Availability Domain, and each Availability Domain contains three fault domains designed to be fault-tolerant. An Availability Domain is an independent data center with its own power, cooling, and network isolation.

Oracle Cloud is Oracle Corporation's cloud computing platform that provides an open, standards-based environment for developing API-first, mobile-first cloud applications. The platform supports container-native and cloud-native approaches as well as low-code development, enabling a range of deployment models. It encompasses a DevOps platform for continuous integration and delivery, and offers diagnostics tools for Java applications to support performance monitoring and troubleshooting. Designed to integrate with both SaaS and on-premises systems, Oracle Cloud supports hybrid configurations and interoperability across environments. Its portfolio of services includes Java and mobile development, digital assistants (drawing on the lineage of chatbots), messaging, Application Container Cloud, Developer Cloud, Visual Builder, API Catalog, an AI platform, and blockchain capabilities, in addition to DataScience.com, which Oracle acquired.

During the Great Migration of 1910–1960, hundreds of thousands of African Americans moved from the rural South to Illinois, most prominently to Chicago, with some settling in East St. Louis. Escaping rural poverty and its limited prospects for education, medical care, and decent housing, they sought better opportunities in urban centers as industrial work expanded. The 1914 restriction on European immigration combined with increased military spending in World War I helped create numerous job openings in Chicago, drawing migrants who would contribute to the city’s economy. In Chicago, African Americans across classes founded churches, community organizations, and businesses, and produced influential contributions to music and literature, helping to shape a distinct urban culture. Across the South Side and also the West Side, Black residents constructed self-sustaining communities for decades before the Civil Rights Movement, living in segregated neighborhoods while pursuing survival and the creation of better lives.

French explorers arrived in the Illinois region in the 1670s–1680s and established the Illinois colony, contributing to regional stabilization. In the 1690s, the Miami and Mascouten subtribes reconstituted two groups—the Miami and the Wea—and moved back east. Following the Yamasee War (1715–1717), the French assisted a breakaway Yuchi faction known as the Chisca to migrate into Illiniwek territory. During the French and Indian War, English influence extended into the Illinois Colony, undermining its stability. The Chisca, who had become largely assimilated into Algonquian culture, split away, returned to Kentucky, took several Illiniwek with them, and came to be known as the Kispoko. The Kispoko soon merged with the Shawnee. With increasing land pressure, the remaining Illiniwek were pushed onto the Great Plains and fragmented. Today, the surviving Illiniwek are represented by a single tribe—the Peoria of Oklahoma.

At the conclusion of the 1996 CONCACAF Gold Cup, the competition's individual honors were announced. The Golden Boot was awarded to the tournament's leading goal scorer, while the Golden Ball recognized the best overall player of the tournament.

Nine national teams participated in the 1996 CONCACAF Gold Cup. Each team was required to register a squad of twenty players, and eligibility to participate was restricted to players included in those registered squads.

The Central Foreign Affairs Commission, the top organ of the Communist Party of China (CCP) for foreign affairs, functions as the principal mechanism through which the CCP leadership deliberates, assigns responsibilities, and oversees the implementation of foreign-related policy across a broad spectrum of activities. Its remit covers traditional diplomacy, party-to-party engagement, external propaganda, foreign trade policy, overseas intelligence activities, counterespionage, and the internal dimensions of Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan affairs. Meetings of the commission are rarely publicized, and information about its proceedings is limited.

The Central Foreign Affairs Commission is the body responsible for policy making, deliberation, and coordination relating to the conduct of the state's external relations. It considers and formulates the nation’s foreign relations strategy, along with the principal principles and policies that guide diplomacy. The commission provides direction for the implementation of these strategies and policies, ensuring coherent guidance across relevant government departments. It undertakes top-level planning, coordination, and comprehensive advancement of foreign affairs work, and supervises the execution of foreign relations initiatives to ensure effective and unified application.

Vladimir Putin secured a second term as president in 2004. Fueled by high oil prices and rising foreign investment, Russia experienced substantial improvements in its economy and living standards during this period. Putin's governance contributed to greater stability, although it also coincided with a consolidation of power and a shift toward a more centralized, quasi-authoritarian political system. In 2008, Putin stepped aside from the presidency to become prime minister while Dmitry Medvedev was elected president for a single term, a configuration frequently described as a tandem arrangement or “tandemocracy” intended to sustain influence beyond formal term limits.

During the 1960s and 1970s, Soviet cinema displayed a broader range of artistic styles, reflecting a diversification of approaches within the state film industry. Prominent filmmakers such as Eldar Ryazanov and Leonid Gaidai produced comedies that achieved widespread popularity, with many of their catchphrases becoming part of everyday speech. From 1961 to 1968, Sergei Bondarchuk directed War and Peace, an epic that earned an Academy Award and was the most expensive film produced in the Soviet Union. In 1969 Vladimir Motyl released White Sun of the Desert, which became a touchstone of the ostern Western genre and is traditionally watched by cosmonauts before space missions. Following the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Russian cinema faced substantial losses in funding and infrastructure. Nevertheless, beginning in the late 2000s, the industry regained strength and has continued to grow and expand.

Metadata for scientific outputs can be created or supplemented to improve the description, discoverability, and interoperability of research results. Some organizations classify and link citations to a study as supporting, mentioning, or contrasting the work. Developments in alternative metrics aim to aid assessment and findability by capturing broader impact beyond traditional citations, including online discussions about a paper on social media such as Reddit, mentions in Wikipedia, and coverage in news media. This approach seeks to complement conventional metrics by reflecting diverse forms of engagement and visibility surrounding a publication. There has been a call for indicating whether the original findings have been confirmed or are reproducible, to convey the robustness of the results.

Descriptive metadata consists of information about a resource that characterizes its content. It serves primarily to facilitate discovery and identification of the item within catalogs and databases. Common elements of descriptive metadata include the title, an abstract or summary, the author or creator, and keywords that reflect the resource's topics.
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) stated that Google Earth poses a security threat to India. It seeks dialogue with Google officials to address the concerns.

In 2009, Google Earth incorporated overlays that projected scans of historical woodblock maps from 18th- and 19th-century Japan onto contemporary geography, creating a juxtaposition of past cartography with present-day imagery. The overlays mark areas associated with the burakumin, a historically stigmatized group formerly known as eta (穢多) and described in historical sources as being relegated to certain occupations, such as leather tanning and butchery. Descendants of this caste continue to face discrimination in modern times. There were concerns that etamura, or eta villages depicted on the maps, could be exploited to identify or target current residents. The maps remain visible on Google Earth, but the labels have been removed where necessary to address sensitivities.

The General Assembly functions as the principal representative organ of the International Radiation Protection Association, and is composed of delegates drawn from the Association’s Associate Societies. It delegates authority to the Executive Council to oversee the organization’s governance and operations, a delegation intended to facilitate the efficient administration of the Association’s affairs.

Since the 1973 IRPA Congress, the opening program of each International Congress has featured the Sievert Lecture, delivered by the recipient of the Sievert Award. The Sievert Award is named in honor of Rolf M. Sievert, a pioneer in radiation physics and radiation protection.

TxDOT intends to designate existing freeway sections that meet the standards of the proposed I-69 system as I-69 at the earliest feasible opportunity. In addition, a bill introduced in the Texas House and later passed would authorize Interstate-quality segments of US 59, US 77, and US 281 to be designated as I-69. The statute would allow such signage and designation even if these segments are not connected to other Interstate Highways, enabling independent adoption of the I-69 designation where appropriate.

Interstate 69 in Texas comprises the mainline segment that begins just south of Rosenberg and proceeds to Sugar Land, enters Downtown Houston, exits the Houston area at New Caney, and ends in Cleveland, where the route continues as U.S. Route 59.

Hiking, as a form of long-distance walking undertaken for exploration and documentation, gained prominence in Europe in the late eighteenth century when numerous travelers crossed the continent on foot and recorded their experiences. Among these early practitioners, Johann Gottfried Seume is cited as a notable example. In 1801, Seume embarked on a pedestrian journey from Leipzig to Sicily, and after about nine months he returned to Leipzig by way of Paris.

Hiking includes a range of long-distance trekking routes, and among them the Camino de Santiago, commonly known as the Way of St. James, stands as an ancient pilgrimage tradition. Over the centuries it has given rise to a large number of extended hiking itineraries, forming a network of pilgrimage paths that converge on the shrine of Saint James the Great. The shrine is housed within the cathedral in Santiago de Compostela, located in Galicia in the northwest of Spain. For many participants, these routes are pursued as a spiritual journey or retreat aimed at personal growth and reflection.

PNG was designed as a patent-free successor to the GIF format to address the LZW patent held by Unisys. It generally offers improved compression and a broader feature set relative to GIF. For most purposes, PNG is better suited to true-color imaging and supports alpha transparency, making it the preferred option for static images requiring lossless compression. However, an important exception is animation: GIF remains advantageous for animated graphics due to its native support and established compatibility. Thus, while PNG provides enhancements for still images, GIF continues to be used when simple animation is required.

The HTML5 video element enjoys widespread compatibility across modern web browsers. Some websites create a looping video element to imitate a GIF, presenting a familiar animated appearance while leveraging the smaller file size and faster playback associated with compressed video formats.

The Lenape signed the Treaty of the James Fork on September 24, 1829, which was ratified by the United States Senate in 1830, leading to their relocation farther west. As part of the agreement, they were allotted lands in Indian Territory in exchange for ceding their Missouri lands along the James Fork of the White River. The Missouri allotment lay in the region that is now Kansas, located west of the Missouri River and north of the Kansas River. The principal reserve encompassed approximately 1,000,000 acres (about 4,000 square kilometers), with an additional outlet strip ten miles wide extending to the west.

The Lenape languages have historically been oral languages, with no conventional written tradition. In 2002, the Delaware Tribe of Indians secured grant funding to support the Lenape Talking Dictionary, a project devoted to documenting and revitalizing the language. The initiative concentrates on the Southern Unami dialect, aiming to preserve linguistic materials and provide digital access through digitization.

Marian Anderson: The Lincoln Memorial Concert is a 1939 documentary covering Marian Anderson's Lincoln Memorial performance. The Daughters of the American Revolution refused to permit her to sing at Constitution Hall because she was Black, and District of Columbia officials barred her from performing in a white public high school auditorium. First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt helped arrange the concert on federal property at the Lincoln Memorial. The Easter Sunday, April 9, 1939 performance drew an audience of about 75,000 people. In 2001 the Library of Congress selected the film for preservation in the National Film Registry.

Yunnan Province, situated in southwestern China, has an economy traditionally anchored by tobacco, which remains the principal export and a major contributor to the province’s gross domestic product. The region also demonstrates considerable competitive potential in its fruit and vegetable sectors, with a distinctive advantage in low value-added products such as fresh vegetables, dried vegetables, and fresh apples, reflecting a durable horticultural competitiveness alongside its tobacco-based export base.

The Dali Plateau Lake Microecology Research Station, situated on the shores of Erhai Lake in Yunnan, specializes in the study of microbial communities in high-altitude freshwater lakes. Researchers assess the diversity of microorganisms and examine their functional roles in preserving water quality and ecological balance. The work aims to provide a scientific basis for the conservation of Erhai Lake and analogous plateau-lake systems, contributing to regional approaches to ecosystem protection and sustainable water management.

Since 2005, macOS X has bundled a dictionary application credited to Oxford American Dictionaries. It contains the complete text of the New Oxford American Dictionary, second edition (NOAD2). The Amazon Kindle platform uses NOAD as its built-in dictionary, and Kindle also offers the Oxford Dictionary of English as an alternative reference.
The New Oxford American Dictionary (NOAD) is a single-volume reference dictionary focusing on American English. It was compiled by American editors affiliated with the Oxford University Press.

Solar wind exists primarily in two distinct states—the slow and the fast component—whose differences extend beyond speed to several key properties. Near Earth, the slow wind streams at roughly 300–500 km/s, with temperatures on the order of 1×10^5 kelvin and a composition that remains close to that of the solar corona. In contrast, the fast wind travels at about 750 km/s, reaches temperatures near 8×10^5 kelvin, and is compositionally more similar to the photosphere. Additionally, the slow wind is denser, containing roughly twice the particle density of the fast wind, and it exhibits greater temporal variability than its fast counterpart.

Solar wind creates a protective bubble around the Sun known as the heliosphere, whose boundary is defined by several factors. The Solar System's extent is commonly considered in terms of the heliopause, the Kuiper Belt, and the distance at which the Sun's gravity is overwhelmed by external gravitational perturbations from other stars and galactic tides. Estimates place the Sun's gravitational influence to extend from about 50,000 astronomical units up to around two light-years, reflecting different models of where solar gravity yields to external forces. The heliopause itself is the outer boundary of the heliosphere, separating solar wind from interstellar space. This boundary was first detected by Voyager 1 at a distance of roughly 120 AU from the Sun, indicating that the heliopause lies far inside the maximum extent of the Sun's gravitational reach.

Anonymous reporting mechanisms are designed to create an environment in which employees are more likely to report suspected or actual wrongdoing or seek guidance on potential violations, without fear of retaliation. These mechanisms were previously noted in discussions of whistleblowing practices. ISO 37001 is the forthcoming standard governing anti-bribery management systems, and anonymous reporting constitutes one of the criteria specified within ISO 37001.

Research on the psychological impact of whistle-blowing remains limited; when negative experiences occur, they can produce a prolonged and substantial decline in well-being. Whistle-blowers frequently report silence or hostility from management or colleagues, and depression is commonly observed among them, with suicidal thoughts occurring in approximately 10 percent of cases. Overall health and self-care are often described as deteriorating, and the symptomatology shares features with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), though diagnostic thresholds remain debated. In addition, whistle-blowers have been described as experiencing an increased incidence of stress-related physical illnesses.

Attitude is a ballet movement in which the working leg is raised with a bent knee while the opposite leg remains extended, and it can be performed on pointe or on demi-pointe. In execution, the back leg is kept straight as the front leg stays bent and lifted; subsequently, the bent front leg straightens along the floor while the raised back leg bends. The sequence is repeated continuously, producing the impression that the dancer is flying across the floor.
Manèges is a classical ballet term that denotes circular movement, describing steps performed in a circular pattern around the stage.

Hans Krankl made his international debut for Austria in June 1973 in a friendly against Brazil, and he later represented his country at the 1978 and 1982 FIFA World Cups. Over his international career, he earned 69 caps and scored 34 goals, with his final appearance coming in April 1985 in a World Cup qualifier against Hungary. At club level, he delivered a standout season in the 1978–79 Spanish Primera División, finishing as the league’s top scorer with 29 goals for Barcelona, an achievement that earned him the Pichichi Trophy.

Hans Krankl began his professional career with Rapid Wien, remaining there for eight seasons aside from a one-year spell with Wiener AC. He earned the European Golden Boot with Rapid Wien in 1978, an accolade that attracted the attention of FC Barcelona, whom he joined thereafter. At Barcelona he helped the club win the European Cup Winners' Cup and scored in the final, while he finished the season as La Liga's top scorer with 29 goals. In 1981 he returned to Rapid Wien, where he served as captain and scored over 100 goals for the club in the ensuing five years. He was a central figure in Rapid's most successful era of the 1980s, contributing to two Austrian League titles (1982 and 1983) and three consecutive Austrian Cup victories. Notably, he scored Rapid's only goal in the 3–1 defeat to Everton in the 1985 European Cup Winners' Cup Final. In 1986 Krankl moved to Wiener Sport-Club, taking on the role of player-manager.

Smog in Los Angeles became a prominent example of motor-vehicle–driven air pollution, and at times served as a shorthand for smog itself. By 1970, under the Clean Air Act, the Los Angeles Basin was the most polluted air basin in the United States, and California had not developed a State Implementation Plan to meet federal standards. Subsequently, regulatory actions at both the state and federal levels, including measures by the California Air Resources Board and the Environmental Protection Agency, imposed strict emissions limits on new California cars and required periodic inspections for older vehicles. These policies contributed to substantial improvements in air quality, with volatile organic compound concentrations declining by a factor of 50 from 1962 to 2012, and nitrogen oxides and ozone levels decreasing by about 70 to 80 percent over the same period.

Smog episodes in Southeast Asia are largely driven by transboundary haze resulting from forest and vegetation fires. In 2002 ASEAN members signed the Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, establishing a formal framework for regional cooperation and response to cross-border haze. The organization subsequently formed the Regional Haze Action Plan and established a coordination and support unit to manage its activities. With assistance from Canada, RHAP developed a monitoring and warning system for fires in forest and vegetation areas and introduced a Fire Danger Rating System (FDRS) to gauge risk levels. The Malaysian Meteorological Department has issued a daily fire danger rating since September 2003, providing regular risk assessments. By contrast, Indonesia has faced difficulty enforcing legal policies against errant farmers, undermining the effectiveness of regional haze mitigation efforts.

Headpiece, also spelled head-piece, denotes a decorative device placed at the outset of a chapter or other division in a book. It is set into the blank space allocated for that location, serving to introduce the ensuing text. The form is typically an ornamental panel, a printer's ornament, or a small illustration, reflecting the diverse practices of book design. Such elements are produced by professional illustrators, highlighting the collaborative role of artists in traditional book production.

Headpieces were a common decorative element in medieval manuscripts and in 15th-century editions of the Bible. They often functioned at the opening of a page or section and sometimes incorporated rubric text or a heading within the design. The imagery within headpieces frequently displayed zoomorphic motifs—animal figures—and anthropomorphic motifs—human-like figures—reflecting the era's stylistic conventions.

Although the GameCube is not designed to function as a general DVD player, an exception exists in the Panasonic Q, a uniquely customized edition of the console that incorporates built-in DVD playback capabilities. This model combines Nintendo's hardware with integrated DVD features and was released exclusively in Japan.

The GameCube game discs feature a BCA mark that is visible to the naked eye. This mark is distinct from the IFPI mark that appears on most optical discs. The BCA is described in Annex K of the physical specification. It can be observed in a band at radii from 22.3 ± 0.4 mm to 23.5 ± 0.5 mm from the disc center. Six additional evenly spaced small cuts just outside the BCA radius are related to copy protection and are visible only under strong illumination. The effectiveness of this protective scheme diminished after Datel demonstrated that the same pattern could be replicated onto a DVD rather than being cut into the disc.

For the Mac Mini G4, critical reception was mixed. CNET praised the unit for its affordability, quiet operation, and compact form factor, but faulted the slow hard drive and noted that the system offered only two USB 2.0 ports, which fell short of expectations. Ars Technica criticized the non-user-upgradable RAM and the lack of upgradeable storage options, as well as the high fees for additional drives. Nonetheless, Ars Technica concluded that the overall performance was reasonably acceptable.

The Mac mini is Apple's compact desktop computer and one of the four current Mac desktop models, alongside the iMac, Mac Studio, and Mac Pro. It represents the entry-level option in Apple's desktop lineup, placed below the iMac, Mac Studio, and Mac Pro in terms of features and target price. Since its launch, it has been sold as a standalone unit without a built-in display, keyboard, or mouse, in line with the BYODKM slogan—Bring Your Own Display, Keyboard, and Mouse. The product was marketed to Windows PC users by highlighting the ability to reuse existing peripherals, offering a cost-effective path to switching to the Mac platform. The branding is stylized as Mac mini.

Salome Zourabichvili was eight years old when she met her first visitor from Georgia in Paris during a visit by a Georgian ballet troupe; the encounter was arranged secretly because the Soviet authorities organizing the visit imposed restrictions on such contact. In a Washington Post interview, she described feeling comfortable balancing Georgian and French identities, effectively navigating between the two cultures. She pursued her education in French schools while also attending the Georgian church of Paris on weekends.

Salomé Zourabichvili, in a May 2022 interview with DW News, stated that Georgia remains in full compliance with international sanctions on Russia and advocates for a quicker, more direct path to NATO and European Union membership. She also commented on a shift in the stance of major Western capitals, noting that France under President Macron and Germany under Chancellor Scholz had moved toward expansionary policies. She argued that this shift predates the August 2008 Russo-Georgian War, and that Paris and Berlin had since embraced broader policy orientations in relation to Georgia and Western security and integration efforts.

Wimbledon is a 2004 film that centers on a professional tennis player who has fallen into a slump. The character is portrayed by Paul Bettany. He forms a connection with a young woman on the women's tennis circuit, played by Kirsten Dunst, and her involvement rekindles his motivation to pursue a Wimbledon title.

Professional tennis players generally receive benefits comparable to those afforded to athletes in other premier sports, including clothing allowances, equipment, and endorsement deals. Like competitors in other individual sports such as golf, they are typically not on a fixed salary; earnings derive primarily from prize money awarded for performances in tournaments. Prize money is earned by participating in events and achieving successful results, with larger rewards for advancing to later rounds and securing higher finishes.

Aliasing is considered inevitable because, in theory, only signals of infinite duration can be devoid of spectral content beyond the Nyquist frequency. In practice, finite signals contain components that extend above this limit and may be folded back into the observed spectrum when sampled. The extent of aliasing can be diminished by employing an anti-aliasing filter with a sufficiently high order, which attenuates frequencies above the Nyquist threshold before sampling. Moreover, increasing the order of the anti-aliasing filter reduces aliasing further, and in principle can make the residual aliasing arbitrarily small.

Volume rendering involves sampling a three-dimensional grid of voxels to produce three-dimensional visualizations of tomographic data. The grid is regarded as representing a continuous region of space, enabling the discrete samples to model the underlying structures. The technique is common in medical imaging, with notable applications including computed tomography (CT/CAT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET). It is also employed in seismic tomography and other applications.

Factual television is a genre of non-fiction television programming that documents actual events and real people. It is also described as observational documentary, fly-on-the-wall, docudrama, and reality television. The genre has existed in various forms since the early years of television. The term factual television has been especially applied to programs produced since the 1990s. The label is most commonly used in the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand.

In September 2012, BBC Television's Top Gear was named by Guinness World Records as the most-watched factual television programme. The designation was awarded by Guinness World Records, and Jeremy Clarkson accepted the Guinness World Records 2013 book on Top Gear's behalf, remarking that he was proud to be involved in a programme grounded in factual content.

Zurich Opera House, historically known as the Aktientheater, was Zurich’s first permanent theatre, constructed in 1834. The venue subsequently became a central locus for the activities of Richard Wagner during his exile from Germany, serving as a focal point for his work in the city.

By the 1970s, the Zurich Opera House required substantial renovation. Some argued that restoration was not worthwhile, and a new theatre for the site was proposed. The reconstruction proceeded from 1982 to 1984, following the Opernhauskrawalle, the protests surrounding the venue. The rebuilt theatre opened with Wagner’s Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg. The inauguration also featured the world premiere of Rudolf Kelterborn’s Chekhov-inspired opera Der Kirschgarten.

Milton returns home while Tammy distracts him with an extended presentation as Skipper and the children are away. The kids spot an unmanned, auto-piloted birthday-party plane created by Mr. Moneyclown, and a flight attendant allows them to board, mistaking them for testers. Skipper and her friends pursue the aircraft, and Erica engages the take-off sequence, triggering a test flight. A limousine sent to collect Skipper and the kids becomes stuck in Malibu traffic, prompting Tammy to videoconference Skipper and arrange a boat trip when they cannot arrive on time. On the boat, Captain Arlene prefers to wait for the fog to lift, while Anna is pressed for time. Skipper enlists the help of dolphins, who agree to guide the vessel back to the park. Milton grows bored with Tammy’s presentation and goes outside as Skipper returns, noting that Milton missed the gaming bus and that customers were satisfied. Erica and Derek inform their mother about the adventure, who assumes it was imagination. Milton contemplates establishing a daycare at the park but rejects renting the gaming bus, while Skipper urges Tammy to speak up; Tammy declares she will open a daycare. Milton appreciates Tammy’s initiative but remains unwilling to rent the bus, and Skipper suggests Tammy’s pool-cleaning idea could serve as a simple, no-cost daycare option, which Milton agrees to. Tammy and Skipper exchange a hug but retreat to maintain boundaries; Tammy also hugs Milton, who considers the gesture not business-like and reminds that not everything is about business. A new daycare opens as Skipper struggles to believe summer is nearly over; Tammy asks her to return next year, praising her babysitting and the park’s increased appeal, and the two share a fist bump with Skipper feeling satisfied. Skipper’s family and Ken visit the park, and Barbie commends Skipper while noting that Tammy is not a bad person, just in need of reminders at times. Joy performs “My Friends” while Skipper DJs, and Milton embraces Tammy.

Barbie: Skipper and the Big Babysitting Adventure follows Skipper as Barbie spends most of the summer on volunteer work in a rainforest. With the aim of reviving her babysitting service, Skipper asks Barbie for help, but Barbie is unavailable due to her rainforest assignment. In Barbie's absence, Stacie and Chelsea attend a sleepaway camp, leaving Skipper at home with their parents, George and Margaret, for most of the season. Navya and Chantal, Skipper's other friends, are also away for the summer, and Ken is busy with his lifeguard duties, preventing him from spending time with Skipper. Facing a lack of support, Skipper decides to seek another job until her babysitting business picks up again.

HomeGrocer, an online grocery retailer, raised about $440 million in investment from a consortium of backers that included Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, Amazon.com, Liberty Media’s John Malone, Solstice, Martha Stewart, and Jim Barksdale.

HomeGrocer was noted for its strong customer support and pursued a rapid expansion of its facilities, opening a series of new locations from May 1999 through May 2000. The first facility was established in Portland, Oregon in May 1999, with a subsequent site in Renton, Washington in September 1999. In October 1999, a facility came online in Irvine, California, followed by additional California locations in Fullerton (January 2000), Carson (February 2000), Azusa (March 2000), and San Diego (April 2000). The expansion concluded with a Dallas, Texas facility in May 2000.

The .NET Foundation began with stewardship of 24 projects, including the .NET Compiler Platform (Roslyn) and the open-source ASP.NET initiatives that had been released by Microsoft Open Technologies (MS Open Tech). Xamarin contributed six projects, among them the open-source MimeKit and MailKit libraries. By May 2020 the Foundation oversaw 556 active projects, encompassing core technologies and tools such as .NET, Entity Framework, the Managed Extensibility Framework (MEF), MSBuild, NuGet, Orchard CMS, and WorldWide Telescope. A number of these projects are also listed in the Outercurve Foundation project galleries.

As of June 2024, the .NET Foundation was governed by a seven-member board of directors, comprising Louëlla Creemers, Mitchel Sellers, Kendall Miller, Chris Woodruff, Glenn Watson, Kevin Griffin, and Chris Sfanos.

Upper-pharyngeal plosives have not been documented as phonemic categories in any of the world's languages, marking a notable gap in the inventory of human consonants. An exception to this general absence appears in the rear closure component of some click consonants, where a constriction may occur in the upper pharynx. Outside of normal language systems, such articulations can arise in disordered speech, illustrating how upper-pharyngeal timing and placement may manifest under atypical conditions. Both voiceless and voiced realizations of upper-pharyngeal plosives have been described.

Pharyngeal consonants, as analyzed by Edmondson and colleagues, are subdivided into several distinct subtypes. Pharyngeal and epiglottal stops and trills are typically produced by contracting the aryepiglottic folds against the epiglottis, a configuration described as aryepiglottal articulation. Pharyngeal fricatives are produced with the root of the tongue retracted toward the back wall of the pharynx. In certain languages, such as Achumawi, Amis of Taiwan, and possibly some Salishan languages, the articulatory gesture combines aryepiglottic fold contraction with epiglottis retraction toward the pharyngeal wall, a configuration referred to as epiglotto-pharyngeal articulation. Because the International Phonetic Alphabet lacks diacritics to distinguish epiglotto-pharyngeal from standard aryepiglottal sounds, Edmondson and colleagues employ ad hoc transcriptions such as ⟨ʕ͡ʡ⟩ and ⟨ʜ͡ħ⟩. In addition, diacritics exist within the Voice Quality Symbols to mark subtypes of pharyngeal sounds.

Hippolyte Pixii (1808–1835) was a Parisian instrument maker who, in 1832, constructed an early electrical generator inspired by Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. The device used a hand-cranked, spinning magnet whose poles passed over a coil wound around an iron core, and it is categorized as a magneto. A current pulse was generated each time a magnet pole passed the coil, with the direction reversing as successive poles altered the flux. Following André-Marie Ampère's suggestion, the addition of a commutator produced pulsating direct current. At the time, direct current was preferred over alternating current. Although Pixii did not fully understand the underlying principles of electromagnetic induction, his apparatus influenced the later development of more advanced machines.

The former commandery, known as the Komturei, has been repurposed into a chain of parks in Tempelhof, comprising Bosepark, Kleiner Park, Alter Park, and Franckepark. Some of these parks preserve ponds that formed part of the artificial moat surrounding the village center. Krummer Pfuhl, a pond located in Franckepark, was converted into public swimming baths in the 19th century; it has since dried out and now serves as an enclosed deer park.

Tempelhof, also known as Tempelhove, is first documented in 1247 in a Walkenried Abbey charter as a Komturhof, or commander’s court, of the Knights Templar. After the fall of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in 1291, the Templar leadership and numerous knights were expelled from that realm. The core of the old settlement, including the church and the original estate, was fortified and initially entirely encircled by water. The Templars were joined by fifteen families of landless sons from the Rhine region, who could not inherit estates due to the fragmentation of property. Legates of the order offered them fertile land and protection within Tempelhove’s stronghold.

Arturo Michelini succeeded De Marsanich as leader of the Italian Social Movement (MSI) in 1954, guiding the party through a period dominated by conservative elements in the 1950s and 1960s and a comparatively moderate course. By the end of the decade, the MSI had become Italy’s fourth-largest political force, reflecting a persistent neo-fascist presence within Italy’s postwar party system, a pattern relatively uncommon in Europe. Michelini pursued the inserimento strategy, aiming to gain legitimacy within liberal democracy by cooperating with other parties. This approach coincided with internal tensions, as radicals dissatisfied with parliamentarism and the party’s image of democratic respectability broke away from the MSI. In 1956, Pino Rauti and others left to found Ordine Nuovo, and in 1960 Stefano Delle Chiaie established the National Vanguard.

Formed in 1946 by supporters of Benito Mussolini, including many from the Italian Social Republic and the Republican Fascist Party, the Italian Social Movement (MSI) emerged as a postwar fascist successor party. It rose to become Italy’s fourth-largest political force by the early 1960s. The MSI provided informal local and later national backing to the Christian Democracy party from the late 1940s through the 1950s, sharing an anti-communist stance. In the early 1960s it was pushed to the sidelines, with gradual political recognition beginning in the 1980s. Internal competition between radical and moderate factions marked the party, with radicals led by Giorgio Almirante in its formative years and moderates gaining influence in the 1950s and 1960s. Almirante’s return as leader in 1969 featured a broad, inclusive big tent strategy.

The Tank watch, conceived by Louis Cartier, was introduced in 1919 and drew its inspiration from the tanks deployed on the Western Front during World War I. In the early 1920s, Cartier established a joint-stock company with Edward Jaeger (later Jaeger-LeCoultre) to manufacture movements exclusively for Cartier, while the maison continued to source movements from other premier firms such as Vacheron Constantin, Audemars Piguet, Movado, and LeCoultre. The company also began stamping a four-digit reference code on the underside of a lug to indicate its reference numbers. Jacques Cartier assumed leadership of Cartier's London operations, eventually relocating the office to the New Bond Street premises.

Cartier traces its origins to 1847, when Louis-François Cartier established a Paris workshop by taking over the studio of his master Adolphe Picard. In 1874, he passed the business to his son Alfred Cartier, who continued the family's involvement in the company. Alfred's sons—Louis, Pierre, and Jacques—then carried forward the enterprise and were instrumental in expanding its presence, helping to establish Cartier’s name on a global scale as a widely recognized jewelry brand.

The genre is characterized by an aggressive sonic and performative approach, with emphasis on simple, direct song forms. It draws on the vigorous rhythms associated with rock and roll, contributing to a confrontational and provocative image. As part of the broader contemporary music scene, it occupies a distinct position within modern music.

Music genre encompasses categories that can be defined in several ways, including broad polar distinctions such as popular music versus art or folk traditions, and religious versus secular distinctions. In modern practice, genre classification increasingly relies on derivative subgenres, fusion genres, and microgenres, with examples such as screamo, country pop, and mumble rap illustrating how boundaries become more fluid. These classifications are inherently subjective, frequently controversial, and can overlap, reflecting the evolving nature of musical practice. As new styles develop, they are often subsumed within existing categories rather than forming entirely new, independent labels.

Nguyễn Cao Kỳ received American backing for his leadership and for continuing the war against the communists, while Washington officials opposed Thiệu, deeming him less firm in pursuing anti-communist aims. Thiệu maintained the support of Marine Lieutenant General Lewis B. Walt, who commanded U.S. forces in I Corps and served as the senior adviser to Thiệu's ARVN forces; Walt's backing intensified tensions in the intra-regime dispute. The dismissal of a senior figure triggered widespread demonstrations in the northern provinces. Civil unrest widened as civil servants, disaffected military personnel, and the urban under-class joined anti-government protests led by Buddhist groups. Although Kỳ remained initially dismissive of the protests, riots broke out in several localities. Even with continued American backing, senior U.S. foreign policy officials judged Kỳ, Thiệu, and their regime to be of very poor quality, with Assistant Secretary of State William Bundy reportedly describing the administration as among the least capable in the eyes of American policymakers.

During the South Vietnamese leadership crisis, American policymakers favored removing Khánh but disapproved of Thảo and Phát. They urged General Nguyễn Cao Kỳ and General Nguyễn Văn Thi, the two most powerful officers outside Khánh, to thwart both sides. Kỳ was unofficially designated to serve as a moderator between the coup forces and Khánh's loyalists in order to avert bloodshed and keep the sides apart until further steps could be taken. In this capacity, Kỳ's actions slowed the advance of several Khánh-loyalist units into the capital. His position was strengthened by Khánh and his faction's mistaken belief that the Air Force commander supported them.

Under the Soviet constitutional framework, autonomous republics, autonomous oblasts, and autonomous okrugs could hold referendums if a union republic chose to secede, to decide whether they would stay within the USSR or depart with the seceding republic. They also possessed the capacity to independently determine their own state-legal status, free from central directives. This prerogative was provided by the Constitution of the Soviet Union.

Autonomous okrugs of Russia are a category of federal subjects of the Russian Federation and also serve as an administrative division type within certain federal subjects. They are sometimes referred to as autonomous districts or autonomous areas. As of 2024, Russia comprises four autonomous okrugs within its 83 federal subjects. The Chukotka Autonomous Okrug is not subordinate to an oblast. In contrast, the Nenets Autonomous Okrug is part of Arkhangelsk Oblast, while the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug and Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug are incorporated into Tyumen Oblast.

Receptor antagonists are agents that prevent receptor activation by endogenous ligands or exogenous agonists. Among them, non-competitive antagonists—also referred to as insurmountable antagonists—reduce the maximal responses that can be produced by any concentration of agonist and are not overcome by increasing agonist levels. They operate via two principal mechanisms: binding to an allosteric site on the receptor, which is termed allosteric antagonism, and irreversible occupancy of the receptor’s active site. Despite these distinct molecular actions, both produce a similar functional outcome: a lowered maximal effect in functional assays, with occasional rightward shifts of the concentration–response relationship. The rightward shift can reflect receptor reserve or spare receptors, such that inhibition becomes evident only after the reserve is depleted. By contrast, competitive antagonists diminish potency (increase EC50) without reducing the maximal response, whereas non-competitive antagonists diminish the Emax.

In receptor pharmacology, the term antagonist derives from the Greek ἀνταγωνιστής (antagonistēs), a word that historically denotes an opponent, rival, foe, or adversary. Its etymology is built from anti-, meaning against, and agonizesthai, meaning to contend for a prize, capturing the sense of opposition that the term conveys.

The 1941–42 Gauliga Donau-Alpenland season saw the addition of two clubs, Post SV Wien and SK Sturm Graz, to the top flight. In February 1942, Sturm Graz withdrew from the competition, yet the club nonetheless retained its place in the league for the ensuing season.

The 1941–42 Gauliga Donau-Alpenland was the fourth edition of the Gauliga Donau-Alpenland. The league had previously been known as the Gauliga Ostmark, reflecting its renaming in the context of the Austrian annexation. During the period from 1938 to 1945, the Gauliga Donau-Alpenland functioned as the top-tier football league in German-annexed Austria.

Professional wargaming is a practice in which analysts model potential military conflicts by incorporating assets not presently possessed by a nation's armed forces, examining possible alliances that are not yet formed, assessing weapons systems that have not yet been procured, and simulating technologies that do not yet exist.

Professional wargaming encompasses structured simulations that model armed conflict across multiple levels, from individual engagements and campaigns to entire wars, with the aim of analyzing capabilities, testing plans, and training decision-makers in a controlled environment. These exercises emphasize military and strategic dynamics, incorporating factors such as doctrine, logistics, and intelligence assessment. By contrast, business wargaming focuses on market competition and corporate strategy rather than military action, and therefore does not belong to the study of armed conflict. Consequently, business wargaming falls outside the scope of this article.

Bombhunters is a documentary project that included a Fulbright Scholarship for its participant(s). The endeavor was funded by the Sundance Institute and the United States Institute of Peace, with additional support consisting of grants from the Office of Weapons Removal and Abatement, which operates within the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Political-Military Affairs.

Bombhunters is a documentary film. The United States Department of State credits the work with influencing Cambodia's national legislation, and the enacted law is associated with a 50 percent reduction in casualties from tampering with unexploded ordnance. The observed change has occurred in Cambodia since the film's completion.

Within the Sustainable Development Goals framework, analyses have pointed to concerns about the means of implementation (MOI) component, noting that the empirical link between MOI and actual development outcomes is not clearly established. The MOI targets, including examples such as Target 6.a, are often regarded as inadequately conceptualized and not presented in a uniform or consistent manner across the goals. Consequently, measuring and monitoring the indicators associated with these targets presents substantial methodological and data-collection challenges, complicating assessments of the MOI provisions’ effectiveness within the agenda.

The Sustainable Development Goals articulate inclusivity as a central principle guiding actions at both national and global levels. At the national level, the framework concentrates on marginalised populations affected by exclusion and unequal outcomes, seeking to address barriers through inclusive governance, equitable access to services, and policies that reach disadvantaged groups. In the international sphere, inclusiveness extends to global governance, with particular attention to the least developed countries to ensure their needs and perspectives are incorporated into development planning and resource distribution. Together, these dual emphases aim to reduce disparities and foster sustainable development through coordinated efforts that span domestic policy and international cooperation.

Gao Ming was born and raised in Wenzhou, Zhejiang. In 1345, he passed the Imperial Examinations to support his widowed mother and was appointed as a minor district official in Zhejiang's Chouzhou. He served under the literary figure Su Tianjue, assisting in the editing of several of Su's works. From 1348 to 1351, he participated in the suppression of the Red Turban Rebellion, taking military action against the rebel Fang Guozhen. Following Fang Guozhen's defeat, Gao was appointed assessor of Shaoxing. Later, Fang Guozhen offered to employ him as a teacher, but Gao declined.

Gao Ming (高明; pinyin Gāo Míng; Wade–Giles Kao Ming) was a Chinese poet and playwright of the Yuan Dynasty, with a life span estimated to be circa 1305 to 1370. In addition to his primary name, he is known under several alternative names, including Kao Ming, Gao Zecheng, and the Cabbage Root Taoist.

Lunacloud has received favorable evaluations of both performance and cost from technology outlets TechWeekEurope, TechRepublic, and CloudSpectator. In their assessments, these outlets compare Lunacloud favorably with competing cloud services, notably Rackspace and Amazon EC2.

Lunacloud is a cloud computing company founded in 2011 by António Miguel Ferreira and Charles Nasser. It publicly launched its services on June 1, 2012, and provides infrastructure as a service (IaaS). Its offerings include cloud servers, cloud storage, and cloud hosting within its IaaS platform.

Parris Cues are a line of snooker cues that have been employed by several professional players. Notable users include Ronnie O'Sullivan, Jimmy White, Steve Davis, Stephen Hendry, Stephen Maguire, John Higgins, and Neil Robertson, demonstrating the brand's presence at the highest levels of the sport.

Parris Cues is a cue manufacturer based in Forest Hill, London, United Kingdom, where its products are produced in a dedicated workshop. The company markets its cues worldwide. In 1987, it undertook its first notable major repair when Steve Davis's cue fractured at the ferrule during the Rothmans Grand Prix. To preserve balance and playability, the repair extended the butt by the same amount that had been lost from the tip, a modification that required sawing the cue in two.
In 1977, Sir Hugh Casson established the Friends of the Royal Academy, a charitable organization whose purpose is to provide financial support for the Royal Academy of Arts.

The Royal Academy of Arts traces its origins to a founding charter signed by King George III on 10 December 1768, which established a body of 34 foundation members and permitted a total membership of 40. The 34 founder members included: Reynolds; John Baker; George Barret; Francesco Bartolozzi; Giovanni Battista Cipriani; Augustino Carlini; Charles Catton; Mason Chamberlin; William Chambers; Francis Cotes; George Dance; Nathaniel Dance; Thomas Gainsborough; John Gwynn; Francis Hayman; Nathaniel Hone the Elder; Angelica Kauffman; Jeremiah Meyer; George Michael Moser; Mary Moser; Francis Milner Newton; Edward Penny; John Inigo Richards; Paul Sandby; Thomas Sandby; Dominic Serres; Peter Toms; William Tyler; Samuel Wale; Benjamin West; Richard Wilson; Joseph Wilton; Richard Yeo; Francesco Zuccarelli. In 1769 the King further augmented the roster by adding William Hoare and Johann Zoffany.

Studio 2, a compact studio within the Television Centre in Newcastle upon Tyne, is used for secondary programming and magazine‑format productions. In its early operations, it shared equipment with other studios and the centre’s outside broadcast unit as a cost-saving measure. The studio is located in the building’s original structure.

Television Centre, Newcastle upon Tyne, previously served as the base for Tyne Tees operations, with the final broadcast from City Road on 1 July 2005 marking the last edition of North East Tonight, presented by Mike Neville in the City Road studios alongside Tyne Tees staff. The following day, 2 July 2005, the news department and playout relocated to Television House at The Watermark in Gateshead, a move that established a smaller, streamlined headquarters for Tyne Tees. These facilities later became home to ITV SignPost and ITV Border, following the 2009 merger that formed ITV Tyne Tees & Border.

The Phalanx CIWS (pronounced “sea-wiz”) is a close-in weapon system designed to defend naval platforms against aircraft and anti-ship missiles, with the capability to engage surface targets as well. It comprises a radar-guided 20 mm six-barreled M61 Vulcan cannon mounted on a swiveling base. The system is installed on the Coast Guard’s National Security Cutters. It can operate autonomously against airborne threats or be manually operated using an electronic optical sight, laser rangefinder, and forward-looking infrared (FLIR) for surface-target engagements.

The United States Coast Guard operates the National Response Center (NRC), which serves as the federal government’s sole point of contact for reporting all oil, chemical, radiological, biological, and etiological spills or discharges within the United States and its territories. The NRC collects and distributes spill and incident information for Federal On-Scene Coordinators and functions as the communications and operations center for the National Response Team. It maintains formal agreements with a range of federal entities to provide additional notifications for incidents that meet established trigger criteria, and it also accepts Maritime Suspicious Activity Reports and Security Breach Reports. The organization and responsibilities of the NRC are detailed in the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan. Additionally, the MISLE database is managed by the Coast Guard to track pollution and safety incidents in the nation’s ports.

Inside Pena Palace, the interiors were adapted for use as the Portuguese royal family's summer residence, reflecting the palace's function as a seasonal retreat. Notable decorative features include intricate stucco work, walls adorned with trompe-l'œil effects, and revetments of 19th-century ceramic tiles. Collectively, these elements remain part of the royal collections, underscoring the palace's continued connection to the monarchy.

Pena Palace is situated on the site of a former monastery in Sintra. During the eighteenth century the monastery endured severe damage from a lightning strike, but the most extensive destruction came with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, which reduced the complex to ruins. The chapel, along with its marble and alabaster works attributed to Nicolau Chanterene, escaped major damage, preserving important artworks within the largely ruined fabric.

Vapour pressure of water denotes the pressure exerted by water vapour in the gas phase, whether in pure form or in admixture with other gases such as air. The saturation vapour pressure is the equilibrium pressure at which water vapour is in thermodynamic balance with its condensed phases. If the surrounding pressure exceeds this saturation value, condensation occurs; if it is below, evaporation or sublimation takes place. Saturation vapour pressure rises with increasing temperature. It can be described or predicted by the Clausius–Clapeyron relation. The boiling point is defined as the temperature at which the saturated vapour pressure equals the ambient pressure. Additionally, water that is supercooled below its normal freezing point possesses a higher vapour pressure than ice at the same temperature, and such a state is unstable.

Alduchov and Eskridge (1996) provide a detailed discussion of the accuracy and limitations of temperature measurements relevant to vapor-pressure analyses. At 100 °C, the simple unattributed formula and the Antoine equation yield reasonably accurate results, but both perform poorly at lower temperatures just above freezing. Tetens’ formulations are considerably more accurate from 0 to 50 °C and remain competitive at about 75 °C, whereas Antoine’s equation becomes superior to Tetens at around 75 °C and above. The unattributed formula is designed to have near-zero error near 26 °C, yet its performance deteriorates markedly outside a narrow temperature range. In meteorological contexts, Tetens’ equations are generally more accurate and easier to apply for everyday temperatures. Buck’s equation for temperatures above 0 °C offers substantially greater accuracy than Tetens, with its advantage increasing beyond 50 °C, albeit at the cost of greater complexity. Compared with the Goff–Gratch equation, Buck provides better performance within the temperature ranges relevant to practical meteorology.

Following World War II, French authorities pursued a policy of conciliating Lao nationalist groups. Discreet contacts with the Lao Issara leaders in Bangkok suggested that clemency or amnesty might be offered. The overtures reflected a strategy to quell hostilities and secure regional stability through political accommodation rather than continued armed struggle. Within the Lao Issara, internal divisions widened over the question of collaborating with the French, revealing contrasting views and strategies among its members.

Lao Issara, the short-lived anti-French government established in Laos after World War II, encountered severe financial strain as military maintenance proved costly and Souphanouvong reportedly refused to account for those expenditures. The administration soon exhausted its funds and was unable to cover its running costs, prompting Finance Minister Katay Don Sasorith to issue a new currency in early 1946 in an attempt to curb expenditure and inflation. The banknotes, infamously nicknamed “Katay’s dried banana leaves” for their poor paper quality and perceived indefensibility, underscored the regime’s precarious financial position. By that stage Lao Issara was effectively bankrupt and ill-equipped, awaiting the French return. In late April 1946 French forces seized Vientiane, and by May they advanced into Luang Prabang, after which Lao Issara leadership fled into exile in Thailand.

On 15 February 2019, Axiata sold its entire stake in M1 to Konnectivity Pte. Ltd. for RM1.65 billion. The divestment was undertaken to reallocate capital and pursue new priorities, aligning with the group’s strategic objective of becoming the Next Generation Digital Champion by 2022.

Axiata's operations in Indonesia are led by Telkomsel as its primary competitor, and in 2019 the group was ranked second in the Indonesian market. In Bangladesh, Axiata operates the Robi network, which likewise finished second in its market behind Grameenphone, the Bangladeshi unit of Telenor.

Hybrid heat systems respond to changes in temperature by automatically selecting the most efficient method to heat or cool the home. Through an integrated control, they switch between a heat pump and a furnace depending on current conditions, optimizing energy use while maintaining comfort. The configuration requires a furnace paired with a heat pump.

Hybrid heat refers to a system that combines a heat pump with a conventional furnace to improve energy efficiency. The heat pump operates by moving heat rather than producing it through burning fuel, which reduces electricity consumption. As a result, such configurations can lower electricity use by as much as 40% compared with standard electric heating. An example cited is pairing the heat pump with a gas furnace, illustrating a fuel-fired option used in hybrid setups.

The Community of the Hungarian Religion (Magyar Vallás Közössége) traces its intellectual lineage to 19th‑century scholarship arguing that Hungarian and Sumerian share a Turanian origin. In the 1930s, Zoltán Bencsi founded the Turanian Monotheist Movement on the basis of these ideas. The organization was banned by Miklós Horthy’s government, prompting some members to seek refuge abroad. In the 1960s, Ótto János Homonnay moved to Canada and established the Hungarian Turul Society to promote Turanist theses. After Homonnay’s death in 1979, leadership passed to János Páll. The movement eventually split, producing a new group led by Albin István Zalezsák, who authored ISA-TEN TAN (Magyar Isme), published in Toronto in 1986.

Within the Hungarian Native Faith movement, two central mythopoetic texts establish two parallel doctrinal streams: Arvisura, authored by Zoltán Paál, and Yotengrit, a four-volume collection by Imre Máté. The mythic themes drawn from these works have been adapted into other media, most notably in the 2010 animated feature Sons of Heaven (Az Ég fiai). A further long-form animation influenced by these narratives—based on ethnographic and historical material framed within the Uralic paradigm and funded by government support—appears as Song of the Miraculous Hind (Ének a csodaszarvasról), released in 2002.

Carte Jaune refers to the international vaccination certificate system established under World Health Organization auspices. On 25 May 1951, the Fourth World Health Assembly adopted the International Sanitary Regulations (WHO Regulations No. 2), thereby replacing the earlier International Sanitary Conventions. The Regulations affirmed the validity and use of international certificates of vaccination (Article 115) and updated the existing model with a revised version (Appendices 2, 3, and 4). The certificates served as proof of vaccination against diseases such as cholera, yellow fever, and smallpox, with the term inoculation no longer used. The old International Certificates of Inoculation and Vaccination remained valid until they expired, after which they were replaced by the new International Certificate of Vaccination or Revaccination (ICV). Additionally, on 23 May 1956 the Ninth World Health Assembly amended the form of the International Certificate of Vaccination or Revaccination against Smallpox, with the changes becoming effective on 1 October 1956.

Carte Jaune refers to a form designed to accommodate supplementary information as necessary. In 2007, the World Health Organization prepared a booklet related to this form, and the booklet itself incorporated additional sections to expand on the material.
Hoeyang County is a county-level division (kun) in Kangwŏn Province, North Korea. It was formed in 1952 as part of a broad reorganization of local government structures.

Hoeyang County is largely mountainous, with the Taebaek and Kwangju mountain ranges passing through the area. The rugged topography is interrupted by two basins, namely the Hoeyang Basin and the Changdo Basin. The highest point is Piryubong, located on Kŭmgangsan. The principal local stream is the Pukhan River, which flows southward and eastward into South Korea. The region experiences a continental climate, with winters that are extremely cold.

Piero della Francesca signed a contract in 1454 to execute the Polyptych of Saint Augustine for the church of Sant'Agostino in Sansepolcro. The central panel has not survived, while the four wing panels depicting saints have been dispersed to collections around the world. A few years later he was summoned by Pope Nicholas V and moved to Rome, where he painted frescoes in the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, of which only fragments remain. Two years thereafter, still in Rome, he produced additional frescoes in the Vatican Palace; these works have since been destroyed.

Piero della Francesca's Double Portrait of Federico da Montefeltro and Battista Sforza was executed in Urbino and is now housed in the Uffizi Gallery. The two figures are presented in profile and the composition draws on the tradition of large bronze medals and stucco roundels that depicted the couple in official likenesses. Among his other Urbino works are the Montefeltro Altarpiece (1474), which is in the Brera Gallery in Milan, and the Madonna of Senigallia, also produced during his Urbino period.

Manuscripts from the classical period through the early Christian era were typically written without spaces between words, a practice known as scriptio continua, which makes reading difficult for those not trained in the convention. Among surviving Greek and Latin manuscripts dating roughly from the 4th to the 8th century, texts are classified by letter case as either entirely majuscule (uppercase) or entirely minuscule (lowercase). Hebrew manuscripts, exemplified by the Dead Sea Scrolls, do not use case distinctions. Majuscule scripts, such as uncial, are generally produced with greater care, and scribes often lifted the pen between strokes to produce a regular and formal appearance; by contrast, minuscule writing can be executed with varying degrees of pen-lift, ranging from neatly separated forms to more cursive styles with little or no interruption between strokes.

Many manuscripts preserved in antiquity’s libraries have been lost, leaving a record that is heavily biased toward a small subset of works. Papyrus, the common writing material in earlier periods, deteriorates relatively quickly in humid climates typical of Italy and the Greek world, generally lasting only a century or two. Consequently, the texts that have survived are predominantly those copied onto parchment, and even among these copies not all have endured. Thus, the extant parchment manuscript record is incomplete. In addition, the surviving parchment copies predominantly date from after Christianity’s broad conversion, which introduces a temporal bias into the surviving corpus.

John Betjeman cultivated an interest in the ghost stories of M. R. James, going so far as to write the introduction to Peter Haining's collection M. R. James – Book of the Supernatural. He was described as a person who was receptive to supernatural phenomena, a trait noted by contemporaries. Diana Mitford recalled Betjeman staying at Biddesden House in Wiltshire during the 1920s, and she related a terrifying dream he had, in which a card edged by broad black borders bore his name and a date that he understood to be the date of his death.

Betjeman cultivated the misapprehension that his degree remained incomplete because he failed the compulsory Divinity examination, a holy scriptures assessment. In Hilary term 1928, he failed Divinity for the second time. He left the university during Trinity term to prepare for a retake and was permitted to return in October. He wrote to G. C. Lee, secretary of the Tutorial Board at Magdalen College, requesting entry for the Pass School, a pathway for undergraduates unlikely to achieve honours. In Summoned by Bells, Betjeman recounts that his tutor C. S. Lewis allegedly remarked that he would have only attained a third, though Betjeman had informed the tutorial board that he did not expect to obtain honours in any class.

During World War II, the Ellice Islands, including Funafuti, were a British colonial possession aligned with the Allies. Japan occupied several of the Gilbert Islands, including Makin and Tarawa, in territory that is now part of Kiribati. The United States Marine Corps landed on Funafuti on 2 October 1942, followed by additional landings on Nanumea and Nukufetau in August 1943. Funafuti subsequently served as a base to support and stage seaborne operations against the Japanese-held Gilbert Islands.

In Tuvalu, measurements of sea level changes relative to its islands have been contentious. The pre-1993 Funafuti sea level records were plagued by measurement problems, prompting improvements in recording technology to enhance reliability. By 2002, assessments acknowledged considerable uncertainty in estimates of sea-level change due to data limitations. To enhance data accuracy, a modern Aquatrak acoustic gauge was installed in 1993 by the Australian National Tidal Facility as part of the AusAID-sponsored South Pacific Sea Level and Climate Monitoring Project.
