A 2011 report from the Pacific Climate Change Science Program indicates that satellite altimeters have measured about 5 millimeters per year (roughly 0.2 inches per year) of sea-level rise near Tuvalu since 1993.

The Dominican Republic national under-23 football team represents the country in international under-23 competitions, including official tournaments and friendly matches. It began its CONCACAF Olympic qualifying campaign in 2020, though the qualifying event was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ultimately held in March 2021, where the U23 side finished last in its group. In parallel, the Dominican Republic’s under-20 team advanced to the final of the 2022 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, a result that earned the nation a berth at the 2024 Summer Olympics—the first Olympic appearance in its history.

Within autonomous buildings, septic tanks require periodic pumping with a vacuum truck to remove accumulated solids that cannot be digested. If pumping is neglected, effluent can overflow the tank, damaging the leach field and contaminating groundwater. Maintenance may necessitate lifestyle adjustments, such as avoiding garbage disposals, limiting the volume of wastewater entering the system, and minimizing non-digestible solids flushed into the tank, with septic-safe toilet paper often recommended as an example. Nevertheless, septic systems remain a popular option because they support standard plumbing fixtures and typically impose only modest changes to daily routines.

Autonomous buildings may employ nocturnal cooling by lowering the thermal mass temperature at night to provide cooling during the following day. This approach often uses a whole-house fan to reduce the thermal mass temperature by exchanging indoor air with cooler night air. Cold air can be routed from a sky-facing radiator or an evaporative cooler directly through the thermal mass, enabling heat transfer that cools the structure for daytime comfort. Sky-facing radiators have the capacity to drive air temperatures below freezing on clear nights, even in tropical regions, thereby enhancing the cooling potential of the mass. A sky-facing radiator may take the form of a repurposed air-heating solar collector, adapted to supply cool air through the mass rather than heat it.

Bream is a common name applied to several species of freshwater fish. They span a broad set of genera, notably the genus Abramis, which includes Abramis brama, the common bream; other genera associated with the term include Ballerus, Blicca, Brama, Chilotilapia, Etelis, Lepomis, Gymnocranius, Lethrinus, Nemipterus, Pharyngochromis, Rhabdosargus, Scolopsis, and Serranochromis.

Bream, sometimes termed sea bream, is a broad common name used for various fish, chiefly within the Sparidae family. The designation covers several genera, including Acanthopagrus, which is represented in Australian waters, and Argyrops. Among Sparidae, the gilt-head bream, scientifically identified as Sparus aurata, is known locally in Italy as orata and in Spain as dorada. The term also extends to the black seabream, Spondyliosoma cantharus, and to red seabreams placed in the Pagrus or Pagellus lineages. In some usages, sea bream may also refer to certain pomfrets, which belong to the Bramidae family.

Cascade, Iowa, according to the 2020 United States Census, had a population of 2,386, with 970 households and 630 families residing in the city. The population density was 1,242.3 people per square mile (479.6 per square kilometer), and there were 1,050 housing units at a density of 546.7 per square mile (211.1 per square kilometer). The racial makeup was 95.3% White, 0.3% Black or African American, 0.0% Native American, 0.3% Asian, 0.1% Pacific Islander, 1.7% from other races, and 2.3% from two or more races, with Hispanic or Latino residents of any race accounting for 3.4% of the population.

Cascade is a city in the U.S. state of Iowa. It has a total area of 1.87 square miles (4.84 square kilometers), all of which is land, with no water within its boundaries. The North Fork Maquoketa River passes through Cascade, contributing to its geographic setting.

The imperial examination system operated with a range of official and informal restrictions on eligibility, evolving across dynasties. Commoners were categorized by occupation into four orders—scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants—while those regarded as socially inferior, often grouped as the “mean people” and including boat-people, beggars, sex workers, entertainers, slaves, and low-level government employees, faced discrimination and were frequently barred from government office and from taking the exams. Certain ethnic groups or castes, such as the degraded Jin dynasty outcasts in Ningbo (about three thousand people), were explicitly prohibited from participating in examinations. Women were excluded entirely, and at times other groups such as butchers and sorcerers were likewise barred. Merchants were barred from the exams until the Ming and Qing eras, though scholar-officials engaged in trade already as early as 955; earlier dynasties such as Sui and Tang restricted artisans from official service. In the Song dynasty, artisans, merchants, clerks, and Buddhist or Taoist priests were forbidden from the jinshi examination, while the Liao dynasty prohibited physicians, diviners, butchers, and merchants from taking the tests (as noted in Liao-shih). Additionally, quota systems were employed at times to limit the number of candidates by region or other criteria.

During the Song dynasty, Emperor Zhenzong established formal quotas limiting the number of degrees awarded through the imperial examination in 1009. By 1090, the city of Fuzhou granted only 40 degrees to 3,000 examinees, roughly one degree for every 75 candidates. In the 13th century, the quota system grew more stringent, with only about 1% of candidates permitted to pass the prefectural examination. Even graduates of the lowest tier of examinations were regarded as members of an elite scholarly class.

Excavations and surveys at Citânia de Briteiros were conducted by archaeologist Francisco Sande Lemos. In 2006, Sociedade Martins Sarmento (UAM) proposed the creation of a protohistoric biological estate to serve as an interpretive centre aimed at revitalizing the site. Stratigraphic layers indicate human occupation predating the reorganization of the urban space. During the period between October and November, a secondary bath was uncovered near the EN 306 roadway.

Citânia de Briteiros is an archaeological site associated with the Castro culture in northern Portugal. It is located in the civil parish of Briteiros São Salvador e Briteiros Santa Leocádia, in the municipality of Guimarães. The site is notable for its substantial size, urban-like layout, and advanced architectural remains, making it one of the most extensively excavated sites in the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It is primarily understood as the remains of an Iron Age proto-urban hill fort (oppidum). Excavations have revealed a long sequence of occupation, spanning from the Bronze Age through the Middle Ages.

The guzheng is a traditional Chinese plucked string instrument whose strings can be made from a range of materials, including nylon, steel, and silk, with the chosen material often reflecting the performer’s genre and tonal preference. The most common form of the instrument today typically features 21 strings. On standard guzhengs, the higher-pitched strings are located toward the player's side, while the lower-pitched strings extend to the opposite end, creating a clear pitch gradient across the instrument. For reference, the strings are numbered from the innermost to the outermost, with numbers 1 through 21.

Guzheng, a traditional Chinese plucked instrument, shows distinct regional repertoires and techniques. According to Mei Han, Hakka melodies resemble Chaozhou styles yet are less embellished. In Chaozhou music, descending notes are minimized, and glissando is performed in a free rhythmic context. Chaozhou pieces also feature irregular beats and alternate between hard and soft string taps. Zhejiang repertoire incorporates techniques similar to those used on the pipa. Tremolo is frequently used, often in conjunction with left-hand glissando. The sidian technique involves rapidly executing sixteenth notes with the thumb, index finger, and middle finger.

In the Middle Ages, the term artisan referred to individuals who produced goods or offered skilled services, and it did not encompass unskilled manual laborers. Within this category, a distinction emerged between those who operated their own workshops or businesses and those who did not; the former were known as masters, while the latter consisted of journeymen and apprentices who did not run independent enterprises.

The term artisanal denotes production that relies on manual or small-scale processing as opposed to large-scale industrial methods, a distinction that is evident in examples such as artisanal mining. In marketing, it is frequently employed as a buzzword intended to convey handmade craftsmanship. It is commonly associated with products like bread, beverages, cheese, and textiles, reflecting historical patterns in which such goods were produced in rural or pastoral settings. In contemporary practice, many so-called artisanal items are now manufactured at larger scales within factories and industrial zones through automated technologies, yet the label continues to imply a connection to traditional craftsmanship even when production has expanded.

The 2025 Lithuanian Football Cup retains the format of the previous edition, excludes B teams, and has A Lyga clubs entering in the second round. The competition comprises 50 participants: ten A Lyga clubs, eleven LFF I Lyga clubs, thirteen LFF II Lyga clubs, nine LFF III Lyga clubs, and nine SFL clubs.

The 2025 Lithuanian Football Cup is a single-elimination football competition held in Lithuania. For sponsorship purposes, the tournament is also known as the FPRO LFF Taurė. The champions earn a place in the first qualifying round of the 2026–27 UEFA Conference League, contingent on meeting sporting criteria and holding a valid UEFA licence. Banga were the defending cup holders.

Harpoon Block III was a planned upgrade package for the U.S. Navy's Harpoon Block 1C missiles and the Command Launch System (CLS), designed to enhance compatibility and capabilities across the service's platform set. The proposed upgrade targeted integration with guided-missile cruisers and destroyers, as well as air platforms such as the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet. The program was canceled by the U.S. Navy in April 2009, as a result of multiple factors including an expanded scope for government ship integration, broader testing and evaluation requirements, and delays in the development of the data-link needed to support the upgraded system.

Block 1J represented a proposed upgrade to the Harpoon missile family, including the A/R/UGM-84J Harpoon, and was commonly referred to as Harpoon 2000. The plan targeted capabilities against both surface ships and land targets, expanding the missile’s versatility. These proposed improvements were later incorporated into the development pathway that produced the Block II variant.

Born in Philadelphia, Mississippi, Derek George is an American country music singer, songwriter, and guitarist. He is signed to Spirit Music Group and is known for his work with the acts Pearl River and Williams Riley. George frequently collaborates with Bryan White.

Derek George contributed to the 1996 recording of the instrumental track "Brickyard Boogie" alongside White, Bryan Austin, and Jeffrey Steele. The piece appears on Steve Wariner's album No More Mr. Nice Guy, and it earned a nomination for Best Country Instrumental at the 1997 Grammy Awards.

In the New Testament, the Pharisees are depicted as prioritizing strict adherence to the law's letter over its underlying spirit, as illustrated in Mark 2:3–28 and 3:1–6. The term has since become a pejorative designation for a legalist or formalist, a usage noted by the Oxford English Dictionary. In Matthew 23:38 they are portrayed as lawless or corrupt; the Greek term employed denotes lawlessness, while the Hebrew suggests fraud or injustice. The name derives from the Hebrew root Perushim, meaning "separatists," reflecting an emphasis on spiritual concerns rather than worldly pleasures.

Within Luke 10:25–37, the Parable of the Good Samaritan appears during a dialogue in which Jesus confronts a Jewish legal expert who seeks to trap him. The examiner asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus answers by reframing the query, asking what is written in the law and implying that the questioner should already know the answer. The lawyer then cites the two central commandments—loving God with all one’s heart, soul, and strength, and loving one’s neighbor as oneself—drawn from Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18. In verse 29, the question of who counts as a neighbor is described as being asked to achieve self-justification. The parable has been used to address the article’s theme of gaming the system, illustrating how narrow interpretations of obligation can be challenged by a broader, more compassionate understanding of neighborly duty.

Bonner Springs, Kansas, as reported in the 2020 census, had 7,837 residents, 3,037 households, and 2,065 families. The population density was 501.4 people per square mile (193.6/km2). The city contained 3,202 housing units, with a housing density of 204.9 per square mile (79.1/km2). The racial composition was White or European American at 76.2% (5,972), including 72.78% non-Hispanic white; Black or African-American 6.7% (525); Native American or Alaska Native 1.07% (84); Asian 0.74% (58); Pacific Islander or Native Hawaiian 0.18% (14); Other races 3.79% (297); and two or more races 11.32% (887). Hispanic or Latino of any race accounted for 13.18% (1,033) of residents.

Bonner Springs experienced a period of growth and economic vitality in the early 20th century, marked by a rising population and the opening of new businesses. In 1908, a major fire caused damages totaling more than $70,000, which is equivalent to about $2.45 million in 2024 dollars, and it destroyed between nineteen and twenty-one local enterprises. The catastrophe highlighted an ongoing deficiency in public utilities, as the town had no water mains at the time, despite the city council having debated the issue for several years.

Out of Exile, Audioslave's second studio album, was released internationally on May 23, 2005, with a U.S. release following on May 24, 2005. It debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, the only Audioslave album to achieve the top position. In the subsequent week it fell to number three as sales declined by about 62 percent, and it later earned Platinum certification. Lyrically, Chris Cornell wrote some of his most personal songs for the record, reflecting positive life changes since 2002. The album has been described as more varied in its musical approach than the band's debut and less dependent on heavy guitar riffs.

Work on a new Audioslave album began in 2003 during the Lollapalooza tour and continued later that year in the studio. In addition to new material, the sessions yielded leftover tracks, with Tom Morello stating that nearly another album's worth of material had already been completed. The lead single from the then-untitled project was "Be Yourself." While some critics criticized the track as limp with directionless lyrics, it nevertheless reached number one on both the Mainstream Rock and Modern Rock charts.

Parthian was written using the Pahlavi writing system, a script that traces its origins to Aramaic, specifically Imperial Aramaic—the script historically employed by the Achaemenid chancellery. The Pahlavi script contains a high incidence of Aramaic vocabulary, with many Aramaic words rendered as logograms or ideograms; nevertheless, these signs are read according to Parthian pronunciation rather than their original Aramaic values.

Parthian distinguishes itself from Middle Persian in a number of pronoun and verb-form features. The language uses the first-person singular pronoun az, meaning "I," rather than the MP form an. For the verb “to do,” the present tense root in Parthian is kar- (originating from kardan), in contrast to the MP kun- found in Middle Persian. Parthian also lacks the Middle Persian linking particle and the relative pronoun i(g) (ī(g)). Instead, it employs the relative pronoun čē “what,” which is used in a manner similar to MP’s i(g).

MEA restructured its frequent-flyer program in 2011 by introducing four tiers—Blue Cedar, Silver Cedar, Golden Cedar, and President's Club—as part of preparations for joining SkyTeam. The tiers are arranged from Blue Cedar, the entry level, up to President's Club, the highest. Members in Silver Cedar, Golden Cedar, and President's Club gain access to the Cedar Lounge at Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport, as well as to outstation lounges at MEA destinations across its network. In addition, Golden Cedar and President's Club include guaranteed economy-seat reservations on eligible flights.

In November 1965 MEA adopted its current name following its merger with Air Liban. The airline's operations were interrupted by the 1967 Arab–Israeli War, and were interrupted again by the Israeli raid on Beirut Airport in 1968, during which MEA lost three Comet 4Cs, two Caravelles, a Boeing 707, a Vickers VC10, and a Vickers Viscount. The carrier restarted operations by acquiring a Convair 990A from American Airlines, which entered service on 24 June 1969.

Adolphe Nicole's keyless winding mechanism, which would become widely adopted in the mid‑19th century, was granted a London patent in 1844 (UK Patent No. 10348). Around 1846, the rights to Nicole's system were acquired by E. J. Dent & Co., according to notes preserved by the British Museum. Consequently, a substantial number of watches from the period bearing the Dent signature incorporated Nicole's mechanism. Auction records have documented early Dent keyless pieces dating to the 1840s, attesting to the swift adoption and commercial use of the invention.

Digital watch technology advanced rapidly during the 1980s, with several landmark developments illustrating the trend. In 1982, Seiko released the TV Watch, which integrated a small television display into the wrist device, while Casio introduced the TS-1000, a digital watch equipped with a thermometer, and another Casio model capable of translating roughly 1,500 Japanese words into English. The 1985 release of Casio's CFX-400 added scientific calculator functionality to a wristwatch. Two years later, Casio unveiled the DBA-800, a model capable of dialing telephone numbers, and a Citizen watch demonstrated the ability to respond to voice input. In 1995, Timex introduced a watch that could download and store data from a computer to the wrist, and subsequent Timex Datalink models adopted USB connectivity and dot-matrix display technology. After the apex of this period, spanning the late 1980s to the mid-1990s, digital watches generally became simpler, more affordable, and less varied between different models.

Recreational use of the Kansas River includes fishing, canoeing, kayaking, and rowing. The river features eighteen public access points along its course. The Friends of the Kaw organization coordinates numerous float trips annually and conducts cleanup activities to maintain the waterway. The Lawrence KOA campground provides canoe rentals for self-guided excursions. Rowing is also a regular activity, with the University of Kansas rowing team training in the pool upstream of the Bowersock Dam, while crews from the Kansas City Boat Club and the University of Missouri-Kansas City compete in the downstream stretches near the river’s mouth and its connection to the Missouri River.

At the mouth of the Kansas River, where it enters the Missouri River at West Bottoms in Kansas City, the longitude is 94°36′ W, a line that formed Missouri’s western boundary from Iowa to Arkansas when Missouri gained statehood in 1821. Today, the segment of that boundary lying south of the Missouri River remains the Kansas–Missouri boundary, while to the north Missouri extended its western limit in 1836 with the Platte Purchase. Although the Kansas River boundary has shifted slightly since its designation, the overarching boundary line has remained in place and is commonly known as the Osage Boundary.

By October 1992, KRCW-TV maintained operations at facilities in both Salem and Beaverton, with management seeking to consolidate its operations in Beaverton. On October 12, 1992, KEBN temporarily ceased broadcasting to conserve funds during the move, a suspension expected to last two to four weeks. At that time, the station was also behind on payments for its tower lease. By late 1993, a receiver had been appointed for the licensee, Willamette Valley Broadcasting, Ltd.

Under Nexstar Media Group, which owns KOIN, the Portland CBS affiliate, KRCW was integrated into KOIN’s operations. On September 19, 2019, KOIN began producing KRCW’s 10 p.m. newscast, taking over from KGW after nearly fourteen years. In October 2019, the late-evening newscast was expanded from thirty to sixty minutes and a weekly sports highlights program, Game On!, was introduced. In early 2020, KRCW relocated its main studio from Beaverton to the KOIN Tower, aligning its facilities with KOIN. By 2022, the station added a morning news extension, pushing the schedule to run from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m.

Vasil Mzhavanadze's ascent within the Soviet party apparatus was closely linked to Nikita Khrushchev's leadership. In September 1962 he resisted Khrushchev's proposal to subdivide local party organizations into two sectors with separate first secretaries for industry and agriculture, though by November 1962 he publicly voiced full support for the reorganization. After Khrushchev's fall, in March 1965 Mzhavanadze asserted that he had discussed with numerous Central Committee members who had informed Khrushchev that the plan would be unworkable. He was among a small circle of high-ranking officials who were aware in advance that Khrushchev would be ousted, a development that occurred in October 1964.

Vasil Mzhavanadze was born in Kutaisi and left school at the age of twelve to work in a factory for ten years. He joined the Red Army in 1924 and became a member of the Communist Party in 1927, later graduating from the Leningrad Military-Political Academy. For the next twenty-nine years he had no record of holding any office in Georgia. During World War II he served as a political commissar, and after the war he was appointed deputy commander for political affairs in the Kiev military district of the Ukrainian SSR, where he served under Nikita Khrushchev, who would later become leader of the Soviet Union.

Original intent is a theory of legal interpretation that centers on identifying the framers’ intended meaning at the time of enactment for constitutional provisions and statutes. Although it is often treated as synonymous with originalism, it represents a distinct strand within the originalist family, marked by differences from other originalist theories. These distinctions have prompted some originalists, including adherents from more influential schools such as original meaning, to articulate a separate category for original intent and to treat it as distinct from other forms of originalism in a manner comparable to how legal realists differentiate different positions.

Original intent is the idea that the convention might have possessed a single, unified aim; however, after two centuries it remains unclear how one could reliably ascertain that aim. Nevertheless, it is often possible to conclude that a proposed interpretation conflicts with the original aims, even when the exact aim remains unknown.

The government asserted that it had maintained close surveillance of the Soviet military buildup in Cuba. In the past week, there has been clear evidence that offensive missile sites were being prepared on the island. The stated aim of these installations was to provide a nuclear-strike capability against targets in the Western Hemisphere.

Strategy is the deliberate process by which an organization defines its aims and prioritizes among competing objectives, recognizing that available resources are typically limited. It encompasses selecting the goals to pursue, determining the actions required to reach them, and aligning or marshaling the necessary resources to carry out those actions. A strategy articulates how the intended ends will be achieved through the use of the available means. Strategies may be formulated intentionally through planning, or they may emerge as recurring patterns of activity as the organization adapts to its environment or competes in its arena. Core strategic activities include strategic planning and strategic thinking, which together help guide decision making and resource allocation.

Following her success in Brazil, Xuxa released her first Spanish-language album, Xuxa 1, which found particular success in Argentina. She then broadened her appeal to Spanish-speaking audiences with an adapted version of Xou da Xuxa, titled El Show de Xuxa. The Los Angeles Times reported in 1992 that more than 20 million Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking children watched El Show de Xuxa each day across 16 Latin American countries, in addition to its presence on Univision in the United States. The program’s production proceeded with the first two seasons produced by Telefé, Argentina’s leading television network, while the 1993 third season was produced independently in Buenos Aires and sold to El Trece. The final Spanish-language edition of the show aired in Latin America on December 31, 1993.

Xuxa expanded her international media presence in 1993 with the premiere of an English-language program in the United States, which aired on more than a hundred stations, including CBS and Freeform, and was distributed to more than 120 countries. The program generated about $7 million in licensing revenue for Xuxa and supported the launch of products in more than 100 markets. To rest between recording sessions, she purchased a home in Calabasas, California; that residence was later bought by Brandy Norwood in September 1999 for $1.7 million. In 1993, Xuxa's licensing activities yielded roughly $220 million, but by the end of the year a spinal problem slowed her work. The following year, the death of Ayrton Senna contributed to a gradual decrease in her workload. Later in 1994, she acquired a Star Island mansion in Miami for $15 million, a property previously owned by Madonna. The Star Island residence is included in the Rich and Famous Tour script, and in present-day terms its minimum asking price is about $65 million.

Within the Leased Territory of Guangzhouwwan, French authorities established a number of institutions, including the French-language school École Franco-Chinoise de Kouang-Tchéou-Wan and a French bank, the Bank of Indochina. Additional institutions were founded to support administration and community life in the enclave. The Church of St. Victor remains an extant example of these colonial-era establishments.

Guangzhouwan was a coastal territorial possession in Guangdong Province, China, leased to France and administered by French Indochina. Its formal designation in French was Territoire de Kouang-Tchéou-Wan. In English, it was historically known as Kwangchowan or Kwangchow Wan. The territory’s capital was Fort Bayard, located at present-day Zhanjiang.

An Archimedes' screw, in industrial contexts commonly known as a screw conveyor, moves bulk materials by rotating a helical screw within a containment tube, drawing material from one end and discharging it at the other when powered by a motor. The arrangement is well suited to handling granular substances, including plastic granules used in injection molding, though it can also be employed to convey liquids under appropriate conditions. In process-control applications, the device can function as a rotary feeder or a variable-rate feeder, delivering a precisely measured amount of material into a process.

Certain variants of the Archimedes' screw are built so that the helical screw is permanently fused to the surrounding casing, forming a single rotating assembly. In these designs, the screw and the casing rotate together, rather than the screw turning within a stationary housing. To seal the interface between the two components, practitioners may apply pitch resin or other adhesives. An alternative manufacturing approach is to cast the screw and casing as a single bronze piece, yielding an integrated unit.

From 1684 onward, settlers from southern Fujian established the earliest Han Chinese settlements near Pingtung. By 1734, much of the Pingtung Plain had been brought under cultivation, reflecting intensified agricultural use. In 1764, the locality experienced expansion, broadening its settled area. Then, in 1836, the government in conjunction with local inhabitants completed the construction of the city’s four gates—North, East, West, and South—and finished the accompanying road network, signaling a formal urban framework.

Pingtung County’s name is traditionally interpreted as denoting the area east of Banping Mountain, a nearby peak. Banping Mountain is known in Chinese as 半屏山, and in the Pe̍h-ōe-jī romanization it is rendered as Pòaⁿ-pêng-soaⁿ.
Afro-Omanis maintain healing rituals that derive from Zanj traditions. These ceremonies are conducted in Swahili and Arabic, illustrating the blend of languages and cultures within the community.

Afro-Omanis are persons in Oman who descend from enslaved Africans, who were transported to the region primarily via Indian Ocean slave networks and the Zanzibar slave trade along the Swahili coast. The community’s historical experience intersects with Oman’s political changes of the late 20th century, notably the 23 July 1970 coup in which Sultan Said bin Taimur was overthrown and his son, Qaboos bin Said, succeeded him. Under Qaboos, Oman embarked on a program of reforms, including the abolition of slavery, which altered the legal status and social integration of Afro-Omani populations.

The 2022–23 LPB season was the 90th edition of Portugal's premier basketball league. Known commercially as Liga Betclic for sponsorship purposes, it marked the 15th season under the contemporary Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol format. The campaign commenced on 24 September 2022 with the regular season and concluded on 11 June 2023 with the final.

Released in 1998, the compilation Everything! gathers the complete catalog of Tones on Tail’s tracks. The recordings have been remastered for the release, and the package also includes a radio interview featuring Daniel Ash and Kevin Haskins.

Tones on Tail released its debut self-titled EP on 4AD in March 1982, followed by the single "There's Only One!" issued by Beggars Banquet Records on 24 September. In the band's lineup, Ash provided vocals and guitar while Campling played bass, with both musicians also handling percussion and keyboards. After Bauhaus dissolved in 1983, Ash and Campling were joined by Bauhaus drummer Kevin Haskins, forming a three-member lineup. The first release as a trio was the Burning Skies EP, issued by Situation Two on 6 May 1983.

An identifier is a label used to distinguish an individual, and a single person may be recognized by multiple identifiers in different contexts. These include variants of the full name, ranging from a long, multi-part rendition to shortened forms that employ initials or a condensed given-name and surname. In addition, common name forms and nicknames are frequently used. Generational distinctions may appear via qualifiers that indicate a younger or older namesake. Relational descriptors identify family roles, such as Aunt, Mom, Grandmom, Nana, or kin-related references like Kelly's mother or Billy's grandmother. Professional designations and titles also serve as identifiers, including courtesy titles and credentials such as Ms., Dr., or a doctoral degree.

An identifier is a designation that serves to identify the identity of a unique object or a unique class of objects. The object or class may encompass abstract ideas, individuals, tangible objects that are countable (or their categories), or substances that are not countable (or their categories). The abbreviation ID is commonly used to denote identity, the process of identifying, or an instance of identification. Identifiers may take the form of a word, a numeral, a letter, a symbol, or any combination of these components.

LDAP Data Interchange Format (LDIF) is a text-based standard used for the import and export of address book data between different applications. It provides a structured, line-oriented representation of contact information to facilitate interoperability among directory services and mail clients. Historically, LDIF was supported by the Netscape Communicator address book as well as by the address book component of the Mozilla Application Suite, illustrating its role as a common interchange format for contact records across multiple software packages.

LDIF, the LDAP Data Interchange Format, is a standard plain-text format used to exchange data within LDAP directories. It supports representing both the content of directories and update requests; directory content is captured as records, with one record per directory object or entry, while update operations—such as Add, Modify, Delete, and Rename—are likewise recorded as individual records, one per update.

ISO 2709 defines bibliographic records as a collection of data fields that are labeled by tags. Each bibliographic field has an associated tag that identifies its type and role within the record. The tags themselves are not stored inside the field data; instead, they are recorded in the record’s directory, which lists each field’s tag together with its length and starting position. This directory functions as an index that maps tags to the corresponding field contents, enabling efficient location and interpretation of the record’s components.
Within the ISO 2709 standard, the record identifier field serves to uniquely identify the record and is assigned by the organization that creates it. The field is represented by the tag 001.

Legnickie Pole is a village located in Legnica County, within the Lower Silesian Voivodeship of southwestern Poland. It was named Dobre Pole from 1945 to 1948. The settlement serves as the seat of the administrative district known as Gmina Legnickie Pole.

Legnickie Pole’s abbey, shaped by the broader postwar order that followed the Treaty of Versailles and its limits on German military strength, was converted into a boarding school for boys in 1920. Under Nazi rule from 1934, it operated as a National Political Institute of Education, reflecting the regime’s educational objectives. During the Second World War, the site housed Oflag VIII-F, a prisoner-of-war camp for French, Yugoslav, and Italian POWs from 1940 to 1942, before the camp was relocated to Moravská Třebová. In March 1943, a separate facility, Oflag 64, was established there for Yugoslav officers and Soviet enlisted men, which was relocated to Szubin in May 1943.

Architects tender bids for projects on behalf of clients and advise on the selection of a general contractor. They facilitate and administer the construction contract that governs the relationship between client and contractor and is legally binding. The agreement outlines insurance requirements and the responsibilities of all parties, governs the status of design documents, provides for the architect’s access to the site, and sets out procedures for the oversight and control of works as construction progresses. Depending on the contract form, provisions for additional sub-contract tenders may be required. The architect may also require warranties covering certain elements, specifying expected lifespans and other performance criteria for materials, products, or workmanship.

Across major architectural bodies, post-nominal designations distinguish fellows by region and status. In the United Kingdom, the Royal Institute of British Architects formerly permitted Fellows to append FRIBA until 1971; from that year onward, chartered members may use the RIBA initials and are not permitted to use ARIBA or FRIBA, while honorary fellows may use Hon. FRIBA and international fellows may use Int. FRIBA. In the United States, the American Institute of Architects awards the FAIA designation to Fellows. In Canada, the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada designates Fellows with FRAIC. In Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Institute of Architects allows chartered members to use HKIA, while special-contribution fellows may adopt FHKIA.

The solar radius is commonly treated as an approximate parameter rather than a precisely defined constant. Determining this distance is challenging and can be approached through several observational techniques. The Sun is not a perfectly spherical body, and its shape deviates from pure sphericity. Consequently, the radius can differ depending on which location on the solar surface or interior is considered. Moreover, the inferred radius depends on the measurement method employed, with different techniques probing different layers or aspects of the Sun.

The solar photosphere radius, as determined by Haberreiter, Schmutz, and Kosovichev in 2008, is 695,660 ± 140 kilometres (432,263 ± 87 miles). This value is consistent with helioseismic estimates, supporting agreement between geometric measurements and seismic inferences of the solar radius. The study also found that prior estimates derived from the inflection-point method tended to overestimate the radius by about 300 kilometres (roughly 190 miles).

The shitik was a coastal transport vessel that, by the 13th century, represented the most widespread form of coastal craft in use. Its construction occurred mainly between the 11th and 17th centuries, with origins on the White Sea coast and along the river systems of Northern Dvina, Sukhona, Vychegda, Vetluga, and Tikhvinka. Over time, shipbuilding broadened to include Siberia and the Far East, and these vessels subsequently operated across the Pacific Ocean.

Shitik is a type of vessel whose underwater hull contours enable it to navigate through ice-covered waters. When subjected to compression, the craft is forced to surface, emerging onto the water’s surface. For docking and for hauling the anchor, Shitik requires the assistance of an osinovka boat.

In 2014, Paul McKenzie stated that he had fired all the American members of The Real McKenzies, and he asserted that the band subsequently returned to a fully Canadian lineup. However, Aspy Luison is from Cambre, Galicia, Spain, a detail that undermines the notion of the group having a lineup exclusively drawn from Canada.

The Real McKenzies covered Turbonegro's Sailor Man, a track that appeared in the 2003 video game Tony Hawk's Underground and in the first volume of the Elementality skateboarding videos. Each year, their rendition of Auld Lang Syne is used as the countdown music on the New Year's Eve edition of Hollywood Babble-On, Kevin Smith and Ralph Garman's live podcast.

By 1674, control of Long Island and its eastern settlements had been reasserted under English authority, even as these communities showed a preference for remaining under Connecticut’s jurisdiction. Connecticut assented to some arrangement, but the Duke of York’s government pressed the issue, and Governor Sir Edmund Andros warned that settlers could lose their land rights if they did not yield. Facing such coercion, the settlers capitulated by 1676, transferring allegiance to the Duke of York. The aggressive campaign reflected a broader personal grievance: the duke harbored resentment toward Connecticut because New Haven had concealed three judges who had sentenced his father, Charles I, to death in 1649, a motive that historians note as informing the late-17th-century shift in control.

African Americans have been an integral part of Long Island's history, with most arriving as enslaved individuals before the Revolutionary War. In bondage they performed both domestic tasks and agricultural labor, contributing to the region's social and economic life. Slavery persisted in New York and on Long Island until gradual abolition laws were enacted in 1799, and the final emancipation of enslaved people was achieved by 1827. Following emancipation, most freedpeople resided in the same communities where they had lived as slaves, forming enduring settlements within Long Island's towns and villages.

During World War II, Berlin housed several Nazi prisons and forced-labor facilities, including 17 subcamps of the Sachsenhausen concentration camp designated for men and women, and including adolescents. These subcamps detained people from diverse national backgrounds, such as Polish, Jewish, French, Belgian, Czechoslovak, Russian, Ukrainian, Romani, Dutch, Greek, Norwegian, Spanish, Luxembourgish, German, Austrian, Italian, Yugoslavian, Bulgarian, and Hungarian. A separate camp in Berlin was established for Sinti and Romani people, linked to the Romani Holocaust. Additionally, Stalag III-D, a prisoner-of-war camp for Allied servicemen of various nationalities, was located in Berlin.

Berlin's telecommunications infrastructure includes UMTS (3G) and LTE (4G) networks provided by Vodafone, Telekom Deutschland, and O2. These networks enable mobile broadband access across the city, supporting high-speed data services throughout Berlin.

In March 2023, Adams launched a podcast associated with the Drowned in Sound brand. The project soon extended to include a newsletter, followed by the creation of a record label. Subsequently, a comprehensive new website was unveiled, featuring expanded editorial content.

Drowned in Sound expanded its activities by launching a dedicated record label, Drowned in Sound Recordings. Founded in 2004, the imprint issued albums for a range of artists, including Brett Anderson, Emily Haines, Jeniferever, Martha Wainwright, Metric, Redjetson, The Stills, ThisGirl, and Youthmovies.

Henry Overholser (April 14, 1846 – August 25, 1915) was an American businessman and county commissioner who played a pivotal role in the early development of Oklahoma City. As a prominent entrepreneur and civic participant, he contributed to the city's growth through investment and construction, including involvement in the city’s first two-story buildings, both of which were demolished in 1907. Through his activities, Overholser helped lay the foundations of the growing metropolis, and his family maintained political influence, with his son from a first marriage, Edward Overholser, serving as mayor of Oklahoma City.

Henry Overholser House, a prominent Oklahoma City residence tied to the Overholser family, is a twenty-room brick-and-stone Victorian mansion situated in the Heritage Hills district and dating to 1903. The property remained within the Overholser lineage until after the deaths of family members, when it was transferred to David Perry, the husband of Overholser’s daughter. In the 1970s, the estate was donated to the state, and it is currently preserved as a historic house museum by Preservation Oklahoma under an agreement with the Oklahoma Historical Society.

In August 2020, Epic Games initiated litigation against Apple Inc., by filing a complaint with the United States District Court for the Northern District of California. The suit concerns Apple's practices in the iOS App Store.

Mac, short for Macintosh, was the official name of Apple’s computer line until 1999. The Mac refers to Apple’s line of personal computers that run the macOS operating system. Personal computers were Apple’s original business line. As of the end of 2024, personal computers accounted for about eight percent of Apple’s revenue.

Björk Guðmundsdóttir, commonly known as Björk, an Icelandic singer and musician, posted on social media in November 2023 during the Gaza war, criticizing the Israeli occupation of Palestine amid accusations by some that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians. In September 2025 she joined the No Music For Genocide boycott, opting to geo-block her music on streaming platforms in Israel in protest of the Gaza genocide.

Vulnicura Strings was announced on 2 October 2015 as an acoustic companion to Vulnicura, incorporating additional string arrangements and the viola organista, a keyboard instrument designed by Leonardo da Vinci. It was released on CD and digital formats on 6 November 2015, with a vinyl edition following on 4 December 2015. Vulnicura Live was announced about a week later and issued as a double CD and double LP exclusive to Rough Trade shops, with each format limited to 1,000 copies; online sales sold out within five days and in-store quantities were available in London and Brooklyn. The Vulnicura Live CD was released on 13 November 2015, and picture disc vinyls appeared about a week thereafter. On 7 December 2015, Vulnicura received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Alternative Music Album. A standard commercial edition of Vulnicura Live, featuring the same performances but newly mixed and with different artwork, was released on 15 July 2016, followed by a luxury version on 23 September 2016. Additionally, the performance of "Come to Me" from the album was included in the box set 7-inches for Planned Parenthood to support women's health.

Thailand's head of state is a hereditary monarch, with the current monarch, King Vajiralongkorn (Rama X), on the throne since October 2016. The constitution limits the king's formal powers, making him largely a symbolic figurehead, although the monarchy has occasionally intervened in politics and issued rulings that are framed as customary royal prerogatives. Some scholars, including Duncan McCargo and Federico Ferrara, have described an extraconstitutional "network monarchy" that operates behind the scenes. The monarchy is protected by strict lèse-majesté laws, and public attitudes toward the institution have varied across different reigns.

Thailand’s environmental performance, as measured by the 2016 Environmental Performance Index, placed 91st out of 180 countries. The most challenging domains were air quality (167th), environmental effects of the agricultural sector (106th), and the climate and energy sector (93rd), the latter largely attributable to high CO2 emissions per kilowatt-hour. By contrast, the country performed relatively better in water resource management (66th) and sanitation (68th). In 2019, Thailand’s Forest Landscape Integrity Index yielded a mean score of 6.00 out of 10, ranking 88th globally among 172 countries.

Interstate 196, together with U.S. Route 31, traverses Allegan County and initially passes two golf courses before continuing north through agricultural fields. Near the community of Glenn, the A-2 designation crosses over the freeway and runs parallel on its east side. The two routes exchange sides when I-196/US 31 turns northeast along the southern outskirts of Saugatuck and Douglas. The freeway then crosses Kalamazoo Lake, part of the Kalamazoo River between Saugatuck and Douglas. North of Saugatuck, A-2 crosses back to the eastern side of the freeway, after which I-196/US 31 proceeds north-northeast toward Holland.

Interstate 196 (I-196) in Michigan has undergone several notable upgrades in the 2009–2016 period. In 2009, access from Jenison was improved by adding a partial interchange at Baldwin Street. In 2010, the Michigan Department of Transportation’s project known as “Fix on I-196” rebuilt the downtown Grand Rapids segment east of the Grand River, added a third travel lane in each direction with weave-merge lanes, and reconstructed several overpasses. In 2016, the portions of I-196 that run concurrently with US 31 north of the M-63 interchange (excluding the ends of the business loop at South Haven) were designated as part of the West Michigan Pike Pure Michigan Byway.

David A. Huffman is best known for developing Huffman coding, a method for data compression. He published Huffman coding in 1952 while pursuing his ScD at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The idea for the algorithm reportedly arose when a professor offered students the choice between taking the traditional final exam or contributing to an improvement of a leading data compression algorithm. Huffman is said to have been more proud of his work The Synthesis of Sequential Switching Circuits, which formed the topic of his 1953 MIT thesis. An abridged version of the thesis was published in the Journal of the Franklin Institute in 1954.

David A. Huffman earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Ohio State University in 1944, followed by two years of service as an officer in the United States Navy. He then completed a Master of Science in electrical engineering at Ohio State University in 1949 and later received a Doctor of Science in electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1953. His doctoral work was supervised by Samuel H. Caldwell and addressed the synthesis of sequential switching circuits.

During the Lisbon Municipal Assembly, all parties expressed support for incorporating the territory of the Oriente parish into the city of Lisbon. Some parties, however, advocated instead placing that same area within the Santa Maria dos Olivais parish. Proponents of the Santa Maria dos Olivais option argued that it would keep Parque das Nações contained within a single parish and avoid creating new parish structures. Implementing that approach would require redrawing Lisbon’s municipal boundaries to include the area presently part of the Loures municipality.

Parque das Nações is a district in Lisbon notable for its modern architecture and the integration of vibrant social spaces, developed as part of a large-scale urban development and requalification program. The initiative transformed Lisbon's eastern zone, which had functioned as an industrial area until the 1990s, revitalizing that part of the city.

José Luis Clerc, commonly known by the nickname Batata, is an Argentine former professional tennis player. Born on 16 August 1958, his name is pronounced in Spanish as [xoseˈlwis ˈkleɾk]. Clerc reached his career-high ATP singles ranking of No. 4 on 3 August 1981, a milestone that came after a 25-match winning streak extending from Wimbledon.

In 1982, José Luis Clerc reached the French Open semifinals for the second consecutive year, where he was defeated in four sets by Mats Wilander. Wilander, a 17-year-old Swedish teenager at the time, went on to defeat Vilas in the final in four sets, thereby becoming the youngest Grand Slam champion up to that point.

The 2016 season of the United Football League in the Philippines was its final edition. This followed the appointment of UFL president Randy Roxas to a task force tasked with establishing the Philippine Football League, which was planned to commence in 2017.

The inaugural season of the United Football League in the Philippines established the competition as the country's premier football league. Due to sponsorship arrangements, the league was officially branded as the LBC United Football League. Its launch and continued operations were made possible by support from a group of local sponsors, including LBC Express Inc., Magma Inflatables, 2GO, Mutual Fund Management Corp., Orient Freight, and ATR Kim Eng.

Fletcher contributed background vocals on Sam Roberts Band's 2014 album Lo-Fantasy and played guitar for k-os. In 2014 he co-founded Beat Cops with Mikey Heppner of Priestess, releasing Mean Streets in 2015. In 2015 he released Punks on the Moon under his project Voizes. He subsequently formed Megative with ex-Stills producer Gus Van Go, the songwriting duo Like Minds (Jesse Singer and Chris Soper), and Screechy Dan. Megative debuted with the single "More Time" in 2017, and released its self-titled debut album on Last Gang Records on July 27, 2018.

The Stills' second studio album, Without Feathers, was released on May 9, 2006, with Vice Records handling the U.S. release and Drowned in Sound Recordings releasing it in the United Kingdom. The record was produced by Van Go and showcased a stylistic shift from the band's debut, moving away from 1980s-influenced post-punk revival toward a brighter, more Americana-tinged sound. Pitchfork described the album as cheerful and heartfelt. Guest contributions came from Sam Roberts, Emily Haines of Metric, and Jason Collett of Broken Social Scene. In 2007, the group supported Kings of Leon on their UK spring tour, and later that year were featured at the Quebec Scene in Ottawa, an event sponsored by CBC Radio 3, alongside Karkwa, The Besnard Lakes, and Mahjor Bidet.

The sitar is a plucked string instrument central to Indian classical music. Its introduction to Western culture was significantly advanced in the late 1950s and early 1960s by the collaboration of Ravi Shankar, the leading sitarist, and Alla Rakha, the renowned tabla player. Their partnership, uniting sitar and tabla, was instrumental in presenting Indian classical music to Western audiences and formed the core of this cultural exchange.

Scholars have proposed that the term sitar derives from a Persian naming pattern for lutes in which tar, meaning “string,” is joined with a word for the number of strings, so the resulting name would indicate the instrument’s string count. This etymological claim is attributed to the German ethnomusicologist Curt Sachs.

Life president is an honorary title awarded by an organization to individuals who have served the organization for a long period. The recipient typically has held a major role within the organization during their tenure, reflecting a sustained contribution to the institution's development and governance.

In some organizations, the office of president is complemented by a designated president-elect, who is elected by the membership. When the current president's term concludes, the president-elect automatically assumes the presidency, establishing a preplanned and seamless succession to the top leadership role. This arrangement provides continuity in governance by enabling an automatic transition from one term of office to the next.

Historically, a portion of the population led a nomadic existence, while many people resided in villages and small towns governed by emirs. The discovery of oil in the 1930s spurred accelerated settlement and migration toward economic centers, reshaping population distribution. Urbanization has continued to rise, with approximately a two percent increase in the urban share during the past decade. The largest cities have attracted substantial numbers of new residents seeking improved employment opportunities, contributing to shifts in demographic patterns. As urban growth has intensified, overcrowding has emerged as a major nationwide concern.

As of 2022, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia had an estimated population of around 35 million people. Foreign nationals comprised more than one-third of the total, indicating a substantial expatriate workforce within the country.

In November 2014, the animated series South Park aired an episode titled Freemium Isn't Free that satirized predatory game-design tactics associated with freemium business models. In 2015, Nintendo released two freemium Pokémon games based on standalone, purchasable titles. One of these titles, Pokémon Rumble World, can be completed without purchasing premium credits, with such credits being optional and designed to accelerate progression at the player's own pace.

Freemium is a business model in which a product is offered at no cost but with limited functionality, while access to expanded features or content is available only through payment. In practice, some free services restrict certain capabilities, such as a free video chat client that may omit three-way video calling unless a paid upgrade is obtained. Similarly, many free-to-play games feature virtual items that are impossible or extremely slow to acquire using in-game currency, encouraging players to purchase these items with real-world money. This approach relies on converting a portion of users into paying customers to sustain the service.

The architecture of the Captain Cook Wing at the Art Gallery of New South Wales does not imitate the building’s earlier classical vocabulary associated with Vernon, signaling a departure from its established stylistic precedent. The design philosophy attributed to Andersons aligns with Robert Venturi’s ideas presented in Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture, which advocate richer and more varied forms of architectural expression. Venturi argued for the deliberate juxtaposition of old and new to achieve dramatic visual impact, while criticizing the pursuit of unity and consistency as mere precepts of conventional practice. Together, these perspectives suggest that the Wing embodies a move away from strict classical imitation toward an approach that embraces complexity and contextual contrasts.

During 2004, the Art Gallery of New South Wales hosted a Man Ray exhibition that attracted more than 52,000 visitors, setting a record for photography attendance at the institution. In the same year, a legal challenge was mounted against Craig Ruddy's Archibald Prize-winning portrait of David Gulpilil, titled David Gulpilil, Two Worlds. The gallery also established the Anne Landa Award, Australia’s first prize dedicated to moving image and new media. Additionally, the Nelson Meers Foundation Nolan Room opened, featuring five major Sidney Nolan paintings gifted to the gallery by the foundation over the preceding five years.

The East Iceland Current (EIC) is a relatively low-density current that flows southward along the eastern edge of Iceland. It encounters a denser northward-moving Atlantic water, and the substantial density contrast between the two water masses inhibits mixing. Following their encounter, the two streams advance eastward along the Iceland–Faeroe Ridge, a submarine feature that connects Iceland to the Faeroe Islands.

The East Iceland Current is a cold-water ocean stream that forms east of Greenland at approximately 72°N, 11°W as a branch of the East Greenland Current. It combines with the Irminger Current, which flows southward, until the current encounters the northeastern region of Iceland. After making contact with Iceland, the flow deflects counterclockwise and proceeds eastward along the Iceland–Faeroe Ridge, before turning north to enter the Norwegian Sea. The current maintains an average speed of about 6 cm/s, with a maximum near 10 cm/s observed when turning eastward.

The Xianyou dialect is notable for its highly extensive system of tone sandhi. In an utterance, all syllables except the final pronounced syllable are subject to tonal alteration through sandhi, while the final pronounced syllable remains unaffected by these rules. This widespread application of tone sandhi yields a dynamic pattern of tonal realization that distinguishes the dialect within its linguistic context.

The Xianyou dialect is a variety of Pu-Xian Min Chinese. In Pu-Xian Min it is known as Sing-iú-uā, and its Chinese designation is 仙遊話. The phonology is indicated by the IPA transcription [ɬiŋ˨ iu˨˦ ua˨˩]. It is spoken in Xianyou, within Putian, along the southeast coast of Fujian province, China.

Tianlong-2 is a Chinese liquid-fueled rocket developed by a private-sector enterprise. It conducted its inaugural flight on 2 April 2023 and subsequently entered orbit, marking the first instance of a liquid-fueled rocket in China developed by a private company.

Tianlong-2 (simplified Chinese 天龙二号; traditional Chinese 天龍二號; pinyin Tiānlóng Èrhào; literal meaning "Heavenly Dragon 2") is a small-lift launch vehicle developed by Space Pioneer, a private Chinese aerospace company. The booster adopts a three-stage configuration, with the first two stages powered by liquid oxygen and kerosene propellants. Its initial payload capacity to low Earth orbit is about 2 tons, with the potential to extend to around 4 tons following future improvements.

ISO 21500, published as guidance on project management, reflects and reinforces the process-based understanding of the discipline that emerged in Europe during the 1980s. The standard centers on applying a coherent set of structured processes across the project life cycle to realise stated objectives. It treats project management as a systematic sequence of activities designed to translate a concept into a tangible outcome, with particular emphasis on defining and refining the processes necessary to meet objectives. The body of research associated with process orientation indicates that organizational effectiveness is shaped by decision-making criteria and goal-directed activities embedded within processes. In this sense, ISO 21500 implicitly endorses a process-driven approach to managing projects.

ISO 21500 presents a process-based framework for project management, arguing that structuring work around a coherent set of processes yields the project lifecycle models used in practice. The approach underpins a number of widely cited PMBOK concepts, which are rooted in process-based project management. The standard identifies several principal areas, including the overall project management processes and the domains of integration management, quality management, and risk management.

In October 2012, eBay announced the launch of an international shipping partnership with Pitney Bowes. The program enables sellers to ship items to a Pitney Bowes facility located in their home country, after which Pitney Bowes forwards the package to the international buyer and handles all international shipping requirements. In addition, eBay established a partnership with FedEx to provide discounted shipping options for sellers.

The case between Tiffany & Co. and eBay began with Tiffany filing suit in 2004, contending that a substantial portion of Tiffany silver jewelry sold on the eBay marketplace was counterfeit and that the company profited from listings infringing its trademark. On July 14, 2008, a United States district court judge ruled that eBay did not have a legal duty to monitor or police users selling counterfeit items on the platform. In 2010, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s decision in Tiffany (NJ) Inc. v. eBay Inc., thereby upholding the finding that eBay was not legally obligated to actively monitor for counterfeit goods.

Firyal Irshaid has been active in relief work in refugee camps in Jordan, contributing to humanitarian aid efforts that address the needs of displaced populations. She has also worked on literacy programs with the nomadic Bedouin tribes, aiming to improve educational opportunities and learning outcomes for these communities. In addition, she established a family planning program, reflecting her involvement in public health and community development initiatives.
Firyal Irshaid founded the International Hope Foundation in 1994. The organization operates under the UNESCO umbrella and is dedicated to benefiting homeless and street children.

Gyrocompass is a navigation instrument that determines true north by exploiting the rotation of the Earth through inertial sensing. An alternative design employs a strapdown architecture in which the sensor suite is mounted directly on the host platform, comprising a triad of gyroscopes and a triad of accelerometers. The gyroscope component can be realized with modern devices such as fibre optic gyroscopes, ring laser gyroscopes, or hemispherical resonator gyroscopes, arranged to measure angular velocity about all three axes. By not relying on mechanical parts to determine the rotation rate, strapdown configurations avoid certain error sources associated with moving components and use digital processing to integrate the sensed rates into the orientation relative to true north.

The gyrocompass is modeled as a gyroscope whose symmetry axis is allowed to rotate. In this framework, the device is also free to rotate in the horizontal plane around the local vertical, yielding two independent angular degrees of freedom in the local frame. The analysis incorporates the Earth's rotation about its north–south axis, and the Earth is idealized as a perfect sphere to simplify the geometry. Friction is neglected, and the model disregards the Earth's rotation about the Sun.

Parking pawl is a device in automatic transmissions that immobilizes the transmission’s output shaft by engaging a pawl with a notched parking gear, thereby preventing the driven wheels from rotating when the vehicle is parked. Its principal components are the parking gear, the parking pawl, an actuator rod, a cam collar, a cam plate, a pivot pin, and the return spring that resets the pawl. The mechanism is arranged so that the pawl tooth engages the parking gear teeth, effectively locking the output shaft by binding with the gear’s teeth; this engagement is designed to occur only after the vehicle has slowed to a safe speed, ensuring a controlled and reliable lock. In contemporary systems, software interlocks prevent engagement until the vehicle has come to rest, adding a safeguard against inadvertent parking while the vehicle is in motion.

A parking pawl is a device within automatic transmissions that locks the transmission when the shift lever is placed in Park. Park corresponds to the first position of the lever, occupying the topmost position on column-shift arrangements and the frontmost position on floor-shift designs. Beginning in 1965, all cars sold in the United States have Park as the initial lever position, standardized by SAE J915. The Park position is standard in most other vehicles worldwide.

In June 2010, security researchers from Goatse Security identified a vulnerability in AT&T's online services that could expose the email addresses of AT&T's 3G iPad customers without requiring authentication. The flaw allowed the collection of thousands of email addresses through a simple script. Goatse Security alerted AT&T to the issue via a third party. Approximately 114,000 email addresses were disclosed to Gawker Media, which subsequently published coverage of the security lapse and its disclosure in the Valleywag blog. Praetorian Security Group later criticized the affected web application as poorly designed.
AT&T Inc. was reportedly affected by a cyberattack in 2024, with the incident attributed to Salt Typhoon, an advanced persistent threat group linked to the Chinese government.

During the 1989–90 Bundesliga season, Stuttgarter Kickers and Hannover 96 finished in the bottom two positions, resulting in direct relegation to the 2. Bundesliga. They were replaced in the top flight by Fortuna Düsseldorf and FC Homburg, who earned promotion to the Bundesliga. Eintracht Frankfurt retained its Bundesliga status by defeating 1. FC Saarbrücken in the relegation/promotion playoff on aggregate.

The 1989–90 Bundesliga marked the 27th edition of Germany's top-tier football league. As the premier competition in West German football, the season commenced on 28 July 1989 and concluded on 12 May 1990. FC Bayern Munich entered the campaign as the reigning champions, having won the previous season.
Nam Từ Liêm was established on 27 December 2013 following the division of the rural Từ Liêm district into two urban districts, Bắc Từ Liêm and Nam Từ Liêm.
Nam Từ Liêm is an urban district that is subdivided into ten wards: Cầu Diễn, Đại Mỗ, Mễ Trì, Mỹ Đình 1, Mỹ Đình 2, Phú Đô, Phương Canh, Tây Mỗ, Trung Văn, and Xuân Phương.

Harrison Ford is an American actor whose career has encompassed enduring film roles and notable philanthropic work. In 2006 he received the Jules Verne Award for promoting the spirit of adventure and imagination throughout his career. The following year, he earned the Scream Awards’ first Hero Award for his iconic characters, including Indiana Jones and Han Solo. He has won three Saturn Awards for Best Actor for those roles, in 1982, 2016, and 2024. In 2008 he was honored with Spike TV’s Guy’s Choice Award for “Brass Balls.” BAFTA Los Angeles awarded him the Albert R. Broccoli Britannia Award for Worldwide Contribution to Entertainment in 2015. In 2018 the SAG-AFTRA Foundation presented the Artists Inspiration Award for his acting and philanthropic work with Conservation International, an honor he shared with Lady Gaga. JoBeth Williams has highlighted Ford’s philanthropic service and leadership for Conservation International.

Harrison Ford has received numerous nominations and honors recognizing his work in film. In 1986, he was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor for Witness, with corresponding nominations from the BAFTA and the Golden Globes in the same category for that film. He later earned Golden Globe nominations for The Mosquito Coast (1987), The Fugitive (1994), and Sabrina (1996). In 2000, Ford was honored with the AFI Life Achievement Award for his body of work, an honor presented by George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He received the Cecil B. DeMille Award from the Hollywood Foreign Press Association at the 59th Golden Globes in 2002. On May 30, 2003, he was awarded a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

Martha Vasconcellos was a Brazilian beauty queen who represented Brazil at the 1968 Miss Universe pageant, held in Miami Beach, Florida. She won the Miss Universe title, defeating 64 contestants. There have been allegations that she had a boyfriend since she was twelve.

Martha Maria Cordeiro Vasconcellos (born June 18, 1948) is a Brazilian beauty queen who won the Miss Universe title, becoming Brazil's second Miss Universe after Iêda Maria Vargas's 1963 victory. She was the fifth Latin American to achieve the crown, following Gladys Zender of Peru (1957), Luz Marina Zuluaga of Colombia (1958), and Norma Nolan of Argentina (1962). A native of the state of Bahia in Brazil, Vasconcellos gained international prominence through her Miss Universe triumph.

On January 14, at the 2023 NCAA Convention, the Division II football membership approved an adjustment to the redshirt regulations. The revised rule permits freshmen to participate in up to three games without incurring the loss of a season of eligibility, thereby preserving that season for those players who appear in three or fewer contests.

Within the article on the 2023 NCAA Division II football season, the coaching changes section documents coaching staff changes that were announced on or after May 1, 2023. It also covers alterations disclosed after a team's final regular-season game but prior to its playoff appearances. The scope is strictly limited to developments that occurred during the 2023 NCAA Division II football season.

In March 2009, VentureBeat entered into a collaboration with International Data Group (IDG) to organize the DEMO Conference. The event served as a platform for startups to unveil new products and pursue financing from venture capitalists and angel investors. The arrangement with IDG terminated in 2012.

Between 2014 and 2015, VentureBeat secured outside funding in the form of venture capital, contributed by a group of Silicon Valley-based investors. The round included investments from Crosslink Capital, Walden Venture Capital, Rally Ventures, Formation 8, and Lightbank, reflecting support from several prominent venture capital firms in the region.

Rescue 911 presented its narratives in a documentary-style format, with filming crews accompanying on-scene responders—paramedics, firefighters, and police—or observing from hospitals to document events as they developed. Episodes commonly integrated multiple incidents within a single segment set at the same medical facility. A notable example cited is the Charles Stuart murder case, which was recorded during an on-duty assignment with Boston EMS.

Rescue 911 is a television series whose segment features a rescue ambulance described as a Dodge. The side panel includes a synopsis for the episode titled "911 Cribbage Choke." In the narrative, paramedics perform a high-risk procedure aboard the ambulance to address an airway obstruction in a young boy who is choking on a cribbage piece, with the goal of saving the child's life.

Hinzert concentration camp was organized around a central muster area, with surrounding zones designated for different functions. In addition to this central space, three other buildings housed local Gestapo offices, administrative offices, and the kitchen. The size of the muster area was later reduced after the SS established a neighboring vegetable patch. A mast with loudspeakers stood at the center of the muster area through which orders were broadcast, and prisoners could be punished by standing still for hours facing the mast. The muster area also served as a drill and exercise space, and prisoners were compelled to jump up and down at 4:30 am to the sound of a drum.

Hinzert concentration camp, established and operated during the Nazi regime, saw approximately 13,600 prisoners pass through its facilities. The initial detainees were German workers who had contributed to the Siegfried Line and were deemed to exhibit anti-social behavior. Soon after, the camp housed forced laborers transported from occupied countries. Beginning in 1941, large groups of inmates were sent to Hinzert, primarily political prisoners from Luxembourg and France, with other detainees including forced laborers and prisoners of war from Poland and the Soviet Union. Beginning on December 7, 1941, under the Night and Fog directive, prisoners designated as NN were transported from Hinzert to larger camps such as Natzweiler, Dachau, and Buchenwald, where they would later disappear.

As of the 2000 census, Wharton County, Texas, had a population of 41,188, 14,799 households, and 10,744 families. The population density was 38 people per square mile (15/km2), and there were 16,606 housing units at an average density of 15 per square mile (5.8/km2). The racial composition consisted of 69.01% White, 14.95% Black or African American, 0.37% Native American, 0.31% Asian, 0.06% Pacific Islander, 13.65% from other races, and 1.64% from two or more races, with Hispanic or Latino residents of any race making up 31.29% of the population. Ancestry data indicate 12.8% Czech, 11.0% German, and 7.0% American. English was the first language for 73.8% of residents, followed by Spanish at 24.0% and Czech at 2.0%.

Wharton County is a county in the U.S. state of Texas. It comprises the El Campo micropolitan statistical area, a core-based statistical area anchored by the city of El Campo. This micropolitan area is included within the Houston-The Woodlands, TX Combined Statistical Area, reflecting its integration into the broader regional framework.

Twango provides multiple ways to upload content beyond browser-based uploading, including submissions sent by email, uploads from mobile phones, and transfers through the Windows web publishing wizard.

Twango provides support for a variety of feeds, including channel feeds, feeds of the most recently added media, and feeds showcasing the most popular items. It also implements several widely used feed formats, namely RSS 2.0, ATOM 0.3, and ATOM 1.0.
Eric Clapton, a renowned guitarist and singer-songwriter, bought one of his early guitars at a shop located in Surbiton. The establishment, known as Bells, has since ceased trading.

Surbiton originated as Kingston-upon-Railway, a settlement that developed in the 1840s with the expansion of the railway. The area features a mix of architectural styles, including large nineteenth-century townhouses, Art Deco-style courts, and newer residential blocks that sit alongside mid-20th-century semi-detached housing estates. In 2016, its population was 45,132, roughly a quarter of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames's total population. The district covers 7.18 km^2 (2.77 sq mi).

In May 2009, India expressed reluctance to host the SAFF Championship, an update announced during the Asian Football Confederation Congress held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The information was relayed by Kazi Salahuddin, president of the Bangladesh Football Federation, after his return from the Congress. Despite the expressed hesitation, India was still reported to retain host status for the eight-nation tournament, while Bangladesh and Nepal submitted fresh bids to host the championship.

On 31 August 2009, reports indicated that Bangladesh would host the SAFF Championship, a development that followed the All India Football Federation's annual congress held at the end of August. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) subsequently formalized the choice, announcing Bangladesh as the host in a press release dated 10 September 2009.

Tougher Than Leather is the twenty-eighth studio album by American country music singer Willie Nelson. It marked Nelson's return to original material after an eight-year interval, following the release of Red Headed Stranger.

Tougher Than Leather is a Willie Nelson album that drew a negative appraisal from Crispin Sartwell, a reviewer for Record, who contended that it does not amount to genuine country music. Sartwell contrasted Nelson's earlier work, which he described as honest ballads grounded in concrete, relatable situations, with the new release, arguing that the album centers on high-handed philosophical preaching. He further faulted the record for lacking musical variety, characterizing it as bland and homogeneous throughout.

Do You Really Like It? is a track described by critic Tom Ewing as distilling UK garage into a pop-friendly form. It employs a sing-along chorus, frequent shouted vocal interjections, and a 2-step beat, and is credited with capturing the communal energy of UK garage at the height of its mainstream appeal. The hook is noted for being memorable and infectious, providing a lasting sense of catchiness. Ewing argues that, taken as a whole, the track lacks coherence, featuring abrupt tempo and directional changes that feel awkward. Nevertheless, the song is regarded as emblematic of UK garage’s ability to attract broader audiences, emphasizing its communal energy and accessible, friendly character in contrast to the darker, underground tracks of the era.

Do You Really Like It? circulated as a dubplate within the Ayia Napa club scene during the summer of 2000. An independent pressing subsequently appeared on the Official Independent Singles Chart in late 2000, released by Soulfood under catalog number SF007. In March 2001, Ministry of Sound and Relentless signed the track, a deal described by Music Week as one of the most expensive two-step arrangements in recent times. The signing followed an earlier licensing appearance on Ministry of Sound’s Real Garage compilation.

Stormin was a versatile MC renowned for his ability to navigate a broad range of tempos, earning praise from both peers and listeners for his adaptability on the mic. He was an early proponent of UK garage instrumentals characterized by dark lyricism, a sound that helped propel grime and reflected US hip hop influences. Among his early affiliations was Dizzee Rascal, with whom he recorded one of his first tracks. In later years he joined the jump-up MC group SaSaSaS and performed under the masked alias Teddy Bruckshot, a moniker inspired by Louie Rankin’s Shottas character; releases under that alias appeared on labels such as Deep Medi Musik.
