Stormin’s distinctive style and sustained activity contributed to his recognition at the Drum and Bass Awards, where he and SaSaSaS won the Best DnB Group award and he collected the Best Crowd Hype DnB MC award on three occasions: 2016, 2017, and posthumously in 2018.

Shaun Lewis (15 February 1984 – 19 February 2018) was a British MC and rapper who performed under the stage names Stormin and Teddy Bruckshot. A native of Plaistow in London, he was associated with the grime and drum and bass scenes and contributed to the city’s underground music milieu during his career.

Founded in the 13th century, Our Lady of Grace Cathedral in Setúbal reflects a later reconstruction carried out in the High Renaissance tradition, with a façade in the Mannerist style. Inside, frescoed columns and tiles dating to the 17th and 18th centuries contribute to the building's interior character.

Our Lady of Grace Cathedral (Sé Catedral de Santa Maria da Graça), also known as Setúbal Cathedral, is a Catholic church building that serves as the cathedral of Setúbal, a city in Portugal. It is situated in the heart of the town's early medieval core, where the city's principal medieval district and its religious and administrative activities arose around the cathedral.

UTC−4 is a time offset used in certain North American time zones. In the Eastern Time Zone, which covers parts of Canada and the United States, the offset is observed during daylight saving time and is known as Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). In the Atlantic Time Zone, the same offset is observed during the standard time period in the winter months, where it is called Atlantic Standard Time (AST).

Ludo Peeters (born 9 August 1953) is a Belgian former professional road bicycle racer. His career spanned from 1974 to 1990, during which he rode in ten editions of the Tour de France and secured three stage victories in the race, in 1980, 1982 and 1986. He wore the yellow jersey as the overall leader for one day in 1982 after a stage win, and he also held the jersey for a single day in 1984.

Pile lighthouses on Florida reefs are tall skeletal towers whose living and working quarters are elevated well above the storm waves to protect occupants during severe weather. Some lights began as screw-pile lighthouses and were subsequently converted for continued use, while others were constructed on piles driven directly into the seabed to secure stability in the marine environment.

Pile lighthouses constitute a category of navigational beacons found in Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. In the United States, their presence is chiefly concentrated in Florida, where several examples are located on open reefs adjacent to the Florida Keys.
Saleh Zakaria is a Kuwaiti football coach who led the Kuwait national team in 1978 and again in 1986, and later served as the team's head coach from December 2006 to June 2007.

Lahti benefits from its close proximity to Helsinki, enabling fast and well-connected rail links between the two cities. In daytime, long-distance and commuter trains serve Lahti at a frequency of at least twice per hour. Commuter services run toward Riihimäki to the southwest and toward Kouvola and Kotka to the east. All eastbound and northeastbound long-distance trains to and from Helsinki call at Lahti. Travel from Lahti to Helsinki Airport is convenient, with journey times to Helsinki via Tikkurila station typically ranging from 49 to 65 minutes.

Lahti has played a notable role in Finnish motorcycle speedway through two venues in the late 20th century. The Kärpänen track operated approximately from the early 1950s to around 1980, located on the site of today’s Kärpäsen koulu sports field; it hosted a qualifying round of the Speedway World Championship in 1957 and staged the Finnish Speedway Championship on several occasions between 1963 and 1978. A new facility, the Pipoo speedway track, was built in 1980 off Vanhanradankatu, and it subsequently hosted the Finnish Championship final in 1980, 1987, and 1990.

Falcon Heavy was originally designed with a propellant crossfeed arrangement to feed the center core engines from the two side boosters until their separation. The concept, rooted in Vladimir Chelomei's UR-700 launch-system proposals, envisaged all engines delivering full thrust from liftoff while the side boosters supplied most of the propellants. In this scheme, the side boosters would be depleted more quickly, and an earlier side-booster separation would reduce the mass the remaining core had to accelerate. As a result, a substantial portion of the center core's propellant would remain available after booster separation.

Falcon Heavy is a high-capacity orbital launch vehicle developed, produced, and launched by SpaceX, the American aerospace company. It incorporates partial reusability, with some components designed to be recovered and reused after flight. The vehicle is capable of delivering substantial payloads to Earth orbit and to destinations beyond it.

Cap-Vert has been identified with the ancient designation Hesperu Ceras, which translates as “the western horn.” The name Hesperu Ceras appears in Classical Graeco-Roman writings, where it is used to denote the westernmost point of the African continent.

Cap-Vert is a peninsula located in Senegal, representing the westernmost point of Africa and of the Afro-Eurasian mainland. It is also known as the Cape Verde Peninsula; in Wolof it is referred to as Kap Weert or Bopp bu Nëtëx. Portuguese explorers named it Cabo Verde, from which the later archipelago derives its name, meaning “Green Cape.” The Cape Verde Islands lie about 570 kilometres (350 miles) to the west and were named after the cape. Dakar, the capital of Senegal, occupies parts of the peninsula, including its southern tip. The landform forms the border between the Grande Côte to the north and the Petite Côte to the south, and it is delimited by two capes, Pointe des Almadies to the northwest and Cap Manuel to the southeast.

The second ministry of Armand-Emmanuel du Plessis de Richelieu preserved most of the ministers from the preceding cabinet. The office of president of the council was transferred from Élie, Duke of Decazes, to the Duke of Richelieu, who did not himself hold a ministerial portfolio. On 21 February, Joseph Jérôme, Count Siméon, was appointed Minister of the Interior.

The second ministry of Armand-Emmanuel du Plessis de Richelieu was the French government established on 20 February 1820, following the dismissal of the Élie Decazes ministry by King Louis XVIII during the Bourbon Restoration. It remained in office until 12 December 1821, when it was dissolved and subsequently replaced by the Ministry of Joseph de Villèle, which assumed power on 14 December 1821.

Soundwave, an Australian music festival, originated in Perth as Gravity Soundwave, the music component of the Gravity Games. The gravity Games were staged in South Perth along the Swan River and emphasized water-based and action sports. In its inaugural year, Vodafone sponsored the event, with reports indicating sponsorship of around one million dollars. Gravity Soundwave formed the festival’s musical program, and the event was held at McCallum Park, located beside the Swan River.

Soundwave, known at the time as Gravity Soundwave, represented the third and final edition of Perth’s Gravity Games festival. The event was relocated from October to December 2006, continuing the festival in the Western Australian capital. The lineup featured the American act Aiden along with Australian groups Gyroscope, Kisschasy, Parkway Drive and The Getaway Plan, complemented by New Zealand band Goodnight Nurse.

The Italian Catholic Electoral Union (Unione Elettorale Cattolica Italiana, UECI) is a political organization in Italy established to coordinate Catholic participation in electoral contests. It was founded by Count Vincenzo Ottorino Gentiloni, who also served as its leader.

The Italian Catholic Electoral Union was established in 1906 in the aftermath of the suppression of the Opera dei Congressi, which followed Pope Pius X’s encyclical Il fermo proposito. From 1909 to 1916 the movement was led by Count Ottorino Gentiloni. The Gentiloni pact of 1913 mobilized a substantial bloc of Catholic voters to back the Liberal Union led by Giovanni Giolitti, on the understanding that Catholic electors would support Giolitti’s candidates who would advance church-favored policies, including state funding for private Catholic schools and the defeat of a proposed divorce law.
Ralph Kimball has offered data warehouse consulting and education since 1992, delivering these services through organizations including Ralph Kimball Associates and the Kimball Group.

Ralph Kimball earned a Ph.D. in 1973 from Stanford University in electrical engineering, specializing in man–machine systems. He subsequently joined the Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC), where he served as a principal designer of the Xerox Star Workstation. The Star Workstation is recognized as the first commercial product to incorporate a graphical user interface featuring a mouse, icons, and windows, marking a pivotal development in the history of personal computing.

ISO 639 refers to the original language code standard, formally approved in 1967, which was later divided into multiple parts, with ISO 639-1 designated as the revised two-letter subset in 2002. The most recently added code to the set was ht for Haitian Creole, introduced on February 26, 2003. The use of the standard was promoted within the IETF through language-tag specifications, beginning with RFC 1766 in March 1995 and subsequently followed by RFC 3066 in January 2001 and RFC 4646 in September 2006. The current edition is ISO 639-1 as defined by RFC 5646, published in September 2009. Infoterm (International Information Center for Terminology) serves as the registration authority for ISO 639-1 codes.

ISO 639-1 establishes two-letter identifiers for languages that are commonly used as prefixes in the URLs of multilingual websites to indicate the language version of the content. This usage is exemplified by sites such as Wikipedia, where the English edition can be reached through the en prefix in the URL, illustrating how language-specific versions are denoted. The concept is related to IETF language tags, which provide a broader framework for identifying languages in computing contexts. By contrast, two-letter country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) are often distinct from these language prefixes, since country codes do not necessarily correspond to language identifiers.

During the 1980s, Finland and other Scandinavian countries witnessed a revival of glam metal, driven by a wave of bands that embraced the genre’s flamboyant style and guitar-driven sound. These acts drew substantial influence from classic American groups such as Mötley Crüe and Guns N’ Roses, while incorporating contemporary production and sensibilities to create a modernized interpretation of the genre. Notable groups associated with this movement include Reckless Love, Santa Cruz, Crashdïet, and Hardcore Superstar.

Finnish rock in the 1950s and 1960s largely reflected international trends, with many bands performing covers or songs translated into Finnish. Among the earliest notable figures of the 1960s were Eero Raittinen and his brother Jussi Raittinen, alongside groups such as Jormas, Topmost, and Ernos. The Renegades, a British band, achieved their greatest success in Finland during the 1960s. Helsinki served as the center of the Finnish rock and pop scene in this period. Love Records emerged as one of the first domestic labels dedicated to Finnish rock, although its catalog also included jazz and politically oriented material. Suomen Talvisota 1939-1940 represented the Finnish underground, with their 1970 album Underground-Rock widely cited as an influential work. In the broader underground and psychedelic milieu, bands such as The Sperm, Apollo, and Blues Section contributed to the scene, and after Blues Section disbanded they gave rise to Wigwam and Tasavallan Presidentti.

During World War II, shaped-charge munitions were developed by several major powers—Germany, Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States, and Italy—leading to a range of weapons designed to defeat armored targets. German examples included the Panzerschreck, Panzerfaust, Panzerwurfmine, and the Mistel project. British designs encompassed the No. 68 antitank grenade, the PIAT, and the Beehive cratering charge. The Soviet Union produced the RPG-43 and RPG-6. The United States fielded devices such as the M9 rifle grenade and the bazooka. Italy contributed Effetto Pronto Speciale shells for various artillery pieces. The widespread development of these munitions transformed anti-tank warfare, making tanks vulnerable to infantry- or aircraft-delivered shaped-charge payloads.

Demolition charges that generate a jet produce a high-velocity stream of metal that travels predominantly at hypersonic speeds. The leading tip attains velocities between 7 and 14 km/s, the jet's trailing portion typically moves at 1 to 3 km/s, and in some cases a residual slug remains below 1 km/s. These velocity distributions depend on charge configuration and confinement, the type of explosive used, the materials involved, and the mode of initiation. At the resulting penetrative velocities, the pressures generated are immense and approach hydrodynamic levels. In analytical terms, the jet and the armor can be treated as inviscid, compressible fluids with material strengths neglected as an approximation.

Eurotower in Frankfurt am Main has long served as the base for the European Central Bank's banking supervision arm, hosting around 1,400 employees. In 2023, the ECB announced plans to vacate the building and relocate its supervisory operations to the Galileo Tower, with completion anticipated by 2025.

Eurotower is a prominent office building located at Willy-Brandt-Platz in Frankfurt's central business district, the Bankenviertel. The tower stands opposite the Opern- und Schauspielhaus Frankfurt and is closely integrated with the city's public transport network, with a subterranean U-Bahn station situated directly beside the structure and an above-ground tram stop in close proximity.

Who's Who (UK) is a long-established biographical reference that profiles notable figures across British public life. Each entry presents the subject’s full name and date of birth, followed by a concise account of their career details and notable achievements. The record often collects educational background and professional qualifications, together with memberships in clubs or professional societies. Publications authored by the individual are listed, alongside notes on recreations or interests. Where available, contact details or professional channels are provided to facilitate appropriate inquiries, although personal contact information is typically limited by privacy considerations.

Who’s Who (UK) maintains lifelong inclusion, with members not being removed from the directory after they leave their positions, such as Members of Parliament. A notable example is the 7th Earl of Lucan, who remained listed following his disappearance in 1974 and after being legally declared dead in 1999. He was still listed in the Who’s Who 2016 edition, the volume published in 2015. As of 2023, the most recent online entry on the Who’s Who & Who Was Who site is dated 1 December 2016. The death certificate for the Earl of Lucan was issued in 2016.

Non-human hominoids are rare and threatened with extinction. Among the gibbons, the eastern hoolock gibbon is the least threatened yet remains vulnerable to extinction. Five gibbon species are critically endangered, while all orangutan and gorilla species are likewise classified as critically endangered. The remaining gibbon species, the bonobo, and all four chimpanzee subspecies are listed as endangered. The principal threat to these taxa is the loss of tropical rainforest habitat, though hunting for bushmeat imperils several populations as well. In addition, the Ebola virus constitutes a major survival threat to African great apes, and since 1990 outbreaks have caused the deaths of at least one-third of gorillas and chimpanzees.

Modern taxonomy seeks to classify organisms in monophyletic groups that reflect common ancestry. The term ape is used variably, sometimes to denote all members of the superfamily Hominoidea, including humans, though many biologists reserve it for non-human members of the group. In this framework, Benton (2005) describes the apes (Hominoidea) as comprising gibbons, orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, and humans. Consequently, contemporary biologists and primatologists often refer to non-human apes to distinguish these species from humans. Outside paleoanthropology, the human lineage is identified as the hominin, a term that has largely replaced hominid in that context. For additional guidance on the naming conventions used for primates, see the terminology of primate names.

The Wall Street Journal's editorial page has been shaped by several prominent editors, including Vermont C. Royster, who led the page from 1958 to 1971, and Robert Bartley, who served from 1972 to 2000, both of whom were noted for presenting a conservative interpretation of the news through its editorials. Paul Gigot is the editor and host of the page, guiding its editorial stance. On Saturdays and Sundays, Gigot, together with three editorial-page writers, appears on Fox News Channel's Journal Editorial Report to discuss current issues with guests.

The Wall Street Journal earned its first Pulitzer Prize in 1947 for editorials written by William Henry Grimes. In May of that year, it launched a Southwest edition based in Dallas, expanding its regional footprint. Two years later, in 1949, the newspaper adopted a marketing slogan portraying the Journal as the publication read by men who were advancing in business. Circulation also grew substantially during the decade, rising from about 32,000 in 1940 to roughly 140,000 by 1949, nearly quadrupling in size. Despite these gains, Kilgore's editorial reforms had not yet entered popular understanding.

Ang Trapaing Thmor is a notable site for the sarus crane (Grus antigone), a very large crane with an average length of about 156 cm. The species is an all-year resident and breeding bird across northern Pakistan and India (especially Central India and the Gangetic plains), Nepal, Southeast Asia, and Queensland, Australia. It typically inhabits freshwater marshes and plains.

Ang Trapaing Thmor is a crane sanctuary located in northwestern Cambodia near the Thai border. The protected area spans roughly 10,000 hectares and lies entirely within Phnom Srok District of Banteay Meanchey Province. Phnom Srok borders Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey provinces; within the district, the sanctuary is bounded to the north by Oddar Meanchey’s Banteay Ampil and Chong Kal, to the east by Siem Reap’s Srei Snam and Kralanh, to the south by Preah Net Preah District (Banteay Meanchey), and to the west by Svay Chek and Thma Puok (Banteay Meanchey). Access is by road from Sisophon, about 70 kilometers away, or from Siem Reap city, approximately 90 kilometers away, via National Highway 6 followed by smaller unsealed district roads to Ang Trapaing Thmor.

A histogram is a graphical representation of a frequency distribution in which data are grouped into consecutive class intervals and depicted by adjacent rectangles. The width of each rectangle matches the width of its class interval, while the area of the rectangle is proportional to the frequency observed in that interval. The height of the rectangle reflects the average frequency density for the interval (frequency divided by the class width). Rectangles are arranged edge to edge to indicate that the classes are exclusive and contiguous, and intervals with zero frequency are shown as empty rather than omitted. For example, adjacent classes may be 10.5–20.5 and 20.5–33.5, sharing the boundary at 20.5, whereas 10.5–20.5 and 22.5–32.5 would create a gap and fail to reflect continuity.

Karl Pearson, in 1895, observed that the term histogram was a newly coined designation; nonetheless, the graphical form it denotes had already been a common method for visualizing the distribution of data.

Gadamer, in Truth and Method, links the hermeneutic circle to the problem of prejudice by arguing that understanding emerges from an ongoing exchange between preconceptions and the phenomena encountered in interpretation. He notes that the Enlightenment project aims to overcome all prejudices universally. Yet this very aspiration can itself be read as a prejudice in its own right, since it prescribes a normative standard for evaluating all viewpoints. Consequently, a central paradox arises: the effort to eradicate prejudice may itself embody a new form of bias.

Truth and Method is a philosophical work by Hans-Georg Gadamer that argues understanding is historically conditioned, since individuals are embedded in and shaped by their histories and cultures. A central idea is the fusion of horizons, whereby interpretation results from the interaction between a text’s historical background and the interpreter’s own situated perspective. Rather than proposing a prescriptive program for a new hermeneutic method, the work presents a descriptive account of the interpretive process. Its aim is to explain what occurs in interpretation from a philosophical standpoint, focusing on the conditions of understanding that exceed the interpreter’s explicit desires or actions.

Within the European Economic Community, efforts to implement a genuine single market faced ongoing enforcement difficulties. The absence of robust decision-making structures and effective governance hindered decisive reform across member states. Protectionist sentiments and vested interests further impeded liberalizing measures. Consequently, replacing intangible trade barriers with widely accepted standards and a common regulatory framework proved challenging, delaying the full integration of markets across the Community.

Scholars have argued that the complete liberalization of capital movements would require a single currency and a shared monetary policy to reduce transaction costs and currency fluctuations. The 1988 Delors Commission report laid the groundwork for the Maastricht Treaty to establish an Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in three stages: completing the internal market, creating the European System of Central Banks to coordinate monetary policy, and fixing exchange rates while introducing a single currency, the euro. As of now, twenty member states use the euro; Bulgaria is in the process of adopting it; Denmark has opted out; and five member states have delayed accession, particularly since the Eurozone crisis. The Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) Articles 119 and 127 require the European Central Bank and other central banks to pursue price stability. This price-stability objective has been criticized as appearing to supersede the EU’s objective of full employment set out in TEU Article 3.

Shock troops, or Stoßtruppen, were German assault formations developed during World War I that employed a von Hutier-style infiltration approach. Their method involved detaching highly trained assault units from the main line to slip through enemy trenches and breach his defenses by penetrating weak points rather than mounting frontal attacks. They were supported by rapid, focused artillery fire aimed at both the front and rear areas to disrupt the enemy's cohesion and command, enabling the infiltrators to operate with reduced frontal resistance. By design, they bypassed strongpoints whenever possible and engaged them only when necessary, leaving decisive confrontation with bypassed positions to follow-on, heavier infantry. The principal objective was to fracture the enemy’s cohesion by creating a breach in the line that could be exploited by the remaining forces. These tactics, embodied by the Stoßtruppen, influenced later infantry doctrine after the war, contributing to developments such as the fire-team concept in postwar military practice.

Companion cavalry were an elite mounted component of Alexander the Great’s forces. Dating to 356–326 BC, they are described as the earliest known example of shock cavalry in Europe, representing a pioneering use of mounted charges to break opposing formations during classical warfare.

There are no surviving records that specify how many people were enslaved by Barbary pirates, including men, women, and children. To gauge the scale, scholars have relied on a rough calculation that estimates the number of new slaves needed each year to maintain a steady slave population in the face of deaths, escapes, ransom, or conversion to Islam. Based on these assumptions, the annual requirement is estimated at about 8,500 new slaves. Extrapolating over the century from 1580 to 1680 yields roughly 850,000 captives, and extending the period from 1530 to 1780 (about 250 years) could raise the upper estimate to as many as 1,250,000.

Following the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815, the Royal Navy no longer required the Barbary states for Gibraltar supplies or for maintaining a Mediterranean fleet, and Britain used this shift to pressure the Barbary powers to end piracy and the enslavement of European Christians. Although treaties were concluded, the Dey of Algiers, Omar Agha, violated the accord when 200 European fishermen under British protection were massacred. In response, an Anglo-Dutch fleet commanded by Admiral Edward Pellew, later Viscount Exmouth, bombarded Algiers in 1816. The Dey capitulated after the allied fleet returned to resume bombardment, and Allied casualties amounted to about 900 dead and wounded. The episode was regarded at the time as more ferocious than the Battle of Trafalgar of 1805.

Puerta del Conde is a historic site that comprises Parque Independencia, a park within El Baluarte del Conde. The park contains the location where Dominican independence was proclaimed in 1844 and is home to the Altar de la Patria. Today it is bounded only by a section of the original defensive wall, La Puerta del Conde. In 1912, architect Antonin Nechodoma redesigned the park to its present state, removing a street that formerly passed through it and facilitating the construction of the Altar de la Patria.

Puerta del Conde, which translates as The Count's Gate, serves as the principal entrance to the fortified city of Santo Domingo in what is today the Dominican Republic. The gate was named to honor Bernardino de Meneses Bracamonte y Zapata, the first Count of Peñalva, who held the office of Governor Captain-General. He is credited with saving the city from a siege in 1655 carried out by English forces under General Robert Venables and Admiral William Penn, during the Third Anglo-Spanish War.
Bugz in the Attic contributed the track "Zombie (Part One)" to Red Hot Organization's tribute album to Fela Kuti, Red Hot and Riot. The group also remixed Zero 7's song "Distractions."

Bugz in the Attic is a West London–based collective of DJs and producers that emerged as a prominent force within the broken beat movement. Its members include Orin Walters (Afronaut), Paul Dolby (Seiji), Kaidi Tatham, Daz-I-Kue, Alex Phountzi (Neon Phusion), Cliff Scott, Mark Force, and Matt Lord. The group was founded in late 1996 and subsequently established the BitaSweet Records label and the BitaSuite recording studio. They also ran a cooperative club night at Plastic People in Shoreditch, London. Over the years, they issued a substantial catalog of singles, remixes, and compilations. The collective's debut album, Back in the Doghouse, was released in July 2006 on V2 Records.

Swan Song is a track performed by Dua Lipa in which the vocal range spans from G3 to D5. The song centers on themes of new beginnings and overcoming obstacles, with the writers drawing inspiration from Alita's fight for marginalized people. Lyrically, it contends that society must articulate its beliefs and injustices and actively use one's voice, aligning with an empowering message drawn from a film. The lyrics were influenced by ACT UP, the 1980s HIV/AIDS activism collective, and the bridge reworks the movement's well-known call that silence can be fatal. The title presents an ironic contrast to its subject matter, while the composition concludes with an abrupt climax and a two-second fade-out.

Reception to "Swan Song" was largely positive among critics. Idolator's Mike Nied described the track as a soaring anthem with epic production and suggested it possessed the potential to dominate the charts for Dua Lipa. Stereogum's Chris DeVille praised its experimental edge and drew a comparison to Lorde's Yellow Flicker Beat (2014). Popjustice's Peter Robinson commended the luxurious, inventive production, noting its economy of texture where appropriate and its dramatic, unpredictable flourishes that culminate in a fade-out. Audacy's Michael Cerio characterized the song as a sweeping epic, building like a battle hymn toward a post-apocalyptic vibe. The track also received formal recognition, being nominated for Best Original Song at the 24th Satellite Awards.

Within the study of Proto-Iranian phonology, the proposed change is not uniform across the Iranian languages. Old Persian and its descendants retain the sibilant /s/ as the reflex, while Kurdish and Balochi are believed to preserve /s/ in some varieties, though this remains uncertain in places. In the Saka languages, the corresponding sound is realized as /š/. By contrast, all other Iranian languages typically exhibit /sp/ as the reflex, or a more distant descendant, such as /fs/ found in Ossetian. This distribution underscores considerable diversification of consonantal outcomes among Iranian languages rather than a single, shared phonological shift.

Proto-Iranian is the reconstructed precursor of the Iranian languages within the Indo-Iranian branch, notable for several distinctive phonological developments inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian. A key feature is the fronting of PIE palatovelars *ḱ, *ǵ (and *ǵʰ) to affricates, realized as *ć and *dź, a stage that is still visible in Nuristani. In Old Iranian, divergent developments are observed: Avestan and most later Iranian languages retain /s/ and /z/, whereas Old Persian exhibits /θ/ and /d/. The ordering of changes implies that the transformation *c > *s must be more recent than the earlier change *s > *h, since the newly arisen /s/ did not undergo the former change. Additionally, the consonant cluster *ts (as in matsya- “fish”) was reduced to a single *c in Iranian.

The hummel, also written as hommel or humle, is an ancient Northern European stringed instrument that bears similarities to an early form of the zither. It is related to the Norwegian langeleik, reflecting its place within the tradition of Nordic stringed instruments.

The hummel is a zither-like instrument that rests on a table in order to amplify its sound. Its melody strings are plucked downward, either with the fingers or with a plectrum. When melody strings are identically tuned, they are often fretted in unison or set to form a major third. A sixth interval can be produced by using the octave string. The strings are typically struck or plucked with a plectrum and are frequently played together, a practice facilitated by the accompaniment strings being tuned to a relatively open chord, such as all strings tuned to D or A.

From 2017 onward, CBS News and BBC News operated a news-sharing agreement, replacing the BBC’s longstanding partnership with ABC News. The arrangement also superseded CBS’s prior deal with Sky News. The Sky News agreement was scheduled to terminate in 2018 following NBCUniversal’s acquisition of Sky News.

From 1973 to 1990, CBS used a distinctive opening title sequence for its animated specials. The seven-second animation preceded each program during that era, featuring the on-screen label A CBS Special Presentation rendered in the ITC Avant Garde typeface. Visual elements presented the word SPECIAL in uppercase, rendered in multiple colors, which would zoom out and then back in as a white word on a black background. The music accompanying the sequence was a jazzy, up-tempo fanfare driven by horns and percussion, edited from Hawaii Five-O's "Call to Danger" (Capitol Records). This sequence appeared immediately before all CBS specials of the period, including Miss USA pageants and the Kennedy Center Honors, in addition to the animated specials.

The 1964 United States Senate election in West Virginia was held on November 3, 1964, concurrently with the 1964 United States presidential election. The incumbent senator, Robert Byrd, sought reelection and won in a landslide.

Incumbent Democrat Robert Byrd sought a second term in the 1964 United States Senate election in West Virginia. The year also featured Lyndon B. Johnson running for re-election as President, and he won West Virginia by a very large margin, contributing to his overall victory in 1964. In the broader electoral outcome, the Democratic Party gained two seats in the United States Senate.

Hard Rock Stadium, a facility primarily used for American football, serves as the venue for the Miami Open tennis tournament. For the event, the center court is established using a modified seating arrangement with temporary grandstands. This center court at the site is reported to have the same seating capacity as Crandon Park’s center court. Spectators have access to the stadium’s luxury seating and suites. In addition, permanent tennis courts were constructed on the stadium’s parking lots, including a new grandstand court.

Over the years, the Miami Open has carried several sponsorship names. In its inaugural year of 1985, the tournament was known as the Lipton International Players Championships and functioned as a premier event on the Grand Prix Tennis Tour. The name was changed to Ericsson Open in 2000, followed by NASDAQ-100 Open in 2002, and then Sony Ericsson Open in 2007. Since 2015 Itaú has been the presenting sponsor.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad Al ash-Sheikh began his professional career in academia after earning his doctorate, serving as a lecturer and later a professor at the Sharia College within Imam Muhammed bin Saud Islamic University. In November 1992 he was appointed minister of justice, succeeding Mohammed bin Jubair. Acting on directives from the king, he drafted the judiciary law enacted in 2007. The reform package proposed the creation of specialized courts that would operate alongside traditional Sharia courts, with particular emphasis on commercial litigation, and it opened the possibility for certain cases to be decided without reference to Sharia. A Supreme Court was also included as part of the reforms. The laws implementing the judicial reforms were passed in October 2007, though their practical implementation progressed slowly.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad Al ash-Sheikh served as Saudi Arabia’s minister of justice and, in July 2008, unveiled a plan of action for judiciary reforms that was submitted to the King. The initiative initially drew little attention and did not become prominent until 2009, when a major cabinet reshuffle led to his removal from the post. On 14 February 2009, Muhammad bin Abdul Karim Issa was appointed to succeed him as justice minister. The reshuffle reflected King Abdullah’s aim to replace conservative incumbents with younger, more progressive figures, and Al ash-Sheikh was described as one of the conservatives in the cabinet who were ousted.

Autumn has repeatedly served as a literary symbol for change, aging, and loss, as reflected in several notable works. In Yeats's The Wild Swans at Coole, the season of maturation functions as a symbol of the ageing self, foreshadowing the approach of old age and death. Verlaine's Chanson d'automne articulates a profoundly somber mood and sorrow associated with autumn. Keats's To Autumn, written in September 1819, interweaves melancholy reflection with an appreciation of the season's abundant natural beauty. The song Autumn Leaves, adapted from Les Feuilles mortes, uses autumn's melancholy and the waning of summer as a metaphor for separation from a loved one. Together these works illustrate autumn's capacity to evoke both elegiac sentiment and sensuous plenitude.

Autumn marks a transitional period in which many summer sport seasons conclude. During this time, sports such as association football in North America, East Asia, and South Africa, Canadian football, stock car racing, tennis, golf, cricket, and professional baseball bring their schedules to a close. The Major League Baseball postseason is commonly known as the Fall Classic. Amateur baseball generally ends by August. At the same time, autumn is associated with the early stages of professional winter sports—ice hockey and basketball—and with the commencement of most European football leagues. In addition, American college basketball and college ice hockey schedule non-conference games in late autumn before conference play begins in winter.

In the Barel case of May 28, 1954, the Conseil d'État addressed the freedom of opinion of civil servants, in the context of several Communists who were refused admission to the École nationale d'administration (ENA). The ruling held that the government cannot exclude applicants for civil service positions solely on the basis of their political convictions, thereby affirming that political beliefs are protected within the process of civil service recruitment.

The Conseil d'État, organized into sections established by a March 2008 order—Finances, Interior, Welfare and Social Security, Public Works, and Administrative Issues—reviews cabinet-issued orders and statutory instruments and examines and signs off on all décrets en Conseil d'État (Orders of Council). These reviews are mandatory but non-binding on the Cabinet. The council also studies legal questions and issues brought before the Cabinet, providing analysis as required. It is responsible for carrying out administrative court inspections, overseeing administrative justice and compliance.

In 2009, AnimalNewYork reported that Complex published a digitally unaltered version of Kim Kardashian's April/May issue cover image on its website. The publication subsequently replaced the image with a retouched version, but the original unedited photo had already gone viral online. Kardashian responded on her blog, stating that she has cellulite and is proud of her body, and she also posted behind-the-scenes photos on her own site. The episode was covered by several online outlets, including Huffington Post, NY Daily News, Business Insider, and Gawker.

In late 2025, ComplexCon, an event produced by Complex Networks, hosted the return of Verzuz, a widely recognized music streaming series. The event was held in Las Vegas and featured a competition between Cash Money Records and No Limit Records.

Strategic offensives in military doctrine refer to major campaigns designed to achieve political and military objectives across a theater, typically involving more than 100,000 troops as part of a broader strategic plan. A prominent example is Operation Barbarossa, a theater offensive that comprised three interconnected campaigns across the southern, central, and northern sectors of Soviet territory. During World War II, Soviet strategic offensives frequently entailed multi-front, coordinated operations spanning multiple theaters. Alongside the Wehrmacht’s campaigns on the Eastern Front, these operations rank among the largest military undertakings of the twentieth century. Historians also document these large-scale Soviet actions in a catalog titled Strategic operations of the Red Army in World War II.

A strategic offensive denotes the deliberate articulation of wartime planning that mobilizes strategic forces as a unified whole and marshals all available resources. Its aim is to secure defined, decisive objectives capable of altering the balance of power between the belligerents. The planning and execution of such offensives rest on theoretical considerations, because full-scale rehearsals of large operations are typically impractical, cost-prohibitive, and difficult to conceal.

The Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity railway is an east–west regional line that begins at Panyu railway station in Guangzhou’s Panyu District, near Guangzhou South, and proceeds eastward beneath the Pearl River, passing through Machong and Hongmei to reach Dongguan West in Dongguan’s Hongmei area. It is planned to function as a major interchange with the Guangzhou–Shenzhen intercity railway and Dongguan Metro Line 1, with a target opening in 2025. The alignment then traverses Dongguan eastward through Daojiao, Nancheng, Dongcheng, Liaobu, Songshan Lake, Dalang, Changping, and Xiegang before crossing into Huizhou’s Huicheng District, where it serves Lilin, Chenjiang, and Huihuan prior to arriving at Huizhou railway station, after which it veers northwest to terminate at Huizhou North railway station. The total length is 146.6 km (91.1 mi), with Guangzhou contributing 31.952 km (19.854 mi) of the route, Dongguan 78.160 km (48.566 mi), and Huizhou 38.808 km (24.114 mi). Of the total, elevated sections amount to 79.563 km (49.438 mi), ground-level segments to 6.586 km (4.092 mi), and underground sections to 60.43 km (37.55 mi).

Within the Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity railway project, the initial plan designated sixteen stations. Subsequently, Huizhou Municipal Railway Construction Investment Group Co., Ltd. and Guangzhou Railway Company reached an agreement to add an additional stop, with the new station situated in West Lake, Huizhou. As a result, the number of planned stations increased to seventeen. The modification underscores ongoing collaboration between the two companies in the development of the Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity railway.

PepsiCo's Latin America Foods segment markets and distributes primarily Quaker- and Frito-Lay/Sabritas/Elma Chips-branded snacks across Mexico, Central and South America, including Argentina, Brazil, Peru, and other regional markets. In 2009, Snacks América Latina acquired Karinto S.A.C., a Peru-based company (along with its production arm Bocaditas Nacionales) from the Hayashida family of Lima; Bocaditas Nacionales operates three production facilities in Peru. The acquisition expanded Snacks América Latina's portfolio by introducing the Karito brand, alongside existing lines such as Cuates, Fripapas, and Papi Frits.

On October 1, 2024, PepsiCo announced its plan to acquire Siete Foods for a purchase price of $1.2 billion, identifying Siete Foods as the target company of the transaction. The deal was completed on January 17, 2025.

Beginning in February 2005, Billboard began incorporating data on paid digital song downloads from major retailers such as iTunes, Musicmatch, and Rhapsody into the Hot 100 chart. Digital download tracking had already been introduced in 2003 with the Hot Digital Tracks chart, but those downloads were not counted toward the Hot 100. The Hot Digital Tracks metric treated each version of a song as a separate entry, in contrast to the later Hot Digital Songs system. This shift marked the Hot 100’s first substantial revision of its chart formula since December 1998.

In the August 11, 2007 issue, Billboard began incorporating weekly data from streaming media and on-demand services into the Hot 100, with AOL Music and Yahoo! Music acting as the first major services to contribute their statistics to Nielsen BDS on a weekly basis. On March 24, 2012, Billboard introduced the On-Demand Songs chart, which ranked web radio streams from services such as Spotify and other on-demand audio titles. Data from the On-Demand Songs chart was subsequently integrated into the Hot 100 calculation, and the broader Streaming Songs chart was launched in January 2013. In February 2013, U.S. YouTube views were added to the Hot 100 formula, and following these changes, "Harlem Shake" became the first song to reach number one under the revised methodology.

Stadia, known in ancient Greek as Στάδια, was an ancient town in the region of Caria. It later developed into a Christian bishopric. Although it no longer serves as the seat of a residential bishop, it continues to be listed as a titular see of the Roman Catholic Church.

In the study of partially ordered sets, a Hasse diagram is a conventional graphical representation of the cover relations. It is NP-complete to decide whether a given partial order with multiple sources and sinks can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings, i.e., as a crossing-free Hasse diagram. A crossing-free Hasse diagram is a planar drawing in which no two edges intersect. The computational landscape changes when the problem is examined through the lens of parameterized complexity: it is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by certain structural features of the transitive reduction of the partial order. The pertinent parameters are the number of articulation points and the number of triconnected components of the transitive reduction. It should be noted that these results pertain to the transitive reduction of the partial order rather than to the partial order itself.

Hasse diagrams offer a visual representation of partially ordered sets by illustrating their cover relations, and the power set of a finite set, ordered by inclusion, forms a graded poset as demonstrated by the first diagram. A subsequent diagram preserves the graded structure but uses longer edges to emphasize a decomposition in which the four-dimensional cube is seen as the combinatorial union of two three-dimensional cubes, and a tetrahedron corresponds to the merger of two triangles within the framework of abstract polytopes. A third diagram reveals some of the internal symmetry inherent in the structure. The fourth diagram arranges the vertices in a 4-by-4 grid.

A URL is an address that identifies a resource on the World Wide Web. A Persistent URL, or PURL, is a web address that redirects to the resource’s current location, thereby separating the identifier from its location. If the resource moves, the PURL can be redirected or updated to point to the new address, allowing users to continue using the same URL. PURLs can be utilized by publishers or Web users to manage information spaces, and the PURL service operates independently of any particular publisher. By enabling reliable redirection, PURLs support the management of hyperlink integrity, a consideration in Web design that can be partially restored by permitting users or third parties to influence how URLs are resolved.

Within the PURL framework, a PURL assigned the type '200' is categorized as an Active PURL. Active PURLs contribute to the creation or aggregation of the metadata they return and incorporate internal computation to determine their output. The concept has been implemented in PURLz 2.0 and The Callimachus Project. They are used to gather runtime status reports, to perform distributed queries, and to support other data-collection tasks where a persistent identifier is desired. In practice, Active PURLs function similarly to stored procedures in relational databases.

Michael Mortensen is a former professional tennis player who attained a career-best doubles ranking of world No. 34 in 1988 and achieved his highest singles ranking of world No. 301 in 1984. Over his career, he claimed five ATP doubles titles.

Michael Mortensen is a Danish former professional tennis player who represented Denmark in Davis Cup competition. He took part in 22 Davis Cup ties from 1979 to 1990, and his records in the event include an 11–13 mark in doubles and a 12–14 record in singles.

ARJ, whose acronym stands for Archived by Robert Jung, is a file archiver designed in 1991 by Robert K. Jung to create highly efficient compressed archives. The software has been released in platform-specific builds, with current versions including 2.86 for MS-DOS and 3.31 for Microsoft Windows. It supports 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit Intel architectures, enabling operation across a range of hardware configurations.

ARJ is a data compression program designed for MS-DOS and Windows platforms. In the early to mid-1990s it was used as part of a broader family of archival tools commonly employed on personal computers. Portions of ARJ were covered by U.S. patent 5,140,321, which has since expired. The software is known for its thorough documentation. It offers an extensive set of command-line options, with more than 150 switches, giving users granular control over archiving and extraction processes.

My Scene Goes Hollywood: The Movie is a film in which production was interrupted when an actress was injured en route to the set and unable to perform. Madison was subsequently called in to replace her. The replaced actress had been slated to portray the movie's lead female villain, a role consisting of five speaking lines.

Critical response to My Scene Goes Hollywood: The Movie was largely unfavorable. Lacey Worrell of DVDTalk described the plot as thin and lacking depth, while arguing that Lindsay Lohan’s frequent overexposure diminishes the impact of her acting talents. The story was seen as relying on a clichéd friends-for-ever premise, deemed unoriginal and reminiscent of the Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen brand. Performances were characterized as wooden, and the film’s message was criticized for implying that people of any race or ethnicity can be as vacuous as the Barbie stereotype. In addition, the presentation was labeled vapid and unrealistic, crossing into the inane. Although the reviewer acknowledged that not all children’s entertainment must be educational, they called for more substance paired with style in future works.

Malaccamax denotes the largest ship size able to traverse the Strait of Malacca, whose depth restricts passage to about 25 metres (approximately 82 feet). The designation applies to bulk carriers and supertankers, and is frequently used in reference to very large crude carriers (VLCCs). In practice, Malaccamax vessels are employed to transport oil from Arabia to China. Typical Malaccamax tankers measure up to around 333 metres in length, with a beam near 60 metres, a draught of roughly 20.5 metres, and a deadweight tonnage of about 300,000 DWT.

Malaccamax denotes the largest class of vessels that can safely traverse the Strait of Malacca, a key chokepoint linking the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. The concept parallels other size-based designations tied to specific waterways, such as Panamax for ships able to pass through the Panama Canal, Suezmax for those able to transit the Suez Canal, and Seawaymax for vessels capable of navigating the Saint Lawrence Seaway. In the same framework of vessel-size classifications, Aframax tankers are defined as ships with a deadweight tonnage ranging from 80,000 to 120,000.

Within the Soyuz-7 (rocket family), on 5 October 2020 a contract was signed for the preliminary design phase of the Amur rocket program. The project aims to establish Russia’s first reusable methane-powered launch vehicle, with design objectives that emphasize high reliability, an operational launch cost target of approximately US$22 million, a reusable first stage, and an expendable second stage.

Soyuz-7 was a proposed family of Russian orbital launch vehicles developed by JSC SRC Progress in the mid-2010s as a successor to the legacy Soyuz after the early 2020s. SRC Progress, which for decades has manufactured and maintained the Soyuz design, framed the initiative within Project Feniks (Феникс, “Phoenix”). The 2013 designation of Soyuz-7 signified a ground‑up redesign not derived from the R‑7 heritage, incorporating liquid oxygen and methane propulsion, a new tank architecture, and revised propulsion systems. The concept called for discarding the Korolev Cross arrangement and implementing thrust vector control in the main engine instead of separate vernier units. Conceived as a scalable trio, the family would span medium to heavy payload applications and was intended to cover three versions aligned with varying mission requirements.

PACCAR expanded internationally in the early 1970s, establishing an overseas manufacturing facility at Bayswater, Melbourne, in 1970 to produce Kenworth Trucks for Australian and Southeast Asian markets; the first locally built truck rolled off the Melbourne line in March 1971, and by 1975 Australian-made vehicle exports had commenced. Despite a slowdown during the 1974 recessions, PACCAR’s sales continued to rise through the decade. In 1975 the company acquired Wagner Mining Company, which produced underground mining vehicles, and International Car Company, while PACCAR International had been formed in 1972 to promote exports worldwide. In 1980 PACCAR established the Paccar Technical Center at Mount Vernon, Washington, featuring test tracks, engine test cells, and materials and structural laboratories, with an Open House held every April in conjunction with the Skagit Valley Tulip Festival; that same year the company acquired British truck manufacturer Foden Trucks, broadening its presence in Europe and Africa. In 1983 the International Car Co Division in Kenton, Ohio (acquired in 1975) was disbanded, as were Paccar Rail Leasing Inc in Renton and RAILEASE Inc in Bellevue. In 1986 the Pacific Car and Foundry subsidiary in Renton was renamed the Paccar Defense Systems Division. Earlier, in 1984 PACCAR posted record sales of $2.25 billion.

Founded in 1905 by William Pigott Sr. as the Seattle Car Manufacturing Company with a capital of $10,000, the firm initially produced railway and logging equipment. After a fire at its Duwamish facility, a new factory was erected in Renton in 1909 to fulfill growing orders. In 1917, it merged with Portland's Twohy Brothers to form the Pacific Car and Foundry Company, with Twohy Brothers remaining its only west-coast competitor. Early products included horse- or ox-drawn logging trucks designed to haul large logs through the Northwest's dense, hilly forests. Subsequently the company specialized in air brakes, open freight cars, refrigerated boxcars, and the universal trailer towed by trucks. It also manufactured hand-finished structural steel used in Seattle-area buildings, including columns and girders. In 1924 William Pigott sold a controlling stake to American Car and Foundry Company, and in 1934 Paul Pigott reacquired a substantial interest from ACF.

Quebec encompasses a total forest area of roughly 750,300 square kilometres (289,700 square miles). In the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region along the North Shore, the forests are predominantly coniferous, featuring species such as balsam fir, jack pine, white spruce, black spruce, and tamarack. By contrast, the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence Lowlands are characterized by deciduous forests dominated by sugar maple, red maple, white ash, American beech, butternut (white walnut), American elm, basswood, bitternut hickory, and northern red oak, with some conifers including eastern white pine and northern whitecedar. Additionally, paper birch, trembling aspen, and mountain ash cover more than half of Quebec's territory.

From the mid-19th century until the onset of the Great Depression, Quebec experienced a pronounced outflow of residents known as the Grande Hémorragie, or Great Hemorrhaging, in which roughly 900,000 Quebecers emigrated to the United States, particularly New England. The emigrants formed dispersed communities termed Little Canadas within several industrial centers across New England. Although a substantial portion eventually returned to Quebec—about half by some estimates—the survivors and their descendants in the United States largely assimilated over time. Today, most of the later-generation descendants who remained have been assimilated into the broader American society, and only a minority of Franco-Americans persists, with some continuing to speak New England French.

In South Carolina, magistrates are appointed for four-year terms by the governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. A former governor indicated that state senators largely control the appointment process. Magistrates serve the county in which they are appointed and hold county-wide jurisdiction. They preside over civil and criminal cases, issue restraining orders, search and arrest warrants, and conduct bond hearings, excluding the most serious offenses such as murder. They conduct preliminary hearings, bench trials, and jury trials. The state has more than 300 magistrates, and the majority have had no prior legal training. Legislation in the state Senate seeks to reform how magistrates are chosen.

In Kentucky, magistrates are elected for four-year terms to serve on the county's Fiscal Court, which is presided over by an elected County Judge-Executive and is functionally akin to a county commission. Counties are subdivided into districts, and residents of each district elect a magistrate to represent them on the Fiscal Court. Under the original Kentucky constitution, the Fiscal Court possessed both judicial and legislative powers for the county; the current constitution reallocates powers so that the Fiscal Court exercises only legislative authority, while the Judge-Executive executes the county’s administrative functions. In some counties, the role of magistrates on the Fiscal Court has been replaced by three at-large County Commissioners alongside the County Judge-Executive, though the magistrates remain elected; their duties in those counties are limited to officiating marriage ceremonies.

Anugerah Planet Muzik (APM) is an annual awards ceremony organized by MediaCorp’s Malay Broadcast Division in collaboration with its radio networks Suria, Warna 94.2FM, and Ria 89.7FM. The event honors achievements in the regional Malay-Indonesian music industry, recognizing artists and productions across Singapore and neighboring markets. It is supported by the Media Development Authority of Singapore (MDA), the Composers and Authors Society of Singapore (COMPASS), and the Indonesian Music Award Foundation (YAMI).

Anugerah Planet Muzik is a regional music awards ceremony that first took place in 2001 and has been held annually since, except in 2010 and 2019. The awards encompass a variety of categories that cover all participating countries, and there are awards that are specifically designated for individual countries.

Grand Tower is a high-rise residential building in Frankfurt am Main that is notable for being Germany’s first such tower marketed on a global scale. The international marketing strategy targeted a diverse set of regions, with Asia, the Arab world, and North America identified as the principal markets.

Grand Tower, formerly Tower 2, is a high‑rise building in the Europaviertel district of Frankfurt am Main, Germany. Completed in 2020, the structure rises to 180 meters (590 feet), making it Germany's tallest residential building at the time and surpassing Cologne's Colonia-Haus, which stands at 147 meters and was completed in 1973. The tower is situated adjacent to the Skyline-Plaza shopping center. The project was developed with an estimated total investment of around €250 million.

The Cardiff Blitz, known in Welsh as Blitz Caerdydd, denotes the bombing of Cardiff, Wales, during World War II. The attacks occurred from 1940 until the final raid in March 1944. Approximately 2,100 bombs fell on Cardiff, and 355 people were killed.

The Cardiff Blitz refers to a series of Luftwaffe bombing raids on Cardiff, Wales, during the Second World War. In 1940, the city was struck on 3 July, 10 July, 12 July, and 7 August, and in 1941 raids followed on 2 January, 3 January, and 10 January. On the night of 2 January 1941, more than a hundred German bombers mounted a prolonged assault lasting about ten hours, beginning at 6:37 p.m. The attacks involved high-explosive bombs, incendiaries, and parachute mines. The initial impact fell on the Riverside district, and in Grangetown the Hollyman Brothers bakery was damaged by a parachute mine, resulting in the deaths of 32 people sheltering in the basement. In total, the raid left 165 people dead and 427 injured, with nearly 350 homes destroyed or demolished.

Within the Republican Party of the United States, notable elected officials include U.S. Senators Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Susan Collins of Maine; governors Joe Lombardo of Nevada, Phil Scott of Vermont, and Larry Hogan, a former governor of Maryland; and Kelly Ayotte, a prominent New Hampshire Republican who has served as state attorney general and later as a U.S. senator.

Since 2005, the Supreme Court has been known as the Roberts Court, reflecting Chief Justice John Roberts's leadership. By 2024, three of its members had been appointed by President Donald Trump, illustrating the enduring influence of the Republican Party on the judiciary. The court has frequently been described as the most conservative since the Vinson Court (1946–1953), marking a notable conservative tilt relative to earlier eras. Some observers regard the Roberts Court as representing the last phase of the traditional Republican establishment's dominance in national politics. Roberts was the only Republican leader to have remained in office into the second term of a Republican president, providing continuity on the Court during Trump's tenure.

In the track's second verse, Madonna observes the sun setting, resolves not to flee from madness, and pledges to continue moving forward. The verse includes a reference to the Tower of Babylon. It also reflects on changes within the music industry, portraying the vocalist as a stranger in a strange land and expressing a sense of being caught between opposing contradictions. The section culminates with a desert metaphor for life, describing an oasis as a source of further confusion.

Wash All Over Me is a track by Madonna that experienced an early demo and the completed recording leaking online prior to the album's release. The official version was issued on March 6, 2015. A preceding mix, rooted in disco and house influences, was subsequently reworked for the album cut. Lyrically, the song sees Madonna confronting insecurities, the release itself, and reflections on her longevity in the music industry. Critics generally received the recording favorably, often drawing parallels to material from Like a Prayer, Ray of Light, and Confessions on a Dance Floor.

The article discusses the live album I Heard They Suck Live!! by the American punk rock band NOFX, and notes that the sole track not originally issued on a NOFX album is "Nothing but a Nightmare (sorta)," which is a cover of a Rudimentary Peni song.

Track 19 on I Heard They Suck Live!! is titled “(Crowd Leaves)” and is occasionally credited as “Outro.” The track features Nina Simone performing the standard “Love Me or Leave Me” (composed by Donaldson and Kahn), which is played over the public address system.

The flugelhorn is a brass instrument that resembles the trumpet and cornet but features a wider, more conical bore. It is typically pitched in B-flat, though some examples exist in C. Classified as a valved bugle, it developed in Germany in the early nineteenth century from the traditional English valveless bugle. The first valved bugle was marketed by Heinrich Stölzel in Berlin in 1828. This innovation influenced Adolphe Sax to design his B-flat soprano (contralto) saxhorns, on which the modern-day flugelhorn is modeled.

Within Dutch and Belgian fanfare orchestras (fanfareorkesten), the flugelhorn occupies a central role in shaping the ensemble’s characteristic sound. Typically between ten and twenty flugelhorns are employed, forming the backbone of the horn section and providing the foundational sonority of the orchestra. The instruments are normally pitched in B♭, with occasional solo parts written for E♭ players. Due to tuning challenges associated with E♭ flugelhorns, many ensembles replace them with E♭ trumpets or cornets to preserve accurate intonation across the section.

Border Security: Australia’s Front Line is an Australian television series that follows border-control officers as they monitor entry points such as airports and seaports. The program served as the basis for an American adaptation titled Homeland Security USA. The American edition began broadcasting in 2009 and consisted of thirteen episodes, with two episodes ultimately not aired.

Border Security: Australia's Front Line is a television series that is broadcast in several markets in Asia, including Hong Kong, Malaysia, South Korea, Thailand, and Macau. In Singapore, the program is shown on Fox Crime. In Canada, it is aired on BBC Canada and DTour.
The Rail to Rail Active Transportation Corridor Project developed a rail trail in Los Angeles County, California, United States, and is owned by the Los Angeles Metro.

The Rail to River Active Transportation Corridor Project, commonly identified as Segment B, is a proposed extension within a broader multi-segment initiative. As Segment B, the plan would traverse portions of Huntington Park, Vernon, Maywood, and Bell in the Gateway Cities area, with the aim of linking to the Los Angeles River bike trails. It is conceived as an active transportation corridor emphasizing bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure. The proposal represents one component of a larger project that comprises several segments.

National-anarchism in its early phase was associated with figures such as Hans Cany, Peter Töpfer, and Troy Southgate, with Southgate later founding the National Revolutionary Faction, a British-based organization that linked far-left and far-right circles in the UK and in post-Soviet states, though this faction is distinct from the national-anarchism associated with the Black Ram Group. In the United Kingdom, national-anarchists collaborated with groups including Albion Awake and Alternative Green (the latter edited by Richard Hunt, a former editor of Green Anarchist) and with Jonathan Boulter to develop the Anarchist Heretics Fair. The movement's proponents have cited a range of influences—Mikhail Bakunin, William Godwin, Peter Kropotkin, Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, Max Stirner, and Leo Tolstoy—as formative figures in their synthesis of nationalist and anarchist ideas.

Nationalism in Spain, as it emerged in the wake of the War of the Spanish Succession, drew on the centralizing impulses associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares and the absolutist program of Philip V. The Decrees of Nova Planta, which integrated the Crown of Aragon into the Castilian crown, marked the first formal step toward a centralized Spanish nation-state. Unification was accomplished through political consolidation rather than ethnic homogenization, with Castilian political and cultural norms imposed upon other communities. Consequently, other ethnic groups were treated as national minorities to be assimilated. Since 1714, assimilation policies toward Catalan-speaking regions—Catalonia, Valencia, the Balearic Islands, and parts of Aragon—as well as toward other minorities such as the Basques and Galicians, have constituted a persistent feature of the Spanish state.

Bill Coleman was an American jazz trumpeter who rejoined Cecil Scott's Bright Boys, the group led by the Scott brothers, in late 1929, and participated in a Victor recording session with the ensemble. He remained with the Bright Boys through early 1930, after which he worked with various New York-based bands. In 1931 he rejoined Luis Russell's orchestra.

Bill Coleman, a trumpeter, was awarded the Ordre National du Mérite in 1974. His autobiography, initially published under the title Trumpet Story, was translated into French by his wife Lily and released in 1981 by Cana éditions. An English edition followed in 1989 from Palgrave-Macmillan in the United Kingdom. In 2004 a heavily illustrated edition with numerous original photographs appeared from Mémoires d'Oc éditions, bearing the title De Paris (Kentucky) à Paris (France), ma trompette sous le bras (From Paris (Kentucky) to Paris (France), with my trumpet under my arm).

Detroit is a major transportation hub in North America, situated near the Canadian border and reinforced by a comprehensive network of facilities including ports, highways, rail infrastructure, and international airports that collectively enable substantial cross-border movement. The city maintains three international border crossings to Windsor, Ontario: the Ambassador Bridge, the Detroit–Windsor Tunnel, and the Michigan Central Railway Tunnel. Among these, the Ambassador Bridge stands as the busiest border crossing in North America. Collectively, these facilities handle a significant share of cross-border trade, with the Ambassador Bridge accounting for roughly 27 percent of total U.S.–Canada trade.

Detroit emerged as a major center of the automotive industry when Henry Ford founded the Ford Motor Company in 1903. Alongside William C. Durant, the Dodge brothers, James and William Packard, and Walter Chrysler, Ford and these pioneering figures helped lay the groundwork for the Big Three automakers. By the early 20th century Detroit had established itself as the world's automotive capital, a status that spurred the growth of adjacent businesses such as garages, gas stations, and component factories. The booming industry attracted workers and supported rapid population growth, and by 1920 the city had risen to the fourth-largest in the United States.

WSB (AM 750 kHz) is a commercial radio station based in Atlanta, Georgia, broadcasting a news and talk format and simulcasting with 95.5 WSBB-FM. Alongside WSBB-FM, WSB serves as a flagship station for Cox Media Group, which also owns three additional Atlanta radio outlets and WSB-TV. The station is regarded as one of the highest-billing radio properties in the United States. Its studios and offices are located in the WSB Television and Radio Group Building on West Peachtree Street in Midtown Atlanta.

Scott Slade served as the host of Atlanta's Morning News on WSB (AM) until February 2023, when he stepped back from full-time hosting. He was succeeded by Chris Chandler, the station's evening news anchor, though Slade remains semi-retired and continues to fill in as needed. In April 2023, Marcy Williams, who had led the morning news program for 31 years, retired from WSB. Williams had written more than 300,000 radio news stories during her tenure.

The Polaris Program is a private human spaceflight initiative organized by entrepreneur Jared Isaacman. It builds on Isaacman's experience as commander of the Inspiration4 mission, the first all-civilian spaceflight. Isaacman contracted SpaceX to establish the program, which comprises two missions flown aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon spacecraft and aims to culminate in the first crewed launch on SpaceX's Starship. Polaris Dawn, the first mission, launched in 2024 and featured the first commercial spacewalk. Isaacman was nominated to serve as Administrator of NASA; if confirmed, he would cancel his SpaceX contract for the additional missions to avoid a conflict of interest with one of NASA's largest contractors.

Polaris Dawn, the inaugural flight of the Polaris Program, launched on 10 September 2024 with a crew comprising Isaacman, Scott Poteet, Sarah Gillis, and Anna Menon. The spacecraft entered an elliptical Earth orbit at an altitude of about 1,400 kilometers (approximately 870 miles). The mission marked the farthest distance from Earth reached by humans since NASA's Apollo program, and the trajectory included passing through portions of the Van Allen radiation belts. Its primary objective was to study the health effects of space radiation and spaceflight on the human body. Later in the mission, after reducing the apogee, Isaacman and Gillis completed the first commercial spacewalk, an EVA that tested mobility and functionality of SpaceX's EVA spacesuit.

During the early 1970s, Qadsia Sporting Club captured its second Kuwaiti Premier League title by winning the 1970–71 season. In contrast, Al-Arabi endured a championship drought that stretched for about a decade, a period without a league crown. This drought for Al-Arabi persisted until the end of the 1979–80 season, when the club secured the title again.

During the season, the Kuwaiti Premier League reduced its number of participating clubs to seven for the following campaign. Al-Arabi secured its second consecutive league title, finishing 18 points clear of the runners-up Qadsia. The champions boasted a potent attack, scoring 45 goals while conceding only six.

Symphony Towers is a downtown development that opened in 1989. It was developed through a partnership between Douglas P. Wilson, the chairman and CEO of Douglas Wilson Companies (DWC), and Charlton Raynd Ventures. In 1988, during construction, the project stalled and was acquired by London & Edinburgh Investment, Inc., a subsidiary of the London-listed London & Edinburgh Trust PLC. After the acquisition, construction was completed and the office building was fully leased. The project was retained by LEI and Charlton Raynd as an investment for several years. The building was designed by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill. Symphony Towers is widely seen as one of downtown's premier locations.

Symphony Towers is a late modernist, two-tower mixed-use hotel and office complex in the Financial District of downtown San Diego, California. The complex encompasses about 1.2 million square feet of total floor space and includes a 34-story office tower offering around 530,000 square feet of leasable space. It also houses the 264-room Marriott Vacation Club Pulse San Diego, a five-level parking structure, and the Jacobs Music Center, which seats 2,255. The penthouse level is occupied by the University Club, a private members’ club, and the complex features a rooftop helipad.

Roy Strong began his career at the National Portrait Gallery, London, as assistant keeper in 1959 and was appointed director in 1967 at the age of thirty-two, a post he held until 1973. As director, he broadened the gallery’s traditional image through high-profile, outward-facing exhibitions, including a major retrospective of Cecil Beaton consisting of 600 portraits spanning 1928–1968. In 1974, he organized a presentation at the Victoria and Albert Museum featuring fedora hats, kipper ties and maxi coats that reflected 1960s and 1970s culture. Under his leadership, the regular introduction of new exhibitions contributed to a doubling of attendance.

Roy Strong married the theatrical designer Julia Trevelyan Oman on 10 September 1971. At the time, she was 41 years old. The wedding ceremony was held at Wilmcote church, near Stratford-upon-Avon, under a special licence granted by the Archbishop of Canterbury. The couple later enjoyed a belated honeymoon in Tuscany. Julia Trevelyan Oman died in 2003 of pancreatic cancer.

Marais des Cygnes River flows through Osage County, Kansas. A dam on the river, constructed by the United States Army Corps of Engineers, impounds water to form Melvern Lake. The resulting reservoir hosts Eisenhower State Park along its shores.

Marais des Cygnes River is notable for its propensity toward flash flooding, with rapid rises in water levels during severe rainfall events. It is mentioned in Chely Wright’s song "The River." The Kansas communities of La Cygne in Linn County and Osawatomie in Miami County are among those most severely affected by floods associated with the river.

The Olivetti Quaderno was described in a 1993 review as a DOS‑compatible machine powered by an NEC V30 processor, with performance comparable to an Intel 8086. Its standout feature was the ability to digitize and record dictation using a built‑in microphone, with the recording controlled by cassette‑deck style controls located on the top of the case. When equipped with the internal fax modem connected to the telephone network, it could function as an answering machine and record voice messages. The system offered expansion options including serial and parallel ports, video output, and a dual‑purpose port that could serve either as a modem connection or for a PS/2 keyboard and mouse. The sockets used a proprietary Olivetti design requiring special cables costing about £10 each (roughly £26 in 2023 terms). Using the fax modem also required additional software costing around £80 (about £209 in 2023 terms), and the software price for the fax modem was regarded as exploitative.

Olivetti Quaderno was a concept laptop introduced by Olivetti in 1992, notable for its A5-sized footprint and approximate weight of 1 kilogram. The initial model featured a relatively capable processor and included distinctive elements such as a built-in microphone and integrated amplifiers. Its commercial failure has been attributed to the limitations of the operating system and bundled software, which did not fully exploit the device’s potential. A year later Olivetti released a revised variant, the Quaderno 33, which was equipped with Windows 3.1.

Cherenkov radiation arises when a charged particle moves through a dielectric medium at a speed exceeding the medium’s light phase velocity, producing a coherent emission that propagates as a cone around the particle’s path. Geometrically, the emitted wavefronts can be represented by a series of similar triangles formed at successive times, with the ratio linking the particle’s displacement to the wavefront radius remaining constant regardless of the chosen time; consequently, these triangles are similar for any time value. This leads to a constant Cherenkov angle, meaning the angular relation between the particle’s trajectory and the emitted light does not vary across the time slices. When one considers emissions from the initial moment up to an arbitrary final time t, the resulting wavefronts again outline similar triangles whose right endpoints converge at a common reference point, illustrating how the expanding fronts preserve their proportional geometry. This time-invariant geometric structure underpins the characteristic radiation pattern and angle observed in Cherenkov radiation.

Historically, Oliver Heaviside, in 1888–1889, envisaged an emanation forming cone-shaped wavefronts around a fast-moving charge, a prediction later echoed by Arnold Sommerfeld in 1904. However, these theoretical insights were largely dismissed after the advent of special relativity, which restricted particles to subluminal speeds, a view that persisted into the 1970s. In 1910, Marie Curie observed a pale-blue glow from a highly concentrated radium solution but did not pursue its origin. Subsequently, in 1926, Lucien Mallet described the luminous emission produced when radium irradiates water, noting that the spectrum was continuous. Together, these early observations and ideas reflect prewar hints and scientific debate surrounding what would later be understood as Cherenkov radiation, a phenomenon that would be named and explained in subsequent decades.

Bob Filner, along with several senior U.S. officials, argued that the MEK should have its terrorist designation removed. He regarded the MEK, a major member of the National Council of Resistance of Iran, as an ally in the effort to oppose the Iranian regime. In line with these views, the U.S. Department of State lifted the MEK’s designation as a terrorist organization on September 28, 2012.

Bob Filner served on the U.S. House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and rose to the chairmanship after Democrats gained the House in the 2006 elections.
