In that role, he pressed for increased funding for veterans' benefits, greater spending on veterans' healthcare, and the enactment of a new GI Bill for Afghanistan- and Iraq-era veterans. Following the 2010 elections, as Republicans won the majority, he remained on the committee as the ranking Democrat.

Pupienus was a member of a twenty-man Senate committee appointed to coordinate operations against Maximinus Thrax until the Gordians could arrive, reflecting his involvement in the crisis following the proclamation of Gordian I and Gordian II as emperors in Africa. After news reached Rome of the Gordians' defeat and deaths, the Senate met in closed session at the Temple of Jupiter Capitolinus to determine the succession. From the committee, Pupienus and Balbinus were selected as co-emperors. Unlike the situation in 161, both were elevated to the rank of pontifex maximus, chief priests of the official cults.

Balbinus and Pupienus ruled as co-emperors for ninety-nine days, during which Balbinus struggled to maintain public order in the capital. Balbinus grew suspicious that Pupienus intended to supplant him by leveraging Pupienus’s German bodyguard. The two resided in different wings of the Imperial palace, a division that left them vulnerable to the Praetorian Guard. The guard, resentful of serving rulers appointed by the Senate, plotted their murders. When Pupienus learned of the threat, he urged Balbinus to call in the German bodyguards; Balbinus refused, believing the move to be part of a Pupienus plot against him. The two argued as the Praetorians burst into the chamber, seized them, and dragged them to the Praetorian barracks, where they were tortured and killed in the bathhouse. Their joint rule lasted only 99 days.

No More Mr. Nice Guy is a 1996 instrumental album by Steve Wariner and marks his final release for Arista Records. The collection comprises twelve instrumental tracks and did not produce any singles. The track The Brickyard Boogie was nominated for Best Country Instrumental at the 1997 Grammy Awards and features Derek George (a former Pearl River member who later founded Williams Riley), Jeffrey Steele (a former Boy Howdy member), Bryan White, and Bryan Austin. Another track, Hap Towne Breakdowne, includes Jimmy Olander, the guitarist from Diamond Rio.

Historically, Sparidae was divided into six subfamilies—Boopsinae, Denticinae, Diplodinae, Pagellinae, Pagrinae, and Sparinae—but these groups did not consistently resolve as monophyletic in phylogenetic analyses. More recent evidence indicates that the family is monophyletic only when the genus Spicara, which was formerly placed in Centracanthidae, is included within Sparidae. Incorporating Spicara further implies the inclusion of Centracanthus within Sparidae, resulting in Centracanthidae being treated as a junior synonym of Sparidae. This revised circumscription reflects an updated understanding of the evolutionary relationships within the group.

Sparidae, a family of marine fishes commonly called breams, are predominantly predatory, feeding mainly on benthic invertebrates. In terms of social behavior, smaller species and juveniles of larger species often form schools, while large adults are typically solitary or less social and prefer deeper waters. Ontogenetic changes are evident in morphology and colour patterns, with juveniles and subadults frequently differing in shape and often displaying more vivid coloration. The reproductive biology of many sparids is hermaphroditic, with some individuals possessing both male and female gonads simultaneously, and others undergoing sex change as they grow, transitioning from male to female or from female to male.

The B-side of the single Longneck Bottle is "Rollin'," an album track from Brooks's last studio release, Fresh Horses (1995). "Rollin'" subsequently charted on the Billboard country charts in late 1995, reaching No. 71 for the chart week of December 9.

Longneck Bottle entered the Canadian RPM Country Tracks chart at number sixty for the week of December 1, 1997, and rose to the top the following week, dated December 8, 1997. It maintained the No. 1 position through the December 15, 1997 chart, while the chart weeks for December 22, December 29, and January 5, 1998 were frozen. The song remained at No. 1 in the January 12, 1998 issue, but on January 19, 1998 it slipped to No. 2 as Shania Twain’s Don't Be Stupid (You Know I Love You) overtook it. It reclaimed the No. 1 spot on January 26, 1998, for its fourth and final week atop the RPM Country Tracks chart.

Species in the genus Gymnocranius, commonly called emperors, inhabit the Indo-West Pacific region. Their distribution runs from the coasts of eastern Africa and the Indian Ocean to the western and central Pacific Ocean. These fishes usually occupy depths from about 10 to 80 meters and prefer sandy or rubble substrates along continental shores. In certain cases, individuals can be found off islands as well.

Gymnocranius was established by Carl Benjamin Klunzinger in 1870 as a monotypic genus, with its sole species at that time being Dentex rivulatus. Dentex rivulatus had been described by Eduard Rüppell in 1838, with the type locality listed as Jeddah; however, subsequent work has shown that the locality corresponds to Cantharus grandoculis, a species described by Achille Valenciennes in 1830 from the Seychelles. As a result, Dentex rivulatus is treated as a synonym of Cantharus grandoculis. Some researchers place Gymnocranius within the subfamily Monotaxinae, though the fifth edition of Fishes of the World does not recognize the traditional subfamilies of Lethrinidae as valid and instead classifies Lethrinidae within the order Spariformes.

During late 1944 and early 1945, the 103rd Infantry Division conducted a series of river crossings and limited offensives as part of the Allied push into western Germany. On 10 December 1944 it crossed the Zintzel River at Griesbach, and by 15 December it had advanced through Climbach, crossed the Lauter into Germany, and assaulted the outer defenses of the Siegfried Line. A subsequent move in late December sent the division west to the Sarreguemines area, where it maintained an active defensive posture. On 14 January 1945 it relocated to Reichshofen to establish positions along the Sauer River, a sector that did not experience an enemy offensive. On 15 January General Anthony 'Nuts' McAuliffe was reassigned to command the division, a position he held through July 1945. Defensive patrols remained active on 19 January, and a limited attack against Soufflenheim was repulsed. The unit withdrew to the Moder River on 20 January, repelling further German advances near Muehlhausen from 23 to 25 January. An offensive then began on 15 March 1945, with the Moder and Zintzel crossed in sequence, the capture of Muehlhausen, a crossing of the Lauter, and a penetration of Siegfried Line defenses.

Constituted in the Organized Reserve on 24 June 1921, the 103rd Infantry Division was allotted to the Eighth Corps Area and assigned to XVIII Corps, with its home area covering Arizona, Colorado, and New Mexico. The division’s headquarters were organized on 31 August 1921 at the Colorado State Capitol in Denver, and on 29 March 1922 it moved to the Kittredge Building at 16th Street and Glenarm Place in Denver, remaining there until its activation for World War II. In 1922, the unit adopted the nickname Rocky Mountain Division to foster esprit de corps, a designation that was later changed to Cactus Division after the adoption of its shoulder patch. A newsletter titled The Cactus was published to maintain communications with officers, and it reported on inactive training sessions, summer training quotas, camps, and CMTC unit assignments.

Meta-analyses of short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy (STPP) report moderate effect sizes when compared with no treatment, with Cohen’s d values typically ranging from about 0.34 to 0.71, and follow-up assessments suggesting outcomes that are slightly better than those of other therapeutic approaches. Reviews focusing on specific disorders indicate larger effects for somatoform conditions (approximately 0.78–0.91 versus no treatment) and a sizable but smaller effect for depression (around 0.69). A 2012 meta-analysis published in the Harvard Review of Psychiatry on intensive short-term dynamic psychotherapy (ISTDP) found effect sizes that varied from 0.84 for interpersonal problems to 1.51 for depression, with an overall ISTDP effect size of about 1.18 relative to no treatment.

Freud's Beyond the Pleasure Principle (1920) employs a Platonic myth to illustrate the instinctual drive's conservative tilt toward a primordial unity. In Plato's narrative, originally globular beings are powerful, self-sufficient, and united, but Zeus divides them into separate individuals as punishment for assaulting the gods. The resulting fragmentation yields a weaker human type whose members continually seek to restore the original wholeness. This restoration occurs through two modalities: (1) the exchange of physical pleasure and (2) collective creative thinking. The latter is illustrated by the group of artists and philosophers around Socrates in Plato's Symposium.

Baba Malay is a Malay-based language variety situated within the region’s broader linguistic landscape, which developed from Malay’s classical and modern literary forms and the formation of regional dialects that followed the rise of the Srivijaya empire in Sumatra, Indonesia. As Malay spread through extensive interethnic contact and maritime trade across Southeast Asia, its use extended to areas as distant as the Philippines, creating a shared medium that facilitated trade and communication. This historical contact gave rise to Bazaar Malay, also referred to as low Malay or Melayu Pasar, a lingua franca of commerce that is generally regarded as a pidgin, shaped by interactions among Malay speakers and traders of Hokkien, Portuguese, and Dutch origin.

Baba Malay is a Malay-based creole language associated with the Gorap people, an indigenous group of western and northern Halmahera in Indonesia (also known as Bobaneigo). The language exhibits lexical influence from Papuan languages and shares vocabulary with several Sulawesi languages, notably Buginese and Cia-Cia. Approximately 60 of its about 200 attested words show overlap with these language families, illustrating substantial cross-linguistic contact in the region.

Brazil has been a pioneer in deep-water oil exploration, with approximately 73 percent of its oil output derived from deep-water fields. In the nuclear sector, uranium is enriched at the Resende Nuclear Fuel Factory, with the enrichment primarily directed toward research purposes. Hydroelectric power dominates the electricity mix, contributing about 88 percent of total generation. Looking to naval capabilities, Brazil's first nuclear-powered submarine is scheduled for launch in 2029.

The Brazilian press traces its origins to Rio de Janeiro in May 1808, with the founding of the Royal National Press by Prince Regent John. Gazeta do Rio de Janeiro became the country’s first newspaper, beginning publication on 10 September 1808. In contemporary Brazil, the leading newspapers by circulation and influence are Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, and O Estado de S. Paulo.

France's constitutional framework endows the general electorate with the authority to approve constitutional amendments proposed by Parliament and legislation submitted by the president through the referendum process. Referendums have long been a decisive instrument in shaping the country's political trajectory and its foreign policy, producing notable votes on matters such as Algeria's independence, the method of electing the president by popular suffrage, and questions surrounding European integration. Voters have also decided on the creation and evolution of the European Union and on reforms to the presidency, including reducing the presidential term. Collectively, these direct votes illustrate the distinct role of referendums in influencing constitutional development, domestic governance, and France's international alignment.

During the 11th century, the House of Plantagenet, rulers of the County of Anjou, extended their authority over Maine and Touraine, building a continental dominion that stretched from England to the Pyrenees and encompassed roughly half of what is now modern France. This extensive territorial span fostered protracted tensions between the French crown and the Plantagenet possessions for about a century. From 1202 to 1214, Philip II of France conquered most of the empire's continental possessions, leaving England and the duchy of Aquitaine under Plantagenet rule.

The Scottish Singles and Albums Charts, during the late 1970s and early 1980s, were compiled by the industry publications Radio & Record News and Record Business and were broadcast on Independent Local Radio stations such as Radio Clyde and Radio Forth. In this period the Scottish charts tended to favor hard rock, punk, and new wave, with soul and other black music styles achieving comparatively lower success. An example from 23 June 1978 comparing UK-wide and Scottish positions illustrates these differences: Heatwave reached UK chart position 15 but was 40 in Scotland; The O’Jays were at 21 nationally and did not appear in the Scottish Top 40; Bob Marley was 26 nationally and likewise absent from the Scottish Top 40; AC/DC were 38 nationally while charting at 20 in Scotland; The Clash were 62 nationally and 22 in Scotland; and The Vibrators were 65 nationally and 39 in Scotland.

The Scottish Albums Chart is compiled by the Official Charts Company (OCC) and ranks albums in Scotland based on physical and digital sales, with these figures contributing to the UK Albums Chart for the region. The Scottish Singles Chart was likewise derived from physical and digital sales that fed into the UK Singles Chart in Scotland, but the chart has not been published since 20 November 2020.

During the Roman era, Christianity began to take root in Georgia in the early first century. Traditional accounts link the diffusion of the Christian faith in the region to the missionary activity of Saint Andrew, Saint Simon the Zealot, and Saint Matata. Despite these early developments, Hellenistic influence, local pagan practices, and the Mithraic cult remained widespread until the fourth century, reflecting a long period of religious coexistence.

Georgia in the Roman era encompasses a roughly six-century span in the South Caucasus during which Rome engaged in a drawn‑out rivalry with its eastern adversaries, the Parthian and later Sassanid Persian Empires. The Parthian and subsequently the Sassanids waged extended campaigns against Rome, a succession of conflicts that is commonly described as the Roman-Persian Wars. Across this period, Georgian polities and communities navigated shifting power balances, bolstered fortifications and trade networks, and formed varying alliances as Rome and Persia contended for influence in the Caucasus.

MPEG-7 is a standard designed to support intelligent multimedia applications by providing a formal description of multimedia content. It leverages low-level multimedia semantics to annotate audio, video, and related data, and employs a formal representation scheme to ensure consistent interpretation across systems. By enabling automated reasoning over the described content, MPEG-7 facilitates tasks such as content-based retrieval, indexing, and analysis.

In MPEG-7, a descriptor (D) serves as the representation of a feature. It is defined in terms of both its syntax and its semantics, providing a formal structure as well as an accompanying meaning. A single, unique object can be described by multiple descriptors, allowing various aspects of the object to be captured.

The Kosovo Campaign Medal ribbon features three central pinstripes of equal width in red, white, and blue. The wearer's right-hand edge is dark blue and abuts a red pinstripe, while the wearer's left-hand edge is red and abuts a blue pinstripe. The red, white, and blue color scheme was proposed by the NATO Alliance, and the pinstripe sequence is intended to represent the colors of the United States flag.

The Kosovo Campaign Medal recognizes eligible service in the Kosovo operations and uses service stars to indicate campaign participation. A service star is awarded for participation in either the Air Campaign or the Defense Campaign. Up to two service stars may be awarded if an individual completes two distinct tours that meet the 30/60 day duration requirements in both campaigns. The medal is thus issued with at least one service star. Additionally, the Fleet Marine Force combat operation insignia is authorized for certain sailors.

Harpinae is characterized by a head with exposed tentacles and by eyes that are conspicuous and well developed. The mantle is simple and enclosed, with no tapering appendage at the front. The foot is large and flat, and it is not reflexed along the sides of the shell.

Sexual imprinting is a form of imprinting in which, after early exposure to humans, some non-human mammals and birds develop a lasting sexual preference for humans or human-associated cues. This can lead to attraction to humans rather than members of the animals’ own species, particularly among individuals reared from a young age by people. A notable example involves Chi Chi, a female giant panda formerly housed at London Zoo, who was moved to Moscow Zoo to attempt mating with the male An An. Although mating did not occur, Chi Chi reportedly performed a pronounced sexual display directed at a zookeeper, illustrating how early social experience can shape later sexual behavior. The case is frequently cited in discussions of imprinting as evidence that early rearing conditions can influence reproductive tendencies, while also underscoring the variability of such effects across species and individuals.

Among peregrine falcons, imprinting occurs on particular features of breeding sites, shaping their later reproductive behavior. Specific structures such as cliff faces and bridges have been identified as imprinted cues. This process results in a lasting preference to breed at the locations associated with the imprinted structures, influencing site selection and reproductive patterns.

Blenko Glass Company has manufactured a wide range of glassware over its history, including decorative and functional pieces. Its stained-glass work is globally renowned and appears in numerous cathedrals and churches around the world. The 384 Water Bottle is frequently cited as the firm's flagship item and typically constitutes its best-selling product. Beginning in 1947, the company has employed designers to create distinctive glassware lines. It has also issued limited-edition collectible glassware that commemorates the state of West Virginia.

Blenko's Kokomo-based glass venture operated for about a decade before ending in failure. Analysts have attributed the collapse to a combination of economic distress stemming from the Panic of 1893 and ongoing recessions, together with protectionist pressures such as the Wilson–Gorman Tariff Act of 1894 that heightened foreign competition and cultivated a belief among Americans that European glass was superior. An alleged tactic associated with Blenko was the shipment of glass to England and back in order to suggest European origin. After the project failed, Blenko and his family relocated to London in July 1905, where he produced the same glass and marketed imported equivalents to U.S. glass studios. About fourteen months later, they returned to the United States and established a permanent home in Pennsylvania.

Thomson Video Networks contributed to the development and definition of the High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) standard, which seeks to achieve about a 50 percent reduction in bitrate relative to the H.264/AVC standard and enables Ultra HD broadcasting. The company maintains active membership in several broadcasting and standards bodies, including ATSC, the MPEG-DASH Industry Forum, DVB, IABM, MPEG, OMA, SCTE, and SMPTE, and it was a founding member of the French research institute B-Com.

Thomson Video Networks offers a suite of broadcast and multi-screen video processing solutions that encompass high-definition and standard-definition encoding, decoding, and transcoding for multiple screens. The range includes multiplexing capabilities and infrastructures designed for redundancy and network management to ensure dependable operation. It also provides a video stream server intended for contribution workflows. These systems are capable of delivering content to terrestrial, satellite, cable, IPTV, and over-the-top services.

Arvīds Pelše joined the Central Committee in 1961. Later that year, following Yuri Gagarin’s return from space, he proposed renaming the Latvian capital to Rīga, a move that Soviet central authorities deemed an extreme measure.

Arvīds Pelše was a Latvian-Soviet political figure who served as a lecturer and political commissar in the Red Army from 1919 to 1929. He completed a history degree at the Moscow Institute of the Red Professoriat in 1931 and pursued graduate studies there from 1931 to 1933. Earlier, from 1929 to 1932, Pelše worked as an instructor at the Institute of Party History at the Central School of the NKVD. He then held the post of First Deputy of the Commissariat of State Farms (Sovkhozes) from 1933 to 1937. From 1937 to 1940 he taught history at the Moscow Higher Educational Institute. Pelše played a leading role in Latvia's admission to the USSR in June 1940. Thereafter, from March 1941 to 1959, he served as secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Latvia for propaganda and agitation. During the Great Patriotic War (1941–1945), he worked to prepare Latvia for the establishment of a communist state.
Esto Perpetua is the motto of Springs Boys' High School in Springs, South Africa, and it has been in use since the school opened in 1940.

Esto perpetua is a Latin motto traditionally attributed to Paolo Sarpi (1552–1623), a Venetian theologian and mathematician commonly known as Fra Paolo. It is reputed to have been uttered on his deathbed, with reference to Venice, and is usually translated as a wish that it endure forever. In 1782, the phrase was invoked by Henry Grattan during the achievement of Irish legislative independence. Emma Edwards Green, who designed the state seal bearing the motto, described the inscription as conveying that it is perpetuated or lasts forever. The expression was cited by Confederate President Jefferson Davis at the conclusion of Rise and Fall of the Confederate Government, where he expressed a desire for the motto to be placed on the arch of the Union. Davis also argued that the war demonstrated the impracticality of dissolving the Union.

The popularity of political ideologies is partly shaped by moral entrepreneurs who may promote particular beliefs for their own political, economic, or personal interests rather than for the public good. In analytical terms, political ideologies are commonly described along two primary dimensions: goals, which denote how a society should be organized and governed, and methods, referring to the most appropriate means to realize those goals through specific proposals, institutions, and policies. This two-dimensional framework helps explain how ideologies attract different coalitions and how proponents justify both their proposed ends and the pathways chosen to achieve them.

Within the list of political ideologies, an ideology may be associated with multiple groupings, reflecting its applicability across different analytical frameworks. There is considerable overlap among ideologies with related roots or objectives, which can blur distinctions between them. Moreover, the interpretation and significance of a political label often vary across countries, shaped by distinct historical and cultural contexts. Consequently, political parties frequently adopt a heterogeneous mix of ideological elements, blending principles from different traditions to form their platforms.

Laas’ anti-Platonism targets positivism rather than Platonism as a whole, situating his critique within a debate over the foundations of knowledge and justification. Positivism maintains that philosophy rests solely on positive facts—both external perceptions and internal experiences—and demands that any belief be proven by those facts or experiences; in this sense the approach is inherently sensualist, seeking to explain phenomena from within conscious life starting with the given. Laas aligns with a sensualist position by arguing that higher mental processes, including thinking and reasoning, are transformations of perceptions, feelings, needs, and memories in living beings, and that only facts deserve consideration. Sensualists deny access to contents or processes that are unexperienced or not scientifically constituted, holding that thinking and higher functions historically arise after original perception and animal desires. In this framework, Laas contrasts with Plato and Kant, who postulate a distinct faculty of reason, whereas Laas contends that epistemology and ethics should begin exclusively with experience and perception. He further contends that Kant, historically, merely replaced scholastic metaphysics with a different term, rather than effecting a genuine shift. Both sensualists and positivists tend to deny the existence of entities such as God and absolute reason, arguing that thinking, judging, and representation are grounded in sensory sensations and facts. For Laas, idealists are characterized by the claim that reason governs thought and action and can make judgments beyond what has actually been experienced.

Laas attributes to Jeremy Bentham the most successful development of Epicurean ethics, arguing that sympathy has been expanded into universal philanthropy and that Bentham’s private ethics finds expression in social policy and legislation. He rejects the notion that ethical goodness inherently aligns with prudence, maintaining that prudent calculation and moral value can diverge. Morality, in Laas’s view, may be built on historical values, with history generally guiding toward appropriate aims and outcomes. He defends a duty-based framework, contrasting it with Bentham’s emphasis on self-interested calculation, and articulates a Kantian-tinged case that moral obligation is categorical rather than conditional on prudential outcomes. Egoists, by contrast, deny any duty, treating moral imperatives as infatuations or folly. The position advanced affirms the primacy of duty and a categorical imperative while not neglecting rights, arguing that duties and rights should be given equal weight. Platonic morality is rejected in favor of a balanced approach that harmonizes duties with rights.

CKUL-FM is a Canadian FM radio station broadcasting at 96.5 MHz. The station received approval from the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission on March 5, 1990 and launched on August 30, 1990 as 96.5 Sun FM, using the call letters CIEZ-FM. Its initial format consisted of easy listening, or beautiful music, but was soon changed to an adult contemporary format. In 2001 the station transitioned to an adult hits format and branded itself FM 96.5. On November 1, 2004 it rebranded as 96.5 Kool FM and adopted the current call letters CKUL-FM. Since then the adult hits format has gradually evolved into classic hits.

CKUL-FM operated for several years as a joint venture between Newcap Radio and CHUM Limited, which later became part of CTVglobemedia, within the five-station Metro Radio Group local management agreement that was disbanded by the CRTC. In 2007, the regulators approved a plan for Newcap and CHUM/CTVglobemedia to convert their remaining Halifax AM outlets, CFDR and CJCH, to FM, resulting in each company owning two wholly owned FM stations in Halifax—the maximum permitted under CRTC rules at that time. Subsequently, Newcap acquired CTVglobemedia's stake in CKUL. Newcap later sold CFDR to Rogers Radio, and the station was rebranded as CFLT-FM.

Alteon WebSystems introduced the ACEswitch 180, a switch that allows per-port autonegotiation to 10/100 or 1000 Mbps, enabling flexible Ethernet speeds across all ports. The company also released the ACEdirector, a Layer 4-7 switch designed as an integrated services front-end and as a server load balancer. Additionally, Alteon introduced Jumbo Frames up to 9,000 bytes, a capability supported by its switches when used with ACEnic adapters.

Alteon WebSystems demonstrated a Gigabit Ethernet network interface card at NetWorld+Interop in September 1996, signaling the company’s expansion beyond its core server-switch offerings into higher-speed networking. In 1997 it expanded its product line with the Gigabit Ethernet NIC, notable for being the first NIC to implement Gigabit Ethernet technology.

During the Belfast Blitz, Belfast had the highest population density in the United Kingdom and the lowest proportion of public air-raid shelters. Before the Belfast Blitz, the city possessed only about 200 public shelters. In addition, around 4,000 households had constructed private shelters. The high water table in Belfast made Anderson shelters largely unsuitable, and because many households lacked gardens, Morrison shelters were provided, though not in the numbers required. Consequently, the local authority focused on the construction of surface communal shelters to bolster protection.

During the Belfast Blitz, Belfast initially lacked searchlights, which only arrived on 10 April, and there was no capability to deploy smokescreens, though barrage balloons were positioned strategically for protection. The city's location lay at the fringe of the German bombers' operational range, resulting in the absence of night-fighter aerial cover. Consequently, on the first raid night no RAF aircraft intercepted the German planes. Ground defenses consisted of 22 anti-aircraft guns around the city (six light and sixteen heavy), of which only seven were manned and operational on the first night.

ISO 31-10, a subdivision of the ISO 31 standard, defined the names and symbols of quantities and units used in the domain of nuclear reactions and ionizing radiations. It enumerated seventy quantities and their corresponding units, and, where applicable, provided conversion factors to facilitate practical applications. The standard was withdrawn in 2009 and superseded by ISO 80000-10.

In June 2022, The Sydney Morning Herald drew global coverage and widespread backlash after columnist Andrew Hornery attempted to out Rebel Wilson. The newspaper’s editor, Bevan Shields, defended Hornery’s column, which was subsequently deleted. Wilson had pre-empted the disclosure by posting on Instagram to confirm her relationship.

The Sydney Morning Herald has consistently backed the Coalition in New South Wales state elections. Since 1973, the paper has endorsed a Labor government only once, in the 2003 election for Bob Carr. On three occasions during this period, it declined to endorse either major party.

The Politburo of the Workers' Party of Korea is the party's top decision-making body, currently comprising 17 senior officials. It oversees both the party apparatus and the central government, and is headed by the general secretary. Unlike many other communist parties, a substantial share of its authority is delegated to a smaller body known as the Politburo Presidium, which concentrates the most powerful decisions.

Within the Workers' Party of Korea, the Presidium functions as the inner core of the Politburo, a body that was formerly known as the Standing Committee. It is elected by the Central Committee of the WPK and oversees the day-to-day work of the party. The Presidium typically comprises the supreme leader and four additional members. In practice, it stands as the highest authority in both the party and the state, with its decisions effectively carrying the force of law.

Muiñeira is a Galician musical tradition in which bagpipe performance plays a central role and exhibits regional variation. In Galicia, three principal bagpipe varieties are used, each associated with a distinctive pitch: tumbal in B-flat, grileira in D, and redonda in C, though there are exceptions and some instruments that fall outside these categories. By contrast, Asturian bagpipe practice commonly accompanies a tambor (snare drum), reflecting a related but separate tradition. The Asturian pipes typically feature only one drone and employ a fingering pattern that differs from that used with Galician instruments. Tunes performed on the gaita are usually vocal in nature, with the singing either supporting the instrumental line or taking turns with it during performances.

Susana Seivane Hoyo (born 25 August 1976) is a Galician bagpipes player who has emerged as a prominent figure in traditional Galician music. Born in Barcelona, Spain, she hails from the Seivane family, renowned for their luthier craft and musical performances, including the Obradoiro de Gaitas Seivane workshop. She began her musical career at the age of three, under the guidance of her father, Álvaro Seivane, and was influenced by her grandfather Xosé Manuel Seivane as well as by Ricardo Portela and Moxenas. Seivane is noted for her contributions to the bagpipe tradition, where she blends the enxebre style associated with ancient players with her own evolving approach enriched by additional influences.

So Much for Pretending includes a brief cameo by Will Clark, who was then the Texas Rangers' first baseman. In the video, Clark is shown walking alongside White down a tunnel at The Ballpark in Arlington.

Io sì (Seen) drew international attention in 2021 as Laura Pausini performed the track at several prominent events following its Golden Globe success. On 3 March 2021, after winning the Golden Globe for Best Original Song, Pausini attended the 71st Sanremo Music Festival on its second night and performed "Io sì (Seen)" with the Sanremo Festival Orchestra. On 25 April 2021, she delivered a performance of "Io sì" at the 93rd Academy Awards from the rooftop of the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, accompanying Diane Warren during the pre-show. She then opened the 66th David di Donatello Awards at the Teatro dell'Opera di Roma with a rendition of "Io sì (Seen)".

The music video for Io sì (Seen) premiered on 30 October 2020 and was directed by Edoardo Ponti. It features a cameo appearance by Sophia Loren, who stars as the lead actress in The Life Ahead, a film directed by Ponti. Io sì (Seen) serves as the theme song for The Life Ahead.

2045 is a tabletop game developed by Mizu Game. The release generated controversy in Taiwan due to its portrayal of a potential China–Taiwan military conflict. The company was founded by KJ Chang, who described the game's aim as allowing players to experience war on the tabletop before it reaches them, while acknowledging that the future remains unpredictable.

2045 is a cyberpunk-themed game set in the year 2045. The gameplay occurs over a ten-day period, during which players engage in a zero-sum contest of military strategy, a characterization described by the Agence France-Presse. Players may select characters representing factions, including a soldier, a collaborator, and an arms dealer, each offering distinct roles within the game's framework.

DF-100 is a Chinese land-attack cruise missile. Its Chinese designation, 东风-100 (Dōngfēng 100), translates literally as "East Wind 100." In NATO nomenclature, the weapon is designated CH-SSC-13 Splinter, and it is also known in other references as CJ-100.

According to a 2020 assessment by the United States Air Force's China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI), at least one operational unit of the People's Liberation Army Rocket Force began receiving the DF-100 ballistic missile in 2019. The assessment also indicated that full operational capability for the DF-100 was expected to be achieved by 2022.

REI originated as a display shelf within the Puget Sound Cooperative Store near Seattle's Pike Place Market, and in 1942 the operation moved to a new space down the hall from The Mountaineers’ club rooms on Pike Street. Jim Whittaker joined as the organization's first full-time employee in July 1955, and the cooperative was incorporated the following year as Recreational Equipment Cooperative. Whittaker led the company as chief executive during the 1960s and was an early board member alongside Nicholas Clinch, who served as president of the American Alpine Club. In May 1963 Whittaker became the first American to summit Mount Everest, an achievement that generated extensive free publicity and contributed to a milestone in 1964, when REI's gross income topped $1 million for the first time.

REI, short for Recreational Equipment, Inc., is an American retail and outdoor recreation services corporation. Historically governed as a consumers' cooperative, the company continues to brand itself as such. It offers a wide range of products, including camping gear, equipment for hiking, climbing, cycling, water activities, running, fitness, snow sports, travel gear, and clothing for men, women, and children. The retailer does not market hunting or fishing equipment.

Within Spain, the inner region of Castile exhibits a characteristic culinary profile shaped by traditional practices. Castilian soups are typically hot and thick, often grounded in bread and garlic as a foundational element. A representative stew from the area is cocido madrileño, illustrating the robust, home-style cooking associated with Castilian cuisine. Preservation traditions also appear prominently, with salting long used to extend the shelf life of cured meats such as Spanish ham. In addition, some cheeses, notably Manchego, have been preserved by immersion in olive oil, demonstrating an alternate method used within Castilian foodways.

On Spain's Atlantic seaboard, the northern regional cuisines of Asturian, Basque, Cantabrian, and Galician origin form a cohesive gastronomic tradition. Common threads include vegetable- and fish-based stews such as caldo gallego and marmitako, while lacón ham is lightly cured as a regional specialty. Across these cuisines, seafood dominates, with notable preparations featuring Basque-style cod, albacore, and anchovy. In Galicia, the repertoire is particularly associated with polbo á feira, an octopus dish, alongside a diverse array of shellfish preparations.

A reduit denotes a fortified structure, such as a citadel or a keep, that serves as a last-resort retreat for defenders when outer defenses have been breached. The term also designates a defensible area within a country that can be held even if the surrounding region is occupied, secured by a perimeter of substantial fortifications or by natural barriers such as mountains.

Reduit refers to a fortification concept in military architecture that typically denotes an outlying defensive position or retreat. In English, the expression national redoubt is commonly used to describe a strategy of concentrating defensive efforts in a central area while relinquishing peripheral regions. The so‑called National Redoubt in the German and Austrian Alps, associated with Nazi leadership, is an example described as a redoubt in the conventional sense. A related term, national reduit (réduit national), appears in English on occasion and more often in French, and it similarly denotes holding the center of a country while abandoning outlying territory.

In early January 1943, operations in Tunisia focused on modifying the front through Axis initiative. Operation Eilbote I, initiated on 18 January, involved the 10th Panzer Division and the 334th Infantry Division advancing from Pont du Fahs with aims to widen the position in front of the Superga and Benigni Sectors, thwart an Allied eastward movement toward Enfidaville, and disrupt Rommel's line of communications. On the Allied side, a westward push against the right wing of the British V Corps at Bou Arada achieved little success. In the southern sector, Axis efforts achieved more notable results as their assault on French positions at the junction of the Western and Eastern Dorsals progressed about 56 kilometers to Ousseltia and 40 kilometers to Robaa. The defenders, though poorly equipped, resisted tenaciously, with seven infantry battalions becoming cut off in the mountains. In response, Anderson dispatched the 36th Brigade to Robaa and requested Combat Command B of the 1st Armored Division to move to Ousseltia, to come under Juin's command on arrival. Fierce fighting continued through 23 January, after which the front line had stabilised.

During the Tunisian campaign, Allied columns advanced toward Djebel Abiod and Béja, while German air power, with the Luftwaffe holding air superiority, imposed pressure as Allied aircraft based in Algeria faced distant harassment. On 17 November, Nehring arrived and the leading elements of the British 36th Brigade confronted a force of 17 tanks and about 400 paratroopers with self-propelled guns at Djebel Abiod; German paratroopers, reinforced by Luftwaffe support and Italian fire from the 1st Infantry Division “Superga,” knocked out 11 tanks and halted the advance, with the combat at Djebel Abiod continuing for nine days. By 22 November, Italian L Special Brigade tanks compelled U.S. paratroopers to withdraw from Gafsa. Subsequently, Allied columns concentrated at Djebel Abiod and Béja with an assault planned for 24 November. The 36th Brigade was to push forward from Djebel Abiod toward Mateur, while the 11th Brigade would move down the River Merjerda valley to Majaz al Bab (Medjez el Bab), then Tebourba, Djedeida, and Tunis. Blade Force was tasked with striking across country toward Sidi Nsir on minor roads between the two infantry brigades and conducting flanking attacks on Tebourba and Djedeida, and its composition included 37 mm M3 Stuart light tanks and 75 mm M3 GMC self-propelled anti-tank guns.

In January 2016, Tyler Perry began filming his seventeenth feature, Boo! A Madea Halloween, his ninth installment in the Madea series. The film was released on October 21, 2016, and a sequel titled Boo 2! A Madea Halloween followed in October 2017. Additionally, Perry, alongside Oprah Winfrey, contributed voice work to his first animated feature, The Star, which is based on the Nativity of Jesus. The Star was developed by Sony Pictures Animation and released on November 17, 2017.

Tyler Perry revised his stage musical repeatedly over six years, but critical reviews remained lackluster. In 1998, at age 28, he retooled the production and restaged it in Atlanta at venues including the House of Blues and later the Fox Theatre. He continued creating new stage productions and toured on the Chitlin' Circuit and the broader urban theater circuit, building a sizable African-American audience. By 2005 Forbes reported that his enterprise had generated more than $100 million in ticket sales, about $30 million in video sales, and roughly $20 million in merchandise. Perry produced approximately 300 live shows per year, with an average weekly attendance of around 35,000.

On December 2, 1959, the vessel was transferred from the Military Sea Transport Service to the United States Maritime Administration at Fort Schuyler, New York, for service with New York Maritime College. The college designated it TS Empire State IV, a designation it retained until 1973. In 1973, the ship was transferred to the Massachusetts Maritime Academy and renamed USTS Bay State.

USNS Henry Gibbins (T-AP-183) experienced significant ice-related damage to its hull during the winter of 1976–77, one of the coldest periods in half a century, while at Buzzards Bay near the Cape Cod Canal. The hull plates were repaired, and the vessel continued in training service for two additional years. In the summer of 1977, it carried cadets to Europe, followed by a Mediterranean training cruise in the summer of 1978.

Steel Connect completed an initial public offering in February 1994, becoming a publicly traded company. In the same month, Wetherell established BookLink, into which Steel Connect invested $900,000. In November 1994, BookLink was acquired by America Online (AOL). The proceeds from the sale financed the creation of CMG @Ventures, a venture capital firm that has backed numerous internet-focused companies.

Steel Connect traces its corporate history to a series of strategic acquisitions in 2000, beginning with the March acquisition of Yesmail, followed by the April acquisition of uBid and the May purchase of Tallan, Inc. for $920 million. In August 2000 the company agreed to pay $7.6 million per year for 15 years to secure the naming rights to the New England Patriots’ home stadium; after the dot-com bubble burst, the arrangement was amended in August 2002 and the stadium name was changed to Gillette Stadium. Earlier in 2000, the firm recorded a $661 million gain when Yahoo! acquired its interest in GeoCities, at a time when its stock price had fallen about 78% from its peak earlier in the year. The corporate expansion continued with the February 2004 acquisition of Modus Media. In September 2008 the company renamed itself ModusLink Global Solutions, Inc. In December 2017 it acquired IWCO Direct for $476 million in cash, and in February 2018 the firm adopted the name Steel Connect, Inc. May 2023 saw Steel Holdings acquire a majority stake in the company and inject $200 million in cash.

Rashid Stadium (Arabic: استاد راشد) is a multi-purpose stadium located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Built in 1948, the venue originally accommodated 8,015 spectators. It is used primarily for football and rugby matches. For the AFC Asian Cup 2019, temporary stands were added, expanding the capacity to 12,056 seats.

Overpressure, or blast overpressure, denotes the portion of a shock wave that exceeds the surrounding atmospheric pressure. It arises from events such as sonic booms or detonations and is used as a key parameter in evaluating the potential destructive effects of explosions. The concept is of particular importance in analyses concerning the effects of nuclear weapons and thermobaric devices, where higher levels of overpressure are associated with greater structural damage and human harm.

A peak overpressure near 500 psi is associated with an estimated 50 percent chance of survival, while pressures in the 70–100 psi range are typically linked to severe injuries. About 15 psi peak overpressure can cause rupture of the eardrum in roughly half of exposed individuals. At around 25 psi, a standing person can be propelled away from the source at a velocity of approximately 10 feet per second. Overall, higher peak overpressures tend to increase both injury severity and lethality, though some injuries can occur at substantially lower pressures, such as eardrum rupture around 15 psi.

Paisley recorded for Arista Nashville from 1999 until the label's closure in 2023. During his tenure, he released twelve studio albums, beginning with Who Needs Pictures. His most commercially successful releases from this period are Mud on the Tires (2003) and Time Well Wasted (2005), both of which have been certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America.

Brad Paisley's discography comprises 12 studio albums, 3 compilation albums, 52 singles, and numerous collaborations. He first appeared on the charts in 1999 with "Who Needs Pictures," which peaked at No. 12 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. Later that year, he also charted with "He Didn't Have to Be," the first of 21 singles (including collaborations) to reach No. 1 on the same chart. Overall, Paisley has 21 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart when collaborations are included. From 2006 to 2009, there was a run of ten consecutive No. 1 singles, beginning with the Dolly Parton duet "When I Get Where I'm Going" and ending with "Then."

A lighthouse tender is a vessel specifically designed to service lighthouses and lightvessels, undertaking tasks such as maintenance, provisioning, and transportation to remote sites. These ships supply facilities with fuel, provisions, mail, and personnel transfers as part of their operational duties. In practice, many lighthouse tenders also perform buoy-tending responsibilities, serving as dual-purpose vessels that deploy, maintain, and recover navigational buoys in addition to their lighthouse-related work.

Lighthouse tenders were vessels originally operated by the United States Lighthouse Service and are now part of the United States Coast Guard. The first American tender of the Lighthouse Service was the former revenue cutter Rushnourder, acquired in 1840. The introduction of steam propulsion produced the service's first steam-powered tender, the Shubrick, completed in 1857 and placed in service on the West Coast in 1858. The Fir was the last active representative of the service and is now designated as a United States National Historic Landmark. These ships illustrate the transition of maritime navigational support from the Lighthouse Service to the Coast Guard and represent an important element of the country's maritime heritage.

In April 1945, United States forces assumed control of most western and northern areas that would later comprise Saxony-Anhalt. The United States Group Control Council, Germany, the precursor of OMGUS, appointed the first leading officials in the region who were not Nazi affiliates. Among them was Erhard Hübener, who had previously been placed on leave by the Nazi regime and was reappointed to the post of Landeshauptmann, or state governor. By early July 1945, the U.S. Army withdrew to allow the Red Army to take the area as part of the Soviet occupation zone, in line with the London Protocol of 1944.

Saxony-Anhalt is a state of Germany, with Magdeburg as its capital and largest city, and Halle (Saale) as the second-largest city. From 1994 to 2003, the state was divided into three Regierungsbezirke—Dessau, Halle, and Magdeburg. Below this level, there were 21 Landkreise (districts). In 2004, the administrative structure was reformed, replacing the previous arrangement with 11 rural districts and 3 urban districts.

RK Hoops–Quezon City participated in the inaugural season of the WMPBL, a competition that comprised six teams all based in Luzon. The regional distribution of member teams favored Calabarzon, which supplied three squads, while Metro Manila provided two teams and the Ilocos Region contributed one.

RK Hoops–Quezon City sits within the evolving landscape of Philippine women's basketball, a field that saw several attempts to establish a professional league prior to the emergence of the WMPBL. Historically, the Women’s Philippine Basketball League operated from 1998 to 1999 and again in 2008, while the Pinay Ballers League was launched in 2014 with support from the Philippine Sports Commission. In addition, the Philippine Basketball Association has hosted women’s 3x3 basketball on two occasions, spanning 2015–2016 and 2024. Collectively, these efforts reflect a continuous push to develop and formalize women’s competition in the country, within which RK Hoops–Quezon City participates.

Reportedly converted from a container ship, the Iranian navy designated the vessel Shahid Bagheri as a drone carrier. The ship’s flight deck is estimated to be 160 to 180 meters in length. It is capable of taking off and landing a mixed air group comprising around 60 drones and helicopters. For protection, the carrier is armed with anti-ship and anti-air missiles. In addition, it carries Ashura-class missile speedboats, with reported numbers ranging from about 30 to 50 vessels.

Drone carriers are platforms designed to support the operation of unmanned aerial vehicles, serving both civilian applications and military missions, though military use is more prevalent. They enable a fleet to launch and recover combat drones (UCAVs) without requiring large traditional aircraft carriers or carrier strike groups. In March 2013, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) initiated programs to develop a fleet of small naval vessels capable of conducting drone warfare without dependence on large carrier formations.

A Season in Hell (French title Une saison en enfer; Italian title Una stagione all'inferno) is a 1971 French-Italian drama film directed by Nelo Risi. It centers on the life and death of the French poet Arthur Rimbaud, and portrays his strained relationship with fellow poet Paul Verlaine. The narrative also incorporates Rimbaud's African sojourn, including his experiences in Ethiopia, as part of the biographical portrayal.

A Season in Hell is a 1971 biographical drama that portrays the relationship between Arthur Rimbaud and Paul Verlaine, showing how their initial friendship evolves into a homosexual romance. Facing societal disapproval, including from Verlaine's wife, the pair move to England, where they endure a stormy life together for a couple of years. Their relationship deteriorates and they quarrel for the last time. Rimbaud then returns to his family farm in the countryside, while Verlaine is arrested for attempted murder.

The Cichociemni, commonly known by the nickname the Silent Unseen, were elite parachute-trained special-operations troops within the Polish Army in exile during World War II. Created in Great Britain, they were organized to operate in occupied Poland and carried out covert missions as part of the Polish resistance under the Armia Krajowa. In Polish, the unit is known as Cichociemni Spadochroniarze Armii Krajowej.

The Special Action Force (SAF) is the elite commando unit of the Philippine National Police (PNP). SAF candidates must complete the SAF Commando Course in order to wear the SAF Beret, a mark of qualification and unit membership. The Commando Course functions as the foundational prerequisite for SAF specialization trainings, serving as the basis from which other advanced programs are pursued, including Explosives and Ordnance Disposal (EOD), the Basic Airborne Course (BAC), the Urban Counter Revolutionary Warfare Course (SURESHOCK), the Basic Under-Water Search and Rescue Operations Course (SCUBA-BUSROC), the SAF Seaborne Warfare Course (SSWC), and additional offerings.

Suzhou pingtan is a seated form of the traditional Chinese narrative performing art known as Quyi. It represents one of the Quyi subgenres and is chiefly carried out as a storytelling performance, setting it apart from other forms such as Pinghua, which is purely spoken, and Tanci, which combines talk with song and is comparable to Pingshu in northern regions. Within Quyi, the repertoire is typically organized into three broad content categories: narrative tale-telling, pieces for light amusement, and songs used to express emotional states. In this framework, pingtan is positioned primarily within the storytelling category.

Suzhou pingtan is a traditional performative art form that originated in Suzhou and later expanded significantly in Shanghai around the late 19th to early 20th centuries, driven by commercial exchange and cultural activity in the Jiangnan region. It rests on a long historical development that provides a solid foundation for its ongoing evolution. The form appears simple in structure but is rich in content, encompassing narrative storytelling, humor and joke-telling, instrumental and vocal music, and aria-style singing. Its artistic character emphasizes coherent reasoning, refined taste, elements of unpredictability, engaging appeal, and meticulous attention to detail. Shaped by pingtan artists, it gained immense popularity across Jiangnan and has evolved into a contemporary performance tradition that continues to innovate while preserving its traditional essence.

Among certain right-wing circles, contemporary discourse draws parallels between present-day Western Christianity and the Crusades era. They contend that Christianity faces an Islamic religious and demographic threat, and advocate the revival of Crusader symbols along with anti-Islamic rhetoric as a response. In their view, these symbols and rhetoric are employed to legitimize and spur a struggle against a perceived religious foe.

In the Iberian Peninsula, Crusade campaigns culminated in 1492 with the fall of the Muslim Emirate of Granada, bringing its territory under Castilian and Aragonese control. In the Baltic region, the Teutonic Knights conducted campaigns against pagan peoples, drawing crusaders from France, the German realms, and England through the early 15th century, with activity persisting into the 1410s. Following the Reformation, the papacy sometimes issued indulgences for campaigns against Protestants, but more often Catholic powers organized papally sponsored Holy Leagues against the Ottoman Empire, continuing into the 17th century.

In 1953, Ben Webster released The Consummate Artistry of Ben Webster, also billed as the King of the Tenors, a session featuring pianist Oscar Peterson. Peterson would become a key lifelong collaborator for Webster during the 1950s, recording under Norman Granz's labels. Webster also toured and recorded with Norman Granz's Jazz at the Philharmonic package, performing with Peterson and trumpeter Harry "Sweets" Edison. That period also included a 1956 album session with pianist Art Tatum, backed by Red Callender on bass and Bill Douglass on drums. On December 16, 1957, Coleman Hawkins Encounters Ben Webster was recorded, featuring Webster and Peterson along with guitarist Herb Ellis, bassist Ray Brown, and drummer Alvin Stoller. The session linked two leading tenor saxophonists who had first met in Kansas City.

Ben Webster joined the Duke Ellington Orchestra as a featured soloist in 1940, and he contributed to the ensemble’s recording of Cotton Tail. Within Ellington’s group, he was notably influenced by alto saxophonist Johnny Hodges, a major figure in the band’s sound. In a 1989 assessment, Gunther Schuller argued that Hodges’s influence steered Webster away from his initial inspiration, Coleman Hawkins. Webster subsequently formed close ties with fellow Ellington newcomers Jimmy Blanton and Billy Strayhorn, thereby integrating into the expanding circle surrounding the orchestra.

Numerous contemporary interpretations of the jota are performed by diverse folkloric groups. Notable among these popular variants are Jota de San Lorenzo, from Huesca; Jota Vieja; Aragón Tierra Bravía; Gigantes y Cabezudos; La Dolores; and la danza de la Olivera.

Mikhail Glinka (1804–1857) was a Russian composer who, after traveling through Spain, adopted a musical style rooted in the jota. He subsequently integrated this jota-derived influence into his composition The Aragonese Jota.

Evidence in what is now Kentucky dates to about 9500 BCE, when Clovis hunter-gatherers left behind stone-tool assemblages reflective of a foraging lifestyle. By around 1800 BCE, the economy began shifting from pure hunting and gathering toward agriculture. Around 900 CE, the Mississippian tradition established a presence in western and central Kentucky, while the eastern part of the state saw the emergence of the Fort Ancient culture. Mississippian centers are distinguished by ceremonial earthwork mounds, a hallmark that is not part of Fort Ancient settlements. The Fort Ancient communities depended primarily on maize, beans, and squash for sustenance. Their agricultural system is noted for ecologically mindful practices, including rotating crops, burning forest sections to create habitat for wild game, relocating villages every 10 to 30 years, and continually shifting field locations to maintain plots in various stages of ecological succession.

From 1860 through the 1990s, Kentucky tended to support the Democratic Party and was viewed as a presidential swing state for much of the latter half of the 20th century. Since the late 1990s, the state has consistently backed Republican candidates in most federal elections, and more recently has supported Republicans in state-level offices as well, reflecting a broader realignment in Kentucky politics.

The publication that would become the Statesman Journal began in 1888 as the Capital Journal, with its first issue published on March 1. It was launched as a for-profit venture and functioned as an outlet for the Republican Party. By the end of 1888 Parry sold the newspaper to William H. Byars, who was elected Salem’s City Surveyor in that year. The Journal subsequently underwent multiple ownership changes in the ensuing years. In 1890 Byars was appointed by President Benjamin Harrison as the U.S. Surveyor General for Oregon.

Statesman Journal, a newspaper in Salem, Oregon, served as the mouthpiece of the Democratic Party and of the Salem Clique that controlled the party in Salem. Bush was known for criticizing rival editors and political figures. Along with Oregonian editor Thomas J. Dryer, Bush helped to ignite a bitter editorial feud between the two papers.

In the 2001 Danish parliamentary election, the Danish People's Party (DF) captured about 12 percent of the vote and 22 seats, becoming the third-largest party in the Folketing. This position gave DF the potential to form a parliamentary majority in coalition with the Conservative People's Party and Venstre. The party was favored by those parties because DF had supported Venstre’s prime ministerial candidate, Anders Fogh Rasmussen, during the campaign, and DF subsequently provided parliamentary backing for a Venstre–Conservative coalition government led by Rasmussen in return for advancing several of DF’s priorities, notably stricter immigration policies. DF also played a key role in drafting the government’s May 2002 immigration law, which the party described as among Europe’s strictest.

During the 2019 Danish general election, the Danish People's Party (DF) recorded its weakest result since 1998, securing 8.7 percent of the vote and 16 seats in the Folketing. This amounted to a net loss of 21 seats compared with 2015, and the party dropped to third place, narrowly ahead of the Social Liberals. Analysts attributed the decline to the party’s reluctance or indecision about entering a governing coalition, which reduced its influence on national policy. Meanwhile, the main parties, including the Social Democrats, adopted many of DF’s positions on immigration and integration policy.

Mercado de Campo de Ourique is a historic market that first opened in 1934. It underwent a renovation in 1991 and was subsequently redesigned in 2013 under the direction of architect António Maria Braga, who was awarded the Rafael Manzano Prize in 2019. The market today includes a range of gourmet food stalls.

Mercado de Campo de Ourique is a neighborhood food market in Lisbon, Portugal. Its English rendering is Campo de Ourique Market. The local Portuguese pronunciation of the market’s name is [mɨɾˈkaðu ðɨ ˈkɐ̃pu ðɨ oˈɾikɨ].

Founded as a news cooperative, the Associated Press entered the broadcasting field in 1941 by supplying news to radio stations. It expanded its reach by creating its own radio network in 1974. In 1994, AP established APTV, a global video news gathering operation, which in 1998 merged with Worldwide Television News to form APTN (Associated Press Television News), a service that distributes video to international broadcasters and websites. The organization relocated its headquarters in 2004 from 50 Rockefeller Plaza to 450 West 33rd Street in Manhattan. By 2019, AP operated more than 240 bureaus worldwide. While its mission has remained constant, digital technology has transformed AP news distribution into an interactive process with U.S. newspaper members, broadcasters, international subscribers, and online customers.

The Associated Press (AP) is an American news organization that won an Academy Award in 2024 for the documentary film “20 Days in Mariupol,” a first-person account that documents the early days of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

PhD, or Doctor of Philosophy, is a doctoral degree awarded across many fields, and in numerous systems there are more than fifty distinct doctoral designations, many of which are rare or have fallen out of use. In formal writing, the degree title is typically placed before the holder’s name in abbreviated form, as in examples such as Dr. rer. nat. Max Mustermann or Dr. Max Mustermann. In certain contexts, the designation may be omitted altogether, though such omission is generally permissible only for non‑honorary doctorates; honorary doctorates, by contrast, must be indicated with Dr. h.c. (honoris causa).

PhD is a research-oriented doctoral degree that typically requires a minimum of two years of graduate-level study, combining advanced coursework with substantial research. Candidates are expected to contribute original, credible work within their field, demonstrated by strong academic performance. The work is presented as a dissertation or thesis prepared under the supervision of a tutor or director. The dissertation is reviewed by a Doctoral Committee, which must include examiners external to the program and at least one external member from outside the institution. A successful defense of the dissertation in the corresponding field leads to the awarding of the doctoral title.

Justices on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court are elected to ten-year terms, after which they undergo a statewide retention vote. If retained, they serve another decade; if not retained, the governor—with Senate approval—appoints a temporary replacement until a special election can be held. By 2005, only a single judge had failed to win retention. In that year, Justice Russell M. Nigro did not secure a majority of affirmative votes amid the pay raise controversy, and he was replaced by Justice Cynthia Baldwin, who was appointed by Governor Ed Rendell in 2005.

Rolf Larsen was the only justice of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to be removed from office by impeachment. In 1994, the Pennsylvania House of Representatives filed seven counts of misconduct against him. The Pennsylvania Senate voted against Larsen on five of those counts, but on one charge reached the two-thirds threshold for conviction, leading to his removal from the bench.

AGATA reinstated Gold, Platinum, and Diamond album certifications in 2023, determined by album sales and downloads. The Gold level was set at 2.5 million listens, Platinum at 4 million, and Diamond at 6 million. In 2024 the program was expanded to include singles, using streaming data excluding YouTube, with the Gold and Platinum thresholds for singles set at 2.5 million and 4 million streams, respectively, mirroring the album thresholds.

AGATA (Lietuvos gretutinių teisių asociacija) is a non-profit performance rights organization established in 1999 in Lithuania. It administers licensing and rights management on behalf of music publishers and performers within the country. In 2011 it was designated as the body responsible for collecting compensation for writers, performers, actors and producers. The organization is an associated member of the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI). Since September 2018, AGATA has published a weekly Top 100 chart ranking the most popular albums and singles in Lithuania, with the rankings based on sales and streaming data from platforms including Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, iTunes, Google Play and Shazam.

The defending doubles champions were Ivan Dodig and Marcelo Melo. Dodig did not participate in the tournament, leaving Melo to team up with Vasek Pospisil. The Melo/Pospisil pair advanced to the semifinals but were defeated there by John Peers and Henri Kontinen.

On 11 July 2025, the United States imposed sanctions on Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel and two senior ministers, Defense Minister Álvaro López Miera and Interior Minister Lázaro Álvarez Casas, for the regime's brutality.

On 23 March 2021, Miguel Díaz-Canel Bermúdez earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree. His doctoral thesis examined a government management framework grounded in scientific research and innovation as a pathway to sustainable development in Cuba.

According to the Sanguozhi, in 195 AD Cao Cao employed the tactic known as the empty fort strategy against Lü Bu at Chengshi County, which lay southwest of present-day Juye County in Shandong. In the summer of that year Lü Bu mobilized roughly 10,000 troops at Dongmin County, northeast of present-day Jinxiang County, to attack Cao Cao. Despite commanding only a small force himself, Cao Cao arranged an ambush, using the ruse of an apparently undefended fort. Lü Bu's forces were defeated.

Empty Fort Strategy is a tactic within the traditional body of strategic thought known as the Thirty-Six Stratagems. It employs reverse psychology to lead adversaries to believe that a seemingly vacant location is safeguarded by traps and ambushes. The deception aims to induce the enemy to withdraw rather than engage in combat. It is the thirty-second entry in the Thirty-Six Stratagems. The article provides illustrative examples in the following sections.

LZJB is a lossless data compression algorithm developed by Jeff Bonwick, who also led the design and development of the ZFS file system. ZFS has been deployed in Oracle’s ZFS storage products and has been adopted by a number of startups, including Nexenta, Delphix, Joyent, and Datto, Inc. In addition to his work on ZFS, Bonwick conceived slab allocation, a memory-management technique that has found use in several operating systems, notably macOS and Linux. Together, these contributions reflect his influence on both file-system technology and memory management in contemporary computing.

LZJB is a lossless compression method devised by Jeff Bonwick. It is used within the ZFS file system to compress crash dumps and other data, and the software is distributed under the CDDL license. As an enhancement of the LZRW1 algorithm, which belongs to the Lempel–Ziv family, LZJB builds on established compression techniques. The name derives from the LZ initials of Lempel–Ziv and Bonwick's surname.

Coercion describes a strategic process in which one actor seeks to compel another to alter its behavior through the prospect or deployment of force. It can manifest in nonphysical forms, notably threats of harm that do not necessitate immediate violence, with credibility and anticipated consequences shaping compliance. Historical and military practice has included measures such as firing squads, employed by armed forces to uphold discipline and to intimidate opponents or civilian groups into submission or quiet acquiescence. In scholarly terms, Byman and Waxman (2000) define coercion as the use of threatened force, potentially augmented by limited actual force, designed to induce an adversary to act differently than it would have otherwise. Importantly, coercion does not inherently entail the destruction of property or life, since the central objective is conformity or compliance.

Coercion is a tactic in which one party uses leverage to compel another to act in ways that run counter to their own interests. It may entail physical harm or psychological abuse, with the latter designed to strengthen the perceived credibility of the threat. The prospect of further harm can push the coerced person to acquiesce. While coercion and persuasion share the aim of influencing decisions, they differ in intent, the willingness to inflict harm, the likely outcome of the interaction, and the range of options available to the person subjected to coercion.

Function spaces can be studied by equipping a topology on the set of maps from X to Y. For continuous maps, the compact-open topology is a standard choice, whose suitability depends on the particular topological spaces X and Y (for instance, in the context of loop spaces). By contrast, when considering all set-theoretic functions from X to Y without a continuity requirement, the set Y^X may be endowed with the product topology. This topology on Y^X is commonly referred to as the topology of pointwise convergence, since convergence is determined by the behavior at each point of X.

Function spaces occupy a central role in functional analysis, characterized by their intricate interrelationships through processes such as interpolation, embedding, representation, and Banach-space isomorphism. The subject is developed through a wide range of fundamental theorems and constructions that formalize and leverage these connections to study operators, norms, and dualities. Illustrative results in this area include the Riesz representation theorem, which connects continuous linear functionals with elements of a given space; the Riesz–Thorin interpolation theorem, which yields bounds for operators acting between different spaces; the Gagliardo–Nirenberg interpolation inequality, which relates norms across different scales; the Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem, which describes when embeddings are compact; and the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function, a cornerstone tool in harmonic analysis with wide implications for regularity and boundedness.

SOMPO Holdings, Inc. is a Japanese insurance holding company, officially known in Japanese as SOMPOホールディングス株式会社 (SOMPO Hōrudingusu Kabushiki-kaisha). It was established on April 1, 2010 through the merger of Sompo Japan and Nipponkoa Insurance, and it is regarded as one of Japan's three leading insurers.

Broadsheet sections are produced in units of eight pages, consisting of four pages on the front and four on the back, and the sheet is halved during the production process. Newsprint rolls, or webs, are defined by the width required to print four front pages, with the term web referring to the width of the roll itself. In the United States, a typical front-page width is 11 inches, which corresponds to a 44-inch-wide newsprint web.

Broadsheets are a newspaper format associated with more scholarly and in-depth journalism than the tabloid press. They tend to feature detailed reporting and place less emphasis on sensationalism, prioritizing thorough coverage and analysis of events. Newspapers adopting this format aim to provide comprehensive storytelling and contextual insight, often benefiting from an expansive layout that accommodates multiple front-page stories. In such designs, the most significant items are placed above the fold to maximize visibility.

During his presidency, Epitácio Pessoa used the federal government to intervene on behalf of state-level interest groups in exchange for congressional support, reflecting the transactional dynamic of Brazilian politics at the time. His administration faced a turbulent period of the Old Republic, marked by the Copacabana Fort uprising on July 5, 1922, the crisis surrounding the so-called cartas falsas, and the Revolt of the Military Club, events that tested the regime’s authority. As the search for a successor began, the process occurred in a highly charged atmosphere, with lieutenants and junior officers of the Armed Forces advocating for profound political reforms that would reshape the country’s political landscape.

Epitácio Pessoa was elected senator for Paraíba in 1911. He lived in Europe from 1911 until 1914, and upon returning to Brazil he soon assumed a role with the Commission for the Verification of Powers.

Napoleon Bonaparte returned from exile on Elba, landing near Cannes on 1 March 1815, and proceeded northward as supporters flocked to him. Louis XVIII addressed the chambers on 16 March 1815, urging defense of the constitutional charter. He departed Paris for Ghent in Belgium on the night of 19–20 March 1815. Napoleon then entered Paris on 20 March 1815 and announced his ministers, signaling the restoration of his governance during the Hundred Days.

During the Hundred Days, Napoleon I established the French Government on 20 March 1815 upon reclaiming the imperial throne, replacing the government of the first Bourbon Restoration that had been formed by Louis XVIII the previous year. Following Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo and his second abdication on 22 June 1815, the Executive Commission of 1815 was instituted as the new governing body. The Commission subsequently declared the Empire abolished for a second time on 26 June 1815.

Bắc Từ Liêm is an urban district (quận) of Hanoi, Vietnam. It was established on 27 December 2013 when the former rural Từ Liêm district was divided into Bắc Từ Liêm and Nam Từ Liêm. The district currently comprises 13 wards and spans an area of 45.32 square kilometres (17.50 square miles). As of 2019, its population stood at 335,110, giving a population density of approximately 7,400 inhabitants per square kilometre.

Bắc Từ Liêm district is a district of Hanoi, in northern Vietnam, located at coordinates 21°3′15″N 105°40′56″E. It is bounded to the north by Đông Anh district across the Red River, to the east by Tây Hồ district, to the south by Cầu Giấy and Nam Từ Liêm districts, and to the west by Hoài Đức and Đan Phượng districts.

Protests occurred during Rosario Murillo's vice presidency. By July 2018, the recorded death toll reached 309, including 25 victims under the age of 17. Murillo and presidential aide Néstor Moncada Lau were sanctioned by the United States, with the sanctions issued as part of a U.S. executive order announced by President Donald Trump on 27 November 2018.

Rosario Murillo began her career in the early 1970s as a secretary at La Prensa, working for editors Pedro Joaquín Chamorro and Pablo Antonio Cuadra. She was arrested in Estelí in 1976 for political activity, after which she fled Nicaragua and spent several months in Panama and Venezuela. Murillo then relocated to Costa Rica, where she engaged in Sandinista movement work, helped establish Radio Sandino, and met Daniel Ortega. She and Ortega were married in a clandestine ceremony in 1979. After the Sandinistas toppled Anastasio Somoza Debayle in 1979, she returned to Nicaragua. In 2005 she remarried Ortega in order to have the marriage recognized by the Catholic Church, as part of an ongoing reconciliation with the church.

Semantic wikis are collaborative platforms that extend traditional wikis by integrating structured, machine-readable semantics, and they show varying degrees of formalization. The semantic layer may be stored within the wiki markup or kept in a separate semantic repository, depending on the implementation. User assistance for adding semantics often includes forms for data entry, autocompletion to suggest terms, proposal generation for new statements, and mechanisms to enforce consistency. Representation languages range from the wiki’s native syntax to established standards such as RDF or OWL, or even a database that the tool populates by deriving semantics from raw data. In some systems, the formalized content enjoys separate version control or correction editing from ordinary page revisions. Provenance support also varies, with author attribution sometimes maintained separately from the semantic data itself.

Semantic wikis are wiki systems that integrate semantic capabilities, enabling the inclusion of structured data and relationships alongside conventional pages. Some implementations run as autonomous semantic wiki applications, with OntoWiki as an example. Other semantic features are delivered as extensions or plugins to existing wiki platforms to enhance their functionality. The most widely recognized extension is Semantic MediaWiki, built for the MediaWiki software. Another instance is the SemanticXWiki extension developed for XWiki.
