In July 2012, Sony Computer Entertainment announced the acquisition of Gaikai for $380 million. The deal was complemented by Sony's acquisition of assets from Gaikai's market rival OnLive, reinforcing its cloud gaming capabilities. At the January 2014 Consumer Electronics Show, Gaikai's technology was positioned to power PlayStation Now, a cloud-based service that enables PlayStation games to be played on a range of devices. In 2014, PlayStation Now entered North America in beta, initially on the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4, to test performance and pricing.

PlayStation Blog is an online, PlayStation-focused blog that forms part of the PlayStation Network. It was launched in June 2007 and features regular content such as announcements of new games, interviews with developers, and updates to the PlayStation Store. In March 2010, a sub-site called PlayStation Blog Share was introduced, providing a platform for PlayStation Network users to submit ideas to the PlayStation team on PlayStation-related topics and to vote on other users’ ideas.

Human-powered aircraft have demonstrated the ability to fly over substantial distances, illustrating the viability of flight powered by human effort. These aircraft are predominantly pursued as engineering challenges rather than for recreational use or practical transportation.

On 11 May 1984, the third Kremer Prize for speed was awarded to the MIT design team for Monarch-B, a human-powered aircraft. The flight completed a triangular 1.5 km (0.93 mi) course in under three minutes, achieving an average speed of approximately 32 km/h (20 mph). The pilot was Frank Scarabino. The prize totaled £20,000, and the rules provided for additional awards of £5,000 for each subsequent entrant who could improve the speed by at least 5%.

In 2001, Lars Eriksson secured his second Allsvenskan title, as Hammarby IF clinched the championship with a 21 October 2001 victory over Örgryte IS, the second-to-last round of the season. Eriksson had announced his intention to retire at the end of the campaign. At Söderstadion, fans praised Eriksson alongside manager Sören Cratz, who was also set to depart the club at season’s end.

Lars Eriksson (born 1965) is a Swedish former footballer who developed his early career in the Stockholm region. He grew up in Haninge, Stockholm County, and began playing football with the local club Vendelsö IK. In 1977, at the age of 12, he moved to Hammarby IF to continue his development as a youth player. During his early teens he spent several years abroad with his family before returning to Hammarby and joining the club’s B-team.

Within debates about the Greater Middle East, Zbigniew Brzezinski argued that the region has experienced a political awakening that could presage a shift toward a multipolar global order. He described the area as the Global Balkans and as a strategic lever on Eurasia, highlighting its potential to influence broader regional and international power dynamics. In a different assessment, Andrew Bacevich, in his 2016 book, contends that the region has long been the theater of a sequence of conflicts dating back to around 1980, with the Iran–Iraq War marking the outset of this ongoing pattern.

The Greater Middle East is a term that denotes the envisioned future trajectory of the region and is often linked to the concept of a "new Middle East." It was popularized by Condoleezza Rice, who was then the United States Secretary of State, and it was introduced in June 2006 in Dubai as part of the Bush administration’s regional strategy. Proponents described the transformation as achievable through a deliberate, disruptive process intended to spur reform and integration, though the precise meaning and feasibility of this approach have been the subject of extensive debate since its articulation. Rice reaffirmed the concept during a press conference with Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert after the onset of the 2006 Lebanon War. Since then, discussions surrounding the plan have focused on its goals, methods, and potential consequences, reflecting widespread scholarly and policy-oriented scrutiny. In some accounts, the broader effort to realize this regional vision is referred to as the Great Middle East Project.

During the 1991 interrogations related to the Austin yogurt shop killings, there is no record of what was said to the two men, making it impossible to determine whether investigators had supplied information to the suspects at the outset. If such information had been provided, the men could have used it as a basis to implicate themselves in subsequent interviews. Springsteen and Scott were brought to trial largely on the strength of their own self-incriminating statements. The prosecution emphasized the acts' brutal nature but presented no hard evidence beyond confessions. Both were convicted of capital murder; Springsteen was sentenced to death, while Scott received a life sentence. In 2005, Springsteen, then 17 at the time of the offenses, had his sentence commuted to life in prison by Governor Rick Perry in light of the Roper v. Simmons decision.

Investigators initially identified a broad range of potential suspects. A 16-year-old was subsequently detained near a local mall a few days later after being found in possession of a weapon of the same caliber used in the killings. The teenager initially provided information that appeared promising to investigators. However, after extensive questioning, detectives concluded that he was attempting to deflect responsibility to avoid the gun charge. Consequently, the teen and three petty-criminal associates he had implicated were ruled out as suspects, with none of the four individuals being older than 17 at the time.

Air supremacy during the Korean War marked the first major conflict in which jet-powered aircraft played a central role in combat. As fighting continued, World War II-era piston-engined fighters such as the P-51 Mustang, F4U Corsair, and Hawker Sea Fury were displaced from air-superiority duties by faster jet opponents. In the early engagements, United Nations air forces equipped with jets like the P-80 Shooting Star, F9F Panther, and Gloster Meteor achieved air superiority over the North Korean People's Air Force, which relied on propeller-driven Yak-9 and La-9 fighters. By early August 1950, the KPAF had been reduced to about twenty aircraft.

During the Persian Gulf War, the Iraqi Air Force was nearly wiped out in the conflict’s opening phase, spanning from August 1990 to February 1991. It lost the majority of its aircraft and its command-and-control capacity largely due to precise Coalition strikes and the flight of many Iraqi aircraft to Iran. Iraqi air defenses, including man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS), were notably ineffective against Coalition air operations. In total, Iraqi anti-aircraft defenses recorded about 75 aircraft losses across more than 100,000 sorties, with 42 losses caused by Iraqi action and 33 the result of accidents. RAF and US Navy aircraft operating at low altitudes to evade radar were especially vulnerable, a vulnerability that diminished once crews were directed to fly above the principal anti-aircraft artillery belts.

Some dance styles require a specific type of dance shoe. The selection of footwear is guided by the goal of harmonizing with the costume while also prioritizing safety and injury prevention. In many cases, the shoes are chosen to blend with the outfit so that attention is not drawn to the feet. When a dance involves a significant amount of turning, the footwear is typically designed to cover the forefoot, including the balls of the feet, to facilitate turning.

Dance costumes are designed to enable the required range of motion while safeguarding the garment from damage during movement. When performances involve lifting, the design emphasizes features that prevent the lifter's fingers from catching on the fabric, reducing the risk of entanglement. To further promote unrestricted movement at the armpit, some costumes employ a higher-than-normal armhole cut, ensuring greater freedom in the shoulder area.

Public relations professionals build and maintain relationships with an organization's target audiences, including the media, trade outlets, and opinion leaders. Their responsibilities typically include designing communications campaigns and producing press releases and other news content. They engage with the press, coordinate interviews for company spokespeople, and draft speeches for corporate leaders. In some cases they act as the organization's spokesperson and prepare clients for press conferences, media interviews, and public addresses. They also generate website and social media content and oversee the management of the company's reputation. Additional duties encompass crisis communications, internal communications, and marketing-related activities such as enhancing brand awareness and coordinating events. The effectiveness of PR work hinges on understanding the interests and concerns of stakeholders, and practitioners seek to address these issues through publicity, a core instrument of the field.

Public relations increasingly relies on social media as a direct channel for organizations to reach their publics. Platforms such as Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and LinkedIn are used by public relations professionals to disseminate news and updates, coordinate communications, and shape messaging. These channels also serve as a means to respond to inquiries and engage in dialogue with audiences. In crisis situations, social media enables rapid information sharing and reputational management. The interactive nature of these networks offers immediate feedback and higher levels of audience participation, influencing how organizations monitor sentiment and adapt their communications strategies.

The Lao language has long been shaped by its close proximity to Thai, with passive cross-influence contributing to broad convergence between the two languages. In historical phonology, Proto-Southwestern Tai *mlɛːŋ yields Lao with an initial m realized as maeng (ແມງ mèng, /mɛ́ːŋ/), while Thai preserves an initial l as laeng (แลง /lɛ̄ːŋ/), though laeng is largely restricted to Royal Thai or restricted academic contexts. The commonly cited form malaeng (แมลง /máʔ.lɛ̄ːŋ/) exists as an archaic variant. In informal speech, Thai speakers also use maeng (แมง /mɛ̄ːŋ/), a development likely influenced by Lao.

Lao language is a Tai language spoken primarily in Laos and within surrounding regions of northern Southeast Asia. The Phuan language, although it is sometimes treated as a Lao dialect in Laos, is a Chiang Saen (Thai) language and is not part of the Lao–Phutai language group. As a Tai language of northern Southeast Asia, Phuan shares many characteristics with related languages such as Tai Dam and Tai Lan Na, reflecting common features across Tai-speaking communities. In the Isan region, Phuan is notable for not losing ground to Thai or Isan at the same rate as some other minority languages, indicating relative language vitality there.

The Wuhan area has a long history of settlement, with evidence indicating human presence in the region for approximately 3,500 years. Panlongcheng, an archaeological site in the vicinity of Wuhan, is linked to the Erligang culture and dates to about 1510–1460 BCE. It is situated in the modern Huangpi District of Wuhan. Earlier, during the Erlitou period, the site was sparsely populated, reflecting a lower-density settlement before the rise of later Bronze Age urban development.

By 1900, Hankou, a Yangtze River boom town, was described by Collier's magazine as a bustling commercial center comparable to the American cities of St. Louis and Chicago. On October 10, 1911, Sun Yat-sen's followers launched the Wuchang Uprising, a pivotal event in the downfall of the Qing dynasty. The uprising precipitated the collapse of imperial rule in China, ending about two thousand years of dynastic governance, and contributed to the establishment of the Republic of China.

In 1992, Judge Consuelo Bland Marshall issued her final ruling, a decision that ran counter to an order issued by two higher courts that had postponed the case for five years after a Supreme Court decision.

Consuelo Bland Marshall was a United States district judge who presided over a First Amendment dispute between Preferred Communications, Inc. and the City of Los Angeles concerning the use of municipal facilities to further speech. In the underlying matter, Chief Justice Rehnquist stated that the city was obligated to permit Preferred Communications to utilize its physical capacity to advance speech. The case was characterized by a prolonged denial of a jury trial to determine damages, lasting about a decade from 1983 to 1992, during which the plaintiffs experienced substantial legal hardship and economic disenfranchisement caused by the continual delays. Additionally, the plaintiffs were not afforded a public hearing to assert their First Amendment rights under the United States Constitution.

Mehrgarh, a Neolithic settlement in the Bolan region of Balochistan, Pakistan, dates from roughly 7000 BCE to 2500 BCE and is central to understanding the emergence of the Indus Valley Civilisation. It stands among the earliest South Asian sites to provide clear evidence of farming and animal husbandry, thereby shedding light on early subsistence strategies in the region. The site shows influences from the Near Eastern Neolithic, a connection that is reflected in domesticated wheat varieties, initial farming phases, pottery styles, and a range of artefacts, along with cultivated plant species and domesticated herd animals. Together, these findings contribute to a broader picture of the cultural and technological developments that preceded and shaped the Indus Valley Civilisation.

The Indus Valley inhabitants demonstrated notable precision in measuring length, mass, and time, and are among the earliest civilizations to establish a coherent system of standardized weights and measures. However, measurement practices varied considerably across the extent of the Indus territories. An ivory scale recovered from Lothal in present-day Gujarat reveals a smallest subdivision of about 1.704 mm, the finest division documented on Bronze Age scales. In addition, Harappan engineers employed decimal division in their metrology, including for mass, a pattern reflected in their six-faced, or hexahedral, weights.
Abdulwahab Al-Awadi (born 2 June 2002) is a Kuwaiti professional footballer who plays as a right-back for Al-Arabi and the Kuwait national football team.

Abdulwahab Al-Awadi is a Kuwaiti footballer who began his career in the youth system of Al-Yarmouk, where he predominantly played as a forward. He finished as the top scorer in the youth league before advancing to Al-Yarmouk's first team, making appearances across two seasons with limited playing time. He was part of the squad that won the 2023–24 Kuwaiti Division One. Midway through that season, Al-Awadi left Al-Yarmouk to sign with Al-Arabi.

James Douglas Ogilby was the eponym for several zoological species, reflecting his impact in natural history. Among the named taxa are Cephalophus ogilbyi, commonly called Ogilby's Duiker, an antelope; Chimaericola ogilbyi, a flatworm; and Rheotanytarsus ogilbyi, known as Ogilby's Midge, an insect.

James Douglas Ogilby was a zoologist whose research focused on reptiles. He produced a substantial number of scientific papers concerning reptiles, contributing to the field's understanding of their biology and diversity. In taxonomic work, he formally described a new species of turtle and described several new species of lizards, reflecting his significant role in expanding the catalog of reptile biodiversity.

Rick Henderson was an American jazz arranger, composer, and bandleader born in Washington, D.C. He studied composition as a high schooler and performed locally in the late 1940s, then served in the Army from 1951 to 1953. After his discharge, he joined Duke Ellington's Orchestra on the recommendation of Clark Terry, contributing arrangements, performing with the band during Ellington's Capitol Records period, and composing tunes such as "Carney." He left Ellington after roughly five years amid a reassessment of the orchestra, though he appeared with the group irregularly through late 1957. Returning to Washington, Henderson led the Howard Theatre's house band until 1964, after which he worked as arranger and composer for jazz orchestras, military bands, and school ensembles. His charts were used by Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Illinois Jacquet, and Billy Taylor. Henderson continued to lead bands into the 1990s, including a run with the University of Maryland Jazz Ensemble from 1977 to 1978. He died in 2004 from cardiovascular complications related to arteriosclerosis.

64-bit computing influenced the compatibility of open-source drivers, since many 32-bit drivers could be adapted or ported for 64-bit architectures, mitigating some of the difficulties typically associated with such transitions. By contrast, hardware manufactured before early 2007 often had limited or problematic support on open-source platforms, a situation largely explained by the small size of the user base for those devices.

During the early development of 64-bit computing, several vendors introduced notable 64-bit architectures: Sun Microsystems released UltraSPARC, a 64-bit SPARC processor; Fujitsu-owned HAL Computer Systems rolled out 64-bit workstations built on HAL’s first-generation SPARC64 CPU; IBM introduced the A10 and A30 microprocessors, the first 64-bit PowerPC AS processors; and IBM also released a 64-bit AS/400 system upgrade designed to migrate the operating system, database, and applications to the new environment.

ATSC is the digital television standard developed in the early 1990s by the Grand Alliance, a consortium of electronics and telecommunications companies formed to establish a high-definition television framework. It is administered by the Advanced Television Systems Committee, and the specification includes several patented elements for which licensing is required for devices that implement those parts. A central component of ATSC’s terrestrial broadcasts is the 8VSB modulation scheme used for over-the-air transmission. The initial version, ATSC 1.0, largely reflects patent contributions from LG Electronics, which held the majority of ATSC-related patents at the time.

ATSC coexists with DVB-T and ISDB-T as part of the global landscape of digital terrestrial television standards. In China, a similar system, ADTB-T, was developed to accompany the DMB-T/H dual-standard framework, and China has officially adopted a dual-standard policy. There is no requirement for receivers to support both standards. There is no support for ADTB modulation from broadcasters or from equipment and receiver manufacturers.

By 2016, Mirantis had become a significant contributor of code to external open-source infrastructure projects, expanding its participation beyond its own product line. Key projects receiving code contributions from the company included Kubernetes, Ceph, OpenContrail, Prometheus, and OPNFV. This shift reflected a broader strategy of engaging with external open-source infrastructure initiatives rather than limiting activity to Mirantis's proprietary offerings.

In September 2020, Mirantis announced the release of Mirantis Container Cloud, a platform that was formerly known as Docker Enterprise Container Cloud and is designed to provide multi-cloud and multi-cluster management capabilities across public and private cloud environments.

Following Bangladesh's independence in the early 1970s, the Bangladesh Football Federation assumed responsibility for the Dhaka League, including the First Division, which had been established in 1948. The league was resumed for the 1973 season after the interruption surrounding independence. In 1993 the Dhaka League was supplanted by a new top-tier competition, the Premier Division. Subsequently, the national league structure evolved to include professional leagues, with the Bangladesh Premier League launching in 2007 (initially as the B.League) and the Bangladesh Championship League starting in 2012. Today, the Dhaka League exists only as a regional competition at the third tier of the national football league pyramid.

In 2010, the Bangladesh Football Federation entered into a sponsorship agreement with Grameenphone, the country’s leading mobile network operator. The deal provided sponsorship for the federation’s football tournaments, aligning Grameenphone’s corporate support with the promotion and development of the sport in Bangladesh.

Great Neck, New York is served by three all-volunteer fire departments on the Great Neck peninsula: the Great Neck Alert Fire Company (founded 1901), the Great Neck Vigilant Fire Company (founded 1904), and the Manhasset-Lakeville Fire Department (M-LFD), which operates as two volunteer companies, numbered 3 (founded 1912) and 4 (founded 1926). The Alert company covers the northern portion of the peninsula, including the Village of Great Neck, and conducts fire suppression and heavy rescue operations; it also responds to select medical emergencies with its heavy rescue vehicle and provides on-scene care prior to ambulance arrival. The Vigilant company serves the middle section of Great Neck and similarly provides fire suppression and heavy rescue services, with emergency ambulance operations serving its own territory as well as Alert’s district. The southern part of Great Neck, including Thomaston and Lake Success, is served by M-LFD Companies 3 and 4, which deliver fire and rescue capabilities across their area. In addition, the M-LFD Ambulance Unit operates two ambulances out of Company 3’s firehouse. EMS responsibilities in the area are further supported by the Nassau County Police Emergency Ambulance Bureau, which provides EMS coverage to the Manhasset-Lakeville fire district.

Great Neck, a village in Nassau County, is connected to Manhattan by the Port Washington Branch of the Long Island Rail Road, with travel to Penn Station typically taking about 30 to 40 minutes from the Great Neck station, where some peak-period trains terminate. Nassau Inter-County Express (NICE) provides bus connections from the village to the station and operates routes to various destinations throughout Nassau County and Queens from this hub. In the southern part of Great Neck, residents have direct access to the Q46 bus along Union Turnpike at the border with Glen Oaks, and to the Q12 bus along Northern Boulevard at the border with Little Neck.

In October 2010, the CIPM voted to submit to the CGPM a resolution noting the intention to redefine the kilogram in terms of the Planck constant h, in conjunction with other fundamental constants. The Planck constant h has dimensions of energy × time (J·s), equivalently mass × length^2 / time. The resolution was accepted by the twenty-fourth CGPM in October 2011 and was discussed further at the twenty-fifth CGPM in 2014. Although progress had been significant, the data were not yet robust enough to adopt the revised definition, and work would continue with a view toward potential adoption at the twenty-sixth meeting in 2018. The proposed definition would permit any apparatus capable of relating the kilogram to h to be used, provided it achieved the required precision, accuracy, and stability. The Kibble balance is one method by which such a definition can be realized.

The kilogram definition is generally consistent with earlier definitions that relied on physical references. It is set so that its mass differs from the mass of one liter of water at its temperature of maximum density by no more than about 30 parts per million (0.003%), a condition tied to water’s properties near 4 °C. At this temperature, water’s density is very close to 1 kilogram per liter.

Texas maintains a highly complex judiciary featuring multiple levels and overlapping jurisdictions. The two courts of last resort are the Texas Supreme Court, which governs civil matters, and the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals, which handles criminal cases. Judges across most levels are selected through partisan elections, with vacancies typically filled by gubernatorial appointment; municipal benches represent an exception to this general pattern. The state has led the United States in executions since capital punishment was reinstated following the Gregg v. Georgia decision.

Texas maintains Mexico as its largest trading partner, reflecting the prominence of cross-border commerce in the state's economy. Mexico imports about one-third of Texas's exports, illustrating the substantial share of Texas goods in the Mexican market. This import/export dynamic is largely the result of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which has encouraged deeper economic integration across the border. In particular, NAFTA has promoted the development of maquiladoras along the Texas–Mexico border, contributing to regional manufacturing activity and trade flows.

The tournament relocated to Mason in 1979, where a permanent stadium complex was constructed and the surface was changed from Har-Tru clay to a hardcourt surface (DecoTurf II). Subsequently, two additional permanent stadia were added, making Cincinnati the only tennis event outside the four Grand Slams to feature three main courts—Center Court, Grandstand Court, and Court 3. In 2010, a new Court 3 was built, expanding the roster to four stadium courts, while the former Court 3 was renamed Court 9. The women’s competition was reinstated for a single year in 1988. A more lasting revival occurred in 2004, when organizers, with the assistance of Octagon, purchased the Croatian Bol Ladies Open and moved it to Cincinnati, reestablishing women’s play at the tournament.

The Cincinnati Open is staged at the Lindner Family Tennis Center, where deliberate design and operational choices have been made to foster an intimate atmosphere that enhances interaction between players and spectators. The layout of the facility facilitates engagement as players move between courts, often in close proximity to fans along the routes. To improve fan access, the tournament publicizes practice schedules across its numerous courts, enabling attendees to observe players during practice sessions.

The B-24 Mk.I was rebuilt as a General Reconnaissance aircraft for anti-submarine patrols, and its configuration included a belly pannier that housed four additional fixed forward-firing 20 mm Hispano cannons (0.787 in). It was equipped with ASV radar, which incorporated two underwing Yagi–Uda antennas and four large antenna masts above the rear fuselage, commonly described as "stickleback" antennas.

Prior to the XB-24’s first flight, early orders for the aircraft totaled 36 from the United States Army Air Corps, 120 from the French Air Force, and 164 from the Royal Air Force. The British designation Liberator was bestowed on the aircraft by the RAF and was subsequently adopted by the United States Army Air Forces as the official name for the Model 24 production series. After the fall of France in 1940, French orders were redirected to Britain. Purchasing commissions from British and French clients created a substantial backlog estimated at 680 million dollars, of which about 400 million represented foreign orders. United States statistics indicated that tooling, plant expansion, and related capacity improvements accelerated American aircraft production by as much as a year. British orders also influenced American production directions beyond individual modifications, with some designs accepted while others were rejected to align with British doctrine. A clear illustration of this influence is the B-24’s generous bomb bay and its ability to carry as much as 8,000 pounds of ordnance.

The Alliance for Romanian Unity (AUR) was an electoral alliance formed by the Republican Party (PR) and the Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR). In the 1990 general elections, the alliance secured 2.1% of the vote for the Chamber of Deputies and won nine seats, while in the Senate it received 2.2% of the vote and earned two seats. All of the alliance's parliamentary seats were won by candidates from the PUNR.
The Alliance for Romanian Unity (AUR) was a political alliance in Romania. In Romanian, it was named Alianța pentru Unitatea Românilor. The group maintained ties with the Romanian Hearth Union.

Convair SM-65B Atlas, also known as Atlas B and designated X-12, served as the prototype for the Atlas ballistic missile program. Its first flight occurred on 19 July 1958. It was the first Atlas variant to employ a stage-and-a-half configuration, featuring an operational sustainer engine together with a jettisonable booster section. Unlike later Atlas models, the booster section was ejected using explosive bolts.

Within the SM-65B Atlas program, turbopump reliability problems were persistent across contemporary missiles Thor and Jupiter, all employing a variant of the Rocketdyne engine with a marginal turbopump design. The principal pump issues included foaming of lubricating oil at high altitude, which compromised lubrication and could lead to pump seizure, and bearings that loosened under the extreme centrifugal forces near 10,000 rpm. In an attempt to remedy the situation, the Army's ABM Division replaced all turbopumps in Jupiter missiles and reported no failures after December 1957. Conversely, the Air Force resisted replacing pumps in Thor and Atlas, arguing that such work would delay the test program. Nevertheless, several pump-related failures occurred on Thor and Atlas during 1958. Experiences with Atlas 6B contributed to the decision to substitute the pumps. Following the Atlas 15A failure in April, the Air Force addressed oil foaming by adjusting gearbox pressure and selecting a different oil viscosity. Despite the potential speed of implementation—about a month—the Air Force chose not to adopt the newer Rocketdyne pump design.

Srivijaya's influence stretched along the coastal areas of Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula, western Java, western Borneo, and the broader Malay Archipelago. It received patronage from Indian and Chinese powers, and its wealth came mainly from trade. At its height, Old Malay served as the official language and lingua franca of the region, eventually replacing Sanskrit in that role.

Beginning in 1299, Sang Nila Utama, a prince of Palembang origin, established the Kingdom of Singapura in Temasek with support from the Orang laut. His dynasty ruled Singapura until the late 14th century, when Javanese forces invaded. In 1400, Parameswara, the great-great-grandson of Sang Nila Utama, founded the Malacca Sultanate heading north. The Malacca Sultanate succeeded Srivijaya and inherited much of its royal and cultural traditions, including a substantial portion of its territories.

The 1996 Telecommunications Act established a nationwide, uniform framework intended to foster competition in local exchange markets, building on the successes achieved through earlier state-level reforms. Although aimed at liberalizing local competition, the act unintentionally spurred the creation of a large number of competitive local exchange carriers beyond what markets could sustainably support. The availability of easy financing from equipment vendors and a surge of initial public offerings helped to form many CLECs, a development that contributed to the late-1990s telecom investment bubble and the subsequent 2001–2002 bust.

Competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) refers to a telecommunications service provider that competes with incumbent local exchange carriers by utilizing alternative means to reach customers. The August 2003 Triennial Review prompted the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to rewrite many rules implementing the Telecommunications Act of 1996, thereby reshaping the regulatory landscape for CLECs. Among unbundling frameworks, two common options are UNE-P and UNE-L, which permit CLECs to access essential local-network elements under specific conditions. UNE-L involves the CLEC operating its own local switching equipment while leasing the incumbent’s copper local loop and directly interconnecting the loop with the CLEC’s switch. Each option presents its own advantages and drawbacks, affecting cost, control, and scalability. In some instances, CLECs elect to bypass the ILEC network entirely by building and using their own facilities, a model known as facility-based LECs. This category includes cable companies that deliver telephone service over existing coaxial cable networks.

The YJ-61 is China's air-launched anti-ship missile developed from the HY-2 land-based anti-ship system. It features a compact airframe optimized for carriage by aircraft, is equipped with a newer active-radar seeker, and uses liquid-propellant fuel. The weapon retains a relatively large warhead inherited from the HY-2, and it entered service in 1986.

The YJ-61, also designated YJ-63 (KD-63) and K/AKD-63, is an air-to-surface, air-launched cruise missile developed from the YJ-6. It is designed for employment from aircraft against surface targets and features an electro-optical seeker. This EO seeker enables terminal guidance with human oversight through a data-link, allowing for man-in-the-loop control during the final phase of flight.

Oscar Pettiford, an influential bassist and bandleader, is linked to a formative episode in which he inadvertently helped bring Cannonball Adderley to wider attention. Reportedly, a fellow musician tricked Pettiford into allowing Adderley, then an obscure music teacher, to sit in on the bandstand. Pettiford assigned Adderley a solo on a demanding piece, and the young saxophonist delivered a remarkably strong performance, an early display of the talent that would later define Adderley’s career.

Oscar Pettiford rejected the prevailing bass playing style of his era and developed his own distinctive approach to the instrument, which helped shape later jazz technique. He drew early admiration from Milt Hinton, who was impressed by his abilities when Pettiford was fourteen. In 1941, Pettiford gave up music, believing he could not earn a living from it. About five months later, he met Hinton again, and Hinton's encouragement persuaded him to resume his musical career.

Following the conclusion of the First Opium War, maritime prohibitions were lifted, enabling the large-scale migration of Cantonese speakers from the Pearl River Delta. Many migrants, including merchants, traveled by boat to other parts of Guangdong and Guangxi, where Cantonese communities were established and in some cases formed enclaves in regions where other Yue dialects or non-Sinitic languages such as Zhuang are spoken, exemplified by the Yong–Xun Yue dialect in Nanning. A substantial portion of migrants also settled overseas, spreading Cantonese to Southeast Asia, as well as to North and South America and Western Europe. Enclaves of Cantonese persist in Chinatowns across major cities outside China. In 1883, James Dyer Ball’s Cantonese Made Easy identified the Xiguan district in western Guangzhou as the source of Cantonese’s prestige variety. This Xiguan prestige is distinguished by a distinctive apical vowel, typically transcribed as /ɿ (sometimes represented as /ɯ/ or /ɨ/ in IPA), which occurs in contexts where modern Cantonese ends with /i/.

Cantonese constitutes the predominant language among Chinese speakers in the United Kingdom. Approximately 300,000 people in the United Kingdom report Cantonese as their first language. This predominance is largely attributed to the sizable population of British Hong Kongers residing in the country. It is also reinforced by a significant portion of British Chinese whose families trace their origins to Singapore and Malaysia, former British colonies in Southeast Asia.
The Harpidae, commonly known as harp snails, form a distinct taxonomic family of large predatory sea snails, marine gastropod mollusks.

Lagwagon is an American punk rock band whose output for the Fat Wreck Chords label comprises twelve releases, including nine studio albums, one EP, one live album, and a collection of B-sides, compilation tracks, and demos. The group has neither achieved nor pursued broad mainstream chart success, yet maintains a committed underground following in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its moderate level of popularity reflected the broader rise of interest in punk rock during the 1990s, alongside acts such as Rancid, Green Day, and The Offspring. The song "May 16" was featured in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2.

According to a 1994 interview with Shawn Dewey, Lagwagon's original lineup coalesced after the members met in a counseling group, a formation attributed to a shared history of childhood abuse. The account describes the founders as neglected youths of roughly the same age, with Jesse Buglione as the notable exception, and states that all of them had experienced physical abuse from their parents.

Denim & Rhinestones is described as a lively, retro-tinged title track that aligns with the album’s overarching concept of complementary elements working in harmony. The album itself traverses a broad musical landscape, balancing a nostalgic throwback vibe with contemporary freshness, drawing on a range of influences while also offering a personal portrait of Underwood as both a person and an artist. The lead single, “Ghost Story,” has been praised for its writers—Josh Kear, Hillary Lindsey, and David Garcia—who know Underwood well, and she felt from the first listen that recording the song was a necessity.

Denim & Rhinestones is a studio album released in June 2023, whose promotion featured television appearances, live performances, and the release of promotional singles. A promotional single, Take Me Out, appeared on June 9, 2023, ahead of the deluxe re-release, followed by Give Her That on August 11, 2023. The album’s promotion included a June 14 performance of Pink Champagne on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, and a late-June series of appearances in London, including an interview on Lorraine; Pink Champagne was also issued as a promotional single in Australia. In mid-August, four Grand Ole Opry performances (August 19–20) featured new songs—Ghost Story, Velvet Heartbreak, Hate My Heart, and Burn—and on August 21 the new material was added to a set at the Iowa State Fair before an audience of about 14,000. On September 29, an hour-long concert in partnership with iHeartRadio presented additional new songs. In November, the artist performed Crazy Angels in an aerial cage at the American Music Awards. The deluxe edition of Denim & Rhinestones was released on September 22, 2023, adding six additional tracks to the standard album.

According to Adriano Cintra, in an April 2011 interview with Folha de S.Paulo, CSS's third studio album is not conceived as a thematically unified work and draws on influences from club music, reggae, and punk. Ana Rezende has stated that the band sometimes produces reggae that others do not recognize as reggae, while they view it as such. The single "Hits Me Like a Rock" from the third album was featured on the FIFA 12 soundtrack.

On 3 July 2012, Adriano Cintra discussed his then-new project Madrid in an interview and addressed his departure from Cansei de Ser Sexy (CSS). He stated that he had grown tired of his bandmates, describing them as difficult collaborators and alleging that they were unable to play their own instruments.

Estonian United Left Party described its approach to social issues as neither liberal nor conservative, opting for a position that did not align with the conventional labels. In 2024, the party announced a restart intended to reposition it as liberal on social issues.

Estonian United Left Party advocates a progressive taxation framework aimed at equitable revenue generation. It supports levying taxes on corporate profits and an inheritance tax to broaden the tax base for public services. The party also seeks to expand social benefits for those in need and to ensure fair wages for workers in essential public services, including teachers, police officers, and firefighters. It further calls for enhanced social security provisions to strengthen citizen protection.

Oversampling increases the sampling rate beyond the minimum required by the Nyquist criterion. For a signal with bandwidth B = 100 Hz, the sampling frequency must satisfy fs > 2B, i.e., exceed 200 Hz. Fourfold oversampling results in fs = 800 Hz. The anti-aliasing filter that accompanies the analog-to-digital conversion has a transition-band width equal to (fs/2) − B; with fs = 800 Hz, this computes to 400 − 100 = 300 Hz. If the system were operated at 200 Hz, the transition band would effectively be zero Hz (fs/2 − B = 100 − 100 = 0), which is impractical for real-world filters. Consequently, a transition band of about 300 Hz is feasible to implement in practice.

Oversampling frequently incorporates a small amount of dithering noise added to the input signal. The dither serves to linearize quantization and, when combined with an increased sample rate, enables higher effective resolution by dispersing quantization error across a broader spectrum. Even modest levels of noise can produce substantial gains in detail and accuracy. The dithering noise can be positioned outside the frequency band of interest so that it minimally affects the intended signal content. Following acquisition, the excess noise can be removed or suppressed through digital filtering, preserving the enhanced resolution while reducing noise within the targeted frequency range.

In naturalized epistemology, Quine argued that moving epistemology into a naturalistic framework does not eliminate the normative elements inherent in the field. He proposed a division in which theoretical epistemology becomes part of theoretical science, while normative epistemology is recast as a matter of engineering—the technology of anticipating sensory stimulation. Consequently, the normative is naturalized rather than discarded, integrated within a scientific approach to inquiry. Nonetheless, there remains an ongoing debate about whether this naturalized account can fully capture the normativity that characterizes epistemology.

Naturalized epistemology, as articulated by Willard Van Orman Quine, questions the fruitfulness of traditional philosophy of science. Its critique rests on the long-standing failure of philosophers to resolve radical skepticism and Hume’s problem of induction, and it is intensified by the Vienna Circle’s program to reduce mathematics to pure logic, a program Quine contends has not succeeded. He argues that analyses of meaning or truth within science do not accomplish the Cartesian goal of achieving absolute certainty. The unsuccessful reduction of mathematics to logic further implies that scientific knowledge must be described using set-theoretic notions that come with a lower degree of epistemic certainty. Even if one accepts some instability in set theory, attempting to encode scientific knowledge purely as logic or set theory is undermined by the absence of a useful translation back to substantive scientific content. Consequently, without a bidirectional translation between scientific knowledge and formal logical structures, the properties of logic or set theory fail to illuminate our understanding of science.

Numerous major companies operate across the Columbus metropolitan area. Honda maintains its largest North American manufacturing complex in the Marysville area, which is also home to Scotts Miracle-Gro Company, the maker of Miracle-Gro and related fertilizers. In the New Albany area, Intel has selected a site for its newest semiconductor fabrication plant, scheduled to open in 2025 and expected to rank among the largest silicon manufacturing facilities globally. American Electric Power, one of the United States' largest electric utilities, is headquartered in downtown Columbus. In the Polaris area, Mettler Toledo produces precision scales and scientific equipment. Worthington Industries runs a major steel-processing operation primarily on the north side of Columbus near Worthington. Ashland Inc. maintains a large office presence in Dublin, while residential builders M/I Homes and Dominion Homes operate in Columbus.

Columbus's metropolitan area features a range of large-scale venues for concerts and events, including Nationwide Arena, Value City Arena, and Mapfre Stadium, alongside a variety of cultural spaces. The city's music scene is anchored by Kemba Live, which has operated under several names such as Express Live, the Lifestyle Communities Pavilion, and PromoWest Pavilion, together with Newport Music Hall. In 2006, public funding was designated for the renovation and reopening of the Lincoln Theatre, which had previously served as a Black culture center in the city. Nearby, the King Arts Complex hosts a diverse slate of cultural programming. Downtown, a cluster of theatres comprises the Palace Theatre, the Ohio Theatre, the Southern Theatre, and the Riffe Center, the latter housing The Capitol Theatre and two studio theatres. The Columbus Association for the Performing Arts (CAPA), established in 1969 to prevent the Ohio Theatre's demolition, now owns, operates, or manages most of the region's theatres, including the Ohio, Palace, Southern, Riffe, Lincoln, as well as the Drexel, the McCoy Center for the Arts, and Hinson Amphitheater. Since 1990, major entertainment-related projects have encompassed facilities such as Crew Stadium, Nationwide Arena, Value City Arena, the Greater Columbus Convention Center, and the Lifestyle Communities Pavilion.

Task Force 1-41 Infantry was a United States Army heavy battalion task force deployed during the Gulf War from January to March 1991. It was the first coalition unit to breach the Saudi border on February 15, 1991, and to commence ground combat operations in Iraq on February 17, 1991, engaging with both direct and indirect fire. Its primary units comprised the 1st Battalion, 41st Infantry Regiment; the 3rd Battalion, 66th Armor Regiment; and the 4th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery Regiment. The force operated under the command of the 2nd Armored Division (Forward). It was based at Lucius D. Clay Kaserne, located about 24 kilometers north of Bremen in the Federal Republic of Germany.

Task Force Tarawa referred to the 2nd Marine Expeditionary Brigade during the 2003 invasion of Iraq (Operation Iraqi Freedom). Operating as a Marine Air-Ground Task Force (MAGTF), the force integrated ground, aviation, and support elements under a unified command structure. It was commanded by Brigadier General Richard Natonski and was attached to the I Marine Expeditionary Force (I MEF) for the duration of the operation.

Development of the Los Angeles Metro Rail network proceeded through a sequence of openings and extensions beginning July 14, 1990, when the Blue Line began service between Pico and Anaheim Street stations, followed by a September 1, 1990 extension to Downtown Long Beach and Pacific Avenue and a February 15, 1991 northern expansion to 7th Street/Metro Center. The Red Line opened January 30, 1993, linking Union Station with Westlake/MacArthur Park, while the Green Line began service August 12, 1995, running from Norwalk to Redondo Beach. The Red Line then extended west to Wilshire/Western on May 22, 1996, and on June 12, 1999 added a Wilshire/Vermont branch to Hollywood/Vine, with the final segment from Hollywood/Vine to North Hollywood completed on June 24, 2000. The Gold Line commenced July 27, 2003, between Union Station and Sierra Madre Villa, and in August 2006 a reconfiguration split the Red Line to create the Purple Line from Union Station–Wilshire/Western, while Union Station–North Hollywood remained Red Line. The Gold Line was extended to Atlantic station on November 15, 2009. Expo Line service began April 28, 2012 between 7th Street/Metro Center and La Cienega/Jefferson, with two additional Expo stations opening June 20, 2012. In March 2016 the Gold Line extended from Sierra Madre Villa to APU/Citrus College, adding six stations, and later that year, May 20, the Expo Line was extended by seven stations to Santa Monica. The K Line opened October 7, 2022, and the Regional Connector project added two new underground stations and rebuilt the Little Tokyo/Arts District station. Aviation/Century station opened November 3, 2024, followed by the LAX/Metro Transit Center on June 6, 2025, and the first phase of the A Line Foothill Extension opened September 19, 2025, introducing four new stations over 9.1 miles.

The Los Angeles Metro Rail is an urban rail transit system serving Los Angeles County, California, operated by the Los Angeles Metro. The network comprises two rapid-transit lines and four light-rail lines that together serve 107 stations over approximately 121.2 miles (195.1 kilometers) of track. In 2019, it recorded an average of 295,889 weekday riders and a total annual ridership of 93.2 million, ranking it among the largest rapid-transit and light-rail systems in the United States by ridership. The rail network is complemented by two Metro Busway lines that provide bus rapid transit service.

The Academy Award for Best Actress has undergone several procedural reforms since its inception. In the first three ceremonies, nominees were recognized as delivering the best overall performance by an individual, with the work from up to three qualifying films associated with the performer listed alongside the award. At the 3rd Academy Awards (1930), however, only a single film was cited for each winner, regardless of how many eligible performances they had. The 4th Academy Awards introduced the contemporary framework in which nominations are tied to a specific performance in a single film. Beginning with the 9th Academy Awards (1937), the category was capped at a maximum of five nominations per year.

For the Academy Award for Best Actress, nominations are determined by members of the Actors Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences through a single transferable vote system, a preferential method used to compile the slate of nominees. After nominations are established, the winner is selected by a plain plurality vote cast by the entire pool of eligible Academy voters. In this arrangement, the process employs two distinct voting methods and pools: STV within the actors branch for nominations, and a broad, all-member plurality for the final award.

Leo Laporte hosted a weekend technology-focused radio program, known as Leo Laporte: The Tech Guy, through December 2022. The program originated on KFI AM 640 in Los Angeles and was distributed to a broader audience via syndication by Premiere Radio Networks. In addition to his radio work, Laporte made regular Friday morning appearances on KFI alongside Bill Handel. Earlier in his career, he also appeared on several television programs, including Showbiz Tonight, Live with Kelly, and World News Now.

Laporte was born in New York City, the son of geologist Leo F. Laporte, and spent his upbringing in Providence, Rhode Island. He studied Chinese history at Yale University from 1973 to 1976 but left during his junior year to pursue a career in radio broadcasting, adopting early on-air aliases such as Dave Allen and Dan Hayes. His first home computer was an Atari 400. By 1984 he had acquired a Macintosh and contributed a software review to Byte magazine. From 1985 to 1988 he operated MacQueue, one of the earliest Macintosh-only bulletin board systems.

Within the Urstromtal system, several major valleys have distinct names for specific sections. The Lusatian Urstromtal and the Aller Urstromtal are subparts of the broader Breslau-Magdeburg-Bremen Urstromtal. In Brandenburg, Baruth Urstromtal, Berlin Urstromtal, and Eberswalde Urstromtäler are commonly used as short designations for the corresponding portions of the Urstromtal.

Urstromtäler, broad glacial outwash valleys in Central Europe, are notably found in areas corresponding to present-day Poland, Germany, and Denmark, and were at times directly linked to the North Atlantic Ocean. This connection ran through a palaeoriver system known as the Channel River, which transported large volumes of meltwater from interior ice sheets toward the ocean. The link existed during the maximum extents of the Pleistocene glaciations, a period when the British and Fennoscandian ice sheets advanced into and merged within the North Sea region. The resulting drainage and sedimentation produced extensive plains that significantly influenced the geomorphology of the Central European lowlands.

Presidente Epitácio is a municipality in the state of São Paulo, Brazil, named in honor of the Brazilian president Epitácio Pessoa. It covers an area of 1,260 square kilometers and has an estimated population of 44,389 as of 2020, with an elevation of about 310 meters above sea level. The municipality is situated on the Paraná River, which at this location forms the border with the state of Mato Grosso do Sul.

Presidente Epitácio was served by Telecomunicações de São Paulo (TSP). In July 1998, TSP was acquired by Telefónica, which later rebranded its Brazilian operations under the Vivo name in 2012. Today, the Telefónica Brazil entity provides a range of services, including mobile telephony, fixed-line telephone service, internet access via fiber optics and 4G, and television services delivered through satellite and cable platforms.

Camrese is a combined oral contraceptive pill used to prevent pregnancy. It exerts its effect primarily by suppressing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus at the opening of the cervix to hinder sperm passage, and altering the endometrium to reduce the likelihood of implantation. Reported adverse effects include nausea, headaches, breast tenderness, mood changes such as depression, and less commonly liver problems and thromboembolic events. The regimen is not recommended during pregnancy, in the first three weeks after childbirth, or for individuals at high risk of blood clots, though treatment may be initiated immediately after a miscarriage or abortion. Smoking is discouraged for users of combined hormonal contraception due to added cardiovascular risk.

Camrese is a combined oral contraceptive containing ethinylestradiol, a synthetic estrogen, and levonorgestrel, a progestin. It is indicated for contraception, relief of menstruation-related symptoms, treatment of endometriosis, and emergency contraception. The medication is administered by mouth. Some formulations include an iron supplement, such as ferrous bisglycinate or ferrous fumarate.

The rate of combustion is defined as the amount of material that undergoes burning per unit time, reflecting how rapidly the combustion process proceeds. This rate can be quantified using standard mass units, most commonly expressed as grams per second (g/s) or kilograms per second (kg/s).

Perfect combustion refers to the complete oxidation of the fuel with the oxidizer under adiabatic conditions, meaning no heat is exchanged with the surroundings. Under these idealized circumstances, the adiabatic combustion temperature, often called the adiabatic flame temperature, can be determined by applying an energy balance derived from the first law of thermodynamics. In such analyses, the chemical energy released by combustion is assumed to be wholly devoted to heating the fuel, the combustion air or oxygen, and the combustion product gases, collectively referred to as the flue gas. Consequently, the final temperature is obtained by equating the heat of reaction to the sum of the sensible heats of all species at the final state, a calculation that depends on the fuel–oxidizer mixture, initial temperatures, and the heat capacities of the participating substances.

Simon & Schuster expanded its publishing activities in 2015 by launching North Star Way, a publishing unit within the Gallery Publishing Group. The imprint focuses on non-fiction works in self-improvement, inspiration, and mind-body-spirit areas and also functions as a platform and services ecosystem designed to extend authors’ reach beyond traditional publishing. Its offerings span online courses, seminars, workshops, mobile applications, video and audio products, sponsorships and partnerships, and podcasts. The venture is led by Michele Martin, the publisher and founder, who described the name as embodying a mission to help readers chart a course toward a better life and to guide authors beyond publication. In an interview with Kirkus, Martin indicated that North Star Way aims to meet consumers across multiple media and to expand ideas across various platforms. The imprint’s name even intersected with a separate entertainment trademark dispute when Marvel Comics sought to register the superhero Northstar in February 2015; the request was denied because Simon & Schuster had already trademarked North Star Way in January 2015.

On November 25, 2020, ViacomCBS announced its plan to sell Simon & Schuster to Penguin Random House for $2.175 billion, with an expected closing in 2022. The deal was subsequently blocked by U.S. federal judge Florence Y. Pan on October 31, 2022. Bertelsmann announced an appeal the following day, on November 1, 2022, but the appeal was canceled on November 21, 2022.

ATN Zoom is an Indian entertainment channel that concentrates on Bollywood and the broader Indian entertainment industry. The channel delivers entertainment news, conducts interviews with leading film stars, and presents film reviews, while also featuring music programming and other related content.
ATN Zoom is a Canadian Category B Hindi-language specialty channel owned by Asian Television Network (ATN). It carries programming supplied by the Zoom network and also airs Canadian content.

Chemdex attracted venture capital totaling $45 million, with notable backers including Robert A. Swanson, the founder of Genentech, as well as the venture firms Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and CMGI.

Chemdex was founded in September 1997 by David Perry, who at the time served as a mid-level manager overseeing refinery operations for Exxon. Perry's business plan for the venture earned second place in a Harvard University competition.

The ecological role of Tyrannosaurus rex—whether it functioned primarily as a predator or as a scavenger—has been a subject of ongoing debate. The discussion traces back to Lawrence Lambe's 1917 analysis, which argued that large theropods might have been mainly scavengers, citing the apparent lack of tooth wear on Gorgosaurus as evidence. That interpretation overlooked the fact that theropod dentition was rapidly replaced, a feature that could mask wear even in active feeders. Since the initial discovery of Tyrannosaurus, most researchers have favored a predatory lifestyle, consistent with its cranial morphology and biomechanics. Nevertheless, as with many contemporary apex predators, Tyrannosaurus would likely have scavenged or stolen kills when the opportunity arose, reflecting an opportunistic feeding strategy rather than a strict classification as either hunter or scavenger.

Tyrannosaurus lived during the Lancian faunal stage of the Maastrichtian age, placing it toward the end of the Late Cretaceous. Its geographic range extended from Canada in the north to at least New Mexico in the south, within Laramidia.

Within the Paranoia tabletop role-playing game, the position of Chief Happiness Officer was introduced as part of the game’s Mandatory Bonus Fun Duties with the 1984 release, and the role was further formalized in the 1986 Acute Paranoia supplement. The officer’s primary task is to ensure that everyone under their care remains happy. In Paranoia’s dystopian setting, happiness is mandatory by law, and failure to comply can incur punishment. The officer is empowered to employ a wide range of means to enforce contentment, from morale-boosting activities such as choir singing to coercive measures, including heavy medications intended to deliver artificial but compulsory happiness.

Chief happiness officer (CHO) is a management role focused on overseeing employee happiness within a company. The position is sometimes referred to as chief fun officer. The role likely originated in North America and has been adopted by European and UK companies. Its primary aim is to ensure workers' welfare needs are met, supporting overall well-being and engagement across the workforce.

Raï'n'B is a musical genre that emerged in France in the early 2000s. It combines elements of Algerian raï with contemporary French R&B, producing a hybrid style that fuses North African melodic traits with Western urban vocal and production practices. The genre’s rhythm and production are influenced by house and dance music, contributing a club-oriented feel to its overall sound.

Raï'n'B is a musical fusion of raï and contemporary R&B. In 2004, two compilations highlighted the blend: Raï'n'B Fever by Kore & Skalp and Des 2 mots by DJ Kim and DJ Goldfingers. French singer Amine has described himself as the godfather of the genre. He rose to prominence in 2005 with the track Ma vie, which peaked at number 15 on the French charts, while his other songs Sobri (a duet with Leslie) and J'voulais also achieved notable chart success in France.

Élisabeth Baume-Schneider completed her secondary education in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1983, then studied social sciences at the University of Neuchâtel, where she earned a licentiate in 1987. She subsequently worked as a social worker in Franches-Montagnes from 1989 to 2002, and later joined the cantonal administration of Jura.

Élisabeth Baume-Schneider, born Élisabeth Schneider on 24 December 1963, is a Swiss politician who serves as a member of the Federal Council for the Social Democratic Party. She was elected to the council on 7 December 2022 and has held office since 2023, becoming the first representative from the Canton of Jura to sit on the Federal Council.

USinternetworking, Inc. (USi) was an application service provider that delivered outsourced business applications hosted over the Internet or through a private network connection. The company's pricing combined an upfront installation charge with a fixed monthly fee. In October 2006, USi was acquired by AT&T.
USinternetworking filed for bankruptcy in January 2002; with financing provided by Bain Capital, the company emerged from bankruptcy in May 2002, and later merged with Interpath.

The Republic of Lucca gained international renown for its exquisite and high-priced textiles, a status driven by a technological edge in weaving and dyeing. It maintained a tightly guarded monopoly over advanced textile technologies, including specialized looms and combs for brocades and velvets, as well as a silk-twisting mill. Luccan artisans could rival Damascus's finest wares, and through the end of the Renaissance Lucca remained the principal Italian center for silk cloth production. Its silk textiles were exported across Europe and into Asia, illustrating a broad distribution network; evidence of this reach is seen in the early sixteenth century when Portuguese traders in Calcutta found Luccan silk in local bazaars, signaling the material's extensive diffusion.

Following the death of Matilda of Tuscany in 1115, Lucca began to develop as an autonomous commune. Its administration was formally recognized by Margrave Conrad in 1120. In 1160, Lucca acquired the feudal rights from Margrave Welf VI, thereby placing the city under the direct sovereignty of the emperors. The recognition of its governance by Emperor Frederick in 1162 reaffirmed its status. Consequently, Lucca retained its status as an independent republic for well over five centuries.

Hal Leonard Corporation is a prominent music publishing company that produces sheet music, songbooks, and method books that include audio components, as well as a broad range of band, orchestra, and choral arrangements, reference books, instructional videos, and instrumental accompaniments. The firm also acts as a distributor for other brands, including Gibraltar, Gretsch Drums, Avid, and Blue Microphones, among many others. In 1989 Hal Leonard acquired Jenson Publications, expanding its catalog with additional band, orchestra, and choral titles. Five years later, the company began distributing Homespun Music Instruction's instructional video and audio materials.

Hal Leonard Corporation is a publisher, distributor, and rights representative for a broad array of print music spanning classical and popular repertoires. In North America, the company holds exclusive license rights to the print catalogs of Disney Music Group and Universal Music Publishing Group. It also serves as the North American distributor for numerous American and European classical publishers, including G. Schirmer, Boosey & Hawkes, Éditions Durand, and Faber Piano Adventures. Through the acquisition of numerous school music publishing houses over the past four decades, Hal Leonard has emerged as one of the largest publishers in music education. Its primary competitor in the educational market is Alfred Music.

In August 2020, AOL Time Warner announced a substantial restructuring that led to the layoff of approximately 800 employees. Of these, around 600 were employees at Warner, while more than 150 came from HBO. The reductions hit WarnerMedia's Atlanta base particularly hard, with the marketing and cable operations teams bearing the heaviest impact.

WarnerMedia International coordinates international variations of WarnerMedia's domestic television channels and region-specific networks. It handles the local execution of WarnerMedia's linear businesses and commercial activities across its markets. The unit also manages legacy streaming services, such as HBO Portugal and HBO Go in countries not yet served by HBO Max, and oversees regional programming for HBO Max to tailor content to local audiences.

Melisma, the technique of singing a sequence of notes on a single syllable, is exemplified in a traditional French carol tune that is used for the English-language carol Angels We Have Heard on High, and in Great Britain is also employed for Angels from the Realms of Glory. The melody is recognized for containing one of the most well-known melismatic sequences in Christian hymn music, particularly within its refrain. In that section, the vowel sound of the word Gloria is extended across a long series of notes, with the o in Gloria sustained for 16 notes, and this prolonged setting occurring twice in the refrain.

Melisma is a vocal technique in which several notes are sung to a single syllable and is commonly used in Middle Eastern, African, African-American, Irish Sean-nós, and flamenco music. African musical traditions infused the blues with melismatic elements, and the influence of African-American music helped melisma become common in Western popular genres. In Gaelic music, the practice appears in early Appalachian music, and it has remained a defining feature of American country and western music since its inception.

Roscommon, Michigan, lies near three state parks: South Higgins Lake State Park, North Higgins Lake State Park, and Hartwick Pines State Park. A 160-acre (65 ha) parcel within the Au Sable State Forest, known as the Roscommon Red Pines, lies about eight miles (13 km) east of the village and represents an old-growth stand of red pines. The South Branch of the Au Sable River passes through Roscommon and is popular for kayaking, canoeing, and fishing.

Roscommon, Michigan, began as a settlement as early as 1845 when George Robinson of Detroit established a presence there, shortly after Roscommon County had been organized in 1840. The community took its name from Roscommon County, which itself derives from County Roscommon in Ireland. The Roscommon post office opened on January 9, 1873, with Alfred Bennett serving as the first postmaster. In 1875, Roscommon was designated the county seat, and it was incorporated as a village in 1882.

Pierfranco Vianelli (born 20 October 1946) is a former Italian cyclist who achieved success at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City, where he won the gold medal in the individual road race. He also earned a bronze medal in the team time trial as part of the Italian squad at the same Games.

William Morgan, an actuary, formed close ties with radical figures in his later life, an association enabled by his uncle, the dissenting philosopher Richard Price. Among those he counted as friends were the pamphleteer Tom Paine, and he also befriended the radical politician Francis Burdett.

William Morgan, an actuary, developed an interest in scientific experimentation under the guidance of Joseph Priestley, a family friend who advised him on such matters. He is credited with being the first to document the non-visible radiation emitted when an electric current passes through a partially evacuated glass tube, an observation that has been described as the earliest x-ray tube.

In June 2018, Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan approved a three-year economic stimulus package worth AED 50 billion intended to bolster the economy over the period. He also commissioned a review of building regulations to spur urban development and support the modernization of the built environment.

Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan (born 11 March 1961), also known as MBZ or MbZ, is an Emirati royal and politician who serves as the third president of the United Arab Emirates and has been the ruler of Abu Dhabi since 2022.

The National Socialist Labor Party of Russia (NSLPR) arose following the Lokot Autonomy's perceived success, which spurred the creation of a Russian faction aligned with National Socialist aims. The organization operated on German territory under German control, reflecting direct German involvement in its supervision. Nevertheless, the NSLPR maintained an independent leadership, with its internal command structure functioning separately from direct German management.

National Socialist Labor Party of Russia (NSLPR) espoused anti-Semitism as a central component of its platform. Bronislav Kaminski asserted that Jews had transformed socialism into Marxism, communism, and Bolshevism, and had recast national imperialism into capitalist imperialism, a viewpoint that contributed to the party's adoption of national-socialist ideology. A further factor cited was the desire to demonstrate loyalty to Germany. The Russian People's Liberation Army, the principal component of Lokot Autonomy's armed forces, operated as a national-socialist army. This force associated itself with agrarianism, a relation that significantly influenced the party's thinking and program, and is regarded as strong evidence of Lokot's collaboration with Germany.

The article details the player rosters for the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup, staged in the United States. Sixteen national teams participated in the tournament, with each team allowed to register up to 20 players. A minimum of two goalkeepers had to be named in every squad. Only athletes appearing on these lists were eligible to take part in the competition. FIFA published the final squad lists on 13 September 2003.

FIFA 17 introduced several notable changes to gameplay, including enhanced attacking techniques, a comprehensive overhaul of player physicality, an Active Intelligence system to guide on-pitch decisions, and a rewritten approach to set pieces. At Gamescom 2016, EA announced that Squad Building Challenges (SBC) and FUT Champions would be incorporated into FIFA Ultimate Team. These features, however, would not be available in the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 editions of the game.

FIFA 17 is a football simulation video game in the FIFA series developed by Electronic Arts. Upon its release, it received positive reviews from critics, who praised the gameplay, the adoption of the Frostbite engine, and the quality of sound and overall presentation. The title also achieved notable commercial success, becoming the fastest-selling edition in the franchise's history.

Based on the 2018 New Zealand census data on space heating, heat pumps were the most common primary heating method in households, representing 47.3% of primary heating usage. Electric resistance heaters accounted for 44.1%, while wood burners made up 32.3%. These figures illustrate the prominent role of electric heating technologies in residential heating at that time.

During 2022, the New Zealand Human Rights Commission advocated policy measures to ease housing costs, including an immediate freeze on rent increases and an expansion of the accommodation supplement to provide relief amid the cost of living crisis. In July 2022, the Commission released its People's Inquiry into Student Wellbeing, which found that around two-thirds of tertiary students could not cover basic living costs such as food, rent, and healthcare.

Scarecrow contains several tracks that were originally recorded by other artists. For instance, Pushing Up Daisies was first cut by Kevin Welch on Life Down Here on Earth (1995); Big Money, issued earlier as It Pays Big Money by Mark Chesnutt on Lost in the Feeling (2000); Don't Cross the River, previously recorded by America for Homecoming (1972); and Squeeze Me In, which had appeared on Lee Roy Parnell's We All Get Lucky Sometimes (1995).

Scarecrow is the eighth studio album by American country music artist Garth Brooks, released on November 13, 2001. The release debuted at number one on both the Billboard 200 and the Top Country Albums chart, reflecting its strong commercial reception. The album has been certified five times platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). In Canada, it received the Best Selling Album award at the 2002 Canadian Country Music Association Awards.

In 2025, the Mahatao Forward Operating Base was established as a military facility located in the municipality of Mahatao on the Batanes Islands. The installation is operated by the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

Public infrastructure in the Batanes Islands included the construction of roads, ports, bridges, churches, and government buildings, forming the framework for administration and daily life. The spread of Spanish limestone construction techniques led to the development of sturdy, fortified bridges, with several examples remaining in Ivana and Mahatao. By 1890, many Ivatans traveled to Manila and joined the ilustrados, bringing home revolutionary ideas associated with the Katipunan. This growing discontent with Spanish rule culminated in the killing of the ruling General Fortea and the declaration of the end of Spanish rule.

John Mayall's Bluesbreakers underwent a series of lineup changes in the late 1960s, beginning with the addition of Mick Taylor, who contributed to the recording of Crusade on 12 July 1967. Subsequently, John McVie left to join Fleetwood Mac, and Tony Reeves replaced him for the Bare Wires sessions, an album that would become the group's highest-charting release in the United Kingdom. Later departures followed, as Reeves, Dick Heckstall-Smith, and Jon Hiseman left to form Colosseum. After the release of Blues from Laurel Canyon, Taylor departed to join the Rolling Stones. Thereafter, the Bluesbreakers name was no longer used on Mayall’s albums.

John Mayall's Bluesbreakers continued to tour and release material, producing more than fifty albums with periods of inactivity, but the group did not reclaim the critical or popular acclaim enjoyed by their early work. In 2003, Eric Clapton, Mick Taylor, and Chris Barber reunited with the Bluesbreakers for Mayall's 70th Birthday Concert in Liverpool, a performance that was subsequently issued on CD and DVD. For 2004, the lineup featured Buddy Whittington, Joe Yuele, Hank Van Sickle, and Tom Canning, and the band conducted a United Kingdom tour with Mick Taylor making a guest appearance.

Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) use large segmented mirrors to collect Cherenkov light produced by extensive air showers initiated by high-energy gamma rays and focus it onto a camera composed of photomultiplier tubes. The PMTs are connected to fast electronics that amplify, digitize, and record the resulting shower image. The most effective observational approach employs a network of telescopes spaced roughly 70 to 120 meters apart, enabling stereoscopic views of the air showers. The array configuration also lowers the energy threshold by discriminating against local muon events, whose narrow Cherenkov light cones are typically captured by a single telescope. Array-based shower reconstruction and background rejection provide about an order of magnitude improvement in sensitivity and yield better angular and energy resolution compared with a single telescope. This advantage has been demonstrated by the H.E.S.S. telescope array, which has used it to detect several new sources of very high energy gamma-ray photons in recent years.

Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) emerged from the efforts of the Whipple collaboration, culminating in the detection of TeV gamma-ray emission from the Crab Nebula in 1989. The Whipple 10-meter telescope subsequently identified the first extragalactic TeV gamma-ray source, the active galaxy Markarian 421. The HEGRA array pioneered stereoscopic observation by employing multiple telescopes to capture three-dimensional images of air showers. The MAGIC project at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma began with a single 17-meter telescope in 2004, with a second 17-meter instrument added in 2009. The FACT, the First G-APD Cherenkov Telescope, facility at the same observatory began operations in 2011. In Namibia, the H.E.S.S. collaboration expanded the field with a 28-meter telescope—the largest IACT to date—that has been operational since July 2012.

In January 2016, the Wikimedia Foundation announced the establishment of an endowment intended to safeguard the organization’s long-term viability. The endowment operates as a donor-advised fund within the Tides Foundation. The Foundation aims to accumulate $100 million over the next decade, with a target date around 2026. The initial gift for the endowment came from Craig Newmark, who contributed $1 million. In 2017, donors linked to the Arcadia Fund, Peter Baldwin and Lisbet Rausing, contributed $5 million.

The Wikimedia Foundation maintains an endowment with a target of growing capital to $130.4 million in the forthcoming fiscal year. Governance and administration of the endowment have been a point of controversy among observers. The Tides Foundation, a 501(c)(3) organization, had pledged to improve transparency; however, seven years on there were still no publicly disclosed details concerning the foundation’s expenditures and personnel compensation. In parallel, the WMF has experienced a substantial increase in salary costs, rising from about $7 million in 2010–11 to $88 million in 2021–22.

U.S. Route 59 is a United States highway that generally runs north–south, although in parts of Texas it is signed as an east–west route. A relatively late addition to the U.S. Highway System, it now spans from the Canadian border to the Mexican border, functioning as a border-to-border corridor and forming part of the NAFTA Corridor Highway System. For much of its length, US 59 runs roughly parallel to U.S. Route 75, remaining within about 100 miles (160 km) of it until it veers southwest through the Houston area. The route’s numbering is considered anomalous, since US 59 lies to the west of or shares alignment with US 71 for much of its course.
