In Missouri, it passes through St. Joseph where it intersects Interstate 229 and Interstate 29. Its northern terminus is near Lancaster, Minnesota, at the Lancaster–Tolstoi Border Crossing on the Canadian border, where it continues as Manitoba Highway 59; its southern terminus is at the Mexican border in Laredo, Texas, where the highway continues as Mexican Federal Highway 85D.

In 1933, a proposal circulated to incorporate a substantial portion of the route now designated as US 59 and all of US 96 in Texas into US 71. The idea was discussed at a meeting of the United States Good Roads Association held in Beaumont, where planners outlined a plan to divert US 71 from Louisiana and reroute it southward from the Texarkana area through East Texas.

Within the Babuyan archipelago, Didicas Island hosts Didicas Volcano, a small volcanic islet. It lies about 22 kilometers northeast of Camiguin Island. The island emerged during a volcanic eruption and subsequently rose to more than 200 meters above sea level, being recognised as a permanent island in 1952.

The Babuyan Group of Islands in the Philippines acts as an aggregation site for endangered humpback whales in Southeast Asia. It is valued for its natural world significance and contribution to Philippine biodiversity, a status that has spurred advocacy for protective measures. Scientific and conservation groups advocate designating the area as a national park and seeking its inclusion on the UNESCO World Heritage List. In recent times, humpback whales have re-colonized the area, which sits as the Philippines’ only wintering ground for these animals. Historical records from the Babuyan Group of Islands regarding humpbacks have not been confirmed.

The Kugelrohr is a compact distillation apparatus in which a tube furnace or electric heater, controlled by a thermostat, heats a sequence of bulbs connected by ground-glass joints. The substance to be distilled is placed in the terminal bulb at the end of the assembly, while the remaining bulbs collect distillates as fractions are produced. Each bulb associated with a collected fraction is cooled with water or ice to facilitate condensation. A motor drives the rotation of the bulb train, reducing bumping, promoting even heating, and increasing the evaporation surface area.

The Kugelrohr, a German term meaning “ball tube,” is a short-path distillation apparatus operated under vacuum. It is used to distill small quantities of compounds, especially those with high boiling points, typically above 300 °C, by carrying out the distillation under substantially reduced pressure. The instrument employs a heated, sealed arrangement in which small spherical vessels rotate inside, enabling vapor to travel a short distance before condensation and thereby increasing efficiency while reducing thermal decomposition risk.

During the 633–656 Islamic conquest of Persia, Peroz, the son of the last Sasanian ruler, and his court sought refuge at the Tang court in Chang’an, where Peroz was appointed head of a governorate of Persia centered near present-day Zaranj in Afghanistan; contemporaneously, the Rashidun Caliphate under Uthman sent an embassy to the Tang court during Persia’s upheavals. Arab sources claim that Qutayba ibn Muslim briefly seized Kashgar from Chinese control and withdrew after an accord, though modern historians discount this account. In 715, the Abbasids deposed Ikhshid of Ferghana Valley and installed Alutar, prompting the deposed ruler to flee to Kucha and seek Chinese assistance; China dispatched about 10,000 troops under Zhang Xiaosong to Ferghana, defeating Alutar and the Arab occupation at Namangan and restoring Ikhshid. The Tang subsequently defeated Arab Umayyad forces at the Battle of Aksu in 717, sending Al-Yashkuri into flight toward Tashkent, while the Turgesh eliminated Arab Umayyad presence in the region. By the 740s, however, Abbasid forces reestablished a foothold in Ferghana and in Sogdiana. At Talas in 751, Karluk mercenaries serving with the Chinese defected and aided the Abbasids in defeating Tang forces under Gao Xianzhi, an clash that is linked to the diffusion of Chinese papermaking to the West, reaching Europe by the twelfth century via Arab Spain. On June 11, 758, an Abbasid embassy arrived at Chang’an simultaneously with Uyghur envoys bearing gifts for the Tang emperor. Finally, in 788–789, China concluded a military alliance with the Uyghur Turks, who defeated Tibetan forces twice—near Gaochang in Dzungaria in 789 and near Ningxia on the Yellow River in 791.

During the Tang dynasty, rice increasingly served as the principal staple in the southern regions, and it also gained widespread use in the north where the central administration resided. Traditionally, Chinese agrarian scholarship enumerated a quintet of staple crops that included sesame, various legumes, wheat, panicled millet, and glutinous millet. Rice was not regarded as part of this five-grain set from the era of Shennong through the early second millennium BCE, a distinction attributed to the unsettled climate of southern China that hindered consistent rice cultivation. By the Ming dynasty, the encyclopedist Song Yingxing noted that roughly seven-tenths of the civilian diet consisted of rice, signaling a long-term shift toward its dominance. In this context, the Tang period marks a transition in which rice cemented its role as the chief staple in the south and expanded its prominence into the northern heartland under central authority.

Vishishtadvaita, a sub-school of Vedanta articulated by Ramanuja in the 11th–12th centuries, holds that individual souls (jivatman) and Brahman (identified with Vishnu) are fundamentally distinct, a difference that remains permanent rather than transcended. It also asserts the unity of all souls and teaches that the individual soul can realize its identity with Brahman within a framework of qualified monism. As a form of qualified non-dualism, it maintains that liberation is achievable for all beings, and like Advaita Vedanta, it posits that both Brahman and Prakriti (the world) are real and absolutes, not illusory, with saguna Brahman (God with attributes) likewise real. God is conceived as possessing both soul and body, and the material universe is described as the manifestation of God’s body. The path to Brahman (Vishnu) lies in devotion (bhakti) to the personal deity, accompanied by constant remembrance of his beauty and love. Accordingly, bhakti directed toward saguna Brahman is presented as the means to liberation.

Vedanta, a major school within Hindu philosophy, developed by assimilating ideas from several orthodox āstika systems and soon emerged as the most influential framework within Hindu thought. Its diverse strands gave rise to a wide range of Hindu traditions. In the south and parts of southeast India, Sri Vaishnavism—based on Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita Vedanta—stands as a prominent lineage. In northern, eastern, central, and western regions, Ramananda founded the Vaishnav Bhakti movement, which drew on Vishishtadvaita to promote devotional practice across vast areas. Across eastern, northern (particularly the Braj region), western and central India, numerous Vaishnavism traditions trace their roots to various sub-schools of Bhedabheda Vedanta. In the northeast, Advaita Vedanta influenced Krishna Vaishnavism in Assam. The Madhva tradition of Vaishnavism, rooted in Dvaita Vedanta, arose in coastal Karnataka.

Kid Cudi, alongside Higgins, introduced the Moon Man comic book series, with the first issue released on January 31, 2024. It quickly sold out due to high demand, outpacing distributor supply and prompting an urgent reprint. The second issue followed on April 17, 2024, and the third on July 10, 2024. On the same day as the third issue's release, Cudi issued the single “Dreams I See” to support the Moon Man launch.

In July 2016, Kid Cudi was announced to join the Fox television series Empire, making his on-screen debut in season three as an independent musician who becomes a rival to Hakeem both in the recording studio and in the show's dynamics. He later departed the series citing creative differences. In 2017, Cudi appeared in the comedy film Killing Hasselhoff.

Motion JPEG (M-JPEG) encodes each frame separately using intraframe compression, with no dependencies between frames. As a result, image quality is governed primarily by the spatial complexity of individual frames rather than by motion or temporal variation. Smooth and monotone frames typically compress well and preserve details with relatively few artifacts. By contrast, frames containing intricate textures or fine lines—such as text—can exhibit discrete cosine transform artifacts, including ringing, smudging, and macroblocking. The absence of interframe references means temporal variation has little impact on quality. In testing video formats, extreme cases of random motion and static scenes are often used to stress interframe codecs, but M-JPEG is not hindered by these extremes.

Motion JPEG encodes each frame as an individual JPEG image; however, its efficiency has become limited relative to modern video codecs. Several later standards replace or augment JPEG-style coding with more effective techniques. For example, H.263v2 Annex I and MPEG-4 Part 2 apply frequency-domain prediction of transform coefficients, while H.264/MPEG-4 AVC uses spatial prediction and adaptive transform block sizes to better exploit redundancy. In addition, entropy coding has grown more sophisticated since JPEG's original design. Taken together, these developments render Motion JPEG an inefficient recording mechanism compared with newer standards.

Surviving members of GWAR released a video statement announcing the formation of the David Brockie Foundation, a charitable fund aimed at encouraging future talent and preserving Brockie's body of work. The foundation's initial objective is to construct a memorial monument to Brockie in Richmond. Former bassist Mike Bishop, known as Beefcake the Mighty, re-joined the band as vocalist for their first performance without Brockie, which took place at the fifth GWAR B-Q at Hadad's Lake. A public memorial service was held the day before; Oderus Urungus was given a Viking funeral.

Adam Green, the creator of Holliston, made several onstage appearances with GWAR, often introducing encores. At various United States performances, GWAR staged a narrative in which the entire Holliston cast was killed onstage and subsequently fed to GWAR's world maggot and a meat grinder. Green was in the process of scripting a third season of Holliston when Dave Brockie, GWAR's longtime frontman, died in March 2014 from a heroin overdose.

In far-field electromagnetic radiation, the source-free Maxwell curl equations establish that the time derivative of one field is proportional to the curl of the other, a relation that leads to the electric and magnetic fields being in phase. Light’s frequency, a measure of how rapidly the fields oscillate, is expressed in hertz, with one hertz corresponding to a single oscillation per second. In general, light comprises a range of frequencies that superpose to form the resulting wave. When such frequencies propagate through a medium, they refract at different angles, a phenomenon known as dispersion.

Electromagnetic radiation is traditionally described by classical waves, but quantum theory treats light as exhibiting wave–particle duality, a central concept in understanding its nature. Quantum objects such as photons can display wave-like or particle-like properties depending on the experimental arrangement, underscoring how observation influences outcomes. In the Copenhagen interpretation, measurement causes the quantum state to collapse to a definite result, whereas the many-worlds interpretation contends that all possible results are realized in branching, parallel universes. A further approach, pilot-wave theory, holds that particle motion is guided deterministically by an accompanying wave. The dual character of single photons has been demonstrated in the double-slit experiment, which reveals interference patterns alongside detected particle events.

The Pacific Fleet extended its operations to the Indian Ocean and, in 1968, established the 8th Operational (Indian Ocean) Squadron. This development followed Britain's announced plan to withdraw forces east of the Suez Canal by 1971. The squadron was intended to provide a defensive counterweight to the United States Navy and to promote Soviet foreign policy objectives. It conducted regular visits and port calls across the Indian subcontinent, the Persian Gulf, and along the East African coast.

The Russian Pacific Fleet has a record of distinguished service, as reflected by extensive recognition awarded to its personnel and units. Thousands of sailors and officers received orders and medals for outstanding military service. More than fifty individuals were awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union. Eighteen ships and fleet formations were designated as Soviet Guards for their exemplary performance, and sixteen ships and fleet units were awarded the Order of the Red Banner. Collectively, these distinctions illustrate the fleet’s significant contribution and prestige within the Soviet naval tradition.

Louisiana is home to a large number of salt domes, geological features that formed when seawater evaporated extensively in a shallow Gulf of Mexico setting. The resulting salt structures number in the several hundreds across the state, with Avery Island among the best known examples. In addition to serving as sources of salt, these domes frequently function as underground traps for oil and gas, making them important reservoirs in petroleum geology.

Beginning in 1719, the importation of enslaved Africans to Louisiana rose significantly. The French ships Du Maine and Aurore arrived in New Orleans with more than 500 enslaved people, marking a shift from earlier patterns in which enslaved laborers were transported primarily from the French West Indies. By the end of 1721, New Orleans's total population reached 1,256, with roughly half of its inhabitants enslaved, illustrating the rapid growth of slavery in the colony during this period.

The initial segment of Guiyang's tram Line T2 is currently under construction as part of the Guiyang Metro system. The phase encompasses 10.92 km of track and includes 13 stations, with a planned opening scheduled for 2025.

Guiyang Metro Line 1 is a rapid transit line in Guiyang that received planning approval in 2006 and construction approval on 6 May 2013. The line traverses the Guanshanhu, Yunyan, Nanming, and Huaxi districts, and it crosses the Nanming River twice, thereby linking the downtown area with outlying districts. It operates with two depots, Xiaohe Depot and Guanshanhu Depot, and is electrified by an overhead line. The alignment runs from the northwest toward the south, forming an east–west oriented corridor that connects central Guiyang with its peripheral areas.

James Purdey & Sons, also commonly referred to as Purdey, is a British gunmaker based in London, England. The firm specialises in high-end bespoke sporting shotguns and rifles. It holds Royal Warrants of appointment as gun and rifle makers to the British royal family and to other European royal families.

James Purdey & Sons has a long-standing affiliation with the manufacture of back-action hammer-ejector shotguns, a tradition shaped by the patronage of King George V and Earl de Grey. The majority of these firearms were produced between 1895 and 1931. In 2004 Purdey reintroduced the Hammer Ejector to its product range. The revived Hammer Ejector employs a sidelock action, styled after Purdey’s 1870s bar-in-wood guns.

Rock music in Bosnia and Herzegovina developed within the broader Yugoslav rock scene, with punk rock entering the country from Slovenia and establishing roots in major urban centers such as Sarajevo, Tuzla, and Mostar. Compared with other Yugoslav republics, the Bosnian scene was dominated by rock music, which played a central role in its musical culture. Among regional acts, Bijelo Dugme is widely regarded as one of the most legendary and influential bands in the Balkans, illustrating the enduring impact of Bosnian rock on the wider area.

Rock music in Bosnia and Herzegovina expanded notably from the late 1990s into the early 2000s, a period that saw a surge of new bands forming across the scene. The genre mix during this era was strongly influenced by heavy metal and alternative rock, shaping a distinctive national sound. Among the more influential groups are Sikter, Letu Štuke, Skroz, Zoster, and Dubioza kolektiv, whose activities helped define the country’s rock landscape in the postwar years. A central figure in the broader alternative music milieu is Elvir Laković Laka, a renowned singer whose work has been closely associated with the genre, and who represented Bosnia and Herzegovina at the Eurovision Song Contest.

Huntersville, North Carolina, had a total of 9,171 households, of which 41.9 percent contained children under 18, 64.6 percent were married couples living together, and 7.5 percent were headed by a female householder with no husband present; non-family households accounted for 25.2 percent. Single-person households represented 19.2 percent, including 3.4 percent where the occupant was aged 65 or older. The average household size was 2.67 persons, while the average family size was 3.09.

Huntersville is a suburban town located in the northern part of Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, United States. As of the 2020 census, the town had a population of 61,376, ranking it as the 15th-most populous municipality in North Carolina. It is part of the Charlotte metropolitan area and lies roughly 14 miles (23 km) north of Charlotte.

The Guangdong Museum comprises several principal display zones, including a gallery for historical artifacts, a nature-focused exhibition space, and a vernacular art area, which together house its permanent collections. In addition, the museum presents rotating temporary exhibitions that are updated frequently, allowing the public to encounter foreign artworks and exotic treasures. The atrium and connecting corridors function as rest areas for visitors, while the administrative offices are situated on the building’s top floor.

An upper-level gallery at Guangdong Museum traces Guangzhou's history from prehistoric times to the modern era. The city has long served as a center of international trade, a legacy reflected in the breadth of its historical collections. A substantial portion of the items from the semi-colonial period in the collection originate from England, including postcards, photographs, and archival documents.

During the 2004 United States presidential election, Michael Badnarik stood as the Libertarian candidate and finished in fourth place, receiving 397,265 votes, about 0.3 percent of the national popular vote. The tally was 12,834 votes more than the Browne/Olivier ticket had secured in the 2000 election.

During the 2004 presidential campaign, Michael Badnarik and Green Party candidate David Cobb were arrested in St. Louis, Missouri, on October 8, 2004, for civil disobedience while protesting their exclusion from the 2004 presidential debates. They crossed a police barricade in an effort to serve an Order to Show Cause to the Commission on Presidential Debates.

Within the broader history of African Americans in San Antonio, the city’s Martin Luther King, Jr. Commission held its first officially sanctioned march in 1987, building on a tradition of demonstrations that began in 1968. The event has since attracted more than 300,000 participants, making it one of the largest marches in the United States.

Across San Antonio and Texas more broadly, the history of African Americans in the city is marked by a pattern of progress alongside persistent inequality. In 2007, the state designated Juneteenth as an official holiday after a bill introduced by Al Edwards, a Houston-based member of the Texas House of Representatives. Juneteenth subsequently gained national recognition when it was designated a federal holiday in 2021. Even as these commemorations grew, observers have noted that more than seventy years after slavery legally ended, African Americans in the region continued to experience unequal treatment in various aspects of public life, reflecting enduring challenges within the area's civil rights history.

By 2011, YouTube recorded over 3 billion video views per day and about 48 hours of new content uploaded every minute, with roughly 30% of videos accounting for 99% of total views, indicating a heavy concentration of audience attention on a subset of content. That year also saw a redesign of the interface and the introduction of a new logo in a darker red hue. A further interface refresh in 2013 aimed to unify the user experience across desktop, television, and mobile platforms. By 2013, uploads surpassed 100 hours per minute, and by November 2014 the rate had grown to around 300 hours per minute.

On September 23, 2025, Alphabet announced that it would reinstate YouTube creators who had been banned for misinformation concerning COVID-19 and the 2020 U.S. election. The decision came amid broader debates about free speech in the United States and alongside the suspension of late-night host Jimmy Kimmel, which some cited in discussions of content moderation; United States Senator JD Vance defended Kimmel’s suspension. Vance invoked a letter from Alphabet's general counsel, Daniel F. Donovan, addressed to House Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan, which alleged that the Biden administration pressured YouTube to remove content that did not violate rules but contained misinformation. Alphabet said it would lift bans on creators linked to the cited content, though those claims have not been formally proven. In a related legal backdrop, the Supreme Court in 2024 dismissed Murthy v. Missouri for lack of standing, ruling 6–3 that Missouri and Louisiana attorneys general and others lacked standing in a First Amendment challenge regarding government pressure on social media. The move to reinstate creators who engaged in misinformation was criticized for prioritizing free expression over factual accuracy.

C# integrates LINQ with IntelliSense support in development environments, aiding developers with autocompletion and contextual code insight when composing queries. It provides strong filtering capabilities for data retrieval while enforcing type safety through compile-time error checking. This combination maintains a consistent approach to querying data across a variety of sources, from in-memory collections to external data stores. Language constructs designed for use with C# and LINQ include query expressions, along with lambda expressions and anonymous types, while features such as implicitly typed variables, extension methods, and object initializers facilitate concise and expressive programming.

C# 2.0 added generics, enabling the use of type parameters with classes, interfaces, and methods to produce type-safe, reusable code. A common example is List<T>, a resizable collection that holds elements of a single specified type T. Type parameters can be constrained to enforce certain requirements, such as T deriving from a particular base type, implementing a given interface, being a reference type, being a value type, or providing a public parameterless constructor. These constraints can be combined, and multiple interface constraints may be applied to a single type parameter.

ISO 3166-1 includes the alpha-3 codes, which are three-letter identifiers assigned to countries. These codes are generally seen as providing a stronger visual link to the corresponding country names than the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, aiding recognition in various contexts.

ISO 3166 is a standard issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). It provides a set of codes for the names of sovereign states, dependent territories, and certain special areas of geographical interest, as well as for their primary administrative subdivisions such as provinces or states. The standard's official designation is Codes for the representation of names of countries and their subdivisions.

During the 1975 OPEC hostage crisis, Carlos the Jackal organized air transport for his team and 42 of the original 63 hostages, routing through Algiers and Tripoli with the plan to fly to Baghdad to kill Saudi oil minister Ahmed Zaki Yamani and Iranian minister Jamshid Amouzegar. In Algiers, all 30 non-Arab hostages were released, with Amouzegar among those not freed; additional captives were released at another stop in Tripoli before the party returned to Algiers. With ten hostages still in captivity, Carlos conducted a phone call with Algerian President Houari Boumédiène, who warned that the deaths of the oil ministers would provoke an attack on the aircraft. Boumédiène offered Carlos asylum and possibly financial compensation for failing to complete the mission. Carlos expressed regret at not being able to murder Yamani and Amouzegar, and he and his collaborators left the plane. Two days after the incident began, all hostages and militants had departed from the situation.

OPEC presents itself as a stabilizing influence in oil markets rather than a coercive anti-competitive cartel. It was established as a counterweight to the historical Seven Sisters, a cartel of multinational oil companies, and it frames its role as maintaining orderly markets rather than constraining competition. Non-OPEC producers retain substantial market shares, preserving ongoing competitive pressure in the global oil market. In practice, a prisoner’s dilemma among members encourages underpricing and production beyond quotas, producing widespread noncompliance that weakens OPEC’s ability to influence prices. Some analysts, notably Jeff Colgan, question the cartel label, arguing that cheating is endemic; he contends that a true cartel should set stringent goals and meet them, whereas OPEC tends to adopt relatively easy targets and falls short of meeting even those.
Tele2 reportedly attempted to divest its German unit in 2007. The divestment was completed in 2020 through a management buyout, after which the resulting company trades as STROTH Telecom GmbH.

Tele2 participated in a multiband spectrum auction held by Agentschap Telecom in the Netherlands, which concluded on 14 December 2012. The company was awarded two blocks of 10 MHz in the 800 MHz band, augmenting its existing 2.6 GHz LTE license and enabling a nationwide, high-capacity, cost-efficient network. Tele2 paid €161 million for these licenses, a sum markedly lower than the amounts paid by rivals—KPN and Vodafone, around €1.3 billion, and T-Mobile about €900 million. The reduced price reflected the government’s reservation of spectrum for a new mobile entrant, creating a favorable acquisition environment. Tele2’s entry was expected to spur lower prices and heighten competition in the Dutch mobile market.

Ibrahim Traoré ordered in February 2024 the suspension of export licenses for small-scale private gold production, aiming to curb illicit trade, including smuggling abroad and evading taxes and regulations. The move seeks to reform the artisanal gold sector and to crack down on illicit activities, ensuring that exported gold is properly documented and contributes to government revenue. Authorities hope the measure will establish a more formal and accountable framework for exporting gold produced on a small scale.
According to Aanu Adeoye of the Financial Times, Ibrahim Traoré presents himself as modeling his leadership on Thomas Sankara, a prominent 20th-century Burkinabé revolutionary leader.

STW remained independently owned until 1978, when it affiliated with the Nine Network, granting access to the network’s programming. In 1984, the station was acquired by Alan Bond for just under AU$50 million, becoming part of Bond Media. Following Bond's subsequent acquisition of the Nine Network from Kerry Packer, STW became a network-owned and operated station.

In February 1964, Swan Television was awarded the licence to operate Perth's second commercial television station. The shareholder group included Ansett Transport Industries. At that time, Ansett Transport Industries was preparing to launch ATV-0, Melbourne's third commercial television station, scheduled for October 1964.

Windows Media Center (WMC) was not included with any edition of Windows 8; it existed solely as the Windows 8 Media Center Pack add-on. The add-on could be obtained for retail Windows 8 Pro installations and as part of the Windows 8 Pro Pack upgrade path through the "Add features to Windows 8" interface. The Windows 8 Pro Pack was priced at US$69.99. The Media Center Pack was offered free from October 26, 2012, to January 31, 2013, as a promotional measure to encourage upgrading to Windows 8. Following the promotional period, the Windows 8/8.1 Media Center Pack price was reduced to US$9.99. The Windows 8/8.1 Media Center Pack was discontinued on October 30, 2015.

Windows Media Center is a media management and playback platform that organizes and presents video and audio content from both the local computer and networked devices. In the music collection, albums can display cover art, which is downloaded automatically or added manually. Users can assemble playlists comprising individual tracks or whole albums. The playback interface offers standard controls such as pause and fast-forward and includes visualizations during music playback. Where hardware supports it, the software also provides analog FM radio reception via a TV tuner.

The SpaceX Dragon 1 spacecraft operated under NASA’s Commercial Resupply Services program, and its mission schedule was expanded in the mid-2010s. In March 2015, SpaceX was awarded three additional Phase 1 CRS missions—CRS-13, CRS-14, and CRS-15—to cover cargo needs anticipated for 2017. On February 24, 2016, SpaceNews reported five further Phase 1 missions were planned: CRS-16 and CRS-17 for fiscal year 2017, with CRS-18, CRS-19, and CRS-20 notionally planned for fiscal year 2018.

SpaceX began development of the Dragon spacecraft in late 2004 as part of its effort to establish private-sector access to space. The project was publicly announced in 2006, outlining plans to enter service by 2009. In the same year, SpaceX secured a contract with NASA to provide Dragon for commercial resupply missions to the International Space Station, marking an important early collaboration with the space agency.

ISO 14644 delineates the minimum requirements for the design, construction, installation, testing, and approval of separative devices. It addresses aspects in which separative devices differ from cleanrooms as described in Parts 4 and 5 of the standard, ensuring appropriate assessment and validation of these systems. The scope encompasses a range of configurations from open to closed systems, with criteria established to evaluate their performance and suitability for their intended use.

ISO 14644 was published as an International Standard in 2004. The standard was submitted to the American National Standards process, and it was subsequently adopted in the United States as ANSI/IEST/ISO 14644-5:2004.

Mortars are a branch of artillery notable for their relatively simple construction and operation compared with other field weapons. The modern mortar originated during World War I, when several patterns were developed, and in the postwar period the Stokes pattern became the standard design. The Stokes pattern is defined by a short, smooth-bore barrel, low muzzle velocity, and a lightweight baseplate that sits on the ground, with elevation typically greater than 45 degrees. Ammunition is designed for drop-fire: the projectile contains its own propellant charge and is dropped down the barrel from the muzzle to strike a fixed firing pin. Since then, a minority of mortars have been produced with rifled barrels and breech-loading capabilities.

Artillery comprises large-caliber weapons designed for long-range indirect fire. In the twentieth century, the development of target acquisition devices such as radar, together with techniques like sound ranging and flash spotting, arose mainly to enhance artillery capability. These tools are typically employed by one or more artillery arms. The widespread adoption of indirect fire in the early twentieth century created a demand for specialist data for field artillery, including survey information and meteorological data, and in some armed forces the artillery branch itself is responsible for supplying this information. Across the Napoleonic Wars, World War I, and World War II, artillery accounted for the majority of combat fatalities. In 1944, Joseph Stalin described artillery as the central force of warfare.

Kseniya Alexandrova is a Russian beauty pageant contestant who represented Russia at Miss Universe 2017. She did not advance to the Top 16 semifinalists. The Miss Universe 2017 title was awarded to Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters of South Africa.

Kseniya Alexandrova represented Moscow in the Miss Russia 2017 pageant, where she finished as the first runner-up. By securing this placement, she succeeded Yuliana Korolkova, the outgoing Miss Russia 2016 who had also achieved a runner-up placement at Miss Universe Russia 2016.

In 686, Cædwalla, a sub-king of Wessex, established overlordship over Essex. Alongside Cædwalla, Sæbbi invaded Kent and expelled King Eadric, after which Sæbbi held lordship over West Kent. It is presumed that during this period Sæbbi founded the original abbey at Westminster.

Sæbbi, also known as Saint Sebbi or Sebba, was a 7th‑century ruler of Essex who was born sometime before 626 and died in 695. He was the son of Sexred and, from 664 to about 683, reigned jointly with his cousin Sighere. Following Sighere's death, Sæbbi ruled Essex as sole king until 694.

Formed by Emperor Napoleon III on 2 December 1852, the third cabinet succeeded the second cabinet of Louis Napoleon at the dawn of the Second French Empire. It remained in place thereafter, undergoing ministerial changes as required, until 17 July 1869, when it was superseded by the fourth cabinet of Napoleon III. In this arrangement, the ministers were accountable to Napoleon III, who acted as both head of state and head of government.

During May 2016, Jason Scheff took a temporary leave of absence to address family health concerns. On October 25, 2016, Scheff departed from Chicago after a 31-year tenure with the group. In the wake of his departure, Jeff Coffey, who had served as Scheff's interim replacement, was elevated to a full-time member. Additionally, Ray Herrmann, who had been filling in for Walter Parazaider on tours since 2005, was made an official member after Parazaider retired from the road; Parazaider himself stepped back from regular touring duties but remained with the band.

Chicago, an American rock band, issued its debut studio album Chicago Transit Authority in 1969 under the group's original name. In 2014, the album was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame. The band subsequently performed two concerts with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra on January 25 and January 28, 2014. In February 2015, Chicago released a two-disc live album, Chicago at Symphony Hall, featuring performances with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra.

On 11 January 1947, a Douglas Dakota III, registered G-AGJX, operated by the British Overseas Airways Corporation, was on a scheduled service from London Heathrow to West Africa with a via Bordeaux. Due to poor weather, the flight made several diversion attempts before crashing during an approach to land at Lympne airfield near Stowting in Kent. Of the 16 people aboard—five crew members and eleven passengers—eight were killed and eight were injured.

On 30 January 1942, a Short Empire flying boat, registered G-AEUH and named Corio, owned by British Overseas Airways Corporation and operated by Qantas, was shot down and crashed off West Timor after being attacked by seven Japanese fighter aircraft; of the 18 people on board, 13 were killed.

Edward G. Jefferson (July 15, 1921 – February 9, 2006) was a British-born American chemical engineer, chemist, and businessman who served as the chief executive officer and chairman of the DuPont Company. Born in London, England, he pursued a career in chemical engineering and chemistry before rising to top leadership at DuPont. His tenure as CEO and chair coincided with a period of controversy for the company, including environmental concerns related to the pollution of public waterways.

Edward G. Jefferson served in the Royal Artillery during World War II and participated in the Normandy invasion in 1944. He then pursued higher education at King's College, University of London, graduating with honors in chemistry and later earning a doctorate from the same institution.

On 24 August 1960, a Lockheed L-1049 Super Constellation, registered VH-EAC, operated by Qantas, crashed during takeoff at Mauritius while on a flight en route to the Cocos Islands, Australia. The takeoff was aborted after an engine failure, causing the aircraft to run off the runway and be destroyed by fire; there were no fatalities among the passengers and crew.

Qantas’s in-flight entertainment offering centers on the iQ system, developed by Panasonic Avionics Corporation, and is installed on a select portion of its fleet, including certain Airbus A380s and Boeing 737-800 aircraft. An AVOD (advertising-supported video on demand) experience was introduced in 2008, marking a shift toward enhanced passenger content. Based on Panasonic’s platform, the iQ system provides expanded entertainment options with touchscreen interfaces and also incorporates communications features such as Wi‑Fi and mobile phone functionality. In addition, it has increased support for personal electronics, including USB and iPod connectivity, reflecting broader compatibility with passenger devices.

Jeniferever released a four-track EP, Iris, through the independent label Big Scary Monsters Recording Company. The group issued its debut full-length album, Choose a Bright Morning, on Drowned in Sound Recordings and it was later reissued by Monotreme Records. Their sophomore effort, Spring Tides, appeared in 2009 on Monotreme Records. The band's third studio album, Silesia, was released on 11 April 2011. A track from the album, "Waifs & Strays," was made available as a free download in January 2011. Although no formal announcement of a breakup has been made, Jeniferever has been on a prolonged hiatus since 2012. During this interval, members formed another band, Ştiu Nu Ştiu.

Jeniferever is a Swedish band from Uppsala, formed in 1996. Their music blends ambient textures with indie rock and post-rock elements, characterized by slow tempos, melodic guitar work, and passages that often swell into an orchestral-like finale. The group's sound has been compared to the work of The Appleseed Cast and Sigur Rós. The name is taken from a Smashing Pumpkins song released in 1989.

According to David Rooney of Variety, Startup.com is described as timely and topical, extending beyond a purely factual account to foreground a vivid human drama. The review underscores themes of Machiavellian manipulation, ambition, torn loyalties, and crushing betrayal, presenting the work as a narrative that integrates personal and professional tensions.

Startup.com chronicles the rise and fall of govWorks, a startup that ultimately did not survive. The venture has since been cited as a reference for entrepreneurial lessons learned from the dot-com era. In 2001, a documentary centered on the company was released, following founders Kaleil Isaza Tuzman and Tom Herman through the 1999–2000 period, as the Internet bubble was bursting.

Telemundo's competitive standing against Univision saw a notable milestone in July 2015 when it achieved its first single-night demographic win over its rival on July 21, 2015, drawing 969,000 viewers and a 0.76 rating versus Univision's 943,000 viewers and 0.74. The 10 p.m. hour was led by El Señor de los Cielos 3, which posted a 1.4 rating to Univision's 0.7 and was the hour’s most-watched program among Adults 18–49. In the week of July 20–24, 2015, Telemundo came within about 40,000 viewers of surpassing Univision in prime-time total viewership. During the 2014–15 season, Telemundo recorded its highest average total prime-time viewership against Univision, averaging 1.46 million viewers (up 23% year-over-year) compared with Univision's 2.29 million (down 21% year-over-year).

As of June 2018, Telemundo operated 28 owned-and-operated stations and maintained current or pending affiliation agreements with 66 additional stations, extending across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. This expansive network makes Telemundo the largest American Spanish-language broadcast network by total affiliates. The network’s estimated national reach covers about 57.23% of U.S. households, equating to roughly 178,837,113 Americans living in households with at least one television.

Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) are distinguished by their comparatively long range and high speed relative to other ballistic missiles. In the broader family of ballistic missiles, there are additional types, including intermediate-range ballistic missiles (IRBMs), medium-range ballistic missiles (MRBMs), short-range ballistic missiles (SRBMs), and tactical ballistic missiles.

Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) emerged within a Cold War strategic framework dominated by the doctrine of mutual assured destruction (MAD). During the 1950s and 1960s, the United States and the Soviet Union pursued anti-ballistic missile (ABM) systems designed to counter ICBMs and thereby alter the balance of nuclear deterrence. The deployment of ABMs was subsequently restricted by the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty, which limited the scale and scope of defenses. The Soviet Union achieved the first successful ABM test in 1961, signaling the viability of interception as a means of defense against long-range missiles. In the 1970s, Moscow deployed a fully operational ABM system intended to defend the capital city, marking a notable milestone in strategic defense capabilities.

Myles Kennedy is best known for fronting The Mayfield Four, whose second and final studio album, Second Skin, was released in June 2001. Kennedy has described the record as one of the most personal projects he has ever made. The album received critical acclaim upon its release, and he has since noted that Second Skin, along with the band's earlier Fallout, has grown in popularity since its initial reception.

Myles Kennedy developed tinnitus after listening to loud recordings following the breakup of The Mayfield Four, a condition that coincided with a period of depression in 2002 in which he felt unable to continue with music, insisting that his ears would not permit it. He became disillusioned with the music industry, took a hiatus, and returned to teaching guitar. In 2002, Slash reached out to form a band in need of a vocalist, but Kennedy declined; some sources contend that he had sent a demo tape yet still refused an audition after Matt Sorum approached. Kennedy himself has recalled being contacted in 2002, that a demo had been sent, and that he left it unattended for about a month before following up.

The Fiat CR.32 was an Italian biplane fighter aircraft designed by aeronautical engineer Celestino Rosatelli. It served in both the Spanish Civil War and World War II, demonstrating its use across multiple conflicts. The aircraft was noted for its compact airframe, sturdy construction, and high maneuverability relative to its era, contributing to its popularity among fighters during the 1930s.

Between 1935 and 1936, the Royal Hungarian Air Force (MKHL) acquired 76 Fiat CR.32 fighters. The aircraft made its combat debut in 1939 during the conflict with Slovakia, and it bore insignia consisting of red, white, and green chevrons. In combat, the CR.32s quickly established air superiority over the Slovak Air Force, with Slovak losses including several Avia B.534s and Letov S-328s.

Respirators require a seal check each time a wearer dons the device to verify an airtight seal and prevent air leakage around the edges. Powered air-purifying respirators (PAPRs) may not require such a check because they do not necessarily seal to the face. The seal check is distinct from a periodic fit test conducted with testing equipment. For filtering facepiece respirators, a positive pressure check can be performed by exhaling with the hands cupped over the facepiece, or a negative pressure check by inhaling, with observation for any leakage. For elastomeric respirators, a similar assessment is carried out by blocking airways through the inlet valves to create negative pressure or through the exhalation valves to create positive pressure, and observing for leakage or flexing. Seal-check methods vary by model, so the manufacturer’s instructions should be consulted for the specific respirator. Some models or filter cartridges include built-in buttons or mechanisms to facilitate seal checks.

Respirators are protective devices worn to limit inhalation of airborne hazards when the source cannot be eliminated or adequately controlled by other means. While they provide a degree of protection, it is widely regarded that relying on respirators to compensate for hazardous or unsafe workplace conditions is ineffective and insufficient as a stand-alone solution; they are best viewed as a last line of defense within the broader hierarchy of controls. The effectiveness of respirators depends on proper selection, correct fit, user training, consistent use, and regular maintenance, and without these factors they may fail to protect workers. Consequently, respirators should augment, rather than substitute for, efforts to remove or minimize hazards through engineering and administrative measures.

The Association of Hungarian Record Companies (MAHASZ) functions as the national body responsible for certifying music sales in Hungary. Its highest certifications for domestic albums were awarded in 2014 to two records: Micsoda buli! by Hungária and Legendás dalok 1. by Locomotiv GT, each achieving ten-times Platinum status. In the international repertoire category, the top-certified release is Mamma Mia! The Movie Soundtrack, performed by the Mamma Mia! film cast, which attained six-times Platinum in 2018. MAHASZ maintains a comprehensive list of all multi-platinum albums certified by the organization, with updates through January 2025.

Established in Hungary in the mid-1970s, the Association of Hungarian Record Companies introduced a formal certification program to recognize commercial success of music releases. The program defined Gold albums as requiring 50,000 units sold, while singles required 100,000 units sold to qualify for certification.

Hanxi Changlong station, located in Guangzhou, underwent a series of proposed names prior to its opening; it was initially designated Hanxi Station (汉溪站) and was subsequently renamed Changlong Station (长隆站). Local residents opposed the Changlong name, perceiving it as favorable to the Chimelong Group, the owner and operator of Chimelong Paradise. In response, the Guangzhou Municipal Government approved a compromise to adopt the name Hanxi Changlong Station, a designation that ultimately satisfied both residents and the Chimelong Group.

Hanxi Changlong Station functions as an interchange between Guangzhou Metro Lines 3 and 7. Line 3 commenced service on 28 December 2006, and Line 7 followed on 28 December 2016. The station is located beneath the eastern side of Hanxi Avenue and the Xinguang Expressway, south of Chimelong Paradise Amusement Park in Dashi Subdistrict of Panyu District, Guangzhou. A free shuttle bus operates to connect the station with Chimelong Paradise Amusement Park.
In September 2018, PayPal banned radio host Alex Jones and his website InfoWars, citing content on the site that was described as hateful and discriminatory against certain religious groups.

By 2010, PayPal had more than 100 million active user accounts in 190 markets and supported 25 currencies. In December 2010, the service experienced distributed denial-of-service attacks after it ceased processing donations to WikiLeaks. The following year, in July 2011, fourteen individuals alleged to be members of the Anonymous collective were charged with attempting to disrupt PayPal's operations. On December 5, 2013, thirteen of the PayPal 14 pleaded guilty to misdemeanor and felony charges related to the attacks.

Theodore Edward Cantor, known in Danish as Theodor Edvard, was a Danish physician, zoologist and botanist who lived from 1809 to 1860. He described several new species of reptiles and amphibians, and six species have been named in his honor.

Theodore Cantor was a notable naturalist whose legacy is reflected in the scientific names of several reptiles. The genus Cantoria honors him, with Cantoria violacea designated as the type species and commonly known as Cantor's water snake. In addition, a number of other species have been named after Cantor, including Acanthodactylus cantoris (Indian fringe-fingered lizard), Elaphe cantoris (eastern trinket snake), Hydrophis cantoris (Cantor's small-headed sea snake), Pelochelys cantorii (Cantor's giant softshell turtle), and Trimeresurus cantori (Cantor's pit viper).

The Neo-Renaissance in Austria emerged as an architectural movement largely through the efforts of Rudolf Eitelberger, who is regarded as its pioneer. He established the Viennese College of Arts and Crafts, which today functions as the University of Applied Arts Vienna. The style achieved particular prominence in Vienna, where a number of streets and entire blocks were constructed in Neo-Renaissance form. Characteristically, the Neo-Renaissance presents a classicalized amalgam drawn from elements of diverse historical periods.

Neo-Renaissance architecture in France drew on earlier French Renaissance forms, including widely copied features such as the monumental staircases at the Loire Valley châteaux of Blois and Chambord. Blois was a favored royal residence during the Renaissance, and the Francis I Wing there, completed in 1524, includes an integral staircase and stands as an early example of the French Renaissance style. French Renaissance architecture fused Gothic tradition with Italian influence, producing arches, arcades, balustrades, and a flowing overall design. The triumphal staircase at Blois was rapidly imitated in subsequent buildings, and this trend of imposing staircases preceded the later double staircase at Chambord, built a few years afterward. The Chambord double staircase is sometimes attributed to Leonardo da Vinci.

Ni-Vanuatu, occasionally written as ni-Van, is a term typically applied to the native peoples of Vanuatu. By contrast, the demonym Vanuatuan is intended to denote any citizen of the country, regardless of ethnicity or origin. The form Vanuatuan, however, is rarely used in English and is considered incorrect by some authors and style guides.

Ni-Vanuatu are the inhabitants of Vanuatu. Bislama serves as the country’s lingua franca, bridging citizens educated under French-language schooling with those educated under English-language schooling. By providing a shared medium, it enables communication among speakers of the archipelago’s many indigenous languages.

The Great Neck School District operates three high schools: North High School, South High School, and The Village School. North High School includes an alternative program known as the Community School. The Village School functions as a small alternative high school. Beyond the high schools, the district comprises two middle schools, four elementary schools, and a nursery school.

Based on the 2020 Niche rankings, the Great Neck Union Free School District is identified as the top public school district in New York and places third nationally among public school districts. The district outperforms neighboring Jericho and Manhasset Union Free School Districts in these assessments. Data from 2017 show that 75 percent of students were proficient in English Language Arts and 78 percent were proficient in Mathematics.

On May 12, 1970, a violent F5 tornado struck downtown Lubbock, damaging the Avalanche-Journal building at 8th Street and Avenue J. With the office incapacitated, the paper produced an eight-page edition by routing reports to its sister publication, the Globe-News, in Amarillo, Texas. The edition, printed in Amarillo roughly 100 miles north of Lubbock, had a print run of about 60,000 copies and featured a front-page headline describing the disaster and its casualties, representing the first published news of the storm. A May 13 edition was issued in the same manner, listing the known dead. By May 14, local printing had resumed, returning the Avalanche-Journal to its own presses.

The Lubbock Avalanche-Journal originated in 1926 when Charles A. Guy and Dorrance Roderick, editors of the rival Lubbock Daily Journal, purchased The Avalanche and merged the two into a single publication. They allied with Houston Harte and Bernard Hanks (who would later become associated with Harte Hanks) and J. Lindsay Nunn of The Amarillo Daily News and Post to establish the new newspaper. In 1928, Guy, Roderick, and Nunn acquired control of the Avalanche-Journal from Harte and Hanks, consolidating ownership. Charles A. Guy became editor and publisher in 1931, a role he held until 1972. Over the ensuing years, the paper was led by a succession of editors, including Jay Harris, Burle Pettit, Randy Sanders, Terry Greenberg, James Bennett, Jill Nevels-Haun, and Adam Young.

Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is used as a coating in some bullets, commonly referred to as Teflon-coated ammunition. The PTFE layer is intended to reduce wear on rifling compared with uncoated projectiles, owing to its low-friction properties. PTFE does not impart armor-piercing properties to a projectile.

Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) has historically been produced with the processing aid perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a chemical that has been described as potentially carcinogenic for those exposed. Elevated PFOA levels have been detected in the blood of individuals working near manufacturing facilities, residents living in proximity to such sites, and people with regular exposure to PFOA-containing products, including ski waxes and stain-resistant coatings. With regard to consumer exposure, non-stick cookware does not constitute a major source of PFOA because the chemical is typically volatilized and removed during production and is not present in the finished PTFE items. Since 2013, non-stick coated cookware has not been manufactured using PFOA. PFOA production has ceased in the United States.

In France, regional councils are elected through a two-round system that combines proportional representation with a majority bonus to determine the council’s composition. Under this framework, it is possible for a list that records fewer votes in the first round to become the overall winner after the second round and the final seat allocation. Although such a list may receive fewer proportional seats based on its initial first-round tally, the post-round coalitions and the majority premium can produce a decisive advantage in the total seat count. This dynamic can lead to a mismatch between the first-round results and the final regional council composition, illustrating that early voting outcomes do not always predict the ultimate winner in the regional council system.

As part of France's decentralisation programme of 1982–1983, implemented during the presidency of François Mitterrand, the regional governance framework was revised to introduce direct elections for regional councils. The direct elections began in 1986, marking a shift away from appointed or indirect selection, and the reforms increased the powers of the regional councils, strengthening their role in regional administration and policy-making.

The iPhone SE (2nd generation) has been interpreted by technology journalists as indicative of a broader move away from compact iPhones. Dan Seifert of The Verge described the model as a decisive blow to the viability of small-screen phones, while CNET observed that Apple’s decision not to introduce a new 4-inch iPhone signals that the tiny form factor is unlikely to return, even in the face of demand. Collectively, these assessments suggest that Apple is prioritizing larger devices and reducing emphasis on the small iPhone segment.

The iPhone SE (second generation) uses the Apple A13 Bionic system-on-a-chip, produced on a 7‑nm process, and includes an integrated M13 motion coprocessor along with the third‑generation Neural Engine. It offers storage options of 64 GB, 128 GB, and 256 GB. The phone features IP67 dust and water resistance, matching the rating of the iPhone 8. It does not include ultra-wideband capabilities, as it lacks a U1 chip present in the iPhone 11 and 11 Pro. The compact form factor may contribute to greater thermal throttling, though its peak CPU frequencies are the same as those of the iPhone 11. Its design is reminiscent of the iPhone 7 and 8, and it omits the 3.5 mm headphone jack, unlike the iPhone 6/6S and the first-generation SE.

Beginning in mid-June 2020, The Oregonian began publishing stories labeled Exclusive to announce an impending paywall. The Exclusive items were typically front-page features. By mid-July 2020, these exclusive articles were moved behind a subscriber-only barrier. On July 27, 2020, the publication implemented a full paywall, restricting access to paid subscribers.

After assuming leadership at The Oregonian, Editor Rowe implemented a major reorganization of the newsroom, replacing many general assignment reporters with subject-area teams. These teams developed deep subject-matter expertise aligned with readers' interests rather than adhering to traditional newsroom boundaries. Examples of such teams included Northwest Issues and Environment; Living In the ’90s/How We Live; Politics and Accountability; Health, Science, and Medicine; Sustainability and Growth; and Higher Education. The changes introduced a bottom-up approach to storytelling, with beat reporters presenting stories to editors rather than editors assigning topics, and team editors determining which stories their teams would cover.

Huahine's name is traditionally interpreted as a reference to the female sex, and is sometimes translated as "pregnant woman." This reading is linked to the profile of Mount Tavaiura, which is said to resemble a pregnant woman lying down.

Huahine is an island noted for its lush vegetation, including a substantial presence of coconut palms. The island is home to two prominent botanical gardens, Ariiura Garden Paradise and l'Eden Parc. Ariiura Garden Paradise preserves traditional Polynesian medicinal flora, reflecting indigenous knowledge of herbal remedies, while l'Eden Parc concentrates on cultivating fruit trees from diverse regions around the world.

OpenNebula 4.6 introduces federation across geographically distributed OpenNebula deployments, enabling a single federated cloud infrastructure that spans multiple data centers. The release also includes a new cloud portal designed for cloud consumers, providing user-facing access to resources and services. Additionally, the App Market is updated to support importing OVAs, enhancing interoperability with existing virtual appliances.

OpenNebula is an open-source cloud-management platform that coordinates storage, networking, virtualization, monitoring, and security technologies in order to deploy multi-tier services as virtual machines across distributed infrastructures. It integrates data center resources with remote cloud resources under defined allocation policies, enabling the deployment of compute clusters as virtual machines on heterogeneous infrastructures. In addition, the platform supports creating and managing compute clusters as virtual machines across mixed environments. A 2010 European Commission report noted that only a small number of cloud-focused research initiatives had begun, with OpenNebula identified as one of the more prominent examples.

Ave Maria, WAB 5 is a 52-bar motet in F major composed by Anton Bruckner for SATB choir with soprano and alto soloists, accompanied by organ and cello continuo. The work proceeds at Andante and features a fugato texture, culminating the opening eight bars with a Marien-Kadenz cadence on the word Maria. This cadence is later recalled by Bruckner in the first movement of his Study Symphony in F minor and in the Adagio of his Symphony No. 3. Bar 9 introduces the alto solo with the text gratia plena, and bar 13 presents the soprano solo with benedicta tu. Between bars 18 and 22 the pace slows to Adagio, during which the choir voices the word Jesus three times; this threefold invocation of Jesus is a motif Bruckner repeats in his two subsequent Ave Maria settings. The second section, bars 23 through 52, is sung by the choir; the texture returns to Andante, opening this part with Sancta Maria sung in canon, and the piece ends by returning to the initial motif.

Ave Maria, WAB 5 is a sacred motet by Anton Bruckner. The original manuscript has been lost, but the work survives through copies housed in several repositories. The score dedicated to Traumihler is preserved in the St. Florian Abbey archive, with further copies stored at Kremsmünster Abbey and in the Austrian National Library (Österreichische Nationalbibliothek). The motet was first edited by Johann Groß in Innsbruck in 1893. It is currently included in volume XXI/19 of the Bruckner Gesamtausgabe.
In 1985, Streets completed its sophomore studio album, Crimes in Mind. The group dissolved shortly thereafter, and approximately a year later Walsh rejoined Kansas.

Streets was an American hard rock band formed in 1982 in Atlanta, Georgia. The group's lineup featured Steve Walsh as singer and keyboardist, Mike Slamer on guitar, Billy Greer on bass, and Tim Gehrt on drums.

Following the decline of the Italian Socialist Party in the 1990s, a notable portion of its former members aligned with other political forces, including a number who joined Forza Italia between 1994 and 1996, such as Giulio Tremonti, Franco Frattini, Massimo Baldini, and Luigi Cesaro. In parallel, Gianni De Michelis, Ugo Intini, and other Craxi loyalists formed a new Socialist Party, while Fabrizio Cicchitto and Enrico Manca established the Reformist Socialist Party. In the 2000s, two groups claimed to be the party’s successor: the Italian Democratic Socialists (SDI), descended from the Italian Socialists, and the New Italian Socialist Party (NPSI), founded in 2001 by De Michelis, Claudio Martelli and Bobo Craxi.

The Italian Socialist Party (PSI) secured 14.3 percent of the vote in the 1987 general election, while the Christian Democrats continued to form the government. From 1987 to 1992, the party took part in four administrations, a participation that enabled Giulio Andreotti to become prime minister in 1989 and to govern until 1992. The PSI held a decisive balance of power, exercising more influence than the Christian Democrats, who depended on PSI support to assemble a parliamentary majority; nonetheless, the party tightly managed this leverage. In 1989, party leader Bettino Craxi put forward the idea of Socialist Unity with other left-wing forces, including the PCI, contending that the decline of communism would undermine the PCI and make Socialist Unity inevitable. Although the PSI was positioned to become Italy’s second-largest party and to lead a new left-wing coalition opposing a Christian Democrat-led government, this prospect did not materialize, due in part to the rise of Lega Nord and the Tangentopoli scandals.

During the 1850 United States Census, the enumeration system was revised to record free persons individually rather than by head of household, and two separate schedules were used—one for free inhabitants and a second for enslaved people. On the free inhabitants form, the color designation was omitted for whites, while non-white individuals were marked with "B" for black or "M" for mulatto. Enslaved people were listed under the ownership of a master rather than as separate individuals, and their entries were categorized by sex and age. In this slave schedule, the color field similarly used "B" for black and "M" for mulatto.

In the 1940 United States Census, data collection was conducted using separate population and housing questionnaires for the first time, marking a methodological shift in census practice. That year also saw the elimination of the race category "Mexican," with individuals of Mexican descent being counted within the white population, a change that altered racial classification in census records.

SAS Shoemakers, officially known as SAS Shoe Factory and General Store, is a footwear production facility and retail establishment located on the South Side of San Antonio, Texas. It lies near the intersection of SW Military Drive and S. Zarzamora Street, placing it within that neighborhood. The facility provides tours of its factory, allowing visitors to observe aspects of its production processes.

SAS Shoemakers participates in community relief during emergencies, supported by organized volunteer efforts aimed at helping those affected by disasters. A dedicated volunteer unit within the organization, known as the Comfort and Support Team, conducts visits to disaster areas. The team provides complimentary footwear to victims and other individuals experiencing hardship, with the service targeted toward people in need.

Priest of Love is a 1981 biographical film about D. H. Lawrence, adapted from a non-fiction biography of the same title. Ian McKellen portrays Lawrence, and the film's narrative centers on his periods in Taos, New Mexico, and in Italy. The source biography on which the film is based covers most of Lawrence's life.

Since 2008, Eastwood has hosted an annual D. H. Lawrence Festival organized to celebrate the author's life and works. In September 2016, Cornwall hosted events commemorating the centenary of Lawrence's connection with Zennor.

Red Bull Editions, introduced in 2013 to expand the brand’s flavor portfolio, began with cranberry, blueberry, and lime variants. The Editions lineup has subsequently broadened to encompass a wide range of flavors, with some releases being seasonal or regional in nature. As of the present, the flavor lineup includes Blue (blueberry), Peach (peach‑nectarine), Winter (iced vanilla berry), Sea Blue (juneberry), and Red (watermelon).

Red Bull is an energy drink that originated in Austria, where it was first introduced at ski resorts, and it later underwent a repositioning to emphasize a trendy, upscale image. This branding differentiates Red Bull from its lower-cost counterpart Krating Daeng in many markets. In Thailand, energy drinks are most popular with blue-collar workers, illustrating distinct regional consumption patterns within the broader category. In many countries, both beverages are available, spanning a wide spectrum of price points from premium to more affordable. The flavouring for Red Bull is produced in Bangkok and exported worldwide.

The Puget Sound region has been linked to a descriptor used by poet Robert Sund that ties the area to a family of river names ending in -ish. This pattern appears in several local rivers, including the Duwamish, Samish, Sammamish, Skokomish, Skykomish, Snohomish, and Stillaguamish, illustrating the recurring -ish ending. The suffix itself derives from Salishan languages, where -ish means “people of.”

Washington State Ferries is a state-operated ferry system serving the Puget Sound region. It links the larger islands to the Washington mainland and provides crossings across Puget Sound on routes that connect communities on its eastern and western shores, thereby enabling the movement of cars and passengers throughout the greater Puget Sound area.

NetBank was an American direct bank that delivered its services primarily over the Internet, operating without traditional branch networks. It functioned from 1996 to 2007. The institution originated as Atlanta Internet Bank in 1996 and was renamed Net.B@nk in 1998 before adopting the NetBank designation. In 2007, the bank experienced a failure and was closed by regulators on September 28, 2007.

NetBank, a Georgia-based online bank, failed on September 28, 2007, in a process overseen by the Office of Thrift Supervision and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. The collapse was the largest failure of a savings and loan association since the 1980s S&L crisis and marked the biggest bank failure in the state of Georgia. Under FDIC management, all customers were transferred to a buyer, including about $1.4 billion in FDIC-insured deposits, along with some loan assets, and the bank was sold to ING Group for $14 million.

In debates about consumerism, critics who identify as anti-consumerist maintain that opposition is not to consumption per se but to growth in consumption that exceeds environmental sustainability. They argue that resource use should be kept within environmentally sustainable limits to avoid exceeding ecological capacity. Jonathan Porritt has argued that consumers are often unaware of the environmental costs associated with producing modern goods and services. The advertising industry is frequently cited as a potent force that reinforces the pattern of increasing consumption.

Consumerism in Britain emerged from a set of interlinked economic and social changes beginning in the 17th century, when agricultural innovations expanded the cultivable area and strengthened the productive base of the English economy. This growth coincided with a rising demand for luxury goods and intensified cultural exchange, prompting the aristocracy and affluent merchants to import items from Italy and the Low Countries. Government policies that promoted cultural borrowing and import substitution further facilitated these purchasing patterns. Among the luxury commodities that gained prominence were sugar, tobacco, tea, and coffee. As demand for these goods increased, production increasingly depended on large Caribbean plantations, historically operated with enslaved labor. By the 18th century, British sugar consumption had surged roughly twentyfold, underscoring the rapid expansion of consumer-oriented behavior during this period.

Origen of Alexandria (c. 185 – c. 253), also known as Origen Adamantius, was an early Christian scholar, ascetic, and theologian. Born in Alexandria, he spent the first half of his career there, establishing himself as a prolific writer who produced approximately two thousand treatises across several domains, including textual criticism, biblical exegesis and hermeneutics, homiletics, and spirituality. His work made him a highly influential yet controversial figure in the development of early Christian theology, apologetics, and ascetic practice. John Anthony McGuckin described him as one of the most remarkable minds produced by the early church.

The establishment of the Caesarean school marked the apex of Origen’s reputation as a scholar and theologian, with him widely regarded as a brilliant intellectual across the Mediterranean. Hierarchs from Palestinian and Arabian church synods considered him the foremost authority on theology. While teaching at Caesarea, Origen resumed his Commentary on John, completing at least the sixth through the tenth books; in the opening of these volumes he compared himself to an Israelite who had escaped the Egyptians’ harsh oppression. At the request of his friend Ambrose and Ambrose’s sister Tatiana, he authored the treatise On Prayer, in which he analyzes different kinds of prayer and offers a detailed exegesis of the Lord’s Prayer.

From 1914 to 1956, riders from Switzerland dominated the event, collecting 34 of the first 41 editions. Among foreign winners, Gino Bartali stood out as the most notable in this period. In the 1946 edition, Bartali beat his arch rival Fausto Coppi in a contentious race, with the two maintaining a blistering pace and pulling away from rivals as Bartali sprinted clear while Coppi was tightening his toe straps. This episode is regarded as the opening chapter of the Bartali–Coppi rivalry. The 1946 race was won at an average speed of 42.228 km/h (26.239 mph), a record speed that endured for more than five decades. In 2004, the Spaniard Juan Antonio Flecha won the edition with an average speed of 42.707 km/h (26.537 mph), setting a new record.

Zürich-Metzgete, a prominent Swiss one-day road race, was included in every edition of the UCI Road World Cup from 1989 through 2004. With the introduction of the UCI ProTour in 2005, the event joined the new series, marking its entry into the professional calendar under the ProTour. That same year it was moved to the end of the season for the first time. The 2007 edition was cancelled due to insufficient sponsorship amid doping-related scandals affecting the sport. In 2008 the race was held on September 7 with a revised format emphasizing amateur competition.

Hypo Alpe-Adria-Bank International's headquarters were designed by the American architect Thom Mayne. The building is situated at Alpen-Adria-Platz in Klagenfurt am Wörthersee, the capital of the Austrian state of Carinthia. In late November 2018, the structure was sold to a Swiss real estate company, with the purchase price not disclosed.

Hypo Alpe-Adria-Bank International A.G., which was owned by the Government of Austria, was dismantled in 2014 as part of a formal restructuring. In the aftermath, Heta Asset Resolution A.G. was established to act as the resolution vehicle for the original bank, functioning as its residual asset entity tasked with managing and disposing of the remaining assets and liabilities.

Following the Nazi seizure of power in 1933, Osram's co-founder William Meinhardt and other Jewish members of the company's managing board were compelled to resign. Under successor Hermann Schlüpmann, Nazi-aligned organizations such as the DAF gained influence among Osram's workforce. In March 1933, Osram allocated 40,000 Reichsmarks to a secret campaign fund of German industrialists intended to bolster support for the Nazi Party.

During World War II, Osram utilized forced labour at its Berlin facilities. As bombing intensified, production was partially relocated from 1942 to eastern German cities. The company outsourced the manufacture of molybdenum and tungsten products to Plauen. Arrangements between Osram officials and the SS led to the establishment of two Flossenbürg concentration camp subcamps adjacent to the factory to secure slave labour. In the Leitzmeritz subcamp, prisoners constructed underground facilities as part of the secret project Richard II designed to protect production during air raids. At least 4,500 prisoners died in the Leitzmeritz subcamp. The firm never moved into the underground space due to the course of the war.

In the context of a federation of digital libraries, search functionality must span multiple repositories to locate materials across diverse collections. One common strategy is distributed searching, wherein a query is sent to several member libraries and the resulting records are collected and merged to present a unified result set, often with deduplication and ranking. A second approach involves searching metadata that has been harvested from the participating libraries and indexed locally, enabling rapid, centralized access to descriptions and links to the original sources. Each method carries trade-offs: distributed searching can offer up-to-date results but may incur higher latency and coordination complexity, while harvested metadata allows faster searches at the expense of potentially stale records if harvesting intervals are infrequent. Hybrid configurations may combine both techniques to improve breadth, currency, and performance.

Enacted in 1998, the Digital Millennium Copyright Act is a United States law addressing digital works and copyright enforcement. It incorporates two treaties adopted in 1996. The statute makes it a criminal offense to circumvent technological measures that control access to copyrighted materials, and it also criminalizes the act of attempting to bypass access controls themselves. The act provides an exemption for nonprofit libraries and archives permitting the creation of up to three copies, with one of these copies allowed in digital form; however, these copies may not be made publicly available or distributed over the web. In addition, it permits libraries and archives to copy a work when its format becomes obsolete, in order to preserve access.

Jushu Station (Chinese: 菊树站) is a metro station on the Guangfo Line of the Guangzhou Metro. During planning, it was referred to as Fangcun Sports Center Station (芳村体育馆站) and Jucun Station (菊村站). The station lies beneath the southwestern area of the Fangcun Sports Center in Fangcun, Liwan District, Guangzhou. It began service on 3 November 2010.

The World Wide Web has become a platform for criminal activity, enabling the spread of malware and a range of cybercrimes such as identity theft, fraud, espionage, and intelligence gathering. Security analyses indicate that web-based vulnerabilities now outnumber traditional computer security concerns, with Google estimating that roughly one-tenth of web pages may contain malicious code. Attacks that target legitimate websites are common, and Sophos notes that these compromises are hosted primarily in the United States, China, and Russia. SQL injection is frequently cited as the most prevalent threat facing websites. Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks exploit HTML, URIs, and JavaScript, and the rise of Web 2.0 and Ajax has amplified scripting usage; by 2007, about 70% of sites were considered open to XSS attacks. Phishing remains another major Web threat, with RSA estimating global losses from phishing at approximately $1.5 billion in 2012. Two notable phishing techniques are Covert Redirect and Open Redirect.

The World Wide Web (WWW/W3/Web) is an information system that enables content sharing across the Internet. It is designed with user‑friendly features to appeal to non‑IT specialists and hobbyists. Through the Web, documents and other online resources can be accessed over the Internet, with access governed by the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP).

Heritage in Saudi Arabia reflects a diverse tapestry shaped by its geographic position at the crossroads of continents. The region is regarded as the cradle of numerous ancient kingdoms and civilizations, and it has long served as a hub of global commerce. Intercontinental trade routes historically traversed the Red Sea coast to the west and the Arabian Gulf coast to the east, enabling sustained exchange among distant societies. These routes encompassed travel along the Gulf shores, seasonal nomadic migrations across the peninsula, and the pilgrimage-driven movements associated with the Hajj, which together contributed to a dynamic and interconnected historical heritage.

Saudi Arabia aligns its heritage policies with international norms, most notably the 1972 UNESCO Convention concerning World Cultural and Natural Heritage.
