Under that framework, components of international cultural heritage are defined as monuments, groups of buildings, and sites that may be entirely manmade or a composite of natural and human elements. National governance further specifies distinctions between urban heritage and archaeological sites through the Law of Antiquities, Museums and Urban Heritage (Royal Decree No. M/3, 2014). The safeguarding of intangible cultural heritage is guided by UNESCO's 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage. The term itself was relatively uncommon in Saudi Arabia until 2008, when the nation ratified UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage List, after which usage broadened. Overall, cultural heritage in Saudi Arabia is organized into two main strands: Tangible Cultural Heritage, encompassing monuments, urban heritage, and archaeological sites, and Intangible Cultural Heritage, which includes oral traditions, literary expressions, performing arts, social practices, rituals and celebrations, traditional crafts and artisanship, and knowledge and practices related to nature and the universe.

The Communist International (Comintern) entered 1934 against a backdrop of a February 1934 joint socialist–communist action in France aimed at countering fascist threats, which stimulated a grass-roots surge toward unity. Within the organization there was growing acknowledgment that previous tactics had failed, a shift associated with Georgi Dimitrov, who became General Secretary in the spring following his Leipzig trial. By mid-May 1934, Dimitrov advocated a broader anti-fascist alliance, including social-democratic parties in a top-down united-front arrangement and other middle-class democratic forces. The year also featured intense Moscow debates between proponents of the new line—Dimitrov, Manuilsky, and Kuusinen—and hard-line opponents such as Knorin, Béla Kun, and Solomon Lozovsky. Stalin's role developed from initial indecision to cautious endorsement of the revised course. Nonetheless, the premature imposition of the new strategy led to purges of dissenters, including Heinz Neumann and Hermann Remmele in Germany and Karl Kilombo in Sweden.

The legacy of the Communist International is broadly interpreted as ambiguous, reflecting a complex and evolving influence across its history. In the 1920s the organization encouraged a variety of theoretical currents, with prominent figures such as Trotsky, Bukharin, and Gramsci offering divergent responses to socialist strategy. During the Popular Front period and World War II, communists presented themselves as anti-fascists and undertook international efforts to resist fascism, notably organizing the International Brigades to aid the Spanish Republic. At the same time, these activities were used to enforce Stalinist orthodoxy within communist movements and to suppress rival left-wing groups. The perceived threat of communism may have prompted capitalist governments to implement social reforms. After the war, communism expanded substantially, and by the end of 1945 organized communists outside the Soviet Union numbered about 14 million. This growth was partly attributable to the Soviet war effort and to the Comintern’s groundwork in consolidating disciplined, internationally connected communist parties.

George Atwood (circa October 1745 – 11 July 1807) was an English mathematician best known for designing the device that would become the Atwood machine, a classic apparatus used to demonstrate Newton’s laws of motion. In addition to his mathematical contributions, he was an accomplished chess player and kept detailed records of many games, including his own and those of other players such as François-André Danican Philidor, who was widely regarded as the leading master of the era. Atwood’s systematic documentation has left a valuable historical record for subsequent generations, contributing to both the study of chess and the understanding of contemporary play.

In 1784, George Atwood left Cambridge and was subsequently appointed patent searcher of the customs by William Pitt the Younger. The position required little attendance, a circumstance that allowed him to devote considerable time to the study of mathematics and physics.

Windows NT 3.51, a maintenance release in the Windows NT line, broadened both hardware compatibility and user interface features. It added PCMCIA support to accommodate portable computer configurations, and introduced NTFS file compression to reduce disk usage on NTFS volumes. The system also included a replaceable WinLogon component, known as GINA, enabling customization of the logon process. In the graphics domain, 3D support via OpenGL expanded the range of capable applications, while networking received persistence for IP routes when using TCP/IP, maintaining specific routes across sessions. On the usability front, a tooltip system automatically displays textual descriptions when the cursor hovers over toolbar buttons, and the platform gained compatibility with Windows 95 common controls to ease development and improve cross-version UI consistency.

Windows NT 3.51 received five service packs during its lifecycle, each providing a combination of bug fixes and new features. The fifth service pack specifically addressed issues related to the Year 2000 problem, mitigating Y2K-related concerns.

Disinvestment campaigns have targeted governments and regimes for political reasons, including Myanmar (Burma) through initiatives such as the Massachusetts Burma Law passed by the state of Massachusetts. Saudi Arabia has likewise been the focus of divestment activism over allegations of gender-based discrimination that have been described by some as gender apartheid. In the United States, campus groups have occasionally debated the issue, with the UC Riverside Hillel chapter reporting a Saudi divestment petition circulating in 2007.

Disinvestment was a campaign by state and local governments to withdraw investments from companies conducting business in Northern Ireland as part of the international response to the Troubles. The movement produced a counterpart to the Sullivan Principles in the form of the MacBride Principles, named after Seán MacBride, which urged nondiscrimination against Roman Catholics and promoted policies resembling affirmative action. Overall, the disinvestment effort achieved limited practical results. In 1998, the United States Congress passed legislation, subsequently signed by President Bill Clinton, requiring American companies with interests in Northern Ireland to adopt most of the MacBride Principles.

Higher education in Mozambique has historically served only a small portion of the population. By 1996, there were about 40 higher education students per 100,000 people, a level far below that of Zimbabwe (638) and the United States (5,339) per 100,000. The first institution dedicated to higher education was established in 1962 and was expanded into the University of Lourenço Marques in 1968. At independence in 1975, the institution was overwhelmingly white, with only 40 African students. The ensuing exodus of staff and students after independence led to a sharp decline in enrolment, with numbers dropping from 2,433 in 1975 to 750 in 1978 at the renamed Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM). At that time there were only ten Mozambican teachers, with vacancies filled by staff from the Communist bloc, and the university was described by observers as akin to a Tower of Babel. The share of foreign teachers declined from 33% in 1991 to 14% in 2001. In the 1980s, many Mozambican students pursued higher education abroad, notably in Eastern Europe and the Soviet Union.

According to the Human Rights Measurement Initiative, Mozambique fulfills 70.3 percent of the right to education relative to its income level. The assessment differentiates by educational level: primary education is shown to meet the full resource-adjusted potential at 100.0 percent, whereas secondary education reaches only 40.5 percent of what would be possible given the country’s resources.

Doesn't Play Well with Others is a project by Joey Cape that was accompanied by a paid subscription service promising a new track each month. The subscription package included a signed, limited-edition CD and a vinyl release containing all twelve tracks. It also featured a DVD produced by Cape, offering videos for each track, live-performance footage, an interview, and behind-the-scenes tour material. The related full-length album was released on June 1, 2011, in both CD and vinyl formats, following a brief delay.

Doesn't Play Well with Others is the second full-length solo album by Joey Cape, the frontman of Lagwagon and Bad Astronaut. It was released on June 1, 2011. In the run-up to the release, Cape employed a staggered pre-release approach in 2010, issuing one track each month on his official website beginning January 18, 2010, to gradually reveal material ahead of the album.

The iTunes Store, Apple's digital storefront for music and other media, underwent a shift away from Digital Rights Management (DRM) beginning in the late 2000s. In February 2007, Steve Jobs published an open letter criticizing DRM and signaling support for ending DRM on music. The following month, Apple struck a deal with EMI to offer iTunes Plus, a DRM-free option featuring higher-quality EMI tracks. By January 2009, Apple had secured licensing deals with all major labels and many independent labels to provide most iTunes music without DRM. On January 6, 2009, Apple announced that DRM had been removed from around 80 percent of its US music catalog. On April 7, 2009, iTunes Plus became fully DRM-free in the United States, supported by a three-tier pricing model. It should be noted that the DRM-free status applied to music purchases from the iTunes Store rather than songs obtained via Apple Music’s subscription service, while television episodes, many books, and films continued to be protected by FairPlay DRM.

In 2004, Which? magazine submitted a complaint to the European Commission asserting that iTunes Store pricing in the United Kingdom was higher than in the rest of the European Union, noting that UK tracks were priced at about £0.79 while elsewhere the price was typically €0.99. The commission opened an inquiry into the pricing disparity, and in 2008 it withdrew the investigation after Apple agreed to end the price disparity across the EU.

The Recording Industry Foundation in Taiwan (RIT) is an organization involved in Taiwan's recording industry. Since 2011, it has participated in and served as a co-organizer of the Hong Kong Asian-Pop Music Festival (HKAMF). The foundation also recommends the Taiwanese participant for the Asian Next Super Nova Competition.

The Recording Industry Foundation in Taiwan (RIT), also referred to as IFPI Taiwan, is a non-profit foundation that represents the interests of Taiwan’s recorded-music industry. Its official Chinese name is 財團法人台灣唱片出版事業基金會, and it was previously known as IFPI Members Foundation in Taiwan (財團法人國際唱片業交流基金會). As the national affiliate of the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry, it holds membership in IFPI.

Charles Dail, who had served in San Diego's government for twenty years, announced in 1963 that he would not seek a third term as mayor. He cited personal and business reasons for stepping down. His tenure encompassed time on the city council and as mayor, and at the time it represented the longest period of elected service in San Diego's history.

Charles Calhoun Dail (born January 11, 1909) was an American insurance professional who later pursued elective office. He was born in Kansas City, Kansas, the son of Charles Darwin Dail and Hester Dail (née Cooksey). On June 28, 1933, he married Dorothy Mae Cook, and prior to entering politics he worked in the insurance industry.

Interstate 70 traverses the Columbus metropolitan area and is central to the region’s transportation network, with Columbus bounded by I-270 and centered at the I-70/I-71 junction. For about 1.5 miles, I-70 shares a single roadway with I-71 in the stretch known as The Split or the South Innerbelt, with I-71 entering and exiting from opposite sides of I-70; this arrangement requires northbound I-71 traffic to cross four lanes of I-70 to continue on I-71, and a similar situation applies to southbound traffic. A major reconstruction of The Split, valued at about $1.4 billion, is targeted for completion by mid-2026. I-670 provides a connection from John Glenn Columbus International Airport to I-270, I-71, and I-70. East of Columbus, the route passes through Zanesville and Cambridge, where it intersects I-77. Proceeding toward West Virginia, I-70 intersects I-470 just east of St. Clairsville; I-470 serves primarily through traffic and offers an alternative to Winter Festival of Lights congestion from Oglebay Park during the Christmas season. In March 1995, a hole created by a former coal mine opened on the eastbound side of I-70 in Guernsey County near Old Washington, temporarily rerouting traffic onto US 40 between Old Washington and Cambridge for several months.

Interstate 70 traverses numerous Illinois counties and passes through several county seats, including Vandalia, which served as Illinois' state capital from 1818 to 1839. The route runs concurrently with Interstate 57 for a segment near Effingham before continuing east toward the Indiana border.

On 25 July 2017, Malaysian singer Yuna appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers at NBC Studios to promote her album Chapters, performing the track “Used To Love You,” which features Jhené Aiko, from the same release; the performance was supported by a full band with a small string section that included violins.

Yuna is a Malaysian singer who began writing her own songs at the age of fourteen. After learning to play the guitar, she began performing publicly at nineteen. Since 2006 she has performed in numerous acoustic shows and events across Malaysia, establishing a presence in the live music scene. In 2006 she auditioned for the inaugural season of One in a Million, advancing to the top forty before being eliminated.

By 1900 Metallwarenfabrik Straub & Schweizer (WMF) stood as the world's largest producer of household metalware. The company's products were primarily produced in the Jugendstil style. Design work was carried out in the WMF Art Studio, under the direction of Albert Mayer. In 1905, WMF expanded by acquiring Orivit, a fellow manufacturer renowned for its Jugendstil pewter.

Jugendstil was a design movement centered in several key European hubs, notably Munich, Vienna, and Weimar, with the Darmstadt Artists' Colony established in Darmstadt in 1901 serving as a major focal point of activity. Its practitioners included Hermann Obrist, Otto Eckmann, Henry van de Velde, Otto Wagner, Joseph Maria Olbrich, Gustav Klimt, Koloman Moser, among others. In its early phase, the style drew on influences from the British Modern Style and Japanese prints. Under the influence of the Secessionists, Jugendstil gradually moved toward abstraction and more geometrical forms.

In the Round of 16 of the 2019 AFC Asian Cup knockout stage, the United Arab Emirates faced Kyrgyzstan. Deep into stoppage time of the second half, Mabkhout squandered a gilt-edged opportunity; moments later, he was fouled in the penalty area by Bekzhan Sagynbaev, earning a penalty that substitute Ahmed Khalil converted to put UAE ahead. Kyrgyzstan pressed for an equalizer, with Bakhtiyar Duyshobekov’s header clipping the upright and, in the final seconds, Rustamov firing a shot against the bar. The UAE defense held firm to secure progression to the quarterfinals.

The knockout-stage clash between Japan and Iran in the 2019 AFC Asian Cup concluded with Japan advancing to the final after a 3-0 victory. In the early stages, Japan created several chances, including Osako's run behind Jahanbakhsh, a cross from Nagatomo, and attempts from Minamino and Dōan that missed the target, while Yoshida's header from a set piece went wide. At the start of the second half, Iran's Dejagah and Hajsafi squandered opportunities. An on-field incident saw Kanaanizadegan confront referee Chris Beath after a collision with Minamino, though Iran's pleas were not heeded. Japan then took the lead when Minamino delivered a cross that Osako headed home. Iran pressed on, with Jahanbakhsh's free-kick saved by Gonda and Pouraliganji's header narrowly off target. A second goal followed when Minamino's pass struck Pouraliganji's arm, awarding Japan a penalty which Osako converted past Beiranvand to double the advantage. In stoppage time, Genki Haraguchi added a third to seal the win and send Japan into the final.

Arthur John Baron (born January 5, 1950), known as Art Baron, is an American jazz trombonist who also plays a variety of other instruments, including the didgeridoo, conch shell, pennywhistle, alto recorder, bass recorder, and tuba.

Art Baron, a graduate of the Berklee College of Music, is a trombonist known for his long association with the Duke Ellington Orchestra. He joined the Duke Ellington band in August 1973 at age 23, during Ellington’s final year leading the ensemble, and was the last trombonist Ellington ever hired. Baron leads The Duke's Men, a group composed of Duke Ellington band alumni. Throughout his career, he has performed and/or recorded with a wide range of notable artists, including Buddy Rich, Bruce Springsteen, Lou Reed, Stevie Wonder, James Taylor, and others.

The Family Friend was an English magazine issued in bound volumes, circulating for much of the nineteenth century. It presented a miscellany of articles selected for their entertainment value and practical usefulness. The publication was aimed primarily at housewives of the era, reflecting its domestic orientation and intended readership.
The Family Friend was a monthly periodical published in London by S. W. Partridge and Company, running from 1849 to 1921, and at its peak achieved a circulation of about 50,000 copies.

In the Cook Islands, congregations that are not organized into a stake are designated as branches, a designation applied irrespective of their size. The Church operates branches in Aitutaki, Avarua, and Mangaia, each with its own meetinghouse. Adjacent to the meetinghouses of these branches are the respective Family History Centers, providing genealogical resources for members and visitors.

The presence of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in the Cook Islands began with brief missionary visits in the mid- to late 19th century, culminating in a formal arrival in 1899 that ended by 1903 due to limited interest. In 1942, Fritz and Maudina Kruger were assigned to establish the church on the island of Rarotonga, and they conducted their work while running a bakery in Avarua. The Cook Islands’ first converts, Samuel Glassie and his family, were baptized on May 12, 1942, marking a turning point in local membership. Church meetings were held in the northern Puaikura District in 1943, and later that year Sunday services were moved to Muri. By June 1946, the congregation comprised 37 members, and around this period the Krugers returned to New Zealand, briefly leaving the church without priesthood leadership.
Within Czech naming practice, a proposal sought to permit women to adopt masculine versions of surnames. The Senate of the Czech Republic endorsed the measure, with approval delivered in July 2021.

Naming in the Czech Republic has evolved from a state-regulated framework to one with greater latitude. Historically, parents were required to pick a child's name from a government-approved roster, and names outside that roster needed special permission, with exemptions for minority groups and foreign nationals. After the Velvet Revolution in 1989, the rule was relaxed and parents could register any name in common use elsewhere in the world, provided it is not insulting or demeaning. In recent years, birth-record offices have often consulted a semi-official catalog titled Jak se bude vaše dítě jmenovat? to determine whether a proposed name is permitted. If the name is not listed there, authorities typically request an odborné stanovisko (professional opinion) from the Czech Language Institute (Ústav pro jazyk český) before it can be registered.

The president of the Senate serves as the presiding officer of the upper chamber of Parliament. Under the Constitution of the Fifth Republic, the president of the Senate is first in the line of succession to the presidency in cases of death, resignation, or impeachment, and accordingly becomes the Acting President of the Republic until a new presidential election is held. This responsibility has been exercised on two occasions: Alain Poher acted as interim head of state from 28 April to 20 June 1969, between Charles de Gaulle's resignation and Georges Pompidou's installation, and again from 3 April to 27 May 1974, between Pompidou's death and Valéry Giscard d'Estaing's installation.

The article provides a comprehensive roster of individuals who have served as president of the Senate of France. It notes the official French designation, Président du Sénat français, and its formal English rendering as Speaker of the Senate. Additionally, the list encompasses leaders of chambers that are assimilated to the Senate, thereby offering a unified record of presiding officers across related legislative institutions.

Influenza infection is typically mild and confined to the upper respiratory tract, but pneumonia remains a relatively common complication. Pneumonia associated with influenza can be either primary viral pneumonia or secondary bacterial pneumonia. Primary influenza pneumonia presents with rapidly escalating fever, a persistent cough, laboring respirations, hypoxemia, and cyanosis, and it is more common among individuals with preexisting cardiovascular disease such as rheumatic heart disease. In contrast, secondary bacterial pneumonia usually follows a period of clinical improvement lasting one to three weeks, then a return of fever, increased sputum production, and fluid buildup in the lungs; it can also appear within days of initial influenza symptoms. About one third of primary viral pneumonia cases are followed by a secondary bacterial infection. The secondary form is most frequently caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus.

Early investigations into influenza included a misidentification by Pfeiffer in 1892, who attributed the influenza agent to the bacterium Haemophilus influenzae, a designation that would later prove inaccurate despite the name. From 1901 to 1903, Italian and Austrian researchers demonstrated that avian influenza, then known as fowl plague, was caused by a microscopic agent smaller than bacteria, a finding supported by filtration experiments in which the infectious agent passed through pores too small for bacterial passage. At that time, the fundamental distinctions between viruses and bacteria were not yet understood, leaving the true nature of this agent unclear despite evidence of its non-bacterial, filterable character.
Beng Per Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area in northern Cambodia. It covers an area of 2,494.08 square kilometers (962.97 square miles) and was established in 1993.

Located south of the Northern Plains Dry Forest Priority Corridor, the Beng Per Wildlife Sanctuary encompasses populations of wild cattle, deer, elephants, and large water birds, and preserves important archaeological sites. The sanctuary faces ongoing deforestation pressures, with more than 2,000 square kilometers (approximately 770 square miles) of forest disappearing each year due to illegal logging, a loss driven largely by the expansion of rubber plantations. This rate of forest loss endangers numerous animal species and threatens the ecological and cultural resources the sanctuary protects.

The Piazza Tasso massacre was an incident in which militias of the Italian Social Republic, allied with the German army, attacked Piazza Tasso, killing five people. The purpose of the shooting remains unclear, with one hypothesis suggesting that it was intended to intimidate residents of the quartiere di San Frediano, including many regime opponents. In the following days, about 17 people suspected of being partisans were murdered at Cascine on July 23.

Decades after the Piazza Tasso massacre, a memorial was erected in the square to commemorate the event. The monument takes the form of a solid block featuring an oval cavity, with two plaques positioned on either side and the whole structure enclosed by a surrounding fence. Visitors sometimes place toys and flowers within the oval recess as offerings.

Across numerous languages, the designation historically used for an unmarried woman is frequently regarded as outdated. In certain jurisdictions, employing such a title may be legally inappropriate or unlawful, reflecting evolving norms around gendered language and statutory rules. The statement functions as a cross-linguistic caveat about terminology, emphasizing that the acceptability and legality of specific titles vary by language and legal context.

The title viscount (and its feminine form viscountess) traces its origin to the Latin vicarius, a word signifying a deputy or substitute. From this same root developed the word vicar and the prefix vice-, both linked to the notion of representing another. Accordingly, the designation can be understood as a direct translation of “deputy count.”

The article presents a compiled list of Hispanic and Latino American individuals who have held judicial roles, whether currently serving or former. It encompasses a range of positions within the judiciary, including judges, magistrate judges, court commissioners, and administrative law judges. Where information is available, the list notes when a jurist has served on multiple courts, identifying the relevant courts and timeframes. The compilation aims to document the presence and career movements of Hispanic and Latino jurists across different courts and jurisdictions.

In the 1968 film Blue, Joanne tells her father, Doc, that Azul saved her and that they nurse him back to health in their home. Ortega locates Azul and begs him to return home, but Azul refuses. Ortega then threatens to wipe out the settlers. Azul responds by organizing the settlers into a defense force that repels and defeats the attackers, including Ortega and Xavier. Before dying, Ortega asks Azul to bury him in Mexico. To fulfill Ortega's dying wish, Azul is shot by Carlos, Ortega's closest ally, who is himself fatally wounded. Joanne later brings Azul's body back to Texas for burial.

Set in 1880, the film centers on Ortega, a Mexican bandit and revolutionary, who has four sons: Xavier, Manuel, Antonio, and Azul, the latter being adopted; Azul’s name derives from the blue hue of his eyes. The narrative progresses as Antonio is fatally shot while attacking Texas settlers, while Manuel makes an attempt to rape Joanne, a settler woman. In the ensuing violence, Azul fatally shoots Manuel, and at the same moment, one of the settlers shoots Azul.

Tagesschau24 is ARD's news channel. It competes with Welt and n-tv. In addition to its news programming, Tagesschau24 broadcasts culture, sports, and science programming. A high-definition simulcast was launched on 5 December 2013.

Tagesschau24 is an ARD digital broadcaster that began on 30 August 1997 under the name EinsExtra. It was positioned as an information channel. Until 2006, its programming largely consisted of re-airings of morning shows, talk shows, and documentaries from Das Erste and the regional public broadcasters. From 2006 to 2009 the channel operated as an all-news network, marked by the launch of the news-centered program EinsExtra Aktuell. On 1 May 2012, EinsExtra Aktuell was renamed Tagesschau24.

The gong, sometimes referred to as chau gong, is a traditional Chinese percussion instrument with prominent ceremonial functions. The oldest known example derives from a tomb at the Guixian site in Guangxi and dates to the early Western Han dynasty. By the sixth century CE, gongs appear in Chinese visual art and are distinguished by their intense, spiritually charged drumming used in ritual settings and in tribal assemblies. Historically, chau gongs were employed to clear a route for important officials and processions, serving as a sonic signal akin to a police siren. The number of strokes struck on a gong could indicate an official’s rank, and in encounters where two officials met unexpectedly, it was possible to determine in advance which of them should bow to the other based on this ceremonial signaling.

A gong is commonly used by drummers in rock music. It is typically struck with a nylon-tip drumstick, and its sound is frequently likened to the chimes of a mantle clock. Some gongs have a hole in the center, while all suspended gongs are mounted by holes near the rim. Smaller gongs, measuring 18–30 cm (7–12 in) in diameter, produce a more bell-like tone, a consequence of their thickness and small diameter.

Within the evolution of the .NET Framework, Microsoft introduced a lighter deployment option called the .NET Framework Client Profile for the 3.5 Service Pack 1 release, designed to support typical desktop applications with a reduced set of components. The Client Profile is considerably smaller than the full framework, containing only the elements most relevant to client desktop software. The 28 MB figure applies to online installations on Windows XP SP2 when no other .NET Framework components are present and Windows Update is used; installations via the offline installer or on any other operating system require roughly 250 MB.

.NET Framework 2.0 was released on October 27, 2005, alongside Visual Studio 2005, SQL Server 2005, and BizTalk Server 2006 as part of Microsoft's 2005 development platform update. The associated Software Development Kit for this version was released on November 29, 2006. Support for the framework concluded on July 12, 2011. It was the last version of the .NET Framework to support older Windows operating systems, including Windows 98, Windows 2000 SP3, Windows ME, and Windows Server 2003 RTM.

Jeniferever / The Next Autumn Soundtrack is a split EP featuring the post-rock bands Jeniferever and The Next Autumn Soundtrack. Released on 1 December 2003 through the independent label Big Scary Monsters, the record divides its tracks between the two groups, with the opening pair performed by Jeniferever and the final trio by The Next Autumn Soundtrack.

Data centers are facilities that house the computing and storage infrastructure essential for delivering digital services. The surge of artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in the late 2010s and into the early 2020s contributed to a global expansion of data-center infrastructure, as organizations sought increasingly powerful, scalable, and energy-efficient systems. Projections released in March 2021 suggested that worldwide data creation would surpass 180 zettabytes by 2025, up from about 64.2 zettabytes in 2020, illustrating the dramatic growth in data volumes that data centers are expected to support.

Data centers originated in the 1940s as dedicated rooms for large-scale computing systems, exemplified by ENIAC. These early installations were difficult to operate and maintain and required controlled environments to function properly. The extensive cabling associated with these machines prompted the development of organization strategies such as standardized rack enclosures, raised floors, and cable trays placed overhead or beneath the floor level. Because a single mainframe demanded substantial power and generated significant heat, reliable electrical supply and cooling were essential to prevent overheating. Security concerns grew in importance due to the high cost of equipment and its military applications, leading to early design guidelines aimed at restricting access to computer facilities.

The Malaysia Basketball Association (MABA) serves as the national governing body for the sport of basketball in Malaysia. It comprises sixteen affiliated members, including thirteen state associations, the Federal Territory, the Malaysian Armed Forces, and the Royal Malaysia Police. MABA joined FIBA Asia in 1957, integrating Malaysian basketball into the regional federation. The first elected president of the association was Quek Kai Dong.

Liverpool University Press (LUP) is a publisher of academic works and is home to the Pavilion Poetry imprint. Through its poetry line, LUP has published notable collections, including Mona Arshi's Small Hands, which earned The Felix Dennis Prize for Best First Collection at the 2015 Forward Prizes for Poetry, and Bhanu Kapil's How to Wash a Heart, which won the 2020 T. S. Eliot Prize.

In 2024, Anthony Cond, the chief executive of Liverpool University Press, became the Association of University Presses’ first president to originate from outside the Americas, marking a historic milestone for international leadership within the organization.

The cantons of Switzerland were, in formal terms, part of the Holy Roman Empire, but over time they established de facto autonomy from imperial authority. This assertion of independence culminated in their defeat of Emperor Maximilian I at the Battle of Dornach in 1499, an outcome that effectively ended imperial overlordship and laid the groundwork for the development of the Swiss Confederation.

Cantons of Switzerland are semi-autonomous entities within the Swiss Confederation, each endowed with its own constitution and a separate legislative body that enacts cantonal laws. They also maintain an independent executive authority, responsible for administration and policy implementation, as well as a distinct police force and a judiciary to administer justice at the cantonal level. The cantonal governments typically operate on a collegial, directive system of governance, in which executive power is exercised collectively rather than by a single leader, a structure that mirrors the broader federal arrangement and emphasizes cantonal autonomy within the confederal framework.

The 33rd Annual Grammy Awards ceremony, held in 1991 to honor the previous year's music, has been described by Variety as one of the most unmemorable broadcasts in memory. The telecast was considered doomed from the outset after Sinead O'Connor announced she would boycott the ceremony over concerns about commercialism. During the program, Garth Brooks' stage setup was described as evoking the sensibilities of a Noël Coward production. In another moment, Billy Idol modified a lyric in Cradle of Love to remark on the song's cheesiness. Elsewhere, MC Hammer appeared to be wrapped in aluminium foil on camera.

The 33rd Annual Grammy Awards saw Bob Dylan receive the Recording Academy's Lifetime Achievement Award, an accolade presented by actor Jack Nicholson. During the ceremony, Dylan performed "Masters of War," a moment that occurred on the night of the first U.S. invasion of Iraq.

The Vietnam Service Medal is authorized to be accompanied by campaign stars to denote participation in or support of operations in the seventeen designated Vietnam War campaigns. Each campaign is indicated by a 3/16-inch bronze service star worn on the medal’s suspension and service ribbon for the period from 15 March 1962 to 28 January 1973. In addition, a 3/16-inch bronze service star is authorized for Operation Frequent Wind (29–30 April 1975) for Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force personnel. A 3/16-inch silver service star may be worn in lieu of five bronze stars.

The Vietnam Service Medal ribbon measures 1 3/8 inches in width and is composed from the center outward of a yellow field with a central yellow stripe (5/32 inch) flanked by yellow stripes (5/16 inch each), interposed with three narrow red stripes (1/16 inch) toward the ends, and edged by narrow green stripes (1/8 inch) on the outermost sides. The yellow-and-red arrangement bears a resemblance to the former flag of South Vietnam. In its symbolism, the yellow reflects the imperial color of Vietnam, while the red denotes the three ancient Vietnamese realms—Tonkin, Annam, and Cochinchina—and the green border alludes to the country’s jungle environment.

Dmitry Ustinov was a prominent Soviet defense administrator whose long career was closely tied to Igor Illarionov, a Soviet Army Colonel General who served as his assistant for three decades. Illarionov described Ustinov as among the most staunch Stalinist figures of the commissars and noted that he was groomed by Joseph Stalin to preserve the existing political and military system. He also observed that, like many of his contemporaries, Ustinov’s outlook was shaped by experiences in the Great Patriotic War. Additionally, Illarionov portrayed him as deeply passionate about his work, with a habit of working late into the night and sleeping only a few hours during the day.

In the early 1990s, it was revealed that five top-secret memos dating from late 1983, written within weeks of the downing of Korean Air Lines Flight 007, existed and were later disclosed by Boris Yeltsin in 1992. The documents purportedly asserted that the Soviet Union had recovered KAL 007’s black box and had deciphered its tapes. In this context, Dmitry Ustinov, who served as Soviet defense minister, together with Viktor Chebrikov, advised General Secretary Yuri Andropov not to publicize possession of the black box, arguing that the tapes did not support the claim that KAL 007 was on a U.S. espionage mission. The memos were published in Izvestia No. 228 on 16 October 1992.

Battery electric vehicles employ two distinct direct-current electrical networks. The low-voltage system, typically operating at about 12 volts, provides auxiliary power for lighting, sensors, and control electronics, performing the same functions as the 12V system in conventional internal combustion engine vehicles. The high-voltage system, which commonly runs in the range of 300–400 volts though exact values vary by model, supplies power to the traction motors. Increasing the traction voltage for a given motor power reduces the current drawn, thereby improving overall efficiency by lowering electrical losses.

In a direct current circuit, both the power source and the load possess positive and negative terminals. Conventional current flows from the power source’s positive terminal through the load and back to the source’s negative terminal, thereby forming a closed loop. If either terminal becomes disconnected, the circuit is opened and the flow of charges ceases.

Harry Potter: The Exhibition opened in April 2009 at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, Illinois, United States. After its premiere, the exhibition toured to a variety of locations around the world. The final venue of this edition was the Pavilhão de Portugal in Lisbon, Portugal, and the tour concluded in March 2020, earlier than originally scheduled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The exhibition presents a curated collection of props, costumes, and other artefacts drawn from the Harry Potter film series. Among the items on display are Harry Potter's wand and his eyeglasses. The display also includes recreations of film sets, notably the Great Hall and the Gryffindor Common Room, both associated with Hogwarts, a central setting in the series. Beginning in 2016, the exhibition expanded to incorporate artefacts from the Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them films.

Siem Pang Wildlife Sanctuary (Khmer: ដែនជម្រកសត្វព្រៃសៀមប៉ាង) is a protected area located in the communes of Santepheap, Thma Keo, and Prek Meas within Siem Pang District, Stung Treng Province, Cambodia. It covers an area of 133,707.73 hectares (516.2484 square miles). The sanctuary was established on November 6, 2019, by Sub-decree No. 161 ANKr.BK, through the integration of the former Siem Pang Wildlife Sanctuary and Western Siem Pang into a single protected area. The two predecessors were created in 2016 as separate designations before being merged in 2019.

Siem Pang Wildlife Sanctuary (Khmer: ដែនជម្រកសត្វព្រៃសៀមប៉្រើង) was established on May 9, 2016 and created under Sub-decree No. 86 ANKr.BK. The sanctuary covers an area of 66,932 hectares (258.43 square miles).

Sawila, sometimes called Tanglapui, is a Papuan language spoken in the Alor archipelago. It comprises several dialects, including Sawila proper, Lona, Salimana, Lalamana, and Sileba. Among its speakers, the language is referred to as Manata.
C++ templates and header-only libraries raise licensing considerations similar to those encountered with Ada generics. LGPL version 3 addresses these cases in section 3.

The GNU Lesser General Public License permits the sublicensing of software received under the LGPL into the GPL, as provided by LGPL v2.1, section 3, and LGPL v3, section 2, option B. This allowance enables the direct reuse of LGPL-licensed code in GPL-licensed libraries and applications, thereby facilitating the integration of LGPL components into GPL-licensed software.

Yul Brynner authored two books, Bring Forth the Children (1960) and The Yul Brynner Cookbook: Food Fit for the King and You (1983). Bring Forth the Children chronicles a journey among the forgotten peoples of Europe and the Middle East. The 1960 volume includes photographs taken by Brynner in collaboration with Inge Morath, a photographer associated with Magnum Photos.

In 2006, Rock Brynner, Yul Brynner's son, published Empire and Odyssey: The Brynners in Far East Russia and Beyond, a book about his father and their family history. He regularly returned to Vladivostok, Yul Brynner's birthplace, and visited there for the Pacific Meridian Film Festival.

Slowly changing dimensions are a class of design patterns in data warehousing that manage changes to dimension attributes over time without requiring reprocessing of the associated fact table. Dimension changes may include the addition of retrospective fields that modify time slices, enabling historical analyses to reflect updated attribute values. Moreover, incorrect dates in the dimension table can be corrected easily, allowing more accurate historical records without restructuring the data model.

Slowly changing dimensions are designed to preserve historical accuracy in data warehousing by maintaining stable relationships over time, with relational database management systems enforcing referential integrity to ensure valid connections between records. The Supplier_Code attribute cannot be used as a foreign key in the Product table, restricting how supplier references are modeled. If the foreign key is defined as Supplier_Key, each product entry is tied to a specific time slice, anchoring its supplier relationship to a particular period for accurate historical analysis.

The Ljung–Box test is widely applied in econometrics and time series analysis to assess autocorrelation in a sequence of residuals across multiple lags. For researchers seeking analogous diagnostic tools, the Breusch–Godfrey test and the Durbin–Watson test offer comparable alternatives.

The Ljung–Box test, named after Greta M. Ljung and George E. P. Box, is a statistical procedure used to determine whether any of a group of autocorrelations of a time series differ from zero. Rather than evaluating each lag separately, it tests the joint hypothesis that the autocorrelations up to a chosen number of lags are collectively zero, thereby assessing overall randomness across multiple lags. As a portmanteau test, it combines information across lags into a single statistic to gauge lack of fit or randomness in the data.

Accreditation in metrology is the formal recognition by an authoritative body that an organization has demonstrated the competence of its staff, the effectiveness of its management system, and the suitability of its facilities to perform specified measurement activities. Achieving international recognition requires the accrediting body to meet established international requirements and engage in ongoing international and regional cooperation, thereby enabling mutual acceptance of results. Laboratories are assessed against international standards, such as ISO/IEC 17025, which set out the requirements for testing and calibration laboratories. To ensure objectivity and technical credibility, accrediting bodies operate independently of other national measurement system institutions. Examples include the National Association of Testing Authorities in Australia and the United Kingdom Accreditation Service.

Metrology encompasses the science of measurement and its application in society. A nation’s National Measurement System (NMS) comprises its network of laboratories, calibration services, and accreditation authorities that establish and sustain the national metrology framework. The NMS shapes how measurements are made domestically and determines whether measurements are recognized by the international community, influencing global interoperability and trust in data. Metrology has wide-ranging societal impacts across economics, energy, environment, health, manufacturing, industry, and consumer confidence. The effects of metrology on trade and the economy are among the most readily observable. To facilitate fair trade, an agreed-upon system of measurement is essential.

Chen Yuanyuan was born in Jiangnan into a poor family and was originally surnamed Xing; after the death of her parents she was taken in by her aunt and adopted her uncle’s surname, Chen. At ten years old she was sold by her uncle to become a courtesan, and she soon excelled in Kunqu and Yiyang opera, often wearing her hair in a high bun known as wo duo ji (倭堕髻). She gained lasting renown as one of the Eight Beauties of Qinhuai, alongside Ma Xianglan, Bian Yujing, Li Xiangjun, Dong Xiaowan, Gu Mei, Kou Baimen, and Liu Rushi. In particular, she was praised for the role of Hongniang in The Romance of the West Chamber, in a performance associated with Zou Shu (邹枢). Beyond her theatrical life, Chen Yuanyuan also wrote poetry, though only three of her works have survived.

Chen Yuanyuan is a historical figure whose arrival in Beijing is recorded with uncertainty, with dates proposed as 1641, 1642, or 1643. According to Mao, he proposed marriage to Chen in 1641 with plans for a union in 1642. However, a spring 1642 visit reportedly found that she had already been taken away, lending support to the 1642 date. The Tian family feared that their daughter Tian Xiuying might lose favor at court and sought to win the emperor’s favor by presenting attractive women from Jiangnan to the court on the family’s behalf. The Ming upheavals caused by Li Zicheng and the Manchu incursion left the Chongzhen Emperor with little opportunity to attend to Chen. Three months after Chen entered the Forbidden City, she was sent back to Tian. She subsequently performed in Tian’s family opera troupe. Later, Chen was either purchased for the Ming general Wu Sangui by Tian’s father or presented to Wu by Tian.

Under Vlasov's leadership, the movement came to be known as the Vlasov Movement, with its manifesto titled the Liberation Movement of the Peoples of Russia emphasizing a multinational character. He initially sought open cooperation with Nazi Germany, but later contended that National Socialism could not be imposed on Russia, arguing that a foreign ideological system would not suit the Russian people. In nationalist speeches he advocated an equal partnership with Germany while pursuing an independent Russia. This stance drew the ire of Himmler, prompting Wilhelm Keitel to order Vlasov to return to the prisoner-of-war camp and to restrict the use of his name to propaganda purposes. Alfred Rosenberg withdrew support and placed Vlasov under virtual house arrest in Dahlem rather than sending him to the camp. Disappointed, Vlasov expressed a desire to return to the camp but was dissuaded by his associates Malyshkin and Wilfried Strik-Strikfeldt.

During World War II, Vlasov was taken to Berlin under the supervision of the Wehrmacht Propaganda Department, where he and other Soviet officers formulated plans for a provisional Russian government and a Russian army of liberation under Russian command. In the spring of 1943, Vlasov authored the anti-Bolshevik Smolensk Proclamation, which was dropped from aircraft onto Soviet forces and territory. In March 1943, he published an open letter titled Why I Have Taken Up the Struggle Against Bolshevism. Before the Russian Liberation Army (ROA) existed, Nazi propaganda disseminated ROA patches and used Vlasov's name to encourage defections. Ultimately, several hundred thousand former Soviet citizens served in the German army wearing the ROA patch, but never under Vlasov's command.

Programming tools, or software development tools, are computer programs designed to assist in creating and maintaining other software. They commonly help manage project files and source code, enabling developers to organize, edit, and track changes within codebases. Examples include source code editors, which provide facilities for editing source text, and compilers, which translate high-level code into machine-readable executables. Build tools extend these capabilities by automating the packaging of software components into distributable bundles, combining executables and data files into installable kits or installers.

Programming tools span both toolchains and integrated development environments. A toolchain is a sequence of software utilities that transform source code through successive stages, with intermediate results passed from one component to the next until a final artifact is produced. Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) consolidate the capabilities of multiple tools into a single application, aiming to streamline development workflows. Most IDEs include a source code editor as a core component, and they typically offer built-in or extensible features to assist with compiling, debugging, and testing, either natively or through plug-ins.

Bageis, also known as Bagis, was a Byzantine-era bishopric located in Asia Minor that functioned as a residential see until it disappeared amid the Turkish–Byzantine wars, probably in the 12th century. Nevertheless, the see continued to be listed in the Notitiae Episcopatuum, the official register of episcopal sees of the Byzantine Church, for some time thereafter.

Bageis is an ancient settlement known from its coinage and later ecclesiastical lists. On its coins, the city name is inscribed as Bageis, which is the genitive plural form of the inhabitants’ ethnonym derived from the Greek ΒΑΓΝΩΝ or ΒΑΓΗΝΩΝ. The form Bagis appears in the Synecdemus of Hierocles, while in later Notitiae Episcopatuum the name is recorded as Bage. Some coins also bear the additional epithet Kaisareōn, indicating a connection with Caesarea.

Morphological similarities between the Nicobarese languages and Austronesian languages have been observed, and some scholars have cited these correspondences as evidence in support of the Austric hypothesis, a proposed genetic connection between Austronesian languages and related groups. The claim is notably associated with Reid (1994).

The Nicobarese languages form a linguistic grouping that appears to be related to Shompen, the language spoken by the interior inhabitants of Great Nicobar Island. Shompen is typically regarded as a separate branch within the Austroasiatic family. However, Sidwell (2017) classifies Shompen as part of a Southern Nicobaric language subgroup rather than as an independent Austroasiatic branch.

A furrier is a craftsman who prepares animal pelts for fur products. Skinning is the initial step in the process, and the animal is frozen beforehand to ensure safe skinning and to prevent the pelt hairs from detaching due to heat exchange. Freezing the carcass prior to skinning also reduces the risk of bleeding during the skinning operation. After the hide is removed, it is fleshed, dried, salted, and pickled, then tanned either chemically or through natural methods, followed by softening. The duration of skinning, tanning, and overall fur processing contributes to the high price of fur products.

Fur has long been used in civilian fashion as a material for accessories, extending beyond military applications. Common fur accessories include hats, hoods, scarves, and muffs. Designs often incorporated animal imagery, with the heads, tails, and paws left attached to the items. In the 19th century, seal and karakul furs were used to make indoor jackets.

Edmond Adolphe de Rothschild owned a 4,000-acre estate located east of Paris. The land had been acquired by his ancestors in the eighteenth century, forming part of the family holdings. On this property, he established the farm Domaine des Trente Arpents, which primarily produced artisanal Brie de Meaux cheese.

Edmond Adolphe de Rothschild acquired a ten percent stake in Rothschild & Co., the family venture associated with his cousin David, in 1982. The stake remained in place until 2018, ending after a settlement resolving a dispute over the Rothschild family name between cousin companies. He was a major shareholder of the Italian bank Banca Tiburtina and held a minority stake in Banca Privata Solari & Blum in Lugano. He was also a shareholder in Banque de Gestion Edmond de Rothschild in Luxembourg and an investor in Israel General Bank in Tel Aviv. Additionally, he maintained investments in De Beers Consolidated Mines.

In February 2019, Ofcom relaxed local content obligations for commercial radio. Heart announced that local breakfast and weekend programming would be replaced with networked London content by the end of the year. Consequently, local programming hours per station were planned to fall from 43 hours per week to 15. The shift was expected to result in the loss of dozens of jobs.

Heart Radio’s development included a notable format change in 1996, when the station dropped its soft adult contemporary approach in favor of a more neutral hot adult contemporary playlist. The network expanded further in 2005, as Century 106 in the East Midlands joined Heart as its third station after Century was sold by GCap Media. A further consolidation followed in 2007, when Chrysalis’s radio holdings were acquired by Global Radio, strengthening its ownership and reach within the Heart network.

Popstars inspired the Pop Idol franchise, created by Simon Fuller. The Idol franchise would go on to dominate reality television for several years, standing alongside other enduring formats such as Big Brother and Survivor.

Popstars is an international reality television franchise aimed at discovering new singing talent. It served as a forerunner to the Idol franchise. The series originated in New Zealand in 1999, when producer Jonathan Dowling helped form the girl group TrueBliss. Over the years, the format became one of the most successful television formats, licensed in more than 50 countries, though it has been off the air in recent years. Among its notable outcomes was the launch of groups such as Girls Aloud, who achieved UK chart success for about a decade following their win. The show also inspired Simon Fuller’s Idol franchise.

The Liberal Popular Alliance, linked to an initiative by Verdini, sought to establish a centrist platform named Moderates for Renzi with the aim of uniting centrists who supported Renzi's government and incorporating other centrist parties backing his administration. After Renzi resigned as prime minister in December 2016, the alliance's relevance diminished. In the 2018 general election, it failed to secure parliamentary representation.

The Liberal Popular Alliance emerged in July 2015 as a breakaway faction from Forza Italia led by Denis Verdini, formed to back the reforms of the Renzi cabinet. It was joined by senators from centre-right groups, including Great Autonomies and Freedom (GAL), Conservatives and Reformists (CoR), and the New Centre-Right (NCD). Lucio Barani, formerly secretary of the New Italian Socialist Party (NPSI), was elected president of the senatorial group. The inclusion of "Autonomies" in the group's name reflected the presence of two MpA–PdS senators among its ranks. Outside Barani (NPSI) and the two MpA–PdS senators, the composition consisted of non-party independents.

Flash Video encompasses the evolution of video support within the Flash platform. In 2002, Flash Player 6 introduced video playback inside SWF files, and the following year Flash Player 7 gained direct support for FLV files. To address limitations of the FLV format, Adobe in 2007 developed new container formats based on the ISO base media file format (MPEG-4 Part 12). Among these, F4V shares a common foundation with MP4 and is sometimes referred to as Flash MP4. Additionally, the Flash Player determines a file’s format by examining its contents rather than relying on the filename extension.

Flash Video refers to the use of the FLV container format for delivering video content within the Flash platform. In common configurations, FLV files encode video using the Sorenson Spark or VP6 codecs. In 2010, publicly released Flash Player versions developed jointly by Adobe and MainConcept added support for H.264 video and HE-AAC audio. All of these compression formats are subject to patent restrictions. Flash Video can be viewed on most operating systems through the Adobe Flash Player plug-in or via other third-party programs. However, iOS devices and most mobile devices do not support the Flash Player plug-in, necessitating alternative delivery methods such as Adobe Flash Media Server.

Defense Media Activity was established following the 2005 Defense Base Realignment and Closure analysis, which recommended merging the separate military-media organizations into a single entity and placing it in the same location as the American Forces Information Service (AFIS). The BRAC Commission endorsed the recommendation and included it in its report to the President dated September 8, 2005. On that date, the President approved the commission’s recommendations and forwarded them to Congress. By September 20, 2005, Congress had not disapproved the BRAC recommendations. Under the Defense Base Realignment and Closure Act of 1990 (Public Law 101-510), the recommendations were effectively approved.

Under a realignment of a leased facility at 2320 Mill Road in Alexandria, Virginia, the Army Broadcasting-Soldier Radio/TV unit was relocated to Fort Meade, Maryland, marking its new location at the Army post.

John Malcolm Bland (born January 30, 1967) is an American college football coach who, since 2024, has served as the quarterbacks coach for the Catholic High School for Boys. His head coaching career includes a stint at Southern Arkansas University in 2000, a tenure at the University of the Cumberlands in Williamsburg, Kentucky, from 2005 to 2013, and a period leading Mississippi College from 2014 to 2023. Bland played quarterback for the University of Arkansas from 1988 to 1991, and he later worked as the quarterbacks coach at Rice University from 2001 to 2005.

Levenshtein coding constitutes a coding scheme for nonnegative integers in which the codeword length for any positive integer n is precisely one bit longer than the length of the Elias omega code for n. A Levenshtein code for zero also exists within the framework. By comparison, applying Elias omega coding to zero would require shifting the numbering so that zero is represented by the code assigned to one.

Glendora, California sits on land traditionally inhabited by Indigenous communities whose daily life centered on communal and kin-based activities. The villages featured dome-shaped dwellings built from willow branches and thatched with tule or other grasses, arranged around a central fire pit with a smoke hole for ventilation. Village sizes ranged from a few dozen to about a hundred residents and were politically autonomous under a local chief, though tied to neighboring groups through kinship and shared language. Economic roles were gendered: men hunted and fished; women foraged, processed plant foods, and wove baskets. Hair was kept long, and both men and women adorned themselves with tattoos and paint. Clothing varied with climate: in warm weather, men wore breechcloths and women skirts of deer hide or woven fiber; in cooler periods, capes or cloaks made from animal skins, and sandals woven from yucca fiber or hide. Spiritual life encompassed ceremonies for events such as the summer solstice and communal mourning rituals for the dead. The people possessed deep knowledge of local plants used for food, medicine, and materials, reflecting a practical and spiritual relationship with the land.

Glendora, California, shifted its city council elections from an at-large format to a district-based system to avert potential litigation under the California Voting Rights Act of 2001. The change also moved the election cycle from odd-numbered to even-numbered years. The transition occurred in two phases: in March 2020 (Phase 1), Districts 2, 3, and 5 elected council members; and in 2022 (Phase 2), Districts 1 and 4 elected.

HY-2, commonly known as the Silkworm, is a sea-skimming anti-ship missile that became notable in the 1980s for its use by both Iran and Iraq during the Iran–Iraq War. China supplied missiles to both sides. In 1987 Iran launched Silkworm missiles from the Faw Peninsula. In October 1987, missiles struck the Sungari, an American-owned, Liberian-flagged tanker, and the Sea Isle City, a U.S.-flagged tanker. Earlier in 1987, five additional missiles hit targets in Kuwait.

Following the Sino-Soviet split and the September 1960 withdrawal of Soviet advisers, the HY-2 achieved its first successful missile test in November 1960. The SY-1 was developed as a domestic copy of the Soviet P-15, forming the design lineage for China’s missile program. Production of the SY-1 began in October 1963 at the Nanchang Aircraft Manufacturing Company, with the first successful test of the system occurring in 1965. Production was officially approved in August 1967, and the SY-1 entered service by the end of the 1960s.

Bauhaus members drew a wide range of early influences that helped shape the band's aesthetic. David J credits jazz luminaries such as Miles Davis, Charlie Parker, and Thelonious Monk as formative inspirations and has cited Television's Marquee Moon as an all-time favorite album. Peter Murphy’s influences span traditional pop and folk from Doris Day, Simon and Garfunkel, the Beatles, and the Everly Brothers, tempered by experiences from Catholic school Mass; his first seven-inch record purchase was the Beatles’ A Hard Day’s Night, and he counts Brian Eno’s Music for Airports among his preferred albums. Daniel Ash’s initial interest was sparked by the Dave Clark Five’s Bits and Pieces, with his older brother’s record collection including the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, Faces, and the Kinks; his first record purchase was Dave and Ansell Collins’ Double Barrel, and his playing style blends a reluctance to learn conventional scales and chords with a desire to sound original, while he has admired Jimi Hendrix, Mick Ronson, Robert Fripp on Bowie's tracks, and Earl Slick, and has appreciated bands such as the Only Ones, the Damned, Television, and Richard Hell and the Voidoids, considering the Stooges’ Raw Power one of his all-time favorite records. Kevin Haskins, at fourteen, saw Led Zeppelin and was impressed by John Bonham’s drum solo but felt inadequate and contemplated quitting; the emerging punk scene, including performances by the Sex Pistols and the Clash, gave him the confidence to pursue a career in music.

Daniel Ash, together with David J. Haskins and his younger brother Kevin Haskins, had performed together from childhood in the local groups Jam and Jackplug & the Sockets, where they covered songs by the Rolling Stones and the Beatles. Ash attempted to recruit his schoolfriend Peter Murphy to join a band, but Murphy initially showed little interest. Ash's group, the Craze, played around Northampton in 1978. After the Craze dissolved, Ash renewed his attempt to recruit Murphy, believing that Murphy possessed the right look for a band. Murphy, who worked in a printing factory, agreed to join despite never having written lyrics or music before. In their first rehearsal, Murphy contributed to the writing of the song In the Flat Field, a pivotal moment in the formation of Bauhaus.

La Presse Médicale is a French peer-reviewed medical journal established in 1983. It is published by Elsevier and edited by Loïc Guillevin and Frédérique Lesaulnier. The publication includes an English-language supplement, Quarterly Medical Review, issued four times annually. In 2003, La Presse Médicale merged with Annales de Médecine Interne, the latter having previously been published under the titles Bulletins et Mémoires de la Société Médicale des Hôpitaux de Paris and Bulletin de la Société Médicale des Hôpitaux de Paris.

Killerspin is a brand of table tennis equipment and accessories. Its products have been featured on television programs such as MTV's Real World, The Simple Life, and HGTV's Don't Sweat It. Additionally, Killerspin gear and its sponsored players have been highlighted in the Hollywood feature film Balls of Fury and in the independent film Ping Pong Playa.

Killerspin is a company involved in table tennis media and products. It has participated in televised table tennis competitions, with broadcasts on Fox Sports Net and ESPN for audiences worldwide. In addition to event production, the firm creates consumer-oriented video content, including instructional DVDs that teach technique and strategy as well as event-focused DVDs that document tournaments and related performances.

The Macau Office in Beijing serves as the representative office of the Macau Special Administrative Region in the Chinese capital, functioning to represent the Macau SAR government in dealings with Beijing's authorities and institutions. Through this office, Macau maintains its official relations with the central government and other agencies located in Beijing. Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.

The Macau Office in Beijing functions as the counterpart to the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Macao Special Administrative Region. It serves as the Central Government of the People's Republic of China’s representative office in Macau, and acts as the official presence and liaison of the PRC government in the territory.

Jeanette Jurado was born in East Los Angeles, California, with her family relocating to Pico Rivera, California during her early childhood. Of Mexican American heritage, she grew up in a vibrant, predominantly Latino neighborhood and is the middle child in a family of three sisters.
Jeanette Jurado grew up in a musical environment and began singing around the age of 15. She has identified Barbra Streisand and The Carpenters as influences on her vocal development.

Georgia comprises five principal physiographic regions: the Cumberland Plateau, the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians, the Blue Ridge Mountains, the Piedmont, and the Atlantic coastal plain. Each region is marked by distinctive geologic and topographic characteristics, resulting in a variety of landscapes across the state. In the northwestern corner, sedimentary rocks such as limestone, sandstone, and shale predominate. These rocks have provided resources including construction-grade limestone, barite, ocher, and small quantities of coal.

Anthropogenic climate change is warming the state's climate, and this warming has already produced significant disruptions across Georgia. A principal consequence is sea level rise, which poses substantial risks to coastal and low-lying areas as a result of the warming. Georgia’s vulnerability to sea level rise is greater than that of many other states due to land subsidence, a process that causes portions of the terrain to slowly sink relative to the sea. Projections indicate that further warming will intensify sea level rise and its related disruptions, with potential impacts on infrastructure, ecosystems, and economic activity.

The Carter–Menil Human Rights Prize, established in 1986 by former president Jimmy Carter and philanthropist Dominique de Menil, aims to promote the protection of human rights worldwide. Administered by the sponsoring foundation, it periodically awards a prize of $100,000 to individuals and institutions that advance human rights. Carter serves as the chairman of the Prize Committee.

The F.A. Premier League Stars is a sports video game developed by EA UK and published by Electronic Arts. It was released in Europe in 1999 for the Microsoft Windows and PlayStation platforms. A sequel, The F.A. Premier League Stars 2001, was released in 2000.

The F.A. Premier League Stars received generally positive feedback from critics, with GameSpy awarding it 87 out of 100 and praising the title as a gem while noting that its appeal would likely be strongest in the United Kingdom and may not translate to broader international audiences.

Design Cities is a UNESCO initiative within the Creative Cities Network, an international program established to advance creativity as a driver of urban development. The Creative Cities Network was launched in 2004 and designates seven creative fields for its member cities: design, crafts and folk arts, music, film, culinary arts, literature, and media arts.

Design Cities (UNESCO) is a designation conferred by UNESCO recognizing cities that foster a robust design sector and integrate design into their cultural and urban fabric. The designation supports the development of a resilient design industry and a cultural landscape shaped and maintained through architecture, urban planning, public spaces, monuments, and transportation infrastructure. It encompasses not only design education and research through schools and centers but also vibrant professional communities of designers who remain active at local and national levels. Cities with the designation typically cultivate a tradition of hosting fairs, events, and exhibitions dedicated to design, creating opportunities for collaboration and visibility. It also provides pathways for local designers and urban planners to harness regional materials and the interplay between urban and natural conditions in their projects. The scope covers design-driven creative industries such as architecture and interiors, fashion and textiles, jewelry and accessories, interaction design, urban design, and sustainable design.

A graduated strand of pearls is characterized by a progressive increase in pearl diameter from the ends toward the center, typically showing at least a 3 mm difference between the smallest and largest pearls. The design gained popularity in the United States during the 1950s, when GIs returning from Japan brought back strands of cultured Akoya pearls and helped popularize the style. An example often cited is a 3.5 momme, 3 mm to 7 mm graduated strand. Such graduated strands were more affordable than uniform strands because the majority of the pearls used are smaller in size.

By 2010, China overtook Japan in akoya pearl production. Japan has largely discontinued producing akoya pearls smaller than eight millimeters, yet it remains a major processing hub within the pearl industry. The country imports a large share of China’s akoya pearl output, which is subsequently processed in Japan—often through basic sorting and matching—before the pearls are relabeled as Japanese products for export.

During the Smolensk crisis, when collapse seemed imminent, Stalin refused to permit the city to be surrendered and condemned the evacuation mindset of front-line commanders as treasonous. In this constrained strategic atmosphere, Timoshenko’s armies were determined to hold their ground rather than retreat, with the overarching objective of recapturing Smolensk guiding operations. Rokossovsky, a senior Soviet commander in the theater, played a role within this framework by directing forces and supporting efforts aimed at reclaiming Smolensk.

Rokossovsky was unable to secure a link with the pocketed forces after a week of strenuous efforts. Nevertheless, sustained Soviet offensives hindered the Germans from consolidating their front. Some elements of the encircled 16th Army managed to break outward from the pocket. By 4 August the line had stabilized, and the defending units trapped inside the pocket either ceased resistance or were destroyed.

Charles Darwin was part of a family that was largely Unitarian, with the Wedgwood side moving toward Anglicanism. His father, Robert Darwin, a freethinker, had him baptised in November 1809 at St Chad’s Church in Shrewsbury, an Anglican parish. Alongside his siblings, Darwin attended the local Unitarian Church with his mother, reflecting the household’s mixed religious affiliations. At eight years old, in 1817, he demonstrated an early interest in natural history and collecting and joined a day school conducted by the local preacher. The death of his mother occurred in July 1817, a significant personal tragedy for the family. In September 1818, he began attending the Anglican Shrewsbury School as a boarder, joining his elder brother Erasmus.

In 1849, Darwin visited the Malvern spa operated by Dr. James Gully to address his chronic ill health, and he experienced some benefit from hydrotherapy. In 1851, his daughter Annie fell ill, and her illness renewed Darwin's fears that his own condition might be hereditary. Annie died later that year after a protracted sequence of crises.

In March 2015, Blue Coat Systems integrated the technologies obtained through the acquisitions of Norman Shark and Solera Networks, consolidating them into a cloud-based product family known as the Global Intelligence Network.

Blue Coat Systems experienced rapid revenue growth in the late 1990s and early 2000s, with revenues rising from $7 million in 1998 to $29 million in 1999 and $97 million in 2001. The company held a significant share of the caching market, comprising 25 percent of the overall caching market and 35 percent of the caching appliance market. However, despite this growth in revenue, the company was not profitable.

JavaScript is a programming language and a core technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and CSS. It was created by Brendan Eich in 1995. Today, it is extensively used on the client side to enable interactive features and dynamic behavior on webpages, with estimates indicating that roughly 99 percent of websites rely on JavaScript for client-side scripting.

JavaScript is a multi-paradigm programming language, meaning it supports more than one approach to programming. A programming paradigm provides a high-level framework for conceptualizing and organizing the construction and operation of a program. In line with this, JavaScript accommodates a broad spectrum of paradigms, enabling developers to apply different styles—such as functional, imperative, and object-oriented—within the same language.

The SM-64 Navaho is on display at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Museum, located at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. The vehicle sustained damage during Hurricane Matthew in 2016 and was subsequently restored with the assistance of the Space and Missile Museum Foundation. It was reinstalled in March 2021 and is exhibited outside the south entrance gate of the Cape Canaveral Space Force Museum.

In the early phase of the SM-64 Navaho program, the United States Army Air Forces issued proposals to 17 aviation firms on 31 October 1945. From these submissions, six companies were awarded development contracts. The longer-range concepts proposed were all based on cruise missile designs, while the shorter-range submissions comprised a mixture of different configurations. All proposals were designated with MX-series designations by the USAAF Experimental Engineering Section.

Geezil Minerve, raised in Florida, began playing music at age twelve and built his early career by performing with Ida Cox, freelancing in New Orleans, and collaborating with Clarence Love and Ernie Fields. After serving in the Army from 1943 to 1946, he briefly reunited with Ernie Fields before joining Buddy Johnson from 1949 to 1957. The 1960s saw him work with Mercer Ellington in 1960, followed by a stint with Ray Charles from 1962 to 1964 and a collaboration with Arthur Prysock (date not specified). Minerve joined the Duke Ellington Orchestra in 1971, filling Johnny Hodges’s chair after Hodges’s death, and remained with the ensemble until 1974, then returned to perform with Mercer Ellington. He continued with the Duke Ellington Orchestra under Mercer Ellington, Duke Ellington’s son, and after the Broadway hit Sophisticated Lady he left briefly for Ruth Brown’s Black and Blue Review in Paris, before returning to Ellington in the 1980s. He also engaged in further freelance work later in the 1970s.
"Merry Go 'Round" was named by Rolling Stone as the 49th best single of 2012. In the magazine's 2021 revision of its 500 Greatest Songs of All Time, the track was ranked at number 362.

“Merry Go 'Round” is a song by American country singer Kacey Musgraves. The track has received notable critical recognition, being included in NPR Music's list of the 100 Favorite Songs of 2012, and it achieved the top position on Billboard's ranking of the 10 Best Country Singles of 2013.

Kasong is an endangered Pearic language of the Austroasiatic family spoken in the Bo Rai District of Trat Province, Thailand, and it has also been referred to as the Chong of Trat. Early lexical comparisons based on a short word list led some researchers to treat Kasong as a dialect of Central Chong, but more extensive word lists and subsequent investigations indicate that Kasong constitutes a distinct language, though it remains closely related to Chong and Samre. The language is nearly extinct, with no monolingual speakers; all current speakers use Thai as their primary language.

Over fifty years ago, the Kasong language was prohibited from being spoken within families and in social settings, a policy implemented by authorities who argued that Kasong speech interfered with Thai language proficiency. Consequently, Kasong families often taught Thai to their children rather than the Kasong language. This policy unfolded within the broader currents of Thai nationalism, which fostered stigma toward the Kasong language and led to neglect of its preservation. The experience of the Kasong language and its speakers thus illustrates Thailand's ethnolinguistic minority groups.

An epiglottal (also termed pharyngeal) plosive, or stop, represents a class of consonantal sounds. It is attested in a number of languages and forms part of their phonemic inventories. In the International Phonetic Alphabet, this sound is indicated by the symbol ⟨ʡ⟩.

An epiglottal plosive is a central consonant. Central consonants are articulated by directing the airstream along the center of the tongue, rather than toward its sides. This distinction highlights how central consonants differ from those articulated with lateral airflow along the tongue.

According to Tennis Magazine's 2008 rankings, Stefan Edberg was recognized as the fourteenth greatest player of the Tennis Era when considering both male and female players; when the assessment was limited to male players, his standing was eighth.

Stefan Edberg’s distinctive service action was once the basis for the Australian Open’s emblem, with a stylized silhouette used as the tournament’s logo for many years.
