Al-Atrash is regarded as a Syrian cultural hero for his defiance of opposing powers; his contributions in the Shruqi genre—narratives about heroines who rebel or about captive poets humiliated by foes—helped propagate Bedouin-themed concepts within urban southern Syria. This written work contributed to bringing Shruqi and related Bedouin ideologies into city life, aided by shifts in the geopolitical climate that encouraged urbanization and the clustering or relocation of nomadic and rural communities. As urbanization progressed, modernized instruments began to blend with traditional oral poetry, permitting the fusion to spread across regions of the Middle East.

Vyasa is tied to the royal lineage through a series of events following Shantanu and Satyavati’s union, which produced two sons, Chitrangada and Vichitravirya, neither of whom lived to sire an heir. When Vichitravirya died childless, his wives Ambika and Ambalika remained without issue. Now widowed, Satyavati urged her stepson Bhishma to marry the two queens, but he refused on account of his vow of celibacy. She then disclosed her secret past and asked Bhishma to bring Vyasa, her firstborn, to impregnate the widows under the Niyoga tradition, in order to continue the dynasty.

Vyasa is traditionally credited with compiling the eighteen major Purāṇas, a central collection within Indian literary tradition. The Purāṇas themselves are works of Indian literature that cover an encyclopedic range of topics and draw upon a variety of scriptures.

Angara is a family of expendable launch vehicles developed by the Moscow-based Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center. The family provides payload capacities to low Earth orbit ranging from approximately 3,800 kilograms (8,400 pounds) to 24,500 kilograms (54,000 pounds). Along with variants of the Soyuz-2, the Angara system was intended to replace several existing launch vehicles.

The Angara family includes a proposed heavy variant, the Angara A7, with an estimated launch mass of about 1,133 tonnes. It would have a payload capacity of roughly 35 tonnes to a 200 km × 60° orbit. An alternative payload configuration envisages an enlarged KVTK-A7 acting as the second stage in place of URM-2, enabling about 12.5 tonnes to geostationary transfer orbit. There are no current plans to develop this heavier Angara A7, as implementation would require a larger core URM-1 to accommodate more propellant, depend on the development of a hydrogen-fueled engine for the KVTK, and require a different launch pad.

Air Austral began operations in 2000 after taking delivery of an ATR 72-500 short-haul turboprop. By that year the airline operated from Roland Garros Airport in Sainte-Marie and Pierrefonds Airport in Saint-Pierre, offering flights to Mayotte, Johannesburg in South Africa, Comoros, Mauritius, Seychelles, and four Madagascar destinations—Antananarivo, Tamatave, Nosy Be, and Majunga. In 2003 it launched its first long-haul service between Réunion and Paris, operated with two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft, and a third 777-200ER joined the Paris service in 2005. Subsequently, a second long-haul route from Réunion to Marseille and Lyon was established.

Air Austral pursued a period of network expansion and fleet renewal between 2007 and 2011. In 2007 the airline inaugurated its third long-haul route, operating from Réunion to Toulouse with a Marseille stopover. The following year, 2008, it introduced newly designed staff uniforms created by Balenciaga. The fleet was augmented with a second ATR 72-500, followed by a third a few months later. In April 2009 the carrier began services to Sydney and New Caledonia, launching Paris–Sydney via Réunion, and it also acquired two Boeing 777-300ERs to support the expansion. In November, Air Austral placed a firm order for two all-economy Airbus A380s, a configuration of 840 seats, with deliveries planned for 2014 for operations on the Réunion–Paris route. In June 2010 the company announced planned services from Réunion to Bordeaux and Nantes, set to begin in February 2011. In August 2011 the airline took delivery of its first Boeing 777-200LR, further extending its long-range capability.

In the area around Hornsey Road within Upper Holloway, the locality was historically known as Tollington. The Tollington name appears in the Domesday Book, indicating its long-standing usage in the region. In modern times, the name has largely fallen from common use, though it persists in two official capacities: as the designation of an electoral ward on the local council and as the name of the parish of the Church of England serving the area. Additionally, a number of local businesses continue to adopt Tollington in their names, preserving a visible link to the historic toponym.

Upper Holloway was historically one of several hamlets within the ancient parish of St Mary Islington. Population growth in the parish necessitated the establishment of a local place of worship, which led to the construction of the Church of St John Upper Holloway. The building was financed under the provisions of the Church Building Act 1818 and was consecrated in 1828. In 1830, the creation of a new ecclesiastical parish marked the beginning of the subdivision of Islington for ecclesiastical purposes.

Law in Washington State comprises constitutional provisions, statutes, administrative regulations, and case law, as well as local ordinances enacted by city and county governments. The Revised Code of Washington (RCW) forms the principal statutory framework, organizing the state's statutory law into a codified body enacted by the legislature.

Decisions of the Washington Supreme Court are published in the Washington Reports, while Court of Appeals decisions appear in the Washington Appellate Reports. Both official reporters are produced by LexisNexis, and slip opinions are made available online. The Reporter of Decisions, a constitutional officer of the Supreme Court, is responsible for preparing decisions and opinions for publication in the official court reports. In addition to the official reporters, Washington appellate court decisions are also reported in the unofficial Pacific Reporter. Historically, from 1854 to 1889, the territorial Supreme Court opinions were published in the Washington Territory Reports, in three volumes.

Since 2003, Law360 broadened its layout and organization by introducing topic-focused sections to complement its daily news coverage, editorial analysis, business of law reporting, and feature pieces. Beginning in 2022, the publication has been organized into a set of distinct sections, including Law360 U.S., Law360 U.K., Law360 Pulse, Law360 Tax Authority, Law360 Employment Authority, Law360 Insurance Authority, Law360 Real Estate Authority, and a collection of additional features.

Law360 Canada is a Canadian legal news publication whose origins lie in 1983, when Ontario Lawyers Weekly was launched by managing editor Michael Fitz-James. The title was later renamed The Lawyers Weekly, and in 2017 the publication shifted from a weekly print newspaper to an online format, adopting the name The Lawyer's Daily. In February 2023, the publication rebranded as Law360 Canada, aligning with the Law360 brand while continuing to cover legal news.
A music video for Move was directed by Keith Schofield and filmed in Barcelona, and has been made available for viewing on YouTube as well as on CSS's official MySpace page.

Following Wang Jingwei's death in Nagoya on 10 November 1944, the Nanjing Central Political Committee convened an emergency meeting on 12 November to reassess the leadership of the collaborationist government. It designated Chen Gongbo as president of the executive committee, acting chairman of the National Government, and chairman of the military committee. Chen Gongbo formally assumed these positions on 20 November, and he affirmed his intention to continue Wang Jingwei's policy and maintain the political course irrespective of how the war developed or how urgent the situation became. In the broader wartime administration, Zhou Fohai was appointed mayor of Shanghai in January 1945.

During the Second Sino-Japanese War, Wang Jingwei, a former premier of the Republic of China and a former Vice Director-General of the Kuomintang, broke with Chiang Kai-shek’s leadership in 1939 and established a separate Kuomintang faction headquartered in Nanking. Aligning with Japan, the split aimed to present the branch as distinct from Chiang Kai-shek’s Kuomintang government in Chongqing. This new party became the sole ruling force of the Wang Jingwei regime, which operated as a puppet state under the Empire of Japan.

Augustinerkirche on Augustinergasse is one of Zürich's five principal medieval churches. It was built circa 1270 as a Romanesque church associated with the Augustinian abbey. Worship ceased during the Reformation. In 1841, the Roman Catholic community proposed rebuilding the structure to commemorate the old Augustinian church. A majority of the Catholic community rejected the decrees of the First Vatican Council in 1870, and the community was expelled from the Catholic Church. The church remains their parish church. Today, it is one of three medieval churches in Zürich's Lindenhof district.

Augustinergasse is bordered to the north by Münzplatz and by St. Peterhofstatt as it extends toward Münsterhof. The street derives its name from the former Augustinian monastery, which is now represented by the Augustinerkirche church. The Rennweg tram stop, previously known as Rennweg–Augustinergasse and served by lines 6, 7, 11 and 13, lies about 150 metres (approximately 160 yards) further south along Bahnhofstrasse.

Historical British performances at Wimbledon traces the annual progress of British tennis players at the tournament, which serves as the home Grand Slam for players from the United Kingdom. The article presents year-by-year results and situates achievements within the distinctive status of Wimbledon for national competitors. In recent years, British players have experienced limited success at the event. A notable milestone occurred on 7 July 2013 when Andy Murray became the first Briton to win the men's singles title at Wimbledon since Fred Perry in 1936. In the ladies’ singles, the last British champion was Virginia Wade, who won the title in 1977.

R1–R4 were contracted to Chatham Dockyard; R5–R6 were initially contracted to Devonport but the order was subsequently transferred to Pembroke Dockyard; R7–R8 were placed with Vickers; R9–R10 were contracted to Armstrong; and R11–R12 were placed with Cammell Laird. In August 1919, the contracts for R5 and R6 were cancelled following the end of World War I. The remaining submarines of the class were completed, with components from the H-class utilized to expedite production.

Within the British R class submarine, approximately 35 percent of the pressure hull’s internal volume was occupied by machinery. Surface propulsion consisted of a single eight‑cylinder diesel engine rated at 480 hp (360 kW). When submerged, propulsion was provided by two large electric motors driving the single propeller shaft. The electric drive was powered by a 200-cell battery of the same type used in J-class submarines. The battery could sustain full-speed operation for about one hour. Recharging the cells required a full day of operation at roughly half the diesel engine’s power, and charging was conducted in harbour using shore electricity or specialized battery-charging vessels.

Aleksandr Krestinin began his professional career in 1995 as a defender with FC Kolos Krasnodar. He subsequently played for a sequence of clubs, including FC Rostselmash-d, FC Kuban Krasnodar, FC Krasnoznamensk, FC Gazovik Orenburg, FC Caspiy, FC Spartak Tambov, FC Reutov, FC Don Novomoskovsk, FC Yassy-Sayram, FC Nara-ShBFR Naro-Fominsk, FC Spartak Shchyolkovo, FC Smena Komsomolsk-na-Amure, FK Metallurg Krasnoyarsk, and FC Neftchi Kochkor-Ata.

Alexander Sergeyevich Krestinin, also rendered as Aleksandr Krestinin, (born 19 September 1978) is a Russian football coach and former professional player. He has pursued a career in football management and previously served as the head coach of the Kyrgyzstan national football team.

Venice, California is frequently used as a filming location for a broad array of movies, television programs, and video games. In practice, productions tend to utilize several local settings, including its piers, the skate park, a variety of restaurants, the canal system, the boardwalk, and nearby schools. These familiar venues contribute to Venice’s distinctive presence in film and media.

Venice Beach Recreation Center, a municipal facility in Venice, California, encompasses a variety of outdoor amenities and recreational spaces. It provides unlit outdoor courts for basketball, handball, paddle tennis, and volleyball, as well as playground areas for children that include a gymnastics apparatus and chess tables for informal games. At the south end of the site is the Muscle Beach outdoor gymnasium. In March 2009, the Venice Beach Skate Park opened as a $2 million development built on the sand toward the northern portion of the recreation area. The Graffiti Walls lie along the beach side of the bike path in the same vicinity.

Java historically included support for the Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) in its standard library, with the CORBA interfaces and runtime exposed under the org.omg.CORBA package. Beginning with Java 9, these APIs were deprecated as part of a broader effort to sunset legacy technologies, and they were ultimately removed from the Java platform with the Java 11 release.

The Internet Inter-ORB Protocol (IIOP) is an implementation of the General Inter-ORB Protocol (GIOP) designed for use over the Internet. It provides a mapping between GIOP messages and the TCP/IP transport layer, enabling CORBA communications to traverse standard Internet networks by carrying remote method invocations and their responses.

Multiplexing is a method of sharing a single communication medium among multiple data streams. In an airport environment, four terminals connect to a central computer, with each terminal operating at 2400 baud; to avoid running four separate circuits, a pair of multiplexers is used to combine their signals onto a single link. A separate arrangement connects the airport ticket desk to the airline data center via a pair of 9600 baud modems and a dedicated analog circuit, providing a direct, higher‑speed link between the two points. In other contexts, some web proxy servers, such as polipo, employ time-division multiplexing (TDM) to pipeline multiple HTTP transactions onto a single TCP/IP connection.

Multiplexing refers to the transmission of multiple signals over a single communication medium. The electric telegraph, the earliest system to rely on electrical wires for long-distance messaging, was closely tied to the development and economic importance of multiplexing. Early experiments in telegraphy demonstrated duplex operation, enabling two independent messages to travel simultaneously in opposite directions over the same line. In the initial implementations, power was provided from batteries at both ends, but later arrangements made it possible to operate with a single power source at one end.

In 1965 Iran Air took delivery of its first jet aircraft, the Boeing 707, alongside six Boeing 727-100s. In 1971 the fleet expanded with the arrival of the Boeing 737-200, and in 1974 three stretched Boeing 727-200s were added. By the mid-1970s the airline served European destinations with non-stop and one-stop services, including London, where it operated more than thirty flights per week. In 1978–1979 it augmented its long-haul capacity by acquiring three Boeing 747 variants: one 747-100B, two 747-200Ms, and four 747SPs.

In January 2012, Iran Air operated flights to and from London Heathrow that used Manston Airport in Kent as a refueling stop. In December 2011, Manston Airport announced it would terminate the fueling arrangement with Iran Air and would no longer refuel its aircraft. The decision followed Iran's closure of its London embassy, a response to the ransacking of the British embassy in Tehran. Manston stated that it had not breached any trade agreements and had no connections with the United States.

A crib lighthouse is a type of offshore lighthouse that rests on a concrete or masonry foundation supported by wooden crib piers. The name derives from the wooden crib pier construction used as the foundation. In construction, wooden cribs are built on shore, towed to the site, filled with stone to cause them to settle and sink, leveled, and capped with concrete or masonry on which the lighthouse is erected. These structures were common in the Great Lakes, where the hardrock bottoms provided stable foundations for such offshore works. A notable drawback is the potential for uneven settlement of the crib, which can lead to operational or structural problems, exemplified by cases such as the Detroit River Light.

Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2008 is a list that summarizes the top-performing tracks on the Billboard Hot 100 over the course of 2008. In an unusual achievement, T-Pain appeared at both the No. 1 and No. 100 positions on the Year-End chart, a distinction described as rare within the chart’s history. The list in question refers specifically to the Billboard Hot 100 Year-End chart for 2008.

Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2008 is an annual list published by Billboard that ranks the year's top-performing songs on the Hot 100 chart. The rankings reflect chart performance across the entire year, with the methodology drawing on data from Nielsen Broadcast Data Systems and SoundScan. The list catalogs the top Hot 100 songs of 2008, providing a retrospective view of the most commercially successful singles in the United States during that year.

The Bowood circle denotes a group of liberal intellectuals centered on Lord Shelburne, named after Bowood House, Shelburne's seat in Wiltshire. Richard Price is recorded as having met Shelburne in 1767 or shortly thereafter, though an alternative account maintains that the introduction may have come through Price's wife, Elizabeth Montagu, a prominent leader among the Blue Stocking women. If such an introduction occurred, it would have taken place after Price published his Four Dissertations in 1767.

Richard Price, in the same year, together with other Dissenters, founded Hackney New College. Price died on 19 April 1791 and was buried at Bunhill Fields. His funeral sermon was preached by Joseph Priestley.

April 2009 saw the inaugural transatlantic tele-audiology trial, in which Dr. James Hall evaluated a patient in South Africa from Dallas, Texas. The session occurred during the AAA conference, and since then interest in tele-audiology has increased significantly.

Tele-audiology refers to the delivery of audiological services via telecommunications technologies in real time, enabling synchronous testing that proceeds as if the patient were in the same room as the audiologist. Practitioners are accustomed to remote testing configurations, such as administering assessments to a patient seated inside a sound booth while the clinician operates from outside the booth, a setup that is functionally similar to Internet-based testing. In this model, the teleconference window functions as the communication interface rather than a physical barrier such as a glass window. The principal difference lies in the physical distance separating clinician and patient, while other elements of the testing process remain largely the same.

MARPAT, the digital camouflage pattern used by the United States Marine Corps, was officially fielded as the standard-issue uniform for officer candidates of OCC-181 at MCB Quantico in late 2002, and for recruits of 3rd Battalion, Mike Company at MCRD San Diego in the same period. Since its introduction, it has remained the Marine Corps' standard-issue uniform pattern to the present.

MARPAT reflects a continuation of the long-standing idea of camouflage built from small patches of color. The concept of employing miniature color swatches for concealment predates MARPAT, and in World War II German troops utilized patterns that were comparable in appearance to Flecktarn. Those schemes relied on tiny dabs of color applied to uniforms to disrupt shape and improve concealment in varied environments.

In 2012, Nighat Dad established the Digital Rights Foundation and served as its executive director. The foundation aims to educate Pakistani internet users, particularly women, to protect themselves from online harassment. Malala Yousafzai, a Pakistani activist for female education and the youngest-ever Nobel Prize laureate, attended Dad's workshops. Malala Yousafzai was shot by the Taliban in October 2012.

Nighat Dad (Urdu: نگہت داد; born circa 1981) is a Pakistani lawyer and Internet activist who runs the non-profit organization Digital Rights Foundation. Through her work in information technology security, she has earned numerous international awards recognizing her advocacy for digital rights.

Column-oriented database management systems organize data by columns rather than by rows. This arrangement yields a higher degree of homogeneity within each column, since all values correspond to the same attribute, unlike the diversity found across multiple rows. The resulting uniformity enhances compression efficiency, leading to a smaller compressed size for the stored data.

Tabular data are two-dimensional, comprising rows and columns. Because computer systems store data in a linear memory model, whether on disk or in memory, a two-dimensional table must be mapped into a one-dimensional space. The arrangement of data depends on the chosen mapping, and among the principal storage schemes are row-oriented and column-oriented.

Huanggang Normal University (HGNC; 黄冈师范学院; 'Huanggang Teachers College') is a provincial public undergraduate college located in Huanggang, Hubei, China. It is affiliated with the Hubei Province and sponsored by the Hubei Provincial People's Government. Despite its English name implying university status, the institution has not been granted university status by the Ministry of Education of China.

Among the Serer people, historical developments following the decline of the Ghana Empire and the emergence of independent regional polities set the stage for earlier encounters with external expansion. In this period, Abu-Bakr Ibn-Umar, the leader of the Almoravids, launched a jihad into the region. Serer oral tradition attributes to Amar Godomat, a Serer bowman, the killing of Abu-Bakr Ibn-Umar with an arrow. In later centuries, the Serer communities actively resisted the 19th-century jihads and the Marabout movement aimed at converting Senegambia to Islam, maintaining traditional religious and social structures in the face of external pressures.

The Faal (Fall) paternal dynasty, which rose in the period after 1549 following the Battle of Danki, governed Cayor and Baol under the title Damel. According to Cheikh Anta Diop, the Faal were originally patrilineal descendants of Black Moors (Naari Kajoor) or of Serer origin, and subsequently adopted the Damel title. The Faal surname is not typically regarded as Serer, although Serer people do include individuals bearing the Faal/Fall name. The maternal grandmother of Damel-Teigne Amari Ngoneh Sobel Faal, Lingeer Sobel Joof, was Serer and descended from Maad Ndaah Njemeh Joof, a medieval king of Laah in Baol; further information on that lineage is available under the Joof family. Prior to the Faal ascendancy, Cayor and Baol were ruled by Serer patrilineages such as Joof/Diouf, Faye, and Njie, supplemented by the maternal line of Wagadou (the Ghana Empire) through marriage into Serer aristocracy.

Social conservatism is a political and social philosophy that emphasizes preserving traditional moral codes, social institutions, and communal bonds, often grounded in religious belief. Advocates typically seek an economic approach that balances market liberalization with policies intended to protect social welfare and cohesion, rather than pursuing unfettered capitalism or comprehensive state control. The movement centers on concerns about the economic well-being of families and communities alongside the maintenance of traditional social norms as foundations of social order. It manifests in various national contexts, including the Christian Social Union in Bavaria (CSU) in Germany; the Family First Party and Katter's Australian Party in Australia; and the American communitarian movement in the United States, each adapting its emphasis to local political landscapes.

Social conservatives felt marginalized within the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada's Red Tory leadership during the late 20th century, prompting some to align with other parties such as the Social Credit Party of Canada and the Reform Party of Canada. Under Preston Manning, the Reform Party sought broader national appeal and was reluctant to fully embrace socially conservative positions, a stance that contributed to his eventual removal in favor of Stockwell Day, a more explicit social conservative, after which the Reform Party rebranded as the Canadian Alliance. The Canadian Alliance was later succeeded by the Conservative Party of Canada through a unifying merger. While the modern Conservative Party includes socially conservative members and ministers, it has not foregrounded social-conservative issues in its platform, and in 2012 it stated that it did not intend to repeal same-sex marriage or abortion laws.

Delta Air Lines adjusted its U.S.–China flight network by suspending the Atlanta–Shanghai service on January 18, 2012, citing poor performance. The carrier later expanded its trans-Pacific offerings from Seattle, announcing a Seattle–Shanghai route that commenced operations on June 17, 2013. This service marked Delta’s second Seattle–China route, following the earlier launch of Seattle–Beijing service around 2010, roughly three years prior.

Northwest Airlines sought authority to operate a Detroit–Beijing service using a Boeing 787 and also submitted an application for a Detroit–Shanghai service to be operated with a Boeing 787. The grant, if awarded, was conditioned on the Detroit–Beijing route not being allocated for service with a Boeing 747-400 in 2007, reflecting equipment-related constraints in the allocation of U.S.–China air services.

In the narrative of Daddy's Little Girls, Willie is injured in a robbery, retires, and sells his shop to Monty, who accepts the offer. During a child custody hearing, Julia contends that Monty should be awarded custody in the children's best interests and submits a written statement from Kat. Jennifer's lawyer counters by arguing that Monty is not suitable, citing a statutory rape conviction from sixteen years earlier. Following this development, Julia feels betrayed, ceases to represent Monty, and leaves the proceedings.

On the day of the custody hearing, Julia leaves for a different courtroom and overhears Monty’s unsuccessful effort to defend himself. He attempts to inform the judge that the girls are living with a drug dealer. After hearing this, Julia agrees to represent Monty. To celebrate her birthday, Monty takes Julia to a jazz club in his neighborhood, where they drink and dance with his friends. Over the following weeks, Monty and Julia grow closer and develop romantic feelings for each other. When Julia encounters Brenda, whom she had previously met Monty with, she learns that they are now a couple. Brenda rebukes Julia, insisting that Monty is beneath her status.

Amur Oblast, a federal subject of Russia in the Far East, was established in 1948 after separating from Khabarovsk Krai and Chita Oblast to form an autonomous oblast within the RSFSR. The region subsequently entered a period of rapid economic growth driven by gold production, with living standards improving as young specialists arrived to support development. As the Far Eastern District expanded, demand for electric power and housing rose, prompting a wave of new construction. New urban centers were established, and the Zeya Hydroelectric Power Plant (Zeyskaya GES) was developed, a facility that continues to supply electricity to a large portion of the Far Eastern District. On 21 May 1998, Amur Oblast concluded a power-sharing agreement with the federal government—alongside Ivanovo, Kostroma, Voronezh Oblast, and the Mari El Republic—granting it a degree of autonomy. The agreement was abolished on 18 March 2002.

In 2007, mining and quarrying accounted for a substantial portion of Amur Oblast's industrial output, comprising about 19.9%, while fuel extraction contributed 2.9%. In the realm of gold, the oblast ranks sixth among Russian regions and holds the country's largest reserves, led by the Pioneer gold mine, which is owned by Petropavlovsk PLC and is accompanied by the Albyn, Malomir, and Pokrovskiy mines in the area. A major uranium mining and processing facility is situated at Oktyabrsky near the Russia–China border. Plans are in place to develop additional mineral deposits, including titanium, iron, copper, nickel, and apatite. Coal production has totaled 3,398 tons, with four coal deposits operated by OOO Amur Coal as of 2007 and two more under exploration. The oblast contains more than 90 lignite and black coal deposits, with overall reserves estimated at about 70 billion tons.

On NBC Sports Boston, The Toucher and Rich Show is a weekday morning program airing from 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m., functioning as a simulcast of WBZ-FM's weekday morning drive radio program. The show is hosted by Fred Toucher and Rich Shertenlieb.

Comcast announced on April 30, 2007, that it would acquire Cablevision’s stakes in FSN New England and FSN Bay Area, thereby gaining full ownership of FSN New England. The network was subsequently rebranded as Comcast SportsNet New England on October 1, 2007. In August 2008, CSN New England and other Comcast SportsNet-branded networks were updated with a new logo and graphics package, mirroring the design adopted by Comcast SportsNet Bay Area after dropping the FSN brand.

Black metal has a long-standing tradition of foregrounding nature and radical environmentalism in its themes and imagery. Within this framework, the subgenre known as eco-metal intensifies attention to ecological concerns and environmental topics. Notable bands associated with this focus include Wolves in the Throne Room, Botanist, Agalloch, Panopticon, and Immortal, whose work exemplifies the integration of natural landscapes and ecological critique into the black metal idiom.

In the decades following World War II, modern classical music increasingly drew inspiration from the natural world, weaving ecological motifs and field-derived sounds into compositional practice. Pioneers such as John Cage and Olivier Messiaen helped forge approaches that treat patterns and processes in nature as material for music. Cage’s work Child of Tree exemplifies this direction by foregrounding environmental sounds and incorporating unconventional sound-producing elements—such as a cactus and a pea pod shaker—alongside other instruments selected by the performer, thereby broadening the traditional sonic palette. John Luther Adams, meanwhile, composes from his surroundings in Alaska and positions himself as an environmentalist who argues that artists have a role in addressing global warming. His sound-and-light installation The Place Where You Go to Listen reflects this ethos by being controlled by natural events as they occur in real time, linking sensory perception with environmental processes and technology.

Meihuayuan Station (梅花园站/梅花園站; Cantonese Yale: Mùihfāyùhn Jaahm) is an underground station on Line 3 of the Guangzhou Metro. The name literally means "Plum Blossom Garden." It is situated along the Meihuayuan Section of Guangzhou Avenue North in Baiyun District, Guangzhou, and it began operations on 30 October 2010.

The official video for the track "Higher Love" was directed by Hannah Lux Davis and released on YouTube on 26 August 2019. The clip opens with a group of men dressed in contemporary clothing walking through what appears to be abandoned warehouses, who become intrigued by a retro 1980s aerobics class led by an instructor portrayed by Canadian actress Vanessa Morgan. After an initial attempt to deter them, the male lead returns to the room in a vintage 1980s aerobics outfit and begins dancing with the female lead, with his male companions soon joining in.

Higher Love is a collaborative single by Kygo and Whitney Houston that achieved widespread international chart success. The song reached the top five in Croatia, the Flanders region, Ireland, Israel, Latvia, Norway, Slovakia, and Slovenia; it climbed into the top ten in the Netherlands, Hungary, Sweden, and Switzerland; and it advanced to the top twenty in Australia, Austria, China, the Czech Republic, and Wallonia. In the United States, it debuted at number 63 on the Billboard Hot 100 with 6.6 million streams in its first week, and that peak position remained. Additionally, it topped the Billboard Dance Club Songs chart in the U.S., giving Kygo his third chart-topping at that ranking and marking Houston's fourteenth.

Brazil has experienced daylight saving time during several distinct periods: 1931–1933, 1949–1953, 1963–1968, and 1985–2019. While the practice was originally applied nationwide, since 1988 it has been limited to select areas of the country, typically in the southern regions. The southern states adopt daylight saving time to accommodate greater seasonal variation in daylight hours. The practice generally lasted from October or November until February or March each year. In Portuguese, daylight saving time is called horário de verão, literally "summer time."

Brazil's principal time zone covers the South, Southeast, and Northeast regions, with the exception of a number of small offshore islands. In addition to these regions, the zone includes the states of Goiás, Tocantins, Pará, and Amapá, as well as the Federal District (Brasília). Approximately 93 percent of Brazil's population lives within this time zone, which accounts for about 60 percent of the nation's land area.

True Entertainment is a British television channel whose license first appeared on the Ofcom website in January 2007. It initially operated under the provisional title Toon TV, before being renamed AnimeCentral in June 2007. In June 2008 it adopted the name True Entertainment, but on 26 August 2008 it was rebranded as Showcase TV. The channel subsequently reverted to the True Entertainment name on 10 June 2009. Its on-screen logo is identical to the design used by True Movies 1 and True Movies 2.

True Entertainment launched on Freesat on 5 July 2010, subsequently expanding to Virgin Media on 1 March 2011. It then entered Freeview on 6 August 2013, occupying channel 61 (excluding Wales transmitters) and introducing a refreshed schedule for new Freeview viewers. On 22 July 2018 at midnight, a temporary duplicate began broadcasting on Virgin Media channel 126, taking over the slot vacated by Alibi in advance of UKTV channel removals. The temporary service remained in place until the network was restored on 11 August 2018.

Hjaltalín recorded their debut album, Sleepdrunk Seasons, over the course of January to October 2007 with sessions held in Reykjavík and Amsterdam. The record was initially released by the Icelandic label Kimi Records, and a European release followed in 2009.

Hjaltalín is an Icelandic indie rock band. As of 2020, they had released four studio albums, with their sophomore release Terminal earning the Icelandic Music Award for Album of the Year in 2010. The group has performed across Europe, including appearances at major festivals such as Roskilde Festival (2009), Latitude Festival (2009), and Sziget Festival (2010).

During the Beiping–Hankou Railway Operation, Japanese forces advanced on Baoding, a city protected by substantial fortifications including a 60-foot wall, two moats, and extensive barbed-wire defenses. Although a properly organized defense could have held out for weeks, Baoding fell in a single day. Following its capture, Japanese troops committed atrocities in the city, including acts of rape and murder at the medical college, which was burned and in which many faculty members were killed by being burned in the fires.

In September, after securing Beiping (Beijing) and its surrounding area, the Japanese army pushed southward in two army formations. The operation’s central objective was to seize major urban centers along the route and to secure the railway lines that connected them, thereby consolidating control over the Beiping–Hankou railway corridor.

Bruce E. Melnick participated in NASA's STS-41 mission aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery. The mission concluded with a successful landing at Edwards Air Force Base on Runway 22, on October 10, 1990, at 13:57:19 UTC.

Bruce E. Melnick served as a vice president at Boeing, directing a NASA contract at the space center that managed payload ground operations. The agreement supported about 1,600 employees and covered engineering, facilities support, and maintenance activities involved in preparing spacecraft and payloads for Space Shuttle missions before launch and after landing. The division additionally provided support to NASA and its contractors for hardware pertaining to the International Space Station.

Crude (2007) is a documentary that examines the global carbon cycle and the role of oil in the climate crisis. Rather than focusing on day-to-day news, the film situates oil within a wider historical and global context, highlighting how energy choices shape environmental outcomes. It notes that nearly seven billion people depend on oil for energy and material needs in contemporary life. The documentary also traces the Oil Age to a period of less than 150 years and suggests that its era could end within the lifetimes of some current viewers.

Crude (2007) is a documentary that received notable recognition for its treatment of earth sciences. At the 2007 Jackson Hole Wildlife Film Festival, the film was honored with the Best Earth Sciences Program award. The director, Dr. Richard Smith, was later recognized in 2008 by the American Geophysical Union with the Walter Sullivan Award for Excellence in Science Journalism for his work on this film.

Wired magazine, in its inaugural issue, surveyed a range of technology-focused topics, including interactive games, cell-phone hacking, digital special effects, and digital libraries, alongside an interview with Camille Paglia conducted by Stewart Brand and features on digital surveillance, Bruce Sterling’s cover story about military simulations, and Karl Taro Greenfeld’s piece on Japanese otaku culture. The publication was among the early magazines to publish the email addresses of authors and contributors, signaling an embrace of direct online communication. In addition, Nicholas Negroponte’s column was presented in a format resembling an email message, but it appeared with a deliberately fake, nonstandard address.

Wired has launched several international editions, including Wired UK, Wired Italia, Wired Japan, Wired Czech Republic and Slovakia, and Wired Germany. The magazine was published monthly until 2024, at which point it shifted to a bi-monthly schedule, producing six issues per year.

By 2018, the majority of Canadian senators were officially independent of any party caucus. Nonetheless, a number of Liberal senators continued to publicly align with the Liberal Party even though they were no longer permitted to sit in the party caucus. In contrast, the Conservative Party did not remove its senators from the party caucus, and many Conservative senators maintained visible partisan affiliations. During the 2019 federal election campaign, Conservative leader Andrew Scheer indicated that he would restore partisan appointments to the Senate if elected prime minister.

Local elections in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea are dominated by independent candidates. The Fatherland Front and other major parties conduct their activities primarily in the urban core, where their presence is strongest. At the local level, formal alliances between independent candidates are prohibited.

Development of the work titled I Don't Give A began with a plan to begin with one song and expand from there, avoiding overanalysis of its legend and aiming to produce something that felt coherent. She wrote one track, then another, and found enjoyment in the process of making music. The period was described as privileged, free from external pressure and with ample time to devote to the project. It was the sole undertaking she had at that time.

Accounts of the recording indicate that Madonna expressed her views on the tracks within a project-wide framework, helping to streamline the process. Contrary to Solveig’s expectation that she would stay only briefly, she remained fully involved throughout the session. She contributed to both the composition and the instrumentation, including input on tonal choices such as whether to use a snare drum or a synthesizer. Solveig observed her active participation during the work, and Madonna praised Solveig’s organized and methodical approach to the production. She also suggested that she could voice disapproval of aspects she did not like without causing offense to Solveig.

In 2025, Matai'an Creek Barrier Lake formed following a massive landslide triggered by Tropical Storm Wipha in July, and the lake subsequently overflowed as rainfall intensified by Typhoon Ragasa led to widespread flooding across Guangfu, Fenglin, and Wanrong Townships. A bridge and several vehicles were swept away along Provincial Highway 9, and areas were buried under as much as five metres (16 feet) of mud. The disaster left at least 19 people dead, 107 injured, six missing, and about 300 stranded, with roughly 60 million tonnes of the lake's water discharged out of a total capacity of around 91 million tonnes. About 60 percent of Guangfu's population, around 5,200 residents, sheltered on higher floors of their homes. The event has been described by observers as a mountain-origin typhoon, underscoring its extreme character, and near 4,000 people lost access to the local water supply.

Guangfu Township, located in Hualien County, Taiwan, is subdivided into fourteen villages and has a population of 11,975 inhabitants. The fourteen villages are Dahua, Daan, Daping, Dama, Datong, Tungfu, Xifu, Nanfu, Beifu, Dajin, Daquan, Daxing, Dafu, and Dafeng Village.

The Regional District of East Kootenay relies on a network of facilities for hospital care, headed by the East Kootenay Regional Hospital in Cranbrook, which is the largest hospital in the region. Additional facilities include Creston Valley Hospital in Creston, Elk Valley Hospital in Fernie, Invermere & District Hospital in Invermere, and Golden & District Hospital in Golden. Primary health services are concentrated at centers in Sparwood and Elkford.

The Regional District of East Kootenay is defined by the Rocky Mountain Trench as its predominant geographic feature, flanked to the west by the Purcell Mountains and to the east by the Rocky Mountains. The district includes the Columbia Valley, with its southern portion within the regional district and the northern portion in the Columbia-Shuswap Regional District. Within East Kootenay, the Elk Valley in the southern Rockies forms a distinct subregion that serves as the gateway to the Crowsnest Pass and has a coal-mining heritage. The bottomlands of the Trench are formed by the Columbia and Kootenay Rivers, and the region also contains the northernmost parts of the basins of the Flathead, Moyie, and Yahk Rivers; Moyie and Yahk flow as tributaries of the Kootenay and enter it in the United States, while the Flathead feeds into the Clark Fork in Montana.

The PGM-11 Redstone served as the foundation of the Redstone rocket family and contributed to several early milestones in the U.S. space program, including the flight that carried the first American into space. The Army retired the Redstone in 1964, replacing it with the solid-fueled MGM-31 Pershing. After its retirement, surplus Redstone missiles were widely used for test missions and orbital launches. The system was instrumental in achieving the United States’ first manned spaceflight. In 1967, Australia launched its first satellite using one of these missiles.

The PGM-11 Redstone is an early United States ballistic missile whose design traces directly to the German V-2 rocket. The V-2 was developed by a team of predominantly German rocket engineers under the leadership of Wernher von Braun. After World War II, this group was brought to the United States as part of Operation Paperclip, and their expertise significantly influenced American rocketry, including the Redstone program.

Formula One cars typically employ a front suspension based on double wishbone or multilink geometries with a pushrod-operated spring and damper assembly attached to the chassis, and a rear suspension following a similar approach, though certain teams have experimented with alternative layouts. Notable departures include Red Bull Racing's RB5 in 2009, which used a rear pullrod arrangement, Ferrari's 2012 car that employed pullrod suspension at both axles, and, in 2022, the McLaren MCL36 and Red Bull RB18 that adopted pullrod front suspension while retaining pushrod rear suspension. In braking systems, carbon-carbon discs are used to reduce weight and increase frictional performance, with the carbon material helping to maintain braking effectiveness under extreme heat; the braking setup features about 1,000 ventilation holes to optimize cooling and performance.

Within Formula One, each car receives a single set of the softest compound tyres designated for use in the Q3 session. Those that advance to Q3 must relinquish these tyres after the session ends, whereas cars eliminated before Q3 may use their softest tyres during the race. Any penalties that modify the starting grid are applied after qualifying is concluded.

Evidence for Old French appears in the Oaths of Strasbourg and the Sequence of Saint Eulalia, and scholars generally place the literary emergence of the language in the 11th century. Early Old French literature tends to concentrate on hagiography, with works recounting saints’ lives such as Vie de Saint Alexis, while other texts address warfare and royal life, as seen in the Chanson de Roland. The period also witnessed the development of extensive narrative cycles, notably those centered on King Arthur and his court, alongside a distinct cycle devoted to William of Orange.

French possesses a vowel system that can comprise up to 17 phonemic vowels, though the full set is not uniformly realized across dialects. The overall inventory includes the oral vowels /a, ɑ, e, ɛ, ɛː, ə, i, o, ɔ, y, u, œ, ø/ and the nasal vowels /ɑ̃, ɛ̃, ɔ̃, œ̃/. In France, there is a tendency to replace certain contrasts, with /ɑ/ increasingly realized as /a/, /ɛː/ as /ɛ/, and /œ̃/ as /ɛ̃/ in many speakers. The distinction between /ɛ̃/ and /œ̃/ remains in Meridional French. In Quebec and Belgian French, the vowel inventory includes /ɑ/, /ə/, /ɛː/, and /œ̃/.

CNOOC Building attracted local attention when residents interpreted its silhouette as resembling a toilet bowl rather than a ship or an oil derrick. The toilet analogy was linked to a tankless toilet model produced by Kohler that was marketed in China. In a further instance connected to the public perception, a local advertiser erected a billboard promoting that Kohler toilet atop a building across the Ring Road.

The CNOOC Building was designed as a counterpart to the substantial Ministry of Foreign Affairs building located on the opposite corner of the intersection of the Second Ring Road and Chaoyangmen Street. Inside, the design centers on a central atrium illuminated by an upper clerestory. Adjacent to the atrium, a series of sky gardens is intended to foster casual, spontaneous meetings among staff. On the exterior, a western courtyard is buffered from the busy street by a three‑story, L‑shaped podium and is accessed through an oversized gateway. This courtyard is designed to invite visitors to explore the building.

In May 2021, more than 600 musicians signed an open letter urging a boycott of performances in Israel until the occupation of the Palestinian territories ends, with Rage Against the Machine among the signatories. Frontman Zack de la Rocha and guitarist Tom Morello later voiced support for a ceasefire in the Gaza war.

In 2007, Rage Against the Machine briefly reassembled for notable public appearances. On April 14, Tom Morello and Zack de la Rocha delivered a short acoustic set at a Coalition of Immokalee Workers rally in downtown Chicago, an event Morello described as extremely exciting for those present, including himself. Later that month, the band returned to headline the final day of Coachella 2007 (April 29), with an EZLN backdrop that accompanied what was reported as the festival’s largest crowd. Morello explained that the reunion was intended to voice opposition to what he characterized as the rightward drift of the United States under the Bush administration since the band’s dissolution.

Paronyan Musical Comedy Theatre has participated in international theatre festivals, extending its reach beyond Armenia and introducing its work to global audiences. The festivals have been held in Armenia, Georgia, Iran, England, and the United States, reflecting the theatre’s substantial international engagement.

Paronyan Musical Comedy Theatre is a theatre whose artistic direction has been led by Yervand Ghazanchyan since 1993. In February 2009, Ghazanchyan received the Best Presentation Award at the Artavazd-2009 festival.

During the 1950s and 1960s the club served as a proving ground for numerous players who would go on to become Real Madrid stars and Spanish internationals, including José María Zárraga, Enrique Mateos, Ramón Marsal, Pedro Casado, Juan Manuel Villa, José María Vidal, Fernando Serena and Ramón Grosso. Juan Alonso finished his playing career with the club. In the early 1960s, singer Julio Iglesias appeared as a goalkeeper for the side, his football career ending due to injury. Miguel Muñoz began his coaching career at the club. In 1972, Plus Ultra folded following the demise of its insurer, and Castilla Club de Fútbol succeeded Plus Ultra in the Tercera División on 21 July 1972, serving as Real Madrid's new reserve team.

Real Madrid Castilla traces its origins to 1948, when Agrupación Deportiva Plus Ultra (AD Plus Ultra), a local amateur club then competing in the Tercera División, agreed to become a feeder club for Real Madrid. AD Plus Ultra had been formed in 1930 and took its name from Spain’s national motto. Real Madrid provided financial support to the club in exchange for the first refusal on its best players. By 1949, AD Plus Ultra made its debut in the Segunda División. In 1952 the club was established as Real Madrid’s official reserve team. In 1959 they reached the quarter-finals of the Copa del Generalísimo, losing 7–2 on aggregate to Granada, the eventual runners-up.

The King Alfred Chair of English Literature was founded in 1881 at the University of Liverpool as one of the university’s original endowments, established with funding from William Rathbone and his brothers Samuel and Phillip Rathbone. In its early history the chair’s designation and remit underwent changes, with the title listed as the King Alfred Chair of Modern History and Literature for 1881–82, then Modern Literature and History from 1882–84, and subsequently Modern Literature and English Language from 1884–1900.

Glass making relies on raw materials that are typically delivered as dusty powders or fine-grained substances. Maintaining effective dust-control systems in such facilities is challenging, given the nature of the materials and processes. The large daily throughput of materials means that even a small release of dust can create operational difficulties. In addition, cullet, consisting of broken or waste glass, is circulated around the plant, and handling it—whether by shoveling or breaking—tends to generate fine glass particles.

Following formation, the container is lifted from the mold by the take-out mechanism. It is then held over the deadplate, where air cooling assists in lowering the temperature of the still-soft glass. The bottles are subsequently swept onto a conveyor by push-out paddles that incorporate air pockets to keep the bottles upright after landing on the deadplate. At this stage, they proceed to the annealing process.

Diego Durán grew up in Tetzcoco (Texcoco) in what is now Mexico, a center of learning notable for its extensive collection of pre-Hispanic pictorial manuscripts known as codices. The local population spoke Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, and Durán acquired Nahuatl in addition to his native Spanish. This fluency later proved valuable in his roles as a Dominican friar and ethnographer working among indigenous communities. He conducted interviews with Nahuatl-speaking people in rural areas, drawing on his linguistic skills to document indigenous customs and history.

Diego Durán was a Dominican friar and chronicler who entered the order in 1556. After completing his training in Mexico City, he was sent to Oaxaca in 1561, and he later resided for a period at a convent in Oaxtepec, where he accessed a substantial network of informants within the Church. It is believed that he was tutored by Fray Francisco de Aguilar, a Dominican who had previously fought as a soldier at the siege of Tenochtitlan; Aguilar later joined the order and imparted to Durán a considerable amount of information about the Aztecs at first contact. Durán frequently cites Aguilar in his History.

Converse relation denotes the transpose of a relation and is analogous to the notation used for inverse functions. While not every relation possesses an inverse in the sense of a function, each relation has a unique converse obtained by reversing the order of its ordered pairs. The converse is a unary operation that is an involution, since applying it twice returns the original relation. This operation endows the set of binary relations on a given set with a semigroup structure equipped with involution, and more broadly it endows the category of relations with the structure of a dagger category. In the calculus of relations, the converse commutes with the standard operations of union, intersection, and complement.

In mathematics, the converse (or inverse) of a relation R ⊆ X×Y is the relation R^−1 = { (y, x) | (x, y) ∈ R }. When R is the graph of a function f: X → Y, its converse is a relation from Y to X; the function f is invertible if and only if this converse relation is itself a function, in which case it serves as the inverse function f^−1: Y → X. Conversely, if the converse is not a function, the original function is not invertible, since a given y would correspond to multiple x values.

In the early 1950s, the parent corporation withdrew from Whitchurch and Hurn, prompting a reorganization of Airways Flying Club operations. Because Denham was too small to accommodate the club, its flying base was transferred to Croydon Airport. For the remainder of the decade, the club ran pilot, navigator, and engineer training programmes for BOAC, BEA, the Air Ministry, and Lufthansa. It also played a role in establishing the National Flying Training School at Bremen and helped set up the Baghdad and Kuwait Flying Schools.

Airways Flying Club relocated following the closure of Croydon Airport, moving first to White Waltham Airfield and later to Wycombe Air Park in 1965, which remains its current base. In 1960 the club operated Chipmunk aircraft from Biggin Hill, with examples bearing the registrations G-AOZU and G-AOZV.

The United States Air Force maintains a peacetime organizational framework tasked with organizing, equipping, and training air units for planned operational missions. When called upon to execute actual operations, the Secretary of Defense directs the Secretary of the Air Force to implement a Change in Operational Control, transferring units from their administrative alignment to the operational command of a regional Combatant Command. In practice, units assigned to Air Force Space Command, Air Force Special Operations Command, Pacific Air Forces, and United States Air Forces in Europe are typically employed under their existing Combatant Commanders, remaining under their current regional CCDR. Air Mobility Command forces that provide support retain compositional control under United States Transportation Command unless they are CHOPped to a regional CCDR. This arrangement supports peacetime readiness and provides a mechanism for centralized control during joint operations across theaters.

Within the United States Air Force, cultural and career-related issues have been cited as factors contributing to a shortfall in unmanned aerial vehicle operators. Although demand for UAVs to provide round-the-clock coverage for troops during the Iraq War was high, the service did not establish a dedicated UAV pilot career field until the war's final year. In 2014, the Air Force revised its training syllabus for remotely piloted aircraft in response to substantial training losses and a Government Accountability Office report criticizing how the drone program was managed. Analysts such as Paul Scharre have argued that a cultural divide between the Air Force and the Army has hindered the adoption of each other’s drone-handling innovations.

Dedicated outdoor air systems (DOAS) deliver outdoor air independently of the primary heating and cooling equipment to meet ventilation requirements, while leaving the space-conditioning system to manage temperature and humidity. In VAV installations that follow ASHRAE 62.1-2004 multi-space calculations, the outdoor-air requirement is typically 20–70 percent higher than the amount provided by a DOAS to ensure proper distribution of air within occupied spaces. The process of cooling and dehumidifying the large outdoor-air volumes in summer and humidifying and heating them in winter is energy-intensive. Accordingly, a DOAS is sized to meet the outdoor-air requirements without the need for oversizing.

Dedicated outdoor air systems have been adopted more widely across many countries, reflecting a growing demand for DOAS equipment. In DOAS configurations, a variety of components are employed, including a wheel designed for total energy recovery, a passive dehumidification wheel, and other relevant equipment. The effectiveness of the total energy recovery wheel is considered a key factor in enhancing DOAS efficiency.

Old English nouns are declined across five cases—nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, and instrumental—distinguishing three genders (masculine, feminine, neuter) and two numbers (singular and plural). They are traditionally divided into strong and weak declensions, with the instrumental largely vestigial and used only in masculine and neuter singular forms, frequently replaced by the dative in normal usage. By contrast, pronouns and strong adjectives retain distinct instrumental forms. There is only sparse early evidence for a sixth locative case in Northumbrian sources, with the locative being inferred from Northumbrian Runic inscriptions, such as readings like “on rodi,” interpreted as “on the Cross.”

Following the Christianisation of Anglo-Saxon England in the late seventh century, literacy in Old English expanded through monastic scholarship and ecclesiastical networks. The oldest surviving Old English composition is Cædmon's Hymn, believed to have been composed between 658 and 680 and later preserved in writing during the early eighth century. The surviving runic material from this period is limited, with inscriptions spanning the fifth to seventh centuries; the earliest coherent runic texts appear in the early eighth century, among which the Franks Casket inscriptions are particularly notable. Around the same time, Old English began to be written with the Latin alphabet, which was introduced in the eighth century.

Bernard Waber authored the children's book Courage in the aftermath of the September 11, 2001 attacks. The book is designed to teach young readers about bravery, exploring the concept through a range of characters and situations to illustrate different expressions of courage.

Bernard Waber was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, the son of Henry and Pauline Waber. He initially enrolled in a finance program at the University of Pennsylvania but left to enlist in the military at the outset of World War II. Waber served in the United States Army from 1942 to 1945, attaining the rank of staff sergeant. After the war, he returned to formal studies at the Philadelphia College of Art, where he completed his degree in 1951.

During the Protestant Reformation, secular authorities began to assume responsibility for recording marriages and for establishing the rules governing them, diminishing the church's exclusive jurisdiction over matrimony. This transition reflected Martin Luther's view that marriage is a worldly, secular concern rather than a mainly religious one. By the 17th century, many Protestant European states had institutionalized state involvement in marriage administration, signaling a shift toward civil oversight of marital matters.

Marriage continues to be associated with various economic practices in many societies, notably dowry arrangements in several countries. Dowry remains a customary expectation in a range of cultures, including Turkey, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Morocco, and Nepal. In India, thousands of dowry-related deaths occur annually, and legislative measures restricting or banning the practice have been enacted. Nepal also moved to outlaw dowry in 2009. Some scholars argue that dowry serves as a marker of social status and a means of signaling or advancing one's position within the social hierarchy.

During the Gulf War, Iraqi accounts claimed an air-to-air success against a B-52G, alleging that Khudai Hijab, a MiG-29 pilot, fired a Vympel R-27R and damaged a B-52 on the conflict’s opening night. The United States Air Force disputed this assertion, arguing that the damage resulted from friendly fire when an AGM-88 HARM homed in on the B-52’s tail gun’s fire-control radar rather than from an Iraqi air-to-air missile. The damaged aircraft was subsequently nicknamed “In Harm’s Way” in reference to the incident. In the wake of the event, General George L. Butler announced the retirement of the tail gunner position on B-52 crews and the permanent deactivation of the gun turrets, effective October 1, 1991.

As of September 8, 2008, four of the eighteen B-52H Stratofortress aircraft based at Barksdale Air Force Base had been retired and transferred to the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group (AMARG) boneyard at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Arizona.

Yu Zhishan was a military figure from Liaoning Province who rose to prominence during the warlord period. In 1923 he commanded the Northwest Army’s 5th Combined Regiment stationed in Shandong, and in 1924 Zhang Zuolin reassigned him to command the 8th Combined Regiment. In June 1927 he was promoted to lieutenant general. He returned to Shandong as commander of the 30th Army and aided Chiang Kai-shek in defeating Yan Xishan in the Central Plains War. His alliance with the Kuomintang was short-lived, and he was recalled to Manchuria to guard against the Northern Expedition. Following Zhang Zuolin’s death in the Huanggutun Incident in 1928, Manchuria descended into chaos; initially he supported Zhang Xueliang, who appointed him commander in chief of the military in the twenty prefectures around Shenyang. After the Mukden Incident in September 1931, he worked with Kan Chaoxi to declare Shenyang independent from the Republic of China, and subsequently cooperated with the Imperial Japanese Army on the Self-Government Guiding Board to establish Manchukuo.

Yu Zhishan held a sequence of senior security and political roles within Manchukuo during the 1930s. In March 1932 he was appointed chief of police for Fengtian Province in Manchukuo. He advanced to the position of Army Minister in the Manchukuo Cabinet in May 1934, and shortly thereafter, in July 1934, was named commander-in-chief of the First Army of the Manchukuo Imperial Army. In July 1937 the Army Ministry was renamed the Ministry of Public Security and assumed control over all policing functions. Following his tenure as a cabinet minister, he was appointed to the Privy Council in April 1939.

The Nazi salute, also referred to as the Hitler salute or Sieg Heil salute, functioned as a formal greeting in Nazi Germany. The gesture involves raising and extending the right arm forward at an upward angle, with a straightened hand, fingers together, and the palm oriented downward. It was typically performed as a public acknowledgment of allegiance within the regime. The act was commonly accompanied by vocal exclamations such as "Heil Hitler!", "Heil, mein Führer!", or "Sieg Heil!".

Following the Battle of Berlin, a number of American soldiers performed the Nazi salute as a gesture of mockery toward Adolf Hitler. They frequently parodied Hitler's distinctive hair and moustache, employing exaggerated imitations of his style as part of their derision.

Peter Cetera was assaulted in 1969 at Dodger Stadium during a baseball game he attended with his bandmates. The four-assailant attack was carried out by Marines who reportedly targeted him for his appearance as a long-haired rock musician who supported the Chicago Cubs. Cetera sustained a broken jaw and required two days of intensive care, with his jaw being wired shut for several months during the ensuing recovery.

Will Lee, a bass player, has stated that Peter Cetera influenced his own approach to playing. Lee described Cetera's style as a relaxed, McCartney-inspired sensibility blended with Chicago funk, and he emphasized the tasteful, melodious quality of Cetera's playing.

Mindoro is predominantly Christian, while the island’s indigenous Mangyan communities traditionally practice animism. The Catholic Church is active in parts of Mindoro, reflecting its historical influence in the region. In addition to Catholicism, other religious groups present on the island include Iglesia ni Cristo, the Philippine Independent Church, and the Baptist Church.

Mindoro was administered as a single province from 1920 to 1950, with Calapan serving as its provincial capital; after the Philippines achieved independence from the United States in 1946, the province remained intact until a 1950 referendum led to its division into two separate provinces, Occidental Mindoro and Oriental Mindoro.

Downtown Transit Center is an intermodal transit facility located in downtown Houston, Texas. It is operated by METRO, the Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County. The center serves the Red Line of METRORail and 19 bus routes, and it stands as the southernmost Red Line station within Downtown Houston. It also provides access to METRO’s headquarters, the Lee P. Brown Administration Building.

In 1993, METRO began evaluating locations for a $17 million downtown bus transit facility intended to reduce bus traffic along Main Street and accommodate a higher volume of downtown buses in line with the Regional Bus Plan. Local business interests favored a site south of the Pierce Elevated (I-45) to minimize disruption to pedestrian corridors, while churches and condominium residents opposed the plan over concerns about noise and vibration. METRO ultimately chose a site just north of the Pierce Elevated, presenting it as a compromise. The facility was planned to open in 1999.

Balneolales is a bacterial taxon whose current taxonomy is based on two principal reference resources, the List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature (LPSN) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). LPSN provides the formal nomenclature and standing for prokaryotic names, while NCBI maintains a comprehensive taxonomy database that supports the hierarchical organization of prokaryotes and links to associated genetic data. Consequently, these sources are used to establish the accepted classification of Balneolales and to convey its position within the bacterial taxonomy.

Ixodes pacificus is a tick species involved in the transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi to humans. For infection to occur, the tick must be attached for about 36–48 hours. Nymphs of Ixodes pacificus are approximately 2 mm in size and often go unnoticed on human hosts, a diminutive size that allows them to stay attached longer. Consequently, the nymphal stage is primarily responsible for transmitting Borrelia burgdorferi.

Ixodes pacificus, commonly known as the western black-legged tick, is a vector of Lyme disease caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi. Transmission of the pathogen generally occurs during a subsequent blood meal after the tick has fed on an infected host, enabling spirochetes to be transmitted to a new host. The majority of transmission events are attributable to the nymphal stage, with adult female ticks contributing in some cases. Nymphs primarily feed on small animals and humans in the spring and early summer, while adults are most active in winter and seek hosts from late autumn through spring.

In the United Kingdom, a hamlet denotes a very small rural settlement that is smaller than a village. By contrast, in Bavaria and Austria the local term Weiler is defined as a settlement consisting of three to nine dwellings, with settlements of ten houses classified as villages. Germany, moreover, has no general statutory definition of Weiler. These regional classifications illustrate how terms for small settlements vary across languages and legal contexts.

In eighteenth-century landscape design, affluent aristocrats and monarchs established hameaux within their gardens as decorative and recreational features. A hameau denotes a compact cluster of rustic yet comfortable residences or farm buildings arranged to evoke a simplified rural village. Notable instances include the Hameau de la Reine at the Palace of Versailles, constructed under the direction of Queen Marie-Antoinette, and the Hameau de Chantilly in Chantilly, Oise, built for Louis Joseph, Prince of Condé.

VMessage is a framework that specifies how personal information may be transferred between mobile devices. The standard encompasses several data categories, including business cards, calendar appointments, and notes, outlining the procedures for exchanging this information across devices.

VMessage is a messaging standard developed by the Infrared Data Association (IrDA) for exchanging short messages over infrared connections. The specification is contained within IrDA's Infrared Mobile Communications (IrMC) version 1.1 suite, which outlines the format and transmission methods for vMessages between compatible devices. For file transfer, vMessage data are typically identified by the .vmg file extension.

A real function is a real-valued function of a real variable. Its codomain is the field of real numbers, typically denoted by R. The domain is a subset of the real numbers that contains an interval, ensuring that the function is defined on a nonempty portion of the real line. In this section, these objects are simply referred to as functions.

Multivariate (multivariable) functions are those that take more than one input parameter and yield a single output value. They are routinely encountered across mathematics and its applications, where several quantities interact to determine an outcome. For instance, the position of a car along a road can be expressed as a function of two inputs: the elapsed time and the vehicle's average speed, with the resulting position derived from these factors.

Screw-pile foundations were employed to support lighthouses on sandy or muddy seabeds, using metal screwpiles that were driven into the substrate. At the end of each pile, a helicoidal cast-iron flange could be augured into the bottom to boost bearing capacity and provide anchorage. Such installations were, however, vulnerable to ice floes. In the Florida Keys, where the seabed consists of soft coral rock, diskpile foundations were constructed instead. Wrought iron piles were driven through a cast-iron or semi-steel disk resting on the seabed, with a pile shoulder preventing further penetration and the disk distributing the weight more evenly. In coral reef areas with sandy substrates, a cast-steel screw at the pile end was used to increase anchorage. Cofferdams were employed in shallow waters to build foundations under dry conditions by pumping water out of the enclosure to expose the bed.

Screw-pile lighthouses are a type of coastal beacon that derive stability from helically threaded piles driven into soft seabed, enabling construction on mud, sand, or swamp. By contrast, non-screw-pile (straight-pile) tubular skeletal lighthouses were built onshore and offshore using cast-iron or wrought-iron piles in similarly soft bottoms. The screw-pile concept was developed by Alexander Mitchell, whose invention marked a major improvement over the traditional straight-pile methods. Mitchell and his son patented the wrought-iron screw-pile design in England in 1833. An early application of the approach was Walde Lighthouse in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France, established in 1859 and based on Mitchell's screw-pile design. Walde Lighthouse was discontinued in 1998 and its lantern removed, and it remains the only surviving screw-pile lighthouse in France.

During the Slovenian presidential run-off, Nataša Pirc Musar, standing as an independent, was widely regarded as the likely victor from August 2022. Her challenger, Anže Logar, also ran without a formal party banner, but he was a member of the Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS), the party led by former prime minister Janez Janša, which had suffered a defeat in the parliamentary elections six months earlier. This connection placed Logar in the political orbit associated with Janša. Janša, for his part, faced accusations during his time in office that he sought to curb freedom of expression and to undermine the independence of the judiciary.

During the first round of Slovenia's presidential elections, Anže Logar won about 34% of the vote, while Nataša Pirc Musar trailed with 27%, with Milan Brglez finishing third at around 15%. In the second round, Golob endorsed Pirc Musar.

In August 2019, media reports alleged that broadcaster Michael Buerk proposed that obese individuals should be allowed to die early in order to save NHS money. In a Radio Times article, he suggested that obesity-related deaths could benefit society. He framed such a stance as a selfless sacrifice in the fight against demographic imbalance, overpopulation, and climate change.

In 2016, Michael Buerk voiced criticism of Emma Thompson, Benedict Cumberbatch, and other celebrities commonly associated with liberal views. The remarks were made in an interview with Ross Kemp. He argued that celebrities visiting people in desperate situations to parade their sympathy often promote simplistic, impractical ideas about what should be done, and he suggested there is a limit to how much of what he characterized as the Emma Thompson–Benedict Cumberbatch worldview one can tolerate.

Transfast is a financial services company that provides cross-border payments in multiple currencies for both individuals and business clients around the world. Remittances are processed through a wholly owned direct-to-bank network, enabling transfers to recipient bank accounts. In addition, the company offers access to a network of approximately 200,000 cash payout points across 120 countries, facilitating cash pickups for recipients.

Transfast, established in 1988 as Trans-Fast, operated primarily in the market for remittance transfers from the United States to Latin America. In 2007 the company secured private-equity investment from Greenhill Capital Partners, LLC, and subsequently adopted the name Transfast Remittance LLC.

Miss Universe Australia 2017 was the thirteenth edition of the national pageant, held on 29 June 2017 at the Sofitel Melbourne on Collins in Melbourne, with thirty-two contestants representing various Australian states. The competition concluded with the reigning Miss Universe Australia Caris Tiivel of Western Australia crowning Olivia Molly Rogers of South Australia as her successor, Rogers sometimes being listed as Olivia Rogers in some sources. Rogers went on to represent Australia at Miss Universe 2017.

Durius, sometimes identified as Durio, was a deity worshiped by the ancient Lusitanians and Celtiberians inhabiting the Iberian Peninsula. He represents the Douro River and is typically depicted in art with a fishing net in hand. A shrine dedicated to him stood near Porto during the Roman period.

Wanhua railway station is organized into two buildings, a west building and an east building. The western structure houses the main entrance, the lobby (concourse), and the ticket counters, while the eastern structure contains the exit, the parcel center, and offices. The station offers two platforms—a central island platform and a side platform—both located underground.
Wanhua railway station, located in the Wanhua District of Taipei, Taiwan, is served by the Taiwan Railways Administration. The station’s Chinese name is 萬華車站, romanized as Wànhuá Chēzhàn.

Oreocryptophis porphyracea primarily feeds on rodents and other small mammals in the wild, with amphibians such as frogs documented as occasional prey. In captivity, the species readily accepts mice as prey, reflecting a preference for mammalian food items under human care.

Oreocryptophis porphyracea is a terrestrial snake in the rat snake lineage, notable for its small, angular head. Its coloration features red or orange tones contrasted by black bands or stripes. The species is adapted to cool environments and is primarily found in upland habitats, being restricted to hills and mountain plateaus. It exhibits crepuscular activity, being active from late evening into the night and again from dawn to late morning. In captivity, it is regarded as one of the more sought-after rat snakes.

In 1688, James II ordered that the Declaration of Indulgence be read from the pulpits of every Anglican church, a move that alienated Anglican bishops who served as the Church’s leading authorities. While the Declaration pleased some beneficiaries of greater religious tolerance, it compelled the Established Church to erode some of its privileges. Concurrently, James sought to reduce the Anglican monopoly over education. At Oxford, he permitted Roman Catholics to occupy important positions in Christ Church and in University College. He also sought to override College governance by pressuring the Fellows of Magdalen College to elect Anthony Farmer as President, a candidate regarded as Catholic and of ill repute, thereby infringing the Fellows’ right to elect their own leader.
