James II lived in exile at the royal château of Saint-Germain-en-Laye in France, under the protection of Louis XIV, with his wife Mary of Modena and a number of supporters who accompanied him, including the Earl of Melfort; the group was predominantly Roman Catholic, though not exclusively so. In 1692, he and Mary welcomed their last child, Louisa Maria Teresa, a birth that occurred during their years in exile. In 1696, a faction of English adherents plotted to assassinate William III in an effort to restore James to the throne; the conspiracy failed and the subsequent backlash weakened James’s political support. That same year Louis XIV offered to have James elected King of Poland, a prospect James declined in order to avoid potential disqualification from the English throne in the eyes of his English subjects. After peace between Louis and William in 1697, French backing for James waned substantially.

In 1965, the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation aired a 140-minute dramatic feature titled If This Is a Man. The program was adapted for radio by George Whalley from Stuart Woolf's translation, and the broadcast was produced by John Reeves. Reeves has written about the radio production.

During a routine meal collection, Levi and a young Alsatian prisoner named Jean fetch the soup for the day. Levi then attempts to recall a passage from Dante’s Inferno—the final speech attributed to Ulysses. The lines, though imperfect, convey a sense of dignity and human striving that momentarily lifts Levi above the camp's brutal, dehumanizing atmosphere. Jean listens closely, suggesting a shared understanding between them. The moment yields unusual intellectual and emotional clarity, a rediscovery of culture and self-worth amid brutality. Although Levi forgets four triplets, the emotional resonance remains, and for a moment he is a man again.

The Applegate Trail was created to provide settlers with an overland alternative to rafting down the Columbia River. It followed the path of the California Trail into north-central Nevada, then headed northwest into northern California and continued toward present-day Ashland, Oregon. From Ashland, travelers proceeded north along the Siskiyou Trail into the Willamette Valley, forming part of the broader network of routes associated with the Cascade Range.

The Cascade Range lies near the Pacific Ocean and is shaped by moist westerly winds that deliver substantial precipitation, especially on the western slopes through orographic lifting. Some parts of the range receive exceptionally heavy snowfall, with annual totals reaching around 1,000 inches (2,500 cm) in certain locales, and Mount Baker’s 1998–99 season established the national single-season snowfall record at 1,140 inches (2,900 cm). Prior to that, Paradise on Mount Rainier held the American snow-accumulation record in 1978. Numerous sites exceed 500 inches (1,300 cm) of snow per year, including Lake Helen near Lassen Peak. The High Cascades are snow- and ice-covered throughout the year. Vegetation diverges between the western and eastern slopes: the western side is densely forested with species such as Douglas-fir, western hemlock, and red alder, whereas the eastern flank is drier and dominated by ponderosa pine, with western larch, mountain hemlock, subalpine fir, and subalpine larch appearing at higher elevations. In the eastern foothills, annual rainfall can be as low as about 9 inches (230 mm) due to a rain shadow.

In 1952, James Mason bought a house that had previously been owned by Buster Keaton. There, he found nitrate film reels of Keaton's work, some of which were believed to be lost, including The Boat (1921). Recognizing their deteriorating condition, Mason arranged for the films to be transferred to safety stock to preserve them.

James Mason began to appear regularly on television across a range of series, including Panic!, General Electric Theater, Schlitz Playhouse, Goodyear Theatre, and Playhouse 90, with several appearances on the latter that featured the episode John Brown's Raid. He then starred in two thrillers directed by Andrew L. Stone, Cry Terror! and The Decks Ran Red, both released in 1958. In Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest (1959), Mason portrayed a suave master spy pursuing Cary Grant, with romantic assistance provided by Eva Marie Saint.

Bornholm is renowned for displaying geological formations in a manner not common in Denmark, with the island exposing a varied geological record across its coastal and inland landscapes. In Knudsker parish, to the east of central Rønne, the Stubbeløkken and Klippeløkken granite quarries continue to operate and are among the few remaining active quarries in the area. The island's diverse topography and seascapes draw visitors to locations ranging from the Hammeren promontory in the northwest through the central Almindingen forest to the Dueodde beaches in the southeast. Notable points of geological interest include the rocky sea cliffs at Jons Kapel and Helligdomsklipperne, the distinctive topography of Paradisbakkerne, and the rift valleys Ekkodalen and Døndalen. In paleontology, Bornholm preserves Furongian (late Cambrian) sediments of the Alum Shale Formation represented by six superzones, with fossils distinguishing three agnostoid and fourteen trilobite zones. A total of 8502 fossils have been recovered from these strata, predominantly disarticulated sclerites, including described genera such as Ctenopyge, Eurycare, Leptoplastus, Olenus, Parabolina, Peltura, Protopeltura, Sphaerophthalmus, Lotagnostus and Triangulopyge.

Musical nationalism is often associated with Giuseppe Verdi, whose body of work came to symbolize Italian national identity during the 19th century. In Verdi's Nabucco, a famous chorus expresses patriotic feeling for a homeland that is beautiful yet lost, illustrating how operatic music could evoke national sentiment. During the Risorgimento, the cry Viva VERDI circulated as a public expression of support for Italian unification; the phrase is commonly read as an acronym for Viva Vittorio Emanuele Re d'Italia, underscoring loyalty to Victor Emmanuel II, the reigning king. Through these associations, Verdi's music is understood to have contributed to nationalist feeling by linking art with political aspirations and the broader project of unification.

Zacharia Paliashvili (1871–1933) was a foundational figure in Georgian classical music and a leading proponent of musical nationalism in the country. He advanced a distinctly Georgian idiom by integrating traditional folk melodies with the Romantic aesthetics of the 19th century, shaping a national repertoire that reflected local identity. As the founder of the Georgian Philharmonic Society and later the head of the Tbilisi State Conservatoire, he played a central role in developing Georgia’s musical institutions and education. His compositions are regarded as providing the basis for the Georgian National Anthem, illustrating the enduring impact of his work on the nation’s cultural and symbolic life.

Bent entrances, defined as passages that bend or turn, are relatively uncommon in European castles, where entry routes tend to run straight; Crac provides an example of a bent layout, but such configurations remain atypical in Europe. Harlech Castle, by contrast, features a long gate passage with multiple doors and murder-holes yet contains no actual turns, illustrating that complexity did not often accompany curved routes. Scholar Cathcart King contends that indirect or bent entrances were less widespread in Europe than in Crusader states. He attributes this disparity to practical considerations of transport in Europe, where carts pulled by draft animals made twisting corridors impractical, whereas in the East, the use of camels would have facilitated navigation of winding passages.

A bent entrance is a defensive architectural feature found in medieval fortifications. The gate passage is narrow and curves sharply, creating a constricted approach that slows attackers and impedes the use of battering rams. It is often paired with active defense measures, such as machicolations, to confine intruders to a narrow killing zone at the gateway. The defensive function of a bent entrance is related to the barbican situated in front of the gate, which reinforces the barrier by prolonging and complicating the assault.

Ellen J. Kullman (born January 22, 1956) is an American business executive who has served as chief executive officer of Carbon since November 2019. She previously held the roles of chair and chief executive officer of E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company (DuPont) in Wilmington, Delaware, a position from which she retired on October 16, 2015. Kullman has also served as a director of General Motors. In 2014, Forbes ranked her 31st among the 100 Most Powerful Women.

Ellen J. Kullman announced her retirement from DuPont on October 5, 2015, with the retirement taking effect on October 16, 2015, following a dispute with activist investor Nelson Peltz and his firm Trian Fund Management, which sought four seats on DuPont's board and argued that the company needed to cut costs and meet its financial targets. Peltz had previously failed to secure a shareholder vote earlier in the year.

In 1926, Ferdinand Rieser, a Zurich wine wholesaler and theatre director, acquired the building and oversaw its renovation to improve its use as a performing venue. In 1938, the property was leased to Neue Schauspiel AG, a company established by the city of Zurich to rescue the theatre from financial difficulties. When the lease expired in 1952, the citizens of Zurich declined to purchase the building for 3 million Swiss francs. Subsequently, UBS AG purchased the structure and arranged a new lease with Neue Schauspiel AG.

Following the rise of the Nazi regime in 1933, a significant number of prominent actors and directors fled Germany and Austria, seeking refuge in Switzerland. The arrival of these émigré artists helped Schauspielhaus Zürich achieve considerable artistic vitality and renown. The theatre staged numerous anti-fascist productions, including the world premieres of several Bertolt Brecht plays. During this period, Schauspielhaus Zürich was regarded as the largest free stage in the German-speaking world, at a time when theatres in Germany and Austria were subject to strict regulation.

The song’s concept originated from a friend of Scott Kirkland who was using ecstasy at the time. This friend left voice mail messages for Kirkland in which he expressed a desire for Kirkland to experience the same kind of trip.

Flake morphology provides insight into the percussion technology used during lithic reduction. Pronounced bulbs of force signal hard hammer percussion, typically from a hammerstone, and the resulting flakes are commonly described as conchoidal. Hard-hammer flaking is generally associated with initial reduction stages, including core reduction and the rough shaping of blanks or preforms. By contrast, softer percussors such as bone, wood, or antler produce more moderate and diffuse bulbs of percussion, yielding bending flakes that are often linked to bifacial thinning and trimming. The relative frequency of hard- and soft-hammer flakes at a site or surface helps reconstruct the dominant lithic activities and tempo of production at that place and period.

A lithic flake is a detached fragment generated during lithic reduction when a piece is removed from a core by a detachment blow or applied pressure. The proximal aspect features a striking platform, the surface where the force is delivered, which may be a natural facet of the core or a surface that has been deliberately prepared. The distal end, or termination, describes how the flake separates from the core and can be categorized into several commonly observed styles: feathered, hinged, stepped, and plunging (also known as overshot or outrepassé). Feathered terminations yield a very sharp edge, with the flake thinning gradually as the applied force exits the core. Hinged terminations arise when the force is deflected and rolls away from the core, leaving a rounded distal edge. Stepped terminations occur if the flake breaks during removal, often producing a squared distal end. Plunging terminations involve the force returning toward the core, sometimes removing material from the ventral side. Abrupt terminations encompass hinge, step, and plunging types and may be deliberate in some instances but are more commonly the result of errors, signaling internal core flaws or prior Hertzian cones. Eraillures, or bulbar scars, are small flake scars on the bulbs of applied force, and their origin remains not fully understood. When eraillures are present, they are relatively uncommon, with very few flakes bearing more than one such scar.

In October 2019, Vladimir Putin visited the United Arab Emirates, where six accords were signed with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Zayed (MBZ). One of these agreements provided for joint investments between Russia's sovereign wealth fund and Mubadala. The package of deals, valued at more than $1.3 billion, spanned the energy, health, and advanced technology sectors. On October 22, 2021, during a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, Putin described the relationship between Russia and Israel as distinctive, highlighting their bilateral ties.

Vladimir Putin has described climate change as a troubling reality with significant consequences for Russia, while acknowledging uncertainty about whether the phenomenon is predominantly anthropogenic. He has outlined Russia's strategy to reduce man-made emissions through forest preservation and a category he terms low-emission energy, which he defines as national natural gas, nuclear energy, and hydroelectric power. He has also urged affluent nations to provide financial assistance and technology to developing countries to help them achieve lower emissions. Some observers have labeled his approach as a mimicry of climate policy, arguing that environmental concerns are employed as a means of extending political influence.

Porcini (Boletus edulis) frequently co-occurs with Amanita muscaria or Amanita rubescens, a pattern that is likely driven by shared growing seasons, habitat preferences, and ecological requirements rather than a direct biological interaction between species. A reported association between Boletus edulis and Amanita excelsa on Pinus radiata ectomycorrhizae in New Zealand has been cited as evidence that other fungal partners may influence the porcini life cycle. A field study conducted in 2007 found little correlation between fruit body abundance and the presence of underground mycelia, even directly beneath the mushroom, suggesting that the triggers for mycorrhiza formation and fruiting are more complex than mycelial presence alone.

Porcini mushrooms are sold fresh in Europe and Russia during the summer and autumn, with dried or canned forms prepared for worldwide distribution at other times. They are eaten in a variety of ways, including raw, sautéed with butter, ground into pasta, and used in soups and numerous other dishes. In French cuisine they appear in preparations such as cèpes à la Bordelaise, cèpe frits, and cèpe aux tomates. Porcini risotto is a traditional autumn dish in Italy. The fungi figure in many culinary traditions, including Provençal and Viennese cuisines. In Thailand, they are used in soups and blanched in salads. For storage, porcini can be frozen either raw or after cooking in butter, though their color, aroma, and taste deteriorate after about four months; blanching (or soaking and blanching) before freezing can extend freezer life to around twelve months. They are also among the few mushroom species sold commercially in pickled form.

Tianhe District, a central district of Guangzhou, China, contains several emblematic landmarks that symbolize the city’s contemporary development, including Citic Plaza, the Guangzhou International Finance Center, the Guangzhou Opera House, and the Guangdong Museum. The district has hosted major sporting events, notably the 6th and 9th National Games of the People's Republic of China, as well as the 2010 Asian Games held in Guangzhou.

Pearl River Tower, located in Zhujiang New Town within Tianhe District of Guangzhou, is a prominent skyscraper noted for being the first zero-energy building in China. The structure is owned by China Tobacco.

Alfred Stieglitz photographed Georgia O'Keeffe's body extensively, including studies of her hands and her nude torso. The image Torso depicts her nude torso from a vantage below, with the arms partially visible and the head not shown within the frame. The composition emphasizes uplifted arms and defined thighs, imparting a sculptural presence to the figure. This sculptural quality reflects the influence of Auguste Rodin, whose work Stieglitz knew well and was exhibited by the Photo-Secession.

Georgia O'Keeffe – Torso is a photograph by Alfred Stieglitz of the artist Georgia O'Keeffe. A print from the work was sold at Sotheby's in New York on February 14, 2006, for $1.36 million, the second-highest price ever paid for a photograph by Stieglitz.

Daniel Akaka's college education was supported by the G.I. Bill. He earned a Bachelor of Education in 1952 from the University of Hawaiʻi and later completed a Master of Education in 1966 at the same university.

Daniel Kahikina Akaka (September 11, 1924 – April 6, 2018) was an American educator and politician who served as a United States Senator from Hawaii from 1990 to 2013. A member of the Democratic Party, his Senate tenure spanned more than two decades, during which he represented Hawaii at the federal level.

Forever 21 plans to relaunch as an online-only retailer in September 2025. The United States e-commerce platform and the men's wholesale segment will be operated by Unique Brands, a company that also owns Bon-Ton, which has shifted to a digital-only presence. Women's wholesale will be run by Mark Edwards Apparel, while Kidz Concepts will oversee the children's wear division. Under these arrangements, no American physical stores will be opened as part of the relaunch.

Forever 21, a fashion retailer, experienced several notable legal and public relations matters in the early 2010s. In April 2010, activist Rachel Kane launched WTForever21.com to catalog Forever 21 items, and the site gained traction after a Jezebel feature, with Forever 21 subsequently demanding its removal or facing potential litigation in June 2011. In 2011 the company reported assets of about $1.4 billion and profits around $124 million, and a Center for Environmental Health investigation named Forever 21 among 25 retailers and suppliers selling cadmium‑containing jewelry, culminating in a settlement of roughly $1.03 million and an agreement to cap cadmium content at 0.03 percent in jewelry. The same year also saw criticism of Forever 21’s T‑shirt designs, some deemed anti‑education or sexist; the company withdrew the shirts after stating that the intent was not to discredit education, according to ABC News. In September 2012 a class action was filed over a return refund that was one cent short of the original purchase price, with reports noting that meeting the $15,000 damages threshold would require about 750,000 additional plaintiffs, and Forever 21 declined to comment while litigation remained pending.

Noise shaping in digital audio is frequently realized through delta-sigma modulation. Direct Stream Digital (DSD) employs this modulation approach as part of its encoding scheme, using a 1-bit audio representation together with a 64× oversampling rate. The theoretical signal-to-noise ratio at audible frequencies for DSD is about 120 dB, indicating a very high potential dynamic range.

Resolution in digital audio is largely determined by the precision of PCM samples, and most audio formats and digital audio workstations encode these samples in floating-point form. WAV and AIFF are containers that support floating-point PCM representations. Floating-point numbers differ from integers in that they are organized as separate fields rather than a single fixed bit pattern. The most widely used standard for such representations is IEEE 754. Under IEEE 754, a number is described by three components: a sign bit, a mantissa, and an exponent. The exponent establishes the magnitude by applying a power-of-two scaling to the mantissa, which is expressed as a binary fraction in base-two floating-point formats.

BRAC 2005 was the fifth base realignment and closure process undertaken since 1988. On May 13, 2005, the Department of Defense released a preliminary list outlining plans to close 22 major U.S. military installations and realign 33 others through expansion or reduction of their activities. President George W. Bush endorsed the BRAC recommendations on September 15, 2005, with Congress limited to blocking them through a joint resolution of disapproval within 45 days. On September 23, 2005, Representative Ray LaHood introduced H.J.Res. 65 in the House, while no parallel measure appeared in the Senate. The House subsequently debated the resolution on October 26, 2005, and it failed by a vote of 324–85, thereby implementing the BRAC recommendations. The plan's implementation was scheduled to begin by September 15, 2007, and to be completed by September 15, 2011.

According to an archived source from the Wayback Machine dated January 29, 2010, the Army Human Resource Command (HRC), which had been based in Missouri, was relocating to the Fort Knox Military Installation in Kentucky.

Youyi County is a county situated in eastern Heilongjiang province in the northeastern part of the People's Republic of China. It is administered as a subdivision of the prefecture-level city of Shuangyashan. The county's name appears in Simplified Chinese as 友谊县 and in Traditional Chinese as 友誼縣, with the pinyin transcription Yǒuyì Xiàn, and it translates to "friendship."

The Johan Cruyff Arena serves as Ajax's home stadium for Eredivisie and European matches. Its opening match took place on 14 August 1996, a friendly between Ajax and AC Milan that ended with a 3–0 victory for Milan. The first goal ever scored in the stadium was by Dejan Savićević of AC Milan, while Ajax claimed their initial goal in the venue with a strike from Kiki Musampa. The first official competitive game hosted there occurred on 21 August 1996, when Ajax faced NAC Breda.

Johan Cruyff Arena features a retractable roof and a natural grass pitch. In 2022 the football match capacity was increased to 55,865, up from 54,990. For concerts, capacities depend on configuration: up to 68,000 spectators with a center-stage arrangement placing the stage at midfield, up to 50,000 for end-stage setups, and 35,000 when the stage is on the eastern side. The venue previously held UEFA five-star stadium status, a designation later superseded by a revised classification system.

Cooling is a fundamental method of food preservation that slows the growth and reproduction of microorganisms and reduces the activity of enzymes that cause spoilage, thereby extending the period during which foods remain safe to eat. The widespread adoption of both domestic and commercial refrigeration significantly improved diets in the Western world by enabling perishable items to be kept for longer periods without compromising safety or quality. Refrigeration facilitates the storage of a variety of foods, including fresh fruit, salads, and dairy products, and helps maintain their texture, flavor, and nutritional value over extended times. The benefits of cooling are particularly pronounced in warm weather, when higher temperatures can accelerate spoilage and microbial growth.

Pasteurization is a method of preserving liquid foods that was originally developed to prevent the souring of locally produced wines, but is now primarily applied to dairy products. In the process, milk is heated to approximately 70 °C (158 °F) for 15 to 30 seconds to destroy bacteria, then rapidly cooled to around 10 °C (50 °F) to inhibit remaining microorganisms from multiplying. The treated milk is stored in sterilized bottles or pouches and kept in cold environments to maintain safety and extend shelf life. The technique was introduced by French chemist Louis Pasteur in 1862.

Within Thailand, minority populations include Khmer and other Mon–Khmer groups, which together comprise about six percent of the population. Thai Malays native to the southern region account for roughly three percent. In the northern provinces, hill-tribe communities such as the Hmong and Mien, the Karen, and other smaller hill tribes collectively exceed one percent.

The term hill tribe (chao khao) began appearing in official Thai documents in the 1960s. It embodies a historic hill-and-valley dichotomy grounded in long-standing social relations in northern and western Thailand, as well as in adjacent areas such as Sipsongpanna and northern Vietnam. Historically, the Dai, Tai, and Thai groups occupied the more fertile intermontane basins and valleys, while less powerful groups resided in higher elevations. This dichotomy was frequently accompanied by master–serf relationships. Today, vestiges of these patterns persist in education outcomes, with roughly 30 percent of ethnic minority children in Thailand unable to read by the end of the second grade, compared with about 1 percent in Bangkok.

Athenae (Pontus) is described by Arrian as an abandoned fortress, while Procopius portrays it as a thriving settlement in his era. In scholarly tradition, Konrad Mannert identifies Athenae with the Odeinus (also rendered Odeinius) named in the Periplus of Pseudo-Scylax, presenting a hypothesized link between the Pontic site and the historical itinerary's geographic nomenclature.

Athenae (Pontus) was a city and port in ancient Pontus. It housed a Greek temple dedicated to Athena. Arrian records its location as 180 stadia east of the river Adienus and 280 stadia west of Apsarus. Procopius offers an alternative account of the toponym, deriving the name from a woman named Athenaea who ruled the land rather than from colonists from Athens. He notes that Athenaea's tomb remained at the site.

The Ph.D. in Demography at the Office of Population Research enrolls a relatively small cohort of graduate students. Applicants typically demonstrate a strong interest in population research and possess a solid quantitative background, with training in statistics and mathematics. The program offers flexibility by allowing students to concentrate in up to two areas, enabling interdisciplinary specialization within the field.

The Office of Population Research at Princeton University coordinates graduate study and research in population science. Doctoral candidates from other departments at Princeton may pursue a specialization in Population, reflecting the program’s interdisciplinary reach. The majority of students pursuing the specialization are affiliated with the Economics or Sociology departments, while a notable minority originate in History or Politics.

Mark Takai was elected to the Hawaii House of Representatives in 1994, representing the 34th district, which includes Pearl City near Pearl Harbor. He was reelected eight times before transitioning to the 33rd district (Aiea) in 2012. Takai chaired the House Committee on Culture and the Arts from 1997 to 2000 and served as vice chair of the House Committee on Higher Education from 1995 to 2002, later holding the chairmanship in 2003–2004. He also chaired the House Committee on Veterans, Military, and International Affairs, as well as Culture and the Arts. Additionally, he served as Vice Speaker of the Hawaii House during the 2005 and 2006 sessions.

E.G. Records, an artist management company and independent record label active primarily in the 1970s and 1980s, was acquired by Virgin Records in the late 1980s after the owners’ investments faltered and financial difficulties followed. Virgin briefly renamed the operation Virgin EG Records, but the imprint was dissolved following EMI’s acquisition of Virgin’s parent company. In a separate dispute, Robert Fripp and his band King Crimson engaged in a lengthy legal battle with E.G., which led to Fripp taking the band’s and his solo catalogs to form Discipline Global Mobile (DGM). For a time, DGM releases were licensed to Virgin for catalog reissues before the label eventually became fully independent.

Virgin Records Canada Inc. was established in 1983 as an independent company, occurring three years before a comparable expansion in the United States in 1986. The Canadian operation adopted distinctive label designs not seen in other territories from that period onward. Between 1983 and 1985, releases used a red label with five horizontal bars at the top and an oversized “scrawl” logo; from 1985 to 1992, the label changed to a purple design featuring a round logo. In 1992, Virgin was acquired on an international level, marking a major change in the brand's global corporate structure.

The USS Edward Rutledge (AP-52), later redesignated APA-24, was an Edward Rutledge-class troop transport (AP) acquired by the United States Navy for World War II use. Its primary role was to transport troops to and from battle areas. On 12 November 1942, during operations in the Mediterranean, the vessel was sunk after being struck by a torpedo from a German submarine in Fedala Bay, Morocco.

On 12 November 1942, the United States Navy transport USS Edward Rutledge (AP-52) was torpedoed by the German submarine U-130, which was commanded by Ernst Kals. The submarine managed to slip past the convoy’s escort screen and sank three transports in the attack. After losing power, the Edward Rutledge attempted to beach herself, but she ultimately sank by the stern, with fifteen men killed.

Warlordism, as Max Weber described classic feudalism in pre-modern Europe, emerges when the state fails to monopolize coercive force, leaving political power distributed among competing warlords. In this arrangement, the monarch depended on the loyalty of knights and the nobility to mobilize private armed retinues for campaigns, effectively outsourcing the use of force. The perspectives of Tocqueville, Hobsbawm, and Skocpol hold that commitment from elites and subjects rested on reciprocal bargains, with crowns granting territory, revenue, status, or privileges in exchange for allegiance and service. Consequently, early European states exhibited weak central authority rather than strong centralized sovereignty. The crown–feudal lord relationship is described as interdependent warlordism, or cooperative warlord politics, underscoring mutual dependence between crown and nobles. This framework is relevant to the Ancien Régime, the French Revolution, and broader democratization in Europe, illustrating how shifts in bargaining power influenced state formation and political change.

Warlordism in Europe developed in contexts where mercenary companies and their leaders acquired de facto political authority within territories, often serving as local rulers in the absence of a strong central government. These chieftains could command private military forces that controlled towns or districts, effectively governing in place of the monarchy or state institutions. The formation of free companies tended to occur when the legitimate central authority collapsed or weakened, creating a vacuum that such leaders could fill. Prominent historical instances include the Great Interregnum in Germany (1254–1278), the fragmentation of royal power in France during the Hundred Years' War after the Battle of Poitiers, and the Kingdom of Scotland's experience during the Wars of Scottish Independence.

A 2020 edited volume entitled The Central Asian Revolt of 1916: A Collapsing Empire in the Age of War and Revolution, edited by A. Morrison, C. Drieu, and A. Chokobaeva, was published by Manchester University Press in Manchester.

B. A. Engel's 1997 article Not by Bread Alone: Subsistence Riots in Russia during World War I is a noted entry in the bibliography on Russia during the war. Published in The Journal of Modern History, volume 69, issue 4, the study runs from pages 696 to 721 and investigates the emergence and characteristics of subsistence riots in Russia amid World War I, focusing on the drivers of mass hunger, price shocks, and public demonstrations and their bearing on wartime governance and social dynamics.

Hotel Widder is a hotel and restaurant in Zurich, Switzerland. Founded in 1995, it is situated on Rennweg in the Niederdorf area of Zurich’s Altstadt (old town) district. The property comprises 49 rooms distributed across nine medieval townhouses, the oldest of which dates back to the 13th century. The name Widder, meaning ram in German, was chosen because one townhouse historically served as the guildhouse for a master butcher.

Hotel Widder is a hotel in Zurich that, in 2003, consisted of eight original townhouses and a total of 42 rooms. It was owned by UBS at that time, which later sold the property to Swiss Life in 2018. The hotel business forms part of The Living Circle group, a Zurich-based organization headquartered on Bleicherweg.

Xiangyang District is a district of Hegang city in Heilongjiang province, China. It forms part of the city's administrative area, and its name is rendered in Simplified Chinese as 向阳区, in Traditional Chinese as 向陽區, with the pinyin transcription Xiàngyáng Qū.

Henry II, like other medieval rulers, drew revenue from a variety of sources during the 12th century. His income combined the proceeds of the royal demesne with funds raised from legal fines, occasional levies, and intermittently collected taxes. In addition, the crown increasingly relied on borrowing to meet its needs, and Henry II expanded this practice beyond that of his predecessors, utilizing a broader network of lenders. Early loans came from moneylenders based in Rouen, with later financing coming from Jewish and Flemish financiers. Ready cash proved essential for paying mercenaries and for financing the construction of stone castles, thereby supporting military campaigns and reinforcing royal power.

Upon his accession in 1154, Henry II inherited a difficult financial situation in England. The royal fiscal system Henry I had established rested on three pillars: a central treasury in London supported by treasuries at key castles, the exchequer as the central accounting and revenue body, and a mobile corps of royal officials known as the chamber who accompanied the king, disbursed funds, and collected revenues. The prolonged civil war disrupted this arrangement, and royal income is estimated to have fallen by roughly 46 percent between 1129–30 and 1155–56. In the broader monetary framework, the postwar stabilization effort included the 1153 introduction of a new coin, the Awbridge silver penny, issued during Stephen’s reign to replace the older currency and restore monetary stability. Financial arrangements in Henry’s continental possessions are less well documented, but Normandy appears to have operated a closely analogous system, and a comparable structure likely existed in Anjou and Aquitaine.

During the Yayoi period, Chinese influence is evident in multiple aspects of material culture and subsistence practices. This influence appears in the production and use of bronze and copper weapons, as well as in ritual artifacts such as dōkyō and dōtaku, which reflect cross-cultural exchange and the emergence of complex ritual or political authority. Agriculturally, irrigated paddy rice cultivation was adopted and expanded, underpinning changes in settlement patterns and social organization. Three major symbols are widely associated with Yayoi culture: the bronze mirror, the bronze sword, and the royal seal stone, which together underscore the period’s technological capabilities and ritual prestige.

In the Yayoi period, the Wei Zhi, a chapter of the Records of the Three Kingdoms, contains the first known reference to Yamataikoku and to Queen Himiko, dating to the 3rd century. Himiko is described as having come to power in Wa as a spiritual ruler after a major civil conflict, while her younger brother administered state affairs, including diplomatic contacts with the Wei court. When Wei envoys asked about the origins of the Wa, the Wa people reportedly claimed descent from Taibo of Wu, a historical figure associated with the Wu Kingdom near the Yangtze Delta. These accounts thus represent among the earliest external testimonies to Wa political organization during the late Yayoi period.

André Maurois married Jeanne-Marie Wanda de Szymkiewicz in 1912, a Polish-Russian aristocrat who studied at Oxford University. The couple had three children. She experienced a serious mental health crisis in 1918 and died of sepsis in 1924. After his father's death, Maurois ceased working in the textile industry. In his 1926 novel Bernard Quesnay, he portrays an alternative life as a textile industrialist, indicating a path he could have pursued.

André Maurois, born Émile Salomon Wilhelm Herzog on 26 July 1885 in Elbeuf, Normandy, was educated at the Lycée Pierre Corneille in Rouen. He came from the Javal family and was the son of Ernest Herzog and Alice Lévy-Rueff, Jewish textile manufacturers. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71, his family fled Alsace and settled in Elbeuf, where they owned a woollen mill; they moved the entire Alsatian workforce to the new plant, and his grandfather was awarded the Legion of Honour for safeguarding a French industry. This industrial background informs aspects of his writing, including the novel Bernard Quesnay, in which a World War I veteran is drawn to directing his grandfather’s textile mills, a portrayal that contains autobiographical elements.

On 8 December, the distribution of Federal Council portfolios for the new term was announced. The four most senior councillors retained their existing departments: Alain Berset remained head of the Federal Department of Home Affairs; Guy Parmelin continued to lead the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research; Ignazio Cassis retained the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs; and Viola Amherd remained in charge of the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. Karin Keller-Sutter was assigned the Federal Department of Finance, taking over from Maurer. The Federal Department of Justice and Police, which Élisabeth Baume-Schneider has led since 2018, was allocated to her for the new term. Albert Rösti assumed the Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications, succeeding Sommaruga. Cassis described the arrangement as consensual, while Greens criticized Rösti’s appointment to the environment portfolio in light of his former role as president of Swiss Oil.

The Green Party considered nominating a candidate for the 2022 Swiss Federal Council election, arguing that its exclusion from the magic formula despite broad popular backing warranted consideration of a bid. They also cited the SVP's alleged flouting of collegiality within the Council as a factor in their deliberations. Ultimately, the Green Party did not field a candidate.

MIPS Technologies presents SmartCE, short for Connected Entertainment, as a reference platform for the connected entertainment sector. The platform brings together Android, the Adobe Flash platform for television, and Skype, and also includes the Home Jinni ConnecTV application along with other applications. By offering these components in a single package, SmartCE is designed to help original equipment manufacturer partners bring integrated products to market more quickly.

MIPS Technologies operated for several years as an independent design house before its 2013 acquisition by Imagination Technologies. In 2017 the company was sold to Tallwood Venture Capital, and the following year it was purchased by Wave Computing. After Wave Computing filed for bankruptcy in 2020, the entity emerged in 2021 under the MIPS name and announced that it would abandon the MIPS architecture in favor of developing RISC-V based designs.

Schlumberger introduced wireline formation testing in the 1950s, and the formation-testing tool was in operation by 1953, employing a shaped-charge mechanism to anchor a rubber pad that expanded in the borehole at the chosen depth. Formation fluids then entered the tool through perforations and tubing into an internal sample chamber, which sealed the sample at formation pressure once filled. The assembled sample could be examined after the tool was retrieved to the surface. In 1956 Schlumberger acquired Johnston Testers, and the company has since continued to perform drill stem tests as well as wireline formation tests in both open and cased wells.

Drill stem testing (DST) is a field procedure that isolates a formation, stimulates it, and enables controlled production to surface in order to assess the fluids present and the potential production rate. Its goal is to evaluate the zone’s commercial viability and overall economic potential for development. Important indicators obtained from DST include productive capacity, reservoir pressure, permeability, and the extent of the reservoir, which together help gauge deliverability and reservoir size. Tests can be performed in both open-hole and cased-hole configurations. The information gathered through DST informs understanding of the reservoir’s nature and its suitability for subsequent development.

Batak is an Austronesian language spoken by the Batak people on Palawan Island in the Philippines. In linguistic usage, it is sometimes distinguished from other Batak languages by the label Palawan Batak to reflect its geographic context.

Batak is spoken in the communities of Babuyan, Maoyon, Tanabag, Langogan, Tagnipa, Caramay, and Buayan. In the surrounding linguistic region, neighboring languages include Southern Tagbanwa, Central Tagbanwa, Kuyonon, and Agutaynen.

Specific thrust is defined as net thrust per unit of intake air mass flow and is a central parameter for turbofans and jet engines. When the fan pressure ratio—the discharge pressure divided by the inlet pressure—rises, the jet exhaust velocity increases, producing higher specific thrust. In a turbofan that carries the same airflow and maintains the same fan pressure ratio, the core must generate enough power to drive the fan through the low‑pressure turbine. If the turbine inlet temperature of the gas generator is kept low, the engine must draw a relatively high core airflow, which corresponds to a comparatively low bypass ratio; conversely, raising the turbine inlet temperature allows a smaller core airflow and thereby increases the bypass ratio. Higher turbine inlet temperatures also tend to improve thermal efficiency and fuel efficiency.

Civilian turbofan engines predominantly employ the configurations that are common in civil aviation, emphasizing efficiency and reliability. Modern military turbofans, on the other hand, are typically basic two-spool designs. An example of a contemporary military two-spool turbofan is the Snecma M88.

Wipkingen Tunnel is one of three rail routes connecting Oerlikon station with Zürich Hauptbahnhof. All three tunnels pass through the intermediate ridge and emerge from adjacent portals just south of Oerlikon station. The Käferberg Tunnel began operation in 1969, providing a link to Hauptbahnhof’s western approaches. The Weinberg Tunnel, opened in 2014, offers access to the lower level of Hauptbahnhof via the eastern platforms.

The Wipkingen Tunnel opened in 1856 to complete the Nordostbahn line from Zürich Hauptbahnhof to Winterthur via Wallisellen, following the prior year’s opening of the Oerlikon–Winterthur section. A bridge over the Limmat, built south of Wipkingen station, provided access to the Zürich Hauptbahnhof throat via a descending embankment. In the 1890s, that embankment was replaced by the Aussersihl Viaduct, which carries the Winterthur line over several streets, railway yards, and the line to Baden. The footprint of the older embankment route is today occupied by Röntgenstrasse.

The Ishikawajima-Harima F3 is a supersonic technology demonstrator variant derived from the IHI F3 engine, developed to evaluate high-speed propulsion concepts and validate performance improvements. It delivers substantially greater thrust than the production F3, incorporates an afterburner to boost power as needed, and includes several aerodynamic refinements intended to optimize operation at supersonic speeds.

The Ishikawajima-Harima F3 is a two-shaft, low-bypass turbofan whose core features a two-stage low-pressure compressor on the LP shaft and a five-stage high-pressure compressor on the HP shaft, fed by an annular combustor. The engine drives a single-stage high-pressure turbine followed by a single-stage low-pressure turbine. A variant designated XF3-400 incorporates an afterburner in the exhaust downstream of the low-pressure turbine, while the production F3 does not include an afterburner.

Shalu railway station (沙鹿車站; pinyin: Shālù Chēzhàn; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Soa-la̍k Chhia-chām) is a railway station on the Western Trunk line of Taiwan Railways. Located in Shalu District, Taichung, Taiwan, the station was built in May 1919.
During the 1680s, Magdeburg saw the establishment of French Huguenot and Walloon communities. By 1700, the Huguenot settlement had a population of 1,282, while the Walloon settlement numbered 1,731.

Magdeburg's Unser Lieben Frauen Monastery, dating from the 11th century, comprises the church of St. Mary. Today the complex serves as a museum of modern art and houses the Nationale Sammlung Kleinkunstplastiken der DDR (National Collection of Small Art Statues of the GDR).

The concept of order of magnitude describes the scale of a quantity when stated in powers of ten. It can be understood intuitively as the number of digits that appear beyond the ones place, equivalently the total digits minus one. In formal terms, it is defined as the integer part of the base-10 logarithm of the value, obtained by truncation. For instance, 4,000,000 has a base-10 logarithm of about 6.602, which gives an order of magnitude of 6, and such quantities lie between 10^6 and 10^7 (between 10^k and 10^(k+1) for order k). Similarly, a seven-figure income corresponds to an order of magnitude of 6, reflecting seven digits minus one. More broadly, an order of magnitude represents a rough position on a logarithmic scale, conveying the scale of a quantity in a concise, standardized form.

Numeral systems define their scale by a base and construct names for successive powers of that base, so the order of magnitude depends on the chosen base. A comparative example using base ten and a base of one million illustrates how the naming shifts with the underlying base. In that framework, the order-of-magnitude naming employs prefixes such as bi- and tri-, corresponding to two and three, and these forms align with the long-scale convention. The -illion suffix signals that the sequence is anchored to a base of one million, yielding terms whose values reflect that base. Within this context, billion and trillion refer to specific magnitudes rather than merely generic names for orders of magnitude.

Metaphysics is a field whose precise scope and method have been the subject of enduring debate and have evolved across historical periods. A prominent conception, the unified-field approach, treats metaphysics as the inquiry into fundamental questions about the nature of reality or the essences of things. In contrast, some scholars question whether metaphysics shares a uniform set of features, opting instead to enumerate the main topics that metaphysicians investigate. Accordingly, definitions of metaphysics may be descriptive, outlining what metaphysicians typically do, or normative, prescribing what metaphysicians ought to pursue or how they ought to conduct their inquiries.

Metaphysics is a branch of philosophy concerned with the most fundamental aspects of reality. Its central topics include the existence of things and the nature of objects and their properties, as well as questions of possibility and necessity (modality), and the nature of space and time, change, and causation. It also explores the mind–body (matter–mind) relation and the status of matter in relation to mental phenomena. Historically, metaphysics is among the oldest divisions of philosophy, having continuously influenced debates across diverse philosophical traditions.

Young Stribling began his professional boxing career in 1921. During his high school years he fought 75 professional bouts, illustrating an exceptionally tight fight schedule. Between 1921 and 1929 he logged 258 bouts, averaging more than 28 fights per year, a pace that reflected an unusually high level of activity for the era.

Following his defeat to Schmeling, Stribling continued fighting for two more years, engaging in 21 additional bouts. The Schmeling loss marked the end of his opportunities to contend for a title. He remained an active boxer at the time of his death, with his final professional bout occurring less than two weeks before his death.

Higher doctorates may be conferred as honorary degrees rather than through standard doctoral study. They can be awarded at the institution’s initiative or following a nomination process. Such honors acknowledge contributions that enhance public prestige, sustained service to the institution, philanthropic efforts, or notable professional achievement. In formal listings, honorary higher doctorates are often indicated with the “honoris causa” designation, and examples include DCL, honoris causa, Hon LLD, or LittD h.c.

Higher doctorates are advanced academic credentials awarded in recognition of a substantial body of original research accumulated over many years. The candidate typically submits a portfolio consisting of previously published, peer-reviewed work. A panel of internal and external academics reviews the submission to determine whether the applicant should be awarded the doctorate. In some European contexts, the higher doctorate bears similarities to the habilitation. Nevertheless, the habilitation is intended to establish qualification for university professorship, whereas the higher doctorate acknowledges a sustained research contribution and does not by itself confer eligibility for a particular academic position.

Prior to October 15, 1977, there were no recorded visits by members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints to Palau, aside from wartime servicemen passing through. On that date, Heber Butler, then a counselor in the Honolulu Mission, traveled to Palau to assess the potential for missionary work. The first known Latter-day Saint missionaries arrived on July 5, 1978. The Palau Branch was organized on April 1, 1980, and was later renamed the Meyuns Branch.

The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Palau refers to the presence and membership of the LDS Church in Palau. The first known missionaries arrived on July 5, 1978. As of December 31, 2024, there were 421 members in Palau organized into a single branch. The branch shares its building with a church family history center.

During the early 1990s, K. T. Oslin expanded her career to acting, making a guest appearance on the television western Paradise where she played a rural mother and performed the song Down in the Valley. She also participated in a Carol Burnett television special, performing a duet of New Way Home. In 1993 she made her feature-film debut in The Thing Called Love, directed by Peter Bogdanovich and set against the Nashville country-music scene; Oslin portrayed Lucy, the owner of the Bluebird Café. Although the film received mixed reviews, her performance was noted for its authentic country character and presence, with critic Louis Black highlighting her convincing portrayal. Later that year she appeared in the television movie Poisoned by Love: The Kern County Murders. The following year, Oslin guest-starred on Evening Shade, in an Arkansas-themed episode in which she played one of three sisters preparing to audition for the Grand Ole Opry.

K. T. Oslin began her performing career in Texas by forming a college folk trio with David Jones and Guy Clark, performing in local clubs and venues around the state. The group provided lead vocals on the track “Brave Young Soldier” for the 1963 folk compilation Look, It’s Us!. She later teamed with Frank Davis to form a folk duo billed as Frankie and Johnny in Hollywood, during which they recorded an album that was never released. Oslin subsequently returned to Houston. In 1966 she auditioned for a Houston-area touring production of Hello, Dolly!, won a chorus girl part, and began touring with the show that year.

Following the initial group stage, the third-placed teams from each group were compared to determine which would advance, and the two highest-ranked third-placed teams earned a place in the quarter-finals.

The 1996 AFC Asian Cup was the eleventh edition of the quadrennial international football championship for Asian national teams, organized by the Asian Football Confederation. The finals were staged in the United Arab Emirates from 4 to 21 December 1996, culminating in Abu Dhabi where Saudi Arabia defeated the hosts to claim the title. The UAE finished as runners-up, earning the right to represent the AFC at the 1997 FIFA Confederations Cup. Saudi Arabia, by virtue of hosting the Confederations Cup in 1997, qualified automatically for the tournament.

In the United States, children may receive a combined vaccine that includes diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis (DTaP) together with inactivated poliovirus (IPV) and hepatitis B (HepB), marketed as DTaP-IPV-HepB. In the United Kingdom, from 1 August 2017 for babies born on or after that date, the routine schedule offers a hexavalent vaccine, DTaP-Hib-HepB-IPV, which pairs DTaP with Hib, HepB, and IPV.

The World Health Organization estimates that globally about 89% of children have received at least one dose of the diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis vaccine (DTP). Approximately 84% have completed the DTP3 primary series, comprising three doses. WHO monitors DTP3 completion rates among one-year-olds on an annual basis, using this measure as an indicator of the overall completeness of childhood vaccination. The DTP3 completion rate is widely regarded as a proxy for vaccination coverage in childhood, while the number of zero-dose children—those who have not received any DTP dose—serves as a proxy for individuals not reached by vaccination programs.

Jamshedpur FC's official supporters group, known as The Red Miners, was founded in 2017 alongside the club's inception. The group has become a notable element of the team's home atmosphere, and players as well as the head coach have acknowledged their backing by referring to them as the 12th Man.

During the 2018–19 season, Jamshedpur FC appointed Cesar Ferrando as head coach. The club overhauled its squad, bringing in Michael Soosairaj, Sergio Cidoncha, Carlos Calvo, and Mario Arques, while retaining key players such as Tiri, Memo, Subrata Pal, and Farukh. Tim Cahill was also signed, marking a high-profile addition for the Indian league. The campaign began with a victory over Mumbai City FC and continued with a home draw against Bengaluru FC. Jamshedpur finished fifth, narrowly missing the playoff places to NorthEast United, a result that echoed the team’s performance in its inaugural season. In the Hero Super Cup held in Bhubaneswar, the side advanced past the Round of 16 via a walkover against Churchill Brothers but were knocked out in the next round by FC Goa.

The Ulbricht Doctrine was a policy advanced by East German leader Walter Ulbricht asserting East Germany’s sovereignty in international relations and seeking recognition of that status by other states. The claim gained acceptance among fellow Communist states, notably Czechoslovakia, Poland, Hungary, and Bulgaria. In alignment with this stance, these governments undertook not to normalise diplomatic relations with West Germany until West Germany officially recognised East Germany’s sovereignty.

The Ulbricht Doctrine, advanced by East German leader Walter Ulbricht, advocated pursuing normalization with West Germany while recognizing the existence of two distinct German states. In response, West Germany abandoned its Hallstein Doctrine and embraced Ostpolitik, a shift toward broader engagement with the East and the GDR. A milestone of this process came in December 1972 with the signing of the Basic Treaty between East and West Germany, an agreement that reaffirmed the two states as separate entities and created formal contact channels through the exchange of diplomatic missions. The treaty also facilitated both German states’ path to full membership in the United Nations.

Tabae, also known as Tabai and recorded in Greek as Τάβαι, was an ancient city in the region of Caria. Classical geographers, notably Strabo, place it in a Phrygian plain at the boundary with Caria, underscoring its position near the frontier of the two regions. The site corresponding to the ancient city is the modern town of Tavas, near Kale in Denizli Province, Turkey. Inscriptions and a substantial assemblage of ancient remains have been found there, illustrating its historical significance.

Stephanus Byzantius records two towns named Tabae, identifying one in Lydia—likely the settlement known as Tabala—and another in Caria. Livy places Tabae on the Pisidian frontier, toward the coast along the Gulf of Pamphylia. The Tabae discussed here is known from its surviving coinage and is said to have been founded by Tabus. Etymologically, the name has been derived in two ways: some scholars connect it with a Semitic root tabi meaning “good,” while others favor a native origin taba meaning “rock,” a reading that appears more plausible.

Thomas Mann, the eminent German novelist, joined Magnus Hirschfeld's 1922 Reichstag petition seeking the repeal of Section 175, the law that criminalized homosexual relations. Adult liability under Section 175 remained in force until its abolition on 25 June 1969, an event that occurred fourteen years after Mann's death and just three days before the Stonewall riots. The evolving legal stance toward homosexuality affected Mann throughout his life, as the Nazi regime labeled him a traitor, and he was wary of incarceration for acts they deemed criminal.

Thomas Mann married Katia Pringsheim in 1905. She was from a wealthy secular Jewish industrialist family and subsequently joined the Lutheran church. The couple had six children: Erika (born 1905), Klaus (born 1906), Golo (born 1909), Monika (born 1910), Elisabeth (born 1918), and Michael (born 1919).

Muskegon, Michigan, hosts Michigan's Adventure, the largest amusement park in the state. Located in Muskegon County, a short distance north of the city of Muskegon, the park includes a midway with roller coasters, various rides and amusements, and a comprehensive water park.

Muskegon, Michigan, is served by freight rail operations through the Michigan Shore Railway, which provides service to local industries. Passenger rail service to the city ended in 1971 with the advent of Amtrak, and the Michigan routes of the former Chesapeake and Ohio Railway were not included in Amtrak’s initial system, making the nearest passenger services available in Holland or Grand Rapids. Historically, before 1971 the Chesapeake & Ohio Railway (the successor to the Pere Marquette Railway) operated day and night trains from Union Station to Holland and Chicago. The C&O became part of the Chessie System in 1973 and later CSX Transportation in 1987. In 2005 CSX leased Muskegon area lines to the Michigan Shore Railroad. Earlier, Grand Trunk Western and the Pennsylvania Railroad operated passenger trains from a separate Muskegon station to various destinations within Michigan.

Bell Globemedia, later known as CTVglobemedia, was a Canadian media conglomerate formed by the combination of CTV, The Globe and Mail, and the Internet portal Sympatico-Lycos, with Lycos subsequently replaced by MSN. Fecan was named president and chief executive officer of the merged firm and remained in that role for the duration of the Bell Globemedia/CTVglobemedia era. In 2002, Monty resigned and was succeeded by Michael Sabia. Monty’s overarching vision did not yield the desired results for the company as a whole, although individual units performed strongly, particularly the CTV network.

In June 2017, Wow Unlimited Media announced plans to acquire a Bell Media specialty channel, which was subsequently identified as Comedy Gold. The proposed transaction aimed to create a new network targeting children and young adults and would have supplied Bell's over-the-top platforms with children's television content; as part of the deal, BCE would receive 3.4 million common voting shares in Wow Unlimited Media. However, the sale did not proceed and was ultimately terminated, with Comedy Gold shutting down in 2019.

The Flag of Earth was borne at peace marches during the 1960s, serving as a symbol associated with anti-war and humanitarian aims. Some observers have suggested that this flag may have influenced Gilbert Baker's later creation of the rainbow flag, which was devised to celebrate LGBT+ rights. The rainbow flag subsequently entered public awareness after its introduction in 1978.

The League of Nations was the first global intergovernmental organization devoted to preserving international peace and security. It was established on 10 January 1920 as part of the settlement reached at the Paris Peace Conference that concluded World War I. The organization ceased operations on 20 April 1946, and many of its organs and agencies were incorporated into the newly formed United Nations.

Elizabeth II served as the Queen of Uganda from 1962 to 1963, a period when Uganda operated as an independent constitutional monarchy. In that capacity she acted as the country's head of state. She was also the sovereign of several other Commonwealth realms, including the United Kingdom.

Queen Elizabeth II paid a state visit to Uganda from 28 to 30 April 1954, during which the Kazinga National Park in western Uganda was renamed Queen Elizabeth National Park to commemorate her visit. She returned to Uganda from 21 to 24 November 2007 to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) held in Uganda.

Dioctyl adipate is a plasticizer whose proper name is di(2-ethylhexyl) adipate, abbreviated DEHA. The common name is sometimes incorrectly used to refer to dioctyl adipate, which can cause confusion because the actual substituents are two 2-ethylhexyl groups rather than simple octyl groups. Additionally, the abbreviation DOA has at times been applied to bis(2-ethylhexyl) adipate (CAS 103-23-1), which is the same compound as DEHA, further contributing to naming ambiguity.

Dioctyl adipate (DOA) is an organic compound widely used as a plasticizer. The molecule is the diester of adipic acid with two octyl substituents, often depicted by the structural formula (CH2CH2CO2C8H17)2. At ambient conditions it appears as a colorless, oily liquid. In polymer systems, DOA acts to enhance flexibility and lower the glass transition temperature; diesters derived from related alcohols such as 2-ethylhexanol, decanol, and isodecanol are likewise employed as plasticizers.
In much of Europe, summer traditionally began with May Day, marking the start of the season. The interval surrounding the summer solstice was regarded as the middle of summer.

Summer is defined differently in the United States and Canada. In the United States, the season typically starts with the Memorial Day weekend, the last weekend of May, and ends with Labor Day, the first Monday in September. This schedule, especially in regions with four distinct seasons, broadly corresponds to the meteorological summer. In Canada, by contrast, summer commences on Victoria Day, approximately a week earlier than the American date, and terminates on Labour Day, which occurs on the same calendar day as in the United States but is spelled Labour Day in Canadian English. Because Canada's vast geographic area produces a wide range of climatic conditions, summer experiences can vary considerably across the country.

ISO/IEC 27002 is an international standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family that outlines a code of practice for information security controls. The standard's lineage begins with a corporate security framework contributed by Shell to a UK government program in the early 1990s, which matured into the British Standard BS 7799 in the mid-1990s. That BS 7799 framework was later adopted as ISO/IEC 17799 in 2000. The document underwent a revision in 2005, and in 2007 it was renumbered as ISO/IEC 27002 to harmonize with the broader 27000-series. Subsequent revisions followed in 2013 and again in 2022 to keep the guidance current. Additionally, in 2015, ISO/IEC 27017 was developed as a companion standard derived from 27002 to address cloud security controls that were not fully defined in the main document.

ISO/IEC 27002 provides guidelines for information security management, including controls over access and identity management. It stipulates that production systems should not host generic or test user accounts, as such accounts can undermine accountability and security. Any creation or enabling of these IDs requires authorization from the relevant Information Asset Owners, ensuring proper governance and traceability. The rule is specifically targeted at production environments, where the risks associated with unmanaged accounts are greatest.

MaxRange data is a research project that maps and analyzes political history by detailing the status and development of institutional regimes for every sovereign state from 1789 onward. It provides a comprehensive, global overview, examining the historical context, trajectories, external influences, and principal drivers of political change, and charts how regimes have formed, persisted, or transformed over time.

The Annales School approach to political history foregrounds geography and economics, prioritizing longue durée analyses that emphasize slow, long-term processes over the immediate history of events associated with high politics. In this view, political and diplomatic factors are deemphasized, with attention redirected toward enduring social, economic, and environmental structures that shape historical change. Fernand Braudel’s The Mediterranean and the Mediterranean World in the Age of Philip II is regarded as the most influential work of the movement, yet its traditional Rankean treatment of Philip II’s Mediterranean diplomacy constitutes only the third and shortest section. Overall, Braudel’s volume concentrates more on long-term generic cycles than on short-term political events, mirroring the broader shift within the Annales School away from conventional political narratives toward analysis of broad trends in economic and environmental history.

Marc W. Miller, together with Chadwick, Banner, and Wiseman, played a pivotal role in persuading Illinois State University to establish SimRAD (Simulation Research, Analysis, and Design) in 1973. SimRAD operated as a college program that enabled both students and instructors to design games, with the revenues from its titles funding innovations in education. Building on this precedent, Miller, Chadwick, Banner, and Wiseman decided to publish a substantial World War II simulation, and they established Game Designers' Workshop as the publishing company for that game.

Marc Miller is a game designer who created Challenge of the Five Realms, published by MicroProse in 1992, and the card game Super Deck!. In 1996, he acquired the rights to the science‑fiction properties Traveller, Twilight: 2000, and 2300 AD and founded Far Future Enterprises, serving as its president. The company then held the rights to these games. Miller subsequently partnered with Sweetpea Entertainment to license media rights for his science‑fiction property in exchange for funding to launch Imperium Games in February 1996, a new publisher dedicated to Traveller material. Through Far Future Enterprises, Traveller and related titles were licensed to several publishers, and Miller worked on a fifth edition of Traveller for the company.

The origin of Proto-Armenian remains a matter of scholarly debate. Proponents of the Armenian hypothesis contend that Armenian emerged through a local development of the Proto-Indo-European language in the Armenian Highlands, beginning in the third millennium BCE. By contrast, the Kurgan hypothesis posits that Proto-Armenian arrived in the Armenian Highlands via migration from the Balkans or through the Caucasus. In this scenario, the incoming population is thought to have settled in the region during the Bronze Age or around the Bronze Age Collapse, approximately 1200 BCE.

Proto-Armenian is the unattested precursor of the Armenian language, reconstructed by linguists. Armenian stands as the sole known representative of its branch within the Indo-European language family. The earliest stage cannot be recovered through the standard comparative method, necessitating a dual approach that combines internal and external reconstruction. Internal reconstruction utilizes data from Armenian itself, while external reconstruction draws on reconstructions of Proto-Indo-European and other related branches. Together, these methodologies have enabled scholars to assemble a coherent account of Armenian's earlier history.

Within Aztec mythology, the Cintēteo designate a quartet of maize deities. They are regarded as the offspring of the goddess Centeōtl and the god Cinteōtl. In Nahuatl, their name is pronounced sinteːˈteoʔ.

By 2023, Berkshire Hathaway Energy had invested $34.1 billion in renewable energy projects, underscoring a substantial shift toward clean generation. In tandem with this transition, the company has ceased coal operations at 18 coal-fired power stations, reflecting ongoing efforts to reduce reliance on coal. Looking ahead, Berkshire Hathaway Energy plans to discontinue coal operations at an additional 15 stations between 2025 and 2030, continuing its strategy of pivoting away from coal-fired generation.

In 2013, Berkshire Hathaway Energy expanded its corporate footprint by acquiring Metalogic Inspections Services, a firm active across oil and gas, electricity generation, fabrication, pipeline activities, and related services. The transaction was valued at $5.4 billion, reflecting the company's strategic diversification into broader energy services.
Gadzoox announced in August 2000 a restatement of its financial results, and subsequently CEO Bill Sickler and CFO Christine E. Munson resigned from their posts.

Gadzoox conducted its initial public offering in July 2000, during the height of the dot-com bubble. The offering was priced at $21 per share, and the stock surged to a first-day high of $87. As a result, Gadzoox achieved a market capitalization of roughly $1.97 billion.

Ilocos Norte Province hosts three wind-energy facilities, located in the municipalities of Burgos, Pagudpud, and Bangui. The Bangui facility is distinguished as the site of the Philippines’ first wind-power generation plant.

During the early phase of Spanish expansion from Manila, which was under colonial rule in 1571, efforts were undertaken to extend conquest northward. Juan de Salcedo, grandson of Miguel López de Legazpi, volunteered to lead the northern expedition. The force consisted of eight armed vessels and forty-five men, commanded by Salcedo at the age of twenty-two. On June 13, 1572, they landed at what is now present-day Vigan and then proceeded to Laoag, Currimao, and Badoc. Along the coast they observed numerous sheltered coves, locally known as looc, where communities lived in relative harmony. The region was named Ylocos, and its inhabitants were designated Ylocanos.

On June 1, 2011, Microsoft unveiled Windows 8, highlighting a redesigned user interface and a suite of additional features. The presentations took place at Computex Taipei and at the D9: All Things Digital conference held in California, where representatives demonstrated the operating system’s new design and expanded capabilities to attendees.

Microsoft launched a comprehensive Windows 8 advertising campaign in October 2012, with the first television commercial premiering on October 14, 2012. The promotional initiative carried a budget estimated at about $1.5 to $1.8 billion, substantially larger than the roughly $200 million allocated for the Windows 95 campaign. In addition, thirty-four pop-up stores were opened in shopping malls to showcase the Surface product line, while retail staff training was conducted in partnership with Intel. To tailor in-store displays, Microsoft introduced a fictional character, Allison Brown, for English-speaking markets, presenting a profile that included photographs, contact details, and email addresses, which was used on in-store demo units of Windows 8 devices.

David Bowie and Iggy Pop relocated to West Berlin to detox from drugs, sharing a Berlin apartment with Bowie's friends. Pop later recalled the period as an interesting experience. Thursday nights constituted their principal weekly gathering, and, if they were still alive and able to crawl to the sofa, they watched Starsky & Hutch.

Iggy Pop's reflections on the relevance of Edward Gibbon's Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire to the modern world were published by Classics Ireland in 1995, appearing in Caesar Lives (Volume 2). In the piece, he considers the extent to which Gibbon's analysis can be applied to contemporary society. Pop explains that reading Gibbon while touring the Southern United States inspired a spontaneous soliloquy known as Caesar. The soliloquy later appeared on his 1993 album American Caesar.

Throughout September 2022, Australia progressively rolled back several COVID-19 measures as transmission remained low and population immunity increased. On 9 September, restrictions were substantially relaxed, including the nationwide removal of the aircraft mask mandate and a shift from daily to weekly reporting of case data. A week later, on 14 September, the COVID-19 disaster payment for individuals required to isolate was extended to cover mandatory isolation periods. By 22 September, all states had ended mask mandates on public transport, Victoria having maintained its mandate for roughly 800 days. Finally, on 30 September, national leaders declared the emergency response finished and the formal isolation requirements ended. Analysts attributed these changes to high levels of hybrid immunity and persistently low case numbers.

Historically, epidemics and pandemics are considered to end when the disease becomes endemic, meaning it becomes an accepted and manageable part of normal life within a society. By March 2024, there was no universally agreed threshold for defining a pandemic, with formal definitions still being developed by researchers and authorities. In interviews conducted by Time in March 2024, experts noted that COVID-19 continued to circulate and cause disease, but there was uncertainty about whether the outbreak should still be described as a pandemic.
Sigma Phi is a fraternity notable for issuing the first public registry of its members in 1834. It was incorporated in New York in 1885 and later underwent reincorporation in 1920.

Sigma Phi began with the Alpha chapter at Union College, which has operated continuously since its founding, making it the oldest continuously active fraternity chapter in the United States. In 1831, the Beta of New York chapter was established at Hamilton College, a milestone that made Sigma Phi the first Greek fraternal organization in the United States to establish a chapter at another college. Consequently, Sigma Phi became the first national Greek-letter organization in the United States.

A Dance to the Music of Time is described by Bellori as having its subject conceived by Rospigliosi, and the painting presents four dancers seen from the back, labeled Poverty, Labour, Riches, and Pleasure or Luxury. These figures collectively illustrate a progression of human fortunes that cycles back to poverty. The sequence has been mapped onto the Four Seasons, with Poverty aligned with Autumn and Labour with Winter, followed by the remaining two in the subsequent seasonal order. The Autumn/Poverty figure at the rear is now generally regarded as male and identified by the museum as Bacchus. This Bacchus reading follows Boitet de Frauville’s Les Dionysiaques, in which Jupiter grants Bacchus and wine to compensate mortal misery. André Félibien offered a similar interpretation, but he associated Summer with Pleasure, whereas Bellori placed Summer with Luxury.

Scholars have debated the intended program of Nicolas Poussin’s A Dance to the Music of Time. Malcolm Bull contends that the identifications commonly assigned to the figures do not reflect the painting’s original intention, arguing instead that the iconography derives from the late Greek poet Nonnus, transmitted through Pierre de Ronsard’s Hymne de l’Automne. Bull maintains that Nonnus’s descriptions of the four seasons, rendered into French, align closely with the arrangement: Spring on the left adorned with a rose garland; Autumn at the rear with windswept hair and an olive-branch brow; Winter next with a bound hairstyle and a shadowed face; and Summer at the front dressed in white with ears of corn braided into her hair. The left-hand herm features Bacchus in a double aspect. Bull further suggests that the competing interpretation, associated with Rospigliosi, was devised during or after the work’s completion. By contrast, Ingamells argues that Poussin was not unduly concerned with precise identification of the figures, allowing for a more flexible allegorical reading rather than a fixed program.

Defense Travel System (DTS) operates at more than 9,500 sites worldwide and processes an average of over 25,000 transactions daily. The system is accessed by about 100,000 unique users each day. Program oversight of DTS is provided by the DMDC PMO-DTS, encompassing acquisition, technical management, and operation and maintenance responsibilities. Functional oversight is maintained by the DTMO.

Defense Travel System (DTS) is a software application used by the United States Department of Defense that enables defense travelers to manage their commercial travel, and it operates in accordance with the government's Joint Travel Regulations.

At Shoshinkai 1996, held November 22–24, the 64DD was fully unveiled, with IGN describing it as one of the convention’s most prominent attractions. Howard Lincoln stated that hardware specifications were finalized and that the 64DD would have its own dedicated booth. Perrin Kaplan announced a launch window for late 1997 in Japan. Core Magazine reported strong backing from both third-party and internal development teams, including sequels for Super Mario 64 and Zelda 64, in addition to original 64DD titles Cabbage and Emperor of the Jungle. Nintendo listed several anticipated developers for the platform—Konami, Capcom, Enix, and Rare. Rare, for its part, dismissed rumors that the product would be cancelled before launch.

In a December 1997 interview with Shigeru Miyamoto and Shigesato Itoi, the long-promised potential of the 64DD peripheral was discussed.
