Miyamoto acknowledged that repeatedly describing or justifying its promise was difficult, noting that it would have been easier if the device had launched with the Nintendo 64 and more challenging to explain after the fact. Itoi asserted that the 64DD held fundamental significance for Nintendo’s game development, with many ideas originating from the peripheral, suggesting that much of Nintendo’s development began with the 64DD. Miyamoto added that almost every new Nintendo 64 project was based on the 64DD, with games typically created on cartridges first and later enhanced by the expansion technology. By 1998, IGN remained optimistic that major cartridge-based N64 titles would incorporate software support for the forthcoming expansion disk. Known third-party developers associated with the 64DD included Konami, Culture Brain, Seta, Japan System Supply, Titus, Infogrames, Rare, Paradigm Entertainment, Ocean, and Factor 5.

Perceptions of socialism and communism in Europe varied with religious and national context. In predominantly Christian Europe, communists were commonly associated with atheism, while in Protestant England communism was viewed as too closely aligned with Catholic ritual, prompting a preference for the label socialism. Friedrich Engels, in 1848, argued that socialism held greater respectability in European discourse than communism, which was treated with suspicion. Within this spectrum, the Owenites in Britain and the Fourierists in France were regarded as respectable socialists, whereas movements calling for comprehensive social change tended to identify themselves as communists. This strand also produced communist writings by Étienne Cabet of France and Wilhelm Weitling of Germany. At the same time, John Stuart Mill, while working within a largely liberal framework, entertained the possibility of an economic order incorporating socialist features; in later editions of Principles of Political Economy (1848) he asserted that economic theory does not preclude such an arrangement and he favored worker cooperatives over capitalist firms. In political discourse of the period, Democrats hailed the Revolutions of 1848 as democratic revolutions promising liberty, equality, and fraternity, whereas Marxists condemned them as betrayals of working-class interests by a bourgeoisie indifferent to the proletariat.

Libertarian socialism is a libertarian tradition within socialism, also referred to as left-libertarianism, social anarchism, or socialist libertarianism. It is characterized by anti-authoritarian and anti-statist aims, opposing centralized state ownership and control, as well as wage-based labor arrangements and the state itself. Proponents stress worker self-management and decentralized organizational forms, arguing that freedom and equality are achieved by abolishing coercive institutions that control production. The approach typically favors direct democracy and federated associations, including libertarian municipalism, citizens' assemblies, trade unions, and workers' councils.

In 2006, Kyrgyzstan participated in the ELF Cup, the tournament’s first edition held in Northern Cyprus. The competition was originally designed for non-FIFA member national associations, and Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan were among the invited teams, although both countries were represented by their national futsal squads rather than their regular football teams in the event.

During the early 2000s, the Kyrgyzstan national football team participated in several international qualifiers. In 1999 it competed in the qualification for the 2000 AFC Asian Cup, finishing last in its group. The following year the squad took part in the WAFF Championship, again ending at the bottom of its group. In 2001 it entered the qualification campaign for the 2002 FIFA World Cup and was eliminated in the first round after finishing third in its group.

Jianghan University is a provincial public higher education institution located in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China. In Chinese, the university is named 江汉大学 (Jiānghàn dàxué). The campus covers about 1.4 square kilometers, with an additional 0.5 square kilometers under construction. It is situated within the Wuhan Economic and Technological Development Zone, by Lake Sanjiao.

Jianghan University is a comprehensive higher education institution whose academic offerings span disciplines including economics, law, education, literature, history, agriculture, science, engineering, medicine, fine arts, design, and management. The university offers 42 undergraduate programs across these fields. It employs about 1,000 full-time faculty members, including 103 full professors and around 400 associate professors. The student body comprises roughly 15,600 full-time students.

Ajax (Asynchronous JavaScript and XML) describes a collection of web development techniques that enable asynchronous communication between a web page and a server. The approach gained prominence after Google deployed standards-compliant, cross-browser Ajax in Gmail in 2004 and in Google Maps in 2005. In October 2004, Kayak.com's public beta was among the first large-scale e-commerce uses of Ajax, with the developers describing the technique informally as the XML HTTP approach. Collectively, these developments increased interest in Ajax among web developers.

Ajax enhances the performance and user experience of web applications by enabling more efficient client–server interactions, reducing server traffic and improving overall speed, a central objective in modern web development. It can render parts of an application without requiring data retrieval, thereby lowering server load and enabling smoother updates. This optimization shortens response times on both the server and client sides, contributing to a more seamless user experience by eliminating or minimizing loading delays during interaction.

During World War I, Morton Prince served as director at Hotel Lotti in Paris, France, where he oversaw an information bureau and a home, the latter intended for soldiers and sailors from Massachusetts.

Morton Prince was an American physician and psychologist known for transmitting European approaches to psychopathology to American audiences, with particular emphasis on dissociative phenomena. Through his research and teaching, he helped introduce continental concepts into early 20th-century psychology and contributed to the field’s intellectual development. In addition to his scholarly work, Prince played a key role in scholarly publishing by helping to establish the Journal of Abnormal Psychology in 1906 and serving as its editor from its founding until his death, thereby shaping the journal’s course and influence.

Vaughn Hebron's 32-yard kickoff return to the Broncos' 42 sparked a 10-play, 58-yard opening drive that brought Denver to the Green Bay 46. On third-and-10, a holding penalty on Packers cornerback Doug Evans negated an incomplete pass from Elway to Willie Green and awarded the Broncos a new set of downs. Terrell Davis then ran 27 yards to the Green Bay 14, followed by a 2-yard gain, and Elway scrambled 10 yards to set up first-and-goal at the two. Davis scored a 1-yard touchdown run to tie the game.

Super Bowl XXXII marked NBC's final year as the American Football Conference broadcast network after a 33-year association, as CBS was awarded the AFC package for the 1998 season. As a result, NBC would not return to NFL coverage until 2006, when it began televising Sunday Night Football and later carried Super Bowl XLIII in February 2009. Concurrent with the rights transition, Greg Gumbel and Phil Simms relocated to CBS to serve as the network's lead NFL broadcast team.

Within Chinese naming practices, the treatment of a two-character given name varies by locale. In mainland China, such given names are typically written without a hyphen between the characters. By contrast, in Taiwan the two characters of the given name are usually separated by a dash, making the two-character given name explicit. In Hong Kong, the conventional form also employs hyphenation to connect the two given-name characters. The use of a hyphen between the two components of the given name thus signals a two-character given name. Taiwanese practice is often viewed as analogous to Korean naming conventions in this respect.

In Chinese naming practices, given names show greater diversity than surnames, yet they are almost universally one or two syllables in length. The writing system encompasses a very large set of characters, with at least 106,000 individual characters including variant forms. As of 2006, the Public Security Bureau of the People's Republic of China supported roughly 32,000 characters for computer input, with many far less commonly used in ordinary writing. Given names are typically chosen for phonetic pleasingness and tonal quality, as well as positive associations or aesthetically pleasing shapes. When a two-character given name is used, each character may carry its own meaning, but the name is treated as a single unit and is usually spoken as a single word even if the combined meaning has become less significant.

Rodong Sinmun is frequently cited by KCNA and by international media as a primary source for official North Korean positions on a broad range of issues. The newspaper is led by editor-in-chief Kim Pyong-ho. An online index of its articles dating back to 1946 is accessible, with the list published on unibook.unikorea.go.kr and nkinfo.unikorea.go.kr.

Since 1996, Rodong Sinmun alongside KCNA, Minju Joson, and Joson Inmingun have published a joint New Year editorial that outlines the year’s policy priorities. The editorials typically praise the Songun policy, the government and leadership, and national development, while criticizing the policies of South Korea, Japan, the United States, Israel, and Western governments toward North Korea and its allies. The 1 January 2006 edition called for the withdrawal of American forces from South Korea and urged a nationwide campaign to drive out U.S. troops, and it referenced Korean reunification. The 2009 editorial drew attention for its lack of critique of U.S. policy and for acknowledging severe North Korean economic problems, while presenting denuclearisation on the Korean Peninsula as a hopeful sign. The 2010 editorial echoed similar themes, advocating an end to hostilities with the United States and a nuclear-free Korean Peninsula.

Originating in Florence in the late 16th century, opera began with Jacopo Peri’s Dafne, which showcased an early monodic approach to singing, and the form subsequently spread from Florence to other parts of Italy and to Europe. During this period, vocal music performed in choirs acquired a renewed sense of identity as composers explored new textures and expressive possibilities. In the early 17th century two principal methods of writing music coexisted: Stile Antico (Prima Prattica) and Stile Moderno (Seconda Prattica), with the former predominating in Northern Europe and the latter favored by Italian composers. The city’s musical influence extended into instrument invention as Bartolomeo Cristofori produced the piano in Florence in 1709. Among Florentines noted for their contributions are Piero Strozzi, Giulio Caccini, and Mike Francis, the latter of whom is cited among prominent locals. Caccini’s Le Nuove Musiche is regarded as a landmark work for performance practice and practical instruction. By the 1630s the term monody came to describe a vocal style that combined a single melody with basso continuo and a text delivered in a free, lyrical, speech‑like manner; this monodic approach was typically supported by a keyboard instrument (such as a harpsichord) that sustained chords while the singer performed the monodic line.

Florence, known in Italian as Firenze and pronounced FLORR-ənss (fiˈrɛntse), is the capital city of the Italian region of Tuscany and the most populous municipality in the region. The city proper has a population of 362,353, while the metropolitan province surrounding it has 989,460 residents as of 2025.

Guillaume maintained neutrality during the dispute. In September 1877, Italian anarcho-communists clashed with Spanish collectivists in Verviers, a confrontation that unfolded at the final congress of the Anti-Authoritarian International. The disagreement centered on economic questions and organizational method: the collectivists argued for employing trade unions as a route to achieving anarchy, while the communists regarded trade unions as reformist, counter-revolutionary, and susceptible to bureaucracy and corruption. As a result, the communists advocated for small, loosely organized affinity groups aligned with anti-authoritarian principles.

Anarcho-communism emerged within the broader socialist milieu as an anti-authoritarian current within the International Workingmen's Association (IWA). Marxists in the IWA described their anti-authoritarian rivals as anarchists, a label rooted in the ideas of Proudhon and Déjacque and accepted by the opponents themselves. The defeat of the Paris Commune in 1871 precipitated a split in the IWA over questions of socialist economics and the means to realize a classless society. Karl Marx advocated seizing state power through political parties, excluding the anarchists from the IWA. The anarchist faction centered on the Jura Federation subsequently reconstituted itself as the Anti-Authoritarian International, emphasizing decentralization and a federal structure. In this milieu, Italy and Spain—two of the IWA's largest branches—rejected Marxism and aligned with the anti-authoritarian platform, laying groundwork for later anarchist-communist currents.

Codec 2 encodes information as digital bytes that are formed from compactly packed bit-field data. These bit fields can be optionally gray coded before they are grouped, a practice that is advantageous for raw transmission, although typical applications often stream the bit fields directly without Gray coding. The bit fields carry parameters that are stored or exchanged, including pitch, energy, voicing booleans, and LSPs.

Codec 2 has been presented at several conferences, where it has drawn attention within technical and amateur radio circles. In 2012, the project received the ARRL Technical Innovation Award, and it was also honored with the Best Presentation Award at the Linux Australia Conference.

On 23 March 1994, at Pope Air Force Base in North Carolina, during a joint Army–Air Force exercise, an F-16D (AF Serial No. 88-0171) from the 23d Fighter Wing, 74th Fighter Squadron, collided with a USAF C-130E while performing a simulated engine-out approach. Both crew members ejected, but the F-16 continued on at full afterburner toward the Green Ramp. A second collision followed when the F-16 struck a USAF C-141 being boarded by U.S. Army paratroopers, resulting in 24 fatalities and at least 100 injuries. The incident is known as the Green Ramp disaster.

The F-16 Fighting Falcon has been slated to remain in United States Air Force service through 2025, with replacement anticipated in the form of the F-35A variant of the Lightning II. The F-35 is expected to gradually supplant multiple multirole aircraft within program member nations. Delays in the F-35 program have prompted the U.S. Air Force to implement life-extension upgrades to its F-16 fleet to sustain operational readiness. In 2022, officials stated that the U.S. Air Force would operate the F-16 for roughly another two decades.

USS Bougainville, the third ship in the America-class, is planned to be the first in the line to include a well deck capable of deploying amphibious vehicles. The design shift reflects the evolution of naval doctrine from the late 1990s, which emphasized lighter ground vehicles, toward experiences in Iraq and Afghanistan that demonstrated the utility of heavier, up-armored vehicles. Anticipated counterinsurgency operations underscore the need for ships able to transport and deliver heavier equipment, including via shore connectors, thereby making a well deck a practical enhancement and offering an alternative to the higher costs associated with airlifting cargo. Incorporating the well deck also necessitates a somewhat smaller island superstructure compared with the two preceding ships of the class. The LHA-8 program timeline includes initial design funding in 2015, followed by detailed design and construction beginning in 2017, with a planned entry into service in 2024.

America-class amphibious assault ships are designed to operate as capable, if limited, aircraft carriers, able to support a carrier air wing with a mix of fixed-wing fighters and rotary-wing aircraft. They typically embark roughly 20 to 25 aircraft, including AV-8B Harrier aircraft and/or F-35B jets, alongside multipurpose helicopters such as the MH-60 Seahawk to perform roles ranging from air defense and reconnaissance to utility support. While they emphasize amphibious assault capabilities, their aviation complement provides a flexible, ship-based air capability in regional operations. Looking ahead, the class’s future ships, beginning with USS Bougainville (LHA-8), are planned with smaller aircraft hangars to free space for a larger amphibious warfare well deck, thereby enhancing the capacity to deploy landing craft and other amphibious vehicles.

Michael Okwu served as a co-presenter of Showbiz Today Reports on CNN from 1997 to 2000. He was a CNN Entertainment News correspondent and contributed reports as a full-time general assignment correspondent.

Showbiz Tonight, an HLN entertainment news program, underwent several scheduling changes during its run. On March 29, 2010, the live broadcast shifted from the 11:00 p.m. Eastern slot to 5:00 p.m. Eastern (2:00 p.m. Pacific). In early May 2011, it returned to an 11:00 p.m. start, with first-run episodes taped hours prior to airing. The 5:00 p.m. edition was subsequently dropped and replaced by HLN Special Report with Vinnie Politan. A weekday morning replay had aired at 11:00 a.m. Eastern (8:00 a.m. Pacific) from 2009 through April 2011. A weekend edition, featuring either a best-of compilation or Friday replay, continued to air on weekend evenings until July 2011.

TvOS, in its early incarnation as Apple TV Software 5, was released on September 24, 2012, for Apple TV devices beginning with the second generation and later. The update is based on the iOS 5 and iOS 6 codebases and introduced several significant features, including the introduction of Shared Photo Streams, support for switching between iTunes accounts, and enhanced AirPlay functionality. It also added a Trailers search feature and incorporated a range of additional minor improvements intended to refine the user experience and performance across supported devices.

On September 9, 2015, Apple unveiled the fourth-generation Apple TV, a model that supports third-party applications. At the same time, Apple renamed the Apple TV operating system to tvOS, adopting camel case naming consistent with iOS and watchOS.

On 8 June, two days after Rome's liberation, Badoglio and representatives of the CLN, with Noel Mason-MacFarlane serving as Allied representative, agreed that Ivanoe Bonomi would become prime minister. Bonomi was sworn in on 18 June, inaugurating his second term as premier in the second Bonomi administration. The cabinet was first seated in Salerno and moved to Rome from mid-July. In addition to the premiership, Bonomi held the posts of interior minister, minister for Italian Africa under Allied occupation, and, until December 1944, foreign minister. The appointment was made without Winston Churchill's knowledge, who deemed Badoglio the safer choice and had Mason-MacFarlane dismissed over the decision. Mason-MacFarlane, aligning with American policy, argued that Badoglio was too discredited to continue and that his fascist associations would undermine the monarchy.

Ivanoe Bonomi was elected to the Constituent Assembly in June 1946, standing on the National Democratic Union list, an alliance between the Liberal Party and the Labour Democratic Party. He served as chair of the Assembly's Treaties Committee. He also participated as a member of the Italian delegation in the preliminary Paris conference held to adopt the peace treaty with the Allied powers.

Cynthia Nixon has spoken publicly about an evolving sexual orientation, noting in 2007 that she had not changed and that she was a woman in love with another woman after previously being partnered with men. She subsequently identified as bisexual in 2012, and from 2018 onward described herself as queer. In political and social advocacy, Nixon supported the legalization of same-sex marriage in Washington state and hosted a fundraising event in support of Washington Referendum 74.

Cynthia Nixon was born in Manhattan, New York City. She is the only child of Walter Elmer Nixon Jr., a radio journalist from Harlingen, Texas, and Anne Elizabeth Knoll, an actress from Chicago, and she has credited her mother with introducing her to theatre. Nixon is of English and German descent, with her grandparents including Adolph Knoll and Etta Elizabeth Williams on her mother’s side and Walter E. Nixon and Grace Truman McCormack on her father’s side. Her parents divorced when she was six years old, with her father often unemployed and her mother serving as the primary breadwinner; her mother also worked on the game show To Tell the Truth, coaching impostors who claimed to be the person described by the host.

Hua Chunying joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China as a section member in the Department of Western Europe after completing her studies, and over more than two decades she rose to the position of spokeswoman. Beginning in 1995, she spent four years in Singapore serving as an attaché. From 2003 to 2010, she worked at China's mission to the European Union, where she was promoted from secretary to counselor.

Hua Chunying is widely described as a leading exponent of wolf-warrior diplomacy. In 2020, she indicated that she was comfortable with such labeling, provided it served to defend China's legitimate interests in sovereignty, security, and development. Scholars have highlighted her markedly assertive manner in diplomatic discourse, a style some compare to that of male colleagues, including Zhao Lijian. Her approach is said to have influenced a younger generation of diplomats, with female officials such as Mao Ning adopting a similar posture, and Mao Ning later becoming the foreign ministry's spokesperson in September 2022.

Siem Reap Province is characterized by the predominance of Theravada Buddhism, which is the state religion of Cambodia and widely observed within the province. The religious composition is heavily skewed toward Buddhism, with Buddhists making up more than 99.3 percent of the population. Small minority groups include Christians, comprising about 0.4 percent, and Muslims, around 0.2 percent, the latter largely belonging to the Cham community.

Siem Reap province is the tenth largest administrative division of Cambodia. By 2019 its population had reached about one million, rendering it the fourth most populous province in the country. The southern boundary is largely defined by the Tonle Sap, and the province forms part of the Tonle Sap Biosphere Reserve, one of nine provinces included in the reserve. The province is notable as the location of the historic Angkor complex, including Angkor Wat, which has been designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It also encompasses the temple sites of Banteay Srei and the Roluos group. Beng Mealea is listed by UNESCO as a tentative site, while Phnom Kulen National Park, also on UNESCO’s tentative list, houses the country’s largest reclining Buddha statue.

Kbal Spean, located in the jungle northeast of Angkor, is noted for a sandstone riverbed bearing numerous Hindu myth sculptures carved into the rock. The Stung Kbal Spean, a tributary of the Siem Reap River, rises in the Kulein mountains north of Banteay Srei. The archaeological site extends along the river from about 150 metres upstream of the bridge head to the downstream falls. The flow of the river over these rock carvings is regarded as sanctifying the site. Downstream, the river bifurcates into the Siem Reap River and the Puok River, with the Puok eventually reaching Tonlé Sap Lake after passing through the plains and the Angkor temple complex.

Kbal Spean lies along a river whose bed and banks are adorned with carved sculptures, and inscriptions at the site are revealed as the water recedes. The central theme centers on creation in Hindu mythology, most notably Vishnu reclining on a serpent in the ocean of milk in meditative slumber, from whose navel a lotus emerges bearing Brahma, the creator. Along the river, reliefs depict Shiva in the form of a Linga, with about a thousand lingams carved into the riverbed, giving the valley its traditional name, the Valley of the Thousand Lingas. The Vishnu motifs are crafted to align with the natural contours of the riverbed and its banks, and a depiction of Shiva with his consort Uma is also visible.

The Kyrgyz Premier League is the highest level of professional football in Kyrgyzstan and is currently known as the OLIMPBET Premier League for sponsorship reasons. In Kyrgyz, the league is titled Кыргыз Премьер Лигасы, with the romanization Kyrgyz Premier Ligasy. Established in 1992 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the competition is contested by eight teams. Dordoi Bishkek is the most successful club in the league’s history, having won thirteen titles.

The Kyrgyz Premier League is the top division of football in Kyrgyzstan. The champions secure a berth in the AFC Challenge League, Asia's third-tier club competition. At the opposite end of the table, the team with the worst record at the end of each season is relegated to the Kyrgyzstan League Second Level.

From July to October 1936, at the outset of the Spanish Civil War, the Nationalist side conducted what is widely regarded as the world’s first long-range combat airlift. The operation employed German Luftwaffe Junkers Ju 52 transports and Italian Regia Aeronautica SM.81 aircraft, operated under the Spanish Nationalist Air Force. The missions ferried troops of the Army of Africa from Spanish Morocco to the Spanish mainland, enabling rapid reinforcement of Nationalist forces in the early stages of the conflict.

During the 1973 Yom Kippur War, the United States Air Force's Military Airlift Command conducted the airlift operation known as Nickel Grass to resupply Israel, which was under a surprise attack by Egyptian and Syrian forces. The mission delivered substantial quantities of military materiel, enabling Israeli forces to mount a counteroffensive against the Arab states. In response, members of OPEC imposed an oil embargo on the United States, a move that contributed to the onset of the 1970s energy crisis.

Haichong Lu station is a Guangzhou Metro station on the eastern extension of Line 3. Construction began on 29 April 2020, the enclosure structure was completed on 27 September 2020, and the main structure was topped out in June 2021. In June 2023, Guangzhou Metro Group proposed naming the station Haichong Lu (Road), with the name officially approved in October 2023. The project completed the transfer of the three rights on 31 May 2024, and the eastern extension of Line 3, including the station, opened on 1 November 2024.

Haichong Lu station is a planned Guangzhou Metro station on Line 3. It first appeared in the 2003 Guangzhou Urban Rail Transit Plan for Line 3. The proposed route would extend from Panyu Square to Guangzhou New Town toward Nansha, with a stop near the intersection of Haichong Road and Yayun (Asian Games) Boulevard. The station was originally named Qianfengcun, but was subsequently renamed Jinguang Dadao. As part of Line 3's East Extension, the project received approval from the National Development and Reform Commission in late March 2017, with the overall plans approved in early January 2018.

Timothy Ray is a United States Air Force general and a native of DeLand, Florida. In February 2018, he was nominated for promotion to general and for reassignment as commander of the Air Force Global Strike Command. The United States Senate confirmed the nomination in March 2018. Before taking command of the Air Force Global Strike Command, Ray served as the Deputy Commander of the United States European Command in Stuttgart, Germany.

Timothy Ray is a retired United States Air Force general who served as commander of the Air Force Global Strike Command. His retirement ceremony was held on July 1, 2021. In August 2021, his deputy, Lieutenant General Anthony J. Cotton, formally relieved him as commander of Air Force Global Strike Command. Ray officially retired from the U.S. Air Force on September 1, 2021.

Yesoteric is a widely distributed, multi-volume bootleg compilation featuring music by the band Yes and related artists. It began circulating among fans in the early 1990s, with initial distribution on cassette tapes before later being issued on compact discs. The compilation was often associated with Notes from the Edge, the Yes fan newsletter.

In the early 2000s, Rhino issued official Yes CD reissues, which were followed by the In a Word box set. A substantial portion of the previously unreleased studio material had already surfaced as higher-quality bonus tracks on these releases, thereby diminishing the necessity for the studio material presented in the Yesoteric collection. Nevertheless, the Yesoteric set continues to circulate largely due to the live recordings incorporated in its Chronicles section.

Baldwin, Nassau County, New York, traces its historical roots to Baldwinsville, a community that, at the time, lay within Queens County. In 1867 the South Side Railroad began operating a station in Baldwinsville, linking the locality to the broader regional rail network. The following year, 1870, Francis Baldwin—son of Thomas Baldwin—took a seat in the New York State Assembly representing Queens County's 2nd District and later served as Queens County treasurer. By 1871, the U.S. Postal Service renamed Baldwinsville to Baldwins to avoid confusion with the upstate Baldwinsville. In 1892, an act of local government officially named the village Baldwin. These successive changes reflect the community’s evolution and its eventual identification as Baldwin in Nassau County.

John J. Kedenburg, a Baldwin High School class of 1964 graduate, served as a Specialist Five with a long-range reconnaissance team composed of South Vietnamese irregular troops within the U.S. Army's 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne) during the Vietnam War. The unit came under attack and was encircled by a battalion-size force of the North Vietnamese Army. Kedenburg conducted a rear-guard action that allowed his team to break out and reach a landing zone, where he directed the defense. In the engagement's final moments, he relinquished the last evacuation opportunity to secure the evacuation of one of his Vietnamese comrades.

In 2013, The New York Times Company sold The Boston Globe along with several other New England media properties to John W. Henry, the principal owner of the Boston Red Sox. The transaction was part of a broader strategy to refocus the company on its core brands and to concentrate efforts on its principal newspaper and digital ventures.

The New York Times Company has been listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker NYT since September 25, 1997. Between April 27, 1967 and January 13, 1969, Class A common stock traded over the counter, and from January 14, 1969 through September 24, 1997, its shares traded on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX). The company maintains two stock classes, Class A, which is publicly traded, and Class B, privately held. Class B is held largely through The 1997 Trust by the descendants of Adolph Ochs, comprising over 90 percent of that class. Adolph Ochs purchased The New York Times in 1896.

William Hull spent his remaining years in Newton, Massachusetts, living with his wife, Sarah Fuller. He authored two works defending his conduct—Detroit: Defence of Brig. Gen. Wm. Hull (1814) and Memoirs of the Campaign of the Northwestern Army of the United States: A.D. 1812 (1824)—both aimed at restoring his reputation after the Detroit surrender. Some later historians have argued that he was unfairly scapegoated for that loss. The publication of the Memoirs in 1824 helped to improve public perception to some degree, and Hull was honored with a Boston dinner on May 30, 1825. In June 1825, the Marquis de Lafayette visited him and spoke of vindication and forgiveness. Hull died at his Newton home on November 29, 1825.

On March 22, 1805, President Thomas Jefferson appointed William Hull as governor of the Michigan Territory and as its Indian Agent. At that time the territory remained largely under Native control, with only two enclaves around Detroit and Fort Mackinac serving as American footholds. Hull pursued a policy of gradually acquiring Indigenous lands to enable settlement by American colonists. In 1807 he concluded the Treaty of Detroit with the Odawa, Chippewa, Wyandot, and Potawatomi, through which much of southeastern Michigan and northwestern Ohio were ceded to the United States, extending to the mouth of the Maumee River, the site of Toledo’s later development. Hull’s expansionist program encountered opposition from Shawnee leaders Tecumseh and Tenskwatawa (the Prophet), who urged resistance to Euro-American cultural influence and to further land cessions.

As of the 2010 census, 6,273 people identified as Yokuts. A substantial portion of the population resides on reservations that operate casinos. These gaming enterprises have been essential in providing employment opportunities, generating revenue, and supporting access to healthcare for Yokuts communities.

The Yowlumne, a Yokutsan group, inhabited the Lower Kern River region near Bakersfield in the southern San Joaquin Valley. Their traditional homeland includes Caliente Creek and lies between Kern Lake and the Tehachapi Mountains, extending as far south as El Paso Creek.

During the 2024 cycle, the Iowa Democratic presidential caucuses held on January 15 were conducted in person and limited to party business, while candidate voting occurred exclusively through mail-in ballots from January 12 through March 5, 2024 (Super Tuesday). The change stemmed from a compromise between the Iowa Democratic Party and the Democratic National Committee. Although Iowa has traditionally opened the nominating calendar with the first caucus or primary, the DNC had initially proposed placing South Carolina first on February 3. A total of 46 delegates to the Democratic National Convention were allocated to presidential candidates.

Following protests at the 1968 Democratic National Convention, Democratic Party leaders reformed the presidential nominating calendar to spread contests across a broader array of states, thereby altering the pace of the nomination process. Iowa’s elaborate multi-tier caucus system, which includes precinct caucuses, county conventions, district conventions, and a state convention, tended to place its caucus activities early in the electoral cycle. As a consequence, Iowa became the first state to hold a Democratic caucus in 1972, and four years later it conducted the first Republican caucus in 1976.

Puget Sound Business Journal traces its corporate lineage to the mid-1980s consolidation of American business journals, beginning with ABJC’s 1986 purchase of the entire slate of publications owned by Mark Vittert and Business Journal Publications Corp for $40 million, a deal that brought in journals in Cincinnati, Baltimore, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, and St. Louis. Later that year, American City merged with Scripps Howard Business Journals, and the resulting Scripps-Howard Newspapers division then operated publications in ten markets, including Los Angeles, Seattle, San Diego, San Francisco, Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Phoenix, Atlanta, Washington, D.C., and Miami/Fort Lauderdale, among which the Puget Sound Business Journal was the Seattle edition.

Puget Sound Business Journal is a regional business news publication serving the Puget Sound area and is part of the national BizJournals network, whose online presence is branded under the overarching title The Business Journal. The network delivers local business coverage from multiple U.S. cities through its centralized platform, and it maintains an extensive archive of more than five million business news articles published since 1996. As of August 2021, the BizJournals site reported a weekly readership of over 3.6 million.

Caïman was a Requin-class submarine of the French Navy constructed in the mid-1920s. Her keel was laid in August 1924, she was launched in March 1927 and commissioned in February 1928. During her career she narrowly evaded engagement with the British light cruiser HMS Ajax on 9 June off the coast of Syria. She was scuttled at Toulon on 27 November 1942 to prevent German capture, later raised in February 1943, and subsequently sunk again on 11 March 1944 by Allied aircraft.

CHLG-FM announced a format flip scheduled for December 26, coordinated with its sister station CKRA-FM in Edmonton, and the new playlist centers on soft- to mid-tempo hits predominantly from the 1980s and 1990s, supplemented by a limited selection of older tracks and several titles from the 2000s.

CHLG-FM is a Canadian radio station whose corporate history includes involvement in a major media merger between Astral Media and Bell Media. On March 16, 2012, Astral announced an agreement to combine its assets with Bell Media for 3.38 billion dollars, a move that followed Astral’s acquisition of CHHR. The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission initially rejected the proposed deal on October 18, 2012. A revised proposal gained approval on March 4, 2013, but only under certain conditions. Among those conditions was a requirement that Bell Media divest several Astral properties, including CHHR-FM.

An archaeological site is a location, or group of locations, in which physical evidence of past human activity is preserved and available for study. The preserved evidence may relate to prehistoric, historic, or contemporary periods, and such sites may have been, or may be, examined through archaeological investigation. They constitute part of the archaeological record, reflecting how past societies used and inhabited landscapes. Sites vary considerably in their appearance, from places where little or no remains are visible above ground to structures that remain standing and in use today.

In archaeology, the distribution of artifacts informs future excavation decisions: sites with a high concentration of artifacts are regarded as particularly promising targets for further fieldwork, while locales with few artifacts are interpreted as indicating comparatively lower levels of past human activity, a point noted by archaeologist Jess Beck. Many archaeological sites are uncovered by accident, and among the most common discoverers are farmers who plow or clear fields. Hikers and pilots also encounter artifacts and typically report their findings to archaeologists. Once a site is identified, researchers are required to record the area; when funding and time permit, investigators may proceed to dig to recover material and study the site more closely.

Oklahoma City contains at least one major park in each quadrant outside downtown, reflecting the distribution outlined in the city’s first parks masterplan. Will Rogers Park forms part of the Grand Boulevard loop, a historic corridor that once connected Lincoln Park, Trosper Park, and Woodson Park, though several segments of the linkage have since disappeared. In the far northwest lies Martin Park Nature Center, a designated natural habitat within the urban landscape. Within Will Rogers Park, the Lycan Conservatory, the Rose Garden, and the Butterfly Garden—constructed during the Works Progress Administration era—are notable features. In April 2005, the skate park at Wiley Post Park was renamed the Mat Hoffman Action Sports Park to honor Mat Hoffman, a local resident and businessman who contributed to its design and who is a ten-time BMX World Vert champion.

Oklahoma City covers a total area of 620.79 square miles (1,607.8 km2), consisting of 601.11 square miles (1,556.9 km2) of land and 19.23 square miles (49.8 km2) of water. The city added 480 net acres through annexation, an expansion carried out during Mayor David Holt’s tenure. These figures come from the United States Census Bureau.

The engagement began and persisted, with the following day seeing the forces of the Banu Hashim advance and seize Bash-Karakol at the Safa corner near the Masjid al-Haram. On the third day, Hamidia, the Ottoman Government Office, was captured together with the Deputy Governor. While in captivity, the Deputy Governor directed his remaining Turkish troops to surrender, but they refused.

The Battle of Mecca in 1916 is widely regarded as marking the beginning of the end for the Ottoman Empire and as a catalytic moment in the reshaping of the Middle East during the Arab Revolt. In the aftermath, the Hashemite Kingdom of Hejaz was proclaimed with Mecca as its capital, and under Hashemite leadership its state gradually extended its influence northward in the region. The battle and its broader consequences left deep scars across the Middle East, contributing to a landscape in which Arab states would come under substantial European influence. Concurrently, the Ottoman caliphate dissolved and Palestine came under British administration, a turn of events that foreshadowed the eventual establishment of a Jewish state in the region. The Sharif of Mecca was eventually deposed by Ibn Saud, and the long-cherished plan for an Arabian state spanning from Yemen to Syria remained unrealized.

Tom Milne was a British film critic and writer who contributed to several major publications, including Sight & Sound, the Monthly Film Bulletin, The Observer, and The Times. In the 1960s he held roles as associate editor of Sight & Sound and as editor of the Monthly Film Bulletin. Milne authored monographs in Thames & Hudson's Cinema One series on Joseph Losey (1968) and Rouben Mamoulian (1969), with the Losey volume incorporating extended interviews with the filmmaker. He wrote a concise study on the Danish director Carl Theodor Dreyer (1971). Milne also edited and translated an anthology collecting interviews and writings on Jean-Luc Godard (1972).

Following his wartime service, Milne studied English and French at the University of Aberdeen, and later pursued further studies at the Sorbonne. He developed an interest in theatre and contributed writings to the magazine Encore, a publication that operated for a decade from 1954 to 1965.

The Hall of Fame section at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is located on the museum's third floor and includes The Power of Rock Experience. The Power of Rock Experience presents a film by Jonathan Demme, one of his final works, shown in the Connor Theater and featuring musical highlights from various Hall of Fame induction ceremonies. From there, visitors move to the fourth floor, where the Foster Theater, a state-of-the-art 3-D venue used for special events and programs, is located.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, a two-night celebration was staged at Madison Square Garden in New York on October 29–30, 2009. The concerts featured a wide-ranging lineup spanning multiple generations, including Jerry Lee Lewis, U2, Patti Smith, Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band, Simon & Garfunkel, Dion DiMucci, Metallica, James Taylor, Bonnie Raitt, Fergie, Mick Jagger, Lou Reed, Ray Davies, Ozzy Osbourne, Paul Simon, Jeff Beck, Buddy Guy, Aretha Franklin, Stevie Wonder, Sting, Little Anthony & the Imperials, and Crosby, Stills and Nash. The first evening extended to nearly six hours and was closed by Springsteen and the E Street Band, who were joined by special guests John Fogerty, Darlene Love, Tom Morello, Sam Moore, Jackson Browne, Peter Wolf, and Billy Joel.

Fred Guy was born in Burkeville, Virginia, and raised in New York City. He played guitar and banjo with Joseph C. Smith's Orchestra before joining Duke Ellington's Washingtonians in the early 1920s. In the early 1930s he shifted from banjo to guitar and remained with Ellington's orchestra until 1949. After retiring, he moved to Chicago and ran a ballroom for twenty years. He died by suicide in 1971.

During World War II, Bucharest endured two major bombing campaigns. The first operation began on April 4, 1944, and consisted of 17 aerial bombardments over roughly four months, conducted by the United States Army Air Forces and the Royal Air Force, involving about 3,640 bombers and 1,830 fighters. Civilian casualties from this campaign included 5,524 killed, 3,373 injured, and 47,974 left homeless. A second operation was carried out by the German Luftwaffe from August 23 to 26, 1944, in retaliation for Romania's change of sides after the fall of Ion Antonescu's regime.

During World War II, Bucharest endured a series of aerial bombardments conducted largely by Allied air forces, aimed at disrupting rail networks and targets connected to the Oil Campaign, including railway facilities and oil infrastructure. After the 1944 coup d'état in Romania, Nazi Germany conducted bombing raids on the capital as part of its strategic operations in the region. The city also served as a storage and distribution hub for a substantial portion of the refined petroleum products produced at Ploiești, integrating the capital into the broader fuel supply chain.

Guia Lighthouse, situated on the Portuguese coast, sustained heavy damage to its tower in the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, necessitating extensive reconstruction and replacement of its equipment. In response to the disaster, the Marquis of Pombal ordered the construction of six new lighthouses to illuminate the coastline, and Guia was among the lighthouses commissioned.

The Guia Lighthouse, known in Portuguese as Farol da Guia, is an active lighthouse on the Portuguese coast. It is situated at Cabo da Guia, about two kilometres west of the centre of Cascais. The structure consists of an octagonal tower built in white masonry, topped by a red lantern. Its light has a range of 18 nautical miles.

Within the ISO 639 system, fifty newly designated collections, referred to as Families, were established exclusively in Set 5. Among these, one Family contains a regular group that already carries a code in Set 2. To ensure compatibility with Set 2, Set 5 collections may incorporate other sub-collections, provided they do not include the remainder groups.

ISO 639 comprises a family of related code sets whose design aims to preserve a consistent meaning for each code across sets, ensuring that a single code does not signify different concepts in different parts of the standard. The coverage of languages is not identical across the sets, and not all languages appear in every set. A language’s treatment varies depending on whether it is included in Set 1 or Set 2, whether Set 2 provides separate bibliographic and terminological codes, and whether the language is classified as a macrolanguage in Set 3. Additional variations in treatment arise from how languages and other elements are handled differently across the sets, reflecting their distinct purposes and structures.

Glenn Danzig, an American musician and songwriter, began his professional career in the mid-1970s. Throughout his career he has explored a spectrum of genres, primarily rooted in punk rock and heavy metal, while incorporating influences from industrial, blues, and classical music. In addition to his performances, Danzig has written songs for other artists, notably Johnny Cash and Roy Orbison.

Glenn Allen Anzalone, known professionally as Glenn Danzig, was born in Lodi, New Jersey, as the third of four sons. His father worked as a television repairman and was a United States Marine Corps veteran who served during World War II and the Korean War, while his mother worked at a record store. The family lived for a time in Revere, Massachusetts. From an early age, Danzig developed an interest in heavy metal, drawing early musical influences from Black Sabbath, the Ramones, Blue Cheer, and the Doors.

Acequia Park is a public park in San Antonio, Texas. The facility provides picnic tables and restrooms, and alcohol is not permitted. Its origins lie in the irrigation network established by Spanish missionaries in collaboration with mission Indians, drawing its water from the San Antonio River. In 1957 the San Antonio Conservation Society and other supporters purchased much of the park’s land to safeguard the area’s environment. Later, SACS and local landowners prevailed in a water-rights and water-flow suit against the San Antonio River Authority, which had proposed reconfiguring the river channel. In 1975 SACS transferred the property to the City of San Antonio with the explicit condition that it be maintained as a public park.

Carly Rae Jepsen first emerged in the public eye after auditioning for Canadian Idol in 2007, prompted by encouragement from her high school drama teacher and performing an original song titled "Sweet Talker." She finished in third place, an outcome later regarded as the most favorable attainable result for contestants on the show. A demo from the performance attracted music manager Jonathan Simkin, which led to a management deal with 604 Records later that year. In June 2008 she released her first promotional single, a cover of John Denver's "Sunshine on My Shoulders." Jepsen's debut studio album Tug of War arrived in September 2008 and sold about 10,000 copies in Canada. The singles "Tug of War" and "Bucket" reached the top 40 of the Canadian Hot 100 and received Gold certifications for shipments of roughly 40,000 units each. The final single from the project, "Sour Candy," was a duet with Josh Ramsay. In 2009 she toured western Canada with Marianas Trench and Shiloh.

Carly Rae Jepsen performed the lead role in the Broadway production of Rodgers and Hammerstein's Cinderella for a twelve-week engagement in the spring of 2014. In June of the same year, she and her co-writers Josh Ramsay and Tavish Crowe were honored with the SOCAN International Achievement Award.

Charles Blagden was born in Wotton-under-Edge, Gloucestershire, as the younger son of John Blagden (1715–1750) and Elizabeth Phelps (1716–1784), a family involved in the local textile industry. He later remarked that he was denied the advantages of public schooling or collegiate education in his youth. He pursued medical studies at the University of Edinburgh, where he earned the Doctor of Medicine degree in 1768. In 1772 he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society. He subsequently entered military service as an army surgeon in 1776 and served aboard the hospital ship HMS Pigot during the American War of Independence. After a period, he returned to a medical post in Plymouth in 1780. In late 1782 or early 1783 he moved to London to become an assistant and amanuensis to Henry Cavendish.

Sir Charles Brian Blagden, FRS (17 April 1748 – 26 March 1820), was an English physician and chemist who served as a medical officer in the Army from 1776 to 1780 and later as secretary of the Royal Society from 1784 to 1797. He was awarded the Copley Medal in 1788 and was knighted in 1792.

Biesdorf is an Ortsteil in the Berlin borough (Bezirk) of Marzahn-Hellersdorf in Germany. Prior to the 2001 administrative reform, it belonged to the former borough of Marzahn, after which it became part of the newly formed Marzahn-Hellersdorf. The German pronunciation of the name is [ˈbiːsˌdɔʁf].

Biesdorf, located in the eastern outskirts of Berlin, is bordered by the districts of Marzahn, Hellersdorf, and Kaulsdorf, as well as Friedrichsfelde, and by Karlshorst in the Lichtenberg district and Köpenick in the Treptow-Köpenick district. The highest point in the area, Biesdorfer Höhe, stands at 82 meters above mean sea level and is part of the Wuhletal park. The locality contains several lakes—Biesdorfer Baggersee, Dreiecksee, Wuhleteich, and Wuhlebecken—situated along the river Wuhle, which serves as the boundary with Kaulsdorf. A small portion of Tierpark and of Erholungspark Marzahn lies within Biesdorf.

Windows CardSpace is a native component of the Windows operating system, integrated into Windows 7 and Windows Vista. For Windows XP and Windows Server 2003, the feature is available through the .NET Framework 3.x package.

Windows CardSpace is a feature introduced with the .NET Framework 3.0. It runs on Windows XP, Windows Server 2003, and Windows Vista, and is installed by default on Windows Vista and Windows 7. For Windows XP and Windows Server 2003, it was made available as a free download via Windows Update. An updated version of CardSpace shipped with the .NET Framework 3.5. In Windows 7, the Credential Manager uses Windows CardSpace to manage and store saved user credentials.

Æthelburh of Barking, the sister of Earconwald, is associated with the establishment of a double monastery at Barking for her and a monastery at Chertsey for her brother. The Barking foundation is described as having occurred before Earconwald´s elevation to the see of London in 675. Traditional accounts assign Barking Abbey a founding date of 666, while Bede implies that Æthelburh led the Barking community during the plague of 664. Some charter evidence has been read as indicating an earlier origin, potentially in the window from 660 to 664.

According to a hagiographic account, a few days before Æthelburh's death, Tortgyth, a nun of Barking, witnessed a vision in which a figure was drawn up to heaven, the ascent accomplished by cords described as brighter than gold.

During the Battle of Veracruz in 1838, the French bomb vessels Cyclope and Vulcain took part in the naval bombardment. The two ships fired the majority of the shells employed by France, and their gunnery produced decisive hits on Mexican ammunition depots.

During the 1770s, the bomb vessels Racehorse and Carcass were reinforced and outfitted for a British Arctic expedition aimed at discovering a northern passage to the North Pole. The voyage did not reach its objectives and was not completed, largely due to the harsh ice conditions encountered in the Arctic. Among the crew was a young Horatio Nelson, who served as a midshipman aboard the Carcass during the mission, marking an early stage in his long naval career.

The company was founded in March 2000 under the name Sterlite Telecom Systems, with an initial focus on the production of telecommunication cables. By August 2000, it was renamed Sterlite Optical Technologies.

Sterlite Technologies entered into a memorandum of understanding with the Department of Electrical Engineering at IIT Madras in 2019 to support a professorship dedicated to 5G network research. Since 2020, the holder of the professorship has been teaching and conducting research on 5G technology. The collaboration merges IIT Madras’s research capabilities and domain knowledge with Sterlite Technologies’ industry expertise.

The Guangzhou Metro serves the city of Guangzhou, the capital of Guangdong Province in the People’s Republic of China. Operated by the state-owned Guangzhou Metro Corporation, the system was the fourth rapid transit network to be established on the Chinese mainland. In 2013 it carried about 1.99 billion rides, making it one of the busiest metro systems in the world.

Leonard Jack Martin (24 November 1901 – 25 December 1967) was a British sailor who took part in the 1936 Summer Olympics as a crew member of the British boat Lalage. Lalage won the gold medal in the 6 metre class at those Games.

In the historical rankings of German chancellors, neither Kurt Georg Kiesinger nor Angela Merkel appeared among the 100 most notable Germans. At the time cited in the ranking, Merkel was serving as the leader of the opposition.

Historical rankings of chancellors of Germany refer to systematic surveys that aim to evaluate and rank individuals who have served as Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany. These studies synthesize assessments of their leadership, measuring perceived success in office alongside levels of popularity among the public or within scholarly or political communities. The scope of the rankings encompasses all persons who have held the office of Chancellor within the Federal Republic of Germany since its founding in 1949.

Maddalena Salvetti Aceiaiuoli (25 March 1557 – 4 March 1610) was a noblewoman of the Grand Duchy of Tuscany who pursued poetry. Born into the Tuscan aristocracy, she lived during the late Renaissance and contributed verse to the region's literary culture.

Maddalena Aceiaiuoli was an Italian poet of the early seventeenth century. She authored the heroic epic Il David perseguitato o vero fuggitivo, which centers on the biblical king David. The work was dedicated to the Tuscan princess Maria Maddalena de’ Medici. The epic remained unfinished during Aceiaiuoli's lifetime, and it was published posthumously in 1611 following her death in 1610.

In 1943, following the Red Army’s initial advances into western Russia and northeastern Ukraine, several partisan formations commanded by Fedorov, Medvedev, and Saburov were redirected to central and western areas of Ukraine that remained under Nazi occupation. At the same time, partisans operating in the Leningrad and Kalinin regions, including the Pskov and Novgorod areas, carried out anti-German operations for up to three years before the Red Army liberated those territories.

Soviet partisans have become a controversial subject in several successor states of the former Soviet Union. In Latvia, Vasiliy Kononov, a former Soviet partisan, was prosecuted and convicted for war crimes against local civilians. The European Court of Human Rights subsequently upheld the conviction.

Baseball caps are used by some military units as part of field uniforms, though patrol caps remain more common and they are often worn with combat attire. Caps may bear a command insignia to indicate affiliation or, when worn by officers, display rank on the front. The color of the cap can denote a specific function or job, with red caps used to designate drill monitors in the US submarine force as an example. In the US Army, red caps identify parachute riggers while black caps are worn by parachute instructors. Within the USAF, civilian auxiliary squadrons issue squadron‑distinctive baseball caps to be worn with the Battle Dress Uniform, typically featuring squadron colors, numbers, and/or patches. Although BDUs have their own headgear, some squadrons use a patrol cap in M81 Woodland or other distinctive covers.

A variant of the baseball cap features a plastic mesh back and a foam front panel bearing a company logo. This style is known as a trucker hat, and it is also referred to as a "gimme hat" because it is frequently distributed as a promotional item at no cost.

No More Parties in LA received generally positive notices from critics evaluating The Life of Pablo, with attention focused on its production, performance, and lyrical wit. Tom Thorogood of The Line of Best Fit credited the beat with a strong sense of propulsion that carries the track to an impressive result. David Edwards of Under the Radar described how the song moves around the Suzie Thundertussy sample, revealing a darker urban underside. AllMusic’s David Jeffries highlighted Kendrick Lamar’s vocal contribution alongside Madlib’s production and the Morrison/Graham samples to create a smooth, rolling soulful feel. The music site Xcel noted that Madlib’s suitably abstract beat allows West and Lamar to trade verses effectively. Alexis Petridis of The Guardian called the track funny and smart, praising its sharp lines and verses within the album’s context. Greg Tate of Spin called it the album’s sole duet, arguing that West shows enough energy to stand with another artist without needing a guest to carry the track.

No More Parties in LA is a 2016 track that drew extensive year-end recognition and commentary from a range of outlets. Reactor 105.7 FM ranked it 78th among the year's best songs, while The Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll placed it 66th with eight mentions, tying for 66th with nine other songs. Pitchfork ranked it 32nd for 2016, with critic Raymond Cummings describing the track as a potential example of West’s most urgently scatterbrained banger and praising the performances of West and Lamar. In the Reader's Poll for Top 50 Songs of 2016, it finished 16th, and HipHopDX placed it 13th; Treblezine gave it its highest ranking, at seventh. Complex highlighted West’s verse as among the year's top twenty, with reviewer Ross Scarano characterizing the verse as a long, unrelenting stretch that unfurls with Forrest Gump‑style momentum and noting its combination of spite, humor, candor, paternal tone, intoxication, and lust. Bustle's Jack O'Keeffe suggested the track could be West's best chance to win the Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance at the 59th ceremony. The song was not nominated in any category at the 2017 Grammys, which critic Sam Rullo described as a snub.

Held in July 1970 in Italy, the tournament was organized by the Federation of Independent European Female Football (FIEFF). It was titled Coppa del Mondo in Italian and carried the Martini & Rossi Cup as its sponsored name. The competition brought together women's teams from seven countries and is the first known tournament to be named a women's football World Cup.

Following the 1970 edition, the 1971 Women's World Cup was held in Mexico. From 1981 to 1988, five Mundialito tournaments took place in Japan and Italy. After the Mundialito series, the 1988 FIFA Women's Invitation Tournament was staged in China, and the subsequent 1991 FIFA Women's World Cup was also hosted in China.

Kayumzhan Sharipov is a Kyrgyz footballer who was regarded as one of the standout players for Kyrgyzstan during the 2014 AFC Challenge Cup qualifiers. He started in two matches and came on as a substitute in another. Sharipov contributed to a 1–0 victory over Pakistan by assisting David Tetteh on the winning goal.
Kayumzhan Sharipov earned his first cap for the Kyrgyzstan national team in 2011, during the qualification campaign for the 2014 FIFA World Cup, with his debut coming in a match against Uzbekistan.

Federation of Socialist Parties from Romania was a short-lived political federation in the Romanian political landscape of the early 1920s. In the 1922 parliamentary elections, it secured a solitary seat in the Chamber of Deputies. The federation did not contest any further elections. In 1927, it was succeeded by the Romanian Social Democratic Party, marking the end of its organizational existence.
The Federation of Socialist Parties from Romania, known in Romanian as Federația Partidelor Socialiste din România (FPSR), was a political alliance in Romania.

In 2013, Pitchfork TV released a one-hour documentary directed by RJ Bentler that examines Belle and Sebastian's 1996 album If You're Feeling Sinister as well as the band's formation and early releases. The film features interviews with all members who contributed to the album and includes archival photographs and video footage from the group's early days. Later that year, the band issued a second compilation, The Third Eye Centre, which gathers B-sides and rarities released after Push Barman to Open Old Wounds, spanning material from Dear Catastrophe Waitress, The Life Pursuit, and Write About Love. In late 2013, Mick Cooke confirmed he had left the band on amicable terms.

There's Too Much Love is a song by Belle and Sebastian that forms a prominent part of the soundtrack for the 2014 Brazilian film The Way He Looks, which centers on a blind, gay teenage boy and his friends.

Non-governmental organizations and human rights advocates have documented individual rights violations in Laos. A notable case involves three men arrested in 1990 for voicing concerns about government policies and advocating economic and political reforms. Two former government officials were imprisoned for expressing dissenting political views and were released in October 2004, while the third dissident who was sentenced with them died in prison in 1998. International human rights groups publicized these cases, underscoring ongoing concerns about political freedoms and the treatment of dissent in the country.

Human rights in Laos have been influenced by the plight and displacement of the Hmong community. Estimates indicate that up to 200,000 Hmong were exiled to Thailand, with a portion later resettling in the United States. During the ensuing decades, a number of Hmong fighters remained hidden in the mountains of Xiangkhouang Province. A remnant of these fighters emerged from the jungle in 2003.

As of March 2018, Celcom reported a notable enhancement in its network performance. The 4G service coverage reached 88 percent of the population, while the 4G LTE-Advanced network extended to 76 percent.

Yoodo is a service operated by Celcom that provides a highly customizable mobile experience. It enables users to assemble their own plans to match personal needs by adjusting data, voice calls, and SMS allowances, and it offers optional add-ons to enhance the service as desired.

On 18 April 2007, the renovation of Terminal 1 at Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (formerly Ferihegy) was awarded a Europa Nostra prize, Europe’s most prestigious heritage preservation award. The prize was conferred jointly by the European Commission and Europa Nostra and acknowledged the contributions of designers, contractors, builders, and investors (BA). It recognized the restoration of protected monument spaces within Terminal 1, including the central hall, the gallery, and the furniture.

Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport marked a notable milestone in 1993 when Malév operated Hungary’s first international service from Budapest to New York–Newark with a layover in Rome. Forecasts for the new millennium suggested that the existing two terminals, which then handled around four million passengers annually, would not be adequate for growing demand. As a result, construction of Terminal 2B began in 1997, and the facility opened in 1998, offering more than 30,000 square metres of space and a newly built apron. At the time of its opening, all foreign airlines were relocated to Terminal 2B. The terminal is designed to accommodate about 3.5 million passengers per year and features seven gates along with five remote stands.

In 2017, IMDb updated its advanced view, renaming it Reference view. The feature is now accessible by appending /reference to the end of a title’s URL; for instance, https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2358891/reference. In addition, former /combined URLs were redirected to the newer /reference URLs to maintain accessibility for existing links and bookmarks.

Hoang v. Amazon.com, Inc. (2011) involved an anonymous actress who sued IMDb after the site publicly disclosed her age (40) without consent, arguing that such disclosure could jeopardize her acting opportunities. U.S. District Judge Marsha J. Pechman of the Western District of Washington dismissed the complaint for lack of grounds to proceed in its anonymous form. The plaintiff later disclosed her identity as Huong Hoang of Texas, who uses the stage name Junie Hoang, and refiled the action. In 2013, Pechman dismissed all claims except a breach-of-contract theory against IMDb, and a jury subsequently ruled in IMDb’s favor on that remaining claim. The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s judgment in March 2015.

During the 117th Congress, Don Young, who had represented Alaska's at-large congressional district since 1973, was the dean of the U.S. House of Representatives. He died on March 18, 2022, and his body lay in state at the U.S. Capitol on March 29, 2022.

At the outset of the 117th Congress, the Senate was controlled by Republicans. On January 20, 2021, three newly sworn-in Democratic senators—Jon Ossoff and Raphael Warnock from Georgia and Alex Padilla from California—joined the chamber. After their swearing-in, the Senate's composition stood at 50 Republicans, 48 Democrats, and two independents who caucus with the Democrats, effectively producing a 50–50 split. This evenly divided configuration had not occurred since the 107th Congress in 2001, and it represented only the third time in U.S. history that the Senate was evenly split, as well as the longest-lasting instance of such a division.

Throughout World War II, the Allied effort benefited from notable participation by people of Mexican origin. Approximately 300,000 Mexican citizens worked in the United States, taking positions in farms and factories to sustain wartime production and supply chains. Additionally, roughly 15,000 U.S. nationals of Mexican origin and Mexican residents in the United States enlisted in the U.S. Armed Forces, serving on multiple fronts around the world. These labor migrations and military service illustrate the cross-border connections that underpinned Allied capabilities during the conflict.

During May and June 1940, the Battle of France ended in the defeat of the Allies and contributed to the collapse of the French Third Republic. Following the campaign, German forces occupied the northern and western portions of the country, paving the way for the creation of a rump government known as Vichy France. This regime subsequently received diplomatic recognition from the Axis powers and from many neutral states, including the United States.

The Green Party of Vancouver fielded nine candidates in the municipal election, with Carr, Fry, and Wiebe elected to the city council, and all of the party's school and parks board candidates winning election.

The Green Party of Vancouver has marked several early milestones in municipal politics. Roslyn Cassells became the first Green elected to public office in Canada when she won a seat on the Vancouver Park Board in the 1999 municipal election. Andrea Reimer was elected as a Vancouver School Board trustee in 2002. In 2008, Stuart Mackinnon was elected as a Park Board commissioner, expanding the party’s representation on Vancouver’s Park Board.

The 1984 Volvo Grand Prix was the professional tennis circuit for that year, serving as the principal tour for male players. It integrated the four Grand Slam championships with the regular Grand Prix tournaments into a unified seasonal calendar. In addition, the circuit included two team events, the World Team Cup and the Davis Cup, which were incorporated into the overall program.

The Council of Science Editors traces its origins to 1957, when the National Science Foundation and the American Institute of Biological Sciences established it. It was first named the Conference of Biology Editors (CBE). In 1965, it was incorporated as the Council of Biology Editors, and its membership was broadened to encompass the full range of scientific publishing activities, from science editors to copy editors. On January 1, 2000, the organization adopted its current name, the Council of Science Editors.

The Council of Science Editors (CSE) is steered by a volunteer board of directors, with its work augmented by several committees that support governance and activities. The organization is administered through a management arrangement with Riggs Enterprise Corp, which handles the operational functions of CSE. Riggs Enterprise Corp is based in New Jersey, serving as the entity responsible for the organization’s administrative management.

Within Thailand, the Governor of Bangkok is the country’s sole elected governor, serving a four-year term that is renewable. The gubernatorial election is conducted on a separate cycle from elections for district councils and the Bangkok Metropolitan Council (BMC). The most recent election for the Bangkok governor took place in 2022.

Following the 2014 military coup, Thailand’s Senate comprised 250 members who were not elected by voters but appointed. The appointments were carried out by the National Council for Peace and Order (NCPO), the military junta that governed the country from 2014 until the 2019 general election. The 2017 constitution did not provide for Senate elections, ensuring that the upper house remained an appointed body under the post-coup constitutional framework.

Change.org operates a public platform for petition campaigns, including a catalog of petitions that have attracted 1.5 million or more signatures. The minimum signature threshold on the site is 1.5 million, a benchmark used to indicate highly supported petitions. Users can verify the status and view details of such petitions on the Change.org website, where pages display current signature counts and related information. Because Wikipedia does not provide external links to Change.org as a general reference, no direct link to the site is included in this article.

Against the backdrop of repeated assaults on medical professionals in India, Dr. Sumit Periwal of Gangtok launched a Change.org petition to raise awareness of the issue. The campaign argues for greater protections for doctors and highlights concerns about security gaps and a perceived absence of deterrence among those who commit violence. The petition has attracted more than two million signatures to date.

Since 1978, historians have questioned the insularity of the traditional portrayal of Richard I, arguing that his reign was conducted within a wider dynastic and international context rather than being confined to English affairs. Gillingham contends that Richard I was the head of a dynasty with responsibilities extending beyond England, indicating a broader political role. In evaluating a ruler's political acumen, scholars emphasize giving greater weight to contemporary opinions over later historical judgments to avoid anachronistic biases.

In March 1199, while campaigning in the Limousin to suppress the revolt of Aimar V, Viscount of Limoges, Richard I ravaged the viscount’s lands with fire and sword despite the observances of Lent. He then laid siege to the small, virtually undefended castle of Châlus-Chabrol. Some chroniclers later claimed that the siege was provoked by a local peasant’s discovery of a hidden hoard of Roman gold, suggesting a possible motive for the assault.

Oil well design involves balancing and integrating numerous elements, including geology, reservoir objectives, drilling technology, casing and cementing schemes, and safety considerations. The planned well path and technical design frequently undergo several cycles of revision as new data, modeling results, and risk assessments inform adjustments. Only after these iterative refinements are completed is the overall plan finalized, providing the basis for the execution phase of the drilling program.

Oil fields near Baku, on the western shore of the Caspian Sea in Azerbaijan, were exploited from the 9th century to produce naphtha for use in the petroleum industry. In the 13th century, Marco Polo described these wells, noting outputs that amounted to hundreds of shiploads. During his 1264 voyage to Baku, he observed oil emanating from natural seeps and recorded a fountain of abundant oil near Geirgine, which, he claimed, could yield about a hundred shiploads at a time. These early practices illustrate the region's long history of petroleum extraction preceding modern industrial methods.

Clay minerals are typically formed through extended chemical weathering of silicate-bearing rocks, though local formation can also occur via hydrothermal processes. The predominant weathering mechanism is acid hydrolysis, which arises from the limited presence of carbonic acid in rainwater and from acids released by plant roots. This acidic action cleaves the bonds between aluminium and oxygen in the mineral structure, releasing other metal ions and silica that can organize as a gel of orthosilicic acid.

Clay is a natural material characterized by fine particles that become plastic when wet and can be fired to form a hard ceramic. It is among the oldest known ceramic substances, with prehistoric societies exploiting its properties for pottery; some of the earliest pottery sherds are dated to roughly 14,000 BCE. Clay tablets also represent one of the earliest media used for writing. In contemporary industry, clay plays a role in papermaking, cement manufacture, and filtration processes in chemical production. A substantial portion of the global population lives in or works in buildings constructed of clay or brick, frequently serving as load-bearing structures. In agriculture, the clay fraction of soil is a key determinant of arability: although clay-rich soils often suffer from poor drainage, they can be more fertile because of a higher cation-exchange capacity.

Eric Jelen (born 11 March 1965) is a German former professional tennis player. He captured one singles title, achieved in Bristol in 1989, and earned five doubles titles during his professional career.

Eric Jelen is a former German professional tennis player who played right-handed. He reached a career-high ATP singles ranking of world No. 23 on 7 July 1986. Jelen contributed to West Germany's Davis Cup victories in 1988 and 1989, partnering with Boris Becker in the doubles in the 1988 final to defeat Sweden and again securing the doubles rubber in the 1989 final to defend the title against Sweden.

Shaun of the Dead's score, composed by Pete Woodhead and Daniel Mudford, functions as a pastiche that nods to the soundtracks of Italian zombie cinema, particularly the work of Goblin and Fabio Frizzi. The music includes several cues drawn from Romero's Dawn of the Dead, which himself had sourced material from the De Wolfe production music library. An assistant editor's acquaintance maintained a library of zombie-film music to aid in locating suitable material. Wright and Pegg also assembled a preproduction mixtape of tracks they wished to license. During editing, Goblin cues were used as a temporary reference, and their strong tonal character ultimately prompted the filmmakers to obtain clearance for their inclusion in the final score.

During the crisis, the group seeks refuge in the Winchester pub, with the undead pursuing Shaun there. Ed inadvertently attracts the zombies by activating the pub’s slot machine. Inside, Shaun fights the surrounding horde, including the pub’s zombified owner. The Winchester rifle mounted above the bar—an item Shaun and Ed had quarreled over—proves to be functional. Barbara reveals she has been bitten and dies shortly after offering her blessing to Liz and Shaun’s relationship. David attempts to shoot Barbara; Shaun intercedes, accusing David of harbouring hatred for him and being in love with Liz. Dianne confirms that David is indeed in love with Liz. Barbara becomes a zombie, forcing Shaun to shoot her, and Shaun’s confrontation with David subsequently escalates.

Turkey has gradually expanded its research and development capacity, with R&D expenditure as a share of GDP rising from 0.47% in 2000 to 1.40% in 2023, approximately half the OECD average. In scientific and technical publishing, the country ranks 16th worldwide in article output and 35th in the Nature Index.
