The Turkish Patent and Trademark Office is 21st worldwide in total patent applications and third in industrial design applications, with the vast majority of applicants being Turkish residents. Overall, Turkish residents rank 21st globally for patent applications across all patent offices. In the Global Innovation Index, Turkey is ranked 43rd in 2025. The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) functions as one of the principal agencies funding and conducting research.

In December 2021, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan urged expanding the official usage of Türkiye, contending that the name best represents the culture, civilization, and values of the Turkish nation. In May 2022, the Turkish government formally requested that Türkiye be used in English by the United Nations and other international organizations, and the United Nations subsequently agreed to adopt Türkiye in its English-language communications.

According to the 2020 Census Bureau data, Washington, D.C. had a racially and ethnically diverse population. Black or African American residents comprised 41.4% of the population, while White residents accounted for 39.6%—of which 37.9% were non-Hispanic White. Asian residents made up 4.9%, American Indian or Alaska Native 0.5%, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander 0.1%, Some Other Race 5.4%, and residents identifying with two or more races 8.1%. Hispanic or Latino individuals of any race represented 11.3% of the population.

Washington, D.C. is home to a native music genre known as go-go, a post-funk, percussion-driven variant of rhythm and blues that emerged in the area. The style rose to prominence in the late 1970s, largely due to the efforts of Chuck Brown, a prominent bandleader from the district who helped popularize the genre.

Municipal governments are organized local governments authorized by state constitutions and statutes to provide general government for a defined area. The territory they govern typically corresponds to a population center rather than a collection of areas within a county, and the category includes cities, boroughs (except in Alaska), towns (except in Minnesota and Wisconsin), and villages. This framework roughly mirrors the Census Bureau’s concept of incorporated places used for population and housing statistics, though New England towns are excluded from that category. The count of municipal governments excludes governmentally inactive places.

Town or township governments constitute a form of organized local government in the United States. They derive their authority from state constitutions and statutes, and they exist in twenty states located in the Northeastern and Midwestern regions. These governments are established to provide general governmental services for a defined territory, with the area typically based on a geographic subdivision of a county.

Single-phase electric power in North America is commonly distributed to homes and small commercial facilities via a three-wire, 240-volt system capable of roughly 100 kVA (about 417 A). In rural regions lacking a three-phase supply, households and farmers may install a phase converter to drive three-phase motors. Larger consumers—such as substantial buildings, shopping centers, factories, office blocks, and multi-unit apartments—typically receive three-phase service. In dense urban areas, network power distribution serves many customers through multiple distribution transformers, providing hundreds to thousands of kilovolt-amperes, with the load concentrated over a relatively small geographic area of a few hundred square meters.

Single-phase electric power, abbreviated 1φ, constitutes the most fundamental category of alternating current (AC) power. In such a system, voltages on conductors rise and fall in synchrony, yielding a single alternating waveform. This configuration is widely employed in residential and small commercial contexts, supporting common applications such as lighting, space heating, and the operation of small electrical appliances.

Minsk Arena speed skating hall features a 400-meter indoor track and is the first indoor speed skating venue in Belarus. The ice surface totals about 10,000 square meters, with roughly 5,000 square meters dedicated to the speed skating rink. Within the enclosure of the track lie two ice hockey fields—measuring 60 by 30 meters and 60 by 28 meters—and two curling fields. The facility also houses an altitude training room where air pressure is reduced and the oxygen content diminished, allowing training under altitude-like conditions.

In January 2016, Minsk-Arena hosted the European Speed Skating Championships, and in the same month it also hosted the Starladder i-League Season 13 esports tournament. The esports event featured competitive matches of Dota 2 and Counter-Strike: Global Offensive.

Liquid tire sealant is used in tubeless tires and can be injected to seal minor punctures, reducing the likelihood of rapid air loss. The practice has generated debate over its compatibility with Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS) sensors mounted inside the tire. Some sealant manufacturers assert that their products are compatible with TPMS sensors, while others warn that contact with the sealant can temporarily disable the sensor until it is cleaned, inspected, and reinstalled by a tire care professional. Additional questions about compatibility have been reported, and the use of such sealants may void the TPMS sensor warranty.

Tubeless tires are designed without an inner tube, allowing operation at lower air pressures than traditional tube-type tires. Their wider profile can reduce the likelihood of punctures compared with regular tube tires. The absence of an inner tube and the tubeless construction help limit air leakage by retaining air longer, giving drivers additional time to drive to a safe location. Punctures in tubeless systems are often easier to repair using a liquid sealant. Operating at higher inflation pressures can provide greater stability and ride comfort. In addition, the elimination of an inner tube reduces rolling resistance, contributing to improved fuel efficiency.

Anton Bruckner Private University for Music, Drama, and Dance is a higher education institution in Linz, located near the composer’s native town of Ansfelden. The institution was named after Anton Bruckner in 1932 and was known as the Bruckner Conservatory Linz until 2004. The Bruckner Orchestra Linz has likewise been named in his honor.

Anton Bruckner was a distinguished organist at St Florian's Priory, where he frequently improvised. Those improvisations were seldom transcribed, and as a result only a small number of his organ works have survived. In the Präludienbuch, five preludes in E-flat major—dated 1836–1837 and assigned the designations WAB 127 and WAB 128—are generally regarded as probably not by Bruckner, and a number of other WAB-unclassified pieces in the same manuscript are likewise considered unlikely to be his work.

Construction for the Yerevan Opera Theatre began with a ceremonial groundbreaking on 28 November 1930, marking the tenth anniversary of Soviet Armenia. The building was formally opened on 20 January 1933. A ballet company was established shortly after the theatre’s foundation to support its performing arts program. In 1935, the venue presented its first ballet production, Swan Lake, composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.

Since its opening, the Yerevan Opera Theatre has been a catalyst for the development of Armenian national operas and ballets. The theatre's first Armenian ballet was Happiness, composed by Aram Khachaturian, and Khachaturian soon expanded Happiness into Gayane, a work that has been performed worldwide. In addition, numerous Armenian composers have written operas and ballets for the institution. Notable artists associated with the theatre include singers Gohar Gasparyan, Tatevik Sazandaryan, Mihran Yerkat, Pavel Lisitsian, Haykanoush Danielyan, Nar Hovhannisyan, Gegham Grigoryan, Anahit Mekhitarian; conductors Konstantin Sarajev, Michael Tavrizyan, Aram Katanyan, Karen Durgaryan, Gianluca Marciano, Yuri Davtyan; ballet masters A. Petrosyan, M. Chmshkyan, Vanoush Khanamirian, Vilen Galstyan, Rudolf Kharatyan; and painters Martiros Saryan, Minas Avetisyan.

Part 7 of ISO 898 provides torsional test procedures for bolts and screws. It applies to fasteners with a nominal diameter of up to 10 mm and is restricted to short bolts and screws whose nominal diameter lies within the 3 to 10 mm range.

Part 3 of ISO 898 specifies the mechanical and physical properties of flat washers, establishing the characteristics required for these components within fastening systems. Flat washers are designed for use in bolted joints and are intended to be employed together with other fasteners.

The Journal of Psychohistory is a quarterly scholarly publication that seeks to offer a fresh psychological interpretation of world events, spanning both historical and contemporary contexts. Its scope encompasses childhood and family dynamics, with particular attention to child abuse; psychobiography that relies on extensive material from early life; political psychology; and psychological investigations into anthropological questions.

The Journal of Psychohistory is an academic journal established in 1973 within the field of psychohistory. It was edited by Lloyd deMause and published by the Institute for Psychohistory (IP). The publication began under the name History of Childhood Quarterly, and in 1976 it was renamed to its current title, The Journal of Psychohistory.

Google App Engine requires users to sign in with a Google account to begin using the service. A Google account can register up to 25 free applications, whereas there is no limit on the number of paid applications that may be registered under the same account.

Google App Engine includes the Google Cloud Datastore, a storage service that uses a SQL-like query language named GQL (Google Query Language). GQL lacks the join capability found in traditional SQL, meaning joins cannot be performed within a single query. To model relationships such as one-to-many and many-to-many, developers typically use ReferenceProperty, which stores references to related entities to express associations.

During the Yom Kippur War of 1973, Admiral Ze'ev Almog stated that the Israeli Navy escorted tanker shipments from the Gulf to the port of Eilat, and that Israeli tankers sailing from Iran were directed to circumvent the Red Sea, moves that, along with the unsuccessful Egyptian Mediterranean blockade, helped sustain deliveries of oil, grain, and weapons to Israeli ports for much of the conflict. A postwar survey claimed that Israel did not suffer oil shortages during the war and even sold oil to third countries affected by the Arab oil embargo. This assessment was disputed by Edgar O'Ballance, who argued that no oil reached Israel during the blockade and that the Eilat–Ashdod pipeline remained empty by the war's end.

On 7 October, the opening day of the Yom Kippur War, Egyptian missile boats targeted Israeli positions along the Sinai coast, firing on Mediterranean sites at Rumana, Ras Beyron, Ras Masala, and Ras Sudar, and hitting the Red Sea outpost at Sharm el-Sheikh. In addition, Egyptian frogmen conducted raids on Bala'eem oil installations, disabling the drilling equipment. That same day saw several small naval engagements, including the Battle of Latakia and the Battle of Marsa Talamat, both of which ended in Israeli victories. The Battle of Latakia involved a clash between Israeli and Syrian missile boats and is noted as the first naval engagement fought exclusively with missiles and electronic deception, culminating in the sinking of all Syrian missile boats.

Thornton Wilder, an American writer, authored The Bridge of San Luis Rey (1927), a novel that centers on a group of unrelated individuals who perish when a Peruvian bridge collapses. The work engages with philosophical questions about why misfortune befalls those who seem innocent or undeserving, and it was awarded the Pulitzer Prize in 1928. In 1998, the editors of the Modern Library named it among the 100 best novels of the twentieth century. The book gained additional exposure when British Prime Minister Tony Blair cited it at the 2001 memorial service for the victims of the September 11 attacks, and its popularity has grown substantially since then. Widely regarded as the progenitor of the modern disaster epic in literature and film, it interweaves the victims’ lives through a single catastrophe and uses flashbacks to explore events leading up to the disaster.

After Wilder died, Samuel Steward claimed that he had sexual relations with him, a contention raised six years posthumously. In 1937 Gertrude Stein provided Steward with a letter of introduction to Wilder. Steward later asserted that Alice B. Toklas told him Wilder liked him and that a Zürich night walk helped him complete the third act of Our Town, which opens with a crowd in a rainy cemetery. Penelope Niven disputes Steward's account, arguing that Wilder worked on the third act over several months and had completed it before he first met Steward. In a 2013 New Yorker review of Niven's biography, Robert Gottlieb claimed Wilder was infatuated with an unidentified man whose feelings were not reciprocated, and criticized Niven's handling of Wilder's sexuality, suggesting Wilder's interest in women was nonsexual and aligned with Steward's latent-homosexual view. Scholarly opinions on Wilder's sexuality remain disputed and nuanced.

Within the relativistic framework developed by Albert Einstein, reference frames are the constructs that specify how a moving observer relates to the phenomena being observed. The observational frame of reference denotes a frame in which the observer is at rest, although the spatial origin need not coincide with the observer’s position. In such a context, the time coordinate is frame-dependent and undergoes transformation between observers in relative motion. This feature stands in contrast to Galilean relativity, where the temporal coordinate is treated as the same for all inertial frames, effectively constituting absolute time.

Brading and Castellani broaden the traditional notion of a reference frame by moving beyond simple space-time coordinate charts to the use of generalized coordinates. This approach treats the description of physical systems as dependent on variables that need not be tied to a particular space-time grid, aligning with the language of both the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations. Generalized coordinates thereby provide a versatile and unifying mathematical framework that applies across diverse areas, including quantum field theory, classical relativistic mechanics, and quantum gravity, where dynamical variables may extend beyond standard space-time components and require a more flexible descriptive apparatus.

Acre Time was reinstated in late 2013 after having been abolished for more than five years. It is used in Brazil's far-western tip, encompassing the entire state of Acre and the southwestern portion of Amazonas west of the line joining Tabatinga and Porto Acre. These areas comprise about 4% of Brazil's territory (roughly the size of Germany) and contain about 0.5% of the country's population, a little over one million people.

Acre Time refers to a daylight saving regime in Brazil that advanced clocks by one hour, from 00:00 on the first Sunday in November to 00:00 on the third Sunday in February. If Carnival fell on the third Sunday in February, the period was postponed by one week. The rule was implemented only in the South, Southeast, and Central-West regions, which account for approximately 65 percent of the population. When DST was in effect, Brasília time shifted from UTC−03:00 to UTC−02:00. States that did not observe the DST still synchronized with Brasília time, effectively adopting the UTC−02:00 offset during that interval.

In the federal Parliament of Australia, Queensland is allocated 30 of the 151 seats in the House of Representatives, a distribution reflecting its population size. Queensland also holds 12 of the 76 seats in the Senate, a level of representation that arises from the constitutional rule of equal representation for each state in the upper house.

Queensland will host the 2032 Summer Olympics in Brisbane, marking the third occasion that Australia has staged the Games, following Melbourne in 1956 and Sydney in 2000. The state also hosts a number of major recurring sporting events, including the Gold Coast 600 (a motorsport race held on the Gold Coast since 1994); the Gold Coast Marathon (an athletics event on the Gold Coast since 1979); the NRL All Stars Game (a rugby league match held on the Gold Coast since 2010); the Townsville 400 (a motorsport event in Townsville since 2009); the Quicksilver Pro and Roxy Pro (leading surfing competitions); and the Australian PGA Championship (a golf tournament held since 2000).

Confucian teachings, values, and practices permeated East Asian societies, exerting a lasting influence on political, educational, and social life. The impact was strongest in Korea, Japan, and Vietnam, where Confucian thought helped shape education systems, informed the selection of civil servants, and guided prevailing norms of ethical and social relations within both public institutions and everyday interactions.

In 498 BCE, Duke Ding of Lu ordered an assault on the city of Cheng with the aim of razing its walls, but the siege failed to achieve its objective. The setback hindered Confucius from implementing his envisioned reforms, including restoring the duke’s legitimate authority. Within Lu, he encountered powerful opposition, especially from Viscount Ji Huan, whose influence grew in part due to Confucius’s own successes. According to sources such as Zuo Zhuan and Records of the Grand Historian, Confucius left Lu in 497 BCE after supporting a failed attempt to dismantle the fortifications of the Ji, Meng, and Shu clans. He departed without resigning, effectively entering self-imposed exile and finding it impossible to return while Viscount Ji Huan remained alive.

Early gliders were hazardous as designers lacked a full understanding of the aerodynamic principles underlying bird wings. Beginning in the 1880s, advances in technology and science produced the first truly practical gliders, with John Joseph Montgomery in the United States cited as an early example of such development. In the 1890s, Otto Lilienthal built a series of controllable gliders and achieved ridge soaring, gathering extensive empirical data through systematic experimentation. His rigorously documented work influenced many later designers and established him as a prominent figure among the early aviation pioneers. Lilienthal's aircraft employed a weight-shift method of control, a configuration that bears a clear resemblance to modern hang gliders.

Hang gliders rely on variometers, compact electronic instruments that measure vertical airspeed to distinguish sustained ascent from descent when encountering thermals; although pilots may sense initial acceleration, persistent vertical motion is often difficult to judge without such a device. A variometer provides climb or sink rates through audible signals and a visual display. Generally electronic and varying in sophistication, variometers commonly integrate an altimeter and an airspeed indicator, with more advanced models adding a barograph for flight data recording and, in some cases, a built-in GPS. The primary function is to assist pilots in locating and remaining within the thermal core to maximize altitude gain, while also indicating sinking air so rising air can be sought. In addition, variometers can compute the optimal speed to fly between thermals according to MacCready theory for specific conditions, and some units automatically perform these calculations by accounting for the glider’s glide ratio, altitude, hook-in weight, and wind direction.

A merlon is the upright solid element of a crenellated parapet on medieval fortifications, forming the barrier between the adjacent openings known as crenels. Merlons may be pierced by narrow vertical slits for observation and firing, often described as embrasures or tooth-like openings. The space between two merlons is called a crenel. A sequence of merlons and crenels constitutes a crenellation, the distinctive battlement pattern of such walls. In later periods, crenels designed to accommodate artillery were sometimes referred to as embrasures.

The word merlon has a contested etymology, with several plausible origins proposed. It appears in French around 1704 as an adaptation of the Italian merlone, and it may also be a shortened form of mergola. Other theories connect the term to the Latin mergae, meaning “two-pronged pitchfork.” Another possibility derives from the diminutive moerulus, formed from murus or moerus, both referring to a wall. A further suggestion traces medieval Latin merulus (late 10th century) as a diminutive of merle, the Latin for “blackbird,” aligning the imagery with a bird perched on a wall. Each hypothesis reflects distinct linguistic pathways by which the term could have come to denote the architectural feature.

Within the Saddlebunch Keys, Bay Point is a small community situated just east of Big Coppitt Key and Shark Key, and west of Sugarloaf Shores. It has fewer than 500 residents and includes a county park and two stores. Bluewater Key lies immediately to the west of Bay Point and is home to fewer than 100 residents. A bike path connects Bay Point and Bluewater Key and continues on to Big Coppitt Key, linking the neighboring communities.

Pieter 'Piet' Aldrich (born 7 September 1965) is a South African former professional tennis player who specialized in doubles. He won two Grand Slam men's doubles titles, securing crowns at the Australian Open and the US Open. In doubles, he reached the world No. 1 ranking in 1990.

Pieter Aldrich is a former South African professional tennis player who achieved notable doubles success in 1990, when he and his partner Danie Visser, another South African, won the men’s doubles titles at the Australian Open and the US Open. The same year, the pair finished as runners-up in doubles at Wimbledon, underscoring their standing on the international doubles circuit.

The Ljungström rig features a two-sail configuration, with each sail controlled by its own independent sheet, allowing for separate trimming. Earlier models employed deck-mounted blocks in the aft section to guide the sheets. A later innovation introduced a vertical pole that raised the sheeting point by approximately one metre, altering the geometry of control. Some versions of the rig include a winch to assist with sheet handling.

In the Ljungström rig, the mast’s upper bearing sits at a deck-level bottleneck, a feature that locates the bearing at the junction of the mast segments. A bracket affixed to the deck’s upper surface secures the bearing in place, preventing the mast from rising off the lower support layer. This arrangement helps maintain the mast’s alignment and stability under load.

Under its governance, the council drafted a provisional constitution and approved chartering the local organization as the Alpha chapter of the national Phi Lambda Chi fraternity. The fraternity was established to serve students from regional and teaching colleges. Expansion followed with the addition of the Beta chapter at Northeastern State University in 1939 and the Gamma chapter at the University of Arkansas at Monticello in 1940.

Phi Lambda Chi is defined by its blue and gold colors, with the white carnation serving as its flower and the lion as its mascot, and its motto is Ever Onward. The fraternity’s coat of arms features two fierce lions flanking a central shield, which bears a Grecian helmet at the upper extremity and a scroll inscribed with the Greek name of the fraternity at the lower extremity. A diagonal bar crosses the shield, separating the eye in the upper right corner from the crossed sabers in the lower left corner.
Ibrahim Benjamin Traoré (born 16 September 1988) is an Ivorian former professional footballer who played as a midfielder. Following his retirement from playing, he has worked as a scout.

Ibrahim Traoré began his senior career in Ivory Coast with CO Korhogo and AS Tanda before signing with Libyan Premier League club Al-Ahly Benghazi in 2013. He then moved to Czech side Táborsko in 2014, competing in the Czech National Football League, the second tier of Czech football. After a breakout season in the 2015–16 campaign in the same division, Traoré transferred to Zlín in September 2016, joining the Czech First League club.

OAG, a provider of aviation data and analytical services, expanded its product lineup in 2012 with the launch of OAG Analyser, an online platform for examining airline schedules. The following year, the company introduced Traffic Analyser as a further element of its analytical suite, developed in collaboration with Travelport, a leading distributor and e-commerce provider for the global travel industry.

OAG (Official Aviation Guide of the Airways) began publication in February 1929 in the United States, presenting a directory of 35 airlines and 300 flights. In 1948, following a takeover of a rival publication, the September issue carried the OAG title for the first time. The company was founded in Chicago and relocated to Oak Brook, Illinois, in 1968. In the United Kingdom, the ABC World Airways Guide appeared in 1946, featuring maps and traveller tips, and would become part of the broader ABC/OAG publishing portfolio. After Reed Elsevier acquired OAG Inc. in 1993, which already owned ABC International, the ABC and OAG brands were integrated. The group expanded in 1992 with the acquisition of SRDS, an advertising rate information company from Macmillan Inc., a sister Maxwell company; SRDS was sold to a buyout firm in 1994. In August 1996, all products from the combined ABC and OAG businesses were rebranded under the OAG name.

The GPL linking exception is a provision that permits library code licensed under the GNU General Public License to be linked with non-GPL software without imposing the GPL’s terms on the resulting executable. Linking refers to the process of combining library code with application code to produce a single runnable artifact, which can occur during compilation or at run time. The Free Software Foundation explains that, in the absence of such an exception, software that links to GPL-licensed library code might have to be distributed only under a GPL-compatible license. Although there has been no court ruling directly testing the legality of the linking exception, settlements have occurred in cases involving alleged linking violations. The GNU Classpath license explicitly incorporates language reflecting the effect of the linking exception, illustrating its practical application within specific licenses.

Under the GNU Lesser General Public License, the linking exception applicable to libraries imposes more stringent conditions than the GNU Classpath license cited previously. Those who link software with the library must be permitted to modify the portions of the library that are used by their program. They must also be allowed to reverse engineer both their software and the library to facilitate debugging of the modifications.

Alfred, Lord Tennyson's religious beliefs defied conventional doctrine, tending toward agnosticism and pantheism or pandeism while integrating contemporary science within an unorthodox Christian framework that reflected a distinctly Victorian synthesis. This inward tension permeates his major works, with In Memoriam commonly read as affirming faith amid honest doubt, and Maud offering a critique of organized religion; Locksley Hall Sixty Years After condemns ecclesiastical hypocrisy by juxtaposing Christian love with the twin of heathen hate, while Becket explores how human uncertainty can shape religious defense of Heaven. His diary entries likewise indicate pantheistic leanings, and a biography by his son portrays him as an unconventional Christian, noting that on his deathbed he praised Giordano Bruno and Baruch Spinoza, with Bruno’s view of God described as resonant with aspects of Tennyson’s own thinking.

Alfred, Lord Tennyson's early poetry is marked by medievalist sensibilities and striking visual imagery, and his work would prove influential on the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. In 1848, Dante Gabriel Rossetti and William Holman Hunt compiled a list of admired literary figures, designating them as “Immortals,” a group that included Keats alongside Tennyson. This cross-pollination helped align Tennyson’s verse with PRB aims, as his poetry supplied subject matter for several of their paintings. In particular, The Lady of Shalott became a recurring painting subject for Rossetti and Hunt, and was subsequently interpreted by John William Waterhouse in three versions, as well as by Elizabeth Siddal.

General Electric's J85 turbojet was originally developed to power the McDonnell ADM-20 Quail decoy missile. The Quail was intended to be released from a B-52 in flight and to fly in formation with the bomber over extended distances. Its mission was to overwhelm ground-based SA-2 surface-to-air missile operators by presenting multiple decoy targets. Achieving this role required a compact engine capable of keeping pace with the jet bomber. In design terms, the propulsion system mirrored the approach of the Armstrong Siddeley Viper, in that it did not require extended life and could be manufactured using lower-quality materials.

The General Electric J85 is a small turbojet engine developed by General Electric. Its fit on the Quail test airframe proved successful, demonstrating the engine’s suitability for compact jet-powered aircraft. In a subsequent development, as with the Viper lineage, later J85 variants were produced using standard materials rather than specialized alloys. The engine powered a range of small jet aircraft, including the Northrop T-38 Talon, Northrop F-5, Canadair CT-114 Tutor, and Cessna A-37 Dragonfly. More recently, J85 powerplants have been used in Scaled Composites’ White Knight, the carrier aircraft for SpaceShipOne, as well as in the Me 262 Project’s reproduction aircraft.

Some observers contend that sexualized advertising is employed in mass media to promote breast cancer awareness through fundraising campaigns, with examples including “I Love Boobies” and “Save the Ta-tas.” This approach has angered and offended breast cancer survivors and older women, groups who are at higher risk, according to critics. Women with breast cancer contend that these campaigns imply that sexually attractive breasts are valued more highly than saving lives, a stance that many perceive as undermining the seriousness of the disease. The resulting messaging is described by opponents as devaluing women as human beings by reducing them to sexualized embodiments within a health initiative.

Exploitation of women in mass media examines how media representations reinforce patriarchal norms by shaping the self-perceptions of men and boys while presenting women primarily through feminine scripts. Across various media texts, femininity is portrayed in narrow, idealized forms that influence how women are treated, interacted with, and pursued in real life. Empirical research by Ward, Merriwether, and Caruthers shows that men who consume a higher amount of men's magazines and spend substantial time watching television are more likely to endorse stereotypical beliefs about women's submission and male dominance, and consequently regard women as sexual objects. These findings suggest a link between particular media consumption patterns and gendered attitudes that support exploitation and objectification.

Geophysicists who have made notable contributions to geophysics, regardless of whether the work was primarily in that field, are included in the list. The compilation acknowledges historical figures who laid the foundations of geophysics as well as contemporary researchers who advanced the discipline. It also notes major accolades associated with the field, including the Vetlesen Prize, which is widely regarded as the geosciences equivalent of a Nobel Prize; the William Bowie Medal, the highest honor of the American Geophysical Union; the Maurice Ewing Medal, the premier distinction of the Society of Exploration Geophysicists; and the Crafoord Prize in geosciences. In some cases, geophysicists have been recognized with general prizes such as the Nobel Prize and the Kyoto Prize, reflecting the broad impact of their work.
Marie Tharp (1920–2006) was an American geologist and oceanographic cartographer who, in collaboration with Bruce Heezen, produced the first scientifically based map of the Atlantic Ocean floor.

According to an interview, Lloyd Banks indicated that a music video for Start It Up would be filmed, although a specific shooting date had not been announced. On November 12, 2010, Banks was confirmed to be shooting his portion of the clip. The G-Unit Riderz were later confirmed via Twitter to appear in a cameo. However, given the challenges of coordinating multiple artists, there was speculation that the video might not come to fruition.

An official extended version of Start It Up was released on December 7, 2010. The extended edition remains essentially the same as the original track, but includes an additional verse performed by Pusha T.

Seeland is a town in the Salzlandkreis district of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Its name, meaning “lakeland,” is pronounced [ˈzeːlant]. The municipality lies to the northwest of Aschersleben. It was established on 15 July 2009 through the merger of the formerly independent communities Friedrichsaue, Frose, Hoym, Nachterstedt, and Schadeleben. Prior to the merger, these municipalities were part of the Verwaltungsgemeinschaft Seeland (collective municipality), which also included Gatersleben. Gatersleben joined Seeland in September 2010.

Peter Norton Computing was acquired by Symantec in 1990, after which it operated as a division within the parent company and was renamed the Peter Norton Computing Group. The business employed 115 people, with the majority of its staff retained by Symantec following the acquisition.

Peter Norton Computing experienced rapid growth in the mid-1980s, recording a milestone of one million dollars in revenue in 1984, the same year that Norton Utilities 3.0 was released. At that time the company operated with a small clerical staff of three while Peter Norton carried out software development, authored publications and manuals, and ran the business; packaging was the only task he did not perform. In July 1985, Brad Kingsbury was hired as the fourth employee and the first programmer, and shortly afterward John Socha, who would later write Norton Commander through 1989, joined the firm. From November 1985 to April 1986, Warren Woodford worked at Norton Computing and contributed to the creation of Norton Guides. Later in 1985, a business manager was hired to oversee day-to-day operations.

Marcello Nizzoli’s Olivetti period saw the creation of the MC 4S Summa, the first in Olivetti’s long series of calculating machines. Designed within Olivetti’s planning and research office, the project benefited from an environment that encouraged collaboration between artists and technicians and came to set the pattern for future ventures. Its development reflects an in-depth consideration of both technical and ergonomic aspects, including a focus on easy user-identification of parts, which contributed to a unified concept. The approach was grounded in careful analysis rather than an a priori formula.

Marcello Nizzoli, trained at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Parma and graduating in 1913, worked as a draughtsman in Milan until World War I, during which his cultural formation was notably influenced by Futurism, especially Fortunato Depero. In 1923 he earned recognition as a draughtsman at the Prima Esposizione Internazionale delle Arti Decorative in Monza. His design range broadened to include fashion accessories such as handbags and shawls, along with poster campaigns for Campari and Martini. In the fifteen years after the war he engaged with several avant-garde movements—Futurism, Cubism, the Viennese Secession, and Novecento Italiano—adapting them to appeal to middle-class tastes. His early Rationalist phase involved designing mannequins for Baldessari's Craja Café (1930) in Milan, a collaboration with Fausto Melotti. In 1931 he met Edoardo Persico; together with Persico and Giuseppe Pagano, Persico helped transform Casabella into a leading forum for architectural debate. Persico's theoretical approach complemented Nizzoli's practical orientation, and their collaboration produced some of the most significant artefacts of Italian Rationalism.

The Annuaire Pontifical Catholique published an extensive directory of titular sees and their holders, providing a detailed record of the titular bishops associated with each see. While regarded as a highly complete reference, the work itself did not claim to be flawless or exhaustive. It lists both the names of the sees and the bishops who bore the titles, with some entries dating back to the fourteenth century.

Established in 1622, the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith served as the principal body coordinating Catholic missionary activity. Its founding gave a strong boost to missionary work in China and Japan, and in other regions there was a substantial rise in the number of bishops. Those bishops were typically granted the titles of ancient, now-abandoned dioceses, later known as titular sees, allowing episcopal status without the assignment of a current diocese.

Microsoft released Windows Vista in January 2007, emphasizing enhanced security, new features, and a redesigned Aero user interface. Concurrently, Office 2007 was launched, introducing the Ribbon user interface. Strong sales of these products contributed to a record profit for 2007. On February 27, 2008, the European Union fined Microsoft €899 million ($1.4 billion) for non-compliance with the March 2004 judgment, related to charging rivals unreasonable prices for information about its workgroup and back-office servers. Microsoft stated that it was in compliance and argued that the fines concerned past issues that had since been resolved. In 2007 Microsoft also established a multi-core computing unit, following peers such as Sun Microsystems and IBM.

According to leaked NSA documents reported by The Guardian and The Washington Post in June 2013, Microsoft was alleged to be the first company to participate in the PRISM program. The disclosures were published in June 2013 and subsequently acknowledged by government officials. PRISM is described as a government program that enables covert access to the communications data of non-U.S. persons hosted by American service providers without warrants. Microsoft denied participation in the program.

Cho Se-whee (Korean: 조세휘; born June 14, 1991), also spelled Cho Se-hui, is a South Korean model and beauty pageant titleholder. She was crowned Miss Universe Korea in 2017, earning the right to represent South Korea at Miss Universe 2017.

Antonino Paternò Castello, Marchese di San Giuliano, was an Italian nobleman and politician elected to Parliament in 1882. He aligned with Sidney Sonnino and represented the conservatives of the old Historical Right. In the early decades of the 20th century his work concentrated on foreign policy amid a polarized environment dominated by the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente. He contended that Italy's national interests could be best advanced by maintaining a balance between the two competing blocs, rather than aligning exclusively with either side.

Antonino Paternò Castello, Marchese di San Giuliano, was an Italian statesman who shaped the foreign policy of the Kingdom of Italy in the early 20th century. He advocated maintaining friendly relations with France while continuing to honor Italy's commitments to Austria-Hungary and the German Empire. He held several high-level positions, serving as foreign minister from 1905 to 1906, ambassador to London from 1906 to 1909, ambassador to Paris from 1909 to 1910, and again as foreign minister from 1910 to 1914. A proponent of Italian colonial expansion, his diplomacy helped clear the way for Italy's occupation of Libya during the Italo-Turkish War (1911–1912). He also resisted Austria-Hungary's expansion in the Balkans and supported Italian economic penetration of Montenegro and Albanian independence.

Bildts is spoken in several towns in the region, including Sint Annaparochie, known in Bildts as Sint-Anne; Sint Jacobiparochie, called Sint-Jabik in Bildts; Vrouwenparochie, known as Froubuurt; Oudebildtzijl, rendered as Ouwe-Syl; Westhoek, referred to as De Westhoek; and Nij Altoenae. In Minnertsga, however, residents do not speak Bildts; they speak West Frisian. Minnertsga lies outside the polder area of the former Middelzee. In 1984, Minnertsga was incorporated into the municipality.

Bildts is a conservative Hollandic dialect spoken primarily in the majority of the former municipality Het Bildt in the Dutch province of Friesland. The dialect preserves linguistic features dating from around 1505, the period when the area was reclaimed from the sea. The reclamation was ordered by George, Duke of Saxony, and involved workers arriving from the Dutch provinces of Holland, Zeeland, and Brabant to undertake the project in Friesland. The apparent resemblance to modern Frisian stems from Frisian’s own development from the sixteenth century to the present.

LHDC, an acronym for Low Latency High-Definition Audio Codec, is a Bluetooth audio codec developed by Savitech. It is designed to enable high-resolution audio streaming over wireless connections and functions as a high-quality option within the Bluetooth Advanced Audio Distribution Profile (A2DP). The codec supports bitrates up to approximately 1,000 kilobits per second, offering a markedly higher throughput than the typical SBC codec, which is around 345 kbps in standard implementations.

LLAC, or Low Latency Audio Codec, also known as LHDC LL, is a variant of LHDC's high-definition wireless audio technology designed for reduced latency and incorporating an auto-detect gaming mode. Built on the LHDC framework, it targets low-latency performance suitable for interactive applications. Savitech reports an end-to-end latency of approximately 30 milliseconds. In terms of encoding parameters, LLAC offers bitrates of 400 and 600 kbps, supports up to 24-bit depth, and handles sample rates up to 48 kHz. A notable feature is that the transmitter requires no dedicated hardware, enabling use with standard transmitters.

For the 2024–25 season, UEFA Nations League A is comprised of sixteen national teams, including the twelve highest-ranked nations from the 2022–23 League A standings. The remaining four places are filled by teams promoted from the 2022–23 League B.

UEFA Nations League A is the top division of the 2024–25 UEFA Nations League, the competition's fourth edition. It comprises the senior men's national teams of UEFA's 55 member associations. The league phase began in September 2024, with the season culminating in the Nations League Finals held in June 2025 to crown the champions.

Linked to the University of Copenhagen, the Geological Museum maintains a long-standing collection that has been assembled over many centuries. The holdings encompass a broad range of geological material, including minerals, fossils, petrology specimens, and meteorites, reflecting the institution’s role as a repository for earth-science knowledge and its history of accumulation.

Two notable items form part of the University of Copenhagen Geological Museum's display: the Agpalilik meteorite, a fragment associated with the Cape York meteorite and weighing approximately twenty tonnes, which is exhibited in the museum's courtyard; and a lunar rock sample from Taurus-Littrow, collected by Apollo 17 astronauts in 1972, that is also on display.

Beginning in 1986, the Texas Department of Transportation adopted the slogan "Don't Mess with Texas" as the centerpiece of a statewide effort to curb litter along Texas roadways. The phrase was prominently displayed on road signs along major highways and was disseminated through television, radio, and print advertising. The slogan remains in use and continues to enjoy broad popularity.
In 2005, the Texas Legislature enacted House Bill 2702, transferring railroad oversight responsibilities from the Texas Railroad Commission to the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT).

During the summer of 2003, Andy Jassy assumed leadership of Bryar's portfolio at the request of Rick Dalzell after Jeff Vermeulen declined the assignment, Vermeulen having been Bezos's first choice for the role. Jassy articulated a vision of an Internet operating system built from a set of foundational infrastructure primitives designed to lower impediments and accelerate the delivery of software applications. By autumn 2003, the initial focus of AWS centered on core infrastructure services, with databases, storage, and compute identified as the first offerings to be launched.

On December 24, 2012, Amazon Web Services experienced an outage that primarily affected the Northeastern United States. The disruption rendered websites such as Netflix unavailable to customers. The incident was attributed to problems within the Elastic Load Balancing service provided by AWS, a component of its cloud infrastructure.

Sudhir P. Mudur served as the director of C-DAC Mumbai, the Mumbai campus of the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, which was formerly known as NCST Mumbai. He is a professor at the Gina Cody School of Engineering and Computer Science at Concordia University.

Dr. Vijay Bhatkar was appointed as the director of the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DACT). The project was envisioned as an initial three-year undertaking, with an initial funding of ₹30 crore, an amount equal to the cost of a Cray supercomputer.

On July 27, at the steps of the Mechanics Institute in New Orleans, approximately 200 Black war veterans participated in the riot. The participants were motivated by abolitionist speakers Anthony Paul Dostie and former Louisiana Governor Michael Hahn, who urged a parade to the Mechanics Institute on the convention day to demonstrate support for their cause.

During the period surrounding the New Orleans riot, white Democrats dismissed the reconvened convention as illegitimate because its electorate was whites-only and had already accepted the constitution. White supremacy formed a central plank of the 1865 Louisiana state party platform, which urged governance by white people, exclusive political benefits for the white race, denied citizenship to Africans, and rejected racial equality. Rufus King Cutler proposed a strategy to mobilize roughly 30,000–35,000 Black voters and 28,000–30,000 White voters while disenfranchising leading rebels, in order to empower Unionists. He argued that with sufficient military force to enforce the provisions, such a government could be established and sustained by Unionists.

According to the Mahabharata, Kindama and his mate were in animal form—a deer and a doe—while mating. Pandu, the king of Hastinapura, was nearby on a hunting expedition and mistook them for real deer, firing arrows at them. Enraged by being slain before completing the act, Kindama disclosed his true form and reproached Pandu for interrupting their union. Before dying, he cursed Pandu that he would die the moment he touched his wife with the intention of making love. The curse is described as explaining Pandu’s eventual death during an attempted sexual act with his wives, shaping a critical turn in the epic’s lineage tale.

Muttaburrasaurus langdoni is known from the holotype specimen QM F6140, recovered from the Mackunda Formation, a geologic unit dating to the Albian–Cenomanian. The holotype comprises a partial skeleton that includes the skull and the lower jaws, with preserved elements such as the underside of the skull, the back part of the mandible, numerous vertebrae, portions of the pelvis, and segments of both the forelimbs and hind limbs.

Muttaburrasaurus langdoni is characterized by a skull that presents a flattened profile with a triangular cross-section when viewed from above, featuring a broad rear and a pointed snout. The snout houses a markedly enlarged, hollow upward-bulging nasal structure, the bulla nasalis, which has been proposed as a potential source of distinctive calls or as a display feature, though such interpretations remain conjectural in the absence of fossilized nasal tissue. Within the genus, the bulla nasalis is shorter in older Muttaburrasaurus specimens, as evidenced by the Dunluce Skull. In addition, the upper portion of the bulla in the holotype has not been preserved. A second skull, by contrast, exhibits a rounded bulla profile, indicating variation in this nasal structure.

Hip-hop's early formation reflects a cross-cultural exchange between American proto-rap and Jamaican studio and sound-system practices. In the United States' proto-rap era, Jamaican influence appeared in toasting over records by performers such as U-Roy, and in tracks like Peter Tosh's "Righteous Ruler" and King Stitt's "Fire Corner" (1969). Jamaican DJs routinely reworked existing recordings to devise new sounds, a technique that would deeply inform later production. Duke Reid's sound system tradition featured live manipulation of records to render tracks unrecognizable through on-the-fly adjustments. In the studio, King Tubby pioneered stripping vocals from original recordings to produce new versions, a practice that helped catalyze the development of dub music. The popularity of these remixes grew to the point where many singles were issued with the original track on one side and a dubbed version on the flip. Taken together, this diverse, experimental approach to production gave rise to dub and is widely considered a key artistic antecedent to hip-hop.

Hip-hop, commonly referred to as rap music, is a popular music genre that originated in the early 1970s in New York City. It developed within a subculture linked to African-American and Latino communities in the city. A defining attribute is the frequent vocal delivery known as rapping, often performed over instrumental tracks. The genre is also marked by elements such as DJing, turntablism, scratching, beatboxing, and the use of instrumental backings. Central to hip-hop is cultural interchange, with the movement drawing on and offering commentary about its social environment.

H2 (A&E Networks) was an American cable channel launched on September 26, 2011, through the renaming of History International into H2. The channel’s lineup was realigned to emphasize documentary programming drawn from its sister network History. This reorientation preceded History’s own transition toward greater emphasis on reality-based programming. The H2 service was discontinued and replaced by Viceland on February 29, 2016.

In the United Kingdom and Ireland, the channel originally known as Military History was rebranded as H2 on 4 May 2013. The H2 service subsequently launched on TalkTalk on 28 August 2014, with BT TV carrying it a few months later. The high-definition variant began carriage on Virgin Media on 1 December 2015 and was later added to BT TV in October 2016. On 6 February 2019, the HD feed was rebranded as History2. Finally, on 27 May 2020, History and History2 were rebranded as Sky History and Sky History2 in the UK and Ireland, aligning with Sky Documentaries and Sky Nature.

Founded as the world's first organization devoted to the systematic study of psychical phenomena, the Society for Psychical Research established a pioneering framework for inquiry. Its stated aim is to examine a broad range of issues without prejudice or preconception, and to pursue investigations in an exact and dispassionate manner that mirrors the scientific method. This ethos of rigorous, objective inquiry has helped illuminate questions that were once obscure or hotly debated, illustrating how disciplined investigation can advance understanding across contested topics.

Controversy within the Society for Psychical Research followed the exposure of William Hope and other mediums as fraudulent, undermining confidence among supporters. Arthur Conan Doyle led a mass resignation of 84 SPR members who believed the organization had become hostile to spiritualism. By the 1900s, most avowed spiritualists had left the SPR and returned to the London Spiritualist Alliance (BNAS), an organization established in 1884, reflecting dissatisfaction with the SPR’s skeptical tone in its investigations.

In January 2020, Scott Lapatine, the founder and editor-in-chief of Stereogum, reached an agreement to acquire the publication from the Hollywood Reporter-Billboard Media Group. The deal resulted in Stereogum becoming an independent publication again, marking its return to autonomous operation after the prior corporate ownership.
Stereogum is a daily online publication focusing on music news, reviews, interviews, and commentary. It was founded in January 2002 by Scott Lapatine.

Altair BASIC was distributed by Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems (MITS) after founder Ed Roberts agreed to release the interpreter. Roberts then recruited Bill Gates and Paul Allen to maintain and improve the software, and Gates left his studies at Harvard to devote himself to the project. The initial release would later be retroactively designated as 4K BASIC following later upgrades. Subsequent versions expanded the offering, including 8K BASIC, Extended BASIC, and Disk BASIC.

Altair BASIC was developed by Bill Gates and Paul Allen for the Altair 8800 after they lacked both an interpreter and access to an Altair system for development and testing. Allen had previously built an Intel 8008 emulator for Traf-O-Data that ran on a PDP-10 time-sharing computer, and the pair adapted this emulator in accordance with the Altair programmer guide to develop and test the BASIC interpreter on Harvard's PDP-10. When Harvard officials learned of the arrangement, they objected, although there was no written policy prohibiting such use at the time. To complete debugging, Gates and Allen purchased access to a Boston-area timesharing service. A Harvard student, Monte Davidoff, suggested replacing the original integer arithmetic with floating-point arithmetic and claimed that the larger package could still fit within the available memory, after which he was hired to write the floating-point package.

JANET is the United Kingdom's education and research network operated by Jisc Services Limited, a subsidiary of Jisc, and is responsible for administering the .ac.uk domain. On 1 December 2012, Janet merged with Jisc Collections to form Jisc Collections and Janet Limited, a subsidiary of Jisc, and in March 2015 that entity was renamed Jisc Services Limited. Despite the corporate name changes, Jisc Services continues to operate under the Janet brand with the same remit. The network traces its origins to the United Kingdom Education and Research Networking Association (UKERNA), and it was previously known as the JNT Association before adopting the Janet title.

In 1995, the SuperJanet2 initiative was launched to advance the JANET network. The program deployed 155 Mbit/s asynchronous transfer mode backbones to increase core bandwidth and added a 10 Mbit/s SMDS network that connected several of the original JANET nodes. As a result, JANET's mandate was broadened to include the operation of metropolitan area networks centered on these sites.

Exhibition areas are linked by a short tram ride that departs from the museum’s own collection. The tram is part of the museum’s holdings and dates back to 1901. Its current exterior reflects the design of the 1960s, the era when it was adapted for touristic services.

Carris Museum provides guided visits for groups, along with a range of interactive offerings such as games activities and educational workshops, and it also hosts children’s birthday parties; all of these activities are subject to prior reservation.

Over a period spanning from 1789 to 1891, the Sauk nation participated in twenty-two treaties. While some early agreements are documented with substantive terms, a number of the later treaties are characterized by scant archival detail, with records often preserving only the dates on which they were signed and offering little information about the substantive provisions.

The Sauk (Sac) called themselves Thâkîwaki, an autonym understood to mean "the people coming forth from the outlet" or "from the water." In current orthography this self-designation is written oθaakiiwaki. The Ojibwe referred to them as Ozaagii(-wag), a name that was subsequently transliterated into French and English by European colonists.

Within Unicode, the code points U+337B through U+337E encode the calendar-era symbols for the Japanese eras Heisei, Shōwa, Taishō, and Meiji (rendered as ㍻, ㍼, ㍽, and ㍾). These glyphs also appeared in older character sets—most notably the NEC special characters extension to JIS X 0208—and were carried into Microsoft's Unicode implementations and into later revisions of JIS X 0213. For the Reiwa era, the corresponding symbol is encoded at U+32FF, with the glyph ㋿ and the official name SQUARE ERA NAME REIWA, and it resides in the Enclosed CJK Letters and Months block. By the time Reiwa began, the CJK Compatibility block had been entirely allocated.

CJK Compatibility is a Unicode block comprising square-shaped characters intended for compatibility with East Asian character sets, and includes both CJK and Latin alphanumeric symbols. It was encoded to preserve interoperability with East Asian encodings and scripts. In Unicode 1.0, the block was divided into two sub-blocks: CJK Squared Words (U+3300–U+337F) and CJK Squared Abbreviations (U+3380–U+33FF).

The AN/URC-117 Ground Wave Emergency Network (GWEN) relied on longwave transmitting towers, each approximately 88–91 meters (about 290–299 feet) in height, to disseminate emergency signals. These towers emitted radio frequency power on the order of 2,000–3,000 watts. Although 240 towers were planned, only 58 were constructed before funding and program support declined. In 1994, a defense appropriations bill prohibited funding for further GWEN tower construction, and a few months thereafter the United States Air Force cancelled the GWEN program. Subsequently, the United States Coast Guard repurposed several former GWEN sites to house the Nationwide Differential GPS system.

Nodes were arranged at roughly 150 to 200 miles apart, a spacing dictated by the practical reach of ground-wave transmission. In the early phase of operations, the relay stations periodically received and forwarded short test messages on a twenty-minute cadence. The system also incorporated built-in redundancy through packet-switching techniques designed to reconstitute connectivity if a portion of the network was damaged, thereby preserving overall functionality.

The Saint Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra (Russian: Симфонический оркестр Санкт-Петербургской филармонии), also known as the Symphonic Orchestra of the Saint Petersburg Philharmonia, is a symphony orchestra based in Saint Petersburg, Russia. Its primary concert venue is the Saint Petersburg Philharmonia.

The Saint Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra achieved its greatest renown during the long tenure of chief conductor Yevgeny Mravinsky (1938–1988). The ensemble undertook relatively few Western tours, with its first foreign visit being a spring 1946 tour to Finland. It produced a substantial number of studio recordings under Mravinsky, and archival live performances have since been released commercially. Under Mravinsky, seven of Shostakovich's symphonies premiered with the orchestra.

Market capitalization is defined as the closing price per share multiplied by the number of shares outstanding. For example, with four million shares and a closing price of $20, the market capitalization would be $80 million. If the closing price increases to $21, the market cap would rise to $84 million, while a decrease to $19 would lower it to $76 million. In mercantile pricing, transaction costs can cause the purchase price, the average price paid, and the sale price to differ from one another.

Market capitalization eligibility requirements apply to the process of adding securities to indices rather than to decisions about ongoing index membership. An S&P index component that appears to fail the addition criteria is not removed from the index solely on that basis. Removals occur only when continuing conditions warrant an index change.

The Libertarian Party of Pennsylvania has achieved representation at the local level, with a number of candidates elected to city and county offices across the state. The party does not hold any federal positions or seats in the Pennsylvania General Assembly. As of June 2024, there are 108 Libertarian officeholders statewide.

On December 28, 2023, Kevin Gaughen, a former executive director of the Libertarian Party of Pennsylvania, issued a press release describing the situation as a collapse of the party. The release attributed the decline in dues-paying members from about 1,600 to 597 to the Mises Caucus and reported a 45.9 percent drop in total party income, with the treasury cited at $17,953, down from $47,377.92 at the time of the takeover. In the 2022 elections, all Libertarians endorsed by the Mises Caucus were defeated, while those Libertarians elected in 2022 were non-Mises, part of the old-guard. Before the takeover, the party had 39 active county or regional committees covering 48 counties; after the takeover, 20 active committees remained, covering 22 counties.

During the 2013 Southeast Asian haze, Indonesian authorities mobilized aerial and ground resources in Riau to support firefighting efforts. By 21 July, four helicopters and one airplane were stationed on standby in Riau to assist with firefighting operations, including cloud seeding and water-bombing. A day later, on 22 July, Indonesia's disaster management agency reported that six aircraft were on standby for cloud seeding purposes. In addition, soldiers were placed on standby to help combat fires.
On 23 July, haze conditions changed again. By 8:00 a.m., the air pollution index readings in Port Klang, Bukit Rambai, and Muar were 105, 116, and 115 respectively.

Liverbirds was initially sold at Cape and Snodgrass's acoustic shows during their February 2010 European tour with Tony Sly, before online sales were later introduced through their webstore on April 1, 2010.

Liverbirds is a collaborative album that gathers songs from Joey Cape's bands Lagwagon and Bad Astronaut as well as from Jon Snodgrass's projects Drag the River and Armchair Martian. The tracks are reinterpreted in new acoustic, alt-country flavored renditions, offering a departure from their original electric arrangements. Each participant contributed five songs to the collection. The album also includes Snodgrass's previously unreleased track, "Spiderman, Wolfman."

Timothy Koogle is described as having pursued several business ventures before entering Motorola’s employ. In 1981 he sold Phase 2 to Motorola, and he subsequently wound down his racing-engine business. Two years later, in 1983, he joined Motorola as a employee.

Timothy Andrew Koogle (born July 5, 1951) is an American executive who served as Yahoo!'s first chief executive officer and president from 1995 to 2001, and as chairman from 1999 to 2003. He was recognized by BusinessWeek as one of its Top 25 Executives of the Year in 1999 and again in 2000.

Masako Owada became Her Imperial Highness The Crown Princess of Japan following her marriage to Crown Prince Naruhito in a traditional ceremony on 9 June 1993. As part of the imperial household, she bore the personal emblem Rosa rugosa 'o-shirushi' (hamanasu), whose colors range from mauve-lilac to crimson or white. The Crown Princess insignia features the imperial household's white chrysanthemum, traced in antique gold. In the Imperial Order of Precedence, she ranks behind Empress Michiko and Empress Dowager Nagako. To commemorate the wedding, the orchid Dendrobium cultivar Masako Kotaishi Hidenka was named in her honour.

Empress Masako, the wife of Emperor Naruhito, faced sustained pressure to bear a male heir, a burden that adversely affected her health. In 2004 she was diagnosed with adjustment disorder, a condition that periodically compelled her to withdraw from public life. Despite these challenges, during her tenure as crown princess and subsequently as empress, she accompanied her husband on official overseas visits and participated in imperial court ceremonies.

During World War II, the Art Looting Intelligence Unit published a directory titled Red Flag Names, organized by country—Germany, France, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, and Luxembourg. Each entry provides a description of the individual's activities and their connections within the spoliation network. Many entries also indicate whether the individual was arrested or imprisoned by Allied forces.

In 2013, the Canadian government established the Holocaust-era Provenance Research and Best-Practice Guidelines Project, an initiative dedicated to provenance research and to developing standards for handling artworks looted or displaced during the Holocaust. The project is evaluating the holdings of six art galleries in Canada as part of its mandate.

Regulation of electronic commerce in California is governed by the California Electronic Commerce Act (1984) and the California Privacy Rights Act (2020); the former was enacted by the state legislature, while the latter originated as a voter-approved measure, illustrating different statutory routes to regulation. In the United States, federal oversight of e-commerce activities is primarily carried out by the Federal Trade Commission, which regulates practices related to commercial emails, online advertising, and consumer privacy. National standards for direct marketing by email are set by the CAN-SPAM Act of 2003. The Federal Trade Commission Act prohibits false or deceptive advertising, with Section 5 explicitly banning unfair or deceptive practices. The FTC has pursued enforcement actions to ensure that corporate privacy statements and commitments regarding the security of consumers’ personal information are upheld. Consequently, privacy policies relating to e-commerce may fall within the scope of FTC enforcement and compliance requirements.

E-commerce is a crucial tool used by businesses of all sizes across the globe, enabling them to sell goods and services directly to customers and to engage with those customers beyond the point of purchase.

The voiced alveolar lateral approximant /l/ exhibits notable allophony across languages. In many languages, including most English varieties, it is pronounced with velarization in certain contexts, a variant commonly described as "dark l." By contrast, a non-velarized realization exists in other contexts, known as "clear l" or "light l," which typically occurs before and between vowels in some English standards. Some languages feature only the clear variant, lacking velarization entirely. Others may not possess a clear l at all, or restrict its presence to preceding front vowels, especially the close front vowel [i].

The voiced alveolar lateral approximant is a member of the lateral consonants, a category defined by constriction that directs the airstream along the sides of the tongue rather than through the central channel. This lateral airflow is a defining feature that differentiates lateral consonants from central ones, while the voicing component indicates that the vocal folds vibrate during articulation.

Prior to 1972, sales of automatic soda-lime glass were largely confined to hardware retailers rather than mass-market outlets. Ravenhead's market research indicated that women accounted for about 80% of household purchasing decisions, prompting the company to use attractive packaging to accelerate the marketing of its product range. Consequently, marketing focus shifted toward supermarkets, with Tesco cited as a notable example, as retailers broadened their assortment beyond traditional hardware channels. At that time, Tesco's non-food division was still relatively new, presenting opportunities for Ravenhead to reach a wider consumer base through emerging retail formats.

Ravenhead Glass expanded its retail range rapidly during its early years, signaling a period of dynamic product development. A key contributor to this expansion was John Clappison, an existing freelance designer, who developed several lines for the company, including Barmasters, Elegance, White Fire, Topaz, Icelantic, and Olympiad, while also refining Hardie Williamson’s Siesta range. Ronald Murphy arranged sponsorship and helped form The Glasshouse in Covent Garden in collaboration with the Royal College of Art. Annette Meech designed the Rosy Tumblers as well as the Apollo and Solar ranges for Ravenhead. Following these design initiatives, Ravenhead received design awards and a number of its products were featured at the London Design Centre.

Tarns are small alpine lakes formed in cirques, bowl-shaped depressions carved by cirque glaciers on mountain slopes near the firn line. These hollows can expand into substantial basins through weathering, ice segregation, and plucking, with the basin deepening as it is eroded by ongoing ice segregation and abrasion. Typically, a cirque is bounded on three sides by steep cliffs, while the remaining side exhibits a moraine lip, threshold, or sill from which a stream or glacier outlets, marking the basin’s drainage path.

Tarn denotes a body of water that forms in a glacial corrie (cirque), which underpins its technical meaning. The Lake District, an upland region in North West England, contains a high concentration of such features in its corries, contributing to a landscape with numerous tarns. In practice, however, many bodies of water in the Lake District are referred to as tarns even when they do not occupy a true glacial corrie and thus do not meet the strict geologic criteria, illustrating the broader local usage of the term beyond its technical sense.

Varanids, commonly known as monitor lizards, are a diverse group of lizards widely regarded for their relatively high behavioral intelligence. Across many species, individuals forage over broad areas and maintain sizable home ranges, exhibiting considerable stamina in locomotion. In the Philippines, three arboreal Varanus species—Varanus olivaceus, V. mabitang, and V. bitatawa—are predominantly frugivorous, setting them apart from more carnivorous relatives. Morphological scaling in living varanids shows positive allometry of the limbs, with limb size increasing disproportionately in larger-bodied species, while the feet become proportionally smaller relative to other limb segments as body size grows. These patterns highlight how body size and ecological niche influence the anatomy and foraging ecology of the group.

Varanids refer to the monitor lizards, whose circumscription has been a matter of taxonomic debate. In the definition proposed by Lee (1997), Varanidae is the clade that comprises Varanus and all taxa more closely related to Varanus than to Lanthanotus, a concept that explicitly excludes the earless monitor lizard from Varanidae. The inclusion of Lanthanotus borneensis within Varanidae is therefore unsettled and varies among authors. Some researchers treat L. borneensis as part of Varanidae, whereas others assign it to a distinct lineage, Lanthanotidae. This divergence is illustrated by different classifications: Vidal et al. (2012) regard the earless monitor lizard as Lanthanotidae, a separate family, while Gauthier et al. (2012) place it within Varanidae. Consequently, the taxonomic status of L. borneensis—and, more broadly, whether Lanthanotidae is separate or nested within Varanidae—depends on the scholarly framework employed.

Vantage Point: Developments in North Korea surveys the role of Naewoe and its publication arm, Naewoe Press, as a source on North Korea. The agency maintained close links with South Korea's intelligence service. Scholar James Hoare notes that Naewoe's output became less partisan after the late 1980s and is a useful resource on North Korea. In 1999 Naewoe merged with Yonhap News Agency, and subsequent materials on North Korea continued to be distributed free of charge as part of the government's propaganda effort. The Library of Congress further reports that Naewoe Press originated as a propaganda vehicle aligned with unification policy, but by the mid-1980s it had become more objective and moderate in its interpretation of North Korea's developments.

In 2016, the first issue of the 39th annual volume of Vantage Point: Developments in North Korea carried an announcement by Park No-hwang, the president-publisher of Yonhap News Agency, that the magazine would be discontinued. He stated that Yonhap would maintain comprehensive North Korea coverage notwithstanding the cessation of the publication, and that the discontinuation would not diminish Yonhap's North Korea news service. He attributed to Yonhap a serious obligation to help realize the Korean people's reunification aspirations by delivering accurate reporting on the realities of North Korea and on the South Korean government's policy toward the North. Yonhap is described as a leading news agency in South Korea, with its work aimed at both domestic and international readers.

Michael Zucchet, a former member of the City Council, briefly served as acting mayor before resigning from the council three days later. He was convicted in U.S. District Court of one count of conspiracy, five counts of wire fraud, and three counts of extortion in connection with an alleged scheme involving Ralph Inzunza and Charles L. Lewis to repeal the city's no-touch laws at strip clubs.

Michael Zucchet served on the San Diego City Council representing the Second District. He won the 2002 council seat by defeating Kevin Faulconer. In December 2004, he was appointed Deputy Mayor. Following Mayor Dick Murphy's resignation on July 15, 2005, Zucchet assumed the duties of acting mayor.

On 13 July 2021, Lumbardh Dellova rejoined Hajduk Split, a club competing in the Croatian First Football League. He agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team and was assigned squad number 16. Five days later, he made his debut for Hajduk in a 2–2 away draw with Lokomotiva, coming on as a substitute in the 81st minute to replace Gergő Lovrencsics.

On 8 September 2020, Dellova joined Prishtina of the Kosovan Superleague on a season-long loan. Eleven days later, he made his debut for the club in a 3–0 home victory over Drenica, and he was named in the starting lineup for the match.

The Brazilian Navy developed in tandem with Brazil's independence, drawing on native-born Brazilians who had previously been prohibited from serving under Portuguese rule and who subsequently joined the naval forces. In addition to these locally born sailors, Portuguese-born individuals who supported independence and foreign mercenaries also participated in the navy. A number of institutions originally established by King João VI of Portugal—such as the Department of Navy, the Headquarters of the Navy, the Intendancy and Accounting Department, the Arsenal (Shipyard) of the Navy, the Academy of Navy Guards, the Naval Hospital, the Auditorship, the Supreme Military Council, the powder plant, and others—were incorporated into the naval structure. Brazilian-born Captain Luís da Cunha Moreira was chosen as the first minister of the Navy on 28 October 1822.

Brazil declared war on the Central Powers in October 1917, and its navy subsequently participated in World War I as part of the Allied effort. On 21 December 1917 the British government requested that a Brazilian force of light cruisers be placed under Royal Navy control. The assembled squadron consisted of the cruisers Rio Grande do Sul and Bahia; destroyers Paraíba, Rio Grande do Norte, Piauí, and Santa Catarina; the support ship Belmonte; and the ocean-going tug Laurindo Pitta, and it was designated the Divisão Naval em Operações de Guerra (DNOG). DNOG sailed on 31 July 1918 from Fernando de Noronha to Sierra Leone, arriving at Freetown on 9 August, before proceeding to Dakar on 23 August for base operations. On the night of 25 August the division believed it had been attacked by a U-boat, with Belmonte reporting a torpedo track. The alleged submarine was depth-charged and reportedly sunk by the destroyer Rio Grande do Norte, although the sinking was never confirmed.

On October 18, 2015, American streamer Angrypug deliberately played the National Anthem of the Republic of China and displayed the Flag of the Republic of China during a Twitch broadcast of the game H1Z1, while shouting a chant asserting Taiwan's primacy. The incident provoked a hostile reaction from mainland Chinese gamers, who directed insults in both English and Chinese, incorporating explicit profanity. The event was later documented in an article titled "Taiwan Number One."

Taiwan Number One is a slogan that is also rendered as "TAIWAN #1" and in Chinese as 台灣No.1. The phrase was coined by American gamer Angrypug and drew anger from Chinese players during a 2015 session of the video game H1Z1. Since its inception, it has become a buzzword in online culture surrounding cross-strait relations.

Article 144 of the Basic Law sets out the amendment framework, with the National People’s Congress possessing exclusive power to amend the law, a provision analogous to that governing Hong Kong’s Basic Law. Amendments may be proposed by the NPC Standing Committee, the State Council, or the Macau Special Administrative Region. For Macau to initiate amendments, it must secure the consent of two-thirds of Macau’s representatives to the NPC, two-thirds of all Legislative Assembly members, and the assent of the Chief Executive. Any proposed amendment is reviewed by the Committee for the Basic Law of the Macau SAR. Amendments must not contravene the PRC’s established basic policies concerning Macau.

The Macao Basic Law provides for amendments to the methods by which the Chief Executive is selected and the Legislative Council is formed to take effect for terms commencing after 2009. Such amendments require the endorsement of two-thirds of all members of the Legislative Assembly and the consent of the Chief Executive, with the proposed changes subsequently reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for approval. The amendment process is described as analogous to the procedure used for Annexes I and II of the Basic Law of Hong Kong prior to 2021.

Edward Enninful began his tenure as editor-in-chief of British Vogue with the December 2017 issue, his first as head of the publication. The issue's cover featured Adwoa Aboah, a British model and activist.

British Vogue's September 2020 issue featured a triple gatefold cover that showcased twenty activists associated with the Black Lives Matter movement, including Marcus Rashford and Adwoa Aboah.
