The accompanying Activism Now edition was photographed by Misan Harriman, marking the first time a Black man photographed a British Vogue cover in the magazine’s 104-year history. Earlier milestones in the publication’s photography history include Nadine Ijewere becoming the first Black woman to photograph a British Vogue cover.

During the investigation into the West Memphis Three case, the West Memphis Police Department faced significant organizational challenges, with records described as disorganized and a small force overwhelmed by the scope of the crimes. The department also declined unsolicited consultation from Arkansas State Police violent crimes experts, a decision that attracted criticism and speculation. Some critics suggested that the refusal to accept outside help reflected broader tensions stemming from an ongoing Arkansas State Police inquiry into alleged theft from the Crittenden County drug task force. In addition, physical evidence was stored in paper sacks obtained from a supermarket, with the bag's branding visible, rather than in proper containers, illustrating shortcomings in evidence handling.

During the appellate proceedings, Echols's defense argued that he did not validly waive his claim of mental incompetence before the 1994 trial, contending that he lacked the capacity to relinquish such a claim. To assist the appeal, the team retained Dr. George Woods, a forensic psychiatrist based in Berkeley, California, whose role was to bolster the defense's case on Echols' mental competence.

During the Qing dynasty (1644–1911), the gong'an or public-case detective genre matured, featuring protagonists known as xia who, alongside judges or magistrates, investigate crimes and contend with injustice. The Justice Bao cycle, including Sanxia Wuyi (三俠五義; later renamed Qixia Wuyi) and Xiaowuyi (小五義), embedded social-justice themes that would become central to later wuxia fiction. Concurrently, xiayi narratives of chivalrous romance emerged, often featuring female heroes and supernatural fighting abilities. Scholarly consensus identifies Shi Gong'an Qiwen (施公案奇聞) and Ernü Yingxiong Zhuan (兒女英雄傳) as the clearest early examples of wuxia novels, marking a transition from detective-justice tales toward a broader tradition of martial heroism.

Wuxia literature traces its roots to Tang dynasty xiake narratives, which marked a turning point in the development of martial fiction of that era. These tales later reemerged in the form of chuanqi, or “legendary tales.” From this period, notable works such as Nie Yinniang, The Kunlun Slave, Thirteenth Madame Jing, Red String, and The Bearded Warrior illustrate the early character of the genre. These writings laid the groundwork for what would become modern wuxia, featuring fantastical elements and typically solitary protagonists who undertake bold and heroic exploits. In the Song dynasty, similar narratives circulated in huaben, short works that scholars have argued served as prompt-books for shuochang, the traditional Chinese mode of storytelling.

New Chilean cumbia refers to a contemporary variant of Chilean cumbia that, while drawing on a range of influences, has its roots in the Chilean cumbia tradition established by Orquesta Huambaly, Giolito y su Combo, Orquesta Cubanacán, La Sonora Palacios, and Sonora de Tommy Rey. The movement is directed at a younger audience, and its typical listeners often come from middle-class backgrounds.

New Chilean Cumbia, also referred to as New Chilean Cumbia Rock, is a subgenre within the broader cumbia tradition that originated in Chile in the early 2000s. It began to surface in mainstream media around 2009–2010. Lyrically, it tends to emphasize urban life more than older cumbia forms. The genre blends rock and hip hop with a wide range of Latin American influences, including Andean music, salsa, son, reggae, boleros, ska, and Latin-African rhythms, as well as diablada. It also incorporates elements of Balkan folklore, notably Klezmer and Romani (Gypsy) music.

During World War II, the Luftwaffe’s day- and night-fighter pilots claimed more than 70,000 aerial victories, with roughly 745 of these credited to Messerschmitt Me 262 jet fighters. Anti-aircraft artillery, or Flak, downed about 25,000–30,000 Allied aircraft. When broken down by Allied nation, losses are estimated at approximately 25,000 American, 20,000 British, 46,100 Soviet, 1,274 French, 375 Polish, and 81 Dutch aircraft, with additional aircraft attributed to other Allied nations.

Some shortcomings were not revealed until actual combat, but by the mid-1930s German aircraft such as the Bf 109 fighter, He 111 bomber, Ju 87 Stuka dive-bomber, and Do 17 light bomber had already demonstrated strong performance. These types first saw active service with the Condor Legion in the Spanish Civil War, where they faced Soviet-supplied aircraft on the opposing side. As experience accumulated, the Luftwaffe concluded that conventional biplane fighters were obsolete, leading to the reassignment of the Heinkel He 51 to trainer duties. In this period, designs from Heinkel and Dornier were particularly notable for their speed and overall capability, with bombers that could outpace many contemporary 1930s-era fighters, which were often still biplanes or strut-braced monoplanes.

Widodo Cahyono Putro began his professional football career in the Galatama era with Warna Agung, prior to the formation of the Liga Indonesia. In the 1994–95 season he transferred to Petrokimia Putra Gresik, where the club finished as runners-up in the league. He subsequently joined Persija Jakarta for the 1998–99 season, a prominent club based in Jakarta. Returning to Petrokimia Gresik, he helped the team claim the Indonesia League title in 2002. He eventually retired at Petrokimia Gresik, the club that first brought him to prominence.
Widodo Cahyono Putro was appointed as the manager of Persita Tangerang on 18 January 2019. Under his management, the club secured promotion by finishing as runners-up in Liga 2.

Rabaul served as a major Japanese fleet base in the South Pacific. Allied air operations against the base began after a January 1942 raid by Royal Australian Air Force Catalina flying boats. Nevertheless, the offensive remained limited in scope and sporadic for nearly two years. The campaign was constrained by scarce resources and the significant distance to the nearest airfield, Port Moresby, located roughly 500 miles away, which restricted range and the tempo of Allied strikes.

On 23 December 1943, the first large-scale air strike against Rabaul was conducted, led by United States Army Air Forces bombers with fighter escorts following in support. Forty Japanese fighters engaged the attackers; Allied fighters claimed 30 of them were destroyed, though Japanese records do not corroborate these losses. After a raid on 24 December (Christmas Eve), U.S. Navy carriers attacked the Japanese force at Kavieng, New Ireland, in coordination with the ongoing air raid on Rabaul. The carrier force later returned to Kavieng on 1 January 1944.

Gandhian socialism advocates a federation of political and economic power distributed among local units, aiming to anchor governance and economic life in grassroots communities. It is rooted in a traditionalist caution toward rapid technological modernization and a reluctance to pursue large-scale industrialisation, favoring instead approaches that cultivate self-employment. Central to the framework is an emphasis on self-reliance, encouraging individuals and communities to become more self-sufficient and economically independent.

Gandhian socialism is a branch of socialist thought that is rooted in a Hindu nationalist reading of Mahatma Gandhi's ideas. It centers on Hind Swaraj, Gandhi's treatise on Indian self-rule, as a foundational text. In the 1980s, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and other leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party attempted to incorporate Gandhian socialist principles into the party's ideological framework as a way to temper Hindu nationalism. This strategic effort, however, did not translate into electoral success for the BJP.

Across the latter phase of the British Empire, Cyprus and Malta illustrate the shift from formal territorial rule to sovereign statehood within the postwar era. In Cyprus, the Greek Cypriot nationalist group EOKA waged a guerrilla campaign against British authority, a conflict that was resolved by the London and Zürich Agreements in 1959 and culminated in independence for the island in 1960. Although independence was granted, the United Kingdom retained sovereignty over the Akrotiri and Dhekelia bases, established as sovereign base areas on Cyprus. In parallel, Malta moved toward independence, achieving it in 1964, after discussions that included proposals in 1955 about integrating Malta with Britain. Together, these developments reflect the broader decolonization process that accompanied the decline of imperial rule and the redefinition of Britain's role in the Mediterranean.

During his tenure as prime minister, Harold Macmillan articulated a shift in Britain's approach to empire, notably in a February 1960 speech in Cape Town in which he described a wind of change sweeping across Africa and sought to avert a costly colonial war such as France's in Algeria. Under his leadership, decolonisation accelerated rapidly: three colonies gained independence in the 1950s—the Sudan, the Gold Coast (now Ghana), and Malaya—with the number of independent states expanding by roughly an order of magnitude during the 1960s. This rapid pace of decolonisation ultimately led to significant constitutional changes, including the abolition of the cabinet post of Secretary of State for the Colonies and the dissolution of the Colonial Office in 1966. The Colonial Office then merged with the Commonwealth Relations Office to form the Foreign and Commonwealth Office in October 1968, a department that later became the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

In October 2011, Danish minister Manu Sareen announced plans to legalize same-sex marriage by spring 2012. On January 18, 2012, the government published two draft bills. The first proposed a gender-neutral definition of marriage, allowing same-sex weddings in civil registry offices and in the Church of Denmark, with registered partnerships able to convert to marriage. The second permitted individual priests to refuse to conduct same-sex marriages, while other religious communities could perform such ceremonies but would not be required to do so. A consultation period ran until February 22, 2012. On March 14, 2012, the cabinet submitted both bills to the Folketing. On June 7, 2012, the bills were approved by 85 votes to 24. Royal assent was granted by Queen Margrethe II on June 12, 2012, with the laws taking effect on June 15, 2012. Opposition to the legislation came from the Danish People's Party and the Christian Democrats, the latter being unrepresented in Parliament at the time. The legislation also provided that ministers may decline to perform same-sex marriages, but the local bishop must arrange a replacement venue for the church building.

In June 2010, the Danish Parliament debated a same-sex marriage bill proposed by opposition parties. The bill was rejected in a 52–57 vote, and a separate motion to legalize same-sex marriage was also defeated.

Early specifications of the International Phonetic Alphabet included cursive variants designed for use in manuscripts and field notes. The 1999 Handbook notes that cursive IPA symbols exist but are probably not widely used in contemporary practice. These forms were more advantageous when transcription was primarily done by hand and speed mattered. Nevertheless, cursive forms are generally harder for readers to decipher. Consequently, it is preferable to employ handwritten styles that closely reproduce the appearance of the printed symbols.

Tony Kushner, an American playwright, is known for a six-word memoir in which he states, "At least I never voted Republican." He has criticized the Israeli government's treatment of Palestinians and the rise of religious extremism in Israeli politics and culture, a stance that provoked controversy among American Jews and contributed to opposition to his honorary doctorate at Brandeis University's 2006 commencement. Quotations critical of Zionism and Israel circulated amid the controversy, which Kushner described as grossly mischaracterized. He told the Jewish Advocate that right-wing websites had taken the remarks out of context and that he regards himself as a reasonable person.

Tony Kushner contributed three pieces to the anthology Love's Fire, namely Terminating, Lass Meine Schmerzen Nicht Verloren Sein, and Ambivalence. A Minneapolis production by the Guthrie Theater Lab opened January 7, 1998, followed by a New York staging at the Joseph Papp Public Theater on June 19, 1998.

Redan holes constitute a class of golf holes defined by deep bunkering, typically with a bunker fronting the left side of the green, while a raised kick mound on or near the right side of the putting surface (occasionally with its own bunker) is used to loft approach shots onto the putting surface close to the hole. The original example is the fifteenth hole on the West Links at North Berwick in Scotland. Green visibility from the tee is a distinguishing feature that adds to the tension as the ball approaches the target, although the original Redan design is notable for presenting a blind green from the tee. The National Golf Links of America (NGLA) version altered this dynamic by introducing a visible green from the tee, a modification that inspired numerous modern replicas. Among golf course designers and connoisseurs, the NGLA hole is frequently regarded as the finest embodiment of the Redan concept, with many arguing it surpasses the North Berwick original.

Redan is a census-designated place in the state of Georgia. The name is thought to derive from redans constructed in the surrounding area, which were built during the Atlanta campaign of the American Civil War.

Menard County is a county located in central Illinois, United States, with Petersburg serving as its county seat. The county experiences a climate in which January typically sees an average low of 17 °F (-8 °C) and July an average high of 87 °F (31 °C). The coldest temperature recorded in the county occurred in February 1905 at -24 °F (-31 °C), while the record high was 112 °F (44 °C) documented in July 1954. Average monthly precipitation ranges from about 1.62 inches (41 mm) in January to 4.06 inches (103 mm) in May.

Menard County, Illinois comprises several public school districts, notably the New Holland-Middletown Elementary School District 88, which administers elementary education, and the Lincoln Community High School District 404, which administers secondary education.

ISO 3166-2:BD is Bangladesh's entry in the subdivision coding standard ISO 3166-2, a component of the broader ISO 3166 standard. ISO 3166-2 provides codes for the names of the principal subdivisions of all countries that have an ISO 3166-1 code, such as provinces or states. The ISO 3166 standard itself is published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO).

Pope Hilarius died on 29 February 468 and was buried in the Basilica of St. Lawrence Outside the Walls. In the Roman Catholic Church, his feast is celebrated on 17 November, while the Eastern Orthodox Church observes it on 28 February.

Pope Hilarius became entangled in the dispute surrounding the synod presided over by Dioscorus I of Alexandria, whose leadership provoked his displeasure. Flavian died on 11 August 449 from injuries sustained in an assault by followers of Dioscorus. In the aftermath, Hilarius apologized to Empress Pulcheria for not delivering the pope's letter after the synod, explaining that Dioscorus had hindered his travel by watching the roads and docks around Ephesus, thereby complicating his escape to report the council’s outcome. Flavian and Eusebius of Dorylaeum had written to the pope, and their letters were probably taken by Hilarius to Rome.

On September 12, 1994, Frank Eugene Corder deliberately piloted a Cessna 150L and crashed it onto the South Lawn of the White House, colliding with the south wall of the Executive Mansion. The incident appeared to be a suicide. Corder was killed, and no other individuals were injured. The resulting damage to the grounds and surrounding property was minimal.

Over its development, refinements to the Cessna 150 led to a higher empty weight, which reduced the aircraft's useful load when compared with earlier configurations. The first model recorded an empty weight of 962 lb (436 kg), while the final Commuter II variant weighed 1,129 lb (512 kg) empty, a rise of 167 lb (76 kg). This increase in empty weight was only partly offset by a 1964 increase in gross weight of 100 lb (45 kg). The introduction of the Cessna 152 subsequently added a 70‑lb (32 kg) increment to the gross weight, bringing the maximum allowable weight to 1,670 lb (760 kg).

Sandra Mason began her judicial career in 1978 as Magistrate of the Juvenile and Family Court, while also serving as a tutor in family law at the University of the West Indies. She discontinued the tutoring role in 1983 but continued to perform her magistrate duties. In 1988 she completed the Judicial Administration course offered by the Royal Institute of Public Administration in London. From 1991 to 1999 she served on the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child since its inception, rising to vice chair from 1993 to 1995 and then chair from 1997 to 1999.

Sandra Prunella Mason was born on 17 January 1949 in Saint Philip, Barbados. She attended St. Catherine's Primary School until the age of nine and then pursued her secondary education at Queen's College. In 1968 she taught at Princess Margaret Secondary School, and the following year she worked as a clerk at Barclays Bank. Mason subsequently enrolled at the University of the West Indies, Cave Hill Campus, where she earned a Bachelor of Laws, becoming one of the first graduates of the Faculty of Law from UWI, Cave Hill, and completed her studies in 1973.

Baldwin Harbor features a very low-lying topography, with the highest point estimated at roughly 20 feet (6.1 meters) above sea level, while the lowest areas coincide with the bays, where land sits at sea level. These elevational details are drawn from data compiled by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Geological Survey.

Baldwin Harbor is a census-designated place (CDP) whose statistics were reported in the 2010 census. At that time, the community had a population of 8,102 residing in 2,687 households and comprising 2,185 families. The population density was 6,751.6 people per square mile (2,606.8/km2), and there were 2,782 housing units at a density of 2,318.0 per square mile (897.4/km2). The racial composition was 61.25% White, 26.57% African American, 0.13% Native American, 4.87% Asian, 3.78% from other races, and 3.36% reporting two or more races, with Hispanic or Latino of any race making up 11.83% of the population.

Humpolec is traditionally an industrial town, with its economy shaped by a small group of major manufacturers. Among the largest employers are Valeo Compressor Europe, a producer of car compressors; the Bernard family brewery, founded in 1597; and BJS Czech, a furniture manufacturer.

The Church of Saint Nicholas originated as an early Gothic church and was subsequently rebuilt between 1721 and 1722 in a Gothic-Baroque style by the architect Jan Santini Aichel. A final reconstruction in 1895 gave the building its present Neo-Gothic form.

Arrow fletching employs natural feathers prepared by splitting and sanding the quill prior to gluing. The feathers can be trimmed to shape, die-cut, or burned with a hot electrically heated wire. Achieving identical drag across all feathers on an arrow is essential, and manual trimming is rarely used by contemporary fletchers. The burning-wire method remains popular because bending the wire enables various shapes, and, following gluing, symmetric trimming can be performed by rotating the arrow on a fixture.

Cresting denotes the application of painted rings or bands on arrow shafts. It is performed with a cresting machine, a device resembling a lathe, which rotates the shaft while guides apply the paint. The practice is usually undertaken for personalization, allowing makers or owners to distinguish individual arrows. Beyond decoration, cresting can enhance the visibility of the shaft in flight or against various backgrounds, performing a function similar to decorative wraps.

During World War II, The Japan Times functioned as a channel for the Imperial Japanese government’s communications and reflected its official editorial stance. The paper went through a sequence of mergers and renamings: from 1918 to 1940 it operated as The Japan Times and Mail following a merger with The Japan Mail; from 1940 to 1943 it was published as The Japan Times and Advertiser after merging with The Japan Advertiser; from 1943 to 1956 it carried the title Nippon Times as a temporary renaming, a change linked to a wartime ban on English-language sentiment in Japan; and in 1956 it reverted to The Japan Times.

The Japan Times maintains an online archive of its printed stories and operates a readers' forum. Since 2013, the newspaper’s website has included a comments section beneath articles, a feature that was introduced during a redesign and redevelopment of the publication. The redesign employed responsive web design techniques to optimize the site for use on a wide range of digital devices. In addition, The Japan Times has maintained a social media presence on Twitter and Facebook since 2007.

The Lumia Camera user interface, originally developed for Nokia’s Lumia smartphones, was subsequently transferred to HMD Global, which acquired the rights to the UI. It was introduced as part of Nokia Pro Camera, with the release occurring in February 2018.

Nokia Camera and the related Lumia imaging applications were a family of imaging applications for Lumia devices, originally developed by Nokia and later by Microsoft Mobile. They were built on Scalado technology, with the exception of Lumia Panorama, which had been developed earlier by Nokia for the Symbian and MeeGo platforms. Initially branded with Nokia in front of their names, the branding shifted to Lumia after Microsoft acquired Nokia’s devices and services. Many updates consisted mainly of branding changes, though Lumia Camera itself received a broad range of new features. Most imaging apps were developed by Microsoft Lund division. With the introduction of Windows 10 Mobile and its integration into Windows Camera and Microsoft Photos, several Lumia imaging apps ceased functioning in October 2015.

During the early industrial era, Henry Maudslay and his colleagues contributed to the development of modest standardization across manufacturing, while numerous firms established in-house specifications that circulated within their respective industries. In 1841, Joseph Whitworth introduced a precise screw-thread system whose measurements were adopted by a broad spectrum of British manufacturers as the de facto national standard, commonly known as the British Standard Whitworth. This specification gained influence beyond Britain, being widely adopted in several other countries and helping to align international dimensions and improve interchangeability of parts.

Global standards, frequently described as industry or private standards, are designed and developed to be applicable worldwide. They differ from internationally recognized standards in that they are not produced by international organizations or standards-setting bodies that operate under a formal consensus mechanism. Instead, these standards are created by actors in the private sector, including non-governmental organizations and for-profit entities. As a result, such standards often lack elements of transparency, openness, or processes that incorporate broad consensus.

Psychoactive substances have long been regarded as markers of social standing in both contemporary and ancient societies. In modern social settings such as nightclubs and parties, the use of recreational drugs is commonly viewed as a cue of belonging or prestige. Historical records also reflect enduring associations between mind-altering substances and status; for example, in ancient Egypt, deities are depicted with hallucinogenic plants, underscoring long-standing links between psychoactive substances and religious or cultural symbolism.

The article on psychoactive drugs concentrates on substances that contain psychoactive ingredients and alter mental processes, mood, or behavior. It provides a survey of commonly used psychoactive substances. The survey includes both legally sanctioned and illegal drugs, reflecting that legal status depends on national or local laws. Legal status varies by jurisdiction; what is legal in one country may be illegal in another.

Neues Deutschland comprises a range of traditional sections, including an advice column, a television schedule, notices and classified advertisements, opinion pieces, and thematic sections covering health, environmental issues, and other topics. Letters to the editor are frequently cited in other media as illustrating viewpoints associated with the Left party. The publication appears on weekdays, Monday through Friday, with a weekend edition issued on Saturdays.
Neues Deutschland (pronounced [ˈnɔʏəs ˈdɔʏtʃlant], literally meaning "New Germany" and abbreviated as nd) is a left-wing daily newspaper published in Germany, based in Berlin.

During Hurricane Katrina, President George W. Bush directed the Secretary of Homeland Security, Michael Chertoff, to coordinate the federal response. Chertoff designated Michael D. Brown, then head of FEMA, as the Principal Federal Official responsible for leading the deployment and coordination of all federal response resources and forces in the Gulf Coast. The administration and Chertoff faced harsh criticism for what was perceived as an inadequate level of planning and coordination. Brown claimed that Governor Blanco resisted their efforts and was unhelpful, while Blanco and her staff disputed these claims. Eight days later, Brown was recalled to Washington, and Coast Guard Vice Admiral Thad W. Allen replaced him as chief of hurricane relief operations. Three days after the recall, Brown resigned as director of FEMA, despite recent praise from President Bush.
Hurricane Katrina moved across the Bahamas as a tropical storm before striking South Florida. In the Bahamas, effects were limited, with winds of only moderate strength reported on several islands.

Although the International Phonetic Alphabet is widely used in linguistic work, its adoption is not universal across dictionaries for languages other than English. In monolingual dictionaries of languages with phonemic orthographies, pronunciation is typically not indicated for most words, and when pronunciation is provided it is usually given as a respelling rather than in IPA, with IPA reserved for words whose pronunciations are unexpected. Dictionaries produced in Israel use the IPA only rarely, and at times foreign terms are transcribed using the Hebrew alphabet instead. In bilingual dictionaries translating into Russian, the IPA is usually employed, whereas monolingual Russian dictionaries may occasionally resort to pronunciation respelling for foreign words. Overall, the IPA is more common in bilingual dictionaries, though there are notable exceptions; for example, mass-market bilingual Czech dictionaries generally apply the IPA only to sounds that do not occur in Czech.

The International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) provides a system of phonetic notation designed to represent speech sounds across languages. Transcriptions can be broad, capturing general pronunciations, or narrow, emphasizing detailed dialectal distinctions. For example, the English word “little” may be rendered in a broad form as [ˈlɪtəl], while more precise, dialect-specific renditions are used in narrow transcriptions such as General American [ˈɫɪɾɫ], Cockney [ˈlɪʔo], and Southern US English [ˈɫɪːɫ].

An amenities ship is a naval vessel equipped with leisure facilities as part of a mobile naval base. These ships typically included cinemas and canteens to provide entertainment and dining options for personnel. They were staffed by mercantile crews of the Royal Fleet Auxiliary, the civilian-manned support arm of the Royal Navy. Their purpose was to offer a place for British Pacific Fleet personnel to unwind between operations, thereby contributing to morale during extended deployments.

Anticipating operations in the vast Pacific far from established shore facilities, the Royal Navy organized mobile base facilities to support flotillas afloat. These mobile bases were established at remote Pacific harbors that lacked suitable shore infrastructure. Each base incorporated repair and depot ships whose tasks included maintaining and servicing smaller craft such as destroyers, submarines, minesweepers, and landing craft. The base ships housed administrative and communications offices responsible for coordinating refuelling and resupply of ships operating from the base. Accommodation ships provided living quarters for base staff and for personnel awaiting transfer.

A project management office (PMO) is a centralized organizational unit responsible for governing project management practices. While it commonly develops and enforces standards and methodologies, its scope may also encompass broader roles in strategic project management, acting as a facilitator or as the owner of the portfolio management process. Core activities include monitoring and reporting on both individual projects and the overall project portfolio, and following initiatives from initiation through to completion. Through regular progress reports to senior leadership, the PMO informs decisions about which projects to continue, adjust, or terminate, thereby contributing to the organization's strategic direction.

A project management office (PMO) is characterized by its functions that continually transform in response to changing organizational needs. At its core, the PMO acts as a catalyst for both change and delivery within the organization, facilitating the execution of projects and the implementation of strategic initiatives.

Windows 2000 introduces a range of user interface enhancements across the Start menu, Taskbar, and Windows Explorer. The Start menu gains support for personalized configurations and expandable special folders, and it enables launching multiple programs without closing the menu by holding the SHIFT key, with a Re-sort control to order items by name. The Taskbar receives balloon notifications that applications can use to deliver brief messages. In Windows Explorer, there are customizable toolbars, and features such as auto-complete in the address bar and Run box, expanded file type association capabilities, and the display of shortcut comments as tooltips. The Details view supports extensible columns via the IColumnProvider interface, and icon overlays provide visual status indicators while an integrated search pane aids file discovery. A sort-by-name function for menus is also included, and the Places Bar is available in common dialogs for Open and Save operations.

Windows 2000 introduced Active Directory as a replacement for the Windows NT domain model. The directory’s hierarchical design enables centralized administration of policies and user accounts, as well as the automatic deployment of software and updates, providing greater scalability for organizations. In Active Directory, user information functions similarly to a phone book for end users. Domains within Active Directory can range from small deployments of a few hundred objects to very large ones numbering in the millions, and they can be organized and linked into a contiguous domain namespace to form trees. Trees, in turn, can be linked across namespaces to form forests.

QR Code is a United States trademark (Trademark 2435991) for the term “QR Code,” filed on 29 September 1998, with the registration subsequently amended on 13 March 2001 and assigned to Denso Corporation. In South Korea, an application was filed on 18 November 2011 but was refused on 20 March 2012, with the Korea Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) citing that the term had become genericized among South Koreans to refer to matrix barcodes in general.

In larger QR codes, the message is divided into multiple Reed-Solomon code blocks. The size of each block is chosen so that each block can correct up to 15 errors, a design choice that helps limit the complexity of the decoding algorithm. The code blocks are interleaved to distribute the data across blocks, reducing the likelihood that localized damage overwhelms the correction capacity of a single block.

Both Buddhism and Jainism organize their communities with a clear distinction between renunciants and lay followers. In Jainism, the Jain sangha comprises monastics—munis for men and aryikas for women—and householders, known as śhrāvaks and śrāvakīs. Buddhism likewise structures its community with renunciates, the bhikkhus and bhikkhunis, alongside male and female laypersons, Upāsaka and Upāsikā, who undertake lay-life vows.

Jainism centers on the doctrine of anekantavada, or non-absolutism, which holds that truth is multifaceted and cannot be captured fully by a single perspective, thereby marking a key difference from Buddhism. The Buddha taught the Middle Way, avoiding metaphysical extremes by rejecting definitive affirmations of existence or non-existence in ultimate questions. In contrast, Mahavira is described as accepting both "it is" and "it is not," though with a cautious "perhaps" qualifier and an effort to reconcile these apparently opposing positions.

Julian Dixon is commemorated in several Los Angeles institutions through namesakes and memorial facilities. The 7th Street / Metro Center / Julian Dixon transfer station, serving the A Line, B Line, D Line, and E Line, is named in his honor, and a plaque at the station acknowledges his role in securing federal funding for Metro Rail construction. In 2004, the Southwestern University School of Law opened the Julian C. Dixon Courtroom and Advocacy Center in the former Bullocks Wilshire building. The Culver City branch of the Los Angeles County Library is named the Culver City Julian Dixon Library.

Julian Dixon, a Democratic politician from California, was elected to the California State Assembly in 1972, where he served three terms. He was subsequently elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1978. In 1983, he co-sponsored a resolution with seven other Representatives seeking to impeach President Ronald Reagan over the Grenada invasion. Dixon chaired the Rules Committee at the 1984 Democratic National Convention, and later headed the ethics inquiry into Speaker Jim Wright. He won reelection to the 107th United States Congress. Dixon died on December 8, 2000, at the age of 66, from a heart attack in a hospital in Marina Del Rey, California.

Handy (company) experienced a sequence of notable developments in 2015. In March, the firm disclosed a funding round led by TPG Growth that raised $15 million. In May, TechCrunch reported that Handy was in talks to acquire rival Homejoy. By June, Handy announced it had reached the milestone of one million bookings. In July, Homejoy ceased operations without being acquired amid lawsuits over worker classification. Following Homejoy’s closure announcement, Handy offered a $1,000 signing bonus to Homejoy workers who joined Handy.
In November 2014, Handy faced a lawsuit alleging labor-law violations, with the complaint accusing the company of deliberately misclassifying its workers as independent contractors.

Draft, designated as d or T, is the vertical distance from the bottom of the keel to the waterline. It is a fundamental parameter for determining the minimum water depth required for a vessel to pass safely. In naval architecture and hydrostatics, draft figures are used to compute displacement from stability tables, since the weight of displaced water corresponds to the ship’s total weight. This displacement value is then used to estimate the mass of cargo on board.

Beam on Centerline (BOC) is a measurement used in evaluating multihull vessels. In catamarans, BOC represents the perpendicular distance between the centerlines of the two hulls, measured at deck level. In trimarans, BOC denotes the perpendicular distance from the main hull's centerline to the centerline of either ama, measured at deck level. BOC is typically considered together with Length Overall (LOA). The LOA/BOC ratio serves as an indicator of stability for multihulls, with smaller values indicating greater stability.

Within Spirochaetota, a conserved signature insertion (CSI) is exclusive to all species, representing a three-amino-acid insertion in FlgC, the flagellar basal body rod protein. FlgC is a component of the distinctive endoflagellar apparatus that underpins the unique flagellar structure of spirochetes. The exclusive presence of this CSI and its location in FlgC have led researchers to suggest that it may be related to the characteristic flagellar properties that govern spirochete motility.

Spirochaetes are a phylum of bacteria distinguished by their endoflagella, also known as axial filaments, which are located in the periplasm between the inner and outer membranes and anchored at opposite poles. These flagella project toward the rear of the cell and generate a distinctive twisting motion that propels the organism. Reproduction occurs asexually by transverse binary fission. Although most members are free-living and anaerobic, numerous exceptions exist. The group shows considerable variation in pathogenic potential, ecological niches, and molecular traits such as GC content and genome size.

The deck gun was adopted by all submarine forces before World War I, with its use most prominently associated with the German Navy. It proved valuable for conserving torpedoes and for engaging enemy vessels that lagged behind a convoy, enabling submariners to strike without expending scarce torpedoes. Consequently, many submarine captains regarded the deck gun as their primary weapon in suitable situations. Torpedoes were costly and not always accurate, and they were employed only when necessary or tactically advantageous. However, deploying the deck gun exposed the submarine on the surface, revealing its position to opponents, whereas torpedoes could be fired underwater or at night, reducing exposure. In World War I-era practice, submarines carried more gun rounds than torpedoes—typically ten or fewer torpedo rounds—while firing the deck gun in volleys of multiple projectiles to increase the probability of hitting a target.

Deck guns refer to unenclosed artillery mounted on the exposed deck of a warship, where they typically function as secondary or defensive armament on surface combatants. A well-known example is the United States Navy's 5-inch (127 mm)/25 caliber gun, which was removed from battleships to be mounted on submarines. Consequently, the term "deck gun" is generally used to describe such weapons when they are installed on submarines rather than on surface ships.

The expansion of their audience increased Tegan and Sara's profile within the LGBTQ community. They won the Outstanding Music Artist award at the GLAAD Media Awards, defeating prominent contenders including Lady Gaga and Elton John. In June 2014, they performed at the closing ceremonies of WorldPride in downtown Toronto at Yonge–Dundas Square. The venue has since been renamed Sankofa Square.

Tegan and Sara have pursued a range of projects that span music and literature. Their 2011 video album Get Along received a Grammy nomination, demonstrating critical recognition for their work. In 2014, they performed the song Everything Is Awesome with The Lonely Island for The Lego Movie soundtrack. The pair published the memoir High School in 2019, and in 2022 High School was adapted into a television series for Amazon Freevee. Both sisters have been active within the LGBTQ community.

TransferJet implements a near-field wireless transfer standard with a maximum physical layer rate of 560 Mbit/s. After accounting for protocol overhead, the practical data throughput is approximately 375 Mbit/s. The data rate can adapt downward in response to variations in the wireless environment, and this adaptive behavior helps sustain a robust link when wireless conditions fluctuate.

TransferJet was established in July 2008 to promote the TransferJet format, develop technical specifications and conformity testing procedures, and foster a market for TransferJet‑compliant, interoperable products. In September 2011, the organization registered as an independent non-profit industry association. By June 2015, leadership rested with five promoter companies—JRC, NTT, Olympus, Sony (serving as consortium administrator), and Toshiba—while about 30 adopter companies participated. The TransferJet Consortium oversees the branding assets, including the standard typeface and logos, which are protected trademarks licensed by the consortium.

Cybersectarianism denotes a phenomenon in which small, highly dispersed practitioner groups operate with a degree of secrecy and often remain largely anonymous within the broader social context. Despite geographical separation, they remain remotely linked to a larger network of believers who share practices and texts, with a common devotion to a particular leader at the center. Overseas supporters provide funding and other forms of assistance, while domestic practitioners distribute tracts, participate in acts of resistance, and relay information about internal developments to outsiders. Members construct viable virtual communities of faith, exchange personal testimonies, and engage in collective study through digital channels such as email, online chat rooms, and web-based message boards.

Cybersectarianism refers to the phenomenon in which new religious movements and other groups exploit the Internet to advance their objectives. Through online channels, these groups engage in activities such as distributing texts, recruiting adherents, and sharing information among members and external audiences.

On August 9, 2021, Sony announced its acquisition of Crunchyroll from AT&T, to be conducted through its FUNimation subsidiary. About a month later, Hidive discontinued its service on September 30, 2021.

Hidive, a streaming service, underwent a major update in March 2024 that introduced a redesigned user interface and added features such as offline viewing, updated history queues, and multiple customized watchlists. In August 2024, the Schedule feature and customized profiles were restored, both of which had been available prior to the update.

Stanley Park is a residential neighbourhood located in the West End of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It lies between Denman Street and the boundary of Stanley Park proper. The district is characterized by high-density development, mirroring much of the surrounding West End, and is regarded as one of the more affluent parts of the area. Beyond the Denman Street corridor, the neighbourhood is notably quiet, making it one of the quietest sections of the downtown peninsula. Park-facing condominiums within the area are among the city’s most expensive properties. The extreme southwest portion of the neighbourhood overlaps with the English Bay neighbourhood.

Postcodes in the United Kingdom are used for PO Boxes, which are available only to Large Users (LUs). Under this arrangement, a receipt and holding service operates at a local Sorting and Delivery Centre, where mail addressed to the PO Box is held until collection. The Large User then takes the mail, although in some cases it is possible to arrange an additional delivery directly to the Large User’s premises.

Following the establishment of the London postal district system, the scheme was extended to other large towns and cities. Liverpool was partitioned into four districts—Eastern, Northern, Southern and Western—in 1864–65. Subsequently, in 1867–68, Manchester and Salford were divided into eight numbered districts.

The List of United States representatives from Arizona is an alphabetical compilation of individuals who have served as U.S. representatives for the state of Arizona, including those who represented the region while it was a territory as well as those who have represented the state since it achieved statehood. For a chronological record of members of both houses from Arizona through the present day, see United States congressional delegations from Arizona. The list thus covers pre-statehood and post-statehood representatives, reflecting the historical evolution of Arizona's federal representation.

Road surfaces are subject to aging and surface abrasion as primary failure mechanisms. Over time, the binder in the bituminous wearing course oxidizes and loses its flexibility, becoming stiffer. As aging progresses, the surface tends to shed aggregates and the macrotexture depth increases markedly. Without timely maintenance, potholes can form. In cold climates, repeated freeze-thaw cycles accelerate deterioration once water penetrates the surface. In addition, researchers have evaluated the use of clay and fumed silica nanoparticles as UV-anti-aging coatings for asphalt pavements to mitigate aging effects.

The English word pavement derives from the Latin pavimentum, which originally signified a floor that has been beaten or rammed down. The term entered English through Old French, and prior to its adoption the sense of a beaten-down floor had become obsolete in English.

The Senate Armed Services Committee is a standing committee of the United States Senate charged with the legislative oversight of the nation’s armed forces. Its jurisdiction encompasses the Department of Defense, military research and development, nuclear energy programs tied to national security, military benefits, the Selective Service System, and other defense policy matters. The committee was established by the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 in the aftermath of World War II, through the consolidation of the former Committee on Naval Affairs (founded in 1816) and the Committee on Military Affairs (also founded in 1816).

The Senate Armed Services Committee is a standing committee of the United States Senate that provides legislative and oversight functions for national defense and the Department of Defense. Its remit includes matters affecting members of the armed forces, such as pay and allowances, the promotion processes within the services, retirement and pension benefits, other benefits and privileges available to military personnel, and overseas education programs for both civilian dependents and dependents of service members. Through hearings and consideration of proposed legislation, the committee seeks to ensure policy coherence and fiscal accountability across these areas while informing broader defense policy.

Following Karna’s death, Duryodhana faced the loss of his principal ally and potential commander of the Kaurava forces. He rejected the final peace overtures presented by Kripa and resolved to persist with the conflict. In line with this determination, he appointed Shalya as the commander-in-chief of the Kaurava army.

Following the division of the realm, the Pandavas established their rule at Indraprastha, where they, with the architect Maya, erected a magnificent palace. To project imperial authority, Yudhishthira organized the Rajasuya sacrifice, an event attended by Duryodhana. During a tour of the new residence, Duryodhana experienced visual illusions, mistaking floors for water and water for floors, which culminated in a public humiliation. Bhima teased him for his missteps, further intensifying the embarrassment. This sequence deepened Duryodhana’s hatred toward the Pandavas.

Open Data Protocol defines how query parameters are conveyed in requests by appending them to the URL after a question mark and separating each parameter with ampersands. Each parameter comprises a name that begins with a dollar sign and a value, with the two parts joined by an equals sign. For instance, the URL OData/Products?$top=2&$orderby=Name demonstrates the use of the $top and $orderby options. Filtering is carried out using predefined logical operators and functions to express criteria. An illustration is $filter=Price lt 10.00 and startswith(Name,'M'), which selects products priced below 10.00 and whose names begin with the letter M.

Open Data Protocol (OData) defines a framework for accessing data services, with URLs to an OData endpoint capable of carrying query options. The protocol specifies a set of system query options that endpoints should accept. These options can be used to filter, order, map, or paginate the data returned by a request.

Parque Warner Madrid is owned and operated by Parques Reunidos, the leisure-park operator responsible for the park’s day-to-day management. Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences holds a 5% ownership stake in Parque Warner Madrid.

During the 2008 season, Parque Warner Madrid introduced a water attraction named Oso Yogui. It also unveiled a new production, The Music of Bugs Bunny, conceived with a Hollywood glamour ethos and a Broadway‑musical sensibility. Following a change in ownership, the park recorded its first annual profit after years of losses.

Caneworking involves assembling cane sections in cross-section through conventional flameworking or bead-making techniques. This approach permits fine gradations in color and tonal shading within the design. It is the standard method for creating murrine portraits.

Caneworking is an ancient technical craft that originated in southern Italy. It is conventionally dated to the latter half of the third century BCE, and several centuries later it was elaborately developed on the Italian island of Murano.

According to the FBI, China runs the world's largest state-sponsored hacking program, surpassing the combined capabilities of all other foreign governments and hindering the United States' ability to keep pace with Beijing's intelligence-gathering activities. CNN reported in 2019 that China had built an extensive cyber-espionage infrastructure over the previous two decades. A former head of FBI counterintelligence stated that China possesses tens of thousands of young hackers, comparable to the brightest graduates of leading American universities, who focus their efforts on the United States. Some hackers work full-time, while others participate on a part-time basis.

Allegations concerning Chinese espionage in the United States include a 2023 case in which a former U.S. State Department consultant was accused of removing classified documents. Authorities reportedly recovered more than 1,000 secret pages from the individual’s residence. The case references meetings with Chinese officials in September 2022 and April 2023, during which topics described as sensitive were allegedly discussed.

Baisha Bay is believed to have formed approximately 800,000 years ago. The bay’s rocky promontories were created by volcanic activity originating from the Tatun Volcano Group, which expelled lava that flowed directly into the sea. During the period of Japanese rule, the beach was known as Kamakura, a name chosen to reflect its scenery, which was said to resemble Kamakura in Japan.

Baisha Bay is a beach situated along the North Coast within the Guanyinshan National Scenic Area in Shimen District, New Taipei City, Taiwan. In traditional Chinese, it is written as 白沙灣海水浴場, while the simplified form is 白沙湾海水浴场; the pinyin transcription is Báishā Wān Hǎishuǐ Yùchǎng.

Cambridge University Press, the publishing arm of the University of Cambridge, maintains a global footprint with publishing hubs and offices in more than 40 countries. It has published over 50,000 titles by authors from more than 100 countries, encompassing more than 420 academic journals as well as monographs, reference works, school and university textbooks, and English language teaching and learning materials, in addition to Bible publications. The press operates a bookshop in Cambridge and distributes its titles through retailers such as Amazon. It also runs a conference venues business in Cambridge, featuring facilities at the Pitt Building and the Sir Geoffrey Cass Sports and Social Centre. In addition, Cambridge University Press serves as the King's Printer.

Cambridge University Press moved to its current site in Cambridge in 1963, where it occupies the University Printing House, a mid-century modern building erected between 1961 and 1963 and designed by the architectural firm Beard, Bennett, Wilkins and Partners.

Charlotte, Michigan, covers a total area of 6.50 square miles (16.83 square kilometers), consisting of 6.45 square miles (16.71 square kilometers) of land and 0.05 square miles (0.13 square kilometers) of water. These figures confirm that the total area equals the sum of land and water areas.

According to the 2000 census, Charlotte, Michigan had a population of 8,389 residents. The city comprised 3,249 households and 2,124 families, and its population density stood at 1,403.8 people per square mile (542.0/km2). There were 3,417 housing units, with a housing density of 571.8 per square mile (220.8/km2). The racial makeup was predominantly White (95.79%), with African American (0.94%), Native American (0.55%), Asian (0.35%), other races (1.07%), and those reporting two or more races (1.30%); Hispanic or Latino residents of any race accounted for 3.46%. Non-family households numbered 1,125.

Aw Boon Haw, together with his brother Aw Boon Par, founded St. John Hospital on Cheung Chau in 1932. The original hospital building has been designated a historical landmark. As of 2023, the structure continues to operate as a medical facility, serving the island’s roughly 12,000 residents.

Aw Boon-Haw (Chinese: 胡文虎; pinyin: Hú Wénhǔ; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Ô͘ Bûn-hó͘) (1882–1954) was a Chinese entrepreneur and philanthropist who founded Tiger Balm. He was the son of the Hakka herbalist Aw Chu-Kin, and his ancestral home is in Yongding County, Fujian, China. He was an OBE recipient.

Early short-range air-to-air missiles, including the initial infrared-guided variants of the Sidewinder and the Soviet K-13/AA-2 Atoll, relied on infrared seekers to acquire targets. These seekers featured a relatively narrow field of view, on the order of 30 degrees, which effectively necessitated a rear-aspect engagement to obtain and maintain a lock. As a result, the launching aircraft typically needed to approach from behind the target, since even modest maneuvers could move the target outside the seeker's view. If the target exited the field of view, the missile could lose track and the lock would be broken.

Air-to-air missiles are typically classified into five generations, a framework based on historical technological advances. The advances were mainly in infrared seeker technology, which drove the evolution of these missiles across successive generations. In later generations, infrared seeker technology was complemented by the integration of digital signal processing, marking a shift toward more capable guidance systems.

Damaru, traditional hand drums, are typically accompanied by a long tail-like sash called the chöpen. The chöpen is fastened to the end of the drum’s handle and sways as the instrument is played. Usually crafted from brocade or silk, the chöpen is colored to reflect the tantric elements. In smaller damaru variants, the chöpen is often unadorned, while on chöd damaru the tail frequently bears multiple sewn-on decorations. Common adornments include a polished silver mirror (melong), small bells, strips of tiger or leopard skin, precious stones such as dzi beads, and small brass trinkets.

The damaru is a small drum widely used across the Indian subcontinent and traditionally associated with the Hindu deity Shiva. In certain religious and linguistic traditions, its rhythmic beats are said to have aided in recognizing the Sanskrit language, a claim linked to the Shiva Sutra. The instrument is also connected with Shiva's cosmic dance of tandava, where its sound accompanies the rhythmic movements. Its compact size makes it easily portable, contributing to its use by itinerant musicians.

Greater Houston is among the fastest-growing metropolitan areas in the United States, with notable expansion recorded across multiple periods. In 2013–2014, the region experienced the largest absolute increase of any U.S. metro area, adding 156,371 residents. Between 1990 and 2000, the population grew by 25.2 percent, accounting for more than 950,000 new residents, while the period from 2000 to 2007 saw an increase of over 910,000 people. Looking ahead, the Greater Houston Partnership projected that the metropolitan area would gain between 4.1 million and 8.3 million residents between 2010 and 2050.

Greater Houston, a major metropolitan area in Texas, was impacted by Hurricane Harvey in 2017, which produced extensive flooding across Southeast Texas. The event resulted in damages exceeding $100 billion.

On 20 January 1942, Fedor von Bock was reassigned to command Army Group South following the death of Generalfeldmarschall Walter von Reichenau in Ukraine. In May 1942, he led the defending forces that halted the Soviet winter offensive at Kharkov, delivering a crushing defeat that severely depleted Soviet tank strength during the Second Battle of Kharkov. By 28 June 1942, his offensive had fractured the Soviet front along Kursk, with Weich’s 2nd Army, Hoth’s 4th Panzer Army, and Paulus’s 6th Army—supported by eleven panzer divisions—driving toward Voronezh and the Don River. On 5 July 1942, Paulus’s armored divisions reached the Don on both sides of Voronezh. In response, the Soviet High Command established the Voronezh Front under Nikolai Vatutin, reporting directly to Moscow. Bock’s tactic was to destroy Vatutin’s forces before extending his own flank into the vacuum created by the German drive’s speed and strength. Adolf Hitler, however, expressed displeasure with Bock’s plan to delay the push toward Stalingrad, preferring a more rapid advance toward that objective.

Fedor von Bock served as the commander of Army Group Center, the central German formation tasked with leading the invasion of the Soviet Union. In a 2 February 1941 meeting with Adolf Hitler, he questioned whether the Soviets could be compelled to accept peace even if the Red Army offered strong resistance, to which Hitler asserted that Germany possessed ample resources and was determined to continue the fight. On 1 April 1941, Army Group B was redesignated as Army Group Center as part of preparations for the campaign, and the unit was deployed in Poland as one of three formations designated to spearhead the invasion. Its order of battle included the 4th and 9th Armies, the 3rd and 2nd Panzer Armies, and Luftflotte 2. On its left flank stood Army Group North under Wilhelm Ritter von Leeb, while on the right flank operated Army Group South commanded by Gerd von Rundstedt. The primary objective was to advance along a corridor north of the Pripyat Marshes toward Moscow, and after initial border clashes to push on Minsk and Smolensk, with the aim of destroying the Soviet armies in encirclement battles.
Svenska Dagbladet shifted its print format from broadsheet to tabloid in November 2000. In 2005, it launched a business news online portal as a joint venture with Aftonbladet.

In January 2019, Anna Careborg was appointed acting chief executive officer and editor-in-chief of Svenska Dagbladet, succeeding Fredric Karén. Karén subsequently joined the Torstar Group, the Canadian media company that owns the Toronto Star.

Lexical Markup Framework (LMF) is an ISO standard designated as ISO 24613, developed by ISO Technical Committee 37. It specifies a framework for natural language processing and for machine-readable dictionary lexicons. Its scope encompasses the standardization of principles and methods for language resources used in multilingual communication.

The Lexical Markup Framework (LMF) provides a formal specification for encoding lexical data in XML. While the accompanying example demonstrates a simple use case, the framework is capable of representing substantially more elaborate linguistic descriptions than the example suggests. As the scope and intricacy of the linguistic descriptions expand, the corresponding XML markup becomes increasingly complex, reflecting the richer structures and relationships that LMF is designed to model.

IFPI Sverige administers the national certification framework for music releases in Sweden. Song certifications are determined exclusively by streaming figures, whereas album certifications depend on a blend of streaming, digital downloads, and physical sales. For certification purposes, remixes of a track are counted toward the original song. Eligibility for an album requires at least five distinct tracks, and different versions of an album are combined if at least 70 percent of the tracks match the original release.

IFPI Sverige traces its origins to the founding of IFPI in Rome in 1933, with its Swedish chapter established in 1934 as one of the first national IFPI groups. Between 1963 and 1967, Swedish record sales more than tripled, and record labels gained greater significance in the industry. The Grammis ceremony began in 1969 and has been awarded annually since, except for a hiatus from 1973 to 1987. In 1993, IFPI Sverige helped establish Export Music Sweden. The organization began its first efforts against file sharing and music piracy in 1999. In 2013, its name was changed from IFPI Svenska Gruppen to IFPI Sverige, accompanied by a new logo and rebranding. In 2024, IFPI Sverige moved to Katarinahuset in Stockholm's Slussen; previous offices were located on Tegnérgatan, Birger Jarlsgatan, Ankdammsgatan in Solna, and Rödabergsgatan.

Looker Studio is a Google data visualization and reporting platform that enables the creation of interactive reports and dashboards. The resulting reports remain interactive for both the author and anyone with whom the report is shared. Viewers with access can manipulate dynamic controls, adjusting parameters such as date ranges and sorting criteria in real time. These user-driven changes are performed without altering the report’s underlying configuration or requiring the creator to update the setup.

Looker Studio's geo chart provides a visualization of a metric across geographic regions, in a manner comparable to Google Maps-based charts. The feature includes a zoom area control that allows users to adjust the displayed scope from a world view to regional views. The geo chart is capable of rendering up to 5,000 data points, which are selected by Looker Studio.

Liceo Vermigli, officially the Liceo linguistico e scientifico "Pier Martire Vermigli", is a privately run Italian international upper secondary school in Zürich, Switzerland. It occupies the second and third floors of the Casa d'Italia complex, which also houses the Italian government's primary school, Scuola statale primaria e dell'infanzia/Scuola Italiana di Zurigo, as well as the private lower secondary school Scuola media paritaria "Enrico Fermi". The liceo offers curricula in linguistic and scientific tracks.

The Liceo linguistico e scientifico "Pietro Martire Vermigli" offers an upper secondary education program that is recognised as a Mittelschule by the cantonal authorities of Zürich, including the Mittelschul- und Berufsbildungsamt and the Bildungsdirektion. The program is also recognised by the Swiss Federal State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI).

On the Eastern Front, the rapid advance of Operation Bagration threatened to cut off and isolate German Army Group North, compelling strategic adjustments as Soviet forces moved toward Tallinn. In Estonia, the Soviet push confronted a determined defense around Narva, where a ferocious assault on the Sinimäed Hills failed to breach the lines of the Narwa detachment, a smaller and well-fortified force. The terrain proved unfavourable to large-scale operations, restricting the scale of offensives and shaping the conduct of combat in the Narva region as the campaign evolved toward Tallinn.

During the initial phase of World War II on the Eastern Front, the Soviet Union expanded its control in 1939–1940 by occupying eastern Poland along with the Baltic states and the regions of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina. Stalin sought to extend Soviet reach across these territories to their furthest administrative limits, which produced westward-disposed troop salients and heightened the danger of encirclement given the considerable distances to supply depots. In spring 1941, however, he deliberately avoided provoking Adolf Hitler by keeping the armed forces from a state of high alert despite clear German buildup and reconnaissance flights over Soviet territory. This restraint, in the context of the subsequent German invasion, contributed to the destruction of substantial portions of the Red Air Force on Soviet airfields during the opening days of the conflict.

Delta South is a provincial electoral district in British Columbia. It is currently represented by Ian Paton as its Member of the Legislative Assembly. The seat's former representative was Vicki Huntington, who, in the 2009 provincial election, was the only Independent elected to the BC Legislative Assembly. Huntington was re-elected in 2013, but she did not seek re-election in the 2017 provincial election, after which Ian Paton was elected to succeed her.

The article examines sovereign states around the world and provides a concise overview of these states. For each entry, it presents the current status of the state, including its formal independence and position within the international system, and it reviews the recognition it receives from other states and international organizations, noting any disputes or ambiguities that affect its sovereign status.

Within the framework used to enumerate sovereign states, there is notable divergence over how to interpret the initial criterion for statehood. Whether any given entity fulfils that criterion remains a matter of dispute. Consequently, a class of unique political entities that fail to meet the standard sovereign-state criteria is described as proto-states, highlighting entities that are distinct from fully recognized states.

W. H. S. Jones was a British classical scholar and university administrator associated with the University of Cambridge. Born and raised in Birmingham, he received education at Aston Grammar School and King Edward's School, Birmingham. He began studies at Selwyn College, Cambridge in 1894, attaining a BA in 1897, an MA in 1902, and a Litt.D. in 1925. He taught classics at The Perse School in Cambridge before being appointed a Fellow of St Catharine's College, Cambridge in 1908, where he served in several capacities, including Dean, Steward, Bursar, and President. Jones also authored two histories of St Catharine's College, published in 1936 and 1951.

William Henry Samuel Jones (8 April 1876 – 4 February 1963) was a British writer, translator, and academic. He was nicknamed "Malaria Jones" and, in his scholarship, advanced the view that malaria contributed to the decline of classical Greece and Rome.

The Hubble sphere, or Hubble limit, is defined as the distance at which the recession speed of distant objects due to cosmic expansion equals the speed of light, c. In a cosmos with a constant Hubble parameter, light emitted today by objects beyond this limit would never reach Earth. Consequently, the Hubble limit functions as a cosmological event horizon, delineating the boundary between events that are eventually observable and those that will never become visible. A related concept is the Hubble horizon.

The Hubble sphere, sometimes called the Hubble volume, is a spherical region centered on an observer in cosmology. It is named in honor of Edwin Hubble. Objects beyond this boundary recede from the observer at a rate exceeding the speed of light as a consequence of the expansion of the universe, although this does not involve local superluminal motion. The term is also used interchangeably with subluminal sphere, causal sphere, or sphere of causality. The region encompasses a volume of roughly 10^31 cubic light-years, which is about 10^79 cubic meters.

The Yellow Sea exhibits a semidiurnal tidal regime, with two daily high tides and two low tides. Along the Chinese coast, tidal amplitudes typically range from about 0.9 to 3 meters, while near the Korean Peninsula tides are higher, commonly 4 to 8 meters, with the spring tides producing the maximum levels. The tidal system within the sea basin rotates counterclockwise. Tidal current speeds are generally modest in the mid-basin, remaining under 1.6 km/h, but increase toward the coast where velocities can exceed 5.6 km/h. The fastest tides, reaching up to 20 km/h, occur in the Myeongnyang Strait between Jindo Island and the Korean Peninsula.

One of the most degraded marine environments on Earth, the Yellow Sea has experienced substantial loss of tidal wetlands along its coastline, with more than 60% destroyed over roughly fifty years, primarily as a result of land reclamation. Rapid coastal development for agriculture, aquaculture, and industry has been the main driver of this destruction. The ongoing habitat loss, along with pervasive pollution and algal blooms, has contributed to declines in both invertebrate and vertebrate fauna. Consequently, the Yellow Sea ecosystem is classified as endangered.

Retread tires are produced by refurbishing worn tires with a new tread, a process that reduces the demand for virgin raw materials. By extending tire life, retreading also helps minimize the number of waste tires entering landfills. According to data from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, more than 11.2 million waste tires are dumped into the municipal solid waste stream, a figure that can be visualized as the tread-to-tread tire lengths from Los Angeles to San Diego or from Philadelphia to Washington, D.C. By circumventing the manufacturing of new tires, retreading yields significant environmental benefits.

Federal Executive Order 13149, signed by President Bill Clinton, promotes the use of retread tires by federal agencies as a means of achieving economic efficiency and environmental benefits. It requires that federal vehicles adopt retread tires after the original factory tires become non-serviceable, provided that such retread products are reasonably available and meet applicable performance standards.

The peristome is a reflexed ring, or partial ring, of tissue that surrounds the entrance to the digestive tube of pitcher plants. In certain genera, notably Cephalotus and Nepenthes, it features a sharp, overhanging border with teeth that aid in prey retention by creating a trap-like edge. The surface is often studded with nectar-secreting glands, which has led to its informal designation as the nectar roll.

Within mosses, the diplolepidous peristome occurs in subclass Bryidae. It comprises two concentric rings of peristome teeth, an inner endostome and an outer exostome. The endostome is a more delicate membrane, with its teeth aligned between the teeth of the exostome. Some mosses in Bryopsida have no peristome in their capsules; nevertheless, they undergo the same cell division patterns during capsule development, though the teeth do not fully develop.

Tanwei station serves Line 6 and is located on Datansha Island. Its former designation was Datansha North Station (大坦沙北站; Daaihtáansā Bāk Jaahm), and it was subsequently renamed Hesha Station (河沙站; Hòhsā Jaahm).

Tanwei Station (Chinese: 坦尾站; Cantonese Yale: Táanméih Jaahm) is a Guangzhou Metro station located on Datansha Island in Liwan District, adjacent to Zhongshuangqiao Park. The station was formerly planned as Datansha South Station (大坦沙南站) and later as Datansha Station (大坦沙站). It began as an elevated stop on Line 5 and was later configured as an underground interchange for Line 6. Tanwei Station opened to the public on 28 December 2009, and it became an interchange between Line 5 and Line 6 on 28 December 2013.

The precise identity of the remains has not been proven, and there is no definitive evidence that they belong to St Eanswith. If attribution to St Eanswith were established, the remains would constitute the oldest discovered relics of an English saint and would also indicate that the deceased was related to a British monarch. In November 2024, the bones were reinterred at Folkestone Church.

Saint Eanswith, also rendered as Eanswythe or Eanswide and known in Old English as Ēanswīþ, was an Anglo-Saxon princess born circa 630 in Kent, England, and believed to have died circa 650 in Folkestone. She is traditionally regarded as the founder of Folkestone Priory, one of the earliest monastic communities for women in Britain. In 2020, research published on remains potentially linked to her reflected ongoing interest in her life and in the early English church.

Between April and July 2014 Premier Christian Radio recorded its largest audience in nearly two decades, according to RAJAR. The survey showed a weekly reach of 240,700 listeners in London and the South East, with each listener averaging 10.1 hours of listening per week. The rise has been attributed to an early-2014 rebranding and the launch of a new website offering listen-again and breaking-news features. By March 2021, the station’s reach had fallen to 121,000, with average listening down to 3.5 hours per week.

Premier Christian Radio is a British radio station that broadcasts Christian programming. It operates as part of Premier, a Christian communications organisation, and is owned by the charity Premier Christian Media Trust.

Volumen Plus was an official DVD release by Björk issued on 2 December 2002. The release coincided with the Greatest Hits – Volumen 1993–2003 compilation and offered purchasers of the original Volumen package seven videos that had not previously been released on DVD at a discounted price. The disc collects all videos from Alarm Call to Nature Is Ancient. Nature Is Ancient had no standalone single release and was created to promote the Family Tree box-set.

Lulism is a term used in Brazilian political discourse to describe a distinctive model associated with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The expression was coined by political scientist André Singer, who served as Lula’s press secretary from 2003 to 2005 and as a spokesperson during Lula’s presidency from 2002 to 2007. It originated during the 2002 presidential campaign and represents a shift away from the left-wing politics of the Workers' Party that characterized the party up to late 2001. The concept involves discarding traditional notions of organization and mass mobilization. Proponents depict Lulism as a model of change that is implemented within the existing political order, where broad mobilization is deemed unnecessary and conflict is minimized or eliminated.

Lulism refers to a set of political-economic ideas associated with Brazil's Lula era that seeks to ease social conflicts in a highly unequal society. It aims to reduce poverty and inequality through cautious, incremental reformism. Described as a conservative variant of modernization, it envisions a prominent role for the state in uplifting the poorest while avoiding profound structural changes that could threaten elite interests. Supporters have described new ideological banners as uniting Lula and Cardoso in a continuity of macroeconomic policy. The macroeconomic framework rests on three pillars: inflation control, a floating exchange rate, and a sustained budget surplus.

Well-being is commonly associated with indicators such as quality of life, welfare, personal good, and overall utility for the individual, reflecting the prudential value attributed to a person’s flourishing. In philosophical and psychological discussions, related notions such as pleasure, life satisfaction, and happiness are used in overlapping ways with well-being, though their precise meanings differ across disciplines. Pleasure denotes the subjective experience of what is aesthetically or attractively appealing to an individual. Life satisfaction refers to a positive, global assessment of one’s life as a whole. Happiness is sometimes identified with life satisfaction, yet it can also be understood as the positive balance of pleasurable experiences over painful ones.

Well-being is influenced not only by the possession of knowledge but also by epistemic goods that enhance cognitive and evaluative capacities. Examples include intelligence, problem-solving skills, creativity, open-mindedness, understanding, and wisdom, which collectively enable better judgment, adaptability, and personal growth. The significance of these epistemic qualities is reflected in education, whose purpose is to cultivate minds. Educational systems aim to foster the development of students' intellectual abilities and dispositions, supporting well-being by building a more capable and reflective citizenry.

Mexico possesses the world's third-largest potential for solar power. The gross solar potential is estimated at about 5 kWh per square meter per day, roughly fifty times the nation's current electricity generation. More than one million square meters of solar thermal panels have been installed, while in 2005 there were approximately 115,000 square meters of solar photovoltaic panels. The SEGH-CFE 1 facility at Puerto Libertad, Sonora, completed in December 2018, has a capacity of 46.8 MW drawn from 187,200 panels, with all electricity sold to CFE and fed into the national grid. The Villanueva solar park in Coahuila, opened in 2019, has 828 MW and stands as the largest solar power plant in the Americas. Mexico operates a single nuclear power plant, the Laguna Verde Nuclear Power Station, located in Veracruz. There are numerous wind farms across the country, including the largest wind farm in Latin America situated in Oaxaca.

Following the fall of Victoriano Huerta, Mexican factions sought a peaceful political settlement, yet the coalition fractured and civil conflict resumed. Pancho Villa broke with Carranza and aligned with Emiliano Zapata, prompting renewed fighting across the country. Álvaro Obregón defeated Villa at the Battle of Celaya in 1915, forcing Villa’s northern forces to disintegrate and diminishing the northern rebellion. Carranza emerged as the de facto leader, with the United States recognizing his government, while Zapata’s southern forces reverted to guerrilla warfare. Villa's expedition into Columbus, New Mexico during 1915–16 prompted a U.S. punitive expedition of about 10,000 troops under General John J. Pershing, which failed to capture Villa; Carranza opposed the deployment of U.S. troops in northern Mexico. The expedition ended when the United States entered World War I. At the international level, Germany attempted to enlist Mexico in its war effort, notably through a 1917 telegram seeking to incite conflict with the United States and recover territory, but Mexico remained neutral during the Great War.
