The Tudela Codex is a mid-16th-century manuscript produced in Mexico during the early colonial period. It was created on European laid paper and consists of three parts: Libro Indígena, Libro Pintado Europeo, and Libro Escrito Europeo.

Codex Tudela is a 16th-century Aztec pictorial manuscript. It is derived from a common prototype shared with the Codex Magliabechiano and the Codex Ixtlilxochitl, as well as with other documents that constitute the Magliabechiano Group.

Yama and Dharmadeva are commonly identified as the same deity in Hindu tradition. This identification is reinforced in certain readings of the Mahabharata, where Vyasa uses Dharmaraja, Vṛsa, and Yama as interchangeable references for Dharmadeva, a practice that has contributed to the impression of a single figure. The epithet Dharmaraja arises from the moral weighing of a person’s conduct by Kala, who judges virtue against vice. Dharmadeva is regarded as the incarnation of Dharma, a characterization that explains one of his names. In some accounts, Kāla is equated with Yama, suggesting that Yama may be his true name. The attribution of the designation Yama to Dharmadeva is sometimes explained by the idea that he embodies Yama through self-control and the moral governance of conduct.

Yama is a term whose primary sense is related to the idea of being a twin, a relationship reflected in the surrounding figure of his twin sister, Yami. Over time, the lexical range of Yama expanded to include the notion of a binder, derived from the root yam, and the term also encompasses ethical dimensions, including moral rule or duty, paralleling the concept of dharma. In addition, it is used to denote qualities such as self-control, forbearance, and cessation.

Elton Gallegly's advocacy centered on animal rights. In 1999 he authored a bill that later became federal law, criminalizing the sale of videos depicting dogfights and other acts of animal cruelty. The legislation aimed to prevent profit derived from the mistreatment of animals. On April 20, 2010, the Supreme Court overturned the law in an 8–1 decision, with Chief Justice John Roberts writing the majority opinion, holding that the statute violated the First Amendment right to freedom of speech and describing it as an overly broad criminal prohibition.

Elton Gallegly assumed office after incumbent Bobbi Fiedler retired to run for the U.S. Senate. He won the 1986 Republican primary with 50 percent of the vote against Tony Hope and then captured the general election with 68 percent. Gallegly was reelected in 1988 with 69 percent of the vote and again in 1990 with 58 percent. In the 1992 election, he defeated Democrat Anita Perez Ferguson, 54 percent to 41 percent. In subsequent elections he was reelected with at least 58 percent of the vote, except in 2000 when he defeated Michael Case 54–41.

Ash derived from wood has historically served as a laundry aid in various traditional settings, leveraging its alkaline properties to help remove soils. It is free to use where wood ash is readily available and easy to produce as a byproduct of burning wood. The practice is often described as sustainable due to its minimal processing and reuse of a waste material. Some accounts suggest that ash can be as effective as standard laundry methods for certain stains and fabrics, though outcomes may vary with ash composition and application.

Ash produced from incinerated wood contains only small quantities of sulfur, chlorine, iron, and sodium. Aluminum, zinc, and boron are present only rarely in wood ash. The trace-element composition of ash reflects the elements absorbed from the soil by the plants before combustion, meaning the ash’s minor constituents are determined by the soil's available nutrients and the plant uptake.

Abui displays a noun-phrase structure in which deictic demonstratives mark the referent’s spatial location and, when accompanied by possessor marking, precede the head noun. After the head noun, adjectives, stative verbs, and quantifiers follow. The final constituent of the noun phrase is typically an anaphoric demonstrative (DEMa) that encodes the referent’s discourse location. Noun-modifying clauses (NMC) usually appear post-head and are linked to the head with the particle ba; however, a subtype of NMCs that elaborates on the referent’s location may occur pre-head, occupying the same position as the deictic demonstrative.

Studies of Abui indicate that speakers of Proto-Alor-Pantar borrowed Austronesian vocabulary before the diversification of Proto-AP. The borrowed items underwent regular sound changes, consistent with the historical phonology of Proto-AP. Consequently, these Austronesian loanwords can be reconstructed for Proto-AP, reflecting an early stage of lexical exchange and contributing to the reconstruction of the proto-language’s lexicon.

By the evening of 26 September, hostilities had largely ceased. Japan subsequently established control over several strategic facilities, including Gia Lam Airbase just outside Hanoi, the rail marshaling yard at Lao Cai on the Yunnan border, and Phu Lang Thuong on the Hanoi–Lang Son railway. To consolidate its position, Japanese forces stationed about 900 troops at the port of Haiphong and roughly 600 in Hanoi.

On 26 September, Japanese forces conducted a landing at Dong Tac, south of Haiphong, and advanced toward the port city. A second landing subsequently brought additional tanks ashore to bolster the assault. Japanese aircraft bombed Haiphong, producing casualties, and by early afternoon the advancing force numbered about 4,500 troops with roughly a dozen tanks, positioned outside Haiphong.

Calvörde is a municipality whose area shows early settlement evidence from the Iron Age Jastorf culture, with archaeological excavations indicating occupation around 600–300 BC. The medieval settlement is first documented in 1196. The toponym likely reflects a ford crossing the Ohre river at the site of a later bridge, and the name has been connected to the idea of a shallow or bare ford; however, local tradition also ties the ford to a man named Kale, yielding the form Kale’s ford. Historically, a trade corridor linking Leipzig and Magdeburg crossed the Ohre at Calvörde, continuing northwest to Lüneburg and Hamburg, with a western branch serving Braunschweig.

Calvörde Castle is first documented in the late 13th century, and from 1318 it was held by Duke Otto of Brunswick. The Welf dukes repeatedly pledged the castle to local noble families, including the House of Alvensleben. The adjacent market town prospered, gaining city walls, a town council, and its own seal. In 1571 Calvörde passed to the Principality of Wolfenbüttel under Duke Julius of Brunswick, and together with surrounding villages and estates it was reorganised as the Amt Calvörde. The Amt remained an eastern exclave of the Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg, situated between the Brandenburgian Altmark to the north and the Archbishopric of Magdeburg to the south.

Solar granules are convection cells on the Sun's photosphere that originate from upwellings of plasma in the adjacent convective zone beneath the photosphere. The grainy texture observed on the solar surface is produced by the tops of these convective cells, and the overall pattern is known as granulation.

Solar granules are the visible manifestations of convective cells in the Sun’s photosphere. Typical granules measure about 1,500 kilometers across, or roughly 930 miles, and their lifetimes are short, on the order of eight to twenty minutes before they are replaced by neighboring upwellings of hot plasma. At any given moment, an estimated four million granules cover the solar surface. Beneath the photosphere lies a broader convective pattern known as supergranulation, which comprises much larger cells. Supergranules can reach diameters up to about 30,000 kilometers (approximately 19,000 miles) and have lifetimes of up to around 24 hours.

The chief risk officer is typically charged with providing a unified view of risk across the organization, but a siloed structure can reduce this role to reactive crisis management rather than an integrated framework. In such environments, no single individual may hold overall accountability for consolidated risk reporting or for the provisioning of risk-related units, undermining coherence and responsibility. Segmentation by risk across multiple business units can diminish the overall effectiveness of risk governance, as coordination and standardization are weakened. Additionally, different units may employ varied methodologies to monitor counterparty risk, leading to inconsistent assessments. This fragmentation can allow total counterparty exposure to grow beyond what the organization can effectively monitor and manage.

Within enterprise risk management, risk transfer is a key component of mitigating uncertainty. The Chief Risk Officer determines whether to spread risk by transferring it to external parties or to retain it internally. If risk is spread, it may be transferred to an external insurer or allocated to a subsidiary within the corporate group. Companies typically accomplish risk transfer by purchasing insurance, with workers' compensation, general liability, and property/casualty insurance representing the three preferred coverage areas.

Edward Moran resided in New York City for most of his life and remained there until his death on June 8, 1901. He was interred at Woodlawn Cemetery in the Bronx. Several years before his death, he presented a series of thirteen paintings to his wife. After his death, a dispute over ownership of the works arose, with the executor of Moran's estate refusing to surrender them, arguing they were under his protection. The Supreme Court in New York City subsequently ruled in favor of Moran's widow.

Around the mid-1840s, Edward Moran began an apprenticeship in Philadelphia with James Hamilton and the landscape painter Paul Weber, with Hamilton guiding him in the development of a marine painting style. In the 1850s, Moran gained recognition within the Philadelphia art scene. He worked in the same studio as his younger brother, Thomas Moran, and went on to receive commissions and complete lithographic work.

Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) is a United States government agency responsible for managing the government's financial operations, including payroll services. In 2003, the Office of Personnel Management selected DFAS to provide payroll services for the federal government. In 2004, the DFAS portal, known as ePortal, was recognized by Nielsen Norman Group as one of the ten best government intranets worldwide. Nielsen also observed that leading intranets tend to exhibit strong usability and clear organization, robust performance metrics, and steady, incremental improvements after reviewing hundreds of intranets.

Reuters reported that the Pentagon spent tens of billions of dollars upgrading information technology in preparation for an audit of its finances, with the upgrades intended to support the audit process. A significant portion of the new systems failed to perform all required functions or were scrapped, and these failures reportedly contributed to waste rather than reducing it. The report situates these developments within the Defense Finance and Accounting Service's efforts to achieve audit readiness.

The term superstructure denotes the upper portion of a structure, typically the span that directly sustains live loads such as traffic and pedestrians, and then transfers those loads to the underlying supports. By contrast, the substructure comprises the elements that provide the foundation and transfer forces to the ground, including components like abutments, piers, and other supporting members. This division reflects the functional separation between the load-bearing superstructure and the supports that anchor the structure to its foundation.

A superstructure denotes the portion of a structure that rises above its base or foundation, representing the upward extension that sits above the baseline. The concept applies across many kinds of physical constructions rather than being limited to a single category. Typical examples include buildings, bridges, and ships, in which the superstructure comprises the elements developed above the supporting lower portions.

Denim & Rhinestones Tour contributes to charity by donating one dollar for every ticket sold to the Tunnels to Towers Foundation, a nonprofit organization that supports veterans and their families. This philanthropic effort continues a practice established on Underwood's prior tours. General admission tickets for the tour went on sale on May 20.

Denim & Rhinestones Tour, as reviewed by Bob Gendron of the Chicago Tribune, showcased Underwood's performance that leaned toward rock influences despite abundant Southern-inspired attire and accents, and was described as a vibrant concert. At the age of 39, the artist signaled the ability to succeed across genres and to perform with apparent ease. A point of contention in the critique was the inclusion of a prerecorded video clip of Jason Aldean performing his part in "If I Didn't Love You," which was described as a serious misstep and perceived as artificial.

The Red Bull Racing RB15 competed at the German Grand Prix with Verstappen qualifying third and Gasly fourth, aided by Ferrari power-unit issues affecting Ferrari drivers. The race was a chaotic wet-to-dry affair. Verstappen secured the victory, marking his seventh career win and second of the season, despite spinning on lap 27. Gasly endured a poor start, dropping several places on the opening lap, spent much of the race in midfield, and retired on lap 62 after colliding with Alex Albon's Toro Rosso approaching Turn 7.

At the Italian Grand Prix, Red Bull Racing's RB15 faced reliability and performance issues for Max Verstappen, who was set to start from the back of the grid after new power unit components were fitted; he also suffered a power unit problem in qualifying, failing to set a lap time. Alexander Albon progressed to Q3 but did not post a time there because several drivers eased off to avoid the slipstream, resulting in an eighth-place grid slot. In the race, Verstappen was held up by slow-moving cars at Turn 1, sustained front-wing damage, pitted at the end of the first lap, and finished eighth, while Albon completed the event in sixth after colliding with Carlos Sainz Jr. at the first Lesmo corner on Lap 3, which sent him into the gravel and cost him positions.

Data center security encompasses a holistic, systems-focused approach to risk assessment and defense across physical infrastructure, network, and application layers. It demands an ongoing program of improvement to keep pace with the evolving data-center landscape, driven by the introduction of new applications and services. In parallel, attackers are growing more sophisticated and frequent, making continual evaluation and updating of security readiness essential to maintain resilience and protection of critical assets.

Layer 2 attacks pose a security concern within data center environments. These attacks exploit vulnerabilities in data link layer protocols and in their implementations, with adversaries targeting the software and firmware that realize these protocols. They predominantly operate on Layer 2 switching platforms, where such weaknesses can be exploited on the switching hardware itself.

Projectile motion is governed by the propelling force acting on the projectile’s mass, which serves as the dominant influence on its movement. In many sports, this initiating force arises from muscular action that accelerates the projectile. Examples of projectiles include a ball, a disc, a javelin, a hammer, and a dart. The magnitude of the propelling force determines the resulting speed and range, with a stronger force yielding greater velocity and longer travel. Related contexts include pitching and bowling.

Projectiles are munitions designed to be propelled toward a target, and they may carry an explosive payload as well as chemical or biological substances. In addition to delivering blasts, some designs aim to produce particular kinds of damage through non-explosive effects. Historical examples include incendiary outcomes intended to ignite targets or surrounding material, as well as toxic effects delivered by poisoned-tipped arrows and similar weapons.
The Tagbanwa script is an indigenous writing system native to the Philippines. It functions as the ethnic writing system of the Tagbanwa and Palawan peoples.

Tagbanwa is an alphasyllabary (abugida) in which each sign represents a syllable formed by a consonant with an inherent vowel /a/. Like other Southeast Asian scripts derived from Indian Brahmic traditions, vowels other than /a/ are indicated by diacritics. The vowels /i/ and /u/ are shown by diacritics placed above the consonant (for /i/) or below it (for /u/). Independent letters exist for the vowels /a/, /i/, and /u/ to spell the standalone vowels. When a syllable ends in a consonant, the writing does not include an explicit final consonant sign. Tagbanwa differs from Baybayin in the shapes of several letters, notably ka and wa, which are markedly distinct.

Within BBC Scotland, the position of Head of Radio, Scotland was a formal post responsible for overseeing the Radio Scotland service and for BBC Scotland’s radio productions that were produced for other networks.

BBC Radio Scotland is a BBC Scotland–operated radio service that offers a broad range of programming, including news, debate, music, drama, comedy, and sport. It broadcasts from its headquarters at Pacific Quay in Glasgow, Scotland. During overnight downtime, the station simulcasts BBC Radio 5 Live.

Jean de Boullonges held several high-level financial and governmental posts in 18th-century France. He began as an adviser to the Parliament of Metz in 1726, later serving as intendant of finance in 1744. He was named a State Councillor and a member of the Royal Council of Finance, and on 25 August 1757 he was appointed Controller General of Finance, succeeding François Marie Peyrenc de Moras. He remained in that office until 4 March 1759.

Deep Medi Musik is an independent record label recognized for presenting immersive electronic music, guided by an ethos described as music that listeners can feel. A notable tradition associated with its signings is that the debut release of a new artist on the label often features a portrait drawn by Tunnidge. Tunnidge himself is an artist who has released multiple EPs through Deep Medi Musik, contributing to the label’s ongoing roster.

During the rollout of fifth-generation networks, some operators promoted upgraded 4G services in ways that suggested 5G capability, presenting enhanced LTE networks as stepping stones toward true 5G or as functionally equivalent improvements. In certain marketing campaigns these offerings were described as precursors to 5G or as ready for 5G, and they leveraged LTE Advanced Pro features such as 4x4 MIMO to raise data speeds. However, they did not meet the 3GPP-defined criteria for 5G.

Analysts have argued that the marketing surrounding 5G has often overstated its capabilities, with critics noting that the practical benefits for many users can be limited in early deployments. While 5G is associated with higher peak speeds and lower latency, real-world improvements are frequently contingent on specific use cases and network conditions. A technical limitation involves the use of millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies, which can provide high data rates but suffer from a short propagation range and limited penetration, necessitating dense infrastructure to maintain coverage. Additionally, some observers have pointed out that improvements not unique to 5G are sometimes branded as 5G, a practice that can contribute to consumer confusion regarding the technology's actual advantages.

UEFA Champions League 2006–2007 served as the official video game tie-in for the 2006–07 UEFA Champions League season. Developed by EA Canada, the title was published worldwide by Electronic Arts under the EA Sports label. It was released in North America on March 20, 2007, in Australia on March 22, 2007, and in Europe on March 23, 2007.

UEFA Champions League 2006–2007 was EA Sports' last title to feature the UEFA Champions League until FIFA 19. An interval of more than eleven years elapsed before EA Sports regained the license. During that period, Konami held the Champions League license, and the competition appeared in all Pro Evolution Soccer games from PES 2009 to PES 2018.

Celebration achieved stronger performance across Europe, with notable success on the UK Singles Chart where it debuted and peaked at number three on 20 September 2009, spending seven weeks on the chart and marking Madonna’s 63rd UK top-ten, a stature not matched again in the UK until 2023's collaboration on “Popular” with The Weeknd and Playboi Carti. The track reached the top position in Scotland, Italy, Bulgaria, Sweden, and Finland, the latter clocking six non-consecutive weeks at the summit. In Italy it earned a Platinum certification from FIMI for shipments of 60,000 copies, while Finland received Gold status from IFPI. It also reached the top five in France and Germany, the top ten in Ireland and Austria, and narrowly made the top twenty in Spain. On the European Hot 100 Singles chart it peaked at number two, behind David Guetta’s “Sexy Chick” in 2009. Outside Europe, the song reached number 40 in Australia and number five in Japan.

Celebration and Revolver were criticized for their unfavorable reception when contrasted with the additional tracks Justify My Love and Rescue Me included on The Immaculate Collection, which many viewed as signaling Madonna’s direction for the coming decade. Pitchfork’s Douglas Wolk described both songs as throwaways, while Slant Magazine’s Eric Henderson characterized them as dance numbers with zero traction, unworthy to kiss the feet of Justify My Love and Rescue Me.

City gates, embedded in the defensive walls of a city, controlled entry and exit for people, vehicles, goods, and livestock. They performed a range of functions beyond access control, including defense and security, public health oversight, regulation of trade and taxation, and the representation of authority. Gate structures were typically staffed by military personnel or municipal officials who managed passage and enforcement. They also functioned as public information points, displaying announcements, tax and toll schedules, standards of local measures, and legal texts. Many gates were heavily fortified and adorned with heraldic devices, sculptures, or inscriptions. In some contexts they served to warn or intimidate, such as by displaying the heads of beheaded criminals or other public enemies.

San Juan is a World Heritage Site, and its historic city walls include five gates. The principal entrance, Puerta de San Juan, remains preserved today and was erected in 1635. The remaining gates are Puerta de San José, Puerta de Santa Rosa, Puerta de San Justo, and Puerta de Santiago. Puerta de Santiago was built between 1635 and 1641 under the direction of Captain General Íñigo de la Mota Sarmiento.

The libgsm project provides a free software codec that can encode and decode GSM Full Rate audio. Libgsm was developed between 1992 and 1994 by Jutta Degener and Carsten Bormann at Technische Universität Berlin. In the implementation, a GSM speech frame is conceptually 32.5 bytes, and the encoder uses a 33-byte nibble-padded frame representation. At a processing rate of 50 frames per second, this padded framing yields 13.2 kbit/s, a figure that is sometimes cited as the GSM bit rate and is thus the basis for an incorrect claim about GSM's actual rate. The codec can be compiled into the Wine compatibility layer to provide GSM audio support within that environment.

Full Rate is a digital representation that can be produced directly by an analog-to-digital converter present in devices such as telephones or computers. It may also be obtained by converting G.711 PCM data, which is 8-bit nonlinear A-law or μ-law encoded, as carried over the public switched telephone network. In the PSTN-originated path, this conversion relies on a lookup table to map the G.711 samples into the Full Rate format.

Jason Miller, born John Anthony Miller Jr., in Queens, New York City, is an American playwright. He was the son of Mary Claire Miller (née Collins), a teacher, and John Anthony Miller Sr., an electrician. Miller's heritage is described as predominantly Irish Catholic, with some German ancestry.

Jason Miller (playwright) was the father of actors Jason Patric and Joshua John Miller. Patric is the son of Miller and his first wife Linda Gleason, who is Jackie Gleason's daughter. Joshua John Miller is the son of Miller and his second wife Susan Bernard.

Dalén light refers to a lighthouse illumination system that was used from the early 20th century until the 1960s, after which electric lighting became dominant. The technology relied on a carbide lamp powered by acetylene, a gas whose development occurred in the early 1900s. Nevertheless, the safe storage of acetylene posed challenges, requiring regular refilling and thereby limiting the practicality of such lamps for lighthouse use. Gustaf Dalén, who was blinded in an acetylene-related accident, invented the AGA cooker in 1922 during his recovery.
The Dalén light is a flashing beacon that operates by burning acetylene gas derived from carbide. It features a solar sensor that automatically activates the beacon only when it is dark.

New York City's climate features cold, damp winters and hot, humid summers. Prevailing winds generate sea breezes that blow offshore, tempering the Atlantic Ocean's moderating effect on the city. Nevertheless, the Atlantic and the partial shielding provided by the Appalachian Mountains help keep NYC warmer in winter than inland cities at similar or lower latitudes. The January daily mean temperature is about 33.3 °F (0.7 °C). Winter temperatures can fall to around 10 °F (−12 °C) on several occasions, while some days in the coldest month can reach about 60 °F (16 °C). Spring and autumn are variable, ranging from cool to warm, but are generally mild with low humidity. Summers are typically hot and humid, with the July daily mean around 77.5 °F (25.3 °C).

New York City operates under a right-to-shelter statute that requires the municipality to provide shelter and meals to anyone in need, irrespective of immigration status, income level, or housing situation. The city actively enforces this obligation to ensure adequate shelter and food are available to those seeking assistance. It is commonly noted as having the largest total homeless population among American cities. Nevertheless, only a small portion of the homeless—about 5 percent—live outdoors, indicating a lower rate of unsheltered homelessness compared with many other major urban areas. In 2023, approximately 92,824 homeless people slept nightly within the city’s shelter system.

The 2000–01 DFB-Pokal was conducted using two time zones to reflect Europe’s daylight-saving adjustments. Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) was in effect for matches up to 28 October 2000 and from 25 March 2001 onward, while Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) was used for fixtures between 29 October 2000 and 24 March 2001. This schedule mirrors the customary European DST pattern, with clocks moved forward in late March and set back in late October.

The 2000–01 DFB-Pokal was the 58th edition of Germany's annual national knockout football cup competition. Sixty-four teams competed in the tournament, which was played over six rounds from 25 August 2000 to 26 May 2001. Schalke 04 claimed the title by defeating Union Berlin 2–0 in the final, with Union Berlin competing in the third tier at that time. The triumph marked Schalke 04's third DFB-Pokal victory.
In 2010, Céu was invited by Herbie Hancock to record a rendition of Tempo de Amor for The Imagine Project, and in the same year she performed at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival.

Céu contributed a rendition of "It's a Long Way" in 2011, collaborating with Apollo Nove and N.A.S.A. for Red Hot Organization's charity compilation Red Hot + Rio 2, which served as the successor to the 1996 collection Red Hot + Rio. In 2012, she earned her third Latin Grammy nomination in the Best Contemporary Brazilian Pop Album category for her third album, Caravana Sereia Bloom.

In 2022, OCLC broadened its membership and governance framework to allow any institution that subscribes to qualifying OCLC products to join. Previously, membership was tied to contributing intellectual content or participating in global resource sharing and reference services. Under the updated criteria, for-profit organizations that are part of OCLC's partner program are excluded from eligibility. The move reflected the expansion of OCLC's services, which grew in response to corporate acquisitions and the resulting broadening of its offerings.

WebJunction, a division of OCLC, offers training services for librarians and provides professional development resources to support library staff. As a subsidiary within OCLC, it focuses on educational programs that address the needs of the library community. The division's activities are financed through grants from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, with funding beginning in 2003.

Software development comprises several methodologies, each optimized for different kinds of projects. The suitability of a given approach depends on a combination of factors, including technical requirements, organizational structure and culture, the nature and constraints of the project, and the skills and composition of the development team. Consequently, organizations typically select methods that align with both the specific goals of the project and the capabilities of the team, rather than relying on a universal solution.

Software development is a discipline that frequently relies on iterative processes in which planning, design, coding, and testing are interwoven to improve flexibility, efficiency, and realistic scheduling. Development proceeds incrementally by concentrating on individual components rather than attempting to complete the entire project at once, enabling tighter focus and progressive integration. This approach supports prioritization of features, as lower-priority items may be dropped later if necessary to meet constraints. Agile has become a widely used development method, originally suited to small or medium-sized projects, and it emphasizes granting developers greater control over the features they work on to reduce the risk of time or cost overruns. Derivatives of Agile include extreme programming (XP) and Scrum. Open-source software development commonly adopts Agile principles, with concurrent design, coding, and testing driven by a distributed network of volunteer contributors.

Woody Woodpecker Goes to Camp follows Woody’s arrival at a summer camp where he befriends the camp director Angie and her daughter Maggie while also inadvertently stirring up mischief. The antagonistic Buzz makes several failed attempts to ruin the camp, yet Woody earns the campers’ trust and helps prepare them for the Wilderness Games. After meeting Buzz and a confrontation, Woody is framed for causing chaos once more. Inspector Wally Walrus arrives and threatens to shut the camp down, but Woody convinces him to grant a further chance by letting the campers compete in the Wilderness Games. Camp Woo Hoo historically loses to Camp Hoo Rah; the Woo Hoos are artistic creators while the Hoo Rahs are tough soldiers, a imbalance that discourages the campers’ self-esteem. After a string of losses, the Woo Hoos begin translating their artistic talents into practical assets that can be used in competition. During the Games, Buzz sabotages Woo Hoo’s chances and communicates by phone with an accomplice to locate a treasure.

Woody Woodpecker Goes to Camp is a 2024 American live-action animated slapstick comedy film directed by Jon Rosenbaum in his feature directorial debut. Produced by Jon Kuyper, the project features a screenplay by Jim Martin, Cory Edwards, and Stephen Mazur from a story by Mazur and Edwards, and is based on the Woody Woodpecker cartoon character. The film acts as a standalone sequel to the 2017 Woody Woodpecker and marks the second installment in the live-action Woody Woodpecker film series. Universal 1440 Entertainment and Universal Animation Studios produced the feature, which was distributed by Netflix and released on April 12, 2024.

On May 17, 2025, Zscaler announced its intention to acquire Red Canary, a U.S.-based provider of managed detection and response (MDR) services. The purchase price for the transaction was not disclosed.

Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange is a platform that consolidates cybersecurity threat protection, data protection, zero-trust connectivity, and business analytics to enable secure, identity-driven access across enterprise networks. The platform was first announced at Zenith Live in June 2023.

During the early spring of 1944 in Ukraine, the weather conditions complicated the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive. Snowmelt began in January, followed by periods of wet snow and rain, while February was characterized by intermittent frosts and snowstorms and a gradual warming toward the end of the month. From 27 January to 18 February 1944, there were ten days of constant rain and wet snow, five days without precipitation, and the remaining days saw ongoing snowfall. Daily mean temperatures ranged from about -5.5°C to +4.9°C. Consequently, rivers swelled and roads became extremely muddy, with terrain off roads becoming difficult to traverse, thereby impacting movement and logistics for military forces.

During the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive, the Wehrmacht sustained heavy losses, with around 20 divisions destroyed, disbanded, or needing major rebuilding. An additional roughly 60 divisions were reduced to about half of their established strength. The campaign also produced severe equipment losses, including thousands of tanks, assault guns, artillery pieces, and trucks. A significant portion of these losses occurred due to abandonment in the spring mud. German military historian Kurt von Tippelskirch described the operation as the Wehrmacht's greatest defeat since Stalingrad.

Uruangnirin is an endangered language whose vitality is declining as younger generations increasingly abandon it in favor of more dominant languages. This shift is primarily toward Papuan Malay, the local lingua franca, and toward Indonesian, the standard national language.

Uruangnirin is an Austronesian language spoken on the islands of Tarak and Faor in Sebakor Bay, West Papua. In addition to native speakers, a portion of the Kalamang population from the nearby island of Karas uses the language as a second language. The closest relatives of Uruangnirin are Onin and Sekar, languages spoken on the Bomberai Peninsula.

From the country’s founding, Pakistan's political leadership has leveraged religious sentiment to bolster a distinctive national identity, a trajectory that contributed to the Islamisation of state policy. This Islamisation drive helped shape an education system oriented toward religious instruction, educating millions of students in religious studies each year. The policy has frequently been linked by analysts to sympathies with extremism and violence and to the entrenchment of religious and communal divides within Pakistani society.

Islamisation in Pakistan involved replacing the penalties in the Pakistan Penal Code for theft and robbery with amputation-based punishments. Theft was punished by the amputation of the right hand, while robbery was punished by the amputation of the right hand and left foot. Provisions on Zina, or extramarital sex, were replaced by an Ordinance, under which unmarried offenders received 100 lashes and married offenders received stoning to death.

Beginning in the mid-2000s, bachata elements were increasingly incorporated into reggaeton, creating a fusion that blended bachata-style guitar work with reggaeton rhythms. Ivy Queen’s releases Te He Querido, Te He Llorado and La Mala epitomized this crossover, featuring guitar textures associated with bachata, slower romantic tempos, and expressive vocal delivery. Other leading artists, such as Daddy Yankee with Lo Que Paso, Paso and Don Omar with Dile, also drew on bachata influences in their tracks. By 2005, producers began releasing remixes of existing reggaeton songs that foregrounded bachata characteristics, marketing these versions under the label bachaton, or bachata in a Puerto Rican style.

In February 1995, the Puerto Rican government initiated a crackdown on non-mainstream music and its perceived cultural influence. Police raids targeted six San Juan record stores, resulting in the seizure of hundreds of cassettes and the imposition of fines under Laws 112 and 117 on grounds of obscenity. Concurrently, the Department of Education prohibited baggy clothing and non-mainstream music from schools. Local media subsequently portrayed rappers and other underground artists as threats to public order, a depiction that endured for months. These actions reflect the intense pushback faced by Puerto Rico’s burgeoning urban music scene in the mid-1990s and illustrate the contextual pressures surrounding the development of reggaeton.

Jerry Sanders is an American politician and business professional whose career includes founding partner and consultant roles for local high-tech start-ups focused on homeland security and infrastructure assessment. He has chaired the board of the San Diego Police Foundation, directing private fundraising to support equipment and programs for the San Diego Police Department. Sanders has held a range of board and advisory positions, including with STAR/PAL, the San Diego Chapter of the National Multiple Sclerosis Society, San Diego State University’s Dean’s Advisory Board, and Coronado First Bank (in organization). He has also served on the boards of the Wells Fargo Community Bank Board, the Mediation Center, and the National Conference for Community and Justice, and acted as an advisory board member for the Vera Institute of Justice on Foster Children and for the Children’s Initiative. In addition, he has been nominated to the National Red Cross Board of Governors.

Jerry Sanders was elected mayor of San Diego in a November 8, 2005 special runoff held after Mayor Dick Murphy resigned amid the city's pension scandal. He won with 54 percent of the vote, defeating City Council member Donna Frye. Sanders became the first mayor under San Diego's strong mayor system of governance. A Republican, he later joined the Mayors Against Illegal Guns Coalition, formed in 2006 and co-chaired by Michael Bloomberg and Thomas Menino. Following Bloomberg's departure from the Republican Party in 2007, San Diego became the largest U.S. city with a Republican mayor.

Line 11 of the Guangzhou Metro was included in Guangzhou’s 12th Five-Year Plan in 2012 and subsequently approved for development. In January 2015, the line’s Environmental Impact Assessment received approval from the Provincial Environmental Protection Agency, and the project feasibility study was approved in July 2015. By the end of 2015, Yuexiu District sought the cancellation of Tianxincun Station due to difficulties with site clearance. In late September 2016, Tianxincun Station was approved for construction, and construction officially began on 28 September 2016. In June 2023, Tianxincun Station was cancelled, reducing the line to 31 stations.

In 2010, the planning maintained Line 8 as an unsplit, an L-shaped corridor, with all sections of the ring-line projecting as new construction. The Grand Central Southern Half Ring was extended to Yijing Road in the Xingang Road Corridor south of Line 8, thereby forming an outer ring that would be designated Line 11 along the current alignment. The initial plan targeted 32 stations, but the final decision added only one station and canceled Ruibao station. Environmental concerns were raised because the proposed route would traverse Baiyun Mountain and the Haizhu Wetland. In 2014, the Dajinzhong Road–Yuntai Garden segment was realigned from under Baiyun Mountain to below Guangyuan Road Middle, and as part of this restructuring the main entrance of Yuntai Garden Station was moved 150 metres south to street level on Guangyuan Road Middle, while a secondary exit at Haizhu Wetland station was removed (the station is now known as Longtan).

Under the Soviet Ministry of Defence, a centralized body known as the Central Directorate for Space Assets of the Missile Troops of Strategic Purpose (ЦУКОС РВСН) was established in 1964 to unify space-related units within the Strategic Missile Forces. In 1970, this directorate was elevated from a central to a main directorate (ГУКОС РВСН), reflecting an expanded remit within the RVSN.

Space exploration in the Soviet Union was conducted as a military undertaking rather than as a civilian program, in contrast to the United States’ NASA. It was an integral part of the Soviet strategic ballistic missile forces, with oversight of space-related development held by the Deputy Minister of Defence for Special Weaponry and Rocket Technology by 1955. The first appointee to that post, from March 1955, was Mitrofan Ivanovich Nedelin, a Marshal of Artillery who would later become Chief Marshal of Artillery. On 17 December 1959, Nedelin's Deputy Minister apparatus was transformed into the Strategic Missile Forces (RVSN).

Within the International System of Units, metrologists distinguish between the conceptual definition of a unit and its practical realization. The SI defines its units by fixing the exact numerical values of seven defining constants when expressed in SI units, thereby anchoring the system's relationships and ensuring coherence across all units. Realization of a unit's definition refers to the procedures and methods by which that definition is applied to determine the value and associated uncertainty of a quantity of the same kind as the unit.

The International System of Units (SI) is described by the BIPM as the modern form of the metric system. In 1968, the unit formerly known as degree Kelvin was renamed kelvin to reflect a simplified nomenclature. In 1971, the mole was established as the seventh base unit of the SI, formalizing its role alongside the other base units.

During the Russian Revolution, Tsar Nicholas II and his family were placed under house arrest by the Provisional Government. In March 1917 they were confined to the Alexander Palace at Tsarskoye Selo, about 24 kilometers south of Petrograd. Amid the upheaval, they were evacuated in August 1917 to Tobolsk in the Urals to shield them from the turmoil. After the Bolsheviks seized power in October 1917, confinement conditions tightened and discussions of bringing Nicholas to trial intensified. With civil war looming in spring 1918, the family was moved to Yekaterinburg, a Bolshevik stronghold, where on 16 July 1918 the Bolsheviks executed Nicholas II and several members of his family.

World War I placed immense strain on the Russian Army. By the end of 1914, about 390,000 Russian men had died and nearly 1,000,000 were injured. In the face of heavy losses, inadequately trained recruits were conscripted for active duty early and recalled repeatedly throughout the conflict. The officer corps underwent significant restructuring, with lower echelons increasingly filled by soldiers promoted from within the ranks. These promoted soldiers, typically from peasant or working-class backgrounds, would come to play a large role in the politicization of the troops in 1917, contributing to the pressures that culminated in revolutionary upheaval.

Within the broader tradition of Judeo-Islamic philosophy from roughly 800 to 1400, Maimonides challenged several Aristotelian assumptions about creation and divine knowledge. He rejected the notion that matter is eternal and argued against the view that God knows only universals, not particulars, asserting that the absence of knowledge of individuals would imply divine change. In his account, God foresees future events and this prescience is unerring, meaning there are no novel facts to be learned by God as individuals come into existence; even a person who does not yet exist, will be born, endure for a time, and then cease to exist, is already known by God beforehand. This perspective is articulated in Moreh Nevukhim, I, 20. In attempting to avoid certain Aristotelian religious consequences, Maimonides nevertheless could not escape the Aristotelian notion of the unity of the soul, leaving him exposed to criticism from orthodox thinkers.

During the second century of the Hijrah, a schism arose within Basra's theological circles, pitting Hasan al-Basri's traditional school against dissenters who were expelled, most notably Wasil ibn Ata. In the wake of his expulsion, Wasil established a new school and systematized radical interpretations associated with earlier sects, particularly the Qadarites. This movement came to be known as the Mutazilites, a label derived from the Arabic root tazala, meaning to withdraw or to dissent. The Mutazilites advanced three central tenets: God is a absolutely unified and simple being with no attributes ascribed to Him; humans possess free will; and knowledge essential for salvation arises from human reason, with understanding attainable both prior to and after revelation, thereby obligating all people at all times and places to seek truth through reason. They styled themselves as Ashab al-Adl wa'l Tauhid, the Partisans of Justice and Unity.

Negotiations in March 1860 secured a lease for the Kowloon area, and the Convention of Peking subsequently terminated that lease after only a few months, with Kowloon formally ceded to Britain on 24 October 1860.

During the latter stages of the Second Opium War, British and French forces considered punitive action against Qing officials by burning the capital; the original plan was to destroy the Forbidden City, but it was altered to target the Old Summer Palace and the Summer Palace in order not to jeopardize the forthcoming treaty negotiations. Consequently, the Convention of Peking emerged from the signing of separate treaties with Britain and France on 24 October 1860 in the Ministry of Rites building, located immediately south of the Forbidden City.

IJsboerke was a Belgian professional road cycling team that competed from 1973 to 1982. During its existence, the team's primary sponsorship shifted from IJsboerke, a Belgian ice cream manufacturer, (1973–1980) to Capri-Sun (German: Capri-Sonne), a juice drink brand, (1981–1982). A notable result for the squad came when Walter Godefroot won the 1978 Tour of Flanders while riding for the team.

Koga Miyata, a Dutch bicycle manufacturer based in Heerenveen, served as a sub-sponsor of the IJsboerke cycling team. In addition to supporting professional outfits, the company also backed amateur cycling teams and sponsored Tulip Computers during the 1991–1992 seasons.

The Leonardo AW609 is a tiltrotor aircraft developed by Leonardo. In the event of a single-engine failure, either engine can drive both proprotors through a common drive shaft, allowing continued flight capability. The design also enables autorotation, providing a safe descent without engine power. It is intended to meet Full Transport Category certification and Class 1 performance while operating safely under single-engine conditions. The aircraft is equipped with a de-icing system and plans call for certification for known icing conditions. Additionally, it incorporates a sink-rate warning system that draws on experience from the V-22 program.

In 2015, Bristow Helicopters and AgustaWestland began a collaboration to adapt the AW609 for dedicated offshore oil and gas transport and search-and-rescue configurations. In March 2015, Bristow Group signed a joint development agreement with AgustaWestland at Heli-Expo, aimed at jointly advancing the tiltrotor for offshore missions. The pact would grant Bristow exclusive rights to direct the tiltrotor’s deployment for offshore operations, including oil and gas tasks. The agreement also suggested that changes could extend beyond the AW609 to influence the design of larger or more advanced models that AgustaWestland planned for the early 2020s. The tiltrotor’s introduction was expected to enable point-to-point operations, allowing the transport of oil personnel from major population centers to offshore platforms with greater safety margins. Industry journalists described the agreement as a commercial endorsement of tiltrotor technology, which had previously attracted interest mainly from military applications.

The Russian-American Industrial Corporation (RAIC) operated under a nine-member Control Board, seven of whom represented the Soviet side owing to unequal financial commitments from the two partners. Day-to-day management of RAIC’s manufacturing facilities was largely entrusted to American skilled workers and technical experts. For the Soviet authorities, a primary appeal of the arrangement lay in the introduction of American production methods into Russia’s relatively underdeveloped industrial sector.

During its fundraising campaign, the Russian-American Industrial Corporation raised approximately $2 million, which was allocated to the establishment or modernization of 34 facilities. The initiative supported employment for about 17,500 garment workers in Soviet Russia. Stockholders received a fixed annual interest of five percent, with payments continuing until the program was terminated in 1925.

The fourteenth century in the Iberian Peninsula was marked by significant upheaval within the Iberian kingdoms and shifting dynastic fortunes. After the death of Peter of Castile (Peter the Cruel), the House of Trastámara installed Henry II as king of Castile, who reigned from 1369 to 1379. In Aragon, the deaths without heirs of John I (1387–1396) and Martin I (1396–1410) paved the way for Ferdinand I of the Trastámara line, who ruled from 1412 to 1416. The Hundred Years’ War extended into Iberia, with Castile providing substantial naval support to France, contributing to France’s eventual victory. Following Henry III’s accession to Castile’s throne, popular anger at Jewish influence sparked violence in Toledo and beyond; in 1391 mobs across Castile and Aragon killed an estimated 50,000–100,000 Jews, according to various sources. Jewish women and children were sold as slaves to Muslims, and numerous synagogues were converted into churches. The scholar Hasdai Crescas notes that roughly seventy Jewish communities were destroyed in the violence.

Between 1275 and 1340 the Iberian Peninsula was shaped by the Strait crisis, with Granada at the heart of events. The period is characterized by a complex and shifting web of alliances among Muslim and Christian powers vying for dominance in the Western Mediterranean, while increasingly unstable Granada–Marinid relations added further complication. The climax occurred in 1340 at the Battle of Río Salado, when the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Othman allied with Granada in an attempt to establish a final power base in Iberia; he was a claimant to the caliphate. The Muslim coalition was defeated by a Christian alliance of Castile and Portugal, supported at sea by Aragon and Genoa. In the aftermath, Christian supremacy emerged on the peninsula, accompanied by the preeminence of Christian fleets in the Western Mediterranean.

In the Indian newspaper market of the mid-1990s, competition among major national dailies affected readership dynamics in key urban centers such as New Delhi and Bangalore. Hindustan Times was the leading paper in Delhi in 1994, while The Times of India pursued aggressive price reductions to erode rivals’ circulation, notably cutting its price by about one-third to 1.5 rupees after expanding its advertising sales force to offset lost circulation revenue. By 1998, Hindustan Times had slipped to second place in Delhi, reflecting ongoing shifts in market share. The Times of India later adopted a similar pricing approach in Bangalore, reducing its price to 1 rupee. This move drew criticism from industry figures such as Siddharth Varadarajan, then an editor, who described the Bangalore price cut as an aggressive tactic intended to undermine competitors.

Ahmedabad Mirror traces its corporate lineage to Times Group’s mid-2000s expansion, beginning with the late 2006 acquisition of Vijayanand Printers Limited (VPL). VPL published two Kannada dailies, Vijay Karnataka and Usha Kiran, along with the English-language Vijay Times, and at that time Vijay Karnataka was the leading newspaper in the Kannada segment. The group continued to broaden its presence with new editions, launching a Chennai edition on 12 April 2008 and introducing a Kolhapur edition in February 2013.

ISO 639-5 defines a set of three-letter codes, referred to as collective codes, that are used to identify language families and groups. As of the update issued on February 11, 2013, the standard comprises 115 such collective codes. The United States Library of Congress maintains the official list of alpha-3 codes that constitute ISO 639-5.

ISO 639-5 provides three-letter codes for language families and groups within the ISO 639 standard, but it does not aim to enumerate all language families used by linguists. The languages included under a single group code are not required to form a single linguistic lineage, and grouped languages may be linked by geographic proximity or by a classificatory category, such as Creole languages, rather than by a strict genetic relationship.

Social accounting challenges traditional accounting, especially financial accounting, by arguing that conventional methods fail to capture the broader relationship between society and organizations. It offers only a limited portrayal of how organizations affect and are affected by social contexts, stakeholders, and ethical considerations. As a result, this restricted perspective can artificially constrain the scope and development of accounting as a discipline.

Social accounting examines the externally visible accounts of large organizations, with a particular emphasis on multinational corporations, while often excluding informal or internally oriented records from consideration. Proponents contend that formal accountability mechanisms are driven by the spatial, financial, and cultural distances that separate corporations from the people and communities affected by their activities. Additionally, the approach questions the assumption that every meaningful insight must be reducible to financial form, arguing that financial data constitutes only one element within the broader language of accounting used to convey organizational impact.

Astroturfing refers to orchestrated campaigns intended to simulate genuine grassroots support for a product, organization, or idea. In many jurisdictions, legal regulations target testimonials, endorsements, and statements about a product’s performance or quality to prevent deceptive advertising and misrepresentation. These rules often require clear disclosure of paid, incentivized, or otherwise compensated endorsements and mandate that such claims be supported by evidence. Within corporate contexts, employees may be considered acting as customers if their actions are not directed by authority within the company, which has implications for the perceived authenticity of endorsements and for determining responsibility and accountability.

Astroturfing refers to the practice of presenting orchestrated political or promotional activity as spontaneous grassroots sentiment. The term itself did not exist in antiquity, but an early instance often cited appears in Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar, Act I, Scene II, where Gaius Cassius Longinus writes letters purportedly from “the public” with the aim of persuading Brutus to join the conspiracy against Caesar. The fake correspondence is intended to simulate popular support, illustrating an early depiction of manufactured public influence that resembles modern astroturfing techniques.

Refreshable braille displays typically integrate a dedicated tactile input area alongside the output mechanism. The input section commonly comprises two banks of four keys situated on opposite sides of the device, resembling the arrangement used on a Perkins Brailler, and users convey braille characters and related commands by pressing combinations of these keys. Output is provided by a row of electro-mechanical braille cells, each consisting of eight round-tipped pins that rise and fall to present the corresponding braille pattern. Some variants employ a standard QWERTY keyboard for input while retaining braille pins for output, while other configurations may be dedicated to input-only or output-only functionality.

Refreshable braille displays convert on-screen text into Braille through an array of refreshable cells, enabling blind and visually impaired users to read electronically presented information. Some models indicate the cursor position by vibrating the dots, providing haptic feedback to help readers track their location. In certain designs, a switch is provided for each cell, allowing the cursor to be moved directly to a chosen cell and thereby speeding navigation.

Handguns are more easily concealable and therefore more commonly used in assassination attempts than rifles, despite certain drawbacks. A study analyzing 74 notable assassination attempts in the United States during the latter half of the twentieth century found that 51% involved handguns, 30% involved rifles or shotguns, 15% involved knives, and 8% involved explosives. Additionally, 16% of cases involved multiple weapons or methods.

Malcolm X was assassinated on February 21, 1965, at the Audubon Ballroom, and his death occurred roughly three years before the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr., who was killed on April 4, 1968, at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee, a site now part of the National Civil Rights Museum.

On July 30, 1981, performance artist Stelarc staged Seaside Suspension: Event for Wind & Waves, a work in which a body was suspended over the water at Jōgashima in Miura, Japan. Documented as part of the chronology of social nudity, the piece exemplifies the use of the human form in an outdoor setting that interacts with the maritime environment.

On October 11, 1992, the Berkeley-based group X-plicit Players staged a nude or topless demonstration in Berkeley, California, traveling from Smokey Joe's Cafe on Shattuck Avenue to Cafe Milano on Telegraph Avenue to support a New York topfree victory.

Tarawa-class amphibious assault ships were developed within the United States Navy's Landing Helicopter Assault (LHA) program. From early in the design phase, the program encountered problems, with the Navy becoming heavily involved in shaping the vessel design, a departure from the intended Total Package Procurement concept. Nine Tarawa-class ships were initially contracted, but in January 1971 the plan was reduced to five ships. The four remaining hulls were never built for the Navy.

Tarawa-class amphibious assault ships are Landing Helicopter Assault (LHA)-design vessels operated by the United States Navy. Five ships of this class were constructed by Ingalls Shipbuilding between 1971 and 1980. Four additional ships were planned but ultimately canceled, and those cancellations were offset by the introduction of the Wasp-class amphibious ships.

War graves refer to burial sites of military personnel who die in connection with armed conflict, encompassing terrestrial graves, ships sunk during wartime, and military aircraft that crash into water, particularly when crew members perish inside the vehicle. The classification covers individuals who die while in active service, not only those killed in combat. For instance, during the Crimean War, deaths from disease exceeded those caused by enemy action.

In Germany, war graves fall under state responsibility, with the government tasked with their care and protection. The category extends beyond soldiers to include victims of National Socialism and individuals who perished under the GDR regime, who are treated as war graves. Abroad, the German War Graves Commission (Volksbund deutscher Kriegsgräberfürsorge) undertakes the care of German war dead in foreign countries. War graves are legally protected and are accorded permanent resting rights. These sites are predominantly integrated into civil cemeteries and can be found in almost all graveyards.

Brome is a village municipality within the Brome-Missisquoi Regional County Municipality in the Estrie region of Quebec, Canada. It lies north of Sutton and is surrounded by the Town of Brome Lake. The community is notable for hosting one of Quebec’s most significant agricultural exhibitions. Its setting affords views of the Sutton Mountains, broad open spaces, a tranquil environment, and a culture of cooperation and solidarity among residents. According to the 2021 Canadian Census, Brome had a population of 341.

According to the 2021 Census of Population by Statistics Canada, Brome, Quebec recorded a population of 341, with 151 of its 169 total private dwellings occupied. This represented a 15.2 percent increase from 296 in 2016. The municipality has a land area of 11.56 km2 (4.46 sq mi), yielding a population density of 29.5 people per km2 (76.4 per sq mi).

Bink Video is a video codec distributed as part of the Epic Video Tools package, alongside Smacker video, the earlier Epic Games Tools codec. It uses a hybrid approach that combines block-transform and wavelet techniques and employs sixteen distinct encoding methods. The design emphasizes lower decoding requirements compared with other video codecs, aiming to reduce the processing load during playback. The software also includes optimizations tailored to the different computer game consoles supported by the tools package.

Bink Video is a software technology employed to deliver continuous-motion video content inside video games. It runs on Windows and macOS, and it has been used on sixth-generation consoles such as the Dreamcast, GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox, as well as on seventh-generation platforms including the Nintendo DS, PlayStation 3, PlayStation Portable, Wii, and Xbox 360.

The mini-LP represents an intermediate format situated between standard EP releases and full-length LPs. It achieved particular prominence as a common album format during the 1980s. Typical mini-LP presentations run approximately 20 to 30 minutes of music and usually consist of about seven tracks.

RCA issued 28 Elvis Presley extended plays between 1956 and 1967, with many reaching the top of the Billboard EP chart. Outside RCA, extended plays were relatively uncommon in the United States and Canada, but the format was widely sold in the United Kingdom and several other European countries during the 1950s and 1960s. In Sweden, EPs were a popular format, accounting for as much as 85 percent of the market in the late 1950s.

Alan Jackson initially hesitated to record and release "Where Were You (When the World Stopped Turning)", wary that it could appear to capitalize on a tragedy. With the approval of his wife Denise and his producer Keith Stegall, he went ahead and recorded the track that week. Following Stegall's guidance, Jackson then played the completed recording for executives at his label. According to RCA Label Group chairman Joe Galante, the executives remained silent for roughly a minute after hearing it.

According to Country Music Television (CMT), Alan Jackson was slated to introduce the new song "Where Were You" during the awards telecast. The performance followed an introduction by the show's host, Vince Gill. Jackson performed the piece seated on a stool, with an orchestra and backing singers behind him. The segment lasted about five minutes and concluded with an immediate standing ovation. This performance, together with Gill's introduction, is used as the song's music video.
Introduced in 1998, Sony released the FD Trinitron/WEGA line of flat-screen television sets. The lineup featured side-mounted speakers and was housed in a silver-colored cabinet.

FD Trinitron WEGA derives its name from the star Vega, a luminous object located in the constellation Lyra. Sony has stated that the WEGA designation was not intended to reference the original WEGA firm.

The Times carried what appears to be the first advertisement for The Reprint Society club, promoting a two-volume edition of Seven Pillars of Wisdom at 3s 6d per volume. The volumes were bound in buckram and featured a gilt-stamped leather title label on the spine. The notice indicated that supplies were limited by wartime conditions. A cheaper cloth-bound edition was also available at 2s 6d.

The Reprint Society was a literary club whose peak activity occurred in the 1950s. Its membership rose from about 2,000 to roughly 200,000, marking a period of rapid growth. Cost-saving measures allowed the reintroduction of its signature buckram bindings, a hallmark of its editions, for which the organization was widely known. It advertised itself as the largest club in the British Commonwealth.

In the 1927 silent film Metropolis, the opening sequence features two clocks, a twenty-four-hour analog dial and a ten-hour decimal dial, displayed in a vertical arrangement. Both clocks are employed to convey the impression of an alien, highly efficient society.

The 24-hour analog dial is a method of representing time that employs a full 24-hour cycle rather than a conventional twofold 12-hour division. It illustrates how the time of day varies with geographic location, reflecting the dependence of solar time on longitude. The concept can be demonstrated with a globe, a map, or a disk used as a visual aid.

In the animated children's series Chip and Potato, Amanda is the mother of Nico and another son, and raises both in Welcome Walk. The character is voiced by Teryl Rothery. Her husband Andy lives apart from the family and travels the world; his occupation involves helping people decorate their homes. Despite their separation, Amanda and Andy maintain a loving relationship.

Howie is a hyena character in the animated series Chip and Potato. Voiced by Brenden Sunderland, he is depicted as a mischievous kindergartener at Rainbow Forest School who frequently causes trouble and enjoys blowing raspberries. Despite his troublesome tendencies, Howie reveals a softer side and demonstrates genuine care for others, contributing to a more nuanced portrayal within the show.

Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana (FIMI) began providing the Italian official albums chart in March 1995. In January 1997, FIMI expanded its role to become the provider of the Italian official singles chart. On 1 January 2008, it replaced the physical singles chart with a digital downloads chart based on legal Internet and mobile downloads, due to a decrease in CD singles sales.

On 10 April 2006, the Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana (FIMI) published Italy's inaugural chart of the best-selling digital singles. The ranking was compiled by Nielsen SoundScan and was based on data drawn from ten digital stores. The first number-one single on the chart was "Sei nell'anima" by Gianna Nannini.

As part of its suite of video coding standards, MPEG-4 AVC was selected as the video compression standard for Brazil's over-the-air digital television service ISDB-TB. The Brazilian implementation of ISDB-TB is based on Japan's ISDB-T system, reflecting its lineage within the international ISDB family.

MPEG, the group responsible for developing international standards for audio and video compression and transmission, was established in 1988. It was founded by Dr. Hiroshi Yasuda of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT) and Dr. Leonardo Chiariglione of CSELT. Chiariglione served as chair, or Convenor, from its inception through 6 June 2020, guiding the body's activities for more than three decades. The organization held its first meeting in May 1988 in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, marking the formal beginning of its standardization work.

Champlain Heights is a district in Vancouver, situated in the city's extreme southeast corner and among its last tracts to be urbanized. Architectural historian Harold Kalman characterized it as a notable planned residential community developed in the early 1970s. The neighbourhood's layout features winding streets with curved roads and cul-de-sacs designed to accommodate a range of housing types and income levels. It is closely associated with the nearby Killarney area and is officially regarded as a sub-neighborhood within Killarney. The built environment consists mainly of townhouse complexes and cooperative housing. Most parcels operate on a leasehold basis, with prepaid 99-year leases granted by the City of Vancouver and set to expire in the 2080s.

Champlain Heights is a family-friendly residential community in Vancouver that provides a diverse mix of housing, including market-rate homes, co-operative housing, and social housing. The district is arranged around green spaces and a network of walking trails, contributing to a pedestrian-friendly environment. Everett Crowley Park is located within the area, and it stands as the fifth-largest park in Vancouver.

Fade In is an American romantic drama film that was produced in 1968 and released in 1973. It stars Burt Reynolds and Barbara Loden in the leading roles. Filming took place concurrently with Silvio Narizzano's Blue, and actors from Blue appeared in uncredited appearances in various scenes of Fade In.

Reynolds's assessment of Fade In fluctuated over time. After production finished, he asserted that it was the best work he had ever undertaken and compared it to an American version of A Man and a Woman. A few years later, Paramount canceled its release and relegated the film to late-night television. He later ruefully remarked that it would have been better titled Fade Out.

Per capita income is a statistical measure of the average income earned by individuals in a given population or sector, and it serves as a basis for comparing wealth across different groups. It is commonly used as an indicator of a country’s standard of living. When making international comparisons, per capita income is typically reported in a common international currency, such as the euro or the United States dollar. It is also one of the three components of the Human Development Index.

Per capita income is a common measure of the average income earned by each person in a given area. It does not account for how income is directed toward development-enhancing factors, notably investments in health, education, and infrastructure. As a result, the metric may not reflect the area’s potential for long-term development or sustainable growth, since such investments influence future productivity and well-being beyond current income levels.

George Michael relocated to a house in Highgate, where a river at the end of his garden was frequented by swans. A neighbour connected with the Swan Lifeline charity approached him about becoming a patron, and he accepted immediately, serving as a patron of the charity from 2005 until his death.

During 2017, George Michael was honored by a number of fellow artists. Adele performed a slowed rendition of "Fastlove" at the 59th Annual Grammy Awards on 12 February as a tribute to Michael. On 22 February at the Brit Awards, Chris Martin performed "A Different Corner" in tribute to him. In June 2017, Geri Halliwell released the charity single "Angels in Chains" to benefit Childline, dedicated to Michael.

Cheng Xuanying (成玄英; pinyin: Chéng Xuányīng; Wade–Giles: Ch'eng Hsüan-ying) flourished 631–655 as a Tang dynasty Taoist monk. His courtesy name was Zishi (子實). A prominent figure in Daoism, he is frequently described as a leading doctrinal teacher at Xihua Abbey and as the principal representative of the Chongxuan, the School of Double Mystery, during the reigns of Taizong and Gaozong. He is best known for his commentaries on core Daoist texts, including the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi, with the latter associated with the edition titled Nanhua Zhenjing.

Cheng Xuanying, born circa the early 7th century in Shan Prefecture (modern-day Henan), lived in seclusion at Donghai until 631, when he was summoned to the Tang capital of Chang'an by an imperial decree of Emperor Taizong and appointed as the head monk of Xihua Abbey. Although later sources sometimes assign him the title of Master of the Doctrine, the New Book of Tang does not record this rank, and many scholars regard it as a probable Song-era fabrication. Prior to his summons, he was renowned as a philosopher who wrote commentaries on the Lingbao scripture, notably the Clarified Meaning of the Scripture of Universal Salvation. Some scholars also contend that his invitation to the capital was intended to secure him as a disciple of Liu Jinxi (fl. 620), a prominent Chongxuan Daoist thinker at the Institute of Education (Wenxueguan).

Within the British Army, the battlegroup is the most common fighting unit, a combined-arms formation built around a core combat element and augmented by supporting capabilities. A battlegroup integrates elements from armour, infantry, engineers, artillery, and support services such as medical care, logistics, and intelligence. For example, a typical composition might comprise two companies of armoured infantry drawn from the 1st Battalion Mercian Regiment, a squadron of heavy armour from the A Squadron of the Royal Tank Regiment, a company of engineers from the 22nd Engineer Regiment (B Company), and a battery from the 1st Regiment Royal Horse Artillery (D Battery), together with attached medical, logistical, and intelligence personnel. Battlegroups are normally organized and commanded by a dedicated battlegroup headquarters and are named after the unit contributing the most combat units, such as the 1 Mercian Battlegroup. They form a self-sustaining mixed formation of armour, infantry, artillery, engineers and support units, typically under the command of a lieutenant colonel.

Throughout its long history, the British Army participated in a broad range of imperial conflicts beyond Europe, reflecting the reach of the British Empire. During the War of 1812 it opposed the United States and operated within contexts shaped by contemporary European rivalries. In Asia it fought in the First and Second Opium Wars against Qing China and later confronted the Boxer Rebellion as part of an international coalition. In the Pacific it fought the Māori in the First New Zealand War, while in South Asia it contended with Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah's forces and, later, with mutineers associated with the British East India Company during the 1857 rebellion. In southern Africa it opposed Boer forces in the First and Second Boer Wars. In North America and the Atlantic world it faced Irish nationalist actions in Canada during the Fenian raids and Irish separatists during the Anglo-Irish War. The period following the Napoleonic Wars was marked by imperial expansion pressures alongside underfunding and inefficiencies within the Army and related forces, and these tensions helped precipitate reforms implemented after the Crimean War to improve organization, readiness, and effectiveness.

In the United Kingdom, a number of quasi-governmental organisations are incorporated as private companies limited by guarantee (CLG). In these arrangements, ultimate control over the bodies rests with a government department or minister. Notable examples of organisations structured as CLGs include the Financial Conduct Authority and Network Rail.

Private companies limited by guarantee are used by some professional services providers. In this arrangement, the members who provide client-facing services are the individual constituent firms operating under a common brand. The company limited by guarantee itself typically does not deliver client-facing services. The Big Four accountancy firms—Deloitte, Ernst & Young, KPMG, and PriceWaterhouseCoopers—are each organized using this structure.

TechCrunch, a technology news website, was owned by Verizon Media from 2015 to 2021, following Verizon's acquisition of AOL and Yahoo and the subsequent consolidation of their properties. In August 2020, chief operating officer Ned Desmond stepped down after eight years with the company, and in December 2020 he announced his intention to join SOSV as a senior operating partner. Subsequently, the COO duties were assumed by two executives: Matthew Panzarino, who had previously served as editor-in-chief, and Joey Hinson, the director of business operations. This arrangement reflected a transitional leadership phase during Verizon Media's ownership.

TechCrunch, which began in New York City in 2010, is a technology news organization that hosts the annual TechCrunch Disrupt conference. The conference is staged in several cities across the United States and Europe, attracting attendees such as entrepreneurs, investors, and technology enthusiasts. During the event, startups present their ideas to a panel of judges, and the program also features networking opportunities, as well as keynote addresses and panel discussions.

Todd Grayson, affiliated with the Libertarian Party of Ohio, served on the Perrysburg City Council in 2013. From 2013 to 2016, he held the post of vice chairman for the Libertarian Party of Wood County, the county-level affiliate of the party. Grayson is noted as the first registered Libertarian in Wood County to hold public office, underscoring the party’s emergence in local government within the county.

The Libertarian Party of Ohio (LPO) operates as Ohio’s affiliate of the Libertarian Party. Nationally, it is the fourth-largest state affiliate within the Libertarian Party. In the state, it stands as the third-largest political party.

Apache OpenOffice 4.0, released on 23 July 2013, incorporated the Symphony code drop and reintroduced the sidebar-style interface derived from Symphony. The update also featured an improved installer, enhanced interoperability with Microsoft Office formats, and overall performance enhancements. The subsequent maintenance release, version 4.0.1, expanded the product’s language support by adding nine new languages.

Apache OpenOffice's OpenOffice.org 3.4 beta, released on 12 April 2011, introduced Scalable Vector Graphics support in Draw, added ODF 1.2 compatibility in Writer, and included enhancements to Calc. A few days after the beta's release, Oracle cancelled the OpenOffice project.

List of magazines by circulation provides a worldwide compilation of magazines arranged by their circulation figures. Circulation is defined as the average number of copies distributed per issue, and the rankings are based on this per-issue average.

Buffer solutions are those that resist changes in pH upon the addition of acids or bases, accomplished by a buffering agent that neutralizes added H+ or OH− and maintains pH within a narrow range even in the presence of other solutes. This stabilizing property is essential for the proper functioning of enzymes and other biochemical processes in biological systems, which require a relatively constant hydrogen ion concentration.
