In human physiology, the carbonic acid (H2CO3) and bicarbonate (HCO3−) system serves as the principal buffering mechanism in blood plasma, providing continuous regulation of pH. Normal blood typically remains within a pH range of about 7.35 to 7.45, and deviations outside this interval, known as acidosis or alkalosis, can rapidly impair cellular function and may be fatal if the buffering capacity is overwhelmed or not restored.

Buffer solutions resist changes in pH by neutralizing added base with the weak acid component. When the acid is predominantly in its deprotonated form—more than 95 percent deprotonated—the system contains only a small fraction of undissociated acid to react with the added alkali. Consequently, the pH rises rapidly because most of the added alkali is consumed in the neutralization of that remaining acid; once this limited buffering capacity is exhausted, further base leads to a steep increase in pH.

Admission to the regulated legal professions in the Netherlands is restricted to holders of a law degree that carries civil effect, known as qualifying law degrees. Such degrees authorize entry into the juridische togaberoepen, the country’s regulated legal professions. To meet the requirements, qualifying degrees must cover four principal areas of legal knowledge: Dutch private law, Dutch criminal law, Dutch administrative and constitutional law, and international or European law.

Admission to the practice of law in Fiji requires the holder of a Bachelor of Law degree, normally a four-year program, to undertake subsequent professional training. After completing the LLB, candidates must satisfy one of several approved pathways, including the Professional Diploma in Legal Practice from the University of the South Pacific, the Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice from the University of Fiji, or an equivalent law degree accompanied by a bar admission course completed abroad. Alternatively, individuals already admitted as barristers or solicitors, or their equivalents in a Commonwealth country, may be permitted to practice in Fiji if they are a Commonwealth citizen, have resided in Fiji for at least three months, and possess sufficient legal experience to satisfy the Chief Justice.

Phi Kappa Theta underwent rapid initial expansion in the first half of 1925, with five chapters chartered, four of which remain active. Growth slowed substantially in the ensuing two decades. From 1930 to 1950 only five new chapters were chartered, a decline attributed to the combined pressures of the Great Depression and World War II. During the Depression, roughly one-third of chapters went inactive, including the Alpha chapter at Brown University. Recovery began in the 1950s, as growth resumed at a steadier pace. By the time of the 1959 merger, which produced the modern Phi Kappa Theta, thirty-six of the thirty-nine chapters were open and active, including Brown’s Alpha chapter.

Phi Kappa Theta traces its early origins to a 1892 meeting of the group then known as Phi Kappa Sigma, convened by M. Joseph Harson to plan an official establishment at Brown University. Harson authored the initiation ritual and the members moved to adopt a formal constitution and organizational structure for the chapter, with Harson elected president. The first new members were initiated in 1893. On April 29, 1902, the fraternity, then known as Phi Kappa, was incorporated under Rhode Island law. Later, on May 27, 1912, the Beta chapter was founded through the incorporation of the Loyola Club of the University of Illinois.

UTV, formally Ulster Television, operated as the ITV franchise for Northern Ireland and, over its history, employed a range of on-screen logos (idents) as part of its branding. These various ident designs accompanied the channel for many years, reflecting evolving presentation choices, and this association with multiple logos occurred prior to the 2020 introduction of ITV's unified branding.
On 13 April 2021, ITV ceased satellite broadcasting of UTV +1. In Northern Ireland, the Sky platform subsequently gained ITV +1 Granada to take the place of UTV +1.

Apache Xalan is an open-source software library developed by the Apache Software Foundation, implementing the XSLT 1.0 specification and XPath 1.0. The Xalan XSLT processor is available for Java and C++ environments. The project combines IBM's LotusXSL XSLT processor with Sun Microsystems' XSLTC compiler, and an Eiffel language wrapper is available.

Instruction-level parallelism (ILP) refers to the capacity of a processor to execute multiple instructions concurrently when they are independent. Out-of-order execution enables instructions to be processed in an order different from the original program sequence, as long as data dependencies are not violated, thereby increasing ILP; notably, this technique operates independently of both pipelining and superscalar organization. Modern processors often discover ILP dynamically during execution by analyzing the running program, extracting parallelism without relying on compiler assistance. Alternatively, ILP can be exposed to hardware through compile-time analysis, in which the compiler decomposes work into independent operations and conveys this information to the processor. However, given the complexity of scaling out-of-order engines, the industry has re-examined instruction-set architectures that explicitly encode multiple independent operations within a single instruction to provide direct parallelism hints to hardware.

Instruction-level parallelism (ILP) refers to the capacity of a processor to execute several instructions concurrently by exploiting independent operations and overlapping execution. In dataflow architectures, ILP is explicitly specified, with execution driven by data dependencies that determine which instructions may proceed at any given moment. A recent example of a dataflow architecture is TRIPS, which illustrates a modern embodiment of dataflow-based approaches to capturing and exploiting ILP.

Brighton School, also known in French as L'école de Brighton, was a loosely affiliated collective of early filmmakers based in the Brighton and Hove area of England. Active from 1896 to 1910, the group primarily produced a series of short films and other early projects shot in the Brighton region, contributing to the development of British cinema during the period.

The Brighton School (filmmaking) is a term coined by the French film historian Georges Sadoul to describe an early group of British filmmakers associated with Brighton. The designation originated in an article he wrote, which was later translated and republished as a pamphlet under the title British Creators of Film Technique. The pamphlet was published by the British Film Institute in 1948.

Within days of the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States’ appeal for assistance and on the basis of a covert request from Grenada’s Governor-General Sir Paul Scoon, the Reagan administration authorized a U.S.-led invasion of Grenada. Scoon did not sign the formal invitation to intervention until October 26, reflecting the sensitive nature of the authorization. Senior civilian and military officials, including Secretary of Defense Caspar Weinberger and Colin Powell, served as key invasion planners. In the broader context of prepared options, the United States had conducted mock invasions of Grenada since 1981 under Ocean Venture ’81, including Operation Amber and the Amberdines. The Amber exercises simulated air and amphibious assaults on Vieques, Puerto Rico, treating Amber as a stand-in for a hypothetical Eastern Caribbean island facing anti-democratic revolutionary activity.

Kitchen ventilation is a specialized branch of ventilation engineering focused on processing the air produced by kitchens. It addresses contaminants unique to cooking environments, notably grease-laden vapors, smoke, and odours, which are not typically encountered in most other ventilation systems.

Kitchen ventilation systems commonly employ range hoods to remove smoke, steam, and odors produced during cooking. The effectiveness of capture increases with larger hoods, and proper positioning further enhances performance. For optimal operation, hoods should extend about three inches beyond the edges of the cooktop and be mounted at a height of roughly 20 to 30 inches above the cooktop. Together, these design features contribute to efficient extraction of smoke and grease from the cooking area.

Rungu is a wooden throwing club or baton used in East Africa. In Swahili, the term denotes this weapon, with the plural form marungu. The object carries notable symbolism and significance within certain East African tribal cultures, functioning beyond its practical utility. It is especially associated with Maasai morans, the male warriors of that community. Traditionally, the rungu has been employed in warfare and for hunting.

Within the category of improvised weapons, the crowbar is commonly used as a makeshift club owing to its metal construction, heft, and leverage. While many crowbars can be wielded with one hand, some models are too large for comfortable single-handed use, diminishing dexterity and control. For these longer implements, classification as staves is often more appropriate, reflecting their length and handling characteristics that align with staff-like weapons rather than conventional improvised clubs.

Hose, Leicestershire is a village in which a medieval Anglican church and a Baptist chapel attest to its religious heritage, while local amenities include a shop with a sub-post office, a village hall with playing fields, and a public house named the Rose and Crown. The village green is known as the Park, and within it lie the premises of a blacksmith, underscoring a traditional rural landscape.

Hose was a village and former civil parish in the north-eastern part of Leicestershire, situated in the Vale of Belvoir. On 1 April 1936, Hose was merged with the neighbouring parishes of Harby and Long Clawson to form a single civil parish. The area lies near the former route of the Grantham Canal, a waterway that has been designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest. In 2014, the canal underwent environmental dredging and planting to restore its ecological value.

State-space planning employs backward search as an algorithm that commences from the goal state and proceeds to the initial state by backtracking through the state space. This approach is sometimes described as back propagation.

State-space planning is a method used in artificial intelligence and programming that concentrates on searching for data or viable solutions within a defined set of possibilities. In data-lookup scenarios, the state space corresponds to the entire dataset available for examination. In AI problem solving, it represents the finite collection of potential procedures or action sequences that could lead to a goal, effectively the universe of candidate approaches. It can also be described as the aggregate of all potential solutions that might satisfy the problem. The core function of state-space planning is to determine which portions of this space should be explored and in which order, with the aim of improving search efficiency and achieving the desired outcome.

Jacob's Pillow Dance Festival maintains long-standing community programs, notably Curriculum in Motion and the Curriculum in Motion Institute. The program was founded by Celeste Miller and J.R. Glover, who are credited as its founders. Miller is a Pillow Artist-Educator, while Glover serves as the Carole & Dan Burack Director of the School at Jacob's Pillow.

Jacob's Pillow Dance Festival traces its origins to 1931, when Ted Shawn purchased a farm to serve as a dedicated dance retreat. As a pioneer of modern dance, Shawn and his wife Ruth St. Denis led the Denishawn Company, which helped popularize dance forms rooted in theatre and traditions from cultures outside the European ballet repertoire. Through Denishawn, a number of future dance pioneers were trained, including Martha Graham, Charles Weidman, Doris Humphrey, and Jack Cole, whose work significantly influenced the development of modern dance. The festival has since carried forward this legacy, presenting a diverse range of dance and reflecting the Denishawn lineage that contributed to its foundation.

The 18th Annual Latin Grammy Awards, produced by the Latin Recording Academy, were held on November 16, 2017, on schedule, despite a postponement in announcing the nominations. This event marked the organization’s second instance of delaying or canceling a signature award ceremony; the first occurred in 2001 when the 2nd Annual Latin Grammy Awards were canceled in response to the September 11 attacks, with winners announced at a press conference the following month.

Initially, nominations for the 18th Annual Latin Grammy Awards were scheduled for September 20, 2017. The announcement was postponed due to the Mexico earthquake that occurred the day before and other natural disasters affecting Spanish-speaking communities. The Latin Recording Academy later revealed the nominations on September 26, 2017 (Tuesday).

Phimai Historical Park was constructed in a style closely resembling Angkor and other Khmer Buddhist temples, reflecting the architectural influences of the Khmer tradition. The religious origin of several structures within its walls remains a matter of scholarly debate. The presence of Dvaravati influence is evidenced by a Wheel of Law sculpture and a Buddha statue, underscoring the site's Buddhist significance. A substantial cache of Buddhist artworks has been uncovered at Phimai, pointing to its historical prominence as a center of Buddhist art and devotion. The discovery of large pots embedded at corner locations has been interpreted as indicating spiritual practices beyond Buddhism. Throughout its history, Phimai has functioned as an important religious landmark for Animists, Buddhists, and Hindus, illustrating the area's diverse devotional landscape.

Phimai Historical Park comprises Khmer temple ruins in Thailand that were largely built under the Devaraja cult, a political-religious framework in which the king is regarded as a divine figure. The term Devaraja translates to roughly “the king who resembles a god,” and the cult is most frequently associated with Jayavarman II. Under this belief system, Shiva was worshiped and the king was viewed as an avatar of Shiva, a concept Khmer rulers used to legitimize their authority and extend Hinduism across their realm. Accordingly, temples at Phimai and other Khmer sites were constructed to glorify the ruler’s reign while promoting Hindu religious practices throughout the region.

The Codex Zouche-Nuttall, also known as Codex Tonindeye, is an accordion-folded, pre-Columbian manuscript of Mixtec pictography. It is part of the British Museum's collection and stands as one of approximately sixteen entirely pre-Columbian Mexican manuscripts that have survived. The codex derives its name from Zelia Nuttall, who first published it in 1902, and Baroness Zouche, who donated the document to the museum.

Believed to have been created in the 14th century, the Codex Zouche-Nuttall comprises forty-seven sections of animal hide and measures 19 by 23.5 centimeters. The manuscript folds in a screen-like manner and is vividly painted on both sides. It remains largely in excellent condition. The codex is one of three surviving works that record the genealogies, alliances, and conquests of Tilantongo’s rulers, a Mixtec city-state in the highlands of Oaxaca, during the 11th and 12th centuries. It is associated with the leadership of Lord Eight Deer Jaguar Claw, who died in the early 12th century at the age of 52.

The song "Welcome to the Fold" examines the concept of a deranged lunatic, reflecting the mindset of a decadent bachelor in his mid‑twenties who is indifferent to the consequences of his actions. Patrick has described his own level of success—wealth, a platinum record, a band, and having everything he desires—coupled with a detached disregard for what his behavior entails. He has described it as his favorite track on the album. The track is approximately ten minutes long and is structured as a single piece that integrates three songs into one.

"Welcome to the Fold" derives its title from an eponymous 1998 album released by the Cleveland-based novelty folk-rock group 100,000 Leagues Under My Nutsack. Filter's bassist Frank Cavanagh was friends with the band's lead singer, and Richard Patrick, Filter's frontman, admired the album enough to name the song after it.

On the British side at the Battle of Loos, the reserves consisted of the Cavalry Corps, the Indian Cavalry Corps, and XI Corps, which had recently arrived in France and whose corps staffs were largely inexperienced. XI Corps was commanded by Lieutenant-General Richard Haking, with the 21st Division under Major-General George Forestier-Walker and the 24th Division under Major-General John Capper. Archibald Murray, then the Deputy Chief of the Imperial General Staff, warned that these reserves, being newly trained, were better suited to long-range exploitation rather than trench warfare. The French leadership doubted that a breakthrough would be achieved. In contrast, Haig and Foch argued for keeping reserves closer to the front to exploit any gains on the first day. The French agreed to reposition their reserves nearer the front but insisted they should not be committed until the second day.

During October, German forces recaptured the Hohenzollern Redoubt on 3 October. On 8 October they launched an assault around Loos, employing five regiments against a portion of the British 7th Division on the left flank to recapture remaining ground. Foggy weather, inadequate artillery preparation, and defenders behind intact wire helped the British and French repulse the attack, with German casualties estimated at about 3,000, and the operation disrupting British preparations and delaying the night of 12/13 October. A final British attack on 13 October failed due to a lack of hand grenades. Haig considered another assault on 7 November, but heavy rain and accurate German shelling in late October led to abandoning the plan.

Wendy Beetlestone began her legal career as a law clerk to Judge Robert S. Gawthrop III of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania (1993–1994). She then spent eight years at Schnader Harrison Segal & Lewis, LLP (1994–2002), earning partnership in 2001. From 2002 to 2005, she served as general counsel for the School District of Philadelphia. Beetlestone continued in private practice as a shareholder at Hangley, Aronchick, Segal, Pudlin & Schiller (2005–2014), where she litigated commercial matters in federal and state courts. In 2023, she was announced as the next chancellor of the University of Liverpool, becoming the eleventh person to hold the post and the first woman and the first Black chancellor.
Wendy Beetlestone (born 1961) is an American judge who serves as the Chief United States district judge of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

The song peaked at number one on the UK Singles Chart, where it remained for four weeks, and was certified Silver by the British Phonographic Industry for shipments over 300,000 units. It also reached the top of the Irish charts for one week. Outside the United Kingdom, its popularity was more limited, including regions where Seven Faces of Woman did not air. In France, the track narrowly missed the top 40, while in the United States it did not chart on the Billboard Hot 100 and appeared only on the lower end of the Easy Listening charts.

The song "She" by Charles Aznavour appears in the opening sequence of the film Notting Hill. A 1999 cover by Elvis Costello, produced by Trevor Jones, was used in the film's final sequence. In the United States release, Costello's rendition was also employed in the opening sequence after test audiences disapproved of Aznavour's original version. Costello's interpretation achieved significant popularity across Europe, charting on numerous charts.

In March 2022, Turku suspended its long-standing sister city relationship with Saint Petersburg, Russia. The partnership had been in place since 1953, spanning nearly seven decades before the suspension. The decision was taken in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Turku has a population density of 794.4 inhabitants per square kilometre and a median age of 42.1 years. This median age is lower than the national average of 43.6 years.

The Uyghur Latin alphabet (ULY) was first introduced in the 1930s in the former Soviet Union as a Latin-based script for Uyghur. It saw limited use in the Uyghur Autonomous Region during the 1960s and 1970s. A finalized version of the ULY was completed in July 2001 at Xinjiang University in Ürümqi, within the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of the People's Republic of China, during the fifth conference of a series that had begun in November 2000. In January 2008, the project was amended and formally identified by the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Regional Working Committee of Minorities' Language and Writing.

The Uyghur Latin alphabet has received extensive public relations coverage online and in official Xinjiang regional media, while authorities sought to downplay the perception that it represented a sweeping reform. Despite these attempts, observers have tended to interpret the change as a major overhaul, and the general public appears cautious or wary toward the reform. A frequently noted feature of the system is its direct mapping between Latin letters and the Uyghur Arabic script, which has been highlighted as a distinguishing characteristic.

Conceived during the period of the First Aliyah, the flag subsequently became the emblem associated with Zionism from its inception in 1897. After the establishment of the State of Israel, it was officially adopted as the national flag on 28 October 1948, with its selection reflecting its popularity among the Jewish population of the country compared with alternative proposals.

Israel's national emblem, designed by the brothers Gabriel and Maxim Shamir, was chosen from numerous proposals submitted for a design competition conducted in 1948 and was formally adopted on 10 February 1949.

Elizabeth II has appeared as a fictional figure in several works of literature, spanning mystery fiction, satire, and literary fiction. In C. C. Benison's Her Majesty Investigates series, the queen is depicted as a detective, with Death at Buckingham Palace, Death at Windsor Castle, and Death at Sandringham House comprising the principal installments in which this portrayal appears. The monarch also features prominently in Sue Townsend's The Queen and I, as well as in her later work Queen Camilla, both of which engage with contemporary royal life from a satirical perspective. In Alan Bennett's The Uncommon Reader, Elizabeth II is presented as a character within a narrative that explores the queen’s encounters with literature. Through these varied treatments, Elizabeth II is depicted across genres as a public figure navigating mystery, social satire, and literary engagement.

Elizabeth II reigned as Queen of the United Kingdom and Head of the Commonwealth from 1952 to 2022, and her public image was widely regarded as favorable throughout much of her reign. She was noted for a modest wardrobe, often choosing solid-colour overcoats paired with matching hats to ensure visibility in crowds during public appearances. Across her long tenure she attended numerous cultural events as part of her official duties, reinforcing her role as a symbol of national identity. Her stated leisure interests encompassed horse racing, photography, and dogs, especially Pembroke Welsh corgis. Reports also highlight a fondness for particular foods, including daily jam sandwiches since childhood, alongside dishes such as fish and chips, chocolate perfection pie, scones with jam and clotted cream, salmon from the River Dee, and Morecambe Bay potted shrimp. Debates about her political views or other private matters were largely conjectural, as she never gave a press interview and kept personal opinions out of the public sphere.

The seashores and adjacent waters around Great Britain hold international importance for marine biodiversity. The fauna in these waters ranges from large cetaceans—such as whales, dolphins, and porpoises—to pinniped species including grey seals and common seals, as well as microscopic animals. The region supports more than 200 species of fish, with diversity extending from small blennies to the basking shark, which is the second-largest shark in the world.

Thais forbesi is a marine gastropod mollusk in the family Muricidae that inhabits seashore environments. The shell reaches a height of about 25–35 mm, with a width that is somewhat less than the height, and the aperture measures roughly half the shell height. The outer lip is typically not toothed, and the spire is moderately pointed. The sculpture consists of two to three spiral rows of pointed tubercles, while the coloration ranges from grey to brown and is often obscured by overgrowth. The interior of the aperture is grey. These characteristics were described by Yankson and Kendall (2001).

The article on the Yuchi language surveys its prosodic system, illustrating both regular and non-regular stress patterns, with all examples provided and glossed. All data cited are drawn from Wagner (1974), unless otherwise noted.

The Yuchi language comprises 49 distinct sounds, of which 38 are consonants and 11 are vowels. This total exceeds twice the number of sounds typical for most Southeastern Native American languages, reflecting a comparatively large phonetic inventory within its regional context.

The locality now known as Friedrichsfelde is first attested in 1265 under the name Rosenfelde. In 1699 the settlement acquired the name Friedrichsfelde, named in honor of Prince-Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg. It functioned as an autonomous municipality within the former Niederbarnim district until 1920, when it was incorporated into Berlin under the Greater Berlin Act.

Friedrichsfelde lies in the eastern suburbs of Berlin. It borders the districts of Lichtenberg, Rummelsburg, and Karlshorst, as well as the areas of Marzahn and Biesdorf, which belong to the Marzahn-Hellersdorf district. In the south-eastern corner lies Tierpark Berlin, Berlin's second zoo.

Among the Palestinian diaspora, the Abu-Ghaben brothers are notable for founding the Cairo-based group Jaffa Phonix. While operating in Egypt, they blend high-energy big-beat rhythms with components of hip hop and vocal punk, illustrating a cross-genre approach within Palestinian music.

During the occupation, Palestinian classical music continued to develop, with an emergence of new names in the field. A number of symphonic ensembles were established, including the Palestinian Youth Orchestra and the West-Eastern Divan Orchestra. The latter, founded by Daniel Barenboim and Edward Said, became a notable example of cross-cultural collaboration through music. In addition, there was growth in chamber music, particularly among string quartets and quintets. As a result, the Palestinian Territories came to host the highest number of orchestras among Arab countries.

In December 2021, Paytm launched Paytm Wealth Academy. In March 2022, the Reserve Bank of India barred Paytm Payments Bank from signing up new customers after an inspection found that customer data leakage occurred to China-based entities that indirectly owned a stake in Paytm Payments Bank.

Paytm, an Indian digital payments and financial services company, expanded rapidly between 2017 and 2019, achieving notable milestones in downloads, product launches, and merchant services. In 2017, it surpassed 100 million app downloads and introduced Paytm Gold, allowing online purchases of pure gold with increments as small as ₹1. The same year saw the launch of Paytm Payments Bank and Inbox, a messaging platform with in-chat payments. By 2018, merchants could accept Paytm, UPI, and card payments directly into their bank accounts with zero processing charges. The company also rolled out the Paytm for Business app, later renamed Business with Paytm App, to help merchants track payments and settlements, and its merchant base exceeded seven million by March 2018. In wealth management, Paytm launched two products, the Paytm Gold Savings Plan and Gold Gifting for long-term savings. In January 2018, a joint venture with AGTech Holdings, which is owned by Alibaba Group, led to the launch of Gamepind, a mobile gaming platform that was rebranded as Paytm First Games in June 2019. Additionally, Paytm Money commenced operations in March 2018 with an initial investment of ₹9 crore to provide investment and wealth-management services.

On 22 January, the royal party traveled by car to Burnham Military Camp and to Ashburton. A public reception was held in Ashburton. They then proceeded to Longbeach, where they relaxed for the weekend of 23–24 January.

During the afternoon of 25 January, the royal party traveled by train to the towns of Oamaru and Palmerston, where public welcomes were extended to greet them. After these engagements, the royal party continued by train on to Dunedin.

Iguazu Falls features the Garganta del Diablo, the principal canyon of the system, which measures about 80–90 meters in width and 70–80 meters in depth (approximately 260–300 feet wide and 230–260 feet deep). To the left of this canyon, the river’s course forms roughly 160–200 individual cascades, which, during flood stages, coalesce into a single front. Among the falls within the complex, the largest include San Martín, Adam and Eva, Penoni, and Bergano.

Iguazu Falls, situated on the border between Argentina and Brazil, is historically linked to the flooding of Guaíra Falls in 1982. The falls record one of the highest average annual discharges of any waterfall, ranking sixth worldwide. By comparison, Niagara Falls sits in fifth place with an average flow of about 1,746 cubic meters per second, while Iguazu has a maximum recorded flow of 45,700 m3/s observed on 9 June 2014. In terms of sustained flow, Niagara averages 2,400 m3/s with a maximum of 8,300 m3/s, and Victoria Falls averages 1,088 m3/s with a maximum of 7,100 m3/s. Together, these figures reflect Iguazu’s status as one of the most voluminous waterfalls globally during peak discharge periods.

AOL established formal partnerships with a wide range of educational organizations and content providers, including the National Education Association, the American Federation of Teachers, National Geographic, the Smithsonian Institution, the Library of Congress, Pearson, Scholastic, ASCD, NSBA, NCTE, Discovery Networks, Turner Education Services (CNN Newsroom), NPR, The Princeton Review, Stanley Kaplan, Barron’s, Highlights for Kids, the U.S. Department of Education, and others. These collaborations accompanied a series of educational milestones on the platform, beginning with online courses offered in 1988 and progressing to real-time homework help—the latter introduced in 1990 as the Teacher Pager after earlier homework-help bulletin boards. In the same period, AOL launched the Teachers’ Information Network in 1990 as the first omnibus service for teachers, and in 1991 introduced Kids Only Online, the first online service created by and for children, followed by the Parents Information Network, the first online service for parents. The year 1991 also saw AOL’s first online exhibit in partnership with the Library of Congress, and the company subsequently introduced the first parental controls, among numerous other online education firsts.

AOL released AOL Desktop Gold in 2017 as a paid version of its desktop client, available for $4.99 per month after a trial period, and it replaced the previous free AOL software. Following the 2017 shutdown of AIM, AOL's original chat rooms remained accessible through Desktop Gold, with some rooms staying active during peak hours, until the chat system was shut down on December 15, 2020.

Meritorious Service Medal (MSM) is a United States military decoration that is typically awarded to enlisted personnel in the Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard at pay grades E-8 and E-9. Among these services, E-8 recipients commonly hold the ranks of senior chief petty officer (Navy/Coast Guard) or master sergeant/first sergeant (Marine Corps). For E-9, typical awardees include master chief petty officer (Navy/Coast Guard) or sergeant major/master gunnery sergeant (Marine Corps). Awards to E-7 or below are very rare and occur only by exception.

The Meritorious Service Medal (MSM) is a United States military decoration awarded for meritorious service of a distinguished character. In the Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard, approval for the award must come from a flag officer or general officer at pay grade O-7 or higher. Typical recipients include senior enlisted personnel such as Navy and Coast Guard master chief petty officers (often serving as command master chiefs) and Marine Corps master gunnery sergeants and sergeants major. The MSM is commonly presented as an end-of-tour decoration and can also be awarded upon retirement.

Pavlos Carrer was a descendant of a noble Zakynthian family. He studied music in his birthplace under Italian instructors Giuseppe Cricca and Francesco Marangoni, and may have pursued studies in Corfu with Nikolaos Mantzaros. His intrinsic musical talent reflected the Ionian Islands’ cultural milieu, which was heavily influenced by Italian opera and Western European culture. He began composing his first small musical pieces in the late 1840s. The operatic scena Il pellegrino di Castiglia attracted public attention after its staging at the Apollon Municipal Theatre of Zakynthos.

Pavlos Carrer was a composer who produced Italianate operas alongside national melodramas. His opera Fior di Maria, with a libretto by Giovanni Caccialupi, was staged at the San Giacomo Theatre in Corfu in January 1868 and is distinguished by its inclusion of realistic and pre-veristic elements. Another work, Maria Antonietta, with a libretto by Giorgio Roma, opened at the Foskolos Theatre in Zakynthos in January 1884 and is regarded as marking decisive steps toward dramatic and musical realism.

The Hunt with John Walsh received a positive reception from audiences at its launch. The premiere episode occupied the 9:00 p.m. ET timeslot among cable news networks and attracted 989,000 total viewers. In the key 25–54 demographic, it drew 330,000 viewers, marking the highest-rated debut for a CNN original series within that demographic.

The Hunt with John Walsh has drawn mixed reception, with much of the critique centered on its format. Variety critic Brian Lowry described it as a contemporary reimagining of Walsh's earlier series America’s Most Wanted and suggested that its tone might be better suited to entertainment-oriented networks such as TLC or Investigation Discovery. The show employs reenactments, including depictions of a dead body with blood presented in a stylized manner. The review also contends that CNN blurs the boundary between news reporting and entertainment, making the program resemble a Lifetime-style feature rather than traditional journalistic coverage.

Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama in 1513 and, upon sighting a large sea to the south, designated it the Mar del Sur, or Southern Sea. Later, during Ferdinand Magellan's 1520 circumnavigation, the ocean was christened Mar Pacífico after the voyage encountered favorable winds; the name, meaning “peaceful sea” in Portuguese and Spanish, provided the basis for the modern designation of the body of water.

In the Pacific Ocean, the pursuit of manganese nodules through deep-sea mining has been associated with substantial environmental risks. The activity involves disturbing seabed sediments and altering deep-sea ecosystems, potentially causing irreversible damage to fragile habitats that are slow to recover. Sediment resuspension and the introduction of chemical pollutants from the extraction process threaten a variety of marine life that depends on the integrity of the seabed environment. Moreover, the mining operation can contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, thereby intersecting with broader climate change concerns. Given these potential impacts, preventing or tightly regulating deep-sea mining is regarded as important for safeguarding the long-term health of the Pacific Ocean and its ecological systems.

On 22 July 1943, King Victor Emmanuel III met with Benito Mussolini to discuss the regime’s position in the wake of the Grand Council of Fascism’s actions. Mussolini pledged to disengage Italy from the war by 15 September, a timetable that allowed for a roughly two‑month postponement while Bastianini began contacting the Allies and Mussolini sought to justify his leadership to the world. According to Badoglio, the King was in agreement with Mussolini, which in turn left the Duce less anxious about the forthcoming Grand Council session. Any coup would depend on royal backing, since it would fail without the King’s aid. Following the meeting, Mussolini was convinced the King would stand by him, whereas Victor Emmanuel was disappointed after being urged to resign, a suggestion he deemed untenable. The King nonetheless had to weigh a putsch seriously, aware that Bastianini was pursuing Allied contact and Farinacci was organizing a move to depose him and bring Italy under direct German control. The decisive moment came once it was known that the Grand Council had approved Grandi’s Order of the Day, a development that effectively sealed Mussolini’s political fate.

Following the fall of the fascist regime in Italy, civilians nationwide removed fascist emblems and propaganda posters from buildings, signaling a broad repudiation of fascist symbols. In Rome, high-ranking fascists were detained at Forte Boccea, Rome's military prison. The reprisals were largely nonviolent, consisting of removing the fascist lapel pin, often referred to as the 'bug', and forcing the detainees to toast to Badoglio.

Lingya District is an administrative district that comprises a large number of subdistricts and villages, including Boren, Lingzhou, Lingsheng, Lingzhong, Lingya, Lingtung, Chengbei, Chengxi, Chengtung, Yicheng, Guzhong, Tianxi, Renhe, Renzheng, Guangze, Meitian, Huatang, Rizhong, Puzhao, Hexu, Qinglang, Putian, Linfu, Linwei, Linan, Guanghua, Linxing, Linhua, Linxi, Linzhong, Linquan, Linnan, Zhongzheng, Shangyi, Tongqing, Kaixuan, Anxiang, Zoujie, Fushou, Funan, Wuquan, Minzhu, Linde, Lingui, Linrong, Yingming, Linjing, Zhaoyang, Fulong, Fuxiang, Fuhai, Fukang, Furen, Fude, Fuju, Futung, Fuxi, Yongkang, Zhengwen, Zhengyan, Zhengda, Wufu, Zhengxin, Zhengdao, Zhengyi, Zhengren, Wenchang, Jianjun and Weiwu Village.

Lingya District derives its name from the coastal traditional community Lingyaliao (苓雅寮), which has several romanizations, including Língyǎliáo in pinyin, Lêng-ngá-liâu in Pe̍h-ōe-jī, and Lêng-á-liâu for 苓仔寮. The name Lingyaliao is linked to 苓仔 (lêng-á), a term denoting a place where fishermen stored nets after use. In 1945, Lingyaliao merged with Guotianzi (過田子), Lingdeguan (林德官), and Wukuaicuo (五塊厝) to form Lienya District (連雅區). In 1952, the original name Lingya (苓雅) was restored.

Willie Cook (November 11, 1923 – September 22, 2000) was an American jazz trumpeter born in Tangipahoa Parish, Louisiana. He grew up in Chicago, where he learned the violin before taking up the trumpet during his teenage years. In the late 1930s he joined King Perry's band and, in the early 1940s, Jay McShann's ensemble. Over his career he performed with a range of prominent artists, including Johnny Hartman, Earl Hines, Jimmie Lunceford, Ella Fitzgerald, Dizzy Gillespie, Duke Ellington, B.B. King, and Count Basie. Cook joined Ellington's orchestra in October 1951 as lead trumpeter and remained with the ensemble for about ten years. After touring Sweden, he moved there permanently in 1982. He died of heart failure on September 22, 2000, at the Maria Regina Hospice in Stockholm.

When a company ceases operations, it may undergo liquidation to settle outstanding obligations and to avoid ongoing legal liabilities. Companies may also form associations and register as new entities under the designation of corporate groups. A corporate group is typically composed of a parent company and its subsidiary corporations, together constituting a structured hierarchy of related businesses.

The English word company derives from the Old French compagnie, first attested around 1150, where it carried meanings such as fellowship, social life, intimacy, and in military contexts a body of soldiers. It ultimately traces to Late Latin companio, meaning “one who eats bread with you.” The term is first attested in the Salic law circa AD 500 as a calque of a Germanic expression signifying “with bread” (gahlaibo). Related forms appear in other early Germanic languages, including Old High German galeipo meaning “companion” and Gothic gahlaiba meaning “messmate.”

Chloroflexota is a bacterial phylum whose origins lie in Carl Woese’s 1987 scheme that split the Eubacteria into eleven divisions on the basis of 16S rRNA (SSU) gene sequences. Within that framework, Woese assembled the genera Chloroflexus, Herpetosiphon, and Thermomicrobium into a cohesive group described as green non-sulfur bacteria and their relatives. This assemblage was subsequently designated Chloroflexi for a time in Volume One of Bergey’s Manual of Systematic Bacteriology, reflecting its status as a distinct bacterial lineage.

Chloroflexota are monoderm bacteria, possessing a single cytoplasmic membrane and lacking an outer membrane. Accordingly, they predominantly stain Gram-negative. By comparison, many well-studied bacterial phyla are diderms, featuring two membranes and also staining Gram-negative. Among monoderms that stain Gram-positive, notable groups include Firmicutes/Bacillota, which are low G+C content Gram-positive organisms, and Actinomycetota, a high G+C Gram-positive lineage.

Brøndby Kommune is a Danish municipality in the Region Hovedstaden, which previously formed part of Copenhagen County. It is situated along the eastern coast of the island of Zealand (Sjælland) in eastern Denmark. The municipality covers an area of 20.85 square kilometers (approximately 8.05 square miles) and has a population of 40,401 as of 2025. The municipal council is led by Mayor Kent Max Magelund, a member of the Social Democrats (Socialdemokraterne).

Brøndby Strand, a district within Brøndby Municipality, consists of two urban centers and features a mix of housing types, including a substantial number of single-family homes as well as twelve high-rise residential estates. It is notable for being the only area in Denmark where a majority of residents are not Danish-born or of Danish descent. The district comprises four neighborhoods, which are commonly referred to collectively as the Southside or South Coast Copenhagen.

The Defense Distinguished Service Medal is a United States Department of Defense military decoration awarded to members of the U.S. Armed Forces for exceptionally distinguished performance of duty contributing to national security or defense. It was established on July 9, 1970, by President Richard Nixon through Executive Order 11545. Nixon awarded the first medal on the day the order was signed to General Earle G. Wheeler, who was retiring from the Army after serving as Army Chief of Staff and later as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

The Defense Distinguished Service Medal takes precedence over the service-specific Distinguished Service Medals awarded by the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Coast Guard. A period of service that has already been recognized with any of these service-level Distinguished Service Medals is not eligible for the Defense Distinguished Service Medal.

Bootle is represented on Sefton Council by three wards: Netherton and Orrell, Derby, and Linacre. Each ward elects three councillors, all of whom are affiliated with the Labour Party. In Netherton and Orrell, the councillors are Susan Ellen Bradshaw, Ian Ralph Maher, and Tom Spring. In Derby, the councillors are Brenda O'Brien, David Robinson, and Anne Thompson. In Linacre, the councillors are John Fairclough, Christine Maher, and Daniel McKee. Altogether, nine Bootle councillors sit on Sefton Council, all of whom are Labour members.

Bootle suffered extensive destruction during World War II as air raids targeted its port facilities and industrial sites. The post-war era saw a period of economic expansion in the 1950s and 1960s. Thereafter, the town experienced a downturn driven by the diminished international importance of Liverpool Docks, changes in industrial patterns, the growth of modern suburbs, and the relocation of industries into the Merseyside hinterlands. By the 1980s, unemployment rose sharply and population figures declined. In recent years, large-scale renewal initiatives have begun to regenerate the local economy.

Kettler's Kettcar, a four-wheeled pedal car, achieved widespread popularity in Germany and has become a generic term for this class of children's pedal vehicles. The term is included in the Duden dictionary, which defines it as a pedal-driven, chain-powered vehicle for children. Etymologically, the name blends the initial segment 'Kett' from the manufacturer Kettler with the German word for chain, 'Kette,' and the trailing 'car' is derived from the English term for automobile.

Kettler was established in 1949 in Parsit by Heinz Kettler and began life in the attic of a sawmill before evolving into a global manufacturing and distribution enterprise. It expanded its operations to sell products in more than sixty countries. After the founder's death in 2005, his daughter Karin assumed leadership of the company, and Ludger Busche serves as the chief executive officer.

In the digital era, music is predominantly released and consumed without physical carriers, with individual tracks commonly treated as separate works rather than as two sides of a physical format. As a result, the traditional A-side/B-side distinction has become obsolete. Some artists, however, augment a single-track release by adding a second track, described as a metaphorical B-side or bonus track. This practice can serve both as an aesthetic choice and as a promotional tool.

A-side and B-side denote the two faces of vinyl records and compact cassettes, with the labels commonly indicating each side as A or B. Technically, neither side is inherently favored in the recording or playback process, as the designation reflects labeling rather than an inherent audio priority. The A-side is typically the track chosen for promotion and radio airplay in order to become a hit, while the B-side serves as the secondary track and generally receives less attention. Nevertheless, there have been instances where B-sides have achieved substantial popularity, at times equaling or surpassing the corresponding A-sides.

Demi-soloist performances in ballet are most commonly choreographed for a pair of ballerinas. They are occasionally created for two or more dancers. Ballets that include dances for one, two, or more demi-soloist couples are comparatively rare.

The term demi-soloist in ballet has two meanings. In its primary sense, it designates a solo role ordinarily performed by a member of the corps de ballet; such roles are often created or performed in pairs by two corps dancers, frequently as mirror-image counterparts. This usage distinguishes dancers who mainly remain within the corps but may be cast in more prominent appearances on occasion. A second meaning of the term is acknowledged but not described in this paragraph.

In 2002, Reynard Motorsport's assets were divided among three buyers. BAR acquired the Brackley facilities together with the Advantage CFD aerodynamic engineering business. International Racing Management, based in Guildford, took over the Formula Nippon operations and the sports car program, with the latter licensed to Zytek Engineering for construction. Walker Racing, the Champ Car World Series team, obtained the rights to the Champ Car chassis, and subsequently sold the package to Ecuadorian entrepreneur Alex Salazar. Salazar attempted to establish a racing series in Ecuador but was unsuccessful, and he remains the ultimate owner of the package.

In the 1990s, Reynard Motorsport broadened its activities beyond traditional motorsport engineering. It undertook a project to design and manufacture lightweight carbon-fibre seats for Virgin Atlantic, a venture connected to Richard Branson. The arrangement stemmed from a personal friendship between Reynard and Branson. Production of the seats was carried out by a joint-venture company based at Reynard's headquarters in Brackley.

Following the withdrawal of ISO/IEC TR 20000-4:2010, the ISO/IEC 20000 family introduced two new documents that provide a Process Reference Model (PRM) and a Process Assessment Model (PAM). These models are based on ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 and were developed by ISO/IEC JTC1/SC7. The revised suite is published as ISO/IEC 33054 for the PRM and ISO/IEC 33074 for the PAM.

ISO/IEC 20000-3:2019 provides guidance to service providers on how to define the scope, determine applicability, and demonstrate conformance with ISO/IEC 20000-1. It is intended for providers seeking to meet the requirements of ISO/IEC 20000-1 or to plan improvements while pursuing ISO/IEC 20000 as a business objective. The standard complements ISO/IEC 20000-2, which offers generic guidance for implementing a Service Management System in accordance with ISO/IEC 20000-1.

Slick Rick, born Walters, began his career in 1985 after joining Doug E. Fresh's Get Fresh Crew, performing under the stage name MC Ricky D. He contributed to the group's singles "The Show" and its B-side "La Di Da Di," delivering rap verses over Doug E. Fresh's beatboxing. The recordings attracted mainstream attention and were presented on television programs such as Top of the Pops and Soul Train as part of the Get Fresh Crew. In Rolling Stone, Questlove lauded Rick, describing his voice as the most beautiful thing to happen to hip-hop culture and naming him the blueprint of the genre, while highlighting his punchlines, wit, melodic sense, cadence, confidence, and distinctive style.

Richard Walters, better known by his stage name Slick Rick, began receiving security from his mother Veronica in 1989 when she hired his first cousin Mark Plummer as his bodyguard. By 1990, Plummer had become a liability, making multiple extortion attempts against Walters. After being fired, Plummer, dissatisfied with his severance, attempted to rob Walters and threatened to kill Walters and his mother. In response, Walters discovered bullet holes at his front door and subsequently purchased firearms for protection. On July 3, 1990, Walters fired at least four shots at Plummer; one bullet struck Plummer and another hit a passerby in the foot, with neither injury deemed life-threatening.

Office supply retailing encompasses the sale of products required for a wide range of business activities. Retailers in this sector cater to the needs of organizations by supplying essential office goods and services. Historically, the majority of revenue came from desk stationery and printing services. In the 21st century, however, income streams have shifted, with technology products and office furniture contributing a growing share of revenue.

Office supply retailing has faced revenue declines from large corporate customers as the adoption of remote and hybrid work reduced demand for traditional office supplies, with the COVID-19 pandemic intensifying this shift. In response, many retailers redirected their emphasis toward selling home office products directly to individual consumers, expanding direct-to-consumer channels. To attract shoppers, retailers broadened the assortment of home office styles and emphasized delivery options that bring products to customers’ residences.

During the Easter Sunday Raid, British fighter pilots waited for a scramble order, but the order never arrived because of a lack of early warning. Consequently, they had to lift off under fire, and they could not initiate the engagement from a pre-positioned aerial formation.

During the Easter Sunday Raid, six Fairey Swordfish from 788 Naval Air Squadron were shot down while transferring from China Bay to Colombo. Their mission was to strike the Japanese fleet, and they arrived at Colombo as the attack unfolded.

Isinai employs a definite determiner that appears in three distinct realizations: ar, ardari, and war. The specific form used is conditioned by the noun’s grammatical relationship within its phrase or clause, so each variant reflects how the noun is related to other elements in the sentence.
Ethnologue lists Dupax del Sur, Aritao, and Bambang as dialects of Isinai, while noting that the Aritao dialect is moribund.

Horace Walpole’s letters document a severe July 1757 heatwave, with a 12 July entry describing exceptionally hot weather and sultry conditions, while Walpole, walking in the garden, confessed that he feared he might die from the heat and suggested that the summer of 1757 would be remembered. Four days later, on 16 July, the heat was described as extremely intense, leaving people unaccustomed to such temperatures and unsure of how to behave. The correspondence also notes that Mr. Bentley was shivering, a detail cited to illustrate the range of responses to the heat and the contrasting reactions among observers.

The July 1757 heatwave refers to a period of extreme summer temperatures in July 1757 that influenced the work of the Quaker poet John Scott of Amwell. In Elegy II, written during the hot weather of July 1757 and included in his 1760 collection Four Elegies: Descriptive and Moral, Scott portrays a drought-affected landscape shaped by the season's heat. The imagery depicts ground that seems to lose vitality, springs that fall low, ditches that dry up, and the valley presenting no verdant spots. Despite the aridity, the poem notes that the streams provide a steady, reliable water supply, offering a measure of relief amid the drought.

The Port of St. Louis is situated along the Mississippi River and encompasses roughly 19.3 miles of riverbank. It handles more than 32 million tons of freight annually, ranking as the second-largest inland port in the United States by trip-ton miles and the third-largest by total tonnage. The port features more than 100 barge docks and 16 public river terminals. In 2012 and 2013, the Port Authority added two small fire and rescue vessels.

St. Louis features the Strassberger Music Conservatory Building, which was constructed in 1904—the same year as the World's Fair—and located at 2300 Grand. The structure was designed by architect Otto Wilhelmi. By 1911, the conservatory enrolled over 1,100 students, illustrating its prominent role in local music education. Today, the building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Among its notable graduates is Alfonso D'Artega.

The kotta mara was not fully completed at the time it was removed, with many ornamental elements presumably missing. Four principal posts of the structure had already been carved when the work was halted. The carvings depict a male figure noted for an exceptionally large nose and a mouth filled with sharp teeth, while the lower portion of the figure's body culminates in a caiman's tail.

Kotta mara refers to a two-layer fortification wall, with the outer layer consisting of vertical timbers placed in close contact and sloping slightly inward to form a parapet about half a meter thick. The inner or second wall is built from horizontal ironwood beams about 0.35 meters in thickness. This inner wall is anchored and braced to prevent backward movement or loosening. The upper surface, or raft, is closed by a cover of heavy components and is rendered bomb-proof by an attic-like framework of beams.

The SNECMA Turbomeca Larzac is a military turbofan engine manufactured by the Groupement Turbomeca-SNECMA (GRTS), a French consortium formed by SNECMA and Turbomeca. The arrangement reflects a collaboration between two French aerospace companies, and the engine’s primary application was to power the Dassault/Dornier Alpha Jet.

Meyers Konversations-Lexikon is a German general encyclopedia. The fourth edition consisted of 16 volumes, issued between 1885 and 1890, and was supplemented by two update-page volumes, published as volumes 17 in 1891 and 18 in 1892. The fifth edition expanded to 17 volumes and bore the title Meyers Konversations-Lexikon. Ein Nachschlagewerk des allgemeinen Wissens, appearing from 1893 to 1897. This edition achieved sales of at least 233,000 sets.

Meyers Konversations-Lexikon, commonly abbreviated Meyers Lexikon, was a leading German-language reference work that appeared in multiple editions and under various titles over its long publication history. Published between 1839 and 1984, it underwent numerous revisions and name changes as it evolved. In 1984 the encyclopedia was merged into the Brockhaus Enzyklopädie, ending its separate existence.

In 1999, GeoCities added a commercial platform named the GeoCities Marketplace. The Marketplace included the GeoStore, a shop offering GeoCities-branded merchandise. Users could redeem GeoPoints to make purchases in the store.

GeoCities, later known as Yahoo! GeoCities, was a free web hosting service that allowed users to create and publish personal websites while also enabling browsing of other sites organized by theme or interest. It remained active from 1994 to 2009. The venture was founded in November 1994 by David Bohnett and John Rezner, initially under the name Beverly Hills Internet before it was renamed GeoCities. The service was acquired by Yahoo! on January 28, 1999, and at the time of the acquisition it was reportedly the third-most-visited website on the World Wide Web.

In March 1795 the Hamburg Chamber of Commerce proposed dispatching a special envoy to Paris to lift the embargo, and Georg Heinrich Sieveking was chosen for his prominence in Paris; he arrived in the French capital on the night of 31 March 1796 with a delegation that included Friedrich Johann Lorenz Meyer. The mission took place against a backdrop of relative political stability following the Vendémiaire uprising of 5 October 1795, which had been suppressed by Napoleon Bonaparte and Paul Barras. On 12 April 1796 Sieveking met with the French Directory, but no agreement was reached. His plan to improve Hamburg’s finances by raising the exchange rate for devalued assignats was rejected by the French as insufficient and by the Hamburg Senate as impracticable. On 27 April 1796 the Hamburg Chamber granted him 300,000 Marks at his discretion, and he used these funds to curry favor with Barras and other Republic figures. In May 1796, after meeting the French finance minister Ramel-Nogaret, the Directory ratified a treaty on 14 June 1796 providing for 13 million livres, personally guaranteed by Sieveking. Barras told him that evening: “Votre affaire est finie.” The official signing occurred about ten days later (late June 1796); Sieveking wrote to Hamburg, expressing concern about being the victim of patriotism. In July 1796 he returned to Hamburg and was received with honours; in a chamber of commerce report he proclaimed the moment among the finest and most important of his life and asserted, “Ich habe Hamburg gerettet.”

Georg Heinrich Sieveking married Johanna Margaretha Sieveking, the daughter of Johann Albert Heinrich Reimarus, a physician, natural historian and economist. Their son Karl Sieveking later held the office of Syndicus of Hamburg from 1820 to 1847.

Korolev pursued specialized aviation studies through 1929 while living in crowded conditions in Moscow with his family, and he took advantage of opportunities to fly both gliders and powered aircraft. In 1928 he designed a glider, which he subsequently piloted in a competition in 1929. Amid a political drive by the Communist Party to accelerate engineering education to address urgent industrial needs, Korolev earned a diploma by the end of 1929 after producing a practical aircraft design.

Sergei Korolev's plan to reach the Moon before Sputnik 1 involved modifying the R-7 Semyorka ballistic missile to carry a lunar package. The concept gained approval in 1958 after Korolev argued that existing technology could reach the Moon. A modified R-7 with a new upper stage was employed, and the final stage engine was the first designed to fire in outer space. Korolev referred to his moon ships as Mechta (dream), while the Soviet program officially designated them Lunas. The first three lunar probes in 1958 failed, in part due to political pressure to hasten launches and insufficient funding and testing. Korolev blamed Moscow infighting and funding issues for the program's troubles, noting that the United States also faced a rough launch record at the time; allegedly, he quipped, "Do you think that only American rockets explode!" under pressure to beat the United States. Luna 1, launched on 2 January 1959, was intended to impact the surface but missed by about 6,000 kilometers; instead it achieved escape velocity, passed near the Moon, and became the first artificial object to orbit the Sun. Luna E-1A No.1 failed at launch, while Luna 2 successfully impacted the Moon on 14 September 1959. Luna 3, launched 7 October 1959, became the first spacecraft to photograph the far side of the Moon.

Data masking is a data security technique that obscures selected data elements within structured data, such as a database table or column, to reduce the risk of exposure while preserving the usability of the data for legitimate tasks. It serves multiple audiences: users who interact with the data may be allowed to view only non-sensitive fragments, such as the last four digits of an account number for banking representatives; developers who require realistic production data for testing but should not access sensitive fields; and outsourcing vendors who need controlled access. Some descriptions characterize masking as a form of encryption, achieved by altering particular characters (letters and digits) to conceal the original values. Access to the unmasked data is restricted to individuals with the appropriate decryption code or privileges. By maintaining data structure and referential integrity, masking enables validation and workflow processes while mitigating exposure risks.

The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) was proposed by the European Commission with the aim of strengthening and harmonizing data protection for individuals within the European Union. It seeks to create a consistent regulatory framework for processing personal data across EU member states and to enhance individuals’ privacy rights. Additionally, the regulation addresses the transfer of personal data to jurisdictions outside the EU, establishing rules intended to safeguard data when it is exported beyond European borders.

In 2013, Lululemon faced customer criticisms regarding product quality, including garments that were too sheer, developed holes, or wore thin after limited use. That year the company also recalled its black yoga pants for being unintentionally transparent and excessively thin, a recall affecting about 17 percent of all women's pants sold and contributing to weaker financial performance. The financial impact and reputational damage from the recall coincided with leadership changes, including the departure of Chief Product Officer Sheree Waterson and Chief Executive Christine Day. In 2014, Lululemon opened its first European store in Covent Garden, London. In February 2015, Wilson resigned from the board, and Michael Casey, the former lead director, was appointed to replace him. In 2018, Laurent Potdevin resigned as chief executive and from the board amid misconduct allegations related to a relationship with a then-employee who later became a contractor.

Lululemon Athletica became a member of the Nasdaq-100 index on December 24, 2018. In 2019 the company invested in MIRROR, a home fitness startup known for its interactive fitness mirrors. On June 29, 2020, MIRROR was acquired by Lululemon for $500 million and rebranded as lululemon Studio. The initiative included plans to develop new content for the device, beginning with meditation classes. At the end of the 2022 fiscal year, Lululemon recorded a post-tax impairment charge of $442.7 million related to the acquisition.

In the Indian Himalayan Region, the Zanskar Range lies to the north of the main Himalaya and functions as the backbone of Ladakh south of the Indus River. It extends roughly 250 kilometers (about 160 miles) from the Karcha (Suru) River near Kargil in the northwest to Tso Kar in the southeast, and it separates the Indus Valley from the Zanskar Valley. The range is distinguished from the main Himalaya by a corridor carved through the Stod, Tsarap and Zanskar valleys, creating a discrete geographic unit. Its principal pass on the Leh-Srinagar road is Fatu La, while trekking routes into the Zanskar Valley traverse passes such as Singge La, Cha Cha La, and Rubrang La.

The Indian Himalayan Region encompasses the northern portion of the Indian subcontinent, extending from the southern foothills known as the Sivalik Hills to the northern edge of the Tibetan plateau, often referred to as the Trans-Himalaya. It is divided into three principal zones—the Himadri (Greater Himalaya), the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya), and the Sivaliks (Outer Himalaya)—which extend almost continuously along the length of the range and are separated by major geological fault lines. Collectively, these zones form a continuous mountain belt that varies in altitude and geology while retaining a distinct structural sequence. A number of ancient rivers, including the Indus, Sutlej, Kali, Kosi, and Brahmaputra, cut steep gorges across the main range as they descend toward the Great Plains, shaping the region's drainage pattern. These rivers predate the uplift of the Himalayas, indicating antecedent courses that were preserved as the mountains rose.

Marienturm uses a reinforced concrete skeleton as its structural framework, with flat reinforced concrete slabs on every floor. The floor plan is defined by columns placed along the exterior perimeter, while four reinforced concrete core areas are embedded within the building. These core areas provide the essential horizontal stiffness needed to resist lateral loads, and they are interconnected by corridor ceilings and supporting beams, creating a continuous and integrated structural system.

Marienturm is a skyscraper in Frankfurt, Germany, completed in 2019 and rising to a height of 155 meters. As of 2022, it ranked as the fifteenth-tallest building in the city, a position it shares with the Deutsche Bank Twin Towers. The structure is located in the Bankenviertel district and was built between 2015 and 2019. It was developed by Pecan Development GmbH for a fund affiliated with Aermont Capital, and it is primarily used for office space.
In March 2023, Sony Music Nashville announced that Arista Nashville would be closed, with its existing roster transferring to other labels under Sony's ownership.

Arista Nashville is an American country music record label established as a division of Arista Records to focus on country artists. The label has featured a roster of notable performers, including Blackhawk, Brooks & Dunn, Rob Crosby, Linda Davis, Diamond Rio, Exile, Radney Foster, Dude Mowrey, The Tractors, and Steve Wariner, whose releases contributed to the label's prominence in the genre.

On September 19, 2024, Netflix released a short teaser for a new tie-in with Cyberpunk 2077, fueling speculation about a potential Cyberpunk: Edgerunners sequel. The teaser followed rumors that a continuation of the Edgerunners series was in development. CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski indicated plans for additional animated tie-ins, signaling the company's intent to expand its animated offerings within the Cyberpunk universe.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 has attracted attention from prominent figures in both the video game and tabletop communities. Renowned game designer Hideo Kojima praised the series, describing it as a remarkable achievement in bringing the Cyberpunk universe to animation and comparing its artistic direction and world-building favorably with the 1990 OVA Cyber City Oedo 808. Similarly, Mike Pondsmith, the creator of the original Cyberpunk role-playing game, commended the show, remarking that it felt as though his own concepts were realized on a large-screen anime format. In November 2022, R. Talsorian Games, the publisher of the Cyberpunk tabletop franchise, announced plans for an expansion based on Edgerunners.

Delta Force, the United States Army's premier special operations unit, maintains a training program that, in certain components, emphasizes espionage-oriented techniques intended for clandestine operations. Trainees learn about covert methods of information and material exchange, including the use of dead drops and brief encounters, as well as procedures for pickups and the signals that govern loading and unloading. The curriculum also covers the use of danger and safe signals to coordinate discreet activities and places emphasis on both surveillance practices and counter-surveillance measures to detect and avoid observation by others.

The 1st SFOD-D, commonly known as Delta Force, received the Presidential Unit Citation in recognition of its combat operations in Afghanistan as part of Operation Enduring Freedom from 4 October 2001 to 15 March 2002, and for its actions in Iraq during Operation Iraqi Freedom from 19 March 2003 to 13 December 2003.

The 1934 United States House of Representatives election in Arizona was part of the nationwide effort to elect members to the 74th Congress. The elections were held chiefly on November 6, 1934, with Maine holding its ballot on September 10, 1934, and occurred during Franklin D. Roosevelt’s first term as president. National results reflected a shift toward the Democratic Party, which gained nine net seats from the Republicans, as the GOP lost seats to the Progressive Party. This contributed to the Republicans falling below one-fourth of the House for the first time since the party’s founding. In the broader political landscape, the Wisconsin Progressive Party—aligned with Democrats—emerged as a notable force in Wisconsin politics. Within Arizona, voters participated in this national realignment, contributing to the composition of the state’s delegation to the 74th Congress.

Arizona's 1934 United States House elections were held against a national backdrop described as a referendum on President Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal policies. Conservatives and some middle-class voters who had not borne the Depression's worst effects viewed the initiatives as radical, while lower-income voters largely supported continuing Roosevelt's agenda. The midterm thus produced a historic national pattern, with the president's party not suffering a net loss of seats in either chamber, a phenomenon that would not be repeated in a midterm until 1998 and again in 2002. Arizona's results reflected this broader national dynamic.

Oesch's die Dritten are a Swiss family band from the Bernese Oberland whose music blends traditional yodeling with contemporary folk influences. They have enjoyed sustained success since the late 1990s, with a notable rise in prominence from around 2008 to the present. The ensemble is distinguished by its instrumental setup, with Hans Oesch performing on the Schwyzerörgeli (a small accordion) alongside guitar, electric bass, and a large accordion. The group is fronted by Melanie Oesch.

Switzerland's musical landscape has been shaped by a diversification of genres, with rap and electronic influences gaining prominence in the 1990s as rappers and DJs broadened the scene. Basel rapper Black Tiger was the first to perform in a Swiss German dialect, marking a milestone in language-based regional rap. From Renens near Lausanne, Sens Unik emerged as a notable rap collective, merging hip hop with a wide array of influences; their debut EP featured a Spanish-language track reflecting MC Carlos's Spanish and Galician heritage. Electronic music forms have long been part of the Swiss soundscape, with Yello issuing its debut album in 1979. In the 1980s, Touch El Arab achieved chart success across several European countries with the song "Muhammar." Basel-born Pat Jabbar founded Barraka el Farnatshi in the late 1980s, a label devoted to Arabic world music—especially Moroccan traditions—melded with Western dance music. While many artists drew on contemporary Anglo-Saxon styles, Christine Lauterburg fused traditional Swiss folk with pop and electronic elements; her rendition of "S'Vreneli vom Guggisberg" provoked polarized reception, attracting both indignation and praise.

CHMJ in Vancouver adopted a sports radio format in February 2004 after its previous format failed, and it was rebranded as MOJO Sports Radio, broadcasting on AM 730. The station competed primarily with CHUM's CKST Team 1040 and served as the radio home for teams such as the Vancouver Giants of junior hockey and the Vancouver Whitecaps of soccer, along with local university squads including the UBC Thunderbirds and SFU Clansmen in football and basketball. It also carried Seattle Seahawks games via Seattle's KIRO and maintained an affiliation with the ESPN Radio network, while sharing certain sports content with CKNW.

CHMJ, a Vancouver-area radio service operated by Corus Entertainment, underwent a restructuring in 2024–25. In June 2024, Corus closed CKGO as part of firm-wide cost-cutting measures. CKGO subsequently carried a transitional simulcast of CKNW. On February 24, 2025, CKNW’s programming and call letters were permanently moved to CKGO’s broadcast signal. Corus explained the change by citing the 730 frequency’s superior signal coverage across downtown Vancouver and the Lower Mainland.

Jacques Pierre Abbatucci served as garde des sceaux during the Second French Empire, and, in the emperor's absence, presided over the Council of Ministers. From 1852 to 1857 he was a senator and an official councillor to Napoleon III. Napoleon III appointed him chargé des affaires for Corsica, and in that capacity he played a central role in advancing the island's development under the Second Empire.

Jacques Pierre Abbatucci began his career as a lawyer and subsequently held a sequence of senior legal appointments. In January 1816 he was appointed procureur du roi at Sartène, and in March 1819 he became conseiller to the royal court of Bastia. In September 1830 he served as président de chambre at the court of Orléans. That same year he was elected député for Corsica, and from 1839 to 1851 he represented Le Loiret in the Chamber of Deputies. In January he held the office of minister of justice, Garde des Sceaux. In December 1852 he was named senator, a post he held until his death.

Yangon contains a cluster of major parks centered around Shwedagon Pagoda, comprising the city’s most extensive and best-maintained green spaces in the vicinity. Southeast of the pagoda, Kandawgyi Lake covers about 150 acres (61 hectares) and serves as the city’s most popular recreational area; it is bordered by Kandawgyi Nature Park (approximately 110 acres / 45 hectares) and the Yangon Zoological Gardens (about 69.25 acres / 28 hectares), which house a zoo, an aquarium, and an amusement park, together with Bogyoke Aung San Park. West of the pagoda, in the direction of the former Hluttaw complex, lies People's Square and Park, a 130-acre (53-hectare) site that historically served as a parading ground on national holidays when Yangon was the capital. North of the pagoda, Inya Lake Park sits a few miles away and covers 37 acres (15 hectares); it is widely frequented by Yangon University students and is a well-known romantic locale in Burmese popular culture.

Tourism is a major source of foreign currency for Yangon, though international arrivals have historically been relatively low by Southeast Asian standards, with about 250,000 visitors recorded before September 2007 during the Saffron Revolution. Visitation declined further following the Saffron Revolution and Cyclone Nargis. In recent years, improvements in the political climate have attracted a larger number of businesspeople and tourists. Yangon International Airport handled between 300,000 and 400,000 visitors in 2011. Years of underinvestment left Yangon with modest hotel infrastructure, totaling around 8,000 hotel rooms, of which only about 3,000 were suitable for tourists. As demand increases, hotel capacity is strained and will require expansion. As part of an urban development strategy, a hotel zone is planned on the outskirts of Yangon, intended to encompass government- and military-owned land in Mingaladon, Hlegu, and Htaukkyant Townships.

Extreme sledding is a sport characterized by performing tricks with a sled in conjunction with the rider’s body. Tricks are executed using apparatus such as ramps, rails, and ledges, or may be performed simply while descending the hill on the sled. The activity borrows elements from snowboarding, skateboarding, aggressive inline skating, BMX, and motocross to shape its technique and style. Equipment varies, with knee-sleds being the most common configuration, in which the rider travels on the knees and may have straps securing the legs.

Mersey flats were flat-bottomed boats used on the Mersey and surrounding waterways. By the end of the 19th century most had been converted to non-propelled barges, necessitating towing by horses or by steam tugs. The larger variants known as Weaver flats were fitted with their own steam engines, and later with diesel engines. Although sail continued to be used for some operations, around 1935 about twenty Mersey flats were still in sailing service. Today, both the Liverpool Maritime Museum and the Ellesmere Port Museum hold Mersey flats in their collections; however, the examples preserved there were not sailing vessels in actual operation.

Mersey flats were shallow-draught working vessels characterized by an oak hull and a deck of pitch pine. Sail plans varied among vessels: some carried a single mast with a fore-and-aft rig, while others were equipped with an additional mizzen mast. The hull combined a flat bottom with curved sides, yet the craft remained notably stable in the water. These boats were common from the 1730s to the 1890s.

Rhode Island features Narragansett Bay as a central element of its topography, containing more than thirty islands. The largest of these is Aquidneck Island, which contains the city of Newport and the towns of Middletown and Portsmouth. The second-largest is Conanicut Island, followed by Prudence Island as the third-largest. Block Island lies about 12 miles (19 km) off the southern coast of the mainland, and it marks the separation between Block Island Sound and the Atlantic Ocean proper.
Rhode Island is the smallest state by land area in the United States, yet it has the second-highest population density among the states, with New Jersey having the highest density.

During Malik-Shah I's reign, Savtegin's campaign against Georgia ended in defeat near Partskhisi, prompting a retreat.
