In some of the larger stars, these layers can constitute a substantial portion of the stellar radius, reflecting an unusually extended outer atmosphere. For instance, in the red supergiant Antares, the chromosphere is estimated to reach a radial extent of about 2.5 times the star’s radius, illustrating how chromospheric envelopes can be very extensive in massive stars.

Breathy consonants in Indo-Aryan languages such as Sanskrit and Hindi, and in comparative Indo-European research, are frequently described as voiced aspirated, with examples including bh, dh, ḍh, jh, and gh, and with reconstructions in Proto-Indo-European like bʰ, dʰ, ǵʰ, gʰ, and gʷʰ. This labeling is articulatorily misleading, since breathy voice constitutes a distinct phonation type rather than true aspiration. Nevertheless, breathy and aspirated stops often yield similar acoustic profiles, because both involve a delayed onset of voicing. Historical language development has seen breathy stops evolve into aspirated stops in some lineages, a pattern observed in Greek and in certain varieties of Chinese.

Breathy voice refers to a phonation in which the vocal folds are only partially adducted along their length, allowing airflow that imparts a perceptible breathiness. A second realization, often described as whispery voice, occurs when the vocal folds are approximated but the arytenoid cartilages form an opening, producing a whisper-like quality. The distinction between these two realizations is phonetically relevant in White Hmong (Hmong Daw).

Friedrich Wölfert conducted a series of early airship experiments between 1888 and 1897, constructing three craft powered by gasoline engines produced by Daimler-Motoren-Gesellschaft. The final airship, Deutschland, was lost when it caught fire in flight in 1897, resulting in the deaths of its two occupants. The 1888 model was equipped with a 2 horsepower, single-cylinder Daimler engine, and it completed a 10-kilometer flight from Cannstatt to Kornwestheim.

During World War I, the Royal Navy sustained its program of rigid-airship development, culminating in eight rigid airships completed by the armistice: No. 9r, four vessels of the 23 Class, two of the R23X Class, and one of the R31 Class. At the end of the conflict, several additional rigid airships were still in advanced stages of completion. France and Italy also maintained airship operations throughout the war; France preferred non-rigid designs, while Italy operated 49 semi-rigid airships in both reconnaissance and bombing roles.

The National Center for Biotechnology Information has been responsible for making GenBank available to researchers since 1992. GenBank operates through coordination with individual laboratories that submit sequence data, and it also aligns its records with other major nucleotide databases, including the European Molecular Biology Laboratory’s EMBL and the DNA Data Bank of Japan.

Entrez Global Query Cross-Database Search System, developed at the National Center for Biotechnology Information, functions as the cross-database search and indexing platform for NCBI’s major resources, including Nucleotide and Protein Sequences, Protein Structures, PubMed, Taxonomy, Complete Genomes, and OMIM, among others. It operates as both an indexing and retrieval system, bringing together data from diverse sources to support biomedical research. The inaugural version, released in 1991, integrated nucleotide records from GenBank and PDB, protein sequences from SWISS-PROT as well as translated GenBank, PIR, PRF, and PDB, together with abstracts and citations from PubMed. Entrez is designed to harmonize data from multiple origins, databases, and formats into a single, uniform information model and retrieval framework, enabling efficient access to references, sequences, and structural information.

Within the New Testament, the opening verse of the First Epistle of Peter identifies the author as Peter, described as an apostle of Jesus Christ. Church Fathers Irenaeus, Tertullian, Clement of Alexandria, and Origen attested to Peter's authorship of the letter. There was little controversy over Peter's authorship of 1 Peter until the eighteenth century, whereas the authorship of 2 Peter was debated in antiquity. Today, many biblical scholars conclude that 2 Peter was not written by Peter. Among those who defend an early date and Petrine authorship for 1 Peter are Kruger, Zahn, Spitta, Bigg, and Green.

The Epistle to the Hebrews is an anonymous work within the New Testament, with no author explicitly identified in the text. Scholarly consensus generally regards Paul as unlikely to have written Hebrews. Nevertheless, Hebrews is frequently grouped with the other thirteen Pauline epistles, a classification that together forms a corpus of fourteen epistles commonly referred to as the Pauline corpus.

In December 2018, Joe Preston, then the Chief Commercial Officer, was appointed president of New Balance, succeeding Rob DeMartini. In March 2020, the company announced that it would convert several of its New England manufacturing facilities to the production of face masks in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

New Balance Athletic Shoe, Inc., commonly known as New Balance, entered a new growth phase in 1972 when Jim Davis, then 28, acquired the company, believing leisure-time footwear would be a high-growth market. At that time the business consisted of six employees producing about 30 pairs of shoes daily, with sales primarily via mail-order and a small number of U.S. retailers. In the 1970s, the Boston area emerged as a center of the running boom, fostering expansion of the product line and rapid sales growth. The United Kingdom factory opened in Workington in 1982 and was relocated to Flimby in 1991.

Formed in Toronto, Ontario, The Band is a Canadian-American rock group whose members include Rick Danko (Canadian) on bass, guitar, vocals and fiddle; Garth Hudson (Canadian) on organ, keyboards, accordion and saxophone; Richard Manuel (Canadian) on piano, drums and vocals; Robbie Robertson (Canadian) on guitar, piano and percussion; and Levon Helm (American) on drums, vocals, mandolin, guitar and bass. Their music blends elements of Americana, folk, rock, rhythm and blues, jazz and country, yielding a distinctive cross-genre sound. The Band’s work has influenced a wide spectrum of artists, with noted impacts on George Harrison, Elton John, the Grateful Dead, Eric Clapton, Wilco and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.

Following the release of its second album, The Band undertook its first headlining tour, marking a new level of prominence for the group. The growing pressures and anxiety surrounding fame contributed to a shift toward more somber subjects—fear and alienation—that would shape their subsequent material. Stage Fright, issued in 1970, was engineered by Todd Rundgren and recorded live at the Woodstock Playhouse in Woodstock, New York. Robbie Robertson was credited with the majority of the songwriting on Stage Fright, as on the prior self-titled LP. Initial critical reception was favorable in its own right but, in comparison with the first two albums, many reviewers framed it as a disappointment for a variety of reasons. After Stage Fright, The Band joined Festival Express, a Canada-by-train all-star tour that featured Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead, and future Band member Richard Bell (then with Joplin's backing group). The 2003 Festival Express documentary footage includes Rick Danko in a drunken jam with Jerry Garcia, Bob Weir, John Dawson, and Joplin as he sings "Ain't No More Cane."

The Porter–MacKenzie debate concerns competing interpretations of the role of empire in nineteenth-century Britain. Supporters of MacKenzie’s position include Catherine Hall, Antoinette Burton, and Jeffrey Richards, who align with a reading that emphasizes particular cultural formations and the ways imperial meanings circulated. In contrast, Andrew Thompson supported Porter, arguing that there was no single or unified imperial culture throughout the nineteenth century and that empire occupied a complex and ambivalent position within British cultural life.

Porter–MacKenzie debate centers on methodological interpretation in history, with Porter employing an archaeological metaphor to argue that historians have uncovered only fragments of limited structural significance. Porter himself was trained as an archaeologist and nearly pursued that field, and he maintains that he has found numerous such fragments in historical materials. He contends that, within archaeological practice, an assemblage of fragments in a deposit indicates the existence of a culture rather than its absence, a point he extends to interpret historical evidence as signaling continuity and presence even where the record is incomplete.

Within this broader framework, the familiar properties of the Fourier transform arise as natural consequences. The operator W2 corresponds to taking the Fourier transform twice, i.e., the square of the Fourier transform, and it functions as an intertwiner associated with the negative identity J2 = −I. Consequently, for any appropriate function f, one has (W2 f)(x) = f(−x), meaning that applying the Fourier transform twice results in the reflection of the function about the origin.

In contemporary practice, the discrete Fourier transform is obtained by evaluating the discrete-time Fourier transform on a uniformly spaced grid of frequency values, effectively sampling the DTFT to produce the DFT for a finite-length sequence. Depending on the desired frequency resolution, a range of efficient procedures is employed, as described in the DTFT section on sampling the DTFT. The DFT serves this computational purpose and is typically carried out using fast Fourier transform algorithms, which provide a substantial reduction in computational cost relative to direct evaluation.

Konz is a town in western Germany, situated in the Trier-Saarburg district of Rhineland-Palatinate. It lies at the confluence of the Saar and Moselle rivers, and is located roughly eight kilometers southwest of Trier. The town is historically known by the Latin name Contionacum, and its German pronunciation is rendered as [kɔnts].

Koppány, also known as Cupan, was a Hungarian nobleman active in the late 10th century who led a pagan opposition to Hungary’s Christianization and held the title of duke of Somogy. He asserted a royal claim based on the traditional principle of seniority, but was ultimately defeated and executed by Stephen, who was born Vajk and was the son of Géza, the preceding grand prince.

Koppány was a member of the early Hungarian nobility who survived Géza’s purge of relatives. According to the Illuminated Chronicle, he bore the title Duke of Symigium, corresponding to the county of Somogy. Some later sources, including Osvát Laskai and a 16th‑century Carthusian monk, also identify him as lord of Zala. In contemporary historiography, he is typically placed as an administrator of southwestern Transdanubia, with jurisdiction likely situated between Lake Balaton and the Dráva. Szabados notes that Koppány’s father had already dominated Somogy and Zala, implying a family power base in the region. László Kontler contends that Koppány received his duchy from Géza as compensation after Géza designated his own son Stephen as heir.

On August 7, 1998, a large tire pile at S.F. Royster's Tire Disposal, located south of Tracy at 29425 South MacArthur Drive near Linne Road, became the focus of a prolonged environmental incident after more than seven million tires were found illegally stored at the site. The resulting tire fire persisted for more than two years before it was finally extinguished. At the time, officials judged that allowing the fire to burn posed less risk of groundwater contamination than actively fighting the blaze. The comprehensive cleanup ultimately cost approximately $16.2 million. During the incident, chemicals released from the tires contaminated groundwater in the surrounding region.

Public transit in Tracy is served by more than one bus network. The local Tracer system consists of seven routes that function as circulators, linking major transit hubs with shopping districts, schools, residential neighborhoods, and the downtown core. The San Joaquin Regional Transit District (SJRTD) operates two county hopper routes that connect Tracy with other communities within San Joaquin County, and it also runs a single commuter service from Tracy to the Dublin/Pleasanton BART station, extending the city’s connectivity to the Bay Area regional rail network.

Groovy was first discussed by James Strachan on his blog in August 2003. The language was submitted to the Java Community Process as JSR 241 in March 2004 and was approved by ballot. A number of releases followed between 2004 and 2006, and as the JCP standardization process progressed, the versioning approach shifted, with Groovy 1.0 released on January 2, 2007. After a sequence of betas and release candidates labeled 1.1, the final 1.1 release was issued on December 7, 2007 and subsequently renumbered to Groovy 1.5 to reflect substantial changes.

Groovy provides several mechanisms for extending classes and behavior at runtime. Prototype-style extensions are facilitated through the ExpandoMetaClass, which allows dynamic addition and modification of methods and properties on existing classes. In Groovy 2, Extension Modules introduce a pluggable system for adding new functionality to the language and its libraries without altering core sources. The language also includes Objective-C–style Categories, enabling targeted, scope-limited augmentation of classes with new methods. Additionally, the DelegatingMetaClass supports flexible method dispatch by delegating calls to alternative implementations, enabling layered and modular customization.

Italy's high-speed rail development proceeded through a series of phased openings: most of the Rome–Naples corridor entered service in December 2005, a partial opening of the Turin–Milan segment followed in February 2006, and the Milan–Bologna route began operations in December 2008. The remaining sections of the Rome–Naples, Turin–Milan, and Bologna–Florence corridors were completed by December 2009. These lines were designed to support speeds of up to 300 kilometers per hour (approximately 190 mph). Consequently, the Turin–Salerno corridor, covering about 950 kilometers, can be completed in under five hours, and the network currently operates more than 100 trains per day.

Trenitalia operates night trains within Italy under the Intercity Notte brand. The routes connect northern hubs such as Turin, Milan, and Trieste with Rome, and extend further south to Lecce and to Sicily, including Palermo and Syracuse. Onboard accommodations range from standard seating to modern couchettes and sleeping compartments.

Vancouver is a member municipality of Metro Vancouver, the regional planning and service-delivery authority that also comprises 20 other municipalities, one electoral area, and one treaty First Nation. The regional government's seat is in Burnaby. Each member municipality maintains its own local governing body, while Metro Vancouver coordinates regional services and planning across the area. Its regional responsibilities include supplying drinking water, managing wastewater and solid waste, administering regional parks, overseeing air quality and ecological health, addressing greenhouse gas emissions, and guiding regional growth and land-use planning.

Vancouver’s newspaper landscape is dominated by several major publications controlled by the Postmedia Network, including the Vancouver Sun, The Province, Vancouver Courier, Surrey Now, Burnaby Now, and Richmond News. This concentration of ownership has coincided with the emergence of alternatives and helped position Vancouver as a center for independent online media. Among these independent outlets are The Tyee, The Vancouver Observer, and NowPublic, which operate outside the traditional newspaper framework. In addition, hyperlocal online platforms such as Daily Hive and Vancouver Is Awesome focus on community events and local arts and culture, complementing the broader media ecosystem in the city.

The Spain national under-19 football team represents the Royal Spanish Football Federation in international under-19 football. The Royal Spanish Football Federation is the governing body for football in Spain. The team is the most successful under-19 national side in Europe, having won twelve continental titles.
Augai (Ancient Greek: Αὐγὰι), also known as Augae, was a coastal town of ancient Pamphylia or Cilicia. It was inhabited during Roman times. The town lay at a distance of 70 stadia from Aunesis.

Historic preservation seeks to manage the tangible aspects of a building or site through ongoing interventions designed to preserve its materials, form, and meaning. The effects of climate change, especially sea level rise and hurricanes, threaten numerous historic structures and places, and in many cases relocation is not feasible to save them in situ. Preservation doctrine and certain regulations restrict moving buildings to higher ground if such actions would compromise their historical integrity or authenticity. This combination of constraints creates a difficult, lingering dilemma for the field, which has yet to be fully resolved as practitioners weigh protection of heritage against the realities of a changing climate.

Historic preservation in Israel has been shaped by a limited regulatory framework that often leaves many heritage resources unprotected. The Antiquities Law extends protection only to buildings or artifacts dated before 1700 BCE, thereby excluding more recent periods from statutory safeguarding. This narrow scope means that much of the country's historic fabric remains outside the law's reach. The Planning and Building Law, which governs land use in Israel, has been amended several times to address preservation concerns, yet enforcement of these provisions has been weak. Consequently, a substantial number of historical sites have been destroyed or damaged. Observers have noted that the state has tended to prioritize developmental and economic objectives over preservation, influencing how heritage resources are managed and protected.

The Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO) is a United States federal statute enacted as Title IX of the Organized Crime Control Act of 1970. It was enacted as Public Law 91-452, recorded at 84 Stat. 922, and took effect on October 15, 1970. The act is codified in 18 U.S.C. chapter 96, and it governs provisions spanning 18 U.S.C. §§ 1961 through 1968.

Scott W. Rothstein, a disbarred attorney who previously served as the managing shareholder, chairman, and chief executive of the now-defunct Rothstein Rosenfeldt Adler law firm, was linked to an alleged $1.2 billion Ponzi scheme used to fund philanthropy, political contributions, firm salaries, and an extravagant lifestyle. On December 1, 2009, he turned himself in and was arrested on charges connected to the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act. Although he initially pled not guilty, he cooperated with prosecutors and pled guilty to five federal offenses on January 27, 2010. His bond was denied by U.S. Magistrate Judge Robin Rosenbaum due to concerns that he could forge documents, signaling flight risk. On June 9, 2010, Rothstein was sentenced to 50 years in a federal penitentiary in Fort Lauderdale.

The North Coast and Guanyinshan National Scenic Area is a national scenic area located in Taiwan. In Chinese, it is named 北海岸及觀音山國家風景區 and is transliterated in pinyin as Běi Hǎi'àn Jí Guānyīnshān Guójiā Fēngjǐng Qū. The designation is commonly abbreviated as North Guan.

The North Coast and Guanyinshan National Scenic Area is a protected national scenic area located on Taiwan’s northern coastline, encompassing the Guanyinshan (Guanyin Mountain) region. It encompasses a range of landscapes and cultural sites, with notable attractions including Fuji Fishing Port, Cape Fugui, Shimen Cave, the Yeliu Tofu Rock formation, and Jinshan Old Street, among other locations.
Dew Process is a record label within the Secret Sounds group, with offices located in Brisbane and Sydney. Its releases are distributed by Universal Music Australia.

Dew Process is an Australian record label noted for its traditional focus on developing domestic musical talent. In addition to nurturing local artists, the company provides promotional, marketing, and distribution services to international acts seeking to establish their music in Australia and New Zealand, facilitating entry into these markets and supporting broader engagement with audiences in the region.

Mehmed V, who reigned as the Ottoman sultan during World War I, presided over a period of intensified imperial involvement in the conflict. In November 1914 the empire entered the war, with Mehmed V publicly sanctioning a jihad against the Allied powers. In 1915 Ottoman forces repelled the Allied Gallipoli invasion and secured the capture of a large British garrison at Kut. That same year, the Committee of Union and Progress began the Armenian genocide, although Mehmed V privately disapproved of the policy, his opposition reportedly having little practical impact. The sultan died on 3 July 1918, as Ottoman forces faced defeats on the Palestinian and Macedonian fronts. With the collapse of the military front and the Arab Revolt, the Ottomans signed the Armistice of Mudros, an event that occurred during the reign of his successor Mehmed VI.

Mehmed V ascended to the Ottoman throne in the wake of the 1908 Young Turk Revolution, a period during which numerous restrictions stemming from autocratic rule were eased. The crown prince Reşad gained public support by taking part in ceremonies commemorating the restoration of the constitution and the new constitutional order. These actions, however, provoked the ire of his brother, who had previously governed with absolute authority.

Taiwan maintains export controls on dual-use goods, restricting shipments to a designated set of countries. In 2023, the government tightened limitations on the export of machine tools to Russia and Belarus. The tightening was implemented in response to reports that certain Taiwanese machine tool manufacturers were contributing to Russia's war effort.

Taiwan's defense industry shows a division between private-sector success and limited export activity by state-owned enterprises, with the T65 and T91 assault rifles exported to a broad range of countries and the T91 upper receiver marketed to the United States civilian market. State-owned arms producers have not yet exported major high-end weapons systems, although the government has become more open to pursuing such exports in the future. Private companies have achieved greater export success, exemplified by Lungteh Shipbuilding, which has supplied multiple generations of Multipurpose Assault Craft to the Philippines. In keeping with this shift, the Taiwanese government has signaled increasing interest in supplying high-end weapons systems and components to like-minded democracies.

ATN Alpha ETC Punjabi, commonly referred to as ATN Punjabi, is a Canadian Punjabi-language specialty television channel owned by Asian Television Network. The service broadcasts a mix of programming sourced from India alongside Canadian-produced content, offering a range of genres that includes feature films, news, dramas, comedies, and talk shows.

On August 30, 2013, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission approved Asian Television Network's request concerning its Punjabi-language service ATN Alpha ETC Punjabi. The decision reclassified the service from a licensed Category B specialty service to an exempted Category B third-language service, thereby altering its regulatory status while continuing to provide Punjabi programming within the Canadian broadcasting framework.

The all-time Primeira Liga table compiles the cumulative results, points, and goals of every club that has competed in Portugal's top division since the league's founding in 1934. The competition itself began in 1934, and the all-time table is current through the end of the 2024–25 season. For comparative purposes, older seasons have been recalculated using the three-points-for-a-win rule to align with the modern scoring system.

The top-tier Portuguese football league has undergone several sponsorship-based renamings, reflecting changes in its commercial partners. For the 2008–09 and 2009–10 seasons it was titled Liga Sagres, after Sagres beer sponsorship. In 2010 the Sagres arrangement was renewed and a second sponsor, ZON Multimédia, was added, producing the Liga ZON Sagres designation. After the sponsorship agreement ended, the Liga ZON Sagres name remained in use through the 2013–14 season. From 2015 to 2021 the competition adopted the Liga NOS branding. Between 2021 and 2023 it was known as Liga Portugal Bwin, and since 2023 the league has been named Liga Portugal Betclic.

Ars Technica was privately held until May 2008, when it was acquired by Condé Nast Digital, the online division of Condé Nast Publications, for $25 million as part of a package that also included two other sites; it was subsequently integrated into the Wired Digital group, which includes Wired and the former Reddit. The organization relies largely on remote work by its staff, while maintaining offices in Boston, Chicago, London, New York City, and San Francisco.

Ars Technica became the focus of controversy surrounding a blocking measure and the accompanying article, which sparked coverage on other websites and fed into a broader debate about advertising ethics. The site’s readers generally accepted Fisher’s persuasive argument. In the day following publication, about 25,000 readers who had installed the software allowed advertisements to be displayed in their browser when visiting Ars Technica. Additionally, around 200 readers subscribed to Ars Premier.

Bob Bernard's career intersected with several major corporate developments in the late 2000s, including Rolta's acquisition of the consulting division of WhittmanHart Inc. on July 29, 2008, and the subsequent rebranding of WhittmanHart, Inc. as Band Digital, Inc. on September 28, 2010.

In December 2000, Francisco Partners LP, a private equity firm, agreed to invest $150 million in the company associated with Bob Bernard, in exchange for preferred stock, with the understanding that the preferred shares, when converted, would represent a 32 percent ownership stake in the company.

ISO 4031 was a former international standard published in 1978 by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). It defined how local time offsets, or time zones, should be represented. The standard was superseded by ISO 8601, which since 1988 has established the accepted formats for expressing local time differentials; as a consequence, ISO 4031 is no longer in use.

Estimation serves as a foundational element for sound project planning in project management. It is applied in both engineering and software development contexts, where forecasting outcomes is essential. A variety of procedures and methodologies have been developed to assist managers in producing more precise estimates.

The development of the subject has been notably advanced by the work of Cartan and Serre. Within the framework of sheaf cohomology, the domain of holomorphy is interpreted through the theory of Stein manifolds, which play a central role in understanding where holomorphic functions can be extended. Beyond Stein spaces, the domain of holomorphy is studied in a broader class of complex manifolds. Moreover, the concept has been generalized to complex analytic spaces, extending its reach to more singular and general geometric contexts.

Within the theory of several complex variables, a complete Reinhardt domain D is star-shaped with respect to its centre a, and this geometric property implies that D is simply connected. Moreover, in the particular case where the complete Reinhardt domain is associated with the boundary line, there exists a method to prove Cauchy's integral theorem without resorting to the Jordan curve theorem.

PDF/UA is a specification intended for developers who create, render, or manage PDF documents. It addresses the accessibility needs of individuals with disabilities who rely on assistive technologies to access electronic content. Conforming PDF/UA files are designed to provide equal access to information for both readers and assistive technologies, within the limitations of the PDF format.

Between 2012 and 2013, the PDF Association organized a series of educational seminars on PDF/UA across Europe, North America, and Australia. The organization also issued a book titled PDF/UA in a Nutshell in both English and German, and released an informational brochure available in English and German.

In continuous distillation, packing material may substitute for trays in a distillation column. Packing tends to produce a smaller pressure drop across the column, which is advantageous when the process operates under vacuum. When packing is employed, design begins with estimating the number of theoretical equilibrium stages. The next step is to determine the height equivalent to a theoretical plate (HETP), which relates the stage count to physical height. The total height of the packing section is obtained by multiplying the number of theoretical stages by the HETP.

Continuous distillation in petroleum refining uses a fractionating column to separate crude oil into a series of product streams, each with its own characteristic boiling range. The naphtha fraction comprises a broad mixture of hydrocarbons and typically boils from about 35 °C to 200 °C. In the column, adjacent cuts are assigned distinct boiling ranges, though the boundaries are not perfectly sharp and consequently overlap between neighboring fractions. The kerosene (jet fuel) cut is commonly withdrawn from the side of the column and has a boiling interval of roughly 150 °C to 270 °C, while the diesel oil cut boils in the vicinity of 180 °C to 315 °C. Beyond these lighter fractions, heavier fuel oil fractions are drawn, and the process ends with the bottoms product, both of which exhibit wide and variable boiling ranges. All of these cuts undergo further processing in subsequent refining steps to upgrade their properties.

Within the Order of Saint-Charles, the rank of Officer is indicated by a badge worn on a chest ribbon that bears a rosette. The officer's cross features a laurel wreath that is thinner than the wreath surrounding the cross worn by Knights of the order.

Within the Order of Saint-Charles, the rank of Grand Officer is signified by the wearing of both a badge and a star. The order’s star is crafted in silver. The badge is worn on a chest ribbon featuring a rosette, or alternatively on a bow. The star is worn on the right side of the chest.

Bunga Jelitha Ibrani, born on 6 September 1991, is an Indonesian actress and model who rose to prominence after winning the Supermodel International title in 2011. She later claimed the Puteri Indonesia crown in 2017, earning the right to represent Indonesia at Miss Universe 2017. At the international pageant, she did not advance to the Top 16, but she was awarded Miss Photogenic.
Bunga Jelitha married Syamsir Alam, an Indonesian professional footballer who plays as a forward for Liga 2 club RANS Cilegon, on 21 March 2020. They welcomed a daughter on 6 January 2021.

By the end of 1985, Jack Roth announced the sale of KONO and its associated station KITY to Duffy Broadcasting, a Dallas-based company, marking the end of Roth family ownership of KONO which had persisted since the station’s founding. Two years later, Duffy entered into a deal with Booth American that culminated in the creation of Genesis Broadcasting.

KONO (AM) entered the early 1980s with a Top 40 lineup that emphasized recurrent hits and carried a softer sound than the 1970s era. However, AM Top 40 outlets were losing audiences to FM competitors, signaling a decline in KONO’s status as a premier contemporary hits station. The station subsequently began shifting toward a gold-based Adult Contemporary direction. Ultimately, the Top 40 format was moved to its sister station KITY, replacing the AC format on that station.

The ISO 9000 family comprises international standards for quality management systems, with ISO 9001 defining the requirements for an organization’s quality management system and ISO 9000 and ISO 9004 providing foundational guidance. The evidence on whether adoption of ISO 9000 directly enhances quality remains uncertain, and questions persist about the kinds and levels of resources necessary to implement and sustain an effective system. Certification costs are a frequent concern, including initial implementation expenditures and ongoing audit and surveillance fees, as well as the broader financial impact of meeting and maintaining compliance. In addition, organizations may face an increase in bureaucratic processes and administrative overhead associated with documentation, audits, and continual conformity assessments. There is also a potential reputational risk if certification is pursued but subsequently withdrawn or found lacking, which can tarnish a company’s image. Critics such as John Seddon contend that ISO 9001 prioritizes specification, control, and procedural compliance over deeper understanding and ongoing improvement, a perspective that informs ongoing debates about the standard’s utility in promoting genuine organizational learning.

In some industries, a sizable share of firms already hold ISO 9000 certification, resulting in a crowded field of certified competitors. This saturation can lead to the belief that the competitive advantage traditionally gained through certification, or through recertification, is diminished. The debate within discussions of the ISO 9000 family therefore addresses how market conditions, certification prevalence, and the quality management practices of certified organizations shape the value and strategic utility of ISO 9000 certification.

Naval artillery relies on a firing solution, a set of aiming instructions used to direct the ship's guns. This solution is transmitted to the gun turrets so they can lay the weapons on the correct bearing and elevation. If a round misses the target, an observer records how far off it landed and in which direction. The miss data are then fed back into the ship's computer along with any updated information. A new shot is attempted using the revised data, enabling iterative refinement of the aim.

John Ericsson independently conceived the concept of a rotating gun turret in the United States, though his design was technologically inferior to Coles' turret. In 1861 he designed the ironclad USS Monitor, whose most distinctive feature was a large cylindrical gun turret mounted amidships above the low-freeboard upper hull, often described as a raft. The turret projected well beyond the sides of the lower hull, enabling the guns to be aimed in multiple directions while presenting a reduced target to enemy fire. A small armored pilot house was fitted on the upper deck toward the bow, a placement that prevented firing straight ahead. One of Ericsson's principal aims was to present the smallest possible target to enemy gunfire.

High modernism in the Soviet Union manifested through architectural reform and large-scale infrastructure initiatives. In the Khrushchev era, the country pursued a widespread program of housing construction, including the mass production of Khrushchyovka apartments. These dwellings were assembled from factory-made components and designed to be functional, rapid to build, and affordable. Alongside housing, the USSR invested heavily in scientific facilities, hydroelectric dam projects, and expanded transportation networks. Collectively, these efforts aimed to demonstrate the efficacy of socialist planning and the forward momentum of modernization.

High modernism is not confined to the modern era; its early manifestations appear in urban planning, where systematic approaches to design emerged well before later intellectual movements. In the fifth century BCE, Hippodamus advanced a grid-based layout as a method of city planning. He applied this plan in the construction of Piraeus, the port of Athens. The grid plan of Piraeus has remained largely unchanged to the present day, illustrating how early planning concepts anticipated later high-modernist tendencies.

Belief is described in diverse ways across philosophy of mind and epistemology. For example, Jerry Fodor treats beliefs as representational states that encode how the world could be, while Richard M. Chisholm characterizes beliefs as dispositions to act as if certain propositions are true. Other theorists, including Daniel Dennett and Donald Davidson, view belief as part of interpretive schemes that people use to make sense of others’ actions. Hilary Putnam, by contrast, describes belief as mental states that perform a particular cognitive function. Some eliminativist perspectives, notably associated with Paul Churchland, argue that there may be no natural phenomenon corresponding to the folk concept of belief. In formal epistemology, many scholars advocate replacing a binary notion of belief with probabilistic credence, i.e., degrees of belief.

Belief is the collective perception of fundamental truths that govern behavior within a group or society. When these beliefs are widely accepted and shared by members of a social system, they tend to persist and resist alteration over time. In particular, strong convictions regarding determinant factors such as security, survival, or honor can drive a social entity to adopt and adhere to prevailing rules and norms.

On 29 October 2008, the United States Navy announced that the destroyer DDG-1001 would be named in honor of Michael A. Monsoor. DDG-1001 is a Zumwalt-class destroyer. Monsoor held the rank of Master-at-Arms Second Class. He was the second Navy SEAL to receive the Medal of Honor for actions during the Battle of Ramadi in 2006, part of the Iraq War. He sacrificed himself by falling on a grenade to protect his SEAL teammates.

On 16 April 2012, Secretary of the Navy Ray Mabus announced that the DDG-1002, a Zumwalt-class guided-missile destroyer, would be named in honor of Lyndon B. Johnson. Johnson was a former naval officer who later served as President of the United States.

Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation (Sony DADC) is a major producer of compact discs in the United States, manufacturing the majority of CDs sold domestically. In November 2008, Sony DADC acquired Glenayre Technologies’ American disc-manufacturing capabilities, which had previously produced discs for Universal Music Group. In the summer of 2009, the company assumed the physical distribution of EMI's North American operations. As a consequence, WEA became the only major label whose discs were not manufactured by Sony DADC, with WEA discs instead produced by the former WEA Manufacturing operations that were sold to Cinram.

Sony Digital Audio Disc Corporation, headquartered in Terre Haute, Indiana, opened on May 2, 1983. It became the United States’ first CD manufacturing facility and released its inaugural compact disc in September 1984, Bruce Springsteen’s Born in the U.S.A. album. The Terre Haute plant continues to serve as Sony DADC’s principal CD manufacturing facility and functions as the company’s central research and development center for optical-disc technologies.

An arrangement in chamber music refers to a group of instrumentalists in which each musician performs a distinct part rather than playing in unison. When the ensemble comprises only violin-family string instruments, its designation corresponds to the number of players: a string trio for three players, a string quartet for four, and a string quintet for five, with the pattern continuing for larger sizes.

An arrangement is a reworking or adaptation of an existing musical work, in which the material of the original is reinterpreted for a new context. It may involve reharmonizing chords, paraphrasing melodic lines, changing textures through different instrumental or vocal forces, and developing the form beyond the source. Unlike orchestration, which concerns assigning the existing notes to specific instruments for performance, arranging encompasses a broader set of compositional tasks. Arranging can introduce new techniques such as additional thematic material for introductions, transitions, modulations, and codas, thereby imparting fresh character and variety to the familiar melody. The central aim is to provide musical variety to an existing melody while preserving its recognizable identity. In jazz, a memorized, unwritten arrangement of a new or previously performed piece is known as a head arrangement.

UEFA Euro 2004 (video game)'s soundtrack comprises rock-based tracks, a deliberate choice reflecting the period's notable resurgence of rock music across Europe and intended to align the audio with prevailing regional trends.

UEFA Euro 2004 uses a revised graphics engine derived from FIFA 2004, refined to deliver improved visuals and performance. The game introduces a wide array of new gameplay features and several new game modes, expanding the interactive possibilities for players. In addition, it broadens features and modes across both the UEFA Euro and FIFA series, marking a cross-series enhancement that extends the scope of both franchises.

Infant respiratory distress syndrome (IRDS) typically develops shortly after birth and is characterized by tachypnea, defined as a respiratory rate exceeding 60 breaths per minute, tachycardia, chest wall retractions, expiratory grunting, nasal flaring, and cyanosis that becomes evident during breathing efforts.

Infant respiratory distress syndrome arises from an inadequate production of pulmonary surfactant during lung development. Surfactant normally lowers surface tension within the fluid lining the terminal air spaces, preventing their collapse as the lungs expand and contract during breathing. In some newborns, insulin produced by the infant inhibits surfactant synthesis, a factor that particularly increases risk in infants of diabetic mothers who exhibit neonatal hyperinsulinemia.

The 2025–26 Serbian SuperLiga represents the twentieth edition of Serbia’s top-tier football competition. The campaign began on 19 July 2025. Red Star Belgrade entered as the defending champions. Radnik and Javor-Matis were promoted to the top flight for the season, joining the league for 2025–26.

The 2025–26 Serbian SuperLiga will contest 16 clubs, comprising the top 14 finishers from the previous season and two clubs promoted from the Serbian First League. The promoted sides are Radnik and Javor-Matis, returning to the top flight after a one-year absence. They replace Tekstilac Odžaci and Jedinstvo Ub, who were relegated after a single season at the highest level.

Following the stampede at a Bangui school, President Faustin-Archange Touadéra announced a three-day period of national mourning from 27 to 29 June. In the aftermath, authorities arranged free medical care for 280 injured students. Education Minister Aurélien-Simplice Zingas offered condolences and announced the suspension of further exams. When government officials reached the scene, locals threw objects at them, accusing the authorities of negligence. Gédéon Cyr Ngaïssé, head of the parents’ association, condemned the incident, cited poor maintenance, and called for a formal investigation. The opposition coalition, the Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution, also criticized the incident and blamed authorities for irresponsibility. International condolences were offered by several governments, including Turkey.

The 2025 Bangui school stampede occurred when an explosion during restoration work on power to a malfunctioning electrical transformer on the ground floor of the main building generated noise and smoke that unsettled students who were taking history and geography examinations. Panic prompted the crowd to flee toward a small door on the upper floors, and a large number of casualties occurred during the ensuing stampede, including sixteen girls who died at the scene; others died later in hospital. Some students died after jumping from the building to escape. Victims were transported by ambulance, pickup trucks, and motorbikes, a response that overwhelmed local hospitals. Abel Assaye, Director General of the Community Hospital, reported that eighty-five patients were treated and fifteen had died, including two pregnant women.

In aviation terminology, a rush bag refers to luggage that has either missed its scheduled flight or has been recovered as lost property. Such bags are sent and transported unaccompanied, without the owner present, as part of dedicated baggage-handling procedures. The primary objective of this process is to ensure the bag is promptly reunited with its rightful owner through the airline’s tracking and delivery systems.

John Michael Lyons of Moncton, New Brunswick, received a patent for the first separable coupon ticket on June 5, 1882. The ticket displayed the issuing station, the destination, and a consecutive reference number to identify the journey. It was designed in two parts: a lower half that remained with the passenger and an upper half that featured a top hole. The upper portion was inserted into a brass sleeve and secured to luggage by a strap, forming an early method of tagging baggage for identification and tracking.

Paul Thomas Anderson’s films are frequently set in the San Fernando Valley and center on realistically flawed, desperate characters. Core themes include dysfunctional families, alienation, surrogate families, regret, loneliness, destiny, forgiveness, and the ghosts of the past that linger across his work. Repetition serves as a formal device to reinforce motifs, with a recurring refrain of inaction appearing in Boogie Nights, Magnolia, Punch-Drunk Love, and The Master to explore questions of responsibility and denial. Visually, his style is bold and dynamic, marked by moving camera work, steadicam long takes, a pronounced use of music, and multilayered audiovisual imagery. Interwoven with these elements are frequent references to the Book of Exodus, whether explicit or implicit; instances include a frog motif alluding to Exodus 8:2 in Magnolia and the plague of blood informing There Will Be Blood, drawn from Exodus 7:19.

Following Boogie Nights, New Line Cinema granted Paul Thomas Anderson creative control over his next project, enabling him to shape the film’s development. He initially sought to make a small, intimate movie, but the screenplay grew in scope, ultimately becoming Magnolia, a 1999 ensemble drama set in the San Fernando Valley that intertwines the stories of multiple characters. The film drew inspiration from Aimee Mann’s music, and Mann contributed songs to the soundtrack. Magnolia received three nominations at the 72nd Academy Awards—Best Supporting Actor for Tom Cruise, Best Original Song for Save Me, and Best Original Screenplay. After its release, Anderson would later describe Magnolia as, in his view, the best film he would ever make.

United States Army Forces Command (FORSCOM) is the largest command of the United States Army, responsible for providing land forces to the Department of Defense's unified combatant commands. Its headquarters are located at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The command comprises more than 750,000 personnel drawn from the active Army, the U.S. Army Reserve, and the Army National Guard. FORSCOM was established on July 1, 1973, as the successor to the Continental Army Command (CONARC), which had supplanted the Army Field Forces and the Army Ground Forces.

United States Army Forces Command (FORSCOM) maintains formations and units at fifteen installations. The National Training Center is located at Fort Irwin, California, and the Joint Readiness Training Center is located at Fort Polk, Louisiana.

VP6 is a video compression technology that forms part of On2 Technologies' On2 Video Codec portfolio. In April 2005, On2 licensed its On2 Video Codec, including the VP6 and VP7 profiles, for use with Macromedia Flash. A few months later, in August 2005, Macromedia announced that VP6 would serve as the flagship codec for video playback in the forthcoming Flash Player 8.

VP6 is part of the VP family of video compression codecs developed by On2 Technologies, a lineage that was followed by later iterations such as VP7, VP8, and VP9. Google subsequently acquired On2 Technologies, and VP8 was released under an open-source license. By contrast, earlier versions such as VP6 remain unsupported.

Lastminute.com disclosed its first-quarter results on 6 May 2000, at a time when its share price was rising. The company processed transactions totaling £7.16 million, representing a 68% increase over the previous period. Investments during the period included a refreshed version of the website and expansion into international markets. Despite the higher level of activity, pre-tax losses increased from £6 million to £11 million. The market responded positively to the results, with the shares finishing the day up 8p at 245p. About two weeks later, however, the stock closed at 141p amid renewed concerns in the dotcom sector following the liquidation of boo.com.

In December 2017, the Lastminute.com Group expanded its footprint in Germany by acquiring Comvel GmbH, a Munich-based company founded in 2004. Comvel GmbH operates the travel portal Weg.de, which is regarded as one of Germany’s best-known online travel sites. Weg.de had been a wholly owned subsidiary of the ProSiebenSat.1 Group since January 2014. The site provides a full range of travel options, with a primary emphasis on package holidays and all-inclusive vacations.

Revolver, released in August 1966 about a week before the Beatles embarked on their final tour, signaled an artistic advance for the group with more sophisticated songwriting, expanded studio experimentation, and a broader stylistic range that encompassed classical string arrangements as well as psychedelic influences. The album’s cover, by Klaus Voormann—an old Hamburg friend—features a monochrome Aubrey Beardsley–style collage and line-drawing caricature of the band. It was preceded by the single Paperback Writer, backed by Rain. Short promotional films were produced for both tracks, which Saul Austerlitz has described as among the first genuine music videos; these clips were shown on The Ed Sullivan Show and Top of the Pops in June.

Magical Mystery Tour, broadcast on Boxing Day, drew about 15 million viewers and was largely directed by Paul McCartney. It marked the Beatles' first significant critical setback in the United Kingdom, as major newspapers offered harsh assessments: the Daily Express criticized it as low-quality and poorly conceived, the Daily Mail branded it as an act of inflated vanity, and The Guardian described it as a fantastical morality drama that exposed the audience's pretensions, warmth, and foolishness. Gould characterized the work as unpolished footage depicting people boarding, alighting, and riding a bus. Despite the large audience, the negative press response led American television networks to lose interest in broadcasting the film.

Hugo Chávez initiated a series of social reforms in Venezuela that is commonly described as the Bolivarian Revolution. The ideological framework of this approach drew more on the theories of István Mészáros, Michael Lebowitz, and Marta Harnecker than on Heinz Dieterich, shaping its critique of capitalism and its emphasis on participatory social change. Marta Harnecker served as Chávez’s adviser from 2004 to 2011, contributing to policy discussions and political education. The designation Bolivarian Revolution derives from the 19th-century liberator Simón Bolívar and stands as a contemporary manifestation of Bolivarianism.

Socialism of the 21st century is a contemporary interpretation of socialist principles promoted by Heinz Dieterich and taken up by some Latin American leaders. Dieterich (1996) argued that both laissez-faire capitalism and 20th‑century socialist models had failed to address fundamental problems, including poverty, hunger, the exploitation of labor, economic oppression, sexism, racism, the destruction of natural resources, and a lack of genuine democracy. The framework incorporates democratic socialist elements while also bearing similarities to Marxist revisionism.

The accession of Elizabeth II in 1952 sparked controversy in Scotland, where there had never been a monarch named Elizabeth II, raising questions about the appropriate regnal number. Winston Churchill proposed applying the higher regnal number derived from either the Scottish or English count, aligning with the pattern set by the Acts of Union of 1707. In the years following the Union, monarchs either bore a higher English regnal number (as with William IV, Edward VII, and Edward VIII) or used names that had not been used since before the Union (such as George and Victoria). The dispute extended into practical symbols, as new Royal Mail post boxes in Scotland bearing EIIR were vandalised; to avoid further problems, boxes and Royal Mail vehicles in Scotland bore only the Crown of Scotland. MacCormick v. Lord Advocate (1953 SC 396) challenged the Queen’s right to style herself Elizabeth II in Scotland on the grounds that it breached the Act of Union. The case was dismissed: the pursuers had no title to sue the Crown, and the numbering of monarchs is regarded as part of the royal prerogative not governed by the Act of Union.

Temple names (miào hào) were conferred on Chinese sovereigns after death to honor ancestors and have been in use since the Shang dynasty. They typically consist of two or three characters, with the final character being either zǔ (祖, “progenitor”) or zōng (宗, “ancestor”). Posthumous names (shì hào) likewise began to be granted after death, a practice that became common from the Zhou dynasty onward. These posthumous names are adjectives intended to reflect a ruler’s life, accomplishments, and moral qualities (or lack thereof). Neither temple names nor posthumous names function as true regnal names, as both are posthumous titles rather than actual names used during a ruler’s reign. Due to Chinese influence, Korea and Vietnam adopted both temple and posthumous naming conventions, whereas Japan incorporated posthumous names only.

The Oregon Treaty of 1818 established a boundary between the United States and Britain along the 49th parallel north, extending from the Lake of the Woods area to the Rocky Mountains. West of the mountains, the region was referred to by Americans as the Oregon Country and by the British as the Columbia District of the Hudson's Bay Company, encompassing the southern portion of the New Caledonia fur district. The agreement provided for ten years of joint occupation of the land, with both nations allowed to claim territory and guaranteed freedom of navigation throughout the region.

Under the Oregon Treaty, Puget's Sound Agricultural Company, a subsidiary of the Hudson's Bay Company, retained its rights to property located north of the Columbia River, and the agreement provided that the company would be compensated for any properties surrendered if required by the United States.

ATSC standards, in conjunction with MPEG-2, permit progressive frames to be encoded within an interlaced broadcast sequence such as 1080i60. Upon MPEG-2 decoding, 1080i60 yields sixty 540-line fields per second. For prime-time programming, these sixty fields can be transmitted as twenty-four progressive frames per second (1080p24). The MPEG-2 metadata guides the decoder to interlace these fields and to apply a 3:2 pulldown prior to display, a process commonly referred to as soft telecine.

ATSC standards define the digital television system used in North America and other regions, outlining technical specifications for video, audio, and data transmission. The audio component includes support for 5.1-channel surround sound through Dolby Digital (AC-3) encoding. In addition, the standards support a range of auxiliary datacasting services, enabling supplementary data broadcasts alongside conventional programming.

The dholak is a two-headed hand drum and folk percussion instrument of South Asian origin. It typically measures 16 to 24 inches in length and features two drumheads of different sizes: a smaller treble head about 5.5 to 8 inches in diameter and a larger bass head around 7.5 to 10 inches, enabling a blend of high and low notes. This dual-head design permits a combination of bass and treble tones within a single instrument. The shell is commonly made from woods such as sheesham or mango, and the larger head bears masala—a tar-clay-sand mixture—that lowers its pitch. The smaller head is usually struck with the dominant hand, while the larger head is played with the weaker hand, producing a complementary playing style. Tuning options include nuts and bolts or rope and steel rings, with regional variations in practice: the Indian subcontinent typically uses one set of rings for the treble head, whereas Caribbean communities in Trinidad, Guyana, and Suriname employ hook screws to tune both treble and bass heads. The dholak is employed across a wide range of genres, including qawwali, kirtan, bhajan, bhangra, chutney, baithak gana, Hindi cinema music, lokgeet, and both Hindustani and Carnatic classical styles, as well as Trinidadian and Guyanese taan. Playing positions vary from resting on the lap or standing to being pressed down with one knee while seated on the floor.

Playing techniques for the dholak differ by region, with notable distinctions between Punjab and Rajasthan. In Punjab, performers typically wear an iron ring on the thumb, a setup that contributes to a distinctive rim articulation often described as a “chak” sound. By contrast, Rajasthan style generally relies on the use of all fingers to produce its strokes.

Ambrosius Brueghel's father died when he was seven years old, and he was subsequently placed under the guardianship of the painters Hendrick van Balen, Cornelis Schut, and Pieter de Jode the Elder. Van Balen fostered his artistic training, while it is possible that Brueghel also trained with his brother Jan Brueghel the Elder.

Ambrosius Brueghel joined the Antwerp Guild of Saint Luke in 1645, and four years later became a member of the chamber of rhetoric De Violieren in 1649. On 21 February 1649 he married Anna Clara van Triest, who came from a well-to-do family; the couple had four children. Brueghel was held in high esteem within his community and served as wijkmeester, or warden, of his district. In 1650 he visited his brother Jan in Paris.

Hexachloroplatinic acid is regarded as the most important platinum compound and serves as a key precursor for a wide range of other platinum compounds. In its own right, hexachloroplatinic acid has applications in photography, zinc etching, indelible ink, plating, mirrors, porcelain coloration, and as a catalyst.

Within modern temperature metrology, the Standard Platinum Resistance Thermometer (SPRT) is one of four thermometer types used to realize the International Temperature Scale of 1990 (ITS-90), which serves as the international calibration standard for temperature measurements. An SPRT relies on a resistance element fabricated from pure platinum. The platinum wire used in SPRTs is produced by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) from bar stock with a purity of 99.999%. Platinum resistance thermometers have broad industrial applications in addition to laboratory use, and standardized specifications for PRTs are set forth in the ASTM E1137 and IEC 60751 standards.

Illinois is a state in the Midwestern United States. It borders Lake Michigan to the northeast, the Mississippi River to the west, and the Wabash and Ohio rivers to the south. It has the fifth-largest gross domestic product among the fifty states and the sixth-largest population, while ranking twenty-fifth in land area. The capital is Springfield, located near the center of the state, and the largest city is Chicago, situated in the northeastern part.

During the process of Illinois’s admission to statehood, the northern boundary was revised twice. The boundary proposed by the original Northwest Ordinance would have left Illinois without any Lake Michigan shoreline. Indiana, by contrast, received a ten-mile northern extension to secure a usable lakefront, a concession that shaped Illinois’s initial statehood bill. When the bill to admit Illinois was introduced on January 23, 1818, the northern boundary was set at the same latitude as Indiana’s—ten miles north of Lake Michigan’s southern tip. Illinois’ delegate Nathaniel Pope pressed to move the line farther north, and Congress amended the measure to place the border at 42°30′ N, about 51 miles north of Indiana’s northern limit. The adjustment added roughly 8,500 square miles (about 22,000 square kilometers) to Illinois, including the Galena lead mining region, and extended its Lake Michigan shoreline by nearly fifty miles along with the Chicago River. Pope and others also envisioned a canal linking the Chicago and Illinois rivers to connect the Great Lakes to the Mississippi River system.

Fruit fool is a traditional English dessert in which puréed stewed fruit is folded into a sweet custard, with gooseberries commonly cited as the classical example. In contemporary preparations, the custard is frequently substituted with whipped cream, yielding a lighter, mousse-like texture. Some recipes include a floral flavoring, such as rose water, to enhance the aroma.

Fruit fool, in this entry, refers to a traditional Norfolk dessert prepared as a layered version of a fruit fool. The recipe centers on thick sweet cream seasoned with mace and a whole cinnamon stick, enriched with the yolks of five to six eggs, and combined with fine manchet bread, sliced dates, sugar, and an assortment of red and white biscuits. The method involves boiling the cream with the spices in a clean skillet, then removing it from heat, discarding the spices, and stirring in dissolved egg yolks to thicken the mixture. As it thickens, slices of manchet bread are arranged in a dish, the warm cream is poured over, and additional bread is added in successive layers until the dish is full. For presentation, the edge is trimmed with carved sippets, the top is garnished with sliced dates, dusted with sugar, and decorated with the red and white biscuits.

A family relations certificate enumerates the individual and their immediate relatives, including parents, spouse, and children. When the certificate includes more than one person with the same name, distinguishing individuals becomes difficult. To mitigate this ambiguity, an individual is not allowed to bear a name that already appears on their parent's family relations certificate. Consequently, a child cannot carry a name identical to those of their parents or grandparents.

South Korea regulates Hanja usage in personal names under Article 37 of the Regulations on Registration of Family Relations, which requires that Hanja in names come from an approved restricted list. Hanja not on the list must be represented in Hangul in the family relations register. In March 1991, the Supreme Court published the List of Hanja for Use in Personal Names (인명용 한자표), comprising 2,854 characters and 61 variant forms, which took effect on 1 April 1991. The list has been expanded on several occasions, with the latest update in 2022. Currently, more than 8,000 Hanja are permitted in South Korean names (including the basic set), in addition to a small number of variant forms. The use of an official list is analogous to Japan's jinmeiyō kanji, though the characters do not completely coincide.

The Macabre is a medieval cycle of wall paintings that originated at Klingenthal, a nunnery in Little Basel, dating to the early 14th century. In the mid-15th century, the work was relocated to the churchyard of the Predigerkloster in Basel. It underwent restoration in 1568, probably under the direction of Hans Kluber. The wall on which it was painted collapsed in 1805, leaving only fragments. Today, only the drawings associated with the series remain.

The macabre motif persisted in art and music beyond the medieval period. In classical music, Franz Schubert's Death and the Maiden, a string quartet completed in 1824, embodies the ongoing preoccupation with mortality. Subsequently, Camille Saint-Saëns's Danse macabre, Op. 40, completed in 1847, offered another musical treatment of death as a haunting, dance-like figure. In cinema, the 1957 Bergman film The Seventh Seal presents a personified Death, illustrating the continued presence of macabre themes on screen. Together, these examples demonstrate how the macabre has endured as a subject across diverse media, reflecting enduring concerns with mortality, fate, and the uncanny.

Following the fourth encounter in his series with Bobby Chacon, Rafael Limón never again challenged for a world title, and he went on to lose the majority of his fights in the years that followed. In the post-series period, his opponents included Héctor Camacho, Julio César Chávez, Rolando Navarrete (in a rematch of their 1982 bout, which Limón had won), and Roger Mayweather. Limón currently resides in Mexico.

Rafael Limón vs. Bobby Chacon IV is framed as the final chapter of the Chacon–Limón rivalry, with commentators portraying the bout as bringing an end to the lingering tension between the two fighters. In the broader arc of Chacon’s career, he had previously been knocked out by Mancini in the third round, a result that contextualizes the culmination of their rivalry and reinforces the view that the Limón–Chacon series had reached its conclusion.

Car boot sales in the United Kingdom are a form of informal second-hand commerce in which buyers and sellers gather on a large field to exchange goods. Sellers drive their vehicles onto the site and display items from the boot, opening the trunk to reveal merchandise for browsing and sale. The items offered range from used goods to newer items, and sales occur directly from the car boot, with buyers selecting items from the trunk area.

Second-hand shops operate within a long-standing and dynamic secondary market for particular categories of goods, which has sustained permanent storefronts devoted to items such as antiques and used books. In the twenty-first century, reuse-focused social movements—exemplified by sustainable fashion—have broadened the economic viability of reselling a wider range of goods, giving rise to specialized stores that concentrate on these items. This evolution reflects a broader shift toward alternative consumption practices and positions reuse as a practical, environmentally conscious model within modern retail.

Guillaume de l'Isle was admitted to the French Académie Royale des Sciences at age twenty-seven, signing maps as "Géographe de l’Académie." Five years later he relocated to the Quai de l’Horloge in Paris, a publishing hub where his business prospered. In 1718 he was awarded the title Premier Géographe du Roi and was appointed to teach geography to the Dauphin (Louis XIV’s son) with a salary. Historian Mary Sponberg Pedley notes that established authority in geography can endure for generations. Delisle's accomplishments surpassed those of his father. He produced maps of European countries and regions including Italy, Spain, Germany, Great Britain, Poland, and the Duchy of Burgundy, and he also contributed to the empire's territorial claims in Africa and the Americas.

Guillaume de L'Isle, a prominent French cartographer of the early 18th century, produced the 1703 Carte du Canada ou de la Nouvelle France, a work widely praised for its accurate rendering of Canada’s latitude and longitude. Although he never visited the New World, Delisle devoted seven years to extensive research, drawing on Jesuit Relations and leveraging his connections with missionaries and explorers to gather reliable landscape information. He also employed eclipse calculations to fix Quebec's longitude with a precision previously achieved only by estimation. The map’s fusion of careful scholarship and mathematical technique established it as a standard reference for later cartography. Its publication underscored French capabilities in New France during the early eighteenth century and represented an early shift toward a dispassionate, scientific style of mapmaking, in contrast to the more impressionistic maps of earlier eras.

Since the abolition of the historic provinces in 2010, Finland's mainland state administration is organized around six regional state administrative agencies (aluehallintovirasto, AVI) and fifteen Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment (ELY-centres). The AVI agencies serve as the principal link between the central government and local authorities, with competence in policing, fire and rescue services, emergency preparedness, basic public services, environmental permitting and enforcement, and occupational health and safety regulation. The ELY-centres are tasked with implementing national labor and industrial policies, delivering employment and immigration services, and promoting culture, while also maintaining highways and other transport networks and infrastructure. They are also responsible for protecting, monitoring and managing the environment, land use, and water resources.

Finland conducts European Parliament elections on a five-year cycle, in parallel with its presidential and parliamentary elections. Local governance elections, by contrast, occur every four years and are held simultaneously across all municipalities.

The Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan occupies a strategic position at the intersection of major north–south inland routes and coastal shipping lanes, with canal connections extending to the Yangtze River inland waterway to the north. The port complex consists of three principal components: Beilun, acting as the seaport, Zhenhai at the estuary, and the older Ningbo harbor functioning as an inland river port.

The Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan is the world's busiest port by cargo tonnage. It lies along the East China Sea coast in Zhejiang province, spanning the cities of Ningbo and Zhoushan at the southeast end of Hangzhou Bay, opposite the Shanghai municipality across the bay. In 2015, the port handled 888.96 million tonnes of cargo.

PASCAL is a scientific bibliographic database maintained by INIST, a unit of the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS). It covers core literature in science, technology, and medicine, with a particular emphasis on European publications.

As of 2012, PASCAL (database) contained more than 17 million records, with approximately 90 percent of these records consisting of author abstracts. Its coverage spans from 1973 to 2012, reflecting long-term bibliographic indexing. The source material is dominated by journals, which account for about 88 percent across 3,085 international titles, followed by conference proceedings at 9 percent, while dissertations, books, patents, and other reports together make up the remaining 3 percent.

Opinio juris sive necessitatis denotes the mental belief by a state actor that a particular practice is legally mandated by international law. Establishing this state of mind is notoriously difficult, since it requires demonstrating that the rule is observed out of a sense of legal obligation rather than for mere expedience or habit. To identify opinio juris, a range of evidentiary sources is consulted, with diplomatic correspondence and official government policy statements, including press releases, serving as important indicators. The opinions of legal advisers and the content of official manuals addressing legal questions are also taken into account, as are legislation, national and international judicial decisions, and legal briefs endorsed by the state. Moreover, a consistent pattern of treaty ratifications containing the same obligations can bolster the inference of obligations under international law. United Nations resolutions and declarations, among other sources, are used to corroborate the presence of opinio juris in practice.

Opinio juris sive necessitatis denotes the belief that a state’s conduct is legally obliged. The concept is most coherent when applied to practices that already constitute customary international law, where states’ belief in legal obligation supports the existence of the norm. However, the approach encounters difficulties with new or evolving customary rules, where the asserted obligation has not yet crystallized. When a practice is not currently governed by customary international law, questioning a state's belief about the legality of that practice is inappropriate. In particular, asking whether the practice believed it complied with a law that does not yet exist is illogical and can obscure the examination of emerging norms.

In 1920, La Nación's Sunday literary supplement was placed under the direction of Arturo Cancela, described as a nationalist Catholic. The newspaper published articles authored by Benito Mussolini, and it also featured writings by Leon Trotsky, who at the time was fleeing from Stalinist authorities.

La Nación, an Argentine daily newspaper, initially endorsed the 1930 coup d'état led by José Félix Uriburu. Subsequently, it condemned the electoral fraud that dominated Argentina from 1931 to 1943, during the Infamous Decade.

On 17 February, General Wenck, who commanded the offensive, sustained serious injuries in a car accident. He had taken over driving from a driver who had been awake for forty-eight hours and then fell asleep at the wheel. Hans Krebs was appointed to replace Wenck, but by that time the initiative had already been lost. Later that day, Zhukov launched a counter-attack with the 3rd Shock Army, redeployed from the area of Jastrow, and the German offensive stalled as a result.

Operation Solstice opened with a general assault the following day. The III SS Panzer Corps broadened the central corridor toward Arnswalde, pushing parts of the Soviet front back by about 8–12 kilometers. The XXXIX Panzer Corps, however, failed to reach Plöne Lake due to resistance from the Soviet 2nd Guards Tank Army, stalling roughly 70 kilometers from Küstrin. Nevertheless, XXXIX Panzer Corps drove the Soviets out of Sallenthin and Muscherin, regained control of land on the eastern shore of Lake Madü, and recaptured Pyritz. Gruppe Munzel advanced about 4 kilometers to Liebenow, while the III SS Panzer Corps advanced about 1 kilometer to Reetz. German Tiger II tanks destroyed Soviet tanks and anti-tank guns, though they incurred losses themselves. Overall, German progress was hindered by strong Soviet resistance.

By eight o’clock in the morning on 19 September, Russian forces had taken Bergen, but their British allies failed to provide timely support, the delay attributed to a discrepancy in timekeeping. The Russians were encircled by the French; General Hermann was captured and Jerepsoff killed. Russian troops then withdrew from Bergen to Schoorl, which they subsequently abandoned, and command of the Russian forces was taken up by General I. Essen. The French asserted that the outcome could have favored them if the British had intervened in time. Following the Battle of Castricum, the Duke of York wrote to Emperor Paul I praising the Russians’ exploits but cautioned that their ardor led them into a pitched battle with superior forces and that they could not be supported in time.

The Battle of Bergen in 1799 produced significant casualties and material losses for the opposing forces. Records indicate 1,785 soldiers were killed or captured, including 1,741 noncommissioned officers and enlisted men and 44 officers. Wounds numbered 1,225, with 49 of the wounded being officers. Additionally, 12 artillery pieces were seized during the engagement.

Phan Châu Trinh traveled to Paris in 1915 to seek support from progressive French politicians and Vietnamese exiles, where he joined with fellow patriots Phan Văn Trường, Nguyễn An Ninh, Nguyễn Tất Thành, and Nguyễn Thế Truyền as part of a group known as the Group of Vietnamese Patriots, based at 6 Villa des Gobelins. The circle produced patriotic articles signed with the name Nguyễn Ái Quốc, a designation later adopted by Hồ Chí Minh, acting on behalf of the group. To support himself in France, Trinh worked as a photograph retoucher. He returned to Saigon in 1925 and died there on 24 March 1926, aged 53. His funeral was attended by more than 60,000 people and sparked widespread protests demanding an end to French colonial rule.

Phan Châu Trinh (Chữ Hán: 潘周楨; 9 September 1872 – 24 March 1926) was a Vietnamese nationalist and reformer active in the early 20th century who sought to end French colonial occupation of Vietnam. He bore the courtesy name Tử Cán and published under the pen names Tây Hồ and Hi Mã, adopting a nonviolent, reform-oriented program that prioritized mass education and civic participation as catalysts for emancipation. Trinh rejected violence and opposed seeking foreign intervention, arguing instead that independence could be achieved by mobilizing the Vietnamese people and appealing to the democratic principles of France. His approach emphasized gradual modernization and political awakening as essential steps toward national self-determination.

The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) was updated in 1974 to introduce a more timely amendment mechanism. Under the earlier SOLAS 1960 framework, amendments required formal notice of acceptance by the International Maritime Organization and a prescribed threshold of states and tonnage, which frequently led to protracted delays before they could take effect. By contrast, the 1974 convention established a tacit acceptance procedure, whereby amendments would take effect on a designated date unless objections were lodged by an agreed number of contracting parties within a specified period.

The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) has undergone several significant amendments to update its safety framework. In 1988, amendments informed by the 1987 International Radio Regulations replaced Morse code with the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS). The GMDSS entered into force on 1 February 1992. The convention’s subject matter is organized into sections that outline the issues it covers. Additional amendments were adopted in May 2011.
Mart Crowley, born Edward Martino Crowley on August 21, 1935, and who died on March 7, 2020, was an American playwright best known for his 1968 play The Boys in the Band.

Mart Crowley is an American playwright who is best known for The Boys in the Band. He has appeared in at least four documentary films, including The Celluloid Closet (1995), which analyzes the portrayal of homosexuality in cinema; Dominick Dunne: After the Party (2007), a biography of his friend and producer Dominick Dunne; Making the Boys (2011), which chronicles the development of the gay play and its Hollywood film adaptation; and The Boys in the Band: Something Personal (2020), which centers on the 2020 Netflix adaptation of the play.
