In 1995 the European Union adopted the Data Protection Directive, which regulates the processing of personal data within the Union. The directive underscores substantial differences between European data protection standards and United States privacy laws. Compliance with these standards is required not only of businesses operating in the EU but also of any organization that transfers the personal information of an EU citizen. In 2001 the U.S. Department of Commerce established an opt‑in Safe Harbor framework intended to ensure legal compliance for U.S. organizations handling EU data. The Federal Trade Commission approved several U.S. entities to certify adherence to the U.S.–EU Safe Harbor program. Since 2010 Safe Harbor has faced criticism, particularly from German publicly appointed privacy protectors, who argued that the FTC had failed to enforce the rules effectively amid ongoing harmonization discrepancies.

Several early web privacy frameworks, such as the Platform for Privacy Preferences Project (P3P) and the ICRA labeling framework, were designed to enable browsers to automatically evaluate a site's privacy practices and grant access when those practices matched a user’s preferences. These mechanisms, however, do not guarantee that websites actually comply with their stated policies and they require users to have a certain level of technical knowledge to configure browser privacy controls. Automated privacy policies have not gained broad popularity among websites or their users. To lessen the burden of interpreting individual privacy policies, Jøsang, Fritsch, and Mahler have proposed reusable, certified policies hosted on a policy server.

Andi Bau Tenri (December 21, 1965 – April 16, 2018), commonly known as Andi Botenri, was an Indonesian actress, television host, model, and beauty pageant titleholder. She won Miss World Indonesia in 1982 and Miss Universe Indonesia in 1983, subsequently representing Indonesia at Miss World 1982 and Miss Universe 1983. Her dual national titles made her the second Indonesian to hold two major crowns in the country’s pageantry history. She was also the second Indonesian to compete in two of the four major international beauty pageants, following Lydia Arlini Wahab, who took part in Miss International 1974 and Miss Universe 1975.

Andi Botenri won Miss Universe Indonesia in 1983 and subsequently represented Indonesia at the Miss Universe pageant of that year. She traveled to St. Louis, Missouri, in early July to participate in quarantine, rehearsals, and preliminary competitions alongside about eighty delegates. She arrived ten days after the events had begun, due to visa problems and protests by Indonesians. The delay was further exacerbated by government pressure, including from former First Lady Tien Suharto, wife of the late president Suharto.

Osiris is a central figure in ancient Egyptian religion, associated with fertility, agriculture, the afterlife, the dead, resurrection, life, and vegetation. In artistic depictions he appears with green skin, a pharaoh's beard, partially mummy-wrapped legs, the atef crown, and the crook and flail, symbols of his royal and divine authority. He is among the earliest gods linked to mummy wrappings. In the myth, Seth killed him and cut him into pieces; Isis, Osiris's sister-wife, and Nephthys searched Egypt to recover his body parts. Isis collected all pieces except Osiris's genitalia and wrapped the body, enabling his return to life. Osiris continued to be widely worshipped until the decline of ancient Egyptian religion with the rise of Christianity in the Roman Empire.

At Philae, the cult of Isis and Osiris persisted at least until the 450s CE, enduring well after the late 4th-century imperial decrees ordering the closure of pagan temples. Consequently, Philae is regarded as the last major ancient Egyptian temple to be closed.

On Twitter, replies to one another are grouped into threads, organizing conversations into threaded discussions. The platform's 140-character limit hindered the ability to convey complete thoughts in a single post. As a result, many users posted dozens of tweets in succession, creating a disjointed sequence that came to be known as a tweetstorm. The term tweetstorm was popularized by Marc Andreessen.

During 2012, Twitter introduced the ability for tweets linking to partner websites to display expanded media beneath the tweet, such as article excerpts or embedded videos. This development followed existing enhancements that provided richer previews for content from Instagram and YouTube. The company also opened a program allowing websites to apply to test Twitter Cards, a feature intended to deliver more informative and media-rich previews to users. Later that year, after Facebook completed its purchase of Instagram, Instagram began cropping images in card previews and announced plans to discontinue the cards feature.

Tagalog is the common language among overseas Filipino communities, though its use abroad is largely limited to communication within Filipino ethnic groups rather than with the host population. The largest concentration of Tagalog speakers outside the Philippines is in the United States, where there are over 1.7 million speakers. In the 2020 United States census data (collected in 2018), Tagalog was identified as the fourth most spoken non-English language at home, behind Spanish, French, and Chinese (combined Cantonese and Mandarin).

In descriptions of Tagalog phonology, a table above enumerates the full range of realizations for each of the language’s five vowel sounds. The precise realization of a given vowel varies with the speaker’s regional origin or level of proficiency, illustrating phonetic variability across speakers. The vowel system is typically described as comprising five general vowels that form the core of the inventory.

FC Dinamo MVD Bishkek is a Kyrgyzstani football club based in Bishkek. The team has competed in the Kyrgyzstan League, the highest level of football in Kyrgyzstan. Its home matches are played at Dynamo Stadion.

Variable-rate belt feeders are built with a rugged, durable design that enables continuous movement of bulk materials. Their ability to operate in low-headroom environments allows installation in constrained layouts, enhancing versatility across mine sites and processing facilities. They are well suited for handling materials such as coal and ore, providing gentle handling while maintaining economical transport of large quantities. Consequently, these feeders function as important components in both the mining and power-generation sectors, supporting reliable material transfer and overall process efficiency.

Variable rate feeders, commonly implemented as belt feeders, are designed to regulate the discharge of bulk materials from storage to downstream processing by delivering material at a controlled, adjustable rate. They handle bulk materials that are light, fine, abrasive, and free-flowing, enabling reliable metering of flow to subsequent equipment. These feeders are typically installed beneath storage facilities such as silos, surge hoppers, or load hoppers, which allows controlled withdrawal from the confinement. They can operate in horizontal configuration or on an incline to save headroom and suit various plant layouts. Belt width is selected based on the size of the material being conveyed and the required throughput, expressed in tons per hour, ensuring adequate capacity for the intended application.

Under a contract awarded in August 1998, the United States Navy procured two APL 65 berthing barges. They were delivered to the Navy in November and December 2000, respectively. The barges were equipped with a range of facilities to support on-board life, including a post office, barber shop, bank, classrooms, laundry, medical facilities, and fitness services.

Following the 1982 Falklands War, the United Kingdom repurposed barracks ships to support the garrison on the Falkland Islands. The vessels chosen for this role were the former car ferries MV St Edmund and TEV Rangatira, which were deployed to Port Stanley in 1982 to provide accommodation and related facilities. Rangatira remained at Port Stanley until September 1983.

Inktank Storage served as the leading development contributor and financial sponsor behind the open-source Ceph distributed storage platform. The company was founded by Sage Weil and Bryan Bogensberger. Its initial funding came from DreamHost, Citrix, and Mark Shuttleworth.

Inktank Storage attracted attention from the technology press in 2012. In May, CRN named the company as one of ten promising emerging vendors. In July, Infostor identified Inktank as one of six storage startups to watch, and CRN later included the company in a list designating the year’s ten most notable storage startups.

The Arctic tree line denotes the northernmost latitude in the Northern Hemisphere at which trees can grow. North of this boundary, the climate remains too cold year-round to sustain tree growth. Extremely low temperatures can freeze the internal sap of trees, resulting in their death. Additionally, soil permafrost prevents roots from reaching the depth required for structural support.

The tree line denotes the northern or elevational boundary beyond which trees cannot persist, and it is principally determined by mean seasonal temperature; disturbances such as logging or grazing can alter the observed or realized tree line by affecting local conditions, but they do not change the climate-determined limit. In climatic terms, the line generally follows the contour where the seasonal mean temperature is about 6 °C (43 °F). That seasonal mean is computed from the subset of days on which the daily mean temperature exceeds 0.9 °C (33.6 °F). For tree growth to occur, a minimum growing season of roughly 94 days above that 0.9 °C threshold is required. Consequently, because the fundamental constraint is climate, most human activities cannot alter the actual tree line unless they induce changes to the climate itself.

Parallel Random Access Machine (PRAM) algorithms assume the ability to access shared memory with unlimited concurrency, but such behavior cannot be achieved with conventional CPU plus DRAM systems, since DRAM cannot provide true concurrent access to a single bank, even for accesses to different addresses within the same bank. As a result, PRAM-style parallelism is typically realized in hardware or by leveraging the internal SRAM resources available on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). When implemented on FPGA on‑chip SRAM, a CRCW (Concurrent Read, Concurrent Write) memory scheme can be employed to emulate PRAM semantics, allowing multiple operations to read from and write to the same location in a way that mirrors PRAM behavior within the hardware design.

A Parallel RAM implementation in SystemVerilog computes the maximum element of an array within two clock cycles. During the first cycle, all element combinations are evaluated in parallel, effectively comparing candidates for the maximum concurrently. In the second cycle, the partial results are merged to yield the final maximum value. The design employs a concurrently writable memory (CRCW), allowing m[i] to be set to 1 and the variable holding the maximum value (maxNo) to be updated with data[i] in the same cycle. Because the concurrent writes target the same memory location only when carrying the same maximum value, no write conflicts arise. The approach is compatible with FPGA hardware and can be implemented on FPGA platforms.

René Clair began his artistic career by contributing songs for the chanteuse Damia, whose influence encouraged him to visit Gaumont studios in 1920. He soon took a leading role in Le Lys de la vie, a film directed by Loïe Fuller and Gabrielle Sorère, and subsequently adopted the stage name René Clair as part of his professional identity. He continued acting in other projects, including Parisette for Louis Feuillade, while in 1922 he shifted toward journalism, becoming editor of a new film supplement to Théâtre et Comœdia illustrés. His work extended beyond France, with a visit to Belgium, and through his brother Henri’s introduction he became an assistant to director Jacques de Baroncelli on several films, gaining practical experience that would inform his later career behind the camera.

René Clair was elected to the Académie Française in 1960. Although not the first filmmaker to be honored by the Academy—preceding film-makers such as Marcel Pagnol (1946), Jean Cocteau (1955), and Marcel Achard (1959) had received the distinction—Clair was the first to be elected principally on the basis of his career as a filmmaker. In 1994, the Académie established the Prix René-Clair, an annual prize awarded to a distinguished filmmaker.

Greek seafaring has deep historical roots and experienced a revival in the late Ottoman era, particularly in the period after the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca and amid the disruptions of the Napoleonic Wars. A substantial merchant middle class emerged from maritime commerce, playing a pivotal role in the Greek War of Independence. In the contemporary era, Greece maintains one of the world’s largest merchant fleets, with a significant share of vessels owned by Greeks and many sailing under flags of convenience. Notable 20th‑century shipping magnates associated with this enduring maritime tradition include Aristotle Onassis, Yiannis Latsis, Stavros G. Livanos, and Stavros Niarchos.

Ethnic Greeks have long been closely associated with the Greek Orthodox faith, a linkage that remained influential after the creation of the modern Greek state in 1830. The 1822 Greek constitution defined a Greek as a native Christian resident of the Kingdom of Greece, a criterion that was removed by 1840, signaling a shift in the basis of citizenship. In the aftermath of the Ottoman Empire's collapse, the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne established a population exchange between Greece and Turkey driven by religious identity, although most of those displaced had already left prior to the treaty. The period also witnessed the Greek genocide, during which Pontian Greeks along the southern Black Sea coast were removed in the context of the Asia Minor Campaign and its aftermath. This sequence occurred within the broader Turkification of the Ottoman Empire and a reorientation of its economy and trade networks, which significantly altered the region’s demographic and economic landscape.

DFK Dainava is a Lithuanian football club based in Alytus that pursued promotion to the A Lyga in 2019 but was unable to secure the sponsorship required from the Alytus municipality, resulting in its remaining in the I Lyga; it finished the 2019 LFF I Lyga in fourth place. The club again sought an A Lyga licence for the 2020 season, but the licence application was declined once more.

In March 2021, DFK Dainava submitted an application for a licence to compete in Lithuania's top-flight league, A Lyga, for the 2021 season. The licence was initially refused on grounds of unstable finances and the absence of a plan to organise a women's team. At that time A Lyga consisted of nine licensed clubs, with DFK Dainava's bid aiming to add a tenth. Following measures to secure sponsorship and financial stability, the Lithuanian Football Federation granted the club a licence to participate in A Lyga. The decision marked Alytus town’s first appearance in the top division with a men's side since the club's revival in 2016. DFK Dainava began the season with a 3-point deduction under federation regulations. The club's first A Lyga match took place on 6 March in Marijampolė against newly promoted FK Nevėžis, with the venue chosen because Marijampolė possesses a full-sized indoor football facility and is the closest city to Alytus.

Caenogastropoda is a large grouping of shelled marine molluscs that consists of numerous families. Among its best known members are periwinkles, cowries, wentletraps, moon snails, murexes, cone snails, and turrids. The clade accounts for about 60 percent of all living gastropods.

Caenogastropoda is a major clade of marine gastropods. The name Taenioglossa is derived from taenio, meaning “band,” together with glossa, meaning “tongue.” In older classifications, Taenioglossa corresponds to the taxon Mesogastropoda, an arrangement considered equivalent to Mesogastropoda. A characteristic feature of this group is the taenioglossate radula, which typically has seven teeth per row.

Plans are in place to extend the River Walk to areas north and south of downtown, broadening its reach beyond the core district. At present, chain restaurants and other chain establishments fill roughly one-third of the riverfront commercial space, prompting city officials to explore limits on such outlets to preserve a distinctly local character. On May 30, 2009, the city opened the Museum Reach, a $72 million expansion that extends the corridor with new attractions. The project incorporates local sites such as the San Antonio Museum of Art and the Pearl Brewery, with the Pearl Brewery area having become one of the most popular locales for residents.

Following the San Antonio River flood of September 1921, which claimed 51 lives and left 23 people missing, city planners developed flood-control measures for the river. One proposal called for constructing an upstream dam, the Olmos Dam, to regulate flow before it reached the city core. Another element proposed bypassing a prominent downtown bend located between present-day Houston Street and Villita Parkway, by paving over the bend and converting it into a storm sewer. These early plans illustrate the period's approach to flood management and helped shape later development along the river.

Extravehicular activity (EVA) took place on March 18, 1965, during the Soviet Voskhod 2 mission and was performed by cosmonaut Alexei Leonov. He spent twelve minutes and nine seconds outside the spacecraft, aided only by a white metal life-support backpack that supplied about 45 minutes of breathing and pressurization oxygen. Movement outside the vehicle was constrained largely to a single tether measuring 15.35 meters in length, providing limited control over orientation and propulsion. After the flight, Leonov described the EVA as easy, though the spacesuit inflated under the vacuum of space, causing it to become rigid to the point that he could not operate the chest-mounted camera shutter.

Thomas Pesquet holds the European record for extravehicular activities (EVAs) and also holds the non-U.S./Russian record for EVAs. He completed six EVAs, totaling 39 hours and 54 minutes, conducted across two International Space Station missions between January 2017 and August 2021.

During the Zhili–Anhui War, Zhili and allied forces organized the Traitor Suppression Army (讨逆军), comprising a single division and nine combined brigades. Wu Peifu served as the army’s front-line commander-in-chief. The force was deployed on two fronts: an eastern sector near Yang Hamlet and a western sector near Gaobei. Separately, Zhang Zuolin ordered a detachment to advance into Shanhaiguan, where it took up positions at Machang and Junliangcheng.

In early July 1920, the Anhui clique organized the National Stabilization Army (Dingguu Jun). The force consisted of five divisions and four combined brigades. Duan Qirui was appointed to the post of commander-in-chief. The unit was deployed on two fronts, with the western front covering Zhuozhou, Laishui, and Gu'an, and the eastern front extending to Liang Hamlet and Beijimiao, just west of Yang Hamlet.

The earliest inhabitants of Melanesia were likely the ancestors of present-day Papuan-speaking peoples. They migrated from Southeast Asia and subsequently occupied Melanesia as far east as the main Solomon Islands archipelago, including Makira. It is possible that these early populations also inhabited smaller islands farther to the east.

The Bonin Islands are part of the biogeographical realm shared with Micronesia and lie in close geographic proximity to Micronesia. This spatial and ecological connection leads them to be commonly classified within the Micronesia subregion of Oceania, reflecting their relationship to that subregion.

Constructivist architecture encompassed a range of collective housing projects designed to embody its social aims, including Ivan Nikolaev’s Communal House of the Textile Institute in Moscow (1929–1931). Prominent examples by Ginzburg include the Moscow Gosstrakh apartments and the Narkomfin Building, while flats in the constructivist style were built across Kharkiv, Moscow, Leningrad, and several smaller towns. Ginzburg also designed a government building in Alma-Ata, and the Vesnin brothers conceived a School of Film Actors in Moscow as part of the movement’s urban agenda. A central tenet of the approach was the belief that workers’ housing should not replicate bourgeois apartment layouts but should be developed in collaboration with the proletariat to foster a new way of life. The period also saw publishing activity by the OSA, which issued the magazine SA, or Contemporary Architecture, from 1926 to 1930. The mass-housing aspect was advanced by rationalist Ladovsky, who completed a Moscow apartment block in 1929. An extravagant counterpoint is Chekists Village in Sverdlovsk (now Yekaterinburg), a hammer-and-sickle shaped collective housing complex for NKVD staff by Ivan Antonov, Veniamin Sokolov, and Arseny Tumbasov, which has since been converted into a hotel.

Constructivist architecture in the Soviet Union reached a pivotal moment with the 1932 Palace of the Soviets design competition, which brought together leading constructivists alongside international figures such as Walter Gropius, Erich Mendelsohn, and Le Corbusier. Held amid widespread critique of Modernism in a largely agrarian society, the contest spurred debate over Modernism’s approach, with critics contending that its forms copied technological progress while relying on conventional, routine construction practices. The competition’s winner, Boris Iofan, signaled the beginning of eclectic historicism within Stalinist architecture. In this context, Stalinist architecture has been read as reacting against Modernism’s cosmopolitanism, perceived ugliness, and inhumanity by mixing historical styles and, at times, incorporating new technologies. Housing projects such as the Narkomfin aimed to reform daily life through measures like shared facilities, gender equality, and collective child-rearing. These social experiments were later superseded as Stalinism revived traditional family values. As older architectural vocabularies were revived, the Moscow Metro helped popularize the notion of the “workers’ palaces.”
The March of Istria was held by the Habsburg monarch after its previous holder, and the designation "Margrave of Istria" was incorporated into the grand title of the Emperor of Austria.

From Aistulf's rise in 749, the Lombard king conducted campaigns against Byzantine territories in Italy and threatened the Papacy in Rome. With little prospect of assistance from Constantinople, Pope Zachary allied with Pepin the Short and recognized him as king of the Franks. In 755 Pepin crossed into Italy and compelled Aistulf to submit to Frankish suzerainty, thereby reconfiguring the political landscape of northern Italy under Frankish influence. Later, Pepin's son Charlemagne, in 773/774, incorporated the Italian kingdom into the Carolingian Empire, cementing Frankish authority over the region.

On March 13, 2007, DreamWorks Animation announced that all of its upcoming feature films would be released in stereoscopic 3D. The plan identified Monsters vs. Aliens (2009) as the first anticipated 3D release. To support this transition, DreamWorks partnered with Intel to co-develop the InTru3D 3D filmmaking technology.

In January 2017, Christopher DeFaria was appointed president of the DreamWorks Feature Animation Group, charged with overseeing slate strategy, development and production, as well as innovation and business affairs. A month later, Universal acquired a minority stake in Amblin Partners, effectively reuniting DreamWorks Animation with a minority stake in the DreamWorks Pictures label, its former parent and distribution partner. On August 1, 2017, DreamWorks Animation announced a collaboration with Blumhouse Productions for Blumhouse’s first animated feature, Spooky Jack, which was initially scheduled for a September 17, 2021 release but was later removed from the schedule when The Bad Guys (2022) claimed that release slot. In October 2017, Abhijay Prakash was named chief operating officer; he would subsequently be promoted in February 2019 to president of the Universal Filmed Entertainment Group following the release of How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World. Roughly three months after that promotion, in May 2019, DreamWorks Animation appointed Randy Lake, previously the head of Sony Pictures Imageworks, as the new chief operating officer. In November 2017, the company launched DreamWorks Shorts, a program to feature original animated short films ahead of its feature releases, mirroring practices at other major studios; Bird Karma became the inaugural short, premiering in spring 2018 and later being tied to the Japanese theatrical release of The Boss Baby (2017).

The 1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas were held on November 5, 1996, to determine the state's delegation to the U.S. House. Texas elected 30 representatives, a size determined by the apportionment following the 1990 United States census.

In the 1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, the sitting Democrat John Wiley Bryant retired from the House to pursue a United States Senate seat. The 5th congressional district was one of thirteen districts that conducted a special election on November 5, the same day as the general election. In that year's process, the contest in each district featured all certified candidates on a single ballot, with participants from all parties competing against one another regardless of partisan affiliation.

Research into combating fake news continues to develop, evaluating a range of methods to counter and reduce misinformation across different forms. Disinformation is defined as the purposeful dissemination of false narratives intended to influence political outcomes or undermine social cohesion within targeted communities. Because fake news encompasses diverse phenomena, strategies are tailored to the specific characteristics of each type. Consequently, interventions vary according to whether the misinformation is intentionally produced to mislead or produced inadvertently without malicious intent.

Polish historian Jerzy Targalski has argued that a network of fake news sites infiltrated public discourse in Poland, with the infiltration largely driven by anti-establishment and right-wing outlets. These platforms republished and reworked material originally produced by Russia Today, contributing to the spread of Russian disinformation within the country. Approximately twenty distinct Polish fake news websites were involved in disseminating such content. An illustrative case circulated by these outlets claimed that Ukraine announced the Polish city of Przemyśl as occupied Polish territory.

Cales, also rendered as Kales, Calles, or Kalles (Greek: Κάλης; Κάλλης), was an emporium or trading place on the coast of ancient Bithynia. It stood at the mouth of the river of the same name, the Cales, after which both the town and the river were named, serving as a notable commercial site in antiquity. The location lay about 120 stadia east of Elaeus.

Disques Dreyfus, also known as Dreyfus Records, is a French record label. The label’s French name, Disques Dreyfus, is pronounced disk dʁɛfys. It has released recordings by a range of artists, notably Jean-Michel Jarre, who was affiliated with the label for more than twenty years.

Disques Dreyfus, established by Francis Dreyfus no later than 1980, expanded its reach to the United States in 1985. As part of the Dreyfus family company, it was owned by Dreyfus Records, a French music distributor. The label ceased operations on January 4, 2013, and its catalog was absorbed by BMG Rights Management Group.

The article presents a list of debtor nations arranged by their net international investment position per capita. A negative NIIP denotes that a country holds net external liabilities rather than net external assets. Data are drawn from national government statistical agencies, Eurostat, and the International Monetary Fund, though many countries do not report NIIP data to the IMF, and parallel reports produced by governments or international organizations may diverge significantly.

Net international investment position (NIIP) measures the net balance of a country’s external financial assets minus its external liabilities. External debt includes obligations incurred by both the public sector and the private sector. In NIIP calculations, external assets held by residents, whether publicly or privately held, are included, capturing the overall net external claims of the economy. Commodity prices and currency movements produce cyclic valuation effects, causing NIIP figures to fluctuate with economic cycles. The article lists creditor nations by NIIP per capita, ranking economies according to their net external position on a per-person basis.

Willem Drees completed his training at the Trade School, where, toward its end, he rejected a brewery position offered by the principal because of his opposition to alcohol. After obtaining a Bachelor of Accountancy in 1903, he began work as a bank teller with the Twentsche Bank in Amsterdam in July of that year. He soon grew dissatisfied with banking and declined his uncle Frits’s suggestion to pursue a career in brokerage and insurance. In July 1906, he left the Twentsche Bank. He subsequently took a position as a stenographer with the municipal council of Amsterdam, and later served as a stenographer at the States General in The Hague from January 1907 to August 1919.

Willem Drees married Catharina Hent on 28 July 1910. Catharina Hent (1888–1974) was born on 6 May 1888 and died on 30 January 1974. The couple had four children, comprising two sons and two daughters. Their two sons, Jan Drees and Willem Drees Jr., were active members of the Labour Party. Drees left the Labour Party around 1970, and subsequently both Jan Drees and Willem Drees Jr. joined Democratic Socialists '70 (DS'70). Drees himself did not join DS'70.

Gender apartheid refers to a system in which individuals are separated or restricted on the basis of gender through deliberate, organized policies and practices that create and sustain division. The mere existence of gender separation does not automatically signal favoritism toward any particular group; however, apartheid and oppressive segregation are defined by intentional, systematic construction of conditions that enforce these divisions. Such conditions manifest across political, economic, social, and geographic dimensions, and are designed to advantage at least one gender group, typically in the near term. Consequently, broad, universal gains for all groups are unlikely, and when they do occur, they tend to be incidental rather than the intended outcome.

Gender apartheid, in this article's context, refers to a campaign initiated by the Feminist Majority Foundation in 1997, the Campaign to Stop Gender Apartheid in Afghanistan, established to highlight human rights abuses against women under the Taliban. The campaign has faced criticism from some quarters for adopting a Western-centric, interventionist posture and for an approach that critics say denigrates Islam. After the fall of the Taliban regime, the initiative broadened and was renamed the Campaign for Afghan Women and Girls. It is chaired by Mavis Leno, and its stated aim is to continue raising awareness of gender inequality in Afghanistan.

The Praemium Imperiale is an international art prize established in 1988 and awarded annually since 1989. In Japanese, it is known as 高松宮殿下記念世界文化賞 (Takamatsu-no-miya Denka Kinen Sekai Bunka-shō), meaning "World Culture Prize in Memory of His Imperial Highness Prince Takamatsu." The award is presented by the Imperial Family of Japan on behalf of the Japan Art Association. It recognizes achievement across five disciplines: painting, sculpture, architecture, music, and theatre and film.

Laureates are announced each September for the Praemium Imperiale, with a prize presentation ceremony and related events held in Tokyo, Japan, each November. The ceremony is presided over by Prince Hitachi, President of the Japan Art Association, at the Meiji Kinenkan in Tokyo, where he presents the prizes to the selected laureates. The award comprises a gold medal and 15 million Japanese yen in prize money. The prize was created by the Fujisankei Communications Group, which funds the program, covering roughly $3 million in expenses annually.

Emma Georgina Rothschild, born in London, England, is a British economist and historian. She is the daughter of Victor Rothschild and Teresa Georgina Mayor, situating her within the prominent Rothschild family on her father’s side. Her maternal lineage includes Robert John Grote Mayor, the brother of novelist F. M. Mayor and a great-nephew of philosopher John Grote, as well as Katherine Beatrice Meinertzhagen, the sister of the soldier Richard Meinertzhagen and the niece of Beatrice Webb. Rothschild is the sister of Amschel Mayor James Rothschild and the half-sister of Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild. At the age of fifteen, she became the youngest woman admitted to Somerville College, Oxford, where she completed a BA in Philosophy, Politics and Economics in 1967. She later studied as a Kennedy Scholar in Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a member of the Rothschild banking family of England. She serves as a trustee of the Rothschild Archive, an international research center based in London dedicated to the history of the Rothschild family.

The fifth-round draw for the fixtures of CONCACAF's 2018 FIFA World Cup qualification took place on 8 July 2016 at 10:00 local time (EDT, UTC−4) at the confederation's headquarters in Miami Beach, United States. The ceremony occurred before the completion of the fourth round, meaning several participants had not yet been determined. Mexico was the only team guaranteed a place in the final hexagonal, having won Group A in the preceding fourth-round group stage, while the other fourth-round qualifiers remained unknown at the time of the draw.

Known as the Hexagonal, the fifth round of CONCACAF's 2018 World Cup qualification was contested from 11 November 2016 to 10 October 2017. The round saw Mexico, Costa Rica, and Panama qualify for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, while Honduras advanced to the inter-confederation play-offs for another chance to reach the tournament. The United States failed to qualify for the World Cup, the first such outcome in 32 years, and Trinidad and Tobago were eliminated in this round.

U.S. Route 26 (US 26) traverses Oregon from the Portland metropolitan area, beginning in Sandy where the corridor is known as the Mount Hood Highway. It proceeds toward Government Camp and Bennett Pass, where it intersects Oregon Route 35 (OR 35); the Mount Hood Highway continues north along OR 35, while US 26 heads southeast toward Madras. In Madras, US 26 intersects US 97 and continues southeast to Prineville, where it meets OR 126. The route then travels east through John Day and reaches Vale, where it intersects US 20. Thereafter, the remainder of US 26 runs concurrently with US 20 to the Idaho state line.

U.S. Route 26 is an east–west United States Numbered Highway that runs from Seaside, Oregon to Ogallala, Nebraska. When first defined, the system covered Nebraska and Wyoming, and by the 1950s its length had been extended to include Idaho and Oregon. Its eastern terminus is at an intersection with Interstate 80 in Ogallala, while the western terminus lies just south of Seaside at a junction with U.S. Route 101. Prior to 2004, the final roughly 20 miles were cosigned with US 101 from south of Seaside to Astoria, with U.S. Route 30's western terminus located at the Astoria intersection. Long segments of the highway follow the historic Oregon Trail. At its maximum extent, just before the Interstate Highway System, US 26 measured about 1,557 miles (2,506 km) and terminated in Astoria.

The film depicts the secret marriage of Romeo and Juliet, undertaken with the help of Juliet's nurse and Friar Laurence, who hope that the union will bring peace to the feuding families. As the Montague and Capulet households remain at odds, street brawls between the two factions intensify. Romeo's close friend Mercutio is killed by Tybalt, and in retaliation Romeo kills Tybalt to avenge Mercutio's death. This sequence of violence leads to Romeo's banishment from Verona.

Romeo and Juliet, a 1936 film, is set in Verona, Italy, against the backdrop of a bitter feud between the noble houses of Montague and Capulet. The story follows Romeo Montague and Juliet Capulet as they meet and fall in love at a masquerade ball, a romance that unfolds amid the families’ longstanding enmity.

Forensic Files II premiered on February 23, 2020, launching with a first season comprising sixteen episodes. On May 12, 2020, the series was renewed to continue with both a second and a third season. The second season began on July 11, 2021, followed by the third season, which debuted on February 27, 2022. The fourth season arrived with a premiere on July 9, 2023.

Forensic Files II did not hire actors for its reenactments, diverging from the approach of the original program. Instead, personnel from CNN and HLN were cast to portray victims, suspects, and other individuals involved in the cases, performing the dramatic recreations of real-life events that formed the series' core presentations.

Krasnoyarsk Krai operates under its Charter, the region’s fundamental law. The Legislative Assembly of Krasnoyarsk Krai serves as the region’s standing legislative and representative body, with authority to enact laws, resolutions, and other normative acts, and to supervise their implementation and observance. The assembly consists of 52 deputies: 22 are elected from 22 single-mandate districts by plurality, two represent Taymyr, and two represent Evenkia, while 26 are chosen through proportional representation from party lists. The highest executive authority in the krai is the Oblast Government, which comprises territorial executive bodies such as district administrations, committees, and commissions tasked with promoting development and handling everyday administrative matters. The oblast administration supports the Governor, who is the krai’s top official and the guarantor of adherence to the krai Charter in line with the Constitution of Russia.

Krasnoyarsk Krai is one of Russia's principal producers of electric power. Its substantial energy output makes it an attractive site for industries with high energy demands. Aluminum smelting plants exemplify the kind of energy-intensive industries drawn to the region.

Myus is an ancient settlement situated well north of the estuarine flood plain, at the bend in the Maeander where the river’s course shifts from northeast to east. It originated as a colony of Aeolian settlers and derives its name from Ancient Magnesia, a district in Thessaly, the homeland of its founders. Historians distinguish the Anatolian site as Maiandros, or Magnesia on the Maeander, to differentiate it from the Thessalian Magnesia. Geographically, the location lies on the Maeander itself and never within the estuary. The nearest modern city is Tekin, located about 52.37 kilometers (32.54 miles) from the mouth of the Maeander.

In the historiography surrounding Smyrna’s incorporation, Vitruvius attributes the city’s admission to the kindness of rulers named Attalus and Arsinoe. Yet the Ionians of that period were independent and acted autonomously, and there were no overarching rulers by those names at that early date; the figures appear only in later Hellenistic and Roman aristocracy. Some scholars have suggested that Smyrnaeans waited centuries for their petition to be approved, implying a protracted or pro forma process. Even if such a delay occurred, the identities of any benefactors remain wholly speculative.
The rhombic triacontahedron is a convex polyhedron with thirty faces, each of which is a rhombus. The rhombi are golden rhombi, having diagonals in the golden ratio.

The diamond shape, in geometric terms, is commonly referred to as a rhombus, a word that derives from the Greek rhómbos, which originally described a spinning object such as a bullroarer or a button whirligig. The term was used by Euclid and Archimedes, and Archimedes also employed the expression “solid rhombus” to denote a bicone formed by two congruent right circular cones sharing a base. In two dimensions, a rhombus can be understood as a cross-section of a bicone, linking its planar form to a corresponding three-dimensional figure.

La Marca del Hombre Lobo (The Mark of the Wolf Man) is a Spanish film released in 1968 that was originally produced in the Hi Fi Stereo 70 format. The picture was later re-edited to include new footage, and in the United States it was released under the title Frankenstein's Bloody Terror, presented in 3D on 35 mm film rather than the original 70 mm format.

The film's original title is Sud sumasschedshikh, and it is also known by several English-language alternate titles, including The Trial of Madmen, Judgment of Fools, and Judgment of the Mad. It was released in the Soviet Union in 1961 or 1962 and was produced for the Sovscope 70 format. The footage was subsequently optically converted to the three-strip Kinopanorama presentation.

Almost Persuaded (song) is a narrative ballad that centers on a married man in a tavern who is instantly captivated by a beautiful young woman. He momentarily forgets his marriage and nearly yields to temptation as they share a slow dance. A pivotal moment occurs when he notices the reflection of his wedding ring in her eyes, a visual reminder of his vows. Recalling his commitments, he chooses to leave the woman and resist the seduction.

Almost Persuaded held the record for the longest uninterrupted run at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart, remaining atop the chart for 46 years and 2 months. This record stood until the week of December 15, 2012, when Taylor Swift's We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together reached its ninth week at No. 1 on the same chart, thereby matching Almost Persuaded's chart-topping longevity.

Founded in 1985, The New Israeli Opera represented the first successful effort to establish a permanent repertory opera company in Israel, following a series of unsuccessful attempts dating back to the 1940s. In 1995, it relocated to its permanent venue at the Golda Center in Tel Aviv-Jaffa.

Shlomo Carlebach is widely regarded as an early figure associated with the emergence of Hasidic rock. In Israel, notable Hasidic rock performers include the group Reva L'Sheva and soloists Adi Ran and Naftali Abramson. The practice is constrained by halakhic restrictions that prohibit women from singing before mixed-gender audiences, which limits women's participation in Hasidic rock performances and leads to gender-segregated concert settings.

Larix lyallii bears seed cones that are 2.5 to 4 cm long, displaying a red-purple tone when young that darkens to brown as they age. The cones possess thin scales with narrow bracts that extend beyond the scales. Pollen and seed cones become active in early summer. The bark is about 2.5 cm thick and shifts color from yellow-gray to dark red-brown as the tree ages, eventually becoming deeply furrowed into small, scaly plates.

Larix lyallii, commonly known as Lyall's larch, is a small deciduous conifer that grows to about 10–25 meters in height, with individuals typically shorter at higher elevations. The trunk is straight and supports a sparse, somewhat conical crown. Branches are arranged horizontally and extend perpendicularly from the trunk, displaying irregular spacing and occasional twisting. The twigs are finely hairy. The needles are four-angled, measure 20–35 millimeters in length, and present a pale blue-green color; they are deciduous and occur in crowded clusters of 30–40 on short spur shoots. In autumn, the needles turn golden yellow.

"Tu t'laisses aller" is a chanson performed by Charles Aznavour. In 1995, the number was presented as part of the Intégrale du spectacle, the complete show, staged at the Palais des Congrès in Paris, with Liza Minnelli as the duet partner.

Tu t'laisses aller portrays a scene in which a husband drinks to muster the courage to express to his wife his entire judgment of her. He proceeds to deliver the harshest criticisms, articulating what he perceives as her faults in blunt terms. After this barrage, he argues that with a bit of effort and a smiling disposition, their relationship could return to its former harmony. The piece concludes with his invitation for her to draw close and release herself from restraint.

At the 2025 Australian Open, the wheelchair men's doubles event was won by Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid, who entered as five-time defending champions. They defeated Daniel Caverzaschi and Stéphane Houdet in the final, 6–2, 6–4.

Sport in Macau encompasses a broad network of associations and clubs that coordinate a range of local and regional competitions across various disciplines. The local sporting scene is largely amateur, with these organizations typically operated by entities that receive government subsidies or corporate sponsorships. The Macau Sport Development Board is charged with advancing sport, managing venues, and organizing major international sporting events within Macau. Notably, the territory’s premier motorsport event, the Macau Grand Prix, is organized by the Macau Grand Prix Committee rather than by the Sport Development Board.

Sport in Macau is organized largely through amateur leagues in which clubs compete against one another. Among these, the leagues that attract the largest numbers of participants include football, basketball, volleyball, dragon boating, and student leagues spanning a range of sports.

Soldier beetle refers to the family Cantharidae, a group of beetles whose fossil record includes notable Cretaceous representatives. Molliberus is the oldest described member of the family, originating from the Early Cretaceous (early Albian) El Soplao amber in Cantabria, Spain, and is classified within the tribe Cantharini of the subfamily Cantharinae. From Burmese amber dating to the early Cenomanian, six genera have been described, five placed in Cantharinae and one in Malthininae, illustrating early diversification within the family. The Cenomanian genus Katyacantharis, described from Agdzhakend amber in Azerbaijan, has been proposed as belonging to Cantharinae. Indeterminate soldier beetle specimens have also been reported from Aptian-aged Koonwarra fossil beds in the Strzelecki Group of Australia, as well as from Barremian-aged Lebanese amber, indicating a broader geographic distribution during the Cretaceous.

Within soldier beetles, larger males show a preference for mating with larger females, indicating mate choice linked to female body size. Male body size is positively correlated with the ability to secure matings, suggesting that bigger males have greater success in obtaining partners. In contrast, female body size is associated with the capacity to evade or resist male advances, implying that larger females may be better at avoiding unwanted courtship. These size-dependent patterns highlight how variation in body size can influence both mating success and resistance, contributing to the sexual dynamics observed in soldier beetles.

Anarchy of production denotes a characteristic feature of commodity production under private property and is regarded as the principal mode of production in the capitalist market economy. The term is used as a critique of market economies, underscoring their inherently chaotic and volatile dynamics in contrast to the planned economies advocated by Marxists.

Anarchy of production is a concept used in some socialist analyses to describe the capitalist market as unplanned, with production decisions made by numerous independent firms and agents rather than by a central planning authority. This lack of coordinated planning is said to produce crises, notably overproduction and underconsumption. The 2008 financial crisis has been cited as a contemporary instance of this phenomenon, with the Socialist Party of Great Britain attributing the crisis to the unplanned character of production under capitalism.

Carl Van Vechten, an American writer and critic, married Anna Snyder during a sojourn in England; she had been a longtime friend from Cedar Rapids. He returned to The New York Times in 1909 and became the first American critic of modern dance. Under the guidance of his mentor, Mabel Dodge Luhan, he grew deeply involved in the avant-garde and frequently attended groundbreaking musical premieres in New York City during the era of Isadora Duncan, Anna Pavlova, and Loie Fuller. He also attended premieres in Paris, where he met the American author and poet Gertrude Stein in 1913. Van Vechten became a devoted friend and champion of Stein, one of her most enthusiastic fans, and the two corresponded for the remainder of Stein's life; Stein appointed him her literary executor and he assisted in publishing her unpublished writings. A collection of the letters between Van Vechten and Stein has been published.

Carl Van Vechten published essays on music and literature from 1915 to 1920. He also served as an informal scout for the publisher Alfred A. Knopf. Knopf released seven of his novels between 1922 and 1930, beginning with Peter Whiffle: His Life and Works and concluding with Parties. His sexuality is reflected in his portraits of working-class men that exhibit homoerotic themes.

Skippy Williams was an American jazz saxophonist who collaborated with several prominent ensembles during his career, including Art Tatum, Fletcher Henderson, Count Basie, Lucky Millinder, and Bob Chester. Although some sources have claimed that he played tenor sax on Bill Haley's recordings of "Rock Around the Clock" and "Shake, Rattle and Roll," those attributions are incorrect and not supported by credible evidence.

Skippy Williams was the professional name of American jazz musician Elmer Williams (also cited as Elbert Williams). A notable tenor saxophonist and musical arranger, he was born on July 27, 1916, and died on February 28, 1994.

On April 21, 2025, Fat Mike and Spike, the founders of Me First and the Gimme Gimmes, announced that the touring component of the group would adopt the new name Spike and the Gimme Gimmes, with the change taking effect for all future touring engagements.
Scott Shiflett, the brother of Chris Shiflett, has been associated with the bands Face to Face and Viva Death. He has filled in for Chris on Me First and the Gimme Gimmes' most recent tours.

Shania Twain’s 1998 release Come On Over was issued in Europe in a remixed pop version with reduced country instrumentation, a move that helped establish her breakthrough across the continent. The album then climbed to No. 1 on the UK album charts for 11 weeks and was the year's best-selling album in Britain, with sales exceeding 1 million copies in Germany and approaching 4 million in the United Kingdom. European attention was driven by pop remixes of singles such as That Don’t Impress Me Much, which reached No. 3 in the UK and charted high in Germany, and Man! I Feel Like a Woman!, which peaked at No. 3 in the UK and in France. In addition, You're Still the One and the pop remix of From This Moment On reached the UK Top 10, while When reached the Top 20. The track You’ve Got a Way was remixed for the Notting Hill soundtrack. A worldwide reissue of the international version added three new remixes. The album set a record by remaining 99 weeks in the Billboard 200 Top 20, and in 1999 Billboard named Shania Twain the most played adult contemporary artist on US radio.

Shania Twain, a Canadian singer-songwriter, emerged as a leading figure in country music and became widely associated with blending country and pop, with Maclean’s in 1998 describing her as the dominant figure in that crossover. She has been recognized by critics for her stature, including American Songwriter’s Joe Vitagliano, who named her among the greatest artists of her era. The New York Times’ Jon Caramanica labeled her the crossover queen of country, noting that her fusion of pop sensibilities and country roots challenged Nashville norms and helped reshape the genre. Rolling Stone further asserted that her body of work defined a period in country music and opened doors for artists who blend genres. The Associated Press’s Kristin M. Hall argued that her global success altered the trajectory of country music for years to come. Nash credits the album Come On Over with redefining the future of country music, and NPR’s Jewly Hight observed that Twain redefined country superstardom and inspired a generation of artists to pursue more flamboyant videos, stronger backbeats, and arena-rock–style performances.

Disposable household and per capita income uses the median equivalised household disposable income as its central statistic; this measure is defined as the median of disposable income divided by the square root of household size, a normalization that accounts for shared costs and economies of scale when people live together. To enable meaningful international comparisons, the figures are adjusted for purchasing power parity and expressed in 2021 United States dollars. The values are presented for each country in a dedicated table covering the year 2021, with the monetary unit specified as the United States dollar.

Disposable household income, defined as household income minus taxes and mandatory contributions, represents the net amount available to households. The mean or median of this disposable income can serve as an indicator of residents’ purchasing power or material well-being within a region. In broader statistical terms, mean income (the average) is calculated by dividing the total aggregate income of a group by the number of units in that group, while median income is the value that separates the distribution into two equal parts, with half the units earning more and half earning less.

At the 2025 Wimbledon Championships in the men's singles, the list of seeded players is derived from the ATP rankings published on 23 June 2025, with the rankings and points considered for seeding prior to the tournament recorded as of 30 June 2025.

Jannik Sinner won the men's singles title at the 2025 Wimbledon Championships, defeating Carlos Alcaraz in the final with a four-set score of 4–6, 6–4, 6–4, 6–4. Alcaraz, the two-time defending champion, saw his undefeated streak in major finals come to an end at five appearances. The victory marked Sinner’s first Wimbledon title and his fourth major singles title overall. Additionally, Sinner became the first Italian to win the Wimbledon men's singles crown.

Throughout the New Testament and subsequent Christian thought, Jesus is designated by several interrelated names and titles that convey his identity and mission. Early Christology employed the imagery of a sacrificial lamb to portray Jesus as the suffering yet vindicated Messiah, an interpretation later contrasted by Augustine who spoke of the passion-associated lamb in opposition to a victorious, resurrection-empowered lion. The epithet Lamb of God appears in prayers and has given rise to the liturgical form Agnus Dei, which is used in worship and as a contemplative invocation seeking mercy and peace. Additionally, Christian interpretation often hearkens to the biblical scapegoat motif, viewing Jesus as bearing humanity's sins and carrying them away.

The title "King of the Jews" is applied to Jesus three times in the New Testament. It appears at the beginning of his life in the Nativity narratives and again at the end in the Passion, with dramatic consequences in both instances. The Magi from the East address the infant Jesus as King of the Jews, an announcement that prompts Herod to order the Massacre of the Innocents. Across all four Gospels, the designation figures into the charges against Jesus that culminate in his crucifixion, including the inscription placed on the cross.

Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a reactive gas whose sources span outdoor and indoor environments. Outdoor NO2 mainly originates from traffic and motor vehicles. Indoor NO2 exposure arises from cigarette smoke and from heating and cooking appliances that burn fuels such as butane or kerosene. In homes with gas stoves, indoor NO2 levels are at least three times higher than in homes with electric stoves. Occupational exposure occurs among workers in industries that use NO2, who are at risk for occupational lung diseases, and NIOSH has established exposure limits and safety standards to mitigate these risks. Workers in high-voltage settings, particularly those involving spark or plasma generation, are also at risk. In agricultural settings, silo environments can release NO2 from grain decomposition in silos, and chronic exposure can lead to silo-filler's disease, a form of lung damage.

Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown gas whose color arises from selective absorption of blue light in the visible spectrum, primarily in the 400–500 nm range, with absorption extending to shorter wavelengths and into the infrared. When radiation with wavelengths shorter than about 400 nm is absorbed, NO2 undergoes photolysis, producing nitric oxide and atomic oxygen. In the atmosphere, the liberated atomic oxygen can then react with molecular oxygen to form ozone.

The Guardian endorsed the United Kingdom's continued membership of the European Union in the 2016 referendum. Ahead of the 2019 European Parliament elections, the newspaper encouraged its readers to support pro-EU candidates, while it did not endorse any particular political party in those elections.

The Guardian has pursued digital diversification to broaden its audience. In 2004 it launched Guardian Soulmates, a dating website; the service was closed on 1 July 2020 amid shifts in the online dating landscape, including the rise of apps and free, rapid ways to meet people. Earlier, an American edition proposed to attract US-based readers under the banner Guardian America, but the project was abandoned in October 2009. More recently, in May 2022, The Guardian established an onion service on the Tor network, with technical assistance from Alec Muffett.

Khayal is an Urdu term borrowed from Arabic, conveying notions of imagination, thought, ideation, meditation, and reflection. It also denotes a song distinguished by imaginative and creative qualities in its conception and performance. The term reached the Indian subcontinent via Persian, reflecting historical linguistic and cultural exchanges. In music, the khayal form is conceived imaginatively, rendered with artistic and ornate execution, and marked by romantic appeal.

The Ghaznavid conquest brought Persian language and culture into northern India, and the Ghaznavids themselves were Turkic rulers based in Ghazni who traced political lineage to the Samanid dynasty of Bukhara. As Delhi emerged as a political center, it inherited Ghaznavid cultural institutions and literary practices, a process that helped spark a flourishing of letters and the arts. Mongol invasions subsequently forced poets to seek refuge and patronage at the Delhi royal court, reinforcing the city’s role as a hub of literary activity. In the early period, Persian poets such as Abu al-Faraj Runi and Mas'ud Sa'd Salman carried forward Samanid literary traditions, shaping the courtly milieu. Amir Khusrau (1253–1325), a North Indian-born poet raised within a Turco-Iranian milieu and serving at the courts of the Mamluks, Khaljis, and Tughlaqs, became closely associated with Delhi’s Chishti Sufi circle; although some scholars speculate that khayal was created by Khusrau, most regard the genre as the product of a gradual evolution within the Delhi Sultanate. Khayal is said to have developed from an ancient sadharani structure, with its melodic style drawing on the rupakalapti form. Later, the Sharqui rulers of Jaunpur patronized fine arts and khayal during the 14th–15th centuries, contributing to its continued growth and institutional support.

Sayed Shubbar Alawi is a Bahraini international footballer who made his senior international debut on 23 March 2009 in a 5–2 friendly victory over Zimbabwe. In December 2018, he was included in Bahrain's squad for the 2019 AFC Asian Cup.

Sayed Shubbar Ebrahim Alawi Hashem (Arabic: سيد شبر إبراهيم علوي هاشم; born 11 August 1985) is a Bahraini professional footballer who plays as a goalkeeper for Al Khaldiya and the Bahrain national football team.

Coal-fired generating stations can be supplied by multiple transport modes, including highway trucks, rail, river barges, collier ships, or coal slurry pipelines. Plants located adjacent to a coal mine may receive coal directly via an on-site conveyor belt, and they may also be served by large diesel-electric-drive trucks delivering coal to the facility.

Particulate matter in fossil fuel power plant emissions varies in chemical composition and particle size. In coal-fired facilities, the dominant form of PM is coal fly ash, which comprises the noncombustible constituents of coal remaining after combustion. Additionally, secondary sulfate and nitrate account for a substantial portion of PM emitted from coal-fired plants.

During the Vietnam War, soldiers wore the OG-107 olive drab fatigue uniforms. At the outset of the conflict, personnel displayed full-color shoulder sleeve insignia, white name tapes, and black-and-gold U.S. Army tapes. In 1966, the Army authorized subdued versions of the shoulder sleeve insignia patches, produced in green and black.

Shoulder sleeve insignia (SSI) were worn by nearly all major U.S. Army formations, including groups, field armies, corps, divisions, and many principal commands, serving as a distinctive emblem of unit identity. SSI designs frequently incorporated symbolism tied to the unit’s origins or history, with motifs chosen to reflect lineage or regional associations. For example, the 82nd Airborne Division adopted the letters "AA" to denote its All-American heritage, while the 29th Infantry Division used a blue-and-gray circular emblem symbolizing its mixed Union and Confederate state composition. Most units possessed unique patches, though armored formations, the I Armored Corps, and the U.S. Army Armor Center shared a common triangular motif that carried the unit number, a design that later received additional labels to indicate specific formations.

Haixinsha Station is a Guangzhou Metro station on the APM line. It is situated underground on Haixinsha Island, which hosted the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2010 Asian Games. The station entered service on 24 February 2011, roughly three months after the games concluded. The station's name is written in Chinese as 海心沙站, with the pinyin transcription Hǎixīnshā Zhàn and the Jyutping transcription hoi2sam1saa1 zaam6.

The 1989 Allsvenskan play-offs marked the eighth edition of the post-season competition for Sweden’s top football league. The four highest-placed teams from the Allsvenskan qualified for the play-offs. IFK Norrköping, finishing as league runners-up, emerged as champions by defeating Malmö FF, the Allsvenskan champions, in the final. The champion was decided through a final series conducted in a best-of-three format, a departure from the format used in prior years.

The 1989 Allsvenskan season featured twelve teams competing in the top tier of Swedish football. Malmö FF finished the league in first place, thereby winning the Allsvenskan title. The Swedish championship was decided through a playoff, in which IFK Norrköping prevailed to claim the national crown.
Backstory and VirusTotal have been made available to Google Cloud customers as elements of an Autonomic Security Operations solution, which also incorporates Looker and BigQuery.

Google Security Operations (Google SecOps), formerly Google Chronicle Security Operations, is a cybersecurity service within Google Cloud Platform. The service is designed as a specialized cloud layer integrated with Google's core infrastructure, enabling organizations to securely store, analyze, and query large volumes of security and network telemetry.

Satis is an ancient Egyptian goddess associated with Elephantine. Her name was originally written with hieroglyph S29, which depicts the shoulder knot of a linen garment, and later replaced by hieroglyph F29, the sign of Anuket's animal hide pierced by an arrow. Among her epithets are a designation linking her to Elephantine as its patroness, and another title interpreted as alluding to the river's swift current.

Satis, an ancient Egyptian goddess associated with the Nile and its floods, was sometimes conflated with Isis as well as Sopdet, the goddess of Sirius. The Egyptians linked Sirius (Sopdet) with the onset of the annual Nile inundation, a connection that informed the cultic associations surrounding Satis. In the interpretatio graeca of later periods, Satis was identified with Hera in Greek tradition and with Juno in Roman sources.

LGBTQ bullying encompasses harassment and discrimination linked to sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. In discussions of this phenomenon, some claims have been made that the selection of school subjects should align with a student’s sexual orientation or gender identity/expression. For instance, it has been suggested that science is better suited to heterosexual male students, whereas drama would be more appropriate for gay male students. Such assertions illustrate stereotyping and discrimination rooted in LGBTQ characteristics, and they form part of the broader context of LGBTQ bullying, underscoring the need for inclusive educational practices and anti-bullying measures.

Egale Canada conducted a survey of more than 3,700 Canadian high school students between December 2007 and June 2009, with the final report, Every Class in Every School, published in 2011. The study found widespread exposure to anti-LGBTQ language in schools, with 70% of respondents reporting daily hearing remarks that demean homosexuality and 48% reporting daily exposure to explicit homophobic slurs. Among heterosexual students, 58% (about 1,400 of 2,400) said such remarks upset them. The research further indicated that students not directly affected by homophobia, biphobia, or transphobia tended to be less aware of its prevalence, a pattern that aligns with empathy gaps in social pain where those not experiencing bullying underestimate its effects and may respond inadequately.

Concert residencies involve an artist delivering a series of performances at a single venue over an extended period, typically with a fixed schedule. Bruce Springsteen's New York residency, Springsteen on Broadway, generated more than $113 million from 236 performances held in locations away from Las Vegas. In a separate example, Billy Joel has maintained a monthly residency at Madison Square Garden since 2014, accumulating approximately $266.8 million in gross revenue. Taken together, these instances illustrate that highly successful, high-earning concert residencies are not exclusive to Las Vegas.

Liberace is credited with establishing the concept of a concert residency, tracing the idea to his 1944 Las Vegas debut. About a decade after that debut, he mounted his own Las Vegas show at the Riviera Hotel and Casino, and the engagement at the Riviera reportedly generated around $50,000 per week. After pursuing other projects in Los Angeles, Liberace returned to a Las Vegas residency, during which his earnings were said to be about $300,000 per week. He died in 1987 from AIDS-related complications.

Between late 2012 and early 2013, Songbird removed public access to its development resources, including the public SVN repository, the project wiki, and other source-code utilities. A Twitter survey conducted by Songbird suggested that POTI planned to close the desktop player source code. POTI reportedly intended to sell an updated version of the desktop player at a later date. That forthcoming version was expected to address a number of long-standing bugs and to fulfill feature requests from users who had felt ignored.

Songbird was an open-source, cross-platform media player and library management application that used Mozilla XULRunner for its user interface and the GStreamer framework for media playback. It ran on Windows and macOS, and in 2012 mobile versions for Android and iOS were released. Although Solaris and Linux had previously been supported, those platforms were later dropped. A fork named Nightingale was created to carry on development, offering compatibility across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Auction Co. experienced a data breach in February 2008, which was publicly disclosed two months later in April 2008. The compromised information included real names, user IDs, resident registration numbers, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, bank account details, and records of purchases and refunds. At first, the breach was estimated to affect about 11 million users. Later, it was claimed that the private information of all Auction members had been exposed, totaling roughly 18.6 million individuals. Following the incident, users filed a lawsuit against the company, but the court ruled that the company was not liable.

The Lower Mainland is a geographic region in southwestern British Columbia that includes the Fraser Valley Regional District, which lies to the east of the Metro Vancouver Regional District. The Fraser Valley Regional District comprises the cities of Abbotsford and Chilliwack, the district municipalities of Mission, Kent, and Hope, and the village of Harrison Hot Springs, along with numerous unincorporated areas in the Fraser Valley and along the western edge of the Fraser Canyon. The Fraser Canyon itself is not part of the Lower Mainland.

The Lower Mainland is a geographic and cultural region on the mainland coast of British Columbia, Canada. It generally encompasses the regional districts of Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. According to the 2021 Canadian census, the population is about 3.05 million, and the region includes sixteen of the province's thirty most populous municipalities. Collectively, these municipalities account for roughly 60 percent of British Columbia's total population.

FIFA Football 2003 introduces Club Championship Mode, enabling players to face seventeen of Europe’s top clubs in their own stadiums, with supporters providing unique chants and songs. A TV-style broadcast package delivers halftime and full-time highlights along with comprehensive analysis. The game adds a Freestyle Control feature that lets players flick the ball on and lay it off to teammates. The title offers greater likenesses of well-known players, such as Thierry Henry and Ronaldinho, and provides more realistic player responses.

FIFA Football 2003 received generally favorable reviews across most platforms, while the PlayStation version garnered average scores according to Metacritic, the review aggregator cited in coverage. On PC, the title was a runner-up for GameSpot's Best Sports Game award, with Madden NFL 2003 taking the honor.

On October 30, 2025, the Federal Bureau of Investigation subpoenaed Tucows, the registrar for the Archive.today domain, as part of a criminal investigation. The subpoena sought to identify the owner or owners of the archive.today domain name. Authorities did not disclose the specific nature of the investigation.

Archive.today is a web archiving service that preserves copies of web pages. During capture, pages are recorded at a fixed browser width of 1,024 pixels. The system inlines CSS, converting styles into inline declarations and thereby removing responsive design and selectors such as :hover and :active. Additionally, content generated by JavaScript during the crawling process is captured in a frozen state, producing static representations of dynamic elements.

In Aztec tradition, Ahuiateteo, also rendered as Āhuiatēteoh and Mācuīltōnalequeh, designates a quintet of deities associated with excess and pleasure. The group embodys both indulgence and the dangers that accompany it, serving as a personification of overindulgence’s risks. The five gods were invoked by diviners and mystics within ritual practices, reflecting their role in divination and esoteric traditions. They are linked with the Tzitzimimeh, a cohort of fearsome beings who symbolize death, drought, and war.

Arnaud de Rosnay, a French photographer and windsurfing pioneer, gained prominence for his open-ocean windsurfing expeditions and long-distance crossings conducted in or through conflict zones. He disappeared at sea in November 1984 in the Taiwan Strait. In 1981 he organized the first speedsailing competition, a 40-kilometre race held in Maui, which attracted about eighty competitors and saw de Rosnay finish second to Robby Naish. He is credited with inventing kite surfing in 1980 and with developing land sailing under the Speedsail concept in 1977. In 1979 he completed a 1,380-kilometre crossing across the Sahara.

Windsurfing's competitive landscape features one-design class racing, which enjoys worldwide popularity because of its relatively low costs and the longevity of equipment, allowing gear to remain in use for many years without mandatory class changes. By contrast, professional windsurf gear evolves quickly, with new setups appearing as often as every six months, and substantial performance advances often restricted to sponsorship-supported programs. The steady, uniform nature of one-design racing makes it accessible for recreation and, importantly, enables entrants with intermediate experience to compete on the same gear as Olympic-class athletes. Among racing formats, one-design classes are regarded as the most social. The most popular one-design classes today include Windsurfer (the original design, now augmented by Windsurfer LT), Mistral One Design, Bic-Techno (intended for youth development), and iQFoil, which is expanding rapidly.

Following the merger, Bernhard announced his retirement and sought to sell Amazing Stories in collaboration with Edward Ferman and Joel Davis, while Jonathan Post believed a deal had been reached but negotiations ultimately collapsed. Bernhard then approached George H. Scithers, who declined but connected him to Gary Gygax of TSR. On 27 May 1982 TSR, Inc. acquired the trademarks and copyrights of Amazing Stories. Scithers joined TSR as editor with the November 1982 issue and was later replaced by Patrick Lucien Price in September 1986, followed by Kim Mohan in May 1991. TSR ceased publication with the Winter 1995 issue. In 1997, shortly after TSR was acquired by Wizards of the Coast, the magazine was revived with Mohan as editor; the relaunch produced ten issues and included a celebration of the 600th issue in early 2000, though Locus described its distribution as weak. The final issue of the 1997 revival appeared in Summer 2000. Paizo Publishing subsequently acquired the title and launched a new monthly edition in September 2004; the February 2005 issue was the last printed, a March 2005 issue appeared in PDF, and in March 2006 Paizo announced that it would cease publication. In September 2011 the trademark was acquired by Steve Davidson. Two online issues appeared in July and August 2012, followed by another in 2014. Davidson relaunched print publication with the Fall 2018 issue, appointing Ira Nayman as editor. In 2022 Davidson stepped down as publisher, with former Creative Director Kermit Woodall succeeding in the role.

The inaugural issue of Amazing Stories, published in 1926 by Hugo Gernsback, consisted entirely of reprinted fiction and opened with Jules Verne’s Off on a Comet, which was serialized at the time. Verne's tale was regarded as one of his less scientifically plausible works, reflecting Gernsback's shift toward a mode of fiction that emphasized speculative science. The selection also featured H. G. Wells's "The New Accelerator" and Edgar Allan Poe's "The Facts in the Case of M. Valdemar," with Gernsback printing all three authors' names on the cover. In addition to these reprints, three newer stories were included: two that appeared in Gernsback's Science and Invention—"The Man from the Atom" by G. Peyton Wertenbaker and "The Thing from—'Outside'" by George Allan England—and a third contemporary tale, Austin Hall's "The Man Who Saved the Earth" from All-Story Weekly.

Sydenham railway station lies on the Windrush line of the London Overground. The London Overground services on this route are operated using Class 378 electric multiple units. In addition to these services, the operator Southern runs supplementary services along the same corridor, using Class 377 electric multiple units.

Sydenham railway station, located in London, was operated by the Southern Railway until nationalisation in 1948 after the Big Four era. From 1948 to 1982 it belonged to the Southern Region; following sectorisation, it became part of Network SouthEast and remained under that umbrella until privatisation. In May 1996, as part of the privatization process, station management transferred to Connex South Central, which was later stripped of the franchise due to poor financial management. In 2001 Govia South Central, operating as Southern, took over the franchise and management, with Southern remaining the sole train operator serving the station until 2010. In 2010 London Overground assumed management and began running services as part of the East London Line extension, now known as the Windrush line.

Nirvana's archival releases expanded in the 2000s, beginning with Live! Tonight! Sold Out!! being reissued on DVD in 2006, followed by the full MTV Unplugged in New York released on DVD in 2007. In November 2009, the band's 1992 Reading Festival performance appeared on CD and DVD as Live at Reading, issued alongside a deluxe 20th-anniversary edition of Bleach. Subsequently, DGC issued 20th-anniversary deluxe packages for Nevermind in September 2011, which included the Live at the Paramount performance. In September 2013, a 20th-anniversary deluxe package for In Utero was released, which included the Live and Loud concert.

In 2012, Nirvana’s Dave Grohl, Krist Novoselic, and Pat Smear joined Paul McCartney for the benefit concert 12-12-12: The Concert for Sandy Relief. The collaboration produced a new song co-written by McCartney and the Nirvana members, titled “Cut Me Some Slack,” and a studio recording of the track was later released on the Sound City soundtrack, the documentary directed by Grohl. On July 19, 2013, the same group performed with McCartney again during the encore of his Out There tour at Safeco Field in Seattle. That Seattle appearance marked the first time Nirvana members had performed there in more than fifteen years.
