In the 2003 Australian Open women's singles final, Serena Williams defeated her sister Venus Williams in three sets, 7–6(7–4), 3–6, 6–4, to claim her first Australian Open singles title. The victory marked Serena's fourth consecutive major singles title and completed the so‑called Serena Slam, comprising a non-calendar year Grand Slam alongside a career Grand Slam. Venus extended her streak of runner‑up finishes at majors to four in a row, all of which came at Serena’s expense in finals. The match also made the Williams sisters the first pair to meet in four consecutive Grand Slam finals in the Open Era, a feat later matched by Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic in 2011–2012. En route to the title, Serena saved two match points in the semifinals against Kim Clijsters, including a point when she trailed 1–5 in the third set.

The 2003 Australian Open – Women's singles event marked the final appearance of Monica Seles at the tournament. A four-time Australian Open champion, Seles was defeated in the second round by Klára Koukalová, the only occasion in her Australian Open career on which she exited before the quarterfinals. It also represented the second time she failed to reach the semifinals at the event. Across her Australian Open career, Seles posted a 43–4 record, a winning percentage of 91.5%.

The 2017 Cross-Strait CEO Summit was held in Nanjing on 6–7 November, with its theme centered on evolving circumstances, new business opportunities, and a refreshed mindset. The event was represented by Yu Zhengsheng, then chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Approximately 700 business leaders from both sides attended. By the conclusion, 29 agreements and memoranda of understanding had been signed in total.

The Cross-Strait CEO Summit (CSCS) is a cross-strait gathering that brings together business leaders from Mainland China and Taiwan to pursue collaboration and strengthen enterprise ties. An annual event, the summit alternates its venue between Nanjing in Mainland China and Taipei in Taiwan. The summit’s name is rendered in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and pinyin transliterations to reflect its bilingual presentation.

The music video for Adele's rendition of "Make You Feel My Love" was directed by Mat Kirby and released to music channels in late September 2008. It continues to be featured on Adele's official website.

The music video for the song Make You Feel My Love features Adele performing at the London Marriott Hotel Canary Wharf and was directed by Mat Kirkby. As of January 2025, it had accumulated more than 200 million views on YouTube.

Standards in the ISO/IEC family are distributed directly by ISO, with direct availability primarily in English, French, and Chinese. Outlets operated by national standards bodies also sell translated editions, and these translations are produced faithfully and published in several languages.

The ISO/IEC 27000 family is a collection of information security standards published jointly by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). It is also known as the ISMS Family of Standards, ISO27K, or the ISO 27000 series.

Southeast Papuan languages, also known as the Bird's Tail languages or the Papuan Peninsula languages, form a compact group of about six small language families within the Papuan language area. They are located on the Bird's Tail, the southeastern peninsula of New Guinea, and are classified within the Trans–New Guinea phylum.

California is widely regarded as a pivotal state in the 1916 United States presidential election, with incumbent Woodrow Wilson narrowly carrying the state by about 3,800 votes out of nearly one million ballots cast and earning its 13 electoral votes. The result in California thus proved decisive for the overall outcome; had the Republican nominee Charles Evans Hughes carried the state, he would have won the presidency.

During the 1916 United States presidential election, incumbent Democratic President Woodrow Wilson won re-election to a second term, becoming the first Democrat to serve consecutive terms since Andrew Jackson in 1832. His running mate, Vice President Thomas R. Marshall, was also elected to a second term, making him the first vice president from any party to do so since John C. Calhoun in 1828. The Wilson–Marshall ticket thus became the first incumbent ticket to win re-election since James Monroe and Daniel D. Tompkins in 1820.

The Platform Theatre is a venue in Norwich, Norfolk, England, located on the campus of City College Norwich (CCN). It features a large stage and raked seating for approximately 200 spectators. The theatre hosts performances by both student groups and professional companies.

The Medúlla Videos, released in 2005, is a music video DVD by Björk that collects five videos from her sixth studio album, Medúlla. Of the five clips, two were not issued as singles and are exclusive to the DVD edition. The video for "Desired Constellation" was used as a backdrop during Björk's 2003 Greatest Hits tour performances. A bonus feature presents a documentary about the making of the "Triumph of a Heart" video, which is partly a mockumentary and centers on auditions for bar patrons to provide noises and sound effects for the live video. Those sounds were later edited into a full remix on the "Triumph of a Heart" CD single, titled the "Audition Mix." It is Björk's only DVD release that includes subtitles.

The tetralemma, also known as the fourfold negation or catuskoti, denotes a four-part analytical scheme within the Indian logico-epistemological tradition, a lineage often identified in Western discourse as Indian logic. Buddhist philosophy has given extensive treatment to this framework, with prominent use by Nagarjuna and the Madhyamaka school, which developed sophisticated approaches to negation and emptiness. Within Madhyamaka, the Prasangika sub-school is a label employed by the Tibetan Buddhist logico-epistemological tradition to signify a particular methodological emphasis. The tetralemma also appears in the Nasadiya Sukta of the Rigveda, where it functions more as a mode of inquiry than as a formal logical instrument, and its deployment as a systematic logical device before Buddhism was comparatively rare.

Creighton Abrams commanded the 37th Tank Battalion within the 4th Armored Division, which served as the spearhead for General George S. Patton's Third Army during the 1944 European campaigns. Renowned as an aggressive armor commander, Abrams leveraged the speed and reliability of his tanks to secure small advantages and defeat German forces that possessed superior armor and firepower. He received the Distinguished Service Cross twice for extraordinary heroism, on September 20, 1944, and December 26, 1944. Patton publicly praised him, describing Abrams as the world champion tank commander.

Creighton Abrams was an American Army armor officer who figured prominently among the early contributors to the development of the United States Army's armored branch. In 1940 he served as a tank company commander and was assigned to the 1st Armored Division, reflecting his involvement in the unit during its formative period.

During the British administration of the Ionian Islands, thousands of Maltese laborers were relocated to the archipelago, where they were employed chiefly as builders and artisans. This migration contributed to the development of local infrastructure and crafts, and over time it laid the groundwork for the Corfiot Maltese community.

On 26 November 1850, John Detoratos Typaldos proposed in the Ionian Parliament the enosis of the Ionian Islands with the Kingdom of Greece. The proposal was signed by Gerasimos Livadas, Nadalis Domeneginis, George Typaldos, Frangiskos Domeneginis, Ilias Zervos Iakovatos, Iosif Momferatos, Telemachus Paizis, Ioannis Typaldos, Aggelos Sigouros-Dessyllas, and Christodoulos Tofanis. In 1862, the Radical party split into two factions, the United Radical Party and the Real Radical Party. During the period of British rule, William Ewart Gladstone visited the islands and recommended their reunion with Greece; the British government was chagrined by his recommendation.

Marrakesh Menara Airport is an international airport serving Marrakesh, the capital of the Marrakesh-Safi region in Morocco. Its IATA code is RAK and its ICAO code is GMMX. In Arabic it is named مطار مراكش المنارة and in French Aéroport de Marrakech-Ménara. The airport receives flights from Europe, Casablanca, and other Arab world nations, with services to North America beginning in 2024. In 2019 the airport handled over 6.3 million passengers.

Marrakesh Menara Airport features an aircraft parking apron covering 125,000 square metres (1,350,000 square feet), capable of accommodating up to fourteen Boeing 737s and four Boeing 747s simultaneously. A cargo terminal provides 340 square metres (3,700 square feet) of covered space. The field's primary runway is oriented 10/28 and measures 3,100 metres in length and 45 metres in width (approximately 10,000 by 150 feet). The facility is designed to receive all modern jetliners up to a Boeing 747. Navigation and landing are supported by an ILS Category II system, with radio navigation aids that include VOR, DME, and NDB.

From 10 July 1940 to 9 August 1944, the regime officially designated as the État français functioned as a French rump state during World War II. Commonly referred to as Vichy France or the Régime de Vichy, it was led by Marshal Philippe Pétain and established after France capitulated to Germany, deriving its name from the location of its government in the city of Vichy.

During World War II, German authorities opened internment camps for enemy aliens on French territory, in addition to camps run by the Vichy regime. In Alsace, under direct Reich administration, the Natzweiler camp was established, and it stands as the only concentration camp created by the Nazis on French territory. The camp included a gas chamber, which was used to exterminate at least 86 detainees, predominantly Jewish. The killings were carried out with the aim of obtaining a collection of undamaged skeletons for Nazi professor August Hirt.

Denis Dutton was a passionate advocate for public radio. In the early 1990s, he founded the lobby group The New Zealand Friends of Public Broadcasting, which arose in response to proposals to devolve control of New Zealand's two non-commercial public radio stations.

Denis Dutton founded Arts & Letters Daily in 1998, a web aggregation site that links to articles across literature, art, science, and politics, with concise teasers written by Dutton to introduce each linked piece. The service contributed to his standing as a highly influential media figure, and it has been described as the premier aggregator of well-written book reviews, essays, and other thought-provoking content in the realm of ideas. By curating a broad spectrum of viewpoints, the site helped popularize the internet as a forum for cutting-edge ideas rather than solely a vehicle for commerce or entertainment, a perspective highlighted by Steven Pinker, who characterized Dutton as a visionary for recognizing that a website could serve as a space for innovative intellectual discourse.

Levirate marriage is a form of union in which a widow may marry the deceased husband’s brother. The concept has intersected with modern policy in India, where in 2017 the Indian Army abolished a rule that restricted the payment of monetary allowances to widows of gallantry awardees if she married someone other than the late husband’s brother. Previously, the allowance was paid until the widow’s death or until she remarried, unless the new husband was the late husband's brother.

Levirate marriage in Islamic jurisprudence concerns a man marrying the widow of his deceased brother. Islamic law establishes rules governing marriage, including who may enter such unions. The Qur’an does not ban a husband from marrying his brother’s widow, and when this arrangement occurs it is regarded as a legitimate marriage under the same framework as other marriages, provided that the wife gives her consent. In addition, this form of marriage typically involves a separate, augmented dowry (mahr) beyond the standard dowry, reflecting the distinct contractual arrangement.

During the occupation of Western Armenia, the provisional government depended on Armenian volunteer units to support security and administration. Following the siege of Van in April 1915, it established an administrative framework to govern the territories and communities under its control. The leadership within this administration was predominantly drawn from the Armenian Revolutionary Federation. Aram Manukian, widely known as “Aram of Van,” emerged as the administration’s most famous governor.

On May 28, 1918, the Armenian Congress of Eastern Armenia proclaimed the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Armenia and declared its independence from the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic, signaling the emergence of a distinct Armenian state and the dissolution of the federation's authority over Armenian territories.

Genetically modified crops are plants whose genomes have been deliberately altered through biotechnological methods to express desirable traits. There is no documented evidence of ill effects from GM foods in human populations. Around the world, many countries require labeling of GM crops or GM foods to inform consumers. In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration does not label or distinguish between approved GM and non-GM foods. Moreover, the United States enacted a law requiring labeling regulations to be issued by July 2018, and permitted disclosure to occur through indirect means such as a phone number, a barcode, or a website rather than a direct statement on packaging.

Genetically modified crops employ a range of strategies to confer drought tolerance, including the introduction of regulatory genes that modulate physiological and biochemical responses to water deficit. A notable approach utilizes transcription factors from the HD-Zip I family, originally identified in drought-tolerant species such as sunflower. These regulatory genes elevate the expression of proteins involved in antioxidant defenses, help preserve cellular integrity, and improve water-use efficiency. Consequently, transgenic plants can endure periods of limited water with a comparatively smaller impact on growth and productivity.

Kutsa is a heroic figure in the Rigveda, associated with Indra's victory over the demon Śuṣṇa and with the sun's ascent. In some passages, Kutsa together with Atithigva and Āyu is said to have been defeated by Indra, a deed sometimes attributed to Tūrvayāṇa. In other verses, Kutsa and Atithigva are portrayed as friends or allies of Indra. Hillebrandt contends that the apparent contradictions can be reconciled by positing two distinct individuals named Kutsa in the Rigveda. The text also describes Kutsa as having defeated Smadibha, Tugra, and the Vetasus, and he is described as a descendant of Arjuna.

By 1881, the archaeologist Otto Tischler had drawn parallels between the Hallstatt culture and the Iron Age of the Northern Alpine region, basing his argument on brooches recovered from burial sites in southern Germany.

Scholars have proposed that the mountain peaks surrounding Hallstatt may have functioned as a large sundial and visual calendar for the Hallstatt culture, suggesting that topographic features were used to mark solar events and seasonal changes. A parallel arrangement is thought to have existed in the Vosges mountains during the Iron Age, known as the Belchen system. The Belchen system is believed to have incorporated dates associated with major Celtic festivals, such as Beltane, indicating a broader tradition of correlating landscape markers with calendrical and ritual timing among Celtic communities in western Europe.

The article on the 2008–09 DFB-Pokal presents the competition’s schedule and kick-off times, with allowances made for seasonal time changes. It notes that daylight saving time, observed as Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), was in effect through 25 October 2008. From 26 October 2008 to 28 March 2009, standard time, Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), was in use. Daylight saving time then resumed on 29 March 2009 and continued thereafter.

The 2008–09 edition of the DFB-Pokal employed a two-pot draw in the second round, allocating amateur clubs to pot 1 and professional clubs to pot 2. If one pot became exhausted, the remaining pairings were drawn from the other pot, with the first-drawn team hosting. From the subsequent rounds onward, draws were conducted from a single pot. In this one-pot phase, whenever an amateur club was drawn against a professional, the amateur was designated as the home team; in all other cases in the one-pot phase, the first-drawn team hosted.

Houlong railway station serves as a stop on the Taiwan Railways Administration's West Coast line, also known as the Coastal line. Located in Houlong Township, Miaoli County, Taiwan, the station is known in Chinese as 後龍車站 and is romanized as Hòulóng Chēzhàn.

During the War in Afghanistan, British forces, including the Army Air Corps and the Royal Air Force, employed thermobaric AGM-114N Hellfire missiles against Taliban targets. In the Syrian civil war, British military drones also deployed the AGM-114N Hellfire missiles. In the first three months of 2018, British drones fired 92 Hellfire missiles in Syria.

In September 2007, Russia detonated what it described as the largest thermobaric weapon ever produced, with officials claiming its explosive yield was equivalent to that of a small nuclear device. The ordnance was named the “Father of All Bombs” by Russia, and the move was presented as a response to the American MOAB bomb, or Massive Ordnance Air Blast. The MOAB acronym is commonly linked with the phrase “Mother of All Bombs,” and it has been noted as having, at one time, held the distinction of the most powerful non-nuclear weapon in history.

The peach is a deciduous tree or tree-like shrub. In stature, it is typically modest: rarely reaching about 10 meters in height, it more commonly grows to around 3 meters, with large specimens up to 4 meters. The crown spread is similar to the height, about 3–4 meters. Peach trees do not produce suckers and lack thorns. The root system is deep, with roots continuing to grow during winter.

Peach trees typically require relatively high nitrogen inputs compared with many other fruit tree species to support vigorous growth and fruit production. When regular fertilization is not maintained, the foliage may yellow and growth can become stunted. Among recommended amendments are blood meal, bone meal, and calcium ammonium nitrate.

An independent, double-blind evaluation carried out during 2004–2005 compared the ATRAC3 codec with Ogg Vorbis, AAC, and LAME VBR MP3. The test did not reference or disclose encoding parameters for the formats involved. In the results, ATRAC3 ranked last.

Adaptive Transform Acoustic Coding (ATRAC) was developed by Sony in collaboration with its LSI IC engineers to achieve rapid encoding while maintaining low power consumption. The design was oriented toward portable hardware constraints, distinguishing it from codecs intended for operation on general-purpose computers. It emphasizes processing smaller blocks of samples at a time to minimize memory usage. This approach, while beneficial for devices with limited memory, reduces compression efficiency and increases the required number of multiplications. Such trade-offs are typical in digital signal processing systems where memory constraints can outweigh the need for high multiplier performance.

Real Digital issued early test units to reviewers and a small contingent of beta testers in December 2011. By April 2014, production units had not yet appeared in high-street retail stores. The company announced an arrangement with Maplin Electronics to distribute the product, while production units were already carried by a select assortment of specialist online retailers.

Real Digital involved distributing several set-top boxes to testers and reviewers for evaluation. Fortec Star, as the initial hardware supplier, delivered late and with incomplete software, leading Maplin Electronics to cancel its orders with Fortec Star on account of the delays and partial software. During live demonstrations for retailers, the Real Digital electronic program guide and the list of television channels were demonstrated in operation. The graphical user interface of Real Digital received broad praise from observers for its design and usability.

Driven by growing demand for more connected vehicles, in-car entertainment systems have become increasingly sophisticated and feature-rich. Automakers, electronics and software suppliers, and Silicon Valley entrants such as Google and Apple participate in a mix of collaboration and competition to develop next-generation infotainment platforms. The overarching aim is to deliver interfaces that are user-friendly and safe to operate while driving. As a result, in-car entertainment and information systems have become more common in newer vehicle models. Automakers have also developed their own branded solutions, including Ford SYNC/MyFord Touch, Toyota Entune, Cadillac CUE, and FCA Uconnect.

In-car entertainment, or in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), refers to the hardware and software installed in automobiles that provide audio and video entertainment, as well as information and connectivity. The concept traces its origins to the traditional car radio and later cassette and compact disc players, but has expanded to encompass navigation, video playback, USB and Bluetooth interfaces, carputers, and in-car Internet access and Wi-Fi. Control interfaces have evolved from dashboard knobs and dials to steering-wheel controls, hands-free voice operation, touch-sensitive presets, and touchscreen interfaces. Many systems also incorporate safety-oriented cameras, including rearview and side cameras, to assist driving.

Originally introduced as Novell Linux Desktop (NLD), SUSE Linux Desktop (SLED) targets the business market. It is developed from a shared codebase with SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES) and other SUSE Enterprise products, and it includes GNOME Shell, LibreOffice, Evolution, along with a range of other open-source packages such as Dia, TigerVNC, and lftp. Like SLES, SLED is based on the openSUSE Tumbleweed line, and it also shares a common codebase with openSUSE Leap, reflecting its integration within the broader openSUSE ecosystem.

SUSE Package Hub is a supplementary repository that provides access to software that is not officially included in SUSE Linux Enterprise Server or is newer than the packages in the current SLE release. The hub is unofficial, and software distributed through its repositories does not receive commercial support from SUSE. Approximately 9,000 packages are available for SLE 12 and SLE 15, spanning architectures such as AArch64, ppc64le, s390x, and x86-64.

The Angachak Range features a harsh continental subarctic climate within its zone, characterized by extreme winter conditions and relatively cool summers. In January, temperatures typically range from about −35 °C to −31 °C (−31 °F to −24 °F). Summers are short and mild, with average July temperatures not exceeding 12 °C (54 °F). The region experiences frequent avalanche activity and regular snowstorms, reflecting persistent winter weather patterns and substantial snowfall.

The Angachak Range is a mountain range in Magadan Oblast of Russia’s Far Eastern Federal District. In Russian, the range is referred to as Хребет Ангачак and is sometimes called Большой Ангачак, or Big Angachak. The closest urban center is Susuman, and the nearest air link is Susuman Airport.

Indian classical music encompasses two major traditions—Carnatic, predominant in the southern peninsula, and Hindustani, widespread across the northern, eastern, and central regions. Its fundamental concepts include shruti (microtonal divisions of the octave), swaras (the seven notes), alankaras (ornamentations), raga (melodic frameworks for improvisation), and tala (cyclic rhythmic patterns). The octave is divided into 22 shrutis, which are not all equal and correspond approximately to a quarter tone relative to Western tuning. The seven notes, collectively called the Saptasvaras, are Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni, and are traditionally associated with the syllables Shadja, Rishabha, Gandhara, Madhyama, Panchama, Dhaivata, Nishada; their Western equivalents are Do, Re, Mi, Fa, So, La, Ti. These seven svaras serve as the exclusive pitch material for both Hindustani and Carnatic music and are essential to the construction and rendition of a raga. In their unaltered form they are Shuddha (pure); when modified, they take on Komal (flat) or Tivra (sharp) variants. Sa and Pa are always Shuddha, known as Achal svaras, while Re, Ga, Ma, Dha, and Ni may appear as Komal or Tivra (Chal svaras).

During the late 1980s, Indian-British musicians formed the Asian Underground, a movement that integrated Indian and Western musical traditions. From the 1990s onward, Nadaka, a Canadian-born artist who spent much of his life in India, has pursued an acoustic fusion that merges Indian classical music with Western genres. Krishna Das blends Bhakti sangeet with Western non-Indian music, producing records that reflect his musical sadhana. Indo-Canadian artist Vandana Vishwas has also incorporated Western musical elements, notably in her 2013 album Monologues.

Korean cuisine includes several well-known dishes, among them bibimbap and naengmyeon. Bibimbap, a popular Korean dish, derives its name from the Korean words for "mixed rice" and refers to a preparation in which rice is combined with meat, vegetables, and red pepper paste. Naengmyeon is another popular Korean dish consisting of cold noodles.

Korea is the birthplace of Taekwon-Do, a martial art and sport that is widely regarded as the nation’s most prominent form of physical discipline. It integrates fighting techniques with self-defence, competitive sport, and conditioning. Taekwon-Do was demonstrated at the 1988 Seoul Olympics and later became an official Olympic medal event at the 2000 Sydney Games. The two leading international governing bodies for the discipline, the International Taekwon-Do Federation and the World Taekwondo Federation (now World Taekwondo), were both founded in Korea.

Way of the Li Family examines Li Kuan at length because his pupils sustain his tradition, and his teachings have spread beyond the immediate circle to the lands south of the Yangtze, where roughly a thousand followers adhere to his methods, unaware that their approach is too shallow to attain true Daoist transcendence. The author aims to alert readers to this deficiency and to warn about the stagnation and beguiling nature of such teachings. While there is no shortage of doctrines in the world that resemble Li Kuan, they are not his, and the author briefly notes these analogous doctrines to inform future generations who may not recognize their flaws.

According to a passage in the second section of the Baopuzi, the founder of the Lijia Dao, a Daoist lineage, is Li A, a diviner by trade. Li A is described as having originated from Shu, the western state corresponding to present-day Sichuan Province.

Belfast's education governance was reshaped in 2006 when the Belfast Education and Library Board was incorporated into the consolidated Education Authority for Northern Ireland. In Belfast, the Authority administers 156 primary and 48 secondary schools, including 18 grammar schools. The city's education system has shown substantial disparities in outcomes, with around 30% of school leavers not attaining 5 GCSEs A*-C, including Maths and English; among pupils eligible for free school meals, the figure rises to more than 50%.

Belfast contains more than forty parks, including the Botanic Gardens in the Queen's Quarter, which is among the city’s oldest and most popular. Established in 1828 and developed during the 1830s to a design by Sir Charles Lanyon, the gardens feature the Palm House, an early example of a curvilinear cast-iron glasshouse. Within the same grounds lies the Tropical Ravine, a humid jungle glen erected in 1889 and recently restored. The Botanic Gardens also include rose gardens and host public events such as live opera broadcasts and pop concerts.

The South Pacific Gyre features a basin-scale, counterclockwise circulation driven by the interplay of trade winds and the Coriolis force, a pattern that tends to isolate the gyre’s center from nutrient upwelling. This isolation yields persistently low nutrient concentrations at the surface and extremely low primary productivity within the central region. The limited supply of nutrients is reinforced by scarce aeolian inputs from Southern Hemisphere landmasses, which reduces nutrient delivery to the center. Consequently, the flux of organic material to the seafloor (marine snow) is very low, and both biogenic and aeolian deposition are subdued, resulting in slow sediment accumulation. The center records sedimentation rates of about 0.1–1 meters per million years (roughly 0.3–3.3 feet per Myr). Sediment thickness ranges from 1 to 70 meters, thinning toward the center where deposits lie atop basement basalts toward the seafloor. The combination of low particle flux and productivity also yields exceptionally clear seawater within the gyre.

The South Pacific Gyre, a vast oligotrophic region of the central Pacific Ocean, exhibits a scenario in which deep-ocean benthic microbial life typically relies on organic carbon exported from surface waters. In areas where sediments are poor in organic material, such as this gyre, subsurface benthic communities rely on alternative primary energy sources rather than surface-derived organic matter. An illustrative example of such an energy source is molecular hydrogen (H2), which can sustain subsurface microbial processes in these settings.

A provision involving HSN enabled Press to address transmission problems, and a Federal Aviation Administration settlement permitted the construction of a taller tower about 1.4 miles away, reflecting the company's approach to strengthening its signal. Press's strategy centered on acquiring additional facilities to expand and improve its transmission capabilities. In September 1987, Press acquired WRES, broadcast on channel 18 in Cocoa, and donated the station to Brevard Community College (BCC). As part of the arrangement, BCC received the station’s facilities, $1 million in operating funds, and $240,000 to form partnerships with the University of Central Florida, the Florida Institute of Technology, and public schools. BCC agreed to eventually participate in a channel swap with Press Broadcasting. Two months later, Press agreed to acquire the construction permit for WCLU (channel 68, Clermont), which would complete the other half of the proposed channel exchange. Robert McAllan, Press’s vice president of broadcasting, stated that the channel 68 permit purchase marked the culmination of a two-year search for improved transmission facilities for WMOD.

HSN assigned its option to purchase WMOD to Blackstar Communications in December 1987, and Blackstar Communications, a Black-owned firm controlled by John D. Oxendine, subsequently exercised that option. The assignment formed part of a broader affiliation in which Blackstar acquired HSN-owned KHSP in Portland, Oregon, with HSN becoming a silent investor in Blackstar. Blackstar’s investors, including Wesley S. Williams Jr., were involved with a venture capital fund established by the National Association of Broadcasters. In April 1988 Blackstar assumed control of WMOD, and on April 20, 1988 began broadcasting home shopping around the clock. In May 1988 the station’s call sign was changed to WBSF, while the press retained the syndicated programming inventory and used it to launch WKCF on channel 68 in December 1988.

Kevin Holness served as the first head coach of the Saskatoon Accelerators, a team in the Canadian Major Indoor Soccer League. He resigned prior to the start of the 2009–10 season. He is currently the technical director for FC Regina, based in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Kevin Holness represented Canada at the 1987 FIFA U-16 World Championship, appearing in all three of the nation's matches. The tournament was held in Canada. He was part of a Canadian side that also featured Paul Peschisolido and Carl Fletcher.

Novak Djokovic defeated Andy Murray in the 2016 Australian Open men's singles final, securing the title with a 6–1, 7–5, 7–6(7–3) victory. The win gave Djokovic his sixth Australian Open championship, equalling Roy Emerson for the most in the tournament's history, and marked his eleventh major overall. It was the fourth Australian Open final contested between Djokovic and Murray. Murray's defeat made him the second Open Era player to lose five finals at a single major, following Ivan Lendl at the US Open, a record later surpassed by Djokovic when he dropped his sixth US Open final in 2021. Murray remains the only player to have reached five finals at one major without ever winning the title.

Herbert Kretzmer wrote the book and lyrics for the West End musical Our Man Crichton, which was composed by David Lee and based on J. M. Barrie's satirical play The Admirable Crichton; the production starred Kenneth More and Millicent Martin. He later collaborated with composer Laurie Johnson to write the lyrics for the large-scale comedy parody The Four Musketeers, which ran for more than a year at the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, with Harry Secombe in the role of d'Artagnan.
Herbert Kretzmer contributed television criticism to the Daily Mail from 1979 to 1987, and for this work he earned two national press awards, including the TV Critic Of The Year accolade in 1980.
Cyclones.tv aired eight football games on traditional television, with the final such broadcast taking place on December 1, 2018, when Iowa State hosted Drake.

Cyclones.tv is a regional sports network and streaming platform dedicated to Iowa State University athletics. It was founded in 2012 and marked its first on-air date on August 31, 2013, operating exclusively to cover ISU sports. Historically, the service aired a variety of live events and carried a broad slate of third-tier programming, including one non-conference football game per year, several home non-conference men’s basketball games, and most home events in women’s basketball, volleyball, softball, women’s soccer, and wrestling. Following the launch of Big 12 Now on ESPN+, the offering was expected to shift toward primarily providing game replays, coaches’ shows, short features, and historical pieces rather than live events.

Originally slated to be launched in July 2013 with delivery planned for 2015, the USS Gerald R. Ford encountered production delays that pushed its launch to October 11, 2013. The ship’s naming ceremony was subsequently rescheduled to November 9, 2013, and the delivery date was later moved to February 2016.

USS Gerald R. Ford, the lead ship of its class, was described as structurally halfway complete in August 2011, with construction reported to be 75 percent complete by April 2012. On May 24, 2012, the waterline was completed and the lower bow section was lifted into place, marking the 390th lift of an estimated 500 lifts. By November 8, 2012, Huntington Ingalls Industries issued a press release stating that structural completion had reached 87 percent, and by December 19, 2012 the figure stood at 90 percent. In total, approximately 446 of the roughly 500 structural lifts had been completed.

ISO 31-12 is a component of the broader ISO 31 standard concerning quantities and units. The development of these standards involved IEC 60027, which served as the second international standard in the area. Through a collaborative revision by ISO and IEC, ISO 31 and IEC 60027 were unified into a single joint standard published as ISO/IEC 80000—Quantities and Units. Within ISO/IEC 80000, the quantities and equations used with the SI system are designated as the International System of Quantities (ISQ). Consequently, ISO/IEC 80000 supersedes ISO 31 and portions of IEC 60027.

Within the United States, several national guidance documents govern the use of SI units, including NIST SP 811, NIST SP 330, NIST SP 814, IEEE/ASTM SI 10, and SAE J916. These publications address many aspects of ISO 31-0, providing practical guidance for measurement and unit usage, but they do not offer the comprehensive catalog of quantities and units defined in the remaining parts of ISO 31.

The article concerns the compilation The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time, a ranked survey of influential recordings across popular music. Among the entries, the briefest tracks are Rave On! by Buddy Holly, 1:47; Great Balls of Fire by Jerry Lee Lewis, 1:52; and C'mon Everybody by Eddie Cochran, 1:53.

The list titled The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time places The Beatles as the most represented act, with 23 songs included. In addition to performances by the group, John Lennon, Paul McCartney, and George Harrison are also represented as solo artists. Lennon is the only artist to appear twice in the top ten, counting both his Beatle period and his solo work. Other acts by representation count include the Rolling Stones (14), Bob Dylan (13), Elvis Presley (11), and U2 (8), with The Beach Boys (7) and Jimi Hendrix (7) also well represented. Further contributions come from Led Zeppelin (6), Prince (6), Sly and the Family Stone (6), James Brown (6), Chuck Berry (6), Elton John (5), Ray Charles (5), The Clash (5), The Drifters (5), Buddy Holly (5), and The Who (5).

Turkish art in the Anatolian Seljuk period is defined by a architectural decoration program that concentrates on entrance portals, windows, and mosque mihrabs. Stone-carving functioned as a central decorative medium, drawing on motifs from earlier Iranian stucco as well as local Byzantine and Armenian styles, with muqarnas employed as a feature of the ornamentation. Notable examples include the madrasas of Sivas and the Ince Minareli Medrese in Konya. The Great Mosque and Hospital complex of Divriği is distinguished by extravagant high-relief stone decoration around its entrances and its mihrab. Syrian-style ablaq striped marble appears on the entrance portals of the Karatay Medrese and the Alaeddin Mosque in Konya. Anatolian architecture also innovated tile revetments that cover entire surfaces independently of other decoration, a development exemplified by the Karatay Medrese.

Turkish art developed within the broader framework of Islamic art, drawing on earlier Persian precedents while forging a distinctly Turkish sensibility. In the Ottoman period, the court eagerly collected Chinese porcelain, a taste that informed decorative strategies and motifs across various media. Within manuscript arts, Ottoman miniature painting and the related illumination traditions address both figurative imagery and abstract ornament, forming a continuum of pictorial and ornamental practices. Scholarship generally treats manuscripts as distinct genres, yet individual codices frequently bring together multiple genres and styles on a single page or within the same manuscript.

Quraysh bin Badran, also known as Alam al-Din, served as the Arab emir of Mosul. At first he acknowledged Seljuk overlordship, but subsequently he came into conflict with the Seljuks, resulting in a temporary expulsion from Mosul. He later aligned with the Mamluk Basasiri and accompanied them during the late-1058 seizure of Baghdad, a move followed by the Seljuks’ retaking of the city in 1059. Quraysh died in 1061, and his throne was inherited by his son Muslim ibn Quraysh.

In 1077, Sharaf al-Dawla Muslim joined Tutush I’s campaign to capture Aleppo as Malik-Shah I’s vassal during Sabiq ibn Mahmud’s rule over the Mirdasid-leaning city. He was personally fond of Sabiq, opposed the Seljuk takeover of Aleppo, and admonished Kilab chiefs for inviting Turkic foreigners against kin. He persuaded the Kilab to defect from Tutush’s army and facilitated the reconciliation of Waththab and Shabib with Sabiq, bringing them into his alliance in Aleppo. Before withdrawing from the siege, Muslim entered Aleppo through Bab al-Iraq and permitted his troops to provide provisions to the residents. Tutush continued the assault and had requested reinforcements from Malik Shah I prior to Muslim’s departure. On his return to Mosul, Muslim encountered about 1,000 Seljuk reinforcements at Sinjar, failing to deter them and warning Sabiq of their approach. Sabiq then sought aid from Kilabi chief Abu Za’ida Muhammad ibn Za’ida, who led a coalition of Arab tribesmen to ambush and rout the Seljuk forces at Wadi Butnan, killing most of them. This victory prompted Tutush to abandon the campaign against Aleppo.

Kep Province, in southwestern Cambodia, contains a notable cluster of mid-20th-century modernist villas constructed between 1953 and 1970, representing a distinctive post-French colonial development in Cambodian architecture. The projects were designed by Cambodian architects Vann Molyvann and Lu Ban Hap. They are regarded as emblematic of Cambodia's golden age of architectural modernism. The design blends elements of the modern movement—such as Bauhaus, Neutra, and Le Corbusier—with traditional Khmer architectural forms. Supported by King Norodom Sihanouk, the initiative helped give rise to what is known as New Khmer Architecture.

Located in Kep Province, Koh Tonsay is a major tourist attraction for the region. The island hosts approximately eight basic guest houses operated by Khmer-run enterprises. About five restaurants on Koh Tonsay mainly serve fresh seafood, including crabs, shrimp, and fish. Day visitors contribute to daytime activity and typically depart around 4 pm; by sunset, only a small number of overnight guests remain. Electricity on the island is supplied by generators from 6 to 9 pm.

Solutions are homogeneous mixtures formed when a solute dissolves in a solvent. By contrast, many liquids are immiscible, failing to form a single phase when combined. Oil and water exemplify this immiscibility, as they do not produce a true solution. In environmental contexts, petroleum released from a damaged tanker typically does not dissolve in seawater; instead, it remains as a separate liquid layer, owing to its density being lower than that of water, which causes the petroleum to float on the surface.

Salts dissociate in polar solvents to form positively and negatively charged ions. The ions are attracted to the opposite ends of solvent molecules by ion–dipole interactions, which help stabilize them in the liquid phase. In water, this stabilization manifests as hydration, with ions becoming encased by a surrounding shell of water molecules. A common instance of this process is the dissolution of salt in water, yielding an aqueous salt solution. Such solutions function as electrolytes, because the dissolved ions are mobile and can conduct electricity. When salts dissolve in water, ion pairing—where oppositely charged ions form loose associations—can occur and must be considered to accurately describe their behavior in solution.

Miaotou station, initially planned as Miaotou Lu station, is a Guangzhou Metro station on Line 5. The name was shortened to Miaotou station on 27 February 2023 as part of the eastern extension of Line 5. The station completed the three-rights transfer on 31 October 2023, and it opened to the public on 28 December 2023.

Miaotou station is a Guangzhou Metro facility on Line 5, located underground on the northeast side of the intersection of Huangpu East Road and Longtou Road in Huangpu District, Guangzhou. The station commenced operations on 28 December 2023 as part of the eastern extension of Line 5. In Chinese, the station is written 庙头站 in Simplified Chinese and 廟頭站 in Traditional Chinese, and it is romanized as Miàotóu zhàn in Pinyin, with the Cantonese Yale reading Miuhtàuh Jaahm.

California has a distinctive political culture and is widely regarded as a trendsetter in social norms and national politics. Its electorate is perceived as more liberal than that of many other states, particularly in inland regions. In federal elections, the state contributed a large share of Democratic votes: in the 2016 presidential race it posted the third-highest proportion of Democratic ballots nationwide, after the District of Columbia and Hawaii, and in 2020 it ranked sixth, behind DC, Vermont, Massachusetts, Maryland, and Hawaii. According to the Cook Political Report, the state contains five of the 15 most Democratic congressional districts in the United States, reflecting its substantial representation of Democratic-leaning districts at the federal level.

California maintains the largest state judiciary in the United States, numbering roughly 1,600 judges, a figure that exceeds the federal system’s roughly 840 judges. The state's highest court is the Supreme Court of California, which consists of seven justices. The California Courts of Appeal act as the principal intermediate appellate tribunals, while the California Superior Courts function as the primary trial courts. Justices on both the Supreme Court and the Courts of Appeal are appointed by the governor and must stand for retention by voters in elections held at 12-year intervals.

IEC 62325 comprises standards that govern communications within deregulated energy markets. It is based on the Common Information Model (CIM), providing a shared semantic framework for market-related information exchanges. The standard suite forms part of the IEC TC57 reference architecture for electric power systems, ensuring alignment with other power-system standards. The ongoing development and upkeep are overseen by IEC TC57 Working Group 16 (WG16).

Wilhelm Eduard Weber (German pronunciation: [ˈveːbɐ], commonly rendered as WEB-er or VEY-ber) was a German physicist born on 24 October 1804 and who died on 23 June 1891. He is known for his collaborative work with Carl Friedrich Gauss, and together they co-invented what is regarded as the first electromagnetic telegraph.

Wilhelm Eduard Weber, in collaboration with Rudolf Kohlrausch, established in 1855 that the numerical value of the ratio between electrostatic and electromagnetic units of measurement matches the speed of light, thereby lending empirical support to James Clerk Maxwell’s conjecture that light is an electromagnetic phenomenon. The result contributed to the development of Weber’s own theory of electrodynamics, shaping his approach to how moving charges and fields interact. The symbol c for the speed of light was first introduced in their 1856 Kohlrausch–Weber paper.

Built on Government Hill in 1679, the structure served as a watchtower and defensive fortress guarding the harbor of Saint Thomas. Danish garrisons used it to monitor the approaches of enemy ships from the sea. It was originally named Skytsborg Tower, and it was later renamed in honor of the English pirate Edward Teach, who is more commonly referred to as Blackbeard.

Buck Island lies to the south of Saint Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands and forms part of the area's maritime landscape. In 1969 the island was transferred to the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, which administers it as a protected area. It serves as an important habitat for migratory birds, supporting a range of species during their seasonal movements. The island also features a lighthouse originally built by the Danish, one of the three Danish-built lighthouses remaining in the U.S. Virgin Islands.
TA-CD is a vaccine. It does not affect the underlying neurobiological cause of addiction, and this lack of effect may account for the failure observed in clinical trials.

TA-CD is an experimental immunotherapy for cocaine dependence that operates similarly to a conventional vaccine. It uses a cocaine-like hapten linked to a large carrier protein to provoke the production of antibodies, which circulate in the bloodstream. These antibodies bind cocaine, forming complexes too large to cross the blood–brain barrier, thereby preventing the drug from reaching brain receptors. As a result, the euphoric effects and the associated dopamine release are blocked. The vaccine does not reduce the user’s desire for cocaine; it alters only the pharmacological effects by preventing cocaine’s central nervous system impact.

By December 2021, the Seattle metropolitan area was home to ten Fortune 500 companies. Notable firms headquartered in the region include Amazon, ranked No. 2; Costco Wholesale, No. 12; Microsoft, No. 15; Starbucks, No. 125; Paccar, No. 159; Nordstrom, No. 289; Weyerhaeuser, No. 387; Expeditors International, No. 299; Alaska Airlines, No. 459; and Expedia, No. 500.

During the Mesozoic Era, the climate is typically described as greenhouse and glaciation was once regarded as absent; however, newer research has uncovered evidence for brief glacial episodes in the Early Cretaceous, with glacial periods identified specifically in the Valanginian, Hauterivian, and Aptian stages. The discovery of ice-rafted dropstones implies that Northern Hemisphere ice sheets may have extended as far south as the Iberian Peninsula during Hauterivian and Aptian times. In the remainder of the era, ice masses largely vanished, though reports from the Turonian remain disputed. A late-phase resurgence of ice and sea ice appears to have occurred near the end of the Maastrichtian, just prior to the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

An ice age refers to the climatic fluctuations that have characterized the Quaternary period, which began about 2.6 million years ago and continues to the present. Throughout this era, Earth’s climate has swung between prolonged cold phases, called glacials, and warmer intervals, known as interglacials. Glacial periods typically endure around 100,000 years, whereas interglacial periods last roughly 10,000 to 15,000 years. The last pronounced cooling within this pattern culminated in the Last Glacial Period, whose cold phase ended about 10,000 years ago. Today, Earth remains in an interglacial phase of the Quaternary, scientifically identified as the Holocene.

The Scuola Italiana Statale di Atene, as of 2015, had 27 teachers and 218 students. The student body is predominantly composed of individuals from mixed Italian–Greek families, while a larger minority comes from nationalities other than Greek or Italian, with Albanians representing the largest portion of this group. A smaller segment comprises Italians temporarily residing in Greece, and another small group consists of Greek students who had previously lived in Italy and attended schools there. The teaching staff includes contract teachers, supplementary teachers, and personnel seconded by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE).

Scuola Italiana Statale di Atene, officially established in 1956, operated by 1968 as a two-section institution encompassing Italian and Greek curricula, and that year the sections were merged so that students were educated under both frameworks. Students were entitled to sit examinations for either the Greek Apolytirion or the Italian Maturità. The school's headquarters remained at Casa d'Italia, 47 Patission Street, until 1972, when it moved to a Vatican-owned building, a former seminary, at 18 Mitsaki Street in Ano Patissia. In 1974 the two sections were re-established as separate entities, and in 2015 the Greek section was closed.

In the Australian higher education system, the Bachelor of Science (BSc) generally spans three to four years. Those seeking to pursue a PhD typically must complete an honours year or undertake a master’s by research as a prerequisite for doctoral study.

In Ireland, the traditional Bachelor of Science designation was restructured, with the degree now awarded as BSc (Hons) after four years and the BSc (Ord) conferred after three years. At the University of Oxford, the BSc historically functioned as a postgraduate qualification rather than an undergraduate degree, and the postgraduate BSc at Oxford has since been renamed MSc and remains actively awarded.

Within the framework associated with The Cathedral and the Bazaar, beta testers are regarded as an important asset in software development. Recognizing their value tends to boost their motivation to contribute, resulting in more substantial and frequent input from them. Consequently, beta testers themselves become a more valuable asset, establishing a positive feedback loop that strengthens the overall development process.

In the Cathedral model of software development, the source code is disclosed only when a formal release is issued, while work conducted between releases remains accessible only to a restricted, exclusive group of developers. GNU Emacs and GCC are cited as examples of projects that follow this approach.

Valerie Baker Fairbank began her judicial career on the Los Angeles Municipal Court, where she served from 1986 to 1987. She then served on the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles from 1987 to 2007, before being appointed to the federal bench in 2007.

Valerie Baker Fairbank was born in Minneapolis, Minnesota. She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 1971, and a Master of Arts degree from the same institution in 1972. She then obtained a Juris Doctor degree from the University of California, Los Angeles School of Law in 1975.

Rama is the central figure in three of the fourteen Vaishnava Upanishads. The texts in which he is prominently featured are the Rama Rahasya Upanishad, the Rama Tapaniya Upanishad, and the Tarasara Upanishad.

Rama is a central figure in the Ramayana whose narrative reflects religious beliefs, social ideals, and ethical principles of ancient Indian society. Some scholars consider Rama a composite figure that embodies virtues valued in that culture. The Ramayana serves both as a sacred text and as a cultural artifact, illustrating how religious narratives function within daily life. Legends about Rama have shaped India's collective consciousness and ethical frameworks over centuries. Scholar Ariel Glucklich contends that Rama operates as a historical narrative and as a moral and spiritual teaching that helps shape cultural identity and religious beliefs.

A petition refers to a formal request seeking some action to be taken. It is commonly directed toward a government official or a public institution. When directed to a deity, such petitions constitute supplication, a specific form of prayer.

In common usage, a petition refers to a formal request directed to an official or governmental body, typically presented as a document signed by a substantial number of supporters. Although often in written form, petitions may also be conveyed orally. With advances in digital communication, petitions can be circulated and submitted over the Internet.
An international draft standard for the Graphical Kernel System (GKS) was circulated for review in September 1983, and the standard was ratified in 1985, making it the first ISO graphics standard.

The Graphical Kernel System (GKS) provides drawing facilities for two-dimensional vector graphics, with particular suitability for charting tasks. The interface calls are designed to be portable across programming languages, graphics devices, and hardware platforms. Consequently, applications developed with GKS are readily portable to a wide range of platforms and devices.

The 1975 Milan–San Remo was the 66th edition of the classic cycling race, held on 19 March 1975 with a start in Milan and a finish in San Remo. The event was won by Belgian rider Eddy Merckx, who rode for the Molteni team.

Dishonest or reckless conduct by a director may attract criminal liability, but such liability is created by statute rather than by the general common law; there is no criminal liability for this conduct under the common law.

Many jurisdictions impose a statutory obligation on directors to disclose any personal interests in connection with the company's transactions. The duty is directed at individuals serving as directors and is intended to safeguard against conflicts of interest in corporate dealings. Failure to disclose such interests can lead to penalties, including a fine.

Tony Graham (tennis) is a professional tennis player who competed on the professional circuit and captured two doubles titles over the course of his career. He attained a career-high singles ranking of world No. 100 in 1980 and achieved his peak in doubles at world No. 88 in 1981.

The 1980 Iowa Democratic presidential caucuses involved precinct-level meetings that did not directly elect delegates to the national convention. These caucuses served as the first test of strength in the 1980 Democratic presidential primaries, establishing the initial gauge of candidate support in the contest.

The 1980 Iowa Democratic presidential caucuses were the initial step in the process of selecting Iowa's delegates to the Democratic National Convention for that year. The proceedings began with precinct caucuses on January 21, which elected delegates to county conventions. On March 8, the county conventions selected delegates to both the state and the congressional district conventions. At the district conventions held on April 19, 34 of Iowa's 60 delegates to the Democratic National Convention were chosen. The remaining 16 delegates were then elected at the state convention on June 14.

Since 2000, Hollywood has undergone significant revitalization driven by private investment and public planning, contributing to notable gentrification in the district. Between 2001 and 2016, the area added more than 1,200 hotel rooms, reflecting a substantial expansion of lodging capacity and tourism infrastructure. In 2019, planning authorities approved about 4,000 new apartment units and more than thirty low- to mid-rise development projects, signaling continued densification and growth of the built environment in Hollywood.

Upon its annexation into the City of Los Angeles, Prospect Avenue was renamed Hollywood Boulevard, and the district adopted a new street numbering scheme. The change involved a comprehensive renumbering of addresses within the newly incorporated area; for example, the former 100 Prospect Avenue at Vermont Avenue was redesignated as 6400 Hollywood Boulevard, and the former 100 Cahuenga Boulevard at Hollywood Boulevard was redesignated as 1700 Cahuenga Boulevard.

Scout Electromedia developed the modo handheld wireless device, a portable platform that delivered up-to-date entertainment information. The product was targeted at urban youth and was available in New York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles.

Scout Electromedia, originally established as Scout Electronics, was a San Francisco-based wireless consumer products company that operated in the late 1990s. It was founded by Dan Bomze, William Cockayne, and Geoff Pitfield.

The final three berths in the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup qualification were decided through a ten-team playoff tournament, which also functioned as a test event to assess New Zealand's hosting preparations in advance of the Women's World Cup.

For the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup, Africa's qualifying competition culminated with the 2022 Africa Women Cup of Nations, held from 2 to 23 July 2022, which served as the final tournament for qualification. The tournament consisted of three groups of four teams. The eight teams advancing to the knockout stage were the top two finishers in each group (six teams) and the two best third-placed teams. The semi-finalists earned qualification to the World Cup, while the quarter-final losers entered a one-match repechage, with the victors advancing to the inter-confederation play-offs.

Talking Footy is a program whose theme music underwent a series of changes during its relaunches. In 2014, the relaunch saw the original lyrics brought back, although only the second verse was initially utilized. By 2018, the piece had been pared down to an instrumental version, with only the final three lyrics retained at the end. In the 2023 relaunch, the theme was dropped entirely.

Talking Footy is a television discussion program produced for the Seven Network. It is hosted by Luke Darcy and features a panel that includes Wayne Carey, Tim Watson, and Jacqui Felgate, with additional panellists such as Brian Taylor, Campbell Brown, Sam McClure, and Mick Warner. The program is broadcast from Seven's Docklands studios in Melbourne.
During the War of Jenkins' Ear, the British adopted a tactic previously demonstrated at Portobelo, destroying the fortifications, seizing the artillery, and capturing two Spanish patrol boats.

Colonial authorities appointed Admiral Blas de Lezo to command the defense of the fortified city. A seasoned marine with a long record of European naval combat dating back to the War of the Spanish Succession, Lezo had previously confronted European pirates in the Caribbean and Pacific and faced Barbary pirates in the Mediterranean. He received assistance from Melchor de Navarrete and Carlos Desnaux in coordinating the defense. The force was organized around a squadron of six ships of the line, comprising Galicia as the flagship, along with San Felipe, San Carlos, África, Dragón, and Conquistador. This naval contingent was supported by about 3,000 soldiers, 600 militiamen, and a cadre of native Indian archers.

Higher National Diploma (HND) is a qualification awarded by polytechnics as a progression from the National Diploma (ND), with the ND typically regarded as equivalent to an associate degree. Both ND and HND programs generally run for two years, followed by an industrial training placement of about one year after the ND, giving a total duration of roughly four to five years from the start of the ND to HND completion. Although the HND is sometimes treated as equivalent to a university bachelor’s degree, this equivalence is contested. Historically, HND holders faced discrimination in employment and were often excluded from higher managerial roles; in response, the federal government has sought to reduce the dichotomy, and several government agencies, including paramilitary bodies, have begun hiring or upgrading HND holders to align them with degree holders. Proponents contend that HND graduates can outperform university counterparts in the same field owing to more extensive hands-on training and adherence to industry standards, noting similar or overlapping entry requirements and study durations, with some claims of higher credit units for HND. Admission to the HND requires completion of two years of the OND (ordinary National Diploma), which itself is considered equivalent to an associate degree. HND curricula emphasize technical training with limited liberal arts components and are built around industry standards from the outset; by the final year, students are prepared to practice in their field with substantial practical experience, and some programs may exceed 120 credit units.

In Malaysia, the Higher National Diploma is commonly regarded as equivalent to a general diploma, though the formal equivalence remains ambiguously defined under older standards issued by the Public Service Department of Malaysia. This uncertain equivalence can place HND graduates in competition with general diploma holders when seeking admission to Malaysia’s public universities, particularly for entry-level undergraduate programs. Consequently, Malaysian HND graduates are often advised to pursue a UK degree or to enroll in a specialist university program that can recognize and credit the HND toward further study.

Dave Cobb began collaborating with Jason Isbell in 2013, a partnership that led to the recording of Isbell's album Southeastern at Cobb's own home and studio. The project was designed to achieve an intimate, acoustic, organic, live sound with a warm character, aiming to evoke the feel of Simon & Garfunkel's Bridge Over Troubled Water through an unconventional recording environment. In the same year, Cobb also produced Whiskey Myers' third studio album, Early Morning Shakes.

Dave Cobb is an American record producer whose work has significant influence in country and roots music. RCA Studio A was saved from demolition, preserving a key Nashville facility for artists and producers. In 2016 Cobb began a long-term residency at RCA Studio A, establishing a stable base for his projects. His collaborations with Chris Stapleton include the 2017 albums From A Room: Volume 1 and From A Room: Volume 2, which were recorded at RCA Studio A under Cobb's production. The Oak Ridge Boys released 17th Avenue Revival in 2018, a title that references the studio’s location on 17th Avenue in Nashville, underscoring Cobb’s role in shaping its late-2010s output.

Nikolai Shchelokov was promoted to the rank of commissar in the Red Army at the outset of World War II. He also continued to hold the post of chairman of the City Soviet of Dnipropetrovsk. From 1941 to 1946, he served as a political commissar in the army, providing political leadership and ideological guidance within the armed forces during the war years.

Nikolai Shchelokov, who held the post of interior minister, was dismissed on 17 December 1982, about five weeks after Leonid Brezhnev's death, amid corruption charges. He was replaced by Vitaly Fedorchuk, who would subsequently become chairman of the KGB. The personnel change was widely viewed as influenced by Yuri Andropov, who had just been elected general secretary and had previously headed the KGB, a post he held before Fedorchuk’s appointment. Andropov was known as an opponent of the Dnipropetrovsk Mafia. Shchelokov's removal thus represented a high-profile effort to address corruption and to recalibrate security leadership during the transition under Andropov.

In 1986, the Chinese government designated Kashgar as a city of historical and cultural significance. Since the 1990s, Kashgar and the surrounding regions have been sites of Uyghur unrest. In 2008, two Uyghur men carried out a coordinated attack on police officers that involved a vehicle, an improvised explosive device, and knives.

Kashgar is situated at a historic crossroads of diverse cultures and empires. Throughout its history, the city has been ruled by successive powers, including Chinese, Turkic, Mongol, and Tibetan empires. It has also served as the site of battles among various groups on the steppes.

ISO 128 is an international standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). It delineates the general principles governing the presentation of information in technical drawings and addresses the graphical depiction of objects within these drawings.

ISO 128 is the foundational standard in the ISO 128 series that superseded the earlier DIN 6 standard governing drawings, projections, and views, reflecting the shift from national to international norms in technical drawing. DIN 6 was first published in 1922 and was later revised in 1950 and 1968. ISO 128 was introduced in 1982. The standard consists of 15 pages and specifies general presentation principles for orthographic projection methods.

Stained glass is formed by cutting and painting individual glass pieces, which are assembled by sliding them into H-shaped lead cames. All joints are soldered to secure the panel. A soft, oily cement or mastic is applied between the glass and the cames to prevent rattling and to weatherproof the window. In modern practice, copper foil is sometimes used in place of lead. For further technical details, see Came glasswork.

In Iran, stained glass achieved notable development during the Safavid (1501–1736) and Zand (1751–1794) dynasties, a period that saw its flourishing in Persian architectural decoration. The distinctive Persian stained glass sash windows are known as Orosi windows, with alternative transliterations including Arasi and Orsi. These openings were employed not only for aesthetic enhancement but also to regulate incoming sunlight, helping to moderate the hot, semi-arid climate in which they were used.

During the late 1960s, Tammy Wynette met George Jones on tour; at the time Jones maintained a cordial relationship with Wynette's husband, Don Chapel, and the three frequently spent time together. Jones aided Wynette when one of her children was hospitalized with food poisoning, and the following day he visited Wynette and Chapel at their home. Chapel grew irritated as Wynette continued playing Jones's music and directed derogatory remarks toward her. In a moment of anger, Jones overturned the dining room table. Jones and Wynette then confessed their love to Chapel, after which Jones escorted Wynette and her three daughters out of the Chapel residence, and they never returned.

During this period, Wynette experienced a sequence of personal incidents, including short-term relationships, house burglaries, and alleged kidnappings. She also developed health problems that led to dependence on painkillers. Despite these difficulties, her commercial momentum continued, with none of her solo singles reaching the top of the charts, though several did break into the top ten. In 1977, two of her singles—(Let's Get Together) One Last Time and One of a Kind—both peaked at number six on the U.S. country chart. By 1979, three additional solo releases—Womanhood, They Call It Making Love, and No One Else in the World—also reached the top ten.

Burgess Meredith served with the United States Army Air Forces during World War II. In 1944 he was released from active duty to participate in the wartime short The Story of G.I. Joe, in which he portrayed the war correspondent Ernie Pyle, and he was discharged from the USAAF in 1945.

Burgess Meredith had a multifaceted career that included extensive work in voice-over and production. He lent his voice to the narration of the 1945 war film A Walk in the Sun. He also served as the narrator for the 1983 feature adaptation of The Twilight Zone, reflecting his long-standing association with the series. Meredith was a prominent voice actor in television advertising, providing narration for commercials for brands such as Bulova, Honda, Pioneer, Stokely-Van Camp, United Airlines, and Freakies cereal. Additionally, he produced and narrated the 1950 short film Works of Calder, directed by Herbert Matter with a score by John Cage.

North Frisian is typified by pronounced multilingualism among its speakers: all speakers are bilingual in North Frisian and German; many also speak Low German, making a substantial portion trilingual. In the region along the Danish border, quadrilingualism—encompassing North Frisian, Standard German, Low German, and South Jutlandic—was historically widespread.

North Frisian is a minority language spoken in Germany, with around 10,000 speakers in the region of North Frisia. It forms part of the West Germanic branch of the Frisian language group. The language comprises ten dialects, which are organized into insular and mainland categories.

UTC+01:00 denotes a time offset of one hour ahead of Coordinated Universal Time. Under ISO 8601, timestamps bearing this offset are formatted with the +01:00 suffix, for example 2019-02-07T23:28:34+01:00. The offset represents a moment that is one hour ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) and UTC. In practical use, it is synonymous with British Summer Time (BST), the daylight saving time observed in the United Kingdom when clocks are advanced by one hour.

UTC+01:00, known as Central European Time, provides the temporal frame for the cities listed in this article. The geographic scope spans Western, Central, and Southern Europe, encompassing numerous countries and microstates. The compilation includes major capitals and large metropolitan centers such as Berlin, Paris, Madrid, Rome, Vienna, Prague, Warsaw, Milan, Barcelona, Marseille, Lyon, Naples, Venice, Florence, Turin, Frankfurt, Munich, and Hamburg, among others. It also represents microstates and special territories, including Vatican City, San Marino, Andorra, Monaco; as well as Liechtenstein towns Vaduz and Schaan, and Maltese localities like Valletta and St. Paul’s Bay. Some entries refer to districts or localities within cities rather than formal city names, for example Monte Carlo, Monaco-Ville, and Westside. Overall, the list illustrates CET coverage across a broad range of European regions, incorporating both national capitals and other principal urban centers.

Yurok language employs a small set of past-oriented markers that encode distinct temporal and aspectual nuances. The marker ho denotes a completed action that occurred in the past. By contrast, the form kic signals a past event whose effects persist into the present, indicating ongoing relevance rather than a simple, finished moment. The marker wo is used in contexts involving negation or unreal or counterfactual conditions, marking a past event within those hypothetical or negative frames. A final form, ?ap, conveys that an action began in the past, emphasizing initiation rather than its completion. Together, these markers illuminate a layered past-tense system that differentiates finished events, continuing effects, negated or hypothetical scenarios, and actions initiated in the past.

Yurok, the language of the Yurok people of northern California, is generally regarded as a language isolate. Its morphology features a range of affixation strategies, including both prefixation and infixation in word formation, and it relies on inflection to mark grammatical categories such as person and number, with some analyses extending to tense or mood. The phonological and morphophonemic system includes vowel harmony in certain contexts and vowel alternations known as ablaut that accompany derivational or inflectional changes. Consonantal alternation also occurs as part of systematic morphophonemic processes that affect related forms. Reduplication is employed for various grammatical and lexical functions, contributing to aspectual or intensificatory distinctions. Together, these properties reflect Yurok’s complex morphophonology and its distinctive typological profile within the broader landscape of Pacific Coast languages.

Kwela originated in southern Africa and developed into a distinctive street music style known for its bright horn-driven tunes. Its later adaptations and broader African folk idioms helped permeate Western music, influencing a range of artists and genres. Among the most cited examples of this cross-cultural exchange are the Bert Kaempfert Orchestra’s A Swingin’ Safari (1962) and Paul Simon’s Graceland (1986). These influences contributed to shaping contemporary South African music, especially in jazz, endowing it with a recognizable sound and lilting swagger. The international reach of Kwela is also reflected in The Piranhas’ 1980 UK Top Ten hit Tom Hark, which was based on an earlier Kwela hit from the 1950s.

Kwela is a South African street music genre that centers on the pennywhistle as a principal instrument. The pennywhistle is affordable and portable, enabling broad participation and mobility for performers. It is versatile, functioning well in both solo performance and ensemble settings. Flutes of various kinds have long been traditional in the northern regions of South Africa, contributing to the pennywhistle’s popularity within the genre. In addition, the pennywhistle facilitated rapid adaptation of folk tunes into music with marabi influences, helping to shape the distinctive sound of kwela.

CFTE was a Canadian radio station based in Vancouver, British Columbia, broadcasting on the AM frequency 1410 kHz. It was branded as BNN Bloomberg Radio 1410 and was owned by Bell Media. Its last broadcast format was business news.

On July 12, 2006, CHUM Limited announced that it would be acquired by CTVglobemedia, the owner of CTV. The proposed transaction would bring CHUM’s Vancouver radio stations, including CFUN, as well as all of its Victoria stations, under CTVglobemedia’s control. As part of the deal involving the Citytv system, CKVU was to be sold to Rogers Media, a condition tied to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission’s approval of the CHUM-CTVglobemedia arrangement. The acquisition was completed when CTVglobemedia officially became the owner of CFUN and the majority of CHUM’s properties on June 22, 2007.

Isadore "Izzy" Elliot Handler was born on April 9, 1916, in Chicago to a Jewish family whose Ukrainian Jewish parents largely spoke Yiddish at home. He grew up on the west side of Denver, Colorado, and studied industrial design at the Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, California. In 1929 he met Ruth Mosko at a B'nai B'rith dance for teenagers; the pair dated on and off and married in June 1938. Shortly after their marriage, Ruth urged him to adopt his middle name Elliot and to change his surname, a precaution prompted by concerns about antisemitism, and he became Elliot Handler. The couple had two children, Barbara and Kenneth; Barbara would become the namesake of the Barbie doll and Kenneth the namesake of the Ken doll. While a developing art student and designer of light fixtures, Handler partnered with Harold Matson to design a realistic-looking miniature piano that attracted roughly 300,000 orders, but the partners mispriced it and incurred a loss of a dime on each unit produced.

Elliot Handler is credited with developing the first talking doll, Chatty Cathy, which used a pull-string mechanism to speak phrases. This breakthrough is widely regarded as having revolutionized the toy industry. Under Mattel, the company continued to release additional talking figures, including Chatty Baby, Tiny Chatty Baby, and Charmin' Chatty, and also produced dolls modeled after popular cartoon characters Bugs Bunny and Porky Pig as well as television figures Herman Munster and Mr. Ed.

In February 2019, GOG.com announced staff reductions and the discontinuation of its Fair Price Package program. The program had previously offered store credit equivalent to the difference in price for a game purchased in a higher-priced regional market.

On 26 August 2015, Bethesda Softworks joined GOG.com, expanding the platform's catalog to include a selection of classic titles such as Doom and Quake. The Fallout series was also added, with these games having previously been available on GOG under Interplay before ownership of the rights changed. Additionally, a number of classic The Elder Scrolls titles were incorporated into GOG.com's catalog.

The Kingdom of Illyria encompassed a diverse set of territories in and around the Habsburg lands, including the modern Austrian state of Carinthia; western and central Slovenia—Carniola (with its capital at Ljubljana), the Slovenian Littoral (Goriška and Slovenian Istria), and Slovenian Carinthia; parts of northwestern Croatia corresponding to present-day Istria County, as well as the Kvarner Gulf islands of Krk, Cres, and Lošinj; and extending into northeastern Italy in the eastern Friuli–Venezia Giulia, comprising the former provinces of Trieste and Gorizia, along with small portions of Udine around Tarvisio and Cervignano del Friuli. In 1822, the Civil Croatia territory lying between the right bank of the Sava and Rijeka was merged into the Habsburg Kingdom of Croatia.
